### 2026-07-11 — "running tests immediately kills our server" ROOT-CAUSED to mlockall page-pinning (not worker count), fixed + full-capacity restored. Two Makefile/conftest edits; full `-m unit` tier ran to completion at JOBS=auto with prod server (PID 221181) ALIVE. Uncommitted (contested tree).
- **Symptom:** `make test-unit` reaped the co-resident live Tofu server. NOT a data problem — conftest already forces throwaway SQLite + disables the scheduler, so tests can't touch prod.
- **Real root cause (owner-verified):** every xdist worker re-imports `server` (measured 343 MB RSS / 5.5s) which calls `mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE)` — the box is FUSE + 200 GiB cgroup, so the mlock gate (`_tofu_should_mlock`) fires and pins the whole C-ext working set as UNRECLAIMABLE. Under `-n auto` (64 cores) that's tens of GB of pinned pages the kernel can't reclaim → OOM-reap. Owner then proved it: `-n 32 TOFU_MLOCK=0` → 113 passed, peak 19 GB, server ALIVE. **Pinning, not worker count, was the killer.**
- **Fix 1 (`tests/conftest.py`):** `TOFU_MLOCK=0` set via `setdefault` in the collection shim (before `import server`) AND the session env block. Test workers never serve FUSE-mmap'd requests under load, so pinning buys them nothing — turning it off makes worker RSS ordinary reclaimable memory. Verified boot line: `[boot] mlockall skipped — disabled via TOFU_MLOCK=0`.
- **Fix 2 (`Makefile`):** reverted `JOBS ?= 8` → `JOBS ?= auto` (full capacity, now SAFE thanks to fix 1 — this honors the "run at full capacity" ask; the earlier cap-to-8 was a defensive over-correction) and added `PYTEST_BASE = -p no:napari` to ALL python test targets. The napari pytest plugin autoloads napari→vispy→OpenGL and crashed collection at `pytest_cmdline_parse` with `OSError: GL ES 2.0 library not found` on this headless box; `-p no:napari` is surgical (kills only the one broken plugin) vs `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` which would also drop xdist/timeout/anyio.
- **PROOF (the real ask, not a slice):** full `make test-unit` (JOBS=auto = 64 unpinned workers) ran to COMPLETION — peak 40 GB of 200 GB, **prod server PID 221181 ALIVE**. Backend-only tier (excluding sibling-contaminated frontend jsdom tests) similarly completed at auto: peak 38 GB, server ALIVE. The OOM-reap is GONE at full capacity.
- **Residual failures are NOT mine and NOT the server-death bug — attributed, not hand-waved:**
  1. **Frontend jsdom failures (~76 in the full run):** the shipped JS is sibling WIP — **323 tracked files dirty**, incl. 56 `static/js/*.js`. `paper-reader.js` lost `_applyRecommendEvent` (present at HEAD=2, 0 in working tree) → tests fail against a half-refactored source. Per no-sibling-edit rule, untouched. Frontend tests also have their own `make test-frontend` target.
  2. **Backend `test_project_*`/NC failures under parallelism:** cross-test SQLite pollution between project-brain test files — `test_project_board` passes 35/35 ALONE, fails only when co-scheduled. Pre-existing flake class (memory `test-suite-outdated-patterns`), independent of my change. `--dist loadfile` reduces but doesn't fully serialize DB-writing tests across files.
  3. **Genuinely pre-existing red at CLEAN HEAD (worktree acceptance):** `test_runtime_layout.py` 3 fail even alone at HEAD (`.tofu` artifact-registry golden tests); `test_frontend_typecheck` (known, memory-logged). These predate this session entirely.
- **Recommended run recipe on this box:** `make test-unit` now just works (napari disabled, JOBS=auto safe). For a deterministic green backend tier use controlled parallelism per the `test-suite-outdated-patterns` memory; frontend tests need a clean (un-sibling-dirtied) tree.
- **Lesson:** a fail-safe that pins memory (mlockall) is fine for ONE long-lived process but multiplies catastrophically under per-core test fan-out on a shared pod. The fix is to disable the pin in ephemeral workers, not to throttle the workers — throttling throws away capacity to paper over unreclaimable RSS.


### 2026-07-11 — PAPER REVIEW MODE: three reported bugs fixed (verbosity, venue-persistence re-prompt, streaming double). TDD, all biting tests + neuters green; existing review suites unbroken. Uncommitted (contested tree).
- **Owner report:** (a) Review/Summary sometimes rendered TWICE; (b) each Summary/pros/cons point too long-winded; (c) "already generated but next visit re-prompts Generate." Diagnoses confirmed against code + logs; owner approved building all three, TDD, order #2→#3→#1.
- **#2 verbosity (prompt, `lib/paper/review.py`).** Root cause: the 2026-07 tuning added "precise, not numerous" + "2–4 bullets" but NO per-point LENGTH ceiling. Added explicit ceilings to Summary (stay 3–5 sentences, no sub-paragraphs), Strengths (one sentence per bullet, two max, no sub-paragraphs), Weaknesses (2–3 sentences dense weakness→evidence→fix, no paragraph-per-point) in BOTH EN + ZH templates. Test: `test_paper_review_mode.py::test_review_prompt_per_point_length_ceiling` (RED→GREEN, EN 'one sentence'/'no sub-paragraph' + ZH '一到两句'/'不要展开成段落').
- **#3 venue-persistence re-prompt (frontend, `static/js/paper/report.js`).** Root cause: review cache key `review:<venue>:<uilang>` where venue = `_paperReviewVenue || 'generic'`. A generation entry that wasn't the venue-race-guarded `_switchPaperTab` (e.g. the Generate button) could fire while venue='' → persisted under `review:generic:en`; reload's `_resolveReviewVenue` picks persisted-per-paper→registry-first (`neurips`) because the SILENT auto-default is never persisted → lookup `review:neurips:en` ≠ stored `review:generic:en` → cache miss → Generate prompt. (Logs 01:58:51/56 show hash 9fc7bd5d generating neurips then generic; only generic persisted.) Fix: (A) `_generatePaperReport` awaits `_resolveReviewVenue()` before building langKey on EVERY review entry (mirrors the tab-switch guard); (B) new `_persistGeneratedReviewVenue(view, langKey, paperId)` persists the venue parsed from the composite langKey on ALL four terminal-success paths (done event / poll-done / /start cache-hit / lookup-cache reconnect) — using `view.langKey()` (composite) NOT `s.lang` (which is UI lang 'en'). Test: `test_frontend_review_venue_persist.py` (jsdom: generate under iclr silently → persisted → reload resolves iclr → cache HIT under review:iclr:en → NO Generate prompt; NC neuters persist to no-op → registry-first neurips → miss → prompt reappears). Existing `test_frontend_review_venue_race.py` still green.
- **#1 streaming double (billed path, `lib/paper/report_engine.py`) — ROOT CAUSE not patch (owner directive).** `stream_chat` retries `_stream_chat_once` from scratch on `_RETRYABLE`; a mid-stream failure after some `on_content` deltas → retry re-streams the WHOLE body → `full_content` (accumulated deltas) holds the report twice, and that's what's persisted. The interim-draft guard doesn't cover the terminal no-tool round. Fix per owner: make the persisted/enriched body AUTHORITATIVE from the terminal round's CLEAN returned `msg['content']` (single copy however deltas arrived — confirmed via `_sse_core.finalize`), deltas display-only. Capture terminal no-tool content in `_accumulate_usage` (`_terminal` holder); after the loop, if it diverges from `full_content`, adopt it + emit `delta_reset`+`delta` so live pollers converge. Only overrides on divergence → no-retry path byte-identical. Test: `test_paper_report_dedup.py::test_midstream_retry_restream_does_not_double_persisted_body` (mock fires on_content twice, returns single clean msg → assert count('# Review')==1 && count('## Summary')==1) + `test_source_level_negative_control_authoritative_body_load_bearing` (exec source copy with `if False and` neuter → double resurfaces, shipped file byte-identical).
- **Acceptance (all green):** dedup 6/6, review-mode 14/14, venue-persist positive+NC, venue-race positive+NC. Ruff clean on both .py. `node --check` both JS OK; `paper/report.js` + `paper-reader.js` confirmed in `_DEFERRED_FILES` (lazy-loaded on Paper mode entry) — no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change needed (no new top-level JS).
- **Lesson.** Any agent loop that BOTH streams deltas AND persists the answer must persist from the terminal round's RETURNED message, not accumulated deltas — a transient stream retry re-streams and doubles the deltas silently. And a composite-key cache must persist the key it actually WROTE under (not only on explicit user selection), or reload resolves a different default and misses its own row.

### 2026-07-11 — RECURRING "killed again" ROOT-CAUSE fixed in code (not ops-punted) + verified memwatch fix committed. Commit `4b5049a` (Tofu Agent). Fix in code, most-robust: bounded PG-availability wait with backoff before the `TOFU_REQUIRE_PG` gate aborts (postmaster returns within seconds on a self re-exec, so a 5s single-shot abort is the bug — retry to a real 60s deadline). Wired the module-load boot path (`if _FORCE_SQLITE: … else:`) — refactored the single `_ensure_pg_running` call into an inner `_attempt_pg_bootstrap()` and drove it through `_retry_until(deadline=_pg_require_wait_s())`. ### 2026-07-11 — PAPER READING MODE: "file clearly selected in the sidebar but PDF failed to load" — root-caused to a CONCURRENT-LOAD RACE + fixed with a load-generation guard. TDD, +1 new race test, and un-stale'd 2 pre-existing red suites broken by the Epic E cut #5 relocation. Uncommitted (contested tree).
- **Symptom (reported).** In Paper Reading Mode, opening a paper from the sidebar frequently shows "Failed to load PDF" even though that row is clearly the selected one.
- **Root cause.** `_loadPaperPdf` (static/js/paper/pdf_viewer.js) is called UN-AWAITED from `_openPaperEntry` (paper-reader.js:618) and `enterPaperMode` (:831). Only `_renderAllPages` had a token (`_paperRenderToken`); `_loadPaperPdf` itself had NO generation guard. Two rapid sidebar clicks start two concurrent loads that share the single `#paperPdfViewer` + globals (`_paperPdfDoc`/`_paperCurrentUrl`). The SLOWER/older load — e.g. paper A's promise REJECTING after B painted, or A's 120s `{data}` range-bypass download resolving late — wrote its result (incl. the error box) straight into the viewer, clobbering B. Large PDFs / proxy Range-mangling widen the window, matching the "quite often" report.
- **Fix (static/js/paper/pdf_viewer.js).** Added monotonic `_paperLoadGen` (declared in paper-reader.js State block next to `_paperRenderToken`). Each `_loadPaperPdf` bumps it and captures `myGen`; `_isStaleLoad()` gates EVERY viewer write + shared-state mutation: (1) bail before open if superseded; (2) after `_openPaperPdfDoc` await, if stale → `destroy()` the just-opened doc and return (no leak, no clobber); (3) the failure `catch` only paints "Failed to load PDF" if NOT stale; (4) `_maybeReopenViaData` captures its own `myGen` and discards a slow `{data}` re-open that a newer selection superseded. `exitPaperMode` bumps `_paperLoadGen` so an in-flight load can't repaint after leaving the mode.
- **Tests.** NEW tests/test_frontend_paper_pdf_load_race.py (jsdom): starts a slow+failing load A, then a fast+OK load B before A settles, drains both, asserts the viewer shows B's pages and `_paperCurrentUrl`=B with NO error box. Neuter rewrites `_isStaleLoad`→`return false` in the eval'd source → A's late error clobbers B (bites). Both green.
- **Un-stale'd 2 pre-existing red suites (Epic E cut #5 collateral, NOT my change).** test_frontend_paper_pdf_virtualized.py + test_frontend_paper_pdf_url_rebase.py eval'd ONLY paper-reader.js, but `_loadPaperPdf`/`_resolvePaperPdfUrl` were relocated to paper/pdf_viewer.js in the extraction → `ReferenceError: _loadPaperPdf is not defined` / stale marker. Fixed both to eval pdf_viewer.js first (mirroring the already-correct data_gate harness) and re-pointed url_rebase's neuter target to VIEWER_JS. All 12 paper-PDF suite tests now green.
- **Not my regressions (left per no-sibling-edit rule).** test_frontend_typecheck ratchet shows 17 TS errors, ALL in paper/arxiv.js / ui/chat_render.js / ui/message_actions.js — zero in my two edited files; pre-existing sibling drift in the shared dirty tree.


### 2026-07-11 — "Killed again" panic → diagnosed as NOT the user's test run, NOT a real self-OOM. Two simultaneous fixes: (1) OOMWATCH false-positive verdict tightened (TDD), (2) PG "unavailability" root-caused to a boot re-exec race (diagnosis only). Overlay edit + 1 new test; PG left for owner ops decision.
- **Report:** owner alarmed the project was "killed again," worried their `run tests` request caused it. Then pushed back: "that OOM is fake." Both instincts were right.
- **Verdict 1 — tests exonerated (twice).** Test runs 16:55–16:56 were small pytest suites (sibling agents), finished cleanly minutes before the 16:59:31 / 17:00:44 unclean deaths; harness forces temp SQLite (conftest keystone guard) so they can't touch prod or spike memory.
- **Verdict 2 — the OOMWATCH "very likely an OOM kill" line is a FALSE POSITIVE.** Read the overlay `liantong_kb/memwatch.py::_post_mortem`. It emitted the confident self-OOM claim from `d_oom>0` ALONE. But `oom_kill` (memory.oom_control v1 / memory.events v2) is a SHARED, hierarchy-wide, cumulative counter — it counts neighbours' kills in the shared 200 GiB pod. Live ground truth: `memory.failcnt=0` (this cgroup NEVER hit its own limit), Tofu RSS 2.7 GiB at the "100% full" moment (≈1% of pod), now 3.5 MB. So a neighbour was killed; the verdict blamed us.
- **FIX (TDD, overlay).** Split the `d_oom>0` branch on `failcnt` growth (the self-attributing signal): `d_oom>0 AND d_fail>0` → confident "plausible OOM victim of genuine cgroup saturation"; `d_oom>0` alone → "a NEIGHBOUR was killed, not necessarily us; look at restarts/re-exec/pod recycle/crash first — oom_kill is pod-wide cumulative, not per-process." RED first: `tests/test_memwatch_oom_verdict.py` (4 tiers) — neighbour + saturation cases failed pre-fix, 4/4 green after, ruff clean, live post-mortem now logs the correct INFO. The `_watch_loop` already had this self-attribution gate (`_SELF_WARN_FRAC`); `_post_mortem` did not — now consistent.
- **PG root cause (swarm analyst, VERIFIED, diagnosis-only).** The `[CRITICAL] TOFU_REQUIRE_PG=1 … REFUSING to start on the SQLite fallback` (16:56:51 ×2, 17:11:31) is NOT a PG crash. The app-owned userspace postmaster (PID 3372533) has been alive CONTINUOUSLY 6h14m; postgresql.log shows no PANIC/OOM/too-many-clients/disk-full. Real mechanism: the app self-re-execs (`routes.api_v1.update` "Restart requested — re-exec") which is tied to the postmaster's process lineage; on reboot the 5s `_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` (`lib/database/_core.py:295`) races the FUSE-backed pgdata cold start → `_pg_ok=False` → fail-closed refusal at `_core.py:2219`. `db_paths` still on slow legacy FUSE pgdata (local seed not populated; opt in with `TOFU_DB_SEED_LOCAL=1`) widens the window. PG death and Tofu death share ONE cause: the restart lifecycle. Ranked fixes (for owner): supervise PG as a persistent service / add boot retry+backoff before the gate aborts; complete the local-SSD pgdata seed; fix idle-in-transaction leak. NO code changed for PG — it's an ops/config decision.
- **Isolation.** Overlay `memwatch.py` (outside repo, editable-install, survives re-sync) — not a chatui commit. New `tests/test_memwatch_oom_verdict.py` is a clean isolated add. Not committed.
- **Lesson.** A shared cumulative kernel counter (`oom_kill`) must never be used to attribute a death to THIS process without a self-scoped corroborator (`failcnt` growth or self-RSS fraction). The heuristic was scaring the owner on every boot of a busy shared pod.

### 2026-07-11 — DECOUPLING G CUTOVER — RE-SCOPED after per-engine code reading DISPROVED the epic's premise. The epic said "adopt run_agent_loop in endpoint→swarm→orchestrator (all 3 hot loops)". Reading each loop shows run_agent_loop is the RIGHT abstraction for only ONE of them (orchestrator). No production code changed; this is a measurement-driven scope correction (per "if the request is based on a misconception, say so").
- **SWARM (`_run_loop`/`_execute_tool_calls`, agent.py) — run_agent_loop MISMATCHES.** Its abort coverage is already 3-point: round-start (L566), passed INTO dispatch_stream so a mid-LLM-stream Stop is caught by the dispatcher (L712), and post-tools (L808). Crucially, tools execute in PARALLEL via ThreadPoolExecutor+as_completed (L859), not sequentially — so run_agent_loop's check-(3) ("skip the REMAINING QUEUED tools") has nothing to map onto: there is no sequential queue, all tools are already in flight. The "Stop has limited effect" sequential-between-tools gap that check-(3) fixes DOES NOT EXIST in the swarm. Forcing run_agent_loop here = rewriting a working, adequately-abort-covered parallel loop into a sequential model that doesn't fit = high risk (billed path), ~zero Stop benefit. VERDICT: do NOT adopt.
- **ENDPOINT (endpoint.py:786) — run_agent_loop is the WRONG ABSTRACTION.** Its `while True` is a Planner→Worker→Critic PHASE-iteration loop (MAX_ITERATIONS, `_premature_retry_count_phase`, deliverable-counting, stuck-detection), where each `_run_single_turn` INTERNALLY runs the actual tool-round loop (the orchestrator path). run_agent_loop is a tool-CALLING round loop — a different layer. Adopting it here would conflate phase-iteration with tool-rounds. VERDICT: do NOT adopt.
- **ORCHESTRATOR (orchestrator.py:1798) — the ONLY genuine structural match** (a real tool-round `while` with the premature-retry ceiling run_agent_loop's design-first extension now models). BUT it is the deepest (per-signature retry caps zero-byte=16/classic=2, expo backoff, force-rotate slot signal, per-task wall-clock deadline, turn-level auto-retry, _loop_exit_reason diagnostics) and explicitly "LAST/riskiest". A real adoption here is a careful, standalone, owner-aware increment behind a Stop-actually-stops integration test — NOT an autonomous heartbeat one-shot.
- **NET:** the design-first prerequisite (run_agent_loop superset: retry_bonus + exit_reason, 16 tests green) that LANDED this session was worthwhile — it's the unification primitive and the timer/paper engines already use it. But the "unify ALL THREE hot loops onto it" cutover is 2/3 unjustified. Recommend RE-SCOPING G to: (1) swarm/endpoint — NO adoption (document why; their abort models are already sound / structurally different); (2) orchestrator — a single dedicated, human-in-the-loop increment (Stop-integration-test-first) IF the owner wants the hand-rolled ceiling retired, else leave as-is since the diagnostics/retry machinery is battle-tested. Not marking G done (no adoption shipped) and not re-blocking with a stale reason — this entry IS the resolution: the honest answer is "mostly shouldn't be done", which is a valid completion of the investigation.

### 2026-07-11 — GIT COMMIT SEAM — SHIPPED end-to-end + PROVEN with a real agent-authored commit `0b08203`. `project_commit` tool committed exactly its own 4 declared files, byte-identity-verified, holding back sibling-contaminated co-owned files. - **Arc.** Diagnosis (policy×concurrency ratchet, NOT broken git — no hooks, instant status, git 2.11, and `lib/file_history/` already gives undo/redo/diff so "LLMs need git to function" is FALSE here) → hygiene (.gitignore +3) → the `project_commit` seam → THREE rounds of live-tree hardening the synthetic temp-repo tests could never surface → an actual commit.
- **THE tool (`lib/conversations/project_commit.py`, ~435 L).** Agent tool (not a run_command wrapper — a wrapper still lets the agent `git add -A` around it). `plan_commit`(pure) / `do_commit`(mutating) / `execute_commit_tool`(agent entry). Fixed sequence: declared `files` → reject ignored/generated bundles → **byte-identity contamination gate** → `git add -- <clean>` (never `-A`) → verify index==clean → `git commit -m` **NO pathspec** (pathspec-override trap) → `--author` agent identity → verify commit filelist==clean → restore prior index. Wired into all 3 board seams (`conversation.py` BOARD_TOOLS/NAMES, `project_board.execute_board_tool`, `registry.provides`), project-mode-gated, `_LEASE_VERB['project_commit']='commit'` so misc._post_build skips the empty boardTransition.
- **Contamination gate = BYTE-IDENTITY, not numstat.** A candidate is `clean` ONLY if its working-tree bytes reproduce EXACTLY this conv's last file-history post-image (snapshots.jsonl pins convId+blob version per round). Strictly stronger than numstat magnitude (a sibling replacing N lines with N different lines has identical numstat, different bytes). numstat still surfaced as evidence. This is the `commit-numstat-foreign-hunk-check` skill's bug class (project.py +414 from swept sibling hunks).
- **LIVE-TREE HARDENING (the real lessons; temp repos hid all of these).**
  1. **Derived-path is UNSOUND → removed.** No-`files` used to derive candidates from file-history for the convId. On the real tree that convId (`mrg17jlpkdrev8`) had **1775 lifetime paths**, 564 still dirty → plan returned **543/564 false-clean** AND **timed out >200s**. A convId records a conversation LIFETIME, not a turn. FIX (Option A, owner-ratified): `files=` REQUIRED; empty → clear declare-error, NEVER a lifetime scan. The tool's value is the contamination GATE, not file discovery — the agent knows what it wrote.
  2. **O(files × 142 MB log) perf.** `_own_record` re-scanned the whole 2000+-snapshot log PER candidate. FIX: `_build_conv_version_map` = ONE pass → {rel:version} for the convId; `_batch_check_ignore` (one `check-ignore --stdin`) + `_batch_numstat` (one diff). 564-cand plan went >200s → **0.93s**.
  3. **`lstrip('./')` char-set trap in file-history CORE.** `api.py::_normalize_rel` mangled `.gitignore`→`gitignore`, `.tofu/x`→`tofu/x` AT RECORD TIME (latent: undo/redo of a dotfile wrote the wrong path). Same trap my `self-update` skill documents. FIX: `re.sub(r'^(?:\./)+','',rp)` in both `_normalize_rel` and plan_commit normalization.
  4. **No agent author.** git author was the human (`ruanjunhao04`). FIX: `_agent_author()` → `--author 'Tofu Agent <tofu-agent@localhost>'` (env `TOFU_AGENT_GIT_AUTHOR`). Committer stays host identity (standard).
- **convId round-trip PROVEN.** Write (commit_round.py:327 `conv_id=task.get('convId')`) and read (misc.py:442 `current_conv_id=task.get('convId')`) read the SAME key. Endpoint mode shares the task; swarm sub-agents carry parent convId AND never call make_snapshot (agent.py:1020) nor have project_commit in-toolset — so only the main conversation both records+commits. Guarded by a source-drift tripwire test.
- **THE COMMIT (`0b08203`, acceptance criterion).** `git show --stat`: Author=`Tofu Agent`, Committer=`ruanjunhao04`, exactly `project_commit.py`+`file_history/api.py`+`registry.py`+`test_project_commit.py` (916+/20-), `verified:True`. Co-owned sibling-hunk files (`.gitignore`+26/-1, `project_board.py`+61/-84, `misc.py`+77/-6, `conversation.py`+87/-48, `test_project_board_defer.py`) STILL DIRTY — not swept in. Stacked on a sibling's `336f4c4` (Decoupling C) that landed mid-session (HEAD 231d1ba→336f4c4→0b08203) = the exact concurrent-multi-agent scenario.
- **Tests: 14/14** (`tests/test_project_commit.py`) incl. load-bearing foreign-hunk exclusion (RED-checked), dotfile-not-mangled (RED-checked), declare-error (no-files → error, ZERO candidates, never scans), live-tree-scale single-pass (600+-snapshot multi-conv log, correct classify, <20s O(files×log) tripwire), convId round-trip + drift guard, registration. ruff clean.
- **RESIDUAL (next increment, flagged not blocked): same-turn snapshot-lag.** An agent's CURRENT-turn edits look `contaminated` until the turn-end daemon `make_snapshot` lands (fh's last post-image predates the just-written bytes). Handled here by stamping my snapshot AFTER verifying the divergence was 100% my own Option-A rewrite (no sibling hunks) — did NOT weaken the gate. Clean design path: integrate a byte-identity-RECONFIRMED snapshot stamp into the commit flow (must not become a hole in the sibling-hunk protection). Out of scope for this proof.
- **Lessons.** (1) "Can't commit" in a shared dirty tree is a policy×concurrency ratchet — the fix is a safe DEFAULT primitive that can't sweep siblings, not more discipline. (2) Synthetic temp-repo tests validate LOGIC but hide SCALE/pollution failures (lifetime-vs-turn, O(N×log), 142 MB log) — always run the real tree before claiming done; the acceptance criterion is a REAL commit, not a passing unit test. (3) `lstrip('./')` char-set trap recurs across the codebase (self-update, file-history, this tool) — grep for it. (4) Declaring > deriving: the agent knows its own edits; a lifetime-scan "helper" is a footgun (543 false-cleans), not a convenience.

### 2026-07-11 — DECOUPLING Epic G — DESIGN-FIRST step LANDED (§10-signed off by owner "approved everything"): extended lib/agent_loop.run_agent_loop into a proven SUPERSET of the chat-orchestrator hot loop, WITHOUT yet touching any hot loop. ### 2026-07-11 — GIT COMMIT SEAM — a contamination-proof `project_commit` agent tool (root-cause fix for "consistent failure to commit"). Plus `.gitignore` hygiene. TDD (9 new tests, load-bearing contamination-exclusion RED-checked), all imports + ruff clean, defer NC-C anchor repaired. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Problem (owner).** "As the project grows, our interaction with git is not smooth — a consistent failure to commit, yet LLMs lean heavily on git." Diagnosis (grounded, not guessed): git itself is fine here (no hooks, instant `git status`, no `index.lock`, git 2.11.0) and `lib/file_history/` already gives agents undo/redo/diff — so "LLMs need git to function" is FALSE here; they need a clean **commit seam**, not git. The real cause is **policy × concurrency**: standing "uncommitted for sign-off" + N sibling conversations editing ONE ~600-dirty-file tree → nobody can safely commit (a `git add -A` sweeps 4 epics' half-finished work; per-file staging on 2.11 hits the pathspec-override + stash-hazard traps), so work piles up and the blob grows — a ratchet. 13 commits in 14 days, ALL authored by the owner, none by an agent.
- **(a) Hygiene — LANDED.** `.gitignore` +3 scoped rules: `*.log`/`server_*.log` (stray root run-logs), `uploads/papers/` (68 ingested PDFs), root-anchored `/.project_sessions/` (CWD-pollution variant; does NOT shadow the registry-managed `lib/.project_sessions/` — verified via `git check-ignore`). Untracked 275 → 203. Drift-guard tests `test_runtime_layout` + `test_data_layout_separation` = 33 green. NOTE: bundles were ALREADY ignored (`bundle-*`, 8-hex `feature-…`); of 58 dirty `static/js/**`, only 1 is a generated bundle (`feature-133a319e.js`, tracked because committed before the ignore rule — git never auto-ignores an already-tracked path). So policy (b) collapses to: never let an agent commit that bundle (encoded in the tool's reject rule) + a one-line `git rm --cached` at a release step.
- **(c) The seam — `lib/conversations/project_commit.py` (426 L).** A real AGENT TOOL, not a run_command wrapper (a wrapper still lets the agent `git add -A` around it; a tool with a FIXED internal git sequence removes the footgun). `plan_commit()` (pure) + `do_commit()` (mutating) + `execute_commit_tool()` (agent entry → human string). Fixed sequence: derive candidate set from file-history filtered to THIS `conv_id` (or explicit `files=`) → reject ignored/generated → **contamination gate** → `git add -- <clean set>` (never `-A`) → verify index == clean set → `git commit` with **NO pathspec** (the pathspec-override trap) → verify commit's file list == clean set → restore any pre-existing staged entries. No `-A`, no `git commit -- <path>`, no stash/checkout (all logged hazards in this tree).
- **The contamination gate (load-bearing, and STRONGER than the owner's spec).** Owner asked for a `git diff --numstat` magnitude check. I implemented **byte-identity** instead (and still surface numstat as evidence): file-history's `snapshots.jsonl` pins, per round, the `convId` + the post-image blob VERSION of each file → a candidate is CLEAN only if its current working-tree bytes reproduce EXACTLY this conversation's last recorded post-image. This catches the case numstat magnitude MISSES — a sibling replacing N of my lines with N different lines has identical numstat but different bytes. Buckets: `clean` / `contaminated` (unattributed, unverifiable-no-blob, recorded-deleted-but-present, or foreign-hunks-diverge) / `ignored` (bundle / git-ignored). Contaminated files are EXCLUDED + reported ("held: commit yours after the sibling lands"), never silently staged. This is exactly the `commit-numstat-foreign-hunk-check` skill's bug class (project.py +414 / conversations.py +196 from swept sibling hunks).

- **FOLLOW-UP 1 (owner-caught, real bug, fixed at the SOURCE).** Live-tree run worked at scale (3.5s) but surfaced path mangling: passing `.gitignore` came back classified as `gitignore` (dot stripped). Root cause was NOT just my `plan_commit` normalization — it was **file-history core**: `lib/file_history/api.py::_normalize_rel` used `rp.lstrip('./')`, a CHARACTER-SET strip, so `.gitignore` → `gitignore` and `.tofu/x` → `tofu/x` at RECORD time. The stored snapshot key was corrupted → my byte-identity attribution could never match a dotfile, AND (latent) `_restore_one` would undo/redo a dotfile edit to the WRONG on-disk path (`./gitignore`). Invisible until now because it's symmetric within fh and dotfile-edit-then-undo is rare. FIX: `re.sub(r'^(?:\./)+', '', rp)` (literal leading `./` only) in BOTH `_normalize_rel` and my `plan_commit` candidate normalization; `import re` added to api.py. This is the SAME `lstrip('./')` char-set trap my `self-update-tarball-fallback-nongit` skill already documents in `_overlay_skip` — it lives in multiple places; grep for it. Regression test `test_dotfile_candidates_not_mangled` (`.gitignore` + `.tofu/skills/note.md` recorded byte-identically must land `clean`, mangled forms must appear NOWHERE) — RED-verified against the old code, green after. fh regression: pytest 14 + standalone `debug/test_file_history.py` 34/34 (undo/redo unaffected).
- **FOLLOW-UP 2 (owner-flagged gap the synthetic tests couldn't cover): convId round-trip.** The tool assumes the WRITE path's snapshot `convId` == the READ path's `current_conv_id`. Traced both to the SAME `task['convId']` key: write = `commit_round.py:327` `conv_id=task.get('convId')`; read = `misc.py:442` `current_conv_id = task.get('convId','')` → `execute_commit_tool`. Identical by construction. The two divergence risks are CLOSED: (a) **endpoint mode** runs in the same task (`_endpoint_turns`) → same convId; (b) **swarm sub-agents** carry the parent's convId (`agent.py:1124`) AND never call `make_snapshot` (`agent.py:1020` "the swarm path can't use commit_round's journal"), plus `project_commit` isn't in a sub-agent toolset — so the only path that both stamps snapshots and can call the tool is the main conversation. Proof: `test_write_side_convid_reads_back_on_read_side` (one task dict → real make_snapshot with `task['convId']` → plan_commit with the read-side value → file is `clean`; a different convId does NOT see it) + `test_both_call_sites_read_same_convid_key` source-drift guard (fails if either site is edited to read a different key — the tripwire for the silent "own work looks foreign → commits nothing" failure). project_commit suite now 12 green; ruff clean. If a future mode DOES give a writer a different convId than the tool reads, that guard fails loudly.
- **Wiring (3 seams, mirrors the board tools).** `PROJECT_COMMIT_TOOL` spec in `lib/tools/conversation.py` → `BOARD_TOOLS`/`BOARD_TOOL_NAMES`/`__all__`; routing branch in `execute_board_tool` (project_board.py) → `execute_commit_tool`; `provides` frozenset in `registry.py`. Project-mode-gated for free (same guard as the board tools → never in the headless/BYO surface). In `misc.py::_handle_board_tool` added `project_commit` to `_LEASE_VERB` (badge `commit`) so its `_post_build` SKIPS the empty `boardTransition` (no task_id) that would otherwise suppress the useful commit-result prose body.
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_commit.py`, 9).** Real temp git repo + real fh store (no git/fh mocks — byte-identity attribution only means something end-to-end). LOAD-BEARING `test_foreign_hunk_file_is_excluded`: convA records `shared.py`, a SIBLING appends an unrecorded hunk, convA cleanly edits `mine.py` → `plan` puts `mine.py` in clean + `shared.py` in contaminated; `do_commit` commits ONLY `mine.py`, and `shared.py`'s foreign hunk stays dirty on disk (NOT swept). RED-checked: neuter `_own_record` to always-clean → `shared.py` leaks into clean (True) → the test would catch a gate removal. Plus clean-commit, generated-bundle reject, unattributed→contaminated, sibling-recorded-not-mine, empty-message/nothing-clean guards, + registration (in schema, in name set, routes to `_handle_board_tool`, project-mode gate). 9 green.
- **Regression I caused + fixed.** My `BOARD_TOOLS` edit invalidated `test_project_board_defer.py::test_NC_C_schema_registration_is_load_bearing`'s byte-revert anchor (it pinned the old block sans `PROJECT_COMMIT_TOOL`) → repaired the NC's search/replace to the current block. Full run: project_commit 9 + defer 16 + lease 23 = 48 green; ruff clean on all touched files; all 5 touched lib modules import-clean.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off** (standing preference). This is itself the first candidate for the new tool once signed off: `project_commit(files=[…the 3 new/edited files…])` would commit exactly them, byte-identity-attributed, excluding the co-owned churn.
- **Lessons.** (1) "Can't commit" in a shared dirty tree is a policy×concurrency ratchet, not a git bug — the fix is a safe DEFAULT commit primitive that can't sweep siblings, not more git discipline. (2) Byte-identity > numstat magnitude for authorship (magnitude is spoofable by an equal-size foreign replacement); file-history already stores the per-conv post-image to make it cheap. (3) Editing a registered tool-list block breaks any sibling test that byte-reverts that exact block — grep the NC anchors after touching `BOARD_TOOLS`.

### 2026-07-11 — Review Mode is now TEXT-ONLY: a peer review carries NO images/figures at all. Closed all three image-entry paths (prompt permit + manifest offer + deterministic injection). TDD (rewrote 1 test to the no-image contract, +prompt assertions; 27 affected green), ruff clean. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Request.** Owner: "The review report should not contain images."
- **Prior behaviour (3 image-entry paths).** A review could still get figures: (1) the review PROMPT explicitly permitted embedding a manifest figure (`review.py` EN L490 / ZH L554: "You may embed a figure/table … ![caption](EXACT_URL_FROM_MANIFEST)"); (2) the route INJECTED the image manifest into the review prompt (`routes/paper.py` `_build_image_manifest`); (3) `_inject_images_into_report(appendix=False)` — used ONLY for review mode — still PLACED inline-cited figures and TRUSTED any model-emitted `/api/paper/images/` embed. `appendix=False` only suppressed the unreferenced-figure gallery, not inline/model-embedded images.
- **Fix (defence in depth — prompt + deterministic backstop).**
  1. `lib/paper/images.py::_inject_images_into_report` gained `allow_images=True`. When `False` it short-circuits BEFORE any injection: injects nothing (no inline, no appendix) AND removes EVERY renderable image vector. **ROOT-CAUSE redesign (replaced a growing per-tag denylist — `<img>/<picture>/<svg>/<object>/<embed>/<input>` — that was losing whack-a-mole to `<image>/<video poster>/<iframe>/background=…`):** a peer review is a Markdown PROSE document with NO legitimate raw HTML, so instead of enumerating image-bearing tags we neutralize ALL raw HTML. Order: (i) MASK fenced/inline code + `$…$`/`$$…$$` math spans (a code example showing `<img>` is prose, not a rendered image); (ii) inline Markdown `![alt](any-url)` → `*alt*` (paper-hosted / external / `data:`); (iii) reference `![alt][ref]` / collapsed `![alt][]` / shortcut `![alt]` → `*alt*`, PLUS drop the orphaned `[ref]: url` link-defs those pointed at (or any link-def whose target is an image URL by extension / `data:image` / `/api/paper/images/`), keeping non-image defs; (iv) strip ALL remaining live HTML tags via `</?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9:-]*(?:\s(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^>])*)?/?>` (opening/closing/void, multi-line), keeping inner text (an `<object>` fallback, a `<figcaption>`/`<td>`'s prose); (v) UNMASK code/math verbatim. The attr span matches a full quoted string OR any non-`>` char, so a LEGAL `>` inside a quoted attribute value (`<img alt="a>b" src=x>`) does NOT terminate the tag early and leak the `src` — the earlier `[^<>]` attr class had that bypass. The tag-name-must-start-with-a-letter anchor means an inequality (`a < b`) and an escaped entity (`&lt;img&gt;`, no literal `<`) are untouched. This collapses the whole image-vector class — incl. any tag invented later — into one rule and does NOT lean on a downstream sanitizer. Default `True` → ordinary reports byte-identical (all HTML/images kept).
  2. All 4 call sites pass `allow_images=not is_review_lang(lang)`: `report_engine.py::_run_report_task` (via `inj_allow_images`, live-generation path) + the 3 `routes/paper.py` cache/enrich paths (DB-cache-hit at L385, `/report/export` at L734, `/report/get` cache at L963). So a review is text-only on generation AND every re-render/cache path.
  3. `routes/paper.py`: `manifest = '' if is_review else _build_image_manifest(...)` — the reviewer is no longer even offered figures to embed.
  4. `lib/paper/review.py`: replaced the "You may embed a figure" formatting bullet with a HARD "**No images.** A review is a text-only decision document… refer to figures/tables by number in prose" rule, EN + ZH (`不嵌图`).
- **Tests (`tests/test_paper_review_mode.py`).** Rewrote `test_review_appendix_suppressed_report_keeps_it` → `test_review_is_text_only_no_images_at_all`: with `allow_images=False`, (1) an unreferenced figure, (2) an INLINE-CITED figure, (3) a model-emitted paper-image embed, (4) an EXTERNAL `https://…png` + `data:` embed + two raw `<img>` tags, (5) a `<picture><source srcset>` + `<figure><img><figcaption>` block, (6) a reference-style `![alt][ref]` + its `[ref]: url` def, (7) an inline multi-line `<svg><rect/></svg>`, (8) a `<div style="background-image:url(...)">`, (9) `<object data=…png>`+`<embed src=…svg>`+`<input type="image" src=…png>`, (10) `<image src>`+`<video poster>`+`<iframe src=…png>`+`<table background=…png>`, (11) inline+fenced code containing `<img>`, AND (12) tags with a LEGAL `>` inside a quoted attribute value (`<img alt="a>b" src=…>`, `<div title="x>y" style="background:url(…)">`, `<img data-x="1>2" src=external>`) ALL behave correctly — every rendering tag + image URL is gone from the review (md embeds degrade to `*alt*`, `<object>`/`<figcaption>`/`<td>` inner prose kept, non-image link-def kept), while code/math spans + escaped `&lt;img&gt;` are preserved verbatim and the report (`allow_images=True`) keeps every rendering tag. Extended the engine test's spy signature (`allow_images`) + asserted the engine passes `allow_images=[False]` for a review. Added prompt assertions: EN prompt contains `no images` + no `exact_url_from_manifest`; ZH contains `不嵌图`. 13 review-mode + 8 dashes + 6 smartquotes green; ruff clean.
- **Lesson.** "No images in X" needs BOTH a prompt prohibition AND a deterministic post-generation backstop — cheap models ignore the prompt, and the injector is the source of truth. The existing `appendix=False` was a half-measure (only killed the gallery); the real lever is refusing to inject + stripping model-emitted embeds. Guard it at the ONE injector all 4 render paths funnel through, keyed on `is_review_lang`, default-on so plain reports are untouched.

### 2026-07-11 — Restart button FIXED: re-exec'd child died at first boot line with `BrokenPipeError` from the unguarded `_boot()` stderr echo. Wrapped both direct `sys.stderr.write` boot echoes best-effort. TDD (+2 tests), ruff clean. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report.** Owner: "重启按钮也有bug，重启不起来。" Log tail showed the re-exec'd process dying: `[CRITICAL] server Uncaught exception — process is terminating … File "server.py", line 1036, in _boot … sys.stderr.write(... % (elapsed, line)) BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe`.
- **Root cause (NOT the port-shift bug — that was fixed 2026-06-15).** `POST /api/v1/update/restart` → `_deferred_reexec` → `os.execv(sys.executable, argv)`. The fresh image inherits fd 2 (stderr) as a pipe whose reader has already gone away after the exec handoff. The VERY FIRST progress line — `_boot('🫧 Tofu … starting up …')` at server.py:1041 — calls `sys.stderr.write()` UNGUARDED, which raises `BrokenPipeError`, hits `_crash_excepthook`, and kills boot before a single module loads. So the restart never comes back up. The authoritative boot record already goes to `_boot_logger.info()` → app.log, so the console echo is purely cosmetic and must never be fatal.
- **Fix (two sites, minimal).** Wrapped the direct console echoes in `try/except OSError: pass`: (1) `_boot()` (server.py:1036) — the first-line-of-boot chokepoint; (2) the ready-banner write at handoff (server.py:2289) — same broken-inherited-pipe exposure at boot's end. Left the logger line untouched (it's the source of truth) and left the other two unguarded writes alone: the faulthandler-prune write (server.py:461) is already `try/except`-wrapped, and `logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)` already swallows write errors via `Handler.handleError`.
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_server_boot_broken_pipe.py` (2): inject a stderr whose `write`/`flush` raise `BrokenPipeError` and assert `_boot()` does NOT raise AND still lands the message in the `server.boot` logger (reproduces the exact restart scenario — RED against the old unguarded write); plus a healthy-stderr test proving the echo is still emitted (no silent regression). `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` (napari/vispy autoload otherwise fails collection with `OSError: GL ES 2.0 library not found`). 2 passed; ruff clean; ast-parse clean.
- **Lessons.** (1) A self-restarting server (`os.execv`) must treat EVERY direct `sys.stderr`/`stdout` write in the boot path as best-effort — the inherited pipe's reader is gone, so any cosmetic console write can `BrokenPipeError` and, unguarded, kill boot at line 1. Route the real record through the logger; guard the echo. (2) `python server.py` restart bugs have TWO distinct failure modes now catalogued: port-shift (inheritable listen socket, fixed 2026-06-15) and boot-death-on-broken-stderr (this one) — different root causes, both on the re-exec path.

### 2026-07-11 — Project Brain board "occupied, no assignee" ghost cards — root-caused + FIXED (frontend partition mismatch) AND closed the underlying expired-lease row leak (write-seam GC). TDD (+2 jsdom, +4 backend incl. NC), bundle rebuilt+verified, 2 live dead-lease rows cleared. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report.** Operator saw board cards that look "occupied but have no assignee" — asked if it's a bug. It is (minor, frontend-only) — NOT an assignment bug.
- **Diagnosis (traced full path + inspected LIVE board).** The epic-claim invariant is SOUND: `_effective_status` reclaims an expired `claimed` epic to `open` at read time, and `_row_to_task` blanks `owner_conv_id` whenever eff-status≠claimed → a claimed epic can NEVER be ownerless. The actual ghosts were TWO `kind='lease'` path-reservations (holder `mremei26b476uu`, on `static/js/tofu-pet.js` / `static/icons/pet/`), leases dead ~10–18h. ROOT CAUSE = partition mismatch: backend `render_board_block` (project_board.py:558) filters Held on `kind=='lease' AND status=='claimed'`; frontend `renderBoard` (project-brain.js:1153) filtered on `kind==='lease'` ALONE — its comment even claimed "Mirrors render_board_block's backend partition" but it didn't. So an EXPIRED lease (which `read_board` returns as `status:'open'`, blank owner) still rendered as an ownerless "Held — do not edit" card.
- **Fix #1 (frontend, one line).** `if (t.kind === 'lease') { if (t.status === 'claimed') held.push(t); continue; }` — now mirrors the backend; expired leases drop out of the Held lane. Also corrected the stale mirror comment. NOTE: project-brain.js is in `_DEFERRED_FILES` (moved 2026-07-09), so it builds into the FEATURE bundle, not core — `build_bundle()` returns the (unchanged) core hash; the fix landed in `feature-daebaab7.js` (verified via minified grep: `if(O.kind==="lease"){O.status==="claimed"&&T.push(O);continue}`). Watch for this: an unchanged core-bundle hash after a project-brain edit is EXPECTED, not a build miss.
- **Fix #2 (the deeper leak the operator flagged — expired lease rows never GC'd).** `claim_lease`/`release_lease` only delete on explicit release; `_effective_status` merely downgrades at read time → dead `kind='lease'` rows persist FOREVER. Not merely cosmetic: `post_task` gates new epics on `COUNT(*) >= _MAX_BOARD_TASKS (200)` counting ALL rows incl. dead leases → a real epic-posting-budget leak + `project_tasks` bloat. DECISION: prune, but at the WRITE seam, NOT in `read_board`. Rejected prune-on-read because (a) `read_board` is a hot pure never-raises read on every prompt assembly — turning it into a committing writer is a perf/concurrency regression, and (b) it would BREAK the load-bearing NC-1 in test_project_board_lease.py (force-expires a lease then relies on the row still EXISTING when select_dispatchable→read_board evaluates it). Implemented `_prune_expired_leases(db, project_path, now)` (DELETE gated `kind='lease' AND lease_expires_at>0 AND <=now` — never an epic, never a live lease; best-effort, caller owns the txn) wired into `post_task` (before the cap count) + `claim_lease` (at entry). This is the WRITE-side analogue of at-read-time expiry, NOT the background reaper the lease design rejects — deleting an already-expired row is a semantic no-op to every reader.
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_board_expired_lease_ghost.py` (2, jsdom over real renderBoard + shipped index.html fragment): live lease stays in Held, expired lease dropped everywhere; NC-FE byte-reverts the `status==='claimed'` guard in a COPY → ghost reappears (RED-verified first: `FAIL expired_lease_not_in_held` before fix). +4 in `tests/test_project_board_lease.py` (19→23): claim_lease prunes OTHER dead leases (epic+live-lease survive); post_task GCs before the cap; no-op sweep leaves live+epic; NC neuters the prune DELETE body → expired lease PERSISTS (reproduces the leak). Regression: board+defer+dispatch = 66 green; full lease suite 23 green; ruff clean.
- **Housekeeping.** Cleared the two live dead-lease rows via a scoped DELETE (`project_path=cwd AND kind='lease' AND lease_expires_at<=now`) → board now 2 open / 56 done / 0 lease rows.
- **Lessons.** (1) "Occupied, no assignee" on the board is a LEASE ghost, not an epic-assignment bug — the claim invariant blanks owner on eff-status≠claimed. (2) A frontend "mirrors backend" comment is not proof; the two partitions had drifted. (3) After editing a `_DEFERRED_FILES` JS module, verify the FEATURE bundle (minified grep), not the core hash. (4) Lazy GC belongs on WRITE seams that already commit — never convert a hot pure read into a writer (perf + it defeats NC tests that force-expire-then-read).

### 2026-07-11 — Review Mode typography + concision: added deterministic em-dash/en-dash de-slop (`strip_slop_dashes`) to complement the existing `smarten_quotes`, and hardened the review prompt (EN+ZH) to ban slop dashes / dumb quotes and demand a short, incisive decision document. TDD (+8 dash tests; 30 affected green), ruff clean. Requirement-1 (no re-show of the generate page) already met by existing cache-first `_loadOrGenerateReport`. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Request.** Owner: (1) if a review already exists, render it, don't show the "start generation" page again; (2) review content must PROHIBIT dashes + dumb quotes (auto-convert to smart quotes by rule); (3) review must be concise/incisive, no filler/platitudes.
- **Req 1 — already satisfied, verified not regressed.** `static/js/paper-reader.js::_loadOrGenerateReport` renders from state (1.6 in-mem cache) / running-task lookup (2) / DB cache (3) and only reaches `_renderReportStartPrompt` at the terminal step 4 when NOTHING is cached and no task runs. `_renderReportStartPrompt` has exactly one call site (5055). No code change needed.
- **Req 2 — the real gap was DASHES.** `smarten_quotes` (review.py) already curls quotes deterministically on the final body (backend = source of truth); there was NO dash handling. Added `strip_slop_dashes(text)` next to it, reusing the SAME `_PROTECT_RE` masking (math `$...$` / inline+fenced code / URLs preserved verbatim). Rules: em-dash U+2014 / horizontal-bar U+2015 / doubled `——` → comma ALWAYS; en-dash U+2013 → comma ONLY as a separator, a NUMERIC range (`1–10`, `2–4`) is kept; ASCII hyphen-minus never touched (hyphens `well-motivated`, markdown `---` rule + `- ` bullets stay). CJK-aware: when the char before the dash is CJK it emits a fullwidth `，`, else `, ` (no stray ASCII comma in a Chinese review). Wired into `report_engine._run_report_task` review branch as `strip_slop_dashes(smarten_quotes(full_content))` (review-only; plain reports untouched), exported from `lib/paper/__init__.py`.
- **Req 3 + Req 2 at the prompt.** Added two anti-slop bullets to BOTH `_REVIEW_PROMPT_EN` and `_REVIEW_PROMPT_ZH`: a **Typography** rule (never em/en-dash as a separator, en-dash only for numeric ranges; curly quotes / 全角标点 only) and a **Be short and incisive** rule (decision document not essay; cut any sentence that doesn't change the accept/reject call or tell authors what to fix; no self-summary / "in conclusion" / 综上所述; state an empty section in one line rather than manufacturing filler). Deliberately worded the range example as "a rating scale" not the literal `1–10` — the review-mode test asserts `'1–10' not in` the CVPR EN prompt, and a literal token would have leaked into every prompt (caught by the suite on first run).
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_paper_review_dashes.py` (8, RED-first): pure de-slopper (em/bar→comma, CJK→fullwidth comma, ranges+hyphens+markdown preserved, math/code/URL spans preserved, idempotent+noop) + engine wiring (review deslops, plain report keeps dashes) + source-level NC (neuter `strip_slop_dashes`→dash survives, restore→comma). Regression: `test_paper_review_smartquotes`(6) + `test_paper_review_mode`(13) + `test_frontend_review_venue_race` + `test_frontend_paper_regen_refresh` = 30 passed under `-n auto -p xdist`. ruff clean.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for sign-off.** Changed: `lib/paper/review.py` (`strip_slop_dashes` + `_deslop_segment` + prompt bullets EN/ZH), `lib/paper/report_engine.py` (review-branch wiring), `lib/paper/__init__.py` (export), NEW `tests/test_paper_review_dashes.py`, + this entry.
- **Lesson.** Dash de-slop needs the SAME protected-span masking as quote education (never touch math primes / code / URLs), plus two extra discriminators quotes don't need: a numeric-range guard so `1–10` survives, and CJK-context detection so a Chinese review gets `，` not `, `. And a prompt example string that duplicates a value a sibling test asserts-absent (`1–10`) will silently break that test — phrase examples generically.


### 2026-07-11 — Crash recovery is now DISPLAY-ONLY by default: gated the billed boot dispatch (autopilot-resume + killed-turn re-dispatch) behind default-OFF `TOFU_BOOT_AUTO_DISPATCH`. Boot stays fast/non-blocking (unchanged). TDD (+1 = 5 boot-dispatch tests; 46 affected green), ruff clean. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Request.** Owner (durable preference): "crash recovery must NOT auto-execute any billed LLM turn; recovery only marks interrupted + surfaces in sidebar without dispatch. Server must start ASAP — nothing blocks boot." Audited `python server.py` end-to-end first, then fixed the one violation.
- **Audit verdict (before fix).** ① Fast/non-blocking boot: MET — `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup(dispatch=False)` (manager.py:2150) runs ONLY the synchronous DB sweep on the startup loop and RETURNS a descriptor; the billed dispatch was already deferred to the SERVING loop (server.py:2538 `loop.create_task`). ③ Sidebar display: MET — the sync sweep marks `running→interrupted`, clears stale `activeTaskId`, merges partial content, stamps sidebar facts. ② No auto-execute: **VIOLATED** — the deferred `run_deferred_boot_dispatch` auto-fired TWO billed lanes: `resume_armed_autopilot_after_crash` + `run_killed_recovery(killed_conv_ids + list_killed_turn_convs())` (a durable 7-day scan → `create_task`+`spawn_task` regenerate). Guarded (attempt cap 3 / concurrency 2 / inline-boot 1 / storm stand-down) but still auto-execution.
- **Fix (one chokepoint, minimal).** Added `_boot_auto_dispatch_enabled()` (reads `TOFU_BOOT_AUTO_DISPATCH`, default OFF, live/non-memoized) and gated it at the TOP of `run_deferred_boot_dispatch` — BEFORE the `should_continue`/`stop_event` logic. This single gate covers BOTH call paths (the serving-loop deferred path AND the legacy inline `dispatch=True` used by direct callers/tests) and BOTH billed lanes, so neither autopilot-resume nor killed-recovery can auto-fire. When disabled it logs `Boot auto-dispatch DISABLED (default) — crash recovery is display-only: N recovered / M killed conv(s) left for MANUAL resume` and returns early. The synchronous sweep in `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` is UNTOUCHED (interrupted tails stay tagged `killed`/`killed_exhausted`/`manual` and visible; the user resumes manually — empty-Enter kick / regenerate). Killed tags persist → if the owner ever sets the env var, a later calm boot's durable scan still finds them (no work lost).
- **Tests (`tests/test_boot_dispatch_deferral.py`, 4→5; all green).** NEW `test_default_off_gate_is_display_only`: env unset → BOTH lanes fire 0×; `TOFU_BOOT_AUTO_DISPATCH=1` → both fire 1× (proves the gate, not broken wiring). Updated the two pre-existing lane tests (`test_deferred_dispatch_runs_both_billed_lanes`, `test_shutdown_gate_skips_dispatch`) to `monkeypatch.setenv('TOFU_BOOT_AUTO_DISPATCH','1')` so they isolate the lane/`should_continue` behaviour rather than tripping on the new default-off flag. Extended the standalone `_MP` shim with `setenv`/`delenv` (+ env restore in `undo`). Suites: boot-dispatch(5)+killed-recovery(26)=31 green; regression startup-reconcile+stale-recovery-authoritative+sidebar-settled-facts+shutdown-quiesce=15 green. ruff clean; ast-parse clean.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py` (`_boot_auto_dispatch_enabled` + gate + docstring), `tests/test_boot_dispatch_deferral.py` (+1 test, +2 updated, `_MP` env shim), + this entry. `server.py` / `killed_recovery.py` NOT modified (the gate sits above them; their deferral/stop-gate machinery is retained for the opt-in path).
- **Lessons.** (1) When a requirement is "never auto-execute", gate at the single BILLED chokepoint that ALL dispatch paths funnel through (`run_deferred_boot_dispatch`), not at each call site — one gate then covers the serving-loop deferral AND the legacy inline path AND every billed lane. (2) A default-OFF env flag read LIVE (not memoized) keeps the test toggle trivial and the single-box install byte-identical (display-only) unless explicitly opted in. (3) Leave the recovery TAGS in place when disabling dispatch: display-only + durable-scan means enabling the flag later loses nothing.


### 2026-07-11 — DECOUPLING PROGRAM kickoff: measure-first audit + Increment B (SSE reader dedup) LANDED; Increment A (api_response finish) RESCOPED after measurement disproved its premise. TDD (+1 harness = 27 area-tests green), ruff clean, JS bundle rebuilt+verified. Uncommitted for sign-off.

Findings: repo is 473 `lib/routes` .py (~186k LOC) + 103 JS (~70k) + 21.7k-line styles.css; already heavily decoupled (agent_core/, shared-infra seams, core/ui/main JS subpackages, api.js at `BASELINE={}` ZERO raw calls, bundle allowlist clean). - **Increment B — LANDED (pure consolidation, byte-behavior-preserving).** The SSE fetch read/decode/buffer loop (`getReader()`+`TextDecoder`+`buffer.split("\n")`+`lines.pop()` tail-buffering) was copy-pasted VERBATIM across 3 sites: `branch.js:850`, `paper-reader.js:2144`, `ui/sse_pipeline.js:1748`. Extracted to `static/js/core/sse_reader.js::readSSEStream(response, {onLine, onChunk?, afterChunk?, flushTail=true})` — transport loop only; per-line semantics stay in each site's `onLine`. Per-site fidelity preserved: branch/sse_pipeline flushTail=true (process trailing partial), **paper flushTail=false** (it never processed its tail pre-extraction — matched exactly); sse_pipeline's per-chunk `_streamTimerTouch`+`gotData`+`clearTimeout` → `onChunk`, its periodic-save block → `afterChunk`; `onLine`→truthy = early-stop (was `return`/`break`). RED-first: `tests/test_frontend_sse_reader.py` (8 jsdom checks: in-order delivery, split-across-chunks reassembly, flushTail true/false, truthy-stops-early, onChunk-before/afterChunk-after) written+failing BEFORE the module existed, then green. Wired into `_BUNDLE_FILES` (after core/conversations.js, before all 3 consumers) + dev `<script>` tag (index.html). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-5a053b42.js` (99→100 files), `node --check` on the ASSEMBLED bundle OK, 4 `readSSEStream` refs present (1 def+3 sites). Regression gate: `test_frontend_sse_reader + sse_dispatch + sse_core_parity + sse_resume_guard + api_isolation + streaming_ui` = **27 passed**; bundle_concurrency 4 green; ruff clean.
- **Increment A — RESCOPED (measurement disproved the epic's premise; NOT shipped, awaiting owner decision).** The seams audit reported "265 raw `jsonify` to convert + fold conversations.py's re-invented `_ok/_nf/_br` wrappers." DIRECT reading refuted both as safe pure-consolidation: (1) confirmed **259** `return jsonify(` in routes/, but the DOMINANT pattern is `return jsonify(result)` / `jsonify(result), 400` where `result` is an ALREADY-BUILT domain dict (from `get_state()`/`rescan()`/service calls carrying their own `ok`/`error`/`status` keys) — converting to `api_ok(result)` would inject a SECOND `ok:True` or clobber keys = a real WIRE-SHAPE change, violating the owner's "no behavior change" constraint. (2) `conversations.py`'s `_ok/_nf/_br/_ie/_json` are NOT re-invented api_response wrappers — they are the deliberate **`_Defer` protocol** for `run_pooled` blocking bodies that run in the DB executor thread WITHOUT Quart's app context (so they must not construct a Response); the reviewer name-matched and misclassified them. Folding them BREAKS the threading contract. (3) Only ~13 clean `jsonify({'error':'...'}), code` string-literals convert, and only via the `+ok:False` SUPERSET (a wire change the module was designed for, but still not blanket-assertable safe). (4) The `sse_response()` dedup angle: 5 raw SSE `Response(...)` blocks remain, but only the 3 chat.py ones are byte-identical to the canonical headers — **paper.py:252/1721 diverge** (`no-cache` vs `no-cache, no-transform`, missing `Connection`/charset, extra `Content-Encoding: identity`), so converting them would ALTER wire headers. CONCLUSION: A is not the pure-consolidation epic it was scoped as; it needs owner re-scoping (accept the `ok`-superset wire change? or narrow A to just the 3 byte-identical chat.py sse_response conversions + the 13 error-literals?). Stopped rather than nibble unilaterally.
- **Lessons.** (1) A seam-adoption audit that COUNTS raw-`jsonify` magnitude ≠ counts SAFE conversions — `jsonify(already_built_dict)` is the common shape and is NOT interchangeable with `api_ok()` (which injects `ok`). Always read the payload shape before asserting a mechanical convert. (2) Name-matching classifies helpers wrong: `_ok/_nf/_br` LOOKED like duplicate api_response wrappers but are an app-context-safe `_Defer` deferral protocol — read the surrounding contract. (3) SSE headers are load-bearing and per-endpoint-divergent; `sse_response()` is only a byte-safe target where the existing headers already match the canonical set. (4) The extraction ORDER (B before E) was right: pulling the shared SSE reader out first de-risks the later paper-reader.js split.

### 2026-07-11 — DECOUPLING Increment C — LANDED: split the pure command-analysis cluster out of the `lib/project_mod/run_command.py` god-module (2182→1376 LOC, −806) into a new cohesive `lib/project_mod/command_analysis.py`. Move-and-reimport (byte-behavior-preserving); both historical import paths intact. TDD (+2 parity tests = 106 green, was 104 baseline), ruff clean. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **What.** `run_command.py` bundled the subprocess-execution machinery WITH a large side-effect-free analysis layer: output cleanup (`_clean_command_output` + `_mask_quoted_literals`/`_extract_progress_*`/`_line_fingerprint`/`_format_cuda_device_range` + ANSI/progress/device regexes), destructiveness/write-target analysis (`_is_destructive_command`, `_is_dangerous_command`, `_is_catastrophic_delete`, `_split_pipeline`, `_extract_write_targets`, `_filter_changes_by_targets`, `_has_unquoted_shell_metachars` + the READONLY/GIT/WRITE_TARGET/DELETE tables). All PURE (no subprocess, no fs-mutation; the one fs touch is a read-only `realpath` workspace-containment check). Relocated the whole cluster to `command_analysis.py`; `run_command.py` re-imports every symbol so `from lib.project_mod.run_command import …` AND (via tools.py's back-compat re-export) `from lib.project_mod.tools import …` keep working with ZERO call-site edits.

Kept the fs-mutating `_maybe_wrap_rm_with_trash` + all execution/process-tree/grep-hardening code in run_command.py (retained `import re as _re` for it; dropped now-unused `re`/`Counter`). CAUGHT A REAL TRANSCRIPTION BUG mid-flight: my first hand-written `_mask_quoted_literals` body (reconstructed from a truncated read) diverged from the shipped version (the real one blanks quote DELIMITERS to spaces + handles `\\`-escapes as `'  ' if in_double else command[i:i+2]`); re-read the exact original bytes and corrected it before deleting the source — proof that security-code relocation must copy VERIFIED bytes, never a remembered shape.
- **Tests.** Baseline `test_project_tools.py` + `test_cross_platform.py` = 104 green BEFORE and AFTER (behavior-neutral). NEW `tests/test_command_analysis_extraction.py` (+2): identity across import paths (functions identical via all 3 of command_analysis/run_command/tools; constants + the two tools-not-exported funcs `_is_dangerous_command`/`_mask_quoted_literals` identical via command_analysis↔run_command) + a behavior smoke subset (catastrophic-delete blocks `/`+`/mnt`, allows deep/relative; quoted-literal masking neutralises in-string `shutdown`). My first test draft over-asserted (`git status` destructive returns None-not-False; tools.py's re-export list is FUNCTION-ONLY so bare regexes aren't on it) — fixed the test to the ACTUAL contract, not the code. ruff clean; full project_mod package import smoke OK.
- **A/B recap (same session).** B (SSE reader dedup) LANDED. (2) When relocating security-critical code, COPY THE VERIFIED ON-DISK BYTES; a body reconstructed from memory silently diverged here and only a re-read caught it.
