### 2026-07-11 — 297s BOOT + `^C`-unresponsive + PG "shutting down" cascade: ONE root cause — killed-recovery re-dispatch spawned carriers ON the startup event loop, so `asyncio.run(_startup())` couldn't tear down until the carrier's whole ~4.5-min LLM+swarm run finished. Split billed dispatch OUT of the startup path onto the SERVING loop; made `^C` abort before Ready; quiesce running tasks before the atexit PG-stop. TDD (+7 new, 103 affected green), ruff clean, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report (owner ran `python server.py`).** Boot took **297s**, a `^C` at 02:28:21 did nothing until 02:32:31, then a flood of `psycopg2.OperationalError: FATAL: the database system is shutting down` + `RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown`. Owner CORRECTED my first hypothesis ("heavy redispatch blocks boot" — wrong; `spawn_task` is background) and pointed at loop-starvation. Verified: the mechanism is subtler than starvation.
- **Root cause (evidence-pinned, MainThread log).** `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` runs on MainThread INSIDE `asyncio.run(_startup())` (server.py). Its inline killed-recovery `spawn_task(carrier)` → `asyncio.get_running_loop()` returns the **_startup loop** → `asyncio.ensure_future(_async_wrapper())` where `_async_wrapper` does `await loop.run_in_executor(_agent_executor, run_task, task)` (lib/tasks_pkg/__init__.py:131-135). The `_startup()` coroutine body finished ~02:27:51, but `asyncio.run`'s teardown (`_cancel_all_tasks` → `run_until_complete`) then WAITS on that orphaned carrier future — and cancelling a `run_in_executor` future cannot interrupt the already-running executor thread (`asyncio_0` running `run_task`). So `asyncio.run` blocked ~4.5 min until carrier `ca98d8f2` (a 111k-token regenerate that spawned a swarm) finished. PROOF: "Ready" printed at **02:32:30 — the exact second** `[Task ca98d8f2][R21] stream_llm_response complete` logged; MainThread was silent 02:27:51→02:32:30; the `^C` handler DID fire at 02:28:17 (set the flag) but nothing awaited it until `_serve()` existed. Then loop returns → Ready → `_serve` sees flag already set → instant teardown → atexit `stop_local_pg_if_owned` stops PG while the DEFERRED carrier `40f1bdb5` was still mid-run → the DB cascade. The re-burned carriers were the sibling conversations `mreraebr`/`mrerffgl` (re-fired every boot → the boot-ring crash loop 23:01→23:05, 02:27→02:32).
- **Fix (4 parts, one keystone).** KEYSTONE: `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup(prev_shutdown, dispatch=False)` now runs ONLY the synchronous DB cleanup (mark stale→interrupted, clear activeTaskId, merge content) and RETURNS a descriptor `{recovered_conv_ids, killed_conv_ids, restart_storm}`; the BILLED dispatch (autopilot-resume + killed-recovery) moved to a new `run_deferred_boot_dispatch(descriptor, *, should_continue)`. `dispatch=True` (default) preserves the legacy inline behaviour for direct callers/tests. **(#2/#3)** server.py `_init_database` calls it with `dispatch=False`, stashes the descriptor in `_DEFERRED_BOOT_DISPATCH`; `_serve()` schedules `run_deferred_boot_dispatch` on the SERVING loop (via `loop.create_task` + `asyncio.to_thread`) so carriers spawn there, gated on `should_continue=lambda: not _shutdown_requested.is_set()`. **(#1)** After `asyncio.run(_startup())` a checkpoint `if _shutdown_requested.is_set(): sys.exit(0)` skips the banner+serve; two intra-`_startup` checkpoints (after DB init, after import validation) short-circuit remaining startup phases. **(#4)** New `quiesce_running_tasks(reason)` in manager sets `task['aborted']` on every running task; `_serve()` calls it after `hypercorn_serve` drains and waits up to `TOFU_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECS` (default 8) for running tasks to stop BEFORE the atexit PG-stop — killing the cascade. Also fixed the misleading `[KilledRecovery] EXHAUSTED after 4 attempts` log (cap=3): the decision counter reaches cap+1 on the degrade decision; now reports re-dispatches actually MADE (=cap) + the cap.
- **Tests (+7, all green; +103 affected regression green).** NEW `tests/test_boot_dispatch_deferral.py` (4): dispatch=False returns descriptor & does NOT dispatch inline; dispatch=True DOES (legacy NC); run_deferred runs both lanes; `should_continue()==False` skips (^C-during-boot). NEW `tests/test_shutdown_quiesce.py` (3): quiesce aborts all running + stamps reason; leaves terminal tasks untouched; NC neuters quiesce → task stays running (proves load-bearing). Regression: `test_killed_recovery` 22, `test_killed_recovery_integration`, `test_chat_manager_migration`, `test_queue_redispatch_after_restart`, `test_startup_reconcile`, `test_server_async`, `test_restart_smoke`, `test_autopilot_startup_granular_phases`, `test_pg_startup_lock` — 103 total green under `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 pytest -n auto -p xdist`. ruff clean; py_compile clean.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `server.py` (dispatch=False split + startup/post-startup shutdown checkpoints + deferred-dispatch-on-serving-loop + shutdown quiesce/drain), `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py` (dispatch param + `run_deferred_boot_dispatch` + `quiesce_running_tasks`), `lib/tasks_pkg/__init__.py` (exports), `lib/tasks_pkg/killed_recovery.py` (exhausted-log wording — note this whole file is itself still uncommitted from the prior killed-recovery epic), NEW `tests/test_boot_dispatch_deferral.py` + `tests/test_shutdown_quiesce.py`, + this entry.
- **Lessons.** (1) `spawn_task` during `_startup` is NOT background: `asyncio.get_running_loop()` binds the carrier to the STARTUP loop, and `asyncio.run` teardown waits on it (executor-backed → uncancellable) — so any billed spawn must happen on the SERVING loop, never the startup one. (2) A signal handler that only SETS a flag is inert until something AWAITS it; if the flag is set during a long synchronous startup, add explicit checkpoints + a pre-serve exit, don't rely on the serve-loop trigger that doesn't exist yet. (3) Shutdown ordering is a contract: quiesce/abort task threads and give them a bounded drain BEFORE the atexit resource-teardown (PG stop), or in-flight threads generate a "resource shutting down" traceback storm. (4) "Boot took Ns" — measure the MainThread-silent window and find what log line coincides with the END of the gap; here Ready@02:32:30 == carrier-done@02:32:30 was the whole proof.

- **FOLLOW-UP (same session, owner caught the missed #5).** The FIRST line of the actual cascade was NOT a quiesced task — it was the killed-recovery DRAIN DAEMON: `02:32:31 [killed-recovery-drain] drain dispatch failed conv=mremenwd: FATAL: the database system is shutting down` at `_drain_deferred:516`. That `daemon=True` thread's `while deferred:` loop had ZERO shutdown awareness: every ~15s tick called `get_thread_db` AND `_dispatch_one → _redispatch_conv → create_task + spawn_task` could spawn a BRAND-NEW carrier during shutdown. `quiesce_running_tasks` only flags EXISTING running tasks — a carrier the drain spawns AFTER quiesce is outside the 8s drain window, and the drain thread itself is the first to hit PG-going-down. FIX: threaded the server's `_shutdown_requested` `threading.Event` straight through as `stop_event` → `run_deferred_boot_dispatch(…, stop_event=_shutdown_requested)` → `run_killed_recovery(…, stop_event=)` → `_spawn_drain_daemon(…, stop_event=)` → `_drain_deferred`. New `_stop_requested(ev)` gate is checked BEFORE every slot-poll, BEFORE every dispatch/DB touch, and the inline `run_killed_recovery` loop is gated too (it also spawns + touches DB). Replaced the two `time.sleep` (15s poll + 0.5-1.5s jitter) with `_interruptible_wait(secs, stop_event)` = `Event.wait(secs)` so shutdown wakes the daemon instantly instead of stalling up to 15s. Un-dispatched convs keep their `killed` tag (burned no attempt) → re-found by the next calm boot's durable scan. Legacy signature preserved (`stop_event=None` → no gate) so all prior callers/tests are unchanged. Tests: +4 in `tests/test_killed_recovery.py` (22→26): pre-set event → zero dispatch + zero DB (tripwire) + no attempt burned; NC neuters `_stop_requested`→always-False → drains DESPITE shutdown (proves the gate is load-bearing), real gate restored → stops; `run_killed_recovery(stop_event=set)` → nothing dispatched, no daemon; event set AFTER first dispatch → stops before the 2nd. Full affected suite 74 green under `-n auto -p xdist`; ruff clean. (Also caught+fixed my own new stub in `test_boot_dispatch_deferral.py` that didn't accept the new `stop_event` kwarg.)
- **Extra lesson (5).** A `daemon=True` thread dying WITH the process is NOT the same as being shutdown-AWARE: between "shutdown requested" and "interpreter exits" it keeps running its loop, and if that loop touches a resource being torn down (PG) or spawns new work, it produces exactly the cascade quiesce was meant to stop. Any long-lived background loop that touches DB / spawns tasks needs an explicit stop gate checked before EACH such action (not once at entry), and its sleep must be an interruptible `Event.wait`, not `time.sleep`.

- **FOLLOW-UP #2 (same session, owner caught the last layer).** The drain-daemon gate stops the FIRST cascade line, but the rest of the `FATAL: shutting down` traceback storm comes from THREE other sources that quiesce/stop-gate can't reach — they are async writes spawned AFTER a task completes, on a NORMAL-run SIGTERM (not just boot): `_run_commit_round_async` (commit-round daemon), `_run_profile_consolidation_async` (profile daemon), and `run_task`'s own finalize chain (`persist_task_result` / `_sync_result_to_conversation` / `checkpoint_task_partial` / `_update_proactive_execution_status` / `_dispatch_queued_message`). Each caught its DB exception and logged `exc_info=True` → a full stack per site. Confirmed there was ZERO shutdown-error recognition in `_core.py`/`_wrappers.py`. ROOT-CAUSE FIX = process-level PG-stopping awareness at the DB layer: (1) `_PG_STOPPING` flag + `mark_pg_stopping()`/`pg_is_stopping()` in `_core.py`, SET at the top of `stop_local_pg_if_owned()`; (2) `_PG_SHUTDOWN_SIGNATURES` ("the database system is shutting down", "server closed the connection unexpectedly", "terminating connection due to administrator command", "in recovery mode") + `_pg_error_is_shutdown` + `_sql_error_is_expected_shutdown` (flag AND signature); (3) `PgCursor.execute` degrades its own SQL-failure log to one INFO line when expected-shutdown; (4) `_new_pg_connection` re-raises a connect-time shutdown error WITHOUT a self-heal reboot (we're going down) — checked BEFORE the dead-signature self-heal since "server closed" overlaps both; (5) public `is_expected_shutdown_error(exc)` + `log_db_finalize_error(log, level, exc, label)` — a SINGLE shared predicate the upper finalize catch-sites call, so detection lives in ONE place and each site just picks presentation. Converted 9 `exc_info=True` finalize catches (5 in manager.py incl. persist_task_result, 2 in commit_round.py, 2 in killed_recovery.py incl. the drain) to route through it. Genuine app errors (e.g. unique-constraint) during shutdown STAY loud (ERROR+stack) — the degrade masks ONLY shutdown-signature errors AND only while stopping. Tests: NEW `tests/test_db_shutdown_log_degrade.py` (4): predicate gated on BOTH flag+signature; helper → single INFO no-traceback during shutdown; NC (flag UNSET, byte-revert-equivalent) → same error logs ERROR+exc_info (loud path intact); a genuine error during shutdown stays loud. 73 affected + 46 DB-suite green under `-n auto -p xdist`; ruff clean; `lib.database` facade re-exports verified.
- **Extra lesson (6).** The DB layer can degrade its OWN log line, but it CANNOT reformat a CALLER's `exc_info=True` statement — so a clean "quiet expected shutdown errors" fix needs BOTH: (a) detection centralized in one predicate at the resource layer (the flag + signature), and (b) each background/finalize catch-site consulting that ONE predicate to choose ERROR+stack vs one INFO line. Scattering the string-match per site would be the anti-pattern; a shared `log_db_finalize_error(log, level, exc, label)` keeps it single-source. And the degrade must be doubly-gated (flag AND signature) so a genuine error during the shutdown window is never masked.


### 2026-07-10 — "why couldn't we start up just now": NOT a server crash — a pytest-xdist × bundle-builder RACE that white-screened the frontend. The real server (PID 3069265) was up the whole time. Root-caused two latent defects and fixed both (atomic temp→rename publish + cross-process flock in lib/js_bundler.py; moved build_bundle() out of server.py import-time into the startup path). TDD (+4 concurrency tests, existing bundle suite 36 green), ruff clean, gitignore extended. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report.** "Why couldn't we start up just now? Investigate thoroughly." Symptom in logs: a flood of `[CRITICAL] lib.js_bundler [Bundle] Built bundle bundle-a1820e73.js FAILED syntax check — refusing to serve it`, in two shapes — a **SyntaxError** truncated mid-string (`This cannot be undone \u2014 you\u2019ll need…`, an i18n string) AND `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the *same* file — plus what looked like ~100 server "starting up" lines/minute at 23:10–23:13.
- **Diagnosis (measured, owner-verified).** The "restart storm" was NOT real server reboots. The `[DB] SQLite backend (forced via TOFU_DB_BACKEND=sqlite): /tmp/tofu-test-shim-gw91-…` lines gave it away: `gwNN` = **pytest-xdist worker ids** (96 distinct, gw0–gw95). Those "boots" were xdist workers importing `server.py`, which called `build_bundle()` at MODULE-IMPORT time (server.py:1635). Proof it wasn't real: only **1 of 238** "starting up" lines in 23:10–23:11 reached "Ready — handing off to Hypercorn"; `data/.server_boots.json` boot-ring had only 4 real entries (workers die during import, before the ring write); no OOM/SIGKILL in the window (cgroup 43%/200GiB). The launching commands were `pytest tests/test_db_paths_local_split.py -n auto` / `test_image_downscale_uniform_cap.py` / `test_wire_fingerprint.py` (each spawns ~96 workers on this box).
- **Two latent defects the storm merely exposed.** (1) `server.py:1635` ran `build_bundle()` at import → *every* importer (incl. 96 test workers) rebuilds the production artifact into the live `static/js/`. (2) `lib/js_bundler.py::_assemble_bundle` wrote the content-hash-named file NON-atomically (`open(path,'w')` → separate `node --check` → `os.remove` on failure) with NO lock. Since the filename is a content hash, every concurrent builder targets the SAME path → one worker's `node --check` reads a half-written file (truncated SyntaxError), another's runs after a third worker's failure branch `os.remove`d it (MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Even a single server can hit this: two `GET /` requests racing the first build.
- **Fix — robust, not env-sniffing (per owner's explicit constraint).** (1) IMPORT-TIME SIDE EFFECT KILLED PROPERLY: wrapped the call in `_build_js_bundle()` and call it from the `_startup()` coroutine (the real startup path, before Hypercorn serves) — a plain `import server` now touches nothing. Did NOT sniff `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`/`TOFU_DB_BACKEND` (fragile; leaves the side effect for any other importer). (2) ATOMIC PUBLISH in `_assemble_bundle`: short-circuit if `bundle-<hash>.js` already exists (hash = exact served bytes → identical); else write a unique `tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.<prefix><hash>.', suffix='.js', dir=JS_DIR)` (suffix MUST be `.js` — `node --check` hard-errors `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on `.tmp`; caught by TDD), gate the TEMP, then `os.rename` into place ONLY on success (atomic within-dir). A failed gate deletes only the private temp; a lost publish race adopts the peer's identical file. Readers never see a partial/absent hash path. (3) CROSS-PROCESS SERIALIZATION: `build_bundle()` runs under `_build_lock()` (fcntl.flock on `static/js/.bundle-build.lock`), fail-open (no fcntl / OSError → proceed unlocked; temp+rename still keeps it correct). Layering verified: with flock neutered, atomic-publish alone still yields ONE valid bundle under 24 threads — flock is the optimization, temp+rename is the correctness guarantee.
- **Tests (`tests/test_bundle_concurrency.py`, NEW, 4).** `test_failed_gate_only_removes_private_temp` (failed gate leaves no bundle-*.js and no `.bundle-*.js` temp); `test_second_build_short_circuits_on_existing_hash` (2nd identical build does NOT re-invoke the node gate); `test_concurrent_builds_produce_one_valid_bundle` (24 threads → one hash, zero `FAILED syntax check` log records, one survivor, big payload intact — this is the incident reproduced); `test_importing_server_does_not_build_bundle` (SUBPROCESS: monkeypatch `build_bundle` to a tripwire BEFORE `import server`, assert not called — the no-side-effect NC). Existing bundle suite (corruption-guard + stale-self-heal + manifest-parity) = 36 green under `-n auto`. TDD paid off: the first run surfaced the real `.tmp`-extension node-gate bug + the `.bundle-build.lock`-matches-`.bundle-` assertion false-positive, both fixed.
- **Housekeeping.** `.gitignore`: added `static/js/.bundle-build.lock` + `static/js/.bundle-*.js` + `static/js/.feature-*.js` (runtime lock + private temps). Deliberately did NOT add a broad `feature-*.js` glob — it would clobber the tracked SOURCE `feature-loader.js`. (Pre-existing unrelated gap noted, not touched: a stale `feature-133a319e.js` hash bundle is currently tracked; the `.gitignore` only lists `bundle-*.js`, not `feature-<hash>.js`.)
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/js_bundler.py` (atomic publish + flock), `server.py` (`_build_js_bundle` + startup wiring), `.gitignore`, `tests/test_bundle_concurrency.py` (NEW), + this entry. Ruff clean; real 99-file production build verified (builds `bundle-a1820e73.js`, 2nd call short-circuits, zero temp leftovers).
- **Lessons.** (1) A "restart storm" in a SHARED log file may be test-harness workers importing the app, not real reboots — the `/tmp/...-gwNN` DB path and the boot-ring/`Ready` ratio disambiguate. (2) Any runtime-assembled artifact keyed by content hash MUST publish atomically (temp→rename) so concurrent builders converge instead of clobbering; the hash-path existence check makes rebuilds idempotent. (3) An import-time build of a shared artifact is a latent multi-writer bug — move it to an explicit startup call so mere import is inert. (4) `node --check` infers module type from the file extension; a temp used for the gate must end in `.js`.


### 2026-07-10 — CROSS-CONVERSATION MESSAGES "displayed incompletely": root cause was a SILENT mid-sentence translation truncation in the Project Brain content-i18n overlay (NOT the feed data). The peer-message THREAD data is complete (summary_full 354–621 chars, correctly forwarded); the visible cut ("请确认你的边界：ar") was a CACHED partial TRANSLATION. Fixed at the source (engine truncation detection + no-cache-when-truncated), surfaced a `truncated` verdict, and made the overlay keep the COMPLETE original rather than a partial. TDD (+11 = 24 green), ruff clean, both JS bundles rebuilt+verified. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report (screenshot, Team panel "跨会话消息").** Cross-session peer messages render cut off mid-word — e.g. "…请确认你的边界：ar", "…涉及 `WALK_FRAMES/GR`", "…新增坐/卷卧/玩耍/伸展姿势". Owner: "displayed incompletely."
- **Ruled OUT the obvious suspects first (measured, not guessed).** (1) FEED DATA is intact: queried `project_events` — the `note` rows store `summary` capped at 280 AND the untruncated body in `payload.summary_full` (354–621 chars); `read_project_feed` + `/api/v1/project/feed` forward the full payload; `project-brain-peers.js extractPeerThread` already prefers `pl.summary_full || ev.summary`, and its jsdom test proves the full body renders. (2) The `<notranslate>` block extractor is a no-op (peer notes carry no tags). (3) The engine's `max_tokens` (8000 for <3000-char input) is ample. So the un-translated body is COMPLETE.
- **Root cause (the overlay's translation view).** The Team thread renders under `project-brain-i18n.js`, a DISPLAY OVERLAY that translates agent/human free-text into the UI language (default ON) via sync `Api.translate.run` → `/api/v1/translate` → `_translate_freetext`. The screenshot is the CHINESE translation of an ENGLISH peer message, cut at ~40%. The English source ends "…confirm your boundary: are you editing…"; the ZH view stopped at "…请确认你的边界：ar" = mid-word on "ar[e]". The engine's truncation detector uses a flat ratio floor (0.30 ZH / 0.20 else); a body that stopped early with `finish_reason=stop` (NOT `length`) at ~40% of the source CLEARS the 0.30 floor → accepted as complete AND cached (backend `translate_cache` + browser IDB `tofu_pb_translate`), so every later view served the same cut-off text. The engine already computed a `_suspicious` soft-flag (ratio < 0.40 ZH) but only LOGGED it — never retried, never refused to cache.
- **Fix — three layers, all root-cause.** (1) ENGINE (`lib/translate/engine.py`): new `_ends_midsentence(text)` (last non-space char not in a terminator/closer set — CJK full-width enders + Latin `.!?…:;,` + closing brackets/quotes/fences). A new truncation branch fires when `clen>200` AND `len(c) < clen*soft_floor` (0.45 ZH / 0.35 else) AND `_ends_midsentence(c)` — catching the finish_reason=stop early stop that lands between the hard floor and a full translation, WITHOUT false-positiving a terse-but-COMPLETE translation (the mid-sentence signal is required, so ratio alone never rejects a finished line). Same retry/model-exclude path as the existing length/flip guards. (2) NO-CACHE-WHEN-TRUNCATED: `translate_cache.put` is now SKIPPED when the terminal verdict is `truncated`, so a later request re-translates instead of re-serving the pinned partial forever. (3) SURFACE + DISPLAY GUARANTEE: sync route returns `truncated` (from `_translate_trace.verdict`); the overlay's `_translateOne` drops a `truncated:true` result (returns null) so the COMPLETE original — always preserved in `data-pb-src` + hover title — stays visible (in its source language) rather than a cut-off translation, and the partial is not cached client-side. Bumped the overlay IDB cache-key salt to `v2` so previously-cached partials are never served again.
- **Verified the CURRENT engine already produces a COMPLETE translation** for the exact screenshot string (ran `_translate_freetext` live: 505→255 chars, ratio 0.505, verdict ok) — confirming the truncation the user saw was a STALE cached partial, not a live regression; the fixes prevent it recurring AND invalidate the stale cache.
- **Tests (+11, all green).** `tests/test_translate_midsentence_truncation.py` (NEW, 5): `_ends_midsentence` pure unit; a mid-word body in (0.30,0.45) ratio is REJECTED+retried→complete; persistent truncation ACCEPTED best-effort but NOT cached (verdict=truncated, `put` capture empty); a complete output accepted first-try + cached; a >200-char source with a terse-but-COMPLETE (ends 。) translation below the soft floor NOT flagged (false-positive guard — proves the mid-sentence signal is load-bearing). `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_content_i18n.py` (+6): a `truncated:true` translation keeps the complete original + is not cached, plus NC-4 (drop the `!d.truncated` guard → the partial replaces the original = bug returns; shipped file byte-identical after). All 24 (5+6 new + 13 existing translate/overlay) green. ruff clean; py_compile clean; core+feature JS bundles rebuilt (feature-d7250867.js) and node-syntax-checked.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/translate/engine.py` (`_ends_midsentence` + mid-sentence truncation branch + no-cache-when-truncated), `routes/api_v1/translate.py` (surface `truncated`), `static/js/project-brain-i18n.js` (drop truncated result + IDB cache-ver v2), `tests/test_translate_midsentence_truncation.py` (NEW), `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_content_i18n.py` (+2), + this entry.
- **Lessons.** (1) A "displayed incompletely" bug is not always a display bug — trace the DATA end-to-end first (feed row → payload → REST → render), which here exonerated the whole peer-thread path and pointed at the translation OVERLAY laid over it. (2) A ratio-only truncation floor cannot distinguish a legit terse translation from a mid-generation drop that lands just above it; the discriminating signal is WHERE it stopped (mid-sentence vs terminator), so combine a soft ratio floor with an ending-punctuation check rather than raising the hard floor (which would reject good terse output). (3) Never CACHE a known-incomplete result — a partial cached under a content-hash key is served forever; refuse the put and, for a client cache you can't purge, bump a key-version salt so stale entries miss. (4) When an overlay REPLACES a complete original with a machine transform, the transform failing must fall back to the original (kept in `data-pb-src`), never show less than the source.

### 2026-07-10 — Project-bar pet⋈scene round 8 (owner follow-up, screenshot): the round-7 dark understory read as an UGLY BLACK BORDER along the clipped bottom rim, worst on the pale SKY scene. Root cause: a DARK near plane is the right depth cue for meadow (grass) but WRONG for a bright/airy scene — a dark mass under a luminous sky reads as dirty pebbles glued to the edge. Fix: make the understory + fg blades scene-family-aware (warm sand for sky, deep teal for pool, dark green only for meadow) and much lower alpha on airy scenes, so depth stays but the band blends into the palette. Reconciled the value-gap tests to a PER-SCENE invariant. 81 green, ruff clean, JS bundle rebuilt+verified.
- **Owner report (screenshot, sky scene).** "The bottom edge has a large black border, which still looks a bit ugly." Rendered the current sky composite (`debug/pet_scene_composite.py sky idle 850`) and confirmed: a heavy dark grey-blue mound row pooled at the base — the round-7 dark understory (`_understory` mounds mixing 62–82% toward navy `#2E3C52`/`#0A1F27` at alpha 0.5–0.88) plus the cloud fg blades (55% toward slate, alpha 0.92–1.0). Against sky's pale warm bg (luma 226) that's a dirty border, not depth.
- **Root cause = a scene-agnostic DARK depth cue.** Round 7's "the near plane must be DARKER than the hazy bg" is correct for MEADOW (a dark grass understory is natural) but FALSE for bright airy scenes: atmospheric perspective there means the near plane is a touch DEEPER/cooler-or-warmer IN THE SCENE'S OWN FAMILY, still light — never a dark mass. Mixing sky's warm-cream near colours toward a COOL navy/grey also introduced a foreign hue that read as out-of-place.
- **Fix (tofu-scene.js `_paintBuffer` seed).** Both the `_fgBlades` shade and the `_understory` shade are now per-`kind`: sway (meadow) keeps deep green `#182A0C`; drift (pool) uses deep TEAL `#245355`; clouds (sky) uses deep WARM SAND `#C89A6E` — all in the scene's own family. Airy scenes use a gentler mix (blades 0.34→0.30, understory 0.55→0.36) and much lower alpha (blades 0.66–0.82 vs meadow 0.92–1.0; understory 0.30–0.46 vs meadow 0.55–0.75). Meadow's dark-grass understory is unchanged (that depth is wanted). The irregular gapped-mound understory shape (rooted below the rim so only tops poke up — already present from a prior pass) is kept; the border came from COLOUR/ALPHA/HUE, not shape.
- **Tests reconciled to a PER-SCENE invariant (pixel suite, still 14).** Renamed `test_foreground_plane_is_darker_than_background…` → `test_foreground_plane_creates_a_near_plane_presence`: meadow must DARKEN the bottom band ≥12/255 (grass depth); pool/sky must show a real near-plane colour change (colorΔ ≥3.5 over the bottom-20 band, which captures blade bodies not just the 6px understory) BUT with a darkening BUDGET (Δluma ≤16) so it can never regress into the dark band. Measured: meadow Δluma 28 / colorΔ 18.3; pool −9.9 / 7.4; sky 6.3 / 4.8. The `test_foreground_base_is_not_a_solid_border_strip` bottom-row-gap test (from a prior pass) still guards the SHAPE: meadow 47% see-through, pool+sky 100%. NC (`test_NEUTER_pale_foreground_has_no_near_plane_presence`) flattens the seed → meadow depth collapses below 12.
- **Verified.** 81 green (39 scene + 14 pixel + 28 pet); ruff clean; `node --check` clean. JS bundle `31a43a8c → a1820e73` carries `C89A6E`/`245355`/`182A0C`. CSS unchanged (JS-only). Final sky composite (`/tmp/FINAL_sky.png`) — warm sandy near haze, no border. UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.
- **Lessons.** (1) A depth cue is NOT scene-agnostic: "make the near plane darker" gives grass depth on a meadow but a dirty border on a bright sky — derive the near-plane shade from the SCENE'S OWN colour family (deepen it), never a fixed dark/foreign hue. (2) When a value threshold in a test forces an ugly visual (here ≥18/255 darkening forced an opaque dark strip → the border), the TEST encodes the wrong invariant — split it per-scene (direction-of-shift differs) rather than chasing the number. (3) Measure presence over the band the mechanism actually occupies: a whole-height average or a too-thin band under-reads a plane whose mass is blade-bodies above the understory — the bottom-20 band was needed to see the airy near presence at all.


### 2026-07-10 — LOG-NOISE ROOT CAUSE: `db_paths.resolve_pgdata_dir` emitted its split-fallback WARNING on EVERY call (3143×/day, the #1 line in error.log), burying real errors. Fix: log each distinct resolver decision at most ONCE per process. Return value byte-unchanged. TDD (+1 = 14 green), ruff clean, uncommitted for sign-off. (Coordinated lane split with sibling conv mrerjm2v via peer messaging — it owns the ImageDownscale + js_bundler/seq/status signals; I own db_paths + SQLite-locked triage.)
- **Signal (log frequency, not a crash).** `logs/error.log` (25k lines) was dominated by `[db_paths] Split engaged but local pgdata=/tmp/tofu/pgdata not yet populated while recoverable history exists … staying on legacy FUSE pgdata` — **3143 occurrences**, still firing at 23:05 today. That is 3143 WARNING lines describing the SAME expected, safe steady state.
- **Root cause (mechanism).** `lib/database/db_paths.py::resolve_pgdata_dir` is a PURE, deterministic resolver called on many hot paths — the `_core` import (`_PGDATA = resolve_pgdata_dir(_DB_DIR)`, once), the Tier-B archiving probe `_bootstrap._pgdata_is_resolved_primary` (line 1170-1172, called per archiving check), and bootstrap gates. On THIS deployment `data_root()` is on a `/mnt/` FUSE mount → `local_data_split_enabled=True`; the target `/tmp/tofu/pgdata` is EMPTY while the legacy FUSE `data/pgdata` still holds the live 3620-conv cluster (`has_recoverable_source=True`). So the ordering-hazard gate CORRECTLY returns the legacy path (never empty-starts) — and logged a WARNING **every single call**. The steady state is permanent because the seed migration (`_seed_local_pgdata_from_legacy`) is OPT-IN (`TOFU_DB_SEED_LOCAL=1`) and the operator hasn't opted in, so local never gets populated and the flip never happens. Result: a benign, by-design fallback screaming thousands of WARNINGs/day.
- **Why it's a real problem despite not being a crash.** The whole point of `logs/error.log` (per CLAUDE.md §2) is that a production bug leaves a diagnosable trace there; 3143 identical benign WARNINGs/day + 1793 lifecycle + 1236 auth-deprecation etc. bury the genuine ERRORs (the `[DB] PG appears dead` timeout, the `MemPrefetch gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview HTTP 404`, the js_bundler CRITICAL) under noise.
- **Fix (root cause, not suppression).** Added a module-level `_LOGGED_RESOLUTIONS: set`. The decision is keyed on `(kind, pgdata, legacy)` — stable for a deployment — and each distinct decision (`'fallback'` WARNING / `'engaged'` INFO) is emitted at most ONCE per process. The RESOLUTION itself stays fully live (a mid-life seed still flips the return value); only the LOG is de-duplicated. Also folded the remediation hint into the message (`Opt into the one-time migration with TOFU_DB_SEED_LOCAL=1`) so the single surviving line is actionable. Byte-identical return values → all 13 existing return-value tests unaffected.
- **Test (`tests/test_db_paths_local_split.py` 13 → 14).** `test_split_fallback_warning_logged_at_most_once`: calls `resolve_pgdata_dir` 50× in the split-on/local-empty/legacy-populated state, asserts every call returns the correct legacy path AND `caplog` captured exactly ONE fallback WARNING. Also cleared `_LOGGED_RESOLUTIONS` in the autouse `_clean_env` fixture so the per-process cache doesn't leak across cases. All 14 pass serially + under xdist; ruff clean. (Env pytest needs `-p xdist` explicitly since `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` is required to dodge the napari/vispy GL collection poison.)
- **Triaged as NON-bugs (in my claimed lane, no fix warranted).** (1) SQLite `database is locked` (79×) — ALL confined to 2026-07-09 20:33–21:16, a bounded heavy swarm/search eval episode on a SQLite-fallback DB; the live backend is PostgreSQL (`3620 conversations, PostgreSQL backend OK`) and none have recurred. Inherent SQLite-under-concurrency, already addressed by the PG-primary architecture. (2) compaction `[Compact] REFUSING — no user message found to anchor preservation` (690+) — every occurrence is a TEST fixture (`Task t`/`test_ref`, `msg_count=1 tokens=3 model=gpt-4`); a legitimate defensive guard in `_layer2` firing on synthetic 1-message unit-test inputs, not production.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/database/db_paths.py` (once-per-process log dedup), `tests/test_db_paths_local_split.py` (+1 test, fixture cache-reset), + this entry.
- **Lessons.** (1) A WARNING that describes an EXPECTED steady state and fires on a hot path is log SPAM, not a warning — de-duplicate it (once per distinct state per process) rather than downgrading blindly or deleting it, so the condition is still visible once and stays actionable. (2) When measuring "so many errors in the logs", FIRST build a normalized frequency histogram and separate test-fixture noise (`[test]`, `Task t`, `/tmp/pytest`, `example.com/hook`, synthetic conv ids) from production signal — the top-3 loudest lines here were all benign, and the genuinely-current ERRORs were a handful hiding underneath. (3) De-dup keyed on stable state, NOT a bare boolean flag: keying on `(kind,pgdata,legacy)` still re-logs if the deployment's paths change mid-process (e.g. a seed flip), which is exactly when you WANT the new state logged.


### 2026-07-10 — MANY-IMAGE COMPRESSION CACHE-CLIFF: collapsed the two-tier Claude image cap (7999px single / 1999px ≥5-images) into ONE uniform 1568px cap in `_downscale_oversized_images`. Owner: "多图片的对话，尤其生成图片的对话，压缩机制有点不好." Root cause: the ≥5-image threshold RETROACTIVELY re-encoded already-cached images the round the 5th arrived → guaranteed prompt-cache miss + per-round WARNING spam, for ZERO quality gain. TDD (+6 green), ruff clean, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report.** Many-image / image-gen conversations felt like the compression mechanism was mis-designed. Log evidence (conv `24ae758a`, this session's context): `[ImageDownscale] many-image request (5 ≥ 5 images) → max_px capped at 1999` firing repeatedly, once per round, on an image-gen chat.
- **Diagnosis (two paths; only one was the culprit).** (A) `executor_image.py::_downsize_for_llm` gives the chat LLM a 1024px thumbnail of each generated image (full-res stays on disk) — fine, under any cap, NOT the problem. (B) `lib/llm/body.py::_downscale_oversized_images` ran on every `build_body` for Claude with a TWO-TIER cap: 7999px while <5 images, dropping to 1999px at ≥5. The moment the 5th image entered the conversation, images 1–4 (previously sent at up to 7999px and already prompt-cached) were re-encoded down to 1999px = a guaranteed cache miss on that round, and because `build_body` recounts every round the WARNING re-fired every round thereafter. In image-gen chats you cross 5 images almost immediately (one per turn), so the cliff hits early and churns.
- **Why the two-tier design bought nothing.** Confirmed against Anthropic's own vision docs + a cross-provider limits comparison (awesomeagents.ai, verified 2026-03): Claude's vision tower internally downscales EVERY image to a **~1568px long edge (~1.15 MP)** before tokenization — an image sent at 7999px conveys the SAME information to the model as one at 1568px. The 7999px single-image allowance only avoided a hard HTTP 400; it added zero quality. Meanwhile uploads are ALREADY shrunk to 2048px on ingest (`routes/upload.py:MAX_UPLOAD_LONG_SIDE_PX`), so the ≥5 retro-shrink was re-encoding a 2048px image down to 1999px — 49px of shrink that destroyed the cache for ~nothing.
- **Fix.** One uniform `_CLAUDE_IMAGE_MAX_PX = 1568`, count-independent. Strictly better on all axes: (1) no retroactive re-encode cliff — an image at ≤1568px is skipped by the idempotent `max(w,h)<=max_px` check whether there are 2 images or 20, so a fixed-size image is re-encoded AT MOST ONCE (its first over-cap send) and byte-identical forever after → prompt cache holds across the 5th-image boundary; (2) no quality loss (model never sees >1568px); (3) still well under BOTH hard limits (8000 single / 2000 many-image) so neither 400 can fire; (4) the per-round WARNING is gone (the count-and-warn block was removed with the threshold). Removed constants `_CLAUDE_SINGLE_IMAGE_MAX_PX` / `_CLAUDE_MANY_IMAGE_MAX_PX` / `_CLAUDE_MANY_IMAGE_THRESHOLD` (no other reader — grep-confirmed).
- **Tests (`tests/test_image_downscale_uniform_cap.py`, NEW, 6).** oversized single-image → shrunk to cap; cap is count-independent (n=1/4/5/6 all → ~1568); under-cap image (1024px thumbnail) left byte-identical; **the cache-cliff NC** — 4 already-capped images + a 5th oversized one: the first four come out BYTE-IDENTICAL (regression guard: if the two-tier retro-shrink came back this flips); band-image (1600px) stable across the 4→5 boundary; non-Claude model untouched. Note: `int()` floor in the resize lands on cap OR cap-1, so assertions are `<= cap` (invariant: never exceed), which my own first run caught. Updated `tests/test_wire_fingerprint.py` docstrings (2 comments) that cited the removed "threshold=5 retro-shrink" as the motivating re-encode example → now "first-send shrink to the uniform 1568px cap"; its assertions use synthetic AAAA/BBBB bytes and were unaffected (9/9 still green).
- **Verified.** `test_image_downscale_uniform_cap.py` 6/6, `test_wire_fingerprint.py` 9/9 (env pytest needs `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 -p xdist` — napari/vispy GL poison, documented). ruff clean + py_compile clean on `lib/llm/body.py`.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/llm/body.py` (uniform cap), `tests/test_wire_fingerprint.py` (2 doc comments), NEW `tests/test_image_downscale_uniform_cap.py`, + this entry.
- **Lessons.** (1) A per-count-tier cap on cached content is a cache-cliff generator: any threshold that changes the WIRE BYTES of already-sent items retroactively busts the prompt cache the round it trips — prefer a single count-independent cap so re-encoding is one-shot and idempotent. (2) When a "generous" allowance (7999px) exceeds what the consumer can actually use (Claude's 1568px tower), it's pure wire waste with a downside (the cliff) and no upside — cap at the consumer's real processing resolution. (3) Uploads were already shrinking to 2048px, so the second-tier shrink was doing 49px of destructive work; always check what UPSTREAM stages already did before adding another shrink stage.

### 2026-07-10 — VU TASK_DONE FREEZE: the clean autopilot close-out held the SSE stream open ~63s ("回答中" frozen on the VU bubble) because the reporter LLM turn + sync translation ran INSIDE the `_autopilot_deciding` window. Fix: settle the turn FIRST, run the summary OFF-THREAD (daemon), mirroring `_spawn_async_commit_round`. TDD (+5 = 29 green), ruff clean, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Report (owner-verified against code + live logs).** In autopilot, every VU run that finished (`[VU: TASK_DONE]`) stayed stuck on the frontend — VU bubble rendered, stop button still showing, conv reading "回答中" — for about a minute before settling. "Shouldn't the conversation be considered finished?" It should; the terminal signal was being BLOCKED behind post-completion reporting.
- **Root cause (mechanism, pinned by logs).** `maybe_run_autopilot` (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`) runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside `_finalize_and_emit_done` (orchestrator.py:1000-1105), between `task['_autopilot_deciding']=True` and the `append_event(done_evt)` + latch-clear. On the clean `_vu_emitted_done` branch it called `_emit_run_summary` = a full **reporter LLM turn** (`run_summary_reporter`) + a **synchronous EN→ZH translation** (`_translate_summary_sync`) BEFORE emitting `autopilot_vu_cancel` and returning. Both `_task_terminal()` (routes/chat.py:1582) and `chat_poll` (routes/chat.py:2014) treat the `_autopilot_deciding` window as still-running (correctly — it's the follow-up-baton guard), so the SSE stream is held open and the poll reports `running` the WHOLE time the summary is composed. Live logs (conv `mres5ivx`): `21:08:47 VU emitted TASK_DONE` → `21:09:35 Summary report ready (8087 chars)` (+48s reporter) → `21:09:50 Translate ap-summary elapsed=14.9s` (+15s) → `21:09:50 concluded` = **~63s frozen**.
- **Two-part harm.** (1) The visible ~63s "回答中" freeze. (2) PERMANENT-stuck angle (owner's point 3): a >idle/proxy-timeout open stream drops the client to poll fallback, which returns `running` the whole window; on TASK_DONE there is NO follow-up baton to re-attach, so if the live `done` was already missed the conv can stay "回答中" until a manual refresh. Verified `sse_poll_fallback.js` settles a TASK_DONE poll response (`data.status !== 'running'` → `twStop`+`finishStream`+return; the autopilot-baton block is only entered when a baton is present) — so emitting the terminal `done` immediately closes BOTH.
- **Why the summary does NOT need the stream open.** The `autopilot_run_concluded` fold record is a human-only SIDECAR (`settings.autopilotSummaries[runId]`) the frontend applies whenever it lands — a connected client folds the run when the report is ready a beat later; a disconnected one recovers it from the sidecar on reload (see the `autopilot-fold-gating-and-sidecar-summary` skill). It does NOT need to ride the terminal `done`. The `_autopilot_deciding` latch exists ONLY to keep the stream open for the follow-up BATON — and on TASK_DONE there is no baton (the loop is ending).
- **Fix (mirrors the established post-done async pattern).** On the clean `_vu_emitted_done` branch: (1) CAPTURE `with_report = _should_generate_run_summary(conv_id)` up front (ordering hazard: it reads `autopilotTurnCount`, which `_clear_run_id` then clears); (2) disarm the marker + `_clear_run_id` SYNCHRONOUSLY so the turn settles now; (3) `_spawn_async_run_summary(task, conv_id, run_id, with_report)` — a NEW daemon-thread spawner (mirrors `_spawn_async_commit_round`/`_spawn_async_profile_consolidation` in commit_round.py) whose body `_run_summary_async` runs `_emit_run_summary` and, on a None (empty/errored) report, falls back to a bare `_store_run_record(reason='task_done')` so the run still folds. `run_id`+`with_report` are passed INTO the thread — the async body never re-reads the cleared run pin. The `vu_cancel` emit + `return None` (shared by all None paths) stay synchronous, so `done` fires and `_autopilot_deciding` clears in ~1s.
- **Scope discipline (owner's point 2).** ONLY the clean TASK_DONE (`_vu_emitted_done`) path changed. The follow-up baton path (VU produced a real reply → `_start_followup_task` → returns `{next_task_id, vu_msg}`) is UNTOUCHED — `_autopilot_deciding` still gates the stream there so the `autopilotNextTaskId` baton isn't stranded (the `autopilot-followup-baton-transport-agnostic` invariant). The two are NOT collapsed. The abnormal-end (budget/stuck) branch and the `arm`/`kick` carriers are likewise unchanged.
- **Tests (`tests/test_autopilot_summary.py` 19 → 24, all green).** NEW: `test_task_done_settles_without_synchronous_reporter` (drives real `maybe_run_autopilot` with a stubbed VU→TASK_DONE; asserts returns None, marker+run-pin cleared + `autopilot_vu_cancel` emitted on the CALLING thread, and the reporter runs on a DIFFERENT thread — the NC that catches a revert to the synchronous call); `test_task_done_captures_with_report_before_clearing_run_pin` (asserts `_should_generate_run_summary` is called BEFORE `_clear_run_id` and the captured flag is handed to the spawn — pins the ordering hazard); `test_run_summary_async_falls_back_to_bare_concluded_record` + `test_run_summary_async_skips_fallback_when_report_written` (the daemon body always concludes, no redundant double-write); `test_spawn_async_run_summary_is_daemon_thread`. UPDATED `test_budget_stop_callsite_passes_with_report_false` to assert the new `_spawn_async_run_summary(...)` clean-path wiring (the old synchronous `summary_rec = _emit_run_summary(...)` string is gone). Also re-ran `test_autopilot_verify.py` + `test_autopilot_budget_guard.py` (47 green — VU verdict + budget guard unaffected). ruff clean; py_compile clean. Env pytest is poisoned by the napari/vispy GL import at collection (documented) → ran with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` (async spawn + settle-first on TASK_DONE), `tests/test_autopilot_summary.py` (+5 tests, +updated call-site assertion), + this entry.
- **Lessons.** (1) An in-flight latch that legitimately holds a terminal transport open (here `_autopilot_deciding` for the baton) becomes a FREEZE bug the moment slow, non-terminal work is placed inside its window — post-completion reporting belongs OFF the hot path (daemon thread + a later `append_event`), exactly like commit-round + profile-consolidation already are. (2) When moving work off-thread, any state the async body needs that a synchronous cleanup will CLEAR (here `autopilotTurnCount` via `_clear_run_id`) must be CAPTURED before the clear and passed in — never re-read cleared state. (3) A ~60s open stream is not just a UX stall: it can exceed an idle/proxy timeout and drop to poll fallback, and if the terminal signal carries no re-attach baton the conv can strand until manual refresh — so emit the terminal event promptly regardless of the async tail.


### 2026-07-10 — INCIDENT part 4: proved the REAL re-dispatch path (not mocks), made recovery-internal FATALs NON-terminal, and rescued the 6 turns the maxTokens bug already stranded via a DURABLE scan. Reviewer's exact objection was right: every prior test mocked the path that broke. TDD (17 unit + 2 non-mocked integration + 10 marker = 29 green), ruff clean, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Reviewer objection (correct, and central).** Part 3 fixed maxTokens=None at 3 layers but EVERY test mocked the failing path: `run_killed_recovery` replaces `_redispatch_conv` with a lambda; the regression tests call `resolve_conv_config` in isolation. Nothing ran the real chain `_redispatch_conv → resolve_conv_config(no overrides) → create_task → _resolve_model_config → build_body` — which is *exactly* what FATALed. A green mocked test of the broken path proves nothing.
- **Point 1 — NON-MOCKED integration test (`tests/test_killed_recovery_integration.py`, NEW, 2).** Seeds a throwaway SQLite conv (TOFU_DB_BACKEND=sqlite + TOFU_DB_PATH + init_db) whose tail is `killed` with a model but NO maxTokens (the incident shape), runs the REAL `_redispatch_conv` (stubbing ONLY `spawn_task` to capture the task — no mock of _redispatch_conv itself), then runs the REAL `_resolve_model_config` + REAL `build_body` on the config it produced and asserts a positive-int max_tokens + no FATAL. This is the test that would have caught the incident: pre-fix it drove the whole chain to the `min(None,int)` TypeError; post-fix it builds max_tokens=128000. Second case: gpt-4o (different clamp ceiling) → positive int, no crash.
- **Point 2 — recovery-internal FATAL is now NON-terminal.** Discovered a FOURTH fix already landed at the SOURCE (`resolve_conv_config`: `ov.get('maxTokens') or defaults.get('maxTokens') or 128000` — never emits None regardless of server_defaults). But the deeper gap the reviewer flagged: a recovery carrier that FATALs shouldn't be permanently downgraded to a terminal error if the MODEL WAS NEVER REACHED. New `is_recovery_internal_fatal(err)` — kind `internal`/`generic` (or a non-envelope error) = recovery-internal fault → recoverable; `ratelimit`/`quota`/`permission`/`prompt_too_long`/`content_filter`/`model_limit` = a real model outcome (COMPLETED turn) → stays terminal. Orchestrator FATAL handler: a `task['_killed_recovery']` carrier that internal-FATALs calls `restamp_killed_after_internal_fatal(task)` → re-tags the conv tail `killed` (drops the partial error), emits a non-error DONE, and returns WITHOUT persisting a terminal error — so a later CALM boot re-dispatches it, bounded by the attempt counter already advanced before dispatch (can't loop past the cap; at-cap → `killed_exhausted`). A real model error falls through to the normal terminal persist. This runs AFTER the transient auto-retry check, so a 429 still auto-retries first.
- **The 6 burned convs — RESCUED via a DURABLE SCAN (the autopilot-resume lesson).** Confirmed from logs the incident re-dispatched 6 convs (`mremenwd, mrer7lha, mreraebr, mrerffgl, mrerjm2v, mrerpjnr` — including THIS conversation `mrer7lha`, the one the owner manually started) and all 6 FATALed. Their DB tails still carry `interruptedReason='killed'` (the FATAL set finishReason='error' but never cleared the tag). But my boot collection `_killed_conv_ids` is a PROXY SET — only convs freshly recovered from a *running* task THIS boot — so these 6 (already-persisted, no running task) would be STRANDED FOREVER. This is precisely the trap the `autopilot-resume-after-crash` memory warns about: "resume must key on the DURABLE marker SCAN, never a proxy set." Fix: `list_killed_turn_convs()` scans persisted state for an assistant TAIL tagged `killed` (recency-bounded to 7d + LIMIT 500 to keep the un-indexable `CAST(messages AS TEXT) LIKE` scan cheap; Python verifies the tag is on the TAIL, not mid-history), UNIONed with the fresh set in `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup`. Verified against the live DB: the scan finds exactly those 6. So on the next calm boot they auto-recover (bounded by the cap).
- **Tests (29 green).** unit `test_killed_recovery.py` 11→17 (+durable-scan tail-only; +internal-FATAL-vs-model-error; +restamp below-cap→killed / at-cap→exhausted; hardened the maxTokens regression to assert the SOURCE resolver never emits None). integration `test_killed_recovery_integration.py` NEW 2 (real unmocked chain). marker 10. ruff clean; py_compile clean on killed_recovery/manager/orchestrator.
- **Left UNCOMMITTED for owner sign-off.** Changed: `lib/tasks_pkg/killed_recovery.py` (durable scan + internal-FATAL classifier + re-stamp), `lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py` (recovery-carrier internal-FATAL branch), `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py` (union durable scan into boot recovery), `tests/test_killed_recovery.py` (+3), `tests/test_killed_recovery_integration.py` (NEW), + this entry. (Part-3's `resolve_conv_config`/`model_config`/`model_info` maxTokens fixes stand.)
- **Known cost.** The durable scan's `CAST(messages AS TEXT) LIKE` is un-indexable and took ~5s on this large DB even recency-bounded; acceptable for a once-per-boot best-effort sweep (wrapped, non-fatal), not worth a dedicated indexed column yet.
- **Lessons.** (1) A test that MOCKS the exact seam that broke re-certifies nothing — for a bug that lived in a call CHAIN, at least one test must drive the real chain end-to-end with only the true I/O boundary (LLM network) stubbed. (2) "Recovery fired" ≠ "recovery worked", AND "recovery ran once" ≠ "the burned work is recoverable" — a re-dispatch that FATALs from OUR OWN bug must not permanently bury the turn; distinguish an internal fault (retry) from a model verdict (terminal). (3) The autopilot-resume rule generalises: ANY boot-time recovery must key on a DURABLE SCAN of persisted state, never a proxy set of "what was in flight this boot" — the proxy silently strands already-persisted cases (here: turns a prior recovery carrier already errored).


### 2026-07-10 — maxTokens=None FATAL: moved the fix to the SOURCE + LANDED it (commit 231d1ba). Prior sessions had the 3-layer fix as uncommitted WIP (downstream coercions + tests) but left the ROOT emitter live: `resolve_conv_config` still returned `maxTokens=None`. Owner correctly rejected that as a patch, not a root-cause fix. Hardened `resolve_conv_config` so no None ever leaves the resolver, re-pointed the recovery precondition test to the new invariant, and committed the checkout-safe subset as one fix.
- **Diagnosis re-confirmed from PG (conv `mrer7lhaaxif2d`).** 4 tasks: 3 `interrupted`(killed) + 1 `error`. The final task `2b33e0d2` FATALed at Round 1 in `lib/model_info.py:453` (`min(limit, effective_limit)` with `limit=None`); `task_events` evt7 carried `detail="'<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType'"`. Same traceback hit **6 conversations at 20:37** (`mremenwdj6fw6m`, `mreraebrilhkzd`, `mrerffglzuxxw5`, `mrerpjnr267rw7`, `mrerjm2v10prwd`, `mrer7lhaaxif2d`) = a boot-time **killed-recovery sweep** re-dispatching every killed turn straight back into the crash.
- **Root emitter (the part the prior WIP left live).** `lib/conv_config.py` `resolve_conv_config` line 234 was `'maxTokens': ov.get('maxTokens', defaults.get('maxTokens'))`. `.get(k, default)` only substitutes for an ABSENT key — so the killed-recovery call shape `resolve_conv_config(conv_settings=settings, is_active=False)` (NO overrides, NO server_defaults) returned `maxTokens=None`. Downstream `_resolve_model_config` did `cfg.get('maxTokens', 128000)` which ALSO passes a present-but-None straight through → `build_body(max_tokens=None)` → `_clamp_max_tokens` → `min(None, int)` → FATAL.
- **Fix — at the source (`lib/conv_config.py`).** `'maxTokens': ov.get('maxTokens') or defaults.get('maxTokens') or 128000`. No None can leave the resolver now. Verified checkout-safe: EVERY reader already coerces (`routes/api_v1/chat.py:470`, `agent_run.py:594`, `chat_direct.py:137` all do `int(cfg.get('maxTokens') or <fallback>)`), and `test_conv_config.py::test_all_expected_keys_present` only checks key presence, not value — so baking 128000 is behaviourally identical to the old None→coerce path. The two downstream coercions (`_resolve_model_config`, `_clamp_max_tokens`) are RETAINED as defense-in-depth for any OTHER caller (compat adapters / llm_fallback / headless).
- **Test re-pointed, not deleted.** `tests/test_killed_recovery.py::test_redispatch_config_has_valid_max_tokens` used to assert `bad['maxTokens'] is None` as a "precondition documenting the bug". That invariant INVERTED: the no-defaults recovery call must now yield `128000`, so the assertion was rewritten to pin the new never-None invariant (+ a `_clamp_max_tokens` non-fatal check). Comments in `test_cc_alignment.py` / `test_backend_unit.py` updated from "resolve_conv_config emits None" → "None fixed at source; this guards defense-in-depth".
- **Verified.** `test_killed_recovery.py` 14/14 (standalone); `test_conv_config.py` 44/44 (unittest); the two tracked maxTokens guards green (driven directly, env pytest is GL-poisoned by napari/vispy at collection — documented); ruff clean + py_compile clean on all edited files.
- **Committed (commit 231d1ba) — 5 checkout-safe files:** `lib/conv_config.py`, `lib/model_info.py`, `lib/tasks_pkg/model_config.py`, `tests/test_cc_alignment.py`, `tests/test_backend_unit.py`. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this commit: `tests/test_killed_recovery.py` (its re-pointed assertion stays as uncommitted WIP) because it `import`s the still-untracked `lib/tasks_pkg/killed_recovery.py` subsystem — committing the test alone would break a fresh checkout's collection (ImportError), and dragging in the whole recovery subsystem would pollute a maxTokens-fix commit. The two committed guards (cc_alignment + backend_unit) are tracked + self-sufficient, so the regression is protected on `master` regardless. `test_killed_recovery.py` lands as a pair with `killed_recovery.py` at that subsystem's own sign-off (as the prior JOURNAL entries scope it).
- **Residual (SEPARATE issue, NOT folded into this fix).** In conv `mrer7lhaaxif2d`'s single 21-tool-round assistant turn, the model re-derived the SAME conclusion ("local conda env polluted with napari/vispy → build a clean uv venv") ~4× across rounds 16/17/19/20, worsened by an L0 compaction at round 6 (`51099→2395` chars) that trimmed the earlier finding so the model kept "rediscovering" it. This is a prompt/compaction-quality analysis-spiral, NOT the crash mechanism — and per the project's standing rule (orchestrator.py `_assemble_tool_list` comment: "如果模型陷入循环，应从 prompt 质量层面解决，而不是在 orchestrator 里粗暴截断") it must be addressed at the prompt layer, never by adding round-count truncation. Left as an open observation for a future prompt/compaction increment.
- **Lessons.** (1) A downstream coercion is a PATCH; the fix belongs where the bad value is BORN — `resolve_conv_config` was the emitter, so harden it there and keep the downstream guards only as defense-in-depth. (2) `dict.get(k, default)` does NOT guard against a present-but-None value — a config that explicitly carries `None` sails past the default; use `or` (or an explicit `is None` check) when None must mean "use default". (3) When a regression test's "precondition" pins the bug's symptom (`assert x is None`), fixing the bug INVERTS that precondition — re-point the assertion to the new invariant, don't just delete the test. (4) Commit scope must be checkout-safe: never commit a test that imports an untracked module; split it out and rely on the tracked, self-sufficient guards.


### 2026-07-10 — ADDENDUM to "INCIDENT part 3" (maxTokens=None FATAL): added cross-suite regression coverage in the GENERAL unit tests. A user re-reported the same traceback (`_clamp_max_tokens` → `'<' not supported between 'int' and 'NoneType'`). Investigation confirmed the 3-layer fix (model_config coercion + `_clamp_max_tokens` None-guard + killed_recovery server_defaults) was already present on disk as uncommitted WIP — so this was NOT a re-fix, it was verification + guarding the fix so it can't silently regress from the OTHER entry points.
- **Why more tests when part-3 already added 3.** Part-3's tests live in `tests/test_killed_recovery.py` (recovery-scoped). But `_clamp_max_tokens` / `build_body` / `_resolve_model_config` are shared HOT_PATH helpers reachable from many callers (compat adapters, llm_fallback, headless API), and their OWN suites (`test_refactored_utils.py::TestClampMaxTokens`, `test_backend_unit.py::TestBuildBody`, `test_cc_alignment.py::TestResolveModelConfigResponseFormat`) had NO None-case — so a future edit to any of those three files could reintroduce the crash without tripping the recovery suite. Added the guard where the helper is unit-tested.
