  - **Sidecar on LOCAL disk, NOT under data/ (FUSE):** the READER runs in the restarting process during the exact FUSE stall being detected, so it must never block — local xfs reads can't; and a loop wedged in a FUSE syscall simply STOPS refreshing the file → age grows = the wedge signal. Wall-clock (a different process interprets it).
  - `_reclaim_stale_instance_lock`: when the holder is a live-local server.py, consult `_holder_wedge_age`; fresh/missing/mismatched-pid/future-dated → keep today's refuse (fail-safe: OOM-orphan protection intact, cross-host guard returns FIRST and is untouched); proven-stale → CRITICAL `WEDGED local server … stale N.Ns` + fall through to unlink+reclaim. `_loop_heartbeat_task` writes the sidecar on every ~1s bump.
  - **The pid-match guard is load-bearing (owner flagged):** the window between a fresh server acquiring the lock and its first heartbeat write leaves the PREVIOUS (wedged) process's sidecar on disk with a mismatched pid → `_holder_wedge_age` returns None → refuse → the just-started healthy process is NOT killed. Do not remove it.
  - Tests `tests/test_instance_lock_wedge_reclaim.py` (9): helper matrix + real `_acquire_instance_lock` with an orphan-held flock (wedged→reclaim, fresh→refuse, missing-sidecar→refuse, foreign-host→refuse-unchanged) + in-memory neuter forcing `_holder_wedge_age→None` (holder stays locked, proving the branch load-bearing).

- **#2 FIX — executor-offloaded, FUSE-stall-safe /static route (server.py).** Disabled the built-in view (`Quart(static_folder=None)` + module-level `STATIC_DIR`) and registered an async `@app.route('/static/<path:filename>')` that moves ALL blocking FS I/O into a worker thread under a hard timeout, so a FUSE stall degrades ONE request to a fast 503 while the loop keeps serving everyone else.
  - `_load_static_bytes(filename)` (sync, in-thread): `werkzeug.utils.safe_join` under STATIC_DIR (traversal-safe — never a hand-rolled join; escape → None → 404), read bytes, adler32 ETag. `_static_offload(loop, filename)` = one-line `run_in_executor` SEAM (single neuter target). `_static_route`: `await asyncio.wait_for(_static_offload(...), timeout=_STATIC_SEND_TIMEOUT)` (default 12s, `TOFU_STATIC_SEND_TIMEOUT`).
  - **404 vs 503 stay DISTINCT:** missing file → `abort(404)` (so `_handle_404`/`resolve_stale_bundle` stale-bundle self-heal still fires — verified stale `bundle-deadbeef.js` → 302 to current); only an executor TIMEOUT → CRITICAL + `abort(503)`. Caching preserved: size/mtime/etag computed in-thread, conditional 304 built on the loop with ZERO FS I/O; `add_cache_headers` still stamps immutable long-cache on `/bundle-` (verified `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` + 304 on If-None-Match).
- **#2 range handling — a REAL bug found, not just a missing test (server.py).** Quart's `_process_range_request` emits an **off-by-one Content-Range** (passes `end-1` to a werkzeug ContentRange that already renders an exclusive stop) → `bytes=0-9` returned `Content-Range: bytes 0-8/…`. Took ownership of ranges in the route: resolve via `werkzeug Range.range_for_length(total)` (half-open, correct for closed/suffix `bytes=-N`/open `bytes=N-`), slice the in-memory bytes, set `Content-Range: bytes {b}-{e-1}/{total}` myself; unsatisfiable → 416 `bytes */{total}`.
  - **If-Range gate (RFC 9110 §13.1.5) — silent-corruption fix (owner-flagged corner).** The route checked `request.range` before consulting `If-Range`, so a STALE `If-Range` + `Range` wrongly returned a 206 of the NEW content → a resuming client stitches a new-file slice onto its old partial. Extracted `_if_range_allows(if_range, etag, mtime)` (pure): honour the range only when If-Range is absent / etag matches / date≥mtime, else serve full 200. Verified: mismatch+Range → 200 full body (no Content-Range); match+Range → 206. HEAD → 200 with correct Content-Length/ETag/Accept-Ranges (ASGI strips the body). If-None-Match+Range → 206 slice (a ranged request is a partial fetch, NOT a cache revalidation → must not collapse to 304).
  - Tests `tests/test_static_route_offload.py` (18): traversal-no-leak, missing→404, stale-bundle-self-heal, timeout→503, ETag+immutable+304, MIME, Range closed/mid/suffix/open, 416, HEAD (+HEAD+Range), If-Range match/mismatch, If-None-Match+Range, + TWO in-memory neuters (offload-run-inline starves a heartbeat coroutine; If-Range-gate forced-True corrupts the conditional-range). All neuters monkeypatch the imported module — server.py on disk untouched → no `_NC_GUARDED_SOURCES` entry needed.
- **Verify.** 43 passed across the four suites (static 18 + server_async 10 + wedge-lock 9 + lock-reclaim 6); ruff clean on server.py + the new test; live-driven through the REAL route on a throwaway SQLite instance (production :15000 NOT restarted). NOT committed — backend Python, so a restart activates it; no bundle rebuild needed.

- **#1 (OWNER's operational step, deferred — do NOT run autonomously).** Complete the pgdata→local-disk seed so the live PG leaves FUSE (the higher-blast-radius half of the same root cause). Machinery exists + is CI-tested (`db_paths` resolver gate + `_seed_local_pgdata_from_legacy` + Tier B); it was just never armed. Confirmed safe to arm: `/tmp` is `/dev/md0p1` xfs real local disk (df -T); the Jul-2 quarantine was the environmental self-heal path, not a seed bug; nightly `pg_dumpall` up to 20260710 present + legacy live. Runbook (`docs/db_durability_rollout.md`): clear stale `pgdata.corrupt.*` → `TOFU_DB_SEED_LOCAL=1` + restart (seed+verify-row-equal, resolution stays legacy) → verify row-equal → SECOND restart flips to `/tmp/tofu/pgdata` (`Local-primary split ENGAGED` + heartbeat names the local path) → legacy PRESERVED as backup. The `no such column: kind` line seen in verify runs is a sibling's uncommitted Project-Brain `project_tasks.kind` migration, unrelated.
- **Lessons.** (1) A flock proves neither liveness nor HEALTH — a loop wedged in a sync FUSE syscall is alive+named+holds the lock; add an independent staleness signal (local-disk heartbeat) and key cross-process re-association on a matching pid, never assume. (2) Quart's built-in static view runs `os.stat`/read on the event loop and bypasses the send_from_directory shim — on a network FS it's a whole-server wedge; own the route and offload the blocking I/O to a thread under a hard timeout, keeping 404 (missing) and 503 (stall) distinct so downstream self-heal survives. (3) When you take over range handling, you inherit the WHOLE surface: off-by-one Content-Range, 416, and especially the If-Range conditional-range gate whose absence silently corrupts resuming downloads — probe HEAD + If-Range(match/mismatch) + If-None-Match+Range empirically, don't assume the framework got them right.


### 2026-07-10 — Pet⋈scene, round 4 (the ARCHITECTURAL fix): near grass is now a LIVE base-anchored blade layer that genuinely FLATTENS (not overlay pop-out), + click STARTLES the cat into a flee dash + daytime naps made rare. Owner: "grass doesn't flatten, it pops leaves; make all bg elements movable; clicking should startle+move it, it sleeps too much." Pixel delta 2.97→6.98/255. TDD, neuter-bitten, bundle rebuilt+verified.
- **Owner's three complaints.** (1) The "press" pops out some grass leaves instead of flattening the background grass — still no real interaction with the background; "I want all background elements movable." (2) Clicking the pet should STARTLE it and make it MOVE. (3) It sleeps very often; after waking + being clicked it just goes back to sleep.
- **Root cause of #1 (the architectural one, flagged since round 2).** The near grass was BAKED into the static offscreen buffer (`_paintBuffer` → `_buf`) and blitted flat every frame — it can NEVER move. Only the thin translucent `_flow` overlay (alpha 0.28–0.6) reacted, and my round-3 "presence boost" made those few overlay dabs ENLARGE/BRIGHTEN under the foot = literally "pops some leaves" over a static photo. Measurability (coord/pixel delta existed) ≠ the RIGHT motion.
- **Fix #1 — LIVE near-grass blades (tofu-scene.js).** Meadow's densest near layer is tagged `live:true` and NO LONGER baked. `_paintBuffer` seeds it into a new `_blades[]` array storing each blade's fixed ROOT (base = tip − len·[cos,sin]ang) + geometry. New `_paintBlades()` renders each blade per-frame as a base-anchored stalk that (a) sways about its root and (b) FLATTENS under the pet: sampling the springy disturbance field at the blade's root x, it rotates the tip toward horizontal AWAY from the foot (`ang += side·q·1.5`), SHORTENS it (`len·(1−q·0.55)`), and darkens toward a pressed crease `#2E3D20`. So the grass genuinely lies down about its root and springs back — a real interactive layer, not a photo. The `_flow` sway-mode deform was de-boosted back to a subtle lie-over (no more enlarge/brighten pop-out); water splash + cloud stir keep their spread (those ARE real). Baked meadow dabs stay 199 (≫60 floor); ~145 blades now live.
- **Fix #2/#3 — pet FSM (tofu-pet.js).** `interact()` (a plain click) now bumps energy +22 and calls new `_startle()` → flash 'surprised' + enter new fast `flee` state (fleeSpeed 120px/s, ~0.65–1.1s) dashing AWAY from the nearest wall; `_step` animates the flee walk-cycle + clamps to bounds; post-flee `_pickNext` forces walk/idle (never nap). Daytime sleep weights slashed: idle→sleep tail REMOVED (was 10%), sit/groom→sleep cut 25%→8% AND gated on `energy<40`, forced-sleep energy gate `<12`→`<8`. Net: a healthy daytime cat never naps; a poke always wakes+moves it.
- **Tests.** Scene: retargeted `test_disturbance_is_large_and_lingers_then_recovers` from the old overlay y-sink to the BLADE ANGLE-FAN signal (pressed blades fan the near-window's max−min angle: measured pressed 3.66rad → after-remove 2.67 (lingers) → recovered 1.26 → rest 0.89); thresholds fan≥1.5 / linger≥40% / recover≤0.6 above rest; decay-neuter still bites. Pixel-diff acceptance ROSE: isolated disturbance foot mean 2.97→**6.98/255**, peak 290→**384/765**, 349× over ambient. Pet: NEW `test_click_startles_the_pet_and_makes_it_flee` (start asleep → click → state='flee' + expr='surprised' + dash ≥20px + never re-sleeps; neuter reverting startle→react bites) and `test_daytime_sleep_is_rare_not_frequent` (healthy hour-14 cat: 0 sleeps across 400 picks; neuter routing idle→sleep bites). Full: scene 32 + pixel 2 + pet 28 = 62 green. `node --check` both OK.
- **DEPLOYED.** bundle `523284ce`→`bfa0d6cc`; `flee`×11 + `fleeSpeed` + `2E3D20` crease confirmed in served bytes. Hard-refresh to see it.
- **Lessons.** (1) "Pops leaves, doesn't flatten" = the reactive thing was an OVERLAY on a baked photo; the only real fix is to make the interacted layer LIVE (base-anchored blades that rotate about their root), not a bigger overlay deform. When the owner says "make the background movable," move the actual background layer out of the bake. (2) When you move a mechanism to a new layer, the OLD test measures the wrong signal (overlay y-sink) and goes falsely green/red — retarget it at the new layer's observable (blade angle-fan), don't just relax the threshold. (3) Bundle-verify with STABLE markers: esbuild mangles local fn names (`_paintBlades`/`_startle`) and normalizes quotes, so grepping those exact strings gives false negatives — check string-literal counts (`flee`×11), unmangled top-level-ish names (`fleeSpeed`), and color literals (`2E3D20`) instead. (4) A phase-swept-RNG neuter can fail to bite if the target branch is only reached at an RNG phase the sweep never hits; make the neuter's effect PHASE-INDEPENDENT (route idle→sleep unconditionally) so the bite is deterministic.


### 2026-07-10 — Streaming "scrolling up keeps yanking me to the bottom + the file-edit block flashes/re-renders several times" ROOT FIX: showStreamingUIForConv now scroll-anchors a parked reader instead of unconditional _forceScrollToBottom. TDD, double-neuter-bitten, bundle rebuilt + in-fn-verified.
- **Owner report.** While scrolling UP from the bottom during a live turn, the view is repeatedly forced back to the bottom, and the file-edit block at the bottom flashes / re-renders several times.
- **Root cause (single bug, both symptoms).** `showStreamingUIForConv()` (`static/js/ui/stream_lifecycle.js`) is the "rebuild the whole chat + re-establish the live streaming bubble" path. It did `inner.innerHTML = html` (a FULL DOM wipe+rebuild — the flash; the browser also hard-resets `scrollTop→0` on a wipe) and then ALWAYS `_forceScrollToBottom(null, true)` (the yank — no near-bottom gate). During a live turn ANY `renderChat()` funnels here via **Guard 1c** in `chat_render.js`. The repeating mid-stream trigger in a file-editing task is `_handleToolCompacted` (`ui/sse_handlers_tool.js:356`): when L1 compaction rewrites an OLDER (cold) tool round it fires `renderChat(_conv, false)` → Guard 1c → `showStreamingUIForConv` → full wipe + force-scroll. So ~once per tool round, while parked up, you get flashed + yanked. (`updateStreamingUI`'s own auto-scroll is correctly `isNearBottom(80)`-gated and was NOT the cause.)
- **Fix.** Give `showStreamingUIForConv` the SAME anchor-preserving treatment `renderChat`'s full-render path and `_bgRefreshChat` already have (shared `_captureScrollAnchor`/`_restoreScrollAnchor` in chat_render.js): BEFORE the wipe, if the reader is parked UP on the SAME conversation (`_lazyConvId === convId` read BEFORE the reassignment, DOM already has `msg-N`, and `!isNearBottom(120)`), capture their viewport anchor; AFTER the rebuild, under the `cv-off` guard (real heights, not the content-visibility:auto estimate) re-pin the anchor to its prior offset instead of force-scrolling. A genuine conversation SWITCH (DOM still shows a different conv → `_sameConvDom` false), a first load, or a near-bottom reader still lands at the bottom via `_forceScrollToBottom`.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_streaming_scroll_anchor.py`, NEW — 3, jsdom over the SHIPPED stream_lifecycle.js).** Deterministic layout model (5 static msgs + a trailing `#streaming-msg`, each 200px; viewport 600) + a faithful copy of the two anchor helpers; models the real browser `scrollTop→0` reset on `innerHTML` set so the restore is observable. First paint (switch) force-scrolls + latches `_lazyConvId`; park the reader at msg-1; a SAME-CONV rebuild must KEEP msg-1's viewport offset (±1px) with `_forceScrollToBottom` NOT called; control: a near-bottom reader still force-scrolls. DOUBLE-NEUTER on the shipped file: `capture` (force `_preSwapAnchor=null`) → offset NOT preserved AND force-scroll IS taken (proves the capture guard diverts a parked reader); `restore` (no-op the `_restoreScrollAnchor` call) → anchor branch still taken (no force-scroll) but scrollTop stays 0 from the wipe → offset NOT preserved (proves the restore call is load-bearing). 3 pass; 10 sibling scroll/streaming suites (full_render_scroll_anchor, bg_refresh_scroll, streaming_ui, stream_deferred_no_wipe, open_conv_scroll_once) still green. Run with `-p no:napari` (the napari plugin OSErrors at collection — "GL ES 2.0 library not found").
- **Deployed.** `build_bundle()` → `bundle-bfa0d6cc.js`; `node -e` confirms both `_captureScrollAnchor` + `_restoreScrollAnchor` + `isNearBottom(120)` are present INSIDE the built `showStreamingUIForConv` body (not just elsewhere). `_preSwapAnchor` is a fn-local `let` so esbuild mangles it — 0 literal refs is expected; that's why the built-file assertion keys on the GLOBAL helper names + the `isNearBottom(120)` guard, not the mangled local. Hard-refresh to ship (hashed filename).
- **Lesson.** Any full-DOM-rebuild render path that can fire mid-stream must NOT unconditionally `_forceScrollToBottom` — it has to capture+re-pin the reader's viewport anchor when they're parked up, exactly like renderChat's full-render path. `showStreamingUIForConv` is reachable from EVERY `renderChat()` during a live turn (Guard 1c), so a per-tool-round event (cold-round `tool_compacted`) turns one missing guard into a repeating yank. When auditing "forced scroll" bugs, the tell is an UNGATED `scrollTop = scrollHeight` / `_forceScrollToBottom` (no `isNearBottom` check); the gated `updateStreamingUI` path is a red herring.


### 2026-07-10 — Auto-translate UNIFICATION: collapse the whole-message paradigm INTO the incremental one. Fixes "only fires when I switch conversations", "hangs then whole-bubble replace", and "tool content flickers on a later tick". 4 coordinated fixes (F1/F2/B1+F3/B2), TDD, neuter-bitten, bundle rebuilt + literal-verified.
- **Owner report.** Auto-translate is over-engineered and buggy: (1) staying focused on a conv → translation never fires at finalize; the moment you switch away a big bar appears; (2) it doesn't stream — hangs, then suddenly replaces the last assistant `content`; (3) tool-round `content` stays English, then the screen flickers and it's replaced on a later tick. "It's all `content`, it should just flow down one by one."
- **Root-cause map (3 parallel coder agents + direct read of the whole subsystem).** The LIVE incremental worker (`lib/translate/incremental.py`) ALREADY implements the wanted paradigm — per-round narration translated as each round closes, streamed via `partialByRound` frames into inline `.seg-narration` slots, deliverable committed separately, `done` frame carrying `segmentsByRound`. Every symptom came from the OTHER path — the WHOLE-MESSAGE `_do_translate` (`lib/translate/runtime.py`), which the retro/switch/frozen-OFF scenario runs — plus a resolver split:
  1. **Only-on-switch** = `finishStream` gated on the FROZEN `convAutoTranslate` (== the backend safety net's resolver), while the on-open retro path used the EFFECTIVE resolver. Conv sent frozen-OFF then global toggled ON → backend won't translate, finalize skips, only a conv-switch (effective-gated `_resumePendingTranslations`) fires it.
  2. **Flicker on a later tick** = `_do_translate` pushed its `done` frame (deliverable only) BEFORE building the segment map; narration reached the client only via the later DB re-read / `notify_conv_changed` = a SECOND render tick. Compounded by `_msgFingerprint` NOT hashing `seg.translatedText`, so a narration-only change couldn't re-render through the surgical `renderChat` diff — only the blunt whole-bubble `_renderMsgInPlace` outerHTML swap.
  3. **Hangs-not-streams** = the retro path delivered nothing per-round (segmented `.translate-preview` suppressed), one big LLM call then one `outerHTML` swap.
- **The 4 fixes (make the whole-message path emit the SAME frame contract as the incremental one, converge the resolver at settle points, fold the fingerprint):**
  - **F1 (stream_lifecycle.js `finishStream`).** Decide with BOTH resolvers: frozen-ON → backend owns it (arm watchdog only); effective-ON but frozen-OFF → schedule the client pipeline (`_startAutoTranslateForMsg`) NOW, in place; effective-OFF → nothing. Kills only-on-switch. The pipeline's `translateClaim` + server `claim_inflight` prevent double-fire.
  - **F2 (chat_render.js `_msgFingerprint`).** Fold a compact per-round `seg.translatedText` signature (`llmRound=len;…`), so a narration-only translation re-renders the row via the SURGICAL diff, coalesced with the deliverable on one tick. Deliverable/terminal segment excluded (tracked by `translatedContent`).
  - **B1 (runtime.py `_do_translate`).** Build the segment map BEFORE the `done` push and carry `segmentsByRound` on the frame — deliverable + all per-round narration land in ONE render tick (kills the later-tick flicker). Same map reused for the frame stamp AND the DB commit.
  - **B2 (runtime.py `_translate_segments_to_map` + `_build_segment_translation_map`).** New optional `progress_cb` emits an accumulating `{str(round):中文}` after EACH narration segment → `_do_translate` pushes `running`+`partialByRound` frames, so the retro path STREAMS round-by-round. Pure/no-op without a cb (backfill migration unchanged).
  - **F3 (tool_rounds.js + translation.js).** Stamp `data-seg-round="L<n>"` on BOTH settled narration renderers (`_renderSegNarrationHTML`, `_renderTimelineBatch`) — the SAME key the live painter uses. New `_applyPartialByRoundToSettled` surgically rewrites just the matching `#msg-N .seg-narration[data-seg-round]` block per round; the running-frame push routes to it (settled node) after the live-`#streaming-msg` painter declines — no whole-bubble swap.
- **Occam.** No dead code removed (all the defensive paths — watchdog, zombie self-heal, legacy `translatePreview` fallback slot — remain as legit degrade backstops). The unification is: the two paths now emit an identical frame shape (`partialByRound` running + `done` w/ `segmentsByRound`) and are applied by one surgical, identity-keyed painter; the resolver converges at every settle point. The retro path's whole-bubble `outerHTML` swap is now a fallback (narration slots absent), not the common case.
- **Tests (TDD, all neuter-bitten).** NEW `tests/test_translate_whole_message_unified.py` (6, backend): done frame carries `segmentsByRound` built-before-push; frame+commit share one map; no-segments → no key (data-neuter); progress_cb streams accumulating map; pure without cb (neuter); `partialByRound` running frames precede `done`. NEW `tests/test_frontend_segtranslation_fingerprint.py` (F2, jsdom): fingerprint moves per-round + on length, ignores deliverable seg, stable without segments (neuter). NEW `tests/test_frontend_settled_perround_translate.py` (F3, jsdom): surgical in-place paint, round preservation, push routes to painter + avoids whole-bubble rerender, `data-seg-round`-strip neuter. NEW `tests/test_frontend_finalize_effective_translate.py` (F1, jsdom): the 4 resolver cases + frozen-resolver neuter (proves the effective gate is load-bearing). Fixed 2 SIBLING harnesses (`test_frontend_streaming_ui.py`, `test_frontend_finishstream_no_put.py`) that eval `stream_lifecycle.js` without `conversations.js` — added the `convAutoTranslateEffective` + `_startAutoTranslateForMsg` stubs the new `finishStream` dependency needs. 64 translate+sibling tests green; ruff clean.
- **Deploy.** `build_bundle()` → `bundle-964db23c.js`; verified via `node -e` that all 5 stable literals (`_applyPartialByRoundToSettled`, `data-seg-round`, `stream-seg-narration`, `convAutoTranslateEffective`, `effective-ON but frozen-OFF`) are IN the served bundle (grep-on-mangled-names is useless; stable literals are authoritative). No CSS change (reused `.seg-narration`). Restart + hard-refresh to ship.
- **Lesson.** When two code paths produce the "same" user feature via different mechanisms, the bugs live in the WEAKER path and in the seams that assume one shape. The fix is not more branches — it's making both paths emit the SAME event contract (`partialByRound`/`segmentsByRound`) and applying it through ONE surgical, identity-keyed renderer, then folding the missing state (`seg.translatedText`) into the fingerprint so the cheap diff path can carry it. A resolver that's "frozen for in-flight safety" must still converge to the live intent at every SETTLE point, or you get "works only when I switch away".


### 2026-07-10 — overleaf-mcp layout ROOT FIX: section_page_map now maps from ONE offline output.synctex.gz parse (O(1) HTTP), not O(sections) live sync/code calls. Kills the eviction race + ~48.6s→3.9ms on the mapping phase. Decoder calibrated against the live endpoint. TDD.
- **Why (owner).** The graceful-degradation from the prior session was a BACKSTOP, not the root fix: `section_page_map` still made ~1 sequential `sync/code` HTTP call per section against a build with a short server lifetime → ~60s on a long paper + the eviction race. Do the elegant fix: parse `output.synctex.gz` once, map every section offline.
- **Calibration FIRST (didn't trust the format blindly).** Probed the live endpoint vs my parse on the ACL paper: for a source `(tag,line)` the endpoint returns the FIRST box record's `page` and `v=(V+Depth)·k` where `k=(72/72.27)/65536` (sp→bp). The Depth term was the missing piece — including it reproduces the live `h/v/width/height` to <0.001 bp. Pinned in a test against observed live values (L142→p1 v=522.235; end v=772.834).
- **Engine (lib/overleaf_mcp/layout.py).** New pure `parse_synctex(raw)` → `{inputs, by_line(first box per (tag,line)), lines_by_tag(sorted), page_bottoms, page_box_vs, max_page}`. `_fetch_and_parse_synctex` downloads+decompresses once (None if missing→live fallback). `section_page_map` resolves all sections from it: `engine="synctex-offline"`, ZERO per-line HTTP. Live `sync/code` retained as the fallback for `locate_in_pdf` single lookups AND when the artifact is absent (`engine="sync-code-live"`).
- **TWO gaps the live EMNLP run exposed (good test — harder doc than ACL), both fixed:**
  1. **Proximity search.** 15 `\subsection`/`\paragraph` headings emit NO box on their exact line → exact-match returned None. The live endpoint does a forward proximity search; `_page_for_line` now falls back to the NEAREST boxed line under the tag (bisect on `lines_by_tag`, tie→later line). → 0 None (was 15). Notably the live endpoint itself returned None for those same lines under load (eviction), so offline is MORE reliable than live here.
  2. **Footer pollution.** "Deepest box on last page" caught the page-number FOOTER (v=802.8 > text_bottom 772.8) → nonsensical text_area_fill 103.9%. `_body_bottom_on_page` caps candidates at `text_bottom + 3bp` (footer sits a full footskip lower) → true last body line. ACL happened not to trigger this; EMNLP did. Now 100.0% / 0.0pt (correct: page is full).
- **Measured before/after (EMNLP `6a1e782e9ba0ae3d7727a668`, 55 sections, A4 16pp).** compile 3.49s + fetch/parse synctex 1.27s + **map 55 sections offline = 3.9ms**. OLD live path = 884ms/section × 55 ≈ **48.6s** of HTTP. Mapping-phase speedup ≈ 12000×; total wall now dominated by the compile the old path ALSO paid. `sync_failures:0`, 0 None, engine synctex-offline.
- **Tests (tests/test_layout.py → 48 pass, 1 skip; +13 over prior).** Decoder page+v pinned to live (L142, end-v); proximity fallback (exact / nearest / tie / past-end / no-boxes→None); footer-cap unit (`_body_bottom_on_page` picks 772.83 body not 802.8 footer; None-geometry→absolute); offline-engine integration asserts ZERO `_sync_code` calls + engine label; live-fallback-when-missing; missing/garbage artifact → None. ruff clean.
- **Lesson.** When a per-item remote lookup in a loop is both slow and racing a server-side TTL, the root fix is to fetch the ONE artifact that already contains all the data and compute locally — but calibrate the offline decode against the live oracle first (the Depth term, the sp→bp constant), and replicate the oracle's fuzzy behavior (SyncTeX's nearest-line forward search) or you'll under-resolve. Separately, ANY "deepest content" heuristic over raw synctex must exclude the footer by capping at the geometry text-body bottom — the same footer/lineno pollution that ruled out using raw V-extents for the page-height earlier.


### 2026-07-10 — Swarm "Parallel Execution" panel FLICKER ROOT FIX: SSE updates now MORPH the panel in place instead of teardown/rebuild — animation clock never restarts, expanded cards survive. TDD, neuter-bitten, bundle rebuilt+hash-verified.
- **Symptom (owner).** The sub-agent (swarm) panel "flickers every time it updates."
- **Root cause (verified in `static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js` ~L691/L698).** Every `swarm_*` SSE event (`_handleSwarmPhase`/`_handleSwarmAgent` → `twUpdate` → `_syncToolRoundsDOM`) ran `slot.innerHTML = _buildSwarmPanelHTML(...)` — a COMPLETE teardown+recreate of the whole `.sw-panel` subtree. Because agent `preview` streams in char-by-char (each delta = an event) and each per-tool-call tick fires an event, this happened many times a second. Two visible effects: (1) `.sw-panel.sw-active` carries `animation:swarmBorderPulse 2.5s ease-in-out infinite` (styles.css) — a BRAND-NEW node restarts that animation from 0% every event → the amber border/box-shadow FLASHES; (2) any agent card the user expanded (`sw-a-open`) collapsed. Ironically the SAME file's 1 Hz timer already documents the correct principle ("update `[data-sw-start]` elements in place: zero re-render … rather than churn the gate") — the SSE path just violated it. Same class as the debug-panel preserve-open bug and `renderChat`'s `data-mfp` surgical diff.
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/streaming_swarm_panel.js`, new `_morphSwarmSlot` + `_swMorphNode`/`_swMorphChildren`/`_swSyncAttrs`).** Patch the EXISTING `.sw-panel` node in place: reuse the live DOM node (animation clock uninterrupted → no flash), recurse the tree syncing only changed attributes + text (unchanged text node = no-op, so a streaming preview doesn't churn), append only genuinely-new trailing children (a freshly-spawned agent card / tool-call row), and remove surplus from the tail. Node identity is by index (agents + `_toolCalls` are append-only, never reordered; an ID-remap just rewrites `data-agent-id` on the same node). Crucially the user-toggle classes `sw-collapsed`/`sw-a-open`/`sw-tl-open` are OLD-node-authoritative (`_SW_PRESERVE_CLASSES`) so an expanded card/collapsed panel survives the fresh render. Falls back to a full `innerHTML` set only on FIRST paint or a genuinely different panel root (not per-event churn). Wired into both swarm rebuild sites in `streaming_ui.js` (the `_isSwarm` re-render branch + the wrong-group relocate branch).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_swarm_panel_no_flicker.py`, NEW — 2, jsdom over the REAL shipped file).** FIX test (10 PASS): after seeding a 2-running-agent panel + expanding card #1, an SSE update (preview grows, phase flips, THIRD agent spawns) → the `.sw-panel` node is the SAME object (`PANEL_NODE_IDENTITY_PRESERVED`, via an `_identityMark` stamped on the live node — the core no-flicker assertion), the expanded card survives as the same node still open (`EXPANDED_CARD_SURVIVES`), the preview text actually updated (`PREVIEW_TEXT_UPDATED` — morph isn't a no-op), the new agent card appended, and identity holds across a 2nd identical update. NEUTER degrades `_morphSwarmSlot` to the pre-fix `slot.innerHTML=html` → `PANEL_NODE_IDENTITY_PRESERVED` and `EXPANDED_CARD_SURVIVES` both flip FAIL (teardown = the flicker + the collapse), proving the morph is load-bearing; shipped file asserted byte-identical. Harness pre-sets `window._swReconcileTicker`/`_swTimerTicker` so the file's load-time `setInterval`s don't hang the node subprocess. Sibling `test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py` + `test_frontend_streaming_interleave.py` green (16 passed).
- **DEPLOYED (not just green).** `build_bundle()` → hash CHANGED `f66ac44f`→`ecf5abb5`; `node -e` confirmed the morph survived esbuild (the `sw-collapsed`/`sw-a-open`/`sw-tl-open` preserve list + `firstElementChild`+`sw-panel` guard + `createElement('template')` path all present in the built bundle). Restart not needed (bundler rebuilds on source-hash) but a HARD REFRESH is (hashed filename changed).
- **Lesson.** A DOM subtree that re-renders on a high-frequency event stream (per-char preview, per-tick timeline) must be MORPHED in place, never `innerHTML=`-rebuilt: a rebuilt node restarts any CSS `animation:… infinite` from 0% (the flicker) and drops user-toggled expand state. Preserve node identity by index for append-only lists, and treat user-interaction classes as old-node-authoritative. jsdom (no `runScripts`) doesn't compile inline `onclick` to a callable — simulate the expand by applying the class the handler toggles.


### 2026-07-10 — Pet⋈scene VISUAL-INTEGRATION acceptance CLOSED with a real PIXEL delta (not a coordinate delta): cairo rasterizer replays the real draw stream, isolated disturbance = mean 2.97/255, peak 290/765, 148× over ambient. Owner's "measurability ≠ visibility" pushback. TDD, neuter-bitten, bundle rebuilt+hash-verified.
- **Owner's pushback (correct).** The disturbance-field coordinate tests prove flow dabs MOVE, but a few faint same-green dabs shifting a few px against the fully-baked non-reactive buffer can still be imperceptible = the original "floats on top" complaint. Demanded the actual acceptance evidence: render the composited canvas at two states and PIXEL-diff the foot region (option 1), else boost the reactive layer's presence so it reads as a value contrast (option 2). Did BOTH.
- **Option 2 (presence boost, static/js/tofu-scene.js `_paintFlow`).** Under strong disturbance `q` a deformed dab now (a) raises opacity toward opaque (`af *= 1+q*1.4`) + enlarges (`sc *= 1+q*0.35`), (b) grass splays WIDER not just shorter (`sc=(1-q*0.7)*(1+q*0.7)`), and (c) TINTS via new `_mixHex()` toward a darker pressed-earth crease `#2E3D20` (grass/clouds) or toward the bright spark (water splash). So the dent is a VALUE contrast against the baked field, not merely a position shift lost on the photo.
- **Option 1 (the acceptance test — the evidence asked for).** Env reality: headless Chromium is UNAVAILABLE (build missing ~12 sys libs — libatk/libcairo/libpango/libgbm… — no apt on the shared host; node-canvas needs the same libs). But `cairocffi` (libcairo — the SAME engine node-canvas wraps) IS importable. So: `tests/_scene_pixeldiff.js` loads the REAL shipped tofu-scene.js under node with a recording 2D context that captures the COMPLETE ordered draw stream (base gradient wash + every resolved brush-dab of the baked buffer AND the per-frame overlay: glow/sparks/flow-deform/wake — each with resolved x,y,rx,ry,ang,color,alpha,composite), pumping frames so the disturbance dome builds like real playback. `tests/test_frontend_tofu_scene_pixeldiff.py` replays that stream into cairo with true source-over / OPERATOR_ADD('lighter') compositing + real linear/radial gradients, and pixel-diffs the foot band. ALL geometry/colour/alpha are the real module's; only the rasterizer is ours.
- **THE ISOLATION (this is the subtle part — my first cut was wrong and the neuter caught it).** First version diffed pet-vs-no-pet → foot delta 9.3/255 but the frozen-field NEUTER STILL spiked 8.3, because pet-vs-no-pet ALSO captures the separate `_paintPetAttention` GLOW under the foot — it conflates two mechanisms. Correct isolation: diff LIVE-field vs FROZEN-field with the pet PRESENT IN BOTH → glow/sparks/base/wake all cancel, leaving ONLY the grass-parting disturbance. Isolated result: **foot mean 2.967/255, peak 290/765 (~97-level single-channel shift = a strongly visible dark crease), control 0.000, ratio 148×.** The test asserts mean≥1.5 AND peak≥40 AND foot≥4× control.
- **Tests (tests/test_frontend_tofu_scene_pixeldiff.py, NEW — 2, @visual).** `test_disturbance_produces_visible_pixel_delta_isolated` (the acceptance assertion above). `test_NEUTER_isolation_collapses_when_field_already_frozen` = a neuter of the TEST'S OWN isolation: frozen-vs-frozen must collapse to mean<0.5/peak<40, proving the signal is the LIVE mechanism, not pet-presence/timing/rasterizer artefact. `_record(freeze=True)` patches the shipped source to inert-disturbance, records, and ALWAYS restores (try/finally + post-restore byte-identity assert — never leaves a shipped file neutered). Module-level `importorskip('cairocffi')` + node-on-PATH skip so a bare box never hard-fails. Coordinate suites unchanged: scene 32 + pet 26 = 58 still green (presence-boost didn't regress), + 2 pixel = 60.
- **DEPLOYED.** `build_bundle()` hash moved `59372041`→`523284ce`; forced rebuild reproduces `523284ce` (source fully built); `#2E3D20` pressed-tint literal confirmed in the served bytes. Hard-refresh to see it.
- **Lesson.** For a "feels integrated / is it visible?" objective, coordinate-delta tests are necessary but NOT sufficient — the acceptance evidence is a PIXEL delta of the composited image. When a real browser is unavailable, record the real module's draw stream and replay through cairo (node-canvas's own engine) — faithful, not a re-implementation. CRUCIAL: to attribute the delta to ONE mechanism, isolate by toggling ONLY that mechanism with everything else (incl. pet presence) held constant — pet-vs-no-pet conflates the disturbance with the attention-glow. A neuter of the test's own isolation (frozen-vs-frozen → ~0) is what proves the number measures what you claim.


### 2026-07-10 — overleaf-mcp layout: graceful degradation on sync/code failure + CLSI build-eviction root cause. section_page_map/locate_in_pdf no longer crash on a real long paper. TDD, live-validated on the 16-page EMNLP paper.
- **Bug (owner, on active EMNLP paper `6a1e782e9ba0ae3d7727a668`).** `section_page_map` crashed with unhandled `httpx.HTTPStatusError: 404` from `sync/code`. The ACL paper never triggered it.
- **Root cause = CLSI build eviction.** A fresh compile + single sync = 200. But the full map fires ~1 sync/section SEQUENTIALLY: EMNLP = 57 sections × ~1s = **~62s wall**. Over that window the CLSI server can EVICT the compiled build (+ its synctex artifact); every subsequent `sync/code` then 404s. ACL (16 sections, ~15s) finished inside the eviction window; EMNLP rides the edge and sometimes crosses it. `_sync_code`'s `r.raise_for_status()` turned ONE 404 into a total crash of the whole map.
- **Fix #1 — graceful degradation.** `_sync_code` now returns `(rects, failed)` and NEVER raises: wraps the GET in try/except, and on non-200 (or bad JSON / transport error) logs `WARNING [layout] sync/code line N → HTTP S` and returns `([], True)`. Callers unpack the tuple: a failed line just gets `page: None`. CRUCIAL distinction preserved — a blank line/comment is a legit HTTP-200 `{"pdf":[]}` → `([], False)`; only a real failure is `([], True)`. So one bad line degrades to `p.?` while the rest of the map returns.
- **Fix #2 — clear message, not a blank map.** `section_page_map` counts `n_synced`/`n_failed`. If EVERY call failed (`n_failed and n_synced==0` → build fully evicted), it returns `error="Layout unavailable — every SyncTeX lookup failed (build likely expired) … recompile and retry"` instead of a misleading all-None map. A PARTIAL failure adds `sync_failures: N` + a formatter note ("N SyncTeX lookup(s) failed (shown as p.?) — likely transient build eviction"). `locate_in_pdf` adds an `error` field on a failed single lookup.
- **Tests (tests/test_layout.py, +5 → 38 pass, 1 skip).** Offline, monkeypatching the network seams (`_compile_with_editor_id`/`_synctex_input_labels`/`_fetch_log_text`/`_page_height` + compile.read_file_web): (a) line-5 404 → partial map, Middle=None, Intro/End mapped, `sync_failures==1`, NO exception; (b) all-fail → clear "Layout unavailable" error; (c) unit `_sync_code` non-200 → `([], True)` never raises (stub `_headers`+`httpx.get`); (d) blank-line 200 `pdf:[]` → `([], False)` (not counted as failure). ruff clean.
- **Live validation.** EMNLP `6a1e782e9ba0ae3d7727a668` now returns a REAL map (16 pages, 57 sections, `sync_failures:0`, last page text-area 100% full / 0.0pt) in ~62s. Forced-eviction repro (poison buildId → CLSI 500/404) confirms `_sync_code` returns `([], True)` with a logged warning and NO stack trace — the exact crash path is closed.
- **Lesson.** A per-item remote lookup inside a long sequential loop must degrade per-item, never `raise_for_status()` the whole batch — one 404 shouldn't kill the report. For SyncTeX specifically the 404 is CLSI build eviction over a long run (not a param bug): distinguish a legit empty result (HTTP 200 `pdf:[]`) from a failed call (non-200) so "blank line" isn't conflated with "build gone", and escalate all-failed → one clear "recompile and retry" message. FOLLOW-UP worth considering: batch the whole map from ONE local parse of `output.synctex.gz` (resolve all section lines offline) to eliminate the N sequential HTTP calls and the eviction race entirely.


### 2026-07-10 — Project-bar "pet floats over an inert scene" ROOT FIX: game-style GROUND-DISTURBANCE FIELD (springy interaction buffer) + the crucial deploy-gap catch. Owner's 3rd-pass pushback ("has it actually been implemented? refer to game rendering logic"). TDD, neuter-bitten, bundle REBUILT + hash-verified.
- **Owner's real question.** After two passes (contact shadow + drag-reads-ground-anchor + livelier flow) the pet STILL read as floating on an inert background. Owner asked, correctly, whether it was actually implemented and whether the background is "not an operable object", and to refer to GAME rendering logic.
- **TWO root causes, both found by measuring (not assuming).**
  1. **DEPLOY GAP (the big one).** The on-disk `bundle-129b51e7.js` was from 11:21 but my prior-turn source edits were 08:07 — I had NEVER rebuilt the bundle last turn, and there is no hot-reload (custom Python bundler). So the browser was served the OLD scene code; a refresh would have shown NOTHING of the previous work. Verified by force-rebuild → hash comparison (the authoritative check). Caveat learned: `grep tofu-scene.js` / `grep _petGroundX` on the bundle is USELESS — esbuild strips the `// ═══ file ═══` headers and mangles function-local names, so absence-of-grep-match is NOT absence-of-code. Only rebuild-and-compare-hash (or `node -e` regex on stable literals) is authoritative.
  2. **ARCHITECTURE ("not an operable object" — owner nailed it).** 95% of the scene is a single baked buffer blitted flat each frame (`c.drawImage(_buf,…)`) — it CANNOT react, ever. The only reactive layer was ~25 translucent same-green flow dabs, and the old deform was tiny (blades −45% + sink 2px) AND snapped to the pet's exact x. A few faint 2px shifts against a static same-colored photo = invisible. My own prior `test_dragged_pet_compresses_the_scene` only asserted coords DIFFER, not that they differ VISIBLY or PERSIST — so a 2px twitch passed while reproducing the bug.
- **Fix — GROUND-DISTURBANCE FIELD (the game-rendering pattern the owner pointed at).** A 1-D disturbance buffer `_disturb[]` across bar width (~1 bucket/6px): `_updateDisturb(dt,w)` PRESSES a rounded dome under the pet's ground x (`_petGround()` — live during drag too) each frame and every bucket SPRINGS BACK (`DISTURB_DECAY=0.9`, frame-rate-independent via `Math.pow(decay, dt*60)`). `_paintFlow` samples it (`_disturbAt(x)`, linear-interp) and applies a LARGE directional deform: grass bends `±q*1.4`rad, compresses `1−q*0.7`, sinks `q*6`px; water spreads `1+q*1.1`/brightens; clouds shove `±q*8`px. Result: the dent LINGERS + recovers after the pet passes (a real footprint), not a spotlight glued to the sprite. Near-ground flow density raised `w/8→w/5`. Press deepens-only (`if(press>_disturb[b])`) so overlapping frames accumulate not flicker.
- **Tests (tests/test_frontend_tofu_scene.py 30→32; grand total 58 incl. pet 26).** New `_PERSIST_HARNESS`: parks a pet at a fixed x for 6 frames (build dent), REMOVES it, pumps 40 more (watch recovery), tracking max near-ground field-dab y-sink in a ±20px window (spark + trailing-3 critter excluded). `test_disturbance_is_large_and_lingers_then_recovers` asserts (1) MAGNITUDE pressed−rest ≥3px (not a 2px twitch — the "floats" bug), (2) PERSISTENCE one frame post-removal ≥50% of the dent remains (spring-back, not snap), (3) RECOVERY back to rest within 1px after 40 frames. NEUTER `DISTURB_DECAY 0.9→0.0` (instant snap) kills the lingering → persistence assertion fails (bites). Drag-neuter re-pointed at the `_petGround()` SOURCE (foot-gate it → dragged cat presses nothing → drag==none). `node --check` OK.
- **DEPLOYED (not just green).** `build_bundle()` → hash CHANGED `129b51e7`→`59372041` (proves new bytes served); `node -e` confirms the `.9` decay literal is in the built file. Restart not needed (bundler rebuilds on source-hash), but a HARD REFRESH is (hashed filename changed). Owner must hard-refresh to see it.
- **Lesson.** (1) "Still not working" after green tests is FIRST a deploy-gap suspicion on this project — the custom bundler has no hot-reload, so ALWAYS `build_bundle()` + verify the hash moved before claiming a frontend fix ships; grep on a minified bundle proves nothing. (2) "It floats on top" when the backdrop is a baked buffer = the background is genuinely not an operable object; the game-correct fix is a springy DISTURBANCE FIELD the reactive layer samples (persists + recovers), not a bigger instantaneous deform glued to the actor. (3) A coords-DIFFER assertion is too weak for a visual-integration claim — assert MAGNITUDE + PERSISTENCE, with a decay-neuter proving the spring-back is load-bearing.


### 2026-07-10 — overleaf-mcp gains PDF LAYOUT PERCEPTION (SyncTeX): 3 new tools (get_page_count / locate_in_pdf / section_page_map) answering "which page is element X on?" + a quantitative fill-to-N-pages signal. Live-validated on a real 8-page A4 paper, TDD, ruff clean.
- **Ask (owner, overleaf-mcp root).** Can the MCP perceive the position of each element on the page (e.g. to support "adjust content to exactly fill 7 pages")? If not, find an elegant solution.
- **Gap.** overleaf-mcp had ZERO layout awareness — only source-level section parsing (char offsets in `.tex`) + compile/download. Nothing mapped source↔PDF page, and it couldn't even report the page count. Layout is only knowable after TeX runs.
- **Solution — SyncTeX via Overleaf's web endpoints** (new `src/overleaf_mcp/layout.py`, 3 tools registered in `server.py`, cookie-only). `GET /project/<id>/sync/code` (the editor's click-to-jump) maps `(file,line,column)` → PDF rects `{page,h,v,width,height}` in bp (v from page top).
- **THE BLOCKER (real discovery, cost several 500s).** `sync/code` requires BOTH `editorId` AND `buildId` query params — Overleaf's `CompileController._syncTeX` throws (→ uncaught 500) if either is missing. `buildId` comes from the compile response's output files; `editorId` is a CLIENT-MINTED UUID that MUST be sent in the compile POST body and then reused on the sync call (server ties the synctex artifact to the requesting editorId). Two more traps: the `file` param is the SyncTeX LABEL not the project path (TeX records `dir/./file.tex`; a top-level root is `./main.tex`) — I auto-detect the compile root + valid labels from the `Input:` lines of `output.synctex.gz` (strip `/compile/`, drop TeX Live `/texmf` files); and a LEADING `./` in the query param triggers a 500 (internal `/./` is tolerated) so it's stripped for the query but kept for the ZIP read.
- **Page count** from `output.log` (`Output written on … (N pages`), PDF `/Type /Page` regex fallback.
- **Fill-to-N-pages signal (owner follow-ups, 2 rounds).** (1) Replaced a hard-coded 792pt page height with the TRUE height from the PDF `/MediaBox` (source label `mediabox` vs explicit `assumed_letter` fallback — the constant can never masquerade as measured). This immediately mattered: the ACL paper is **A4 (841.89bp), not Letter** — 792 was wrong by ~50pt. (2) Added the MARGIN-AWARE figure: the raw "remaining_pt to physical page bottom" INCLUDES the bottom margin (looks like free space but content can't go there). The clean text-body bottom is NOT derivable from raw SyncTeX per-page V-extents (polluted by footer + `lineno.sty` margin numbers → 805.7pt, past the text block) — but the log's `geometry` dump gives it exactly: `text_top = 1in(72.27pt) + voffset + topmargin + headheight + headsep`, `text_bottom = text_top + textheight`, ×72/72.27 (pt→bp). Verified numerically: computed text_bottom = **772.834bp = the observed last-line v to 3 decimals**. So `section_page_map` now returns BOTH `fill_pct`/`remaining_pt` (physical) and `text_area_fill_pct`/`text_area_remaining_pt` (body, margin-excluded) + a "~N more lines fit" estimate. On the ACL last page: physical 91.8% / 69.1pt (the 69 = margin) vs text-area **100.0% / 0.0pt** — correctly "no more lines fit", where the naive number would have wrongly suggested ~6 lines of room.
- **Tests** `tests/test_layout.py` (26, offline): page-count regex, PDF `/Type/Page` (excludes `/Pages`), synctex Input-label extraction (+ system-path negative control), label resolution (dir/./file, leading-./, basename fallback), MediaBox parse (Letter/A4/nonzero-origin/absent), geometry-field parse + text-block math (matches observed v; None without required fields; tracks textheight), and a load-bearing guard that a NON-LETTER height CHANGES the fullness figure (blocks the 792 from creeping back). Full suite 34 passed, 1 skipped; ruff clean. README updated (18→21 tools). Needed `beautifulsoup4` (the existing `[compile]` extra) in the venv.
- **Lesson.** For "where is X on the page" in LaTeX, SyncTeX is the right primitive but the web endpoint needs editorId(client-UUID-in-compile-body)+buildId or it 500s. For "how full is the page", DON'T trust raw synctex V-extents (footer/lineno noise) — the page height comes from the PDF MediaBox and the printable-body bottom from the log's geometry dump; a `\dimen` in pt must be ×72/72.27 to match bp coordinates. Always separate physical-page fullness from text-area fullness — the difference IS the margin, and only the latter answers "can I add a line?".


### 2026-07-10 — MCP credential-health probe: quietly detect an EXPIRED Overleaf session cookie in the background and surface it in the settings panel. New second health axis (transport-alive ≠ credential-valid). TDD, double-neuter-bitten, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Overleaf MCP credentials expire (~30 days). After install, the tool should quietly test them in the background and, if expired, update the status prompt in the settings panel.
- **Root cause.** A "connected/ON" MCP card only means the subprocess launched and listed tools — the `OVERLEAF_SESSION` cookie is NEVER exercised at connect time, and the keepalive `send_ping()` checks only the TRANSPORT. So an expired cookie leaves the card green while `list_projects` returns a *successful MCP result whose TEXT is* `"Error fetching projects … session cookie has expired"`. Transport-health and credential-health were conflated into one axis.
- **Fix — a SECOND health axis (credential probe), env-gated, non-blocking.**
  - **Catalog declares the probe** (`lib/mcp/registry.py`): new optional `health_probe = {tool, args, fail_patterns}` on `CatalogEntry`; Overleaf entry ships `list_projects` (cookie-only, cheap read) + the expired-cookie substrings the server emits (`session cookie has expired`, `not authenticated`, `OVERLEAF_SESSION`, `error fetching projects`, `session may have expired`). Looked up by name via a LATE `get_catalog_entry` import to avoid a registry↔client cycle — so it works for already-installed servers and is naturally absent for custom servers.
  - **Bridge** (`lib/mcp/client.py`): `_cred_health[name]={status,checked_at,detail}` (status ∈ ok/expired/unknown) + `get_cred_health()`. `_run_cred_probe()` (sync, worker-thread safe) calls the probe tool, lowercases the result, matches `fail_patterns` → `expired`, else `ok`; a RAISED call → `unknown` (never `expired` — a transport blip must not cry wolf). Fired (a) once on connect via `_probe_cred_health_async()` (daemon thread, never blocks the handshake) and (b) periodically in the keepalive sweep on a healthy-ping server when `_cred_probe_due()` (once per `MCP_CRED_PROBE_INTERVAL`, default 900s) — offloaded via `loop.run_in_executor` because `_run_cred_probe` drives `call_tool`, which re-enters the MCP loop and would DEADLOCK if run inline (same trap the reconnect path documents). State dropped on `_disconnect_one`/`disconnect_all`. New const `MCP_CRED_PROBE_INTERVAL` (`TOFU_MCP_CRED_PROBE_INTERVAL`, `types.py`); 0 disables the periodic probe (connect-time still runs), <0 disables entirely.
  - **Routes** (`routes/api_v1/mcp.py`): `cred_health` added to every entry of `get_catalog_v1` (curated + custom) and `list_servers_v1`, alongside `breaker`.
  - **Frontend** (`static/js/settings/mcp.js`): a connected card with `cred_health.status==='expired'` renders an amber "Credentials expired" badge (`alertTriangle` SVG icon, NOT emoji) in place of the green ON badge + an "Update credentials" button that opens the reinstall modal (existing env prefills). i18n keys `mcp.credExpired`/`credExpiredTitle`/`updateCreds` (zh+en); CSS `.mcp-app-status.cred-expired` + `.mcp-app-card.cred-expired` (amber-warning tone, reads as "attention needed, not offline").
- **Tests (both NEW, double-neuter-bitten).** `tests/test_mcp_cred_health.py` (8, unit): Overleaf entry declares the probe; classifier → expired / ok / unknown-on-raise; no-op without a spec (custom) or when not connected; `_cred_probe_due` interval gating; disconnect drops state. `tests/test_frontend_mcp_cred_expired.py` (2, jsdom over the REAL shipped `_renderMcpCatalog`): expired → amber badge + update button + NO green ON + card modifier class; healthy → green ON only; no-cred_health → green ON (back-compat). NEUTER forces `credExpired=false` on a COPY → the expired card falls through to green ON (proving the branch is load-bearing); shipped file asserted byte-identical. In-memory Python neuters need no `_NC_GUARDED_SOURCES` entry.
- **Verify.** 30 passed (cred_health 8 + cred_expired 2 + call_health 7 + catalog_internal_only 7 + install_nonblocking 6 — no regression). `node --check` mcp.js OK; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-129b51e7.js`. ruff clean on all my edited files (the 3 remaining `F401`s — `get_bridge`/`MCPConnectError`/`sys` — are pre-existing in `install_from_catalog_v1`/registry imports, outside my edits). Restart + hard-refresh to ship.
- **Lesson.** For a credentialed MCP server, "connected" is only transport health — a live subprocess can hold a dead cookie/token. Detect credential health as a SEPARATE axis by running a declared read-only probe tool and classifying its RESULT TEXT (the server returns auth errors as successful tool results, not exceptions), gate it to once-per-interval, and NEVER run the probe inline on the MCP event loop (it re-enters via call_tool → deadlock). A raised probe is `unknown`, never `expired`, so a transient blip can't false-alarm a valid cookie.
- **FOLLOW-UP (same session, owner ask): generalized the one-off Overleaf field into a STANDARD, documented, validated interface any MCP (curated or custom, present or FUTURE) can opt into.** New single-source-of-truth module `lib/mcp/health_probe.py` (mirrors the `agent_verdict.py` pure-logic pattern): the `health_probe = {tool, args?, fail_patterns?}` CONTRACT + `HEALTH_PROBE_SCHEMA` (machine-readable, API-advertised) + `validate_health_probe()` (normalizes, merges defaults, WARN-logs + rejects malformed specs so a bad future registration gets feedback, never crashes the sweep) + `classify_probe_result()` (PURE text→verdict). TWO tiers of support, both ~1 line: (a) ZERO-CONFIG for servers following the project's structured auth convention (`.tofu/skills/mcp-tool-error-hint-pattern.md`) — `DEFAULT_CRED_FAIL_PATTERNS` (EN+中文 auth phrases) + `STRUCTURED_EXPIRED_MARKERS` (`"login_required": true`) catch them with just `{"tool": "whoami"}`; (b) free-text servers (Overleaf) pin their specific phrases, which MERGE with the defaults (so the Overleaf entry trimmed from 6 patterns → 2 server-specific ones). `_cred_probe_spec` now resolves the probe from the LIVE `handle.config` FIRST (so a user's custom `mcp_servers.json` entry opts in with a `health_probe` key, zero code change — the config loader already stores arbitrary keys verbatim and `handle.config` retains them) then falls back to the catalog. `GET /api/v1/mcp/catalog` advertises `health_probe_contract` (reflected from the schema, no drift). New suite `tests/test_mcp_health_probe_contract.py` (15): validation normalize/reject/repair; classifier structured/default/中文/explicit/healthy/no-false-positive; schema shape; custom-server-config-declares-probe; empty-list dual-defense fallback; + an in-memory monkeypatch NEUTER proving `STRUCTURED_EXPIRED_MARKERS` is load-bearing (the JSON `login_required` underscore form matches NO space-separated free-text phrase). 45 MCP tests green; ruff clean on all new files.
- **Generalization lesson.** When a per-server feature (here Overleaf cred-probe) is really an instance of a reusable capability, lift it into a declarative CONTRACT with (1) a machine-readable schema advertised via the API, (2) a validator that gives future registrations actionable feedback instead of silent no-ops, (3) a PURE classifier, and (4) sensible zero-config defaults that recognise the project's EXISTING convention (the structured `login_required` signal) — so compliant servers get it free and free-text servers add one line. Resolve the declaration from live config first so custom (non-catalog) servers participate without a code change.


### 2026-07-09 — Agent API extensibility surface made DISCOVERABLE: /api/v1/capabilities now advertises tool-registration (per-request custom_tools + tofu.tools plugins). Closes the last "functioning normally end-to-end" gap. TDD, neuter-bitten, no drift regression.
- **Gap (surfaced during the "how do others add tools?" review).** The mechanism was real — `agent_run.py` parses `body['tools']` → `mint_tool_env`, the `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/tool_result` handoff route is wired, and `tofu.tools` entry-point plugins load via `discover_plugin_specs` — but `/api/v1/capabilities` advertised NONE of it. `_tools_summary()` only enumerates built-in native tools; no per-request `tools=[…]`, no `available_plugins()` listing, no `count`/modes, no `config.plugins` doc. For a headless API a capability that can't be discovered is effectively not functioning end-to-end.
- **Fix (routes/api_v1/capabilities.py — `_extensibility_summary()`, wired into the payload between `tools` and `agents`).** New `extensibility` block, reflected from CANONICAL sources so it can't drift: (1) `custom_tools` — `submit_via=/api/v1/agent/run`, `request_field=tools`, `scope=agents:run`, `name_prefix`/`name_pattern` (from `tool_env._NAME_RE`/`CUSTOM_TOOL_PREFIX`), `result_callback=/api/v1/tasks/{id}/tool_result`, `modes={client,webhook,sandbox}` each with an `enabled` flag — `sandbox.enabled` reflects `_sandbox_allowed()` (`TOFU_CUSTOM_TOOLS_ALLOW_SANDBOX`) + carries `requires_env`, and `limits` from `ToolLimits()`; (2) `plugins` — `available` = `available_plugins()` verbatim (no hand-maintained duplicate), `opt_in_field=config.plugins`, `env_default=TOFU_DEFAULT_TOOL_PLUGINS`. Both sub-blocks best-effort (log-and-continue).
- **TDD (tests/test_capabilities_extensibility.py, NEW — 8, unit).** Drives the real uncached `_build_capabilities()` under a `patch.dict(os.environ, clear=True)` so the sandbox flag is read live. Asserts: block exists + shape; contract+modes (valid `custom__get_weather` matches the advertised pattern, bare `get_weather` doesn't; `result_callback` present); modes carry enabled flags (client+webhook always on); **sandbox OFF by default**, **flips ON when `TOFU_CUSTOM_TOOLS_ALLOW_SANDBOX=1`**; limits present; plugins block lists `available`+opt-in; `available` equals `available_plugins()` (drift guard). RED-first (8/8 KeyError before impl). NEUTER-PROVEN: hardcoding `sandbox 'enabled': False` flips `test_sandbox_mode_enabled_when_env_set` RED; restored byte-identical (`cmp -s` yes).
- **Verify (real counts, `-n 0 -p no:napari`).** 68 passed: extensibility 8 + capabilities_agents_drift 4 (NO regression) + agent_options 17 + agent_poll_routes 9 + custom_tool_isolation 17 + plugin_isolation 13. ruff clean on both edited files. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Lesson.** For a self-describing headless API, a capability isn't "done" until `/capabilities` advertises it — and the advertisement must be REFLECTED from the canonical source (`_NAME_RE`, `ToolLimits`, `_sandbox_allowed`, `available_plugins()`), never a hand-typed copy, or it drifts the moment the mechanism changes. Reading an env-derived flag in a test needs `patch.dict(clear=True)` because the payload build reads it live.


### 2026-07-10 — Debug panel "closes itself when new content streams in" ROOT FIX: preserve expanded blocks across the full-render fall-through, keyed on STABLE IDENTITY not positional index. TDD, double-neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Symptom (owner).** With the debug panel expanded, it "always closes automatically when new content is generated." Nothing actually hides the panel's `.visible` class — what collapses is the message BLOCK(s) the user expanded to inspect.
- **Root cause (verified in `static/js/core/debug_panel.js`).** `showMessagesInDebug(...)` fires on every `messages_snapshot` SSE with `isUpdate=true`. The incremental path preserves `.open` blocks, but it FALLS THROUGH to a full re-render (`p.innerHTML=""`, then `p.scrollTop=0`) when the snapshot diverges: `roleMismatches>1 || (existingCount>0 && Math.abs(newCount-existingCount)>existingCount)`. That trips routinely early in a generation: the panel is first populated by the small cold `/debug-messages` server reconstruction, then the first live wire snapshot has enough extra messages to blow past the threshold → full wipe → every expanded block collapses + scroll jumps to top.
- **Fix.** Capture the open blocks + tools-open + scroll BEFORE the wipe, re-apply AFTER the full render (incremental path already preserved them); only snap scroll to top on a genuine first render, else restore `_prevScroll`.
- **Review pushback (correct) → identity keying.** First cut keyed capture/restore on `data-idx` (positional). But `data-idx` is exactly the drift class the mutation paths (regenerate/patch/delete) were hardened against by resolving on `_msgId`: a snapshot reflecting a COMPACTION/RECONCILE can drop/reorder an earlier message, so index N after the render is a DIFFERENT message → the wrong block re-opens. Re-keyed on a stable per-message identity: new `_debugMsgIdentity(msg)` = explicit id when present (`_msgId` / `tool_call_id` / assistant `tool_calls[0].id`) else `role + text-length + djb2(text, Math.imul-base36)`; stamped as `block.dataset.mid` in `createBlock`, refreshed on the incremental fingerprint-change path. Capture collects `.open` blocks' `data-mid` into `_openMids`; restore iterates FRESHLY-rendered blocks and re-opens by matching `data-mid`, so the opened block follows its content to wherever it now sits and a different message landing at the old index is NOT spuriously opened. Tools block shares `.debug-msg-block` but has no `data-mid` → cleanly excluded from the mid set, restored separately via `_toolsWasOpen`.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_debug_preserve_open.py`, NEW — 3, jsdom over the REAL shipped file).** (1) FIX: expand SYSTEM block → divergent live snapshot forces the fall-through → block stays open with body re-rendered (≥12 PASS). (2) NEUTER #1: patch a COPY so `_openMids.add` swallows every add → the block collapses (`FAIL EXPANDED_SURVIVES_FULL_RERENDER`), proving the restore is load-bearing. (3) NEUTER #2 (the reviewer's option-2 disproof): degrade capture+restore to POSITIONAL (`data-idx`) → the DRIFT case (drop an earlier message, marked block shifts idx 4→3) re-opens the WRONG block + leaves the target collapsed (`FAIL CORRECT_BLOCK_OPEN_AFTER_DROP`/`wrong_block_not_opened`), proving index-based restore CANNOT pass the drift case, i.e. stable identity was required. Both neuters assert the shipped file stays byte-identical. Existing `test_frontend_debug_approx_chip` + `test_frontend_debug_brain_badge` stay green (7 total). `node --check` OK; ruff clean; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-51a42b00.js` (identity survives minification: `dataset.mid`×6, `_debugMsgIdentity`×3). Restart + hard-refresh to ship.
- **Lesson.** When the server can reconcile/compact/shrink a persisted list out from under the client, ANY handle used to re-associate DOM state across a re-render must key on a STABLE message identity, never a positional index — the same drift rule already enforced on regenerate/patch/delete. A single-frame "block reappears" test proves the restore FIRES; only a drop/reorder case with a uniquely-tagged target proves it restores the RIGHT block, and a positional-restore neuter is what makes that assertion load-bearing.

### 2026-07-10 — Autopilot VU turns never auto-translated (real gap) + deployed the undeployed streaming-interleave fix. Diagnosis-confirmed by owner; both parts fixed, TDD neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Symptom (owner report, on conv mre58lxth33ncr).** (1) Auto-translate "doesn't trigger" for this conversation; (2) tool-call content + thinking "disappeared" on the frontend. Verified independently: DB fully intact (29 toolRounds each with `assistantContent`+`thinking`, all matching segment ids), so #2 is NOT data loss.
- **Root cause #1 (the real, unfixed gap).** The conv is an AUTOPILOT run. Assistant turns auto-translate via `manager._sync_result_to_conversation → _maybe_auto_translate_assistant`. But the autopilot VU turns are persisted on a SEPARATE path — `autopilot._append_vu_message_to_conv` — and `autopilot.py` had ZERO `_maybe_auto_translate_*` calls (`grep` = NONE). So every VU turn is left untranslated unless a viewer happens to fire a manual `/api/translate` (exactly why msg2, which the owner was viewing, got translated and msg4, the last turn, didn't — confirmed in app.log: msg2 via `Translate.v1 started … msg=2`, msg4 nothing).
- **Fix #1 (lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py).** New `_maybe_auto_translate_vu(conv_id, vu_msg_id, content)` helper called at the VU-append success site in `maybe_run_autopilot` (right after `_append_vu_message_to_conv` returns non-None). It re-reads the persisted messages, resolves the VU row INDEX by matching `_msgId == vu_msg_id` (authoritative — never a guessed positional), then delegates to the role-agnostic `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant(conv_id, content, vu_idx, db=db)`. CRUCIAL: passes NO `task` — the parent task's `_assistantMsgId` and its incremental per-round accumulator belong to the ASSISTANT turn, not the VU content; handing them in would mis-anchor + adopt the wrong accumulator. The whole-message thread is the right path. Idempotent against a concurrent frontend manual translate: the safety net's own gates (`resolve_auto_translate` off / already-Chinese / existing `translatedContent` / `claim_inflight` dedup keyed by `_msgId`) all still apply. Best-effort (never raises into the autopilot loop). `_run_autopilot_kick` needs NO separate wiring — it calls `maybe_run_autopilot`, so the single site covers both the natural-stop and idle-kick VU-append paths.
- **Root cause #2 (already-fixed-but-undeployed).** #2 is the live-STREAMING segment-interleave bug diagnosed + fixed in sibling conv mrbylvashtemxh (epic pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5 step 5b): the SETTLED/DB render already interleaves per-round thinking+narration, but the streaming path blindly zeroed `content`/`thinking` on every `delta_reset`, so round N's prose vanished live and the bottom content zone showed only the last round's tail. That fix (delta_reset per-round capture + `_renderStreamRoundProse` + `Math.imul` fingerprint + `.translate-preview` suppression) was UNCOMMITTED in `streaming_ui.js`/`sse_pipeline.js` but there was NO `static/js/bundle-*.js` on disk → the server was serving the OLD path. Not a code bug — a deploy gap.
- **Fix #2 (rebuild the bundle).** `build_bundle()` → `bundle-fe7cf240.js`; `get_styles_filename()` → `styles-02962770.css`. Verified the streaming symbols survive esbuild mangling in the BUILT core bundle: `_renderStreamRoundProse`×1, `stream-seg-en-narration`×1, `Math.imul`×2, `delta_reset`×1; and the CSS rules are in the built stylesheet: `[data-xlate="1"] … .stream-seg-en-narration{display:none}`, `.seg-timeline .seg-thinking`, `.seg-timeline .seg-narration`.
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_autopilot_vu_auto_translate.py` (4, unit): drives the REAL `_append_vu_message_to_conv` + `_maybe_auto_translate_vu` against a stateful fake DB — asserts the safety net is enqueued exactly once for the VU turn at its ACTUAL index (2, resolved from `_msgId`, not 0/guessed), with the live db threaded through and `task=None`; a missing-`_msgId` row fires nothing; a source-order guard that the translate call FOLLOWS the append site; and an in-memory NEUTER (`neutered_source`, read-only — no `_NC_GUARDED_SOURCES` entry needed) that breaks the `_msgId`→index resolver → the translate MISSES a row that IS present (bites). Streaming repro: existing `tests/test_frontend_streaming_interleave.py` 5/5 green (Part A round-0 prose survives round-1's `delta_reset`; Part C bottom `.translate-preview` absent when timeline renders + reappears under the flag-off neuter — the exact "reappears on pause" repro cleared), each double-neuter-bitten. Combined run: 13 passed; ruff clean.
- **Lesson.** When a message class is persisted on a code path SEPARATE from the main assistant finalize (autopilot VU, and structurally like the endpoint-critic before it), the server-side auto-translate safety net does NOT reach it — wire it explicitly at that path's persist site, resolve the row index from the stable `_msgId` (never a positional guess), and pass NO parent `task` (its accumulator/anchor belong to a different turn). And "translation still broken" can be a DEPLOY gap: an uncommitted frontend fix with no `bundle-*.js` on disk means the custom no-hot-reload bundler never shipped it — rebuild + restart + hard-refresh.
- **FOLLOW-UP (same day, owner pushback): forward-only doesn't fix the ALREADY-persisted turn on the REPORTED conv.** The Fix #1 wire only translates NEW VU turns; conv mre58lxth33ncr's msg4 was already on disk untranslated, so the named conversation stayed visibly broken. Added the one-shot backfill, mirroring the `segments_backfill` REUSE pattern (conv-OOM lesson: a write-path fix is incomplete without a backfill that REUSES, not copies, the write-path logic):
  - **Shared pure collector** `lib/conversations/vu_translate_backfill.py::collect_untranslated_vu_turns(messages)` → `[{idx,msgId,content}]` for `role=user`+`_isVirtualUser` rows with non-empty `content` but no `translatedContent`. Pre-filter ONLY — no language/settings gate (those belong to the safety net).
  - **Migration** `tests/_migrate_backfill_vu_translations.py` (dry-run default; `--id`/`--limit`/`--apply`) uses the collector then DELEGATES each hit to the SAME production `_maybe_auto_translate_vu`, so the safety net's own gates run verbatim (autoTranslate-off / already-Chinese / existing-translatedContent / in-flight dedup) — the script adds NO gate and NO raw `messages` write of its own; the only state change is the normal `_commit_translation_to_db` (CAS on updated_at + notify_conv_changed). Because the safety net spawns a daemon thread, `--apply` POLLS the row until `translatedContent` lands (`--settle-timeout`, default 120s) so it reports a VERIFIED result, not fire-and-forget.
  - **Acceptance on mre58lxth33ncr (RAN it):** dry-run flagged exactly idx=4 (msgId df7e0006, 2316 chars, tc=0). `--apply` → committed 1227 chars. DB re-read confirms msg4 now: `translatedContent`=1227 chars, **predominantly Chinese**, `role=user`+`_isVirtualUser=True`, `content` (2316) unchanged as the 原文, **`originalContent` ABSENT** (proves it took the DISPLAY-translation path — writes `translatedContent`, NOT the normal user→English `originalContent` path that would corrupt it), `_translateDone=True`/`_showingTranslation=True`. Re-run `--apply` = 0 to do (idempotent — the collector's `translatedContent` skip). (Model note: dispatch chain hit a 404 on one gemini variant then fell through to a working model — expected fallback, translation succeeded.)
  - **Tests** `tests/test_vu_translate_backfill.py` (6, unit): collector selects only the untranslated VU turn, skips translated-VU + normal-user + assistant + empty-content + non-list; a reuse-guard that the migration binds the shared collector AND `_maybe_auto_translate_vu`; an in-memory NEUTER (`neutered_source`, read-only) dropping the `translatedContent` skip → a translated VU turn wrongly re-flags (bites). All green (15 across the two VU suites + streaming).
- **Symptom-2 LIVE acceptance (not just green tests): the running :15000 server actually serves the fix over HTTP.** `GET /` returns 200 and its rewritten HTML tags `bundle-fe7cf240.js` + `styles-02962770.css`; `curl`-ing the served bundle bytes shows `_renderStreamRoundProse`×1 / `stream-seg-en-narration`×1 / `Math.imul`×2, and the served CSS carries the `.stream-seg-en-narration` suppress rule — so the OLD streaming path is no longer what the browser receives (bundler rebuilt on source content-hash; no self-restart needed, hard-refresh pulls the new hashed names).
- **Backfill lesson.** Forward-wire + one-shot backfill are the TWO halves of a persisted-state fix — the objective named a specific conversation, and only the backfill heals it. Reuse the live gate (delegate to `_maybe_auto_translate_vu`), don't re-implement it; when the healer is async (thread → LLM → commit), the migration must POLL to a verified result. And "confirm the fix is deployed" means curl the SERVED bytes, not just assert the source/built file on disk.

### 2026-07-09 — Headless Agent API billing-leak ROOT FIX: settlement rebound from the HTTP request lifecycle to the TASK TERMINAL event (both /agent/run + /chat/completions) + BaseException terminal-emit in run_task. Audit found the defects; fixed TDD, neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Audit verdict (rigorous "is the Agent API healthy?" pass).** Core workflow sound — 102 tests green across agent_run/byo/ephemeral/trajectory/admission/task_runtime/agent_loop; terminal signal robust (single seam `manager.append_event → notify_task(terminal) → fire_terminal_callbacks`, fires exactly once under lock); admission acquire↔release + slot/tool_env disposal balanced on all exit paths; capability advertisement no-drift (30/30). BUT surfaced a **systematic billing-reservation leak**: settlement was bound to the HTTP request lifecycle, so it was skipped on (a) blocking-timeout-then-late-finish (`agent_run.py:678` / `chat.py:547` early-return only `unregister_waiter`s) and (b) mid-stream client disconnect (`_stream_generator` `except (GeneratorExit, CancelledError)` re-raises without settling). The 30-min janitor only *refunds* stale reserves → under-bills genuinely-consumed tokens (a revenue-correctness bug, not just hold-duration). Multi-user/credits installs only (all billing helpers no-op when `user_id` empty).
- **Root cause + fix (both surfaces).** Settlement belonged on the TASK terminal, not the request. Moved `settle_task(...)` INTO the terminal callback `_on_done` — the SAME seam that already releases the admission slot (`routes/api_v1/agent_run.py` + `routes/api_v1/chat.py`). One move settles every terminal path exactly once against ACTUAL final usage: timeout, disconnect, spawn-fail, reaper, AND happy path — because they ALL reach terminal via `append_event(DONE) → fire_terminal_callbacks → _on_done`. `settle_task` is already idempotent on `ref_id=task_id` (ledger `settle`/`reserve_release` idempotent), so the pre-existing request-lifecycle settle + the stream generator's `_settle_once`/`_settle_streaming_billing` become harmless redundant second calls (defense-in-depth, left in).
- **Settle-vs-release semantics chosen (disconnect path).** SETTLE against real usage, NOT a blanket refund — the work actually ran; refunding would under-bill consumed tokens. The generator is NOT the settle authority (a disconnect skips it); the terminal callback is. A task that genuinely never terminates still falls to admission-slot TTL (1h) + billing janitor (crash backstop).
- **Deeper root cause (from the runtime audit).** `run_task`'s FATAL handler caught `except Exception` — a `BaseException` (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit / asyncio.CancelledError) slipped past it → task stayed NON-TERMINAL → slot + reservation leaked until TTL. Added a sibling `except BaseException as be:` (orchestrator.py) that stamps error status + emits terminal `DONE(error)` (so `_on_done` fires → slot released + billing settled) then RE-RAISES to preserve cancel/shutdown semantics. Skips the emit when `_endpoint_managed`. The reaper path (`_finalize_reaped_stuck_task`) needed NO change — it already emits `append_event(DONE)` → `_on_done`, so the callback binding subsumes it (correctly: the reaper has no billing context — that lives in the route closure — so putting release code there would be wrong).
- **TDD (tests/test_api_billing_terminal_settle.py, NEW — 7, unit, real SQLite ledger + billing-user-bound key + funded wallet).** Leak invariant asserted = the janitor's own detector `_stale_reservations`: after terminal, NO `reserve` row without a matching `reserve_release`/`debit`. (1)+(2) agent_run + chat blocking-timeout-late-finish settle (RED before route fix, GREEN after — driven through the REAL route + real `_on_done`); (3)+(4) agent_run + chat stream-disconnect settle — driven END-TO-END via Quart test-client `conn.disconnect()` (first cut wired its own `_on_done` = false green; rewrote to exercise the real route), assert reservation stays OPEN mid-flight then balances post-terminal; (5) settle idempotency (double-settle debits once); (6) reaper finalize settles via terminal callback; (7) run_task BaseException emits terminal DONE + fires on_terminal, then re-raises. NEUTER-PROVEN: reverting the `except BaseException` body to a bare `raise` flips test (7) RED; restored byte-identical (`cmp -s` yes). The 4 route-leak tests were confirmed RED against pre-fix code before the fix landed.
- **Verify (real counts).** New suite 7/7. Full regression 186 passed (agent_run 14 + byo 10 + ephemeral 11 + trajectory 8 + byo_polish 11 + admission 9 + billing 19 + billing_janitor 5 + relay_billing_gate 27 + task_runtime 28 + agent_loop 11 + stuck_reaper 8 + turn_auto_retry 12 + compat_narrator 6 + new 7). ruff clean on all edited files. `-n 0 -p no:napari` (napari plugin crashes collection otherwise). Uncommitted for owner attribution.
- **Lesson.** Bind resource settlement (billing, slot, disposal) to the TASK terminal event, never to the HTTP request lifecycle — the request can end (timeout / disconnect) long before the task does, and a task can be force-finalized by a reaper the request never sees. The terminal-callback seam is the single choke point that covers every exit. Make the settle idempotent so redundant call sites are harmless. Broaden a process-fatal handler to `BaseException` (emit-terminal-then-reraise) so cancel/kill still frees resources. When driving an SSE disconnect test, use the real test-client `disconnect()` through the real route — a hand-wired callback copy is a false green.


### 2026-07-09 — Edit-on-every-bubble robustness gap CLOSED: an in-place edit now realigns the SEGMENT SoT (not just `content`). Owner-flagged before sign-off. TDD + neuter, golden byte-identity intact.
- **Owner's concern (correct to force).** Agent/autopilot bubbles with tools/thinking render via the segment timeline; many agent bodies "render from segments, not content". If so, editing `msg.content` would PATCH a field the bubble doesn't display → silent no-op.
- **VERIFIED IN SOURCE — the premise is HALF right.** The visible deliverable answer does NOT render from segments: `renderSegmentTimelineHTML` (tool_rounds.js:2792-2793) EXCLUDES terminal/deliverable segments ("caller renders the deliverable separately, after the panel"); the body renders from `msg.content` in the un-gated `else if (msg.content)` block (chat_render.js:1305), and `saveEditOnly`→`renderMessage` re-runs it. Wire rebuild `_build_assistant_messages` also appends `final_content = msg['content']` (segment reconstruction produces only the TOOL messages). So the visible bubble + next-turn wire DO reflect a content edit. NOT the silent no-op feared.
- **REAL latent gap (this is what I fixed).** The stored `msg.segments` keeps its own `deliverable:true` terminal text = the PRE-EDIT answer. Content wins in today's readers, but the charter makes segments the authoritative SoT and `deliverable_text()` ALREADY prefers `derive_content(segments)`.
