Editing content while leaving segments stale = a second-source-of-truth divergence that resurfaces the old answer on any segment-driven read (headless/compat). Fixed at the authoritative layer so every caller stays consistent.
- **Fix.** New pure helper `lib/tasks_pkg/segments.py::apply_edited_deliverable(segments, new_content)` — the inverse projection of `derive_content`: rewrites ONLY the terminal deliverable text (thinking/narration/tool_use untouched), returns None on no-op (empty list / already-consistent), appends a terminal deliverable when none exists + content non-empty. Wired into `_patch_message_blocking` (routes/conversations.py): when `content` is edited and the row has `segments`, realign in place (best-effort, never blocks the edit). Exported in `__all__`.
- **Tests (tests/test_edit_realigns_segments.py, NEW — 4 + neuter).** Pure: rewrites only terminal deliverable + derive_content round-trip; no-op→None (empty/consistent); append-when-no-terminal + skip-empty. DB-backed: the REAL PATCH route realigns the persisted segment. NC monkeypatches `apply_edited_deliverable`→None → segment keeps 'ORIGINAL ANSWER' while content='EDITED ANSWER' → divergence assert fires (load-bearing). Golden `test_segment_model.py` 62/62 still green (byte-identity of derive_content/thinking/tool_rounds intact — the helper is additive). ruff clean.
- **Lesson.** When a value is stored in two places and one is (becoming) the SoT, an edit path must update BOTH or the SoT resurfaces stale data — even if the CURRENT visible reader happens to prefer the other field. Realign at the authoritative backend layer (PATCH), not per-frontend-reader. Verify "renders from X" claims by reading the actual render gate: here the timeline deliberately EXCLUDES the deliverable, so content was already the visible source.


### 2026-07-09 — Edit button on EVERY bubble (edit-in-place) + drift-proof delete (stable-id DELETE). Epic pt_00fc6bd07d79404d. TDD, neuter-bitten, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** (1) Agent / autopilot / other bubbles should have an Edit button top-right, like user turns do. (2) "Deletion doesn't work well and often fails."
- **Issue 1 root cause (edit).** `chat_render.js:1377` gated Edit on `_humanAuthored = isUser && !msg._isVirtualUser`, and `startEditMessage` (edit_message.js) early-returned for any `role !== 'user'`. So assistant/autopilot-VU/critic/planner bubbles had NO Edit affordance at all. A load-bearing test (`test_frontend_autopilot_flat_render.py`) even asserted VU had no edit.
- **Fix 1.** Edit `editH` is now emitted UNCONDITIONALLY on every bubble; Regen stays human-only via the unchanged `_humanAuthored` line (regenerating from a synthetic driver turn is nonsensical). `startEditMessage`/`saveEditOnly` branch on `_isHumanUser = role==='user' && !_isVirtualUser`: a human user turn keeps the full editor (Save / Save & Resend + attachment tray); every other lane gets EDIT-IN-PLACE only (Save → PATCH content, no resend, no tray). GUARDED the shared-input tray: the paste handler now only stages images when `#editImagePreviews` exists, and `saveEditOnly` only touches `pendingImages` / calls `_restoreInputFromBackup()` for the human-user editor — otherwise an in-place edit of an assistant bubble would clobber the user's live composer input. VU/critic edits still reset+re-run the display-translation as before.
- **Issue 2 root cause (delete "often fails").** The DELETE endpoint was INDEX-ONLY, while regenerate/patch were already hardened with stable `_msgId` addressing (routes/chat.py `truncateToMsgId`). All the recent server-side reconcile / ghost-sweep work SHRINKS the persisted list, so the client's index drifts from the server's → `_delete_message_blocking` returns 400 "Index N out of range" or pops the WRONG message. That is the reported failure.
- **Fix 2 (mirror the regenerate drift-correction).** `_delete_message_blocking` now takes `msg_id` (route reads `?msgId=`); when present it resolves the CURRENT index via `find_message_by_id` (index is the fallback), logging drift corrections. `api.js deleteMessage(convId, idx, mode, {msgId})` sends it. `message_actions.js` captures the target message OBJECT(s) before the request and removes them by IDENTITY (`indexOf`) after — the server may resolve a different index, so its returned `deletedIndices` are SERVER indices that need not match the local array; identity removal is drift-proof (falls back to server indices only if a target isn't found by ref).
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_delete_message_by_msgid.py` (4 + neuter, DB-backed, standalone+pytest): stale-index single resolves by msgId; stale-index turn-mode deletes the user+assistant pair at the RESOLVED position; absent msgId → index fallback; unresolved msgId → index fallback. NC monkeypatches `find_message_by_id`→(None,None) → the stale-index delete removes the WRONG msg (m3 not m2), proving the resolver is load-bearing. UPDATED `test_frontend_autopilot_flat_render.py`: `a3_vu_no_edit`→`a3_vu_has_edit` (VU now carries edit-in-place), VU still `no_regen`; NC-3 now only breaks Regen (Edit is unconditional). Verify: 8 pytest + standalone-neuter all green; ruff clean; `node --check` on all 4 JS files OK; bundle rebuilt.
- **Lesson.** When the server can reconcile/shrink a persisted message list out from under the client, EVERY index-addressed mutation (regen, patch, delete) needs stable `_msgId` resolution with an index fallback — delete was the last one still index-only. On the client, remove by object identity, never by trusting server-returned indices against the local array.


### 2026-07-09 — Project-bar pet⋈scene INTEGRATION pass: contact shadow (planted, not floating), DRAG now compresses the background, and a livelier moving field. 4 new neuter-bitten tests. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Owner complaint (two parts).** (1) Dragging the pet causes no compression/interaction — it floats on top of the background. (2) The background doesn't move; only simulated light spots twinkle.
- **Root causes (verified in source).** (a) NO grounding: the sprite is a `position:absolute` `<img>` with no shadow, so it reads as floating in every state. (b) `_petFootX()` (tofu-scene.js) returns null while `state==='drag'`, so during a drag BOTH the flow-deform (grass parting) AND the wake spawner were suppressed → nothing under the held cat reacted. (c) The FLOW overlay was thin (`~w/12` dabs) with tiny amplitude (sway ±0.28rad/±1.4px), so the only visible motion was the sun-glow + specular sparks = "just light spots".
- **Fix 1 — contact shadow (CSS, static/styles.css `.tofu-pet::after`).** Soft radial-gradient ellipse on the POSITION layer (`.tofu-pet`, translateX only) — NOT the img layer — so it stays on the ground while the sprite bobs/breathes above it (a real cast shadow doesn't bounce). `z-index:-1` behind the sprite. `[data-state="drag"]::after` shrinks (22×5→12×3px) + fades (opacity .55) + nudges down: the classic "object rises, shadow detaches" cue, the visual counterpart to the airborne cat no longer pressing grass.
- **Fix 2 — drag interacts (tofu-scene.js).** New `_petGround()`/`_petGroundX()` helper = same source as `_petFootX` but WITHOUT the drag gate, so it stays live while lifted. `_paintFlow` deform now reads `_petGroundX()` → grass/water/clouds compress under a DRAGGED cat too. CRUCIAL invariant preserved: the WAKE spawner (`_trackPet`) STILL uses `_petFootX()` (null under drag), so `test_dragged_pet_leaves_no_wake` holds — a lifted cat parts the grass it's over but leaves no footstep trail in thin air. Both couplings still fully guarded (no TofuPet → no-op).
- **Fix 3 — livelier field (tofu-scene.js).** Flow-dab count `w/12`→`w/8`; sway band widened (`0.6..0.98`→`0.5..0.99`); sway amplitude ↑ (rock ±0.28→±0.42rad, x ±1.4→±2.6px) + a new vertical breathe (±0.8px); drift/cloud glide speeds ~1.7×; a slow global `gust = 1+0.6·sin(ms·0.00022)` swells the whole field as one so it reads as WIND, not per-dab twitch. Sway deform's `y = f.y + k*2.2` → `y += k*2.2` so the press-down composes with the breathe. Glow constants UNTOUCHED (still ≤0.20 peak — the locked dim invariant).
- **Tests (tests/test_frontend_tofu_scene.py, +7, all neuter-bitten). Scene suite 27→30 (grand total 56 incl. pet 26).**
  - `_DRAG_HARNESS` records every visible-canvas dab `translate(x,y)` for ONE deterministic ms=0 frame with a STATIONARY pet; at ms=0 the only pet-dependent dab-position contributor is the flow-deform (wake foot-gated=silent under drag, sparks/critter/glow move no dabs), so drag-vs-none coord difference ⟺ the drag deform fired. `test_dragged_pet_compresses_the_scene` (drag≠none, same length); NEUTER reverting `_petGroundX()`→`_petFootX()` makes drag==none (bites). `test_css_pet_has_contact_shadow_that_detaches_on_drag` + NEUTER stripping `.tofu-pet::after`.
  - **FIELD-MOTION (owner's 2nd-pass pushback — the 3rd complaint was NOT actually proven).** Every prior scene test inspects ONE frame, so a regression freezing the flow layer while sparks kept twinkling would pass all of them AND reproduce "only the light moves". New `_MOTION_HARNESS` pumps TWO frames (elapsed 0 → 2000) with NO pet, capturing per-dab `(fill,x,y,ang)`. Field is ISOLATED from light by construction: dab() order in `_paintFrame` is sparks(fill==pal.spark) → flow-field(near colors) → critter(always the trailing 3 dabs, no wake w/o pet), so `_field_dabs` drops the last 3 and excludes the spark colour. `test_field_animates_between_frames_for_every_scene` asserts ≥50% of field dabs displaced (all 3 scenes). `test_light_moves_even_when_field_frozen_control` proves the split is real (the spark dabs move on their own). `test_NEUTER_frozen_field_is_caught` injects `ms=0` INSIDE `_paintFlow` (runs AFTER the spark loop) → field static, sparks still twinkling = the EXACT reported bug; the motion assertion fails for every scene (bites) while the light-moves control still holds (bite is field-specific, not "nothing moves").
  - **Harness gotcha (cost me the first run):** `_loop` guards `if(!_t0)` and `_t0` starts `0` (falsy) — pumping `cb(0)` then `cb(2000)` re-triggers the guard and resets elapsed to 0, so both frames were identical. Pump at NON-zero ts (100 → 2100) so `_t0=100` is truthy: frame A elapsed 0, frame B elapsed 2000.
  - `node --check` both JS OK.
- **Lesson.** "Floating pet" is two distinct fixes: GROUNDING (a cast shadow on the position layer, not the bobbing img) and INTERACTION-WHILE-HELD (a separate ground anchor without the foot's drag gate — but keep the footstep wake foot-gated so a lifted cat doesn't stamp thin air). "Only light moves" = the flow layer was too sparse/low-amplitude; a shared low-freq gust term makes a field read as alive far more than louder per-dab jitter. CRUCIAL test lesson: a single-frame count/coord test proves a layer is PAINTED, never that it's ANIMATED — to guard "the field moves, not just the light" you MUST compare TWO frames AND isolate the field from the light (by paint-order + colour), with a neuter that freezes ONLY the field while the light keeps moving. Otherwise a frozen-field regression sails through green.


### 2026-07-09 — Unified turn-initiation attribution: every AUTO-INITIATED turn is now visually attributable (was: proactive/timer/brain rendered as the human "You", swarm-continue as bare "Agent"). One backend `_initiator` seam + one frontend registry. TDD, sibling-coordinated, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Bug (owner-confirmed).** `chat_render.js` user-lane avatar/label branched only on `_isEndpointReview`/`_isVirtualUser`/`_peerMessage`, so `_proactive`/`_timer`/`_brainDispatch` injected user turns fell through to the onigiri "You"; swarm auto-continuation was an assistant turn showing the plain "Agent". Each auto-source hand-rolled its OWN boolean; no single seam.
- **Backend — ONE authoritative field + ONE resolver (`lib/conversations/turn_initiation.py`, NEW).** `_initiator` vocabulary (`human`/`autopilot`/`proactive`/`timer`/`brain`/`peer`/`operator`/`swarm`); `stamp_initiator(msg, initiator)` = the ONE write seam (human = no-op, unknown = logged+dropped); `resolve_initiator(msg)` = the ONE read seam — prefers `_initiator`, else falls back to the legacy booleans (ONE-directional migration; the ONLY place that reads them). Wired into the three real injection choke points: `message_queue.dispatch_next_queued` (brain/peer/operator, alongside the legacy markers it already stamped), `scheduler._shared.inject_and_run_task` (proactive/timer, on both the user msg + assistant placeholder), `swarm.integration._start_autocontinue_turn` (swarm, on the assistant placeholder). `reconcile._is_special_turn` now routes its "auto-initiated?" check through `is_auto_initiated()` — so ALL auto sources are ghost-sweep-protected, not just the two markers it hardcoded.
- **Frontend — ONE registry (`settings/branding.js`).** `INITIATOR_REGISTRY` (id → {avatar glyph, i18n labelKey, cls, lane}) with distinct inline-SVG glyphs (§3.4, no emoji) for proactive(bolt-in-circle)/timer(hourglass)/brain(two-lobe)/swarm(nodes); `_resolveInitiator` (mirrors the backend resolver one-directionally) + `_initiatorPresentation(msg)`. Consumed by `chat_render.js` (user-lane proactive/timer/brain → registry avatar+label; assistant-lane swarm → avatar+label+`init-badge`), `streaming_render.js` `_streamingBubbleHTML` (new `swarm` role sourced from the registry + `@param role` JSDoc updated for `test_frontend_typecheck`), and the reconnect/initial-render role selection in `sse_pipeline.js`+`stream_lifecycle.js` (pick `swarm` for `_swarmAutoContinue`). i18n keys `initiator.{proactive,timer,brain,swarm}` (zh+en). No new top-level JS file → no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change; all registry refs are runtime (function-body), and branding.js already loads after chat_render/streaming_render.
- **Tests (both neuter-bitten).** `tests/test_turn_initiation.py` (21, pure): resolver defaults/precedence/legacy-fallback (parametrized all 8), stamp validation, the three seams' source contains `stamp_initiator`, reconcile protects every auto-initiator. `tests/test_frontend_initiator_attribution.py` (jsdom, ≥24 PASS): proactive/timer/brain user turns → registry label (NOT "You") + glyph (NOT onigiri); legacy-boolean-only resolves identically; swarm assistant → "Auto-continued" + badge (NOT "Agent"); human→You / agent→Agent no-regression; NEUTER stubbing `_initiatorPresentation`→null makes every auto-initiator fall back to You/Agent (bug reproduces). Harness gotcha: assistant-lane render needs `_segTimelineEnabled`/`renderFinishInfo`/etc. stubbed, and a top-level `const` (INITIATOR_REGISTRY) is NOT a global under `(0,eval)` scope — assert it via the hoisted `_initiatorPresentation` instead.
- **Verify.** 21+1 new green; regressions green (peer-header-identity, autopilot-vu-verbatim, typecheck, settle/startup reconcile); `node --check` on all 6 edited JS files OK; ruff clean. Coordinated a `branding.js` path lease with live sibling mre5ajl8 (pet-imagery) — they confirmed no collision (their work is in tofu-pet.js/icons/pet). Restart + hard-refresh to ship (bundled JS hash changes).
- **Lesson.** When many code paths each stamp their own provenance boolean, don't add an Nth reader that knows the whole zoo — collapse to ONE authoritative field + ONE resolver that reads legacy markers as fallback, and route EVERY consumer (backend reconcile + frontend registry) through it, so "migrating away from scattered inference" doesn't spawn a second scattered layer.


### 2026-07-09 — Empty "Agent" air-bubble ROOT FIX #3 (render-time BELT) + fixture-pollution cleanup: epic pt_b02486c823944ed3 objective MET (all 3 layers landed, tested, neuter-bitten). Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **#3 belt (static/js/ui/chat_render.js).** Early return in `renderMessage`: an ORPHAN empty-assistant placeholder produces NO DOM (`return ""`). Two new helpers: `_streamBoundToMsg(msg)` — IDENTITY-based live-stream check (an activeStreams entry whose bound `assistantMsg` IS this object, or whose `taskId === msg._taskId`), never array position, mirroring the connecttotask _taskId convention; `_isOrphanEmptyAssistant(msg)` — role=assistant AND no content AND no thinking AND no toolRounds AND no finishReason AND no error AND NOT stream-bound. Deliberately NOT keyed on merely-empty content, so a legit "Preparing…" pre-first-token bubble (empty but stream-bound) still SHOWS. Returning '' is safe across all three render paths: surgical `outerHTML=''` removes, append skips null firstElementChild, full render contributes nothing. Render-only — never splices/persists (that's #1/#2's job); this is purely the last line so a ghost escaping both never renders.
- **TDD (tests/test_frontend_orphan_bubble_render_guard.py, NEW — 3 pytest cases, jsdom).** A empty+stream-bound → SHOWS; B empty+orphan → HIDDEN ('') (RED before, GREEN after); C finishReason / D thinking / E toolRounds / F error / G stream-bound-by-taskId / H normal-content → each SHOWS (controls: proves not keyed on empty content, and identity works via both object-ref and taskId). Double neuter-bite: nc_guard_off (orphan predicate → false) → B fails; nc_ignore_stream (drop the live-stream clause) → A fails. Regression: autopilot flat-render(4)+vu-timeline(2)+report-affordance(2)+convview-dedupe(2) = 10 passed (belt hides only orphans). chat_render.js is in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (edit ships; hash changes on restart).
- **Fixture-pollution fix (owner-flagged before close).** test_get_path_reconcile.py + test_settle_time_reconcile_dropped_task.py used HARDCODED conv_ids → leaked state when run in the same pytest process as other reconcile suites (a latent way a real regression could be masked in CI). Added a `_uid(stem)` per-run unique-suffix helper (uuid4 hex[:8]) to every conv_id/task_id in both files. Verified order-independent: get-path+settle+reconcile_conversation+error_husk+committed_parity = 25 passed in one process (both orderings).
- **Epic status: DONE.** #1 warm-open adoption + #2 settle-time reconcile + #3 render belt all landed, each RED-first + neuter-bitten, no regressions. The ghost is now killed at BIRTH (#2 sweeps the dropped-task placeholder at task-end), the server's reconciled list is authoritative on EVERY open (#1), and even an escapee never renders (#3). Moves the app to the commercial-grade posture (server log is the render source of truth). Uncommitted across: static/js/core/conversations.js, lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py, static/js/ui/chat_render.js + 3 new tests.
- **Lesson.** A three-layer defense for a persisted-state ghost: (1) adopt the authoritative server list on every open, (2) sweep at the source (task-end), (3) render-time belt keyed on the FULL orphan predicate incl. an identity-based live-stream check — never on empty content alone, or the belt blanks a legitimate pre-first-token bubble. Give DB-backed test fixtures unique per-run ids or they mask regressions via cross-suite pollution.


### 2026-07-09 — Startup-path reconcile wired (epic pt_bdbf5cb865f04b43): recover_stale_tasks_on_startup now runs the backend ghost reconcile in the SAME recovery commit. Closes the last reconcile-trigger gap + turns the 2 pre-existing test_startup_reconcile reds green.
- **Ask (autonomous board dispatch).** The GET path reconciles on every user-visible open, but a conversation cleaned ONLY at server-restart (crash recovery, never re-GET'd before display) got neither husk-collapse nor buried-ghost sweep persisted. Wire `reconcile_conversation_messages` into `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` (manager.py), persist same-commit, stamp `_reconciledAt`. Non-blocking (no "two agents" regression — GET covers the visible open); overlaps sibling mrdkf10v's settle-time reconcile (a DIFFERENT trigger).
- **Root cause of the 2 reds (verify-first).** `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` had ZERO `reconcile_conversation_messages` / `_reconciledAt` references — the startup reconcile was designed (test + docstring existed) but never wired. `test_buried_ghost_swept_and_persisted` + `test_reconcile_fires_history_rewrite_signal` were red because the sweep+signal had no production caller on this path.
- **Fix (lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py, inside the `for cid, crow` recovery loop, just before the sidebar-stamp block; ~40 lines).** After the interrupted-content merge, reconcile the MERGED list when a merge happened else the STORED list (a buried ghost must be swept even when the interrupted task added no content — the `messages_json`-still-None case, which is exactly the buried-ghost fixture). `cache_prefix_count=0` — post-restart the prompt-cache state is empty so the whole list is mutable (EDITABLE_TAIL_COUNT single-source invariant; byte-identical to the pure-fn default). On a real change only: set `messages_json` to the cleaned list, stamp `settings._reconciledAt`, and fire `notify_history_rewrite(cid)`. Best-effort (reconcile failure logs + falls back to the unreconciled list; never aborts recovery).
- **notify_history_rewrite NOT notify_compaction (load-bearing, per the L2 cache-prefix invariants skill).** They are OPPOSITES: compaction SILENCES the wire-diff (expected L2 edit); history_rewrite only NAMES an UNEXPECTED backend edit and must NEVER let `_wire_proven_identical` flip True. A startup reconcile is an unexpected history edit → history_rewrite. `test_reconcile_fires_history_rewrite_signal` asserts exactly this seam has a production caller now.
- **Tests / verify (real numbers).** `test_startup_reconcile.py` 3/3 (was 1/3): buried-ghost swept+persisted+`_reconciledAt`, history_rewrite fired, clean-conv NOT stamped (no false-positive). DOUBLE-NEUTER proven: forcing the reconcile call to `_base_msgs, False` → buried ghost survives (`['user','assistant','user','assistant']`) → `test_buried_ghost` FAILS; restored byte-identical → green. Regression: GET-path double-neuter green, 30 pytest green (pure reconcile 6 + husk-collapse 9 + equivalence 5 + cache_prefix_stability 9 + 1). Uncommitted for owner sign-off (restart-only path — no bundle).
- **Coordination.** Claimed the board epic. My change adds a reconcile call at the STARTUP trigger; sibling mrdkf10v owns the SETTLE-TIME/task-end trigger (GATE-1 dropped-orphan case). Both call the same pure `reconcile_conversation_messages` — no overlap, additive at the shared call site. All three reconcile TRIGGERS (GET, PUT, startup) now run the same authoritative verdict; only the settle-time trigger remains (sibling-owned).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A designed-but-unwired reconcile is invisible in review (test+docstring look complete) yet leaves a whole trigger path uncovered — grep the production module for the call, don't trust the test's existence. When wiring a backend history mutator, pick the signal by SEMANTICS: expected/window-fit → notify_compaction (silences); unexpected/attributable → notify_history_rewrite (names). On the startup path cache_prefix_count=0 is correct (cache empty post-restart); a mid-session trigger MUST pass the live get_cache_prefix_count.


### 2026-07-09 — Empty "Agent" air-bubble ROOT FIX #2 (settle-time reconcile keyed by taskId): sweep the orphan placeholder AT THE SOURCE (task-end) instead of leaving it for a future warm reopen. manager.py trigger only — calls the existing pure reconcile fn; NO reconcile.py/GET-path edit (sibling's leased files untouched). TDD, double-neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Why #1 wasn't enough (owner's pushback, correct).** #1 (warm-open adopts the reconciled list) only HEALS a ghost when the user happens to re-open the conv — the placeholder is still minted, persisted, and synced. The mechanism hole is that a task which DROPS before its first token never cleans the placeholder the frontend minted as its stream target.
- **Source hole (verified).** `_sync_result_to_conversation` (lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py:~1023) early-returns on the drop-before-first-token case (`if not content and not thinking and not error: return`) — BEFORE the DB is even opened. And the GET-path reconcile can't reach it (routes/conversations.py GATE 1 skips reconcile while a task is live, because a live stream target is byte-identical to a ghost). So the orphan lingers as a blank "Agent" bubble until a warm reopen.
- **Fix (manager.py — trigger only).** New `_reconcile_orphan_placeholder_on_settle(task)` called at that skip path. It runs the SAME authoritative pure `reconcile_conversation_messages` (whose `classify_ghost_tail` already returns 'delete' for a bare empty trailing assistant) at TASK-END, then CAS-writes the shorter list + clears `activeTaskId` + `notify_conv_changed`, cache-neutral via `get_cache_prefix_count`. NO edit to reconcile.py or the GET path — I only ADD a new TRIGGER and call the existing gated pure fn (the boundary mrc05uc4 confirmed was mine; their `is_superseded_error_husk` verdict comes along for free).
- **THE GATE IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME (mirrors the GET-path live-task gate).** Keyed by taskId: reconcile ONLY when `_latest_task_for_conv(conv_id) == task['id']`. If a NEWER task superseded this one, that newer task owns any live placeholder — deleting it would be the exact data-corruption the GET-path test warns about. Safe here because the trigger fires at task-end (this task is no longer producing tokens once confirmed un-superseded).
- **TDD (tests/test_settle_time_reconcile_dropped_task.py, NEW — 3, real DB via TOFU_DB_PATH).** A dropped+latest → orphan swept at settle (RED before, GREEN after); B superseded-by-newer-task → placeholder SURVIVES (control); C settled real tail → never deleted (control). DOUBLE neuter-bite: NC-1 disable the trigger → A fails, B/C pass; NC-2 disable the taskId gate (`if False and …`) → B fails (superseded task deletes the newer task's live placeholder = corruption), A/C pass. Restored byte-identical. Regression sweep GREEN: settle(3)+get_path_reconcile(4)+reconcile_conversation(6)+committed_message_parity(3)+error_husk_collapse(9) = 25 passed.
- **Epic status (pt_b02486c823944ed3).** #1 warm-open adoption DONE; #2 settle-time reconcile DONE. REMAINING: the belt (#3) — a render-time guard keyed on "no live stream bound AND no finishReason AND no thinking" (NOT merely empty content, or a legit "Preparing…" pre-first-token bubble blanks), with a show/hide test. Belt is the last line so even a ghost escaping #1+#2 never renders.
- **Lesson.** Sweep the placeholder at BIRTH (task-end), not on a later reopen — the drop-before-first-token skip path is the source. Reuse the existing pure reconcile verdict (add a TRIGGER, don't fork the classifier). A settle-time reconcile is safer than the GET path (task already terminal) but STILL needs the keyed-by-taskId gate, or a superseded task deletes its successor's live placeholder.


### 2026-07-09 — Closed the LAST cross-device sync hole: folder ops now push a `folders_changed` frame (create/rename/delete/reorder), and a delete reconciles every device's conversations off the removed folder. Emit + apply tests, neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Mandate (owner).** The prior pass wired the 7 conversation-mutating gaps but I set folders aside as "out of scope". Owner: not my call — the objective is COMPREHENSIVE auto-sync, folders are a visible part (ChatGPT/Claude/DeepSeek all sync folder org live), and folder ops had NO real-time channel at all → create/rename/delete/reorder on one device stayed stale on another until refresh.
- **Design (dedicated frame, NOT a faked conv_changed).** Folders live in `data/config/folders.json` (a separate per-install store, not a `conversations` row), so reusing `notify_conv_changed` would fake a `conv_changed` for a non-existent conv id. Instead added `routes/api_v1/folders.py::_notify_folders_changed(*, deleted_folder_id=None)` → pushes `{type:'folders_changed', deletedFolderId?, userId}` on the SAME `notify` channel the conv-sync subscription already listens on fleet-wide (`push_event('notify', '__folders__', payload)`). Wired into all 4 mutating routes: create (after write), update (only when a folder was actually found — a 404 emits nothing), delete (carries `deletedFolderId`), reorder. Best-effort try/except — a push failure never breaks the folder mutation. `userId` is forward-safety for multi-user (client drops a foreign-user frame).
- **Frontend apply (`_onFoldersChangedPush` in cross_tab_sync.js, routed from the existing `_wireConvSyncPush` notify subscription).** create/rename/reorder → DEBOUNCED (400ms, visible+not-editing gated) `loadFolders()` which re-renders the sidebar in place (mirrors the conv-list debounced non-destructive pattern). DELETE (item 2 of the mandate) → unassign local conversations off the removed folder ON THIS DEVICE (`c.folderId=null` + ConvCache.put + saveConversations(null) metadata-only), splice the dead folder out of the in-memory `getFolders()` array so the tree doesn't flash it, renderConversationList, then reload. The deleting device already did this client-side in `deleteFolder()`; the frame makes every OTHER device reconcile too.
- **Tests (both neuter-bitten, same standard as the conv pass).**
  1. `tests/test_folders_notify_emit.py` (6, `pytest.mark.unit`): drives the REAL routes via `flask_client` (open mode → test client's `<local>` peer → loopback synthetic admin) with the folders.json store redirected to a tmp file, captures `push_event`. Asserts each of the 4 ops emits exactly one `folders_changed` frame; delete carries `deletedFolderId`; TWO negative controls (a 404 update emits nothing; a NEUTER stubbing `_notify_folders_changed` → no frame while the write still lands). Source-level neuter PROVEN: commented the delete emit → `test_delete_folder_emits_frame_with_deleted_id` FAILED; restored (grep=1) → green.
  2. `tests/test_frontend_folders_notify_push.py` (2): drives the REAL `_onFoldersChangedPush` under jsdom (captured-not-fired timers). Scenario A: a plain frame schedules loadFolders() (debounced, not sync) then fires it. Scenario B: a delete frame flips the referencing conv's folderId to null, leaves an unrelated conv intact, drops the dead folder from the tree. Scenario C: a foreign-userId frame is ignored. NEUTER strips `c.folderId=null` → the conv KEEPS the stale folderId (the "second device still shows it in the dead folder" bug), proving the unassign is load-bearing.
- **Verify.** Full sweep: folders emit (6) + folders apply (2) + conv-changed-notify (7) + conv emit-coverage (6) + frontend-conv-notify-push (1 harness) = 22 passed; `node --check cross_tab_sync.js` OK; ruff clean. Uncommitted for owner attribution. Restart (import-time route) + hard-refresh (bundled JS hash changes). The auto-sync objective is now end-to-end: every conversation-mutating path AND every folder-mutating path pushes a live signal — no forced refresh anywhere.
- **Lesson.** A separate-store resource (folders.json) can't ride the conversations rev signal — give it its OWN typed frame on the shared `notify` channel rather than faking the conv frame, and carry the deleted id so the reconcile (unassign referencing convs) can run on every device, not just the actor's.


### 2026-07-09 — run_command token waste ("always re-emits cd / abs python-pip"): added a STICKY per-conversation cwd anchor — stateless derived affinity à la OpenCode's Instance.directory, NOT a persistent shell / NOT env-snapshot (so the CONDA/pip contamination guard + multi-tenant isolation stay intact). config+tools+run_command+schema, 11 tests neuter-bitten, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Mandate (owner).** run_command burns tokens re-emitting `cd /mnt/.../chatui;`, re-activating envs, and using absolute `python`/`pip` every call. Owner explored a per-conversation persistent shell but flagged it "troublesome" (store an env per conv), then asked the harder question: as an Agent-Server serving many apps, how do we avoid one app contaminating the server env — AND find a MORE THOROUGH fix than the existing history guard. "Let's look at how OpenCode does it."
- **Research (real source, not guessed).** TWO OpenCode generations made OPPOSITE choices: the OLD Go `opencode-ai/opencode` (→ archived → Crush) HAD a `PersistentShell` (state persists between commands) but framed completion via per-command TEMP FILES + polling (never stdin sentinels) — i.e. even they dodged the sentinel-spoof bug. The CURRENT TS `anomalyco/opencode` DELETED it: bash tool now `spawn(cmd,{shell:true, cwd:Instance.directory})` = FRESH /bin/sh per call, cwd anchored server-side; the explicit "persistent shell mode" request #7750 was Closed-as-not-planned. Their multi-tenant env answer is req #12018 `shell.env` = a PURE FUNCTION of cwd→env recomputed per call, hard rule "secrets never become app state." Lesson: replace ACCUMULATED mutable state with DERIVED state re-computed per call from a stable anchor — no mutable state to corrupt/leak/scrub. (Sources: deepwiki opencode-ai/opencode 6.2; issues #7750, #3479, #12018.)
- **Design shipped (stateless, two layers).** (1) STICKY working_dir: a per-conv cwd registry mirroring `_conv_roots` EXACTLY (same `_lock`, LRU cap `MAX_CONV_ROOTS`, cleared in `clear_conv_state`). When a call passes `working_dir` (or a trailing `cd` sticks — layer 2), the resolved abs cwd is remembered; a later call with NO `working_dir` resumes there instead of project root. (2) cd-CAPTURE: `tool_run_command` wraps the exec command with a trailer that writes `pwd -P` to a dedicated TEMP FILE (never stdout → no sentinel spoof) and re-exits with the stashed `$?` (exit code preserved). NO persistent shell, NO env-delta persistence → `_get_cmd_env` still re-derives venv/PATH + the PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV / CONDA-strip / portable_sandbox jail per call, fully intact. That scrub IS the multi-tenant isolation answer, not a wart to work around.
- **HARD ISOLATION invariant.** `set_conv_cwd` only remembers a cwd INSIDE one of that conv's registered roots (`_cwd_within_conv_roots`, same conv-scoped registry + global fallback the resolver uses). A `cd /etc` or a hop into app B's tree is refused, anchor unchanged → app A's cwd can never leak into app B. Keyed by conv_id. `get_conv_cwd` also safe-degrades a vanished (deleted/renamed) sticky to None (never hands a dead cwd to Popen).
- **Gates / safety.** Env-gate `TOFU_STICKY_CWD=0` disables both layers. Layer-2 capture is Unix-only (needs POSIX sh) AND skipped under `portable_sandbox` (a jailed TMPDIR would make the host-side read miss) — layer-1 explicit-working_dir stickiness still works everywhere. Capture setup/read failures are best-effort (anchor just stays unchanged). The standalone/headless `execute_standalone_command` path has NO conv_id → sticky correctly inactive there (no-project fallback).
- **Files.** `lib/project_mod/config.py` (_conv_cwd registry + `get_conv_cwd`/`set_conv_cwd`/`_cwd_within_conv_roots` + clear); `__init__.py` (exports); `lib/project_mod/tools.py::_exec_run_command` (sticky default + remember-on-explicit + `cwd_sink`); `lib/project_mod/run_command.py` (`_build_cwd_capture`/`_read_cwd_capture`/`_sticky_cwd_capture_enabled`, `cwd_sink` param threaded through both simple + interactive runners via `finally`); `lib/tools/project.py` (working_dir schema doc).
- **Tests (`tests/test_run_command_sticky_cwd.py`, NEW — 11, unit).** Drive the REAL `_exec_run_command` (real subprocess): set/get within-root; reject outside-roots; vanished-dir clears; clear_conv_state drops; explicit working_dir → sticky; anchor default when no sticky; trailing `cd` captured + resumed; exit code preserved through capture (`false` → exit 1); `cd /tmp` NOT captured (isolation); `TOFU_STICKY_CWD=0` disables. NEUTER-PROVEN: `set_conv_cwd`→`return False` at source flips the 5 stickiness tests to FAIL, restored byte-identical → 11 green. ruff clean; regression `test_tool_root_pill` + `test_log_noise_reduction` (both touch clear_conv_state) still green.
- **Verdict.** Token win (no repeated `cd`, no abs python/pip — venv auto-derived from the anchor) achieved the robust way: stateless, restart-safe, worker-agnostic, and STRENGTHENS multi-tenant isolation instead of weakening it (rejected the persistent-shell + env-snapshot designs precisely because they'd defeat the contamination guard). Uncommitted for owner attribution.

### 2026-07-09 — Empty "Agent" air-bubble ROOT FIX (#1 of the two-part plan): the frontend now ADOPTS the backend's reconciled (possibly shorter) message list on a WARM re-open, instead of a render-time band-aid. Owner pushed back on "just stop rendering empty bubbles" (correctly — it hides corrupt data, the ghost stays persisted + re-syncs). TDD, coordinated with two live siblings, neuter-bitten. Uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** After many prior duplicate/ghost fixes, still a large number of blank "Agent" bubbles (assistant msg with `content:''`, only a 分支 button). Owner's framing: this is ARCHITECTURE, not scale — commercial webs (ChatGPT/DeepSeek/Kimi) render the server's event log as the single source of truth and never fabricate a placeholder slot; ours holds a mutable in-memory array patched from 4 sources (SSE/poll/GET/IDB) and INFERS lifecycle by pre-minting `content:''` placeholders.
- **Root cause (both halves verified in source, not guessed).** The backend GET-path reconcile (`routes/conversations.py:490` `_reconcile_conv_on_get_blocking` → `lib/conversations/reconcile.py`) DOES exist and IS wired (corrects the stale JOURNAL "unwired" note) and sweeps orphan ghosts — but the frontend never adopts its result in the exact window ghosts are born: (1) BYPASS — `loadConversationMessages` early-returns for any in-memory conv (`if (!conv._needsLoad && conv.messages.length>0) return conv;` ~:1168), so a warm RE-OPEN never re-fetches the reconciled list; (2) MERGE NON-ADOPTION — with a lingering (finished-task) `activeTaskId` + no live stream, MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK only APPENDED when server was LONGER (~:1503), never adopted a SHORTER reconciled list. Net: client mints ghost, server sweeps it, client never adopts the sweep → ghost persists until hard refresh.
- **Fix (static/js/core/conversations.js — #1, owner-approved order #1→#2→belt).** New pure predicate `_openConvMayHoldOrphanGhost(conv, convId)`: tail is assistant AND empty content/thinking/toolRounds AND no finishReason AND no error AND `!activeStreams.has(convId)`. It ONLY decides whether to RE-VERIFY against the server — never splices on its own verdict (avoids the banned frontend-lifecycle-inference pattern); the server stays authoritative (adopt whatever it lists). Two adoption points: (a) weakened the warm-open early-return with `&& !_openConvMayHoldOrphanGhost(...)` so an idle ghost-holding conv falls through to Phase-2 → OVERWRITE adopts `serverMsgs` verbatim; (b) added a MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK ENTRY gate `activeTaskId && hasLocalData && !activeStreams.has && serverMsgs.length<conv.messages.length && _openConvMayHoldOrphanGhost` → adopts the shorter list. CRITICAL placement: the adopt must run BEFORE the existing "upgrade lastLocal from lastServer" block, which otherwise copies the server's PREVIOUS settled reply INTO the empty ghost → a DUPLICATE instead of a removal (this was the first-cut B-fail).
- **Invariants preserved (peer asks + logged guardrails).** Never truncate when `activeStreams.has(convId)` (would orphan the connectToTask assistantMsg ref) or in KEEP_LOCAL (`localHasUnsynced`); every adoption branch settles `_needsLoad=false` + `_serverMsgCount=Math.max(server,local)` (state-snapshot-keep-longer-guard). Shrinking is ONLY for the authoritative reconciled GET list — NOT the reconnect `state`/`done` snapshot, which stays keep-longer (opposite correct behavior, different path).
- **TDD (tests/test_frontend_warm_open_adopts_reconciled_list.py, NEW).** Drives REAL shipped core/conversations.js under node. A warm-idle + B stale-activeTaskId → ghost dropped (RED before, GREEN after); C live-stream + D KEEP_LOCAL-fresh → NOT truncated (controls, green both ways). Neuter-bitten: `_openConvMayHoldOrphanGhost → return false` flips A/B red, leaves C/D green, restore → green. 8 neighbouring reconcile/load-state/dedupe tests still pass (open_conv_body_reconcile, keep_local_settles_load_state, state_snapshot_keep_longer, connecttotask_taskid_dedupe, cross_device_reconcile).
- **Coordination.** Both source seams were owned + LIVE: conversations.js sync seams by mrc606du (confirmed non-overlap — their edits at :539/:1002-1028/:1064-1065 SET `_needsLoad`, mine ACTS on it — they compose), reconcile.py/GET-path lease by mrc05uc4 (confirmed #2 settle-time/task-end reconcile is MINE; GATE 1 stays skip-while-live; they only added the `is_superseded_error_husk` verdict my task-end trigger gets for free). Held a path lease on the two edit regions while editing; released after.
- **REMAINING (this epic pt_b02486c823944ed3, still claimed).** #2 settle-time reconcile keyed by taskId (call the same `reconcile_conversation_messages` at task-end so a live-task placeholder that DROPS is swept at the source — closes the routes/conversations.py:490 GATE 1 hole) — gated on mrc05uc4 releasing the reconcile.py/GET-path lease. Then the belt: a render-time guard keyed on "no live stream bound AND no finishReason AND no thinking" (NOT merely empty content, or a legit "Preparing…" pre-first-token bubble blanks), with its own show/hide test.
- **Lesson.** "Stop rendering empty bubbles" is a coat of paint — the ghost stays persisted, re-syncs, resurfaces via other render paths. Fix the mechanism: make the server's reconciled list authoritative on EVERY open (not just cold loads), and sweep the placeholder at task-end. When adopting a shorter list inside MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK, adopt at branch ENTRY before the checkpoint-upgrade block mutates the ghost tail, or you convert a removal into a duplicate.

### 2026-07-09 — Pillar #6 peer messaging: THREE crash-poisoned NC-neuters found live in the shipped `project_peer.py` (storm cap, hard-abort audit gate, `_peerHuman` stamp) — all restored to canonical; then shipped increment (3): a bounded RECEIVE-side reply affordance. TDD, neuter-bitten, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Context (owner design question).** "Peer messages arrive as a User message and the recipient can't reply — how should a reply mechanism be designed, without endless A↔B chatter, kept transparent and tool-shaped?" My analysis: send is already a well-behaved observable tool; the gap is entirely on the RECEIVE side (represented as a passive user turn, framing tells the model *not* to engage, no reply affordance). Recommended: explicit tool reply (never auto-relay — honors charter invariant #2), keep in-turn round-boundary injection for live targets / fresh-turn for idle (a hard constraint, not a bug), add a bounded reply protocol + surface the sender's full reply id. Owner approved increment (3), deferred (4) render-as-tool-artifact to a separate frontend increment.
- **PRECONDITION the owner caught — the safety foundation was NOT live.** `lib/conversations/project_peer.py` in the working tree was NC-neutered (crash-poisoned-source class this project has hit before): `_prune_and_check` → `return True, kept+[now], 0.0  # NC-STORM` (rate cap a no-op — storms NOT bounded), `_authorize_hard_abort` → `return True, 'approved'  # NC-GATE` (hard abort bypassed the human-approval audit gate). My original "storms are mathematically impossible" claim rested on a disabled cap. **A THIRD neuter surfaced only when I ran the full suite:** `_peerHuman` payload stamp disabled (`# NC-HUMAN-PAYLOAD`). All three restored byte-identically to the canonical form the NC-test `_patch_restore` anchors encode (the anchor's `old` string IS the canonical code). While neutered, those NC tests were themselves red at `assert old in original` — restoring both re-arms the guard AND unbreaks the NC suite.
- **Lesson reinforced.** When you find ONE NC-neuter in a file, grep the WHOLE file for `NC-`/`disabled)` before declaring the foundation restored — they cluster (a crashed `_patch_restore` `finally` can leave several). Post-restore scan of project_peer.py: zero remaining neuter markers.
- **Increment (3) — receive-side reply affordance (two parts, respecting the no-auto-relay invariant).** (a) `render_peer_protocol_block` gained a RECEIVE clause: "when you RECEIVE a peer message … you MAY reply EXACTLY ONCE via `project_message(to_conv_id=<reply id>)` — only to CONFIRM a boundary / HAND OFF / DECLINE; your rate-limit budget is the ceiling; coordination, not a chat channel." The reply MECHANICS (tool name + arg) live ONLY in the ambient block. (b) The received agent-peer BODY now surfaces the FULL sender id (`reply id {from_conv_id}`, not just the 8-char display prefix) so a reply targets it verbatim and can't fail on a mistyped/ambiguous prefix — but the body stays PLAIN content: it keeps the `advisory` framing and NEVER names a send tool. This preserves `test_no_auto_relay_body_is_plain_content` (body must contain "advisory", must NOT contain "project_message") — receiving a message can never auto-trigger a send.
- **Why replies don't need forbidding to stay storm-safe.** The per-ordered-(sender,target) sliding window (`_PEER_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW=3`/`120s`) caps A→B and B→A independently, so total peer traffic per window ≤ N·(N−1)·cap — a storm is impossible by construction even WITH replies enabled. The budget is the throttle; the "reply once" wording is guidance, the rate cap is the hard bound.
- **Tests (`tests/test_peer_coordination_register.py`, +5 in new `PeerReplyAffordanceTest`).** Part A: block teaches a bounded reply (names `project_message(to_conv_id=`, "once", rate-limit-ceiling, "not a chat channel"). Part B: body surfaces `reply id convSENDERfull` AND preserves no-auto-relay (contains "advisory", not "project_message"). TWO byte-reverting NEUTERS, both PROVEN to bite: revert the receive clause out of the block → `project_message(to_conv_id=` absent → Part-A test fails; revert body to 8-char-only framing → `reply id …` absent → Part-B test fails. unittest-class tests drive DB-free via `_pytest.monkeypatch.MonkeyPatch` (can't take the fixture) + identity `_resolve_target_conv_id`.
- **Verify.** ruff clean on project_peer.py + the test. Full peer set green: `test_project_peer.py` (26) + `test_peer_coordination_register.py` (14) + `test_peer_message_round_boundary.py` (16) + `test_project_peer_human_nudge.py` (7) = **63 passed**. The two isolated neuters re-run standalone → both PASS (anchor found → revert → affordance absent → restored byte-identical). Uncommitted for owner attribution.
- **Deferred (owner-agreed).** (4) render BOTH directions (send delivery-card + receive inbox-card + any reply) as tool-round artifacts for full symmetry/observability — separate frontend increment, touches the timeline (`tool_rounds.js` / `PEER_INBOX_INJECT`).
- **RECURRENCE ROOT CAUSE closed (why this file shipped neutered TWICE).** The autouse nc-guard belt (`tests/conftest.py::_restore_nc_patched_sources`, `_NC_GUARDED_SOURCES`) that self-heals a crashed `_patch_restore` did NOT list `lib/conversations/project_peer.py` — so its NC-target source healed from nothing and a crashed run left the guards disabled indefinitely. Added it. Also found + added `lib/message_queue.py`, a confirmed live `_patch_restore` target in `test_project_peer_human_nudge.py` (NC-DISPATCH-HUMAN neuters `dispatch_next_queued`) that was equally unguarded. Both now in `_NC_GUARDED_SOURCES`; verified content-clean (no NC markers, guards live) after a full 63-test peer run. ### 2026-07-08 — Closed epic pt_2fd936cd15c34a7f (finding #4: IDB re-PUT resurrects a remotely-deleted conv). The local-only RESCUE loop now distinguishes deletion from offline-creation via the `_serverRev` signal. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Context.** Peer conv mrc8uwtf's review closed with finding #4: my rev-authority work fixed the list-MERGE branch but NOT the local-only RESCUE loop (conversations.js ~:1053). That loop re-PUT (`syncConversationToServer`) ANY conv absent from the server list with `messages.length>0` — so a conversation DELETED on another device gets RESURRECTED on the next list refresh. Real bug in my file; the disambiguator is the same `_serverRev` signal I just made authoritative.
- **Fix (uncommitted, `static/js/core/conversations.js`).** In the rescue loop, split on `const wasServerKnown = (typeof lc._serverRev === 'number')`: a conv that EVER carried a `_serverRev` was once server-known → its absence from the server list = DELETED elsewhere → drop it locally + `ConvCache.remove(id)` (prune the IDB paint-cache; mirrors the conv_deleted notify tombstone path `_applyRemoteConvDeleted`), do NOT re-PUT. A conv that NEVER had a `_serverRev` is a genuine "sent while server unreachable" local creation → rescue (re-PUT) as before. The ACTIVE conv is left in place if server-known-but-absent (don't yank it mid-view) but still NOT re-PUT, so it can't resurrect.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_list_merge_rev_authority.py` extended, real shipped conversations.js under node, +2 scenarios +1 neuter).** deleted-elsewhere (server-known, absent) → NOT resurrected, dropped locally, IDB pruned; genuine offline (never server-known) → survives (not pruned, not dropped). NEUTER pins `wasServerKnown=false` (the OLD blanket behaviour) → the deleted conv is no longer pruned (takes the rescue path) → proves the `_serverRev` disambiguator is load-bearing. All 3 tests (13 merge invariants + 2 neuters) green.
- **Harness trap (worth remembering).** conversations.js DECLARES `async function syncConversationToServer(...)` — a hoisted decl that SHADOWS a pre-eval `global.syncConversationToServer` stub, so you cannot observe the rescue re-PUT by stubbing that name. First attempt asserted `offline_rescued` via the stub → always FAIL. Correct move: assert the OBSERVABLE SURVIVAL outcome (offline conv is neither pruned nor dropped) rather than re-simulating `syncConversationToServer`'s full body (it runs extractLightMessages→Api.put; over-specifying it fights the shadowing for a path this epic doesn't even change). The deletion branch — the actual fix — uses ConvCache.remove + array filter, fully observable.
- **Verify.** node --check OK; list-merge suite 3/3; adjacent conv_notify_push / conv_changed_notify (7) / cross_device_reconcile green. Bundle → `bundle-ada8b68f.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh. This closes the peer's entire render-authority review: #1 (their lane), #2 (parity, mine), #3 (rev-authority merge, mine), #4 (this).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Absent from the server list" is AMBIGUOUS: it means DELETED-elsewhere for a conv that was ever server-known, but OFFLINE-CREATED for one that never synced. The monotonic `_serverRev` is the exact discriminator (server-issued → its presence proves prior server knowledge). A blanket "rescue everything absent" re-PUT silently defeats cross-device deletion. Honor the same signal everywhere: merge staleness, notify rev-gate, AND deletion-vs-rescue.


### 2026-07-09 — Tablet model-picker regression: two root causes, both from the WebView viewport class + the tablet-drawer "full toolbar" assumption. Fixed + TDD-guarded (uncommitted; CSS still tangled with sibling rewrite).
- **Symptom (tablet WebView, coarse pointer, ~837–1280px):** the model-picker Preset Toggle "can't be seen" AND tapping it "shows nothing." Two distinct defects, both in the tablet-drawer `@media(min-width:769px) and (max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` block (styles.css:16878–16975).
- **Defect A — clipping (self-inflicted):** the blank-screen fix added `[data-theme="tofu"] .chat-wrapper{overflow:hidden!important}` to this block. `.preset-dropdown` is a DOM descendant of `.chat-wrapper` and (desktop form) opens UPWARD `position:absolute;bottom:calc(100%+6px)`, so it was clipped away → "nothing happens." Desktop keeps `.chat-wrapper{overflow:visible}` as the dropdown-escape hatch (styles.css:13315); my `overflow:hidden` broke it here. FIX: give the coarse block a `position:fixed` bottom-sheet `.preset-dropdown` (escapes ANY ancestor overflow), `max-height:min(60vh,calc(var(--vh100,100vh)*0.6))` (not bare dvh → WebView-collapse safe).
- **Defect B — sliver collapse (missed on first pass):** the drawer block keeps the FULL desktop toolbar (it does NOT inherit the ≤768 `···`-sheet compaction). At ~837px the submenus (增强/工具/模式) + action btns + search + send fill the nowrap row, and the model picker — fully shrinkable down the chain (`.input-actions-scroll{flex:0 1 auto}` → `#modelGroup{flex-shrink:1}` → `.preset-toggle-wrapper{flex:0 1 auto}`, all `min-width:0`, `.preset-toggle{overflow:hidden}`) — collapses to an invisible SLIVER. NOT `display:none`, which is why a grep-for-hidden missed it (owner caught the too-fast dismissal). This is the documented "width-only compaction can't tell tablet from narrow desktop" class. FIX (root-cause, per the mobile-breakpoint memory — apply the phone's compaction, don't fight flex): in the coarse block hide `#submenuAI/Tools/Mode` + `#imageGenBtn/#projectBtn`, show `.mobile-more-btn` (··· → toggleMobileSheet, which already mirrors those toggles), and pin `#modelGroup{flex-shrink:0}` + `.preset-toggle{flex-shrink:0;min-width:96px;max-width:200px}`.
- **TDD:** `tests/test_preset_dropdown_coarse_escape.py` (5 tests, red→green, 2 neuters proven biting): dropdown escapes via position:fixed; bottom-sheet max-height not bare dvh; toggle can't collapse (compaction + shrink floor). Env-independent CSS parse; `_media_block` disambiguates the 3 blocks sharing the coarse opener via `body_contains='.chat-wrapper{overflow:hidden'`.
- **Verify:** CSS parses clean (braces 6982/6982), served `styles-26bde07c.css` carries both fixes; `mobileMoreBtn`/`submenuAI/Tools/Mode` present in HTML, `toggleMobileSheet`/`updateMobileSheet` in bundle → compaction is functional (features still reachable via ···). NOT verified on-device (no tablet here); owner runs that gate.
- **Commit status:** uncommitted. This `styles.css` change + the new test join the deferred changeset that must be separated from a sibling session's ~1786-line uncommitted styles.css rewrite before commit (viewport-guard commit d4f888b already landed the 12 `--vh100` overlay lines cleanly via a surgical hunk-patch).



### 2026-07-09 — Full-scale test-suite hardening for CI green: ROOT-FIXED xdist DB isolation, repaired crash-poisoned NC source files + added a durable nc-guard belt, drove tsc 94→0, and fixed ~20 test-drift/frontend failures. N workers hammering one SQLite file → lock storm. FIX: key the shim path on `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` (worker-unique file) AND have `_configure_test_env` REUSE the frozen `_core.DB_PATH` + run `init_db()` up front so a worker that runs only direct-DB tests still has a schema. This is a real CI bug (workers inherit the controller env in CI too).

Under xdist a per-test split / timeout / crash leaves the `finally` un-run → the source stays NEUTERED, cascading into every later importer. Found `lib/conversations/project_charter.py` (`if False and pid…` NC-3, `pop(0)` NC), `project_board.py` (`_effective_status` NC-B, `post_task` NC-5), `project_dispatch.py` (NC-1 filters, NC-2 claim) ALL stuck in their neutered forms before I touched anything. Restored each to canonical; ADDED a durable belt: `tests/conftest.py::_restore_nc_patched_sources` (autouse) snapshots the NC-target sources once and after EVERY test restores any left byte-different — so a crashed patch can poison at most the ONE crashing test, never the session/tree. PROVEN: after a full xdist run the sources scan CLEAN.
- **#3 tsc --checkJs ratchet 130→0 (BASELINE=0 was breached).** A generated `feature-<8hex>.js` deferred bundle (347 KB, untracked) was being type-checked (31 spurious dup-decl errors) + 94 genuine undeclared-`window.*`/DOM-expando errors from newer modules (tofu-pet, tofu-scene, project-brain*, cross_tab_sync, voice, …). FIX: exclude `feature-????????.js` + `**/*.nc_copy.js` in tsconfig + broaden the harness `_BUNDLE_RE`; declared the cross-file globals in `static/js/globals.d.ts` and fixed a handful of genuine source nits (Symbol→null sentinel in tool_rounds.js:2787; ScrollBehavior/Node casts; JSDoc @param) — no `any`/`@ts-ignore` blankets. Now 0, both ratchet tests green.
- **#4 ~20 test-drift + frontend-isolation fixes (all TEST-only, source was right).** jsdom harnesses missing `escapeHtml`/`convIsBusy` stubs after legit source refactors (test_frontend_project_brain ×3, autopilot_queue_badge, sidebar_settled_facts); NC neuter anchors drifted after source refactors (open_conv_body_reconcile `_contentStale`, board_lease `_row_to_task`); the review-venue-race harness assumed auto-generation the source deliberately removed (re-anchored the NC to the on-entry lookup langKey); obsolete `test_frontend_presence.py` (the "who's working" strip was replaced by the Collaboration Bar — coverage now in test_frontend_collab_bar.py) DELETED; fixed-name `.nc_copy.js` files made unique per test-module so sibling NC tests can't clobber each other; `test_user_profile` `tmp_data_dir` now monkeypatches `_server_data_dir` (the `TOFU_DATA_DIR` env override was a dead no-op vs the frozen `_BASE`, so it read the dev box's real profile); backend drift: legacy_api allow-list (`/api/push/debug/presence`), conv_config (`langCorrectionEnabled`), stuck-reason rename (`stuck_no_output`→`stuck_no_progress`), brain_summary (`statusLine`), project_feed (`_store_run_summary`→`_store_run_record`), presence_subagent (`write_file` must be a KNOWN tool now that the hallucinated-tool guard rejects unknowns).
- **Local-env quirk:** a `napari` pytest plugin in this conda env crashes collection (`GL ES 2.0 library not found`) — NOT a CI dep; run with `-p no:napari -p no:napari-plugin-engine -p no:npe2`. CI (`pip install -e .[test]`) never sees it.
- **STILL RED (reported, NOT fixed — deliberately out of scope):**
  1. **Owner's in-flight WIP cluster** — `test_warm_resume_reasserts_toolrounds` (untracked), `test_startup_reconcile`, `test_terminal_cas_retry`, `test_partial_checkpoint_no_search_text`, `test_chat_send_supersedes_autopilot` (untracked), `test_persist_vertical_block_relocate` (untracked), `test_project_feed_read_tool`: these assert behavior the WORKING-TREE-uncommitted `manager.py`/`chat.py`/`reconcile.py`/autopilot code has only PARTIALLY implemented (e.g. `reconcile_conversation_messages` exists but is unwired; warm-resume never re-emits a `state` snapshot; terminal-sync lacks the CAS retry the checkpoint path has). NOT test-infra rot — the owner is mid-feature. Left for the owner (modifying half-finished concurrency code would collide with their work).
  2. **Pre-existing NC-xdist reload-pollution** — the `_patch_restore` + `importlib.reload` NC tests still fail transiently under `-n auto` (worst under `worksteal`'s per-test split; better but non-zero under `loadgroup` per-file affinity) because reloading one brain module leaves stale cross-module references in others sharing a worker process. Sources no longer stay corrupted (the belt), but the in-run reds remain. Fully fixing needs removing `importlib.reload` from ~15 NC files (a large, separate refactor). CI dist mode kept at the original `worksteal`; added an INERT-under-worksteal per-file `xdist_group` conftest stamp so a future `--dist loadgroup` switch keeps a file's tests serial. - **Lesson.** On-disk source-mutating + module-reloading NC tests are fundamentally xdist-hostile: a crashed patch poisons the shared tree, and per-test worker-splitting races concurrent patches of the same file. The durable mitigation is a session belt that re-snapshots+restores the target sources after every test (heals corruption regardless of dist mode); the real cure is to stop reloading modules / patching shipped files in place (patch a temp copy the harness evals). Also: a test's env-override fixture is a silent no-op when the value it targets was frozen at import (`_BASE`, `_core.DB_PATH`) — patch the resolver seam, not the env var.


### 2026-07-09 — "Failed to load: bundle-95e8203d.js" banner in Chrome but not the WebView app: ROOT-CAUSED (stale index.html → deleted hash) + DURABLE self-heal (stale bundle/feature-hash 404 → 302 to current). server.py + js_bundler.py + new test (7, neuter-bitten), uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Symptom (owner).** Chrome intermittently shows the LoadGuard banner `⚠️ Failed to load: bundle-95e8203d.js. Reload.`; the self-developed WebView app never does. Not a code bug.
- **Root cause (code-verified, not guessed).** `index.html` is served `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` with the bundle `<script>` tag INJECTED at request time (`routes/common.py:495` + `_get_bundle_tag`); the built `bundle-<hash>.js` is served `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (`server.py`); on every rebuild `_clean_old_bundles` DELETES all prior hashes (`lib/js_bundler.py`, anchored `_BUILT_BUNDLE_RE = ^(?:bundle|feature)-[0-9a-f]{8}\.js$`). So a client holding a STALE `index.html` (bfcache / long-lived tab / a caching proxy defeating `no-cache`) requests a hash the server already deleted → 404 → `_onScriptError` → banner (`index.html:79`,`:2765`). WebView escapes it by loading the URL FRESH each open (no persistent tab / bfcache / shared proxy) → always the current hash.
- **Fix (durable self-heal, minimal blast radius).** New pure `resolve_stale_bundle(filename)` in `lib/js_bundler.py`: returns the CURRENT filename only when the request is a genuinely-built `bundle-/feature-<8hex>.js` of a DIFFERENT hash (reuses `_BUILT_BUNDLE_RE`, so `feature-loader.js` can't be mismatched); returns None for the current file (serve normally) and for any non-built name (a REAL 404 — never masked). Hooked into the EXISTING `@app.errorhandler(404)` in `server.py` — real files (incl. current bundle) never reach it, so only a genuine miss is inspected → `302` to `/static/js/<current>` + `logger.warning('[StaleBundle] Self-healing stale request: %s -> %s …')`. A `<script>` follows a 3xx transparently (`onerror` does NOT fire on a redirect), so the banner is genuinely SUPPRESSED, not merely delayed — verified.
- **Cache guard (the trap).** The redirect's request path `/static/js/bundle-<hash>.js` matches the `/bundle-` immutable branch, which would FREEZE the 302 for a year and permanently pin one stale→current mapping. Fixed both belt (set `Cache-Control: no-store` on the redirect in the handler) and suspenders (`add_cache_headers` now short-circuits `300 ≤ status < 400` under `/static/` → `no-store` + early return, before the immutable branch).
- **Four acceptance criteria — all independently verified (not asserted):** (1) stale CORE hash → 302 to current; (2) stale FEATURE hash → 302 to current (ran, NOT skipped — deferred bundle present); (3) unknown path AND non-hashed `bundle-loader.js` still 404 (miss handler not turned into a catch-all); (4) current hash keeps `immutable, max-age=31536000` while the stale redirect is `no-store` with NO `immutable`.
- **Test (`tests/test_stale_bundle_self_heal.py`, NEW — 7, `pytest.mark.unit`).** Drives the real app via `flask_client`. NEUTER-BITTEN: `resolve_stale_bundle` → `return None` flips the 4 positive tests to FAIL while the 3 negative controls (unknown-404, non-hashed-404, current-immutable) stay green — proving the redirect tests depend on the fix AND the 404-masking guard is real. Restored byte-identical → 7 pass. Log line confirmed on the owner's EXACT hash: `[StaleBundle] Self-healing stale request: bundle-95e8203d.js -> bundle-e781ebc0.js`.
- **Verify.** `pytest -p no:napari`: self-heal (7) + `test_bundle_manifest_parity` (13) + `test_bundle_corruption_guard` (12) = 32 passed. `ruff` clean on `server.py`, `lib/js_bundler.py`, the test. Uncommitted for owner attribution. Restart needed (import-time handler).
- **Remaining root-cause gap (documented, NOT done this turn — deeper leak).** The redirect self-heals `<script>` GETs but does not stop a misbehaving caching PROXY from serving the stale `index.html` in the first place. Optional later hardening: add `no-store` (stronger than the current `no-cache`) to the `index.html` response so an intermediary can't cache the document that points at deleted hashes. That closes the root cause; the redirect closes the symptom for every client regardless.
- **Lesson.** A `no-cache` HTML that injects an `immutable`-cached, delete-on-rebuild hashed asset is inherently fragile to any stale-HTML source (bfcache / proxy). Serve stale-hash requests gracefully (302 to current, `no-store`) rather than 404 — a `<script>` follows the redirect with no `onerror`, so the fix is invisible to the user. Guard the redirect against inheriting the asset's `immutable` cache, and pin "miss handler is not a catch-all" with negative-control tests.

### 2026-07-09 — Frontend "feels heavy" → measured, then DEFERRED the Project Brain cluster out of the eager bundle (−16.2 KB gzip / −3.9% first-paint). Two dead-end shortcuts ruled out first (esbuild already running; i18n-split is a documented-rejected regression). js_bundler + feature-loader + parity-test pins; neuter-bitten; uncommitted for owner sign-off.

Deferred bundle (70 KB gz) + CSS (128 KB gz) secondary. 71.7k LOC / 103 bundled files, ZERO dead/unbundled files (manifest clean — not a "delete cruft" job). i18n.js alone = 187 KB minified (10.3%), tool_rounds 121 KB, chat_render 51 KB.
- **Two shortcuts KILLED before touching code (both would have wasted the turn):**
  1. **i18n locale-split — DOCUMENTED-REJECTED** (`.tofu/skills/i18n-locale-split-rejected-caching-regression.md`, 2026-07-05). i18n rides the `immutable,max-age=1yr` bundle = FIRST-VISIT-ONLY cost; any active-locale inline into the `no-cache` HTML trades that for a per-reload download, and `tofu_ui_lang` is localStorage-only so the server can't pick a locale. Owner caught that I hadn't searched skills before proposing it "biggest win" — lesson logged.
  2. **esbuild "not running" — FALSE.** The served bundle's 1276 lines READ as "minify-only", but esbuild wraps at ~5000 chars (not one line): the served bytes are BYTE-IDENTICAL to esbuild's output. Proven: `_minify_js`-only core = 466 KB gz; esbuild (served) = 411 KB gz → esbuild is ALREADY saving 54 KB gz / 360 KB raw. No free win left. `_resolve_esbuild()` → real binary (node v24).
- **Per-cluster deferral audit (verified against SOURCE, not rotted manifest comments).** SAFE = Project Brain cluster (project-brain{,-peers,-status,-i18n}.js): top level is only decls + `window.*` exposes; `pushSubscribe` lives INSIDE `openFeed()`. BLOCKED (kept eager, proven boot-path couplings): **branch.js** (`isBranchTaskId` @ main_init_tasks.js:82/152 is a real orphan-recovery dependency — a deferred stub returning undefined flips the `typeof` guard → live branch task misrecovered as orphan → duplicate); **artifacts.js** (always-on conv-render path: `hydrateConversation` conversations.js:1193 + `renderChips` chat_render.js:1300); **memory.js** (submenu/conv-switch); **skills/preferences** (Settings tabs via always-eager `openSettings`, no clean onclick trigger).
- **THE deferral trap (owner-flagged, load-bearing).** `_installFeatureStub` makes every listed entry point a BUNDLE-LOADING stub. `projectBrainRefresh` is called on EVERY conv-switch (main.js:637) and `closeProjectBrain` on the overlay onclick — stubbing EITHER would fetch the feature bundle seconds into boot, negating the entire deferral. Fix = deliberate split: LOADING stubs only for the 3 true user-triggered openers (`openProjectBrain` [collab-bar click presence.js:247], `toggleProjectBrain`, `openProjectBrainInfluence` [conv-scoped deep-link]); `projectBrainRefresh`/`closeProjectBrain` left ABSENT at boot so their existing `typeof …==='function'` guards skip them (refresh has nothing to refresh, close nothing to close, until the panel is first opened). Openers are wired via JS addEventListener, NOT index.html onclick → no LoadGuard inline-stub entry needed; overlay's inline `onclick="closeProjectBrain()"` is a plain no-op call, safe absent.
- **Edits.** `lib/js_bundler.py`: 4 files core→`_DEFERRED_FILES` (ordered project-brain.js FIRST — siblings read `window.ProjectBrain._state` at runtime), 3 openers→`_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS`, replaced the core-block comment with a "why deferred + why refresh/close are NOT entry points" note. `static/js/feature-loader.js`: same 3 openers into its own hardcoded list (guarded by `test_feature_loader_entry_points_match_jsbundler`). Dev-fallback `<script>` tags in index.html STAY (loader's `!__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__` guard keeps real fns in dev).
- **Measured win (deterministic before/after: assemble core WITH vs WITHOUT the cluster, esbuild-min + gzip).** core BEFORE 411.2 KB gz → AFTER 395.0 KB gz = **−16.2 KB (−3.9%) off EVERY first paint**. Deferred bundle 87.6 KB gz absorbs it (also `immutable`-cached → zero per-reload cost; idle-prefetch keeps first open non-laggy). Marginal < standalone-18.6 KB (gzips better in the big shared dictionary — the recipe's known effect).
- **Tests.** Extended `test_bundle_manifest_parity.py` (+2): `test_project_brain_is_deferred_not_core` (residency pin + within-deferred ordering + openers declared) and `test_project_brain_conv_switch_fns_are_not_loading_stubs` (THE no-load design proof — refresh/close must NOT be entry points in EITHER list). NEUTER-BITTEN: wrongly adding `projectBrainRefresh` as a loading stub in both lists → the no-load test FAILS; restored byte-identical (`cmp -s` yes) → passes. Full sweep: parity (13) + corruption-guard (12) + artifacts-registration (11) = **36 passed**. `node --check` clean on BOTH rebuilt bundles.
- **Verdict / deploy.** Objective met the robust way — reduced what blocks first paint, no per-reload penalty, all 5 acceptance criteria verified not asserted. Uncommitted for owner attribution. Restart (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle names bundle-3af2a182 / feature-7654c1f3). Remaining heavy targets for a later increment: CSS (128 KB gz, measure per-selector first), and the two eager giants i18n.js (locked-optimal) + tool_rounds.js (121 KB — chat-critical, not deferrable).
- **Lesson.** For a generic-import feature deferral, the entry-point set is NOT "stub everything for defense-in-depth" — any fn on a boot/conv-switch path that becomes a loading stub silently negates the win by fetching the bundle early. Split entry points into user-triggered openers (stub) vs boot-path fns (leave absent, rely on the existing typeof guards), and PIN the split with a test that bites when a boot-path fn is wrongly stubbed.


### 2026-07-09 — Reading Mode "loads the PDF too slowly" ROOT-FIXED: `_renderAllPages` was eager (rasterized EVERY page up front); replaced with a virtualized render (shells up front → page 1 now → lazy raster on scroll + release off-screen). Frontend + CSS + jsdom test, measured, uncommitted for sign-off.
- **Symptom / objective (owner).** Reading mode takes too long to show the PDF. Owner ruled A-vs-B for me: the network/Range path is already handled (prior `conditional=True` + `{data}` fallback), the structural culprit is the RENDER — `_renderAllPages` (static/js/paper-reader.js) rasterized all N pages at `_paperScale × devicePixelRatio` in a sequential `await` loop, plus N text layers, before load was "done." Time-to-first-page grew with page count.
- **Fix (render layer, verify-then-write).** Rewrote `_renderAllPages` into three phases: (1) build every page WRAPPER up front (cheap `getViewport` math, no raster) so the scroll height/scrollbar is correct immediately; a shimmer `.paper-page-placeholder` fills each shell; (2) create an `IntersectionObserver` (root = `#paperPdfViewer`, the `.paper-pdf-container overflow:auto` scroller; `rootMargin:150%` pre-render band) that lazy-rasterizes a page when it nears the viewport and RELEASES its canvas+text-layer when it scrolls far off (wrapper keeps width/aspect-ratio → layout stable); (3) force page 1 raster NOW so TTFP is ~constant. New helpers `_rasterizePage` (idempotent via `dataset.rendered/rendering`; preserves ALL correctness invariants — CSS-viewport layout, hi-res `×dpr` buffer CSS-sized down, `--scale-factor`, transparent absolute text layer), `_releasePage`, `_maybeReopenViaData` (single-flight `{data}` range-bypass re-open). Per-run `_paperRenderToken` makes a stale loop (zoom mid-render) self-cancel. jsdom / no-IO engines fall back to eager render (old correctness, no virtualization).
- **Raster-failure fallback GENERALIZED.** Old code re-opened via `{data}` only on the initial whole-doc render-fail. Now `_rasterizePage` RETURNS a reopen-needed signal on any page's raster failure (the mangled/truncated-Range case that passes the page-1 probe); the lazy path fire-and-forgets `_maybeReopenViaData`, the eager/page-1 paths await it. So a later-page truncation at ANY scroll position recovers, not just on load.
- **Zoom.** `paperZoomIn/Out`, `paperSetScaleFromSlider/Input`, `paperFitWidth`, ctrl+scroll all call `_renderAllPages()` unchanged — it now bumps the token, rebuilds shells at the new scale, re-observes, and the observer re-fires on already-visible pages → visible pages re-rasterize at the new scale. `_rasterizePage` re-measures the viewport so a zoom between shell-layout and raster stays correct.
- **Instrumentation (measurement-first, owner pref).** `_loadPaperPdf` now `debugLog`s `doc opened in Nms (viaData, pages)`, `page shells laid out in Nms`, and `first page painted in Nms` (new `_paperNow()` perf clock) — on-device evidence splitting transport vs render, same style as the Range-fix acceptance logs.
- **Measured before/after (deterministic, jsdom harness counting `page.render` calls on a 40-page doc).** BEFORE (eager) = **40 raster ops on load, 40 canvases**; AFTER (virtualized) = **1 raster op on load, 1 canvas, 40 wrappers** → **40× fewer rasterizations before first paint**. TTFP goes from O(N pages) to O(1). Wall-clock TTFP is emitted per-load by the debugLog lines for real on-device confirmation.
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_paper_pdf_virtualized.py`, NEW — 2 tests).** jsdom harness with a controllable `IntersectionObserver` stub drives the REAL `_loadPaperPdf`/`_renderAllPages`: asserts N wrappers built up front, ONLY page 1 rasterized on load (1 canvas), all wrappers observed, feeding an intersecting entry for page 5 lazy-rasterizes it, feeding a non-intersecting entry releases its canvas (placeholder restored, `rendered='0'`, shell kept). NEUTER = force `IntersectionObserver` undefined → source falls to eager render → all 8 pages rasterize on load, which fails `only_page1_on_load` → proves the assertion bites.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK. `tests/test_frontend_paper_pdf_virtualized.py` (2) + `test_frontend_paper_pdf_data_gate.py` (1, all 4 `{data}` fallback scenarios still green — fallbacks preserved) + `test_paper_pdf_range.py` (5) = **8 passed**. CSS braces balanced (6974/6974). Feature bundle rebuilt (`feature-dd216614.js` — paper-reader.js is a DEFERRED/lazy feature bundle, not the main `bundle-*.js`; all new symbols present). Frontend + CSS + test, uncommitted for owner attribution. Restart (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle).
- **Lesson.** "Loads too slowly" for a multi-page viewer with no virtualization = eager all-pages raster before first paint; the fix is the standard pdf.js-viewer pattern (shells up front → render visible → IntersectionObserver lazy-raster → release off-screen), NOT touching the already-fixed transport. Keep the per-page correctness invariants byte-identical when moving raster into a lazy helper, and route the existing `{data}` recovery through a RETURNED signal so it works at any scroll position, not just on load. `#paperPdfViewer` IS the scroll container → it's the IntersectionObserver root.

Drives a live sequence: `tool_start(web_search)` → timeline mounts WHILE searching showing the real query + `isStreaming=true`; `tool_done` → round flips to done with `_elapsed='3.4s'` + results attached + re-renders; second `fetch_url` round + `interpret_done` → both rounds persist, renderer receives ALL accumulated rounds. NEUTER (`if(false) s.toolRounds.push` in a COPY) → no round accumulates → timeline never mounts → assertion fails; shipped file byte-identical after. Both green.

The three paper tabs emit an identical `tool_start`/`tool_done` schema; the fix for a lagging tab is to accumulate into `toolRounds` and hand them to `renderToolRoundsHTML` exactly like the reference tab — not to invent a second display.
