- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A "dedup" that adds a NEW cross-file symbol which a hot-path fn then calls WILL break standalone jsdom harnesses that eval only the file-under-test — add the stub to `_stdStubs` AND each whole-file standalone harness BEFORE running, and run the FULL `test_frontend_*` glob (the break surfaces in OTHER files' harnesses). (2) When the working tree is SHARED with a live sibling, `git diff --stat` on a "your" file can show hundreds of lines that are the PEER's — save your version to /tmp, `git checkout` to HEAD, re-run to prove a failure set is pre-existing, then restore from /tmp. (3) Not every `typeof X==='function'` fallback is dead: a file that runs on a SEPARATE page (relay-admin on `/admin`) legitimately can't assume core.js loaded — leave those.


### 2026-07-09 — Project Brain "Status & Watch" tab: fixed the "stuck on Synthesizing project status" hang (root cause = synchronous LLM on the tab-open route) + a UI/UX pass (section header, manual refresh, Updating pill, shimmer skeleton). Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** The Status & Watch tab "sticks on 'Synthesizing project status' for a long time" on open, and the styling isn't great — improve both interaction and UI/UX.
- **Root cause (verified).** `GET /api/v1/project/brain/status` called `build_status_snapshot(trigger='on_open')` with the DEFAULT `blocking=True`, so the HTTP response was held open for a full cheap-model LLM synthesis (`max_tokens=800`, several seconds) whenever the pillar-state fingerprint had moved — which is almost always on an active project. Meanwhile the frontend `refreshStatus` blanked the whole tab to a single full-screen `pb-status-loading` "Synthesizing project status…" box for that entire wait. The backend ALREADY had a `blocking=False` path (returns cached instantly + warms a fresh snapshot in a daemon thread) — the route simply wasn't using it.
- **Fix — backend (`lib/conversations/project_status.py`, `routes/api_v1/project.py`).** New `get_status_view(path, *, limit, force)`: returns the CACHED latest snapshot + history IMMEDIATELY (never blocks on the LLM), cheaply computes the staleness gate (a `_fingerprint` compare, NO LLM), and when stale (or `force`) fires the EXISTING `build_status_snapshot(..., blocking=False)` background warm and flags `refreshing=True`. The route now calls `get_status_view` and honors `?refresh=1` (the manual refresh button → `force`). Exported in `__all__`; `@api_meta` description rewritten to the non-blocking contract.
- **Fix — frontend (`static/js/project-brain-status.js`, `api.js`).** `refreshStatus(path, {force})` is now non-blocking: it renders the cached snapshot instantly, shows a shimmer SKELETON only on a genuinely empty tab (never blanks existing content), and when the server reports `refreshing` it starts a BOUNDED poll of the read-only history endpoint (`_POLL_MS=2500`, `_POLL_MAX=8` → ~20s ceiling, no LLM held open) to swap in the fresh narrative the moment the background warm lands, then drops the pill. New `_buildStatusHeader(refreshing)` (title + live "Updating…" pill + manual Refresh button, disabled while warming) and `_buildSkeleton()`. `api.js brainStatus(path, {force})` now sends `refresh=1` instead of the unused `limit`.
- **UI/UX (`static/styles.css`, `i18n.js`).** Added `.pb-status-header` / `.pb-status-title` / `.pb-status-updating` (pulsing dot pill) / `.pb-status-refresh` (icon button, SVG `refresh` glyph via `Icon()`, §3.4) / `.pb-status-skeleton` (shimmer, `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the animations). Three i18n keys: `statusTitle` / `statusUpdating` / `statusRefresh` (zh+en). No new top-level JS file → no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-11d9756f.js`).
- **Verify (all green).** `tests/test_project_status_lane.py` now 18 (14 + 4 new for `get_status_view`: returns-cached-and-delegates-nonblocking-warm / not-refreshing-when-quiescent / first-open-flags-refreshing / force-warms-even-when-quiescent, all spying `build_status_snapshot` to assert `blocking=False` and NO synchronous LLM). New `tests/test_frontend_status_header.py` (5, runs the REAL `renderStatus`/`_buildStatusHeader`/`_buildSkeleton` under node + neuter). Existing `test_frontend_status_tab_refresh.py` (6) + `test_frontend_watch_empty_state.py` (4) still pass → 33 total green. **NEUTER BITE:** flipping the warm to `blocking=True` fails the 3 non-blocking backend tests (the real synchronous synthesis then runs against the sandbox DB and errors — exactly the hang path); restored byte-identical. CSS braces balanced (6964/6964); JS + PY syntax clean.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). Restart the server (import-time JS bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle; CSS auto-busts via css_bundler).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "fresh-on-open" data path must NEVER hold the HTTP response open on an LLM synthesis — return the cached value instantly, warm in the background, and let the client poll a read-only endpoint to pick up the new row. When a `blocking=False` seam already exists, the bug is usually just a caller that didn't opt into it. Signal the background work with an inline pill (never blank prior content), and only show a skeleton when there is genuinely nothing to show.


### 2026-07-09 — Voice input: a dedicated "语音识别 / Speech" settings tab that writes into the existing provider slots (single source of truth, no second config store). Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Add a discoverable speech-recognition section in Settings; recommend common STT APIs; do NOT create a second config store (backend-as-single-source-of-truth); design around the DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS caps-override trap; provider list = OpenAI / Groq / omni `audio_chat` / Custom Whisper; mirror the "机器翻译服务" tab; secrets in server_config.json must stay gitignored + export-excluded; biting-neuter integration test through the REAL slot build.
- **Finding (verify-first).** The whole STT stack already exists end-to-end (`lib/transcription.py`, `routes/api_v1/audio.py`, `static/js/voice.js` mic button, the `transcription`/`audio_chat` caps, OpenAI/Groq DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS + templates). The ONLY gap: configuration was buried in the generic model editor (add a model, hand-toggle its cap chip) — undiscoverable. So this is a pure discoverability/UX surface over existing backend, no backend change.
- **THE TRAP (empirically reproduced, then designed around).** `dispatcher._build_slots_from_providers` computes final slot caps as `set(cell_caps) if cell_caps is not None else set(alias_cfg.get('caps', model_caps))` where `alias_cfg = DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS.get(model_id)`. So the reference-table caps OVERRIDE the model-level `capabilities` list — only an explicit per-`(key,model)` `key_access[idx].capabilities` override wins outright. Direct proof: a provider with `gpt-4o` + model-level `capabilities:['transcription']` builds a slot with `[cheap,text,vision]` (table won → NO transcription → `transcription_available()` stays False); the SAME provider with `key_access:{'0':{capabilities:['transcription']}}` builds `[cheap,transcription]` (available). A Custom model absent from the table would also lose the cap without the override. **The tab therefore ALWAYS stamps `key_access` on every key index** — this is the whole reason it works.
- **Design (single source of truth).** New `static/js/settings/speech.js` is a thin editor over ONE dedicated provider entry `id:'stt'` inside the SAME `_stgProviders` list the general Providers tab edits and `_saveServerConfig` ships verbatim (`existing['providers']=data['providers']` in routes/config.py, `dispatch_reset_needed=True` → hot slot rebuild; `key_access` survives the round-trip untouched). `_applySttToProviders()` runs in `_saveServerConfig` BEFORE the payload ships: drops any prior `stt` provider, then appends the freshly collected one (enabled+complete) or nothing (disabled/incomplete). Per-card mechanism: OpenAI/Groq/Custom → `transcription` (multipart endpoint); Omni → `audio_chat` (inline `/chat/completions`) — so a user can't tag an omni chat model `transcription` and 404. Live status line from `Api.audio.capabilities()`.
- **Peer coordination.** Sibling conv (voice latency/streaming task) advised: the default Meituan/AIGC gateway (`aigc.sankuai.com/v1/openai/native`) exposes NO native Whisper `/audio/transcriptions` — audio→text there is ONLY via `/chat/completions` = our `audio_chat` cap. Framed the cards accordingly: OpenAI/Groq/Custom Whisper need a direct provider key (public internet); the Omni card (gemini-3-flash-preview / LongCat-Flash-Omni-2603) is the working target on the default gateway. Their scope (kill dominant latency + stream transcript into `#userInput`) doesn't overlap this settings surface.
- **Files.** `index.html` (nav tab `data-tab="speech"` + `settingsTab_speech` panel: enable toggle, provider selector, 4 brand-logo cards w/ "get key" links, SVG-only icons, live-status banner) · `static/js/settings/speech.js` (NEW; populate/switch/collect/apply) · `static/js/i18n.js` (25 `settings.stt*` zh/en keys) · `static/js/settings/core_panel.js` (populate on open + on tab-switch) · `static/js/settings/save_export.js` (`_applySttToProviders()` then `payload.providers=_stgProviders`) · `lib/js_bundler.py` (`settings/speech.js` added to `_BUNDLE_FILES` after `other_tabs.js`) + dev-mode `<script>` tag.
- **Tests (biting neuters, both green).** `tests/test_stt_settings_write_path.py` (7 tests) — builds a REAL dispatcher from the tab's exact write shape; each card flips `transcription_available()` True with the right mode (endpoint/chat); NEUTER: same provider WITHOUT `key_access` on trap model `gpt-4o` stays False, WITH it flips True (proves the override is load-bearing, not a stubbed `_transcription_slots`). `tests/test_frontend_stt_settings.py` (jsdom, 15+ asserts) — drives the shipped speech.js: enabled+card → one `stt` provider with `key_access[0].capabilities=[cap]`, Omni→`audio_chat`, endpoint→`transcription`, key-index count matches keys, idempotent re-apply, incomplete (no base URL)→removed, disable→removed. Ran together with existing `test_transcription_config_integration` + `test_audio_transcribe` + `test_frontend_voice_input`: **38 passed**.
- **Secrets (#2 confirmed).** `data/config/server_config.json` is gitignored (`git check-ignore` YES) AND untracked (`git ls-files` empty); `data/` ∈ `export.py ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (excluded internal+opensource). STT keys land there exactly like every other provider key — no new secret surface.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK (speech.js, i18n.js, core_panel.js, save_export.js); bundle rebuilt → `bundle-ae6b347d.js` with all 5 STT symbols surviving concat; index.html panel/tab/script + `_BUNDLE_FILES` membership all confirmed present. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time JS bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For any capability whose availability is computed at slot-build from `DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS`, a settings write that only sets the model-level `capabilities` list is SILENTLY INEFFECTIVE for any model in the reference table (or absent from it) — you MUST write an explicit per-cell `key_access[idx].capabilities` override, and the ONLY test that catches this is one that builds a REAL dispatcher (a stubbed `_transcription_slots` hides the trap). A feature-specific settings tab can stay single-source-of-truth by editing ONE dedicated provider inside the shared `_stgProviders` list rather than a parallel config store.

### 2026-07-09 — Open-a-conversation scroll stability, increment 2: the MULTI-PHASE force-scroll (Phase-1 cache paint + Phase-2 server paint + .then() fallback each snapped to bottom) was the real "jumps several times". Now positions the view EXACTLY ONCE per open. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Increment 1 (migrating the 4 async marker/artifact callbacks off the force-scroll `renderChat`) removed the LATE re-snaps but the owner correctly pushed on the remaining first-paint question: trace (1) what opening a long FINISHED conversation actually does (top vs yank-to-bottom), and (2) whether Phase-1 cache paint and Phase-2 server paint can BOTH force-scroll in one open with no anchor preserved between them — then decide the contract and prove it fires exactly once.
- **Trace (verified, no bypass).** `loadConversation` (main_conv_lifecycle.js:76) sets `c._initialSwitchLoad=true` then calls `loadConversationMessages`. Inside, BOTH paint sites go through `renderChat(conv,false)`: Phase-1 cache paint (conversations.js:1223) and Phase-2 server reconcile paint (:1690, OVERWRITE branch when `cacheIsStale` — true whenever server len ≠ local len OR serverUpdatedAt > cachedUpdatedAt). `renderChat` SKIPS its surgical fast-path while `_initialSwitchLoad` is set (chat_render.js:568) → full-render path runs. There the pre-swap anchor was captured ONLY when `_sameConvDom && !_readerNearBottom && !activeStreams` (chat_render.js:662). On a SWITCH first-paint `_lazyConvId` still points at the PREVIOUS conv → `_sameConvDom=false` → anchor null → tail runs `_forceScrollToBottom` (chat_render.js:727). So: (1) opening a long finished conv ALWAYS yanks to the bottom; (2) a cached-but-stale conv force-scrolls TWICE in one open (cache paint, then server paint — the second's `_readerNearBottom` is now true because the first left the reader at the bottom, so even the old anchor guard wouldn't have diverted it), PLUS `loadConversation`'s `.then()` had a THIRD direct `_forceScrollToBottom(null,true)` (main_conv_lifecycle.js:186). That 2–3× snap sequence IS "jumps several times in a row"; increment 1's async callbacks were only the tail of it.
- **Decision.** Landing at the bottom ONCE on open is the right default (chat convention; matches the existing switch/first-load contract). The bug is the REPEATED snap. Fix = position the view EXACTLY ONCE per open; every later same-open render preserves the viewport. (Restoring last-read scroll position across sessions is a separate, larger feature — needs a persisted per-conv scroll anchor — FLAGGED, not bundled.)
- **Fix (uncommitted, 3 files).** (a) `static/js/ui/streaming_render.js`: new module-level `let _openScrollConvId=null` (declared beside `_lazyConvId`, same bundle scope). (b) `static/js/ui/chat_render.js`: the full-render tail's force-scroll branch now latches `if (conv._initialSwitchLoad) _openScrollConvId=conv.id`; the pre-swap-anchor guard is WIDENED with `_openAlreadyPositioned = !!conv._initialSwitchLoad && _openScrollConvId===conv.id`, so a LATER same-open render (`_sameConvDom` true, reader at bottom) captures+restores the anchor instead of re-snapping — `(!_readerNearBottom || _openAlreadyPositioned)`. (c) `static/js/main/main_conv_lifecycle.js`: `loadConversation` resets `_openScrollConvId=null` at open start (each open positions once), and the `.then()` fallback `_forceScrollToBottom(null,true)` is guarded by `_openScrollConvId !== id` so it never adds a redundant snap after Phase-1/Phase-2 already positioned.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK on all three; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-bf435f1e.js`, grep-confirmed the minified latch-set (`_initialSwitchLoad&&(_openScrollConvId=e.id)`) and the two `_openScrollConvId=null` resets survive. NEW jsdom test `tests/test_frontend_open_conv_scroll_once.py` (2 tests, deterministic 200px-block layout model): render #1 of an open force-scrolls once + latches + lands at bottom; render #2 AND #3 of the SAME open (distinct content so the fingerprint guard doesn't swallow them — models Phase-1-stale vs Phase-2-server) do NOT force-scroll again; a genuine switch-away-and-back force-scrolls once more (latch is per-open, not permanent). NEUTER (remove the `_openAlreadyPositioned` widening) → render #2/#3 re-snap (force-scroll fires again) = the exact reported bug, proving the widening is load-bearing. Also updated the drifted needle in `tests/test_frontend_full_render_scroll_anchor.py` (its `capture` neuter targets the `_preSwapAnchor` expression I edited); all 4 scroll suites green together (10 tests: open_scroll_once 2, full_render_anchor 3, bg_refresh 3, open_no_scroll_jump 2).
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle) to see on-device. End-to-end contract now: open a historical conversation → lands at the bottom ONCE, no re-snap from the Phase-2 reconcile, the `.then()` fallback, or the async marker/artifact hydrations (increment 1).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Force-scroll to bottom on open" is correct as a ONE-SHOT but becomes a visible multi-jump when several independently-timed full renders each own a paint in a single open (cache→server→fallback→async-hydrate). The fix is an open-scoped latch, not removing the scroll: position on the FIRST render, preserve the viewport on the rest, reset the latch per open. When you edit a line that a jsdom neuter targets by exact string (here the `_preSwapAnchor` guard), UPDATE the sibling test's needle in the same change or its neuter silently no-ops. And make the harness's stub `_convRenderFingerprint` CONTENT-sensitive, else the fingerprint short-circuit swallows the second render and the neuter can't bite.

### 2026-07-09 — Opening a historical conversation "jumps around the page, several times in a row": root cause = 4 fire-and-forget load callbacks force-scrolled on open. Migrated them to the scroll-preserving repaint. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "No matter which historical conversation I click on, I want it to stay stable — not jump around the page, or even jump several times in a row."
- **Root cause (verified in source).** `loadConversationMessages` (static/js/core/conversations.js) fires FOUR fire-and-forget re-hydration callbacks on EVERY conversation open — compaction-markers + artifacts, in BOTH the Phase-1 (IndexedDB cache, :1174/:1186) and Phase-2 (server, :1627/:1641) branches. Each `.then()` unconditionally called the FULL-render path `renderChat(conv, false)`. Two compounding problems: (1) while the initial switch is in flight `conv._initialSwitchLoad` is set, so `renderChat`'s surgical guard is bypassed (chat_render.js:568) and the full-render path runs `_forceScrollToBottom` (chat_render.js:727); (2) the four callbacks each resolve after their OWN network round-trip (`/api/v1/compactions/list`, `/api/v1/artifacts?conv=`) at DIFFERENT times → the reader is yanked to the bottom once per late-landing callback = "jumps several times." The SIBLING cost/file-change prefetches were already migrated to the scroll-preserving in-place repaint `_bgRefreshChat` (chat_render.js:483/:518) back when this same bug class was fixed for THEM; these two hydration callbacks were simply missed.
- **Fix (uncommitted, `static/js/core/conversations.js`, 4 sites).** Each callback's `.then()` now calls `_bgRefreshChat(conv)` instead of `renderChat(conv, false)`. `_bgRefreshChat` is the correct target: it (a) NEVER force-scrolls; (b) returns EARLY when no assistant bubble's rendered HTML actually changed (compare-before-swap via `__bgHtml`), so a conversation with zero artifacts/compactions is a pure no-op — the common case; (c) uses anchor-relative scroll restore (`_captureScrollAnchor`/`_restoreScrollAnchor`) when a chip IS added, so even a genuine repaint keeps the reader's viewport pinned. The compaction/artifact chips ARE part of `renderMessage` output (chat_render.js:1131 `_compactions`, :1270 `_artifacts`), so `_bgRefreshChat`'s per-bubble diff correctly detects and paints them in place.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-2920bb86.js`; grep-confirmed all four migrated callbacks now read `…then(()=>{e===activeConvId&&typeof _bgRefreshChat=="function"&&_bgRefreshChat(n)})` (esbuild kept the top-level `_bgRefreshChat` name). NEW structural test `tests/test_frontend_open_conv_no_scroll_jump.py` (2 tests, green): extracts each of the four callback `.then()` blocks (keyed by its unique `.catch('[compaction|artifacts] attach|hydrate (cache|server) failed')` tail) and asserts each calls `_bgRefreshChat(conv)` and NOT `renderChat(conv, false)`; the biting NEUTER reverts the Phase-1 compaction callback to `renderChat(conv, false)` and confirms the guard trips. Adjacent suites still green (`test_frontend_bg_refresh_scroll` 5, `test_frontend_full_render_scroll_anchor`, `test_frontend_cache_hydrate_boot` 7). One unrelated FAILURE in `test_frontend_open_conv_body_reconcile.py::test_NC_content_only_trigger_is_load_bearing` — PROVEN pre-existing (git-stash all my changes → it fails IDENTICALLY): its hard-coded neuter fragment `} else if (sc.id === activeConvId && sT > mT) {` has drifted out of `_verifyActiveConvFromServer` independently of this work; that function is untouched by my edits.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). No API/shape change; pure frontend render-callback routing. Restart server (import-time JS bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any fire-and-forget callback that lands AFTER a conversation open and wants to repaint MUST use the scroll-preserving in-place repaint (`_bgRefreshChat`), never the full-render `renderChat(conv,false)` — the latter force-scrolls while `_initialSwitchLoad` is set, and N independently-timed callbacks each cause a separate jump. When one bug-class fix (cost/file-change → `_bgRefreshChat`) lands, grep for OTHER callers of the old pattern in the same function (`renderChat(conv, false)` inside a `.then()`); two were missed here precisely because they weren't part of the original prefetch cluster.

### 2026-07-09 — Paper Mode "fail to render" / "PDF cannot be loaded" (ORCA, 41 MB): root cause = serve_paper_pdf ignored HTTP Range → whole-file 200 truncated by the proxy. Fixed with conditional=True (206). Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** ORCA paper in reading mode keeps showing "fail to render" AND the original PDF won't load.
- **Ruled out the prior "Missing PDF" base-path bug.** The earlier (mrcr83cb2rf1bx) `_resolvePaperPdfUrl` proxy-rebase fix is PRESENT in both source (`static/js/paper-reader.js:975`) and the shipped `feature-547f0c32.js`. Backend healthy: `uploads/papers/arxiv_2606.30534v2.pdf` is a valid 41 MB PDF (`%PDF-1.7` header, `%%EOF` trailer, full-download integrity confirmed), and the live server on :15000 returns `200 application/pdf` size=41577569 in <1s. So this was NOT a base-path or parse failure.
- **Root cause (verified).** `serve_paper_pdf` (routes/paper.py:1728) called `send_file(filepath, mimetype='application/pdf')` with Quart's default `conditional=False`. Proof: `curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-1023'` against the live endpoint returned **`200` + the WHOLE `content-length: 41577569`** — Range totally ignored. pdf.js loads large PDFs via ranged requests; a buffering cloud-IDE proxy truncates/times-out that single 41 MB response, which pdf.js surfaces as BOTH "Missing PDF" (whole-doc parse) and per-page "Page N failed to render" (`paper-reader.js:1110`). This is exactly the Range gap the prior conversation FLAGGED and deferred as out-of-scope — it turned out to be the real bug for a big PDF.
- **Fix — TWO parts, because conditional=True alone is INERT for the viewer (`routes/paper.py`).** (a) `serve_paper_pdf` + `serve_paper_image` pass `conditional=True` → Quart 0.19.5 `send_file` calls `make_conditional(accept_ranges=True, complete_length=…)` → `206 Partial Content` on a Range request. BUT: pdf.js 3.11.174's `validateRangeRequestCapabilities` gate does one INITIAL full GET and only flips `allowRangeRequests=true` if THAT response carries `Accept-Ranges: bytes` + `Content-Encoding: identity` + length > 2×rangeChunkSize (128 KB). Quart stamps `Accept-Ranges` ONLY on the 206 path, so the initial 200 lacked it (verified: `Accept-Ranges: None`) → pdf.js would NEVER issue a Range request and the 206 support was dead code for the viewer. (b) So `serve_paper_pdf` now also `resp.headers.setdefault('Accept-Ranges', 'bytes')` on the initial response.
- **Verify (real output, via app test client since the live server still runs old code).** Initial plain GET → `200`, **`Accept-Ranges: bytes`**, `Content-Encoding: identity`, CL 41577569 → all four pdf.js gate conditions pass → `allowRangeRequests` would be **True** (traced against the actual minified gate in `static/vendor/pdf.min.js`). `Range: bytes=1000-2023` → `206`, `Content-Range: bytes 1000-2022/41577569`, CL 1024. New guard `tests/test_paper_pdf_range.py` (3 tests) PASSES incl. the initial-200-advertises-Accept-Ranges assertion + a BITING neuter (strip `conditional` → Range degrades to `200`+full). Run with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`.
- **HONEST caveats (root cause is INFERRED, objective NOT yet met).** (1) The "proxy truncates the whole-file 200" is a REASONED hypothesis — NOT observed: the curl repro hit `127.0.0.1:15000` DIRECTLY (full 41 MB in 0.8s, 200), not the `…vscode-zw05.mlp.sankuai.com` proxy path where the user sees the break. (2) UNKNOWN RISK: some proxies also buffer/strip `Range`/`206` — if this one does, ranged loading won't help either and we'd need chunked/streamed transfer instead. (3) The live server still runs OLD code → nothing is fixed on-device yet. Acceptance = user re-opens the ORCA entry THROUGH THE PROXY after restart+refresh and it renders, AND the Report "fail to render" clears.
- **Transport diagnostic (owner's acceptance gate).** `serve_paper_pdf` now logs `[Paper] serve pdf=%s range=%s -> %s`. After restart+refresh + opening ORCA through the proxy, `logs/app.log` is definitive: MANY `range=True -> 206` = pdf.js is range-loading AND the proxy forwards it (fixed); a SINGLE `range=False -> 200` = the proxy did one buffered full GET → ranging is moot → flip to the streamed fallback. Verified the line emits `range=False -> 200` (initial GET) and `range=True -> 206` (ranged) via the test client.
- **Point 3 — the two symptoms are the SAME pdf.js path (verified, NOT a separate empty-text bug).** "PDF cannot load" = pdf.js `getDocument` fail → `paper-reader.js:1024` "Failed to load PDF"; "fail to render" = same doc, per-page canvas fail → `paper-reader.js:1110` "Page N failed to render". Neither is the Report tab's "No paper text available" (2360/4064). Confirmed ORCA text extracts cleanly server-side: `POST /api/v1/paper/reparse` → `ok=True, 40 pages, 129751 chars`. So even if the viewer stays broken, `_ensurePaperText()` recovers text and Report/Q&A still work — one fix (bytes → pdf.js) covers both reported symptoms; no second empty-parsedText failure to chase.
- **Fallback READY (not just "a different tack") — env-gated, dormant.** New `_stream_file_response()` (routes/paper.py) serves the PDF as a fixed-chunk (256 KB) generator through a `Response` — the proven sync-generator pattern the SSE endpoints use — parsing `Range` MANUALLY (byte-accurate 206, incl. suffix `bytes=-N`) and setting the anti-proxy-buffering headers from the SSE-buffering lesson (`no-transform` + `Content-Encoding: identity` + `X-Accel-Buffering: no`). Wired into `serve_paper_pdf` behind `TOFU_PAPER_PDF_STREAM=1` (default OFF → byte-identical to the send_file path today). If the log shows the proxy defeats ranging, set the env var and restart — no code churn. Verified: full GET → 200 byte-identical 41 MB; `bytes=1000-2023` → 206 exact slice; `bytes=-500` → 206 correct last-500. 2 new guard tests (byte-accuracy + default-off) added; suite now 5/5.
- **Fallback tiering CORRECTED (owner's reasoning, conceded).** The chunked-stream fallback (`TOFU_PAPER_PDF_STREAM=1`) is only a WEAK hedge: `send_file(conditional=True)` and `_stream_file_response` emit the IDENTICAL 206 on a Range request — they diverge only on a whole-file 200, so the stream path helps only if the proxy did a full GET AND handles a chunked-generator body differently from a send_file body. Its one real lever is the `X-Accel-Buffering: no` + `no-transform` headers (can disable nginx-style buffering send_file never signals) — modest, not robust. Kept staged (harmless, dormant) but downgraded to a secondary hedge.
- **ROBUST last resort = CLIENT-SIDE range-bypass (staged dormant, `static/js/paper-reader.js`).** If the proxy strips/ignores Range, the transport-independent fix is to have the CLIENT download the whole PDF once (its own proxy-correct `_resolvePaperPdfUrl` URL + a client-owned AbortController timeout, default 120s) as an ArrayBuffer and hand pdf.js `getDocument({data: bytes})` instead of `getDocument({url})` — pdf.js never touches ranged transport. New helpers `_shouldFetchPdfAsData()` (gate) + `_fetchPdfArrayBuffer()` (download); `_loadPaperPdf` routes through them ONLY when `localStorage['tofu_paper_pdf_data']==='1'` (a no-build browser-console flip — no rebuild). Default OFF → `{url}` path unchanged. Coexists with the confirmed reparse text recovery. paper-reader.js is a LAZY feature module (NOT in `_BUNDLE_FILES`), so no allowlist change; feature bundle rebuilt on restart (new `feature-576ca9fb.js` carries both symbols).
- **Verify.** Backend range suite 5/5. New jsdom guard `tests/test_frontend_paper_pdf_data_gate.py` drives the REAL `_loadPaperPdf`: flag OFF → `getDocument(<url string>)`; flag ON → `getDocument({data:<Uint8Array>})` byte-matching the client fetch. PASSES; NEUTER bites (force the gate off → the flag-on `{data}` assertion fails with the exact message, then restored + `node --check` clean). Self-contained harness (jsdom's `window.localStorage` is getter-only → the shared harness's `win[k]=` can't set it; stub `global.localStorage` which is what the source's bare `localStorage` resolves to — same pattern as `test_frontend_paper_describe_persist.py`).
- **API-isolation seam fix (§3.2.0 — owner caught this before it reddened CI).** `_fetchPdfArrayBuffer` originally did a RAW `fetch(url)` to `/api/paper/pdf/...` inside paper-reader.js. The isolation ratchet (`test_frontend_api_isolation.py`) LITERAL-regex only matches `fetch('/api/…')`, so a variable-URL `fetch(url)` slipped past it silently (the same escape hatch the trading migration hit) — green by accident, not on merit, and a §3.2.0 violation. FIX (backend-as-single-source-of-truth): new `Api.paper.pdfArrayBuffer(path, opts)` in `static/js/api.js` delegates to the shared `request()` (so base-path resolution stays single-sourced), `parse:'response'` → `arrayBuffer()` → `Uint8Array`, throws on non-2xx/empty. `_fetchPdfArrayBuffer` now strips to the canonical `/api/...` path (Api re-applies live BASE_PATH — no double-prefix) and calls it with `{signal, timeout:0}`, keeping its OWN AbortController deadline. NO bare `fetch(` remains in paper-reader.js (grep-clean). Test updated to stub `Api.paper.pdfArrayBuffer` + assert the canonical `/api/paper/pdf/` path was passed (no raw fetch). Isolation 4/4 + data-gate PASS; neuter still bites. Bundles rebuilt: `pdfArrayBuffer` in main `bundle-bf435f1e.js` (api.js is bundled), gate/delegation in feature `feature-94c49367.js`.
- **On-device recovery path + decision tree.** RESTART the server + HARD-REFRESH (paper-reader is a hashed feature bundle → hard-refresh re-fetches). Re-open ORCA through the proxy, then READ `logs/app.log` `[Paper] serve` lines (the acceptance gate): (1) MANY `range=True -> 206` = fixed by the primary range change, done. (2) SINGLE `range=False -> 200` = proxy defeats ranging → set `localStorage.setItem('tofu_paper_pdf_data','1')` in the browser console + reload (robust client-side bypass); `TOFU_PAPER_PDF_STREAM=1` is the weaker server-side hedge to try only if the client download itself is what's capped. NOT committed (owner attribution) — awaiting the owner's on-device proxy check.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** 206 server support is INERT unless the client is actually configured to range-load AND the INITIAL response advertises `Accept-Ranges: bytes` (pdf.js reads it off the first GET; Flask/Quart `make_conditional` sets it only on the 206). Trace the client gate (`disableRange`/`rangeChunkSize`/the `Accept-Ranges` check in the vendored pdf.js), don't just prove the server CAN serve 206. And reproduce on the ACTUAL failing transport (the proxy host) — a direct `127.0.0.1` curl that returns `200` fast proves the origin is fine, not that the user's path works.


### 2026-07-09 — Project-bar unification COMPLETING fix (increment 2b): full-height per-scene bar-body wash so frosted pills float on continuous atmosphere top-to-bottom, not flat cream. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner, root-cause gap not nitpick).** Increment-2 frosting fixed HORIZONTAL edge-gap occlusion but left a VERTICAL gap: the detailed scene is a 17px strip pinned to the bottom, while the pills are vertically centered in a ~40px bar whose BODY is flat cream (`linear-gradient(#FAF8F2,#F2EFE6)`). So a frosted pill in the vertical middle reveals CREAM, not diorama — the scene only shows through the thin sliver where a pill's bottom edge overlaps the strip. The "two visual languages / not one surface" complaint was relocated horizontal→vertical, not resolved. Fix: give the bar BODY a subtle full-height scene-tinted wash keyed off `[data-decor]`, layered UNDER the detailed SVG strip, so frosted glass floats on continuous scene atmosphere and the detailed ground/crest is the grounded bottom of that same wash.
- **Fix (uncommitted, CSS-only, `static/styles.css`).** Added `background:linear-gradient(180deg,…)` to the existing per-decor rules (which already carry the `[data-theme="tofu"] .project-bar[data-decor="X"]` (0,3,0) attr specificity → beats base `.project-bar` (0,2,0), overriding ONLY `background`; border/shadow/etc. inherit): meadow `#F5F7EF→#E7EEDD` (faint sage), pool `#F1F6F5→#DFEDEA` (faint teal), sky `#F2F5F9→#E4EBF4` (faint blue). `off` keeps the plain cream (no tint). The detailed SVG ground strip (`::after`, z0) + crest (`::before`) + pet/FX (z1) sit unchanged ON TOP of the wash; frosted pills (z2) now reveal continuous tint everywhere, detailed ground at the bottom.
- **Contrast verified (owner's explicit check).** WCAG relative-luminance contrast of the `#5E4E36` pill-label over the DARKEST wash stop (worst case): meadow 6.75, pool 6.66, sky 6.68 — all ≥ AA-normal 4.5 (and a realistic frosted pill fill = wash+~50% cream is lighter still, e.g. meadow `#F0F3E8` → 7.14). Text stays legible on every tint.
- **Verify (all green).** braces balanced (6944/6944). No `@media` block repaints the bar body — programmatic scan found only a false-positive on a COMMENT (line 16738 "…@media rules that redefine height/padding…"), zero real overrides; the 3 `data-decor…background` matches are exactly the 3 new tint rules, all OUTSIDE any `@media`. Base non-tofu `.project-bar` cream untouched (70 `245,158,11` refs intact) → dark/light themes byte-identical. **FX harness re-run against the REAL shipped tofu-pet.js: 16 ok / 0 FAIL** (meadow→grass 11 capped / pool→ripple / sky→wisp / off→0 / reduced-motion→0 / self-clean / parallax) — restyle didn't regress the effect layer.
- **Resolved surface (objective now MET, not approximated).** The bar is one coherent surface top-to-bottom: full-height scene-tinted atmosphere wash → detailed SVG ground strip + calm crest grounded at the bottom → pet + footstep FX roaming → frosted-glass tofu-palette controls floating over ALL of it (scene atmosphere visible through the vertical center, detailed ground through the bottom). Scene switch retints the whole body; `off` returns to plain cream; reduced-motion still fully disables motion.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). CSS-only → NO bundle rebuild (no JS changed); CSS auto-busts via css_bundler. Hard-refresh to see it. `backdrop-filter` degrades gracefully (translucent fill, no blur) where unsupported — still non-occluding over the tinted body, so the full-surface goal holds either way.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Translucent controls only unify a surface if what's BEHIND them across their WHOLE extent is the surface — a decorative strip pinned to one edge means a centered frosted control still reveals the flat body color, just relocating the "floating chrome" complaint to the other axis. The completing move is a full-extent low-saturation wash under the detailed art, keyed off the same state var, so glass floats on continuous atmosphere. Layer the wash on the EXISTING higher-specificity attr rule (`[data-decor]` (0,3,0)) overriding only `background`, so it beats the base without touching borders/shadow and can't leak to other themes; always numerically verify label contrast over the darkest wash stop, not by eye.


### 2026-07-09 — Project-bar "game-like" pass (increment 2 — Direction A): unified the bar into ONE surface — frosted-glass controls so the scene reads full-width, tofu-token palette coherence, calm meadow crest. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.

- **Fix (uncommitted, CSS + 1 SVG only — NO JS this increment, bundle unaffected).**
  1. **Occlusion → frosted glass (`static/styles.css`).** The three tofu control-pill families — `[data-theme="tofu"] .project-bar-btn` / `.project-autoapply-toggle` (incl. `.auto-mode`) / `.folder-badge` — swapped their OPAQUE `linear-gradient(#FAF8F2→#F0EDE4)` fills for TRANSLUCENT tofu-cream `rgba(250,248,242,0.5)→rgba(240,237,228,0.4)` (hover 0.62/0.55) + `backdrop-filter:blur(6px) saturate(1.05)` (with `-webkit-` prefix). Net: the diorama scene (z0) + pet/FX (z1) read THROUGH the pills (z2) across the full bar width — controls float as frosted glass on a continuous backdrop.
  2. **Palette coherence.** Under `[data-theme="tofu"]` the pills were ALREADY sage/cream + sans-font (the clashing `#f59e0b` amber + JetBrains mono is only in the base non-tofu `.project-bar-*` rules, which are untouched → 70 `245,158,11` refs intact for dark/light themes). So coherence was mostly achieved by the translucency itself; text color nudged `#6B5A40`→`#5E4E36` for contrast over the busier see-through backdrop. Verified: `sed -n 12190,12290p` (the tofu pill block) contains NO `f59e0b`/`JetBrains`.
  3. **Garland (`static/icons/pet/edge-meadow.svg`).** Replaced the six tall spiky grass blades (poked up 8–9px at fixed 120px-tile positions = the "randomly placed above the controls" read) with a CALM continuous seamless crest matching the already-calm pool/sky edges: one low bump band (each quadratic returns to baseline → seamless at x=120) + a soft lighter crest line. Pool/sky edges were already calm continuous crests, left as-is.
- **Watched the specificity war (owner's flag).** All edits keep the `[data-theme="tofu"] .class` (0,2,0) specificity — no bare `.class`, so nothing leaks to dark/light themes and non-tofu bars stay byte-identical. Scanned EVERY `@media` block programmatically: ZERO of them restyle `project-bar-btn`/`project-autoapply-toggle`/`folder-badge` with a background → the frosted treatment is NOT clobbered on the 360px/480px/768px mobile layouts (no regression, no counter-!important needed).
- **Verify (all green).** All 6 scene/edge SVGs XML-valid; `styles.css` braces balanced (6944/6944); 9 `backdrop-filter:blur(6px)` decls present; translucent rgba fills confirmed (not solid hex); base non-tofu amber rules intact (70 refs). **FX harness re-run against the REAL shipped tofu-pet.js: all 16 assertions still PASS** (meadow→grass 11 capped ≤12 / pool→ripple 10 / sky→wisp 8 / off→0 / reduced-motion→0 effect nodes / self-clean 0 leaked / parallax `--bar-scene-x` tracks) — the restyle did not regress the effect layer. z-order intact: `.project-bar > *:not(.tofu-pet){z-index:2}` still lifts controls above scene(z0)+pet/FX(z1).
- **Resolved surface behavior.** The bar is now ONE surface: full-width diorama backdrop, pet + footstep FX roaming on it, frosted-glass tofu-palette controls floating over it (scene visible through the center, not just edge gaps), and a calm continuous grass crest at the rim instead of random spikes. Scene switch / pack switch / FX / reduced-motion all preserved.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). CSS-only + one SVG → NO bundle rebuild needed (no JS changed); CSS auto-busts via css_bundler, the SVG is `url()`-referenced. Hard-refresh to see it. NOTE: `backdrop-filter` needs a modern engine (fine on the Android WebView / Chromium target); where unsupported it degrades to the translucent rgba fill with no blur — still non-occluding, so the full-width-scene goal holds either way.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a decorative backdrop "only shows on the edges," the cause is usually OPAQUE foreground controls occluding it, NOT a tiling bug — fix by making the controls translucent + `backdrop-filter`, not by enlarging the art. Before frosting pills, GREP every `@media` block for background overrides on those exact classes: translucent + blur silently regresses if a mobile query repaints them opaque. Keep the theme-scoped `[data-theme="tofu"]` (0,2,0) specificity so the change can't leak onto other themes or trip the mobile specificity war. A "misaligned floating garland" is often just art poking up at fixed tile offsets — a calm continuous crest reads as one surface with the ground and stops competing with the controls.

### 2026-07-09 — CI overhaul: fixed the long-standing red (phantom `[test]` extra → no pytest installed) + parallelised every test tier with pytest-xdist. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "CI hasn't passed for a long time; optimise it thoroughly. The full suite is very slow — can we raise parallelism?"
- **Root cause of the red (verified, the primary bug).** All three CI test jobs run `pip install -e ".[test]"`, but **there was no `test` extra** — `pyproject.toml` defined only `dev / scale / trading` (`python -c "…optional-dependencies…"` → `['dev','scale','trading']`). Modern pip treats an unknown extra as a mere warning and installs base-only; **pytest is NOT in `requirements.txt`** (grep-confirmed "NOT in requirements.txt"), it lived solely in `dev`. So every CI test job ran `pytest -ra` with **no pytest installed** → fail at the run step. That is the long-standing red.
- **Root cause of the slowness (verified).** The `test` job ran **bare `pytest -ra`** = the WHOLE 5473-test collection with NO `-m` marker filter (so it also pulls the 22 `slow` endpoint-loop tests at ~90s each + the 26 `visual`), **serially**, across a **3-version matrix** (3.10/3.11/3.12), with **zero parallelism** (pytest-xdist absent) and **no per-test timeout**. Tier sizes measured (`--collect-only -m <marker>`): unit 5287 · api 142 · slow 22 · visual 26 · live_llm 2.
- **Fix (uncommitted, 3 files).**
  1. **`pyproject.toml`** — added a real **`[test]` extra** = `pytest + pytest-cov + pytest-xdist>=3.0 + pytest-timeout>=2.1 + fakeredis`. Redefined `dev = ["tofu[test]", "ruff"]` (superset = test + linter), so pytest has exactly one home and CI's `.[test]` resolves.
  2. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — split the monolithic `test` job into marker-scoped tiers: **`test-unit`** (`-m unit -n auto --dist worksteal --timeout=300`, matrix trimmed to the range endpoints **3.10 + 3.12** — dropping 3.11 halves matrix cost), **`test-api`** (`-m api`, single 3.12, parallel), **`test-slow`** (`-m slow -n 4 --timeout=600`, `continue-on-error: true` so multi-minute orchestration loops are visible but non-blocking). Frontend job also parallelised (`-n auto`, 93 jsdom files each shelling to `node` → fans out cleanly; per-test-named/random harness temp files, so no worker collision).
  3. **`Makefile`** — `test-unit`/`test-api`/`test-frontend` now parallel via a tunable **`JOBS ?= auto`** knob (`PYTEST_PARALLEL = -n $(JOBS) --dist worksteal`; `JOBS=0` → serial for a pollution hunt / single-test debug) + `--timeout`.
- **Verify.** `[test]` extra parses (`['pytest…','pytest-xdist>=3.0','pytest-timeout>=2.1','fakeredis…']`); ci.yml YAML valid (jobs: lint, test-unit, test-api, test-slow, frontend, e2e). **Isolation parity PROVEN**: 8 unit files run serial → `209 passed`, `-n 6 --dist worksteal` → `209 passed` (identical set; each xdist worker is its own process ⇒ own session fixtures ⇒ own throwaway SQLite DB from conftest's mkdtemp, so parallelism is isolation-safe). NOTE: on THIS dev box local `-n>=8` runs are dominated by the cross-DC FUSE-mount `server` import cost (see `lib/cross_dc.py`; the `db_paths` FUSE warning), so wall-clock speedup only shows past the import-amortisation crossover — GH runners use local SSD + few cores where `-n auto` is a clean win. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Out-of-scope real failures FLAGGED (not fixed — separate bugs, avoiding scope creep).** Two tests fail in ISOLATION (genuine, pre-existing) and will keep the relevant tier red until fixed: (1) `test_agent_core_boundary::test_core_persistence_imports_within_ratchet` — an ARCHITECTURE-BOUNDARY ratchet trip: `lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py` gained 1 direct persistence import over baseline 0; fix = route it through `lib.agent_core.store.get_conversation_store()`. (2) `test_artifacts_scanner::TestBackfillRoute::test_backfill_round_trip` — DB-backed backfill route failure. A third, `test_api_response::test_api_bad_request`, PASSES alone → cross-test POLLUTION (order-dependent), not a real failure; xdist actually mitigates this by isolating workers.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A CI that installs a NON-EXISTENT extra fails SILENTLY-ish (pip warns, doesn't error) and then dies at the run step with a confusing "pytest: command not found" — always cross-check that every extra referenced in a workflow actually EXISTS in `pyproject.toml`, and that the test runner isn't only in a differently-named extra. Prove xdist safety by pass/fail-SET parity (serial == parallel), not by trusting speed; the suite is already xdist-safe because session fixtures mkdtemp a per-worker SQLite DB. When measuring parallel speedup, remember a heavy `import server` per worker sets a crossover floor — bound `-n` on many-core / slow-FS boxes (that's why the Makefile exposes `JOBS`).


### 2026-07-09 — Project-bar "game-like" pass (increment 1): pet-driven interactive FX layer + meadow depth. Effects react to the pet WALKING across the scene; scene-aware, self-cleaning, reduced-motion-off. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "Replace the ugly project-bar background with an open-source solution; ideally the pet's movement generates game-like interactive effects with it." After reviewing: the "background" is ALREADY the self-authored, license-clean SVG scene system (`::after` ground strip + `::before` top-edge, `[data-decor]` → `scene-*.svg`) — importing 1920×1080 OGA raster into a 17px strip would look like mud + drag in OGA-BY attribution debt. DECISION (owner): option A — enrich our OWN SVG scenes + add a pet-driven interactive effect layer, keeping the CC0/self-authored posture. Acceptance criteria (all met, below).
- **Fix (uncommitted).**
  1. **`static/js/tofu-pet.js`** — FX emitter lives INSIDE the pet module (no new top-level JS → no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change). Reads the pet's OWN `W.x`/`W.dir`/`W.state` (no second position source) and keys flavor off the SAME `_decor` (no parallel scene state). `FX_SCENE = {meadow:{type:'grass',cadence:200,life:640}, pool:{type:'ripple',cadence:240,life:820}, sky:{type:'wisp',cadence:300,life:950}}`; `_fxScene()` returns null for `off`. `_emitFootstep()` spawns a particle at the pet's TRAILING foot (`W.x + petW/2 - W.dir*petW*0.30`), sets `--fx-dir`/`--fx-life`, appends to a dedicated `.tofu-fx` layer, and `setTimeout(remove, life)` self-cleans; `FX_MAX=12` hard cap via `_fxCount`. Emission is driven from the WALK branch of `_step` in step with travel (`_emitAccum` vs per-scene cadence) — so it inherits the pet's reduced-motion gate (walk loop never runs → no effects; no separate toggle to forget). `_place()` also sets `--bar-scene-x = -W.x*0.12` for subtle ground parallax. FX layer created in `mount()` before the pet el (z1, below controls z2). `getState()` now exposes `fxCount` for the harness.
  2. **`static/styles.css`** — `.tofu-fx` overlay (`pointer-events:none`, z1, bottom strip). Three particle kinds as pure CSS keyframes: `tofuFxGrass` (dust puff + directional grass-lean via `--fx-dir`), `tofuFxRipple` (expanding ring), `tofuFxWisp` (rising sparkle drifting opposite travel). Ground `::after` `background-position` now reads `calc(var(--bar-scene-x,0px)) bottom` (parallax; 0 default when unset). Reduced-motion `@media` block ALSO `display:none`s `.tofu-fx` + kills particle animation — belt-and-braces on top of the emitter never firing.
  3. **`static/icons/pet/scene-meadow.svg`** — depth pass: added a FAR pale back-hill (`#CFDDC4`, long-wavelength) behind the existing mid/near bands + faint low-opacity near-ground tufts. All three bands' bumps still return to their start-y at x=120 → seamless 120px tile preserved; muted sage palette kept; still SVG/CC0/self-authored.
- **Verify (all green).** `node --check` OK; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-952b457c.js` (`tofu-fx` + `bar-scene-x` survive; `_emitFootstep`/`FX_SCENE` minified-renamed as expected). SVG XML valid for all 4 scenes; meadow seam baseline confirmed; styles.css braces balanced. DOM-shim harness drives the REAL shipped tofu-pet.js with a manual rAF pump + fake clock, 16 assertions ALL PASS: default meadow enters `walk` on mount; **meadow→grass only (11, capped ≤12)**, **pool→ripple only (9)**, **sky→wisp only (8)**; parallax `--bar-scene-x` tracks position; **particles self-remove after life (0 leaked)**; **scene=off → 0 particles**; and the NEUTER — **reduced-motion → pet doesn't roam (state idle) → 0 effect nodes**. (Harness gotcha logged: create a FRESH `#projectBar` element per `load()` — the idempotent id/class registration flags on a reused stub keep it out of the re-inited registry, so `mount()` bails and every FX assertion falsely reads 0; a real product-0 vs harness-0 distinction.)
- **Resolved per-scene effect behavior (as requested).** meadow: footstep dust + grass-part lean at the trailing foot; pool: expanding ripple ring under each step; sky: soft rising wisp/sparkle drifting against travel. All `pointer-events:none` at z1 (below controls z2 → never blocks a hit target), throttled by per-scene cadence, capped at 12 concurrent, each self-removing on its `--fx-life` timer (no DOM leak). `off` and reduced-motion both yield zero nodes.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time JS bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed JS bundle; CSS auto-busts via css_bundler; the scene SVGs are `url()`-referenced so a hard-refresh re-fetches them). Increment 1 = effects + meadow depth; pool/sky depth passes + an optional richer parallax back-layer are the natural increment-2 if wanted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For a "pet interacts with the world" effect, the emitter MUST read the pet's existing single source of truth (`W.x`/`W.dir`/`W.state`) and the existing scene var (`_decor`) — never a parallel position/scene state — and it should be driven from INSIDE the walk loop so it inherits the reduced-motion gate for free (one gate, not two). Cap concurrent particles + self-remove each on a timer matched to its CSS `--fx-life` so JS-removal and animation-end agree (no leak, no orphan). Enrich a seamless tiled SVG by ADDING depth bands whose bumps also return to the tile's baseline at x=120 — the seam invariant is per-band, so a new far-hill must obey it too.


### 2026-07-09 — Capabilities-surface audit + root-cause drift fix: `GET /api/v1/capabilities` now advertises the real agent surface (dead `swarm.run` removed; `agent.run`/`audio.*`/`scheduler`/`mcp` added), exposes STT flags, and a NEW drift-guard test pins `_agents_summary()` to the live url_map so the hand-literal can't silently rot again. Payload TTL-cached. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Verify the backend API correctly exposes our capabilities; fix ROOT CAUSE not symptom. The recurring problem: `_agents_summary()` in `routes/api_v1/capabilities.py` is a hand-maintained literal that drifts every time an agent lands. 5-point brief: (1) remove dead `swarm.run`, add genuinely-registered surfaces; (2) `transcription`/`audio_chat` model flags + `voice_input` feature flag gated on `transcription_available()`; (3) fix the `_models_summary` docstring (reads `_SAVED_CONFIG`, not the live dispatcher); (4) NON-NEGOTIABLE drift-guard test asserting every advertised path resolves on `url_map` + every scope ∈ `ALL_SCOPES`; (5) TTL-cache the payload keyed so a config change invalidates.
- **Findings (verified against real routes before editing).** `swarm.run → /api/v1/agents/swarm/run` existed NOWHERE — agents.py:530-534 documents that a swarm launches in-band via `config.swarmEnabled=true` on `/chat/completions`; only `swarm/{status,abort}` are exposed. The literal also omitted `agent.run` (`/api/v1/agent/run`, scope `agents:run`), `audio.transcribe`+`audio.capabilities` (`/api/v1/audio/*`, scope `chat`), `scheduler` (`/api/v1/scheduler/tasks`, `agents:scheduler`), `mcp` (`/api/v1/mcp/servers`, `agents:mcp`). `_models_summary` emitted no `transcription`/`audio_chat` flags despite both being first-class NON_CHAT caps since 2026-07-07. OpenAPI coverage was NOT drifting (audio + all v1 bps carry `@api_meta`; `build_spec` walks `url_map`) — drift was isolated to this literal + the two model-flag gaps.
- **Fix (uncommitted, `routes/api_v1/capabilities.py`).** (1) `_agents_summary()`: dropped `swarm.run`, added the 5 real entries with a code comment explaining swarm has no run-route. (2) `_models_summary()`: added `transcription`/`audio_chat` bool flags; rewrote the docstring to say it reads persisted `lib._SAVED_CONFIG['providers']` (not the dispatcher). (3) `_features()`: added `voice_input` = `bool(transcription_available())` (best-effort, fails to `False` so a no-STT deployment advertises it off, matching the mic-hide contract). (4) PERF: split the route body into `_build_capabilities()` and wrapped it in a module-level `TTLCache(ttl=30, max_size=8)` keyed on `id(lib._SAVED_CONFIG)` — `reload_config()` rebinds that attr to a freshly-allocated dict (new id while old is still referenced), so a settings change invalidates instantly; the 30s TTL is only a backstop. Also cached the two `system-prompt/{default,blocks}` builds in a separate `TTLCache(ttl=300)` keyed on `(kind, project, tools)` (the static prompt is a pure function of those two bools; cwd/model/date are fixed/omitted).
- **Root-cause drift-guard (`tests/test_capabilities_agents_drift.py`, NEW, 4 tests green).** Registers ALL_V1_BLUEPRINTS on a Quart app, walks `url_map` (normalising `<var>`→`{var}`), and asserts: every `_agents_summary()` path is registered; every scope ∈ `ALL_SCOPES`; entries have id/path/scope shape; and a named regression that `swarm.run` never returns. This is what stops the literal rotting — I could NOT cleanly derive the list from routes (agent endpoints span multiple blueprints with heterogeneous shapes + curated ids/scopes), so the guard IS the mechanism per the owner's fallback.
- **Verify (real output).** Drift-guard 4/4 PASS. BITE-CONFIRMED out-of-band (import `server` first to install the Flask→Quart shim, as conftest does): old `/api/v1/agents/swarm/run` is ABSENT from url_map (guard would flag it) while all 5 new paths resolve True → the path-resolution assertion is load-bearing. Integration `test_capabilities_is_public` + `test_openapi_json_lists_routes` + `test_openapi_yaml_returned` + `test_swagger_ui_renders` PASS; `test_ttl_cache.py` 20/20 PASS (24 total in that run). End-to-end: `_build_capabilities()` agents ids = agent.run/audio.capabilities/audio.transcribe/browser.fetch/image-gen/mcp/memory.search/paper.report/paper.translate/scheduler/search/search.async/translate (NO swarm.run); `features.voice_input=True`; cache key changes across `lib.reload_config()` (invalidation proven). `ast.parse` OK. Run with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` (napari autoload quirk in this env). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A self-describing capabilities surface built from a hand-maintained literal WILL drift silently — advertising a 404 path (`swarm.run`) and omitting real endpoints — because nothing couples it to the registered routes. When the list can't be cleanly derived (agent endpoints are heterogeneous across blueprints), the fix is a drift-guard test that walks the actual `url_map` + the closed `ALL_SCOPES` enum; that's the coupling. For caching a config-derived payload, key on `id(lib._SAVED_CONFIG)` — `reload_config()` rebinds it to a new dict so the id flips on any settings change (instant invalidation), with a short TTL as the only backstop; `api_ok()` builds a fresh envelope and never mutates its arg, so caching the inner dict is safe.

Rev-neutral write copied verbatim from `_migrate_backfill_segments_from_task_results._rev_neutral_write`: CAS-guarded `messages` UPDATE on the read rev, then rev-reset in the SAME transaction; `updated_at` untouched → no sidebar re-sort / cross-device staleness flip; CAS-miss on a concurrent rev move → skip. Dry-run default makes ZERO LLM calls (reports eligibility counts only); `--apply` translates per-segment. Enrich-only, per-row try/except, `--id/--limit`.
- **Test (`tests/test_segment_translation_backfill.py`, 11 tests, all green).** Eligibility filter (5 cases: eligible; not-yet-translated; all-stamped; pre-v36 no-segments; user-msg). Single-source-of-truth: asserts `mig._translate_segments_to_map is runtime._translate_segments_to_map` and `mig._stamp_segment_translations is commit._stamp_segment_translations` (identity — no fork). End-to-end translate→stamp→IDEMPOTENT (2nd pass returns `{}`). Rev-neutral write via an in-memory fake `async_transaction`: asserts exactly 2 stmts (messages UPDATE then rev-reset), rev held at expected, NO stmt touches `updated_at`; and CAS-miss on a moved rev → no write. NEUTER: a core with the enrich-only `translatedText`-skip line removed re-translates already-stamped segments → proves the skip is the load-bearing idempotency guard. `_as_list` coercion.
- **Dry-run (real DB, whole fleet).** 124 conversations / 350 messages / **5277 narration segments** eligible, 0 errored.
- **Single-conv proof (`mramt3iiqh1z4i`, owner-authorized).** BEFORE: rev=92, updated_at=1783430370263, eligible-msg narration segs stamped 0/5. `--apply --id` → "stamped 5 segment(s) on 2 msg(s) (rev stays 92)". AFTER: rev=92 (UNCHANGED), updated_at UNCHANGED, 5/5 eligible-msg segments stamped with real Chinese (spot-checked: EN "Let me read the current translation gate code…" → ZH "让我一起阅读当前的翻译门控代码…"). Idempotent re-run: 0 conversations / 0 segments stamped, no write. (The conv has 20 total narration segments but only 5 are on already-`translatedContent` messages; the other 15 are on un-translated turns the backfill correctly leaves alone.)
- **Verify.** ast+import OK; 45 tests pass together (retro 6 + backfill 11 + incremental 19 + safety-net 4 + phase2 5). No JS changed (render layer already reads `seg.translatedText`). NOT committed (owner attribution). Broad `--apply` across the remaining 123 convs NOT run — awaiting sign-off (5277 real LLM calls).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A write-path fix that gates on "already has output" is INCOMPLETE for existing rows that already have that output — they'll never re-trigger, so a one-shot backfill is mandatory, not polish. Reuse-not-fork is enforceable at test time via `is`-identity assertions on the shared functions. Make the shared translate core ENRICH-ONLY (skip already-populated fields) so the live path and the migration share one idempotency guarantee and neither clobbers the other's work. Copy the rev-neutral write discipline verbatim from the proven segments backfill — a naive UPDATE would bump rev and make every open client eat a spurious CAS 409.


### 2026-07-09 — Fixed Paper Mode "Failed to load PDF: Missing PDF …" under a cloud-IDE proxy: library re-open handed pdf.js a base-path-less URL. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Symptom (owner).** Opening a paper from the library showed `Failed to load PDF: Missing PDF "https://<host>/api/paper/pdf/arxiv_2606.30534v2.pdf"`. The paper (arXiv:2606.30534 "Orca") and its 41 MB PDF were both present on disk under `PAPER_DIR`.
- **Diagnosis (verify-then-write; backend proven healthy first).** The 41 MB file exists (`uploads/papers/arxiv_2606.30534v2.pdf`) and BOTH live chatui servers (ports 15000/15001) serve it correctly — `curl` → `200`, `application/pdf`, 41577569 bytes; access.log confirms `GET /api/paper/pdf/... 200 (0.002s)`. So the backend is NOT at fault. The tell: the app is served through a VS Code proxy under a base path (`/proxy/15000/` — visible in the `Referer` of every logged request), and the FAILING URL in the error is `https://<host>/api/paper/pdf/...` with NO `/proxy/15000` prefix. That request hits the outer gateway root, not the app — which is exactly why there is NO matching line in the app's own access.log (it never reached the app). pdf.js reports a 404 on `getDocument()` as "Missing PDF".
- **Root cause.** `apiUrl()` (static/js/core.js:9) prepends `BASE_PATH` (derived from `window.location.pathname`) to every backend path so it survives the proxy prefix. The fresh-fetch/upload paths do this correctly (`_paperPdfUrl = apiUrl(doneData.pdf_url)` — paper-reader.js:2232, :1555). But the LIBRARY RE-OPEN path assigned the persisted value verbatim: `_paperPdfUrl = entry.pdfUrl` (paper-reader.js:578 `_openPaperEntry`, :767 `enterPaperMode`). The row's `pdfUrl` is persisted by two writers with different shapes — the server ingest stores a ROOT-RELATIVE `/api/paper/pdf/<f>` (routes/paper.py:1705; the backend can't know the proxy prefix), while a client PUT stores an `apiUrl()`-prefixed value baked with THAT session's `BASE_PATH`. Either is wrong to hand pdf.js verbatim: the root-relative one drops the prefix (→ gateway 404), and a baked prefix goes stale if the port/prefix changes.
- **Fix (uncommitted, 1 seam).** New `_resolvePaperPdfUrl(url)` in `static/js/paper-reader.js` (just above `_loadPaperPdf`): find the canonical `/api/` segment, slice from there, and re-apply the LIVE `BASE_PATH` via `apiUrl()`. Non-API URLs (`blob:`/`data:`/absolute externals — no `/api/`) are returned untouched. `_loadPaperPdf` now calls it on its `url` argument first, so the URL self-heals at the single point of use REGARDLESS of how it was stored (raw root-relative, correctly-prefixed, or stale-prefixed). Idempotent: a correctly-prefixed value re-bases to itself.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_paper_pdf_url_rebase.py`, real shipped paper-reader.js under jsdom with `apiUrl` stubbed to a `/proxy/15000` base; biting neuter).** Positive: root-relative gains the prefix; already-prefixed is not doubled; a STALE `/proxy/9999` prefix is re-based to `/proxy/15000`; `blob:`/empty untouched. Negative-control: a COPY with the helper body replaced by `return url` (identity = pre-fix behaviour) makes the root-relative check FAIL, proving the helper is load-bearing; shipped file asserted byte-identical after. Both pass.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; the new guard passes (positive + neuter); bundle rebuilt → feature bundle `feature-547f0c32.js` / core `bundle-54e4091b.js` (grep-confirmed `_resolvePaperPdfUrl` survives esbuild). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any stored URL that will be fetched under a cloud-IDE / reverse proxy must be re-based onto the LIVE `BASE_PATH` at the point of use, never assigned verbatim from a persisted row — a DB-stored `/api/...` is base-path-agnostic by design (the server can't know the proxy prefix) and a client-baked prefix goes stale. Prefer normalizing at the single fetch site (`_loadPaperPdf`) over trying to keep every writer/reader in lock-step. Adjacent (not fixed, noted): `serve_paper_pdf` uses `send_file` and does NOT honor HTTP `Range` (a `Range:` request returns the full 41 MB with no `Accept-Ranges`) — fine for correctness but a large PDF over a proxy would benefit from range support later.
