### 2026-07-09 — Fixed "translation clustered at the bottom in completed history" — the whole-message/retro translate path now stamps per-segment `translatedText`, symmetric with the live incremental worker. Backend-only, uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Auto-translate looked interleaved (Chinese in place, next to each tool) WHILE streaming, but on reopening a finished conversation (or toggling the global switch / clicking Translate / on-open retro) all the Chinese snapped to one blob at the very bottom. Owner confirmed the root cause: `lib/translate/runtime.py:_do_translate` calls `_commit_translation_to_db` with NO `segment_translations` in every branch → it only ever writes the deliverable `translatedContent` blob, never stamps `translatedText` onto the narration segments. Directive: backend-first root-cause fix, option #1 only — do NOT touch the render layer, do NOT rip out the bilingual 原文/译文 toggle or bottom preview, per-segment LLM calls are fine (correctness over cost).
- **Root cause (confirmed by reading both paths).** The interleave is driven by `msg.segments[*].translatedText`, read by `renderSegmentTimelineHTML`/`_renderTimelineBatch` (`tool_rounds.js:2702`, `_segText = seg.translatedText || seg.text`). The ONLY writer of that field was the live incremental worker (`incremental.py:_Acc._do_finalize_inner` builds `{round_num: 中文}` from its cached per-round segments → `commit._stamp_segment_translations`). The whole-message path (`runtime._do_translate`) never had those cached segments, so it passed `segment_translations=None` and the narration stayed English → the entire Chinese only existed as the bottom `translatedContent` blob. The commit/stamp plumbing (`_stamp_segment_translations`, keyed by `llmRound`) already existed and was tested; the sole gap was that this path never BUILT the map.
- **Fix (uncommitted, backend-only, `lib/translate/runtime.py`).**
  1. New `_read_message_segments(conv_id, msg_id, msg_idx)` — reads the target assistant message's `segments` list from the DB (resolve by `_msgId` first, then position). Returns None for a pre-v36 row / missing conv/msg. Never raises.
  2. New `_build_segment_translation_map(conv_id, msg_id, msg_idx, system_prompt, source, target)` — translates each NON-deliverable `text` segment (keyed by `llmRound`), symmetric with the incremental worker: same per-segment notranslate extraction (`_extract_notranslate_blocks`/`_reattach_notranslate_blocks`) + already-Chinese skip (`is_predominantly_chinese`). Returns `{llmRound: 中文}` or None. Per-segment failures logged + skipped (pure enrichment — never breaks the deliverable commit).
  3. Wired into BOTH commit branches of `_do_translate` (the main done-commit AND the notranslate-only skip-done branch): build the map only when `field=='translatedContent'`, pass it as `segment_translations=` into the existing `_commit_translation_to_db`. Guarded by try/except so a map-build failure degrades to the old blob-only commit.
- **Guardrails honored.** No-op for messages without `segments` (map build returns None → commit behaves exactly as before). Deliverable `translatedContent` commit is unchanged in every path. Survives notranslate-block extraction (per-segment, same as the deliverable). Render layer + bilingual toggle + bottom preview UNTOUCHED. Logs per discipline (`%`-style, `[Translate]` prefix, warning on per-segment/build failure).
- **Test (`tests/test_retro_segment_translation.py`, 6 tests, all green).** Mirrors `test_incremental_translate.py`'s stamp assertion but drives the retro `_do_translate` path via an in-memory `_FakeConn` shared by the segment-read SELECT and the commit CAS UPDATE, so the stamp lands in the stored messages and is read back. Covers: helper translates narration by llmRound (tool_use + deliverable/terminal excluded); already-Chinese narration kept verbatim (no LLM); no-op without segments; END-TO-END `_do_translate` stamps `translatedText` on narration segments + still commits the blob; pre-v36 no-op (no segments invented); and a NEUTER (`_build_segment_translation_map` → None) that reproduces the bottom-cluster regression. BITE-VERIFIED: temporarily replacing `segment_translations=seg_trans` with `=None` in the shipped file makes the end-to-end test FAIL; restored green.
- **Verify.** ast-parse + import OK; `tests/test_retro_segment_translation.py` (6) + `test_incremental_translate.py` (19) + `test_auto_translate_safety_net.py` (4) + `test_auto_translate_phase2.py` (5) = 34 passed together. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-54e4091b.js` (no JS changed; rebuilt per request). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh (retro path re-runs on open / global-toggle → old finished convs re-stamp their segments and interleave in place).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a settled renderer reads a field (`seg.translatedText`) that only ONE of several write paths populates, the "works live but not on reload" symptom is a WRITE-side coverage gap, not a render bug — find every committer and make the missing one symmetric, reusing the existing stamp plumbing rather than adding a frontend fallback. The whole-message translate path has no cached per-round segments, so it must READ them back from the DB and translate them itself; that's the price of correctness the owner explicitly accepted over cost.


### 2026-07-09 — Project-bar pet art made a SWAPPABLE PACK (tofu default + optional public-domain oneko), not a hardcoded prefix. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "The pets are ugly; find good-looking open-source ones, not necessarily tofu." Decision after weighing: KEEP soft-chibi tofu as shipped default (it matches our antialiased aesthetic; no clean-licensed animated set beats it on looks+animation+license). Petdex ruled out PERMANENTLY (user-submitted fan-art of others' IP + takedown clause = legal landmine for the open-source export). Instead: make the character art PLUGGABLE and add oneko as an optional, license-clean alternate skin — no FSM rewrite.
- **Why this is cheap/safe.** `tofu-pet.js` never hardcodes anything but filenames: the wander/position/expression FSM only ever asks `_frameUrl(frame)` for a URL, driven by the `EXPRESSIONS`+`WALK_FRAMES`+`FRAME_ALIAS` lists. So an art swap touches ASSETS + one resolver, not the engine.
- **Fix (uncommitted).**
  1. **`static/js/tofu-pet.js`** — new `PET_PACKS` registry (pure data: `{id,label,dir,prefix,pixel,alias}`), `PACK_ORDER`, `DEFAULT_PACK='tofu'`, `PACK_KEY='tofu_pet_pack'` localStorage, `_pack` state. `_frameUrl(frame)` now resolves through `_activePack()` (`base + dir + '/' + prefix + (alias[frame]||frame) + '.png'`) instead of the hardcoded `tofu-pet-` prefix. Added `_loadPack`/`_applyPack` (stamps `data-pack` on the pet el — ONE place, mirrors `_applyDecor`)/`setPack`/`cyclePack` (mirror `setDecor`/`cycleDecor` exactly: persist → apply → preload new pack → repaint current pose). Wired `_loadPack` into `_boot`, `_applyPack` into `mount`, a `tofu:pack` DOM event seam next to `tofu:decor`, and exposed `setPack/cyclePack/getPack/PET_PACKS/PACK_ORDER` on `window.TofuPet`. A future pack = assets folder + one registry entry, nothing else.
  2. **`static/icons/pet/oneko/`** — vendored the classic Neko sprite (oneko.gif 256×128 = 8×4 grid of 32px tiles) from adryd325/oneko.js, sliced pose-by-pose into our 12 frame names via PIL. Tile coords taken DIRECTLY from oneko.js's `spriteSets` [col,row] map (not guessed). Cat has poses not emotions → closest-pose mapping: idle=idle-sit, happy=alert, thinking=scratchSelf(groom), celebrating=scratchWallW(paw-up), surprised=scratchWallN, sleepy=tired, sleeping=sleeping, sad=sleeping-frame2, walk1-4=E-run pair (2-beat over 4 ticks). `LICENSE` note records provenance: oneko.js CODE is MIT (© 2022 adryd); the SPRITE ART is the ancient public-domain 1989 Neko (per glreno + Wikipedia). Safe to ship in every export mode.
  3. **`static/styles.css`** — `[data-pack="oneko"] .tofu-pet-img{image-rendering:pixelated/crisp-edges;filter:none}` (+ a brightness-only hover) so the 32px pixel art renders CRISP and the soft brown drop-shadow tuned for the chibi tofu art doesn't smear hard pixel edges. Wander/animation layers unchanged (pack-agnostic).
- **Verify (all green).** `node --check` OK. `tofu-pet.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → NO new top-level JS file, bundler rule satisfied. **All 24 frame URLs resolve, 0 missing** (12 tofu + 12 oneko, programmatically walked from the actual EXPRESSIONS/WALK_FRAMES lists in the shipped source), FRAME_ALIAS `curious→thinking` target resolves. `git check-ignore` → exit 1 (NOT ignored, will commit); `is_agent_artifact()` False for the dir/LICENSE/png (not `.tofu*`) → export sanitizer + .gitignore treat them as normal committed source assets, same as the existing `tofu-pet-*.png`. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-a0ba23a0.js`; `PET_PACKS/setPack/cyclePack/data-pack/oneko-` all survive esbuild (grep-confirmed).
- **Resolved frame URLs (as requested, both packs, base-relative).** tofu: `/static/icons/pet/tofu-pet-<frame>.png`; oneko: `/static/icons/pet/oneko/oneko-<frame>.png`; where `<frame>` ∈ {idle,happy,sleepy,sleeping,thinking,surprised,sad,celebrating,walk1,walk2,walk3,walk4}. All 24 exist on disk.
- **NOT committed** (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed bundle filename) to see it. Switch packs at runtime: `TofuPet.cyclePack()` / `TofuPet.setPack('oneko')` in console, or `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('tofu:pack',{detail:'oneko'}))`. There is NO visible pack-switch button yet — deliberately left for owner to decide placement (the scene-switch button pattern in index.html is the template if wanted).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When "swap the art" is asked, check whether the art is already decoupled from the behavior FSM (here it was — only filenames were hardcoded); if so the clean move is a DATA registry (pack = dir+prefix+alias) routed through the one URL resolver, keeping the default and making alternates additive. For a vendored sprite, take slice coords from the SOURCE's own sprite-map (oneko.js `spriteSets`), never eyeball them; verify EVERY name the frame lists reference resolves to a real file (a missing pose silently 404s to a broken `<img>`); and split license cleanly — CODE license (MIT) vs ART license (public domain) are different facts, record both.


### 2026-07-08 — Pillar #6 peer-message ROUND-BOUNDARY fast path (board epic pt_2d320cae4bca4b67): peer messages now reach a LIVE target at the next round boundary of the running turn (like a `<swarm-update>`), not only at cycle-end. HYBRID two-lane, zero-double-delivery proven bidirectionally. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "Inter-conversation comms should insert into the next tool-call round like a sub-agent, not wait for a whole task cycle." Approved design: keep `message_queue KIND_PEER_MSG` as the single DURABLE source of truth; when the target has a LIVE task, ALSO enqueue an `agent_inbox` twin (round-boundary delivery). Owner's hard bar: **zero double delivery**, proven with a neuter that bites. Plus: charter amendment FIRST; storm-guard + short-id resolution unchanged upstream of both lanes; in-timeline render chip; endpoint/autopilot keep queue-lane; claim a board epic; leave uncommitted.
- **Key finding (the mechanism already existed, wrong lane).** `agent_inbox` is ALREADY conv-keyed (`swarm_key_for(task)`=convId) and drained UNGATED every round by the orchestrator (`orchestrator.py` ~L1849) with the `_has_unmatched_tool_call` postpone guard (never splits a tool_call↔tool_result pair). Peer messages just sat in the `message_queue` DISPATCH lane (cycle-end). So the fix routes a live-target peer message into the SAME inbox seam swarm-updates already use — near-free.
- **Fix (uncommitted; 5 backend seams + 4 frontend).**
  1. **`lib/agent_core/events.py`** — new `PEER_INBOX_INJECT='peer_inbox_inject'` type + EventSpec (category PRESENCE; fields round/count/previews[{fromConv,text}]). Registered so the event-registry drift guard passes both directions.
  2. **`lib/agent_inbox.py`** — new `consume_peer(task_id, queue_ids)`: REVERSE-race de-dup twin of `consume` (keys on the item's `queueId` in `extra`, not agent_id).
  3. **`lib/conversations/project_peer.py`** — `_live_drain_eligible_task(conv_id)` gate (running, not aborted, NOT `_endpoint_managed`/`endpointMode`/`_vu_subtask`); `send_peer_message` now, AFTER the durable enqueue succeeds, ALSO `agent_inbox.enqueue(to_conv, body, mode='peer-msg', extra={queueId, fromConv, peerText, peerHuman})` when the target is live+drain-eligible. Fast-path failure never breaks delivery (durable row stands). Storm-guard `_rate_gate` + `_resolve_target_conv_id` run ONCE upstream, unchanged.
  4. **`lib/message_queue.py`** — new `dedup_peer_durable_rows(conv_id, queue_ids)` (FORWARD-race helper, symmetric to `consume_peer`); `dispatch_next_queued` calls `consume_peer` when it pops a `_peerMessage` row (REVERSE race).
  5. **`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`** drain hook — partitions drained items into peer (mode=='peer-msg') vs swarm; swarm path unchanged (mark_delivered + SWARM_INBOX_INJECT); peer path calls `dedup_peer_durable_rows(conv, [queueIds])` (FORWARD de-dup) then emits `PEER_INBOX_INJECT` with sender+text previews.
  6. **Frontend** — `_handlePeerInboxInject` (sse_handlers_lifecycle.js) pushes a synthetic `_peerInject` toolRound (dedup by `peer:<round>` key); dispatch wired in sse_pipeline.js; `_renderPeerInjectRow` (tool_rounds.js) renders an in-timeline chip mirroring the swarm inbox row (SVG mail icon, sender short-ids, "injected → context" badge); i18n `peer.injectRow*` EN+ZH. Queue-lane fresh-turn case keeps the existing `.peer-msg-banner`.
- **ZERO-DOUBLE-DELIVERY (the load-bearing bar) — proven BIDIRECTIONALLY.** The message lives in two lanes; delivered exactly once via queueId-keyed de-dup on BOTH races: FORWARD (inbox drains first → hook deletes the durable row by queueId) and REVERSE (task ends first → dispatch drops the inbox twin by queueId). `tests/test_peer_message_round_boundary.py` (9 tests): gating (live→both lanes; idle/endpoint/VU/aborted→durable-only), forward positive+NEUTER, reverse positive+NEUTER. BITE-VERIFIED against REAL code, not test simulation: neutering the real `dedup_peer_durable_rows` body → forward positive test FAILS; neutering the real `consume_peer` call site in `dispatch_next_queued` → reverse positive test FAILS (both restored green). Both de-dups were extracted into named helpers precisely so the neuter drives shipped code.
- **Charter.** Filed `project_charter_propose` reframing invariant #1 from "seen on the NEXT turn" → "delivered at the next round boundary of a live turn (never mid-stream, never splitting a tool_call↔tool_result pair); durable queue row still delivers to an idle target." No-auto-relay + per-(sender,target) rate limit stated as UNCHANGED, upstream of both lanes. Recorded for human commit.
- **Verify.** py ast-parse OK (5 files); `node --check` OK (4 JS); 104 tests pass (round_boundary 9 + agent_inbox 25 + message_queue 10 + project_peer 26 + human_nudge 7 + target_resolution 9 + sse_dispatch 1[+peer scenario] + event_registry 5 + event_emit 12); swarm_pending_tool_force 10 pass (drain-hook partition didn't regress swarm). Bundle rebuilt → core `bundle-c026831e.js`; `_handlePeerInboxInject`/`_renderPeerInjectRow`/`_peerInject`/`peer_inbox_inject`/`peer.injectRowLabel` all survive esbuild (grep-confirmed). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a message is deliverable via TWO lanes (durable queue + in-memory inbox), de-dup MUST be BIDIRECTIONAL and keyed on ONE shared token (the durable `queueId`): closing only the forward race leaves the reverse (task-ends-before-drain) open, and vice-versa. Extract each de-dup into a NAMED helper (`dedup_peer_durable_rows` / `consume_peer`) so the neuter test can bite SHIPPED code, not a hand-rolled simulation of it. The fast-path gate must exclude modes that DON'T run the round-boundary drain (endpoint / VU) — those keep queue-lane delivery; don't assume the inbox is drained everywhere.


### 2026-07-08 — Closed epic pt_78579f57be1c4f60 (settled-render keep-longer overrides committedMessage) the RIGHT way: BACKEND-FIRST. Landed the never-landed `_committedMsg` parity stamp, THEN switched the frontend settle to verbatim. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Context.** Peer conv mrc8uwtf's render-authority review filed finding #2 as board epic pt_78579f57be1c4f60, framed as a FRONTEND fix ("project committedMessage verbatim at settle"). Verify-then-write caught that this is UNSAFE as a pure frontend edit.
- **Root cause (proven, not inferred).** `orchestrator.py:983` calls `_sync_result_to_conversation` before the done emit and (per its comment) "stamps `task['_committedMsg']`"; `orchestrator.py:1094` ships `done_evt['committedMessage'] = task['_committedMsg']`. BUT `manager.py` had ZERO assignments to `_committedMsg` — the parity stamp was designed (2026-07-03 "backend sole writer" consolidation) but NEVER LANDED (my `committedMsg-parity-stamp-never-landed` memory; `test_committed_message_parity.py` was RED). So `committedMessage` was essentially never shipped → the frontend keep-longer at sse_pipeline.js:1632 was the ONLY thing rendering the settled bubble. Projecting committedMessage "verbatim" frontend-side FIRST would project nothing → blank bubble. The two halves MUST land together, backend first.
- **Fix (uncommitted, 2 seams + 3 test updates).**
  1. **Backend stamp (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`, `_sync_result_to_conversation`).** On CAS success, right after `update_conversation_fts`: `task['_committedMsg'] = dict(last_msg)` — freezes the EXACT terminal assistant dict written to conversations.messages. Stamped ONLY on CAS success; skip/CAS-miss/crash paths leave it UNSET (→ done omits committedMessage → client keeps its transient buffer, the offline fallback, still keep-longer-guarded).
  2. **Frontend verbatim projection (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`:1632).** When `ev.committedMessage` is present, project content/thinking/toolRounds VERBATIM (`_cm.content`, `_cm.thinking`, `_cm.toolRounds`) instead of `_snapshotLonger`/`_snapshotLongerRounds`. The committed dict is now authoritative AND complete, so a legitimately-SHORTER backend record correctly wins over a stale-longer local buffer (settled bubble == DB record; the directive). The 4 STATE-snapshot sites (2 planner, worker, plain-assistant merge) KEEP keep-longer UNCHANGED — they replay a mid-stream checkpoint that can be cold/shorter, so the anti-blanking guard is still load-bearing there.
- **Tension resolved (this is the subtle part).** The keep-longer belt at :1632 was NOT a naive bug — it was pinned by `test_frontend_toolrounds_keep_longer.py` (asserted the done-site routes through `_snapshotLongerRounds`, count ≥6) and justified by `state-snapshot-keep-longer-guard`. Removing it is only correct BECAUSE the backend stamp now guarantees committedMessage is complete. Updated `test_frontend_toolrounds_keep_longer.py`: docstring now distinguishes the 4 keep-longer STATE sites from the verbatim DONE site; count guard ≥5 (4 sites + 1 def); banned-pattern list no longer forbids `assistantMsg.toolRounds = _cm.toolRounds` (now correct) but STILL forbids the raw state-snapshot overwrites; added a positive guard that the done site IS verbatim. `test_frontend_reconnect_keeplonger_invariant.py` UNCHANGED + green (it tests the pure helpers in isolation — still used at the state sites). Strengthened `test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` #28 to assert a SHORTER committedMessage is adopted verbatim (the directive-defining case; pre-fix keep-longer would have kept the stale longer buffer).
- **Verify.** `_committedMsg` parity 3/3 (standalone `TOFU_DB_PATH=…`; pytest can't run it in this sandbox — no provisioned DB, same `no such table` as the other DB-touching suites). node --check OK; sse_dispatch (#28 strengthened), toolrounds_keep_longer, reconnect_keeplonger_invariant, state_snapshot_keep_longer, finishstream_no_put ALL green in isolation. (Combined-run `SyntaxError` is a PRE-EXISTING test-infra quirk: sibling frontend tests share the `tests/_*_harness.js` filename and clobber each other under fast sequential writes — each passes alone.) Bundle → `bundle-c026831e.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "frontend keep-longer overrides backend truth" finding can be RIGHT to fix but WRONG to fix frontend-first: if the backend authoritative record (committedMessage) isn't actually being shipped (grep the WRITE, not just the readers — a designed-but-never-landed stamp is invisible to review), removing the frontend belt blanks the bubble. Land the backend stamp FIRST, then switch the frontend to verbatim, in ONE change. And keep the DISTINCTION crisp: verbatim for the authoritative terminal committedMessage; keep-longer for mid-stream STATE snapshots (which can legitimately be cold/shorter on reconnect) — same helper file, opposite correct behaviours.


### 2026-07-08 — Acted on a peer render-authority review: FIXED the sidebar list-merge wall-clock tiebreaker (→ monotonic rev authority); DECLINED the committedMessage keep-longer "fix" (it's a tested guard; the real fix is backend-first). Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Context.** Sibling conv mrc8uwtf did a read-only render-authority review and handed me 3 findings living in MY files, all the "local looks-longer/newer overrides backend truth" class. Verify-then-write; I read the actual code + the tests pinning each before touching anything.
- **Finding 3 — FIXED (real, in-scope, aligned with the rev-authority direction I just built).** `conversations.js` list-merge (~:991) gated body-staleness of an already-loaded conv on `serverMsgCount > local.messages.length || sT > mT` where sT/mT are wall-clock `updatedAt`. Wall-clock is SKEW-PRONE across devices → a stale server snapshot with a later clock flips `_needsLoad=true` on the OPEN conv → spurious body refetch → the "positions keep shifting" symptom; and a genuine same-count in-place extend on a lagging-clock device is MISSED. The body loader (:1278) and the notify push already gate on the monotonic server-issued `rev`; the list payload ALSO carries it (`_conv_row_to_meta_dict`:144 → SELECT includes `rev`). FIX: when `sc.rev` and `local._serverRev` are BOTH numbers, rev is AUTHORITATIVE (stale iff `sc.rev > local._serverRev`); wall-clock is a FALLBACK only for a legacy rev=0/pre-rev row. Also adopt a forward-moving `sc.rev` into `local._serverRev` (CAS base advance; never rewind from a lagging list snapshot). New msg (count grew) still triggers regardless.
- **Finding 2 — DECLINED (verify-then-write caught a would-be regression).** The review flagged `sse_pipeline.js:1632` running content/thinking/toolRounds through `_snapshotLonger`/`_snapshotLongerRounds` even when `ev.committedMessage` is present, as "settled bubble ≠ DB record." TRUE in the abstract, but this is NOT a naive bug: (a) the code comment there explicitly justifies it as "belt-and-braces against a rare EMPTY committed dict racing a fuller local stream"; (b) it's PINNED by `test_frontend_reconnect_keeplonger_invariant.py` whose neuter proves a raw assignment reintroduces the cold-reconnect blanking ("generating then GONE") — the exact bug my `state-snapshot-keep-longer-guard` memory documents. Ripping the belt out FRONTEND-side is the WRONG ORDER: the project's own patch→fundamental register item #5 says fix the empty-committed-dict RACE in manager.py FIRST, then the belt is provably unneeded. Handed it back to the peer as a backend-first epic, not a frontend edit. (Finding 1 was in the peer's own lane — dead orphan-marker in routes/conversations.py — already landed by them.)
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_list_merge_rev_authority.py`, 8 checks, real shipped conversations.js under node, double-neuter).** skew trap (equal rev, later clock → NOT stale); higher rev (same count → stale + adopt as base); rev-not-rewound (lower list rev, later clock → base kept, not stale); legacy wall-clock fallback (no rev either side → wall-clock still triggers); count-grew → stale. NEUTER reverts BOTH the outer gate and the inner content-stale decision to wall-clock-only → the skew case WRONGLY marks stale → proves the rev-authority gate is load-bearing; asserts the shipped file is byte-identical after. (Trap fixed while writing it: the fetch stub needs a `headers.get()` — its absence threw and aborted the merge before the branch, masking 3 cases.) Adjacent GREEN unchanged: conv_notify_push (38), conv_changed_notify (7), cross_device_reconcile, reconnect_keeplonger_invariant (finding-2 guard, untouched), caseb_server_authoritative_merge — 15 passed together.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; 15 relevant tests pass; bundle → `bundle-b4370053.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A peer/audit finding of the form "local keep-longer overrides backend truth" is sometimes a DELIBERATE, TESTED anti-blanking guard, not a bug — before removing it, read the justifying comment AND grep for a regression test that pins it; if one exists with a biting neuter, the correct move is the BACKEND root-cause fix (kill the race that makes the belt necessary), NOT deleting the belt. For cross-device staleness, prefer the MONOTONIC server `rev` over wall-clock `updatedAt` everywhere (list-merge, body loader, notify) — wall-clock can't survive two-device clock skew; make rev authoritative when comparable and keep wall-clock only as the legacy pre-rev fallback.


### 2026-07-08 — CLOSED the last gap in the empty-bubble fix: the active-conv notify verify now adopts an EQUAL-COUNT trailing turn that grew IN PLACE (not just a new message). `forceRecoverFromServer`'s count-only guard missed it → the exact "partial agent bubble that only fills after several manual refreshes" case. So a trailing assistant turn that GROWS at the SAME message count (fills in / regenerates / continues, or persisted short then extended by the backend task-save) is NOT adopted — the viewing device stays on a stale/empty bubble until a manual refresh. Owner noted the inconsistency: `_recoverOfflineConversations` in the SAME file already handles equal-count via `serverContentLen > localContentLen`, but my notify path routed to the one function that doesn't.
- **Fix (uncommitted, `static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js`).** New `_verifyActiveConvFromServer(convId)` replaces the `forceRecoverFromServer` call in the active-conv debounce timer. It fetches the authoritative server copy (`Api.conversations.get`) and adopts NON-DESTRUCTIVELY, covering BOTH cases: (1) server has MORE messages → adopt the full set; (2) SAME count but the trailing assistant turn is larger in content/thinking/toolRounds → adopt those fields IN PLACE (mirrors the equal-count `serverContentLen > localContentLen` adopt `_recoverOfflineConversations` already does for the offline lane). Contract: keep-longer (`sc >= lc` — never shrink a locally-longer answer, since the two-writer race can make local briefly longer); advance `_serverRev` from the authoritative GET on EVERY outcome (even a no-op, so the frame won't re-verify); re-render ONLY when something actually changed (no scroll reset on a no-op). Never `conv.messages = cache`; never `loadConversationMessages` (its Phase-1 IDB repaint is the original destructive root cause).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_conv_notify_push.py` rewritten, 38 checks, real shipped file under node, timers captured-not-fired; two double-neuters).** Adds the GAP case: an active conv whose local trailing assistant is empty + server has SAME count but LONGER content+thinking + newer rev → verify adopts content & thinking, count unchanged, re-renders. Plus: count-grew full adopt; NO-OP (equal content → GET but no render, rev still advanced); KEEP-LONGER (local longer → not shrunk, not rendered); rev-gate no-GET; self-echo via `_localWriteAt` + caught-in-timer; metadata/unknown → list; background → stale+list no GET; editing/live-stream suppressed; delete; multi-user. NEUTER-A strips both `_localWriteAt` guards → wrongly verifies. NEUTER-B replaces the equal-count adopt branch `if ((sc > lc || st > lt || sr > lr) && sc >= lc)` with `if (false)` → the same-count/longer-content server copy is NOT adopted (bubble stays empty) + not rendered → proves the branch (the fix for the reported symptom) is load-bearing.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; 38/38 harness checks; 9 relevant pytest tests pass (conv_notify_push + conv_changed_notify + cross_device_reconcile); bundle → `bundle-e30227fc.js` (`_verifyActiveConvFromServer` survives esbuild). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh. [PROGRESS: resolved=4 remaining=0]
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `forceRecoverFromServer` adopts ONLY on a strictly-greater MESSAGE COUNT — it does NOT handle a trailing turn that grows IN PLACE at the same count (the fill-in/regenerate/continue/extend case). For a cross-device change signal on the OPEN conv, use an equal-count-aware in-place adopt (content/thinking/toolRounds larger, keep-longer, advance rev even on no-op, render only on change) — mirror the `_recoverOfflineConversations` equal-count branch, don't route to the count-only recover. A rev bumps whenever the messages column changes, INCLUDING an in-place extend of the last turn, so the notify frame fires correctly; the bug was purely the client's adopt guard being count-only.

### 2026-07-08 — FOLLOW-UP to the event-driven sync epic: fixed the "empty agent bubble that needs several refreshes" + "positions keep shifting" reports. Root cause = the notify handler's active-conv reaction was DESTRUCTIVE + missed a two-writer self-echo race. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "Signal is good, but the frontend still shows empty agent bubbles that only fill after several refreshes, and within a conversation the positions keep shifting due to sync delays."
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; full read of the notify handler + loadConversationMessages + syncConversationToServer + the rev writers).** My first cut of `_onConvNotifyPush` reacted to a newer-rev frame on the OPEN conv by calling `loadConversationMessages(convId)`. That function's Phase-1 does `conv.messages = cached.messages` from IndexedDB then a full `renderChat` — so on the ACTIVE conversation it (a) painted the possibly-stale/empty IDB copy = the empty bubble, and (b) reset scroll/positions on every turn. Worse, the rev-gate could NOT neutralize the originating device's own echo because a completed turn has **TWO independent server writers**: the backend `_sync_result_to_conversation` (writes result → rev=A → emits `notify{rev:A}`) AND this device's own `finishStream`→PUT (rev→A+1, advances `_serverRev` only on the PUT RESPONSE). The push frame RACES our PUT; when push wins (usually — it's faster than a separate PUT round-trip), `_serverRev` is still stale at gate-check → `frame.rev > _serverRev` → spurious destructive repaint of the conv we're viewing. Every turn. = "constantly shifting."
- **Fix (uncommitted, 2 seams).**
  1. **`static/js/core/conversations.js`** — on a successful PUT stamp `conv._localWriteAt = Date.now()` (right where we adopt the post-write rev). This is the fast-path marker for "we just wrote this conv locally".
  2. **`static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js` `_onConvNotifyPush`** — the ACTIVE-conv branch is now NON-DESTRUCTIVE + DEBOUNCED + self-echo-aware:
     - SELF-ECHO fast-path: skip a frame within `_CONV_SELF_ECHO_MS` (6s) of our own `_localWriteAt` (catches the two-writer race the rev-gate can't).
     - Active conv, genuinely-newer rev → `clearTimeout` + debounce `_CONV_ACTIVE_VERIFY_DELAY_MS` (1s) so our own PUT lands and advances `_serverRev` first; the timer body then RE-checks the rev-gate (`_pendingRev <= c._serverRev` → silent no-op) AND the `_localWriteAt` window before doing anything. When something is genuinely newer it calls `forceRecoverFromServer(convId)` — the EXISTING non-destructive recover (adopts ONLY if the server has MORE messages, advances `_serverRev`, re-renders ONLY on adopt). It NEVER calls `loadConversationMessages` for the open conv (no Phase-1 cache repaint, no scroll reset).
     - Background conv → unchanged: mark `_needsLoad` + debounced sidebar refresh (next open re-fetches); viewport never touched.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_conv_notify_push.py` rewritten, 24 checks, all green, real shipped file under node; timers CAPTURED not auto-fired so the debounce is driven explicitly).** active→deferred (no synchronous verify) then verify-after-debounce via `forceRecoverFromServer`, NEVER `loadConversationMessages`; rev-gate equal/older no-op; self-echo skipped via `_localWriteAt`; self-echo caught INSIDE the timer when our PUT advances `_serverRev` during the debounce; metadata/unknown → debounced list; background → stale+list no repaint; editing/live-stream suppressed; delete; multi-user gate; DOUBLE-NEUTER strips BOTH `_localWriteAt` guards (top-level `conv.` + timer-body `c.`) → a just-written active conv WRONGLY verifies (guard load-bearing). test_conv_changed_notify (7) + test_frontend_cross_device_reconcile still green.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK (cross_tab_sync.js, conversations.js); 9 relevant tests pass; bundle → `bundle-f2bf2f8e.js` (symbols `_localWriteAt`/`_CONV_SELF_ECHO_MS`/`forceRecoverFromServer`/`_CONV_ACTIVE_VERIFY_DELAY_MS` survive esbuild). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server + hard-refresh.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A cross-device change signal must NEVER trigger a DESTRUCTIVE reload of the conversation the user is VIEWING — `loadConversationMessages`'s Phase-1 replaces `conv.messages` from the IDB cache + full renderChat, which flashes stale/empty content and resets scroll. Use a NON-DESTRUCTIVE adopt-only-if-server-has-more path (`forceRecoverFromServer`) for the open conv. And a rev-gate alone can't kill self-echo when TWO writers touch the same conv per turn (backend task-save + frontend PUT) — the frame can outrun the client's `_serverRev`; add a `_localWriteAt` window + a debounce so the client's own write lands and collapses the frame to a rev-gate no-op.


### 2026-07-08 — Segment-timeline "the three are boxed together" fix: STREAMING per-round prose now renders as INDEPENDENT SIBLINGS of the tool card (in `.ptool-panel-body`, before the card), at PARITY with the settled render — thinking, narration, and each tool are separate blocks, none wrapped in one bordered box. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Screenshot of a mid-stream turn (tofu theme): thinking + narration + a tool call all glued inside ONE bordered box per round. "The three should be completely separated — not enclosed in a single box that frames all three; each tool still separated from the others." Chose OPTION A (keep chronological interleave, kill the shared frame), explicitly rejected de-interleave (Option B), and named the core bug: fix the streaming↔settled divergence.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; full read of BOTH render paths).** The SETTLED render (`renderSegmentTimelineHTML`→`_renderTimelineBatch`, tool_rounds.js) already concatenates `[.seg-thinking][.seg-narration][.ptool-turn card]` as FLAT SIBLINGS in `.ptool-panel-body` — prose was already OUTSIDE the card. The LIVE STREAMING path did NOT match: `_renderStreamRoundProse` (streaming_ui.js:394) inserted the per-round thinking+narration INSIDE the `.ptool-turn` group (above the tool slots), and the incremental translator (`_renderStreamingTranslatePreview`, translation.js:329) inserted the Chinese narration inside the group too. Under tofu, `.ptool-turn` carries a cream border+shadow card — so the live view visibly framed [thinking+narration+tool] as one box = exactly the screenshot. This was the deferred "step 5b" half; the just-shipped interleave got the ADJACENCY right but nested the prose in the card.
- **Fix (uncommitted; 2 JS seams + 2 CSS retargets, ZERO `.seg-*` fork — sibling mrbyt1x8 still owns `.seg-thinking` sizing).**
  1. **streaming_ui.js `_renderStreamRoundProse`** — now inserts `.seg-thinking` (English) + `.stream-seg-en-narration` into `groupEl.parentNode` (the `.ptool-panel-body`) with `body.insertBefore(el, groupEl)`, tagged `data-seg-round`=the group's `data-llm-round` key so each prose block is located idempotently and stays adjacent to its own card. A final ordering pass re-inserts thinking→English-narration→Chinese-narration before the card so order is deterministic regardless of which path (tool-sync vs. translate-push) created a node first. The panel still carries `seg-timeline`, so the settled `.seg-timeline .seg-*` slim CSS applies via the ANCESTOR — inheritance preserved even though the prose moved out of the card.
  2. **translation.js `_renderStreamingTranslatePreview`** — routes each round's Chinese `.stream-seg-narration` into `group.parentNode` (panel body) before the group, `data-seg-round`-tagged, mirroring #1. Same graceful-degrade (round with no `.ptool-turn` yet → blob fallback), same blob-exclusion of routed rounds.
  3. **styles.css** — retargeted `.ptool-turn > .stream-seg-narration` → `.ptool-panel-body > .stream-seg-narration` (rhythm rules) and `[data-xlate="1"] .ptool-turn > .stream-seg-en-narration` → `.ptool-panel-body > .stream-seg-en-narration` (hide English while auto-translate live). No `.seg-*` sizing touched.
- **Parity guarantee.** Finalize is a visual no-op by construction: the settled `_renderTimelineBatch` already emits prose as panel-body siblings, and streaming now produces the identical DOM shape (prose sibling, before card, in panel body, under the `seg-timeline` ancestor). No de-interleave — chronological thinking→narration→its-tool order kept per round.
- **Tests (all driven on the REAL shipped JS via jsdom, double-neuter each; 23/23 green in the 3 suites).**
  - `test_frontend_streaming_interleave.py` Part B REWRITTEN (`test_streaming_interleave_renders_prose_as_sibling_of_card`, min_pass 15→18): drives REAL `_syncToolRoundsDOM`; asserts each round's `.seg-thinking`/`.seg-narration` is a `:scope > *[data-seg-round]` child of `.ptool-panel-body`, `!th0.closest('.ptool-turn')` (NOT nested), parent IS the panel body, `.seg-timeline` ancestor still resolves, and interleave order thinking(L0)→narr(L0)→card(L0)→…(L1). NEUTER: flag OFF → no `[data-seg-round]` prose nodes.
  - `test_frontend_streaming_translate_unified.py` interleave test flipped: Chinese `.stream-seg-narration` is a panel-body sibling (`data-seg-round`), `!closest('.ptool-turn')`, above its card; NEUTER (drop byRound) still bites.
  - `test_frontend_segment_timeline.py` NEW jsdom pair (`test_settled_prose_is_sibling_not_nested_in_tool_card` + `test_NC_settled_nesting_prose_in_card_bites`): parses REAL `renderSegmentTimelineHTML` output (with a `_renderToolGroupsHTML` that emits real `.ptool-turn` cards) → asserts NO `.seg-*` node is a descendant of ANY `.ptool-turn`. NEUTER wraps the batch output in a `.ptool-turn` → the non-nesting assertion FAILS (has teeth).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK on both edited JS; tinycss2 0 errors + braces balanced; 3 target suites 23/23; broader `-k "frontend and (stream|segment|translate|tool|render|sse)"` = 107 passed, the 2 failures (test_frontend_presence, test_frontend_mobile_client_entry) are PRE-EXISTING, reference NONE of my files (sibling-owned presence harness / main.js+index.html mid-edit). Bundles rebuilt → core JS `bundle-eebe7481.js`, feature `feature-ea939983.js`, CSS `styles-36b115fb.css`; `data-seg-round` + `stream-seg-narration` survive minification (grep-confirmed in core bundle), CSS selector present. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a live-streaming render and its settled counterpart must look byte-identical, the DOM SHAPE (not just class names) has to match: the settled path put prose as a SIBLING of the tool card in the panel body, so the streaming path swallowing it INTO the card was the whole "boxed together" bug — parity means same parent, same sibling order, same ancestor for CSS inheritance. Tag interleaved siblings with a stable key (`data-seg-round`=llmRound) so idempotent lookups don't depend on DOM position, and the `.seg-timeline` slim CSS still applies via the panel ancestor even after the prose leaves the card (zero fork of the sibling-owned `.seg-*` rules).


### 2026-07-08 — Cross-device conversation sync is now EVENT-DRIVEN (server `notify` push), not poll-only: a sibling device reconciles the instant a change lands, no manual refresh. Rev-gated targeted merge; polling demoted to a WS-down fallback. Uncommitted for owner sign-off. (board epic pt_063c2278f1eb492d)
- **Ask (owner).** "Our project currently requires a manual refresh to sync — rework this mechanism." Owner then ratified: Option A (event-driven `notify` push, poll demoted-but-kept as WS-down fallback); use the ALREADY-LANDED `rev` (not an `updatedAt` tiebreaker); emit from the single DB-write seam covering rename/delete/folder/edit — not just task-completion; targeted per-conv merge not a full list re-pull; make self-echo a cheap no-op; scope for multi-user (D4) forward-safety.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; full read of the sync pipeline).** Conversation-list sync was PULL-only: same-machine `BroadcastChannel`, `visibilitychange` refocus, a 25s `_crossDeviceReconcile` poll, and `_startOfflineRecoveryPolling` (no-op unless `server_offline`). NOTHING pushed a conversation-change signal to clients — confirmed `push_event` was only called by `update.py`/webhooks; the `notify` channel existed in `lib/agent_core/push.py` (documented) but had ZERO publishers. So a device caught a sibling's change only on refocus or the next 25s tick, and never while mid-stream / editing / backgrounded = "needs a manual refresh."
- **Key architecture finding (the elegant single seam).** EVERY authoritative conversation mutation already funnels through `invalidate_meta_cache(user_id)` (lib/conversations/meta_cache.py) — save/PUT/rename/delete/folder/settings/message-edit + task-save/autopilot/queue. It is ALREADY user-keyed (Epic D4) and ALREADY publishes on the shared push_bus (inproc→local, redis→fan-out). So the real-time signal is a near-free add ON TOP of it. Also confirmed: the DB `rev` trigger bumps ONLY on a `messages` change (IS DISTINCT FROM) — so rename/folder/settings/activeTaskId do NOT move rev. That shaped the two-mode frame.
- **Fix (uncommitted; 1 new seam + wiring at ~13 call sites + frontend handler + 3 test files).**
  1. **Server emit seam** — new `notify_conv_changed(conv_id, *, rev=None, deleted=False, user_id=DEFAULT_USER_ID)` in meta_cache.py: calls `invalidate_meta_cache(user_id)` (unchanged) THEN best-effort `push_event('notify', conv_id, {type, convId, rev?, userId})`. Frame is a targeting HINT, not the data. `rev=None` → omit rev (metadata-only). Fail-open (a push error never breaks the mutation; try/except-wrapped). Re-exported via `lib/conversations/__init__.py` + `routes/common.py` as `_notify_conv_changed`.
  2. **Wired the named seams** to carry the RIGHT scope: content changes carry the post-write `rev` (save_conv PUT, delete_message, patch_msg, patch_msg_id, manager `_sync_result_to_conversation`); metadata-only pass `rev=None` (rename, generate-title, settings/folder PATCH, chat send/regen/continue activeTaskId, autopilot next-task, queue dispatch); delete passes `deleted=True` (only after the commit succeeds — `_deleted_committed` flag). Bulk startup-recovery invalidate left as plain `invalidate_meta_cache` (no single conv).
  3. **Frontend handler** `_onConvNotifyPush` (static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js): rev-GATE — a `conv_changed` whose `rev <= conv._serverRev` is a NO-OP (this is what makes the ORIGINATING device's own echo free — it already advanced `_serverRev` from its PUT/GET response). A strictly-newer rev → TARGETED `loadConversationMessages(convId)` for the ACTIVE conv (mark `_needsLoad`, route through the existing keep-longer/count-drop guards = ADD/UPDATE only); a background conv → mark stale + debounced list refresh. Metadata-only (no rev) or unknown conv → ONE debounced `loadConversationsFromServer()` (so a busy conv can't spam the list endpoint). `conv_deleted` → shared `_applyRemoteConvDeleted` (extracted from the BroadcastChannel path so both remote-delete lanes share it). Multi-user gate: drop a frame whose `userId !== window._currentUserId` (absent today = single-user = every frame ours) — D4 forward-safe. Never disturbs a conv with a live stream or mid-edit (its own SSE/poll lifecycle owns it).
  4. **Poll demoted to fallback** — `_crossDeviceReconcile` now runs on a SELF-RESCHEDULING `setTimeout` at `_reconcileIntervalMs()`: 90s when `pushIsConnected()` (push carries the load), 25s when the WS is DOWN (poll is the only path — prior default). Recursive setTimeout (not fixed setInterval) so the fallback tightens the instant the socket drops and relaxes on recovery. Idle guard + `_bootLoadInFlight` latch UNCHANGED (memory invariants preserved).
  5. **Wiring** — `_wireConvSyncPush()` (idempotent) does the `pushSubscribe('notify','*', …)`; called from main.js boot, NOT at cross_tab_sync.js IIFE load (that file is bundled BEFORE push.js → `pushSubscribe` undefined at load time).
- **Tests (double-neuter each; all green).** `tests/test_conv_changed_notify.py` (7): frame shape per mutate kind (content→rev, metadata→no rev, delete→conv_deleted, userId forwarded, non-int rev dropped-not-crashed), NC = plain `invalidate_meta_cache` emits NOTHING (proves the frame is what carries the signal), fail-open on push error. `tests/test_frontend_conv_notify_push.py` (24 PASS, real shipped cross_tab_sync.js under node): newer rev→targeted body refetch; self-echo/stale rev→no-op; metadata→debounced list; unknown conv→list; background→stale+list; editing/live-stream→suppressed; delete→removed; multi-user gate; NC strips the rev-gate → a stale rev WRONGLY refetches (gate is load-bearing). Integration smoke against the REAL hub confirms `('notify','conv_changed',9)` etc. Also fixed a PRE-EXISTING harness gap in `test_frontend_cross_device_reconcile.py` (it never stubbed `Api`/`AbortSignal` for the stale-pin sweep → `Api is not defined`; the JOURNAL's known-failing cross_device_reconcile) — added the stubs, now green.
- **Verify.** py ast-parse OK (8 files); `node --check` OK (cross_tab_sync.js, main.js); new symbols survive esbuild minification (grep-confirmed in `bundle-02821ee1.js`: `_onConvNotifyPush`, `_wireConvSyncPush`, `_applyRemoteConvDeleted`); 32 relevant tests pass. Byte-identical single-box: `notify_conv_changed` under the inproc bus == `invalidate_meta_cache` + one local `push_event` (no new dependency). To PROVE the 6 `no such table: conversations` failures in test_conv_rev_monotonic/test_api_integration were pre-existing (sandbox DB not provisioned), I reverted ALL backend edits to the committed tree and re-ran → failed IDENTICALLY → then re-applied every edit (13 route/lib call sites + import + seam). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The elegant place to add a cross-cutting real-time signal is the ONE seam every mutation already funnels through (`invalidate_meta_cache`) — don't scatter `push_event` across N routes. The DB `rev` trigger bumps ONLY on a messages change, so a change signal needs TWO modes: content (carry rev → rev-gated targeted body refetch) and metadata (omit rev → debounced sidebar refresh). The rev-gate is what makes self-echo free (the originator already advanced `_serverRev`) — no separate "is this my own change?" bookkeeping needed. A push-fed real-time path should DEMOTE, not delete, the poll — keep it as the WS-down fallback and stretch its cadence when the socket is up. Bundled-BEFORE-push.js files can't `pushSubscribe` at IIFE load; wire from main.js boot.


### 2026-07-08 — REMOVED the orphaned-user-turn "继续回答 / Resume" affordance entirely (owner: "if all else fails, just remove it"). Kept the load-bearing no-auto-fire invariant intact. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Screenshot of the bottom-of-transcript banner "这条消息还没有回复 · 继续回答". Owner: "feels strange it appears"; then, after I laid out the options (A remove / B fold-into-provenance-strip + tighten the 24h window), owner chose **A — remove it**.
- **What it was.** The orphan-resumable affordance ("patch→fundamental-fix #2"): the backend GET-path classifier `classify_orphan_resumable` (lib/conversations/reconcile.py) stamped `conv._orphanResumable` when the AUTHORITATIVE reconciled tail was an unanswered user turn (no live task, <24h, non-image-gen); the frontend rendered an explicit Resume button that flowed through the normal user-initiated `startAssistantResponse`. It had itself REPLACED the old dangerous Case-E `age<5min` auto-fire (which minted a billed turn from a client-side inference and could double-answer).
- **The load-bearing distinction (why this wasn't a trivial delete).** Removing the *button* must NOT reopen the Case-E auto-fire. The button and the auto-fire are DIFFERENT things: the button was an explicit, human-clicked affordance; the auto-fire was an inference-driven billed dispatch. Removal = "no button, and still no auto-answer." The invariant that guards this — `initActiveTasks` calls `startAssistantResponse` ZERO times — is unchanged and still tested.
- **Removal (verify-then-write; full cross-reference sweep first, 7 seams).**
  1. `lib/conversations/reconcile.py` — deleted `classify_orphan_resumable`, its `ORPHAN_RESUMABLE_MAX_AGE_MS` policy constant, and the `_last_real_turn` helper (only that classifier used it); dropped both from `__all__`; updated the module docstring (frontend no longer "auto-starts an orphaned user turn"). `reconcile_conversation_messages` (the ghost sweep/tail classifier) is UNTOUCHED — import surface now `['is_buried_empty_ghost','classify_ghost_tail','reconcile_conversation_messages']`.
  2. `routes/conversations.py` — deleted `_attach_orphan_marker` + both GET-path call sites (changed + unchanged branches). `time` still used elsewhere (kept).
  3. `static/js/ui/chat_render.js` — deleted `_orphanResumeAffordanceHtml` / `_syncOrphanResumeAffordance` / `_resumeOrphanTurn` + both `_syncOrphanResumeAffordance(conv)` call sites (lazy-render + full-render paths).
  4. `static/js/core/conversations.js` — deleted the `conv._orphanResumable = data._orphanResumable || null` assignment (the marker no longer arrives from the server).
  5. `static/js/i18n.js` — deleted `orphanResume.label` / `orphanResume.hint`.
  6. `static/styles.css` — deleted the `.orphan-resume` / `.orphan-resume-hint` / `.orphan-resume-btn` block (+ the two `[data-theme="tofu"]` variants).
  7. `static/js/main/main_init_tasks.js` — refreshed the two Case-E comments (no more affordance/classifier reference; the invariant text stays: no auto-dispatch, orphan left unanswered until re-send).
- **Tests.** Deleted the two now-obsolete suites: `test_orphan_resumable_classifier.py` (classifier gone) and `test_frontend_orphan_resume_btn_class.py` (button gone). KEPT + refreshed `test_frontend_casee_no_autostart_after_ghost_delete.py` — it guards the surviving invariant (drives the REAL `initActiveTasks` under node, asserts `startAssistantResponse` called 0×, with a double-neuter that re-injects an auto-fire and proves the guard bites); only its stale comments (which referenced the removed classifier/affordance) were updated. Also dropped the now-dead `_syncOrphanResumeAffordance` noop stub from three render harnesses (autopilot_flat_render / autopilot_report_affordance / full_render_scroll_anchor).
- **Verify.** `py_compile` OK (reconcile/conversations/casee test); reconcile import surface confirmed; `node --check` OK on all 4 edited JS files; tinycss2 0 errors + braces balanced. Tests: casee no-autostart 2/2, reconcile JS↔backend equivalence 5/5, the 3 adjacent render suites 8/8 — all green. Rebuilt bundles → JS `bundle-d393aa2a.js`, CSS `styles-e0074854.css`; grep-confirmed ZERO `orphanResume`/`orphan-resume`/`_resumeOrphanTurn`/`_syncOrphanResumeAffordance` survive in either. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When removing a feature that was itself a REPLACEMENT for a dangerous mechanism, separate the affordance from the invariant: delete the UI + its backend marker, but KEEP the test that proves the dangerous predecessor (here: the Case-E `age<5min` billed auto-fire) has not returned. A feature can be "not good enough" and removable while the safety property it embodied must stay enforced. Sweep ALL seams before editing (backend classifier + route stamp + 3 frontend files + CSS + i18n + tests) — a stamped-but-never-read marker or an orphan noop stub is silent debt.

- **Ask (owner).** "Project bar still ugly; when can the background change (pool/sky/…)?" Diagnosis confirmed: the meadow/pool/sky/off swap ALREADY existed but was reachable ONLY via the pet's `contextmenu` handler (`tofu-pet.js:402` → `cycleDecor()`) — a 30px roaming character you must right-click = undiscoverable, which is why the owner didn't know backgrounds could change. Called from the EXISTING `_applyDecor()` — since `setDecor`/`cycleDecor` both route through `_applyDecor`, the button reflects state through the ONE path (no new state mechanism, reuses the persisted `tofu_bar_scene` key). Exposed `SCENE_LABELS` on `window.TofuPet`.

Static markup → NO `_BUNDLE_FILES` change needed (confirmed: only top-level `static/js/*.js` files go in the manifest; index.html is served/rewritten directly). ALSO replaced the raw `✕` close glyph (`project-bar-close`) with an inline SVG (CLAUDE.md §3.4 bans glyph controls).

Button inherits the existing tofu `.project-bar-btn` SNES-3D styling automatically.

- **Verify.** `node --check tofu-pet.js` OK; 19/19 pet tests pass; tinycss2 0 errors + braces balanced; bundles rebuilt → core JS `bundle-50526a55.js` (new `SCENE_LABELS` + `scene-switch-label` survive minification, grep-confirmed), CSS `styles-ebb7d9ca.css`. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A feature reachable only via a hidden gesture (right-click a roaming 30px pet) is effectively invisible — the "it doesn't exist" complaint was really "I can't find it." When adding a UI mirror of existing state, sync it through the SINGLE existing state path (`_applyDecor`) and expose only labels, never a parallel toggle — a NEUTER test on that one call proves there's no second source of truth. ### 2026-07-08 — Project-bar diorama REDESIGN: replaced the raster clip-art grass/wave/cloud strips with seamless FLAT-VECTOR SVG scenes in the muted tofu palette. The bar no longer looks like vocational-college clip-art. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.

Research (CSS-Tricks jagged/SVG-mask edges, svgbackgrounds.com "3 ways SVG can help websites look less blocky", GetIllustrations flat-design principles) converged on the pro fix: seamless flat-vector SVG in a tonal palette.

SEAMLESS by construction: every quadratic/cubic bump returns to the baseline so tile-end `(120,y)` meets tile-start `(0,y)` with no seam (no raster repeat artifact). Two-tone bands per scene in the tofu palette — meadow sage `#B7CBA8`/`#8FAE7B` + sparse blades + two daisies (`#FBF7EE` petals, `#E0A867` center); pool dusty-teal `#AFCDC8`/`#83B0AB` + foam line `#EAF3EF`; sky warm cloud `#EAE2D2`/`#FBF9F3`. Resolution-independent (crisp at any DPR).
  2. **CSS (`static/styles.css`, tofu-scoped).** `--bar-scene`/`--bar-edge` vars repointed `.png`→`.svg` for all three `[data-decor]` worlds. `::after` ground: `background-size:120px 100%` (was `auto 100%`), opacity `.92`→full (the SVG is already muted so it doesn't shout), height `20px`→`17px`. `::before` edge: GENTLED — `top:-14px`→`-6px`, height `22px`→`14px`, `left/right:6px`→`8px`, softer drop-shadow — a restrained silhouette that breaks the neat rectangle without a busy fringe. `clip-path` rounded-inset on `::after` kept (bar is `overflow:visible` so the edge can poke).
  3. **tofu-pet.js** — docstring scene-asset comment `.png`→`.svg` (pet expression/walk frames STAY PNG; only the scenery changed).
  4. **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_tofu_pet.py`, 16, all green).** `test_decor_scene_assets_exist` now requires `scene-<s>.svg` + `edge-<s>.svg`; `test_decor_css_wires_every_scene` asserts `scene-<s>.svg`/`edge-<s>.svg` referenced + the refined `top:-6px` poke. Temp mocks cleaned. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time CSS bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Seamless horizontal SVG tiling needs the band's start/end y-values to MATCH — build every bump as a `q`/`c` that returns to the baseline so `repeat-x` shows no seam (raster strips can't do this without hand-painting the wrap). For decorative scenery on a warm-cream card, pick a MUTED tonal palette from the card's own family (sage/dusty-teal/warm-cloud), not saturated clip-art color — the loudness, the seam, and the raster fuzz were the three things reading as "amateur." Verified empirically: esbuild in SCRIPT mode (no import/export → script mode) does NOT rename top-level `var`/`function`/`const`; a controlled sample kept `loadConversation`/`closeSettings`/`renderChat`/`pushSubscribe` AND an unused-but-global fn (no tree-shaking); only function-LOCAL params mangled. NOT added to bootstrap.py (its LLM-repair only fires on a crash; missing node = no error = nothing to repair). node_modules/ already gitignored (.gitignore:91). ANSWER to owner's "one-time?": YES — `npm ci` populates node_modules/ once, persists across restarts, server.py never re-runs it.

Files: lib/js_bundler.py, tests/test_js_minify.py, tests/test_bundle_corruption_guard.py, package.json, package-lock.json, install.sh, docs/JS_BUNDLING_RATIONALE.md §5d. Uncommitted for owner sign-off. [PROGRESS: resolved=5 remaining=0]

### 2026-07-08 — Android client (rangehow/tofu-android) blank-screen ROOT-CAUSE fixed + diagnostics removed + pull-to-refresh. Also FILING a known chatui follow-up: the multi-stream boot-reconnect storm.
- **Context.** Built a thin native Kotlin WebView shell (separate repo `rangehow/tofu-android`, CI-built + published as a debug-signed `android-preview` release; in-app "Get App" button + Settings-footer entry both resolve a direct APK deep link served from `routes/common.py` `mobile_client_url`). After it shipped, the app showed a **blank cream screen** on the tablet while the SAME URL rendered fine in the tablet's Chrome.
- **Blank-screen ROOT CAUSE (verified via an on-screen probe walking the height-chain).** `window.innerHeight=799` was correct, but CSS `html{height:100%}` / `body{height:100dvh}` both resolved to **0** in this Android WebView (initial containing block measured indefinite-height) → the whole `.main → .chat-wrapper → #chatContainer` flex chain collapsed to `height:0` → nothing painted. Desktop Chrome resolves the %/dvh correctly; the WebView does not. The only constant across both blank sessions (837px drawer + 1280px non-drawer) was `pointer:coarse` (i.e. the WebView), NOT login/network/bundle/crash/drawer.
- **Fix (chatui, `static/js/main.js`, uncommitted-staged for owner sign-off).** `_installViewportHeightGuard()` pins `html`/`body` height to the known-good `window.innerHeight` in px (sidestepping broken %/dvh), re-applied on rAF + resize + orientationchange, installed FIRST in the boot IIFE. JS-only → applies on reload, no APK rebuild. (An earlier tablet-drawer CSS `overflow:hidden` re-assert in `styles.css` was necessary-but-insufficient — the real collapse was higher in the chain.)
- **Also this session:** removed the on-screen "Logs" diagnostic overlay + PROBE layout probe from the app now that the cause is found (kept renderer-death recovery, reauth-on-401, JS-console→logcat, chrome://inspect); added **pull-to-refresh** (`SwipeRefreshLayout` around the WebView, armed only at scroll-top) as the one genuine robustness gap (recovery from a bad page state without force-killing); committed a fixed debug keystore so CI builds share one signature (installs upgrade cleanly, no uninstall).
- **★ KNOWN FOLLOW-UP (do NOT fix casually — needs its own session + double-neuter tests).** Every app boot logs `⚠️ MULTI-TASK RECONNECT: reconnecting N tasks simultaneously — elevated cross-talk risk!` (observed N=6): on load the frontend reconnects the SSE stream for ALL conversations that were mid-stream, at once. Real battery/CPU/network drain on a tablet, and its own log text flags cross-talk risk. This is **chatui-side SSE state code** (`initActiveTasks` / `connectToTask`, `static/js/…`) affecting desktop too — NOT an Android-app issue. Proper fix (likely: reconnect only the VISIBLE/active conversation on boot, lazily reconnect others on switch) is delicate state-consistency work and MUST land with double-neuter tests proving no regression to the multi-conversation resume path. Filed here so it isn't lost; code left untouched this turn.


### 2026-07-08 — Segment-timeline STREAMING interleave (epic pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5, step 5b) DONE: the LIVE streaming path now interleaves per-round thinking+narration adjacent to its tools (was LOST on every delta_reset), the legacy bottom translate-preview no longer fights the timeline, and the root-cause fingerprint-precision bug it exposed is fixed. Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Screenshot of a mid-stream turn: thinking content is being lost and the bottom content is incomplete because the streaming path never got the step-5b interleave (each tool call had thinking, but the front-end never rendered it interleaved). Also: during generation, if auto-translate fires the styling is disrupted, and on pause the `translate-preview` block reappears — it "should not exist standalone when following the inline tool timeline." Owner decision: OPTION 1 — fix the root cause, full streaming interleave now, NO "capture-but-hold-the-render" half-state (streaming and settled must look byte-identical). Claim board epic pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write, full source read of the render pipeline).** The SETTLED/DB render already interleaves via `renderSegmentTimelineHTML` (ui/tool_rounds.js, reads `msg.segments`; flag `_segTimelineEnabled()` DEFAULT ON). The LIVE path was explicitly DEFERRED (design doc §5 "step 5b", the "highest-risk half"): `updateStreamingUI` paints THREE flat global zones (all tools / one thinking accumulator / one content accumulator). On every tool round the backend emits `DELTA_RESET` and the frontend (sse_pipeline.js ~910) BLINDLY did `content=""; thinking=""` — so round N's reasoning+narration vanished live the instant round N+1 started (it only reappeared at finalize when segments re-derived it). The per-round prose IS preserved backend-side (`tool_dispatch.py:726-730` stamps `round_entry.thinking`/`assistantContent` before `_discard_pretool_prose` zeroes the accumulators), and `assemble_segments` puts it on the FIRST entry of each llmRound batch — so the fix is to make the LIVE view stamp+render the same shape.
- **Fix (uncommitted, 4 seams + 1 root-cause).**
  1. **Part A — capture on delta_reset** (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`): BEFORE zeroing the accumulators, stamp the closing llmRound's `content`(→`assistantContent`)+`thinking` onto that batch's FIRST `toolRounds` entry (matched by `ev.round === llmRound`; fallback = last round). Exactly where `assemble_segments` puts it → finalize is a visual no-op. Backend stays SoT: the terminal `committedMessage` overwrites with the authoritative copy.
  2. **Part B — render inside the group** (`static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`): new `_renderStreamRoundProse(groupEl, round)` renders each round's `.seg-thinking` (collapsed disclosure) + `.seg-narration` (English) INSIDE its `.ptool-turn`, ABOVE the tool slots (thinking→narration→tools order, the settled `_renderTimelineBatch` mirror). The live panel now carries the `seg-timeline` class so the SETTLED `.seg-timeline .seg-*` CSS applies VERBATIM — **ZERO CSS fork** (honors owner constraint #1; coordinated a peer note + path-lease with sibling mrbyt1x8 who owns `.seg-thinking` sizing). English narration uses a `stream-seg-en-narration` marker so it never collides with the translator's `.stream-seg-narration` (Chinese). Idempotent (keyed on last-rendered text).
  3. **Part C — kill the standalone translate-preview** (`chat_render.js` + `translation.js`): when the timeline renders (`_segTimelineRendered`), suppress the bottom `.translate-preview` block AND stamp `data-seg-timeline="1"` on the loading shell so the in-place poll patch (`_patchTranslateLoadingDom`) also skips re-creating it. This is the block that "reappeared on pause" — proven cleared by the neuter (flag OFF → it reappears).
  4. **CSS (`static/styles.css`, one streaming-scoped rule)**: `[data-xlate="1"] .ptool-turn > .stream-seg-en-narration{display:none}` — hide the English per-round narration while auto-translate is live (translator paints the Chinese into `.stream-seg-narration` in the same group). No touch to `.seg-thinking` sizing (sibling's).
  5. **ROOT CAUSE the interleave exposed** (`streaming_ui.js`): `_syncToolRoundsDOM`'s change-detect fingerprint was a running `_fp = _fp * 31 + x` FLOAT that OVERFLOWS 2^53 within a single round (the live repro showed fpAfter≈1.3e33 ≈ 2^110). A LATE small field change (the prose length Part A stamps onto an already-rendered round) then rounds away → colliding hash → the gate silently bails → captured narration never paints (this is why the final round's prose was dropped in the repro). Fixed all 25 accumulation steps to `Math.imul(_fp, 31)` (32-bit exact). This latently also dropped late `compactionLayer`/swarm/`_hgTranslating` changes on long turns — now fixed for all of them.
- **Reproduction (driven, not asserted).** A standalone node+jsdom repro plays a realistic 3-round SSE sequence (thinking→narration→tool per round, then a terminal no-tool deliverable) through the REAL `dispatchSSEEvent` + REAL `_syncToolRoundsDOM`, then dumps the live `#streaming-body` DOM. VERDICT after fix: `[L0]` and `[L1]` each show their own thinking+narration adjacent to their tool (`thinkingAboveTool=true`), no cross-talk, `bottom .translate-preview: 0`, terminal answer intact. Before the Math.imul fix, `[L1]` (the last round) rendered EMPTY — that regression is what surfaced the fingerprint bug.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_streaming_interleave.py`, 4 tests, JSDOM, all green, double-neuter each).** Part A (real dispatchSSEEvent: round-0 prose survives round-1 start + no crosstalk; NC wipes the captured fields → prose gone). Part B (real `_syncToolRoundsDOM`: per-round `.seg-thinking`/`.seg-narration` land inside their group above the tool, reuse the settled classes, thinking-before-narration; NC flag OFF → no prose nodes + no `seg-timeline` class). Part C (real `renderMessage`: flag ON → no bottom `.translate-preview` + loading shell stamped `data-seg-timeline`; NC flag OFF → the preview REAPPEARS). Part D (fingerprint precision: a last-round late stamp changes the `Math.imul` fingerprint + stays a safe integer; NC patches `Math.imul`→`*` → the same stamp COLLIDES and safe-integer is lost). All 4 neuters bite.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK on all edited JS; tinycss2 0 errors, braces balanced. New suite 4/4; adjacent suites GREEN unchanged: streaming_translate_unified (2), segment_timeline (14), sse_dispatch characterization (82 checks), rendermessage_segment_gate (13). Full `-k frontend` run: 407 passed; the 7 failures (autopilot_queue_badge, cross_device_reconcile, presence, review_venue_race, sidebar_settled_facts×2, typecheck) are PRE-EXISTING — they reference NONE of my 5 changed files and fail identically on the clean tree (they exercise sibling-owned image-gen.js/main.js/presence/sidebar mid-edit). JS bundle → `bundle-9f778045.js`, CSS → `styles-ba34e0b1.css`; all new symbols survive minification (grep-confirmed). NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A running `_fp = _fp * 31 + x` fingerprint OVERFLOWS 2^53 within one tool round — late small deltas silently round away and the change-detect gate bails; use `Math.imul(acc, k)` for any incremental 32-bit hash so every field registers. (2) The streaming and settled renders must reuse the SAME classes: adding the `seg-timeline` class to the live panel activates the settled `.seg-timeline .seg-*` CSS verbatim → zero fork, and finalize is a visual no-op by construction. (3) When two renderers can write the same interleave slot (English narration vs. live Chinese translation), give each a distinct marker class (`stream-seg-en-narration` vs `.stream-seg-narration`) and gate visibility on `data-xlate` — never let them fight for one node.

### 2026-07-08 — Root-caused the "Autopilot 启动中… frozen after every hard refresh" ghost: a transient `_streamingVu` VU placeholder was leaking into the IndexedDB cache. Stopped caching it (write side) + filter it out on cache load (read side). Uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Screenshot: an "Autopilot 启动中…" bubble WITH full message actions (Copy/Edit/Regen/Translate/delete) + a timestamp — sitting there frozen after a hard refresh ("there was already content, and it should be streaming"). Autopilot's sync feels different from Agent's; hard refreshes make history display unstable. Optimize.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; full source read of the VU lifecycle + cache).** The screenshot bubble has ACTIONS + a timestamp → it's a FINALIZED `renderMessage` bubble, NOT the live `#streaming-msg` (which carries no actions). Its body is the `_streamingVu` warm-up pulse (chat_render.js:942, `msg._isVirtualUser && msg._streamingVu && !msg.content`). Chain, all confirmed in code: (1) backend `maybe_run_autopilot` emits `autopilot_vu_start` IN-MEMORY ONLY — a VU turn is persisted to the DB EXCLUSIVELY on `autopilot_vu_done`, which deletes `_streamingVu` first (autopilot.py:1683-1706, 1795). (2) frontend `_beginVuStreaming` pushes `{role:'user', content:'', _isVirtualUser:true, _streamingVu:true, _msgId:vuMsgId}` then calls `ConvCache.put(conv)` (streaming_render.js:203). (3) `idb-cache.js::_stripMessage` did NOT drop `_streamingVu` → the transient placeholder was written to IndexedDB. (4) hard refresh → `loadConversationMessages` Phase-1 cache hit restores it and `renderChat` draws it as a STATIC actioned bubble = the "启动中…" ghost. (5) the `autopilot_vu_start` SSE replay then EARLY-RETURNS (`if (_findVuMsgById(conv, vuMsgId)) return;` streaming_render.js:196) because it finds the cached ghost → never stands up a fresh live `#streaming-msg` → frozen forever. Phase-2 server GET can't correct it: on cache hit `hasLocalData` is true → NOOP/MERGE, never OVERWRITE. Same "don't persist an unsettled placeholder" principle as the ghost-tail sweep, but for the VU lane (which is explicitly EXCLUDED from that sweep, so nothing was cleaning it).
- **Fix (uncommitted, 2 seams).**
  1. WRITE side — `static/js/idb-cache.js::put()`: filter `_streamingVu` messages out of `conv.messages` before building `msgOrder` (`var msgs = conv.messages.filter(m => !(m && m._streamingVu))`), and `if (msgs.length === 0) return;` so a conv that is ONLY a ghost writes nothing. The cache now agrees with the server (which never has the placeholder).
  2. READ side — `static/js/core/conversations.js::loadConversationMessages` Phase-1: filter `_streamingVu` out of a cache hit (`conv.messages = cached.messages.filter(...)`) so a PRE-FIX cached ghost is dropped on load; the reconnect replay then re-creates a live bubble (or `autopilot_vu_done` supplies the settled one). Belt for already-poisoned caches.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_vu_ghost_not_cached.py` (2, green): a capturing fake-IDB harness runs the REAL shipped `idb-cache.js` → asserts a put() of a conv whose tail is a `_streamingVu` VU placeholder persists msgOrder with ONLY the real msgs (ghost absent, count=2, no ghost body row); NEUTER (revert the filter on a COPY) → ghost IS written → proves the filter is load-bearing (shipped file left byte-identical). Existing suites still green: `test_frontend_idb_put_onabort` (2), `test_frontend_autopilot_vu_verbatim` (2), `test_frontend_autopilot_warmup` (3).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK both files; 7+2 = 9 relevant tests pass (PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 — an unrelated napari/vispy pytest-plugin crashes collection otherwise). Rebuilt bundle → `bundle-9f778045.js` (7 `_streamingVu` refs present). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A bubble WITH message actions + timestamp is a FINALIZED render, never the live `#streaming-msg` — so a "frozen streaming state" after refresh means a transient placeholder got PERSISTED, not that a stream stalled. Any in-memory-only, backend-unpersisted placeholder (`_streamingVu`, and by analogy any `_streaming*`/warm-up flag) must be filtered at BOTH cache seams (write in `_stripMessage`/`put`, read in the Phase-1 cache-hit), because the server GET can't correct a cache hit (NOOP/MERGE, not OVERWRITE). The `_findVuMsgById` reuse-guard turns a cached ghost into a permanent freeze by suppressing the live re-create — reconnect idempotence guards assume the matched slot is LIVE, so never let a settled/persisted copy of a streaming-only object exist.


### 2026-07-08 — RESEARCH follow-up (no feature code wired): MEASURED whether adding a `node` dependency is worth it for the JS bundler. Only reachable win on the current global/IIFE code is stronger minification (tree-shaking/scope-hoisting/manifest-retirement are ALL ESM-gated). Verdict = QUALIFIED GO for an OPTIONAL fail-open esbuild enhancer; extended docs/JS_BUNDLING_RATIONALE.md §5.
- **Ask (owner).** node is fine operationally (bootstrap.py conda-PG pattern is a clean template; npm ci is one-time) IF there's a real benefit. Decide against a pre-stated threshold: ≥15% additional gzip over `_minify_js` → go; <8% → no; 8–15% → argued judgment. Measure don't estimate; if esbuild can't install in sandbox, report blocked. Persist analysis; don't wire in — bring the number + go/no-go first.
- **Decisive fact (owner-confirmed).** `static/js` has ZERO `export`/`import from` — all `window.*`/IIFE, load order in the hand-ordered `_BUNDLE_FILES`. So tree-shaking / scope-hoisting / retiring the manual manifest are ALL gated behind an ESM rewrite of ~105 files. Adding node buys NONE of those on current code. Only reachable win = identifier-mangling minification (esbuild/terser work on globals; `_minify_js` only strips comments/whitespace).
- **Measured (node v24 / esbuild 0.28.1 / terser 5.48.0; installed to a temp dir, no repo pollution; all 3 passed `node --check`; temp cleaned).** Baseline = current on-disk `bundle-502911e9.js` (already `_minify_js`'d), 1,868,722 B raw / **466,074 B gzip-6** / 350,482 B brotli-11. esbuild `--minify`: 1,511,175 raw / **411,158 gzip-6** / 315,419 brotli → **−19.1% raw / −11.8% gzip / −10.0% brotli**. terser `-c -m`: 1,438,303 raw / **398,481 gzip-6** / 301,809 brotli → **−23.0% raw / −14.5% gzip / −13.9% brotli**.
- **Verdict — QUALIFIED GO (optional enhancer, esbuild), NOT wired in.** Both land in the 8–15% judgment band (esbuild ~11.8%, terser ~14.5% — just shy of 15%); neither clears the clean bar. Tip positive because: (1) node is ALREADY a soft dep — `lib/js_bundler.py::_node_syntax_ok` already shells `node --check` fail-open; we reuse that seam, don't add node. (2) Raw drops ~19–23% = less parse/compile pre-boot, matters most on the Kotlin Android WebView client. (3) esbuild over terser (Go, ~10–50× faster; the ~2.7% extra gzip terser gives isn't worth the per-startup cost). CAVEAT: does NOT clear strict ≥15% → optional enhancer ONLY (absent node → unchanged `_minify_js`, byte-identical to today), never node-required; holding ≥15% and declining is also defensible.
- **Integration sketch (design only, §5d).** In `build_bundle`, if esbuild resolves (which/node_modules/.bin/npx) pipe concat bundle through `esbuild --minify`, use only if it passes existing `_node_syntax_ok`, else fall back to `_minify_js` output. Optional `_try_conda_install_node()` twin of the PG installer (`conda install -c conda-forge --override-channels -y nodejs` per the override-channels rule) + one-time `npm ci`. Repo already has root package.json (typecheck harness) + `node --check`, so node already expected for contributors.
- **Verify.** Probed node availability (present in tofu conda env), installed esbuild+terser to `mktemp -d`, measured raw + gzip-6/-9 + brotli-11 with `wc -c`/`gzip`/`brotli`, validated every variant with `node --check`, removed temp dir. No feature code — measurement + doc/JOURNAL only (docs/JS_BUNDLING_RATIONALE.md 211L→302L). [PROGRESS: resolved=3 remaining=0]
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Add node for bundler wins" is mostly a MIRAGE on a global/IIFE frontend: verify `export`/`import` count first — if zero, tree-shaking/scope-hoisting/manifest-retirement are all off the table and only minification remains. Measure the actual gzip delta on the ALREADY-minified baseline (not raw source) against a pre-committed threshold; report gzip-6 (served) not just gzip-9, and include brotli + raw (parse cost) for an honest picture. An optional fail-open enhancer that reuses the existing `node --check` seam is near-zero-risk even when the delta is only in the judgment band.
