### 2026-07-08 — Reload-safety refinement of the connectToTask dedupe (prompted by a peer-conversation FYI). The completed-turn predicate `finishReason && _taskId && _taskId !== taskId` had an over-narrow `_taskId &&` clause that REGRESSED the page-reload case; corrected to `finishReason && _taskId !== taskId`.
- **Trigger.** Peer conv mra402ve noted (advisory) that the backend now persists a stable `_msgId` on assistant messages — while (per the connect-to-task-stale-tail-guard memory) `_taskId` is NOT persisted. That distinction exposed a gap in my just-shipped predicate.
- **The gap (verify-then-write; read the live guard + main_init_tasks Case A).** My predicate required `_taskId` to be TRUTHY to consider a completed tail stale. But on a fresh page reload, a DB-loaded completed assistant has `finishReason` and (now) `_msgId` but NO `_taskId` (never persisted). So `finishReason && _taskId && …` was FALSE for it → connectToTask would REUSE that foreign completed turn as the new task's stream target → the old turn replays into the new bubble — exactly the stale-tail bug the original `!!finishReason` guard existed to catch. I'd protected fresh placeholders with the `_taskId &&` clause, but they're already protected by the `finishReason` gate (a fresh placeholder has none), so the clause was unnecessary AND harmful.
- **Fix.** `_isCompletedTurn = !!assistantMsg.finishReason && assistantMsg._taskId !== taskId`. Reuse a completed tail ONLY when it's confirmed this task's own slot (`_taskId === taskId`, set at bind time / by done+poll handlers). Every other completed tail — different `_taskId` OR absent (reloaded foreign turn) — pushes fresh. The reconnect-to-just-finished dedupe still holds (own slot has `_taskId===taskId` → not stale → reused, no duplicate). The `_staleTaskId` line is unchanged (it legitimately keeps `_taskId && _taskId !== taskId` — only fires on a DIFFERENT non-null id).
- **Tests.** Added Scenario D (reloaded foreign completed tail, `_taskId` absent → must push fresh; asserts 2 assistants + target is the fresh one) and an OVER-NARROW neuter (the rejected `_taskId &&` intermediate → wrongly reuses the old turn, proving the clause was harmful). Source-anchored assert updated to require the refined predicate AND to reject the over-narrow completed-turn form (scoped to the finishReason line so it doesn't false-match the legitimate `_staleTaskId` line). `python -m pytest tests/test_frontend_connecttotask_taskid_dedupe.py -p no:napari` → 2 passed. Bundle → `bundle-502911e9.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `_taskId` is NOT persisted; `_msgId` is. Any predicate that keys on `_taskId` truthiness silently changes behavior across the reload boundary (in-memory task has it, DB-loaded turn does not). For "is this completed tail MINE?", test `_taskId === taskId` (reuse) vs the complement (push fresh) — never gate on `_taskId` being truthy, or an unpersisted reload slot slips through. A peer's incidental architecture note (msgId now persisted, taskId not) was the tell that surfaced this — worth verifying, not just acknowledging.

### 2026-07-08 — Follow-on to the committedMessage keystone: closed the duplicate-bubble BIRTH sites in connectToTask (the compensation layer). Made assistant-slot resolution IDENTITY-FIRST (by _taskId, never by array position) so a done+reconnect/poll race can no longer append a second empty "agent" bubble under one user turn.
- **Ask (owner).** The restored committedMessage only removes the CAUSE of divergence; the duplicate-bubble births still live in the compensation layer, now load-bearing. Proceed (don't wait for the segment-timeline epic): (1) dedupe connectToTask appends by _taskId, kill the positional messages[-1] matching key; (2) on reconnect re-target, never append; + neuter test, coordinate with mrbylvas, rule on the error-path errAssistant residual.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write, full source read of connectToTask sse_pipeline.js:150-320 + all 7 call sites).** `connectToTask` resolved the slot to accumulate into by ARRAY POSITION (`conv.messages[length-1]`), then a "stale-prior-turn guard" pushed a FRESH empty placeholder whenever the tail carried a `finishReason` — WITHOUT checking whether that completed tail was THIS task's OWN reply. On a reconnect/poll-takeover to a JUST-FINISHED task (its assistant has finishReason + _taskId=T, and `finishStream` already deleted the activeStreams entry so there's no stream to re-target), the guard fired for the task's own completed reply and appended a SECOND bubble → "user → two agents". `_isCompletedTurn = !!finishReason` was the exact buggy predicate.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner sign-off; 3 coordinated edits + 1 helper).**
  1. `conversation_list.js` — new `_resolveAssistantByTaskId(conv, taskId)` (tail-up scan for an assistant whose `_taskId===taskId`). Mirrors the existing `_resolveAssistantById` msgId resolver.
  2. `sse_pipeline.js` connectToTask — IDENTITY-FIRST resolution: after the existing-stream stable-id re-target, try `_resolveAssistantByTaskId(conv, taskId)` BEFORE falling back to the positional tail. A slot already bound to this task is re-targeted, never duplicated.
  3. `sse_pipeline.js` stale-guard — completed-turn predicate scoped to a DIFFERENT task: `finishReason && _taskId && _taskId !== taskId`. A same-task (or never-bound) completed tail is OUR slot → reuse. A genuinely different prior completed turn still appends (verified in test scenario B).
  4. `sse_pipeline.js` bind point — stamp `assistantMsg._taskId = taskId` at `activeStreams.set(...)` time (before any token), so a reconnect landing after finishStream cleared the stream entry resolves by identity (closes the gap for a task that finishes/drops before the done/state/poll handlers stamp _taskId).
- **Error-path residual RULED OUT with evidence (owner's explicit ask).** The `errAssistant` push in `saveEditAndResend` (edit_message.js:507) / `regenerateFromUser` (main_regen_continue.js) canNOT coexist with a recovery-pushed assistant: the catch is a mutually-exclusive `else if (…&& await _recoverTimedOutChatTask(…)) {…} else { push errAssistant }`, and `_recoverTimedOutChatTask` (main_send_pipeline.js:1099) pushes an assistant ONLY on its `return true` paths — every `return false` pushes nothing. Recovery-wins short-circuits the else; recovery-fails pushed nothing. Structurally exclusive. HONEST residual flagged (NOT fixed here, different mechanism): if the server task starts AFTER the ~30s recovery window (error bubble persisted+synced), a later orphan-recovery reconnect could append the real assistant after the error bubble. Its proper home is the PARKED backend GET-path reconcile (reconcile.py collapsing stray empty/error placeholders), not this frontend increment — did not overreach.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_frontend_connecttotask_taskid_dedupe.py` (2 tests, node harness re-implementing the real resolution+stale-guard predicates + a SOURCE-ANCHORED assert that the shipped file actually contains `_resolveAssistantByTaskId(`, the `_taskId !== taskId` completed-turn predicate, and the bind-time stamp — so it rots with the code, not a copy). Scenario A (reconnect to finished task) → NO append, single assistant, re-targets own slot; B (different prior completed turn) → still appends (2 assistants); C (fresh send, empty placeholder) → no append; NEUTER (old `!!finishReason` predicate) → duplicate returns (2 assistants) — proven load-bearing. 2 passed. Full regression set 15 passed under pytest (the 2 parity failures are the DOCUMENTED DB-warmup quirk: fail under bare pytest `no such table: conversations`, pass 3/3 run directly — reconfirmed).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK both files; bundle order conversation_list(25) before sse_pipeline(41) but the resolver is only CALLED at runtime so order is moot; rebuilt bundle → `bundle-6935ffac.js`, both new symbols present (2 each). Path-lease held on sse_pipeline.js during the edit + advisory ping to mra402ve (adjacent segment-timeline STEP 5, targets streaming_ui.js rendering — orthogonal to connectToTask slot resolution); lease released. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** NEVER resolve a stream's accumulation target by array position — a splice, reload, or reconnect makes `messages[-1]` a different message than the one the task owns. Match by IDENTITY (_taskId / _msgId), stamped at bind time so it's resolvable the instant the stream exists. A "completed turn" guard must be scoped to a DIFFERENT task (`finishReason && _taskId !== taskId`); `!!finishReason` alone treats the task's own just-finished reply as stale and duplicates it. This generalizes the existing stream-target-resolution-by-msgid + connect-to-task-stale-tail-guard rules to the append/dedupe decision.

### 2026-07-08 — RESEARCH (no feature code): why tofu's JS bundler is a no-build-step Python concatenator, and whether HTTP/2 obsoletes it. Deliverable = verified findings + a persisted reference note (docs/JS_BUNDLING_RATIONALE.md), uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** "The bundle mechanism has pros and cons — do open-source/commercial LLM chat projects all use this? It was originally made to quickly fix Mac unusability." Then (follow-up): PERSIST it to docs/ + JOURNAL so it doesn't evaporate; and turn the two real costs into a VERIFIED answer — confirm the cache-header seam and state with current byte numbers whether a volatile/stable core split is worth doing now.
- **Verified facts (direct source + web, not assumed).** (1) tofu bundles like everyone, but UNUSUALLY: a pure-Python runtime concatenator, NO npm/webpack/Vite — `lib/js_bundler.py` reads `_BUNDLE_FILES` (101) + `_DEFERRED_FILES` (4) = **105 modules**, scan→`_minify_js`→concat→sha256→`node --check` at startup. Competition all use build-time toolchains: LibreChat/Open WebUI = **Vite**, Lobe Chat = **webpack** (all code-split). tofu's differentiator = the project's "vanilla JS, no build step" value (CLAUDE.md §3.2). (2) The "Mac quick fix" is a LIVE path, not dead: `server.py:1751-1771` — tofu speaks H2 only when it terminates TLS itself; drops to HTTP/1.1 behind a proxy, without `cryptography`, or with `--no-tls`. (3) Even under H2, 105 files > USWDS's ~50 threshold → concatenation still wins on gzip efficiency + per-file disk reads (Rolldown "HTTP/2 does not mean you can stop caring about number of requests"; USWDS cites Khan Academy 300-file H2 regression). Sources: rolldown.rs/in-depth/why-bundlers, designsystem.digital.gov/performance/http2, konnorrogers "Why we still bundle with HTTP/2 in 2022".
- **Cache verdict — MEASURED, volatile/stable split is PREMATURE.** Seam confirmed: `server.py:1207-1208` gives `/bundle-` paths `max-age=31536000, immutable` (hash-in-filename = correct busting); injected `index.html` is `private, no-cache` (`routes/common.py:494`) so a new hash lands next load; the **deferred split is the only current churn mitigation.** Current on-disk bytes (measured, supersedes remembered 493 KB): core `bundle-3d9e4964.js` = 1,866,346 B raw / **465,481 B (454.6 KB) gzip**; deferred `feature-1595e5c5.js` = 339,479 B raw / **79,505 B (77.6 KB) gzip** (core dropped below 493 KB since image-gen/paper/orchestration/task-mode moved to the feature bundle). Whole-core invalidation costs one 454.6 KB gzip re-download per client PER UPDATE — only bites under frequent-redeploy-to-many-cached-clients (CDN/SaaS), NOT tofu's self-hosted pull-and-restart model. A finer split adds the exact con we avoid (more manual `_BUNDLE_FILES` ordering) for a benefit tofu's deployment shape doesn't realize; same logic that rejected the i18n locale-split. Cheap lever IF ever measured: more deferred sub-bundles via existing `_assemble_bundle`, not webpack.
- **One real gap found (flagged, NOT applied).** The deferred `feature-<hash>.js` is content-hashed but its path is `/feature-`, not `/bundle-`, so it MISSES the `server.py:1207` immutable branch and falls to `max-age=300, must-revalidate`. Safe but suboptimal — should get the 1-year immutable header (broaden the substring test to also match `/feature-`). Left for owner sign-off.
- **Verify.** Read `lib/js_bundler.py` (bundler + manifest counts), `routes/common.py::index_page` (strip/inject + no-cache HTML), `server.py:1207` (immutable header keyed on `/bundle-`), `server.py:1751-1860` (TLS/H2 fallback). Measured bundle bytes live with `wc -c` + `gzip -c | wc -c`. No feature code — research deliverable only (docs/JS_BUNDLING_RATIONALE.md, 211L). [PROGRESS: resolved=2 remaining=0]
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "HTTP/2 killed bundling" is an over-read: verify the app's ACTUAL protocol path (tofu falls to H1 in 3 real cases) AND count files against the ~50 threshold before believing it. When asked "is cache churn worth fixing," don't hand-wave "not yet" — confirm the header seam in code and quote the current gzip bytes; the answer turns on deployment MODEL (self-hosted pull-restart vs CDN/SaaS), not bundle size alone. Re-measure served bytes each time — a remembered number (493 KB) drifts as modules move between core and deferred bundles.


### 2026-07-08 — KEYSTONE root-cause for "chaotic message orchestration / user → two agent bubbles": the Phase-1 backend `_committedMsg` parity stamp was NEVER LANDED in `_sync_result_to_conversation`. Restored it (4-line write on CAS success); the failing parity test now passes. This re-enables backend-as-single-source-of-truth for settled bubbles, defusing the whole tower of frontend placeholder-guards.
- **Ask (owner).** "Task message orchestration feels chaotic — edit/regen/autopilot mechanisms interact badly; frontend often shows a user followed by TWO agents. Unsure if it's network sync, backend, or frontend render. Fix properly."
- **Method (diagnose-first, verify-then-write).** 4 parallel coder sub-agents mapped the independent subsystems (backend commit, frontend render/dedupe, edit/regen truncation, autopilot/queue). Then I VERIFIED the one consequential claim myself instead of trusting the agent — because it was big enough to change the whole picture.
- **Root cause (empirically proven, not inferred).** `orchestrator.py:1094` ships `done_evt['committedMessage'] = task['_committedMsg']`; `test_committed_message_parity.py` + `docs/CHATINNER_COMPLETION_REFACTOR.md` both assert `_sync_result_to_conversation` STAMPS `task['_committedMsg']` with the re-SELECT-post-CAS tail. But `_committedMsg` appears NOWHERE in `manager.py` — not in the file, not in its entire git history. The readers/test/docs shipped; the WRITE was never landed. **`python tests/test_committed_message_parity.py` was RED** ("_committedMsg was NOT stamped — parity gap OPEN"). Consequence chain: never stamped → `if task.get('_committedMsg')` always false → `done` event NEVER carries `committedMessage` → SSE done handler (`sse_pipeline.js:1583 const _cm = ev.committedMessage`) always sees it absent → **frontend ALWAYS falls back to its transient buffer for settled state.** That is exactly the frontend↔backend divergence the ~5 "push a fresh assistant placeholder" branches in `connectToTask` (`sse_pipeline.js:206/250/294`) exist to paper over — and each such branch is a place a SECOND agent bubble can be born on a flaky reconnect/poll race.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner sign-off, `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`).** On CAS success in `_sync_result_to_conversation`, after `update_conversation_fts`, stamp `task['_committedMsg'] = dict(last_msg)` (shallow copy freezes the row AS WRITTEN so later task mutations can't bleed in). Deliberately LEFT UNSET on skip/freshness/CAS-miss/content-guard paths → done event omits `committedMessage` → client keeps its transient buffer (the offline-fallback invariant `test_no_committed_msg_on_skip_path` guards). 4-line additive change.
- **Verify.** `tests/test_committed_message_parity.py` → 3/3 PASS (was 1 failing). Adjacent completion-workflow tests all green: `test_frontend_finishstream_no_put`, `test_frontend_sse_dispatch`, `test_frontend_toolrounds_keep_longer`, `test_frontend_reconnect_keeplonger_invariant` (3 passed under pytest). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server to load new lib/.
- **Sub-agent findings TRIAGED (the other three).** (a) autopilot/queue: all 3 memory-noted invariants INTACT (`_autopilot_spawned_followup` gate at manager.py:976-981; `_is_autopilot_task` keys on background markers not `config.autopilot`; conv-level baton dispatch idempotent) — NO double-dispatch window. (b) edit/regen: `_needsLoad` stale-resurrection fix PRESENT (both flows set `_needsLoad=false` before POST and never reach `startAssistantResponse`); backend aborts stale tasks before DB read. Residual: error-path `push(errAssistant)` could theoretically coexist with a recovered live one (low-pri). (c) frontend render: the `connectToTask` positional tail-fallback (`sse_pipeline.js:185`) + the stale-prior-turn placeholder push (`:206-217`) + the queued-placeholder push in `stream_lifecycle.js` are the strongest DUPLICATE-BUBBLE sites — but they are the SYMPTOM/compensation layer for the missing committedMessage, not an independent root cause. Next increment (owner sign-off) = once committedMessage rides again, tighten those branches to dedupe by `_taskId` and stop pushing on reconnect when the target already exists.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When readers + a test + a design doc all reference a field (`_committedMsg`) but grep finds ZERO assignments, don't assume "it's elsewhere" — RUN the test. A designed-but-never-landed write is invisible to code review (every reference looks correct) yet silently defeats an entire architectural consolidation and forces the other side to compensate with fragile heuristics. The compensation layer (frontend placeholder guards) is where the visible bug (double bubble) surfaces, but the fix belongs at the un-landed seam.

Then: don't ask, PERSIST — extend the note (broaden scope, keep chatinner its own section; add warm-bg lever to Tier 1 w/ both sources + off-black nuance; add BeeLine to §2 reject; add chatinner CPL table + flag the wrong styles.css:16577 comment; frame measure as project-wide) + a JOURNAL entry.
- **New Tier-1 lever — warm/reduced-glare background (2 independent sources).** Rello & Bigham 2017 (ACM ASSETS, n=341, 89 dyslexic): warm backgrounds (Peach/Orange/Yellow, black text) significantly FASTER reading than cool (Blue/Green/Blue-Grey ~45% slower); "comparable for both groups" so non-dyslexic readers benefit too. Corroborated by British Dyslexia Association style guide + Rello & Baeza-Yates 2015 eye-tracking (n=92): black-on-cream = shortest fixations. NUANCE: avoid *high* contrast (pure #000/#fff "vibration") → off-black on off-white/cream. **tofu's cream theme is already evidence-aligned** — action is verify tofu body text is off-black + consider optional warm surface for dark/light reader containers.
- **New §2 reject — BeeLine Reader (gradient line-coloring), same fate as Bionic.** Koornneef & Kraal 2022 (*Computers in Human Behavior Reports* 6:100197): helped ONLY badly-laid-out text; on well-formatted text made 2nd-graders slower + hampered 3rd-grade comprehension; beginners preferred plain black. The oft-cited positive WestEd study is vendor-commissioned. Telling: BeeLine only helps text that's ALREADY typographically bad — fixing measure/leading removes its only benefit condition.
- **chatinner CPL — computed (owner-verified live against CSS).** `.chat-inner{max-width:820px;padding:0 24px}`=772px col; `.message` flex reserves 40px avatar+12px gap → `.md-content`~720px at FIXED 14.5px (styles.css:344, NOT scaled by --reader-font-scale). CPL=px/(0.5em·font): **desktop ~99 !!**, **tablet (≤1024, max-width:920px) ~113 !!**, phone (~360px) ~45 OK. Flagged the inline comment at **styles.css:16577** ("still under the ~90ch upper bound") as FACTUALLY WRONG at 14.5px (~113 CPL) — computed ch against a larger assumed font. To-fix item.
- **Framing = project-wide typography lever.** Both Reading-Mode default (~99 CPL) AND chatinner (~99/~113) over the 60–80 band for the SAME reason (measure too wide for body font) → the measure fix is shared across prose surfaces, not reading-mode-only. Kept chatinner as its OWN §6 (chat=skim/scan vs reading=sustained) with a lever-transfer table: measure + warm-bg transfer HIGH; focus-dim LOW-moderate (bubbles already segment; "dim old turns" is the analogue); reading-ruler LOW; high-legibility-font moderate (shared --md-sans). Respected the input-toolbar-chat-decoupled-layout convention (change measure, not the decoupling).
- **Verify.** Confirmed anchors before writing: `.chat-inner{max-width:820px;...}` styles.css:317; `.md-content{...font-size:14.5px...}` :344; tablet `max-width:920px` + wrong ~90ch comment :16577. Note edits applied 7/7 (195L→294L). No feature code — research deliverable only. [PROGRESS: resolved=4 remaining=0]
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When asked "does this transfer to surface B", COMPUTE B's numbers against its ACTUAL CSS (chatinner's fixed 14.5px + flex-reserved avatar gutter give a different column than the paper reader's scalable one) rather than assuming the reading-mode findings port wholesale — and keep skim/scan vs sustained-reading surfaces as SEPARATE sections since levers transfer selectively. New candidate levers (BeeLine here) get held to the same ≥2-independent-source bar as the originals before they enter the note; vendor-commissioned studies are flagged, not counted as independent corroboration.


### 2026-07-08 — Project bar reconceived as a living DIORAMA: the tofu pet now ROAMS a scene ground (grass lawn / pool lane) with a wander-FSM, passing BEHIND the controls. Replaced the busy full-wrap floral garland (owner: "too ugly").
- **Ask (owner).** The dense flower-garland wrap read as cluttered wallpaper. Owner's much better idea: "transform this bar into a lawn, a swimming lane, or other long strip scenes, and have pets roam within it — but avoid interfering with the functional display. Design with ultimate innovation." + "learn from others' solutions."
- **Research (swarm researcher, grounded in real source).** Read oneko.js (100ms tick, hard position clamp, idle→sleep probabilistic FSM), Shimeji behaviors.xml (frequency-weighted state graph, Floor border-turn), XPenguins/eSheep (baseline walkers), Desktop Goose (rare surprise), WCAG 2.3.3/2.2.2. Key patterns adopted: (a) layered depth — low-contrast scene BEHIND, character on a baseline, opaque control pills ON TOP (occlusion, not avoidance); (b) soft-bounds TURN-around (not clamp-freeze); (c) idle/sit weighted heavily so it's not hyperactive; (d) reduced-motion = DON'T roam, tab-hidden = pause, aria-hidden + pointer-safe.
- **Art (generate→edit→chroma-key pipeline, per the prior lesson).** Two seamless ground strips (`scene-meadow.png` grass+daisies, `scene-pool.png` lane) + a `tofu-pet-walk.png` mid-stride pose, all generated on a **magenta** screen (grass would be eaten by a green key) and keyed with a vectorized magenta matte (`(r>120)&(b>110)&(g<min(r,b)*0.6)`). Verified seams tile + pet stands on the baseline on a checkerboard. Old `garland-*.png` deleted.
- **CSS (`static/styles.css`, tofu-scoped).** `.project-bar` → `overflow:hidden` container; `::after` = the `--bar-scene` ground strip tiled along the bottom (z0); `[data-decor]` swaps meadow/pool/off. THREE nested pet layers so transforms don't fight: `.tofu-pet` = POSITION (translateX, z1), `.tofu-pet-facing` = DIRECTION (scaleX ±1), `.tofu-pet-img` = per-frame LIFE anim (breathe / new `tofuPetWalk` bob). **Occlusion invariant:** `.project-bar > *:not(.tofu-pet){position:relative;z-index:2}` lifts every real control above the pet so it passes BEHIND them and can never block a hit target.
- **JS (`static/js/tofu-pet.js`, ~445 lines).** Added a WANDER ENGINE: a rAF loop + 1-D FSM (walk/idle/turn/sit/sleep/react) with research weights; `_measure()` computes a SAFE TRACK `[chip.right+pad, controls.left−pad]` via getBoundingClientRect (re-run on ResizeObserver + resize) so the pet turns around BEFORE the pills; walk speed ~34px/s; deep-night/low-energy → sleep in place. Kept the whole expression/mood model + public API; `setDecor` now switches SCENES (`meadow`/`pool`/`off`, key `tofu_bar_scene`, right-click pet to cycle). Reduced-motion (live via matchMedia change) → stand still + single frame; visibilitychange → pause loop.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_tofu_pet.py`, 14, green).** Harness beefed up (matchMedia/rAF/ResizeObserver/getBoundingClientRect/offsetWidth stubs; forces reduced-motion so `_resolve()` — not the roaming 'walk' frame — drives the asserted expr). New/updated: scene assets + walk frame exist on disk; CSS wires each scene to `--bar-scene` + the `>*:not(.tofu-pet)` occlusion lift; wander clamps to `[min,max]` and turns at bounds; all prior FSM + neuter tests still bite.
- **Verify.** node --check OK; tinycss2 0 errors; braces balanced; 14/14. JS `bundle-b3efcafd.js`, CSS `styles-a4bb06aa.css`. Rendered a 3-position wander mock — pet strolls the lawn and passes cleanly behind the Auto pill. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server + hard-refresh.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For "ambient life in a functional bar", the winning pattern is a DIORAMA with z-order occlusion (scene behind, character mid, controls in front) + a bounded wander FSM that turns at the controls' edges — NOT decoration layered over the whole bar (reads as clutter). Chroma-key choice depends on the SUBJECT: green screen for the cream tofu (prior fix), MAGENTA screen for green grass/scenery. Always confirm the safe-track math against live getBoundingClientRect so the roamer can never sit under a hit target.


### 2026-07-08 — RESEARCH (no feature code): how to enhance user focus / ADHD support in Reading Mode. Deliverable = verified findings + a persisted design note (docs/READING_MODE_ADHD_FOCUS_RESEARCH.md), uncommitted for owner sign-off.
- **Ask (owner).** Research ways to enhance user focus / help ADHD readers in reading mode — content, style, or any angle. Then (follow-up) compute the one claim I'd hand-waved (Wide preset CPL), and PERSIST the research so it doesn't evaporate. Explicitly: do NOT write feature code — the objective is research.
- **Bionic Reading = do NOT ship as flagship (3 independent sources).** The most-hyped ADHD reading feature is the best-debunked: (1) peer-reviewed eye-tracking JEMR (PMC12565662) — no significant change to fixations/speed, no word "auto-complete"; (2) Springer 2025 *Atten. Percept. Psychophys.* (s13414-025-03067-w) — first-half bolding "led to costs relative to regular unbolded reading", beneficial for no population; (3) Readwise field test n≈1,916 — 2.6 WPM *slower* (paired t two-tail p=0.055), identical 88% comprehension. Subjective preference is real → at most an opt-in, explicitly-experimental toggle, never the headline.
- **Evidence tiers (in the note).** T1 typography (60–80 CPL line length; line-height ≥1.5 — we're at 1.75; left-aligned not justified — verified none in reader; ~2× para spacing; ≥16px; NO "dyslexia font" beats a good sans — OpenDyslexic no objective gain, Rello&Baeza-Yates 2013 / Wery&Diliberto 2017; defensible = Atkinson Hyperlegible + Lexend). T2 interaction (dim-non-active-paragraph focus, active-line guide, progress cues; AVOID RSVP/Spritz — Schotter 2014 shows killing regressions hurts comprehension). T3 content (Chan et al. 2023 ADHD meta-analysis g=0.96 is about CHILD decoding remediation, NOT adult UI — do not over-read; but structure-aids-comprehension supports TL;DR/scaffolding/glossary, which we already have).
- **CPL — computed, not guessed (the owner's #1 correction).** `CPL = measure_px/(0.5em·font_px)`, tofu base 14.5px as worst case (smallest of the 3 theme bases → highest CPL) ⇒ `CPL = measure/(7.25·scale)`. Result: **Wide/860 exceeds the 90-CPL return-sweep failure threshold at EVERY scale (91–140)** — stronger than my "likely". Bonus defect: **the DEFAULT 720@scale-1.0 is already ~99 CPL**, above the 60–80 band out of the box; 720 only enters band at scale 1.3. Only Narrow/640@≥1.2 and 720@1.3 sit cleanly in-band. Caveats logged: padding shaves a few CPL (favorable); dark/light 15px base slightly lower CPL; CJK is full-width (~1em advance → 720px≈49 chars, different standard) so the 60–80 band is Latin-specific.
- **Prioritized gaps mapped to existing seams (proposals only, no code).** (1) re-tune `--reader-measure` presets so the common case is in-band (styles.css:1227 + `_READER_WIDTHS`), verify vs the CPL table; (2) Focus mode = dim non-active paragraph + optional active-line guide (CSS-var + body class on `#paperReportContent`/`#paperReviewContent`, same pattern as comfort controls); (3) optional high-legibility reader font Atkinson/Lexend via the per-theme font-var chain; (4) do NOT build Bionic (or gate it experimental).
- **Verify.** Confirmed on-disk anchors before writing: `--reader-measure:720px` default + `.paper-report-article{max-width:var(--reader-measure)}` at styles.css:1227-1228; line-height 1.75; no `text-align:justify` in reader. Note written to docs/READING_MODE_ADHD_FOCUS_RESEARCH.md (uncommitted). [PROGRESS: resolved=4 remaining=0]
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a readability claim is computable (CPL, contrast ratio, tap-target px), COMPUTE it against the actual token values — "likely too wide" is not a finding, "91–140 CPL at 860px, and 99 at the default" is. Use the smallest theme base as the CPL worst case. And a research deliverable must be PERSISTED (docs/ note + JOURNAL), not left only in chat, or it evaporates.


### 2026-07-08 — tofu New Chat button re-skinned as "buttered toast": golden toast-crust gradient + a melting-butter radial sheen + puffy bread edges (inset top butter-rim / baked bottom crust), deep toast-brown text. Fits the food-themed tofu palette; kept the neutral-clay drop shadow the drift-guard requires.

Reworked into toast: idle `background` = a `radial-gradient(130% 80% at 50% -12%, cream…)` butter sheen layered over a `linear-gradient(180deg,#EAB65F→#DA9E4C→#C4863D)` toast crust; `color:#5C3B18` (baked-brown, readable on gold); `border:1px solid rgba(150,100,45,0.35)` crust edge; `border-radius:12px`; box-shadow = neutral clay drop (`rgba(92,72,44,…)`, kept per guard) + `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,249,228,0.6)` top butter-rim + `inset 0 -2px 3px rgba(150,95,40,0.28)` baked bottom crust; subtle `text-shadow` cream highlight. Hover melts the butter brighter (lighter crust + stronger sheen) with the usual −1px lift; active presses in with an inset crumb shadow.
- **Constraint respected.** `tests/test_frontend_new_chat_btn_style.py` requires: background stays a `linear-gradient` (primary weight); box-shadow carries NO accent glow (`rgba(193,121,75,…)`) — only neutral `rgba(92,72,44,…)`; and the literal `rgba(92,72,44,0.10)` token stays present (the neuter test rewrites it). All satisfied — the butter sheen is a SEPARATE radial layer, the crust remains the linear-gradient the guard checks.
- **Verify.** `python -m pytest tests/test_frontend_new_chat_btn_style.py -p no:napari` → 3/3 green. tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6916/6916. Playwright preview couldn't render (sandbox missing chromium libs, exit 127) — CSS is sound, just no on-box screenshot. NOT committed (owner attribution); CSS is content-hash served (`lib/css_bundler.py`) — restart/refresh to see it.
- **Follow-up (owner: "needs texture").** First texture attempt used offset `radial-gradient` pore TILES on `::before` — but a screenshot (real render, see next) showed they form a MECHANICAL polka-dot GRID = reads cheap/plasticky, not organic. Replaced with an inline-SVG `feTurbulence fractalNoise` grain (multiply) = genuine irregular baked grain. Kept the pseudo-element approach (freed retired sparkles, so the guarded main rule stays untouched); lifted content with `.new-chat-btn > *{z-index:1}` + wrapped the bare "New Chat" text in a `<span>` (a text node can't be raised by `> *`, else the multiply overlay darkens the label).
- **Follow-up #2 (owner: "still doesn't look good" + screenshot).** VERIFIED VISUALLY THIS TIME (headless-shell recipe, memory `headless-browser-screenshot-recipe`: `hb` conda env + LD_LIBRARY_PATH). The render exposed the real tell: a bright glossy top sheen + saturated orange made it read as an AMBER CANDY/PLASTIC PILL, and the grain at `opacity:.14` was invisible. Toast is MATTE, UNEVENLY toasted, with VISIBLE crumb. Fixes: (a) killed the glossy sheen — dropped the strong top `rgba(255,250,232,.75)` highlight to a soft `.28`, inset top-rim `.70→.34`; (b) desaturated the crust (`#EBC079→#DFAA5A→#CE9648` → `#E6C486→#D8B168→#CA9F52`); (c) added 3 irregular off-center `radial-gradient` toast blotches so baking is uneven; (d) grain `opacity .14→.30` (finer tile 120×52, `baseFrequency .82`, 3 octaves) so the crumb is actually seen; hover grain stays `.24` (was fading to .10). Re-rendered → now reads as matte buttered toast, not candy. Screenshot confirmed at 2× zoom (fine crumb visible, no gloss).

Keep the drop shadow in tofu's neutral `rgba(92,72,44,…)` clay vocabulary; colored glow is the dark-theme idiom and the test rejects it. TEXTURE goes on the (already-retired) `::before`/`::after` — free real estate that dodges the guarded rule entirely — but remember a `multiply` overlay at `z-index:0` will darken bare inline text: lift it with `> *{z-index:1}` and wrap any bare text node in a span.

### 2026-07-08 — Composer submenu-dropdown redesign: it read as "a big square" because it (a) floated detached from its trigger and (b) stacked a column of filled icon TILES. Added a pointer caret + decluttered the resting icons (bare glyph, accent tile only on the active row).
- **Ask (owner).** The composer toolbar submenu-dropdown (增强 / 工具 / 模式 popovers, `.submenu-dropdown` in index.html:716/743/790) "still needs a lot of optimization; not attractive, looking like a big square." Requested searching online for design solutions.
- **Research.** Web search for modern dropdown/popover patterns — the generic listicles were low-value; the useful convergent signal came from popover design systems (Red Hat popover, Mobbin popover glossary, shadcn/Raycast/Linear command-menus) + the owner's own logged UI preference ("single-card containment; avoid concentric borders/shadows; use recessed trays or typography for hierarchy"). Two concrete root causes, not a color problem.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write, direct source read of styles.css:711-733 + the tofu override at :12241).**
  1. **Detached rectangle.** `.submenu-dropdown` floated with `bottom:calc(100% + 8px)` and NO caret, so it read as an unanchored box with no visual tie to the button that opened it.
  2. **Column of filled icon tiles.** `.submenu-item-icon` painted a `28px` `--bg-tertiary` (tofu `#E8E5DC`) filled square behind EVERY row's glyph at rest — a stack of filled boxes inside the bordered card = exactly the concentric-box clutter that reads "blocky." The tofu override forced the tile on all items too.
- **Fix (CSS-only, uncommitted for owner attribution, `static/styles.css`).**
  1. **Pointer caret** — `.submenu-dropdown::after` = a 10px rotated-45° square with right+bottom borders, `bottom:-5px`, centered; fill/border tokenized so it inherits each theme's surface. Base uses `--bg-secondary`+`--border-light`; tofu override re-tints to the `#F4F2EB` pixel-window fill + `#A89878` warm edge (bottom:-6px for the 2px border); light override uses `var(--border)`. Hidden on mobile (`.submenu-dropdown::after{display:none}` in the ≤bottom-sheet media query — there the dropdown is a full-width sheet, no trigger to point at).
  2. **Decluttered icons** — `.submenu-item-icon` background `--bg-tertiary`→`transparent`, color→`--text-tertiary`, size 28→26px (KEEPS the alignment gutter so names still line up, just drops the box). Hover no longer paints the tile (the row `--bg-hover` already lifts) — only brightens the glyph. tofu `.submenu-item-icon` box → transparent + `#8A7A5A` glyph; the `#E8E5DC` tile is now scoped to `.submenu-item.active .submenu-item-icon` ONLY, so the filled tile becomes a SELECTION cue (mirrors the base `.submenu-item.active` accent-subtle tile) instead of ambient clutter.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6916/6916. `tests/test_frontend_submenu_dropdown_style.py` 4/4 (the two locked invariants — single `transform`, non-black light shadow — untouched). CSS bundle rebuilds content-hashed at import time — NOT committed (owner attribution); restart server + hard-refresh to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A dropdown that "looks like a big square" is usually TWO separable problems: no anchor (add a caret keyed to the trigger) + filled per-row icon tiles (strip to bare glyph, reserve the fill for the active/selected state). Caret fill+borders MUST be tokenized/overridden per theme (tofu paints an explicit `#F4F2EB` fill + pixel border, not the base token) or the caret shows the wrong surface color; and hide it wherever the dropdown reflows to a full-width bottom sheet.

### 2026-07-08 — Settled interleaved tool-log leaked raw ⟦NT_n⟧ / <nt> translation markers into the per-round narration — the ONE translated-content render site missing the notranslate strip. Fixed defense-in-depth to match every other site.
- **Ask (owner, from a screenshot of a 13-tool interleaved turn).** The Chinese narration interleaved into the tool log (rounds 11 & 12) — check the translation text for errors being rendered into the tool log.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; direct source read).** `_renderTimelineBatch` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js:2651`) renders the per-round translated narration (`seg.translatedText`, stamped at finalize by `lib/translate/commit.py::_stamp_segment_translations`) straight through `renderMarkdown(_segText)` with **no `stripNoTranslateTags()`**. It was the ONLY translated-content render site in the frontend missing that guard — the streaming preview (`translation.js:341`), the settled bilingual view (`chat_render.js:1165/1231/1261`), the partial preview (`chat_render.js:1300`), and the sidebar (`conversation_list.js:541`) all strip first. The backend translation pipeline wraps preserved spans in `<notranslate>`/`<nt>` → `⟦NT_n⟧` placeholders (`lib/translate/notranslate.py`), and its own docstring + `_reattach_notranslate_blocks` warn that cheap LLMs frequently mangle/localize these (swap `⟦⟧` for CJK 【】/〔〕, insert spaces, leave stray `<nt>`). That reattached text becomes `translatedText` and is persisted. So the user saw a clean streaming preview (stripped) → a dirty snap at finalize (unstripped) when a marker survived: a visible `【NT_0】` / `⟦NT_0⟧` / `<nt>` fragment in the settled tool log.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner attribution, 1 JS edit).** `tool_rounds.js:2651` — insert `const _segClean = (typeof stripNoTranslateTags === 'function') ? stripNoTranslateTags(_segText) : _segText;` and render `_segClean`. Mirrors the streaming path's `renderMarkdown(strip(zh))` exactly. `stripNoTranslateTags` (defined in `conversation_list.js`, loaded before `tool_rounds.js` in the bundle) is only CALLED at runtime inside the function body, so bundle order is moot; the `typeof` guard is belt-and-suspenders.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_segment_timeline.py`, +2 = 14 total, all green).** Added a real `stripNoTranslateTags` stub to `_STUBS` (mirrors the shipped impl) + `_NT_STRIP_HARNESS`: a segment whose `translatedText` carries a raw `<nt>` tag, a full-width `⟦NT_0⟧`, and a CJK-localized `【NT_1】` — asserts kept text survives and every marker form is gone (5 checks). NEUTER `_NC_NT_STRIP_HARNESS` removes the strip call → confirms `⟦NT_0⟧` LEAKS (proves load-bearing). Plus a source assert that `stripNoTranslateTags(_segText)` is present. `python -m pytest tests/test_frontend_segment_timeline.py -p no:napari` → 14 passed; `node --check tool_rounds.js` OK.
- **Second finding INVESTIGATED with byte-level evidence, PROVEN legitimate (NOT a bug) — my turn-1 characterization was WRONG.** I first hand-waved the round-11 italic CJK glyph as "a lone `*样*` misfire in the SOURCE narration parsed by the CJK preprocessor." Owner pushed for evidence. Traced the ACTUAL screenshot conv (`mrbylvashtemxh` msg 1): the round-11 narration `seg[41].text` (source EN) is a BALANCED `*styling*` pair (the model italicized the word); the persisted `msg.translatedContent` (offset 729) faithfully carries it as a BALANCED `*样式*` pair (样式 = "styling", TWO chars — not the "lone single-char `*样*`" I claimed). Rendered the exact bytes through the vendored `marked v12.0.2` + the real `_cjkFriendlyPreprocess`: `*样式*思维` → `<em>样式</em>思维`, and RAW-vs-preprocessed output is BYTE-IDENTICAL (the preprocessor is NOT involved — it neither creates nor removes this; CommonMark renders `*`-emphasis intraword by design, `_` is the one with the intraword restriction). CONCLUSION: it's genuinely balanced, model-intended emphasis, faithfully translated, rendering CORRECTLY. Not a translation artifact, not a preprocessor misfire. No code change warranted (suppressing intraword `*` for CJK would break legit emphasis like `这是*重点*内容`). The only nuance is typographic (Han has no true italic → synthetic oblique looks slightly odd on a lone term) — a design call for the owner, not a fix.
- **Guardrail / lesson (this turn).** Don't ship a mechanism claim ("lone `*` misfire in the preprocessor") without reading the actual bytes — verify-then-write means pull the real source AND translated fields from the DB and render them through the REAL vendored renderer. The truth (balanced `*styling*`→`*样式*`, correct `<em>`) was the OPPOSITE of the guess. Method to find a screenshotted turn: grep `conversations.messages` for distinctive on-screen phrases (here "附近有几个兄弟任务" / "消息指纹" uniquely pinned the conv); beware false-positive self-matches (my own analysis text in THIS conv also contained `*样*式思维`).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any site that renders translated content MUST call `stripNoTranslateTags()` before `renderMarkdown()` — the backend's notranslate placeholders are known to survive/mangle, so the frontend strip is the last line of defense, not optional. When adding a NEW translated-content render path, mirror the streaming/bilingual sites' `strip → render` idiom. A clean streaming preview that goes dirty at finalize is the fingerprint of a render site that forgot the strip.


### 2026-07-08 — Send-while-generating INTERRUPTED the visible reply instead of queuing (root cause: autopilot-supersede misclassified the PRIMARY armed turn as background). Keyed the supersede on background markers only, not the bare config.autopilot flag.
- **Ask (owner, from a screenshot of conv mrbrixou93j8fr — AUTOPILOT armed).** Typed a message while a turn was generating, expecting it to QUEUE; it INTERRUPTED the running turn. Also a strange re-render: the previous agent bubble disappeared first, then an incomplete bubble appeared after a delay, then incomplete agent content appeared again. Fix both.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write; 2 parallel coder sub-agents + direct source read).** The send gate's autopilot-supersede rule (`routes/chat.py::chat_send`) is designed so a human send behind an INVISIBLE background autopilot follow-up aborts+starts-now instead of waiting minutes in queue. But `_is_autopilot_task` checked `config.autopilot` FIRST — and `arm_autopilot` (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py:2140`) flips `config['autopilot']=True` on the PRIMARY, VISIBLE worker turn the user is watching (so its end-of-turn hook fires). So the turn on screen classified as "background autopilot" → `has_running_worker` stayed False → the send SUPERSEDED (aborted) the reply the user was watching instead of queuing behind it. The genuine background turns the rule targets ALWAYS carry a distinguishing marker (`_autopilotParent` on follow-ups autopilot.py:1322 / VU subtasks :613,:1036; `_autopilot_kick` :1979); only the visible primary turn has the bare flag with no marker.
- **Bug #2 (the render flicker) was a DOWNSTREAM consequence of #1.** The wrongful abort tore out the old bubble (`sse_pipeline.js:291` removes `msg-N`), pushed a fresh placeholder, and a delayed `state` snapshot from the just-aborted old task raced the new SSE connect → disappear → incomplete → content-again. Fixing #1 means the visible turn is no longer aborted, so this ordering window never opens in the reported path. The stale-tail guard (sse_pipeline.js:191-217) + abort/supersede state-drop guard remain for the legitimate background-supersede path.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner attribution, `routes/chat.py`).** `_is_autopilot_task` now returns True ONLY on a background marker (`_autopilotParent`/`_vu_subtask`/`_autopilot_kick`) — dropped the bare `config.autopilot` predicate. Result: an armed-but-visibly-streaming turn is treated as a real in-progress reply → the human send QUEUES behind it (correct); a genuine invisible follow-up still supersedes (unchanged). No frontend change needed.
- **Tests (`tests/test_chat_send_supersedes_autopilot.py`, +1 = 4, all green).** New `test_armed_primary_turn_queues_not_superseded`: arm the marker + a running PRIMARY turn (`config.autopilot=True`, NO background marker) → send returns `{queued:true}`, the turn is NOT aborted, queue depth 1. The 3 originals still pass (background follow-up still superseded; normal worker still queued; worker-wins-over-coexisting). Double-neuter confirmed: restoring the old `config.autopilot`-first predicate makes the new test FAIL (queued != true), fix restored → 4/4. Ran with `-p no:napari` (project harness).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `arm_autopilot` mutates the LIVE visible task's `config.autopilot`, so that flag is NOT a "background turn" signal — it's true on the turn the user is watching. Any code that wants to distinguish a background VU/follow-up turn from the visible primary turn MUST key on the spawn markers (`_autopilotParent`/`_vu_subtask`/`_autopilot_kick`), never on `config.autopilot`. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server to load new routes/ (import-time).


### 2026-07-08 — Pet mascot ROOT-CAUSE fix: my background-removal step was eating the tofu BODY (cream ≈ pale bg), leaving a floating face — regenerated the whole set on a chroma-green screen so the keyer preserves the body. Now a genuinely refined chibi tofu-character brand mark.
- **Ask (owner, angry — rightly).** "This pet design is hideous and not at all refined. Could you at least put some effort into creating a decent brand image?!" The bar showed a floating little FACE with no body.
- **Root cause (verify-then-write: read the actual on-disk PNGs, didn't trust prior claims).** The `generate_image` art was FINE (a full chibi tofu character), but my post-process DESTROYED it. The pipeline flood-filled from the corners over any pixel within a color-distance `tol` of the sampled background. The tofu BODY (`#FBF0D6`) is nearly identical to the flat PALE generation background, so the fill bled straight through the body and erased it, leaving only the dark eyes/mouth/teardrop = the "hideous floating face." A corner-seeded flood-fill CANNOT separate a near-bg-colored subject from the bg — wrong tool for a cream subject on cream.
- **Fix = chroma key.** Regenerated the idle base with an explicit **solid bright chroma-green `#00d000` background** (high contrast to cream), then derived all 7 expressions via **edit mode** (`source_image=_src-idle.png`) keeping the green bg. New keyer `key_green()` (vectorized numpy): bg = pixels where `g>90 and g>r*1.15 and g>b*1.15` → alpha 0; plus a green-spill de-fringe (`g>max(r,b)+16 → pull g down`) so no green halo survives on the outline. Proved on the idle frame FIRST (40k opaque body px preserved, checkerboard shows clean edges) before committing the whole set. Then crop+pad+downscale to 128px (~14KB each). `_src-*.png` green intermediates deleted after keying; final `tofu-pet-<expr>.png` names unchanged so JS/CSS/tests needed no rewiring.
- **Result.** 8 on-model frames (idle/happy/thinking/celebrating/surprised/sad/sleepy/sleeping) each with a FULL cream body + arms + feet, crisp linework, no halo — verified on a checkerboard grid. The chibi character (arms/legs, per the earlier ask) reads as a polished Sanrio-style brand mascot. Paired with the full-bar flower-garland wrap (top+bottom ::before/::after, rose/sakura/wildflower styles via `[data-decor]` + `TofuPet.setDecor`, right-click pet to cycle) from the prior increment.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_frontend_tofu_pet.py` 13/13 green. Had to add `document.querySelectorAll` to the node DOM stub — the new `_applyDecor()` uses it and the stub lacked it (10 tests failed with `querySelectorAll is not a function` until added; production DOM always has it).
- **Verify.** node --check OK; tinycss2 0 errors; JS bundle `bundle-147e81e0.js`, CSS `styles-3ce00dbb.css`. Rendered a final mock (pet + rose garland wrap) — reads clean and refined. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server + hard-refresh to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** NEVER background-remove a subject whose fill color is close to the background via corner flood-fill / color-distance — it eats the subject. For a cream/white subject, GENERATE on a saturated chroma background (green/magenta) and key on the chroma channel, with a spill-suppression pass. And when the owner says "hideous," re-open the actual asset file and LOOK (inspect_image) before regenerating — the bug was in MY pipeline, not the generator, and staring at the file surfaced it immediately.


### 2026-07-08 — Interleaved timeline: per-round "思考过程" thinking made a QUIET chrome-less disclosure (was reusing the full bordered .thinking-block card → a wall of big boxes on a 12-round turn users rarely open).
- **Ask (owner, from a screenshot of a 13-tool / 12-round turn).** In the interleaved segment timeline the thinking-content blocks are "a bit too huge"; users rarely read them, so design them more appropriately / better-looking.
- **Root cause (verified in code).** `_renderTimelineBatch` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`) emits each per-round thinking segment with the SAME `.thinking-block` markup the standalone single-turn thinking uses. The only interleaved override was `.seg-timeline .seg-thinking { margin: 2px 0 8px 0 }` (styles.css:7203-ish) — so every per-round box kept the full card chrome: base `1px border + bg + radius`, and under tofu `[data-theme="tofu"] .thinking-block` forces `2px border + clay shadow + 14px radius + overflow:visible` (higher specificity). Stacked across 12 rounds = the "too huge" wall.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner attribution, CSS-only, scoped to `.seg-timeline .seg-thinking`).**
  1. Base rule: strip the card chrome (`border/background:none; border-radius:0; box-shadow:none; overflow:visible`); shrink the header to a slim muted one-liner (`padding:3px 0; opacity:.55; label 11px/500; toggle 9px`; hover lifts opacity, no bg fill); expanded text becomes a subtle left-rule indent (`border-left:2px var(--thinking-border); padding-left:11px; 12px; opacity:.9`). KEPT `margin:2px 0 8px 0` (left=0) so the flush-left alignment invariant still holds.
  2. Tofu override (`[data-theme="tofu"] .seg-timeline .seg-thinking`) — needed because the tofu clay card has higher specificity; neutralizes `border/box-shadow/background/border-radius` and re-tints the left-rule to the tofu purple `rgba(151,139,184,0.35)`.
  - Scope is strict: the STANDALONE single-turn `.thinking-block` (no tools), the streaming live thinking, and branch-view thinking are all UNTOUCHED — only the interleaved per-round variant changes.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_segment_timeline.py`, +2 = 10 total, all green).** Env-independent CSS-parse asserts: base `.seg-timeline .seg-thinking` border+background are `none`; tofu override border is `none` (proves the higher-specificity clay card is neutralized). NEUTER re-injects a `1px solid red` border and confirms the compact invariant FAILS (has teeth). Ran `-p no:napari` (napari's GL-ES import breaks bare collection).
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6911/6911. `test_frontend_segment_timeline.py` 10/10. CSS bundle rebuilds at import time (content-hashed) — NOT committed (owner attribution); restart server + hard-refresh to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a compact inline variant REUSES a full card component's classes, the base override is not enough on the tofu theme — `[data-theme="tofu"] .thinking-block` (0,1,1)+ wins over `.seg-timeline .seg-thinking` unless you add a theme-scoped override at matching-or-higher specificity. Always pair a base chrome-strip with its tofu counterpart and assert BOTH in the drift guard.



### 2026-07-08 — P5 DESIGN NOTE (captured for later, NOT implemented): the growing conversation body is anchored only by the short-TTL moving tail breakpoint → whole-body re-bill on conversations with gaps > the tail TTL (default 5m).
- **Status.** Documentation-only. No code change. This is the one remaining item from the cache/compaction optimize pass (P1–P4 resolved + tested); owner will weigh it separately as a structural design question.
- **Corrected framing (grounded in `lib/llm/cache.py::add_cache_breakpoints`, verified — supersedes the audit's looser "no second stable breakpoint" wording).** Anthropic allows 4 `cache_control` markers (`_MAX_CACHE_BP`). The allocator RESERVES 1 for the last tool def + 1 for the conversation tail, and gives the system phase only the leftover (≤2). On a Claude conv WITH tools the steady-state split is: system×2 + tool×1 + tail×1 = 4, all consumed. System + tools carry `ttl='1h'` (`_cc_stable`); the tail carries the DEFAULT 5m TTL (`_cc_tail`). The tail marker sits on the LAST message and therefore MOVES every round.
- **Why the body is NOT actually unanchored (the audit over-stated it).** Anthropic reads the longest byte-identical cached prefix. Round N's tail breakpoint at position P writes a cache entry covering `[0..P]`; round N+1 (tail now at P+k) reads that entry back for `[0..P]` and only freshly writes `[P..P+k]`. So the moving tail breakpoint incrementally anchors the growing body — the standard Anthropic pattern. In steady, fast turn-taking there is NO whole-body re-bill.
- **The GENUINE, NARROW failure mode.** That incremental anchor lives ONLY at the tail's 5m TTL. If the gap between turns exceeds the tail TTL (default 5m — user thinking, tool-wait, overnight resume), round N's tail cache entry EXPIRES. Round N+1 then finds only the 1h system+tools prefix still cached, so the ENTIRE conversation body past tools-end is re-billed uncached. On long, slow, or resumed conversations this is a real recurring cost — and it is exactly the class `cache_tracking.py` now SURFACES (post-P1) as a `prefix_mutation`/`no_reuse` break attributed to TTL, rather than masking it.
- **CORRECTION — there is NO free slot to "steal" (grounded in `_MAX_CACHE_BP` reservation model + memory `cache-breakpoint-tail-starvation-system-blocks`).** The audit's "add a second stable breakpoint" framing is WRONG for the production shape. `add_cache_breakpoints` RESERVES tool+tail up front and gives the system phase only the leftover (`_system_bp_budget = _MAX_CACHE_BP - _reserve`). In the real production system prompt (static + memory + swarm = 3 candidate blocks) the ≤2 system budget is ALREADY fully consumed AND system blocks already DROP harmlessly past the budget — that reservation model was itself the fix for the tail-starvation cost-runaway (conv `mqj7x0t8bu11qv`). So all 4 markers are spoken for: system×2 + tool×1 + tail×1. P5 CANNOT add a 5th marker and has no idle slot to repurpose. **The real P5 question is therefore narrower: whether to re-purpose the EXISTING tail marker's TTL and/or placement** — NOT whether to add one.
- **The design question (the tradeoffs to weigh — do NOT rush).**
  1. **Re-purpose the existing tail marker's PLACEMENT + TTL** (the only lever, given no free slot). Move BP#4 off the literal last message onto the immutable-prefix bound (`len - EDITABLE_TAIL_COUNT`, the single-sourced boundary in `cache_tracking.py`) and give it `ttl='1h'` (`_cc_stable` shape), so the SETTLED body survives long gaps. Cost: the genuinely-volatile ≤2-msg editable tail then rides the residual (uncached, or a coarsely-advanced marker) — acceptable because the tail is small.
  2. **ORDERING CONSTRAINT (hard — from memory `anthropic-cache-breakpoints-mixed-ttl`).** Anthropic requires all `ttl='1h'` entries to appear BEFORE any `ttl='5m'` entry in the array. Placing a 1h BP at `len - EDITABLE_TAIL_COUNT` with a 5m tail AFTER it satisfies this. Making the literal-tail BP 1h while an earlier BP stays 5m would VIOLATE it → HTTP 400. State this in the impl so it doesn't trip the ceiling+ordering guard.
  3. **Just widen the tail TTL to 1h unconditionally?** REJECTED by measured data (see below): blanket 1h-tail RAISES cost on fast turn-taking and only wins on long-gap/resume. A/B: A −0.2%, B **+3.3%**, C **+3.2%**, D (mixed empty-content assistants / long gaps) **−16.1%** — because 1h cache WRITES cost 2.0× vs 1.25× for 5m, and fast turns never reach the gap where 1h pays off. So any 1h change MUST be gap-gated, not always-on.
- **Recommended shape IF pursued (not a decision — a GAP-GATED starting point).** Keep the 4-marker layout (do NOT add a marker — none is free). Re-purpose the tail marker: when a long inter-turn gap is observed/probable, place BP#4 on the message at the immutable-prefix bound (`len - EDITABLE_TAIL_COUNT`) with `ttl='1h'` (ordering-safe: 1h before the residual tail), anchoring the SETTLED body across the gap; when turn-taking is fast, keep TODAY's behavior exactly (BP#4 on `msg[-1]` at 5m) so fast convs pay ZERO extra. The gate signal already exists — `detect_cache_break` tracks inter-round `elapsed`, and `latch_extended_ttl(task_id)` is the per-session TTL latch. Gate on observed gap, NOT a static flag.
- **ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (mandatory — this is the go/no-go, not "it helps resumes").** Run `debug/test_cache_validation.py --ttl` across BOTH the fast-turn arms (A/B/C) AND the long-gap/resume arm (D). The change ships ONLY if it is **net-neutral-or-better on the fast-turn arms** (i.e. does not reproduce the blanket-1h regressions B +3.3% / C +3.2%) AND positive on the long-gap arm. A win on resumes that costs fast turns is a REJECT — the common case must not regress to help the rare one.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "No cache anchor for the body" was an over-statement (the moving tail already anchors it); the precise bug is "the body's only anchor has a SHORT TTL, so it re-bills across turn gaps longer than that TTL." There is NO spare marker — the reservation model already spends all 4 — so P5 is a TTL/placement re-purpose of the existing tail marker, gap-gated, not a new breakpoint. Any change is benchmark-justified across fast AND slow arms, never asserted. P1's fix is the PREREQUISITE: the TTL-expiry cost is now VISIBLE in the break metrics (attributed, counted in `total_breaks`) instead of masked, which is what makes the benchmark measurable at all.


### 2026-07-08 — Cache P1 (highest-$ finding) FIXED: the per-turn user-profile splice used notify_compaction, which MASKED a real full-prefix re-bill on every profile turn. Swapped to notify_history_rewrite (labels the cause without suppressing detection) + gated the anonymous leading-indicator warning.
- **Ask (owner, follow-up to the compaction audit).** "Fully optimize" isn't done — P1 was only flagged, not fixed. It's the "backend as single source of truth for cost visibility" class. Not a risky design change: the project already has the right primitive (`notify_history_rewrite`), and using `notify_compaction` on a re-billing mutation is exactly the `l1-compaction-notify-masks-detection` anti-pattern.
- **Root cause (verified in code).** `system_context.py:~724` spliced the user-profile / detail block into `messages[0]`'s carrier — which after the first tool round sits INSIDE the cached prefix — and then called `notify_compaction(_cid)` to silence the `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED` warning. But `notify_compaction` sets `compaction_pending`, which in `detect_cache_break` BLANKET-suppresses all 4 break detectors AND skips the wire diff AND can flip `_wire_proven_identical→True`. A profile splice is a genuine prefix *mutation that re-bills the whole body uncached*, NOT a prefix *drop* — so the real, recurring cost was laundered into a false "server-side — PROVEN" verdict and hidden from `total_breaks`.
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner attribution, 2 source edits).**
  1. **`system_context.py:730`:** `notify_compaction(_cid)` → `notify_history_rewrite(_cid)`. This primitive (already in `cache_tracking.py`, documented as the deliberate OPPOSITE of `notify_compaction`) NAMES the cause but does NOT gate any break classifier and does NOT skip the wire diff — so the re-bill is still detected, attributed to the exact `msg[i].field`, counted in `total_breaks`, and surfaced as `prefix_mutation`.
  2. **`cache_tracking.py:~614`:** a plain swap was INSUFFICIENT — the anonymous `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED …without compaction` leading-indicator warning was gated only on `not compaction_pending`, so it would still spam every profile turn. Gated it additionally on `if not _was_history_rewrite:` — keeps `_prefix_mutated=True` (confirmed NAMED break still fires) but suppresses ONLY the anonymous alarm (the cause is now known/named). The leading indicator is only useful when the cause is UNKNOWN.
- **Test (`tests/test_cache_prefix_stability.py::test_profile_splice_labels_without_suppressing_the_rebill`, new, pure/no-DB, registered in the runner list).** Drives the HASH-based in-prefix mutation path across 2 rounds on 3 arms with a WARNING-capturing log handler: (CONTROL, no notify) anonymous alarm FIRES + break surfaces — proves the warning path is live; (history_rewrite) anonymous alarm SILENT, YET `prefix_mutation` surfaces + `total_breaks>=1`; (compaction) anonymous alarm silent AND break MASKED (`total_breaks==0`) — proving WHY the splice must not use it. Smoking-gun log confirmed: `p1-ctrl` prints "PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED …without compaction"; `p1-hr` does NOT, but still prints "PREFIX MUTATION BREAK … the whole body was re-billed uncached".
- **Verify.** AST + import OK; only ONE live `notify_history_rewrite(` call remains in system_context.py (grep). `tests/test_cache_improvements.py` + `test_l2_cache_roi.py` = 62 passed; the new P1 test + the 8 other prefix-stability tests pass via the standalone runner. The one `test_settled_tail_wire_identical_when_scrolled_into_prefix` ✗ (`_committedMsg not stamped`) is PRE-EXISTING (proven: fails identically with my two files `git checkout`-reverted — a DB-fixture artifact, unrelated to cache logic; it also halts the standalone runner's final "ALL PASSED" banner via `sys.exit(1)`). Skill `cache-tracking-prefix-mutation-mutators.md` REWRITTEN to distinguish the two notify primitives (was stale: advocated the `notify_compaction` anti-pattern + referenced the dead `compaction.py:3344` path). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Status.** [PROGRESS: resolved=4 remaining=1]. Remaining = P5 (second stable breakpoint in `llm/cache.py`) — left for owner to weigh as a genuine structural design question.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `notify_compaction` = "an expected FREE prefix DROP happened" (blanket-suppress). `notify_history_rewrite` = "prefix bytes CHANGED and re-bill — NAME it, don't mask it". Never use `notify_compaction` on an in-place prefix edit that re-bills: it hides a recurring cost (the single-source-of-truth-for-cost violation). When suppressing a false-positive log, gate ONLY the anonymous/leading-indicator line on the "cause known" flag — keep the detection state (`_prefix_mutated`) live so the confirmed, attributed break still fires.

Public `window.TofuPet` (react/setActivity/interact/getState/setState/refresh/EXPRESSIONS/frameUrl) + `tofu:activity` / `tofu:react` DOM event seam + localStorage-persisted mood/energy so the future pet system has hooks. Self-driven by the clock + interaction; touches nothing in the chat/streaming pipeline.
- **CSS (`static/styles.css`, tofu-scoped).** `.tofu-pet` + `.tofu-pet-img` with whole-element motion (`tofuPetBreathe` idle; `tofuPetSnooze` when sleepy/sleeping; `tofuPetHop` ×3 on celebrate; `tofuPetJolt` on surprise) — the art carries the sparkles/Zzz, so no more per-part SVG animation. New `[data-theme="tofu"] .project-bar::after` lays the `flower-vine.png` garland into the bar's top-right (pointer-transparent, opacity .85). `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` holds a static frame. Non-tofu themes hide `.tofu-pet` and have no `::after` vine → dark/light bars byte-identical to before.
- **Wiring.** `tofu-pet.js` registered in `lib/js_bundler.py:_BUNDLE_FILES` (after main.js) + `index.html` dev-fallback `<script>`. Assets in `static/icons/pet/` (8 pet frames + vine + sprig).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_tofu_pet.py`, 11, all green).** Runs the REAL module under node with a DOM/Image/localStorage stub (must `process.exit(0)` — the pet's setInterval keeps the loop alive). Asserts: every expression resolves to an art frame that EXISTS on disk; curious→thinking alias frame exists; the FSM at representative hours/moods (deep-night sleeps, night sleepy, morning happy / afternoon idle, low-mood sad, loading→thinking beats the clock, success→celebrating); bundler + index.html registration; NEUTER strips the deep-night `return 'sleeping'` branch → a 2am pet stops sleeping (proves the night test bites). Harness gotcha logged: route `activity` through `setActivity()` (celebrate/surprise live there, not `setState`), and DON'T re-run an empty `setState` afterward (it re-resolves and clobbers the transient reaction).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; tinycss2 0 errors, braces balanced; pet suite 11/11. JS bundle → `bundle-881ceb72.js`, CSS → `styles-88e6099e.css`. Rendered a mock project bar (pet left + vine top-right) — reads as a cared-for little corner, matches the welcome aesthetic. NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart server (import-time bundlers) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a brand mark must be cute AND on-model across many variants, GENERATE a polished base with the image tool then use EDIT mode (`source_image`) to derive each variant changing only the face — hand-drawing look-alikes drifts and reads as ugly (owner rejected 6+ hand-drawn iterations across two sessions). Flat-background generations are made transparent with a corner-seeded flood-fill + auto-crop in PIL. A pre-rendered `<img>`-frame mascot with a small JS state machine is far simpler and prettier than a hand-authored inline-SVG face rig, and leaves a clean `window.TofuPet` + event seam for a fuller pet system later.


### 2026-07-08 — Tool-surface audit tranche 2: fixed the `ask_human` headless task-wedge (the one real correctness defect the audit surfaced beyond tranche 1). Attendance-aware guard mirrors the write-approval gate.
- **Ask (owner).** The audit found `ask_human` blocks INDEFINITELY on a headless/API run with no listener — a task-wedging defect on `/api/v1/agent/run` + the OpenAI/Anthropic compat surfaces + scheduler + swarm sub-agents (all first-class product paths). Fix it root-cause, not by filing an epic.
- **Root cause.** `_handle_ask_human` (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/misc.py`) had two branches: autopilot → VU answers; else → `request_human_guidance(guidance_id, task=task)` which blocks on a 2s abort-poll loop with NO timeout (`lib/tasks_pkg/human_guidance.py:26` — "blocks indefinitely"). On an unattended run nobody ever calls `resolve_human_guidance`, so the turn wedges until the reaper/abort fires. (The reaper heartbeat at human_guidance.py:64 deliberately keeps it ALIVE, so it isn't even reclaimed as stuck.)
- **Fix (attendance-aware, mirrors the write-approval gate).** Confirmed via grep that `task['_attended']=True` is stamped ONLY by the three interactive entry points in `routes/chat.py` (L205/397/798); every headless surface omits it — the exact signal `tool_dispatch.py:956` already uses for the auto-apply default. Added a middle branch: `elif not task.get('_attended'):` → log a warning, set `round_entry['status']='unanswerable'`, finalize the round with an `unanswerable` badge, and return a clear sentinel tool result: *"Cannot ask the user in this execution mode — no interactive session is available to answer. Proceed with your best assumption or use the tools available to you…"*. The autopilot branch is unchanged and still wins (it's the `if` above), and the attended `else` still blocks on the real human wait — the interactive UI path is untouched.
- **Tests (`tests/test_tool_audit_tranche1.py`, +3 = 16 total, all green).** Drives the REAL `_handle_ask_human` with `request_human_guidance` replaced by a TRIPWIRE (records if the blocking wait is entered, returns immediately so the test can't hang) + stubbed finalize/append/meta + autopilot OFF: (a) unattended task → sentinel content + `status=='unanswerable'` + tripwire NOT hit (no block); (b) `_attended=True` task → tripwire HIT (still uses the human wait) + does NOT emit the unattended sentinel (proves the interactive path isn't neutered); (c) neuter guard on the branch marker `elif not task.get('_attended'):` + the `round_entry['status']='unanswerable'` stamp (contiguous source, since the sentinel sentence is split across string-concat).
- **Verify.** AST OK on misc.py. New suite 16/16. No regressions: `test_abort_dangling_tool_round` + `test_project_peer` + `test_refactored_utils` = 73 passed. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server to load new lib/ (import-time).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any indefinite backend block that waits on a human action (`request_human_guidance`, `request_write_approval`, stdin) MUST be attendance-gated on `task['_attended']` — an unattended headless/compat/swarm task has no one to answer and will wedge. The single source of the attended signal is `routes/chat.py`; new blocking-on-human seams should reuse it, never invent a parallel flag. (String-concat-split sentinel sentences also break raw-source neuter greps — assert on a contiguous marker.)

### 2026-07-08 — Chatinner (tofu) typography crispness pass: killed subpixel fringing (auto→antialiased), replaced phantom weights (450→real 400/500), darkened ink (AAA), and adopted Inter as the REAL self-hosted reading body (was a phantom stack entry).

Diagnosis (owner-confirmed against files): tofu forced `-webkit-font-smoothing:auto` (subpixel) at two points over the base `antialiased`; `.md-content{font-weight:450}` had no matching master (Plus Jakarta Sans self-hosted only as discrete 300/400/500/600/700); Inter was named in `--sans-body` but NEVER loaded in `vendor/google-fonts-local.css`, so Plus Jakarta always won. - **Scope.** tofu ONLY. base/light `.md-content` verified already crisp+dark: base uses `antialiased` (styles.css:12), light ink `#272732` on `#f4f2ed` = 13.2:1 and its 420/500 weights snap to real masters — no thin/grayish read → left untouched (no CJK tail touched on any theme).
- **Changes (uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Self-hosted Inter** (`static/vendor/google-fonts-local.css`): added a two-file `@font-face` block (variable weight 100–900) — `fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` (48KB) + `fonts/Inter-latin-ext.woff2` (85KB), downloaded from gstatic (wOF2 magic verified), with the upstream `unicode-range` subsets so latin-ext is fetched only on demand.   - **`--sans-body`** (styles.css:10663): `'Plus Jakarta Sans','Inter',var(--cjk-fallback),…` → `'Inter','Plus Jakarta Sans',var(--cjk-fallback),…` (Inter first, Jakarta retained as fallback, CJK tail intact).
  - **Smoothing** (styles.css:10679 block + :10828): both `-webkit-font-smoothing:auto;-moz-osx-font-smoothing:auto` → `antialiased`/`grayscale`.
  - **Ink** (styles.css:10634): `--text-primary:#373126` (12.04:1) → `#2E2822` (13.6:1) — subtle darkening, comfortably WCAG AAA on `--bg-primary:#FAF7F0`.
  - **Weights**: tofu assistant body `.md-content` `font-weight:450`→`400` (styles.css:10685); user-message body `.md-content.user-content` `450`→`500` (styles.css:10688) — keeps it a touch heavier than the assistant body but now a REAL loaded master, and avoids a new 400/450 split within the same chat. Left the two NON-chatinner 450s (`.paper-qa-msg-content` :2149, a tertiary label :10965) per scope.
- **Tests** (`tests/test_frontend_tofu_typography_crispness.py`, new, 6, env-independent CSS-parse): every tofu `-webkit-font-smoothing` is `antialiased` (+ grayscale companion); tofu `.md-content` weight is a real loaded instance (mult-of-100, not 450); Inter is first in `--sans-body` before Plus Jakarta with the `--cjk-fallback` tail; Inter is self-hosted (`@font-face` + woff2 file on disk). Two NEUTERs (re-poison smoothing→auto and weight→450) both bite. All green.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6896/6896, CJK-fork audit reads **0** raw CJK faces on tofu rules. CSS bundle → **`styles-d333957a.css`** (grep confirms `--sans-body:'Inter',…`, `#2E2822`, `md-content.user-content{font-weight:500}`, `-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased` all survived minify). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) `-webkit-font-smoothing:auto` = subpixel AA → color fringing that reads as "blurry" on dark-ink-over-light-paper; use `antialiased`/`grayscale` for crisp reading surfaces. (2) A `font-weight:NNN` that isn't a loaded master (450 against discrete/variable masters that snap) renders a weight you never chose — always use a real instance.
