### 2026-07-08 — Tool-surface audit tranche 1: fixed 4 verified correctness gaps + 5 doc-drift contradictions across the tool schemas/handlers, batched into one prompt-cache-prefix edit, tested with neuter guards.
- **Ask (owner).** Following a parallel 5-family audit of the ~60-tool surface (report only), implement the verified root-cause fixes in ONE batch (description edits are prompt-cache-prefix bytes — dribbling them across sessions repeatedly busts the ~65k cache prefix). Skip create_memory default-alignment (handler always passes scope → latent, not live).
- **Method.** Audit ran as 5 parallel `reviewer` sub-agents (project-file / search-browser / conv-brain / memory-todo-guidance / swarm-mcp-registry). Every HIGH/MED finding was RE-VERIFIED by direct read before editing — one memory finding (create_memory `scope='global'` backend default) was **downgraded HIGH→LOW** after confirming `handlers/memory.py:24` always passes `scope=fn_args.get('scope','project')`, so the backend default never fires for tool calls.
- **Correctness fixes (root-cause, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  1. **spawn_agents `depends_on` was dead within a single call** (`lib/swarm/tools.py`). The per-agent item schema had no `id` field, so a model could never set an id for a sibling's `depends_on` to reference → backend minted random uuids. Backend at `lib/swarm/integration.py:706` ALREADY honors `agent_def.get('id', uuid…)`, so the fix was purely additive: added an optional `id` string to the item schema (description ties it to `depends_on`). No backend change needed.
  2. **todo_write "exactly one in_progress" not enforced** (`lib/tools/todo.py::_normalize_todos`). The description promised it; nothing enforced it. Added a demotion pass: keep the FIRST in_progress in document order, flip the rest to `pending`, `logger.warning` the demoted count. The list-replace contract was already honored.
  3. **merge_memories silent partial-delete** (`lib/memory/storage.py::merge_memories`). Merged copy is created then originals deleted in a loop; a failed delete was dropped from `deleted_ids` with no log → duplicated content survived silently. Now collects `failed_ids`, `logger.warning`s them (delete_memory already logged the OSError/guard reason), returns `failed_ids` in the result; `handlers/memory.py::_memory_merge` surfaces "⚠️ N source memory(ies) could NOT be deleted" + a "(N kept)" badge so the model sees the half-merge.
  4. **search/fetch batch abort inert** (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/search.py`). `run_batch_concurrent` already accepts an `abort` predicate (short-circuits queued items) but both batch call sites passed none — so the documented "keeps a Stopped task from spraying dozens more searches" protection was dead. Wired `abort=lambda: bool(task.get('aborted'))` into both call sites, matching the `task['aborted']` convention used across orchestrator/endpoint/autopilot.
- **Doc-drift fixes (contradictions between description and real backend behavior).**
  - `run_command` (`lib/tools/project.py`): prose said "Commands run **without a timeout by default**" but the backend (`lib/project_mod/run_command.py:1197`) auto-detects 60s (FS-heavy) / 300s. Rewrote the prose to match the backend + `timeout=0` for genuinely long jobs.
  - Silent batch caps now documented: grep_search/find_files batch = **max 20 entries** (`read_tools.py:MAX_BATCH=20`), apply_diffs/insert_contents = **max 30 per call** (`write_tools.py:MAX_EDITS=30`) — extras were silently dropped. Also documented that `grep_search max_results is ignored in count_only mode` (backend omits `-m` under `-c`).
  - `browser_screenshot` prose said `fullPage=false` but the real param is `full_page`; `browser_hover` told the model to use `time.sleep()` (no Python available to it). Fixed both (`lib/tools/browser.py`).
  - `project_intervene` (`lib/tools/conversation.py`): its advisory path routes through `send_peer_message` sharing the SAME per-(sender,target) 3/120s budget as `project_message` (verified `project_peer.py::intervene_peer` L546-549 → `_rate_gate`), but the description never said so. Added a rate-limit note.
- **Tests (`tests/test_tool_audit_tranche1.py`, 13, all green).** One test per fix + neuter/behavior checks: spawn id-in-schema + backend-honors-id source guard; todo demote-extras + single-untouched + neuter (demotion loop present); merge failed-delete monkeypatched (x ok / y fails → `failed_ids==['y']` + warning) + handler surfaces count; both batch call sites regex-match the `abort=…task.get('aborted')` lambda + the adapter primitive actually short-circuits on `abort=lambda:True` (ran==[]); run_command prose (assembled desc, not raw split source); batch caps + count_only; browser full_page/no-time.sleep; intervene rate-limit note.
- **Verify.** AST-checked all 8 edited files. New suite 13/13. No regressions: `test_todo_continuation` (13) + `test_project_tools` (81) + `test_tool_registry` (16) + `test_swarm_tool_scoping` (14) + `test_memory_global_server_store` (6) = 130 passed; `test_swarm_async` 50 passed (spawn schema change safe). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server to load new lib/ (import-time). Board epic pt_ae25411334604553.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) When a schema advertises a cross-reference field (`depends_on`) but omits the field it references (`id`), the feature is DEAD even though the backend supports it — always check the item schema exposes the referent. (2) A described-but-unenforced contract (todo "one in_progress"), a silently-dropped batch tail (edits>30, queries>20), and an accepted-but-unpassed predicate (`abort`) are three flavors of the same bug class: the description promises behavior the code doesn't wire. (3) Raw-source substring tests break on Python string-concatenation boundaries and multi-line calls — assert against the ASSEMBLED description dict / use DOTALL regex spanning the call.


### 2026-07-08 — Compaction/caching/context-concat design audit: fixed the O(n²) reactive head-truncate + a duplicate per-round token walk + two untraceable debug-level failure logs. Flagged (NOT changed) the higher-risk cache-prefix findings for owner judgment.
- **Ask (owner).** Re-analyze context compression + caching + the "very complex variety of context concatenation" for design flaws causing extra overhead / untraceable logs; fully optimize + test.
- **Method.** Fanned out 3 parallel `coder` audits (compaction / cache / context-concat), then VERIFIED every top finding against the real code before touching anything (sub-agents can misread). Confirmed vs rejected each.
- **FIXED (surgical, uncommitted for owner attribution — all in the compaction subsystem):**
  1. **O(n²) `_head_truncate` (`lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_reactive.py`).** Both trim loops re-summed/re-serialized the ENTIRE message list on every `.pop()` — quadratic on the exact large (MB-scale / near-window) payloads this distress path fires on. Token loop → **exact** running total (`_estimate_total_tokens == sum(_estimate_msg_tokens)`, so subtracting each popped msg is bit-identical to a fresh walk). Byte loop → running wire-byte total (subtract `len(json.dumps(popped))+2` for the `, ` sep; true whole-list value recomputed ONCE after the loop for the log/audit). Guarded by new `test_head_truncate_running_total_matches_full_walk` (asserts impl drop-count + `tokens_after` == naive O(n²) reference, anchor survives).
  2. **Duplicate token walk in `reactive_compact`.** `tokens_before_snap` (pre-archive) and `tokens_before` (Phase 0) were the same value with NO mutation between them (archive is read-only) → walked the whole list twice. Now reuses the snapshot.
  3. **Two untraceable failure logs bumped to `warning`+`exc_info` (CLAUDE.md §2 severity rule):** reactive pre-snapshot archive failure (was `debug` → silent transcript-snapshot loss) and PreCompact-hooks failure in `_pipeline.py` (was `debug` → silent snapshot/archive-hook loss).
- **CONSIDERED-THEN-REVERTED (bad risk/reward).** Audit P2: skip the heuristic-floor walk inside `_count_tokens_authoritative` when far below the gate threshold. Reverted — the floor is the load-bearing anti-FATAL safety (the `force-compact-empty-summary-fatal-loop` memory): heuristic can run ~1.26× the authoritative count, so ANY `< k*threshold` cutoff can drop a case where the floor WOULD have triggered the gate, risking the OOM loop. Saving one O(n) string scan next to a per-round LLM API call is not worth reintroducing that risk. `_tokens.py` is byte-unchanged by me (the `2/1` git-diff there is pre-existing sibling work, not mine).
- **FLAGGED for owner (NOT changed — conflicts with a documented decision or is load-bearing):**
  - **Cache P1 (highest $):** `system_context.py:724` calls `notify_compaction` to silence the prefix-mutation warning when the user-profile block is spliced into `messages[0]`. That sets `compaction_pending=True`, which in `detect_cache_break` suppresses the api_break gate AND the wire-diff — so a genuine full-prefix re-bill on every profile turn is invisible. BUT this is a DOCUMENTED choice (`.tofu/skills/cache-tracking-prefix-mutation-mutators.md`); a fix would route it to `notify_history_rewrite` (labels without suppressing). Needs owner call — do not flip unilaterally.
  - **Cache P5:** `lib/llm/cache.py` tail breakpoint is on a moving message with no SECOND stable breakpoint anchoring the frozen body below the tail → mid-conversation body past system+tools may re-bill on long convs. Structural design question.
  - **Context-concat #2:** `wire_messages.py` inject path has a broad `except`→un-injected messages return (could ship a promptless request); #4 marker-substring dedup could double-inject if compaction rewrites a block's wording. Both plausible but need deeper repro before changing hot assembly code.
- **Verify.** `python -c ast/import` OK on all 3 edited modules. Suites: compaction-improvements + invariants + gate-tokens + usage-counting + longhorizon = **200 passed**; reactive/head-truncate/binary-blob-guard slice = 18 passed. One `test_cache_prefix_stability::test_settled_tail_wire_identical_when_scrolled_into_prefix` failure is **PRE-EXISTING** (proven: fails identically with my two files `git checkout`-reverted; it's a DB-fixture `no such table: conversations` isolation error, unrelated to compaction/cache logic). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The "variety of context concatenation" concern was mostly UNFOUNDED per the audit: `_transform_messages`/`_inject_system_contexts` run ONCE per task (before the round loop), not per-round — no O(n²) whole-history rebuild. The real overhead was the reactive O(n²) truncate. When a hot loop calls a whole-list aggregate (`_estimate_total_tokens`/`json.dumps`) inside a `while ...: pop()`, convert to a running total — but ONLY claim exactness when the aggregate is a pure per-element sum (tokens are; wire-bytes aren't, so that stays an approximation with a single true recompute for the log).


### 2026-07-08 — SoC root-cause: Case-B crash-recovery merge now decides local-vs-server by the SERVER-ISSUED STATUS, not a frontend content-length referee (the last "looks-longer wins" data-conflict in the reconcile path).
