- **Audit (4 parallel coder auditors — streaming/segment render · conversations.js reconcile/merge · constant/threshold copies · broad transform/validation/mechanism).** Every candidate re-verified by hand against source + guard tests. Confirmed KEEP/RESOLVED (do NOT re-flag): `_snapshotLonger`/committedMessage (pinned test_frontend_sse_dispatch #28/#29 + test_committed_message_parity), `_isContentBearing` (pinned test_frontend_autopilot_warmup), segment timeline (renders verbatim from backend `msg.segments`), KEEP_LOCAL fires only on `_hasFreshLocalActivity||_localHasPendingSync`, wall-clock tiebreaker REMOVED, rev-based 409 CAS rebase (executes a server verdict), context-policy/translation-policy/status-cycle all served, `_discard_pretool_prose` lives only in orchestrator.py. GENUINE-but-low-value (logged, not taken this pass): token-total re-derivation triplicated (context-bar.js:118 + finish_info.js:272/694 — but live path already reads server `_liveLastRoundUsage.tokensIn`; persisted `apiRounds` carry only RAW usage so the JS fallback can't be fully removed → display-only, no consistency hazard); crude `/[\u4e00-\u9fff]/` CJK test in main_send_pipeline.js:432 + edit_message.js:177/408 (only gates the local "translating…" spinner); `_PRICING_TIERS_JS` 3.0/15.0 copy in template_actions.js:138 (re-derived server-side as defence-in-depth).
- **The fix I picked (highest value vs "prevent data conflicts"): `static/js/main/main_init_tasks.js` Case-B recovery.** The old code merged the finished-task poll result into the trailing assistant msg with a FRONTEND referee: `if (localContentLen > serverContentLen) KEEP LOCAL; else adopt td.content` (same for thinking), then re-PUT via `syncConversationToServer`. That is the exact "looks-longer wins" data-conflict class the project already retired for the sidebar (`localNewest>serverNewest`): a stale-but-longer local buffer (e.g. prior partial-render IDB cache) WINS over a freshly-committed `done` server tail and gets PUT back, re-clobbering fresh truth. Root cause = conflict resolution decided in JS. Verified `/api/v1/chat/poll/<id>` (routes/chat.py:2043) returns a server-issued `status`. FIX: key the merge on `td.status === 'done'` (settled TERMINAL verdict → adopt the persisted tail VERBATIM even when local is longer); keep-longer-local now survives ONLY as the offline RESCUE when the task did NOT cleanly settle (`interrupted`/crash → local SSE buffer may hold un-acked content the checkpoint lacks). +12 lines net.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_caseb_server_authoritative_merge.py`, 2, node-drives-REAL-initActiveTasks).** conv-done: local LONGER, poll status='done' with a SHORTER canonical tail → server MUST win verbatim (content+thinking). conv-interr: local LONGER, poll status='interrupted' → local MUST be kept (offline rescue). NEUTER reverts the status gate (`_serverSettled = false`) on a COPY → the settled conv wrongly keeps the stale-longer local → invariant FAILS (test bites); + byte-identical-after-neuter assertion on the shipped file. Verify: `node --check` OK; suites caseb-merge 2/2 + casee 2/2 + ghost-tail 1/1 + buried-ghost-sweep 1/1 = 6 passed. `main_init_tasks.js` already in the bundle allowlist (concatenated before main.js) → no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change. NOT committed (owner sign-off).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) VERIFY against code before calling anything a violation — the charter register is months-stale (`tofu-stale-migration-status-docs`); I initially proposed deleting a live+test-pinned function. (2) A crash-recovery merge that picks the winner by `content.length` is a frontend-owned conflict resolution — replace the length compare with the server-issued terminal STATUS as the authority, and demote keep-longer-local to a NOT-cleanly-settled-only offline rescue. Same fix shape as the retired wall-clock tiebreaker.


### 2026-07-08 — Project Brain "Team" panel de-clutter: the nudge composer was OPEN under every peer card (CSS [hidden] cascade defeat), and the peer status line printed the file twice ("editing X · 正在编辑 X").
- **Ask (owner, screenshot).** "The team panel in the project brain is too ugly and needs further optimization." Screenshot showed each conversation card carrying a big open `给这个会话发一条建议…` textarea + 取消/发送 box, and the status line reading `editing static/styles.css · 正在编辑 static/styles.css`.
- **Root cause #1 (composer always open — CSS cascade defeat).** `_buildNudgeAffordance` correctly sets `composer.hidden = true`, but the author rule `.pb-peer-nudge-composer{display:flex}` (styles.css:20683) out-ORDERS the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` at equal specificity → the `[hidden]` attr had NO effect and the composer rendered open under every card. The exact class of bug the project already handles at styles.css:9744 (`.recent-search-clear[hidden]{display:none}`). jsdom tests never caught it — jsdom resolves `.hidden` but does NOT apply external stylesheets. FIX: added `.pb-peer-nudge-composer[hidden]{display:none}` so the attr wins; the composer now stays collapsed behind the "发消息" toggle.
- **Root cause #2 (duplicated file in the "doing" line).** `buildPeerCard` pushed the RAW backend `statusLabel` (already "editing static/styles.css", formed in `lib/presence/registry.py::_status_label`) verbatim AND then ALSO appended `currentFile` re-localized as "正在编辑 static/styles.css" → the file printed twice. FIX: (a) new `_localizeStatusLabel(sl)` in project-brain-peers.js mirrors `ui/tool_rounds.js::_localizePeerStatusLabel` (maps generating/working/idle + "editing X"/"working (phase)" to i18n, unknown passes through) so the label reads in the UI language; (b) only append `currentFile` on its own when `rawLabel.indexOf(currentFile) === -1` (the "editing X" label already carries the file).
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_frontend_peer_nudge_composer_hidden.py` (2, CSS-parse + NEUTER): asserts the `[hidden]{display:none}` rule exists / the guard flips when removed (jsdom can't see this). Existing jsdom suites still green: peer-nudge-composer 2/2 (`composerHiddenInitially===true` unchanged — JS still sets `.hidden`), project-brain-peers 2/2 (roster peer has `currentFile` + no `statusLabel` → still surfaces the file, dedupe path not triggered), peer-stop/header/title 10/10.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6916/6916; JS bundle → `bundle-60421730.js` (`_localizeStatusLabel` ×2 present). styles.css is served DIRECTLY (not bundled) — hard-refresh picks it up; restart server for the JS bundle (import-time bundler). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A `[hidden]`-toggled element that ALSO has an author `display:{flex,block,…}` class rule renders open regardless of the attr — the author rule beats the UA `[hidden]{display:none}` at equal specificity + later source order. Always pair such a class with an explicit `.klass[hidden]{display:none}` (project precedent: styles.css:9744). And never surface a backend status string AND a re-derived field that the string already contains — dedupe by checking the label doesn't already name it.


### 2026-07-08 — project_feed_read activity card: (1) stop showing raw `conv <id>`, (2) show the FULL summary (was truncated mid-word).
- **Ask (owner, screenshot of the feed tool card).** Two complaints: "why is the conv id still being displayed?" and "the text content is not fully displayed".
- **Root cause #1 (raw id).** `_renderFeedActivity` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js:~1017`) computed `who = ev.title || ("conv " + convId.slice(0,8))`. Task-lifecycle events (`started`/`completed`/`aborted`) are emitted by `manager.py:225` + `orchestrator.py:664` with NO `title=` arg → `ev.title` is empty → the raw `conv mrbu4tpo` fallback fired. The sibling peer-delivery card was already routed through `convTitleById`, but the feed card was missed, and the backend `_post_build` never backfilled a title either.
- **Root cause #2 (truncated text).** `emit_project_event` stores a 280-char DISPLAY `summary` (`_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`) and preserves the untruncated text in `payload['summary_full']`. But the feed `_post_build` in `lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/misc.py` forwarded only `ev.get('summary')` (the capped value) → decision/note rows ended mid-word ("…but", "…backen").
- **Fix (uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Backend (`misc.py` `project_feed_read` post_build):** backfill titles for empty-title events via the SAME DB resolver `build_peer_status` uses (`lib.conversations.project_peer._titles_by_conv` → real stored title, else a snippet of the opening user turn — never an id); and forward `payload.summary_full || summary` so the full text renders.
  - **Frontend (`tool_rounds.js` `_renderFeedActivity`):** `who = ev.title || (convId && convTitleById ? convTitleById(convId) : short-id)` — resolves the id to a title client-side too (defense-in-depth for when the backend backfill can't resolve but the conv is loaded in the sidebar), falling back to a short id only when nothing resolves.
- **Tests.** Extended `tests/test_frontend_brain_tool_render.py` harness with a no-title feed event whose `convId` is loaded → asserts the row shows `Overlap Watch Conv` (title) and NOT `conv cdef1234` (raw id). 12 passed (`-p no:napari`). **Backend end-to-end (owner-requested — the frontend jsdom stub alone doesn't prove the SOURCE fix):** added two tests to `tests/test_project_feed_read_tool.py` that drive the REAL `project_feed_read` `_post_build` through `_execute_tool_one` against a live SQLite feed + `conversations` table: (1) seeds a conv row with a genuine stored title, emits a **title-less** `completed` lifecycle event (exactly as `manager.py`/`orchestrator.py` do), asserts `feedActivity.events[0].title == 'Real Stored Title'` (never `conv <id>`); (2) emits an over-`_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` summary, asserts the forwarded `summary` equals the FULL text (not the 280-char cap). Double-neuter confirmed: disabling the title-backfill line and the `summary_full` forward each fails its test; restored byte-identical (0 NEUTER markers, 660 lines). Suite 16 passed (`-p no:napari`).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; backend import OK (`_titles_by_conv` callable). JS bundle → `bundle-60421730.js` (grep confirms `convTitleById(ev.convId)` survived minify ×1). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any card that renders a `conv_id` must route it through `convTitleById` (frontend) AND backfill via `_titles_by_conv` (backend) — a raw id is meaningless to a human, and this is a recurring bug class (peer-delivery card fixed earlier, feed card missed). When a store keeps a capped DISPLAY value + a full copy in `payload['summary_full']`, downstream consumers must forward the full copy or text truncates mid-word.


### 2026-07-08 — Autopilot "no longer generates reports" was a LOST DISPLAY AFFORDANCE, not a generation regression: re-homed the run close-out report button onto the concluding VU turn's action bar (the 2026-07-07 flatten deleted the run-fold that used to carry it).
- **Ask (owner).** "Why does it seem like the autopilot mode no longer generates reports?" Independently confirmed: `_openApSummaryModal` / `_apRunSummary` / `_summarizeAutopilotRun` sat in `static/js/ui/chat_render.js` as DEFINITIONS with ZERO callers, and the `apf-report-btn` markup that invoked them was gone — while the backend is demonstrably still writing reports to `settings.autopilotSummaries[runId].content` on every clean TASK_DONE (`logs/app.log`: dozens of "Summary report ready (N chars)" + "✅ Stored concluded run record in sidecar" today).
- **Root cause (diagnosed, not guessed).** The 2026-07-07 "flatten" (owner directive, option A) deleted the `autopilot-run-fold` `<details>` card so each VU turn regains its own delete button. That fold's summary header was the ONLY place the "查看报告 / View report" (+ manual-stop "Summarize this run") button rendered (added 2026-07-02). Removing the fold removed the button; the functions it called were left as dead code (the flatten journal entry itself flagged them as "dead but harmless, prune later"). Net: report generated + persisted, but no affordance to open it → reads as "reports stopped".
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`, render-layer only, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Owner-chosen placement: the report entry point is now a PER-TURN action-bar button on the run's CONCLUDING VU turn, alongside copy/translate/delete.
  - New `_isRunConcludingTurn(conv, msg)`: true iff `msg` is the NEWEST message stamped with its `_autopilotRunId`. Because only VU turns carry `_autopilotRunId` (never agent follow-ups — verified autopilot.py:1260) and a newer run / real user msg carries a DIFFERENT (or no) run id, "newest turn with this runId" is the correct owner even when superseded — NO run-boundary sibling-walk reintroduced (that walk was exactly what the flatten removed, and it historically swallowed the following human turn).
  - New `_apRunReportAffordance(conv, msg)`: gated on the concluding turn + the backend-authoritative concluded record (`_apRunRecord(...).status==='concluded'`). Report present (clean task_done) → `.ap-report-btn` → `_openApSummaryModal(runId)`; concluded + `reason==='stopped'` + no content (manual stop) → `.ap-summarize-btn` → `_summarizeAutopilotRun(runId,this)`; running/un-concluded → nothing. Inline SVG document glyphs per §3.4 (no emoji). Wired into the `.message-actions` template between translate and export. Buttons reuse the existing `.msg-action-btn` base class → no new CSS.
  - `_summarizeAutopilotRun` was NOT on `window` (only `_openApSummaryModal` was) — inline onclick runs in global scope, so added `window._summarizeAutopilotRun = …` (would've been a ReferenceError otherwise). Both previously-dead functions are now genuinely invoked.
- **Known gap (flagged, not silently dropped).** If a run's report exists in `settings.autopilotSummaries[runId]` but NONE of its VU turns survive in the loaded message window (e.g. compaction dropped them), there is no turn to hang the button on and the report is currently unreachable from the transcript. The RECORD is not lost (still in settings); a future run-index surface could reach it — out of scope today. Documented in `_apRunReportAffordance`'s docstring.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_autopilot_report_affordance.py`, new; jsdom drives REAL `renderMessage`).** Case A clean task_done → `.ap-report-btn` wired to `_openApSummaryModal('R1')`, no summarize btn, modal fn exposed; Case B manual stop (concluded, no content) → `.ap-summarize-btn` wired to `_summarizeAutopilotRun('R2',this)`, no view-report, fn exposed on window; Case C running/no-record → NEITHER; Case D superseded run (two VU turns share R4) → only the NEWEST turn owns the button. NC neuter: strip `${apReportH}` from the action-bar template on a COPY → Case A presence assertion FAILS (load-bearing). 13 checks green.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK on chat_render.js. Suites: report-affordance 2/2 + `test_frontend_autopilot_flat_render.py` 3/3 = 5 passed. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-27ac1b67.js`; grep of built bundle confirms survived minify: `ap-report-btn` ×1, `ap-summarize-btn` ×1, `_openApSummaryModal(` ×2, `_summarizeAutopilotRun(` ×2, `_apRunReportAffordance`/`_isRunConcludingTurn` ×2 each, `window._summarizeAutopilotRun` ×1. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (content-hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a feature "stops appearing" but its backend is demonstrably still running, suspect a deleted DISPLAY AFFORDANCE before a generation regression — grep for the functions that render/open it and check for ZERO callers (dead-but-defined). A "prune later" leftover from a UI restructure (here the flatten's orphaned fold helpers) is the classic tell. Re-home such an affordance onto a REAL message keyed by an explicit id stamp (`_autopilotRunId`) rather than re-deriving structural boundaries — it survives surgical re-render and needs no fragile sibling-walk.


### 2026-07-08 — Composer toolbar redesign: moved the awkward floating attach button INTO the toolbar (leftmost), and DELETED the confusing "···" overflow submenu by folding its 2 launchers into the 工具 (Tools) submenu.
- **Ask (owner, screenshot).** "Let's redesign the tool layout in the input box; it's a bit too cluttered right now, and the attach-file button on the left doesn't look good either. Also, the three dots (···) are too confusing for users to understand."
- **Three concrete problems fixed (index.html + styles.css, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  1. **Attach button floated top-left beside the textarea** — it was the first child of `.input-row` (`index.html`), so the 📎 sat awkwardly at the top-left corner of the text field. MOVED it out of `.input-row` (textarea is now a clean full-width field) and made it the LEFTMOST control inside `.input-actions` — the conventional "+" attach spot. Every control now lives in one toolbar row.
  2. **The "···" overflow submenu was a mystery button** — `#submenuMore` was an icon-only `···` trigger holding just 2 one-shot launchers (image/creative mode + project assistant). Users couldn't tell what it did. DELETED `#submenuMore` entirely; folded its two launchers into the existing **工具 (Tools)** submenu below a new `.submenu-divider` (toggles above the divider, one-shot launchers below). Relabeled the image-gen launcher from the ambiguous "AI 绘图" (which collides with the "AI 绘图" *tool toggle* already in Tools) to **"创作模式 / Creative Mode"** so the two are distinguishable.
  3. **Toolbar clutter** — visible row is now `[+] [Model▾] [增强▾] [工具▾] [模式▾] … [🎤] [Search] [→]` with NO mystery dots.
- **ID preservation (load-bearing).** Kept the element IDs `imageGenModeBtn` / `projectToggle` on the folded-in `.submenu-item`s, because `main.js:448 _applyImageGenUI` (optional-chained `.active` toggle) and `project.js:854 _updateProjectUI` (`toggle.classList.remove/add("active")`, UN-guarded → would throw if the id vanished) both reference them. Their `onclick` now closes `submenuTools` instead of the deleted `submenuMore` (`toggleSubmenu('submenuTools');enterImageGenMode()` / `…;openProjectModal()`).
- **CSS.** Removed the now-dead `.submenu-trigger-icon` variant + the `#submenuMore .submenu-dropdown` right-anchor rules (only the deleted overflow used them). Added `.submenu-divider{height:1px;margin:5px 8px;background:var(--border-light)}`. Aligned the desktop `.attach-btn` from 34px→**32px** (radius 10→8) to match the toolbar band (mic/send/triggers are 32px). Mobile block: dropped `#submenuMore` from the submenu hide-list; re-tuned the mobile `.attach-btn` (was `align-self:flex-end;margin:0 0 2px 4px` as a `.input-row` child → now `margin:0;flex-shrink:0` as a toolbar child, still 40px square).
- **i18n.** Added `toolbar.attachFiles` (附加文件…) for the attach title + `toolbar.creativeMode`/`toolbar.creativeModeDesc` (创作模式 / 切换到图像创作画布) for the relabeled launcher. i18n key-coverage ratchet green.
- **Tests.** Rewrote `test_frontend_toolbar_declutter.py` part #2 (jsdom): launchers now asserted INSIDE `#submenuTools` (`igInTools`/`projInTools`), `#submenuMore` asserted GONE (`moreGone`), toggle drives `submenuTools`. Deleted the obsolete `test_overflow_dropdown_is_right_anchored` from `test_frontend_submenu_dropdown_style.py` (it targeted the removed `#submenuMore .submenu-dropdown` rule; the other 4 style invariants stay). Depth-footer-survives-rebuild (#1) unchanged.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6834/6834; `node -e require('jsdom')` harness OK. CSS bundle → `styles-739ea29b.css`, JS bundle → `bundle-5fccc191.js`; grep of built files: `submenuMore` ×0 in JS bundle, `submenu-divider` ×1 + `submenu-trigger-icon` ×0 in CSS bundle, `creativeMode` present. Suites: toolbar-declutter 2/2 + submenu-style 4/4 + i18n-coverage 8/8 + voice-input 1/1 + composer-floor 2/2 + icon-box 8/8 = **24 passed** (`-p no:napari`). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filenames) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An icon-only "···" overflow that holds only 1–2 items is worse than no overflow — users can't predict its contents; fold those items into an already-labeled sibling submenu under a divider instead. When RELOCATING a toolbar control keep its element id if any handler references it un-guarded (`project.js:854`) — a moved-but-same-id node keeps every `getElementById`/`.classList` caller working. When a folded-in launcher's default label collides with an existing toggle's label ("AI 绘图" appeared twice in Tools), rename the launcher to a distinct concept ("创作模式") so the menu isn't ambiguous.


### 2026-07-08 — Two assistant-turn header fixes: (1) learned/updated preferences now fold into the quiet turn-provenance strip like memory activity (was a prominent standalone box); (2) parallel-batch header swapped the fork-icon/round-number order so the round number leads.
- **Ask (owner, two screenshots).** (1) "Updating preferences is like updating memories — just use a tool to display them" (the "已记住: …" box read as a loud standalone card while a written memory is quiet/collapsible). (2) In the "N 个并行调用" header the fork icon sat BEFORE the round number "1"; the two should be swapped (round number first).
- **#1 root cause (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`).** `renderPreferenceLearnedHtml` rendered EVERY learned item (informational `added`/`reinforced` AND actionable `pending`) into a prominent `.pref-learned-box` above the tool panel. But auto-applied consolidation facts are purely informational — same status as a written memory — and memory activity already folds into the quiet collapsible `renderTurnProvenanceHtml` strip as a `tp-seg` segment. So preferences were louder than memories for equivalent information.
- **#1 fix.** New `_prefsLearnedSegment(learned)` (filters to `!p.pending` informational rows) wired into the `renderTurnProvenanceHtml` seg list (after `_prefsAppliedSegment`): collapsed = `check` icon + "记住 N 条偏好" label; expanded detail = a `.pa-list` bullet list with a bold lead-in ("已记住"/"已更新你的偏好档案") + inline-markdown summaries via the existing `_tpInlineMd`. `renderPreferenceLearnedHtml` trimmed to render ONLY actionable `pending` rows (the legacy propose-then-confirm gate with Confirm/Dismiss); returns `""` when there are none, so purely-informational turns no longer show the box at all. i18n: `prefs.learnedTagN`/`Ns`/`learnedHeadline` (zh+en). CSS: `.tp-seg-prefs-learned`/`.tp-detail-prefs-learned`/`.pl-seg-lead` sharing the teal preference accent (+ tofu/light overrides).
- **#2 fix.** In `_renderTurnHead` (single source — the streaming sync path in `streaming_ui.js` reuses it), swapped `${_turnForkSvg}${rnoHtml}` → `${rnoHtml}${_turnForkSvg}` so the round number renders before the fork glyph. One-line, no CSS change (`.ptool-turn-head` is a flex row with `gap`).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK on both JS files. Extended `tests/test_frontend_provenance_strip_render.py` with Case 5: informational learned prefs appear as `tp-seg-prefs-learned` in the strip (bold markdown rendered, no literal `**`), the box returns `""` for informational-only, and a `pending` row DOES render in the box with Confirm/Dismiss while informational rows are NOT duplicated there. Suites: provenance-strip + tool-completion + streaming-ui + i18n-key-coverage + autopilot-flat-render = 14 passed. JS bundle → `bundle-5fd1f724.js`; CSS bundle → `styles-b91a1ef8.css` (grep confirms `tp-seg-prefs-learned` survived minify); tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6837/6837. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Auto-applied "learned" facts (preferences, and any future consolidation output) are INFORMATIONAL and belong in the quiet turn-provenance strip alongside memory activity — a prominent standalone box should be reserved for ACTIONABLE affordances (a `pending` propose-then-confirm row). Filter the informational rows into a `tp-seg` segment and keep the loud box for what the user must decide on.


### 2026-07-08 — Project Brain gains a SEVENTH pillar: the human↔brain status lane (increment 1 — read-only synthesis).


### 2026-07-08 — Pillar #7 increment 2: the WATCH lane — a standing "things I care about" list (concern/question/goal) the brain addresses on a recurring basis, with an append-only response trail and a single human-gated promote-to-charter bridge to agents.
- **Ask (owner).** "A place to input the things I care about, questions, and goals, and see the brain attending to them on a recurring basis." Distinct from increment 1's ephemeral Ask (one-shot, unpersisted) and from the Charter (coarse durable intent). Owner locked 3 decisions: (1) human-facing-only + ONE explicit bridge = promote-to-charter (the only path to agents; routes through the human-gated charter commit; no auto-steer/new-write/fan-out); (2) append-only response trail per item (a concern's answer changing over time is the signal); (3) cadence = on-tab-open + event-driven now, closed-panel scheduler DEFERRED.
- **What shipped (uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Schema:** `project_watch_items` (human input — TEXT PK `item_id`; kind concern|question|goal; status open|resolved; `promoted`; `response_fingerprint` for the staleness gate) + `project_watch_responses` (append-only, composite PK `(item_id, seq)`, monotonic per-item seq, bounded `_RESPONSES_KEEP=100` prune-on-insert). Both in Core `_core_schema.py` + created in sqlite/pg bootstraps w/ indexes. Placed AFTER `PROJECT_STATUS_SNAPSHOTS`'s closing `)` (heeding the increment-1 insert-split trap) — PROJECT_TASKS re-verified intact.
  - **Core (`lib/conversations/project_watch.py`):** human CRUD + `address_watch_item` (reuses `collect_pillar_state` + the SAME `_fingerprint` gate + `_build_synthesis_source` from the status lane — no second aggregation; per-kind system prompt: question→answer, concern→at-risk assessment, goal→progress+alignment) + `address_open_items` (recurring, non-blocking daemon) + `promote_watch_item` (the bridge → `commit_charter`, adds `[Goal/Concern/Question — promoted by owner] <text>`; failed/skewed commit does NOT flag promoted).
  - **REST:** `GET /brain/watch` (refresh=1 re-addresses open items = fresh-on-open), `POST /brain/watch/{add,update,address,promote}`. api.js: `brainWatchList/Add/Update/Address/Promote`.
  - **Triggers:** the SAME board-event + charter-commit hooks that warm the status snapshot now ALSO `address_open_items(blocking=False)`.
  - **Frontend:** watch lane appended to the Status tab (`project-brain-status.js`) — kind-select+text composer, per-item card (kind badge, latest response + meta, collapsed older-response trail, actions: Re-check/Promote-to-charter/Resolve↔Reopen/Delete). Exposed `_boardConvId` from project-brain.js so the watch lane reuses the same conv-id source as board mutations. 17 i18n keys (EN+ZH), CSS block appended.
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_watch_lane.py`, 10, all green).** CRUD+validation; **live-state NEUTER** (stub `_build_synthesis_source`→ live north-star/epic vanish from the item prompt — manually confirmed the real path carries them + neuter drops them); append-only trail + retention prune + monotonic newest-first + staleness gate (no LLM when unchanged, re-synth when pillar-state moves); edit-text-forces-readdress; **promote calls charter commit not the agent path** (fake `commit_charter` spy asserts project_path + `[Goal…]` decision text; item flagged promoted) + version-conflict propagation (item NOT flagged); **human-facing-only source guard** (system_context.py references none of project_watch/address_watch_item/list_watch_items/add_watch_item/generate_item_response).
- **Verify.** Ruff clean; **116 passed** (watch 10 + status-lane 14 + status-tab-refresh 6 + core-schema-parity 52 + peer 26 + context-trace 8). JS bundle → `bundle-60421730.js` (`brainWatchPromote`×2, `buildWatchItem`×3, `pbWatchSection`×3), CSS → `styles-1ae4f09e.css` (`pb-watch-*` present). system_context.py has ZERO watch refs.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A durable human-input list that the brain addresses recurringly must (1) reuse the existing pillar-state assembly + staleness gate (never a second aggregation, and free on a quiescent project), (2) keep an append-only per-item trail (drift is the signal), and (3) reach agents ONLY through the existing human-gated charter-commit bridge — never a new write path. The human-facing-only invariant is enforced by a source-grep test, same as the status memory.

### 2026-07-08 — Pillar #7 follow-up: fresh-on-tab-open was actually fresh-on-PANEL-open. Owner caught that clicking the Status tab only toggled CSS visibility and never re-fetched — closed the gap against decision #4.
- **Ask (owner, verify pass).** Decision #4 required a fresh read on tab-open so status is never stale. But `_refreshStatus` fired only on whole-panel open + project-switch; `_selectTab('status')` just toggled `pb-tab-panel-active` visibility. Repro: open Brain on Charter, sit while siblings finish epics, click Status → see the panel-open snapshot, not a fresh read. Real stale-status case the owner works hard to avoid (drifting facts).
- **Fix (`static/js/project-brain.js`, uncommitted for owner attribution).** `_selectTab` now captures `prev = _state.tab` and calls a new `_onTabSelected(name, prev)` hook at the end; the hook re-fetches via `_refreshStatus(_state.path || _displayedProjectPath())` ONLY when switching INTO status (`name==='status' && prev!=='status'`) — so unrelated tab clicks and re-selecting an already-active Status tab never re-fetch. Cheap by design: the backend staleness gate returns the cached snapshot with NO LLM on a quiescent project, so triggering on every status-tab-entry costs nothing on a quiet project but always reflects sibling progress made while the user was on another tab.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_status_tab_refresh.py`, 6, node-extract-and-eval of the REAL `_selectTab`+`_onTabSelected`).** selecting-into-status refreshes; unrelated tab click does NOT; re-selecting status (prev===name) is a no-op; switch-away-then-back refreshes AGAIN (the drift case); empty `_state.path` falls back to `_displayedProjectPath()`; NEUTER strips the `_onTabSelected(name, prev);` call from `_selectTab` → a status click triggers no refresh (bug returns). All green + neuter bites.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; status+tab+cascade+peer suites 49 passed; JS bundle → `bundle-e3d0beca.js` (`_onTabSelected` present ×2 = source+minified).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Fresh on open" for a tab inside a multi-tab panel means fresh on TAB-SELECTION, not just panel-open — tab switching is usually pure CSS visibility toggling with no re-fetch. Gate the re-fetch on switching INTO the tab (`prev!==name`) so unrelated tab clicks don't thrash the backend; a cheap backend staleness gate makes the on-select re-fetch free on a quiescent project.
 Closes "human perception diminishes as automation increases": ask the PROJECT where it is / whether it's drifting, backed by an append-only trail of synthesized status snapshots.
- **Ask (owner).** The Brain makes N conversations feel like one mind, but it "cannot connect with humans" — as automation increases the human loses sight of where the project is / whether it tracks their goal. Wanted (a) a way to talk to the unified brain and (b) better persistent memory so that conversation reflects real-time, comprehensive project status. Owner locked 4 decisions: (1) read-only synthesis FIRST (propose-actions is a separate later increment; never a new inter-conv write; the ratified no-fan-out decision stands); (2) a new Brain TAB (primary) + a one-line status in the always-visible collab-bar (ambient); (3) APPEND-ONLY history of status snapshots (the human works with facts that drift — needs the trail, not one overwritten narrative); (4) regenerate BOTH event-driven (epic done / decision committed / blocked) AND fresh-on-open (staleness gate). Hard constraint: HUMAN-FACING ONLY — never in the system-context ambient prompt-injection path.
- **The gap (named precisely).** The collab-bar summary (`build_brain_summary`) is only a COUNTS aggregation; per-conv summaries (`project_summary`) are never synthesized into a project-level "where are we". The Charter is durable memory of INTENT; the Feed is a raw ephemeral pulse. Nothing accumulates STATUS.
- **What shipped (increment 1, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Store (append-only):** new Core table `project_status_snapshots` (composite PK `(project_path, seq)`, monotonic per-project seq minted under a module lock — mirrors `project_events` exactly), created in `_schema_sqlite.py` + `_schema_pg.py` with an index; bounded retention (`_SNAPSHOTS_KEEP=200`, prune-on-insert). Each row: narrative + `pillar_state` JSON EVIDENCE (epic open/claimed/done/blocked counts, in-flight epics+owners, pending decisions, charter version, active peers, recent blocks, sibling digest) + trigger + ts.
  - **Generator (`lib/conversations/project_status.py`):** `collect_pillar_state` reads LIVE state across all six pillars (board/charter/pending/presence/feed/digest) — same cross-pillar assembly `build_brain_summary` uses. `build_status_snapshot` gates on a cheap fingerprint (reuse `ensure_summary` laziness — NO LLM when quiescent), then a bounded cheap-model synthesis produces the narrative + explicit alignment-to-north-star DRIFT read. Best-effort, never raises; keeps prior snapshot on LLM failure. `answer_status_question` = read-only Q&A (writes NOTHING). `status_line` = first sentence of latest, for the bar.
  - **Triggers (non-blocking, daemon):** `complete_task`/`block_task` (project_board.py, via `_fire_status_snapshot`) + `commit_charter` (project_charter.py) fire `build_status_snapshot(..., blocking=False)` — a settled action leaves a fresh status without waiting on an LLM. `build_brain_summary` now also carries `statusLine` for the collab-bar.
  - **REST (all read-only):** `GET /api/v1/project/brain/status` (fresh-on-open via staleness gate → latest + history), `GET .../status/history` (trail, no synthesis), `POST .../status/ask` (read-only Q&A).
  - **Frontend:** new "Status" tab (`data-pb-tab=status`) in the Brain panel; `static/js/project-brain-status.js` (registered in `_BUNDLE_FILES` after peers, before the i18n overlay; script tag in index.html) renders latest narrative + evidence chips + a read-only ask composer + the history trail; wired into `openProjectBrain`/`projectBrainRefresh` via `_refreshStatus`. 21 i18n keys (EN+ZH). CSS block appended (tofu vars, no new !important).
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_status_lane.py`, 14, all green).** collect reads all pillars + degrades when one raises; **synthesis prompt carries the LIVE north-star + in-flight epic title** (proves not a stub) + its **NEUTER** (empty/stubbed state → live values vanish, "no charter" marker appears — manually confirmed the stub also drops the north-star from the real prompt and restore re-inserts it); staleness gate elides the LLM when unchanged + re-synthesizes when pillar-state moves + force bypass; append-only monotonic seq + newest-first history + retention prune; **ask is READ-ONLY (appends no snapshot)**; status_line = first sentence; **no-ambient-injection SOURCE guard** (system_context.py must not reference the status module / its entry points).
- **Verify.** Ruff clean (9 files). Suites: status 14/14 + core-schema-parity 52/52 + peer 26/26 + bundle-corruption-guard 12/12 + context-trace 8/8 = 112 passed. Core DDL round-trips on sqlite; `PROJECT_TASKS` intact (12 cols, correct order) after a mid-edit insert-split was repaired. JS bundle → `bundle-5fd1f724.js` (status module + `brainStatusAsk` present), CSS → `styles-b91a1ef8.css` (`pb-status-narrative` present). Design doc `docs/PROJECT_BRAIN_STATUS_LANE.md`; charter amendment proposed for the record.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) When inserting a new `define_table(...)` block via an anchor, place it AFTER the previous table's closing `)` — an anchor that lands mid-column-list splits the prior table (orphaned `created_at`/`updated_at` → SyntaxError). Always re-verify the neighbor table's columns after such an insert. (2) The status memory is the seam where the human↔brain lane must NOT blur into agent↔agent: the no-ambient-injection guarantee is enforced by a source-grep test on system_context.py, not just convention. (3) Reuse `ensure_summary`'s fingerprint-laziness for any event-driven LLM-backed cache so a quiescent project costs nothing.


### 2026-07-08 — Tofu tool-round cards read as "shallow, one-sided depth": replaced the directional light-TL/dark-BR bevel + near-invisible clay-sm shadow with a uniform border + all-around enclosing shadow.
- **Ask (owner, screenshot of the tool panel).** "The tool invocation might look better if it's fully enclosed. Currently the shadow is deepened only on the right and bottom sides, the separation feels too shallow, a bit tiring to look at."
- **Root cause (`static/styles.css:13428`, `[data-theme="tofu"] .ptool-turn`).** The round card used a deliberate DIRECTIONAL bevel — `border-top/left-color:#FFFCF6` (lit) + `border-right/bottom-color:#B8AE98` (dark) — which by construction draws depth only on the right+bottom edges (a raised-chip look), and paired it with `box-shadow:var(--clay-sm)` = `0 1px 2px rgba(92,72,44,0.05)`, far too faint to separate the card from the parchment. So each card looked half-framed and barely detached → the "shallow, one-sided, tiring" read.
- **Fix (CSS-only, tofu-scoped, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Dropped the 4-color bevel for a single uniform `border:1px solid #D6CCB8`, and replaced the faint shadow with a THREE-layer enclosing stack: `0 0 0 1px rgba(196,149,106,0.05)` (an even hairline ring wrapping all four sides equally = the "fully enclosed" feel) + `0 2px 6px rgba(92,72,44,0.09)` + `0 5px 16px rgba(92,72,44,0.06)` (two soft warm drops that ground the card and deepen separation without hard offsets). Symmetric on every side now, calmer in a long panel. Only the tofu block touched; base/light `.ptool-turn` (styles.css:7117/7168) unchanged.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6837/6837. CSS bundle → `styles-d44646d9.css` (grep confirms the new 3-layer shadow survived minify and the old bevel color `#B8AE98` is gone, count 0). Coordinated around 3 live siblings churning styles.css (composer/submenu regions ~L495-720/L11266/L13189/L16550) — no overlap with the L13428 card block; took + released a `project_claim_path` lease on it. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A light-TL/dark-BR 4-color border bevel puts depth on exactly TWO edges — it reads as a one-sided lift, never as "enclosed". For a card that should look fully wrapped, use a uniform border + a symmetric `0 0 0 1px` ring (all four sides) plus soft centered drops; reserve directional bevels for genuinely raised/pressed affordances (buttons), not passive content tiles.


### 2026-07-08 — Collapsed project-rail selection ring vanished when a folder had a GENERATING conversation (tofu-theme box-shadow animation clobbered the ring), + default (未分类) tile de-clashed: glyph enlarged and set to blink.
- **Ask (owner).** Two things about the sidebar folder rail: (1) the collapsed rail draws the selected folder with a big circle, but "if a conversation is being generated inside a folder, selecting this folder won't show a circle"; (2) the default folder's style clashes with the others — enlarge its SVG logo and let the icon blink.
- **Root cause #1 (CSS animation clobber, tofu-theme-specific).** The collapsed-rail "selected" ring was `box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--bg-tertiary),0 0 0 4px var(--accent)` on `.folder-tab.active .folder-tab-dot` (styles.css:132 desktop + :163 drawer). When a folder has a live conversation the dot gains `.streaming`; under the **tofu** theme streaming runs `tofuBreathing` (styles.css:10585-10590) which ANIMATES `box-shadow` — an active animation wins over the static declaration, so the selection ring was entirely replaced by the pulse glow → the circle disappeared. (Dark theme's `folderDotPulse` only animates opacity, so it never hit this — a tofu-only failure.) FIX: draw the ring with `outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px` — no keyframe touches `outline`, so the ring survives streaming on every theme. Applied at both ring sites (base + drawer block).
- **Root cause #2 (visual clash).** The 未分类 home tile's inner glyph was 12px in a 20px `folder-tab-inbox-dot` while project tiles are bold colored monograms → it read as flat/dead. FIX: enlarged `.folder-tab-inbox-dot svg` to 15px (18px in collapsed rail) and added `@keyframes folderInboxBlink{0%,88%,100%{opacity:1}94%{opacity:0.3}}` (4.8s loop) so it periodically blinks and reads "alive". No conflict with the pulse animations: the blink targets the inner `svg`; the pulse targets the `.folder-tab-dot` container; and the inbox row (`data-folder-id=""`) never enters `streamingFolderIds` (conversation_list.js:367 `continue` on `!c.folderId`), so its dot never gets `.streaming`.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6806/6806; CSS bundle → `styles-55291add.css` (grep confirms both the `folderInboxBlink` keyframe/usage AND the two `outline:2px solid var(--accent)` ring rules survived minify). Guard suites: `test_frontend_project_rail` 6/6, `test_frontend_portrait_rail_expandable` 3/3, `test_frontend_rail_cls` 3/3 = 12 passed. New `tests/test_frontend_folder_ring_and_inbox.py` 5/5 (env-independent CSS-parse): ring uses outline not box-shadow at both sites; inbox glyph blinks + keyframe defined; inbox glyph enlarged past 12px; + two NCs (poison the ring back to box-shadow → flagged; strip the blink → flagged). CSS-only change — no JS/bundle-allowlist impact. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A static ring/border drawn with `box-shadow` is SILENTLY DEFEATED when the SAME element also runs a keyframe animation that sets `box-shadow` (the animation's computed value always wins) — and this can be theme-specific (tofu's `tofuBreathing` animates box-shadow; the dark theme's opacity-only pulse does not, so it hides in one theme only). Draw persistent state rings with `outline` (which no animation here touches) so they coexist with a pulsing/breathing element.


### 2026-07-08 — Portrait-tablet reading mode: restored the TOC, killed the pointless horizontal swipe, and clamped glossary hover-cards into the column (no more drag-to-read)
- **Ask (owner, screenshots of the report reader on a large portrait tablet).** Three complaints: (1) the table of contents doesn't show at all; (2) it still allows left-right swiping, which is pointless in single-pane; (3) the swipe-able overflow causes term-definition hover-cards to render off to the right, needing a drag to read them fully.
- **Root causes (three symptoms, two roots).**
  1. **No TOC** — the enhanced report grid `.paper-report-doc > .paper-report-toc` is hidden by `@media(max-width:900px)` (styles.css:2504-2507), which correctly drops the sidebar on a narrow *handset* but ALSO swallows a ~820px portrait tablet. On a coarse-pointer tablet the reader single-panes to the FULL viewport width (the `≤768 ∪ (≤1024 ∧ coarse)` block), so there's ample room for the contents nav — it was just being suppressed.
  2. **Pointless swipe + card off-right (ONE root)** — the reader prose panes `.paper-report-content`/`.paper-report-body` are `overflow-y:auto`, which computes `overflow-x` to `auto`. The glossary hover-card (`.paper-term-card`, `position:absolute; left:0; max-width:320px`) overflows the right edge for any term near the right of a narrow column → the pane became horizontally scrollable (the "pointless swiping") AND the card rendered in that off-screen region (needing a drag).
- **What shipped (`static/styles.css` + `static/js/paper-reader.js`, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Kill the swipe** — `overflow-x:hidden` added to BOTH `.paper-report-content` and `.paper-report-body` scroll rules (styles.css:1268-1269). Now a wide child is clipped, not swipe-revealed.
  - **Restore the TOC on the tablet band** — new `@media(min-width:769px) and (max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` block placed AFTER the `max-width:900px` collapse (source order → wins): re-grids `.paper-report-doc` to `1fr minmax(150px,190px)` (slightly narrower sidebar than desktop's 216px) and sets `.paper-report-doc > .paper-report-toc{display:block}`. The existing sticky-TOC + scroll-spy machinery just works.
  - **Clamp the hover-card** — since overflow is now clipped, a right-edge card would be half-hidden. New `_positionGlossaryCard(term)` (paper-reader.js, before the model-dropdown outside-click listener) runs on reveal via delegated `mouseover`/`focusin`: measures the term + scroller rects + card `offsetWidth`, shifts the card left by a negative inline `left` just enough to sit inside the scroller content box (8px margin), clamped so it never overshoots. Recomputed every reveal (widths change with the EN/中 toggle + font-scale). Left-edge terms get no shift.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_portrait_tablet_chat_reading.py` +4 (now 19): `test_reader_panes_clip_horizontal_overflow` (BOTH scroll rules are `overflow-x:hidden` — scans all rules for the `overflow-y:auto` one, not the earlier `--reader-measure` combined rule), `test_tablet_portrait_reveals_report_toc` (band block sets the TOC `display:block`), + two neuters (strip `overflow-x:hidden` / flip TOC to `display:none` on a COPY → invariant FAILS). New `tests/test_frontend_paper_glossary_card_clamp.py` (2, jsdom extraction-and-eval): drives the REAL `_positionGlossaryCard` — a right-edge term's card is shifted left inside the scroller, a left-edge term's card is not shifted; neuter (no-op the fn on a COPY) → the right-edge clamp FAILS, shipped file byte-identical after.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6801/6801; CSS bundle → `styles-eefcb7f6.css` (grep confirms `overflow-y:auto;overflow-x:hidden` ×2 + the tablet TOC reveal survived minify); JS feature bundle → `feature-1595e5c5.js` (paper-reader.js is a `_DEFERRED_FILES` module; grep confirms `_positionGlossaryCard` ×3). Suites: portrait-tablet 15/15 → 19/19, glossary-clamp 2/2, + reading-anchor / reader-prefs / paper-mobile-responsive unaffected = **23 passed**. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A `max-width:900px` phone collapse of an enhanced grid ALSO hits a portrait tablet that single-panes full-width — re-show the collapsed sidebar in a `min-width:769 ∧ …coarse` block AFTER it (source order) to reclaim the tablet's room. (2) `overflow-y:auto` implies `overflow-x:auto` — an absolutely-positioned child overflowing the right edge silently makes the pane horizontally swipe-able; pin `overflow-x:hidden` when you don't want that, then any popover that would overflow must be JS-clamped into the box (it's now clipped, not drag-revealed). (3) A selector that owns multiple rules (`--reader-measure` combined rule + the flex/overflow prose rule) breaks a first-match regex — scan all matches for the one carrying the declaration you mean.


### 2026-07-08 — Paper-reader landing: huge dead side-gutters + the arxiv input clipping its placeholder — the upload/search card column was hard-capped at `max-width:400px` regardless of pane width.
- **Ask (owner, screenshot).** Reading-mode empty state: "there's too much whitespace on both sides; this causes the prompt text in the input field to not be fully displayed."
- **Root cause.** `.paper-landing` centers `.paper-landing-actions` (the upload button + arxiv search row + describe box), and that column was `max-width:400px` (styles.css:1306) with NO wider desktop/tofu override. In a wide PDF pane the 400px column strands the content between big left/right gutters (the arrows in the screenshot), and inside it the arxiv `<input>` also loses ~36px of width to its left search-icon padding AND shares the row with the 搜索 button — so at 400px it's too narrow to render the full placeholder `搜索标题，或粘贴 arXiv 链接 / 编号`. NOT a viewport bug: the column simply never tracked the available pane width.
- **Fix (`static/styles.css`, CSS-only, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Raised `.paper-landing-actions{max-width:400px→520px}` — one base rule, so the card uses more of the pane, shrinks the side gutters, and gives the arxiv input enough room for its full placeholder at every theme. Still `width:100%`-capped so it never overflows a narrow pane; the ≤768 phone block (`.paper-arxiv-input{flex-direction:column}`, styles.css:1483) and the portrait-tablet re-inflate block are unaffected (they tune padding/stacking, not this cap).
- **Drift-guard (owner-requested).** New `tests/test_frontend_paper_landing_width.py` (2, env-independent CSS-parse; `_strip_comments`+brace-split per the styles.css test trap): asserts `.paper-landing-actions` max-width >= 520px (extracts the LAST `max-width:<N>px`, later-wins); NEUTER reverts the cap to 400px on a COPY and confirms the `>=520` assertion flips False (guard is load-bearing). 2/2 green.
- **Headroom check (arithmetic — could NOT browser-measure).** `box-sizing:border-box` globally (styles.css:12). At a 520px column the arxiv row is 520px; minus the 搜索 button (`padding:10px 20px`, 2 CJK @13px bold ≈ 66–70px) and the 8px flex gap → input box ≈ 444px; minus its `padding:10px 14px 10px 36px` (36 left icon + 14 right) + 2px border → **≈ 392px usable text width**. Calibrated against the screenshot (which clipped at the old 400px column ⇒ available text there ≈ 272px, so the placeholder `搜索标题，或粘贴 arXiv 链接 / 编号` renders ~275–290px): at 520px, 392px − ~285px ≈ **~105px headroom (~27%)** — comfortable, not thin, so 520 stands (no bump to 560 needed). Caveat: exact CJK glyph advance is font/DPI-dependent; the number is a calibrated estimate, not a rendered measurement.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6801/6801. CSS bundle → `styles-eefcb7f6.css` (grep confirms `max-width:520px` survived minify). NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device. Coordinated around live sibling `mrbqjyhe` (editing styles.css reading-mode TOC/term-card blocks ~L1488/L2478/L2504 — no overlap with the L1306 landing rule); took + released a `project_claim_path` lease on the landing block.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A centered action column with a fixed `max-width` reads as "too much whitespace" the moment it lives in a pane wider than that cap — size the cap to the form factor, not a single small magic number. Watch the double-squeeze: an input that both shares its row with a button AND reserves internal padding for an icon needs noticeably more column width than its own text implies before a placeholder fits.

### 2026-07-08 — Input box too narrow on wide landscape displays: `_reflowToolbar` collapsed the composer to the (now decluttered ≈540px) toolbar-content width; floored it to the `.chat-inner` reading column so it lines up with the messages at every resolution.
- **Ask (owner).** "Our input box is currently too narrow on large landscape displays. I need optimizations for various different resolutions."
- **Root cause.** The composer width is driven ONLY by `.input-inner{max-width:var(--toolbar-w,820px)}` (styles.css:499), and `_reflowToolbar()` (main.js:183) set `--toolbar-w` to the MEASURED natural width of the toolbar content, floored at just **480px** (`Math.max(480, Math.min(w, maxW))`). Meanwhile the message column `.chat-inner` is a fixed **820px** (styles.css:312; 920px on the portrait-tablet band, styles.css:16385). After the recent toolbar declutter (buttons folded into 增强/工具/模式 submenus + a "···" overflow), the toolbar's natural content shrank to ≈540px — so on any wide landscape display the composer sat ≈540px under an 820px message column: the reported "input box too narrow", a ~280px mismatch that reads as cramped/centered. NOT a viewport bug — the width simply stopped tracking the reading column once the toolbar got smaller.
- **Fix (`static/js/main.js`, uncommitted for owner attribution).** In `_reflowToolbar` step 3, replaced the flat `w = Math.max(480, Math.min(w, maxW))` with a reading-column FLOOR: read `.chat-inner`'s computed `max-width` (single-source in CSS → 820 desktop / 920 portrait-tablet, auto-adapting per resolution) and `w = Math.min(Math.max(w, readingFloor), maxW)`. So the composer now lines up with the messages by default, a genuinely wider toolbar can still EXPAND beyond it, and the viewport cap (`maxW = clientWidth − 48`) still wins on a narrow window so we never overflow. `readingFloor` defaults to 820 if `.chat-inner` is absent. Mobile is untouched — the ≤768 block overrides `.input-inner{max-width:100%!important}` (styles.css:16542), and the resize handler already re-runs `_scheduleReflow` on orientation/breakpoint crossings so the floor re-reads 820↔920 automatically.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; JS bundle rebuilt via `build_bundle()` → `bundle-4f1de2b5.js` (grep confirms `readingFloor` present ×3 in the minified bundle). New `tests/test_frontend_composer_reading_floor.py` (2, jsdom, extraction-and-eval running the REAL `_reflowToolbar`): a ~540px decluttered toolbar under a 1600px viewport + 820px `.chat-inner` is floored UP to ≥820; NEUTER restores the old `Math.max(480,…)` line → composer stays <820 (proves the floor is load-bearing). Suites: composer-floor 2/2 + `test_frontend_toolbar_declutter` 2/2 = 4 passed (`-p no:napari`). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a shared width is derived from a MEASURED sibling (`--toolbar-w` = toolbar content width) but must visually align with a FIXED sibling (`.chat-inner` reading column), floor the measured value to the fixed one rather than trusting a magic px floor (480) — a later change that shrinks the measured element (the toolbar declutter) silently breaks the alignment. Read the floor from the CSS so the responsive value stays single-source and adapts across resolutions instead of forking a JS constant.

### 2026-07-08 — Project-bar tofu mascot: retired the rejected hand-drawn pixel sprite; the left mark now REUSES the real welcome asset (`static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg`) so it's guaranteed identical to the welcome icon.
- **Ask (owner, screenshot).** "The pet on the far left of the project bar is too ugly; it doesn't resemble Tofu at all and lacks the feel of our welcome icon. Please optimize it thoroughly."
- **Context (a long prior saga — conv `mrarxhiv2bwk3j`).** That left mark is `[data-theme="tofu"] .project-bar::before` (styles.css ~11832), an empty inset the tofu theme fills. It went through five hand-drawn iterations the owner rejected one after another: smooth editorial glyph → 16×16 pixel sprite → 24×24 volumetric block → 3×3-eye fix → "geek nerd-glasses" sprite. The screenshot's ugly pet was that last **cyan-lens nerd-glasses pixel sprite** (data-URI `crispEdges` SVG). The owner's north star is now explicit: it should have "the feel of our welcome icon" — the polished 3-D isometric tofu cube with sparkly eyes + pink cheeks at `static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg` (used by the welcome screen, favicon, sidebar brand, README).
- **Root-cause fix (`static/styles.css`, tofu-scoped only, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Stopped hand-drawing. Replaced the whole data-URI pixel sprite in `[data-theme="tofu"] .project-bar::before` with `background-image:url("icons/tofu-welcome.svg")` — i.e. it now RENDERS THE REAL WELCOME ASSET, so the mark is byte-identical to the welcome icon by construction and can never drift from it (single source of truth). Dropped `image-rendering:pixelated` + the `steps(2)` retro hop; sized 24→**26px**, `left:12→11px`, added a soft `drop-shadow(0 1px 1.5px rgba(120,100,70,0.22))` to seat it on the parchment bar, and a springy `cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)` hover (`scale(1.12) rotate(-6deg)`) matching the theme's other bounce affordances. Still `[data-theme="tofu"]`-scoped — base/light/dark have NO `.project-bar::before` rule, so untouched by construction.
- **Path is proxy-safe.** The stylesheet is served as `static/styles-<hash>.css`, and CSS `url()` resolves relative to the STYLESHEET, so `url("icons/tofu-welcome.svg")` → `static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg` — correct behind a BASE_PATH / VS Code proxy without hardcoding an absolute path (CLAUDE.md §3.5).
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6798/6798. CSS bundle → `styles-2e201df4.css`; grep confirms `icons/tofu-welcome.svg` present ×1, old `crispEdges` sprite + cyan lens `#7FD4D0` both ×0 (gone). Rendered `tofu-welcome.svg` at the actual 26px display size — the 3-D tofu cube with glinted eyes + pink cheeks stays clearly legible and matches the welcome icon exactly. NOT committed (owner attribution) — restart server (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (hashed filename) to see on-device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a small brand mark is supposed to MATCH an existing polished asset, don't hand-redraw a look-alike (it drifts and invites endless "still ugly" rounds — five here). Point the CSS `::before`/background at the ACTUAL asset file via a stylesheet-relative `url()`; it's a true single source of truth, and other themes stay untouched because they never declared the pseudo-element.


### 2026-07-08 — Composer toolbar `.submenu-dropdown` polish: killed dead duplicate `transform`, added an anchored scale-pop entrance, closed the light-theme dark-shadow gap, + drift-guard test with neuters.
- **Ask (owner).** "The `submenu-dropdown` style also needs significant optimization." (The 增强/工具/模式/··· composer toolbar popovers.)
- **Root causes found (not cosmetic churn).** (1) **Dead CSS** — base `.submenu-dropdown` (styles.css:707) declared `transform:translateX(-50%)` TWICE in one rule; the first was immediately clobbered by the later `…translateY(4px)`. (2) **Light-theme shadow gap** — the shadow was hardcoded `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`, a harsh dark drop-shadow that reads as a smudge on light theme's pale `#eceae4` surface; there was NO `[data-theme="light"] .submenu-dropdown` override (tofu already had its own clay override at ~L12121, light did not). (3) Flat entrance (opacity + 4px slide, no `transform-origin`) vs the sibling `.preset-dropdown`'s refined cubic-bezier pop.
- **What shipped (`static/styles.css`, base + light only; tofu & mobile untouched, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Base rule: removed the duplicate transform; anchored scale-pop entrance (`translateY(6px) scale(.97)`→`scale(1)`, `transform-origin:bottom center`, `cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)` matching the preset dropdown); shadow moved to a `--submenu-shadow` token with the dark value as fallback; softer `--border-light`, radius 12→14, padding 4→5, min-width 220→236. New `[data-theme="light"] .submenu-dropdown{--submenu-shadow:0 10px 30px rgba(50,42,26,0.14),0 2px 8px rgba(50,42,26,0.08);border-color:var(--border)}` (warm-neutral tint). `#submenuMore` overflow popover: matched the scale-pop + `transform-origin:bottom right`. `.submenu-item`: roomier rhythm (gap 10→11, pad 8→9, radius 8→9) + icon-tile hover feedback.
- **Overflow anchor confirmed (owner asked).** `#submenuMore .submenu-dropdown` is specificity **(0,1,1)** (id+class) vs base `.submenu-dropdown` **(0,1,0)** — so `left:auto;right:0` wins on SPECIFICITY, not merely source order. The rule also re-declares `transform`/`transform-origin`, so the base `left:50%`/`translateX(-50%)` cannot half-center it. Fully right-anchored.
- **Insulation.** The tofu override (~L12121) re-declares `border-radius`/`border`/`box-shadow`/`background`, so the base changes don't bleed into tofu. Mobile bottom-sheet (~L16667) overrides `transform:none`, so phones are unchanged.
- **Drift-guard (owner-requested — the genuine remaining gap).** New `tests/test_frontend_submenu_dropdown_style.py` (5, env-independent CSS-parse; `_strip_comments` before brace-splitting per the logged styles.css test trap): (1) base `.submenu-dropdown` declares the `transform` PROPERTY exactly once (regex excludes `transform-origin` + the `transform` keyword inside `transition`); (2) `[data-theme="light"] .submenu-dropdown` EXISTS, sets `--submenu-shadow`/`box-shadow`, and carries NO raw `rgba(0,0,0,…)`; (3) overflow popover keeps `left:auto;right:0` + `transform-origin:bottom right`. Two in-test detector NCs PLUS a real-CSS poison run (reintroduce the duplicate transform + revert light to black) → the two positive invariants both FAIL, restore → 5/5 green.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6798/6798; CSS bundle → `styles-8b8c8eff.css` (grep confirms new base rule + light override survived minify). Suites: new submenu drift-guard 5/5 + `test_frontend_toolbar_declutter` 2/2 = 7 passed. Coordinated around sibling `mrbqjyhe`'s lease on the paper-reader region of styles.css (no overlap — my hunks are ~L707 & ~L12121-insulated); took + released my own `project_claim_path` lease on the submenu blocks.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A shadow hardcoded as `rgba(0,0,0,…)` is a latent light-theme smudge — route popover shadows through a `--submenu-shadow`-style token so each theme can re-tint (dark keeps the fallback, light gets warm-neutral, tofu keeps clay). A duplicate `transform` in one rule is silent dead code the cascade discards — worth a one-line drift-guard given how many parallel siblings churn styles.css daily.

### 2026-07-08 — Warm SSE reconnect stranded the tool-round panel at "round 10": the `Last-Event-ID` resume replayed only post-cursor deltas and NEVER reasserted the toolRounds snapshot, trusting client cache. Now emits a leading full-snapshot state (keep-longer adopts it). Backend-only.
- **Ask (owner).** Conv `mrbf9px2g5mct3` generated in the background; VS Code↔server link dropped and resync-on-reconnect misbehaved — "the first round of tool calls displayed is already the tenth round." Suspected intermediate storage preventing the DB from being the sole source of truth.
- **Two-finding forensic pass (verified in logs + code BEFORE any edit).** (1) **Which reconnect branch fired** — grepped `logs/app.log` for the four `routes/chat.py` markers. For this conv's tasks (`3dae0f20`/`292aa602`/`7af96628`) only `[Chat] SSE stream 3dae0f20 reconnecting with Last-Event-ID=48/186` appears; `full-snapshot resync`, `cold replay from event_log`, `served from DB` fire for NONE of them → the operative path is the **warm `Last-Event-ID` resume** (`_warm_resume_serviceable()` True → `missed_evts = task['events'][resume_from:]`), which replays only post-cursor events and never re-sends `state['toolRounds']`. (2) **Is the in-memory list lossy?** `task['toolRounds']` is reset to `[]` ONLY at turn-start (orchestrator.py:373 auto-turn-retry, :2541 endpoint `_run_single_turn`, + initial run_task) and mutated SOLELY by append (executor.py:533) — no `.pop`, no slice, no size cap. So the live list is COMPLETE. Verdict: **branch (a) purely** — the warm-resume path omits the snapshot; the deeper "in-memory store is lossy" hypothesis is ruled out. The strand happens when the reconnect lands on a fresh empty assistant placeholder (initActiveTasks Case A stale-tail / connectToTask stale-turn guard, `toolRounds:[]`) → delta-only replay renders from whatever round the first missed `tool_start` carries.
- **Fix (`routes/chat.py::chat_stream`, backend-only, uncommitted for owner attribution).** In the warm-resume branch, build a `resume_state = build_event(STATE, content, thinking, status)` + `resume_state['toolRounds'] = task['toolRounds']` under `task['events_lock']` (same consistency as the fresh path), then yield it as an **id-less** `data:` frame (via `_dumps_yielding`, mirroring the fresh-connection snapshot at ~1712 so it can't collide with the first replayed event's cursor) BEFORE replaying `missed_evts`. Because the frontend's `_snapshotLongerRounds`/`_snapshotLonger` keep-longer guards only let a snapshot GROW a message, the reasserted FULL list is ADOPTED when the client cache is short (fixes the strand) and harmlessly IGNORED when the client is already equal/longer — a shorter buffer can never collapse a longer one. Emitting the complete list is exactly what makes keep-longer adopt it.
- **Tests (`tests/test_warm_resume_reasserts_toolrounds.py`, 2).** (1) BEHAVIORAL end-to-end: drives the REAL `chat_stream` via a Quart test client with a `Last-Event-ID` header on a task carrying 10 done rounds; asserts the FIRST `data:` frame is a `state` snapshot with NO `id:` carrying all 10 rounds (`roundNum` 1..10, ordered) + the content, emitted before the replayed deltas. Task is marked terminal (append `done` + status) before consuming so the resume replay returns instead of blocking on the live loop. (2) SOURCE guard: the warm-resume block must build `resume_state` from the full `task['toolRounds']` and yield it id-less before the replay.
- **Verify.** NEUTER CONFIRMED: gating the emission (`if False and resume_state…`) → the behavioral test FAILS (first frame is no longer the full-rounds state), then restored + re-green. Suites (`-p no:napari`): new 2/2 + `test_frontend_toolrounds_keep_longer` 1/1 + `test_frontend_state_snapshot_keep_longer` 1/1 + `test_chat_stream_snapshot_offload` 8/8 = **12 passed**; ruff clean. Backend-only Python change — no JS/CSS bundle rebuild. (Note: an unrelated uncommitted `chat_send` autopilot-supersede hunk from a sibling conversation coexists in `routes/chat.py`; left untouched.)
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A warm `Last-Event-ID` SSE resume must reassert the AUTHORITATIVE structural snapshot (full `toolRounds` + content/thinking) BEFORE replaying post-cursor deltas — never trust the client's cached rounds, because a reconnect can land on a placeholder-reset message (empty `toolRounds`) and strand the user at a later round. The snapshot must be the COMPLETE in-memory list (so keep-longer adopts it) and carry NO `id:` (so it can't collide with the first replayed event's cursor), mirroring the fresh-connection path. This is safe precisely because `_snapshotLongerRounds` only grows, never shrinks.

### 2026-07-08 — Portrait project rail could not be expanded: the drawer-viewport icon-only compaction was force-locked with `!important`, overriding the `.rail-collapsed` toggle the expand chevron drives (CSS-only, root-cause).
- **Ask (owner).** "Folders in portrait mode cannot be expanded."
- **Root cause (CSS, not JS).** The expand/collapse chevron works fine — `_toggleProjectRail()` (main_folders_mobile.js:260) toggles `.rail-collapsed` on `.sidebar` and persists it; the renderer self-heals the class every render (conversation_list.js:379). But the drawer-viewport block (`static/styles.css:148`, `@media(max-width:768px),(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)`) applied the icon-only rail compaction to **`.sidebar.has-rail`** unconditionally, with `width:var(--project-rail-w-collapsed)!important` + `.folder-tab-name{display:none}`. The block's own comment stated the intent: *"!important beats the desktop .rail-collapsed toggle so the drawer is icon-only regardless of the stored expand choice."* So on portrait phone AND portrait touch-tablet the chevron toggled the class but the `!important` locks ignored it — folder NAMES could never appear. The design assumed a drawer should be permanently icon-only; the owner wants it expandable like desktop.
- **Fix (`static/styles.css`, CSS-only, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Re-scoped all 12 rules in that drawer block from `.sidebar.has-rail …` → **`.sidebar.has-rail.rail-collapsed …`**, so the drawer now respects the SAME `.rail-collapsed` toggle as desktop: default labeled/expandable, tap the chevron to collapse to a touch-tuned (30px tiles, taller rows) icon strip. The desktop base collapsed rules (styles.css:78–132) already render a correct icon-only rail whenever `.rail-collapsed` is present at every viewport; the drawer block now just adds the touch-size tuning on top of the same trigger. The two per-block drawer WIDTH overrides (styles.css:16320, 16425 — `.sidebar.has-rail,.sidebar.has-rail.rail-collapsed{width:…drawer…!important}`) are UNCHANGED: they reset the *sidebar* geometry so the fixed 360px/82vw drawer isn't widened by the derived desktop `has-rail` width — orthogonal to the *rail* (inner column) width the toggle now drives.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6796/6796; CSS bundle → `styles-816936e1.css` (grep confirms `has-rail.rail-collapsed .project-rail{width` survived minify). Guard suites: `test_frontend_rail_cls` 3/3, `test_frontend_project_rail` 6/6, `test_tablet_label_truncation` 4/4, `test_breakpoint_coordination` 8/8 = 21 passed. New `tests/test_frontend_portrait_rail_expandable.py` 3/3 (env-independent CSS-parse + brace-matched `@media` iterator): INVARIANT = no drawer `@media` block may hide `.folder-tab-name` via display:none without a `.rail-collapsed` scope; positive lock that the compaction block exists AND is collapse-scoped; POISONED-FIXTURE NC injects an unconditional `.sidebar.has-rail .folder-tab-name{display:none}` → scanner must flag it.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a control's state is driven by a JS-toggled class (`.rail-collapsed`), a responsive `@media` block that hard-codes the compacted appearance with `!important` SILENTLY DEFEATS the toggle — the class flips but nothing renders. Scope the responsive compaction on the SAME toggle class (`.rail-collapsed`) rather than the always-present container (`.has-rail`), and keep any orthogonal geometry override (drawer width) separate from the toggle-driven inner width.

Wrapped the model list in a dedicated `#presetDropdownList`; `_populateModelDropdown` now writes into THAT (falls back to `#presetDropdown` for old markup) so a model-list rebuild doesn't wipe the folded-in footer. `_applyModelUI` depth show/hide simplified to `display:''/'none'` on the wrapper — its visibility no longer changes toolbar width so the row-fade + reflow-for-depth machinery is gone. Mobile: whole `.ps-dd-depth-wrap` hidden (depth lives in the bottom sheet's `.mobile-depth-bar`).

Icon-only trigger variant `.submenu-trigger-icon`; `#submenuMore .submenu-dropdown` right-anchored (`left:auto;right:0`) so it can't clip the right edge. Mobile hide-list updated: `#submenuMore` hidden (its two entries already exist in the bottom sheet), dropped the now-relocated standalone ids.

### 2026-07-08 — Portrait-tablet optimization for CHAT + READING interfaces: touch-reveal hover-only message actions + inflate the phone-cramped reader on the 769–1024px coarse-pointer band (landscape/desktop untouched).
### 2026-07-08 — Thinking-depth control unreachable in landscape: pinned the depth footer sticky at the bottom of the model dropdown (root-cause, all viewports > 768px).
- **Ask (owner).** "I can't even adjust my depth of thought in landscape mode."
- **Root cause.** The thinking-depth control (`#thinkingDepthSection` / `.ps-dd-depth-wrap`) lives ONLY at the bottom of the model dropdown (`#presetDropdown`) for any viewport > 768px — the ≤768 phone path routes depth to the bottom-sheet `.mobile-depth-bar` and hides `.ps-dd-depth-wrap` (`display:none!important`, styles.css:16561). The dropdown is `max-height:50vh; overflow-y:auto` (styles.css:2676) and the depth footer sits AFTER the full scrollable model list. On a LANDSCAPE viewport (short height → 50vh ≈ 200px; and width > 768 so the phone bottom-sheet affordance `.mobile-more-btn` is `display:none`), the depth footer is stranded below a long model list in a tiny upward-opening dropdown → cannot be scrolled to → **unreachable**. NOT caused by my earlier tablet work — a pre-existing gap the landscape form factor exposes.
- **Fix (`static/styles.css`, CSS-only, uncommitted).** Pinned the footer as a `position:sticky; bottom:-5px` element so it stays visible while the model list scrolls UNDER it, on every viewport (`z-index:2`, opaque `background:var(--bg-secondary)` + `border-top` so the scrolled list doesn't bleed through; `margin-bottom:-5px;padding-bottom:5px` swallows the dropdown's own 5px bottom padding to sit flush to the rounded edge). Added a tofu override `[data-theme="tofu"] .ps-dd-depth-wrap{background:#F4F2EB;border-top-color:#C2BCA4}` since tofu's dropdown bg differs (#F4F2EB). Light theme uses `var(--bg-secondary)` (no dropdown override) so the base rule already covers it. Phones unaffected — the ≤768 block still `display:none`s the wrap and uses the bottom sheet.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6796/6796; CSS bundle → `styles-16540986.css` (grep confirms `position:sticky` + tofu bg survived minify). Guard grows to 11/11: added `test_depth_footer_is_sticky` (base `.ps-dd-depth-wrap` is `position:sticky` + has opaque bg; regex anchored `(?<![\]\w ])` to skip the earlier tofu-prefixed override), `test_depth_footer_opaque_under_tofu`, + NC `test_nc_depth_footer_sticky_is_load_bearing` (strip `position:sticky`→`static` FAILS). `test_breakpoint_coordination` 8/8, `test_tablet_label_truncation` 4/4 unaffected.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a control is folded into a scrollable dropdown/popover as a trailing section, a short viewport (landscape phone/tablet) can push it below the `max-height` scroll fold where it's unreachable — pin it `position:sticky` (with an opaque bg matching EACH theme's popover bg) rather than relying on the user scrolling a tiny upward-opening menu. A base-rule regex `\.foo\{` will match an earlier `[data-theme=x] .foo\{` override first — anchor with a negative lookbehind to get the true base rule.

- **Ask (owner).** "Landscape styling is nice, but PORTRAIT mode needs optimization in the chat interface, and the same for the reading interface — for the portrait reading interface, enhance the layout for tablet adaptations."
- **Measure-first finding (two concrete portrait-tablet defects, band = `769–1024px ∧ pointer:coarse`).**
  1. **CHAT** — base `.message-actions` is a HOVER-REVEAL (`opacity:0` → `1` on `.message:hover`, styles.css:2676). The existing tablet-drawer block (styles.css:16232) only converted the sidebar to a slide-over; it never re-showed the actions. A coarse-pointer tablet can NEVER fire `:hover`, so copy/edit/regenerate/delete were **invisible and unreachable** at 769–1024px. (The ≤768 phone block already re-flows them inline; the tablet, which keeps the roomier desktop message layout, fell through the gap.)
  2. **READING** — the reader single-pane predicate `≤768 ∪ (≤1024 ∧ coarse)` (styles.css:1418) applied the SAME 360px-phone compaction to a ~900px tablet: `.paper-report-content{padding:14px}`, shrunk `.paper-tab-btn{padding:10px 6px;font-size:12px}`, stacked full-width arxiv rows. Wasted the tablet's room + finger-hostile targets.
- **What shipped (`static/styles.css`, CSS-only, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - **Chat** — appended a touch block to the existing tablet drawer `@media(min-width:769px) and (max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` (ends ~L16268): `.message-actions{opacity:1}` (always visible in the same absolute top-right slot as desktop hover — `.message:hover` still works on a hybrid mouse device), `.msg-action-btn{padding:6px 10px;min-height:36px}` + the `[data-theme="tofu"]` (0,2,0) re-assert (same specificity war the phone block fights), `.send-btn{40×40}`, `textarea{font-size:16px}` (no iOS zoom).
  - **Reading** — new dedicated `@media(min-width:769px) and (max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` block AFTER the shared single-pane block (source order → re-inflates for the tablet only, ≤768 phone untouched): reader padding 14px→`24px 28px` (tofu pdf-container 20px), `.paper-tab-btn{padding:12px 16px;font-size:13px}`+15px svg (tofu re-assert), `.paper-reader-set-btn{height:36px}`, `.paper-toolbar-btn{36×34}`, `.paper-mobile-switch-btn{font-size:14px}`, un-stacked the arxiv landing (`flex-direction:row`, show search icon, `btn width:auto`), `.paper-lib-item{padding:14px;min-height:48px}`.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6784/6784. CSS bundle rebuilt via `lib.css_bundler._build_minified()` → `styles-73b791e9.css`; grep of the MINIFIED file confirms `.paper-report-content,.paper-report-body{padding:24px 28px}` + `.message-actions{opacity:1}` survived minification. Guard suites (`-p no:napari`): `test_tablet_label_truncation` 4/4, `test_breakpoint_coordination` 8/8, `test_frontend_paper_mobile_responsive` 2/2 (unaffected — CSS-only). New `tests/test_portrait_tablet_chat_reading.py` 6/6.
- **New test (`tests/test_portrait_tablet_chat_reading.py`).** Reuses the brace-matched `_iter_media_blocks` iterator; `_is_tablet_portrait` matches ONLY the exact `min-width:769 ∧ max-width:1024 ∧ pointer:coarse` band. Invariants: base `.message-actions` really is `opacity:0` (precondition anchor); a tablet block reveals `opacity:1`; tablet reader padding > 14px; tablet `.paper-tab-btn` horizontal padding > 6px. TWO neuters (each on a COPY, shipped file byte-identical): revert reveal→`opacity:0` (invariant FAILS); shrink reader padding→14px (invariant FAILS). Both bite.
- **Coordination.** A live sibling (`mrblwc24`) was editing styles.css MARKDOWN-PROSE rules (fonts/spacing) — a different region. Took a `project_claim_path` lease scoped to the two `@media` blocks I touched; my hunks are in the tablet band + reading-mode area, no overlap with prose rules.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A hover-reveal (`opacity:0 → :hover`) control is INVISIBLE on any coarse-pointer surface — every responsive touch band (phone ≤768 AND portrait-tablet 769–1024 coarse) must independently re-show it; the phone block doing so does NOT cover the tablet. When a single-pane predicate unions phones + tablets (`≤768 ∪ (≤1024 ∧ coarse)`), a phone-tuned compaction inside it silently over-compacts the tablet — add a `min-width:769 ∧ …coarse` block AFTER it (source order) to re-inflate for the roomier form factor without touching the phone.

- **Follow-up (owner review — two more gaps closed).**
  1. **CHAT reading measure on the tablet band.** Once the sidebar becomes a slide-over drawer the chat pane spans the FULL viewport, but base `.chat-inner{max-width:820px}` left ~102px dead gutter each side at a 1024px portrait tablet (iPad Pro 12.9"). Widened to `.chat-inner{max-width:920px}` in the chat band (~52px gutters at 1024px, edge-to-edge below ~968px; content ~872px after 24px inner padding, still a comfortable measure). Phones keep the base cap via their own `max-width:100%` overflow rule.
  2. **PDF fit-to-width was subtracting a HARDCODED 32px** (`container.clientWidth - 32`, assuming 16px padding each side) at TWO sites in `paper-reader.js` (initial-load fit ~L987 + `paperFitWidth` ~L1173). FIX: new `_paperViewerPadX(container)` reads the container's REAL `getComputedStyle` `paddingLeft+paddingRight` (fallback 32 on 0 / throw, debug-logged). Now every theme × breakpoint fits exactly — corrects desktop light/tofu AND all tablet cases in one root-cause change.

Test grows to 8/8: added `test_tablet_portrait_widens_chat_measure` (>820px) + its NC (revert→820px FAILS). Paper harnesses unaffected: `test_frontend_paper_mobile_responsive` 2/2, `reader_prefs`/`instant_paint`/`reading_anchor` 6/6.
