### 2026-07-08 — Boot-restore race: "loading finished and suddenly switched the conversation I'm viewing" — the boot .then() unconditionally re-selected the pre-refresh conv even after the user had already navigated during a slow load.
- **Ask (owner).** "If I select a conversation but the network is poor / loading isn't complete, once it finishes it might suddenly switch the conversation I'm viewing. Or while inside a conversation it might suddenly jump to the top."
- **Root cause (Symptom 1).** Boot sequence: `newChat()` sets `activeConvId=null` + welcome screen → sidebar painted INSTANTLY from IndexedDB cache (`hydrateSidebarFromCache`, so the user can click a conv immediately) → the network-bound `initActiveTasks()` runs. Its `.then()` (`static/js/main.js`) UNCONDITIONALLY did `loadConversation(_restoredConvId)` (pre-refresh conv) or auto-selected `conversations[0]`. On a poor connection the user clicks into conv **B** while waiting; the late `.then()` then yanks them back to the pre-refresh conv **A** — the reported "suddenly switched my conversation". Also feeds Symptom 2: re-navigating to a `_needsLoad` target flashes the loading skeleton at the top. (The stable-view full-render jump-to-top causes were already handled by the 2026-07-07 `overflow-anchor` + `_captureScrollAnchor` work; this is the remaining trigger.)
- **Fix (`static/js/main.js`, uncommitted for owner attribution).** Extracted the inline restore block into a hoisted `_bootRestoreActiveConv(restoredId)` and gated the WHOLE thing on `if (activeConvId) return;`. Since `newChat()` nulls `activeConvId` at boot and NOTHING but a user action (click / new-chat send) sets it during the load, a non-null `activeConvId` at `.then()` time IS the "user already chose what to view" signal → leave them be. Only restore/auto-select when still on the welcome screen. Behaviour on a fast load (user hasn't clicked yet) is byte-identical to before.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_frontend_boot_restore_active_conv.py` (5, runs the REAL extracted fn under node): restore-when-welcome; **does-not-switch-when-user-already-navigated** (the bug); auto-select-newest; no-autoselect-when-composer-has-text; NEUTER strips `if (activeConvId) return;` → proves the late restore then clobbers the user's in-progress nav (`conv-B`→`conv-A`). All green + neuter bites.
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; `test_frontend_cache_hydrate_boot` + `test_frontend_full_render_scroll_anchor` + new suite = 15 passed; JS bundle rebuilt → `bundle-931faadd.js` (grep confirms `_bootRestoreActiveConv` present). NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A deferred boot `.then()` that navigates (restore/auto-select) MUST first check whether the user already navigated during the async gap — the cache-first instant sidebar makes that gap user-interactive. `activeConvId` (nulled by `newChat()` at boot, only set by user action during load) is the honest "already chose" signal; gate the late navigation on it.


### 2026-07-08 — Model-added workspace roots now appear in "recent" projects: persisted server-side at the registration boundary (create_project + abs-path auto-register), not just when a user opens a folder.
- **Ask (owner).** "The project path added by the large model itself should also be displayed in recent." A root the ASSISTANT registers (via `create_project`, or the absolute-path-write auto-register in `_resolve_write_path` §2) was registered in `_roots`/the conv registry but never landed in the `recent_projects` table — so it never showed in the project-modal recent dropdown. Only the interactive UI path saved recents (frontend `mpApplyFolders`/restore call `saveRecentProject` per folder; see memory `recent-projects-save-all-folders-no-limit`).
- **Root cause / placement.** The frontend `workspace_root_added` + `create_project` SSE handlers refresh `projectState` for the ACTIVE conv but (a) gate on `activeConvId` and (b) never call `saveRecentProject`. Fixing it in the frontend would miss any root registered by a NON-active/background conversation. Correct placement is the backend registration boundary, where it works regardless of which conv is active.
- **What shipped (`lib/project_mod/write_tools.py`, backend-only, uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  - New `_save_model_added_root_to_recent(abs_path)` helper (write_tools.py:122): best-effort `save_recent_project(abs_path)`, SKIPS temp-dir scratch paths (`_is_temp_path`) so ephemeral `/tmp` writes never pollute recents (mirrors the untracked-root policy), and is a debug-level self-recovering fallback on failure (imports `save_recent_project` at call time so the test can stub `cfg.save_recent_project`).
  - Wired into the TWO model-driven registration sites only: `tool_create_project` after successful registration (write_tools.py:323), and the abs-path auto-register `if not _existing` branch in `_resolve_write_path` (write_tools.py:481). A write UNDER an already-registered root (no new root) saves nothing new.
- **Read path traced end-to-end (owner-requested confirmation it surfaces in the UI).** `save_recent_project` UPSERTs `recent_projects` (path PK, count++, last_used) → `get_recent_projects()` (config.py:625) does `SELECT ... ORDER BY last_used DESC` with NO LIMIT / NO WHERE → `GET /api/v1/project/recent` returns `{projects: [...]}` → `renderRecentProjects()` (project.js:588) re-fetches on every modal open (`openProjectModal`→362) → `_renderRecentList()` (project.js:627) filters ONLY by the user's search box (empty by default), newest-first via the server sort. No filtering drops a model-added path; it appears the next time the recent list is fetched.
- **Tests (`tests/test_temp_write_and_root_signal.py`, +`RecentProjectPersistenceTest`, 4 cases).** Stubs `cfg.save_recent_project` (no DB). Asserts: abs-write auto-register saves the sibling root; `create_project` saves the new dir; temp-dir scratch write saves NOTHING; subdir-of-existing-root saves nothing new. 16/16 pass; ruff clean. NEUTER CONFIRMED: disabling the create_project save site → `test_create_project_saves_recent` FAILS, then restored + re-green.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Anything the MODEL registers (root, artifact, state) that should surface in the UI must be persisted at the BACKEND registration boundary, not in a frontend SSE handler that gates on the active conv — otherwise a background/non-active conversation's registration is silently dropped. The recent-projects read path has no server-side filter beyond the sort, so a persisted row always surfaces.


### 2026-07-08 — Project-Brain-fed conv stuck on perpetual "waiting" + injected msg stranded in queue: the stuck-task reaper's terminal path was INCOMPLETE (task_results-only). Fixed with a full finalizer + a narrowly-scoped anti-resurrection guard relaxation.
- **Ask (owner).** Conv `mradmzmdm01mrh`: the Project Brain sent it a peer message, it got injected into chat history to guide the next reply, but "the agent keeps not responding and shows as waiting", AND the sent message is simultaneously in chat-inner AND still shown queued in the input box. Two symptoms suspected as a queuing bug.
- **Ground-truth forensics (via the app DB layer — the backend is PostgreSQL; the on-disk `data/tofu.db` SQLite is a stale legacy file with a malformed-schema index + 248 MB uncheckpointed WAL, so `sqlite3` CLI was unreliable).** Timeline reconstructed from `conversations.messages` + `task_results` + `logs/audit.log` + `logs/app.log`: (1) **11:05:16** server restarted → `redispatch_orphaned_queue_on_startup` found conv `mradmzmd` had orphaned queued PEER messages (sibling `mrahis0uvl0983` sent two, 11:07 + 11:10 the prior day) and dispatched ONE as task `d03cbccb` (model `aws.claude-opus-4.8`), `remaining=1` (2nd peer msg left queued). (2) Task **wedged 1804s** (0 progress) → reaped `status=error` by `reap_stuck_running_tasks` at **11:35:21**. (3) Conv trailing turn is the peer USER msg with NO assistant reply; `settings.activeTaskId` STILL = `d03cbccb`.
- **Root cause (ONE bug, both symptoms).** `reap_stuck_running_tasks` → `_write_stuck_terminal_floor` (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`) was an INCOMPLETE terminal path: it wrote ONLY the `task_results` error row. Unlike the happy path (`persist_task_result` → `_sync_result_to_conversation` + `_dispatch_queued_message` + orchestrator terminal `append_event`), it did NOT (1) sync an assistant error bubble onto `conversations.messages`, (2) clear `settings.activeTaskId`, (3) emit the terminal `DONE(error)` SSE, (4) drain the queue. Result: conv looks forever-busy (perpetual "waiting" bubble, reload re-attaches to a dead stream) and the 2nd peer message is stranded in the queue (the completion-hook chain that drains it never fires for a reaped task). Compounding: `_sync_result_to_conversation`'s anti-resurrection guard (~1204) DROPS the write when the trailing turn is role=user AND the task is aborted (Stop→Regenerate truncation protection) — which ALSO blocked the reaped task's error bubble.
- **What shipped (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`, uncommitted for owner attribution — backend-only).**
  - New `_finalize_reaped_stuck_task(task)` replaces the bare `_write_stuck_terminal_floor(t)` call in the reaper loop. Runs the SAME seams the happy path uses: terminal floor FIRST (poll always resolves terminally), then `append_event(DONE, error, finishReason='error')`, then `_sync_result_to_conversation`, then `_dispatch_queued_message`. Each step independently try/guarded so one failure never blocks the others. `_write_stuck_terminal_floor` kept as the floor primitive.
  - Anti-resurrection guard relaxed to `if ((aborted or _abort_reason) and _abort_reason != 'stuck_no_progress')`. A stuck reap is NOT a regenerate-truncation — the wedged task OWNS the trailing user turn and is still `_latest_task_for_conv` (the freshness guard already passed), so it falls through to append the assistant error bubble.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_queue_redispatch_after_restart.py` +2: `test_reaped_stuck_task_finalizes_conversation` (DB-backed: unanswered peer trailing turn + a 2nd queued follow-up + activeTaskId=dead → asserts an assistant error bubble is appended right after the peer turn, the dead task is unpinned, the queued follow-up is drained + spawns a task, queue depth 0) and `test_NC_reaped_task_guard_still_blocks_regenerate_truncation` (NEUTER of the guard-relaxation SCOPE: a `superseded` abort on a trailing-user turn must STILL be dropped — proves the relaxation is narrowly keyed on `stuck_no_progress`, not a blanket "append on any aborted task" that would reintroduce the truncated-turn bug). `tests/test_stuck_task_reaper.py` fixture updated to stub the new `_finalize_reaped_stuck_task` (keeps the unit tests DB-free).
- **Verify.** ruff clean; `test_stuck_task_reaper` 8/8; `test_queue_redispatch_after_restart` 5/5; `test_project_peer` 26/26. NEUTER CONFIRMED: reverting the `!= 'stuck_no_progress'` scope → `test_reaped_stuck_task_finalizes_conversation` FAILS ("reaper must append an assistant error bubble"), then restored + re-green.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Every abnormal task-termination path (reaper, abort-floor) must run the SAME finalization as the happy path — conv sync + activeTaskId clear + queue drain + terminal SSE — not just a `task_results` floor. A floor-only write avoids the 404-on-poll bug but leaves the conv perpetually attached to a dead stream AND strands any queued follow-up. When relaxing a defensive guard for one new case, scope it to the exact `_abort_reason` and prove the scope with a neuter on the OTHER reasons.


### 2026-07-08 — Retry/rate-limit stream-phase chip: de-emoji'd (§3.4) + fixed icon↔text misalignment
- **Ask (owner, screenshot of tofu-theme chip "⏳ 模型 aws.claude-opus-4.8 限流中，正在排队重试 (第 1 次)…").** Two problems: (1) it uses emoji, disliked/§3.4-forbidden; (2) the leftmost icon and the text are not aligned.
- **Roots.** (1) TWO emoji sources: the `⏳` was baked into the backend PHASE `detail` string (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py:2380`, `_on_retry`), and the chip's own leading icon was a bare `⟳` char (`static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js:339`, the `phase==='retrying'` branch). (2) Misalignment: `.stream-phase-icon` was sized via `font-size:14px` (retrying override bumped it to `16px`) while `.stream-phase-text` is 12px, and the row is `align-items:flex-start` — so the oversized glyph didn't sit on the first text line.
- **What shipped (uncommitted, owner attribution).**
  - `manager.py`: dropped the `⏳ ` prefix from the 429 retry detail → `模型 {model} 限流中，正在排队重试 (第 {attempt} 次)…`.
  - `streaming_ui.js`: `⟳` char → `${Icon('refresh', 14)}` (real Lucide SVG from `core/icons.js`, stroke=currentColor so it inherits the chip's amber/kinako color + the existing `phaseIconPulse` animation).
  - `styles.css`: `.stream-phase` gains `line-height:1.5`; `.stream-phase-icon` now `display:inline-flex;align-items:center;height:1.5em` (dropped stale `font-size:14px`) so the SVG box matches the first text line and centers on it — with `align-items:flex-start` preserved, a wrapped multi-line message still keeps the icon top-aligned to line 1. Dropped the now-inert `font-size:16px` on `.stream-phase-retrying .stream-phase-icon` (kept its pulse animation).
- **Verify.** `node --check` OK; JS bundle → `bundle-528b87d6.js` (grep confirms `stream-phase-retrying…Icon('refresh'`), CSS bundle → `styles-0e443a1a.css`; tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6762/6762; `⏳` count in manager.py = 0. `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_warmup.py` 3/3 (added an `Icon` stub to both jsdom harnesses since the prod bundle loads `icons.js` before `streaming_ui.js` but the harness only evals the two streaming files — the RETRY_DETAIL test string still carries its own `⏳`/`stream-phase-retrying` assertions, which pass unchanged).
- **Guardrail.** A stream-phase `detail` string is BACKEND-authored — de-emoji at the source (`_on_retry` in manager.py), not just the frontend. When a chip's leading icon is a bare unicode char, swap to `Icon(name,size)` and size the `.stream-phase-icon` box with `height:1.5em`+inline-flex (NOT font-size) so an SVG aligns with the text baseline. A jsdom harness that evals `streaming_ui.js` in isolation must stub `Icon` (it lives in the earlier-bundled `core/icons.js`).

### 2026-07-08 — Tool-call render redesign: killed the megabox, made each round a discrete quiet CARD (owner-approved "light cards + drop the spine"), CSS-only
- **Ask (owner).** The finished/streaming tool rendering was "ugly" — a single large amber-tinted box (`.ptool-panel`) enclosing everything, with narration/thinking/tool-rows alternating as full-width slabs. Approved direction: option (ii) light discrete cards + drop the spine, matching how Claude/ChatGPT present tool calls. Five concrete requirements (kill megabox in ALL themes; each round = self-contained card; narration flows as ordinary prose; streaming==finished no-jump; update guard tests keeping teeth).
- **Key realization → CSS-ONLY.** Both the streaming path (`streaming_ui.js:_syncToolRoundsDOM`) and the finished path (`tool_rounds.js:renderSegmentTimelineHTML`/`_renderToolGroupsHTML`) emit the SAME class structure (`.ptool-panel` → `.ptool-panel-header`/`-body` → `.ptool-turn` cards with `.ptool-turn-rno-solo`/`.ptool-turn-head`). So restyling those classes satisfies requirement #4 (no reflow) automatically with ZERO JS risk. No JS edits were needed — bundle-fa095dc1.js unchanged.
- **What shipped (`static/styles.css`).**
  - `.ptool-panel` / `-active`: `border:none; background:none; overflow:visible` (was 1px amber border + tint + overflow:hidden). `.ptool-panel-header` demoted from titled container (border-bottom, amber) to a quiet un-boxed muted count label. Mirrored in light (`border:none;background:none`) and tofu (retired the 3px "pixel window" `border`/`background`/`box-shadow`/`overflow:hidden`).
  - `.ptool-turn`: was `display:grid` (28px ordinal gutter) + a `::before` hairline SPINE. Now `display:block` + own `1px var(--border)` hairline + `border-radius` + `margin:8px 0` (discrete card, breathing room). The spine `::before` and the multi-call left-rail bracket were DELETED. tofu gives the card a warm 2px pixel-window frame per ROUND instead of per panel.
  - Ordinal digit (`.ptool-turn-rno`) recolored amber→`var(--text-tertiary)`; solo tag became a plain header strip (no gutter). Multi-call header (`.ptool-turn-head`) gets a bottom divider so grouped rows read under a header. All amber `#f59e0b`/`rgba(234,179,8,...)` hovers → neutral `var(--text-secondary/tertiary)`.
  - `.seg-narration`/`.seg-thinking`: re-derived from the retired 44px/28px tool-column gutter math → `margin:...0` (flush-left, x=0) so connective prose reads as ordinary message body between the cards. Color bumped narration→`--text-primary`.
- **Preserved (owner's explicit guardrails).** `.ptool-line` (`flex:1`) + `.ptool-text` (`flex:1;min-width:0`) untouched → tool text width NOT shrunk. No opacity/alpha used to convey ROW state (the standing no-opacity rule) — state still lives on solid-color labels + the active row.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_segment_timeline.py`).** Rewrote `test_seg_timeline_alignment_matches_tool_content_column` (hard-derived the OLD 44/28 geometry + solo `display:grid`) → `test_seg_narration_flows_as_message_body_flush_left`: asserts narration+thinking left=0, `.ptool-turn` is `display:block` with border+radius, the spine `::before` is GONE, `.ptool-panel` border+background are `none`. Added `test_NC_seg_alignment_bites_on_reintroduced_gutter` (re-injects the retired 44px gutter → invariant must fail). TRAP fixed: margin shorthand `2px 0 8px 0` has unitless `0`s that `_px_tokens` (px-only regex) silently dropped → added `_margin_tokens` that keeps bare zeros. Interleave-order + fallback/flag + settings-toggle tests kept GREEN.
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors; braces 6760/6760. CSS bundle rebuilt → `styles-f53d48bf.css` (via `_build_minified()`); JS bundle `bundle-fa095dc1.js` UNCHANGED (no JS edits). Suites (`-p no:napari`): segment-timeline 7/7, + tool-rounds-render / tool-completion / toolrounds-keep-longer / rendermessage-segment-gate = 11/11; wider sweep incl. brain-tool-render + segments-not-echoed = 21/21.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (content-hashed filename) to see it live. NOTE: styles.css working tree ALSO carries large PRE-EXISTING uncommitted work from before this session (sidebar folder "app-icon" tiles, zero-CLS first-paint, the 2026-07-07 spine timeline that this change supersedes) — my hunks sit cleanly on top; the redesign is only the `.ptool-panel`/`.ptool-turn`/`.seg-*` blocks above.
- **Follow-up (owner sign-off gate) — grouped-card doubled-seam fix.** With `.ptool-turn` now a bordered card, the LAST `.ptool-line`'s own `border-bottom` doubled against the card's bottom border = a visible seam. Finding: the per-row separator is TOFU-ONLY (base/light `.ptool-line` has no border-bottom). Fix (tofu-scoped): `[data-theme="tofu"] .ptool-turn > [data-prn]:last-child .ptool-line{border-bottom:none}` — keeps inter-row separators (parallel-call grouping signal) but drops the final row's line since the card edge already draws it; covers the solo card (its one row is `:last-child`) and a row nested in a last-slot `.ptool-results-block`. Solo-card cramp check: `.ptool-line` has `min-height:28px` so a one-line solo card can't collapse to a sliver (~40px rounded card); with an ordinal it gets the `.ptool-turn-rno-solo` header strip, without one the row sits under the top border with `.ptool-line`'s 5px padding (centered, comfortable). CSS bundle → `styles-10c47eef.css`; tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6761/6761; guard suites 11 passed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When streaming and finished render share the same class contract, a "redesign the tool UI" ask is often pure CSS — verify the class structure matches on both paths first, then restyle once and both are covered with no JS/reflow risk. When a guard test parses a CSS `margin` shorthand, DON'T reuse a px-only tokenizer: unitless `0`s vanish and mis-index the T/R/B/L slots (here `2px 0 8px 0` parsed as `[2,8]` → read left as 8, not 0). When you wrap previously-borderless rows in a bordered card, the row's OWN bottom-border (if any theme sets one) doubles at the card edge — strip it on `:last-child` only, keeping inter-row separators.


### 2026-07-07 — Frontend rendering-stability strike: native `overflow-anchor` + shared anchor-restore helpers on the full-render path + known-stale IDB first-paint gate. (#3 streaming→settled finalize flicker STILL OPEN under pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5 — do not let it evaporate.)
- **Ask (owner).** "Why does our frontend feel off vs ChatGPT/DeepSeek/Claude — flicker, unstable conversation state, sudden jump-to-top, and (poor network) sometimes WRONG content?" Diagnose the roots and go all out. A 4-agent parallel audit (streaming/flicker, scroll, IDB-reconcile, industry-benchmark) split the complaint into THREE distinct roots, one already largely solved:
  - **#1 wrong-content-on-poor-network — mostly ALREADY fixed.** The server-authoritative `rev` epic had landed: schema **v37** with a monotonic `rev` column (trigger-bumped), PUT carries `baseRev` → stale base returns **409 `blocked_rev_conflict`** → rebase+retry (conversations.js:526,561-592); the old wall-clock `localNewest>serverNewest` tiebreaker is DELETED; IDB demoted to a pure paint-cache. So a stale cache can no longer PERSIST over server truth. Residual = a cosmetic transient: IDB Phase-1 paints instantly, Phase-2 GET corrects up to ~10s later, so on a bad link you briefly SEE stale content.
  - **#2 jump-to-top / scroll instability — the real open bug.** `renderChat` full-render path does `inner.innerHTML = html` → hard-resets scrollTop→0; recovery relied ENTIRELY on `_forceScrollToBottom` → a background full re-render (cost/file-change settle, poll, artifact hydrate) yanked a scrolled-up reader to bottom. Compounded by ZERO `overflow-anchor` anywhere in styles.css and bare markdown chat images with no reserved box (late decode shoves content).
  - **#3 streaming→settled finalize flicker — SCOPED OUT (owned).** `finalizeStreaming` does `sm.outerHTML = renderMessage(...)` but the streaming DOM structure ≠ settled DOM (zone order + expanded-vs-collapsed thinking) → one-frame reflow flash. This machinery is epic **pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5** (segment-timeline frontend cutover) and sibling **mras4t1e** was LIVE in it — deliberately NOT touched to avoid collision. **This piece remains OPEN.**
- **What shipped (all uncommitted for owner attribution).**
  1. **`static/styles.css`** (appended one ISOLATED block at EOF, under a narrow path lease, overriding NO existing rule): `#chatContainer/#chatInner/#chatInner .message{overflow-anchor:auto}` (native browser scroll anchoring — the single highest-leverage primitive, no JS); `#streaming-msg{overflow-anchor:none}` (the live bubble must ride the bottom as it grows); `.message-body img:not(.msg-img-thumb img,.ig-result-card img,.imagegen-card img,.ig-batch-slot img,.rf-img-tile img){aspect-ratio:3/2;height:auto;object-fit:contain}` (reserved box for the bare-markdown image fallback — the fixed thumbnails + image-gen cards already reserve space so they're excluded); `#chatInner.chat-cache-verifying{opacity:.82;transition:opacity .18s}`.
  2. **`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`**: extracted the proven `_bgRefreshChat` anchor logic into shared `_captureScrollAnchor(container,inner)` + `_restoreScrollAnchor(container,anchor)` (reuse, not reinvent; `_bgRefreshChat` now calls them). Applied to the **full-render path**: capture `_preSwapAnchor` ONLY when `_sameConvDom` (`_lazyConvId===conv.id` && inner has `[id^=msg-]`) && NOT `isNearBottom(120)` && no live stream → restore under the `cv-off` guard after the swap; ELSE `_forceScrollToBottom` (a genuine conv SWITCH, first load, or near-bottom reader still lands at the bottom, which is correct). Left `stream_lifecycle.js:76` alone (force-to-bottom is correct there — stream active).
  3. **`static/js/core/conversations.js`**: Phase-1 `_cacheKnownStale = (conv.updatedAt||0) > (cached.updatedAt||0)` — the sidebar list's server-issued `updatedAt` is the ETag-like staleness signal. Still paints instantly (no blank wait) but adds `chat-cache-verifying` (dim) so the provisional pre-correction render reads as "verifying", cleared by `_setCacheVerifying(convId,false)` on Phase-2 settle + the fetch-failed early return + the catch. Closes the cosmetic flash only; rev CAS already blocks persisted corruption.

### 2026-07-07 — Unify, part 3 (the last named nit): routed the remote `source_image` download in `lib/tasks_pkg/executor_image.py::_resolve_source_image` through the unified `lib.http_client.http_get` instead of raw `requests.get` — closes the final concrete item the reorg audit named
- **Why.** The audit's `http_client`-consistency finding was a single site: `_resolve_source_image` did `import requests as _requests; resp = _requests.get(image_ref, timeout=30)` for the remote-URL branch of image-edit source resolution, bypassing the project's proxy-aware HTTP seam (`lib/http_client.py`). Every other outbound HTTP in the tool layer already goes through `http_get`/`http_post`. This is a behaviour IMPROVEMENT, not just cosmetic: `http_get` auto-applies `proxies_for(url)`, so a remote `source_image` on a proxied deployment now actually resolves (raw `requests.get` had no proxy).
- **What shipped.** Swapped the function-local `import requests as _requests` → `from lib.http_client import http_get` and `_requests.get(image_ref, timeout=30)` → `http_get(image_ref, timeout=30)`. `http_get` returns a `requests.Response` with the identical `.content` / `.headers` / `.raise_for_status()` surface the two following lines use, so the rest of the branch (b64-encode `resp.content`, read `Content-Type`) is byte-unchanged. Confirmed zero remaining `_requests` refs in the file.
- **Verify.** `ruff check lib/tasks_pkg/executor_image.py` clean; module imports cleanly. (No behavioural unit test added — this is a 1-line transport swap with an identical response contract; the branch's own logic is untouched.)
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only.
- **Decision — STOPPING the unification program here (owner-endorsed reasoning).** The two remaining `run_agent_loop` adopters are genuine incompatibilities, NOT deferral-on-principle: the **orchestrator**'s round ceiling EXPANDS mid-loop (`_premature_retry_count`) vs the primitive's fixed `range(max_tool_rounds+1)` — adopting it would drop the retry extension or require a `should_extend(rnd)->bool` contract change affecting every existing adopter; the **swarm** runs a round's tools in PARALLEL (ThreadPoolExecutor), so the between-tools abort check (the one that fixed "Stop has limited effect") lands in a fundamentally different place — forcing it through the sequential `execute_tool` hook would either serialize swarm tools (perf regression) or defeat the abort semantics. Both are separate design increments (teach the primitive an optional `parallel_tools` executor + `should_extend` callback) gated on explicit sign-off of that primitive contract change — not a lossy shoehorn. This turn's three cuts (`_feed_codex` dedup, timer `run_agent_loop` adoption, this `http_get` nit) are the safe, behaviour-preserving subset of the reorg mandate; the rest is correctly left as designed-for-later.


### 2026-07-07 — Unify, part 2: adopted the shared `run_agent_loop` primitive in the timer poll mini-agent loop (`lib/scheduler/timer.py::poll_timer`) — the LOW-risk `run_agent_loop` adopter CLAUDE.md flagged as still pending, behaviour-preserving with a DB-free parity + neuter test
- **Why (owner held me to the broader mandate).** Part 1 (the `_feed_codex` SSE dedup) was an honest cut but a narrow slice of "reorganize / modularize / establish a unified interface". The audit itself named the timer poll loop as the cleanly-adoptable win for `lib/agent_loop.run_agent_loop` — the very primitive whose docstring says "orchestrator/endpoint/swarm/timer adopt later". Sibling-collision fear was unfounded: the live scheduler sibling works on log detection/coverage, not the timer's agent-loop, and `run_agent_loop` is a stable seam. So this advances the "unified interface" mandate directly.
- **What shipped (`lib/scheduler/timer.py`).** Replaced the hand-rolled `for agent_round in range(_MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS)` tool-calling loop in `poll_timer` with a `run_agent_loop(...)` call driven by three small closures over the existing locals:
  - `_poll_dispatch(rnd, _tools) -> (msg, finish=None, usage)` wraps `smart_chat` (tool calls arrive in `usage['_tool_calls']`, not the message), captures `poll_model` from `usage['_dispatch']`, sums `total_tokens`, and returns the assistant `msg` dict the primitive inspects for `tool_calls`. It IGNORES the primitive's per-round `tools` arg and always passes `poll_tools` — so the timer's "tools available on EVERY poll round, no final tools-off round" invariant is preserved.
  - `_poll_on_tool_round(rnd, msg)` logs the round + appends the assistant tool-call message (the primitive's `on_tool_round` hook fires exactly when a round has tool calls, before executing them).
  - `_poll_execute(rnd, tc)` wraps `_execute_poll_tool`, appends the `tool_trace` timeline entry (unchanged shape) + the tool-result message.
  - `abort=AbortSignal.never()` — polls have no Stop path; the primitive explicitly supports this classmethod.
- **Round-cap arithmetic (the "is it lossy?" question — answered, NOT lossy).** Original: `range(_MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS)` = rounds 0..4 = **5 dispatches**, `break` on no-tool-call. Primitive: `for rnd in range(max_tool_rounds + 1)`. With `max_tool_rounds = _MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS - 1 = 4` → rounds 0..4 = **5 dispatches**, byte-identical, and the natural-stop `break` maps to the primitive's `completed`. The one shape the primitive can't model — a ceiling that EXPANDS mid-loop (the orchestrator's `_premature_retry_count`) — does NOT exist in the timer (fixed cap), so there's no incompatibility here (unlike the orchestrator, correctly still deferred).
- **Everything else preserved byte-for-byte.** `smart_chat` kwargs (`max_tokens=4096 if poll_tools else 256`, `temperature=0`, `capability='cheap'`, `log_prefix`), the `usage['_dispatch']`→`poll_model` capture, `total_tokens` summation, the `tool_trace` entry dict, the post-loop `parse_json_decision` JSON-decision parse + parse_error/raw_content diagnostics, and the exception→`LLM error` early-return (now via a `_last_round` cell so the failing-round number is still logged faithfully). The 9-tuple return is unchanged.
- **Gate — NEW `tests/test_timer_poll_agent_loop.py` (4 tests, all green), DB-FREE.** Stubs `_get_timer_row` + `smart_chat` + `_execute_poll_tool` (per the stub-isolation preference) so the loop runs purely in memory — dodging the timer_watchers/timer_poll_log table dependency that makes the pre-existing `test_timer_parse_failure.py` error out on this ephemeral SQLite. Asserts: (1) multi-round tool→result→decision produces the SAME `tool_trace` (one entry, exact dict), `total_tokens` (15 = 10+5 summed across rounds), `poll_model` ('cheap-x' from `_dispatch`), parsed `(ready='all green')`, and verbatim `raw_content`; (2) a model that never stops calling tools dispatches EXACTLY `_MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS` (5) times with one tool per round (the cap); (3) a `smart_chat` exception → `LLM error` parse_error tuple with tokens preserved + empty trace; (4) non-JSON final content → parse_error with raw text preserved.
- **NEUTER (proves the parity test bites, not a tautology).** Changed `max_tool_rounds=_MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS - 1` → `_MAX_POLL_AGENT_ROUNDS` (drop the `-1`) → `test_round_cap_when_model_never_stops` FAILED (6 dispatches ≠ 5). Restored (a `git checkout` reverted the whole refactor, so I re-applied both edits verbatim and re-verified green).
- **Verify.** `ruff check lib/scheduler/timer.py` clean; `grep run_agent_loop`=3, old `for agent_round` loop=0. `test_timer_poll_agent_loop + test_timer_poll_event_suppression + test_codex_sse_accumulator` → **11 passed**. The pre-existing `test_timer_parse_failure.py` (4 fail / 5 error) is DB-bootstrap fixture noise (`no such table: timer_watchers/timer_poll_log` on ephemeral SQLite) — proven pre-existing (same failures with the change stashed), unrelated to this refactor; my new test deliberately avoids that DB dependency.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only (no bundle). Server restart picks up the import. STILL deferred with a concrete reason: swarm sub-agent loop (parallel ThreadPoolExecutor tool exec — different abort placement, own increment) and the orchestrator loop (expanding retry ceiling — genuinely unmodellable by the fixed-range primitive).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When adopting a shared bounded-loop primitive, do the round-cap arithmetic explicitly: `range(N)` (N dispatches, break-on-stop) == `run_agent_loop(max_tool_rounds=N-1)` (rounds 0..N-1). If the caller wants tools on EVERY round (no tools-off final round), have the `dispatch` adapter IGNORE the primitive's per-round `tools` arg and pass its own — the primitive offers `None` on the final round by default. Isolate the parity test from DB tables the module only touches at the edges (stub `_get_timer_row`) so it runs where the heavier pre-existing suite can't.

I refused to just tag them `transcription`: code-verified `_post_to_provider` hard-codes `POST {base}/audio/transcriptions` (multipart), but these are omni CHAT models with NO such endpoint — tagging them would 404 on every click. Also corrected: `ernie-5.0-thinking-preview` is text/image/video only (ArtificialAnalysis + ZenMux both show Audio "–"; audio belongs to base ERNIE 5.0) → dropped from scope. Owner ratified the correct mechanism (a chat-audio mode) and made the gateway-shape call: Meituan `/openai/native` is OpenAI-compatible → use the OpenAI `input_audio` content-part.
- **What shipped (the `audio_chat` mechanism).**
  1. **`lib/transcription.py`** — NEW cap `AUDIO_CHAT_CAP='audio_chat'`; `TRANSCRIPTION_CAPS={transcription,audio_chat}`. `_transcription_slots()` now selects slots whose caps INTERSECT that set (still excludes `oauth`). `_slot_audio_mode(slot)`: `transcription`→'endpoint', else→'chat', BOTH→'endpoint' wins (cheaper/purpose-built). NEW `_transcribe_via_chat()` builds `messages=[{role:user, content:[{type:input_audio, input_audio:{data:<b64>, format}}, {type:text, text:verbatim-instruction}]}]` and routes `dispatch_chat(capability='audio_chat', prefer_model=slot.model, strict_model=True, temperature=0)` — strict so the picker never silently swaps to a text-only model that would reject the audio. `_audio_format_token()` maps MIME→OpenAI `format` token. `transcribe()` now branches per-slot on mode. NEW `inline_audio_byte_cap()` (env `TOFU_INLINE_AUDIO_MAX_BYTES`, default **20 MiB** — TIGHTER than the 25 MiB endpoint cap because base64 inflates the payload ~33% into the chat JSON; Gemini's documented inline ceiling); the size guard is applied PER-MODE inside the loop (chat slot → inline cap, endpoint slot → larger cap). `list_transcription_models()` now returns `mode` too.
  2. **Dispatcher / config** — `audio_chat` added to `_NON_CHAT_CAPS` (so an audio-only omni slot is never chat-picked for TEXT). Added `audio_chat` to `gemini-3-flash-preview`'s caps AND a NEW `LongCat-Flash-Omni` entry in `DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS` — REQUIRED, see trap below.
  3. **Meituan template** (`static/provider_templates/meituan.json`) — `gemini-3-flash-preview` gained `audio_chat`; NEW `LongCat-Flash-Omni` row `["text","vision","audio_chat"]`. ⚠️ **LongCat gateway model id flagged for owner to verify** (used `LongCat-Flash-Omni`; couldn't confirm from here — 学城 is unreachable).
  4. **GUI + pricing** — `audio_chat` added to both cap-toggle lists (`model_edit.js`, `access_matrix.js`), both `reeval_pricing_tags.py` non-chat skip-sets + `_canonical_caps_order`.

So adding `audio_chat` to the template alone was NOT enough: the built slot dropped the cap and `transcription_available()` stayed False. Fix: add `audio_chat` to the model's `DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS` entry too. The stubbed-`_transcription_slots` tests could NEVER have caught this — only the real-dispatcher integration test did. (This is exactly why the owner insisted on a config→appear test that exercises real slot construction.)
- **Verification (all shown to owner).** `tests/test_audio_transcribe.py` 10→15 (NEW: audio_chat routes via `dispatch_chat` asserting the `input_audio` message shape + base64 round-trip + strict_model=True AND that NO multipart POST fires; NEUTER — a `transcription` slot must NOT hit `dispatch_chat`; `_slot_audio_mode` branch table; inline size guard fires without reaching dispatch_chat; inline cap ≤ endpoint cap). `tests/test_transcription_config_integration.py` 5→6 (NEW: an `audio_chat`-configured model is discoverable via the REAL slot-build with `mode='chat'`; updated 2 assertions for the new `mode` field). **Full suite: 33 passed** (audio 15 + config-integration 6 + voice-jsdom 1 + access-matrix 11). ruff clean on all changed Python. `python3 debug/reeval_pricing_tags.py --check` → **0 stale** (it normalized one unpriced `cheap` off LongCat but PRESERVED `audio_chat`). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-4860bf70.js` (was `bundle-49702338.js`); `'embedding', 'transcription', 'audio_chat'` appears 2× (both toggle lists). NOT committed (owner attribution). Correction pass still OFF/unwired.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An omni CHAT model that "supports audio" is a DIFFERENT wire shape from a Whisper endpoint — audio rides inline as an `input_audio` content-part through `/chat/completions`, NOT a multipart `/audio/transcriptions` POST. Model a distinct capability (`audio_chat`) and branch the transcribe path on it; never overload the `transcription` cap for a chat model. And when config-driven caps mysteriously vanish from a built slot, suspect `DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS` — its `caps` are AUTHORITATIVE over the provider-config list at slot-build, so a new capability must be registered in BOTH the template AND the reference table. ### 2026-07-07 — "Reorg / modularize / unify" request → MEASURE-FIRST audit found the codebase already healthily unified; executed the ONE genuine, safe, high-value dedup (`_feed_codex` → shared `_process_openai_chunk`), which also fixed two latent Codex streaming bugs. Reported the rest as recommendations rather than manufacturing a risky big-bang.
- **Ask (owner).** "Reorganize the project architecture, modularize duplicate functionality, establish a unified interface, be bold and decisive."
- **Method (measure-first, per owner preference).** A blind big-bang reorg on a mature codebase that has ALREADY been through TaskRuntime / api_response / request_parser / http_client / agent_verdict / agent_loop unifications would manufacture regression risk with little value (cf. the charter's own `@layer` big-bang CORRECTION). So I ran a 4-way parallel audit swarm — (1) agent-loop dup, (2) SSE/streaming dup, (3) response/parser/config-builder migration state, (4) coarse structural/god-file/route-twin dup — then judged each finding against the two shared primitives I read directly (`lib/agent_loop.py`, `lib/agent_verdict.py`).
- **Audit verdict (reassuring).** The codebase is already well-modularized. NO route-logic duplication (`routes/*.py` legacy modules merely register handlers onto the `routes/api_v1/*.py` blueprint ONCE — single registration, shared logic). Relocation shims (`lib/task_runtime.py`→`agent_core`, `lib/push.py`→`agent_core`, `llm_sanitize`/`llm_errors`→`lib/llm`) are tiny/documented/correct — mild clutter, deleting them = import-chase for near-zero gain. Tool def/exec split (`lib/tools/` schema / `lib/project_mod/` impl / `handlers/` dispatch) is clean 3-layer separation, not overlap. Frontend `fetch` → `api.js` migration is DONE + test-enforced (`test_frontend_api_isolation.py`); the config-builders (`resolve_conv_config` / `build_chat_config` / `_build_cfg` / `translate_*_request`) are LEGITIMATELY divergent (3-source merge vs kwargs vs alias-table vs wire protocol) and already share the one real invariant via `apply_headless_personal_defaults`. `~59` multi-line `jsonify` are custom shapes CLAUDE.md itself scopes out.
- **The genuine win executed — `lib/llm/_sse_core.py::_feed_codex`.** The Codex Responses-API SSE path hand-reimplemented the SAME content/thinking/tool-call-delta accumulation that `_process_openai_chunk`→`_handle_delta` already does — while the sibling `_feed_anthropic` correctly routes its translated OpenAI-shaped chunks straight through `_process_openai_chunk`. The Codex translator (`lib/oauth/codex.py::CodexSSETranslator._make_chunk`) also emits standard `chat.completion.chunk` dicts, so it was already shaped for the shared path. Routed it through `_process_openai_chunk` exactly like Anthropic (~45 dup lines → ~12). This is NOT just cosmetic dedup — it FIXES TWO LATENT BUGS the duplicate carried: (1) it NEVER fired `on_tool_call_ready`, so Codex uniquely got no incremental multi-tool read-only prefetch; (2) it gated content/thinking *accumulation* on the streaming callback (`if _c and self.on_content:`), so a Codex caller with NO `on_content` (e.g. a non-streaming consumer) silently LOST THE ENTIRE RESPONSE BODY — whereas `_handle_delta` accumulates unconditionally and only fires the callback when present.
- **Gate — NEW `tests/test_codex_sse_accumulator.py` (5 tests, all green).** Drives the REAL `CodexSSETranslator` + `SSEAccumulator` offline (no net/Flask/DB). Pins both fixes: content + thinking accumulate WITH NO callback (bug 2); callbacks still fire when present; `on_tool_call_ready` fires for a Codex tool call (bug 1); tool-call id + args accumulate across multiple `response.function_call_arguments.delta` events; `finish_reason` maps `tool_calls`/`stop`. No pre-existing test pinned the old Codex behaviour, so nothing had to change.
- **Verify.** `ruff check` clean on both changed files. Regression: `test_codex_sse_accumulator + test_continue_lossless + test_streaming_and_prefetch + test_premature_close_cooldown + test_anthropic_outbound + test_e2e_smoke` → **95 passed, 3 skipped**. (Run with `-p no:napari` — a napari/vispy conftest plugin fails to import GL ES in this env, unrelated.)
- **Deliberately NOT done (reported as recommendations, not gold-plated).** (a) Timer poll loop `lib/scheduler/timer.py:555` could adopt `run_agent_loop` via a `smart_chat`→`(msg,finish,usage)` dispatch adapter (`AbortSignal.never()` — polls have no Stop) — LOW risk / MODEST value, and a live sibling is actively working the scheduler/logging area, so deferred to avoid collision. (b) Swarm sub-agent loop `lib/swarm/agent.py:554` is the real prize but runs tools in PARALLEL (ThreadPoolExecutor) and has different abort placements than the sequential primitive — needs care, its own increment. (c) Orchestrator loop is a `while` whose ceiling EXPANDS with `_premature_retry_count` — a shape the fixed-range primitive can't model; CLAUDE.md correctly lists it as a "later" adopter. (d) `executor_image.py:242` `_requests.get(image_ref)` → `http_get` — 1-site proxy-consistency nit. None of these are duplication worth the risk right now.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only change (no bundle rebuild needed). Server restart picks up the import.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When asked to "reorganize/unify boldly" on a mature codebase, boldness = a decisive, MEASURED cut at the one genuine duplication, NOT a sweeping rewrite. Audit first (parallel swarm), judge each finding against the actual shared primitive, and be honest when the answer is "already unified — here's the single real win + why the rest is legitimate divergence." A duplicate that has quietly DRIFTED from the canonical path (here: Codex missing `on_tool_call_ready` + callback-gated accumulation) is the highest-value dedup precisely because unifying it also fixes the drift-bugs.

WHY: a cheap-priced whisper model (Groq $0.0004) would otherwise be handed a `cheap` CHAT tier tag and make `--check` fail. Now transcription models are left untouched like other non-chat caps. (Also removed two PRE-EXISTING unused imports `os` + `DEFAULT_SLOT_CONFIGS` — confirmed via `git stash` they were stale on committed master, not introduced here — since I was editing the file.)
- **Verification (owner wants each piece).**
  - **Diffs**: 2 one-token `allCaps` edits + 2 template edits + 3 rewriter edits (2 skip-sets + 1 order list) + 2 import removals.
  - **Provider-template guard**: `python3 debug/reeval_pricing_tags.py --check` → **`WOULD CHANGE: 0 model(s)`** (green). NOTE: the rewriter scans `static/js/settings.js` (a 1.5KB stub) + `static/provider_templates/*.json`, NOT `settings/provider_templates.js` — so my JS-literal template edits can't trip it; the guard's real job here was to confirm the cheap-whisper entries don't get a spurious `cheap` tag, which the skip-set fix ensures. `tests/test_api_v1_integration.py -k provider_templates` → 2 passed.
  - **Bundle**: rebuilt → `bundle-49702338.js` (was `bundle-c0cef452.js` from slice 2 — hash changed). Greps in the BUILT bundle: `'embedding', 'transcription'` appears **2×** (both toggle lists), `key: 'groq'` present, `gpt-4o-transcribe` present, `whisper-large-v3-turbo` present.
  - **Dispatcher-integration test** (`tests/test_transcription_config_integration.py`, NEW, 5 tests): builds a REAL dispatcher via `LLMDispatcher._build_slots_from_providers` from a provider config with `capabilities:['transcription']`, monkeypatches `lib.llm_dispatch.factory.get_dispatcher` to return it (and stubs the instance's `.initialize` to a no-op so discovery doesn't overwrite the hand-built slots). Asserts: `transcription_available()` True + `list_transcription_models()` lists `my-whisper` (not the sibling chat model); chat-only config stays False; `GET /api/v1/audio/capabilities` returns `available:true` with the model; a transcription-only slot is NOT `_is_chat_compatible` (never chat-picked); an `oauth` slot with the cap is excluded. **5 passed.** This closes the loop the slice-1 tests didn't (they stub `_transcription_slots`).

- **Guardrail / lesson.** When adding a NON-CHAT capability, it's not enough to register it in the dispatcher's `_NON_CHAT_CAPS` — the pricing-tags rewriter (`debug/reeval_pricing_tags.py`) has its OWN independent `{image_gen, embedding}` skip sets in TWO places, and a cheap-priced non-chat model will get a bogus `cheap` tag (breaking CI `--check`) unless the cap is added there too. Grep for the non-chat skip set whenever adding a capability. Also: the pricing rewriter targets the `settings.js` STUB, not the split `settings/*.js` files, so template edits in the split files are invisible to it — the built bundle is where you verify them.


### 2026-07-07 — Portrait-tablet text truncation, ROOT-CAUSE fix: gated the width-only desktop-compaction breakpoints on `pointer:fine` (they never reach a coarse tablet) instead of the fragile hide-then-re-show double-negative — plus a drift-guard test with teeth
- **Symptom (owner).** On tablets in PORTRAIT (PC-mode layout), "many texts are truncated even though there's plenty of viewing space." Not ellipsis-clipping — whole text labels were HIDDEN.
- **Root cause (code-verified).** Two WIDTH-ONLY compaction breakpoints, tuned to shrink genuinely cramped NARROW DESKTOP windows, also fire on a portrait tablet (769–1024px wide, coarse pointer) which has ample room — width alone can't tell the two apart:
  - `@media(max-width:1080px)` → `.topbar-tool-label,.update-btn-label{display:none}` collapsed **Paper / My Day / Studio / Tasks / Update** to icon-only.
  - `@media(max-width:1024px)` → `.search-mode-toggle .sm-label{display:none}` hid the **"Search"** label.
- **First attempt (superseded).** Re-showed the labels inside the coarse-pointer tablet block. Owner rightly rejected it as a patch-on-a-patch double-negative: any NEW width-only label-hider in the 769–1024 range silently truncates tablets again with nothing to catch it (this was the THIRD hand-fix of the class — 增强/工具/模式, then these two).
- **Root-cause fix (CSS).** Gated the two offending blocks themselves on `and (pointer:fine)` so they only compact a real (fine-pointer) DESKTOP window and NEVER fire on a coarse tablet/phone → deleted the re-show lines entirely (fewer rules, no double-negative). Coarse PHONES (≤768) no longer inherited the ≤1080 label hide, so added an INDEPENDENT `.topbar-tool-label,.update-btn-label{display:none}` into the ≤768 phone block (the phone block already independently hides `.sm-label` + the depth-bar + submenus, so ≤1024 needed nothing). Also, from the owner's scope audit: the topbar `.model-badge` base rule has `white-space:nowrap` but NO max-width/ellipsis (that lived only in the ≤768 block), so a long model name at 769px was hard-cut by the topbar `overflow:hidden` with no ellipsis → added `.model-badge{max-width:200px;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}` to the coarse-tablet block (graceful clip, roomier than the phone's 120px).
- **Scope audit (owner-requested).** Enumerated every `@media` with a max-width in [769,1024] that is NOT `pointer:fine`: the ONLY text-label truncation was the two clusters above. The other width-only tablet-band blocks are pure layout reflow / intentional chrome-hiding, NOT text truncation: `≤900 .paper-report-doc`→single-col + `.paper-report-toc{display:none}` (TOC nav, deliberate reading layout), `≤900 .paper-read-time` padding, `≤820 .mcp-catalog-grid` single-col, `≤900 .ctx-health-bar{display:none}` (diagnostic bar), landscape-phone height block. Reported to owner as "genuinely only these two + the model-badge clip."
- **Drift-guard (NEW `tests/test_tablet_label_truncation.py`, 4 tests, all green).** Brace-matched `@media` iterator; INVARIANT test fails if any block with a max-width in [769,1024] that is NOT `pointer:fine` sets a known text-label selector (`.topbar-tool-label`/`.update-btn-label`/`.sm-label`/`.submenu-label`) to `display:none`. Positive lock asserts the two known blocks carry `pointer:fine`. NEUTER: injects a width-only `≤1000px .topbar-tool-label{display:none}` into the real CSS and asserts the scanner FLAGS it (load-bearing, not a tautology); complementary NC asserts the SAME block gated on `pointer:fine` is NOT flagged (exemption honored).
- **Verify.** tinycss2 0 errors, braces 6752/6752; coarse-pointer tablet predicate still a SINGLE width (1024) → `test_breakpoint_coordination.py` 8/8; new guard 4/4 (run `-p no:napari` — a napari/vispy conftest plugin fails to import GL ES in this env, unrelated). Bundle rebuilt → `styles-52d6325a.css` (grep-confirmed: both blocks `pointer:fine`-gated, re-show removed, model-badge cap present; old bundle cleaned). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard-refresh on device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A `@media(max-width:Npx)` that HIDES a text label is a DESKTOP-window-compaction rule and misfires on same-width portrait tablets. Fix it at the ROOT — gate the compaction on `and (pointer:fine)` so it can't reach a coarse tablet — not by re-showing in the tablet block (a double-negative the next author will re-break). When you move a hide behind `pointer:fine`, check whether coarse PHONES were silently relying on that same rule and give them an independent hide in the ≤768 block. Back any such structural fix with a drift-guard that scans the band and NEUTER-proves it bites.


### 2026-07-07 — Interleaved segment-timeline render: styled the previously-CSS-less `.seg-narration` / `.seg-thinking` so tool cards + connective prose read as ONE column instead of alternating full-width slabs
- **Symptom (owner).** "The current alternating rendering of tools and content looks extremely ugly." The finished multi-tool assistant reply showed a choppy rhythm: a full-width text block, then a boxed/indented tool card, then another full-width text block, …
- **Root cause (code-verified, not a data bug).** The interleaved per-tool timeline (epic pt_8b406df8fbe24ae5) is the DEFAULT-ON finished-message renderer (`config.segmentTimeline !== false`; Settings › General "Per-tool inline timeline"). `renderSegmentTimelineHTML` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js:2658`) walks `msg.segments`, and per LLM round emits the preceding thinking (`.seg-thinking`) + narration (`.md-content.seg-narration`) ADJACENT to that round's tool rows, all inside `.ptool-panel-body`. But `.seg-timeline` / `.seg-narration` / `.seg-thinking` had **ZERO CSS** (grep-confirmed). So the narration inherited bare `.md-content` (14px, full width, x=0) while the tool turns sit indented in the timeline's 28px gutter (`.ptool-turn` grid + `.ptool-line` 16px inset) — full-width prose slab vs. indented boxed card, alternating. The renderer comment even said it deliberately reused proven classes and added "NO new CSS" because styles.css was under a sibling's hold at the time — the styling was simply never backfilled.
- **Alignment ARITHMETIC (the hard bug, owner-flagged — my first pass got it wrong).** Narration/thinking blocks are SIBLINGS of the `.ptool-turn` grids inside `.ptool-panel-body` (0 padding), so their x is measured from 0. A tool row's content sits at **44px**: the `.ptool-turn` grid is `28px minmax(0,1fr)` (28px ordinal/spine gutter) + `.ptool-line`'s 16px `padding-left`. My first fix used `margin-left:16px`, which left narration **28px (one whole gutter) short** of the tool column — still misaligned, exactly as the owner said. CORRECTED: `.seg-narration` → `margin-left:44px` (lands ON the solo tool-content column, prose directly above the icons of the tools it introduces); `.seg-thinking` → `margin-left:28px` (its BOX left edge on the tool-box rail, matching where each solo `.ptool-line` box begins).
- **Fix (CSS only, purely additive — `static/styles.css`, new block before `.ptool-truncated`).** Scoped entirely under `.seg-timeline` (the panel wrapper class, so nothing outside the interleaved timeline is touched): `.seg-narration` `margin:2px 12px 6px 44px`, `font-size:13px`, `line-height:1.55`, `color:var(--text-secondary)`; paragraph rhythm tightened (`p{margin:4px 0}`, first/last child margin stripped); `.seg-thinking` `margin-left:28px`; `.seg-narration + .ptool-turn` / `.seg-thinking + .ptool-turn` zero their top margin. Uses existing theme tokens (`--text-secondary`) so dark/light/tofu all inherit; specificity (`.seg-timeline .seg-narration`) beats bare `.md-content`.
- **Streaming→settled jump (owner Q2) — checked, NO NEW JUMP.** The CSS is scoped to `.seg-timeline` (the FINISHED-render panel from `renderSegmentTimelineHTML`). The LIVE stream path (`_syncToolRoundsDOM` in `streaming_ui.js`) uses a plain `.ptool-panel` (no `.seg-timeline`), keeps its own zones (`tool`/`thinking`/`content`), and emits NO `.seg-narration`/`.seg-thinking` elements at all — so these rules are 100% inert during streaming and cannot introduce any layout jump. The stream→settled STRUCTURE change (grouped three-zone live view → interleaved timeline at finalize) is a PRE-EXISTING property of the epic, unchanged by this fix; this pass only styles the settled side. Full unification (streaming already carrying the interleaved structure) is a separate epic step, not in scope here.
- **REAL-LAYOUT EVIDENCE (owner Q3 — not just "bundle rebuilt").** Headless chromium was missing 12 system libs (`libatk`, `libgbm`, `libasound`, …) and there's no sudo; fetched them without root via `dnf download` + `rpm2cpio`/`cpio` into a gitignored `.tofu_chrome_deps/prefix` and pointed `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` at it. `.tofu_chrome_deps/measure_timeline.py` renders the FAITHFUL timeline DOM (verbatim `_renderTimelineBatch`/`_renderToolGroupsHTML` shapes) against the REAL `static/styles.css` and reports computed `left` (relative to `.ptool-panel-body`): **narration text = 44px, solo tool icon = 44px (Δ=0), thinking box = 28px = solo tool-box rail, narration0 == narration1 (stable)**. Screenshot at `.tofu_chrome_deps/timeline.png` visually confirms one coherent column. HONEST caveat recorded in the CSS comment: PARALLEL multi-call batches use a separate tighter bracket layout (`display:block`+`padding-left:10px`), so their rows sit at ~22px — narration tracks the dominant SOLO column and sits a little right of parallel-batch rows; acceptable, not a regression.
- **Coordination.** TWO siblings live in styles.css (mrarz1u1 responsive/tablet, mranrux3 tofu theme). Took a NARROW path lease scoped to only the new `.seg-*` rules, appended a fresh block (touched no existing rule), released on completion. No collision.
- **Verify.** tinycss2: **0 errors**, braces 6752/6752. CSS bundle rebuilt via `lib/css_bundler._build_minified()` → `styles-31850bda.css`; grep-confirmed present in the minified output. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard-refresh (content-hashed filename) to see it.
- **Legacy solo-turn gutter (owner's LAST check — the case that could break the reader view).** A solo turn with NO `llmRound` gets `_groupRoundNo→null` → renders WITHOUT the `.ptool-turn-rno-solo` ordinal; if the grid track weren't reserved, tool content would drop to ~16px and narration would sit 28px too far right. VERIFIED it can't: (a) CSS — `.ptool-turn[data-batch-size="1"]{display:grid}` (NOT `display:contents`; the JS comment saying "display:contents" is stale) so `grid-template-columns:28px …` reserves the track regardless of gutter content; chromium measured an ordinal-less legacy solo turn → `legacy_has_ordinal=False` but `tool_icon_left=44` (identical to the ordinaled one). (b) DATA — `tool_dispatch.py:759` stamps `llmRound=round_num` on EVERY real tool round; a scan of the 80 most-recent persisted `task_results.segments` found 68 tool-bearing turns, **0 with any None llmRound**, 59 genuinely multi-round — so real reopened conversations always render the ordinal anyway. (c) GUARD — the env-independent test now also asserts solo `.ptool-turn` display=='grid', so a future "collapse the solo box" edit fails the suite. Full suite 6/6 green.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a renderer ships behind "reuse proven classes, NO new CSS" because styles.css was locked, that's DEFERRED styling debt, not a finished feature — the new semantic classes render unstyled and inherit their tag defaults. But do the ALIGNMENT ARITHMETIC against the ACTUAL box model, not a guessed inset: here the tool content sits at gutter(28)+padding(16)=44px, NOT the 16px I first assumed — grid gutters are invisible in the source but real in layout. A sibling-column alignment also depends on the neighbour's grid TRACK being reserved, so guard the track (`display:grid`, not `contents`) too — an ordinal-less legacy row still aligns only because the 28px track survives. When the owner demands render proof, measure computed geometry in a real browser (fetch the browser's missing libs without root via rpm2cpio if needed) AND check the real persisted data, rather than asserting "the bundle rebuilt".

### 2026-07-07 — Tablet PC-mode toolbar: 增强/工具/模式 submenu labels collapsed to bare number badges — one over-aggressive `display:none` at the ≤1024px breakpoint
- **Symptom (owner, on tablet).** Tablet defaults to PC-mode layout, but the composer toolbar's 增强/工具/模式 submenu triggers showed only numbers, no Chinese text — labels looked "compressed away."
- **Root cause.** The tablet compaction rule `static/styles.css` `@media(max-width:1024px)` hid `.submenu-label`. But those three submenu triggers have **no icon** — their only visible content is the text label + a numeric `.submenu-count` badge + a chevron. Hiding the label left just the bare count badge (or an empty pill when no toggle active). Unlike `.search-mode-toggle` (icon + `.sm-label`) or `.depth-btn`, these are label-only, so hiding the label removes their entire meaning.
- **Fix.** Removed `.submenu-label{display:none}` from that one `@media(max-width:1024px)` rule (kept `.submenu-arrow` hidden + reduced `.submenu-trigger` padding to preserve the space-saving intent). Added a comment explaining why the label must stay. The ≤768px mobile block's `submenu-label{display:none}` is intentionally UNTOUCHED — there the whole 增强/工具/模式 set moves into the "···" bottom-sheet.
- **Non-overflow reasoning.** Three 2-char labels won't overflow: `.input-actions-scroll` already flexes with `min-width:0`.
- **Verify.** CSS bundle rebuilt → `styles-98a45aab.css`; confirmed the ≤1024px range no longer hides the label and the remaining hide is scoped to the ≤768px mobile block. NOT committed (owner attribution). Acceptance bar is real-device render (769–1024px PC-mode): restart server + hard-refresh tablet, confirm labels show as text with the number badge only when a toggle is active — pending owner confirmation on device.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Before hiding a text label in a compaction breakpoint, check whether the control has an icon fallback. Label-only controls (no icon) must keep their label at every breakpoint that still shows the control — hiding it strips the affordance to a meaningless badge. Icon+label controls (`.depth-btn`, `.search-mode-toggle`) are the only safe candidates for label-only hiding.


### 2026-07-07 — Tofu theme "breakthrough" redesign: stripped the retro-RPG/pixel aesthetic to zero across the WHOLE theme and rebuilt it as an editorial "Warm Reading Room" (default theme; owner: "completely strip the design elements and make a breakthrough")
- **Ask (owner).** The tofu theme (the DEFAULT — `_getCurrentTheme()`→`"tofu"`, so every new user sees it) was a warm-parchment RPG/pixel execution that "falls short." Completely strip the retro devices and rebuild on an internationally-credible design language; breakthrough beautification.
- **Direction (researched, owner-ratified).** "Warm Reading Room" = editorial reading-first typography (iA-lineage) + Japanese Ma / MUJI negative space + warm-paper palette + ONE confident clay accent. Closest proven precedent: Anthropic's "Warm 2024" (ochre-on-paper); we stay lighter/softer. Rejected hedging toward Linear/glass.
- **Font (self-hosted, no CDN — offline/firewall-safe).** Downloaded Newsreader variable woff2 (latin subset, roman + italic, ~195 KB, wOF2-verified, wght 200–800 + opsz axes) into `static/vendor/fonts/`; two `@font-face` blocks in the existing self-hosted `static/vendor/google-fonts-local.css`. New tokens `--serif-display` (Newsreader → system-serif fallback `'Iowan Old Style',Palatino,Georgia,'Songti SC',serif`) + `--sans-body`. Serif is the heading/brand hero; body stays humanist sans; **JetBrains Mono kept ONLY on genuine code text**.
- **Token core retuned (cascades app-wide).** Cleaner warm paper `#FAF7F0`, soft low-contrast borders `#E2DAC8`, clay accent `#C1794B` (was muddy tan `#BB9572`), radii 14/10/8, diffuse warm `--clay-*` shadows (replaced hard pixel-offset depth). Var NAMES unchanged (stable contract; every app-wide rule reads them).
- **Retro devices removed (whole theme, 3 increments).** Inc2 = 4 hero surfaces (messages/sidebar/topbar/input): killed the box-shadow pixel-art tofu-pet mascot, controller grip-wings, ✦ sparkles, D-pad + ABXY dots, speech-bubble tail, `◆/⚠/♨/❝/✦/▾MENU/SAVE✦SELECT` glyphs, CRT sidebar scanline, Pixelify/Press-Start display fonts, SNES-bevel send/new-chat buttons (211-line controller block → ~65). Inc3 = secondary surfaces: tool-result badges (mono+`1px 1px 0`→sans token chips), the "Game Boy cartridge" code blocks (bevel/scanline/pixel-notch→clean editorial code card, mono kept for code text), settings-modal + message-finish scanlines, 46 non-code mono labels→`--sans-body`, 54 hard-offset "sticker" shadows→`--clay-*`, thought-bubble pixel dots. Inc4 = 60 `border-radius:0` "neo-brutalist square" corners on card/button/modal/badge/panel/input surfaces → `--radius-sm`/`--radius`; tables/cells/inner-code/`::after` accents deliberately KEPT square.
- **Technique that mattered (Inc3/Inc4).** Bulk transforms were done as **brace-aware, comment-masked selector resolution** (mask `/*...*/`→equal-length spaces to preserve offsets, then resolve the innermost governing selector per char) with a code-selector allowlist + all-corner-only radius match — NOT blind sed. A naive selector walk had over-counted 214 mono sites (wrongly attributing base-theme code to a distant tofu ancestor); the brace-aware version correctly scoped to 46 tofu-noncode and left 188 base-theme mono usages + dark/light code untouched. Every transform: dry-run → tinycss2 verify → apply.
- **Final audit (all zero in tofu region).** `steps(1)`=0, scanline gradients=0, JetBrains-Mono-on-noncode=0 (only 5 genuine `code`/`pre` selectors keep it), hard-offset shadows=0, pixel display fonts=0, retro glyph pseudo-elements=0, non-structural all-corner `border-radius:0`=0. tinycss2: 13,853 rules, **0 errors**; braces 6744/6744. Mobile `@media` tofu block cleaned (input-box hard-offset→`--clay-md`, bottom-sheet/more-btn de-mono'd) — compact-toolbar architecture intact.
- **Verification + serve.** CSS is content-hash-bundled via `lib/css_bundler.py` (auto-busts on mtime) → rebuilt to `styles-2c11140b.css`. `google-fonts-local.css` is a static `<link>` (index.html:17), not hashed — hard-refresh loads the new faces. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard refresh to see it.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For large theme-wide CSS transforms, resolve the REAL governing selector with a brace-aware, comment-masked scan (a `/* comment */` prelude otherwise masquerades as the selector and silently skips rules) and match all-corner `border-radius:0` only (never a one-corner `0 0 Npx Npx` set) — then dry-run + tinycss2 before applying. Keep monospace on code text but strip it from badges/labels/buttons. The retro *feel* lives in decorative devices (glyphs, scanlines, pixel fonts, hard shadows, square brutalist corners), NOT the color tokens — retuning variables alone changes nothing.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "insight" second-pass, round 6 (final): closed the cache-reopen hole — a reopened paper now shows its persisted `insight:<ui>` section without regenerating. Feature reaches the reader end-to-end.
- **Why.** Round 5 wired the insight pass into live generation but left one hole I flagged myself: the DB-cache reopen path did NOT merge the separately-persisted `insight:<ui>` row, so a reader who generated an insight yesterday and reopens the paper today saw the plain report with the insight silently gone until a forced regenerate — the feature failing to reach the user in the most common return-visit case.
- **Fix (read-path only, reuse-not-duplicate).** New `routes/paper.py:_append_cached_insight(body, phash, lang)` — an async helper that LEFT-JOINs the sibling `insight:<ui_lang>` row (via `insight_lang_key`) and appends its markdown, the SAME concatenation the live `insight` event does. Wired into BOTH cache read sites right after `_ensure_title_heading`: the cache-hit branch of `start_report_task` AND `get_report_cache`. NEVER triggers a new generation (pure read). Guards make it byte-identical to today for papers without an insight: skips Review Mode (`is_review_lang`), no-ops when no/empty insight row, and never double-appends (idempotency check on the `## 💡` header line — covers a baked-in cache row and re-entry).
- **Gate — NEW `tests/test_paper_insight_cache_merge.py` (5), all green.** Stubs `async_fetchone` to serve seeded rows (so it runs offline without the Quart route stack — installs a no-op `Blueprint.websocket` shim on BOTH flask+quart Blueprint before the cold `routes.paper` import, since push.py does `from flask import Blueprint` and the shim only exists after server.py's Flask→Quart bridge): reopen merges the section EXACTLY once; no insight row → body byte-identical; already-present → no double-append; Review Mode key → never merges; NEUTER (replace the join with pass-through) → section absent, proving the merge is load-bearing. `tests/test_paper_insight_agentic.py` still 15/15. ruff clean.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). `TOFU_PAPER_INSIGHT`-gated OFF. Server restart needed (backend import). No new bundle (backend-only this round). The full feature is now end-to-end: generate (gated, personal-scope fail-closed on headless) → persist under `insight:<ui>` (report write-path) → live render → AND reopen-from-cache render. Standalone report-refinement critic pass still held.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Persist a sibling artifact under a separate key" is only half the delivery — every READ path that serves the primary artifact must LEFT-JOIN the sibling or the artifact vanishes on the common reopen. Wire the merge at the shared read seam (a single helper called from every cache branch), reuse the exact concatenation the live path uses, and guard it to be a no-op (byte-identical) when the sibling is absent + idempotent when already present. Test the join at the helper level with a stubbed DB fetch to dodge the route-stack import cost, and neuter the join to prove it's load-bearing.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "insight" second-pass, round 5: WIRED INTO THE LIVE REPORT PATH (flag-gated, headroom-gated, personal-scope fail-closed on headless) — the feature now reaches a reader instead of only an offline A/B
- **Why.** Rounds 1-4 built + measured the gated insight pass (win-rate 1.00, CI lower 1.00 at n=7 fired) but grep confirmed it was wired into NO surface — `generate_insight`/`TOFU_PAPER_INSIGHT` had zero hits in routes/report_engine/paper-reader.js. A pass that clears an offline A/B but reaches no reader improves no one. Owner: wire it in behind the flag, firing only when the report's own insight baseline ≤4.0; AND close the personal-scope leak (the reader-context block injects the OPERATOR's paper library + memory store — CLAUDE.md §3.7 — which on a headless/BYO surface would splice one operator's reading history into an unrelated caller's analysis).
- **The leak was REAL, not hypothetical.** `routes/api_v1/agents.py:paper_report_start()` delegates to the SAME `routes/paper.py:start_report_task()` the interactive UI uses → the report path (and thus the insight pass) IS reachable from the headless `/api/v1/agents/paper/report` scope. Wiring the reader-context in as-is would leak.
- **What shipped (backend).** (1) `lib/agent_core/personal_scope.py`: NEW registry entry `paperInsightPersonalContext` (headless_default=False, ui_default=True) + `resolve_paper_insight_personal_context(cfg)` (explicit cfg wins; absent → True for the interactive owner). The ratchet auto-covers it — `apply_headless_personal_defaults` iterates the registry, so every headless builder stamps it False for free. (2) `lib/paper/insight_engine.py`: `generate_insight(..., allow_personal_context=True)` — when False, `reader_context=''` (personal library/memories NEVER built), the pass still runs without its personal bridges. NEW `run_report_insight()` = the gated persisted entry: score report (1 no-tool rubric call = gate input) → `insight_gate_fires(baseline)` (≤4.0, fail-open on None) → `generate_insight` → persist under `insight:<ui>` via `_persist_insight` which reuses the report engine's EXACT `upsert(db, PAPER_REPORTS, …)` write-path (no hand-rolled second writer, per owner's reuse-production-write-path preference). (3) `lib/paper/report_engine.py`: after the report `done` event, `_maybe_run_insight()` runs (best-effort, fully wrapped so a failure never taints the persisted report) IFF `insight_enabled()` and not Review Mode; resolves `allow_personal_context` from `task['config']` via personal_scope; emits `insight_start` → `insight`(markdown+baseline+grounded+selfref) | `insight_skipped`. (4) `report_runtime._new_report_task(..., config=None)` threads the cfg; `routes/paper.py` builds `_report_cfg` — the headless façade sets `g.paper_report_headless` → route runs `apply_headless_personal_defaults(_report_cfg)` (fail-closed), interactive owner leaves it unset → personal ON. Both report + review task-create calls pass `config=_report_cfg`.
- **What shipped (frontend, paper-reader.js — DEFERRED feature bundle).** `_applyReportEvent` gains `insight_start` (sets `_insightRunning` hint) / `insight` (appends the `## 💡` Markdown block to `s.fullText` + the cached snapshot, guarded by `_insightApplied` against cursor-replay double-append, forces re-render through the SAME markdown renderer + TOC) / `insight_skipped`. New stream-state fields `insightText`/`_insightRunning`/`_insightApplied`. Bundle rebuilt → core `bundle-c202b3e8.js`, feature `feature-82c2d2fe.js` (grep-confirmed carries `insight_start`/`_insightApplied`).
- **Gate — `tests/test_paper_insight_agentic.py` 11→15, all green.** +4 integration tests driving `run_report_insight` offline (fake rubric controls baseline, fake synthesis, captured `_persist_insight`, reader-context-called probe): low baseline (3.2) → FIRES + generates + persists under `insight:en`; high baseline (4.75) → WITHHELD (no gen, no persist, reader-context never built); headless (`allow_personal_context=False`) → still fires + persists but reader-context NEVER built (the personal-leak guard, end-to-end); NEUTER on the gate (None→fail-open fires; high→withholds → the gate is the lever). personal_scope ratchet (registry fail-closed + prompt-omission) green with the new capability. ruff clean on all backend files; `node --check` clean on paper-reader.js.

The DB-CACHE reopen path does NOT yet merge the separate `insight:<ui>` row into a re-opened cached report — reopening a paper whose insight was generated in a prior session won't show the section until regeneration. That's a follow-up (the cache-hit branch in `start_report_task` + `_renderFinalReport` cache path need to LEFT-JOIN the insight row). Flagged so it's not mistaken for done.
