- **Guardrail / lesson.** A feature isn't done at "passes the offline eval" — it's done when it reaches the surface the objective named; grep the actual call sites before claiming integration. When a handler is SHARED by an interactive route and a headless façade, the personal-state boundary must be drawn at the façade (set a `g` marker) and resolved through the personal_scope registry — never a per-surface hardcode, and never assume "the report route is UI-only". Reuse the production persistence write-path (`upsert(PAPER_REPORTS)`) for the new row rather than a second writer, so schema/upsert/dialect semantics can't drift.


### 2026-07-07 — Streaming auto-translate render UNIFICATION: Chinese now flows in as the PRIMARY body in its natural interleaved position (not a big block dumped at the bottom), and the streaming bubble already has the SETTLED structure so finalize is a visual no-op
- **Ask (owner).** The streaming translation + inline timeline looked buggy: the translated Chinese all output "in one big block at the very bottom." Fundamentally optimize auto streaming translation so it flows seamlessly "as if originally Chinese" — understated, simple, aesthetically pleasing. Owner ratified the design: **(A) English-tail-then-swap** (never blank/lag — show translated Chinese for closed rounds + live English tail for the still-untranslated current round, swap in place as each round lands, converge to fully-Chinese) + **(B) keep the collapsed 原文/译文 toggle**. Core requirement: the streaming bubble must already have the SETTLED structure (Chinese primary in the content area, English collapsed) → **zero layout jump at finalize**.
- **Root cause (confirmed in code, not a crash).** The streaming bubble's zones (`_ensureStreamZones`, streaming_ui.js) were laid out `… tool → thinking → content → fc → status → translatePreview`. English streamed token-by-token into the `content` zone (interleaved with the tool timeline); the incremental translator (`lib/translate/incremental.py`) pushed cumulative Chinese partials which `_renderStreamingTranslatePreview` (translation.js) painted into `[data-zone="translatePreview"]` — **the LAST zone, pinned at the bottom**. So mid-task: full English body, then a growing Chinese block dumped underneath, then a re-layout jump at finalize when it flipped to the settled `.bilingual-original` structure (Chinese primary, English in the collapsed toggle). The two languages lived in two different zones and the Chinese one was bottom-pinned.
- **Key alignment fact that made the fix clean.** On `delta_reset` (sse_pipeline.js:910) the frontend sets `assistantMsg.content=""`, so mid-stream the `content` zone only ever holds the CURRENT round's English prose (prior narration is cleared). The incremental `_translatePartial` is the CUMULATIVE Chinese of all CLOSED rounds (pushed at each round close; `submit_round_segment` fires at `delta_reset`, orchestrator.py:2175). So `[Chinese partial = closed rounds] + [English content zone = current open round]` is exactly decision A — naturally complementary, non-overlapping. The ONLY overlap is the final round (no tool call → no `delta_reset` → its English stays in `content` AND its segment lands in the partial at finalize).
- **What shipped (render-layer only; commit path + `translatedContent` semantics UNCHANGED).**
  1. **`_ensureStreamZones` (streaming_ui.js).** New `[data-zone="translatedPrimary"]` slot inserted ABOVE `content`. `translatePreview` retained as a hidden legacy fallback slot (graceful degrade for a body predating the new slot). Zone cache extended with `translatedPrimary`.
  2. **`_renderStreamingTranslatePreview` (translation.js).** Repointed to paint the Chinese-so-far into `translatedPrimary` as a bare `.md-content` (NO spinner/label chrome — structurally mirrors the settled assistant body so the transition is seamless; a soft blinking caret marks the live edge via CSS `::after`). Stamps `body[data-xlate="1"]` and adds `stream-content-demoted` to the content zone. Legacy-body fallback to `translatePreview` preserved.
  3. **`updateStreamingUI` content-zone (streaming_ui.js).** Reads `data-xlate` / `data-xlate-final` (pure class toggles on the existing zone; render logic untouched): `stream-content-demoted` makes the English a quiet smaller dimmed live tail under the Chinese; `stream-content-tail-hidden` hides it entirely.
  4. **Push subscriber (translation.js).** On the finalize `running`+`statusKind:'started'` frame (the worker is about to assemble+commit the final Chinese), stamp `body[data-xlate-final="1"]` → the closing round's English tail is hidden so it never doubles with its just-arriving Chinese (the single overlap case). No-op when not the live bubble.
  5. **CSS (styles.css, under the leased `.translate-*`/`.stream-*` territory, OFF `.ptool-turn`).** `.stream-translated-body` (fade-in + caret), `.stream-content-demoted` (12.5px, `--text-tertiary`, opacity .72), `.stream-content-tail-hidden` (`display:none`). Understated — no boxes/chrome; the two languages read as one flowing body converging to Chinese.
- **Coordination.** Claimed a narrow styles.css path lease (`.translate-*`/`.bilingual-*`/`.stream-*` only) for the whole edit because two siblings were live in styles.css (`mranv6zy` `.ptool-turn` timeline; `mranrux3` tofu-theme rewrite); stayed entirely off `.ptool-turn`; released on completion.
- **Tests (measure-first, real shipped JS under jsdom, each guard neuter-gated).** NEW `tests/test_frontend_streaming_translate_unified.py` drives the REAL `_ensureStreamZones` / `_renderStreamingTranslatePreview` / `updateStreamingUI` + the registered translate push subscriber: asserts translatedPrimary sits above content; Chinese lands in translatedPrimary (a node ABOVE content), not a bottom block; content zone demoted; primary has no spinner chrome (settled-structure match); demotion survives a re-stream; the finalize `started` frame stamps `data-xlate-final` and hides the tail. **NC-1** (delete translatedPrimary → forces the legacy fallback → Chinese lands BELOW content = the original bottom-block bug) and **NC-2** (clear `data-xlate-final` → tail stays visible = the finalize doubling) both prove the guards load-bearing. 16/16 PASS. Regression: `test_incremental_translate` (16) + `test_frontend_retro_autotranslate` (1) + `test_auto_translate_safety_net` (4) + new (1) = **22 passed**.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on both JS files. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-c202b3e8.js`; grep-confirmed `translatedPrimary` ×3, `stream-translated-body`, `data-xlate-final` ×2 present in the bundle, and both `ui/streaming_ui.js` + `translation.js` are in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard refresh (content-hashed filename) to see it.
- **Preserved (non-regressions).** The `TOFU_INCREMENTAL_TRANSLATE` kill switch + end-only graceful degrade (no `_assistantMsgId` → `_push_progressive` is a no-op, finalize still commits at task end) untouched; the settled-view render (chat_render.js:1062), watchdog, stale-partial / zombie-heal / in-flight-dedup machinery, and `translatedContent` commit semantics all unchanged — this is purely a render unification.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a "streaming translation" reads as a dumped block, check the ZONE ORDER before touching the translator: the Chinese was correct and timely, it was just painted into a bottom-pinned zone. The unification fix is to make the streaming bubble carry the SETTLED structure from the first partial (translated-primary above, English demoted) so finalize is a no-op — and to exploit that `delta_reset` already keeps `content` = current-round-only, making cumulative-Chinese + current-English naturally non-overlapping except the final round (killed with a one-flag tail-hide on the finalize `started` frame).

### 2026-07-07 — Blocked-domain chips restyled (phantom-token bug) + a new "reader" fetch tier in tofu-search so x.com status URLs are READ (public syndication endpoint) instead of blunt-blocked; auth-source match moved before the skip gate.
- **Part 1 — chip styling (real bug, not taste).** `static/styles.css:3977` `.chip*` referenced FOUR CSS variables that are defined NOWHERE (`--border-color`, `--accent-color`, `--accent-soft`, `--accent-red`), so every `var(...,fallback)` silently used its hardcoded blue/red literal — which is why the "屏蔽域名" pills read cold blue-grey on the warm tofu parchment palette. Swapped to the REAL tokens (`--border`, `--accent`, `--accent-subtle`, `--error-text`) + polish (focus ring, `color-mix` themed borders, round 17px `×` hit-target, placeholder color). Now adapts per-theme (warm kinako under tofu, purple under dark). styles.css is served directly → hard refresh only.
- **Part 2 — reader/site-handler tier in `tofu-search` (owner decisions given up-front).** New middle tier in the fetch policy: `skip (never fetch) → reader-handled (public text endpoint) → normal fetch`.
  - **`tofu_search/fetch/readers.py` (NEW).** Extensible registry (`SiteReader` base + `register_reader`/`get_reader`/`get_readers`), first-match-wins, defended (a reader whose `matches` raises is skipped). First reader `TwitterReader`: matches x.com/twitter.com `/status/<id>` (and `/i/web/status/`, www./mobile.) via `extract_tweet_id`, reads `cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result`, parses author+timestamp+text with parent (reply-to) and quoted-tweet inlined; tombstone/empty → None. Token = Vercel react-tweet's `((id/1e15)*π).toString(36).replace(/(0+|\.)/g,'')`, ported via yt-dlp's public-domain `js_number_to_string` (V8 float→base36). NOTE the token is NOT server-validated (3 independent sources; a random string works) — the faithful port is purely forward-compat. Readers reuse `http_client.http_get` — NO duplicated request logic. Built-ins auto-register on import. Every hit/miss logged.
  - **`core.py::fetch_page_content` re-ordered.** New order: normalize → cache → **reader tier** → **auth-source (MOVED before the skip gate)** → `_should_fetch` skip gate → SPA/normal. Two blunt-block bypasses now sit BEFORE `_should_fetch`: (1) a recognized reader URL, (2) an auth-cookie-connected domain. So a *status* x.com URL is READ while a bare `x.com/home` STAYS blocked (no reader match → skip bites, no network call). Fires for BOTH web_search result-fetch and direct fetch_url (single entry point). Reader precedence over auth per spec.
  - **Exports.** `SiteReader`/`register_reader`/`get_reader` from `tofu_search.fetch`; `SiteReader`/`register_reader` at top-level `tofu_search` so a host can add site readers.
- **Tests — `tests/test_reader_handlers.py` (NEW, 37, offline).** Token: 5 EXACT vectors from yt-dlp PR #12107 (e.g. `1874097816571961839`→`4jjngwkifa`) + no-0/no-dot invariant. Routing: 7 status shapes match, 7 non-status (home/profile/search/wrong-host/empty) → None. Parser: valid/screen-only/reply-inlines-parent/quote-inlines-quoted/tombstone→None/empty→None. Reader read via mocked `http_get`: HIT, HTTP-error/tombstone/exception→None, truncation. Integration (monkeypatch `readers.http_get` + `core._do_request`): skip-domain status URL is READ; non-status x.com asserts NEITHER reader NOR network fires (block holds); auth-source-connected skip-domain bypasses via auth path; CONTROL — no-reader-no-auth skip-domain stays blocked (proves bypasses are load-bearing).
- **Verification.** New suite 37/37; regression `test_file_assets`+`test_security`+`test_vertical_fetch` 73/73; FULL tofu-search suite 253 passed. ruff clean (removed one unused `urlparse`). Smoke: `twitter` auto-registered on import, routes status→TwitterReader / profile→None, `register_reader` top-level exposed. NOT committed (owner attribution). chatui `search_bridge.sync_search_config` passes `skip_domains` through `configure` unchanged — no bridge change needed; the reader tier is inside the library so chatui gets it on the next tofu-search import.
- **Deferred (owner).** UI "reader vs blocked" list split not yet surfaced — backend tier landed first, per instruction.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A `var(--x, fallback)` where `--x` is never defined is invisible dead theming — grep the token DEFINITION (`--x:`) not just usages when a themed element looks off-palette. For an undocumented external API (tweet syndication) verify the algorithm against ≥2 independent sources AND port a canonical reference impl with its own test vectors, even when the field it computes turns out to be unvalidated — the vectors make the port self-checking.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "insight" second-pass, round 4: the GATED variant clears the bar. Fix #2 (self-reference suppression) turned the worst loss (bd79f6 −1.25) into a win; a-priori headroom gate + fired-subset bootstrap → win-rate 1.00, CI lower bound 1.00 (n=7 fired, 4 zh), gate precision 2/3. Conditional-but-real uplift, ready to wire behind the flag.
- **Why.** Round 3's honest n=9 negative (always-on win-rate 0.44, CI lower 0.22) was ACCEPTED — an always-on pass is a coin-flip. But the wins were real and transfer-driven, just CONDITIONAL, and the data handed the condition over. Owner approved building the GATED variant: (1) fix the foundational-paper backfire, (2) an a-priori headroom gate, (3) re-measure on the FIRED subset with the selection-confirmation trap explicitly controlled. Acceptance: gated variant, fix #2 applied, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0.5 on the fired subset at n≥7, AND bd79f6 (or comparable foundational paper) either correctly rejected or its self-ref suppressed.
- **Fix #2 — self-reference suppression (the crux; a headroom gate alone would NOT catch bd79f6, which is low-baseline yet the worst loss).** Root cause re-confirmed by inspection: on the Transformer paper the "connect to your library" moat INVERTED — the model bridged the paper back to ITSELF ("attention in *Attention Is All You Need* is a generalized form of the attention in *Attention Is All You Need* itself"), claimed `arxiv_id:1706.03762` (the paper's own id), and grounding then fuzzy-matched a spurious title-meme paper → passed the anti-hallucination gate as "5 grounded, 0 dropped" while being vacuous. NEW in `lib/paper/insight_engine.py`: `_self_identity(phash, report_md, self_arxiv_id, self_title)` resolves the paper-under-analysis identity (explicit args → paper_library row → report head `# title` + arXiv id in head); `_is_self_reference(ref, conn_text, self_aid, self_title)` fires on THREE signals checked on the CLAIMED ref BEFORE grounding (so a self-titled ref can't be masked by grounding): (1) claimed arXiv id == own id; (2) claimed title `_title_grounded`-matches own title; (3) circular prose — own title named ≥2× in the bridge text. `_ground_insight` now takes `(self_aid, self_title)` and REMOVES self-ref connections ENTIRELY (the surrounding prose is the circular text, worse than nothing), returns `(grounded, dropped, selfref)`. `generate_insight` gained `self_arxiv_id`/`self_title` params + `out['selfref']`. **PROOF it works on the real case: bd79f6 re-gen dropped 1 self-ref connection (`selfref=1`), and its score went −1.25 (B=2.08) → +0.08 (B=3.75).** The catastrophic loss is fixed.
- **A-priori headroom gate.** `INSIGHT_GATE_THRESHOLD=4.0` + `insight_gate_fires(baseline_overall)` (fires iff report's own insight-rubric overall ≤4.0; fails OPEN on None so an instrument error never silently withholds). Threshold FIXED from the round-3 clean split (wins ≤3.9, losses ≥4.5) BEFORE this round's measurement — not tuned post-hoc.
- **Measurement — selection-confirmation trap controlled.** New `debug/insight_batch.py --phase gated`: partitions every cached paper by `insight_gate_fires(its OWN arm-A baseline)`, then reports BOTH (a) FIRED subset win-rate + bootstrap CI lower bound (production behaviour), AND (b) REJECTED subset gate-precision (a WIN among rejected = the gate discarded value). Gen now passes self-identity from paper_library.
- **RESULT (10 papers scored, gate applied on each paper's own baseline).** FIRED n=7 (4 zh): e135b7[zh] 2.67→4.58 (+1.92), 82840[en] 3.25→4.00 (+0.75), 25ee[en] 3.62→4.33 (+0.71), 25ee[zh] 3.67→3.75 (+0.08), bd79f6[en] 3.67→3.75 (+0.08), 8739af[zh] 3.92→4.33 (+0.42), 216bef[zh] 4.00→4.38 (+0.38). **win-rate 1.00, mean Δ +0.62, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound 1.00 → CLEARS the 0.5 gate at n=7.** REJECTED n=3: 82840[zh] 4.33→4.38 (+0.04 marginal WIN), 378da9[zh] 4.67→4.50 (LOSS), fd6773[zh] 4.75→4.17 (LOSS) → **gate precision 2/3** (one marginal +0.04 leak — a near-tie at the boundary, not a discarded strong win).
- **HONEST caveats (reported, not buried).** (1) The fired n=7 includes 25ee in BOTH en+zh, so it's 6 DISTINCT papers + 1 language-variant. I re-ran the strict distinct-paper subset (n=6, dropped 25ee[zh]) → still win-rate 1.00, CI lower 1.00, mean +0.71. The verdict does NOT hinge on the duplicate. (2) Two wins are marginal (+0.08) — real but small; the bulk of the value is the 3 large wins (+0.42 to +1.92). (3) fd6773's baseline is noisy across runs (3.00 in round 3, 4.75 here) — a reminder the gate reads a noisy instrument; failing-open on the boundary is the right default. (4) The one rejected "win" (+0.04) is within scorer noise of a tie, so gate precision is effectively clean.
- **Gate — `tests/test_paper_insight_agentic.py` 8→11, all green.** Added: `test_selfref_connections_dropped_legit_survives` (foundational-paper fixture: id-match + circular-prose connections DROPPED, legit EvoLM bridge SURVIVES, self-titled ref never grounded/rendered) + NEUTER `test_neuter_selfref_guard_is_load_bearing` (no identity supplied → all 3 connections survive, proving the guard removes them) + `test_headroom_gate_threshold` (fires ≤4.0, withholds above, fails open on None). Fixed the pre-existing grounding-test fixture to make the paper-under-analysis DIFFERENT from the cited paper (the realistic case) so the new guard doesn't false-fire on it. ruff clean on engine + harness + tests.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Still `TOFU_PAPER_INSIGHT`-gated OFF, non-destructive (`insight:<ui>` persist key). NEXT (owner's call): wire into the report route behind the flag, firing only when the report's own insight baseline ≤4.0 (needs the report route to score its own report once — cheap, one no-tool rubric call — or a lightweight heuristic). Standalone report-refinement critic pass still held.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A headroom gate and a quality fix are BOTH needed and are NOT substitutes: bd79f6 passed the headroom gate (low baseline) yet failed on quality — only fix #2 caught it. When a "connect to related work" feature meets a FOUNDATIONAL paper, its own descendants tempt a self-referential bridge; check target-≟-self BEFORE grounding, because grounding proves existence, not non-vacuousness, and will happily match a self-titled ref to a spurious paper. When measuring a gated variant, report the REJECTED subset's precision too, or you've only proven "it wins where I let it win". And watch for same-paper language duplicates inflating n — re-run the distinct-item subset to prove the verdict doesn't depend on them.


### 2026-07-07 — Merged the two stacked Project-Brain bars into ONE bar (owner directive, plan A) — kills the duplicate clickable chrome without losing either dataset
- **Ask (owner).** Two slim bars stacked on the chat view read as a duplicate: `#presenceStrip` (the project-wide Collaboration bar, `presence.js`, "项目 · N个会话在线 …") and `#convInfluenceBar` (the per-conversation Influence bar, `project-brain.js`, "本对话 · 受章程约束 …"). Both are clickable, both open the same Project Brain panel (the collab bar plainly, the influence bar deep-linked to the influence lens + flash). Owner: merge into ONE bar (plan A) — keep BOTH datasets, decouple their sources, one click hot-zone; delete the extra DOM node + its elbow-connector CSS + the paper-mode override for the deleted element.
- **What shipped — ONE bar, two composed clusters.** `presence.js` remains the SOLE owner of the bar element (`#presenceStrip`). Its `_render()` now composes a **PROJECT cluster** (`.collab-cluster-project`, from `brainSummary`, push-driven — peers/epics/decisions/conflicts, unchanged content) + a **CONV cluster** (`.collab-cluster-conv`, opaque chip HTML supplied by `project-brain.js`). A `.collab-cluster-divider` renders ONLY when both clusters are present. Each cluster shows only when non-empty; the whole bar hides only when BOTH are empty (or not in project mode) — the merged empty-hide gate. Whole-bar click → `openProjectBrain()`; the conv cluster has its own click handler that `stopPropagation()`s and deep-links to `openProjectBrainInfluence()` (preserved the lens deep-link — owner said optional, kept it since it was low-cost).
- **Data sources stay DECOUPLED (owner requirement #2).** New `_convSeg` Map (root→cluster HTML) in presence.js + public `CollabBar.setConvSegment(root, html)` (also `window.CollabBar_setConvSegment`). `project-brain.js`'s `renderConvInfluenceBar` was rewritten: `_convInfluenceClusterHTML(inf)` builds the chips (or `''` when no influence) and hands them to `CollabBar.setConvSegment(path, html)` instead of writing its own DOM node; `refreshConvInfluenceBar` still pulls `Api.project.brainInfluence` on conv-switch (`convInfluenceRefresh` hook in main.js) and clears the cluster on missing prereq/stale reply/error. So project cluster = brainSummary/push cadence, conv cluster = brainInfluence/conv-switch cadence — composed only at render, never coupled into one request.
- **Deletions.** Removed the `#convInfluenceBar` `<button>` from index.html; removed the standalone `.conv-influence-bar` bar CSS + the `.presence-strip:not([hidden]) + .conv-influence-bar` elbow-connector/tree-join block (replaced by `.collab-cluster*` styles); the `body.paper-mode-active` override now targets only `#presenceStrip`. No new i18n keys — reused existing EN+ZH entries (`collab.project`, `projectBrain.barLead`/`infCharterBound`/`infOwns`/`infAvoid`/`infPending`).
- **Tests (4 suites updated + 2 new neuters; measure-first, real jsdom driving real shipped JS).** `test_frontend_collab_bar.py`: existing project-cluster assertions survive unchanged (substrings preserved inside `.collab-cluster-project`); NEW `test_merged_bar_composes_project_and_conv_clusters` drives `CollabBar.setConvSegment` through all four states (project-only=no divider / both=divider+conv-deeplink / conv-only=bar still visible / both-empty=bar hidden) + NEW neuter `test_NC_merged_empty_hide_gate_is_load_bearing` (disable the both-empty gate → `both_empty_hidden` FAILS). `test_frontend_project_brain_influence.py`: rewrote the bar harness to load BOTH presence.js + project-brain.js and assert the CONV cluster on the real `#presenceStrip` (re-pull on switch convA-MINE→convB-CHARTER, hide on convSolo); NC re-pull anchor updated for the new `clear` closure; NEW `test_NC_empty_conv_cluster_hide_is_load_bearing` (neuter `_convInfluenceClusterHTML`'s empty gate → merged bar stays up on a no-influence conv). `test_frontend_project_brain.py`: dropped the stale `#convInfluenceBar` mount from the deep-link harness (element removed; `openProjectBrainInfluence` unchanged). `test_frontend_paper_describe_persist.py`: CSS regex + docstring updated to the single `#presenceStrip` override.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on both JS files; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-c744cfff.js` (presence.js + project-brain.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no new file to register). **ALL 36 tests in the four suites PASS in one run, no exclusions** (collab_bar 6, influence 7, project_brain 19, paper-persist 4). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard refresh needed (import-time bundler + content-hashed filename).
- **Also fixed a PRE-EXISTING harness hang (owner ask).** `test_cross_project_isolation_at_push_routing` + its NC `test_NC_isolation_wildcard_subscription_leaks` were timing out at the 60s subprocess cap — VERIFIED identical on clean HEAD, so a dormant bug, not merge collateral. Root cause: the `_HARNESS_ISOLATION` jsdom script (push.js + project-brain.js) never called `process.exit(0)`, so push.js's reconnect interval kept node's event loop alive after the assertions printed. Added `process.exit(0)` right after its `console.log(out.join('\n'))` (the exact pattern the file's other harnesses already use). Both tests now PASS in seconds and guard real cross-project push-routing isolation as intended.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** To merge two sibling UI bars without coupling their data, keep ONE module owning the DOM element and expose a setter (`setConvSegment`) the other module feeds opaque HTML into — the owner composes clusters + owns the empty-hide gate, the feeder keeps its own fetch cadence. When a test run shows failures, check whether they reproduce on HEAD before attributing them to your change: these two were a dormant harness bug (missing `process.exit`) surfaced only because the merge run happened to include that file, not caused by the merge.


### 2026-07-07 — Project rail pass 2: turned the lone-letter dot into a colored monogram "app tile", and gave the 未分类/+ chips a matching-footprint system-tile look (owner: "default tile doesn't match, feels small, one letter tells you nothing")
- **Ask (owner).** In the sidebar project rail (esp. the collapsed icon-strip in the screenshot): (1) the default 未分类 tile didn't match the colored folder squares and felt slightly small; (2) each project was a single letter, which doesn't convey WHICH folder it is. Redesign/beautify.
- **What shipped — render (`static/js/ui/conversation_list.js`).** New pure helper `_folderMonogram(name)`: multi-word names → initials of the first two words (`Machine Learning`→`ML`, `auto-verifier`→`AV`, split on `\s-_/.`); single word → first two letters (`chatui`→`CH`); CJK (Han/Kana/Hangul) → first two chars raw (already dense); empty/symbol-only → `•`. The project row now emits `data-initial="<mono>" data-mono-len="<1|2>"` on `.folder-tab-dot` instead of a 1-char `slice(0,1)`. DOM contract otherwise UNCHANGED (still `.folder-tab[data-folder-id]` + `.folder-tab-dot` + name + count) so every delegated handler + the fast-path hash keep working.
- **What shipped — CSS (`static/styles.css`, theme-token only per §3.5).** `.folder-tab-dot` is no longer a 9px circle — it's a **20px colored rounded-square tile** (`border-radius:6px`) centering the monogram in white 700-weight, with `data-mono-len="1"` bumping to 12px and `[data-mono-len="2"]` at 9.5px + tighter tracking. The inbox (未分类) + add tiles become the SAME 20px footprint but a **neutral system chip** (`--bg-hover` surface + `inset 0 0 0 1px --border` ring, centered glyph) so they group with yet stay distinct from the colored project tiles; active inbox / add-hover swap to the accent-subtle surface + accent ring. Collapsed strip + drawer tiles enlarged 22/26px → **30px** (`border-radius:9px`, 12px mono / 16px single), and centered-tile "selected" now reads via a 2px-gap **accent ring** (`box-shadow:0 0 0 2px --bg-tertiary,0 0 0 4px --accent`) instead of the far-left `::before` bar (hidden when centered). Streaming pulse simplified to an opacity breathe (no transform, so a monogram tile doesn't jiggle). Tofu adapts for free: folder color rides the inline `style`, and the inbox/add tokens (`--bg-hover`/`--border`/`--accent-subtle`) are already redefined under `[data-theme="tofu"]`.
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_project_rail.py`, extended not new).** Added 3 checks to the existing jsdom harness — `mono_f1_two_char` (`cadtrans`→`CA`), `mono_f2_initials` (`auto-verifier`→`AV`), `mono_len_hint` (`data-mono-len==2`) — plus a NEW neuter `test_NC_monogram_is_load_bearing` that reverts `_folderMonogram` to a lone-letter `slice(0,1)` and asserts the two monogram checks FLIP to FAIL while `rail_has_list`/`rail_has_f1` stay PASS (proves the helper is load-bearing + surgical + shipped file byte-identical). Suite 5/5 green; combined with folder-longpress 9/9 green.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on conversation_list.js. Bundle rebuilt via `lib.js_bundler.build_bundle()` → `bundle-1e5d7769.js` (grep-confirmed `_folderMonogram` ×2 + `data-mono-len` present); note the file lives at `static/js/bundle-*.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard refresh (content-hashed filename) to see it.
- **Follow-up (owner-approved, same session).** Uncolored folders previously all fell back to the single `var(--accent)` → N uncolored projects were one indistinguishable color block, defeating the at-a-glance goal. Added `_folderColor(f)`: explicit `f.color` verbatim; else a STABLE per-key HSL (hash of `f.id||f.name` mod 360 at fixed `52% 55%` pastel — reads on dark + parchment); empty key → `var(--accent)`. Pure ⇒ same folder = same color forever. `.folder-tab-dot` render now uses `_folderColor(f)` instead of the `f.color ? … : var(--accent)` ternary. Tests +5 (`color_explicit_honored`/`color_uncolored_is_hsl`/`color_uncolored_not_accent`/`color_deterministic`/`color_distinct_keys`) + neuter `test_NC_folder_color_is_load_bearing` (revert fallback to `var(--accent)` → distinct/hsl checks FAIL, explicit-color + render still PASS). Suite 6/6 green. Bundle → `bundle-e80f331b.js` (`_folderColor` ×4 + hsl expr grep-confirmed).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A single-letter avatar is a weak recognition cue — a 1–2 char monogram derived from word-initials (CJK-aware) is far more legible at icon size and costs one pure helper. When several tiles must "belong to the same family but not be confusable" (colored project tiles vs system inbox/add chips), give them an IDENTICAL footprint + differ only by surface treatment (brand color vs neutral-surface+ring). And when a tile is CENTERED (collapsed rail), a left-edge `::before` accent bar detaches from it — switch the active affordance to a ring on the tile itself. A single shared `var(--accent)` fallback for "no color chosen" silently collapses recognition when there are many uncolored items — derive a stable per-item hue from a hash instead.



### 2026-07-07 — Project Brain Charter is now EDITABLE + DELETABLE from the panel, styled, and auto-translates to the UI language (default-ON overlay)
- **Ask (owner).** The charter within Project Brain needed to be editable and deletable (it was read-only for committed decisions), its styling improved, and its content auto-translated into the UI language when the UI is Chinese.
- **Backend (`lib/conversations/project_charter.py`).** Added three HUMAN-GATED, optimistic-locked, feed-audited mutations mirroring `commit_charter`'s contract: `update_decision(index, text, expected_version)`, `delete_decision(index, expected_version)`, `delete_charter(expected_version)`. Decisions have no stable id, so they're addressed by list INDEX guarded by `expected_version` — a matched version guarantees the list is exactly what the caller rendered, so the index can't silently hit the wrong row after a concurrent edit. Each bumps `version` and emits a `decided` feed event (auditable). North-star editing already existed via `commit_charter(content=...)`. Extracted the shared upsert into `_persist_charter()`. `delete_charter` on a missing row is a no-op success. `__all__` updated.
- **Routes (`routes/api_v1/project.py`).** Three new endpoints: `POST /charter/decision/update`, `POST /charter/decision/delete`, `POST /charter/delete`. Stale `expected_version` → 409 (`version_conflict`); out-of-range index / missing path → 400. Shared `_parse_expected_version` helper. Rate-limited like the existing charter routes.
- **API client (`static/js/api.js`).** `Api.project.updateDecision / deleteDecision / deleteCharter` (all optimistic-locked). api-isolation ratchet stays green (routed through api.js, no raw fetch).
- **Frontend (`static/js/project-brain.js`).** `renderCharter` now renders the north star + each committed decision with hover edit/delete affordances + a delete-whole-charter footer. `_wireCharterEditControls` drives all mutations through the optimistic-locked routes carrying the rendered `version`, then `refreshCharter` (backend-authoritative — never a local DOM mutation). Edit opens an inline textarea (`_openInlineEditor`); delete uses a two-step inline confirm (`_confirmInline`, arms for 4s) instead of `window.confirm`. **Load-bearing i18n invariant:** the editor seeds from `data-pb-src` (the ORIGINAL text) via `_charterSrcText`, NEVER the translation overlay laid over innerHTML — so an active auto-translated view can never leak into a saved decision.
- **Auto-translate default-ON (`static/js/project-brain-i18n.js`).** The content-translation overlay (`ProjectBrainI18n`) already existed but was default-OFF. Flipped `isEnabled()` from `=== '1'` to `!== '0'` (opt-out): absent pref → ON. The overlay's local CJK already-target gate keeps a same-language surface at ZERO cost, so default-on is free when content already matches the UI language. Language switch already re-applies via `_onLanguageChange → applyAll()`.
- **i18n + CSS.** Added `projectBrain.editNorthStar/editDecision/deleteDecision/deleteCharter/save/saving/cancel/confirmDelete` (zh+en). CSS: hover-revealed row actions, inline textarea editor, delete-charter footer, armed-confirm red state (all tofu-theme vars, existing `edit`/`trash` Icon glyphs).
- **Tests (measurement-first, neuter-gated).** Backend `tests/test_project_charter.py` +11 (edit-in-place, delete-only-that-one, both optimistic locks, whole-charter delete + lock + missing-noop, route roundtrip, route 409s, route validation) + NC (neuter `decisions.pop(index)`→`pop(0)` deletes the wrong row) — 36/36 green. NEW `tests/test_frontend_charter_edit_delete.py` (jsdom, drives REAL `renderCharter`+`_wireCharterEditControls`+`ProjectBrainI18n` against a recording fake Api): asserts north-star/decision edit → correct route + args, editor seeded with ORIGINAL not translation, two-step delete (one click does NOT fire), delete-charter, overlay default-ON; TRIPLE NEUTER (NC-1 seed-from-translation, NC-2 fire-on-first-click, NC-3 revert default-off) — 4/4 green.
- **Verification.** ruff clean on all changed Python. Backend 36/36; new frontend 4/4; api-isolation 4 + bundle-corruption-guard 12 green. Existing project-brain frontend suites: 26 passed; the 2 push-isolation-harness tests TIME OUT but are PRE-EXISTING (proven — they fail identically on pristine HEAD `project-brain.js`; they exercise `_onPush`/`_subscribePanelLive`, untouched here). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-8a4a2ceb.js` (new charter code + default-on flip verified present). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard refresh needed (import-time bundler + content-hashed filename).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a translation overlay lays a VIEW over innerHTML, any EDIT path must read the source of truth (`data-pb-src`), never `textContent` — prove it with a neuter that seeds from the translation. Address id-less list items by INDEX only under an optimistic-version lock so the index can't drift onto the wrong row. A destructive action in an overlay should use a two-step inline confirm, not `window.confirm`.


### 2026-07-07 — Input language identification, built as a cascade: Tier-0 script fast-path → Tier-1 fastText lid.176 (guarded-optional) → Tier-2 LLM "typeless" correction for the ambiguous tail; replaces the Latin-ratio gate that misread German/Spanish as English.
- **Ask (owner).** Add high-accuracy input language identification; allow a lightweight LLM for correction (a built-in "typeless" feature). Owner ratified: general `detect_language()` API (not just an inline gate); guarded-optional `fast-langdetect` default OFF; LLM tier gated by config + `personal_scope` fail-closed on headless; replace the `is_predominantly_english` gate; measurement-first proof; policy constants backend-served.
- **Root cause it fixes (our own memory).** `is_predominantly_english` is `latin_ratio ≥ 0.55`; German/Spanish/Italian/Portuguese all read ~0.97 Latin, so the send-path gate wrongly SKIPPED them as "already English." Confirmed empirically: heuristic-only gate scores 54% is-English accuracy on a 24-case short-text set; the cascade lifts it to 83%.
- **What shipped.**
  1. **`lib/text_lang.py` cascade (additive; every existing fn untouched).** `detect_language(text, *, allow_llm, llm_corrector) -> DetectionResult(code, confidence, source)`. Tier-0 `detect_script()` decides CJK/Kana/Hangul/Cyrillic/Arabic/Hebrew/Greek/Thai/Devanagari at ~1.0 (≥50% of non-ws chars in one block; abstains on a stray glyph → that's the `mixed` case). Tier-1 guarded-optional fastText loader (`_get_ft_detector`, memoized + `reset_for_test()`, mirroring `lib/rate_limit_store.py`) behind `TOFU_LANGDETECT_BACKEND` (default `script` → Tier-1 disabled, box byte-identical; `fasttext` → lazy import bundled lite `.ftz` 917 KB, offline, fail-open to heuristic). Tier-2 escalation via `_needs_llm_correction` (low-confidence / very-short / thin-Latin top1−top2 margin), with a `LANG_HIGH_CONFIDENCE=0.90` short-circuit that trusts a strong verdict outright — this DROPPED the measured escalation rate 70.6%→41.2% (don't pay the LLM for confident-correct short inputs like `Ciao`@1.00).
  2. **Policy constants backend-served.** `LANG_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.70`, `LANG_HIGH_CONFIDENCE=0.90`, `LANG_SHORT_TEXT_CHARS=20`, `LANG_THIN_LATIN_MARGIN=0.15` → `detect_language_policy()` → `/api/v1/server-config` under `langDetect` (same pattern as `stale_translation_policy()`/`translation`). No magic numbers in the gate.
  3. **LLM tier decoupled from the detector.** `detect_language` takes an `llm_corrector` callable (no LLM import in `text_lang`). `lib/lang_correct.py` supplies `llm_language_corrector` (cheap-tier `smart_chat`, `max_tokens=8`, returns an ISO code or None) + `resolve_lang_correction_allowed(config)`. New `personal_scope` capability `langCorrectionEnabled` (headless_default=False, ui_default=True, `prompt_block=''` — it injects NO operator state but CAN silently bill, which is why it's registered). `resolve_conv_config` defaults it ON for the UI; `apply_headless_personal_defaults` forces it OFF headless unless the caller opts in. Ratchet `tests/test_personal_scope_headless.py` still green (14).
  4. **Gate replaced.** New `_should_translate_input(text, config)` in `lib/chat/turn_builder.py` is the ONE source of truth for both `auto_translate_user` (UI) and `translate_user_text_to_english` (headless API): pinned `translateSourceLang` wins; else the cascade decides (skip only on a CONFIDENT `en`; `unknown` falls through to translate — a false "translate" is cheap-safe, a false "skip" leaves a non-English message untranslated). LLM tier consulted only when `resolve_lang_correction_allowed` is True.
  5. **Endpoint extended (contract preserved).** `/api/v1/text/detect-language` keeps `{language, cjk_ratio, latin_ratio, is_chinese}` and ADDS `detected:{code, confidence, source}`. Never fires the billed LLM tier (unauthenticated detection surface).
- **Measurement (`debug/lang_detect_eval.py`, 24 labeled short-text cases incl. the Fin hard cases `im need help`/`buenas dias`/`App store?`).** Exact-code: heuristic 54.2% → cascade 79.2%. is-English gate: 54.2% → 83.3%. Escalation: 41.2% of fastText cases (after the high-conf cap). Reproduced the Fin failure class offline on the lite model (`buenas dias`→pt@0.90, `im need help`→de@0.74, `App store?`→no@0.40/it@0.38 — all correctly flagged for escalation). Documented residual limit: a confident-but-wrong short case (`im julia`→de@1.00) can't be caught cheaply — accepted.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_lang_detect_cascade.py` (21 tests, each tier NEUTER-gated: blanked script ranges → CJK undecided; backend OFF → German misread as English; high-conf cap removed → escalation returns; corrector-declines → Tier-1 stands). fastText tests `skipUnless` the dep is importable, so vanilla-box green. 55 passed across new + `test_text_lang.py` + `test_personal_scope_headless.py`. ruff clean. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Dep note.** `fast-langdetect` installed into the `tofu` conda env for measurement (pip needs `PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV=false`). It is NOT in core `requirements.txt` — guarded-optional, default OFF.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A cascade beats any single model here: script fast-path handles CJK/non-Latin at zero cost + ~100%, fastText fixes the Latin-language gotcha, and the LLM tier only touches the genuinely-ambiguous tail. When adding an escalation trigger, MEASURE the escalation rate — the naive "short text → escalate" rule fired on confident-correct inputs too; a high-confidence short-circuit halved the cost. Keep the LLM out of the pure detector module (pass a corrector callable) so `text_lang` stays dependency-free and testable.

- **FOLLOW-UP (same day) — criterion C was unmet on the DEFAULT box; fixed at root.**
- **FOLLOW-UP 2 (same day) — verified the real `smart_chat` call path + fixed a latent chatty-reply parser bug the stub tests couldn't catch.** Owner flagged that no test had verified `smart_chat`'s actual signature/return-shape — if wrong, the corrector throws, the `except` swallows it to None, and the gotcha silently regresses (invisible because caught). VERIFIED (`inspect.signature`): `lib/llm_dispatch/api.py:1768` `smart_chat` accepts `capability`/`log_prefix`/`max_retries`/`max_tokens`/`temperature`; returns `(content, usage)` on BOTH paths (dispatch_chat api.py:370 + lib.llm.chat fallback chat.py:254) — my 2-tuple unpack is correct, no change needed. BUT writing the chatty-reply test exposed a REAL bug: the old parser did `code.split()[0]` → for `'The language is German (de).'` that's `'the'`, a 3-letter alpha token passing `isalpha()` → it returned the garbage code `'the'`. Fixed: replaced first-word-grab with an ANCHORED whole-string match `_CODE_RE=^([a-z]{2,3})(?:[-_][a-z0-9]{2,4})?$` — a chatty multi-token reply fails the match and is rejected (→None), a region suffix (`zh-CN`) reduces to the primary subtag (`zh`). New `LlmCorrectorRealCallPathTest` (5 tests) patches `smart_chat` at the DISPATCH boundary (not the corrector stub): well-formed `'de'`→`'de'` + asserts the exact kwargs my code passes are accepted; chatty reply→None (not `'the'`); `zh-CN`→`zh`; `smart_chat` raising→None (swallowed, no propagate); `unknown`→None. 65 passed, ruff clean.
- **FOLLOW-UP (same day) — criterion C was unmet on the DEFAULT box; fixed at root.**
 Owner caught that the gate was mechanically swapped but the gotcha still fired where it matters: on the vanilla deployment (`TOFU_LANGDETECT_BACKEND` unset → `script`, fastText OFF), `detect_language('Guten Tag, wie geht es dir heute Abend?')` returned `en@0.94 (heuristic)` and the gate answered "skip." Root cause: the heuristic branch escalated to the LLM corrector ONLY on `res.code == 'unknown'`, so a confident-WRONG heuristic `'en'` (every multi-word German/Spanish/French/Italian/Portuguese input) never reached the corrector — the fix only materialized when the optional fastText dep was enabled, i.e. never by default. Fix: new bounded predicate `_heuristic_en_is_unreliable(text)` (≥2 word-tokens of ≥2 letters) — because the latin-ratio heuristic literally cannot separate English from other Latin-script languages, a multi-word heuristic-`'en'` is inherently unreliable and MUST be adjudicated by the corrector when `allow_llm`. The heuristic branch now escalates on `unknown OR (en AND multi-word)`, and only adopts the correction when it's a DIFFERENT non-en code (corrector returning `en`/`None` leaves the verdict intact — genuine English survives at one cheap classifier call). BEFORE→AFTER on the default box: `en@0.94 heuristic` → `de@0.70 llm`. This makes the UI product's gotcha fixed by the LLM backstop even with fastText off, and belt-and-suspenders fixed statistically when fastText is on. Added `DefaultBoxLatinGotchaTest` (4 tests incl. a neuter: corrector returns None → falls back to the un-fixed `en@heuristic`, proving the escalation is load-bearing; + a multi-word bound test so single-token English isn't needlessly billed). 60 passed, ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A cascade beats any single model here: script fast-path handles CJK/non-Latin at zero cost + ~100%, fastText fixes the Latin-language gotcha, and the LLM tier only touches the genuinely-ambiguous tail. When adding an escalation trigger, MEASURE the escalation rate — the naive "short text → escalate" rule fired on confident-correct inputs too; a high-confidence short-circuit halved the cost. Keep the LLM out of the pure detector module (pass a corrector callable) so `text_lang` stays dependency-free and testable. BIGGEST lesson: a "mechanically swapped" gate is NOT a fixed gate — verify the fix on the DEFAULT deployment (the one users run), not just the feature-enabled path; the gotcha lived entirely in the `== 'unknown'`-only escalation condition and only surfaced by tracing the vanilla `script`-backend path end to end.



### 2026-07-07 — Gave `todo_write` a real UI: a collapsible checklist progress card (state-glyph rows + slim progress bar), rendered off the structured `meta.todos` the backend was ALREADY attaching but the frontend never used.
- **Ask (owner).** Make `todo_write`'s rendering prettier — "reference how other tools do it."
- **Diagnosis (not guessed).** `todo_write` had NO dedicated frontend renderer. It fell through to the flat generic `_renderUnifiedToolLine` row: just an icon + the backend title `Checklist · N/M done` + a plain `N/total` badge — no items, no progress. Meanwhile the backend handler (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/misc.py:_handle_todo_write`) ALREADY attaches the full structured list via `_build_simple_meta(..., extra={'todos': todos})` (each `{id, content, status}`), and peers like memory (`_renderMemoryBlock`) / conv-meta / board / peer each get a rich collapsible card off exactly that structured meta. So the data was there; only the render was missing.
- **What shipped (render-layer only, `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`).**
  1. **Icon.** Added `todo_write` to `_TOOL_DISPLAY` (label "Checklist", green) + a clipboard-with-check inline SVG to `_webToolSvg` (§3.4 SVG-only). Previously it hit the generic wand glyph.
  2. **`_renderTodoBlock(round, svg, q, badgeHtml)`** — a `<details>` card mirroring `_renderMemoryBlock`'s collapse affordance. Header: icon + localized "任务清单 · done/total" + a done/total count chip (green when 100%). Body: a slim progress bar (accent while in-flight → green `--s-done` when complete) + one row per item with a distinct state glyph — ✓ tick (completed, struck-through+muted), clock (in_progress, highlighted accent row + bold, since that's what the agent is doing RIGHT NOW), empty circle (pending, dim). Reads `meta.todos` (fallback `round.todos`); returns `null` → generic line when absent. **Default-open while any item is unfinished; auto-collapses once all done** so a finished checklist stops dominating the transcript.
  3. Hooked into `_renderUnifiedToolLine` right beside the memory-block hook (`if (round.toolName === "todo_write")`).
  4. CSS `.ptool-todo-*` added next to `.ptool-memory-*` in `styles.css`. Uses `var(--s-done, #10b981)` with a literal green fallback everywhere because `--s-done` is `.settings-panel`/`.myday`-scoped and NOT in tool-panel scope — degrades to green under all themes (same pattern Task Mode's `--tm-ok` uses).
  5. i18n keys `todo.headDone` / `todo.cleared` / `todo.emptyBody` (zh+en).
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on both edited JS files. Bundle rebuilt via `lib.js_bundler.build_bundle()` → `bundle-04659c73.js`; grep-confirmed all 14 `.ptool-todo-*` classes + `_renderTodoBlock` are in it. Brace-extracted the REAL `_renderTodoBlock` and eval'd under node against sample data: 9/9 assertions green — in-flight card is `open` with `1/3` chip + `width:33%` bar + highlighted in_progress row; all-done card collapses (no `open`) with the `count-done` class; returns `null` when `meta.todos` absent. NOT committed (owner attribution). CSS served directly + content-hashed bundle → server restart + hard refresh to see it.
- **Trap hit + lesson.** `insert_content` with an anchor that included a template-literal fragment landed my new function INSIDE `_renderMemoryBlock`'s backtick string, splitting it (`node --check` caught it: `Unexpected identifier 'meta'`). Fix: repaired both boundaries with `apply_diffs`. Lesson: when inserting a whole function near another, anchor on a UNIQUE structural line OUTSIDE any string/template literal, and always `node --check` before rebuilding. Broader lesson: when a tool "renders ugly," check whether the backend already emits structured meta (it usually does here — `extra={...}` on `_build_simple_meta`) before touching the backend; this was a pure frontend gap.
- **Redesign v2 (owner: "unify the font with the other tools — this looks ugly; collapse by default + expand on click; keep pushing the design").** The v1 card had two real flaws: (a) item text rendered in the DEFAULT SANS body font at 12.5px while EVERY other tool row (`.ptool-text`) is `'JetBrains Mono' 11.5px` — that font mismatch was the "ugly" the owner saw; (b) it defaulted OPEN, so a fresh 0/8 checklist dominated the whole transcript (exactly the screenshot). Rework:
  1. **Collapsed by default** (dropped the `open` attr entirely). It now reads as a normal one-line tool row until clicked.
  2. **At-a-glance progress WITHOUT expanding** — the collapsed header carries an inline 54px **mini progress bar** + the `done/total` count chip (green at 100%) + the **current in-progress step's text** as a quiet caption with a pulsing dot, so you see WHAT's happening now without opening.
  3. **Font unified** — item rows + empty state are now `'JetBrains Mono' 11.5px`, matching `.ptool-text`. The "Checklist" label is the plain monospace tool label (i18n `todo.head` = 任务清单 / Checklist; dropped the `· N/M` from the label since the chip carries it).
  4. **Body is a vertical-timeline stepper** — a connector line (`.ptool-todo-list::before`) threads the state glyphs; each glyph sits on a solid disc (`box-shadow` ring in `--bg-primary`) so the line reads as passing BEHIND the nodes. Glyphs: green ✓ (completed, struck-through), a filled clock-disc (in_progress, bold text), a neutral ring (pending). Per the global `tofu-tool-row-no-opacity-rule` memory, STATE is conveyed by solid glyph color + strike-through, NEVER by fading a row.
  - **Verify v2.** `node --check` clean; brace-extract + node-eval of the REAL `_renderTodoBlock` → 10/10 assertions green (collapsed-no-open; header mini-bar `width:33%`; `1/3` chip; current-step preview "Design cascade"; timeline list; in_progress item; plain "Checklist" label; all-done → no preview + `count-done` + `width:100%`; `null` when no todos). Bundle → `bundle-c744cfff.js` (grep-confirmed `ptool-todo-minibar`/`ptool-todo-current`/`ptool-todo-list` + `todo.head`); CSS 6 hits for the new classes. i18n `todo.headDone`→`todo.head`. NOT committed. Restart + hard refresh.
  - **Lesson (v2).** "Ugly" was concretely a FONT mismatch — a custom block dropped into a monospace-uniform panel MUST adopt the panel's type (`'JetBrains Mono' 11.5px`, the `.ptool-text` contract) or it sticks out regardless of how nice the layout is. And a status card that defaults OPEN hijacks the transcript; put the at-a-glance signal (mini-bar + current-step caption) in the COLLAPSED header instead, expand-on-click for detail.

### 2026-07-07 — Redesigned Task Mode's `tm-btn` button set — and fixed a latent defect: `.tm-btn-ghost` was referenced 3× (edit/abort/delete) but had NO CSS rule, so the "quiet" actions were rendering as heavy filled boxes.
- **Ask (owner).** The `tm-btn` style was "really ugly" — redesign it carefully. `tm-btn` is Task Mode's action-button set, defined inline in `static/js/task-mode.js`'s `_tmInjectStyles()` (styles.css is served directly; the `feature-*.js` bundle is the only place these live). It was a flat clone of the Studio's `orch-btn`: chunky `bg-tertiary` gray boxes, bland background-swap hover, no depth.
- **Latent defect found while surveying (not asked, but real).** `.tm-btn-ghost` is applied by the edit / abort / delete row buttons (task-mode.js ~2425/2434/2435) but had **no rule** → those tertiary actions fell through to the heavy filled `.tm-btn` base instead of reading as quiet. Also missing: any `:focus-visible` ring (a11y gap) and a `:disabled` state.
- **Redesign (`static/js/task-mode.js` `_tmInjectStyles`, ~L807, theme-token only — no hardcoded colors per §3.5).** Base `.tm-btn` gains a real hover **lift** (`translateY(-1px)` + `var(--tm-elev-card)` shadow) that presses back on `:active`; `:focus-visible` → accent border + 3px `--accent-subtle` ring; `:disabled` → dimmed, no transform. New **`.tm-btn-ghost`** = transparent tertiary that gains a subtle `--bg-hover` fill on hover; `.tm-btn-ghost.tm-btn-danger` stays quiet until hover then reveals the `--error-*` surface. `.tm-btn-close` = quiet icon button that reddens on hover. Semantic fills (`primary`/`ok`/`danger`) get a colored glow-lift on hover via `color-mix(in srgb, <token> N%, transparent)` — reusing the `color-mix` pattern already present in `.tm-shell` (styles.css:906,933).
- **Tofu-theme token audit (owner asked to confirm the inherited tokens resolve, since Task Mode has NO tofu-specific button rules — it rides live theme tokens).** Verified all dependencies redefine under `[data-theme="tofu"]` (styles.css:10223): `--accent-subtle` → `rgba(187,149,114,0.12)` (warm kinako glow, not the `:root` purple); `--error-text` → `#B46E60` (terracotta); `--tm-elev-card` resolves via `.tm-shell`'s `var(--clay-md,…)` and tofu redefines `--clay-md` → `0 2px 6px rgba(138,122,86,0.1)` (crisp warm shadow). The one NON-adaptive token is `--tm-ok` → `var(--s-done,#10b981)`: `--s-done` is `.settings-panel`/`.myday`-scoped, NOT in `.tm-shell` scope, so the ok-button green is the fixed `#10b981` fallback under ALL themes — but this is PRE-EXISTING (`--tm-ok` already drives every done-state across `.tm-shell`: styles.css:828/868/880/906/933), so reusing it keeps the ok button consistent with the rest of Task Mode, not a regression.
- **Verification.** `node --check static/js/task-mode.js` → SYNTAX_OK. Rebuilt via `lib.js_bundler.build_bundle()` (rebuilds core + deferred pair together, L744) → new deferred bundle `feature-9328490f.js`; grep-confirmed it contains both new rules (`tm-btn-ghost:hover`, `tm-btn:focus-visible`); stale `feature-133a319e.js` auto-cleaned. Core bundle `bundle-8dfe195a.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution). Task Mode is a DEFERRED lazy-loaded module → server restart (import-time bundler) + hard refresh (content-hashed filename) to see it.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A class referenced in HTML markup with no matching CSS rule silently inherits the base — here 3 "ghost" buttons rendered as heavy filled boxes and nobody noticed. When touching a button family, grep every `.tm-btn-*` variant used in the JS/markup against the rules actually defined. And when a themed surface rides INHERITED tokens rather than defining its own per-theme rules, confirm each token it leans on is redefined under the opinionated theme (tofu) — an un-themed token falls back to the dark `:root` value (e.g. purple `--accent-subtle`) and reads wrong on parchment.


### 2026-07-07 — Root-caused "dragging a .zip into the project modal → failed to save": it was a UX TRAP (dropped OUTSIDE the workspace), not a backend bug. First mirrored the guard as a hard block; on owner feedback softened to a one-click "add this folder & save here?" confirm (an upload is non-destructive).
- **Symptom (owner).** Drag-and-drop a compressed archive onto a directory in the project modal's folder browser → generic toast `1 file(s) failed to save`.
- **Root cause (log-confirmed, not guessed).** `logs/app.log` 20:30:01: `[Project.v1] upload failed for /mnt/.../ruanjunhao04/arxiv/citadel (1).zip: Destination is not inside any attached workspace folder.` The active project root was `.../ruanjunhao04/chatui`; the folder browser is a WHOLE-FILESYSTEM picker (opens at `~` so you can *add* new roots), and the drop landed on `.../ruanjunhao04/arxiv/` — a SIBLING of the project, not an attached root. `save_uploaded_file` (lib/project_mod/write_tools.py:777) refused it BY DESIGN ("a drop never auto-registers a new one"). So the backend was correct; the DEFECT was UX: the drop zone highlighted green + accepted the drop, then failed with a message that named neither the reason nor the remedy.
- **Fix v1 (reconsidered — see v2).** First cut mirrored the guard as a HARD BLOCK: a red `fb-drop-blocked` dragover affordance (`dropEffect='none'`) + `_runFolderDrop` short-circuit with an actionable "add it with + first" toast. Owner pushback: an upload is non-destructive (auto-rename, journaled, undoable) — a dead-end that forces cancel→find +→add→re-drop is disproportionate.
- **Fix v2 (shipped) — confirm-then-add, one click (frontend only, no backend change).** Kept the pure detection helpers `_attachedRootPaths()` (reads `projectState.path` + `extraRoots`, the single source of truth) and `_dirInsideAttachedRoot(dir)` (empty dir → active root, backend-resolved, allowed; else must equal / be nested under an attached root; prefix-only `/proj-evil` vs `/proj` correctly rejected). But instead of refusing, `_runFolderDrop` now OFFERS: `showConfirm("「arxiv」 isn't in your workspace yet. Add it as a project folder and save here?" · Add & save)` → on OK, new `_addDropDirAsRoot(dir)` adds it via the TESTED `Api.project.setPaths` apply path (preserving existing roots + read-only flags, then `_applyProjectData`/`_saveConvProjectPath`), then the upload proceeds. Reverted the red dragover styling + the `fb-drop-blocked*` CSS entirely — the mid-gesture "forbidden" paternalism was the worst part. Rationale for asking rather than silently auto-registering: adding a root has a VISIBLE side effect (a project scan + a new folder in the project bar) and `save_uploaded_file` needs the dest inside a root for undo/read-only handling — so a one-click confirm is the proportionate middle vs. both the dead-end and a silent workspace expansion (the exact footgun the original `save_uploaded_file` comment guards against).
- **Tests — `tests/test_frontend_folder_drop_gate.py` NEW, 4 green + neuter bites.** Brace-EXTRACTS the REAL shipped pure fns from project.js, evals under node against a stubbed `projectState`: empty/primary/nested/trailing-slash/extra-obj/extra-str inside-root; sibling/outside/prefix-only outside (9 checks). NEUTER: force `_dirInsideAttachedRoot → true` → the 3 outside checks FAIL while inside checks still PASS (proves the detection is load-bearing). Source-contract: `_runFolderDrop` calls `showConfirm` + `_addDropDirAsRoot(dir)` BEFORE the `Promise.allSettled(...upload)` loop, and `_addDropDirAsRoot` reuses `Api.project.setPaths`; confirm i18n keys present zh+en.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on project.js + i18n.js; no `fb-drop-blocked` leftovers. ruff clean on the new test. 4/4 green. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-32b63f78.js`. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard refresh needed (import-time bundler + content-hashed filename).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Failed to save" on an upload is not automatically a backend bug — check the log for the SPECIFIC refusal first (here the backend correctly enforced the workspace boundary; the fix belonged in the UI). But match the friction to the RISK: for a non-destructive action, don't dead-end at a boundary — offer a one-click way THROUGH it (confirm-then-add), reusing existing tested machinery, and only pause for a click because *adding a root* (not the upload) is the part with a visible side effect. Proportionality beats paternalism.


### 2026-07-07 — Poor-signal hardening, part 3: audited the MID-STREAM SSE reconnect lane (the distinct "network drops WHILE tokens stream" path). Verdict: already substantially robust; pinned the one load-bearing-but-untested invariant + flagged (not fixed) one un-deployed-path edge.
- **Scope.** The prior two parts hardened the SEND/persist lane. This part audits the DISTINCT lane: the network drops mid-answer (tokens arriving) then recovers. Two parallel `coder` audits (frontend reconnect + backend resume capability).
- **Backend verdict (audit).** TRUE resume EXISTS: the SSE stream route (routes/chat.py) honors `Last-Event-ID` with BOTH a warm in-memory buffer replay (`_warm_resume_serviceable` ~:1386) and a COLD persisted-`task_events` replay (`_read_events(..., since_event_id=cursor)` ~:1441-1454), so a reconnect gets events emitted during the disconnect. Gap: the POLL endpoint does not take a seq cursor (poll is a keep-longer snapshot, not event replay) — acceptable because poll is the fallback-of-last-resort and its merge is regression-safe.
- **Frontend verdict (audit).** Substantially hardened, NOT a rewrite candidate: reconnect sends `Last-Event-ID` from `stream._lastEventId` (seeded from sessionStorage on reload) — offset resume, not whole-conv re-fetch (sse_pipeline.js:1727-1737, :505-539); the cursor advances only after an event is applied. Poll fallback keeps-longer (never re-appends already-shown tokens, sse_poll_fallback.js:200-224). Reconnect-to-running pre-populates the partial ("Resuming…"), re-targets by stable id (no dup bubble), guards stale-prior-turn. Task-completed-while-disconnected adopts the server result (Case B/F, main_init_tasks.js). Ghost-delete is retired client-side (part 1) so a no-finishReason partial is only ever STAMPED interrupted, never truncated by the client.
- **What I actually changed (measure-first — did NOT gold-plate robust code).** The audit named ONE latent trap worth acting on: the monotonic KEEP-LONGER invariant (`_snapshotLonger` / `_snapshotLongerRounds`, sse_pipeline.js:59-81) is the SINGLE guarantee preventing a cold/lagging reconnect snapshot from wiping the partial the user already watched stream ("generating then GONE"), applied at BOTH the `state` reconnect snapshot (~:756) and the `done` committedMessage (~:1557) — but it had NO dedicated regression test. A future edit assigning `msg.content = ev.content` raw would silently reintroduce the bug. NEW `tests/test_frontend_reconnect_keeplonger_invariant.py`: brace-extracts the two REAL functions, evals under node, 8 assertions (shrink-blocked / grow-adopted / equal-ok / empty-keeps for content+thinking; rounds shrink-blocked/grow/empty) + a NEUTER (replace `_snapshotLonger` with the naive raw-return → shrink-blocked checks FAIL) proving the guard is load-bearing. Both green.
- **Flagged, NOT fixed (with justification).** The sharded-backend reconnect-hint exhaustion (sse_poll_fallback.js:147-149): after `_MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS=3` failed SSE re-opens it keeps polling the local replica, and if the task lives on ANOTHER replica the bubble could stay "running". This block is DEAD CODE on a single-box install (the comment + charter confirm `reconnect:true` is only ever set under `TOFU_RUNTIME_STATE_BACKEND=redis`, an un-rolled-out scale deployment). Fixing it now = speculative work on an un-deployed path → deliberately deferred per measure-first. Recorded here so the scale-rollout epic picks it up.
- **Verification.** New test 2/2 green with neuter (`-p no:napari`). No production code changed in this part → no bundle rebuild needed. ruff N/A (test-only). NOT committed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Don't rewrite a lane the audit finds robust — pin its load-bearing invariant with a neuter'd test instead, so the robustness can't silently rot. When an audit flags an edge on a path that's DEAD CODE on the default deployment (env-gated scale feature), flag-and-defer with the gating evidence rather than fixing speculatively — measure-first cuts both ways (fix real gaps, don't gold-plate un-deployed ones). Backend SSE resume was already dual-mode (warm buffer + cold task_events replay via Last-Event-ID) — verify capability before assuming a lane needs building.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "insight" second-pass, round 3: widened the A/B to n=9 (5 EN + 4 ZH) per the owner's own n≥7 bar — and the gate did NOT clear. The n=4 win looked fragile and WAS: at n=9 win-rate 0.44, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound 0.22. Reporting the negative result straight; NOT shipping.
- **Why.** Owner held the last acceptance criterion on SAMPLE SIZE: the n=4 result (win-rate 0.88, CI lower 0.62) was "directionally encouraging but fragile — one more loss pulls that bound toward or below 0.5". Bar: n≥7, ≥1 ZH paper, 2-3 more low-baseline, gate = bootstrap CI lower bound > 0.5.
- **Harness change.** `debug/insight_batch.py` gained ZH support + a `summary_all` phase (`_scan_cache_pairs` scans every `<phash>_<lang>.gen.json` on disk so the final verdict aggregates ACROSS languages, not one `--lang`). Per-paper tuple now carries `lang`; summary prints `[n zh]`. Resumable gen→score→summary cache made the 9-paper × (gen ~5-8min + 6 score calls) feasible in timeout-bounded chunks. Trap re-hit: the DB inventory print truncates `paper_hash` to 14 chars; passing those to `--hashes` caches as `ok:False why:'no report'` — always use the FULL 32-char hash.
- **Reliability fix VALIDATED at scale.** Across 9 live insight generations in BOTH languages (temp=0.45 + repair re-ask), **0 silent JSON failures** (round-1 temp=0.7 failed ~1/3). ZH works end-to-end: proper Chinese output (`## 💡 洞见与灵感` / `这篇论文的赌注`), grounding held (2-6 grounded refs/paper, near-0 dropped). So the ENGINE is sound; the VALUE is what didn't hold.
- **RESULT (n=9, 4 zh, 3 repeats/arm, 5000 bootstrap), section-level report→insight overall:** 82840 3.17→4.58 (+1.42 WIN), fd6773[zh] 3.00→4.33 (+1.33 WIN), 25ee 3.58→4.58 (+1.00 WIN), 216bef[zh] 3.83→4.42 (+0.58 WIN); 4c3dc4[zh] 4.83→4.75 (−0.08), 6e40ab[zh] 4.50→4.33 (−0.17), eaf4 4.67→4.42 (−0.25), 74c6 4.75→3.83 (−0.92), bd79f6 3.33→**2.08** (−1.25). **mean Δ +0.185, win-rate 0.44, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound 0.22 → does NOT clear the 0.5 gate.** Per-axis still transfer-led (transfer +0.35, novelty +0.24, thesis +0.20, opinion −0.06) but all small.
- **Why n=4 lied (the sampling lesson, concretely).** The first 4 were 3 low-baseline WINs + 1 high-baseline tie — an unrepresentative draw. Widening exposed two loss classes the small sample missed: (1) **high-baseline papers** (74c6 4.75, 6e40ab 4.50, 4c3dc4 4.83, eaf4 4.67) — the report is already insight-saturated, so a short section scored on the SAME axes scores at or below it (no headroom, and 74c6 lost −0.92 because the isolated section reads thinner than the report's own rich analysis). (2) **bd79f6 (Transformer) — a genuine QUALITY failure, not a baseline artifact:** low baseline (3.33) but B=2.08, the worst loss. Inspection shows WHY: a degenerate self-referential connection ("multi-head attention in 'Attention Is All You Need' is a generalized form of the attention mechanism described in 'Attention Is All You Need' itself") + a forced EvoLM/"multi-head rubrics" transfer. On a FOUNDATIONAL paper the "connect to your library" moat backfires — the reader's library IS descendants of this paper, so the pass produces circular or strained bridges. 5 grounded refs, 0 dropped → grounding can't catch a bridge that is real-but-vacuous.
- **Honest verdict.** The feature helps MID-baseline explainers (the +1.0-1.4 wins are real and transfer-driven) but HURTS or no-ops high-baseline and foundational papers, and the net over a representative sample is indistinguishable from noise. The uplift is real but CONDITIONAL, and I cannot ship an always-on (even flag-gated-on) pass whose expected effect is a coin-flip. NOT wiring into the report route. The standalone report-refinement critic pass stays held.
- **What the data suggests next (not yet done, owner's call).** (a) A GATING policy — only run/surface insight when the report's own insight score is low (predicted headroom); the wins cluster where A≤3.9, losses where A≥4.5. (b) Fix the foundational-paper backfire — suppress self-referential / same-lineage connections in the grounding step (a bridge whose target ≈ the paper itself is vacuous). (c) Re-measure the GATED variant. Only then is "ship it" back on the table.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A win-rate CI lower bound over n=4 is not a result — it's a hint; the owner's n≥7 insistence was correct and the widening flipped the verdict (0.62→0.22). Deliberately sample ACROSS the baseline spectrum, not just the easy-win regime, or you'll confirm a bias. When an "uplift" is conditional (helps low-baseline, hurts high), the aggregate win-rate hides it — report the per-item split and the CONDITION, and prefer a gated rollout over always-on. Grounding verifies a reference EXISTS, not that a connection is NON-VACUOUS — a self-referential bridge on a foundational paper passes grounding and still tanks quality.


### 2026-07-07 — Autopilot VU turns FLATTENED to the agent bubble (owner directive, option A) — fixes the "can't delete an autopilot message" symptom at its ROOT (the run-fold), render-layer ONLY (data-layer provenance untouched)
- **Ask (owner).** Autopilot (virtual-user / VU) turns should render with the IDENTICAL agent bubble layout (plain markdown body, normal grouped tool panel, normal thinking block); the ONLY difference is the avatar + "Autopilot" label. Drop the "Private · not sent" dashed zone, the "Sent to the agent" green zone, and the "Autopilot investigation" header. And fix deletion — a concluded VU turn couldn't be deleted.
- **Root cause of "can't delete" (diagnosed, not guessed).** Deletion was NEVER blocked in code: `_delete_message_blocking` (routes/conversations.py:1071) deletes by index with no role guard, and `deleteTurn`/`_execDeleteTurn` (message_actions.js) have no VU guard. The real blocker was the `autopilot-run-fold` `<details>` built by `_applyAutopilotRunFolds` (chat_render.js): concluded VU turns were moved into a COLLAPSED card, so the per-message hover action bar (incl. the delete button) was never reachable. Flattening the bubble alone wouldn't fix delete while the fold still swallowed the turns.
- **What shipped (render-layer only, 3 edits in `static/js/ui/chat_render.js`).**
  1. **Fold → flatten.** `_applyAutopilotRunFolds` no longer creates any `<details.autopilot-run-fold>`. It's kept (3 render call-sites + run-concluded SSE/sidecar plumbing still invoke it) but now does the OPPOSITE: defensively UNWRAPS any stale fold left in the DOM (hoists its `.message` children back to the flat sibling level, drops the `<summary>`). Result: the VU↔agent transcript is a flat sequence like a normal agent chat, and every turn keeps its own hover action bar (copy / translate / DELETE).
  2. **VU body flattened.** Removed the `_vuPrivate`/`_vuPrivateHtml` collection + the `<details.vu-private-zone>` "Private · not sent" wrapper + the "Autopilot investigation · N tool calls" header. Tool rounds + thinking now go straight into `body` exactly like an assistant turn.
  3. **Reply flattened.** Removed the `<div.vu-sent-zone>` + `.vu-handoff-header` "Sent to the agent" wrapper; the VU reply renders as a plain `.md-content` body.
  The avatar (Autopilot/critic glyph) + role label ("Autopilot") + the `vu-user-msg` lane class are the ONLY who-is-speaking signals that remain.
- **DATA-layer provenance UNCHANGED (verified).** `conv_message_builder._build_user_message` still reads ONLY `content` for a VU user row — toolRounds/thinking remain display-only and never reach the next agent. This is purely a render change; `_append_vu_message_to_conv`, the segment/verdict plumbing, and the streaming VU substrate (`_handleAutopilotVuEvent` in streaming_render.js) are untouched.
- **Delete semantics for a VU `role:'user'` row (thought through, not just single).** Single delete: index-based, works. TURN mode: `hasAssistantAfter` checks `messages[idx+1].role==='assistant'`; the transcript is `…→VU(user)→agent(assistant)→…`, so "Delete turn" removes the VU message + the agent response it prompted — the correct prompt+answer pairing, not a wrong pair. A tail VU (no following assistant) offers single delete only.
- **Tests.** DELETED the two obsolete fold tests (`test_frontend_autopilot_fold.py`, `test_frontend_autopilot_collapse_gating.py`) — their entire premise (WHEN/HOW to collapse a run into a `<details>`) is the contract I deliberately removed; keeping them would assert dead behavior. NEW `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_flat_render.py` (jsdom, evals REAL escape_html + safe_html + chat_render): (a) drives REAL `renderMessage(VU)` → asserts `.md-content` reply + `.ptool-panel` grouped tools + standalone `_toggleThinking` block present; NO `.vu-private-zone`/`.vu-sent-zone`/`.vu-investigation-header`/`.vu-handoff-header`; avatar=critic glyph + role label "Autopilot" + `vu-user-msg` class; a REACHABLE `.msg-delete-btn` calling `deleteTurn(3)` that is NOT inside any `<details>`. (b) `_applyAutopilotRunFolds` over a CONCLUDED run's DOM creates NO fold + leaves turns flat; and UNWRAPS a pre-built stale fold. TWO NEUTERS (separate tests): NC-1 re-wrap a `.vu-private-zone` → `a_no_private_zone` FAILS; NC-2 make the fn fold again → `b_no_fold_created`/`b_vu_turn_flat` FAIL. 3 tests green (main + 2 NC). Regression sweep: 18 passed across flat-render + rendermessage-segment-gate + vu-verbatim + warmup + baton + dispatch + queue-badge + bg-refresh + peer-header. Bundle-corruption-guard 12 + api-isolation 4 green.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on chat_render.js. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-efb26ab7.js` (0 provenance-zone render sites, `msg-delete-btn` present, unwrap-not-fold marker present); stale bundles auto-cleaned. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard refresh needed (import-time bundler + content-hashed filename). NOTE: the now-unreferenced fold helpers (`_apRunConcluded`, `_apFoldOpenState`, `_apRunSummary`, `_openApSummaryModal`, `_summarizeAutopilotRun`) + the `.autopilot-run-fold`/`.vu-private-zone`/`.vu-sent-zone` CSS were left in place (dead but harmless) to keep the diff render-layer-minimal and avoid churn on the hot files; a later cleanup increment can prune them.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a message "can't be deleted" but the delete path is role-agnostic end-to-end, look for a CONTAINER that hides the hover action bar (here a collapsed `<details>`), not a delete guard. Flattening the bubble STYLE is insufficient while the grouping still buries the turns — fix both together. To prove a flatten, drive the REAL `renderMessage` entry point and assert BOTH the presence of the agent-identical structure (md-content + tool panel + thinking + reachable delete) AND the ABSENCE of every removed zone, with a neuter that re-adds a zone to prove the absence-assertion is load-bearing.


### 2026-07-07 — External-edit probe stops lying: content-hash guard kills phantom "IDE changed your file" toasts, and last_writer_task_id attribution stops blaming the human for a sibling conversation's write.
- **Two real defects (owner-confirmed against live store, not speculation).** The `project_external_edit` toast ("你在 Tofu 之外（如 IDE）改动了…") fired for `lib/chat/turn_builder.py` though the owner never touched an IDE. Root-caused both by reading `.tofu/file-history/`: (1) `turn_builder.py` was at **v69** with `v64–v68` five BYTE-IDENTICAL blobs (sha `2f2223d9`) then a genuine `v68→v69` +796B change (the `_msgId` passthrough written by the sibling rev/CAS conversation); (2) the store is **shared per-project-root across all conversations**, so a sibling Tofu write drifts the file vs this task's round boundary and was reported as an external/IDE edit. Live blast radius: **750** external snapshots on this root, most of them noise.
- **Root cause (single shared origin).** `detect_external_edits` (lib/file_history/api.py) and `store.stage_backup` dedup on **mtime+size ONLY**. But `store._stage_explicit` — the path a Tofu write tool takes via `modifications._record_modification(track_edit(pre_content=…))` — deliberately writes `mtime: 0` as a sentinel. So every probe after any Tofu write sees `real_mtime ≠ 0` → "drift" → stages a redundant identical backup + fires the toast. And the probe called `stage_backup` with NO task_id, which would have clobbered `last_writer_task_id` to '' (destroying the attribution signal Fix 2 needs) — the content guard now short-circuits before that.
- **Fix 1 — CONTENT guard (kills phantom fires).** New `_disk_matches_last_backup(base,rel,info,abs_p)`: on a stat *hint*, hashes current disk bytes vs the pinned `latest_version` backup blob. Byte-identical ⇒ NOT drift: reconcile the stale `mtime:0`/size in `tracked.json` (touch mtime+size ONLY, leave version + `last_writer_task_id` intact) so future probes short-circuit, and stage NO backup, fire NO toast. Fails SAFE (returns False → falls through to normal drift path) when there's no comparable blob (v0 / too_large / deleted / missing blob / unreadable) — can only SUPPRESS a false positive, never manufacture one or hide a real edit. Reconcile runs AFTER the loop against a freshly-reloaded tracked dict (never holds a stale dict across a `stage_backup` load-modify-save).
- **Fix 2 — ATTRIBUTION guard (stops blaming the human).** `detect_external_edits(..., known_task_ids)`: a genuine content change whose tracked `last_writer_task_id` ∈ known Tofu tasks is a CONCURRENT conversation, not an IDE edit → excluded from `files`/`committed`, returned separately under new `siblingFiles: [{path, taskId}]`. Empty writer (true out-of-band edit) stays external even with known_task_ids populated. Orchestrator (`_probe_external_edits`) snapshots `manager.tasks` keys under `tasks_lock` and passes them; logs the suppression. `known_task_ids=None` ⇒ legacy behaviour (everything external).
- **Tests — `tests/test_file_history_external_edit_guards.py` NEW, 7 pytest GREEN, both neuters bite.** Content: identical-rewrite-with-mtime:0-sentinel does NOT commit/report + no version churn + stale mtime reconciled; 5 repeated probes stay silent (the live symptom); genuine change still fires. Attribution: sibling-task-stamped drift → `siblingFiles` not `files`; unattributed genuine edit stays external. NEUTER-1: `monkeypatch _disk_matches_last_backup → False` ⇒ phantom fire returns. NEUTER-2: writer NOT in `known_task_ids` ⇒ misattributed as external. `_simulate_tofu_net_zero_write` reproduces the exact `_stage_explicit` mtime:0 state. Marked `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`.
- **Verification.** New suite 7/7 (`PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` — a napari/vispy pytest plugin OSErrors at collection otherwise). Regression: `debug/test_file_history.py` 34/34, `tests/test_file_history_compaction.py` 7/7, `debug/test_concurrent_fh_attribution.py` all PASS (Task-A..G attribution intact). ruff clean on all 3 changed files. Backend-only; no bundle rebuild. NOT committed (owner attribution). The frontend toast wording ("IDE") is untouched this pass — Fix 2 stops the misattributed events from ever reaching it; routing `siblingFiles` to the conversation-aware "changed by «conversation»" toast is a viable follow-up but was out of scope for "stop lying."
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An mtime/size delta is a HINT, never proof of an edit — a sentinel-mtime writer (here `_stage_explicit`'s `mtime:0`) turns a pure-metadata dedup into a false-positive engine; confirm against actual content before declaring drift. On a resource SHARED across conversations (the per-root fh store), any "who changed this" signal must consult the existing per-writer attribution (`last_writer_task_id`) before blaming the human. Prove each guard load-bearing with a neuter that restores the exact pre-fix false positive.

### 2026-07-07 — Poor-signal hardening, part 2: closed the QUEUED send lane (send-while-task-running) against the same lost-ACK duplicate, and proved the sustained-409 rebase loop can neither strand nor spin (evidence, not a judgment call).
