- **Why re-open again (owner).** After the immediate-send lane was hardened, the owner flagged a SECOND equally-common poor-network path: send-while-a-task-is-running. The turn is enqueued and later persisted by `dispatch_next_queued` (lib/message_queue.py), NOT by the immediate `/api/chat/send` persist that was fixed. Two holes named + confirmed.
- **Hole 1 — legacy queue build dropped `_msgId`.** `dispatch_next_queued`'s legacy branch (no `_user_msg`) built `user_msg = {role, content, timestamp}` from scratch, never carrying `payload['_msgId']` → a queued-then-rescued message duplicates exactly like the immediate lane did pre-fix (rescue-PUT rebase keyed on `_msgId` can't match the server copy). **Fix:** carry `payload['_msgId']` in the legacy build (mirrors the turn_builder fix).
- **Hole 2 — pre-built path unverified end-to-end.** `/api/chat/send` stashes the (now `_msgId`-bearing) `user_msg` as `queue_payload['_user_msg']`; `dispatch_next_queued` appends it directly. Correct by construction, but there was NO test proving `_msgId` survives enqueue→JSON round-trip→dispatch append. **Now proven.**
- **Tests.** NEW `tests/test_queue_msgid_preservation.py` (standalone, real DB): drives the REAL `enqueue_message` + `dispatch_next_queued` (create_task/spawn_task stubbed — the user-msg PERSIST happens BEFORE task creation, so the persisted `conversations.messages` row is asserted directly) for BOTH sub-paths; asserts the persisted queued msg carries the client `_msgId`. NEUTER (subprocess): strip the legacy carry line → legacy test fails → carry is load-bearing. Baseline + neuter green.
- **Sustained-409 termination — evidence, not a hand-wave.** Owner required proof the rebase-on-409 loop can't strand a message or spin forever. Reasoned + tested: a "give-up" path would be HARMFUL (giving up = drop the client msg [strand] or force-overwrite [clobber] — the two things CAS prevents), so KEEP-and-retry is correct. NEW `tests/test_frontend_rev_conflict_termination.py` (3 tests, real `syncConversationToServer`+`_rebaseUnackedTail` under node): (1) NO concurrent writer → retry with the just-GET'd rev DETERMINISTICALLY succeeds (no livelock — a re-409 requires a concurrent writer in the GET→PUT window, never deterministic); (2) transient conflicts (burst then quiet) → message lands EXACTLY once, bounded PUTs ≤ N+1, concurrent writers' msgs preserved; (3) sustained conflict (never quiets in one call) → per-call depth guard (≥3) returns false WITHOUT clobber (`accepts==0`), message RETAINED locally (`m-mine` still in conv.messages) → poller re-offers it. Poller cadence verified: fixed 12s `setInterval`, self-cancels the instant no conv has a pending marker (`_flushPendingSyncs` clears the interval) → bounded background retry, not a hot spin. Every 409 also means some OTHER write LANDED = global progress. CONCLUSION (measure-first): leave retry semantics as-is; adding speculative backoff would slow the common transient-recovery case. Owner's "prove it" bar met with tests.
- **Env note (not a regression).** A pytest run mid-session started crashing at COLLECTION with `OSError: GL ES 2.0 library not found` — the `napari-plugin-engine` pytest entrypoint auto-loads and imports vispy, which needs a GL lib absent on this headless host. Unrelated to the code; worked around with `-p no:napari`. The two `test_queue_append_cas.py` pytest "failures" (`sqlite3.O…`) are the KNOWN standalone-runner DB-bootstrap artifact — both pass via `python tests/test_queue_append_cas.py`.
- **Verification.** 19 pytest green (frontend rebase/cross-tab/termination/lost-ack/allowtruncate/idempotency/reconcile-equivalence, napari disabled) + 4 standalone real-DB suites green WITH neuters (queue_append_cas, queue_msgid_preservation, conv_cas_put, conv_rev_monotonic). ruff clean. Bundle → `bundle-efb26ab7.js`. NOT committed. Server restart + hard refresh needed (the `_msgId`-on-payload frontend↔backend pair must deploy together).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When you fix a persist path, enumerate ALL persist paths — the queue lane (`dispatch_next_queued`) is a second, easily-missed writer of the user turn with its own from-scratch build that silently dropped `_msgId`. And "could it spin forever?" deserves a termination PROOF, not a shrug: model the retry as CAS (retry base = last-GET rev) → a re-conflict requires a concurrent writer → no deterministic livelock; verify the message is RETAINED (never stranded) and the server never force-overwritten on give-up-to-poller; confirm the poller is bounded-cadence + self-cancelling.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "insight" second-pass, round 2: fixed the temp=0.7 silent-failure bug (repair re-ask + lower temp) and re-measured with a SECTION-LEVEL paired bootstrap that removed the whole-document dilution confound → transfer-led win, CI lower bound CLEARS 0.5
- **Context.** Round 1 shipped `lib/paper/insight_engine.py` (agentic transfer-first synthesis after the fidelity report, grounding gate, rubric critic, flag-gated `TOFU_PAPER_INSIGHT`, `insight:<ui>` persist key) + `insight_prompts.py` + 6/6 neuter test + a first A/B harness. Owner accepted the seam but held the last acceptance criterion open for TWO reasons the round-1 report itself surfaced: (1) the A/B was CONFOUNDED — it scored the whole 39k-char document, so a 3k insight section literally can't move a whole-doc mean and on the strong paper went NEGATIVE (4.83→4.58) purely from dilution; (2) a RELIABILITY bug — temp=0.7 broke strict-JSON ~1/3 of runs and the feature then silently returned nothing (watched two real runs die on `No usable insight JSON`).
- **Fix #1 — robustness (root cause, not a shortcut).** Lowered `_INSIGHT_TEMPERATURE` 0.7→**0.45** (keeps some divergence, restores JSON reliability) AND added a one-shot **repair re-ask**: on final-content parse failure, `_repair_json_reask()` re-asks the SAME conversation (model still has its research + reader context in-context) with a strict "return ONLY the JSON object" instruction at **temp=0, no tools** — a deterministic reformat of what it already produced, not a fresh generation. Feeds back the bad content (capped 6k) so it reformats THAT. `_research_and_synthesize` now parses, and only on failure calls the repair. Empirically the temp drop alone fixed it: all 6 batch gens parsed first-try (0 silent failures where round-1 saw 2/3 fail); repair is the belt-and-suspenders net.
- **Fix #2 — measurement (isolate the artifact).** New `debug/insight_batch.py`: arm A = the PLAIN REPORT scored on the 4 INSIGHT axes (the insight a reader gets today = incumbent); arm B = the INSIGHT SECTION ALONE on the SAME rubric (the rubric already tells the judge to ignore factual coverage, so scoring a focused section vs a long report is fair on the INSIGHT dimension). Per paper each arm scored `--repeats`× and averaged (kills the single-shot rubric calibration noise the owner flagged — same report scored 5.0 then 3.75 back-to-back in round 1). Then a **paired bootstrap over papers** → section-beats-report win-rate + one-sided 95% CI lower bound (the 50%-gated convention); clears iff lower bound > 0.5. Also reports per-axis mean delta to see which axis carries it. Harness is PHASED + resumable (on-disk `.insight_cache/`: `gen`→`score`→`summary`) because live insight gen is ~5-8 min/paper (real web_search) and a single N-paper run overruns any timeout — each phase runs in bounded chunks and re-runs skip cached work.
- **RESULT (n=4 EN papers, 3 repeats/arm, 5000 bootstrap).** Per-paper report→section overall: eaf4 (rubrics paper, high baseline) 4.50→4.50 TIE (no headroom); 82840 (dUltra, low baseline) 3.50→**4.92** (+1.42) WIN; 25ee 3.88→**4.83** (+0.96) WIN; 74c6 3.67→4.08 (+0.42) WIN. **mean Δ +0.70, win-rate 0.88, bootstrap 95% CI lower bound 0.62 → CLEARS the 0.5 gate.** Per-axis mean (report→section): thesis +0.54, **novelty +1.04**, defensible-opinion +0.21, **transfer_concreteness +1.00** — the hypothesised moat (transfer) plus novelty carry the win; the confirmatory finding is that the win is BIGGEST on low-baseline papers (dry explainers) and vanishes only where the report was already insight-saturated (your own-domain paper). Grounding held throughout (2-4 grounded refs/paper, the one hallucinated ref dropped).
- **Gate — `tests/test_paper_insight_agentic.py` 6→8, all green, ruff clean.** Added `_RepairPatched`: synthesis round returns prose-wrapped+truncated garbage, model emits clean JSON ONLY on the repair re-ask (detected by `_REPAIR_INSTRUCTION` in the last user msg). `test_repair_reask_recovers_unparseable_json` (recovered insight flows through grounding+render, no silent no-op) + **NEUTER** `test_neuter_repair_is_load_bearing` (`break_repair=True` → repair ALSO returns garbage → feature yields None, proving recovery comes from the repair and nowhere else). Original 6 (agentic-loop-ran-before-write, date-anchor, grounding-drops-hallucination, rubric-clamp-recompute, loop-neuter, flag-off) still pass.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Still flag-gated OFF (`TOFU_PAPER_INSIGHT=1`), fully non-destructive (persists under `insight:<ui>`, never touches the report row / report prompt). NOT yet wired into the report ROUTE/frontend — the standalone report-refinement critic pass remains HELD per agreement until pass-2-alone was measured (now done: it clears). Backend-only → server restart for live use.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) When an added artifact is a small fraction of a large document, NEVER measure it by scoring the whole document — the dilution swamps the signal and can flip the sign; score the ARTIFACT in isolation against the same rubric. (2) A creative-divergence temperature and strict-JSON output are in tension — before reaching for higher temp, check the structured-output failure rate; the reliable fix here was a modest temp (0.45) + a deterministic temp=0 repair re-ask, not 0.7-and-hope. (3) A single LLM-judge rubric call is too noisy to trust as an A/B instrument — repeat-average per arm AND bootstrap over items with a CI lower bound; report the gate, not a lucky single sample. (4) Deliberately include LOW-baseline items in an uplift eval — the strong-baseline items have no headroom and will mask a real win (here the feature's whole value showed up on the dry explainers, exactly where a reader needs it most).

Asserts: delivery card shows the resolved TITLE not `conv mradmzmd` (id demoted to `title=` tooltip); queue source line renders `from «Title»` (+ `from operator «Title»` for a human nudge) with the clean full text; a plain real turn has no source line; an unknown id falls back to localized "Untitled chat", never a bare id. **POISONED NC** (`convTitleById`'s `if (typeof conversations…)` → `if (false)`): BOTH surfaces lose the real title and show `«Untitled chat»`, proving resolution is load-bearing not a tautology of the fallback. DOM shim gotcha: the id setter registers the element into `_els` so the real `renderPendingQueueUI`'s `getElementById('pendingQueueBar')` retrieves the container it created + set `.id` on (mirrors "in the DOM, retrievable by id").
- **Fixed the wrong-reason pass — `test_frontend_brain_tool_render.py` (12 tests, unchanged count).** Its harness now defines `convTitleById` + a `conversations` list, so the delivery card exercises the REAL resolver. `peermsg_target` now asserts the resolved title `Overlap Watch Conv` (was: `includes('cdef1234')`), + new `peermsg_target_id_in_tooltip` (`title="cdef1234"`) and `peermsg_target_not_raw` (`!includes('conv cdef1234')`). New `test_NC_delivery_card_title_resolution_is_load_bearing`: neuter the `convTitleById` branch in shipped `_renderPeerDelivery` → target reverts to raw `conv cdef1234` → the two title checks FAIL while the card still renders.
- **Verification.** All affected suites together = 62 pass (`test_message_queue` 10 + `test_project_peer` 26 + `_human_nudge` 7 + `brain_tool_render` 12 + `peer_title_resolution` 6 + `peer_header_identity` 1); ruff clean on the new/modified test files. No production code changed this session — regression guards only. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A frontend test that stubs a helper to `undefined` and asserts the FALLBACK output silently stops testing the real path the moment you add that helper — it "passes for the wrong reason". When you add an id→title resolver, the guard MUST define it + real data and assert the RESOLVED value, with an NC that neuters the lookup. For a backend branch that transforms stored data (framed→clean, cap change), the faithful test SEEDS the payload exactly as the real writer does and the NEUTER re-implements the OLD transform to reproduce the reported symptom.


### 2026-07-07 — Root-caused "finished conversation, yet my message gets stuck in 排队中": a real user send now SUPERSEDES an in-flight AUTOPILOT turn instead of queuing behind it (Option A, backend abort + disarm)
- **Symptom (owner, log-verified).** On a conversation that had used autopilot and *looked* ended, sending a follow-up got silently QUEUED and only ran minutes later. Traced to the exact conv in the screenshot (`mra3utj4`): at 19:23:10 the autopilot loop spawned follow-up worker task `012f06a5`; at 19:23:59 the user's "这个什么sdk是需要我干嘛的" was QUEUED because that task was still `status='running'`; the follow-up ran **8.5 min / 16 rounds / ¥74** and only at 19:31:48 did it dequeue + dispatch the human message (task `ec4450fc`). Not lost — blocked behind an *invisible* long autopilot turn (the follow-up baton not attaching to the visible chat is the SEPARATE `conv._apPendingBaton` known issue; sidebar dot correctly showed "answering").
- **Root cause.** The queue gate in `routes/chat.py::chat_send` (~L603) enqueued whenever ANY running non-aborted task existed for the conv — it did NOT distinguish a real worker turn from an autopilot follow-up. The queue design already ranks a human `KIND_REAL` ahead of the `KIND_AUTOPILOT` sentinel, but that priority was never extended to the *in-flight* turn.
- **Fix (Option A, root cause — NOT a "show a hint" band-aid).** Replaced the single `has_running_task` bool with a type discriminator, computed under `tasks_lock`:
  - `_is_autopilot_task(t)` = `config.autopilot` truthy OR `_autopilotParent` OR `_vu_subtask` OR `_autopilot_kick`. (The real workhorse marker is the follow-up's `config.autopilot=True` + `_autopilotParent`, since `_start_followup_task` does `cfg=dict(task['config'])`. The VU sub-task runs `convId=''` so it never matches the conv filter anyway.)
  - Bucket running non-aborted tasks into `has_running_worker` (normal) vs `autopilot_running_ids`.
  - **Only-autopilot running** → NOT queued: mark those task ids `aborted=True` + `_abort_reason='superseded_by_user_send'` in the SAME `tasks_lock` section (a REAL backend stop, so the invisible turn actually dies + the zombie is reclaimed even if the baton dropped), then call `disarm_autopilot(conv_id)` (clears armed marker + flips live `config.autopilot=False` + `conclude_run(reason='stopped')` — the canonical human-cancel close-out, one source of truth), then fall through to the normal immediate-start path (append→persist→`_start_task_for_conv`, which re-aborts as belt-and-braces + writes the aborted terminal floor).
  - **Normal worker running** → unchanged: still enqueues (a human correctly waits behind a real in-progress reply). Worker-bucket takes PRECEDENCE — if a worker + autopilot task coexist, we enqueue and do NOT force-abort the autopilot from the send gate.
- **Tests (`tests/test_chat_send_supersedes_autopilot.py`, 3, all green + neuter-verified).** Drive the REAL `/api/v1/chat/send` via the sync test client, stub `spawn_task`, seed a real conv row + inject synthetic running tasks: (1) FIX — lone autopilot follow-up + armed marker → send returns `taskId` (NOT queued), autopilot task `aborted`, marker cleared, queue depth 0; (2) NEGATIVE CONTROL — lone normal worker → send returns `{queued:true}`, worker NOT aborted, depth 1; (3) GUARD — worker+autopilot coexist → still queued, autopilot NOT force-aborted. NEUTER (revert gate to old blunt behaviour) → test #1 fails (queued at position 2), controls stay green; restore → 3/3.
- **Verification.** ruff clean on `routes/chat.py` + the test. Regression sweep 38 passed (supersede + `test_autopilot_arm` 11 + `test_message_queue` 10 + `test_chat_send_idempotency` 3 + `test_autopilot_kick` 11). NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only, no schema/bundle change; server restart picks it up (import-time route).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A queue gate that keys only on "is a task running" conflates two priorities. When the queue model already ranks turn *sources* (human > autopilot), extend that ranking to the LIVE turn too — discriminate task type at the gate. Supersede via a REAL backend abort + the existing `disarm_autopilot`/`conclude_run` seam (never a frontend hide), so it also reclaims a zombie autopilot task whose follow-up baton was dropped. The baton-visibility fix (`conv._apPendingBaton`) is related but independent — kept out of this change per owner.


### 2026-07-07 — Peer/queue surfaces showed a raw conv ID where a TITLE belongs, and truncated the message: three coordinated display fixes (backend `_peerText` + un-truncated `get_queue`, frontend `convTitleById` resolver) so both the delivery card and the queued peer message name the source conversation + show the full text.
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** (1) The project_message delivery card read `发送消息 › conv mradmzmd` — a bare id, meaningless to a human. (2) The queued peer message in the input bar showed the raw framed body `[Peer message from a sibling conversation of this project (conv mradmzmd)] … Done — I shipped the ren` — again a raw id AND cut off mid-word.
- **Three root causes (all display-layer, traced not guessed):**
  1. **Delivery card** — `_renderPeerDelivery` (static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js) hard-coded `conv ${pd.toConv.slice(0,8)}`, never a title.
  2. **Queued preview truncation** — `get_queue` (lib/message_queue.py:401) capped the preview at `[:100]`. For a peer turn the stored `text` is the model-facing FRAMED body (`[Peer message … (conv X)]\n\n<real msg>\n\n(advisory…)`), whose wrapper alone is ~74 chars → only ~26 chars of the real message survived ("Done — I shipped the ren").
  3. **Raw id in the queued body** — the frontend rendered that framed body verbatim, so the embedded short id leaked into the UI.
- **Fix (backend).** `send_peer_message` now ALSO stores the clean, unframed original message as `payload['_peerText']` (added AFTER the existing `payload = {…}` + `_peerHuman` block so the peer-marker/human-nudge NC test anchors stay byte-identical). `get_queue` prefers `_peerText` for a `_peerMessage` row, raises the truncation cap 100→2000 (generous soft bound, no mid-word cut — frontend already wraps/scrolls), and surfaces `isPeerMessage`/`fromConv`/`isPeerHuman` so the client can attribute the source. The FRAMED `text` is untouched — the receiving AGENT still gets full provenance on dispatch.
- **Fix (frontend).** New single seam `convTitleById(cid)` in core/conversations.js: id → title, matching full id then unique-PREFIX (an 8-char display id still resolves against the loaded `conversations` list), falling back to a localized "Untitled chat" — NEVER a bare id; window-exposed. `_refreshServerQueue` carries the new fields; `renderPendingQueueUI` renders a clickable "from «title»" source line (chat-bubble SVG per §3.4, jumps to source on click) above the (now full) message text for peer turns. `_renderPeerDelivery` resolves `toConv` → title (id kept in the `title=` tooltip). i18n: `queue.fromConv` / `queue.fromOperator` (zh/en).
- **CSS-hold-aware.** static/styles.css is under a sibling edit-hold (folder-rail redesign), so the new source line + `.queue-item-body` flex-column wrapper are INLINE-styled on the elements (mirrors the existing DB-banner / recover-button inline pattern), touching zero held files.
- **Verification.** `test_message_queue` 5 + `test_project_peer` 26 + `test_project_peer_human_nudge` 7 (incl. all peer-marker/human-nudge/NC anchors) = 38 pass; `test_frontend_brain_tool_render` 11 (delivery card `peermsg_target` still passes — the jsdom stub lacks `convTitleById` so it falls back to `conv cdef1234`, which still contains the id) + `test_frontend_peer_header_identity` 1 = 12 pass. `node --check` clean on all 4 JS files; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-51a33d40.js` (11 hits for the new symbols/keys). Backend-behaviour + display only.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart (import-time bundler) + hard browser refresh (content-hashed bundle) needed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a peer/coordination surface stores a MODEL-FACING framed string (provenance wrapper + short id) but a HUMAN surface needs the clean original, carry BOTH — a separate `_peerText` — rather than trying to un-frame the wrapped body in the UI or truncating it. A conversation id is never a user-facing label: route every id→title through ONE resolver (`convTitleById`) that resolves by unique prefix (short display ids) and falls back to a localized "Untitled", never a bare id. And a preview cap that predates a framing wrapper will silently eat the real content — size the cap to the un-framed text.


### 2026-07-07 — Poor-signal send hardening: a measure-first swarm audit of the lost-ACK path found the rev/CAS epic had left 5 real "message displays abnormally on bad network" defects; all fixed + neuter-gated. Root fix: server preserves the client `_msgId`; rebase drops the stale error bubble; the residual wall-clock tiebreaker is finally removed.
- **Why re-open.** Owner pushed: "I don't want a message sent on poor signal to display abnormally or ruin a conversation." The rev/CAS epic fixed the STATE/persist layer but I had NOT audited the SEND pipeline to the same depth. Three parallel `coder` sub-agents audited (a) backend `_msgId` persistence, (b) residual reconcile heuristics, (c) pending-sync/offline-recovery edges. They converged on 5 genuine bugs — the "victory" was premature.
- **The LOST-ACK class (the owner's exact fear).** On poor signal the send `fetch` frequently SUCCEEDS server-side (user turn + real assistant reply persisted, `rev` bumped) but the RESPONSE is lost → the client thinks it failed, appends an error-only assistant bubble, marks pending-sync, later rescue-PUTs → CAS 409 → `_rebaseUnackedTail`. Two abnormal displays fell out of this:
  1. **DUPLICATE user bubble.** `build_user_msg_from_payload` (lib/chat/turn_builder.py:342) built the user msg field-by-field and NEVER copied the client `_msgId`; `_assign_message_ids` (manager.py:378) then minted a fresh server UUID. So server `_msgId` ≠ client `_msgId` → the rebase (keyed on `_msgId`) didn't recognise the server's copy and appended the client's as a second user row. **Fix:** ship the client `_msgId` on the send payload (main_send_pipeline.js — mint via `_newClientMsgId()` into `msgPayload` + reuse for the optimistic `userMsg`) and carry it through in `build_user_msg_from_payload` (only when present; `_assign_message_ids` fills MISSING ids so it's preserved). Now server + client agree on ONE turn identity.
  2. **ERROR bubble coexisting with the real answer.** Hardened `_rebaseUnackedTail` (conversations.js): a local ERROR-ONLY assistant (`_isErrorOnlyAssistant`: error set, no content/thinking/toolRounds/ig) is DROPPED when the server already carries a real trailing assistant reply for the turn. If the server did NOT answer (genuine failure) the error bubble is KEPT. Also added a defensive (role=user, timestamp) dedup fallback — the backend's own idempotency key (`append_user_msg_idempotent`) — so an old-bundle client whose `_msgId` diverged still can't duplicate a user turn.
- **The residual wall-clock tiebreaker (wrong-data-on-reconnect root, thought-fixed but wasn't).** `conversations.js` `localHasUnsynced` STILL had a third disjunct `hasLocalData && !cacheHit && localNewest > serverNewest` — a pure timestamp compare that let a stale IDB/in-memory copy win KEEP_LOCAL and get PUT back over fresh server truth. And CAS did NOT save it (rev adopted at :data.rev → the stale re-PUT carried a MATCHING baseRev). **Fix:** removed the disjunct entirely; KEEP_LOCAL now fires ONLY on genuine un-acked signals (`_hasFreshLocalActivity` || `_localHasPendingSync`). Freshness is decided by the monotonic `rev`, never by clocks.
- **Two `_serverRev` non-adoption paths** (prefetch combo-load block + `forceRecoverFromServer`): both applied server messages but never adopted `data.rev`/`prefetchedConv.rev`, so the conv's first PUT sent no baseRev (fail-open, no CAS). **Fix:** adopt `rev` in both (also changed the prefetch `_serverMsgCount` from `Math.max(server,local)` to `serverMsgs.length`, dropping the last longest-wins bookkeeping on that path).
- **Tests (all green WITH neuters).** NEW `tests/test_frontend_lost_ack_poor_network.py` (drives real `_rebaseUnackedTail`: no-dup user + error-bubble-dropped + ts-fallback dedup + genuine-append-kept + error-KEPT-when-no-server-reply; neuter: force `_isErrorOnlyAssistant`→false → error bubble no longer dropped). NEW backend assertion in `tests/test_chat_send_idempotency.py::test_build_user_msg_preserves_client_msgId`. Regression: rev-rebase + cross-tab + allowtruncate + send-failure-persists + reconcile-equivalence + api-isolation = 23 pytest green; backend CAS + rev-monotonic standalone green with neuters. Bundle → `bundle-51a33d40.js` (`_isErrorOnlyAssistant`×3, `_newClientMsgId` shipped, `localNewest > serverNewest` count = 0). ruff clean. NOT committed. Server restart + hard refresh needed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A CAS + rebase that dedups on `_msgId` is only correct if the server PRESERVES the client's `_msgId` — verify the id survives the whole send→persist path, don't assume. On a lossy network the dangerous failure is the LOST-ACK (send succeeded, response dropped), not "never arrived": design the rescue/rebase for "the server may already have this turn AND answered it." And when you claim a heuristic was "replaced," grep the actual disjunction — the wall-clock tiebreaker survived as a third OR-term long after rev landed. Measure-first swarm audit before declaring an objective done paid off: 5 real bugs, zero of them hypothetical.


### 2026-07-07 — Project-rail CLS hole closed at the root: pre-paint `html[data-rail]` width hint (theme-no-FOUC pattern) so the sidebar paints at steady-state width BEFORE the async folders round-trip — zero layout shift. Neuter-gated.
- **Gap (owner caught it).** The rail widens the sidebar 280px → `calc(rail + list-min)`, but `.has-rail` was added only by the async `_renderFolderTabsInner` AFTER `loadFolders()` resolved → every ≥1-folder user saw the sidebar jump wider on each load, animated by `transition:width`, pushing the chat column sideways. Contradicted the zero-CLS bar.
- **Fix (root, mirrors the theme no-FOUC script).** `index.html` `<head>` inline IIFE reads a persisted `tofu_has_folders` hint and stamps `html[data-rail="full"|"collapsed"]` BEFORE first paint. CSS `html[data-rail="full"] .sidebar` / `[collapsed]` give the correct width immediately — byte-identical to the `.sidebar.has-rail` rules, so when the async render later adds `.has-rail` the computed width doesn't change → the transition never fires → no shift. The render reconciles CONTENT only. New/zero-folder users (no hint) paint single-column, unchanged.
- **Sync path.** `_persistRailHint(hasRail)` (conversation_list.js) writes/removes the localStorage hint AND toggles `html[data-rail]`, called in BOTH render branches (so a first-folder-created appears, and the rare zero-folder correction after a fresh install clears it). `_toggleProjectRail` (main_folders_mobile.js) updates `data-rail` full↔collapsed on toggle so the next load matches the collapsed choice. Mobile drawer blocks extended to also reset `html[data-rail] .sidebar` width (JS hasn't added `.has-rail` at first paint, so the hint alone must not widen the fixed 82vw/360px drawer).
- **Gate — `tests/test_frontend_rail_cls.py` NEW, 3 tests GREEN.** (1) CSS: `html[data-rail=full/collapsed] .sidebar` width == `.sidebar.has-rail[.rail-collapsed]` width (byte-identical → no shift), pure-Python regex, no node. (2) jsdom: running ONLY the EXTRACTED index.html inline IIFE (bare `localStorage`/`document` bound as node globals + indirect eval — a swallowed ReferenceError would silently no-op, so the binding is what makes it real) with the hint set stamps `data-rail` while `#folderTabs` is STILL EMPTY (order proof: width settled before renderFolderTabs could run); no-hint → no stamp; `_persistRailHint(true/false)` from the REAL source sets/clears both key + attribute. (3) NEUTER: strip the `setAttribute('data-rail',…)` from the extracted script → pre-paint stamps FAIL, no-hint + runtime-sync still PASS. Sweep: rail-CLS 3 + project-rail 4 + longpress 5 + conv-list-collapse 1 + breakpoint 8 = **21 passed**.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean; JS bundle `bundle-954e4c24.js` + CSS `styles-8388b35a.css` rebuilt (data-rail/tofu_has_folders/_persistRailHint markers present). NOT committed (owner attribution). Restart + hard refresh needed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any width/geometry a user's persisted state implies must be applied at FIRST PAINT via a pre-paint `<head>` hint (the theme-no-FOUC pattern), not by async JS after a round-trip — otherwise it's guaranteed CLS. Make the pre-paint rule byte-identical to the JS-applied steady-state rule so the later class-add is a no-op (no transition). Test the pre-paint stamp by extracting and running the SHIPPED inline script in isolation and asserting the attribute lands while the render target is still empty (proves ORDER), then neuter the setAttribute to prove it's load-bearing.


### 2026-07-07 — Segment-timeline 5a LAST MILE: renderMessage-level gate test proves flipping the toggle actually changes the render (interleave ON vs grouped OFF, no duplicate thinking) + NC
- **The remaining seam.** Prior tests proved renderSegmentTimelineHTML interleaves (called DIRECTLY) and the GET route DELIVERS segments — but nothing exercised the DECISION inside the render entry point: the `!isUser && !_vuPrivate && _segTimelineEnabled() && msg.segments.length>0` gate AND the `_segTimelineRendered` suppression of the duplicate standalone `msg.thinking` block. A wrong condition or double-rendered thinking would leave every test green while the owner-visible output was wrong.

Asserts — FLAG ON (`config.segmentTimeline=true`): `seg-timeline` panel emitted + batch narration present + ZERO legacy `_toggleThinking` standalone thinking blocks (suppression fired) + per-batch `this.classList.toggle('expanded')` thinking present. FLAG OFF: NO seg-timeline, legacy `ptool-panel` present, standalone thinking block present (count==1). NC: force `_segTimelineEnabled` → false (in tool_rounds.js, where it lives) → even with segments + config ON the timeline branch does NOT fire → falls back to grouped + standalone thinking (proves the gate call is load-bearing). 13 internal PASS checks.
- **jsdom harness traps hit + fixed (per the extraction memory).** (1) tool_rounds.js registers a top-level `document.addEventListener` at load → node eval needs a `document` stub (added no-op document). (2) renderMessage calls collaborators from OTHER modules not eval'd here → stub as no-ops: `getToolRoundsFromMsg` (return msg.toolRounds — REAL renderSegmentTimelineHTML + legacy renderToolRoundsHTML both need it), `renderFinishInfo`, `_TOFU_*_SVG`, `calcCostCny`, provenance/branch/error renderers. Did NOT stub renderSegmentTimelineHTML/renderToolRoundsHTML — those are the REAL fns under test.
- **Verification.** New test green (13 PASS). Full frontend segment suite 11 (rendermessage-gate + segment_timeline 5 + segments_not_echoed 5). Regression on sibling harnesses that eval the same files (peer_header_identity, autopilot_fold, translate_preview_survives_rebuild, finishstream_no_put) = 4 green — no stub-breakage introduced. NOT committed.
- **Objective status.** The static/DB path is now proven end-to-end: server DELIVERS segments (GET-route test) → renderMessage GATE flips on the owner-facing toggle (this test) → renderSegmentTimelineHTML INTERLEAVES (direct test). Flipping the Settings toggle genuinely changes what the owner sees. 5b (live-streaming mid-turn interleave) stays parked pending the owner's architecture decision.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** To prove a flag "actually changes what I see", drive the REAL render ENTRY POINT (renderMessage), not just the leaf helper — the gate condition + the sibling-suppression (no duplicate thinking) live in the entry point and no helper test covers them. Assert BOTH the ON output (feature present + duplicate suppressed) AND the OFF control (legacy present + duplicate back), plus an NC on the gate. jsdom-eval of a hot-path render file needs a `document` stub (top-level addEventListener) + no-op stubs for every cross-module collaborator it reaches — but NEVER stub the functions under test.

- **Guardrail / lesson.** When replacing a horizontal wrapping pill bar with a vertical rail, KEEP the row DOM contract (`.folder-tab[data-folder-id]` + inner dot/name) identical so every delegated handler + existing test survives — change only the container markup + CSS. Derive the two-pane width from CSS vars (`rail + list-min`), never a magic number. A drawer viewport must reset any derived desktop width or it leaks into the fixed drawer. And a "green" sibling test that can't actually run (missing viewport stub) is a latent trap — stub the load-time IIFE deps so the harness exercises the real code.

### 2026-07-07 — Lower-right background toasts made CONVERSATION-AWARE + ACTIONABLE: external-edit & workspace-root events now name their SOURCE conversation (clickable → jump) and carry a "what/why/what-to-do" hint. Bilingual, SVG-only, neuter-gated jsdom test.
- **Ask (owner).** The lower-right toast must say WHICH conversation triggered it and push VALUABLE info — e.g. for external file-change discovery: when it pops, what CAN the user do and what SHOULD they do?
- **Root cause of the poverty.** Two background SSE events surface as toasts from `static/js/ui/sse_handlers_misc.js`: `project_external_edit` (IDE/other-tool edits to tracked files, auto-snapshotted into file-history) and `workspace_root_added` (an assistant write outside all roots auto-registered a new root). Both fire from a SPECIFIC task's stream — often a BACKGROUND conv, not the one on screen — yet the old toasts were English-only, emoji-prefixed (`📝 Captured N external edit(s) — a.py, b.py`), named NO source conversation, and offered NO next step. `c.convId` was in hand the whole time but unused.
- **Fix 1 — `showToast` gained an opts seam (core/toast.js).** New optional 5th arg `opts={convId, convTitle, hint, onClick}`: renders a clickable "from «title»" source badge (chat-bubble SVG) + a quieter guidance `hint` line under the detail; a navigable toast (has convId+loadConversation, or an onClick) gets `.toast-clickable` and jumps to the source conv on body/badge click (Enter/Space on the badge too), with the close button exempted (`stopPropagation`). All opts fields escaped via escapeHtml. Passing no opts is byte-identical to before. GOTCHA fixed mid-build: an earlier draft aliased the toast element to `const t`, which BOTH hit TDZ on `typeof t` AND shadowed the global i18n `t()` — renamed the element to `el` throughout so `t()` stays reachable.
- **Fix 2 — both handlers rewritten.** `_handleProjectExternalEdit`: full-form `showToast('', title, detail, 7000, {convId, convTitle:_toastConvTitle(convId), hint})` — title `Captured N external file change(s)`, detail `files · snapshot <sha7>`, hint explains the edits were auto-saved to file history + revertible + click-to-open-source. NOTE: passing `'info'` as arg2 would trip the SIMPLE-form detection (`'info' in _toastTypes`) and drop detail/opts — used empty icon + neutral title so type infers to `info`. `_handleWorkspaceRootAdded`: same treatment; hint explains the assistant wrote outside known roots so a root was auto-registered, and to revert + adjust scope if unwanted. New `_toastConvTitle(convId)` helper resolves title from `conversations` with an `Untitled chat` fallback.
- **i18n (zh/en parity).** `toast.fromConv`, `toast.untitledConv`, `externalEdit.title/detail/moreN/hint`, `workspaceRoot.hint`. `externalEdit.title` uses the `{s}` plural convention (handler passes `s: n>1?'s':''`, mirroring `fileChanges.filesChanged`).
- **CSS.** `.toast-conv-src` (accent-tinted pill, ellipsised title, role=button + :focus-visible outline), `.toast-hint` (top-bordered tertiary guidance line), `.toast-clickable` cursor. SVG-only (§3.4).
- **Gate — `tests/test_frontend_toast_conv_source.py` NEW, 1 test / 24 checks, PASS.** jsdom loads the REAL escape_html+i18n+toast+sse_handlers_misc, drives both handlers, asserts: source badge names the bg conv, hint present, files+sha shown, no emoji leak, body-click navigates to the SOURCE conv, close-button does NOT navigate, unknown-conv fallback title, plain simple-form toast unaffected. **NEUTER**: reassigning the LEXICAL `showToast` binding (not just the global prop — direct-eval scope) to a pre-fix version that ignores opts makes badge+hint vanish and the toast non-navigable → proves opts is load-bearing. Harness needed `global.localStorage` (i18n.js reads it at load). Regression: test_frontend_sse_dispatch + test_frontend_delete_conv_undo = 3 passed; ruff clean.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-18f91682.js` (11 hits for the new symbols/keys). Server restart + hard refresh needed (import-time bundler + content-hashed filename). Frontend-only.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `showToast(msg, 'info')` is the SIMPLE form — to attach detail/opts you MUST use the full form with a non-type arg2 (empty icon works, type infers from title). When neutering a handler's dependency in a direct-eval jsdom harness, reassign the BARE identifier, not `global.X` — the handler closed over the lexical binding. A background toast is only useful if it names its source and says what to do; `c.convId` from the SSE ctx is that source.


### 2026-07-07 — Resolved the KNOWN-DEFECT epic: `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` `report_generated_in_zh/en` failures were a STALE TEST, not a code bug — the two checks asserted a superseded auto-generate-on-language-switch contract that the no-autostart preference deliberately removed. Rewrote them to pin the current contract, neuter-verified.
- **Dispatched to** the pre-existing-failure epic I'd logged during the reader-UX work. Investigated root cause before touching anything (owner's measure-first discipline).
- **Root cause (definitive).** `_setReportLang(lang,'report')` for a NEVER-SHOWN language routes through `_loadOrGenerateReport` → step (4), which (per user preference 2026-07-02) renders a MANUAL Generate prompt and issues ZERO `/report/start` — so the user can tune model/generation-language/venue before the billed run. The two failing checks (`report_generated_in_zh`/`report_generated_in_en`) asserted the OLD behavior — that a language switch auto-issues `reportStart` with the new lang — and the test's own docstring said it "kicks a load/generate in the new language." That contract was superseded and is now guarded by `test_frontend_paper_no_autostart.py` (which even has a source-level negative control reverting step 4 to `_generatePaperReport(false,view)`). The lang-toggle test simply wasn't updated when no-autostart landed. Confirmed the current preference in the USER PREFERENCE PROFILE too ("never auto-generate on tab open").
- **Why fix the TEST, not the code.** Making the code satisfy the stale checks (auto-start on switch) would re-break the no-autostart guarantee — a regression, not a fix. The code is correct; the test's expectation is stale.
- **Fix.** Replaced the 2 stale checks with `report_switch_{zh,en}_no_autostart` (switch fires zero `reportStart`) + `report_switch_{zh,en}_shows_generate_btn` (the `.paper-report-generate-btn` manual prompt is rendered — `_renderReportStartPrompt` is NOT stubbed in the harness, so this exercises the real seam). Updated the docstring's REPORT + negative-control bullets. Kept ALL still-valid assertions unchanged (persist-per-paper, reload-reads-zh, the snapshot repaint-no-regen regression, and the entire review translate path). 20/20 checks now pass (was 18 with 2 failing).
- **Neuter-verified load-bearing.** Reverting step 4 to `_generatePaperReport(false,view)` in a COPY flips all four new checks to FAIL (`node --check` clean, shipped file byte-identical after) — proving they pin the no-autostart contract, not a tautology. Mirrors the negative control in `test_frontend_paper_no_autostart.py`.
- **Verification.** Full paper frontend suite (lang-toggle + no-autostart + reader-prefs + reading-anchor + mobile-responsive) = 9 passed. NO production code changed → no bundle rebuild needed. `paper-reader.js` untouched. Test-only diff.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a jsdom behavior test fails on a green codebase, first ask whether the TEST encodes a superseded contract — grep for a sibling test that asserts the OPPOSITE (here `test_frontend_paper_no_autostart.py` proved the new behavior was intentional + guarded). A test that stubs the render fn (`_renderFinalReport`) but asserts on a call-spy (`reportStart`) is testing the CONTROL FLOW, so a control-flow policy change (auto-start → manual prompt) silently invalidates it. Fix the stale expectation and re-prove load-bearing via the same step-4 neuter the canonical guard uses — don't bend the code back to satisfy an obsolete test.


### 2026-07-07 — Root-caused the "frontend rendering flicker / wrong-data-on-reconnect" class: made the SERVER authoritative for conversation history via a monotonic per-conv `rev` + compare-and-swap PUT, retired the frontend guess-and-truncate ghost sweep, demoted IndexedDB to a pure paint-cache. 6/6 objective criteria, all neuter-gated.
- **The felt problem (owner).** Tofu flickered and showed stale/wrong data on bad-network reconnect where ChatGPT/Claude don't. Root cause was architectural, not cosmetic: the browser was a **writer-of-record** for message history (client PUTs the whole conv back, `allowTruncate` can shorten it, JS ghost-classifiers splice/truncate persisted history on a guess), and the reconcile winner was chosen by **wall-clock timestamp** (`conversations.js` `localNewest > serverNewest` + `_serverMsgCount = Math.max(...)`) — so a stale IDB/optimistic copy with a newer ts could beat fresh server truth and get PUT back, re-clobbering the server. Four competing sources of truth (server DB, in-memory, IndexedDB, settings mirror) negotiated on every load.
- **Phase (a) — retire frontend guess-and-truncate.** The backend GET-path reconcile was already live (`routes/conversations.py::_reconcile_conv_on_get_blocking` → `lib/conversations/reconcile.py`, persists in the same commit, stamps `_reconciledAt`). Deleted ONLY the inference-driven Case-D buried-ghost sweep + its two `allowTruncate:true` PUTs in `main_init_tasks.js` (kept the user-initiated `allowTruncate` in regen/edit, and the non-destructive interrupt stamp). Gated the deletion on `tests/test_reconcile_js_backend_equivalence.py`: a 15-fixture shared corpus fed to BOTH backend `reconcile_conversation_messages(…,0)` and the real JS `_sweepBuriedGhostAssistants`+`_classifyGhostTail` under node, asserting identical applied survivors+finishReason+changed, + two neuters (drop special-turn guard; collapse interrupt→delete) + a documented prefix-gated divergence + a documented whitespace-thinking divergence.
- **Phase (b/i) — server-issued monotonic `rev` (schema v36→v37).** New `conversations.rev INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, bumped by a **DB trigger** (`conversations_rev_bump_trg`: PG `BEFORE UPDATE OF messages` sets NEW.rev on `messages IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.messages`; SQLite `AFTER UPDATE OF messages` nested rev-only UPDATE, non-recursive via `OF messages`). Chose a trigger over per-writer `rev = rev+1` because there are 11+ heterogeneous message writers (5 via `upsert`, 6 raw UPDATE) — a trigger fires in the same statement as every writer, is impossible to forget, and the `IS DISTINCT FROM` guard means settings/title-only writes never bump (no false CAS-409). GET returns `rev` via a tolerant `_row_rev()`. `tests/test_conv_rev_monotonic.py`: rev bumps by exactly 1 on raw-UPDATE + upsert message writers (monotonic), NOT on no-op/settings-only/title-only writes; neuter drops the trigger on a fresh DB → messages UPDATE leaves rev=0.
- **Phase (ii) — compare-and-swap PUT.** `save_conv` accepts a message write only if `baseRev == current rev`, else 409 `{error:'blocked_rev_conflict', serverRev}`. **Fail-open** (non-negotiable): absent `baseRev` (old bundle / compat / headless) falls through to the legacy `blocked_msg_regression` guard — a v36-era client against a rev=0 row never eats 409s. CAS scoped to message-bearing writes (settings/title-only never assert). Success returns the post-write `rev`. `tests/test_conv_cas_put.py`: conflict→409, fail-open + neuter (absent baseRev→200 vs coerced-0→409 proves the `is not None` skip is load-bearing), metadata-scope.
- **Phase (#1) — frontend rebase-on-409 through the EXISTING pending-sync path.** `syncConversationToServer` sends `baseRev` from `conv._serverRev`, adopts `resp.rev` on success (so a double-sync carries a fresh base), and on `blocked_rev_conflict` GETs the server row → `_rebaseUnackedTail` (append-missing-tail keyed on `_msgId`, preserving ids verbatim so no spurious rev bump) → adopts fresh rev → re-PUTs via the SAME path (recursive call, depth-bounded ≤3). Append-missing-tail (not full merge) because CAS only catches concurrent APPENDS — edits/regens bypass CAS via the `allowTruncate` user-action path. `tests/test_frontend_rev_rebase_on_conflict.py`: stateful CAS server, asserts final server state contains BOTH server + client-un-acked messages; blind-re-PUT neuter loses the server message.
- **Phase (iii) — cross-tab.** Traced `cross_tab_sync.js`: it has NO message-history PUT of its own — handlers PULL (`loadConversationsFromServer`) or local read-adopt (`_recoverOfflineConversations`); the SOLE server writer is `syncConversationToServer`. So cross-tab inherits CAS+rebase for free. `tests/test_frontend_cross_tab_rev_guard.py`: two in-memory tabs share one server stub; Tab B's stale-rev write does NOT clobber Tab A's message (409→rebase, both survive); neuter (blind re-PUT) restores the clobber. IDB demotion confirmed by grep: `_serverRev` is written in exactly 4 places, ALL from the server (PUT resp, 409 GET, Phase-2 GET); the IDB `conv_meta` field set `{id,title,updatedAt,cachedAt,settings,msgOrder,msgCount}` has NO rev → a cache-hit conv can't supply a base, and Phase-2 always runs to set it from the server. IndexedDB can no longer win a reconcile.
- **Verification.** 71 pytest (frontend+reconcile+CAS+schema parity) + 3 DB-backed standalone suites (`test_conv_cas_put`, `test_conv_rev_monotonic`, `test_get_path_reconcile`) all green WITH their neuters; live PG migrated (rev column + trigger present); bundle rebuilt. `test_chat_manager_migration.py`'s 4 pytest "failures" are the KNOWN standalone-runner DB-bootstrap artifact (all 21 pass via its `main()`), NOT a regression — confirmed by running the standalone runner. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard browser refresh needed (schema is import-time; bundle content-hash changed).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When the client is a writer-of-record with a wall-clock reconcile tiebreaker, "server is source of truth" is a comment, not a fact. The structural fix is a server-issued monotonic version + compare-and-swap, with fail-open on absent version so the rollout is byte-safe for old clients. Bump the version via a DB trigger (not per-writer code) so a 12th writer can't forget it, and scope it to genuine content changes so metadata writes don't false-conflict. Rebase on conflict through the EXISTING durable-retry path (never a blind retry, never a parallel mechanism), and preserve `_msgId` verbatim during the merge or the next write spuriously bumps rev.


### 2026-07-07 — Paper "describe-to-recommend" made AGENTIC: replaced the memory-guess interpretation with a real web_search/fetch_url research loop (date-anchored), so it surfaces genuinely current papers instead of hallucinating a "conference hasn't happened yet" correction
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** Describe box "icml26 扩散语言模型的最佳论文" returned a confident **false** correction banner ("ICML 2026 hasn't happened, so there's no best paper") + only older papers. But today is 2026-07-07 and ICML 2026 is literally in progress (Jul 6–11, Seoul — icml.cc/Conferences/2026), and recent 2026 diffusion-LM papers exist. Owner: "did this fuzzy match not call any external tools?"
- **Root cause (diagnosed first, then fixed).** `lib/paper/recommend_engine.py` used ONE `dispatch_chat` call with NO tools and NO current-date anchor: the model guessed candidate titles from frozen training memory, and arXiv was used ONLY to GROUND (verify) those guesses — never to DISCOVER current work. So (1) anything posted after the model's cutoff was structurally invisible, and (2) with no "today" in the prompt the model treated an in-progress year as the future and manufactured the false correction. Grounding was correct; the *interpretation* was blind.
- **Fix — agentic interpretation.** New `_research_and_interpret()` seam runs the SHARED `run_agent_loop` (lib/agent_loop.py) with `_REPORT_TOOLS` (web_search + fetch_url via `_execute_report_tool`, same as the report/QA engines) and a **date-anchored** system prompt (`date_anchor_clause(ui_lang) + _RECOMMEND_SYSTEM`, reused from prompts.py). The model must research the live literature (search arXiv/web, open hits, verify any venue/award claim) BEFORE returning its final strict-JSON candidates/correction. `_MAX_RECOMMEND_TOOL_ROUNDS=5`. The **grounding gate is UNCHANGED** — no card surfaces unless its arXiv id resolves via `search_arxiv`/`fetch_arxiv_title` (still the anti-hallucination guarantee). Interim-draft discard on tool rounds so scaffolding prose never pollutes the JSON parse (report-engine pattern). `iter_recommend_events` + blocking `recommend_papers` wrapper keep their exact streaming/aggregate contract; new optional `on_tool_event` callback forwards research `tool_start`/`tool_done` events.
- **Streaming UX.** `recommend_task.py` forwards `on_tool_event` into the append-only task event log; frontend `_applyRecommendEvent` handles `tool_start` → `researchCount`/`researchLabel`, and the status line shows `paper.recommendResearching` ("正在检索最新文献（第 N 次搜索）… <query>") before interpretation lands, then the existing grounding progress. New i18n key (zh/en). `.paper-rec-research-q` styled inline (styles.css was under a sibling hold).
- **Tests.** Repointed the two existing suites from faking `dispatch_chat` to faking `dispatch_stream` (final JSON in one no-tool round) so they drive the REAL agentic loop + grounding offline — `test_paper_recommend_grounding.py` 10/10 (incl. its double-neuter on the grounding gate), `test_paper_recommend_stream.py` 5/5 (fixed the neuter's `_non_streaming_iter` to accept `on_tool_event`). NEW `test_paper_recommend_agentic.py` 4/4: proves the loop actually EXECUTES the model's web_search call before proposing candidates, the system prompt is date-anchored, tool events are forwarded, + a NEUTER (break the loop → round-0 answers immediately → research tool NEVER runs). `test_agent_loop.py` 11/11 + `test_frontend_recommend_stream_render.py` 3/3 still green. ruff + `node --check` clean.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (import-time). Bundles rebuilt: core `bundle-8a862231.js` (i18n) + feature `feature-133a319e.js` (paper-reader `researchCount`).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "verify against a real source" step (grounding) is NOT the same as a "discover current facts" step — grounding a memory-guess can only confirm/reject what the model already knew, never surface what it doesn't. Any feature that must know about *current* events needs a real tool-using research loop AND a current-date anchor in its prompt (the report/QA engines already had both via `date_anchor_clause` + `_REPORT_TOOLS`; recommend was the odd one out). Reuse the shared `run_agent_loop` + `_execute_report_tool` seams rather than hand-rolling a second loop.


### 2026-07-07 — "Failed to fetch" jargon → actionable recovery UX, scoped by RECOVERABILITY not by coarse "connection-class". server_offline gets a friendly truthful title + hint + inline Recover button (reuses the existing offline-recovery path); network/premature_close/abnormal_stop deliberately do NOT
- **Symptom (owner).** A long opus-4.8 turn behind a VS Code port-forward tunnel dropped the SSE/HTTP link (tunnel idle-timeout); the assistant bubble ended on a red **"Network error / Failed to fetch"** with `hint:''` — pure jargon, no guidance, no recovery affordance. The server had actually FINISHED (persisted conv body grew 555KB→1.0MB across GETs); the frontend just gave up on the connection.
- **The load-bearing scoping subtlety (owner caught it; I'd have shipped a lie).** My first instinct — "network + server_offline are the same connection class, give both the Recover button" — was WRONG. `_recoverOfflineConversations('manual_button')` (cross_tab_sync.js) only recovers convs whose TAIL `finishReason==='server_offline'`/`'interrupted'`. The `network` envelope is stamped at `context:'chat-start'` (main_send_pipeline.js) when the POST that STARTS the turn fails → **no task ever ran server-side**, finishReason is never `server_offline`, so a Recover button there scans, finds nothing, no-ops — while telling the user "your result may be saved". That is the exact false-hope I'd (correctly) rejected for `premature_close`. So the button + "result may be saved" copy is scoped to **`server_offline` ALONE**. Confirmed by two project memories (vscode-disconnect-recovery + connection-failure-display-accuracy).
- **Kind taxonomy (the honest per-kind advice).** `server_offline` = task WAS running, may have finished → friendly copy + Recover (adopt server copy, NOT regen). `network` = chat-start POST failed, nothing ran → honest "couldn't reach the server, check connection then Retry", NO button. `premature_close`/`abnormal_stop` = UPSTREAM server↔gateway failures emitted only after server-side retries exhausted (stream_handler.py:432, turn_retry.py:67) → no saved result, keep existing Retry hint. Left the last two untouched.
- **What shipped (4 core-bundle files).** (1) `core/error_envelope.js`: `_envIsRecoverable(env)` (`env.kind==='server_offline'`) + `_envT()` guard; `renderErrorEnvelope` overrides the "Server offline" jargon label with `t('err.conn.title')`, swaps the (often empty) hint for `t('err.conn.hint')`, and appends an inline Recover button (`Icon('refresh',12)` SVG per §3.4, `onclick="_recoverOfflineConversations('manual_button')"`) — ONLY for the recoverable kind; every other kind renders byte-identical. (2) `main_send_pipeline.js`: the `network` stamp's `hint:''` → `t('err.net.hint')` (honest Retry guidance, still no button). (3) `health_stream_timer.js` `_forceFinishDeadStream`: the `server_offline` stamp's `hint:''` → `t('err.conn.hint')` so guidance never depends on which path stamped it. (4) `i18n.js`: reused the `err.conn.*` keys a live sibling (mrahis0u) had already landed; added `err.net.hint` (zh/en); fixed the misleading comment that grouped `premature_close` into the connection-class block.
- **CSS-hold-aware.** `static/styles.css` was under an active sibling hold (folder-rail redesign) — so the Recover button is INLINE-styled on the element (like the existing DB banner / force-finish affordances), touching zero held files.
- **Coordination.** This exact feature was in-flight in sibling **mrahis0u** ("前端中断对话无缝恢复"), which had landed only the i18n keys. Owner verified the board (no hold on my 4 targets) and told me to proceed; I messaged the sibling to split scope (it keeps keys, I took render+stamp+test) + flagged the premature_close mis-grouping.
- **Gate — `tests/test_frontend_conn_error_recover.py` 7/7 (Node extraction-and-eval, real renderErrorEnvelope + real i18n runtime under BOTH zh+en).** server_offline → localized title+hint+button wired to `_recoverOfflineConversations` (both langs); network/premature_close/abnormal_stop → NO button + no `_recoverOfflineConversations` wiring (scoping guard); **poisoned-NC** neutering `_envIsRecoverable`→false makes server_offline revert to the "Server offline" jargon AND drop the button (proves title/hint/button are load-bearing). Regression: i18n-key-coverage 8/8 + api-isolation 4/4 green; `node --check` clean on all 4 files; ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **core `bundle-5b540d97.js`** (+ feature `feature-56277aa2.js`); grep-confirmed it carries `error-block-recover-btn` / `_envIsRecoverable` / `err.conn.title` / `err.net.hint`.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + hard-refresh needed (core bundle content-hash changed).

### 2026-07-07 — Sidebar didn't show crash-interrupted conversations until you clicked in: pure DISPLAY-layer gap — meta path strips messages so the frontend classifier had no data. Fixed by stamping RAW settled-turn facts into settings (3 write points), surfaced to _convStatusFlags's stripped-shell fallback. Verified recovery was already correct; NO parallel convergence added.
- **Symptom (owner).** After the OOM crash, many conversations were interrupted, but the sidebar showed no "未完成" dot — you had to open a conv and wait a beat before it showed incomplete.
- **Two-phase verification FIRST (owner insisted, no blind implement).** (1) `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` DID run this OOM restart (`Marked 71 stale running task(s)`, `Recovered 13 conversation(s)`) and the DB is CORRECT — direct read shows recovered convs carry `finishReason='interrupted'` on their tail (`mraev0ad`/`mrafevic`/`mra3utj4`/`mrafgvdl`), and `mra8gpik` (genuinely completed) correctly kept `stop`, NOT misjudged. So the proposed "startup batch-convergence" was REJECTED as duplicate of the existing recovery. (2) Root cause = pure DISPLAY layer: `_convStatusFlags` (static/js/ui/conversation_list.js) computes the amber/red dot from the tail assistant's `finishReason` in `c.messages`, but the sidebar loads via `?meta=1` → `_conv_row_to_meta_dict` (routes/conversations.py:127) + `refresh_meta_cache_if_stale` (lib/conversations/meta_cache.py:173) BOTH strip `messages`. No messages → the classifier block is skipped → no dot until you open the conv (loads full messages). Unrelated to `chat_poll`'s lazy re-mark.
- **Fix — settings-carried RAW facts, NOT a new column (owner-ratified).** `settings` already flows through both meta payload paths (zero schema migration) and has the `lastMsgRole` precedent. Backend stamps THREE raw facts (never the `incomplete`/`errored` classification — that stays frontend-side so there's ONE classifier): `settings.lastFinishReason` (str|null), `lastMsgError` (bool), `lastMsgHasOutput` (bool = content|thinking|toolRounds|_igResults). Written at ALL THREE settle points, each folded into that point's EXISTING settings-merge (no new SELECT→mutate→UPDATE that would clobber, per the settings-store convention): (1) `persist_conv_messages` (lib/chat/persistence.py, the `lastMsgRole` block); (2) `_sync_result_to_conversation` (lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py, the settings-merge block ~L1409); (3) `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` (manager.py — derived from the FINAL merged tail after `finishReason='interrupted'` is stamped, folded into the SAME atomic multi-column UPDATE, keeping the settings-store multi-col-atomic exception intact). Frontend: `_applySettingsToConv` (static/js/core/conversations.js) surfaces the 3 fields onto the conv; `_convStatusFlags` gains an `else if (!streaming && !c.messages && c.lastMsgRole==='assistant')` fallback running the SAME `_FINISH_ERR`/`_FINISH_NORMAL` classifier. Honest scope: `awaiting_human` + autopilot-concluded downgrades still need full messages (not in meta) → precise only after open; not a regression (pre-open showed nothing).
- **Edge covered.** The `mra8htdw`-class dangling placeholder (tail `finishReason=None`, content/thinking empty) → `lastMsgHasOutput=False` → fallback classifies `incomplete` (matches the frontend's existing "no finishReason + no output" branch).
- **Gate — all green, both neuters bite.** Backend `tests/test_sidebar_settled_facts.py` 5/5 (drives the REAL 3 write points against the session DB; asserts facts stamped; `stop` not misjudged; empty-placeholder hasOutput=False; **NEUTER** proving recover's stamp is load-bearing — facts absent pre-recover, filled post). Frontend `tests/test_frontend_sidebar_settled_facts.py` 2/2 (jsdom extract-and-eval of the REAL `_convStatusFlags`; 6 shell cases incl. interrupted→incomplete, error→errored, stop→clean, empty→incomplete, user-tail→clean; **NEUTER** deleting the fallback branch → interrupted shell goes `incomplete===false`). ruff clean on both lib files + both tests; `node --check` clean on both JS files.
- **Two test failures ruled NOT-mine.** `test_active_task_id_settings_only_write` failed once with an ImportError for `set_conversation_settings` then PASSED on retry — TRANSIENT, a sibling session has a ~15k-line uncommitted JS+lib diff in flight (also breaks the full JS bundle build — pre-existing, reproduced with my 2 JS files reverted to HEAD). `test_committed_msg_equals_db_tail` fails because `_committedMsg` does not exist in `manager.py` even on committed HEAD (`git show HEAD:…|grep -c` = 0) — that feature isn't in this tree; my diff is purely additive (only the 3 new fields). Neither is caused by this change.

Stamp RAW facts, keep the classifier single-sourced on the frontend. Fold the write into each point's existing settings merge — never a fresh read-modify-write (clobbers concurrent settings writers), except the recover path's deliberate multi-column atomic UPDATE. ### 2026-07-07 — Auto-update data-separation follow-up #3: closed the defect I introduced in #2 — `.project_sessions` was RELOCATED but never REGISTERED, so `runtime_layout` (the single-source registry) didn't recognise it + a false docstring claim. Registered `lib/.project_sessions/`, retired the parallel hardcoded `.gitignore` line, updated golden+guards+neuter
- **How it started (owner caught a real defect).** Review of follow-up #2: "`project_sessions_root()`'s docstring asserts `.project_sessions/` is *in `lib.runtime_layout.INSTALL_STATE`* — it is NOT. I dumped the registry: it has only `data/ logs/ uploads/ outputs/ overleaf_cache/ static/js/bundle-`. False claim in a load-bearing comment (violates honest-verdicts), and the consequence is concrete: `is_overlay_skipped('lib/.project_sessions/…/modifications.json')` → False, `is_runtime_state(…)` → False. The path's only update-protection is a HARDCODED `.gitignore` line (`**/.project_sessions/` L114) not derived from `gitignore_lines()` — exactly the drift `runtime_layout` was built to kill." [PROGRESS resolved=4 remaining=1].
- **Verified all three consequences before touching anything** (honest verdict, not a docstring patch): dumped the registry (no `.project_sessions`), ran the two predicates (both False), `gitignore_lines()` (omits it), and `grep -n project_sessions .gitignore` → the orphan hardcoded `**/.project_sessions/` at L114. All confirmed exactly as the owner stated. Root cause: #2 wired the RESOLVER (`project_sessions_root`) + the CONSUMER (`config.SESSIONS_DIR`) but never added the path to the runtime-state REGISTRY — the update-skip / dirty-classify / gitignore-generation authority — so its protection lived only in the parallel hand-maintained ignore line.
- **Fix — register it once, retire the parallel list.** (1) Added `RuntimeEntry('lib/.project_sessions/', 'data', …)` to `INSTALL_STATE` (the real in-tree location — nested under `lib/`, matched anchored by `_matches`'s startswith; the RELOCATED `data/project_sessions` is already covered by the `data/` entry, so registration only ADDED in-tree coverage as the owner required). (2) Replaced the hardcoded `.gitignore` `**/.project_sessions/` with the scoped registry-derived `lib/.project_sessions/` + a comment saying it's registry-derived / don't hand-maintain. (3) Fixed BOTH docstrings (runtime_layout module dir-list + `project_sessions_root`) to be factually accurate.
- **Coherent drift-guard updates (the entry ripples into 3 registry-derived checks by design).** Golden `_GOLDEN_RUNTIME_STATE` += `lib/.project_sessions/` (byte-identity now reflects the intended set). Export drift-guard: `export.py` prunes by path-COMPONENT (`part in ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` over `Path(rel).parts`), and `.project_sessions` (basename) was ALREADY in `ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` — so export functionally excluded it all along; updated the guard to compare on `os.path.basename(prefix)` to mirror how export actually matches a nested registry prefix. Gitignore drift-guard passes unchanged (its `_ignored()` candidate set matches the new scoped line).
- **Gate — 50 passed across the layout family.** `test_runtime_layout.py` 9/9 (golden + classification now cover `lib/.project_sessions/…` AND `data/project_sessions/…`). NEW `ProjectSessionsRegistryTest` in `test_data_layout_separation.py` (4 tests): both predicates recognise the undo store; `gitignore_lines()` emits it; the live `.gitignore` carries the scoped line and NO LONGER the over-broad `**/` glob (proves the parallel list retired); **NEUTER** — drop the registry entry (+ recompute the derived tuples) → both predicates go False AND `gitignore_lines()` drops it → proves the entry is load-bearing, not covered incidentally by another prefix; restore → green. Full family (`test_data_layout_separation` + `test_runtime_layout` + `test_self_update_tarball` + `test_desktop_install_paths`) = 50 passed. ruff clean on all touched files. NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only → restart for the live process.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Relocating a state dir onto a resolved base is only HALF the separation — the path must ALSO be registered in the single runtime-state authority (`runtime_layout.INSTALL_STATE`) so the update-skip / dirty-classify / `.gitignore` generation all recognise it from ONE source; otherwise its only protection is a parallel hand-maintained ignore line = the exact drift the registry exists to eliminate. Never assert "X is in the registry" in a docstring without dumping the registry to confirm (a false load-bearing comment is a real defect, not cosmetic). When a registry entry is a NESTED prefix (`lib/.project_sessions/`) rather than a top-level dir, check every derived consumer's matching MODE — the classifier matches anchored-startswith, but export prunes by basename component — and align the drift-guard to each consumer's real matching, not a uniform assumption.

### 2026-07-07 — Auto-update data-separation follow-up: closed the critic's "not EVERY state consumer follows the resolved base" gap — `uploads/` (images/paper-PDFs/PPTX) was still hardcoded to the code tree; added `uploads_root()` + routed 7 consumers, anti-split teeth test + neuter
- **How it started.** Objective: robust auto-update for any install method via a clean user-data↔code boundary. - **Byte-identical default.** In the default in-tree layout `_BASE == _REPO_ROOT`, so all four asset dirs resolve to `<repo>/uploads/{images,papers,pptx}` exactly as before — verified by import-smoke asserting `PAPER_DIR==uploads_root()/papers` etc. Only a RELOCATED base moves them, and then they co-locate with `data/tofu.db`.

NO migration for existing users (their populated in-tree `data/` keeps everything in-tree, byte-identical).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "keep user state out of the code tree" guarantee is only as complete as its LEAST-migrated consumer. `data/`+`logs/`+memories were relocated but `uploads/` — genuine DB-referenced user state — was silently left computing `<repo>/uploads` from `__file__` in 7 places.
