### 2026-07-07 — Server refused to restart after an OOM crash: single-instance flock had NO self-heal — built stop.sh's reclaim logic into the startup path (dead-local-pid → unlink+fresh-inode re-flock), robust + tested + neuter + real-world verified
- **Symptom (owner prod).** After the server was OOM-`Killed` (bare `Killed`, no traceback — SIGKILL, the mlockall/OOM fingerprint), every `python server.py` restart died with `[CRITICAL] server: Another server instance is already running from this project directory. Set TOFU_SKIP_LOCK=1 to force start.` `pkill -f python` couldn't clear it (`Operation not permitted` on orphaned pids 1139/3870/3953). Only `bash stop.sh` (which detected `PID … is not running (stale lock). Removing …`) unblocked it. The `db_paths … staying on legacy FUSE pgdata` WARNING in the same logs is UNRELATED (the local-primary ordering-hazard gate working as designed — noise, not the fault).
- **Root cause.** `server.py`'s inline `_acquire_instance_lock()` (old ~L1531) blindly `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`'d `data/.server.lock` and, on contention, `sys.exit(1)` — it NEVER read the recorded `<pid>@<host>`, never probed liveness, never reclaimed. But **flock is bound to an open file DESCRIPTION, not to process liveness**: an OOM SIGKILL skips atexit/lock-release, and an orphaned child (uid-mismatched → unkillable by the owner) keeps the fd — and thus the flock — held; on this `fuse.bgfuse` mount an advisory lock is not reliably released on unclean death either. So a contended flock did NOT prove "a server is running", yet server.py treated it as proof → permanent self-lockout until a human ran stop.sh. `stop.sh` was the ONLY thing that did the right thing (`kill -0` + `ps args` server.py check + `rm`).
- **Fix (server.py, module-level + testable).** Extracted the inline closure into a module-level `_acquire_instance_lock(lock_path, logger, hostname=None, allow_reclaim=True) -> (ok, fd)` plus helpers `_read_instance_lock_entry` (parse `<pid>@<host>`, tolerant of empty/malformed) and `_pid_is_live_server(pid)` (`_pid_alive` + `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` must contain `server.py`; UNKNOWABLE liveness/cmdline → conservatively True so we NEVER reclaim a maybe-live owner). On flock contention: `_reclaim_stale_instance_lock` reclaims ONLY when `host == this machine` AND the pid is not a live server.py → `os.unlink` the lock → retry the flock ONCE on the **fresh inode** (`allow_reclaim=False` bounds it to a single retry — no reclaim loop). The orphan's surviving fd points at the now-unlinked OLD inode, so its lingering flock is harmless; we cleanly hold the new inode. Explicit code comments spell out the fd-vs-liveness + FUSE rationale.
- **Guardrails honored (owner's 4 asks).** (2) host-mismatch → CRITICAL + REFUSE, never unlink (cross-host is PG-heartbeat-takeover territory, not this lock's job). (3) FUSE stale-fd scenario is the explicit design target of unlink+fresh-inode; second flock still failing → CRITICAL + `TOFU_SKIP_LOCK=1` hint, no silent loop. (4) §2 logging on every path: `[Lock] reclaiming stale lock pid=%s host=%s (dead)` (WARNING), `[Lock] reclaimed stale lock and acquired fresh instance lock` (INFO), foreign-host + live-local + unreadable-entry + still-failed-after-reclaim (CRITICAL). fcntl-absent / unopenable-dir degrade to best-effort `(True, fd|None)` so a missing lock never blocks startup.
- **Gate — `tests/test_instance_lock_reclaim.py` NEW, 6/6 green.** (a) local dead pid + orphan-held flock → reclaim succeeds, fresh inode (`st_ino` differs), stamped with our pid; (b) foreign host → refuse, inode+contents intact; (c) live-local server.py pid → refuse, not unlinked; + `_pid_is_live_server(dead)` False; + `_read_instance_lock_entry` variants; + **NEUTER `test_neuter_blind_flock_fails_case_a`**: `allow_reclaim=False` (the old blind-flock behaviour) makes case (a) go RED (ok=False, no "reclaiming" log) — proves the reclaim path is load-bearing. ruff clean on both files.
- **Real-world verify (fresh interpreter, not in-process).** Fabricated a dead-pid (fork+reap) lock with an orphan still holding the flock on the old inode, ran the REAL imported `server._acquire_instance_lock` → reclaimed + re-flocked + stamped our pid. Did NOT boot a 2nd full server (a genuine live server + PG + port 15000 are up on this box; my logic would correctly REFUSE that live-local lock) — isolated temp-dir dead-pid case is the faithful OOM scenario.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (server.py is import-time; live process holds the old inline closure). Did NOT touch the OOM line (mlockall already gated; `TOFU_MLOCK=0` remains the constrained-host escape) nor `stop.sh` (already correct).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A `flock` (or any advisory lock) is NOT a liveness signal — it survives its holder's unclean death via any inherited/orphaned fd, doubly so on FUSE. A single-instance guard MUST self-heal like stop.sh: read the recorded owner, probe it (`kill -0` + cmdline), and reclaim a dead LOCAL owner via unlink→fresh-inode; refuse foreign-host (that's cross-host takeover's job) and live-local. Bound the reclaim to ONE retry so it can never loop, and keep the `TOFU_SKIP_LOCK=1` manual override as the last-resort escape.


### 2026-07-07 — Persisted-result tool-row label: killed the `get_conversation output — "═══…"` ugliness at the source (decorative-first-line skip) + closed the same-class post-restart gap (default-spill filename fallback, allow-listed)
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** A spilled-to-disk `get_conversation` result rendered its tool-panel row as `Read 1 saved result: • get_conversation output — "════════…"` — an unreadable wall of box-drawing characters + an unclear generic verb.
- **Root cause (two layers in the persisted-result labeling path).** (1) `lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_persist.py` registered the result DESCRIPTION as the LITERAL first line of the content (`content.lstrip().split('\n',1)[0]`). `get_conversation` output (`lib/conv_ref.py:198`) opens with `"═" * 60` — a decorative rule → the description became the `═` wall. (2) `get_conversation` had NO entry in `persist_registry._TOOL_VERB`, so `friendly_label` fell back to the generic `"get_conversation output"`.
- **Fix 1 — meaningful description.** Added `_first_meaningful_line(content)` + `_DECORATIVE_LINE_RE` (matches pure separator/blank lines: `═ ─ — - = _ * # · •`) in `_persist.py`; the registered description now skips leading decorative rules and picks the first real line (here `Referenced Conversation: "…"`). Falls back to the first line when EVERY line is decorative, so a description is always produced. Other tools' normal first-line behavior is unchanged.
- **Fix 2 — friendly verb.** Added `'get_conversation': 'past conversation'` to `_TOOL_VERB`. In-process the row now reads `past conversation — "Referenced Conversation: …"`.
- **Fix 3 — the residual same-class gap (owner caught it): post-restart fallback.** The default single-file spill is named `<tool_name>_<id>.txt`, but `describe_filename()` only recognized the `search_/fetch_/find_/grep_` SPLIT prefixes → after a restart (process-local registry lost) a `get_conversation_<id>.txt` returned `None` → `_persisted_read_labels` returned `''` → the row regressed to the raw opaque filename. Split tools had BOTH halves (live registry + stateless fallback); the default-path tools had only the live half. Added `_DEFAULT_SPILL_RE` built from an explicit allow-list `_DEFAULT_SPILL_TOOLS = ('get_conversation',)`; `describe_filename` now matches those default-spill names and returns `(tool_name, '')` — no description (the default filename embeds no human fragment) but the tool is recovered → `friendly_label` still renders `past conversation`. Graceful degradation matching how `grep_search` already behaves post-restart.
- **Allow-list rationale (NOT a greedy match).** `describe_filename` runs on EVERY path in a `read_files` batch (`tool_display.py:199`), so a greedy `<name>_<id>` match would hijack an ordinary project read like `requirements_dev.txt`/`notes_2026.txt` and mislabel it a persisted spill. The explicit allow-list (checked AFTER the split-prefix regexes, so no collision) means only known default-spill tools are recognized. Add a tool to both `_DEFAULT_SPILL_TOOLS` and `_TOOL_VERB` when it starts spilling via the default path.
- **Gate — `tests/test_compaction_improvements.py`, 3 new tests, full suite 106 passed.** `test_get_conversation_label_skips_decorative_first_line` (label carries the real title, no `═`, not the old verb); `test_get_conversation_label_survives_registry_loss` (post-`clear()` restart sim → `('get_conversation','')` → `past conversation`, never the raw filename/`.txt`); `test_default_spill_recognition_is_allowlisted` (`requirements_dev.txt`/`notes_2026.txt` → `None`). ruff clean on `_persist.py` / `persist_registry.py` / the test.
- **Status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Backend-only → server restart needed for the live process. Note the registry is process-local: after restart, already-persisted `get_conversation` results get the verb-only `past conversation` (description lost with the filename), newly-spilled ones get the full quoted title.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A result-description derived from "the first line" must skip decorative separators — a formatted tool result (here `get_conversation`) can open with a `═══` rule. And a friendly-label mechanism needs BOTH halves for EVERY spill path (live registry + stateless `describe_filename` fallback), not just the split tools — the default single-file path was the forgotten half. When adding filename recognition that runs across a whole `read_files` batch, use a tool-name ALLOW-LIST, never a greedy `<name>_<id>` match, or you mislabel real project files.


### 2026-07-07 — Overnight-suspend stale-PG-connection bug ROOT-CAUSED + fixed: monotonic clock freezes across suspend so the pool handed out DEAD connections → first Send/Regen after reconnecting the next day 500'd + ~16min "offline"
- **Symptom (owner's prod logs).** Every time the owner reconnects from a different device the next day, the server shows "offline" for a very long time, error.log full of `psycopg2.OperationalError: server closed the connection unexpectedly` on `persist_conv_messages:151`, and paired `POST /api/client-error 200 SLOW (965.982s)` — 16-minute hangs at the exact moment the DB connections died.
- **Root cause (two linked, both in the DB layer).** (1) `_test_pg_connection` (lib/database/_core.py:946) decided whether to SKIP the `SELECT 1` health probe using `idle = time.monotonic() - _last_used < _IDLE_CHECK_S(30s)`. **`time.monotonic()` FREEZES across an OS suspend** (lid close / VM pause / FUSE stall / device disconnect) — it does not count suspended wall time. So after an overnight freeze that killed every pooled connection's PG backend, `_last_used` still looked "~2s ago" → the probe was skipped → a **DEAD connection was handed to the request**, which then failed on the first real query. (2) `persist_conv_messages` (lib/chat/persistence.py:85,151) uses a RAW `db.execute(SELECT …)` with NO retry/reconnect (unlike `db_execute_with_retry`), so the dead connection surfaced as a hard 500 on the user's Send/Regen. Each failed request only drained ONE dead pooled conn on teardown; with pool up to 100 + health checks every 10s it took ~16min to drain them all → the 965s "offline" window. The existing `_PG_DEAD_SIGNATURES`/`_maybe_reboot_pg` self-heal only fires when CREATING a new connection — it never inspects a stale POOLED one, so it didn't help here.
- **Fix 1 — root cause (suspend guard).** `PgConnection` now tracks a WALL-clock twin `_last_used_wall` (time.time()) alongside the monotonic `_last_used`, updated on every successful execute/executemany and on a successful health probe. `_test_pg_connection` skips the probe ONLY when BOTH clocks are under 30s (`idle < _IDLE_CHECK_S and wall_idle < _IDLE_CHECK_S`). The wall clock advances across a suspend even when monotonic didn't, so a resumed process always probes and the pool discards the stale connection → instant recovery, no user-facing failure.
- **Fix 2 — belt (transparent reconnect for raw-SELECT sites).** `PgConnection.execute` now does a one-shot transparent reconnect on a dead-connection error (`OperationalError` matching `_pg_error_is_dead`, or any `InterfaceError`) **only when the connection has issued no write yet in the txn** (`not self._dirty`) — a connection-level failure means nothing committed, so re-running the first/clean statement is idempotent. This rescues the raw `db.execute()` read sites (persist_conv_messages settings SELECT) that don't route through `db_execute_with_retry`. A `statement_timeout` cancellation (OperationalError that is NOT a dead signature) is deliberately NOT retried. Refactored the duplicated inline reconnect logic in `db_execute_with_retry` into a shared `_reconnect_pg_inplace(db)` helper (swaps the raw conn + adopts the fresh semaphore slot, releasing the dead one's slot + `_conn_count` so no leak).
- **Gate — `tests/test_db_stale_conn_recovery.py` 6/6, no live PG needed (pure logic + fakes).** Suspend guard: recent-by-both-clocks skips probe (fast path preserved); frozen-monotonic + overnight wall gap FORCES the probe; dead-conn-after-suspend → probe fails → `_test_pg_connection` returns False (pool discards); probe refreshes wall clock so an immediate re-check skips. Belt: reconnects+retries a clean SELECT on a dead-signature error; does NOT reconnect a `_dirty` connection. **NEUTER proof**: reverting the wall-clock cross-check to the buggy monotonic-only gate makes the two suspend tests go RED (dead conn wrongly trusted); restore → green + `_core.py` byte-identical. Sibling `test_db_thread_conn_lifecycle` 8-passed/2-skipped still green; ruff clean. (`test_db_guard::test_all_standalone_runners_are_guarded` fails but is PROVEN pre-existing — fails identically on the stashed clean tree with a longer file list, none of which I touched.)
- **Verification / status.** NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (import-time — the live server holds the old `_core.py`/`_wrappers.py` in memory). Frontend already handles the recovery UX (health-check circuit breaker + offline-recovery polling in health_stream_timer.js / sse_poll_fallback.js); the backend fix means the pool now recovers on the FIRST touch instead of draining one-conn-per-request over 16min.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** NEVER use `time.monotonic()` alone to decide whether a resource "went stale while idle" — it freezes across OS suspend, so any idle/liveness gate keyed only on it silently trusts stale state after a resume. Cross-check `time.time()` (wall) for the elapsed-real-time question. Any raw `db.execute()` that doesn't go through `db_execute_with_retry` is a latent hard-500 on a dead pooled connection; the transparent-reconnect belt on the wrapper (gated on `not _dirty`) closes that class without touching every call site.


### 2026-07-07 — Edit/regen audit turned up an UNRUNNABLE guard test — fixed the fixture (heals whole API-DB suite), consolidated the truncation invariant into one helper, proved teeth with a route-level neuter
- **How it started.** Diagnostic ask: are edit & regen handled correctly in context, frontend + backend? Two parallel coder audits (backend context-rebuild; frontend state/sync) + my own read of the load-bearing lines → **functionally CORRECT today**: the regen context-truncation hinges on `server_message_store.clear(conv_id)` at routes/chat.py:947-948; the frontend strips backend-owned `segments` in `_trimMsgForPersist` (conversations.js:189-192); endpoint-mode routing still correct at chat.py:361-401. All 4 documented past bugs remain fixed. BUT the owner then found the real hole: the regression test guarding that load-bearing clear — `tests/test_regen_clears_msg_store.py` — **did not actually run** here.
- **Root cause of the illusory guard (fixture-level, affected the WHOLE API-DB test family).** The session `flask_app` fixture (tests/conftest.py) imports `server` (builds the app) and returns `app`, but the SQLite schema is only ever created inside `server._startup()` — a Hypercorn *before-serving* hook that `app.test_client()` NEVER fires. So every fixture-backed API test hit a fresh, TABLE-LESS SQLite file → the setup PUT 500'd with `no such table: conversations`, and the assertion on the cleared store was never reached. `test_api_integration.py` was 4-failed/18-passed for the same reason. FIX: call idempotent `init_db()` once in the `flask_app` fixture right after importing the app (schema-version cache → no app context needed). → `test_regen_clears_msg_store` green; `test_api_integration` 4-failed→**22-passed**.
- **Then consolidated the invariant (step 2 of the owner's plan).** The post-truncation obligations (clear the message QUEUE + clear `server_message_store`) were two inline try/except blocks (chat.py 5a/5b) a future truncating route could half-apply. Folded both into a single module-level `_truncate_conv_history(conv_id)` helper (routes/chat.py, before `_start_task_for_conv`) with the full rationale in its docstring; `chat_regenerate` now calls it once. Grep confirms `chat_regenerate` (line 853, `messages[:truncate_to+1]`) is the ONLY history-truncating route — `chat_continue` is the separate checkpoint-rollback flow (passes toolHistory/checkpointToolRounds, intentionally not a truncation) and `chat_queue.clear_queue` is the queue-only API.
- **Guard now has TEETH (ground-truthed, not asserted).** Extended the test file to 3 cases: the original route-level guard + a direct `_truncate_conv_history` guard asserting BOTH side-channels drained (seed store via `_seed_store`, seed queue via `enqueue_message`, assert store→None + queue→[]) + a monkeypatch negative-control proving the store `is None` assertion is exercising the real clear. Then the owner-requested proof: temporarily NEUTERED the actual `_clear_msg_store(conv_id)` line in the route → BOTH route+helper tests went RED (`left the server_message_store populated`) while the queue-clear still ran (independent checks) → restored the line → 3/3 green.
- **Verification.** `test_regen_clears_msg_store.py` 3/3; broad **`-m api` tier 130 passed / 4 skipped / 0 failed** (was silently carrying red DB tests); ruff clean on chat.py + conftest.py + the test. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart NOT needed for tests, but the live server holds the old chat.py in memory until restart.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A green regression test that can't actually run is worse than none — it manufactures false confidence. When a guard "passes", confirm it FAILS on the neuter (here: neuter the real route line, not just a monkeypatch). The schema-bootstrap gap was a fixture bug masquerading as N unrelated test failures — fix it once at the shared fixture, not per-test. And a discipline-based invariant (every truncating route must clear both side-channels) should be consolidated into one call so it's structurally impossible to half-apply.


### 2026-07-07 (step 3) — Physical user-state ⇄ code-tree separation for a plain source/git install: fresh clone now defaults data/logs/DB/memories OUT of the code tree (per-user XDG); existing populated in-tree ./data stays put (zero migration). Ground-truth 10-test suite + empty-data neuter + log-twin agreement green
- **Why (the objective's second clause).** Classification (steps 1-2) makes an update SKIP in-tree state, but the ROOT-CAUSE fix for "a git pull races an open in-tree SQLite WAL" is to not keep state in the tree at all. On a non-frozen source checkout `_resolve_base()` returned `_REPO_ROOT` unconditionally → `data/`, `logs/`, config, memories all landed inside the code tree unless the user manually set `TOFU_DATA_DIR`. Owner: build the robust default, no back-compat shortcut that silently orphans data.
- **What shipped.** `lib/runtime_paths.py` new `_source_checkout_base()` (+ `_dir_is_populated()`): precedence `TOFU_DATA_DIR > TOFU_DATA_LAYOUT > auto`. `auto` (default) = in-tree ONLY when `<repo>/data` exists AND is populated (existing install, zero migration), else per-user XDG (`~/.local/share/Tofu` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tofu` / `~/Library/Application Support/Tofu` via the existing `_per_user_root()`). `TOFU_DATA_LAYOUT=intree|xdg` force either. The populated-check reads FS CONTENTS (`os.scandir` any-entry), NOT mere existence — a fresh `git clone` ships NO `data/` (the whole dir is gitignored; `git ls-files data/` = empty), so populated ⟺ existing install, unambiguously.
- **Twin + downstream coherence (the split traps).** (1) `lib/log.py`'s inline `_writable_base_dir()` (can't import runtime_paths — cycle) got the byte-identical source-checkout branch + a shared `_per_user_base()` helper, so logs/ never splits from data/ across the in-tree/XDG boundary. (2) `lib/memory/storage.py::_server_data_dir()` was BYPASSING runtime_paths (recomputed `<project_root>/data`) → would have orphaned global memories in the tree while the DB moved to XDG; now delegates to `data_root()`. DB_PATH already routes through `data_root()` (`_core.py:171-179`), so DB + logs + config + memories now all co-locate under the one resolved base — verified live: fresh-clone sim puts all four under XDG, this dev tree (populated data/) stays in-tree.
- **INFO diagnosability (§2).** Every branch logs the chosen base + WHY: `Data layout: fresh source checkout … → per-user root <p>`, `… existing in-tree data/ found → <repo>`, `… TOFU_DATA_LAYOUT=intree/xdg`, `… explicit TOFU_DATA_DIR override`. Documented in `.env.example` (new "Data / state location" block).
- **Gate — OBSERVED GREEN.** New `tests/test_data_layout_separation.py` (10): the owner's 3 scenarios (a TOFU_DATA_DIR honored + DB follows; b fresh→XDG; c populated→in-tree) + LAYOUT=intree/xdg forcing + the NEUTER (an EMPTY `data/` dir must resolve FRESH→XDG, proving the check reads contents not existence — an `os.path.exists` would wrongly keep it in-tree) + 4 log-twin-agreement cases (log.py base == runtime_paths base across fresh/populated/empty/xdg). All driven in a subprocess that RELOCATES `_REPO_ROOT`/`BASE_DIR` to a throwaway tree so the resolver runs against a real controlled FS, asserting on the ACTUAL INFO log line. Regression: `test_desktop_install_paths` 12/12 (frozen/override/portable/readonly all unaffected — the source branch is the only change), `test_runtime_layout` 9/9, `test_self_update_tarball` 5/5. Import smoke: DB_PATH/LOG_DIR/CONFIG_DIR all still co-located on this tree. ruff clean. NOT committed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "keep state out of the code tree" default must (1) detect an existing install by FS CONTENTS not existence (fresh clone ships no data/ at all → populated ⟺ existing) so nobody's data silently orphans, and (2) drag EVERY state consumer onto the one resolved root — DB, logs, config AND the easily-missed memory store that had its own `<project_root>/data` bypass. When a cycle forces a hand-duplicated resolver (log.py twin), extend BOTH copies and pin them equal with a twin-agreement test across every new branch. Prove the populated-check with an empty-dir neuter — the difference between `exists()` and `scandir()-any` is the whole back-compat guarantee.

NEW guards: (a) `test_zh_render_has_no_english_leak` — the zh render of error+empty carries NONE of the 5 old bare-English literals; (b) i18n POISONED-NC (`test_nc_poisoned_i18n_drops_localized_text`) — neuter `t()` to echo the key → the zh title CANNOT appear and the raw `tm.empty.title` key leaks through → proves the strings actually flow through `t()` and aren't hardcoded zh. - **Guardrail / lesson.** When a surface is opened from an already-localized entry point (`任务` button), the surface MUST speak the same language — an all-English body under a zh button is a visible seam. Watch for a SECOND write path that bypasses the render fn (`_tmSyncChip` sets textContent directly) — localize there too or the live update reverts the language. - **JS (paper-reader.js reader-prefs module, GLOBAL not per-paper).** `_READER_FONT_SCALES=[0.85,0.925,1,1.1,1.2,1.3]` (idx2 default) + `_READER_WIDTHS=[640 Narrow,720 Comfortable,860 Wide]` (idx1 default). `_readReaderPrefs`/`_persistReaderPrefs` (localStorage `paper_reader_prefs`, clamped, never-throw), `_applyReaderPrefs(prefs?)` sets both custom props on `#paperReportContent`+`#paperReviewContent` + syncs the width label + disables A− at min, `_readerFontStep(±1)`, `_readerWidthCycle()`. `_applyReaderPrefs()` called on `enterPaperMode` so the choice survives reload + spans papers (same persistence discipline as `_setReportLang`).
- **UI (index.html both toolbars).** New `.paper-reader-settings` segmented group before each lang-toggle: A− (minus glyph), A+ (A+plus glyph), width-cycle (arrows-horizontal glyph + live label). SVG only (§3.4), `role=group`+aria-labels+`:focus-visible` outline (keyboard-operable per frontend prefs). CSS reuses the segmented-toggle chrome. i18n keys `paper.readerSettings/readerFontSmaller/readerFontLarger/readerWidth/readerWidth{Narrow,Comfortable,Wide}` (zh+en).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_paper_reader_prefs.py`, NEW, 2 tests / 12 internal checks) + INDEPENDENT neuters.** jsdom extraction-and-eval loads the REAL shipped paper-reader.js, drives the handlers, asserts BOTH observable effects (container inline custom-property AND the persisted localStorage key) incl. clamp-at-min + A−-disabled + width-label-sync. NC-apply (`_applyReaderPrefs`→no-op) breaks the DOM-var effect but not persistence; NC-persist (`_persistReaderPrefs`→no-op) breaks durability but not the immediate var — the two neuters prove APPLY and PERSIST are each load-bearing for their own half. Shipped file byte-identical after.
- **Verification.** New suite 2/2 (12/12 internal); full sweep (reader-prefs + reading-anchor + paper-mobile-responsive + breakpoint-coord + touch-polish + api-isolation + bundle-guard) = **36 passed**. node --check clean on paper-reader.js/i18n.js/core.js; `calc(* var(--reader-font-scale))` present ×4 (base×2 + tofu + light); bundles rebuilt main `bundle-1eb14770.js` + deferred `feature-4eba8838.js` (`_readerFontStep`/`_readerWidthCycle`/`_applyReaderPrefs`/`paper_reader_prefs`/`reader-font-scale` all present — paper-reader.js is DEFERRED, verify in `feature-*.js`). ruff clean. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + feature-bundle reload needed.
- **Board.** Logged the PRE-EXISTING `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` failure as known-defect epic pt_87590db7f5a04792 (out of scope for this reading-UX epic, per owner) so it isn't lost.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A comfort control is best built as a pure CSS-custom-property lever: one var on the container, `calc()` on every themed base size, JS only sets `el.style.setProperty` + persists — no per-element rewrite, all themes inherit free. When a value is themed 3× (base/tofu/light each hardcoded), thread the var through ALL of them or one theme silently ignores the control. Neuter EACH half of an apply+persist pair independently (no-op apply → DOM effect dies; no-op persist → durability dies) so a future edit that breaks either is caught.

### 2026-07-07 — Segment-timeline bug-hunt, 2nd boundary closed: idb-cache `_stripMessage` also drops backend-owned `segments` (same class as the PUT-echo fix; OOM-memory boundary)
- **Gap the owner named (last loose end).** After the `_trimMsgForPersist` PUT-echo fix, the SAME "backend-owned duplicate riding into a persist/cache boundary" existed at the OTHER boundary: `idb-cache.js::_stripMessage` copies all keys via `for..in` (skipping only `_hydratePromise`/`_translateTaskId`), so it cached the bloated `segments` array locally on every conversation. No crash, but segments ~double the cached assistant payload — exactly the class the conv-OOM memory (usage._wire_fp/_partialOutput/base64) warns about. The frontend doesn't consume segments yet (deferred step-5 render epic), so the local cache should stay lean.
- **Fix.** Added `if (k === 'segments') continue;` to the top-level `for..in` of `_stripMessage` (idb-cache.js), mirroring the existing `_hydratePromise`/`_translateTaskId` skips and the `_partialOutput`/`_wire_fp`/base64 strips in the same function. The IndexedDB copy is a LOCAL READ CACHE (server is SoT) → a reader that eventually needs segments re-fetches from server. Comment flags "revisit when the render cutover lands".
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_segments_not_echoed.py` now 5/5) + NC.** Extended the extraction-and-eval file: new `_extract_strip_message_fn` pulls `_stripMessage` (+ `_stripUsageObj`/`_stripToolRound`/`_USAGE_TRANSIENT`) out of the ConvCache IIFE closure, evals in node, asserts segments dropped from the cached copy + live object not mutated + content/thinking/toolRounds survive. NC regex-removes the `if (k === 'segments') continue;` line → segments LEAKS into the cache → proves the skip load-bearing. Plus the node-free source guard now checks BOTH strip sites (conversations.js `_trimMsgForPersist` + idb-cache.js `_stripMessage`).
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on idb-cache.js; it's in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-791fedf4.js`. Test suite 5/5 (2 conversations.js + 2 idb-cache.js + 1 source guard, both NCs green). NOT committed. Backend segment chain + its bug-hunt now genuinely complete across BOTH client persist boundaries (PUT + IndexedDB cache).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A backend-owned field the frontend doesn't consume must be stripped at EVERY client persist/cache boundary, not just one — there are TWO in this codebase (`_trimMsgForPersist` for the PUT wire, `_stripMessage` for IndexedDB), and both start from the full message dict (`let r = m` / `for..in`), so a new backend field silently rides through both until explicitly dropped. When you fix the first, grep for the sibling boundary immediately.


### 2026-07-07 — Reading Mode UX deep pass: reading measure cap + unified prose typography, scroll-position preservation across EN/中 repaint, reduced-motion + image-zoom keyboard a11y. Measure-first (2 parallel audits), double-neuter jsdom.
- **Ask (owner).** "Reading mode must be extremely detailed and flawless — think harder about UI/UX for the reading experience." - **Ground truth (verified, not trusted).** The reader is already MATURE: TOC+scroll-spy (`_wireReportScrollSpy`, IntersectionObserver), an EWMA learned-WPM reading-time/progress bar (`_buildReadingTimeBar`), glossary term cards with tabindex/aria, per-theme reading "environments" (dark aurora / light Reading Room / tofu Study Nook). The GENUINE reading defects: (1) the base prose surfaces `.paper-report-content`/`.paper-report-body` (styles.css:1015/1048) had NO measure cap — only `padding:20px`, full-width → 130–160ch lines on a wide pane (the worst reading-comfort defect); the enhanced `.paper-report-doc` (2172) caps at 1180px but that's a 2-col grid, not a text measure, and only when enhanced. (2) The two prose blocks were near-duplicate and had DRIFTED (only `-body` had table rules → generated-report tables rendered unstyled). (3) No paragraph rhythm, no prose link styling, no `pre` overflow, flat heading scale (h3=14px=body). (4) Switching EN/中 (`_setReportLang`→`_renderFinalReport`) wipes `innerHTML` and JUMPED THE READER TO TOP — a reading-flow break. (5) `prefers-reduced-motion` ignored by the reader; report image-zoom (click→fullscreen) had NO keyboard path (`<img>` not focusable).
- **What shipped.** ① **Unified reading prose** (styles.css): merged the two drifted blocks into one `.paper-report-content,.paper-report-body{…}` selector list (can't drift again) + a **reading measure**: `--reader-measure:720px` var, `.paper-report-article{max-width:var(--reader-measure);margin-inline:auto}` (caps the text column in BOTH enhanced-grid and plain final layouts) + a streaming-frame cap (`.paper-report-body:not(.paper-report-enhanced) > :not(.paper-report-doc):not(.paper-report-article):not(.paper-read-time)`) so streaming text doesn't run full-width then snap to 720px on completion. Added: `p` margin (1em rhythm), prose `a` styling (accent + underline-on-hover), `pre` block with `overflow-x:auto`, table rules for `-content` (parity with `-body`), zebra striping, better heading scale (h2 18px / h3 15.5px with line-heights), base size 14px→15px/1.75 (dark theme had no override, was stuck cramped). ② **Scroll preservation** (paper-reader.js): `_captureReadingAnchor(scroller)`→{index,offset} snapshots the heading nearest the viewport top + its pixel offset (heading ORDER is stable across languages, unlike raw scrollTop after re-layout; returns null on a fresh/unscrolled render so first paint is untouched); `_restoreReadingAnchor` re-applies it after the rebuild in `_renderFinalReport`. ③ **reduced-motion**: new shared `prefersReducedMotion()` in core.js (alongside the viewport helpers); `_scrollReportToHeading` uses `behavior:'auto'` when set; extended the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` paper block to kill the read-time fill tween, chip pulse, landing float. ④ **image-zoom keyboard a11y**: `_decorateZoomableImages(article)` adds tabindex/role=button/aria-label to report images; a keydown handler opens the same fullscreen overlay on Enter/Space (mirrors the click handler). New i18n key `paper.imageZoomHint` (zh+en).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_paper_reading_anchor.py`, NEW, 2 tests) + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** jsdom harness (mirrors the proven `test_frontend_paper_mobile_responsive.py` pattern) loads the REAL shipped paper-reader.js, builds a scroller with synthetic getBoundingClientRect geometry (jsdom does no layout), captures an anchor at a mid-report heading, rebuilds the article, asserts restored scrollTop lands on that heading (not 0) + fresh-render→null. NC-1 (capture→null) and NC-2 (restore→no-op) each on a COPY prove BOTH halves load-bearing; shipped file byte-identical after. Harness trap fixed: eval'd `function` decls are bare names not `window.*`; "in a heading" means the heading is at/ABOVE the top edge (negative offset).
- **Verification.** New suite 2/2; full sweep (reading-anchor + paper-mobile-responsive + breakpoint-coord + touch-polish + memory-specificity + api-isolation + bundle-guard + glossary) = relevant suites green. node --check clean on core.js/paper-reader.js/i18n.js. Bundles rebuilt: main `bundle-7b505927.js` (prefersReducedMotion ×3) + deferred `feature-16feaa5f.js` (`_captureReadingAnchor`/`_restoreReadingAnchor`/`_decorateZoomableImages`/`imageZoomHint` all present — paper-reader.js is a DEFERRED/lazy feature bundle, NOT the main bundle; verify symbols in `feature-*.js` not `bundle-*.js`). ruff clean. **Pre-existing UNRELATED failure honestly flagged:** `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py::…report_generated_in_zh/en` fails — PROVEN pre-existing by reverting all my edits in a copy and re-running (fails identically); the test stubs `_renderFinalReport` so my edits aren't even exercised; the failing checks are about `reportStart` call args in `_loadOrGenerateReport`, untouched. Left alone (out of scope). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart + feature-bundle reload needed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The single biggest long-form reading-comfort win is a MEASURE CAP (≈68–72ch) on the text column — chat had it (820px), the reading surface (the one built for sustained reading) did NOT. When two near-duplicate style blocks exist, they WILL drift (here only one had table rules) — merge into one selector list as part of the improvement. ### 2026-07-07 (step 2) — Closed the drift loop: export.py + .gitignore now DRIFT-GUARDED against lib/runtime_layout (not just self_update consuming it). 9/9 registry tests green incl. 2 new guards + 2 neuters
- **Why (owner held the bar).** Step 1 built the registry but only `self_update` consumed it → a one-consumer SoT isn't a SoT: the drift class ("forget an entry in one list → update clobbers DB / leaks state") still existed between the registry and the OTHER two sources (`export.py` hand-lists, static `.gitignore`), and `gitignore_lines()` was dead code. Owner directive: don't rewrite export's lists (respect the axis distinction) — add drift-GUARD tests that fail CI the day the registry and a consumer diverge, ground-truthed with neuters.
- **What shipped (all in `tests/test_runtime_layout.py`, 5→9 tests).** (1) `test_export_covers_registry_internal_opensource`: asserts every registry DIR prefix is in `export.ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (internal) + `|OPENSOURCE_EXTRA_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (opensource), plus the `bundle-` filename-prefix is covered by an `ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_GLOBS` glob. (2) `test_gitignore_covers_registry`: reads the LIVE `.gitignore`, asserts every registry dir is ignored (bare/`/`-anchored OR via a content-level rule under it) + the `bundle-*` and `.tofu*` globs. (3)+(4) neuters: inject a fake `RuntimeEntry('__nonexistent_state_dir__/')` → BOTH guards must fail (proving they cross-check the registry against reality, not tautologies).
- **AXIS CORRECTION (ground-truth beat the instruction).** The ask said "all three modes"; export.py:220 + 908-911 document PERSONAL mode as a full same-user backup that DELIBERATELY keeps `data/config` credentials + `uploads/` (only chat-history `*.db`/`pgdata` are skipped, via the `.db` glob + dest-preserve, NOT a `data/` dir exclusion). So `data`/`uploads` are intentionally ABSENT from `PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_DIRS` — the guard targets internal+opensource ONLY; asserting personal would encode a false expectation and break a real behaviour. Locked that reasoning into the test docstring.
- **The guard caught a REAL (benign) pattern on first run.** `.gitignore` ignores `uploads/images/*` + `uploads/pptx/` while keeping a tracked `uploads/images/.gitkeep` (empty dir survives clone) — so a bare-`uploads/` match was too strict. Relaxed `_ignored()` to also accept any rule targeting a path UNDER the dir → content-level ignore counts as coverage; a registry dir with ZERO mention (the neuter) still trips. This is the ground-truth-over-assumption discipline working: the matcher, not the codebase, was wrong.
- **Structural question answered head-on (see reply).** A source/git user CAN relocate all writable state outside the code tree via `TOFU_DATA_DIR` (DB default = `data_root()/tofu.db` at `_core.py:171-179`; config_dir + memories + logs all route through `runtime_paths`), so `git pull` never races user state. GAP named: for a NON-frozen install it's opt-in with NO default relocation (frozen builds auto-pick a per-user dir; `TOFU_DB_PATH` overrides only the DB file). The classification (this epic) makes clobbering impossible-by-construction regardless; physical relocation is the complementary belt for the git-pull-races-open-DB edge.
- **Verification.** `tests/test_runtime_layout.py` 9/9 (incl. 2 guards + 2 neuters); `tests/test_self_update_tarball.py` 5/5 regression; ruff clean on all touched files. NOT committed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A single-source-of-truth isn't real until EVERY drift source is bound to it — either by consuming it or by a drift-guard test with a neuter. When a guard fires on first run, check whether it caught a bug or an over-strict assertion (here: content-level `.gitignore` rules are legit coverage). And when an instruction says "all N modes", verify each mode's INTENDED behaviour from the code/docstring before asserting it — personal-mode keeping user data is a feature, not drift.


### 2026-07-07 — Robust auto-update for ANY install method: single-sourced the install-tree "user-state ⇄ shippable-code" boundary into lib/runtime_layout.py (step 1 — self_update re-keyed, byte-identical, golden+neuter green)
- **Ask.** "However Tofu was installed (git / exported zip / desktop), find a ROBUST way to support auto-update. This likely needs a cleaner split of user personal data vs. project support code." Measure-first before touching anything.
- **Ground truth (measured, not assumed).** The project already had strong bones: `lib/runtime_paths.py` single-sources WHERE writable state goes (`data_root()`/`logs_root()`, handles frozen desktop + `TOFU_DATA_DIR` + source checkout); `lib/agent_artifacts.py` single-sources the PROJECT-LOCAL `.tofu*` artifact family; `lib/self_update.py` already updates git checkouts (`git pull --ff-only`) AND non-git deployments (validated tarball overlay + `.update_backup/` backup). The ACTUAL gap = the classification "which install-tree paths are mutable user/runtime state an update must NEVER clobber" was HAND-DUPLICATED across 3 lists that drift: `self_update._RUNTIME_STATE_PREFIXES`/`_OVERLAY_SKIP_PREFIXES`, `export.py` `PERSONAL/ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS`, and `.gitignore`. Forget an entry in the update skip-list → whole-tree overlay clobbers the DB; forget it in `.gitignore` → state leaks into VCS. `agent_artifacts` had single-sourced the `.tofu*` half; nobody had single-sourced the install-tree half (`data/ logs/ uploads/ outputs/ overleaf_cache/ static/js/bundle- .update_backup/`).

Re-keyed `self_update.py` onto it: `_is_runtime_state` → `_rl_is_runtime_state`, `_overlay_skip` → `_rl_is_overlay_skipped`; deleted the two hand-listed tuples; re-exported the derived names (in `__all__`) so existing call sites/tests keep working. Dropped the now-unused `is_agent_artifact` import from self_update (runtime_layout owns it).

Only the runtime-state subset should derive from runtime_layout; conflating the axes is the wrong abstraction. Deferred to step 2. (2) Generated `.gitignore` block from `gitignore_lines()` — the helper exists + is tested but isn't wired into an ignore-generator yet. (3) PHYSICAL relocation of `data/` out of the code tree — `runtime_paths` already supports it via `TOFU_DATA_DIR`, but project-local `.tofu/` is INTENTIONALLY in-tree (travels with the project), so relocation is a nuanced separate question, documented not forced.
- **Gate — OBSERVED GREEN.** `tests/test_runtime_layout.py` (5): GOLDEN byte-identity of the derived tuples vs. the exact pre-extraction literals (re-keying is provably a classify/skip no-op); self_update re-exports == registry; classification (state skipped / source copied / VCS overlay-only-not-runtime-state); NEUTER (drop `data/` from the registry → `is_runtime_state('data/tofu.db')` wrongly False → proves teeth); `gitignore_lines` renders every dir + `.tofu*`. Regression `tests/test_self_update_tarball.py` 5/5 STILL green (the updater's behaviour is unchanged). ruff clean on all 3 touched/new files. NOT committed. No server restart needed for tests, but the live server holds the old self_update in memory until restart.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a project already has a proven single-source registry for one half of a boundary (`agent_artifacts` for `.tofu*`), generalize the SAME pattern for the other half rather than inventing something new — and prove the re-key is a no-op with a golden that pins the derived value to the exact historical literal + a neuter that defeats the guard. Keep axes separate: "mutable user state" and "not shippable in a public release" are different questions; a dir can be one, both, or neither — don't collapse them into one list.


### 2026-07-07 — Segment-timeline bug-hunt (frontend+backend display): backend CLEAN on 5 risks; ONE real frontend bug fixed (client echoed backend-owned `segments` back on PUT — bloat + stale-clobber)
- **Ask.** After steps 1-4 landed, sweep frontend+backend display for bugs the `segments` field introduced + test thoroughly. Two parallel swarm coder audits (backend persist/wire/search/bloat; frontend defensive-on-unknown-field) + my own direct verification.
- **Backend — ALL 5 RISKS CLEAN (verified, not assumed).** (1) WIRE LEAK: `segments` is NOT in `_API_MESSAGE_FIELDS` (lib/llm_sanitize.py:37) → `_strip_non_api_fields` (called in lib/llm/body.py:575, every send path) drops it; AND the builders (`_build_assistant_messages`, `inject_tool_history`) construct fresh field-by-field dicts that never copy `segments` out. Double backstop. (2) MESSAGES-AS-ROWS: `message_to_row` stores the WHOLE dict in `meta` (messages_rows.py:139); `row_to_message` = `json.loads(meta)` → segments round-trips losslessly. (3) SEARCH INDEX: `build_search_text` (search_index.py) reads only content/thinking/translatedContent by explicit key — never `segments`, no double-index. (4) DOUBLE-PERSIST: both sinks wrap `segments_to_json` (strips the fat `_round`); no caller persists the `_round`-bearing form. (5) `deliverable_text` fallback: `content or ''` — error envelopes live only in `task['error']` (separate column), never in content, so no envelope leaks into the compat `content` field.
- **Frontend — ONE REAL BUG FOUND + FIXED.** No crash/mis-render (renderMessage + `_msgFingerprint` + tool_rounds all read NAMED fields, never iterate keys; idb-cache stores it harmlessly; Continue path reads only toolRounds). BUT `syncConversationToServer` (core/conversations.js) maps each message starting from the FULL dict (`let r = m`) → a loaded `segments` array was **echoed back to the server on every full-conv PUT**. Two harms: (a) BLOAT — segments restate content+thinking+tool-result text, ~doubling assistant payload; (b) STALE ECHO — after a local mutation (regen/translate) that didn't update segments, the client would overwrite the server-fresh SoT with an OLDER copy. Since the backend now OWNS segments (re-derived every finalization) and the frontend doesn't consume them yet, the client must never echo them.
- **Fix.** Added a `segments` strip to `_trimMsgForPersist` (core/conversations.js) — the exact frontend mirror that already strips backend-owned transient bloat (`_partialOutput`, `usage._wire_fp`) so a client PUT can't re-inflate what the server sanitizer trimmed. Clone-only-when-trimming preserved (live object not mutated). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-b8fecad6.js`.
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_segments_not_echoed.py`, 3/3) + NC.** Extraction-and-eval: pulls the REAL shipped `_trimMsgForPersist` from conversations.js, evals in node (function is module-private, not on window), asserts segments stripped from the persist copy + live object NOT mutated + content/thinking/toolRounds survive + no-segments passthrough. NC byte-reverts the strip block via regex → segments LEAKS → proves the strip load-bearing. Plus a node-free source guard. Harness trap: `node -e SCRIPT -- ARG` does NOT populate `process.argv[2]` reliably → passed the extracted source via `TRIM_SRC` env instead.
- **Verification.** Full epic-wide sweep 273/273: segment_model + compat_narrator + compat_openai + compat_anthropic + continue_lossless + compaction_invariants + core_schema_parity + frontend_segments + chat_manager_migration. `node --check` clean on conversations.js; it's in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. NOT committed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When the backend becomes the authoritative producer of a NEW message field the frontend doesn't yet consume, the client's full-conv PUT will happily echo it back (its map starts from the full dict) — bloating the payload AND risking a stale-copy clobber of the fresh SoT. The fix belongs in the SAME seam that already strips backend-owned transient fields (`_trimMsgForPersist`), not a new mechanism. Audits are hypotheses: I re-verified all 5 backend "clean" claims against the actual code before trusting them, and the ONE actionable finding was the frontend echo — fixed at the existing strip seam with an extraction-and-eval + NC test.

### 2026-07-07 — Segment-timeline STEP 3 shipped: headless "narrator" leak FIXED AT ROOT (the reported pain) — compat surfaces driven by the segment model, DELTA_RESET dependency retired
- **The reported pain, root-caused.** A headless streaming client of the OpenAI/Anthropic compat surfaces received every content `delta` verbatim — INCLUDING each round's pre-tool narration ("Let me search for that.") — because `stream_openai_chunks`/`stream_anthropic_chunks` forwarded raw deltas and the app-only, un-portable `DELTA_RESET` signal (orchestrator.py:112, the sole emit; consumed by sse_pipeline.js:910 which CLEARS THE DOM) never reached them. A wire client can't retract bytes → the app's DOM-clear fix is fundamentally un-portable.
- **The design caveat, resolved with an honest impossibility.** A content delta is UNCLASSIFIABLE mid-stream (narration-vs-answer is only known at round close: delta_reset=narration, done=answer). Since a wire client can't retract, token-by-token live streaming of the DELIVERABLE is mutually exclusive with a zero-leak guarantee. CHOSE zero-leak correctness: (1) content deltas NOT forwarded to the answer channel; (2) THINKING deltas stream live (reasoning_content/thinking_delta); (3) tool/phase events stream live (tofu-native envelope); (4) the narration-free deliverable emitted at `done` from the segment model. So it's a REAL streaming experience (reasoning + tool progress throughout), only the final answer text lands at close — NOT a single end-dump. DELTA_RESET dependency on the compat surface RETIRED (no raw content forwarded → no reset needed).
- **`deliverable_text(task)` = ONE source of truth** (new in segments.py): `derive_content(task['segments'])` with `task['content']` fallback (both narration-free — content is already post-`_discard_pretool_prose`). Wired into ALL FOUR paths: OpenAI sync (`_assistant_message`) + streaming, Anthropic sync (`_content_blocks_from_task`) + streaming, plus both late-connect terminal-fallback branches (a client connecting after completion still gets the answer).
- **Gate — ground-truth + triple-neuter, OBSERVED GREEN (`tests/test_compat_narrator_fix.py`, 6/6).** Drives the REAL multi-round `run_task` (narration → web_search tool call → answer) through the ACTUAL compat generators. OpenAI+Anthropic × streaming+sync: wire contains the ANSWER and ZERO narration. NC-1: the old forward-raw-deltas path LEAKS the narration (proves suppression is the fix) + confirms the real generator doesn't. NC-2: mis-mark the answer deliverable=False + clear the content fallback → answer DISAPPEARS (proves the flag drives emitted content). Skips-with-reason on a DB-less env.
- **Two contract-shift tests updated (behavior change is intended):** `test_compat_openai.py::test_streaming_yields_done` + `test_compat_anthropic.py::test_streaming_emits_named_events` — synthetic tasks that fed raw content deltas with no segments/content now set `content` and assert the deliverable is emitted at `done` (raw deltas no longer streamed). This is the correct new contract, not a regression.
- **Verification.** compat_openai + compat_anthropic + narrator_fix + segment_model = 84/84; event_registry + event_emit = 17/17 (touched NO event type — DELTA_RESET still exists for the app path, only the compat surface stopped depending on it). ruff clean on all 5 touched files. NOT committed. Server restart needed (compat module import-time).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a fix relies on an out-of-band signal to RETRACT already-emitted output (DELTA_RESET clears the DOM), it cannot port to a passive wire protocol that can't retract — the durable fix is to NOT emit the unclassifiable content in the first place and emit the classified deliverable at close. Streaming UX is preserved by streaming the channels that ARE classifiable live (thinking, tool progress). Route every surface (sync+streaming × both APIs) through ONE `deliverable_text` helper so the answer definition can't drift between paths.

### 2026-07-07 — Segment/block timeline epic (pt_cb8f98b0cb9b47fb) STEP 1 shipped dark: pure segment SoT + byte-identical 3-channel projections, golden+NC-1 gate green
- **Ask.** Replace the three parallel assistant-turn channels (`task['content']` deliverable string / `task['thinking']` string / `task['toolRounds']` list) with ONE ordered typed-segment list — the robust long-term fix for both the headless "narrator" leak (streaming compat forwards every `delta` incl. scaffolding prose; the app only dodges it via the un-portable `DELTA_RESET` event at `events.py:230` + the lossy `_discard_pretool_prose`) and the grouped-by-type UI. Owner ratified all four §7 decisions: absorb parked epic pt_2f7b65aab89a49ef (segment log IS the authoritative render source); ship steps 1-3 first (frontend timeline = separate follow-on after the responsive epic); keep derived channels as a compat view until every reader migrates then delete; approve the `segments` JSON schema bump (lands step 2, NOT yet applied). Build ONLY step 1 (ships dark) gated on a golden byte-identity test.
- **The two traps, answered from ground truth (2 parallel swarm audits + direct read).** (1) **Append seam = `persist_task_result` (`manager.py`, right after the existing `_merge_tool_rounds` call)** — NOT a token-level hook. The interleaving is ALREADY fully captured at finalization: each llmRound batch's pre-tool prose+thinking+signature is stamped onto the FIRST entry of that batch (`tool_dispatch.py:725-733`) BEFORE `_discard_pretool_prose` zeroes the accumulators, and every entry is `llmRound`-tagged; the terminal round's deliverable prose survives in `task['content']`/`['thinking']`. So ordered `_merge_tool_rounds(task)` + terminal strings = a complete lossless record, and a token-level observer fighting the `content_lock` hot path (`manager.py:2182`) would be redundant. (2) **`deliverable` rule = position-based, INDEPENDENT of the discard:** a `text` segment is `deliverable=False` iff it's the `assistantContent` of a tool-round batch, `deliverable=True` iff it's the terminal `task['content']`. Because assembly reads the pre-tool snapshot and the terminal string by position (not by whether the reset ran), classification stays correct even if `_discard_pretool_prose` were deleted — pinned by `test_deliverable_rule_is_position_based`.
- **Implementation (additive, dark).** New `lib/tasks_pkg/segments.py`: pure `assemble_segments(task, merged=None)` (SoT) + `derive_content`/`derive_thinking`/`derive_tool_rounds` projections. `tool_use` segments carry a nested `result` + a `_round` mirror of the origin dict → `derive_tool_rounds` is byte-identical to `_merge_tool_rounds` BY CONSTRUCTION (the lossless-superset proof; `_round` retires when readers migrate off toolRounds in step 4/6). Wired one best-effort `task['segments'] = assemble_segments(task, merged=_merged_tr)` at the persist seam. Nothing reads it yet.
- **Gate (`tests/test_segment_model.py`, 23/23).** Golden byte-identity of all three derived channels over 5 transcript shapes (single-round / multi-round-with-2-call-batch / thinking-terminal / no-tools / continue-checkpoint). Interleaving-order + once-per-llmRound-prose + signature-preservation asserts. TRIPLE NC-1: strip the terminal `deliverable` flag → `derive_content` returns '' (the classic "discard ate the answer" regression) → diverges; flag narration `deliverable=True` → leaks into content → diverges; drop a `tool_use` segment → `derive_tool_rounds != _merge_tool_rounds`. Regression: `test_continue_lossless` + `test_task_runtime` 59/59 green. ruff + AST clean. NOT committed (owner attribution). No schema/frontend/compat touched — those are steps 2-5.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Before adding a new streaming SoT, check whether the ordering is ALREADY recoverable from finalized state — here it was (merged toolRounds are ordered + llmRound-tagged + carry the pre-tool prose snapshot), so the "single seam" is the existing terminal persist chokepoint, not a hot-path token hook. Make the new SoT a lossless SUPERSET (mirror the origin round under `_round`) so the byte-identity gate is by-construction, not a fragile field-by-field rebuild. And make the deliverable classification depend on POSITION (pre-tool snapshot vs terminal string), never on a sibling reset having run — then an NC can prove that independence.

### 2026-07-07 — Segment-timeline step 1 HARDENED: golden extended to 4 real producer shapes + a real-run_task ground-truth test (owner held the gate higher — synthetic fixtures aren't proof)
- **Why.** Owner accepted step 1's design but held the byte-identity gate to a higher bar: the golden only proved identity for *hand-authored* fixtures (shapes I imagined). Production emits `toolRounds` shapes the fixtures didn't cover, and a golden that never sees them can pass while the real derivation silently diverges — the poisoned-fixture / ground-truth-over-assumption discipline this project runs on.
- **Four production shapes added (each read from its PRODUCER, not imagined).** (1) **Prefetch `fetch_url`** rounds (`executor.py:532`) = `{roundNum,query,results,status,toolName}` — NO llmRound/toolCallId/toolArgs/toolContent → a `None` llmRound would collapse multiples into one phantom batch. (2) **Image-gen** rounds (`executor_image.py`) carry `query`/`results` (a data-uri meta), `toolContent`=None. (3) **Rejected/hallucinated** rounds (`status='rejected'`, `_rejected` set, never executed, toolContent None; from the hallucination-rejection branch). (4) **Non-content terminal** (`tool_rounds_exhausted`/`budget_exceeded`/`content_filter`) — `task['content']` empty + error envelope + trailing tool call. Each asserts: round-trips through `derive_tool_rounds`, no spurious/phantom deliverable, `derive_content` == the (possibly empty) channel.
- **Robustness fix surfaced by shape #1.** `assemble_segments` batch-key was the raw `llmRound`; changed to `lr if lr is not None else ('__no_llmround__', idx)` so each None-llmRound round is its own batch (harmless today — those rounds carry no prose — but a future prose-bearing None shape would be silently swallowed). Verified by the prefetch-interleaved fixture (2 prefetch + 1 real grep → 3 tool_use segments, narration once).

Then asserts the three derivations byte-identical to the ACTUALLY-PRODUCED `task['segments']` (populated dark by the real persist path) — plus that the real `_discard_pretool_prose` ran (narration NOT in `derive_content`). No LLM, no network.
- **Ground-truth OBSERVED GREEN (owner held the gate: skipped ≠ proven).** Owner rightly refused a skipped linchpin test ("a test that never ran could hide a wrong stub signature / a run_task needing more config / a persist path that doesn't populate segments on this route"). Corrected the env DRIFT (not a hack — aligning to the project's OWN pin): `python -m pip install 'sqlalchemy>=2.0'` into the tofu conda env (needed `PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV=false`; box had 1.4.54, `requirements.txt:110` pins `>=2.0`, `_core_schema.py:218` uses 2.0-only `sa.Double`). Did NOT restart the running server (it holds the old package in memory; on-disk swap doesn't reload it). Then `TestGroundTruthRealRunTask::test_derivation_matches_produced_task_dict` **PASSED for real**.
- **The ground-truth test EARNED ITS KEEP on first real run.** It caught what NO hand fixture could: the real `run_task` appends a Sources footer to `task['content']` (`orchestrator.py:456`, because the stubbed answer cited none of the pages it opened). My initial tail assertion hardcoded `content == 'The answer is 42…'` and FAILED — but the THREE byte-identity golden assertions (`derive_content/thinking/tool_rounds`) had already PASSED, proving the segment model itself was correct and only my test's assumption was wrong. Fixed the assertion to the real invariant: answer PRESENT in content + exactly one deliverable segment whose text == the FULL terminal content (footer included). This is the poisoned-fixture lesson in action — the produced dict is the oracle, not my mental model.
- **Verification.** `tests/test_segment_model.py` **40 passed, 0 skipped** (was 23, then 39+1skip). Regression on SQLAlchemy 2.0: continue_lossless + task_runtime + core_schema_parity **111/111** (the drift-fix also un-skipped the 23 schema-parity tests). ruff clean. NOT committed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A byte-identity golden is only as good as the shapes it sees — enumerate the PRODUCERS (grep every site that appends to `toolRounds`: normal dispatch, prefetch, image-gen, rejection) and fixture each, don't trust your mental model of "the" shape. The strongest gate asserts against a dict the real pipeline BUILT (stub the LLM, run the real loop), not a synthetic one. When the ground-truth path needs infra the local env lacks, degrade to a concrete-reason SKIP (never a silent pass, never a spurious red) and PROVE the gap is pre-existing (run an unmodified sibling) before blaming your change — then leave the shared env alone.

New `tabletDrawerMediaQuery()` = `'(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)'` (byte-matches the paper-mode second predicate). `isTabletDrawerViewport()` = `matchMedia(that).matches && !isMobileViewport()` (matchMedia so the `pointer:coarse` half is honored → a fine-pointer desktop narrowed to 900px stays on the split; the `!isMobileViewport` half hands ≤768 to the phone path). `isDrawerViewport()` = `isMobileViewport() || isTabletDrawerViewport()` — the UNION predicate the drawer behaviors now gate on. Migrated 4 drawer gates in main_folders_mobile.js (toggleSidebar backdrop, initMobileLayout auto-collapse, patchMobileConvSelect auto-collapse-on-select) to `isDrawerViewport()`. The swipe gesture already gates on `"ontouchstart" in window` (fine for tablets). Kept the visualViewport KEYBOARD handlers on `isMobileViewport()` (phone-specific, not a drawer behavior). Added a resize/rotate **crossing** handler: track `_wasDrawer`; on landscape→portrait crossing INTO the drawer viewport, auto-collapse (so a left-open desktop sidebar doesn't cover chat with no backdrop); on crossing OUT, drop the backdrop + un-collapse.
- **CSS (new scoped block, styles.css:16011).** `@media(min-width:769px) and (max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` — re-declares ONLY the drawer essentials (`.sidebar` fixed slide-over `min(360px,80vw)`, transform states, tofu-specificity overflow overrides, `.main` full-width, 44px header-action touch targets, 48px conv rows). Deliberately does NOT inherit the ≤768 360px compaction (topbar badge-hiding, avatar removal, font shrink) a ~900px tablet doesn't need. `min-width:769px` lower bound hands ≤768 to the phone master block so the two never both apply. `.toggle-sidebar-btn` is `display:flex` at all widths (verified) so the hamburger is already present to open the drawer; the backdrop is already `position:fixed` + JS-toggled `.visible`.

- **Verification.** Both breakpoint suites 14/14 (incl. all NCs); node --check clean on core.js + main_folders_mobile.js; bundle rebuilt `bundle-eb7ab1f5.js` with `isDrawerViewport`(9)/`isTabletDrawerViewport`(4)/`tabletDrawerMediaQuery`(4)/`tablet:`(1) surviving minification; full sweep (breakpoint + touch-polish + memory-modal-specificity + frontend-api-isolation + bundle-corruption) = **35 passed**. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (bundle + core.js import-time constant).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a viewport needs new BEHAVIOR (not just styling), extend the JS single-source predicate and gate the behaviors on it — a CSS-only widen ships a broken half-state (drawer opens, no dismiss). Reuse an EXISTING sibling predicate byte-for-byte (`(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` from paper mode) so surfaces stay consistent and the drift-guard is a plain equality. `pointer:coarse` must be checked via matchMedia (not innerWidth alone) or a narrowed desktop wrongly gets the mobile drawer — and prove it with a fine-pointer NC. Extraction-and-eval (brace-extract the fn + run under node with a stubbed window) is the right tool for a matchMedia predicate jsdom can't resolve; a poisoned-fixture (`return false`) control proves the eval isn't a tautology.


### 2026-07-07 — Cross-device coordination: single-source-of-truth mobile breakpoint (kills ≥7 hardcoded 768s) + orientation-aware landscape + tofu touch-polish. Measure-first (3 parallel audits), triple double-neuter.
- **Ask (owner).** "Strengthen frontend layout coordination across devices of different aspect ratios (phone/tablet/computer). Further enhance UI/UX, especially the tofu theme." Per the raw-ground-truth preference I ran THREE parallel swarm audits (breakpoint landscape / tofu cross-device quality / JS responsive logic) as HYPOTHESES, then re-verified every flagged token with `read_files` before touching the shared 20k-line `styles.css`.
- **Ground truth confirmed (not trusted from the audit).** (1) ZERO `@media (orientation:)` / `(aspect-ratio:)` queries exist app-wide — everything keys on `max-width` alone; the ONLY orientation-aware rule was one `@media(max-height:500px) and (max-width:900px)` landscape-phone guard. (2) The `768` breakpoint was hardcoded in ≥7 JS sites (a local `MOBILE_BP=768` in mobile_panels.js, two `matchMedia('(max-width:768px)')` in orchestration.js, 7 bare `innerWidth<=768` in main_folders_mobile.js) that had to hand-stay in lock-step with the CSS master `@media(max-width:768px)` block — **no shared source of truth → silent drift risk** (the exact "coordination" weakness named). (3) Two tofu decorations anchored OUTSIDE their box (`.conv-item.active::before` left:-11px; `.thinking-block::after` left:-10px) are NEVER hidden on mobile → clipped by the mobile `overflow:hidden` containers. (4) tofu `.msg-action-btn` (0,2,1... actually 0,2,0 `padding:3px 6px`) out-specifies the plain mobile `.msg-action-btn` (0,1,0 `padding:7px 12px`) → cramped content in the 44px touch box.
- **What I did (3 increments, all shipped + guarded).** ① **tofu touch-polish** (`styles.css` master mobile block): re-assert `[data-theme="tofu"] .msg-action-btn{padding:7px 12px;font-size:11px}` at matching specificity; hide the two overflow-clipped decorations on mobile. ② **orientation-aware landscape**: `@media(max-height:500px) and (max-width:900px)` → `@media(orientation:landscape) and (max-height:600px) and (max-width:900px)` (covers the 540–599px-tall handsets the 500px ceiling missed). ③ **SINGLE-SOURCE breakpoint** in `core.js`: `const TOFU_BP=Object.freeze({mobile:768})` + `isMobileViewport()` + `mobileMediaQuery()` (all on `window`); migrated all ≥7 call sites to them (each keeps a `|| 768` / `|| '(max-width:768px)'` fallback for the core-not-loaded case). core.js loads early in the core bundle (idx ~3) so mobile_panels + main_folders_mobile (core bundle) and orchestration (deferred, runtime-read) all see it.
- **Deliberately NOT done (discipline over momentum, gaming vs improvement).** Did NOT collapse the 720/768/820/900 CSS breakpoint sprawl into one token, and did NOT add a portrait-tablet chat drawer. The drawer is NOT a CSS-only change — its BEHAVIOR (auto-collapse-on-load, backdrop, tap-to-close, swipe) is gated in JS on the mobile predicate; widening only the CSS would ship a broken half-state (sidebar opens on load, no backdrop, no dismiss). Paper-reading mode ALREADY single-panes on portrait tablets via its `(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` predicate, so chat was the sole gap — and closing it right needs a coordinated JS+CSS "tablet drawer" increment, flagged to the owner rather than half-shipped.
- **Tests (2 NEW suites, 10 tests) + TRIPLE double-neuter.** `test_mobile_tofu_touch_polish.py` (6): reuses the sibling `test_memory_modal_specificity.py` specificity engine but adds a `_mobile_cascade()` builder (globals with other @media stripped + the master mobile block, comments stripped so brace-split parsing survives an explanatory `{padding:…}` in a comment) to resolve the winner AT MOBILE WIDTH; NC-1 delete the msg-btn override → tofu cramped `3px 6px` wins again; NC-2 remove a decoration-hide → presence assertion flips; NC-3 revert the landscape header to 500px-only. `test_breakpoint_coordination.py` (4): the JS `TOFU_BP.mobile` MUST equal the CSS master-block `@media(max-width:Npx)` (drift-guard) + a ratchet forbidding new bare `innerWidth<op>768` / `MOBILE_BP=768` / standalone `matchMedia('(max-width:768px)')` in source JS (fallbacks next to the shared helper allowed). All on-disk neuters restore byte-identical.
- **Verification.** New bundle `bundle-c30871ad.js`; grep-confirmed `isMobileViewport`(12)/`mobileMediaQuery`(3)/`TOFU_BP`(5) survive minification. `node --check` clean on all 4 touched JS. Sweep of the touched-area suites (breakpoint-coord + touch-polish + memory-modal-specificity + frontend-api-isolation + bundle-corruption) = **31 passed**; ruff clean. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (bundle rebuild + core.js import-time constant).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When asked to "strengthen coordination across devices," the highest-leverage fix is often a SINGLE-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH for the magic number that N surfaces silently duplicate — plus a drift-guard test that fails if JS and CSS disagree — NOT a cosmetic breakpoint reshuffle. A responsive change that spans CSS+JS behavior (drawer) must move BOTH or ship a broken half-state; verify the JS predicate before widening the CSS. And when slicing a media block for a specificity test, remember the sibling engine's brace-splitter chokes on comment-embedded `{...}` — strip comments first, and model the TRUE cascade (globals + the block), not the block alone, or an NC won't bite.

### 2026-07-06 — Path-LEASE completeness: the HUMAN-facing Held lane (Team panel) — a lease no longer renders as a phantom claimed epic / inflates the badge
- **Gap the owner caught (same class as the deferred→Open-lane leak).** After the backend lease landed, `read_board` returns `kind='lease'` rows (status='claimed') to the board API, but `renderBoard` (`static/js/project-brain.js`) bucketed purely on `t.status` with NO `kind` awareness → a path-lease rendered as a **claimed epic in the Claimed lane** AND inflated the attention badge (`open + claimed`). The agent saw a clean backend "Held" section; the operator saw a phantom claimed epic. The agent-facing + backend halves were solid but the human surface was incomplete.
- **Fix (mirrors the Parked/deferred lane exactly).** `renderBoard` now partitions `t.kind === 'lease'` rows OUT of the status buckets into a dedicated `held` array (badge counts only real `open+claimed` epics — lease excluded). New `_heldCard(t)` renders the held path + holder chip with NO epic lifecycle actions (a reservation isn't work the operator completes/blocks/parks — it auto-expires or the holder releases it). New "Held (do NOT edit)" lane rendered only when non-empty, between Claimed and Parked. New `lock` Lucide glyph in `core/icons.js` (§3.4 SVG, no emoji). i18n `projectBrain.laneHeld`/`heldBy` (zh+en). CSS `.pb-board-card.pb-board-held` (amber left-accent) + `.pb-board-lane-held .pb-board-count` + `.pb-board-held-by`, consistent with the deferred lane.
- **Bundle.** Rebuilt → `bundle-096123e1.js`; grep-confirmed `laneHeld`/`heldBy`/`pb-board-lane-held`/`_heldCard`/`kind === 'lease'` all survive minification. All edited JS already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_board_lease_ux.py`, NEW, 2/2) + NC-FE.** jsdom drives the REAL shipped `renderBoard` over the ACTUAL `#projectBrainBoardBody` from index.html (mirrors `test_frontend_board_defer_ux.py`): a `kind='lease'` status='claimed' row lands in the Held lane NOT the Claimed lane, shows the holder, has no `.pb-board-act` buttons, and the badge reads '2' (open 1 + claimed 1, lease excluded) via the real `_setTabCount`→`#pbTabCountBoard` write. NC-FE byte-reverts the `if (t.kind === 'lease')` partition in a COPY → the lease leaks into the Claimed lane + badge inflates to 3 → `lease_not_in_claimed_lane`/`badge_excludes_lease` flip. Shipped file byte-identical after.
- **Regression caught + fixed (my edit's fault, honest).** Inserting the `heldLane +` line between `lane('claimed')` and the deferred line broke `test_frontend_board_defer_ux.py::test_NC_FE`'s contiguous `anchor_lane` string → updated that NC-FE anchor to include the interposed `heldLane +` line (byte-revert still valid). Full ordered sweep: **184 passed** (7 backend/schema suites + 2 frontend UX suites). `node --check` clean on both touched JS; `test_frontend_api_isolation.py` 4/4 (no raw fetch added).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A board `kind` discriminator must be honored on BOTH surfaces: the agent-facing `render_board_block` (Python, done first turn) AND the human-facing `renderBoard` (JS). A backend partition without the matching frontend partition = the exact "row silently renders in the wrong lane + inflates the badge" bug the deferred lane already taught us. When inserting a new lane between two existing `el.innerHTML` concatenation lines, re-check any NC test that anchors on those lines being contiguous.


### 2026-07-06 — Project Brain broadcast question: broadcast REJECTED, durational file-avoidance served by a Board resource/path-LEASE (kind='lease' column) — complementary to detect_overlaps, triple-neutered
- **Question (owner).** "Is Project Brain complete? Is there a broadcast mechanism? Does it need designing?" Two rounds of push-back sharpened the answer.
- **Verdict (code-verified, not asserted).** NO broadcast/fan-out agent verb exists (the three `project_peer.py` verbs — `build_peer_status`/`send_peer_message`/`intervene_peer` — are all single-`to_conv_id`), and one MUST NOT be added: the blackboard already IS the one-to-many mechanism (Charter = durable info ambient to all incl. future convs; Board = coarse work; feed-note = ephemeral pull; per-target message/intervene = targeted). A `project_broadcast()` has no unique justified use case and would reintroduce the exact storm-class Pillar-#6 invariant #2 (per-(sender,target) window cap) was built to retire (one call = N billed turns = N² fan-out). The owner correctly reframed the ONE real gap — durational file-avoidance ("I'm rewriting styles.css for an hour, hold off") — as a STATE (resource reservation), not a message: a broadcast is ephemeral + active-peers-only (misses the idle sibling the heartbeat wakes 2 min later) + wrong-lifetime; a soft-lease Board claim is durational (TTL) + reaches EVERY sibling incl. future ones (the `[PROJECT BOARD]` block is re-read every prompt assembly) + reuses `_effective_status` for reaper-free expiry.
- **The mandatory `kind` column (NOT cosmetic).** Verified the defect: `select_dispatchable` filters `if t['status'] != 'open'` and `_effective_status` reclaims an expired `claimed`→`open`, so a lease encoded as a plain epic would, at TTL expiry, be selected by `sweep_dispatch` + `_drain_idle_target` and spawn a spurious BILLED kickoff. Fix: `project_tasks.kind` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'epic' (Core def + sqlite `ADD COLUMN` + pg `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, schema v34→35, mirroring the `dispatched` int migration). `select_dispatchable` DENYLISTS `kind=='lease'` (denylist not allowlist → a pre-migration None/'' kind still reads as a dispatchable epic). `render_board_block` partitions leases into a "Held (do NOT edit …)" section, out of the epic lanes. New `claim_lease`/`release_lease` + tools `project_claim_path`/`project_release_path` (ttl_ms exposed; re-claim by same conv refreshes; wired into BOARD_TOOLS/BOARD_TOOL_NAMES so they auto-advertise + auto-route via `_handle_board_tool` — no handler edit).
- **Complementarity with `detect_overlaps` (DRY invariant honored).** `lib/presence/conflict.py::detect_overlaps` is REACTIVE + active-peers-only + file-level (flags two live peers whose presence `files` sets already collide). The lease is PROACTIVE + all-siblings-incl-future + path-level (reserves BEFORE the edit). The lease PREVENTS the collision detect_overlaps would later REPORT; the render branch + dispatch filter read `project_tasks` rows, re-deriving NOTHING from the presence snapshot → no second file-collision aggregation. Presence is the wrong home (ephemeral/heartbeat/active-only, no TTL-claim, NOT injected into a woken sibling's prompt). Charter proposal filed capturing all of this for sibling alignment before code; board epic pt_93ba145251c84d36 posted+claimed+completed.
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_board_lease.py`, NEW, 19/19) + triple-neuter.** NC-1 revert the `select_dispatchable` lease-skip → an EXPIRED lease LEAKS into candidates (proves the billed-kickoff defect + filter). NC-2 neuter the "Held" render branch → held path invisible to siblings. NC-3 revert the `_row_to_task` nullable `kind` default → a pre-migration (kind-less) row raises KeyError instead of normalizing to 'epic' (migration-safety on pre-existing rows). NOTE: NC-3 exercises `_row_to_task` with a synthetic kind-LESS row (a true SQL NULL is impossible — the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'epic', which IS the schema-level backfill guard). Updated the schema-parity golden DDL (both PG+SQLite) with the `kind` column after `depends_on`.
- **Two PRE-EXISTING test-isolation bugs surfaced (not caused) by the new suite's `init_db()` — fixed surgically.** (1) `test_project_board_defer.py::test_NC_C` reloaded `lib.tasks_pkg.executor`, recreating the `tool_registry` singleton and STRIPPING every `@tool_set` handler for the rest of the pytest session (the documented reload-pollution trap) → converted it to the NON-POLLUTING schema-level pattern (reload ONLY `lib.tools.conversation`+`lib.tools`, assert the schema drops the tool; routing proven separately via `tool_registry.lookup`) — exactly mirroring the feed suite's NC-SCHEMA. (2) `test_project_peer.py`'s two `test_handler_hard_abort_*_from_surface` + `test_project_feed_read_tool.py::test_peer_abort_route_stops_target` relied on `_resolve_target_conv_id` fail-open (no `conversations` table); once a sibling suite runs `init_db()` the resolver returns `unknown_target` for synthetic `cB`/`cTARGET` → added the same identity `_resolve_target_conv_id` stub the sibling DB-free tests already use. Both are test-only fixes; the product resolver behaves correctly.
- **Verification.** Full alphabetical-order sweep of all 7 project-brain + schema suites = 177 passed. Lease triple-neuter confirmed load-bearing (3/3). ruff clean on all 7 touched files. `test_project_feed.py::test_auto_path_emits_one_run_concluded` fails IN ISOLATION too (pre-existing autopilot run-record lookup, untracked file, unrelated to this change) — left untouched (out of scope). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed for the schema migration (v35) + new tools to take effect.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When asked "do we need a broadcast?", reframe to root-cause: an ephemeral fan-out MESSAGE and a durational resource RESERVATION are different mechanisms — the blackboard's ambient-injection (charter/board) already IS one-to-many, and a lease reaches the future/woken sibling a message can't. A soft-lease reservation on the Board needs a `kind` discriminator or it gets auto-dispatched as billed work at TTL expiry (verify `select_dispatchable` + `_effective_status` before assuming a plain row is safe). And a new suite calling `init_db()` will SURFACE pre-existing test-isolation bugs in sibling suites (executor-reload registry pollution; resolver fail-open depending on table absence) — diagnose whether they're pre-existing (run in isolation, `git status` the files) before assuming your change broke them, then fix the sibling test surgically.

- **Ask (autonomous board pickup).** Backport OMC TodoWrite + Claude Code TodoWriteTool (Rec 1) and the continuation enforcer that re-injects "incomplete todos!" on a premature stop (Rec 2), per docs/omc-claude-code-backport-analysis.md.
