- **Measure-first verdict (a swarm coder audit + my own read).** The three mechanisms are COMPLEMENTARY, not redundant: (a) zero-deliverable fires on INACTION (no state-changing tool ran this turn) — an agent editing a file every turn never trips it; (b) `_check_suspicious_completion` (orchestrator.py:115) only LOGS content-shape anomalies post-hoc, never prevents/redrives; (c) NEITHER models "agent DID work, declared a checklist, but leaves items ❌ at stop". The enforcer covers exactly that productive-but-premature-stop gap, and cheaply (mid-loop reminder vs a full Critic round). Highest value in the plain `orchestrator.run_task` loop, whose only stop-guard is log-only. Conclusion: BUILD.
- **#1 tool (`lib/tools/todo.py`).** `TODO_WRITE_TOOL` schema (`todos:[{id,content,status∈pending/in_progress/completed}]`, full-list-replace, idempotent) + PURE core `apply_todo_write(fn_args)→(normalized, summary_text)` (drops malformed, coerces bad status→pending, synthesizes missing id) + helpers `incomplete_todos` / `render_todo_list`. Handler `_handle_todo_write` in `handlers/misc.py` persists onto `task['_todos']` (on the TASK dict, NOT in `messages`) and emits `extra={'todos':...}` structured meta for a future UI panel. Registered as a declarative `ToolSpec('todo', _build_todo, phase='capability', provides={'todo_write'})` in `lib/tools/registry.py`, gated on `has_base_tools` (attaches whenever any real tool exists — like memory tools; no new user toggle). ★ Deliberately NOT in `STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS` (verified) → it never resets the zero-deliverable streak, keeping the two guards orthogonal.
- **#2 enforcer (`lib/tasks_pkg/stream_handler.py`).** Single clean seam: the "Normal exit" branch of `analyse_stream_result` (where finish_reason=stop + real content + no tool_calls would `break`). Before breaking: if `task['_todos']` has incomplete items AND real content AND under the nudge cap → inject a `[SYSTEM: TODO CONTINUATION REQUIRED]` user message listing the incomplete items and return `action='continue'` (re-drive) instead of `break`. Bounded by `_todo_continuation_max()` (env `TOFU_TODO_CONTINUATION_MAX`, default 3, fail-open, 0=disabled) tracked in `task['_todo_continuation_count']` — a runaway guard so a model that refuses to finish OR update the list can't loop forever (same discipline as the retry caps). Gated on `round_content.strip()` so an EMPTY stop keeps its own retry path (no hijack). Emits a `phase:todo_continuation` event for UI.
- **`_todos` survives compaction (epic hard requirement).** Confirmed structurally (`grep _todos lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/` = 0 hits — compaction only rewrites `messages`) AND by a live test that runs `execute_compact_tool` over a 60-message list with a fake summary and asserts `task['_todos']` byte-identical after.
- **Tests + TRIPLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_todo_continuation.py`, NEW, 13/13).** Pure core (normalize/summary/incomplete/clear); enforcer positive (redrive + reminder carries the incomplete item), all-complete→break, no-todos→break (plain turns unaffected), cap-bounded→break (runaway guard), env-disabled→break, empty-content→not-hijacked. TRIPLE-NEUTER on the flagship: baseline fires; NC-1 monkeypatch `todo.incomplete_todos→[]` → no re-drive (incomplete detection load-bearing); NC-2 monkeypatch `stream_handler._todo_continuation_max→0` → no re-drive (cap/gate load-bearing); RESTORE implicit via monkeypatch teardown. Plus the compaction-survival test. Harness trap: `analyse_stream_result`'s `append_event` needs `task['events']`+`events_lock` — added a `_task()` helper (a bare dict KeyErrors on the continue path only, which is why only the positive test caught it).
- **Verification.** New suite 13/13. Registration probe: handler + spec present, `todo_write ∉ STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS`. Regression: empty_stop + retry_budget + compaction_invariants 90/90 (enforcer shares the file with the retry logic; the new tool schema injects on every tool turn), tool_registry 16/16. ruff + AST clean on all 4 touched files. Marked Rec 1+2 ✅ SHIPPED in the analysis doc.
- **Scope/Git.** New: lib/tools/todo.py + test. Edited: registry.py, handlers/misc.py, stream_handler.py, docs. NO frontend change (Rec 1's UI panel is explicitly optional/follow-on; structured `extra.todos` is already emitted for it). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed (new tool schema + handler registration are import-time).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Before backporting a "safety" mechanism, MEASURE it against what already exists: here three completion-guards look overlapping but partition cleanly by SIGNAL (inaction vs declared-unfinished-work vs content-shape) — the new one is justified precisely because it's the only one keyed on structured declared scope. Put the enforcer at the SINGLE seam where the loop decides to stop (the normal-exit branch of analyse_stream_result), gate it on real content (don't hijack the empty-stop retry path), and ALWAYS bound a "re-drive until done" loop with a fail-open cap. Keep the todo state on the `task` dict (not `messages`) so it's compaction-immune by construction, and keep the tool out of STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS so sibling guards stay orthogonal.


### 2026-07-06 — #4 CSS epic CLOSED on evidence: one genuine convertible cluster (memory-modal, done+tested), no second exists, @layer big-bang NOT warranted (audit magnitude refuted)
- **Autonomous-dispatch re-pickup of epic pt_717db1c78ffe4991** (title embeds the original audit's claim: "~60 of 173 project-vs-project !important, worst forcing ~30 counter-!important, introduce @layer base,theme,components").
- **Final verification pass (per the stale-docs lesson: verify code, don't trust the epic prose).** Checked the two largest UNVERIFIED clusters from the ground-truth scan: `search-mode-toggle` !important = `::before{display:none}` (decorative-pseudo hide, §3.4) + a mobile `@media` 40px compact override — both LEGITIMATE same-context. `timer-panel`'s count was a grouping artifact (leading-token attribution of multi-selector rules), no convertible war. Confirmed the ONLY over-broad `[data-theme="tofu"] .modal <descendant>` rules left are `.modal > h3` (scoped direct-child, per the generic-modal-redesign memory) + `.modal .modal-actions` (one border-color, no !important) + the `.modal input` I ALREADY fixed with `:not(.memory-modal)`. → NO second convertible foreign-bleed cluster exists.
- **Disposition: epic GOAL achieved, closed done-on-evidence (NOT as an @layer migration).** The convertible foreign-bleed pattern (over-broad higher-specificity ancestor of a DIFFERENT subtree forcing a nested own-token component to counter-!important) applied to exactly ONE cluster — `.memory-modal` — which is DONE: `[data-theme="tofu"] .modal:not(.memory-modal)` source-exclusion (3 selectors), 18 !important removed, `tests/test_memory_modal_specificity.py` 5/5 (specificity engine + on-disk NC-1 neuter + over-narrowing control). The remaining ~185 !important declarations are VERIFIED legitimate (mobile @media, decorative-pseudo hide, metric-locks, equal-specificity variant modifiers, cross-theme overrides) — deleting them ships regressions with zero benefit.
- **@layer big-bang explicitly NOT done, on purpose.** It's the HIGH-RISK global-cascade rewrite the audit itself flagged; it CANNOT be piloted incrementally (a layered rule loses to ALL un-layered rules → wrapping one subtree makes it worse); and with no remaining war it has no payoff. Charter proposal filed correcting the audit magnitude (203 decls total; convertible=the one memory-modal cluster ~18, not ~60/~30). Marked the board epic done.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When an epic TITLE embeds an audit's quantitative claim ("~60 project-vs-project, introduce @layer"), treat the number as a hypothesis, not a mandate — verify by reading the actual competing rules. Here the audit over-counted 3×: it conflated legitimate !important (mobile/decorative/metric-lock/equal-specificity-variant/cross-theme) with specificity-war debt. The correct deliverable was ONE surgical source-exclusion + test, then STOP — not a 20k-line @layer rewrite justified by a phantom cluster count. "Full force" = convert every GENUINE instance rigorously, not force the mechanism onto legitimate code.


### 2026-07-06 — #4 CSS: `.stg-mx` cluster is NOT convertible (audit mis-attribution refuted by direct verification) — measure-first stopped a wrong conversion
- **Directive.** "Full force on #4, extend the source-exclusion to the `.stg-mx` cluster (~20 project-vs-project !important per the audit)."
- **Measure-first REFUTED the premise (3 independent checks).** (1) `.stg-mx` has only **2** `!important` lines, not ~20: `.stg-mx-apply` (L5149-5157) + `.stg-mx-edit:hover` (L5399). (2) There is **NO `[data-theme="tofu"] .stg-mx*` rule** — the tofu `.stg-*` overrides all target a DIFFERENT subtree (`.stg-modal`/`.stg-field`/`.stg-btn`/`.stg-auto`, L12121-12399). (3) Both `.stg-mx` `!important`s are **legitimate intra-design-system overrides, NOT a foreign bleed**: `.stg-mx-apply` is `class="stg-btn-add stg-mx-apply"` (access_matrix.js:186) — two EQUAL-specificity (0,1,0) classes, so its green apply-button color needs `!important` to beat the earlier-in-source `.stg-btn-add{background:none}` sibling; `.stg-mx-edit:hover` beats the same-element `opacity:0`/`0.85` base. Deleting either reverts the button/edit affordance. Same category as the kept light-theme memory-modal `!important`.
- **Second audit ALSO unreliable — verified, didn't trust.** A follow-up swarm audit proposed `.stg-field`/`--s-*` inputs as the #1 convertible cluster (~14 deletable via `:not(.stg-field)` on `[data-theme="tofu"] .settings-panel input`). DIRECT read REFUTED it: `.stg-field input` (L3625-3648) carries **ZERO !important**, and the tofu rule at L11945 is DELIBERATELY CO-DESIGNED with it (comment: "Settings-panel inputs override tofu modal reset — keep pixel-art shadow" — both produce `#fff` + `2px solid var(--s-ink)` + pixel shadow). Intentional COOPERATION, not a war — nothing to convert. The audit conflated the legitimate button `!important` (L5150-5157) with a non-existent input-bleed.
- **Ground-truth cluster counts (direct AST-ish scan, 203 !important DECLARATIONS total).** Largest: mcp-store-header 21, input-box 17, timer-panel 15, sidebar 14, search-mode-toggle 8, paper-left 6, finish-tag 6. The prior "~60 project-vs-project" figure counts LINES differently and over-states convertibility — the big clusters are mobile `@media` overrides (same-context intentional), metric-locks (mcp-store-header 36px baseline), and variant-modifiers on the same element (equal-specificity → !important is the only lever) — all LEGITIMATE.
- **Honest conclusion (discipline over momentum).** The `.memory-modal` conversion was a genuine foreign-bleed (tofu `.modal input` 0,2,1 reaching a nested `--m-*` component). `.stg-mx` does NOT have that pattern. "Full force" does NOT authorize forcing `:not()` onto a cluster the evidence says is legitimate — that fixes nothing and risks regressions. Reported back to the owner for redirection rather than shipping a hollow conversion. The `.memory-modal` pilot (18 !important removed, double-neuter green) stands as the one proven #4 conversion; a NEXT genuine target needs its own measure-first diagnosis (candidates NOT yet verified: `finish-tag` HUD which the audit says is foreign-vs-own and not `:not()`-fixable).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Delegated CSS audits mis-attributed cluster sizes TWICE (counting `!important` by naive line-grep misses multi-line blocks AND conflates a button override with an input bleed). ALWAYS verify a proposed CSS conversion target by reading (a) the exact `!important`-bearing rule, (b) its real same-property competitor, and (c) whether they're different-specificity foreign bleed [convertible] vs equal-specificity sibling / co-designed cooperation [legitimate] — BEFORE editing. A `:not()` source-exclusion only helps when an over-broad HIGHER-specificity ancestor of a DIFFERENT subtree is the competitor.


### 2026-07-06 — Long-horizon (year-scale) run correctness: immutable OBJECTIVE ANCHOR in compaction + autopilotSummaries/transcript_archive retention (measure-first swarm audit → 3 root-cause mechanisms, each double-neutered)
- **Ask.** Owner: can the autonomous driving mechanism run correct over a YEAR-scale horizon without drift, and can context management be optimized? This is a DIFFERENT failure class from the loop guards (turn budget / stuck / diminishing-returns shipped earlier today): those stop a runaway; this keeps a long run COHERENT. Measure-first: 2 parallel coder audits (compaction durability + autopilot/scheduler state durability) + my own read of the L2 pipeline. Converged on 5 gaps; owner ruled BUILD in order #1 retention → #2 archive retention → #3 objective anchor, each double-neutered, holes A+B closed.
- **#3 OBJECTIVE ANCHOR (the correctness centerpiece).** Root cause: `_find_turn_boundary` (`_layer2.py`) preserves only recent turns by token budget; the ORIGINAL objective (first user message) fell into the summarized `old_messages` EVERY compaction → paraphrased, then re-paraphrased (summary-of-summary drift), and `_head_truncate` (L3) could drop it entirely. Only leading `system` msgs were unconditionally kept; the §6 "All User Messages" prompt rule is a SOFT instruction that degrades each pass. Fix: new pure `_objective_anchor_index(messages)` = first real user msg (SAME definition the autopilot `_extract_objective`/`autopilotObjective` pin derives from — ONE notion of "the objective", not a parallel one). `execute_compact_tool` PULLS the anchor out of `old_messages`, summarizes everything-else, and re-inserts the anchor VERBATIM exactly once right after the system block. `_head_truncate` gets a `_drop_pos()` that skips the anchor (pop the next-oldest instead). **Hole B (idempotency):** the anchor is a GENUINE existing message re-used, not a synthesized prepend — a subsequent compaction finds the same message already at the front and never duplicates it (present exactly once, byte-identical, cache-prefix-stable). Verified: survives 3 successive forced compactions verbatim + exactly-once.
- **#1 autopilotSummaries retention.** `_store_run_record` ACCRETES one close-out record per run in `settings.autopilotSummaries` with NO prune; it re-serializes into every settings PUT + IDB write → O(n) per-turn write cost on a year-scale conv. Fix: `autopilot_summary_retention()` (single-source `agent_verdict.py`, env `TOFU_AUTOPILOT_SUMMARY_RETENTION` default 30, fail-open, 0=unlimited) → prune to N most-recent by `ts` inside the serialized RMW; the CURRENTLY-concluding run is force-kept (ts=+inf) so a clock skew can't evict the live fold's own record.
- **#2 transcript_archive retention.** Every force+reactive compaction inserts a full `messages_json` row; only deleted on whole-conv cleanup → unbounded DB growth. Fix: new `DefaultConversationStore.prune_archives(conv_id, keep)` (+ protocol entry) ring-buffers to the newest N per conv via a correlated-subselect DELETE (cross-backend, no OFFSET dialect issue); GC-on-insert in `_archive_transcript`, gated by `archive_retention()` (`_constants.py`, env `TOFU_COMPACTION_ARCHIVE_RETENTION` default 50, fail-open, 0=unlimited). Best-effort — a prune failure never breaks archival/compaction. Recoverability for the compaction VIEWER is now bounded to the last N; the LIVE message list is untouched.
- **Hole A (objective re-anchoring across runs).** `_clear_run_id` wiped `autopilotObjective` on every conclude → the next run re-derived by re-scanning live messages, and after compaction that scan could return a later, now-oldest-surviving turn (drift) instead of the true original. Fix: `_clear_run_id` NO LONGER clears `autopilotObjective` (only the run-scoped `autopilotRunId`/`TurnCount`/`VuHistory`/`Progress`). The pin is durable across run boundaries = consistent with "objective = first user message" (the pin equals what a clean re-scan WOULD return) and robust when the first turn aged out. Verified by a test where the objective survives conclude while counters reset.
- **Tests + NEUTERS (`tests/test_longhorizon_durability.py`, NEW, 15/15).** #3: anchor-index helper (first-real-user, skips VU/empty/system, None when absent); ★survives-3-compactions verbatim + exactly-once (fake paraphrasing summary that NEVER echoes the objective → if the anchor fails the objective is provably gone); anchor position after system; head-truncate preserves objective. NEUTER-#3a: `_objective_anchor_index→None` in L2 → objective IS summarized away. NEUTER-#3b: same in `_head_truncate` (patched at the SOURCE module — it imports the helper locally) → objective IS dropped. #1: retention caps at N, current-run kept, 0=unlimited; NEUTER: retention→0 → grows unbounded. #2: ring-buffer keeps newest N, other conv untouched, noop under cap; env fail-open matrix. Hole A: objective pin survives `_clear_run_id`.
- **Regression + a HALF-LANDED SIBLING caught (honest, git HEAD vs working tree).** 5 `test_autopilot_summary.py` tests failed with `no such table: conversations`. Proved NOT mine: `git show HEAD:autopilot.py` shows `_store_run_record` used `get_thread_db` DIRECTLY (which the test's `lib.database` monkeypatch intercepts) — but the WORKING TREE migrated it to route through `lib.conversations.settings_store.update_conversation_settings` (the charter-DONE "shared serialized settings-RMW helper" epic, "migrate ~13 bare-RMW sites"), which binds `get_thread_db` in the settings_store namespace at import, so patching `lib.database.get_thread_db` no longer intercepts it. My retention code lives INSIDE the `_mut` closure that never runs (the DB read fails first). Fixed the STALE test monkeypatch (patch `settings_store`'s bound names too) since it now covers MY modified functions — 5→green. Also updated my own `test_clear_run_id_resets_counters_atomically` for the intended Hole-A behavior (objective now persists). Full sweep: **249/249** (longhorizon 15 + compaction_invariants + improvements 175 + autopilot_summary 11 + budget_guard 24 + verify 17 + endpoint_finalize 7). ruff clean on all 11 touched files.
- **Scope/Git.** Edited: agent_verdict.py, autopilot.py, persistence_store.py, protocols.py, compaction/{_archive,_constants,_layer2,_reactive}.py + 3 test files (1 new). NO frontend/bundle change (all Python; the incomplete-escalation UI shipped earlier). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server restart needed for the (unchanged this entry) VU prompt from the earlier Part-2 work; these compaction/retention changes take effect on restart. Deferred (owner, follow-up): compaction-audit #2 (summary-of-summary anti-drift: re-summarize from the DB archive, tag `_is_summary`) + #5 (proactive/recurring-agent default budget) — second-order to keeping the objective alive.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Long-horizon correctness ≠ runaway prevention: the distinct risk is the ORIGINAL GOAL drifting/vanishing as context is repeatedly compressed. Fix it structurally — a never-summarized, never-dropped anchor keyed to the FIRST user message (the same thing every "objective" derivation already means), re-used verbatim so it's idempotent (no prefix-growth, cache-stable). Any accreting per-conv map (autopilotSummaries) or append-only table (transcript_archive) on a long-lived conversation MUST have a retention cap or it degrades every turn's write cost / grows the DB unbounded. When a test suddenly fails with an infra error (`no such table`), diff git HEAD vs working tree BEFORE assuming it's yours — a sibling's uncommitted RMW-helper migration silently broke a monkeypatch target, not my logic.


### 2026-07-06 — #4 CSS pilot gets its missing double-neuter (owner-held acceptance criterion): a pure-Python CSS-cascade resolver encodes the specificity invariant
- **Gap the owner caught.** The #4 memory-modal pilot shipped structurally-sound but with ZERO test coverage — "it's visual, no pixel test" was only half true: the AESTHETIC isn't unit-testable, but the STRUCTURAL invariant claimed "provable by specificity math" absolutely is, and unproven specificity math is exactly what silently regresses on the next edit of this 20k-line file. Encode it, don't assert it.
- **Test (`tests/test_memory_modal_specificity.py`, NEW, 5/5).** jsdom can't do this (resolves classList but doesn't apply the external stylesheet or resolve cascade specificity). Mirrors the existing `test_project_brain_tab_css_cascade.py` pattern but needs a REAL specificity engine: `_specificity(sel)` computes the (a,b,c) tuple with correct `:not()`/`:is()` arg-recursion (`:where()`=0), `[attr]`/class/pseudo-class → b, type/pseudo-element → c; `_selector_matches` resolves descendant combinators against a flat ancestor model. Three owner-specified things: (1) DELETION — every `.memory-modal .memory-*` input rule carries NO !important; (2) EXCLUSION LOAD-BEARING — a memory input resolves to its own `var(--m-white)`/`var(--m-border-sm)`, NOT the tofu bleed (`#F5F3ED`/`rgba(184,176,160,0.4)`), PLUS a pure specificity-math assertion (memory `.memory-modal .memory-search-input`=(0,2,0) > base `.modal input`=(0,1,1); tofu bleed `[data-theme=tofu] .modal input`=(0,2,1) WOULD beat memory → that's WHY the source `:not()` exclusion, not an !important on the memory rule, is the correct fix; exclusion=(0,3,1)); (3) NO OVER-NARROWING control — a GENERIC tofu `.modal` input (browser/apply) STILL resolves to the tofu bleed, proving `:not()` removed memory-modal ONLY.
- **NC-1 double-neuter (on-disk, subprocess).** Reverts `:not(.memory-modal) input` → `.modal input` in the REAL styles.css → the memory input now inherits the tofu bleed → resolution flips to `#F5F3ED` → assertion fires; restored byte-identical (verified: 3 exclusions still present post-run). The control test (#3) IS the NC-2 (over-narrowing would strip the theme from all modals).
- **Two resolver bugs found+fixed during authoring (honest).** My first bespoke matcher (a) matched `[data-theme="tofu"] #previewModal` (id selector, spec 1,0,0) against an id-less input because the target-compound check ignored `#id` tokens → dominated everything; (b) matched `[data-theme="tofu"] ::selection` against an input (pseudo-element target) and mis-extracted `.modal:not(.memory-modal)`'s classes as BOTH `modal`+`memory-modal` (didn't strip `:not()` before the class regex) so the generic `{modal}` ancestor failed. Fixed by rewriting to ONE shared `_compound_matches_element` that rejects id/pseudo-element/state-pseudo/unmodelled-attr targets and strips `:not()` before positive-class extraction. Lesson: a hand-rolled CSS matcher must reject the token classes it doesn't model (id/pseudo-elem/attr) rather than ignore them — ignoring = false-positive match at whatever specificity that foreign rule carries.
- **Verification.** 5/5 green (baseline + specificity-math + control + NC-1 neuter+restore); ruff clean; styles.css byte-intact after the subprocess neuter cycle (grep still 3 exclusions). The #4 pilot now meets this project's patch→fundamental standard (load-bearing double-neuter), matching #1/#2/#3. NOT committed (owner attribution). NEXT (owner-authorized): extend the identical source-exclusion mechanism to the `.stg-mx` cluster (~20 more war-!important) with its own analogous test.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A CSS specificity claim IS encodable even when the pixels aren't: parse the real stylesheet, resolve the winning rule with a correct (a,b,c)+source-order engine, assert the winner's value + a pure spec-tuple relationship, and neuter by reverting the source-exclusion on disk. This catches the exact regression class (someone widens the tofu rule back / drops the `:not()`) that a screenshot review would miss on an unrelated future PR.


### 2026-07-06 — Reliability #3: wire premature-SSE-close detection → per-upstream health scoring (log-and-forget symptom → cool-the-bad-slot mechanism), both sync+async dispatch sites, triple-neuter
- **Ask (owner, after a feature-gap audit).** A whole-project feature audit (DEVELOPMENT_DIRECTION.md v0.9.2 baseline vs actual v0.13.0 — ~85% executed) found the flagship remaining agentic backport (todo_write + continuation enforcer) got CLAIMED by a sibling (pt_18abd9ac64094448) mid-analysis; handed that epic's owner the owner-ruled design (B lenient/decaying, cap 2, engagement gate) via project_message rather than duplicating. Pivoted to the single open RELIABILITY gap: premature-SSE-close detection exists but is disconnected from the health scorer.
- **Diagnosis (code-verified, not guessed).** `lib/llm/_sse_core.py::SSEAccumulator.finalize` DETECTS a gateway closing the stream before `[DONE]` — sets `usage['_missing_done']`, and ONLY when `not aborted and not saw_done` (line ~806) — but historically only `logger.warning`ed it. `slot.record_truncation()` (slot.py:286) already cools a slot after 3 consecutive soft failures (exp-backoff, 300s cap). The EDGE between them was missing: both `dispatch_stream` (api.py ~1137) and `async_dispatch_stream` (api.py ~1449) success paths have the slot identity AND the `_missing_done` flag in scope (it rides back on `usage`, alongside the `_dispatch` stamp) but never fed it to the scorer → the offending upstream (the a.md opus-4.7 52×/day cluster) kept getting re-picked. Slot identity does NOT need threading into `_sse_core` — the dispatch layer already owns `slot.key_name`/`slot.model` and the flag arrives on `usage`. That's the correct seam.
- **Fix.** New module helper `_cool_slot_on_premature_close(slot, usage, prev_consecutive_errors)` (api.py, one source of the edge; both sites call it). Guard = reuse the `_missing_done` predicate itself (clean close `saw_done` / client abort never set it → never cooled — the over-cool guard is FREE, not re-derived). Reuses the existing `consecutive_errors>=3 → exp-backoff/300s-cap` thresholds — **NO new hyperparameter** (no §10 sign-off needed; stated plainly). Emits `audit_log('premature_close_cooldown', key_name, model, consecutive_errors, cooldown_until, elapsed_ms, chunks, trace_id)` + a WARNING (CLAUDE.md §2: the new state change leaves a trace, not silent).
- **★ The real bug the neuter caught (design flaw, fixed).** First test run: consecutive premature closes NEVER accumulated past 1 → slot could never reach the `>=3` cooldown. Root cause: `record_success` runs on every dispatch (its latency/throughput/RPM-recovery work is legitimately valid — the connection DID stream) and ZEROES `consecutive_errors`; then `record_truncation`'s `+= 1` starts from 0 every time → self-cancels. This would have shipped INERT. Fix: capture `prev_consecutive_errors` BEFORE `record_success` at each call site, and in the helper restore `consecutive_errors = max(current, prev)` under `slot._lock` before `record_truncation` bumps it → accumulation survives the zeroing while keeping the valid perf-stats update. Caught purely because the positive test asserted accumulation to 3, not just "recorded once."
- **Both sites or half-fixed (owner criterion #6).** Confirmed the async path shares the SAME `_sse_core.finalize` via `lib/llm/astream.py::async_stream_chat` → identical `_missing_done` flag. Wired BOTH `dispatch_stream` and `async_dispatch_stream`. The other two `record_success` sites (:302, :1573) are non-streaming `chat`/`smart_chat` — no premature-close concept, correctly excluded.
- **Tests + TRIPLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_premature_close_cooldown.py`, NEW, 5/5).** Harness modeled on `test_dispatch_stream.py` (`_make_slot`/`_FakeDispatcher`, monkeypatch `lib.llm.stream_chat`; async patches `lib.llm.astream.async_stream_chat` — the DEFINING module, per the existing async suite's pattern, NOT the `lib.llm` re-export, or the `from lib.llm import` at call-time resolves the real fn). Positive: 3 premature closes → consecutive_errors 1→2→3 + cooldown set + `score()==inf`; single close → recorded not-yet-cooled; async parity → same accumulation on the async site. NC-1 (load-bearing) = disable the helper body → 3 premature-close tests FAIL (slot stays hot), guards still pass. NC-2 = drop the `_missing_done` guard (cool on any close) → both over-cool guards FAIL (clean close + client abort wrongly cooled), positives still pass. Each restored byte-identical; final 5/5.

And when the action path sits AFTER a `record_success` that resets the very counter you bump, a single soft failure looks fine but CONSECUTIVE ones silently never accumulate → assert accumulation-to-threshold in the positive test (not just "recorded once"), or a load-bearing fix ships inert. A shared health signal that arrives on the returned `usage` dict belongs at the layer that owns slot identity (dispatch), not threaded down into the transport-agnostic SSE core.

Kept the 1 legit `[data-theme="light"] .memory-modal{...!important}` (intra-design-system override, specificity 0,2,0 = same as shell, legitimately needs !important — NOT a foreign specificity war). Braces balanced 6584/6584; CSS rebuilt → `styles-aa2c5bc4.css` (3 exclusions + reduced !important confirmed in the served minified bundle).

This is a VISUAL change with NO automated regression coverage — the only real verification is a human viewing the rendered memory-modal across tofu/light/dark. Shipping the whole 78-rule war "with full force" without eyes on pixels violates execute-with-care on exactly the un-unit-testable change class where it matters. The memory-modal cluster is a self-contained, specificity-proven pilot; `.stg-mx` (~20) and the broader tofu-theme layer are the next increments AFTER visual sign-off. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new CSS hash serves next start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **"Lift gateway protections / full force" — declined the literal reading, delivered the spirit.** Did NOT disable read-before-edit / write-approval / no-autonomous-commit gates (a one-time "go faster" is not standing authorization to bypass safety on a shared tree with a live sibling). Pushed maximally WITHIN the guardrails: posted the missing epics, shipped the safe #4 pilot, blocked+deferred the genuinely-collision-blocked #6.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) `@layer` is a big-bang-only tool — it can't pilot one subtree because layered<un-layered globally; for a bounded specificity-war fix, exclude the over-broad rule AT ITS SOURCE with `:not()` (narrows match → zero regression surface for siblings) and let the component's own rules win by natural specificity. (2) Distinguish a foreign specificity-war !important (deletable once the source stops bleeding) from an intra-design-system override !important (same-specificity sibling — legitimately stays). (3) A visual CSS change with no automated pixel test stops at a human sign-off gate no matter how "full force" the directive — provability by specificity math covers correctness of the cascade, not the aesthetic outcome.

(2) `paper-reader.js` exposes its reconciler as bare `function`/`var` declarations, NOT `window.X=` assignments; under `eval(readFileSync)` in a CommonJS module they hoist into the ENCLOSING function scope, so reference them by BARE NAME (`_applyRecommendEvent`, `_recStream = s`), not `win._applyRecommendEvent` (which is `undefined`). Mark a CHILD node and assert its survival. Always confirm a neuter bites BEFORE trusting the positive test. jsdom-under-`node -e` needs an IIFE wrapper (bare `return` is illegal) and bare-name refs for `function`/`var`-declared (non-`window.`-assigned) module symbols.

### 2026-07-06 — Paper Reading Mode: tablet / foldable responsiveness (A+B+C) — single-pane breakpoint now covers portrait tablets/foldables + a real fold/orientation refit-on-crossing handler + finger-friendly divider
- **Ask (owner, verified).** "Great mobile paper reading, incl. folding phone / tablet." Measure-first confirmed the mature mobile stack (single-pane + fixed bottom PDF⇄Reader switcher, `_setPaperMobileView`) is decided by a SINGLE `max-width:768px` CSS cliff with ZERO `matchMedia`/`orientationchange`/`resize` listener anywhere in paper-reader.js → a fold/unfold or rotate does NOT re-fit the PDF or re-decide the split, and portrait tablets / unfolded foldables (769–1024px, touch) fall into the DESKTOP split with a 6px finger-hostile `col-resize` divider. Scope A+B+C (skip D). Non-rewrite: extend, don't replace.
- **A — breakpoint policy.** Single-pane predicate widened from `@media(max-width:768px)` to `@media(max-width:768px),(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)` (styles.css:1187). Touch tablets/foldables ≤1024px now get the clean full-screen single-pane + bottom switcher; a MOUSE narrow desktop window (fine pointer) deliberately KEEPS the draggable split; a wide landscape tablet (>1024px) keeps the split (its touch divider already works). Verified the per-theme flair blocks (dark/light/tofu `.paper-*`) touch COSMETICS ONLY (`background`/`border`/`backdrop-filter`/`box-shadow`) — grep confirmed NONE set `display`/`flex-direction`/`position:absolute`/`width` on the panes, so none re-introduce the split at tablet width; the mobile block's existing `!important` display rules win regardless of the 0,2,0 tofu selectors.
- **B — divider hardening.** For the still-split coarse-pointer case (landscape tablet), a transparent `::before` overlay widens the finger hit target to 28px WITHOUT changing the visible 6px line or layout width (`@media(pointer:coarse){.paper-divider::before{...}}` styles.css:904).
- **C — the real fix (foldable/orientation).** New named+global `_paperResponsiveOnCrossing()` inside the existing divider IIFE (NOT a new module): captures `matchMedia('(max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse)')` (mirrors the CSS predicate) + listens `orientationchange`; on a crossing it (a) re-asserts `data-paper-view` — defaulting to `pdf` when entering single-pane with NO view (a desktop-origin body has none → would otherwise show neither pane), via the REAL `_setPaperMobileView` — and (b) rAF-defers `paperFitWidth()` (pane just changed width). rAF-COALESCED (`_scheduleCrossing` single pending flag) so a drag-resize storm fits at most once per frame. Reuses the existing `paperFitWidth`/`_setPaperMobileView` seam, no parallel path. Init moved into `_initPaperResponsive()` (still `DOMContentLoaded`-gated; deferred-bundle load lands with readyState=complete → else-branch runs immediately).
- **Test + TRIPLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_paper_mobile_responsive.py`, NEW, 2 tests / 9 checks).** jsdom drives the REAL `_paperResponsiveOnCrossing` + REAL `_setPaperMobileView` with a controllable MediaQueryList (flip `.matches`, `dispatch()` its `change` listeners) and a spy `paperFitWidth`; synchronous rAF/setTimeout so the coalescing frame AND the nested fit rAF both fire. HARNESS TRAP (caught + fixed): jsdom evals at `readyState==='loading'`, so the module defers init to `DOMContentLoaded` — the harness must `dispatchEvent(new Event('DOMContentLoaded'))` after eval or the crossing wiring never runs. Positive asserts: predicate string == the coarse-1024 mirror, fn exposed, baseline no view, fold-IN defaults to pdf + refits, user switch→reader, fold-OUT refits, fold back IN PRESERVES reader (default only when no valid view), orientationchange refits. TRIPLE-NEUTER (each on a COPY, shipped file byte-identical after): NC-1 = `if(singlePane)`→`if(false)` → fold-in never asserts a pane → view check FAILS (retargeted from the redundant `cur='pdf'` line, which `_setPaperMobileView`'s own invalid→pdf coercion rescues — the load-bearing unit is the BRANCH running); NC-2 = disable the handler's own `paperFitWidth()` → fold-OUT + orientation refit FAIL (fold-IN is masked because `_setPaperMobileView('pdf')` itself refits — so NC-2 must assert the non-pdf-path refits); NC-3 = break the matchMedia predicate to `min-width:99999px` → the predicate-mirror check FAILS.
- **Isolation of a pre-existing failure (git HEAD vs working tree).** `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py::...report_and_review` fails, but `git diff HEAD -- paper-reader.js` shows a HUGE uncommitted sibling diff (+2866/−282; mine is ~77 lines). Proved NOT mine two ways: (1) that harness references NONE of my touched symbols; (2) ran it against a COPY with ONLY my block reverted → STILL fails (file restored byte-identical). It's the half-landed report-generation-language refactor another conversation left in the tree — flagged, not touched (stop-and-report discipline).
- **Verification.** New suite 2/2 (9 checks + 3 neuters). `ruff` clean on the test. `node --check` clean on paper-reader.js. Bundle rebuilt: `paper-reader.js` is a `_DEFERRED_FILE` (lazy feature bundle) → new **`feature-4ff4feac.js`** (grep-confirmed survivors: `_paperResponsiveOnCrossing`×3, `_scheduleCrossing`×4, `_wireResponsiveCrossing`×2, `max-width:1024px) and (pointer:coarse`×1, `orientationchange`×1 — comments stripped). Core bundle `bundle-dce80a8e.js`. CSS auto-content-hashed → **`styles-a3e9f31e.css`** (both new rules survived minification: coarse-1024 predicate + `paper-divider::before`). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundles serve on next natural start; hard-refresh picks them up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A responsive layout decided purely in CSS by a media predicate needs a JS twin that MIRRORS the exact predicate in `matchMedia` and re-asserts state + refits on a crossing — the CSS flips instantly but the PDF laid out at the old width stays wrong until JS refits. (2) When a "default" value is redundantly protected downstream (`_setPaperMobileView` coerces invalid→pdf), neuter the BRANCH that runs, not the redundant line — else the neuter is rescued and looks non-load-bearing. (3) A refit that's ALSO triggered by a sibling path (view-assert→`_setPaperMobileView('pdf')` refits) must be neuter-tested on the path that ISN'T masked (fold-out / orientation). (4) jsdom evals at readyState=loading → fire `DOMContentLoaded` in the harness or DOMContentLoaded-gated init never wires.

### 2026-07-06 — Project Brain content translation as a DISPLAY OVERLAY (charter / decisions / epic titles / activity + peer summaries follow the UI language, source of truth never mutated)
- **Ask (owner).** The Project Brain items should translate with the UI language — anti-flicker/anti-lag, drawing on our front-end rendering experience. Confirmed decisions: all FOUR content sites; a Project-Brain-SCOPED toggle default OFF; translate-only-on-language-mismatch. Hard constraints: (1) original is source of truth — a machine translation must never overwrite/lose the authoritative governance text, and the commit/reject buttons must act on the ORIGINAL proposal, never the translated display; (2) reuse the existing WHOLE-DOCUMENT translate engine (its mixed EN+ZH wrong-language-flip guard + skip-already-target CJK heuristic), do NOT invent a new path; (3) anti-flicker via the patterns we trust (render original first, compare-before-swap in place, rAF-coalesce, (hash,lang) mem+IDB cache, translate only visible, lazy-on-expand, hook `_onLanguageChange`).
- **Measure-first split (the crux).** Read every render path: the CHROME (tab labels/buttons/lane names, ~60 `t('projectBrain.*')` keys) ALREADY tracks the UI language — nothing to do. Only the agent/human-AUTHORED free-text CONTENT renders verbatim: charter north-star + committed decisions (`renderCharter`), board epic titles (`_boardCard`), activity summaries (`buildActivityRow`), peer-message notes (`_buildThreadRow`). This is unbounded MT, NOT an i18n-dict job — a different mechanism. Three of the four sites route through ONE seam, `_clampBlock(innerHtml, rawText)`; the peer note is the fourth.
- **Design — a VIEW laid over the original, never a mutation.** New `static/js/project-brain-i18n.js` (`window.ProjectBrainI18n`). `_clampBlock` now stamps `data-pb-src="<rawText>"` on the content element (`.pb-clamp-inner`/`.pb-clamp`); the peer note stamps it on `.pb-peer-msg-body`. The overlay's `apply(root)` walks `[data-pb-src]` nodes and, per node: revert-to-original when (toggle OFF | empty | already-target | off-screen | collapsed-long-clamp); else translate and `_applySwap` writes the translation into `innerHTML` while `data-pb-src` stays untouched and `title`=original (hover reveals source). The commit/reject buttons read their OWN `data-text` (the original proposal) which the overlay NEVER touches — a translated display can't drift a committed decision. Toggle OFF reverts every node byte-for-byte.
- **Reuse the engine, zero-cost gates.** Translates via `Api.translate.run` (sync, NO convId → NO DB side-effect — pure display), one small call per unique source through a bounded pool (limit 6). Local CJK-ratio `_alreadyTarget` gate: Chinese target skips ratio≥0.30, English target skips ratio<0.10 → an EN charter on an EN UI and a ZH line on a ZH UI do ZERO work / ZERO calls (the engine's own flip-guard is the backstop for mixed input). Cache by `(fnv1a(src)|target)` in a mem map + a dedicated IndexedDB store (`tofu_pb_translate`, fail-open) → a language re-flip is instant/offline.
- **Anti-flicker specifics.** Render fns paint the original immediately (unchanged); `_applyContentI18n(el)` lays the overlay after. `_applySwap` is compare-before-swap (`el._pbShown === translated` short-circuits → no DOM write on re-apply/re-render) and rAF-coalesced (`_scheduleSwap` batches). Visibility gate = only the active `.pb-tab-panel` (class-based, deterministic under jsdom) + the influence banner. Lazy-on-expand: a collapsed `.pb-clamp` (long text) waits until the toggle adds `.pb-clamp-open`, at which point `_wireClampToggles` re-invokes `apply(clamp)`. Re-runs on tab switch (`_selectTab`) and UI language switch (`_onLanguageChange` → `initToggle()`+`applyAll()`).
- **Toggle = PB-scoped preference, decoupled from chat autoTranslate.** `localStorage tofu_pb_translate` (`'1'`/`'0'`, default OFF) — NOT the chat `autoTranslate` flag (different surface/intent). ### 2026-07-06 — Vertical-search block dropped from the LLM's immediate context on the oversized-web_search disk-offload path (debug-panel gap) — relocate the block into the persist index, with an over-greedy DATA-LOSS guard
- **Ask.** Owner (via the debug panel): the vertical search "didn't attach any information to the tool results." Root-caused end-to-end, then implemented the fix + a robustness follow-up the owner flagged.
- **Diagnosis (traced against live data, not guessed).** The vertical plumbing is fully correct: streaming pre-executor threads `vertical` → cache tuple carries it → `tool_dispatch` replays `round.verticals` → the purple vertical card renders in the transcript. The gap is ONLY on the oversized-result offload path. For conv `mr96r7vjcivrf0`, a batch `web_search` returned 2.2 MB (over the 30 KB `web_search` budget), so `budget_tool_result` → `_persist_to_disk` → `_persist_web_search_split` wrote one file per hit and returned an INDEX as the new LLM-facing `toolContent`. The handler had prepended `_vertical_header_for_llm`'s `═══ Vertical Search … ═══ … ═══ Web Search Results ═══` block, but the split boundary is the 20-char `════` per-result separator, NOT the 3-char `═══` header rules — so the block got glued onto **result-1's split file** and dropped out of the index. Verified in the stored row: `has_verticals_field=True` (card OK) but `header_in_toolContent=False`; and on disk the block survives glued to result-1 (grep `Vertical Search` hit 3 of 57 split files — one per batch query). The debug panel shows exactly the header-less index because `/debug-messages` → `build_wire_messages` → `_reconstruct_tool_call_messages` rebuilds each `role:tool` message straight from the stored `toolContent`.
- **Fix (leaf change, `lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_persist.py`, +~40 lines).** Detect-and-relocate, no handler reach-in (the block text already lives in `content`). New module-level `_VERT_BLOCK_RE` (MULTILINE|DOTALL, lazy) matches `[=== Search: <q> ===] ═══ Vertical Search … ═══ … ═══ Web Search Results ═══` — covers both single-search (one leading block) and batch (one block per `=== Search: <q> ===` section). At the top of `_persist_web_search_split`: `findall` the blocks, strip them off `content` before the `════` split, prepend them verbatim to `index_lines`. Result: the vertical block stays in the model's immediate context AND the per-result split files no longer carry a stray header.
- **Owner-flagged robustness follow-up — the over-greedy DATA-LOSS window.** `_VERT_BLOCK_RE` is lazy+DOTALL: if a block's own close `═══ Web Search Results ═══` is missing/truncated (earlier budget pass) OR a real result body literally contains that string at line-start, `.*?` runs FORWARD to the first downstream close — swallowing real result bodies. Since the block is RELOCATED (sub'd out of `content`), an over-greedy match would DELETE result text from the split. Confirmed empirically: a poisoned fixture (broken leading header + result-2 body containing a line-anchored close) produces ONE match spanning results 1–2; an unguarded `sub()` would drop them. GUARD: a legitimate vertical block contains NEITHER a `════` separator NOR a `^[N]` result marker (verified against the 3 real on-disk blocks), so if any match does → over-reach → abandon relocation, leave `content` untouched (worst case: block stays glued to result-1, the pre-fix COSMETIC behaviour — never data loss). Second belt: only commit the stripped body when it STILL matches `^[1]`, else keep original.
- **Fall-through trace conclusion (the crux the owner asked to verify).** The fall-through PRESERVES original content. `_persist_to_disk` passes `content` (a `str`) to the splitter; inside, `content = _VERT_BLOCK_RE.sub(...)` REBINDS the local param only (strings immutable — proved with a minimal reassignment repro). On `return None` the caller's `content` is untouched and the default single-file branch re-persists the ORIGINAL, block intact. So the pre-existing `^[1]`-lost case was already data-safe; the new guard additionally prevents a non-None MANGLED index (the case the `^[1]` check alone can't catch because the stripped body still has `[1]`).
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_persist_vertical_block_relocate.py`, NEW, 7/7).** (1) single-search → block in index, NOT in any split file; (2) batch → both per-query blocks relocated; (3) no-vertical offload byte-unchanged (index still starts `Search returned`); (4) ★ over-greedy guard → poisoned content splits with EVERY `[N]` result body surviving (index+files), distinctive result-2 marker `more body text` preserved; (5) e2e: real `budget_tool_result('web_search', …)` (offload confirmed via "saved to separate files") → `_reconstruct_tool_call_messages` → the debug-panel wire `role:tool` message contains `═══ Vertical Search`; (6) NEUTER: on-disk patch `vert_blocks = _VERT_BLOCK_RE.findall(content)` → `vert_blocks = []` in a FRESH subprocess → `IN_INDEX=False IN_FILES=True` (bug reproduced: block reverts to glued split file), source restored BYTE-IDENTICAL; (7) reload-after-restore still relocates.
- **Verification.** New suite 7/7; `test_compaction_improvements.py` 103/103 (no regression); ruff clean on both files; `_VERT_BLOCK_RE` cleanly lifts the block off all 3 real `mr96r7vjcivr` split files. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (Python-only; no bundle change — the debug panel reads the persisted `toolContent`, which is now correct for FUTURE offloads).
- **Scope note.** Fixes LLM-facing content on FUTURE offloads only; the already-persisted `mr96r7vjcivr` row is not retroactively rewritten (would need a backfill like the oversized-conv migration — not requested). Latent identical gap exists in the other splitters but vertical only rides on `web_search`, so only that one needed it.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) When a symptom-patch RELOCATES text via a lazy+DOTALL regex whose close marker isn't guaranteed present, add an over-reach detector (the extracted span must not contain the sibling structural markers it's supposed to sit ABOVE) — a lazy match is only safe when the close is guaranteed. (2) A splitter that mutates a `str` param and `return None`s is data-safe for the caller by Python value semantics (rebind ≠ mutate), but a non-None MANGLED return is NOT caught by a downstream format-sniff alone — guard the extraction, not just the post-condition. (3) Debug-panel "nothing attached" = check the PERSISTED `toolContent` the wire builder reconstructs from, not the live `round.verticals` (card) — they diverge exactly on the offload path.


### 2026-07-06 — Autonomous-loop stability guards, Part 1: autopilot/VU gains endpoint's two backstops (turn budget + detect_stuck) + a shared cap-stop ESCALATION contract (finishReason='incomplete' / record.incomplete), all via the agent_verdict single source
### 2026-07-06 — Autonomous-loop stability guards, Part 2: diminishing-returns / no-value-progress guard — the fixation detector Jaccard is structurally blind to (VU emits a HARD [PROGRESS: resolved=X remaining=Y] signal)
- **Ask (owner, mandatory not optional).** Part 2 is the literal heart of the objective ("over-fixating on trivialities / meaningless parameter tuning"). Repetition (Jaccard `detect_stuck`) does NOT catch it: a verifier flagging a genuine-but-tiny item emits NON-similar feedback each turn (stuck never fires) while the worker ships a REAL edit each turn (zero-deliverable guard never fires) — yet zero net objective progress. Owner decision: signal must be HARD, not prose-heuristic → require the VU to emit a structured progress line; a fixation guard that itself guesses is not root-cause-correct. Thresholds signed off: window=4, min_resolved=1, target-overlap Jaccard≥0.5, all env-overridable.
- **Single source of truth — `lib/agent_verdict.py`** (pure; both loops delegate): (1) `parse_progress(text)` → `(resolved, remaining)` from `[PROGRESS: resolved=X remaining=Y]` (last match wins; `(None,None)` when absent → fail-open). (2) `autopilot_progress_window()` reads `TOFU_AUTOPILOT_PROGRESS_WINDOW` (default 4; `0`/`<2`→DISABLED; garbage→default; fail-open). (3) `detect_diminishing_returns(ledger, window=4, min_resolved=1, overlap=0.5)` — fires iff ALL over the last `window` turns: (a) every turn shipped edits (non-empty `targets` — a read-only turn breaks the churn run), (b) every turn carries a hard progress signal (no `None` delta → else FAIL OPEN, can't prove no-progress), (c) net new resolved across window `< min_resolved` (≈zero forward progress), (d) every consecutive turn re-touched a substantially overlapping target set (per-pair file-Jaccard `≥ overlap` — re-editing the same spot). `no_progress` was already in `INCOMPLETE_STOP_REASONS` (Part 1) → escalation is automatic.
- **VU prompt (`_VU_ROLE_PROMPT`).** Appended ONE instruction: end every reply with exactly `[PROGRESS: resolved=X remaining=Y]` (X = acceptance criteria VERIFIED done cumulatively, based on what the VU actually checked this turn, NOT the assistant's claims; Y=0 on the TASK_DONE reply). Content-derived `VU_PROMPT_VERSION` auto-rebumped (vd9ce9ecf) — the version-marker test adapted with no edit; **server restart required** to load the new prompt (Python-side, no bundle impact).
- **Plumbing (`autopilot.py`).** Extended the SAME choke-point `_record_vu_turn_and_check_budget(conv_id, vu_text, targets=)` (all three guards in one serialized RMW): parses the VU's progress line, appends a per-turn ledger entry `{resolved_delta, cum_resolved, targets}` to `settings.autopilotProgress` (capped 8, cleared with the run pins in `_clear_run_id` — added in Part 1's clear list preemptively). `resolved_delta` = cumulative-resolved-now minus last-known-cumulative (never negative; `None` when no `[PROGRESS]` line → fail-open). Guard priority `elif` chain: budget_exhausted → stuck → no_progress (stuck is the more specific diagnosis when the VU repeats verbatim). `targets` = the WORKER's `task['modifiedFileList']` paths, populated by the orchestrator (orchestrator.py ~L785) BEFORE `maybe_run_autopilot` runs — verified. Fail-open throughout.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (extended `tests/test_autopilot_budget_guard.py` to 24).** Pure: parse_progress (incl. last-match-wins + absent), fires-on-same-target-zero-progress, NOT-when-real-progress / different-targets / missing-signal(fail-open) / read-only-turn / disabled-window, progress-window env fail-open matrix. Integrated (fake serialized store): `no_progress` fires end-to-end on a baseline turn + 4 flat same-file turns with distinct nudge TEXT (so stuck doesn't pre-empt — a subtlety: the shared `[PROGRESS]` suffix + boilerplate can trip Jaccard≥0.6, so nudges must be lexically distinct to isolate the no_progress path); NOT-when-files-differ. Neuter: monkeypatch `autopilot_progress_window→0` on the imported module → the SAME churning input never stops → guard is load-bearing. 24/24 green.
- **Verification.** Full budget suite 24/24; regression sweep 60/60 (endpoint_finalize 7 + orchestration_engine 45 + autopilot_resume 8); autopilot_verify 17/17 (prompt-content + version-marker adapted). ruff clean on all 5 touched files. No bundle rebuild (Part 2 is Python-only; the incomplete-escalation UI shipped in Part 1's `bundle-7daf54b5.js`, and `no_progress` reuses that exact `record.incomplete`/`finishReason='incomplete'` path). NOT committed (owner attribution). **Server restart needed** for the new VU prompt.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A fixation guard needs a HARD signal or it's just another heuristic — make the driver EMIT structured progress (`[PROGRESS: resolved=X remaining=Y]`) rather than parsing its prose. Fail-open on the signal's absence (a turn with no progress line can't prove no-progress). The detector needs BOTH axes — net-resolved AND target-overlap — because either alone false-positives: zero-progress-but-different-files is legitimately hard multi-file work, and same-file-with-progress is normal iterative refinement; only zero-progress-AND-same-target is fixation. Test-data trap: when isolating one guard in a shared choke point, make inputs distinct enough that a SIBLING guard (stuck's Jaccard) doesn't pre-empt — the boilerplate/suffix you repeat for realism can itself trip it.

- **Ask.** Owner: does our autonomous driving mechanism ensure stable long-term operation without deviating or getting stuck in local unproductive effort (over-fixating on trivialities, meaningless parameter tuning)? Measure-first audit (2 parallel coders over endpoint + autopilot) found: ENDPOINT is well-guarded (MAX_ITERATIONS=10, MAX_REPLANS=3, MAX_ZERO_DELIVERABLE_TURNS=2, `_detect_stuck` at endpoint.py:1018), but AUTOPILOT/VU has — per its own docstring — "No turn cap, no state-change watchdog", never imports `detect_stuck`, and its "refuse to declare victory" driver prompt structurally biases toward never stopping. And BOTH loops' cap-stops were outcome-neutral (endpoint `_finalize` mapped max_iterations/max_replans/stuck → `done`/`finish='stop'`, identical to a clean approval). Owner approved Part 1 as specced.
- **Structural crux (drove the whole design).** The autopilot "loop" is NOT a loop in one function — it's RECURSIVE ACROSS SEPARATE TASKS (`maybe_run_autopilot` hook → spawns a fresh follow-up task each turn). So there is no in-memory counter to bump; the turn budget + VU-request history MUST persist per-run in `conversations.settings`, keyed to the existing `autopilotRunId` pin, written through the serialized `update_conversation_settings` RMW (never a bare clobber). This is what makes both owner-flagged correctness holes fall out for free (see below).
- **Single source of truth — `lib/agent_verdict.py`** (pure logic; both loops delegate, no copies): (1) `detect_stuck` gained an optional `window` param DEFAULTING TO 2 → endpoint's semantics are byte-identical (verified: test_orchestration_engine 45/45 green); autopilot passes `window=3` (three near-identical VU nudges in a row = non-converging; two can be a legit "try again"). Extracted a shared `_jaccard` helper. (2) `autopilot_max_turns()` reads `TOFU_AUTOPILOT_MAX_TURNS`, FAIL-OPEN: unset→default 40, `0`/<=0→unlimited (pre-guard behaviour), garbage→default. (3) `INCOMPLETE_STOP_REASONS` + `is_incomplete_stop()` — the shared "cut off by a cap, not finished" classification (max_iterations/max_replans/stuck/budget_exhausted/no_progress).
- **Autopilot plumbing (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`).** New `_record_vu_turn_and_check_budget(conv_id, vu_text)` — serialized RMW increments `autopilotTurnCount` + appends to `autopilotVuHistory` (capped 6), returns `{stop, reason, turn}`; fires `budget_exhausted` at the ceiling or `stuck` via `detect_stuck(hist, window=3)`. FAIL-OPEN (any settings error → no-stop). Wired into `maybe_run_autopilot` AFTER the VU turn is persisted (reply preserved in history) and AFTER the real-user/abort race-close checks, BEFORE `_start_followup_task` — so a deferred-to-real-message path never ticks the count (hole #2). ### 2026-07-06 — Patch→fundamental-fix program, Item #3: pin a LIVE conv's workspace-root registry against LRU eviction (root cause of the tools.py:323 "conv-state race" self-heal firing)
- **Register framing was WRONG; corrected by measure-first code read.** The epic register called `_roots` a "shared process global" to bind to conv. Reality (lib/project_mod/config.py): a conv-scoped `_conv_roots` OrderedDict with STRICT isolation in `resolve_namespaced_path(conv_id=)` ALREADY exists (2026-05-05 fix), and the key namespaces are already aligned (`convId or id` at both register + resolve ends). So #3 is NOT a missing binding. The genuine residual bug: `set_conv_roots`'s LRU loop `while len(_conv_roots) > MAX_CONV_ROOTS: popitem(last=False)` evicts strict-oldest with NO task-liveness check → a LIVE conv's registry can be evicted by newer convs' cap pressure → its next `name:rel/path` resolve falls to the (clobbered) global `_roots`.
- **Two failure variants; the self-heal only catches one.** If the global lacks the name → `UnknownWorkspaceRootError` → tools.py:323 self-heal recovers via base_path-basename match. But if the global holds a COLLIDING-BASENAME root at a DIFFERENT path → resolve SUCCEEDS and returns the WRONG base → silent write misroute into another conv's tree. The self-heal is exception-only and never sees this silent case. The pin fixes BOTH.
- **Measure-first log evidence (6 days app.log, Jul 1–6, ~60MB).** `Self-heal namespaced path`=0, `unknown root` refusal=0, `workspace root` in error.log=0, across 782 project-task runs. Latent, NOT dead: `MAX_CONV_ROOTS=512` is sized for the SWE-bench profile (comment cites "1236 unique convs"); the eviction-of-a-live-conv path only triggers at >512 recent convs, which this single-user box never approaches. The CLASS fired for real historically: 76 "Unknown workspace root" events on 2026-05-04 under 9-way SWE-bench concurrency (the original global-clobber, pre-per-conv-registry). Verdict: real-but-latent concurrency bug on the exact workload the cap targets → matches the epic's longevity goal. The self-heal STAYS (legit-defensive: model typo/basename-match + genuinely-absent conv_id); NOT retired.
- **Fix (lib/project_mod/config.py).** New `_conv_has_live_task(conv_id)` — reuses the SAME runtime signal as #1's GET-path reconcile (`manager._latest_task_for_conv` + `_chat_runtime` status in pending/running); fails OPEN (probe error → treat idle → never block eviction, since unbounded `_conv_roots` is worse than a rare mis-evict the self-heal covers). New `_evict_conv_roots_over_cap()` — evicts oldest IDLE conv, preserving live ones; if ALL over-cap candidates are live (pathological) force-evicts oldest + WARNs (memory bound wins). `set_conv_roots` now calls it instead of the blind popitem loop; the just-registered conv is newest so never the victim.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_conv_roots_live_eviction.py`, NEW, 3/3 + 2 neuters).** ★ #1 = the corruption case: colliding basename 'src', live convA→/wsA/src, decoy global _roots['src']→/wsB/src, flood past a monkeypatched cap of 3 → assert convA SURVIVES and resolves `src:foo.py`→/wsA/src (never /wsB/src). #2 idle conv still evicted (fix didn't disable eviction). #3 all-live force-evict bounds memory. On-disk neuters run each positive in a FRESH subprocess: NC-1 (`_conv_has_live_task`→`return False`) uses a dedicated variant that registers the live task in the REAL runtime (not the runtime stub the positive tests install — a source neuter would be masked by the stub) → live convA evicted → SILENT MISROUTE to /wsB/src → FAILS; idle-eviction control holds. NC-2 (drop the force-evict fallback → `break`) → all-live unbounded growth → #3 FAILS; misroute control holds. Byte-identical restore verified by post-restore baseline.
- **Verification.** New suite 3/3 + double-neuter green; ruff clean on config.py + test. Regression: `test_readonly_roots` 12/12, `debug/test_project_state_race` (self-heal + isolation + 8-way stress, ok=24 error=0) PASS, `test_tool_root_pill` 7/7 — existing self-heal + per-conv isolation untouched. NOT committed (owner attribution; heavy sibling diffs in tree). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a register says "bind X to conv (it's a global)", VERIFY the primitive first — the binding may already exist and the real bug be narrower (here: unguarded LRU eviction of a live entry). A cache/registry LRU that can evict an in-use entry must gate eviction on liveness; reuse the ONE liveness definition (`_latest_task_for_conv`+runtime status) rather than inventing a second. A self-heal that recovers from an EXCEPTION cannot catch the SILENT-success variant (colliding key resolves to the wrong value with no raise) — prove that variant explicitly in the test. When a test installs a runtime stub for a fn, a source-level neuter of that fn is MASKED — the neuter needs a dedicated variant that exercises the real (un-stubbed) path.


### 2026-07-06 — Poor-network stability, follow-up: pending-sync convs reloaded as `_needsLoad` SHELLS are now detected + hydrated + flushed (closed the durability gap one layer up from the message-level marker)
- **Ask (owner, after accepting the half-open-WS + idb-onabort fixes).** "Improve stability under poor network" is the objective, not "land two fixes." My own audit surfaced a gap that UNDERMINES the durability guarantee this project already built: pending-sync convs reloaded as `_needsLoad` shells are never flushed. Close it root-cause, not patch.
- **Root cause (traced precisely).** The poor-network durability feature marks a failed-send turn two ways: message-level `_pendingSync` (durable in the IDB *messages* store) AND conv-level `_pendingSyncAt` (a runtime flag `convHasPendingSync` checks FIRST). But `_pendingSyncAt` was set only at runtime — `idb-cache.js` `_extractSettings` did NOT whitelist it into the META row. So after a reload a NON-active conversation comes back as a lazy shell (`messages:[]` + `_needsLoad`, the pending tail living only in the IDB messages store), and `convHasPendingSync(shell)` reads `conv.messages` → false. The shell is invisible to `_flushPendingSyncs` (which iterates `conversations.filter(convHasPendingSync)`), so the rescued message is silently stranded until the user happens to open that exact conversation. Same silent-data-loss class as the message-level bug, one layer up. And even if detected, `syncConversationToServer` early-returns on 0 messages — a shell can't be synced directly.
- **Fix (root cause, 3 coupled parts).** (1) `idb-cache.js` `_extractSettings` now persists `_pendingSyncAt: conv._pendingSyncAt || 0` into the META record → the cheap `getAllMeta()` boot scan spots a stranded pending tail WITHOUT joining the messages store; `_clearPendingSyncMarkers`→`ConvCache.put` writes `0` back, clearing the meta marker on a confirmed sync. (2) `hydrateSidebarFromCache` (`conversations.js`) restores `_pendingSyncAt` onto the reloaded shell (so `convHasPendingSync` returns true) and, when any hydrated shell carries a pending tail, kicks `_startPendingSyncPolling()` + `_flushPendingSyncs('cache_hydrate')`. (3) `_flushPendingSyncs`, for a pending SHELL (`messages:[]` + `_needsLoad`), HYDRATES it via `loadConversationMessages(id)` (the cache path restores the durable `_pendingSync` message tail from the IDB messages store) BEFORE syncing, re-reads the conv from the array, and skips (no sync) if the conv vanished / hydration failed / marker cleared — NEVER syncs an empty shell (which would risk clobbering the server). The clobber-guard is load-bearing: an unhydratable shell (cache miss + server empty) is left marked for a later retry, not force-synced.
- **Tests + TRIPLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_pending_sync_shell_flush.py`, NEW, 3 tests / 14 asserts).** Fake IDB with the real meta/message split (meta carries `settings._pendingSyncAt`; `get()` returns the durable `_pendingSync` tail only when a `HYDRATABLE` env toggle is on) + a healthy server that has NOTHING (it never received the failed send). Drives the REAL shipped `hydrateSidebarFromCache` → `_flushPendingSyncs` → `loadConversationMessages` → `syncConversationToServer` under node. (A) shell reload restores `_pendingSyncAt` so `convHasPendingSync(shell)` is true; (B) flush hydrates the empty shell + syncs → server receives the stranded message + markers cleared; (C) an unhydratable shell is NOT synced (no clobber) + marker survives. **TRIPLE-NEUTER** on the hydrate-before-sync step: original fix → (B) passes (message delivered); invariant → the PUT is NEVER an empty message list (`put_never_empty`); defuse (replace `await loadConversationMessages(conv.id)` with `await Promise.resolve()` on a COPY) → shell stays empty → guard skips it → `flush_synced_shell`/`server_got_stranded_msg` FAIL. Real file left byte-identical (`diff`-clean). Console trace confirms the path is genuinely exercised (hydrate→cache-hit→`syncToServer msgs=1`→re-synced), not passing trivially.
- **Verification.** New suite 3/3. Regression sweep 22/22 (pending-sync durability 5 + shell-flush 3 + cache-hydrate-boot + send-failure-persists + idb-onabort 2 + delete-conv-undo). `node --check` clean on both edited JS; ruff clean on the new test. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-2c14eb39.js`** — verified all 3 new fix fragments landed (`_pendingSyncAt: conv._pendingSyncAt`, `shell(s) carry a pending-sync tail`, the flush hydrate-guard `if (!target || !target.messages...) continue` + `cache_hydrate` trigger) AND the two prior fixes survive (`half-open socket to force reconnect`, `put tx aborted (likely QuotaExceeded)`). NOTE: the bundler STRIPS comments, so verify bundled changes by CODE fragments, not comment text (an early grep for the comment string returned 0 and looked like a miss). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A conv-level durability marker is only useful if it rides the CHEAP metadata read (the boot `getAllMeta` scan), not just runtime state — a DB-first sidebar reloads non-active conversations as `messages:[]` shells, so any poller that tests `conv.messages` is blind to them. Persist the marker into the meta whitelist, restore it onto the shell at hydrate, and HYDRATE the shell (cache/server) before acting — but fail-closed: never sync/persist an empty shell you couldn't materialise (that trades a stranded message for a clobbered server row). Same shell-hydration discipline as the `delete-undo-must-hydrate-shell-conv-before-snapshot` skill.


### 2026-07-06 — Poor-network stability hardening: two silent-data-loss / silent-stall gaps closed (half-open push WebSocket wedge + IndexedDB put() hang on quota abort)
- **Ask.** Owner: "Improve the stability of our project under poor network conditions." This area already has heavy layered prior work (durable pending-sync rescue, SSE `state`/`done` keep-longer snapshots, `_pollFallback` null-guard + 2-min recovery wait, VSCode-disconnect recovery). Goal here: find the REMAINING gaps, not redo covered ground.
- **Method — measure-first, 4 parallel audit sub-agents** (frontend SSE/reconnect · WS-push + Api client · backend streaming/LLM-transport/terminal-persist · offline-coordination + IndexedDB). Each briefed with the already-done fixes so it reported only NEW gaps with file:line + scenario + one-line fix. Consolidated punch list; picked the two clearest, most surgical, highest-value (silent data loss / stuck UI) items to fix this session; the rest recorded below as a backlog.
- **Fix #1 — half-open push WebSocket never reconnects (`static/js/push.js` `_sendPing`).** On a poor network a socket goes HALF-OPEN (TCP-dead, `readyState` still OPEN): `_ws.send()` doesn't throw and no `onclose` fires, so push frames (paper/translate/chat/project) silently stop with NO reconnect. TWO coupled defects: (a) `_lastPingSentAt` was OVERWRITTEN every 4s interval, resetting the outstanding ping's age before the 8s `PING_TIMEOUT_MS` could elapse → half-open NEVER detected on a foregrounded tab; (b) even when detected the timeout branch only set latency state, never closed the dead socket. Fix: keep ONE outstanding ping (don't re-send until `_onPong` clears `_lastPingSentAt`, so age accumulates) and on timeout `_ws.close()` → `onclose`→`_scheduleReconnect` (existing exp-backoff+jitter+cap path) re-establishes the socket. Verified the normal ping/pong latency flow (net-latency badge) is intact: first ping on open, latency measured on pong, fresh ping next interval.
- **Fix #2 — `ConvCache.put()` hangs forever on a QuotaExceeded transaction abort (`static/js/idb-cache.js`).** `put()` is the DURABLE local write behind the poor-network send-rescue (`markConvPendingSync` → `await ConvCache.put(conv)`). The write tx wired `oncomplete`+`onerror` but NO `tx.onabort`. A `QuotaExceededError` ABORTS the tx WITHOUT bubbling as a request `onerror` — only `onabort` fires — so the awaited promise NEVER resolves (hangs the rescue caller) and no room is reclaimed for the next write. Fix: add `tx.onabort` (logs, fires a reactive `evict()` so the next write has space, resolves) + route `oncomplete`/`onerror`/`onabort` through a single-resolve latch `_done()` (a request-error bubbles to `onerror` AND then aborts the tx → resolve exactly once).
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (both NEW, all under node/jsdom, skip cleanly without node).** `tests/test_frontend_push_half_open_reconnect.py` (2): a FakeWS whose `send()` no-ops (half-open) + controllable clock/timers drives the REAL push.js — asserts the socket is NOT closed inside the timeout window, IS force-closed once one outstanding ping crosses 8s, and a reconnect is scheduled + a new socket built. Neuter = strip `_ws.close()`+single-ping guard on a COPY → `half_open_socket_closed` FAILS. `tests/test_frontend_idb_put_onabort.py` (2): a self-contained fake IndexedDB with a working tx event model whose next readwrite tx can be armed to `onabort` drives the REAL `ConvCache.put()` under a hard 2s deadline — asserts it RESOLVES on abort (before the fix: hangs → deadline loses), that a reactive evict tx fires, and a normal put still resolves. Neuter = remove the `tx.onabort` handler on a COPY → `put_resolves_on_abort` reports a HANG. Both neuters leave the shipped file byte-identical.
- **Verification.** New suites 4/4. Regression sweep 23/23 (pending-sync durability + connection-failure display + push-latency + cache-hydrate-boot + the 2 new). `node --check` clean on both edited JS; ruff clean on both new tests. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-f3f013ce.js`** (grep confirms both `half-open socket to force reconnect` + `put tx aborted (likely QuotaExceeded)`); push.js + idb-cache.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (no allowlist change). NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Pre-existing FAILURE, ATTRIBUTED NOT-MINE.** `test_frontend_project_brain.py::{test_cross_project_isolation_at_push_routing, test_NC_isolation_wildcard_subscription_leaks}` time out (60s node subprocess) — these eval the REAL push.js + the heavy project-brain.js. I ran the isolation harness manually against BOTH my edited push.js AND a reconstructed pre-edit push.js (reverted only my `_sendPing` diff): BOTH time out at 90s → environmental FUSE+node+jsdom slowness, already documented by a sibling on an unmodified push.js. Not my regression.
- **Backlog (audit findings NOT fixed this session — candidates for a follow-up).** Backend: `_sync_partial_to_conversation` CAS-exhaustion drops a checkpoint at debug-level (escalate + one blind write); orchestrator zero-byte retry-cap vs loop-ceiling mismatch (unify the budget constant); `_interruptible_sleep` only checks `aborted` not supersession; terminal-sync DB-blip swallow has no `_persist_degraded` signal to poll. Offline/IDB: pending-sync convs reloaded as `_needsLoad` shells (`messages:[]`) are skipped by `_flushPendingSyncs` (needs a conv-level `_pendingSyncAt` from an IDB scan at hydrate); a backgrounded SSE that dies WITHOUT a `server_offline`/`interrupted` finishReason isn't re-probed on refocus (probe `activeTaskId`-but-no-live-stream convs via `Api.chat.active()`+`connectToTask`). Frontend SSE: mid-stream idle watchdog only guards first-byte (30s), cleared permanently after; poll path has no last-content-growth watchdog; stuck-detection gated on tab visibility.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A ping/pong liveness probe only detects a HALF-OPEN socket if it keeps ONE outstanding ping so its age can cross the timeout — re-stamping every interval defeats it; and detecting the timeout is useless unless you `close()` to trigger the reconnect path. (2) An IndexedDB write promise MUST wire `tx.onabort` (not just `onerror`) — QuotaExceeded aborts without an request-level error, and a missing handler hangs the awaited caller silently; route all three tx outcomes through a single-resolve latch. (3) When a slow-node/jsdom test fails after you edited the file it evals, ATTRIBUTE it: reconstruct the pre-edit file and time the harness against both — don't assume your change caused an environmental timeout.

WHERE id=?` via `async_execute` (the wrapper does `?`→`%s` + JSONB coercion, same path the conv upserts use); `json_dumps_pg` for null-byte/surrogate safety; `audit_log('conversation_trim_backfill', …)` per write.

Integrity re-check: 0 residual `_wire_fp`, 0 residual done `_partialOutput`, msg67 keeps all 85 apiRounds + 84 toolRounds + `trace_id`/`total_tokens`/`toolContent`. Then `--apply --min-mb 2` across the fleet: **128 rows shrunk, 0 errored, 285 MB reclaimed**; re-run = fully idempotent. New fattest row post-migration is `mqessbrumv5q94` 27 MB = **20.5 MB base64 imageDataUris** — the EXPECTED kept-server-side case (base64 is the render source; the frontend IndexedDB cache strip drops it locally).
