### 2026-07-06 — Conversation-click browser OOM ROOT-CAUSED & FIXED: transient/diagnostic fields (`usage._wire_fp`, done-round `_partialOutput`, inline base64) persisted into message JSON balloon a conv to 100+ MB — trim at every persist boundary
- **Ask.** Owner: clicking certain conversations makes the browser show a memory-exhaustion crash (e.g. mr8vq54hcqch36). Is it frontend rendering? Investigation proceeded in 3 escalating rounds.
- **Rounds 1–2 (elimination, proof-backed).** mr8vq54hcqch36 turned out a red herring (58 KB / 2 msgs — renders in 47 ms / 141 MB RSS via the REAL bundle in jsdom). Then proved the re-render-LOOP theory dead too: drove the real `loadConversation` re-entrant cascade (`_prefetchConvCosts`/`_prefetchConvFileChanges`/`attachCompactionMarkers`/`Artifacts.hydrate` all `.then(renderChat(conv,true))`) and measured each prefetch's `didFetch` — file-changes seq `true,false,false` (stabilizes; `_fcFingerprint` deterministic on the same array → WeakMap re-stamp always lands), cost `false,false,false` (no usage). No self-sustaining cycle. (See memory conv-click-oom-not-render-loop-repro-method.)
- **Round 3 (the real cause = PAYLOAD SIZE, conv-specific).** Owner supplied the size distribution; the fat convs are unmistakable. Pulled them and found THREE transient/diagnostic fields leaking into persisted `messages` JSON:
  1. **`usage._wire_fp`/`_wire_static`** — the DOMINANT vector (19.65 MB in the actually-clicked 121 MB conv mr80gsd8rywph9). A ~226 KB canonical-message LIST per round, captured in `lib/llm/_sse_core.py::SSEAccumulator.finalize` purely for same-run cache-miss diagnosis by `cache_tracking.py` (which keeps its OWN in-memory `prev.wire_fp`). NO render path reads it (grep static/js → 0). Rides into `apiRounds[].usage`, final `usage`, and frontend-only `_liveLastRoundUsage.usage`.
  2. **`toolRounds[]._partialOutput`** on a `done` round — the live run_command terminal buffer (18 MB in mqxbemdr7asicp while authoritative `toolContent` was 2 KB). Never rendered on a completed round.
  3. **`toolRounds[].results[].imageDataUris[].uri`** — multi-MB inline base64 data: URLs (9 MB in mr8l9rq09d34n3). These ARE the render source → keep in DB/PUT, strip only from the local IndexedDB cache.
- **Empirical OOM repro (numbers).** Rendering the RAW fat convs via the real bundle in jsdom drove RSS 140 MB baseline → **362–402 MB** for ONE conversation (survives in node's 4 GB heap; exhausts a real tab given base64→bitmap decode + the payload held simultaneously in the /getResponse download string + JSON.parse result + `conversations` array + `saveConversations` JSON.stringify + `ConvCache.put` serialize). `mqxbemdr7asicp`'s 18 MB `_partialOutput` produced only 354 KB of innerHTML — pure dead weight.
- **Fix (trim at every persist boundary; server is authoritative, frontend mirrors so a re-PUT can't re-bloat).**
  - Server `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`: new `_sanitize_usage_for_persist` / `_sanitize_api_rounds_for_persist` / `_trim_round_for_persist` (returns same obj when nothing to strip → free common case). Wired `_trim_round_for_persist` into `_merge_tool_rounds` (single choke point feeding BOTH task_results + conv-sync; already shallow-copies rounds for thread-safety, trim layers on top, never mutates the live round). Sanitized final `usage` + `apiRounds` in `build_result_meta`. KEEP `usage._dispatch`/`trace_id` (finish_info.js reads them). `_sync_partial_to_conversation` already skips usage/apiRounds.
  - Frontend PUT `static/js/core/conversations.js`: `_trimMsgForPersist` in the `lightMsgs` mapper (strips _wire_fp across apiRounds + _liveLastRoundUsage.usage + done-round _partialOutput; KEEPS base64). Clone-on-trim, never mutates the live message.
  - Frontend cache `static/js/idb-cache.js` `_stripMessage`: also drops base64 `imageDataUris[].uri` (keeps format/filename; render filters descriptors without `uri` → degrades to no-thumbnail, not broken img) + _wire_fp + done _partialOutput.
- **Proven results (data-level).** mr80gsd8rywph9 121MB→8MB DB (92%); mqxbemdr7asicp 22MB→0.5MB (97%); mr8l9rq09d34n3 20MB→11MB DB (base64 kept) / 2.2MB cache.
- **Test + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_oversized_field_persist_trim.py` — 9 checks: server sanitizers (direct import: strip _wire_fp, keep _dispatch/trace_id, keep running-round _partialOutput, non-mutation, free-when-clean), frontend PUT trim (node harness on real `_trimMsgForPersist`), frontend cache strip (node harness on real `_stripMessage`), each paired with a neuter that reverts the trim and asserts the bloat SURVIVES. 9/9 green; ruff clean; `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-2e7aba03.js` (both trims present).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: manager.py (+3 helpers, 4 wires), conversations.js (+_trimMsgForPersist), idb-cache.js (+_stripMessage extensions), new test. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). **Known pre-existing (NOT mine):** `test_chat_manager_migration.py` has 4 failures (`message_queue` table missing in fixture) — verified they fail IDENTICALLY on committed HEAD manager.py.
- **Guardrail / lessons.** (1) A backend-only diagnostic (`_wire_fp`) that is relayed into a widely-persisted struct (`usage`) is a latent 100-MB bomb — diagnostics consumed within a run must be stripped before persist, at the choke point (`_merge_tool_rounds` / `build_result_meta`), and mirrored on every client write path (PUT + IndexedDB) or a re-PUT re-bloats. Any NEW transient per-round field must join `_USAGE_TRANSIENT_KEYS` (py + js) or the trim helpers. (2) `_partialOutput` must be dropped once `status==done` but KEPT while running (reconnect replay). (3) TOOLING GOTCHA: do NOT `git stash`/`git show HEAD:file > file` to A/B a working file that carries heavy uncommitted sibling diffs — on error it silently loses your edits with no stash created; copy to /tmp and diff instead. To A/B a change against HEAD safely: `cp file /tmp/mine; git show HEAD:file > file; <test>; cp /tmp/mine file`.


### 2026-07-06 — Scroll-up "flicker then jump-to-bottom" ROOT-CAUSED: background cost/file-change prefetch callbacks re-rendered via the force-scroll path — added a scroll-preserving `_bgRefreshChat`
- **Ask.** Owner: "Every time I click into a conversation and scroll up for a while, after a moment the page flickers back and forth then jumps to the bottom. Consistently hard to solve — I want a fundamental fix of the rendering method. Maybe translation is replacing the text?"
- **Diagnosis (traced, not guessed).** Translation itself is scroll-safe (`translation.js::_renderMsgInPlace` snapshots + restores `scrollTop` under a `cv-off` guard). The real culprit is a chain translation (and other background events) *triggers*: THREE background-data callbacks repaint via the FULL re-render path.
  1. Opening a conversation calls `renderChat(conv,true)` which fires two async BATCH fetches — `_prefetchConvCosts` (`/api/v1/messages/cost/batch`) and `_prefetchConvFileChanges` (`/extract-file-changes/batch`). Their data is DELIBERATELY excluded from `_msgFingerprint` (async-derived), so the surgical diff can't see it — the original author's workaround was to bypass the fingerprint guard with `renderChat(conv,true)`.
  2. You scroll up → lazy-load kicks in, `_lazyRenderedFrom` shrinks to include older messages.
  3. ~1s later the batch responses land → `.then()` calls **`renderChat(conv,true)`** (chat_render.js:414 & 436) → the full-render path (a) RESETS the lazy window to the last `_INITIAL_RENDER` (20) messages (dropping your force-loaded history), (b) toggles `cv-off` across the whole list forcing offscreen height recompute (**the flicker**), (c) ends in `_forceScrollToBottom()` (**the jump**). A third site: `renderFileChangesBar`'s per-message async fallback (finish_info.js:1022) called a bare `renderChat(conv)` (defaults to full render + force-scroll).
  Translation completing calls `renderChat(conv,false)`, which re-enters those same prefetch callbacks at the top of the function → retriggers the chain — which is exactly why the owner intuited "translation is replacing the text."
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`, +`_bgRefreshChat`).** New scroll-preserving in-place repaint: repaints ONLY `role==='assistant'` bubbles (they alone carry the cost/file-change/finish bars) via `outerHTML`, leaves user bubbles + their reply-quote/ref DOM untouched, snapshots `scrollTop` and RESTORES it exactly (never scrolls), all under the same `cv-off` guard `_renderMsgInPlace` uses so the swap doesn't collapse `content-visibility:auto` intrinsic-size caches and mis-resolve the restore. No-op during streaming (`#streaming-msg` owned by the live UI) or before any message is laid out (welcome/skeleton). Routed all THREE callbacks through it: the two prefetch `.then()`s (chat_render.js) + the file-changes async fallback (finish_info.js, with a defensive `renderChat(conv,false)` fallback where the helper is somehow absent). Net effect: a data-only refresh landing while you read history is now INVISIBLE — the viewport never moves.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_bg_refresh_scroll.py`, NEW, 3/3).** jsdom harness evals the REAL `chat_render.js`, seeds a 4-message conv (user/assistant/user/assistant) + a scrolled-UP reader (`scrollHeight=5000`, `scrollTop=1200`, i.e. NOT at the 4200 bottom), then calls `_bgRefreshChat`. Asserts: `scrollTop` UNCHANGED (===1200) and ≠ bottom (the core anti-jump invariant); assistant bubbles (1,3) repainted, user bubbles (0,2) NOT re-rendered; user DOM nodes keep their `data-orig` sentinel; assistant nodes get the repaint marker; empty-inner (welcome) → no-op no-throw. HARNESS GOTCHA: `chat_render.js` DEFINES its own `renderMessage` (a hoisted function declaration) that shadows any pre-eval stub and pulls in `renderFileChangesBar` (undefined in the harness) → first run threw `ReferenceError`; fix = REASSIGN `renderMessage` to a marker version AFTER `eval(src)` (the eval-scope binding is rebindable). **DOUBLE-NEUTER (source-text substitution via argv):** NC-scroll (`scrollTop = sv` → `scrollTop = scrollHeight`) → the 2 anti-jump checks FAIL, the scope checks still PASS; NC-scope (drop the `role !== 'assistant'` guard → repaint every msg) → the 2 user-untouched checks FAIL, the scroll checks still PASS. Each neuter flips ONLY its own invariant (specificity), proving both are load-bearing.
- **Verification.** New suite 3/3; `node --check` clean on both edited JS; ruff clean on the test. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-4c074384.js` from my run; a live sibling's rebuild then re-minted it to `bundle-2e7aba03.js` — verified to still contain the fix: 4× `_bgRefreshChat` + the minified `scrollTop = sv` restore). Both edited files (`ui/chat_render.js`, `ui/finish_info.js`) are already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` — no allowlist change. Pre-existing UNRELATED failure noted: `test_frontend_autopilot_collapse_gating.py` fails identically WITH MY CHANGES STASHED (`FAIL fn_exposed _applyAutopilotRunFolds missing` — an environmental harness issue), so it is NOT a regression from this change.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `static/js/ui/chat_render.js` (+`_bgRefreshChat`, 2 prefetch callbacks rerouted), `static/js/ui/finish_info.js` (1 file-changes fallback rerouted). NEW: `tests/test_frontend_bg_refresh_scroll.py`. Frontend-only. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A background data-refresh re-render must NEVER move the reader. When async-derived data (cost, file-changes) is intentionally left OUT of the surgical-diff fingerprint, do NOT reach for the `forceScroll=true` full-render escape hatch to repaint it — that resets the lazy window AND force-scrolls to the bottom. Use a dedicated scroll-preserving in-place repaint scoped to the bubbles that actually carry that data, and restore `scrollTop` exactly. Reproduce the "flicker + jump" by simulating a scrolled-up reader (scrollTop well above scrollHeight) and asserting scrollTop is unchanged — asserting only "didn't throw" would miss the whole bug.
- **FOLLOW-UP (same day, owner-directed hardening — the raw-pixel restore was still a smaller version of the same defect).** Owner correctly rejected raw `scrollTop = sv` as the finished state: in the EXACT bug scenario the above-fold heights are NOT static — on first open the cost/finish bars aren't fetched yet, so above-fold assistant bubbles render SHORT and GROW ~1s later when the batch lands; restoring the raw pixel then drifts the reader DOWN by the total added bar-height above the fold. A residual drift in the very scenario that spawned the bug isn't "fundamental." Shipped BOTH flagged hardenings as root-cause mechanisms:
  1. **Anchor-relative scroll restore.** Under the `cv-off` guard, find the topmost `[id^="msg-"]` element still intersecting the viewport (`rect.bottom > containerTop+1`) and record its offset from the container top BEFORE the swaps; after the swaps re-measure that same element and `scrollTop += (newOffset - anchorOffset)` to re-pin it. Correct even when above-fold bubbles change height — the reader's viewport is preserved, not just the raw pixel.
  2. **Compare-before-swap.** Each freshly-rendered assistant bubble is stamped `node.__bgHtml`; a bubble is `outerHTML`-replaced ONLY when its new HTML differs from `__bgHtml`. Unchanged bubbles keep their exact DOM node → manually-expanded tool-round `<details>` state survives a background refresh, and no needless layout. If NOTHING changed the fn returns before touching DOM or scroll at all (same principle as the `data-mfp` surgical diff, extended to the fingerprint-omitted async data).
- **Tests REWRITTEN for the hardening (`tests/test_frontend_bg_refresh_scroll.py`, 3/3).** The old raw-`scrollTop`-unchanged assertion is obsolete (anchor logic now MOVES scrollTop on purpose). jsdom does no layout, so the harness installs a DETERMINISTIC layout model: a `getBoundingClientRect` override + a backed `scrollTop`/`scrollHeight`, in which assistant bubbles grow `short(100)`→`tall(130)` the instant they carry the stub's `data-repainted="1"` marker (simulating the bar landing). Reader parked at `scrollTop=510` so msg-3 is the anchor while above-fold msg-1 grows. Asserts: `anchor_offset_preserved` (anchored element's viewport offset within ±1px after the growth), `scroll_actively_adjusted` (scrollTop DID move to compensate — a raw restore wouldn't), `node_identity_retained` (second identical refresh reuses the SAME node object + a `__keepMarker` survives → expand state safe), plus repaint-scope + user-DOM-intact + empty-inner-noop. **DOUBLE-NEUTER, one per invariant:** NC-anchor (`scrollTop += (newOffset-anchorOffset)` → `+= 0`, i.e. raw restore) → the 2 anchor checks FAIL, `node_identity_retained` still PASSes; NC-compare (`if (el.__bgHtml === fresh) return` → `if (false)`) → `node_identity_retained` FAILs, the 2 anchor checks still PASS. Each flips ONLY its own invariant.
- **Verification (hardening).** New suite 3/3; regression `test_frontend_autopilot_fold.py` + `test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py` + `test_bundle_corruption_guard.py` = 24/24; `node --check` clean; ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-f3f013ce.js`** (verified: 4× `_bgRefreshChat` + `anchorOffset` + `__bgHtml`). NOT committed (owner attribution). Acceptance gate is now the provable one the owner demanded: the rendering method does not move the reader WHEN ABOVE-FOLD HEIGHTS CHANGE — asserted, not eyeballed.
- **Guardrail / lesson (hardening).** "Restore scrollTop exactly" is NOT scroll-stable when content above the viewport changes height — and that's the common case for lazily-arriving bars/badges/translations. The correct primitive is anchor-relative: pin a visible element's viewport offset across the mutation, don't preserve a raw pixel. Pair it with compare-before-swap so an in-place repaint of "the whole region" never re-creates unchanged nodes (which would nuke user-toggled `<details>`/selection state). To test anchor-restore under jsdom (no layout engine), install a deterministic `getBoundingClientRect`+backed-`scrollTop` model where the mutation actually changes heights, and assert the ANCHOR's offset — not the raw scrollTop, which the correct code legitimately moves.


### 2026-07-06 — Mobile browser UX: folder rename/delete was UNREACHABLE by touch (contextmenu-only) + swipe opened the sidebar drawer BEHIND an open bottom-sheet
- **Ask.** Owner: "Promote the optimization design and user experience of the mobile browser interface." The mobile stack is already mature (drawer sidebar, portaled timer/optimizer panels, `.mobile-bottom-sheet`, visualViewport keyboard handler, swipe gestures, the whole tofu-theme specificity war neutralized). So this was a MEASURE-FIRST audit, not a rewrite. Ran an independent `reviewer` sub-agent for a fresh punch list; it confirmed NO remaining specificity bugs and flagged mostly polish. I shipped only the two genuinely high-value mobile-only fixes and deliberately SKIPPED the debatable ones (the flow-sheet `✓` is a consistent selection tick across all sheet items — changing one file would DE-unify it; the 40px composer row is documented-intentional; Escape-on-delete-dialog helps desktop keyboard users, not mobile).
- **Fix #1 (HIGH — unreachable control). `static/js/main/main_folders_mobile.js` `_initFolderTabs`.** Folder rename/delete was bound ONLY to a `contextmenu` listener, which mobile Safari/Chrome do NOT reliably fire on a long-press → the menu was effectively hidden on phones. Added a touch long-press path (guarded by `"ontouchstart" in window`): `touchstart` arms a 500ms `setTimeout` that opens the SAME `_showFolderTabMenu(fid, x, y)`; `touchmove` >10px or an early `touchend`/`touchcancel` cancels it; a capture-phase `click` handler swallows the trailing tap (`_lpFired`) so the folder isn't switched out from under the menu. Reuses the existing menu + prompt fns — zero new UI.
- **Fix #2 (MED — modal swipe bleed-through). Same file, `initMobileGestures`.** A horizontal swipe while a bottom-sheet / portaled panel was open still ran the sidebar-drawer gesture, opening the drawer BEHIND the sheet. Added `_isMobileOverlayOpen()` (`.mobile-bottom-sheet.open, .mobile-panel-portaled.visible, .mobile-panel-backdrop.open, .mobile-bottom-sheet-backdrop.open`) and an early `tracking=false; return` at the top of `touchstart` — the swipe is simply not tracked while a modal surface is up.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_folder_longpress.py`, NEW, 3/3).** jsdom harness (indirect eval → globals, mirroring the concatenated bundle) stubs the many globals `_initFolderTabs` closes over + a deterministic fake `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` (IDs start at **1** — real browsers never return 0, and the source's `if (_lpTimer)` cancel guard treats 0 as "no timer", so a 0-based id would silently defeat clearTimeout; that was the initial 2-test red before the fix). Drives: long-press→menu-opens, trailing-click-swallowed, quick-tap→no-menu, move→cancel, + 3 source-contract asserts for the swipe guard. **DOUBLE-NEUTER on disk:** NC-1 drops the `_showFolderTabMenu` call in the timer body → `longpress_opens_menu` FAILs, quick-tap/move controls still PASS; NC-2 defuses the click-swallow (`if(_lpFired)`→`if(false)`) → `longpress_click_swallowed` FAILs, menu-open still PASSes; both restore byte-identical (`diff` clean, asserted in `_nc`).
- **Verification.** New suite 3/3; regression `test_frontend_recent_project_search` + `test_artifacts_bundle_registration` 17/17. `node --check` clean on the edited JS; ruff clean on the new test. `main_folders_mobile.js` is in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → rebuilt via `build_bundle()` → **`bundle-4c074384.js`** (grep confirms `_isMobileOverlayOpen` + `_lpFired`, 6 hits). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** On touch devices, `contextmenu` is NOT a reliable long-press signal — any desktop right-click affordance needs an explicit `touchstart`+timeout long-press path or it's dead on mobile. And any modal overlay (bottom-sheet / portaled panel) must GATE the global swipe-gesture tracker, else the swipe reaches a surface behind the modal. When jsdom-testing time-based handlers, fake-timer IDs must start at 1 — a 0 id is falsy and silently breaks any `if (timerId)` cancel guard in the code under test.


### 2026-07-06 — Project Brain Team panel showed a bare "conv <id>" instead of the conversation title — backfill the real title from the DB in build_peer_status
- **Ask.** Owner screenshot of the Team/Peers column: every card header read `conv mr93whup` / `conv mr933kr4` (opaque 8-char id). "No need to display 'conv' + the id; at minimum prioritize human-readable conversation titles."
- **Diagnosis (backend, not render).** The frontend `buildPeerCard` (`static/js/project-brain-peers.js`) and the agent-facing `_fmt_peer_status`/`_fmt_feed` (`lib/conversations/project_peer.py`) ALREADY prefer `p.title`, falling back to `conv <shortid>` only when it's blank. But `title` is fed by the presence snapshot, populated at `announce()` time from `cfg.get('convTitle') or ''` (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py:1233`) — which is usually EMPTY (the task config often has no title yet), so `title` is blank and every consumer fell through to the id. Root fix belongs at the aggregation seam, not the renderer.
- **Fix (`lib/conversations/project_peer.py`).** New `_titles_by_conv(conv_ids)`: one `SELECT id,title FROM conversations WHERE id IN (…)`; accepts a stored title (skips literal 'Untitled'), and for never-titled convs falls back to a 60-char opening-user-turn snippet via `first_user_text` (second `messages` query only for the missing set). Best-effort → `{}` on any DB error. Wired into `build_peer_status` AFTER the `_join_peers` call: collect peers whose joined `title` is blank, resolve, and fill (never clobbering a presence-supplied title). This corrects BOTH the Team panel AND the agent-facing `project_peer_status` in one place.
- **Frontend polish (`static/js/project-brain-peers.js` + `i18n.js`).** For the rare genuinely-unresolvable case, replaced the hardcoded English `'conv ' + shortid` (2 sites: `buildPeerCard` header + `_buildStopAffordance` confirm prompt) with a localized `projectBrain.peerUntitled` (`会话 {id}` / `conversation {id}`) — zh UI, no bare "conv" literal.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_peer_status_title_backfill.py` (5, seeded SQLite via `reset_sqlite_for_tests`): `_titles_by_conv` resolves a stored title / falls back to opening-question snippet / omits unknown ids; `build_peer_status` backfills blank-title peers from the DB AND does NOT overwrite a presence-supplied title (stub `presence.registry.snapshot`). NEUTER = `if False and need_titles:` disables the backfill loop → `test_build_peer_status_backfills_titles` FAILS (view keeps blank title); the two `_titles_by_conv` unit tests + the keep-presence-title test correctly stay green (they don't exercise the wiring). Restored byte-identical.
- **Verification.** `test_peer_status_title_backfill` 5/5 + `test_project_peer` 26/26 + `test_peer_message_target_resolution` 9/9 = 40 passed. `node --check` clean on both JS; ruff clean on module + test; 1 (no dup) `peerUntitled` i18n key. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-740bac5d.js`** (grep confirms `peerUntitled` ×3). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves next start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a UI shows an opaque id where a name is expected and the renderer already prefers a `title` field, the defect is usually UPSTREAM: the field is populated from a source (here presence `announce` with `convTitle or ''`) that's frequently empty. Fix at the aggregation seam by backfilling the authoritative value (DB title, snippet fallback) so ALL consumers — panel + agent tool output — benefit at once, rather than patching each renderer's fallback string.


### 2026-07-06 — Drag-and-drop files INTO a project folder (folder browser) — binary-safe save-to-disk, distinct from the chat-attach drop
- **Ask.** "Design a feature so dragging files for upload works not only on the chat window but directly onto the project folder." Owner delegated the design call ("best possible solution").
- **Root gap (traced, not guessed).** The full-page chat drop (`main.js:873` → `#dropOverlay`) routes ALL document-level file drops into `pendingImages`/`pendingPdfTexts` — ephemeral, parsed-for-the-model, never on disk. The project folder browser (`project.js::browseDirectory`, `#folderBrowser`→`.folder-item`) had `mkdir`/`rmdir` but NO way to put a file into a folder. The only file-writing endpoint, `POST /api/v1/project/write`, is TEXT-ONLY (`{path, content}` str → `open(w).write`) — cannot carry image/PDF/binary bytes. So save-to-disk-on-drop was genuinely unsupported.
- **Design decisions (my calls).** (1) Keep the two drop semantics DISTINCT: chat = attach-to-message; folder = persist raw bytes. (2) NEW binary endpoint `POST /api/v1/project/upload` (multipart) since `/write` can't carry bytes. (3) A UI drop must target an ALREADY-ATTACHED root — it does NOT auto-register a new workspace root the way an agent's absolute-path write does (that surprising side effect stays reserved for the model; a stray UI drop is surfaced with "Add it as a project folder first"). (4) Collision → AUTO-RENAME `name (n).ext` (never clobber; reversible). (5) Recorded via `_record_modification` so drops appear in the file-changes bar and are UNDOABLE exactly like agent writes. (6) Full-page chat overlay STANDS DOWN while the project modal is open (`window._tofuProjectModalOpen`).
- **Backend (`lib/project_mod/write_tools.py`).** New `save_uploaded_file(base, rel_path, data, …, on_conflict='rename')` — writes `wb` bytes, reuses `_resolve_write_path` (relative form) / an explicit inside-a-registered-root check (absolute form), `_enforce_not_readonly`, `_dedupe_target` (bounded `name (n).ext`), `_touch_for_vscode`, `_should_record_modification`+`_mod_attribution`+`_record_modification`. New route `project_upload()` in `routes/api_v1/project.py` (multipart `file`+`dir`+optional `name`; `os.path.basename` strips any dir the browser attached to the filename; `@rate_limit(20/60)`). Added `import os`.
- **Frontend.** `Api.project.upload(formData)` in `api.js` (FormData passthrough, `timeout:0`). `project.js`: capture-phase `dragover`/`dragleave`/`drop` bound to `#folderBrowser` (+ `stopPropagation` to beat the document chat-drop handler), target-dir resolution (dropped-on `.folder-item[data-dir-path]` → its dir, else `_browseState.path`), `_runFolderDrop` (parallel `Promise.allSettled` uploads → toast with saved/renamed/failed counts → `browseDirectory` refresh + `loadProjectStatus`). `data-dir-path` added to folder rows. `openProjectModal` sets `_tofuProjectModalOpen=true` + `_attachFolderDropZone()`; `closeProjectModal` clears it. `main.js` chat-drop `dragenter`/`drop` skip while the flag is set. i18n `folderDrop.*` (zh primary). CSS `.fb-drop-active` / `.fb-drop-row`.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_project_upload_drop.py` (8): binary bytes land intact, relative→active root, collision auto-renames (original untouched + `a (1).bin` written), RO root refused, unattached dir refused WITHOUT auto-registering it, write recorded for undo, `_dedupe_target` unit. NEUTER-1 (dedupe returns target unchanged) → the 2 rename tests FAIL only. NEUTER-2 (`if False and not inside_root`) → the unattached-dir test FAILS only. Both restored byte-identical (`diff -q`), 8/8 green. Regression: `test_readonly_roots` 12 + `test_project_tools` = 101 passed. ruff clean on all touched py.
- **Bundle.** `project.js`/`main.js`/`api.js`/`i18n.js` are all CORE-bundle files → rebuilt to **`bundle-6317d3e7.js`** (node-check clean; grep confirms `_attachFolderDropZone`/`folderDrop.savedInto`/`project/upload`/`_tofuProjectModalOpen`). NOTE: an earlier `build_bundle()` returned None once with a transient "Unexpected end of input" at EOF; a deterministic rebuild (and an incremental per-file node-check bisect showing every file + growing concatenation is balanced) was clean — treated as a racy first build (likely a concurrent sibling rebuild mid-write), not a real defect.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up). 4 active sibling convs at start, all on unrelated files — no overlap.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Two drop surfaces with DIFFERENT semantics must be structurally separated: bind the folder-drop handler to the panel in the CAPTURE phase + `stopPropagation`, AND make the document-level chat-drop stand down while the owning modal is open — either alone leaves a race where one file both saves to disk and attaches to chat. A UI file-drop should NOT inherit the agent's auto-register-a-root behaviour: surface the mistake instead of silently expanding the workspace.


### 2026-07-06 — Paper Reader describe-to-recommend follow-ups: draft now persists across mode switches + the global Project-Brain docked bars no longer bleed through the reader
- **Owner-reported (screenshot).** (1) Text typed into the landing "describe it" textarea vanished the moment you left paper mode and returned. (2) The two Project-Brain docked bars (`项目 · N个epic推进中 · N个会话在线` + `本对话 · 受章程约束 · 需避让N项`) showed at the bottom of the reading UI too — "why does project brain appear in the reading interface?"
- **Root cause #1 (draft).** `_showPaperLanding` (`static/js/paper-reader.js`) rebuilds the landing DOM on every entry with an EMPTY `<textarea id="paperDescribeInput">` — nothing captured or restored the in-progress text. Paper mode is an SPA overlay, not a route, so re-entry re-runs the render → blank.
- **Fix #1.** Module-level `var _paperDescribeDraft=''`; the textarea now renders with `escapeHtml(_paperDescribeDraft)` as its body and an `oninput="_paperDescribeDraft=this.value"` save. Draft survives leave→return (kept until the user changes it / opens a paper). Minimal — one state var + a seed + a save.
- **Root cause #2 (bars).** The bars are two SEPARATE global surfaces docked on the chat view: `#presenceStrip` (presence.js) and `#convInfluenceBar` (project-brain.js). `enterPaperMode` hid `.chat-wrapper`/`.input-area` but not these; both toggle their OWN `hidden`/`display` on every push update, so poking their state from paper-reader would be fought by the next push.
- **Fix #2 (decoupled).** `enterPaperMode` adds `document.body.classList.add('paper-mode-active')`, `exitPaperMode` removes it; a CSS rule `body.paper-mode-active #presenceStrip, body.paper-mode-active #convInfluenceBar{display:none !important}` suppresses both. The `!important` override always wins over the bars' own push-driven toggling — zero sibling JS touched (presence.js / project-brain.js unmodified). Confirmed both element IDs exist in index.html and no prior `paper-mode-active` class.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_paper_describe_persist.py`, NEW, 4/4).** jsdom harness eval's the REAL `paper-reader.js` (indirect eval → globals, mirroring the concatenated feature bundle; stubs `localStorage`/`escapeHtml`/`Icon`/`t`/`debugLog`) and drives `_showPaperLanding` twice with a draft (incl. CJK + `<>&"` escaping) seeded between renders → asserts the rebuilt textarea carries the draft (the exact bug). Plus 3 source-contract asserts: draft state+wiring present; `enterPaperMode` adds / `exitPaperMode` removes the body class (region-scoped); CSS override targets BOTH bars with `display:none !important`. **DOUBLE-NEUTER on disk:** reverted the draft-seed + removed the body-class add + broke the CSS rule → all 4 FAIL; restored byte-identical (`diff -q` clean) → 4/4 PASS. NOTE on the jsdom quirk: an inline `oninput` handler runs against the jsdom `window` while indirect-eval binds `var _paperDescribeDraft` to Node's `globalThis` (two globals in Node, one in the browser) — so the RESTORE (the bug) is tested by setting the global directly; the SAVE wiring is covered by the source-contract assert instead.
- **Verification.** New suite 4/4; regression sweep 37/37 (describe-persist 4 + recommend-grounding 10 + bundle-registration 11 + corruption-guard 12). `node -c` clean on paper-reader.js; ruff clean on the new test. Bundles rebuilt from the restored tree: CORE **`bundle-8dab4a7f.js`**, DEFERRED **`feature-3c239929.js`** (grep confirms `_paperDescribeDraft` + `paper-mode-active`; paper-reader.js is deferred → its symbols land in the feature bundle). NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundles serve on next natural start; hard-refresh picks them up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A landing/empty-state built by a re-render function keeps NO input state across SPA mode switches — persist any in-progress text in a module var and seed it back on render. And to hide a GLOBAL push-driven surface from an overlay, use a `body`-class + `!important` CSS override rather than mutating the surface's own visibility state (which its next push would overwrite) — keeps the two subsystems decoupled and touches no sibling JS.


### 2026-07-06 — Autopilot "streaming" perception bug: the bare "Autopilot…" is the SILENT pre-stream window, not a missing stream — attributed it with backend setup phases
- **Ask.** Owner: autopilot has no streaming generation; users watch a vague "Autopilot…" not knowing what's blocking. Whatever blocks the backend must be named truthfully on the frontend, never a vague term. Owner explicitly required DIAGNOSIS-FIRST against a real run (two candidate bugs: phases-emitted-but-not-rendered [frontend] vs genuinely-silent-window [backend]) before any code.
- **Diagnosis (12 real runs, `task_events`).** In EVERY run the first forwarded `autopilot_vu_event` after `autopilot_vu_start` is a `phase` frame (`llm_thinking`/"Generating response…"), correctly wrapped — so the forward/render path is SOUND (a phase supersedes the placeholder once it arrives; verified `_beginVuStreaming`→`twStart` creates the `streamBufs` entry with `phase:null` BEFORE any event, so `buf` is non-null when a phase lands). The defect is the SILENT window BEFORE that first phase: 2.5–26.7s (worst: run 825ff390, event 3062→3063 with zero events between). That window is `run_virtual_user`'s pre-stream work (objective DB read + message assembly + `create_task` + `run_task` warm-up to round-0), which emitted nothing. **Verdict: bug #2 (backend silent window), NOT a frontend render bug.** Repro: `debug/autopilot_warmup_window_probe.py` (run `PYTHONPATH=. python3 …`) prints the vu_start→first-phase gap per run.
- **Fix (backend, `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`).** New `_emit_vu_setup_phase(task, vu_msg_id, detail)`: emits a `working` phase wrapped as `autopilot_vu_event` — the SAME envelope `_VUEventForwarder` uses — so it routes into the VU bubble by `vuMsgId` and renders through the existing `updateStreamingUI` `working` branch (detail verbatim). No new event type; frontend already handles it. Emitted on the PARENT task (the sub-task + forwarding event list don't exist yet at these steps). Two call sites in `run_virtual_user`: before objective-resolution ("Autopilot：核对助手回答、确定下一步…") and before sub-task build ("Autopilot：整理对话上下文，准备生成回复…"). Placeholder made honest: i18n `autopilot.warming` `Autopilot…` → `Autopilot 启动中…` / `Autopilot starting…` (superseded the instant the first phase lands).
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_autopilot_warmup_setup_phase.py` (2): drives REAL `run_virtual_user` (LLM turn + create_task + objective DB read stubbed) and asserts (a) two attributed `working` setup phases carrying `vuMsgId`, and (b) DECISIVELY both precede the sub-task's `_run_single_turn` marker (they fill the silent window, not follow streaming). SOURCE-level neuter = revert helper body to an unconditional early return → positive test FAILS; restored byte-identical (`diff -q`). Monkeypatch NC (`test_nc_neutered_helper_…`) also confirms no setup phases when helper is a no-op. Updated `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_warmup.py` assertions for the new label (`Autopilot 启动中…`).
- **Verification.** `test_autopilot_warmup_setup_phase` 2/2, `test_frontend_autopilot_warmup` 3/3, `test_frontend_autopilot_vu_verbatim` 2/2. `node --check` clean on i18n.js + streaming_render.js + streaming_ui.js; ruff clean on autopilot.py + new test + probe. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-ee22e0bc.js`** (grep confirms `启动中` present; backend `整理对话上下文` detail is Python-side, correctly not bundled). `test_frontend_typecheck` FAILS but ONLY in sibling-modified files (image-gen.js/main.js/net-latency.js/project-brain-peers.js — heavy uncommitted concurrent diffs in the tree, e.g. main.js +160/−39); NONE of my 3 edited JS files appear and my only JS change is a value-only i18n string — pre-existing, not my regression. NOT committed (owner attribution).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Autopilot warm-up is model quota, not fixable in frontend / keep placeholder minimal" (a prior 2026-07-02 ruling) was PARTLY WRONG: the streamed part IS surfaced (phases forward + render), but the pre-stream SETUP window (objective read + message assembly + task build) emitted nothing and IS fixable by attributing each step. When a bubble sits on a vague placeholder, split "emitted-but-not-rendered" (frontend) from "genuinely-silent" (backend) via a real-run event dump FIRST — the fix location depends entirely on which. Attribute every pre-stream step; name what blocks, never a bare placeholder. Skill `.tofu/skills/autopilot-mode.md` updated (Warm-up section rewritten; diagnosis recipe corrected).

- **Why a follow-up.** The initial search-box add (entry below) shipped CSS I hadn't visually verified — owner screenshot exposed 3 real render bugs, then a second round flagged 2 "unify & beautify" gaps still open (hardcoded English on a zh UI; the search input didn't match the Workspace input it was meant to unify with).

Also gave the input a fixed `height:32px`+`box-sizing:border-box` so it reads as a compact component.

Static strings via `data-i18n`/`data-i18n-title`/`data-i18n-placeholder` in `index.html` (label + 2 tooltips + placeholder). JS-rendered empty states in `project.js::_renderRecentList` now use a guarded `const _t = (typeof t==='function')?t:(k)=>k;` → `_t("pm.recentNoMatch"|"pm.recentEmpty")` (the guard is only for jsdom harnesses that eval project.js WITHOUT i18n.js; production always has it → zh). NO `data-i18n*` on the JS-owned empty-state div (would clobber JS output per the known trap).
- **Gap 2 — font unification.** `.recent-search-input` now `font-family:'JetBrains Mono',monospace` (+ `::placeholder{font-family:inherit}`) to match the Workspace `.mp-path-input` "Paste or type a path…" field, so the two right-rail cards genuinely read as one component.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (the i18n assertions ARE green — this is why the entry is marked complete).** Extended `tests/test_frontend_recent_project_search.py` (3→6 tests). NEW `test_recent_search_i18n_zh` loads the REAL i18n.js (zh default, `localStorage` bridged so `tofu_ui_lang`→null→'zh') + project.js under jsdom in a DOM mirroring the real Recent-card markup, runs `_applyI18n()` for the static attrs + drives `_renderRecentList()` for the JS empty states → asserts label=最近 / placeholder=搜索最近… / clear-all title=清空全部 / clear-search title=清除搜索 / no-match=无匹配项目 / empty=暂无最近项目 / no raw `pm.*` key in visible textContent. Two neuters: `test_NC_empty_state_uses_t` (revert empty-state to English literal → `nomatch_zh`/`empty_zh` FAIL, static-attr checks PASS) and `test_NC_i18n_keys_defined` (blank the zh value of `pm.recentSearchPlaceholder` in a COPY of i18n.js → `placeholder_zh` FAILs empty, empty-state keys PASS). Both restore byte-identical (diff-verified). Harness gotchas solved: reset the filter via `_filterRecentProjects('')` not a stray outer-scope `_recentFilter=''`; check raw-key leak on `textContent` not `innerHTML` (the `data-i18n*` ATTRIBUTES legitimately contain the key).
- **Verification.** 6/6 green in this file; i18n ratchet `test_frontend_i18n_key_coverage.py` 8/8; NO duplicate i18n keys (1921 total, 0 dups; all 6 `pm.*` present); `node --check` clean on project.js + i18n.js; ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-4c074384.js`** (grep confirms `pm.recentSearchPlaceholder`/`pm.recentEmpty`/`pm.recentNoMatch`/`_filterRecentProjects` survived minify). CSS not bundled (served directly via css_bundler hash at request time) → no rebuild needed. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) NEVER ship CSS you haven't reasoned about the CASCADE for — an absolutely-positioned child ignores parent flex centering; a class rule with an explicit `display` beats `[hidden]` (add `.cls[hidden]{display:none}`); a theme override must MATCH or exceed the specificity of the base rule it fights (`.modal input` = 0,2,1). (2) On a zh-default UI, hardcoded English on a user-facing surface is a display-accuracy defect, not a cosmetic nicety — route through `t()`/`data-i18n`. (3) To i18n-test without a browser: load the real i18n.js (zh default) under jsdom, run `_applyI18n()` + the JS render fn, assert the zh output; neuter both the render call AND a key value to prove each layer is load-bearing.

### 2026-07-06 — Paper Reader "describe it → recommend" landing feature: fuzzy free-text → arXiv-GROUNDED, addable paper cards + false-premise correction banner
- **Ask.** Owner half-remembered "a few diffusion **language model** papers won Best/Outstanding at NeurIPS 2025" but forgot the titles, and wanted to *describe* a paper in the empty-state UI and get a nice UX recommending likely papers to add. The empty state (`_showPaperLanding`) only supported exact-title search / arXiv-ID paste — useless when you only recall *what a paper was about*.
- **Reality-check baked into the feature (the actual product value).** Verified against the NeurIPS blog + `neurips.cc/virtual/2025/awards_detail`: there were **7 award papers** (4 Best + 3 Runner-up); exactly ONE touches diffusion — *Why Diffusion Models Don't Memorize* (`2505.17638`), a **generalization-theory** paper, NOT an LM. The buzzy diffusion-LM work the owner meant — LLaDA `2502.09992` (Oral), d1 `2504.12216` (poster), Prophet `2508.19982` (poster) — were **Orals/posters, never award winners**. So the premise was a conflation; the feature *corrects* it rather than feeding it back.
- **Backend — grounding engine (`lib/paper/recommend_engine.py`, NEW).** `recommend_papers(description, max_results)`: one `dispatch_chat` turn (strict-JSON system prompt) interprets the fuzzy description into candidate {title, arxiv_id?, venue?, why} + an optional {correction.note, correction.paper}. **Hard grounding gate (the whole point):** NO card surfaces unless it resolves through the EXISTING `search_arxiv`/`fetch_arxiv_title` seam to a real arXiv paper — `_ground_candidate` (a) prefers an exact-id match among search hits, (b) accepts the top hit only when `_title_grounded` (≥2 shared significant tokens, stopword-filtered, ≥40% of the claim) so a tangential top hit is rejected, (c) falls back to direct-id verify via `fetch_arxiv_title` when search misses a real id, else DROPS it (debug-logged). The model's interpretive prose (`why`/correction `note`) is kept; the *papers* it points at are always arXiv-verified. Every failure path logs per §2 (LLM call fail → `error`+`llmError:true`; JSON parse miss → `warning`; grounding miss → `debug`; nothing grounded → `info`). Exported via the `lib.paper` facade.
- **Backend — route (`routes/paper.py`).** `POST /api/v1/paper/recommend` (native-async, mirrors `search_arxiv_route`; `recommend_papers` runs off-loop via `asyncio.to_thread`). Returns `{ok, query, llmError, correction:{note,paper}|null, results:[…card…]}` where every card carries a real `arxiv_id`.
- **Frontend (`static/js/paper-reader.js` — DEFERRED feature module, already in `_DEFERRED_FILES`, NOT `_BUNDLE_FILES`).** Added a "describe it" affordance below the arXiv box on `_showPaperLanding` (divider + labelled textarea + Recommend button; Ctrl/⌘-Enter submits). New `_submitPaperDescribe` → `_recommendPapers` (calls `Api.paper.recommend`) → `_renderPaperRecommendations`, which **REUSES the existing `.paper-result-card` markup** (added a "why this matches" line + venue chip) and clicks straight into the existing `_fetchArxivPaper(arxiv_id)` — **zero new ingest code**. The **correction banner is first-class**: an SVG info glyph (CLAUDE §3.4, not emoji) + note + an optional "the paper that actually won" card wired to `_openRecommendCorrection`. `llmError` (interpretation failed) is distinguished from "grounded nothing" (empty state / note-only).
- **API client (`static/js/api.js`).** `Api.paper.recommend(description, maxResults)` → `POST /api/v1/paper/recommend` with `onError:'null'`. No raw fetch (api-isolation guard stays 4/4).
- **i18n (`static/js/i18n.js`, +13 `paper.*` keys, zh primary).** `describeOr/describeLabel/describePlaceholder/describeBtn/recommending/recommendTitle/recommendHint/recommendNoResults/recommendFailed/correctionTitle/correctionActual`. Guarded `_tt` fallback used at every JS render site. The recommend view is transient (reverts to landing on relaunch) so the existing `_onLanguageChange` `paperMode` block already re-renders the landing; no new refresh hook needed. Key-coverage audit: MISSING none, DUP none.
- **CSS (`static/styles.css`).** `.paper-describe-*` (divider/label/textarea/button), `.paper-result-why` (accent check-glyph line), `.paper-card-venue` chip, `.paper-correction*` warn-toned banner + offer card. Reuses card tokens; served directly (hard-refresh only).
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_paper_recommend_grounding.py`, NEW, 10/10).** Fully offline (monkeypatches `dispatch_chat`/`search_arxiv`/`fetch_arxiv_title` on the engine module + a fake-arXiv title→metadata map). Covers: hallucinated candidate dropped + both real dLLM papers grounded; cards carry model why/venue + REAL arXiv title/authors; correction grounds the actual winner; correction note survives an ungroundable offered paper; tangential real top-hit rejected; direct-id-verify fallback; llmError flag; unparseable reply; empty description. **DOUBLE-NEUTER** `test_neuter_confirms_gate_is_load_bearing`: real engine BLOCKS the hallucination → neuter `_ground_candidate` to a pass-through fabricator (unique minted id per candidate so dedup can't mask the leak) → hallucination LEAKS (invariant breaks) → restore BLOCKS again. (First neuter attempt falsely passed because the passthrough gave id-less candidates a shared fallback id → dedup hid the leak; fixed to mint unique ids — a reminder that a neuter must isolate the ONE mechanism under test.)
- **Verification.** New suite 10/10; existing `test_paper_title_recovery` 18/18 (no regression); guard suites `test_artifacts_bundle_registration`/`test_bundle_corruption_guard`/`test_frontend_api_isolation` 27/27. `node -c` clean on all 3 edited JS; ruff clean on engine + route + test; facade import OK. Bundles rebuilt from the shared tree: **CORE `bundle-33adbe06.js`** (has the `paper.*` keys + `Api.paper.recommend`) + **DEFERRED `feature-c5c8f5b6.js`** (has `_submitPaperDescribe`/`_recommendPapers`/`_renderPaperRecommendations`/`_openRecommendResult`/`_openRecommendCorrection`/`paper-describe-box`). NOTE: `paper-reader.js` is a DEFERRED module → its symbols land in `feature-<hash>.js`, NOT `bundle-<hash>.js`; verify the right bundle (an early check grepped only core and looked empty).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Live-peer check before editing: 4 active siblings all on Project-Brain work (mr933kr4/mr93529f/mr939tdu/mr93i46r) — no `paper-reader.js`/`routes/paper.py` overlap. NEW: `lib/paper/recommend_engine.py`, `tests/test_paper_recommend_grounding.py`. Edited: `lib/paper/__init__.py`, `routes/paper.py`, `static/js/{paper-reader.js,api.js,i18n.js}`, `static/styles.css`. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundles serve on next natural start; hard-refresh picks them up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When adding an LLM-assisted "find me a thing" surface, the trust boundary is a GROUNDING GATE, not the prompt: interpret freely with the model, but only surface items that resolve against a real, authoritative index (here arXiv via the existing seam) — drop+log anything else. And when moving/adding functions to a DEFERRED feature module, verify symbols in the `feature-<hash>.js` bundle, not the core one.


### 2026-07-06 — Debug-panel messages showed "one letter per line" for the modified-files reminder: `_extract_recently_accessed_files` iterated a string-typed `reads` char-by-char
- **Symptom (owner screenshot, conv `mr4e8pnxbv440z`).** The `<system-reminder>` "## Recently Modified Files" block in a conversation's `messages` rendered each list entry as a SINGLE CHARACTER (`  - [`, `  - {`, `  - "`, `  - p`, `  - a`, `  - t`, `  - h`, …) followed by the correct real file paths lower down. Owner asked for the root cause.
- **Root cause (confirmed against the LIVE DB, then reproduced byte-for-byte).** `lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_layer2.py::_extract_recently_accessed_files`, the `read_files` branch, did `for spec in args.get('reads', []) or []`. In this conversation several `read_files` tool calls were stored with `reads` as a JSON **string** (sometimes truncated/malformed), e.g. `'[{"path": "human_eval_web/materials/web_items.py", "start_line": 366, "end_line": 418]'`. Iterating a `str` yields individual CHARACTERS; the `elif isinstance(spec, str): p = spec.strip()` branch then accepted each char as a "file path". They were deduped by `files_set` (→ the *unique* chars of `[{"path":...}]`) and rendered one-per-line by `lib/tasks_pkg/attachments.py::_get_modified_files_attachment` (`'\n'.join(f'  - {f}' for f in files)`). Verified by loading the real conv via `DefaultConversationStore.load_conversation_messages` and scanning its stored `toolRounds`: found `reads` values of type `str` on msgs 9/55/57; a standalone repro produced EXACTLY the screenshot's `['[','{','"','p','a','t','h',':','u','m','n','_','e','v','l','w','b','/','r','i','s','.','y',',','3','6','d','4','1','8',']']`.
- **Fix (`lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_layer2.py`, surgical).** New helper `_coerce_spec_list(value)`: returns a real list unchanged; for a `str`, `json.loads` it and return the result ONLY if it decodes to a list, else `[]` (never iterate the raw string). Routed all three list-args through it — `read_files.reads`, `apply_diff/apply_diffs.edits`, `insert_content/insert_contents.edits` — and DROPPED the char-accepting `elif isinstance(spec, str)` branch (a valid `read_files` spec is always a dict; a bare-string element was never a real path). Added an `if not isinstance(args, dict): continue` guard right after the `json.loads(arguments)` parse (a bare-string/list decode would otherwise `AttributeError` on `args.get(...)`). Net effect on the real conv: the mangled `web_items.py` read is skipped and the SAME file is recovered cleanly from its other well-formed reads → the reminder now lists real paths, zero single-char entries.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_recently_accessed_files_string_reads.py` (5): malformed-truncated-string `reads` → `[]` (asserts NO len-1 entries); valid JSON-string `reads` → path recovered; normal list `reads` unchanged; non-dict `arguments` → `[]` (no raise); string `edits` for apply_diffs → `[]`. NEUTER #1 = revert the `read_files` branch to `for spec in args.get('reads',[]) or []` + the `str` branch → the two read_files string tests FAIL with the exact char-garbage `['[','{','"','p','a','t',...]` signature; restored byte-identical. NEUTER #2 = revert the `apply_diffs` branch to `for edit in args['edits'] or []` → that test still passed (that branch was already dict-only and never had the `str` acceptance defect — the `_coerce_spec_list` there is a consistency/robustness improvement, so the garbage bug was solely the `read_files` `str` branch, which IS double-covered). Full sweep: 77 passed (5 new + 72 `test_compaction_invariants.py`), ruff clean on both files.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `lib/tasks_pkg/compaction/_layer2.py` (+`_coerce_spec_list`, non-dict-args guard, 3 branches routed, dropped char-`str` branch). New: `tests/test_recently_accessed_files_string_reads.py`. Backend-only — no frontend/bundle change. NOT committed (owner attribution). No server restart needed (pure function; picked up on next start). The upstream defect — a streamed/partial tool-call persisting `reads`/`edits` as a JSON string instead of a list — is the deeper cause but is out of scope here; this fix makes the CONSUMER robust so no garbage reaches the prompt/debug panel regardless.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any code that iterates a tool arg expected to be a list (`reads`/`edits`/…) MUST first assert/coerce it is actually a list — a JSON **string** silently iterates char-by-char and Python's `isinstance(x, str)` element check then HAPPILY accepts each character as a value. Never trust the stored/streamed shape of a tool-call argument; a partial or double-encoded arg is a real in-the-wild state. Confirm "weird rendering" report bugs against the LIVE stored data and reproduce byte-for-byte before fixing.
- **CORRECTION (same day, owner-caught regression).** The fix above ALSO deleted the element-level `elif isinstance(spec, str)` branch, calling it "never a real path" — that was WRONG and introduced a regression. The two shapes are ORTHOGONAL: (1) the **container** is a string (`reads='[{"path":...}]'`) → the char-iteration bug → `_coerce_spec_list` handles it; (2) a list **ELEMENT** is a bare string (`reads=["human_eval/foo.py","scripts/bar.py"]`) → a LEGITIMATE, documented Claude-Opus output shape that the tool executor itself normalizes (see skill `compaction-tolerates-malformed-tool-call-args` + `read_files-stringified-reads-garbled-display`). By dropping the `str` element branch, that common input now returned `[]` — real paths SILENTLY vanished from the reminder (traded "garbled paths" for "no paths"). **Re-fix:** restored the branch AFTER `_coerce_spec_list` — since the container is then guaranteed a list, a string element is a genuine full path (never a stray char): `if isinstance(spec, dict): p = spec.get('path','')` / `elif isinstance(spec, str): p = spec.strip()`. Added 2 regression tests (`test_bare_string_list_elements_preserved` → `["a.py","b.py"]` returns both; `test_mixed_dict_and_string_list_elements` → dict+string list preserved in order). **Double-neuter is now genuinely two-sided:** NEUTER A (remove the `str` element branch) → the 2 bare-string-element tests FAIL (`[]`/`['a/first.py']`) while char-garbage tests stay green; NEUTER B (revert `_coerce_spec_list` to pass-through `value or []`) → the 2 char-garbage tests FAIL with the single-char signature while bare-string-element tests stay green — proving the container-guard and element-branch protect distinct invariants. Sweep: 79 passed (7 new + 72 invariants), ruff clean. Real conv `mr4e8pnxbv440z`: 25 clean paths, zero single-char entries. **Lesson:** when hardening a consumer against one malformed shape, do NOT collapse a DIFFERENT legitimate shape that shares a surface type (`str`). "Container is a string" ≠ "element is a string" — coerce the container, keep the element. A double-neuter must have one neuter per invariant; if a neuter doesn't flip any test, that invariant isn't actually protected (and here the un-flipping neuter had actually deleted a real feature).

### 2026-07-06 — CORRECTION + root-cause fix: the truncated peer-target id ALSO breaks message DELIVERY (not just the hover preview) — resolve to the canonical full id at the send/enqueue seam
- **Why this supersedes the prior entry's claim.** The immediately-following entry asserted "message DELIVERY was unaffected — only the display-string leaked into `toConv`". That was WRONG, and owner-corrected. Traced the full peer path: `project_peer_status` prints ids as `[{convId[:8]}]` (`project_peer.py`), the model copies that 8-char id verbatim into `project_message`/`project_intervene`, `send_peer_message` passes it straight to `enqueue_message(to_conv_id, …)` as the QUEUE KEY, but `dequeue_next` / `redispatch_orphaned_queue_on_startup` / the task registry all key on the FULL 14-char id (`message_queue.py`). So a peer message addressed by the short id lands in a PHANTOM queue that conversation `mr7hh5n6llzwnm` never drains → silently NEVER delivered, and `mr7hh5n6` registers as an orphaned-dispatchable conv mapping to nothing. The `from==to` self-guard and the per-(sender,target) rate-gate were also keyed on the mismatched id. This is the more serious half — it breaks the whole point of the peer-messaging pillar whenever an agent uses the short id it was shown.
- **Fix (root cause, at the send/enqueue seam — `lib/conversations/project_peer.py`).** New `_resolve_target_conv_id(to_conv_id) -> (full_id, '')|('' , reason)`: exact `WHERE id=?` match, else UNIQUE-prefix `WHERE id LIKE ? LIMIT 2`; refuses with `ambiguous_target` (>1 match — never guess a row) or `unknown_target` (no match); fail-OPEN on a DB error (returns the id unchanged — no worse than before). Wired into BOTH `send_peer_message` AND `intervene_peer` BEFORE the self-check, rate-gate, enqueue, and feed emit — so delivery is correct AND the FULL id is what gets stored in the feed payload's `toConv` going forward (canonical ids for new rows). `intervene_peer`'s hard-abort path also benefits (its `abort_running_tasks_for_conv` keys on the full id). `execute_peer_tool` maps the two new errors to clear agent-facing messages ("no conversation matches …, check project_peer_status" / "… too short to be unambiguous, supply more characters"). The `/preview` prefix-resolution from the prior entry STAYS as defense-in-depth for the historical rows already stored truncated.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_peer_message_target_resolution.py` (9, seeded SQLite via `reset_sqlite_for_tests` incl. an ambiguous `dupdupab*` pair): the resolver (exact/short-prefix/ambiguous/unknown) AND end-to-end `send_peer_message` — a short-id message ENQUEUES UNDER THE FULL id (`get_queue(full)`==1, `get_queue(short)`==0), ambiguous/unknown are REFUSED with nothing enqueued to either candidate, and self-send-via-short-id is caught on the RESOLVED id. NEUTER = revert the resolution call in `send_peer_message` → exactly the 4 delivery/refusal tests FAIL (short-id enqueues under the phantom id; ambiguous/unknown slip through; self-send-via-short-id slips through) while the 5 resolver-unit / full-id-happy-path tests stay green (specificity); restored byte-identical (diff -q). The existing DB-free suites (`test_project_peer.py` 26, `test_project_peer_human_nudge.py` 7) keep synthetic ids `cA/cB` by stubbing `_resolve_target_conv_id` to identity in each `_stub_io` fixture + the self-refuse test + the module-reloading NC `run()` closures (reload rebinds the real fn) — all 33 still pass. Full sweep 46/46 (+13 with the preview suite); ruff clean.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `lib/conversations/project_peer.py` (resolver + 2 wire-ins + 2 error branches), `tests/test_project_peer.py` + `tests/test_project_peer_human_nudge.py` (identity-stub the resolver to stay DB-free). NEW: `tests/test_peer_message_target_resolution.py`. Backend-only. NOT committed (owner attribution). No server restart needed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A display/short id (`[:8]`) is NOT a safe lookup key. If a value is surfaced to an agent in a truncated form, the agent WILL echo it back — so resolve it to the canonical id at the WRITE/DISPATCH seam (not just the read side), and REFUSE on ambiguity rather than mis-deliver. When a resolver is added to a function that DB-free unit tests exercise with synthetic ids, stub it to identity in those tests (and re-stub inside any module-reloading negative-control closure, since reload rebinds the real function). Don't declare a data-truncation bug "display-only" without tracing every consumer that uses the value as a KEY.

### 2026-07-06 — Project Brain hover-preview always "未命名对话/暂无消息" for the SECOND (target) id: the /preview endpoint did an EXACT lookup but the panel/feed carry a TRUNCATED 8-char id
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** In the Project Brain cross-conversation-messages (跨会话消息) thread, hovering the FIRST id in a `from → to` row showed the right preview, but the SECOND id always fell back to "未命名对话 / 暂无消息". Owner asked why.
- **Root cause (confirmed against the LIVE PG DB, not guessed).** The panel renders TRUNCATED 8-char display ids (`_shortConv = String(cid).slice(0,8)`), while real conversation ids are 14 chars (`mr7hh5n6` → `mr7hh5n6llzwnm`). The `GET /api/v1/conversations/<id>/preview` endpoint (`routes/conversations.py::conv_preview`) did an EXACT `WHERE id=? AND user_id=?` lookup → a truncated id misses → `api_not_found` (404) → the frontend `_fetchConvPreview` caches null and `buildConvPreviewCard` renders the "Untitled / no messages" fallback. WHY only the SECOND id: the peer-note feed payload stores `fromConv` = the acting conv's FULL id but `toConv` = the TRUNCATED 8-char id (the agent addressed the target by its displayed short id, and `send_peer_message`/`emit_project_event` persist whatever `to_conv_id` it was given). Verified in `project_events`: e.g. `{fromConv:'mr7hn42qp518zu', toConv:'mr7hh5n6'}`. The chip `data-conv-id` (`project-brain-peers.js:382-385`) faithfully carries those exact values, so the full-id side resolves and the short-id side 404s.
- **Fix (`routes/conversations.py`, surgical).** In `conv_preview`, when the exact lookup misses, resolve the id by UNIQUE PREFIX: `SELECT … WHERE id LIKE ? AND user_id=? LIMIT 2` with `conv_id + '%'`, accept the match ONLY when exactly one row comes back (ambiguous prefix → 404, unknown → 404). Uses the already-imported `async_fetchall`. This heals the display without changing the stored data. NOTE: the upstream data defect (short `toConv` persisted) is the deeper cause but is not display-critical — the peer-message DELIVERY still uses the full id at enqueue time (the truncation is a display-string that leaked into the payload's `toConv`), so no message was mis-delivered; only the hover preview 404'd.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_conv_preview_short_id.py` (4): seeds a fresh SQLite DB with realistic 14-char ids (incl. an AMBIGUOUS pair sharing an 8-char prefix), then drives the REAL `conv_preview` endpoint — patching the async DB facade (`async_fetchone`/`async_fetchall`) onto the seeded thread-local DB (the executor-pool connections don't follow `reset_sqlite_for_tests` in-process) and wrapping the call in `app.test_request_context()` (api_ok/api_not_found need `jsonify` → a request context). Asserts: exact id resolves; truncated 8-char resolves to the full row + populated firstUserMessage; ambiguous prefix → 404; unknown → 404. NEUTER = revert the prefix-resolution block to an immediate 404 → `test_truncated_short_id_resolves_by_prefix` FAILS while the other 3 stay PASS (branch-specific); restored byte-identical (diff -q). 4/4 green, ruff clean.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `routes/conversations.py` (conv_preview prefix-resolution). New: `tests/test_conv_preview_short_id.py`. Backend-only — no frontend/bundle change (the chips already carry the right `data-conv-id`; the endpoint just couldn't resolve the short form). NOT committed (owner attribution). No server restart needed (route logic; picked up on next start).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A short/display id (`[:8]`) that leaks into a stored payload (`toConv`) and is later used as a lookup KEY silently 404s an exact-match endpoint. When an endpoint resolves an id that the UI may pass in truncated form, resolve by UNIQUE prefix and REFUSE on ambiguity (never guess a row). Confirm "no messages"-type report bugs against the LIVE DB first — here the conversations existed and were rich; the id was simply truncated, not empty.


### 2026-07-06 — Poor-network sync chaos: extended keep-longer to toolRounds, settled the KEEP_LOCAL reconcile branch, and stopped the send-path activeTaskId write from clobbering a live checkpoint
- **Ask.** "When the signal is poor the frontend↔server sync is chaotic — I see various incorrect things on the frontend." This is a heavily-patched area (state-snapshot keep-longer, terminal CAS retry, pending-sync durability, connection-failure display all landed earlier). Ran a 3-way parallel audit (reconcile-on-reload / SSE-reconnect render / backend persist) to find the REAL *remaining* root-cause gaps rather than pile on more speculative patches, then verified the top findings against the actual code before touching anything.
- **Fix #1+#2 — toolRounds keep-longer (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`).** Content/thinking already routed through `_snapshotLonger` at all state-snapshot sites, but `toolRounds` was assigned VERBATIM (`= ev.toolRounds` at the 2 planner + worker sites; `existing.concat(ev.toolRounds||[])` at the plain-assistant merge; `= _cm.toolRounds` in the terminal `done`). A cold/empty reconnect snapshot (or a racey shorter `done` commit) therefore COLLAPSED the on-screen tool-round panel (searches / file edits) mid-stream — the exact content-regression class the text fix solved, never extended to rounds. Added a sibling helper `_snapshotLongerRounds(current, incoming)` (adopt incoming only when `incoming.length >= current.length`; array-null-safe) and routed all 5 toolRounds write sites + the `done` committedMessage assignment through it. The endpoint-critic snapshot block has no toolRounds assignment, so it is correctly NOT among them (5 calls + 1 def = 6 occurrences).
- **Fix #3 — KEEP_LOCAL reconcile branch settles load-state (`static/js/core/conversations.js`).** In `loadConversationMessages` the `if (localHasUnsynced)` (KEEP_LOCAL) branch — unlike MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK and OVERWRITE — never set `conv._needsLoad=false` nor updated `conv._serverMsgCount`. Two poor-network consequences: (a) `_needsLoad` stays truthy → a later refocus/cross-device poll re-enters Phase-2 and, once the fresh-activity window closes, takes OVERWRITE → the just-sent local message BLANKS; (b) the stale (higher) `_serverMsgCount` makes `syncConversationToServer`'s count-drop guard silently DROP a subsequent legitimate edit/truncate. Appended `conv._needsLoad=false; conv._serverMsgCount=Math.max(serverMsgs.length, conv.messages.length);` at the branch end (Math.max so the longer KEPT local tail stays authoritative) — mirrors MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK exactly.
- **Fix #4 — send-path activeTaskId write no longer clobbers a live checkpoint (`routes/chat.py`).** After `_start_task_for_conv` spawns the task thread, step 6 recorded `activeTaskId` via `_persist_conv_messages(db, conv_id, messages, title, {'activeTaskId': task_id})` — a FULL-ROW upsert that rewrites the `messages` column with the route's STALE, user-only tail (the assistant slot doesn't exist in the route's local copy yet) AND bumps `updated_at`. Between step 5 and step 6 the task thread can already have checkpointed the assistant slot (`_sync_partial_to_conversation`) → the full-row write REWINDS it to the pre-start snapshot → on a poor network (frontend `finishStream` may never sync) the reload reads `conversations.messages` and shows "等待中…/Waiting…" over an answer that WAS generated. Routed all THREE post-`_start_task_for_conv` sites (send:626, regenerate, continue) through `set_conversation_settings(conv_id, {'activeTaskId': task_id}, db=db)` — the established per-conv serialized SETTINGS-ONLY seam (`lib/conversations/settings_store.py`, the `settings-column-serialized-write` convention) that never touches `messages`/`updated_at`. This is the cleaner of the two options (settings-only vs. CAS-on-updated_at): the only new info at step 6 IS `activeTaskId`, so there is no reason to rewrite the array at all.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (all 3 fixes).** NEW `tests/test_frontend_toolrounds_keep_longer.py` (node harness on the REAL pure `_snapshotLongerRounds` + 4 source guards; NEUTER = revert helper body to `return inc;` → empty/shorter-incoming cases FAIL; restored byte-identical). NEW `tests/test_frontend_keep_local_settles_load_state.py` (source-region isolation: locates the KEEP_LOCAL branch between its two stable anchors and asserts BOTH settle statements live INSIDE it — not merely elsewhere in the function; NEUTER = delete the two lines → region no longer contains them → FAIL; restored). NEW `tests/test_active_task_id_settings_only_write.py` (real-DB behavioral: seed stale user-only tail → simulate task-thread checkpoint → fix path PRESERVES the assistant content + records activeTaskId; the SECOND test runs the exact OLD `persist_conv_messages` path and asserts it CLOBBERS the checkpoint to 1 msg — the neuter/restore contrast built into one run). All three neuters confirmed to BITE, all restores `node --check`/byte-verified.
- **Verification.** New 3 green post-restore. Regression sweep 15/15 (state_snapshot_keep_longer, state_snapshot_no_wipe, pending_sync_durability, send_failure_persists_message, sync_allowtruncate_guard, casee_no_autostart) + settings_store 4/4. `node --check` clean on both edited JS; ruff clean on `routes/chat.py` + new test. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-1a9855f4.js`** (grep confirms `_snapshotLongerRounds` ×6 and 3 `_serverMsgCount` settle sites incl. KEEP_LOCAL). NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **DEFERRED to follow-up (lower severity, from the same audit — not yet done):** (#5) elapsed HUD resets to 0s on every reconnect (`health_stream_timer.js` `twStart` unconditionally sets `startTime`); dead-HUD/Force-Finish can linger a tick after recovery; `_forceFinishDeadStream` doesn't null `conv.activeTaskId` so a probe can un-finish the bubble; MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK trailing-append doesn't de-dup by `_msgId` (possible duplicate bubble); interrupted-only recovery convs don't adopt finished server content; backend audit's #3 (`persist_conv_messages` has no CAS on the FIRST-turn full write) / other secondary persist gaps.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The "keep-longer" monotonic invariant for reconnect/resync snapshots must cover EVERY accumulated field, not just text — `toolRounds` is a first-class casualty of a cold-replay snapshot exactly like content/thinking. When adding a reconcile branch, it MUST settle the same load-state bookkeeping (`_needsLoad`/`_serverMsgCount`) every sibling branch settles, or a later poll re-enters and undoes it. And a write whose ONLY new information is a settings key must be a settings-only merge (`set_conversation_settings`) — never a full-row `persist_conv_messages`, which drags the caller's stale `messages` snapshot over a concurrent task-thread checkpoint.

- **Owner ruling.** After the banner/toast i18n, the single most connection-failure-specific surface was still hardcoded English: the in-stream liveness HUD in `_updateStreamTimerUI` (`health_stream_timer.js`). When a stream stalls or the server dies the user saw `server not responding`, `Server not responding (Ns silent) — health check failed`, `still working`, `Server alive — still working (…)`, `No update for Ns…`, and the `Force Finish` button — all English on a zh UI. Same defect class as the banners; finished it (not a separate "live HUD" concern outside scope).
- **Strings routed through a guarded `_connT()`, new `conn.hud*` + `conn.phase*` keys (zh primary).** All four HUD branches (dead / still-working / severe-silence / warn-silence) in both the header timer span AND the `_setBubbleLiveness` in-bubble line, plus the `Force Finish` button label → `conn.hudNotResponding`/`conn.hudNotRespondingFull`/`conn.hudStillWorking`/`conn.hudStillWorkingFull`/`conn.hudProcessing`/`conn.hudNoUpdate`/`conn.hudNoUpdateSevere`/`conn.hudNoUpdateWarn`/`conn.forceFinish`, with `{n}`=silent-seconds and `{what}`=activity-label interpolation preserved. `_streamPhaseLabel`'s OWN fallback labels ("running tools"/"thinking"/"reasoning"/"compacting context"/"retrying"/"working"/"autopilot is generating the next reply") → `conn.phase*`. **Backend `p.detail` still passes through verbatim** (same ruling as assistant/critic prose: live server text isn't UI chrome — only our generic English fallbacks are localized).
- **Guarded `_connT()` (module-level).** `function _connT(key,params){ return (typeof t==='function') ? t(key,params) : key; }` — production always has i18n.js (bundle-first) → zh; the guard exists ONLY so the several jsdom harnesses that eval this file standalone (e.g. `test_frontend_stuck_placeholder_heal`) don't throw `ReferenceError: t`. Fallback returns the key, never English.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** Added `test_stream_hud_renders_zh_on_dead_server` to `tests/test_frontend_connection_failure_display.py` (now 3 tests): loads the REAL i18n.js (zh default) + drives the REAL `_updateStreamTimerUI` into the dead-server branch (`_lastHealthResult:false`, `_healthChecking:true` to skip the async re-probe) AND the still-working branch (`thinking_active` phase) — asserts the header renders `服务器无响应`+`强制结束` (NOT "Force Finish"/"server not responding"), the bubble renders `服务器无响应（静默…健康检查失败`, and the still-working line renders `仍在处理`+`推理中`. **Harness quirk solved:** `_streamTimers` is a file-scoped `const` (unreachable from the outer eval scope — only `function` decls leak), so the harness appends `;globalThis.__seedTimer=(cid,o)=>_streamTimers.set(cid,o)` to the eval string to seed in-scope. NEUTER = revert the dead-server branch to the English literal on a COPY → the 6 dead-branch assertions FAIL while the still-working 2 stay PASS (proving branch-specificity); restored byte-identical (diff -q).
- **Verification.** 15/15 regression sweep green (this file 3 + stuck_placeholder_heal 2 + pending_sync_durability 5 + send_failure 3 + finishstream_no_put 1 + cross_device_reconcile 1). `node --check` clean; NO duplicate i18n keys (global scan: none). ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-b342f8e4.js`** (grep confirms `conn.hudNotResponding`/`服务器无响应`/`conn.forceFinish`/`强制结束`/`conn.phaseReasoning` present).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `i18n.js` (+17 `conn.hud*`/`conn.phase*` keys), `health_stream_timer.js` (+`_connT` helper, localized `_streamPhaseLabel` + all 4 HUD branches + Force Finish), test file (+3rd harness/test). NOT committed (owner attribution; heavy sibling diffs in tree). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up). Connection-failure display i18n is now COMPLETE across banners + toasts + envelope + HUD.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a jsdom harness must drive a function that reads a file-scoped `const` (Map/Set registries like `_streamTimers`), you can't reach it from the outer scope — append a one-line `globalThis.__seed=(…)=>_const.set(…)` bridge to the eval string so the accessor runs in the same lexical scope. And for phase/label helpers: localize only YOUR OWN generic fallback strings; backend-supplied `detail` stays passthrough (it's live server text, not translatable UI chrome).
