### 2026-07-06 — Connection-failure DISPLAY & LOG accuracy: stale banners cleared, frozen net-badge watchdogged, silent health catches logged
- **Ask.** "Optimize the frontend display when a connection to the server fails. Accuracy must be ensured, and the same for logs." Open-ended, so I ran a 3-way parallel audit (i18n hardcoded strings / logging-accuracy / stale-display bugs) over the mature existing infra (boot-reconnect banner, offline-recovery poll, durable pending-sync, stream-stuck liveness) to find REAL gaps rather than duplicate work. Focused this pass on the two accuracy axes the owner named; the language-i18n cleanup (bilingual hardcoded strings on the same paths) is a separate cosmetic epic left flagged.
- **Fix #1 — DB-unavailable banner lingered FOREVER (worst display bug).** `_checkDbHealth` (`static/js/core/health_stream_timer.js`) only ever ADDED the red "Database Unavailable" banner — no clear-on-recovery, no re-poll. Once PG came back (documented recovery = server restart with PG up) the banner stayed until manual Dismiss/reload, falsely claiming the DB was still down. Added `_clearDbWarningBanner()` (called when `db_ok !== false`) + a self-stopping `_startDbHealthPolling()` (15s, visible-gated, stops when the banner is gone or DB healthy) that mirrors `_startOfflineRecoveryPolling`'s shape.
- **Fix #2 — net-latency badge could FREEZE on a stale reading.** The badge repaints only when `pushOnLatency` fires; a wedged WS (stuck CONNECTING / reconnect scheduled but open never lands) stops emits and the badge kept showing e.g. green "120ms" while disconnected. Each reading now carries an `at` timestamp (`push.js` `_emitLatency` + `getLatency`) and `net-latency.js` runs a 4s watchdog that forces the OFFLINE display when the newest reading is older than `_STALE_MS` (9s ≈ 2 ping windows) and wasn't already offline.
- **Fix #3 — silent health catches (CLAUDE §2).** `_checkServerHealth`'s bare `catch {}` swallowed the ping-failure reason (a 3s AbortSignal.timeout under load vs a real outage were indistinguishable on the path that flips the user-visible "server offline" verdict) → now `console.debug('[StreamTimer] health ping failed:', …)`. `_checkDbHealth`'s comment-only catch now logs (a `.json()` parse failure / 200-with-garbage was invisible). `push.js` `onmessage` malformed-frame `catch { return }` now `console.debug`s the drop.
- **Fix #4 — interrupted-only recovery left a stale badge.** In `cross_tab_sync.js::_recoverOfflineConversations`, convs in `_interruptedOnlyIds` `return` early; if such a conv ALSO carried a stale `server_offline` error envelope it was never cleared (server is reachable by then — the health check above passed). Now clears the envelope + persists + re-renders before the early return, so the bubble doesn't stack a misleading "Server Offline" badge over the (correct) interrupted verdict.
- **Fix #5 — two banners overlapped.** `db-warning-banner` (z-index 10000) and `boot-reconnect-banner` (9999) were both `top:0` → the boot banner hid behind the DB one. Boot banner now offsets `top` by the DB banner's height when both are present, so they STACK.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_connection_failure_display.py` (jsdom, 2): (A) flippable `db_ok` drives the REAL `_checkDbHealth` — banner shown when down, CLEARED when `db_ok` flips true, idempotent when healthy; (B) captures net-latency's render cb + watchdog interval, paints a fresh GOOD reading, then ages `Date.now` past `_STALE_MS` and runs the watchdog → asserts `badge.dataset.state==='offline'`. NEUTER-A removes `_clearDbWarningBanner()` from the recovery branch → DB test FAILS; NEUTER-B stubs the watchdog's forced-offline `_render` → latency test FAILS. Both restored byte-identical (diff -q confirmed). Sweep 12/12 green (new 2 + stuck_placeholder_heal 2 + pending_sync_durability 5 + send_failure 3); `node --check` clean on all 5 edited JS; ruff clean.
- **Bundle / scope.** 5 bundled JS edited (health_stream_timer.js, push.js, net-latency.js, cross_tab_sync.js, main.js) → rebuilt **`bundle-dbd19554.js`** (grep confirms `_clearDbWarningBanner`/`_startDbHealthPolling`/"health ping failed"/"no fresh reading for" present). New test file. Live-peer check: no active siblings at start. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A failure-state banner/badge is only accurate if it has a CLEAR path, not just a show path — audit every "show on failure" UI for "who removes it on recovery" (a show-only banner lingers forever). A push/poll-driven indicator that only repaints on an event freezes silently when the event source wedges → give it a staleness watchdog keyed on a per-reading timestamp. And an early-return recovery branch must still clear stale error envelopes for the convs it skips, or a correct verdict gets a wrong badge stacked on top.

### 2026-07-06 — Tool-panel image thumbnail "enlarge" did nothing (bundling regression) + inspect_image "cropped" ops chip now i18n'd
- **Symptom (owner-flagged).** Clicking an image thumbnail in the tool-call panel to enlarge it did nothing. Also: the inspect_image transform chip showed a raw English "cropped" (and a hardcoded English tooltip) regardless of UI language. Asked whether it was a style vs crop issue — it was NEITHER.
- **Root cause #1 (enlarge = bundling regression).** The thumbnails rendered by `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js` (read_files / inspect_image / browser_screenshot) and the image-gen cards in `ui/chat_render.js` call `_openImageFullscreen(this.src)` / `_downloadGenImage(this)` via inline `onclick=`. Those two helpers were DEFINED in `static/js/image-gen.js`, which was MOVED to the DEFERRED feature bundle on 2026-07-05 (loads only on first entry into Image-Gen mode). They were NOT registered as `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS`, so `feature-loader.js` installed NO lazy stub. Net: in any session that never opened Image-Gen mode, the thumbnail onclick pointed at an `undefined` global → silent no-op. (paper-reader.js was immune because it `typeof`-guards the call; chat/tool-panel did not.)
- **Fix #1.** Extracted the two dependency-free helpers (DOM APIs only) into a NEW CORE module `static/js/ui/image_fullscreen.js`, registered in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (before `ui/chat_render.js` + `ui/tool_rounds.js`) + a dev-fallback `<script>` tag in index.html. Replaced the definitions in image-gen.js with a NOTE comment (do-not-re-add). Now always present regardless of feature-bundle state.
- **Root cause #2 (i18n).** The inspect_image ops chip (`tool_rounds.js`) rendered the backend's English `inspectOps` string ("cropped, zoom 2×", built in `lib/file_reader.py` as LLM-facing text — correctly English there) verbatim, with a hardcoded `title="Applied transform"`. The backend string is fine (it's for the model); the DISPLAY chip needed render-layer translation.
- **Fix #2.** New `_localizeInspectOps(t, ops, mode)` in tool_rounds.js splits the comma-joined ops and translates each token (cropped / rotated {deg} / zoom {factor} / fit to {size} / grid overlay / full frame) via new `inspect.*` i18n keys (zh+en, `opsSep` too), preserving the dynamic numbers; `mode="title"` returns the localized tooltip. Chip body + title now both localized; unknown tokens pass through verbatim.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_inspect_image_render.py` (jsdom, 3): drives the REAL `_renderUnifiedToolLine` on an inspect_image round with a zh `t` stub + evals the REAL `ui/image_fullscreen.js` — asserts (a) `_openImageFullscreen`/`_downloadGenImage` are defined by the core file, (b) the thumbnail onclick wires to `_openImageFullscreen(this.src)`, (c) chip renders zh "已裁剪"/"放大 2×"/"已应用的图像变换" and NOT `title="Applied transform"`. NC-A reverts the chip to raw English + hardcoded title → the 4 localize checks FAIL, enlarge wiring still PASSES. NC-B renames the helper definition → `helper_defined` FAILS, localize checks still PASS. Both restore byte-identical. Extended `tests/test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py` with `test_image_fullscreen_helper_in_core_not_deferred` (asserts core-membership + load-order + that image-gen.js no longer defines the helper + dev-fallback tag).
- **Verification.** 66 green across the sweep: new inspect render 3, bundle-registration 11, feature-lazyload 4, inspect_image backend 18, bundle-manifest-parity 11, brain-tool-render 7, bundle-corruption-guard 12. `node --check` clean on all edited/new JS; no dup i18n keys; ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → CORE **`bundle-ee7401fa.js`** (has `_openImageFullscreen` + `_localizeInspectOps`) + deferred **`feature-45738d51.js`** (helper correctly ABSENT).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** New: `static/js/ui/image_fullscreen.js`, `tests/test_frontend_inspect_image_render.py`. Edited: `image-gen.js` (removed 2 fns), `lib/js_bundler.py` (+_BUNDLE_FILES entry), `index.html` (+dev tag), `ui/tool_rounds.js` (+`_localizeInspectOps`, localized chip), `i18n.js` (+9 keys), `tests/test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py` (+1 guard). Live-peer check: 2 siblings active (mr8ko0nl, mr8kvopr) on unrelated files — no overlap. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; hard-refresh picks it up).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When moving a JS module to the DEFERRED feature bundle, AUDIT every function it defines for inline `onclick=`/`onload=` callers that render in the CORE bundle. A deferred function referenced from a core render path is a silent no-op until the feature loads — either register it as a `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINT` (lazy stub) OR, if it's a small shared leaf with no feature deps, extract it to a core module (preferred for cross-cutting helpers like an image lightbox). Also: a backend-built op/label string that is LLM-facing (text_fallback) is correctly English; if the SAME string is also shown in the UI, translate it at the render layer, don't change the backend.


### 2026-07-06 — Poor-network send-failure data loss: made the rescue DURABLE end-to-end (the earlier same-day patch only healed a transient blip)
- **Why a follow-up.** The earlier entry this day (clear `_sendInFlight` before the catch-path rescue sync) was necessary but NOT sufficient — reviewer flagged three gaps that leave the REAL failure case (network still down at catch time) losing the message on refresh: (1) the rescue `syncConversationToServer` PUT is best-effort with no retry — on the poor network that failed the send it usually ALSO fails; (2) `saveConversations()` does NOT write IndexedDB (only `ConvCache.put()` does), so a failed PUT leaves the message ONLY in the volatile in-memory array → gone on reload; (3) even if cached, the reload reconcile takes the OVERWRITE branch (no fresh-local-activity, no activeTaskId, no stream) and replaces the local tail with the SHORTER server copy.
- **Fix — durable, all three gaps closed (`static/js/core/conversations.js`).** New pending-sync durability seam: `markConvPendingSync(conv)` stamps the trailing turn's messages with a `_pendingSync` FIELD (a real message field → `ConvCache._stripMessage` preserves it → survives reload; a conv-level flag would NOT, the cache only persists whitelisted settings) and calls `ConvCache.put(conv)` so the message is durable locally even when the server never got it. `syncConversationToServer` now RETURNS a boolean (true only on a confirmed PUT) and on success calls `_clearPendingSyncMarkers(conv)`. Retry-until-synced: `_flushPendingSyncs(trigger)` re-attempts every conv with `convHasPendingSync` true (health-gated, skips live streams), driven by `_startPendingSyncPolling` (12s self-stopping interval) + hooks on the `online` event, `visibilitychange`, and boot (main.js after initActiveTasks). Reconcile: added `_localHasPendingSync` as a term of `localHasUnsynced` so a durable pending tail is authoritative (KEEP_LOCAL → re-sync via the poller), never OVERWRITTEN by the shorter server copy. The PUT body mapper STRIPS `_pendingSync` (clone-and-strip, doesn't mutate the live msg) so the client-only marker never echoes to the server and wrongly re-triggers KEEP_LOCAL forever.
- **sendMessage catch (`main_send_pipeline.js`).** Both persisting branches now `const _synced = await syncConversationToServer(conv); if (!_synced) markConvPendingSync(conv);` — so a failed rescue PUT immediately makes the turn durable + starts the retry poller.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_pending_sync_durability.py` (5): (A) END-TO-END harness drives the REAL `syncConversationToServer`+`markConvPendingSync`+`convHasPendingSync`+`_flushPendingSyncs` against a mock IndexedDB + a FLIPPABLE network — PUT fails (net down) → marker set + written to IDB → simulate RELOAD (rebuild conv from mock IDB only) → message still present + `_pendingSync` survived → network returns → poller flush syncs it, server now has the msg, markers cleared; (B) PUT body does NOT carry `_pendingSync`; (C) idb-cache `_stripMessage` preserves `_pendingSync` (source-contract); (D) reconcile `_localHasPendingSync` is a term of `localHasUnsynced` + double-neuter (remove the term → assertion fails). Extra strip-on-send source assertion. Updated the earlier `test_frontend_send_failure_persists_message.py` to the new durable clear-then-sync-then-mark fragment. Proved the end-to-end neuter BITES: neutering `markConvPendingSync` to a no-op → nothing written to IDB → harness crashes (returncode 1, caught by the `returncode==0` assert). 15/15 across the sync/snapshot suites; `test_frontend_api_isolation` 4/4; ruff clean; `node --check` clean on all 4 edited JS.
- **Bundle / coordination.** 4 bundled JS edited. Sibling conv mr8l58uj was concurrently rebuilding the bundle; the current shared `bundle-ee7401fa.js` ALREADY contains my durability symbols (its rebuild read the shared working tree — grep confirms markConvPendingSync/_localHasPendingSync/_flushPendingSyncs present, 12 hits). Sent a project_message flagging the file overlap so the sibling doesn't revert my hunks. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "rescue sync on failure" is only real if it's DURABLE: (1) persist to the durable local store (IndexedDB via ConvCache.put — `saveConversations` alone is in-memory and dies on reload), (2) mark the record with a field that SURVIVES the cache round-trip (message-level, not conv-level — the cache only keeps whitelisted settings) and retry until the PUT actually lands (poller + online/visibility/boot hooks), and (3) make the reload reconcile treat that durable-pending tail as authoritative or the shorter server copy wins the OVERWRITE. A single best-effort PUT on the same network that just failed the send is not a fix. Strip client-only durability markers from the server payload so they can't echo back and pin the conv in KEEP_LOCAL.

Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-7be8ed93.js`** (grep confirms `buildConvPreviewCard`/`pb-conv-preview`/`/preview` present). **KNOWN pre-existing flake (NOT mine):** `test_cross_project_isolation_at_push_routing` + `test_NC_isolation_wildcard_subscription_leaks` TIME OUT at the 60s node cap — they load `push.js` whose `setInterval` ping keeps node's event loop alive (documented 2026-07-05); my change touches no timers.

### 2026-07-06 — Frontend data-loss on poor network FIXED: a failed `/chat/send` left `_sendInFlight=true` so the catch-path rescue sync was silently skipped → the user's message vanished on refresh
- **Symptom (owner-flagged, screenshot).** A message SENT while the network is very poor disappears from the frontend after a page refresh (e.g. conv mr80gsd8rywph9). The optimistic user bubble was visible, then gone on reload.
- **Root cause (confirmed by reading the full send→sync→reload path).** `sendMessage()` (`static/js/main/main_send_pipeline.js`) pushes the optimistic `userMsg` into `conv.messages` and sets `conv._sendInFlight = true` BEFORE the `Api.chat.send(...)` fetch. That flag exists so `syncConversationToServer` (`static/js/core/conversations.js:173`) SKIPS its "rescue PUT" during the send window — on the SUCCESS path the backend `_chat_send` is the sole owner of the first-turn persist, and a racing PUT would plant a duplicate untranslated row. BUT `_sendInFlight` was only cleared in the `finally` block, which runs AFTER the `catch`. So on a fetch FAILURE (timeout / network drop — exactly the poor-network case) the catch block's `syncConversationToServer(conv)` ran while `_sendInFlight` was STILL `true` → the guard returned early → **the PUT never fired**. The message then lived ONLY in the in-memory `conversations` array (`saveConversations()` does NOT touch IndexedDB). On refresh, `loadConversationMessages` fetched the server copy (which never got the message) and the OVERWRITE branch wiped it. The `finally` comment even claimed "catch path, error fallback already syncs" — but that sync was a dead no-op.
- **Why the guard's duplicate concern is VOID in the catch path.** `chat_send` THREW, so there is no concurrent backend persist to collide with. Clearing `_sendInFlight` before the rescue sync is safe: the rescue PUT becomes the message's only lifeline instead of a silent no-op.
- **Fix (`main_send_pipeline.js`, both persisting catch branches).** Set `conv._sendInFlight = false;` immediately BEFORE the rescue sync, and `await syncConversationToServer(conv)` (was fire-and-forget) so the PUT has a chance to land before the user can reload. Applied to (1) the user-clicked-Stop-during-translation branch and (2) the generic error branch. The `finally` still clears the flag (harmless idempotent) so the success/queued paths are unchanged.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_send_failure_persists_message.py` (3): (1) MECHANISM harness drives the REAL shipped `syncConversationToServer` under node — `_sendInFlight=true` → PUT SKIPPED, `_sendInFlight=false` → PUT FIRES with the message body (this is the exact behaviour the fix relies on); (2) source-level assertion that BOTH catch branches carry the clear-then-sync pair (`conv._sendInFlight = false;` immediately before `await syncConversationToServer(conv)`); (3) DOUBLE-NEUTER removes the clear on an in-memory copy → the fixed-fragment count drops 2→0, proving the assertion discriminates the fix. 3/3 green; ruff clean; `node --check` clean. Regression: `test_frontend_sync_allowtruncate_guard` 2/2, `test_frontend_state_snapshot_keep_longer` 1/1.
- **Bundle.** `main_send_pipeline.js` is in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (js_bundler.py:429) → rebuilt bundle **`bundle-646ddb94.js`** (grep confirms both clear-then-sync pairs present, minified newline-preserving). Serves on next natural server start; hard-refresh picks it up.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edited: `static/js/main/main_send_pipeline.js` (2 catch branches, +comments), NEW `tests/test_frontend_send_failure_persists_message.py`, rebuilt bundle. Live-peer check: no active siblings. NOT committed (owner attribution; tree carries heavy sibling diffs). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A flag that gates a persistence-rescue path MUST be cleared on EVERY code path where the thing it guards against can no longer happen — not just in `finally`. Here `_sendInFlight` protects against a duplicate row the backend would create on SUCCESS; on the FAILURE (catch) path the backend created nothing, so the flag must be cleared BEFORE the rescue sync or the sync is a silent no-op and the data is lost. `finally`-only cleanup is too late when the catch itself needs the flag cleared. The poor-network path is exactly when the backend is the only writer left, so a skipped rescue PUT = permanent loss.

### 2026-07-06 — Backend data-loss bug class FIXED: non-CAS read-modify-write on the conversations.settings JSON column silently clobbered concurrent writers' keys → new shared serialized settings_store + all 13 sites migrated
- **Root cause (surfaced by a fresh backend audit).** The `messages` column has a CAS write seam (`DefaultConversationStore.cas_update_conversation_messages`), but the `settings` column had NONE — ~13 call sites each did a bare read-modify-write of the WHOLE settings blob (`SELECT settings` → `json.loads` → mutate ONE key → `UPDATE conversations SET settings=?`). Because each rewrites the ENTIRE blob, two concurrent settings writers silently clobber each other's keys (last-writer-wins). Real single-box collisions: a tool-toggle `PATCH /chat/tool-state` (worker thread) dropping a just-stamped `activeTaskId` (queue-dispatch thread) → orphaned SSE re-attach; an autopilot `autopilotSummaries` store (task thread) wiping the `projectSummary` cache (daemon thread) → lost run record. `project_summary._persist_summary` had a module `threading.Lock`, but it only serialized SIBLING summary generators — NOT cross-writer collisions with autopilot/tool-state.
- **Why NOT CAS-on-updated_at (the messages-column tool).** Settings-only writers DELIBERATELY do not bump `updated_at` (a tool toggle must not reorder the sidebar). A CAS keyed on `updated_at` would either regress that or spuriously miss. The correct single-box fix is to SERIALIZE the read+mutate+write per `conv_id` behind an in-process lock, so every writer merges its key onto the FRESHEST blob.
- **Fix — new `lib/conversations/settings_store.py`.** `update_conversation_settings(conv_id, mutate, *, user_id=1, db=None)` — acquires a per-conv lock (a `WeakValueDictionary` of locks, GC'd when no writer holds one), RE-READS settings under the lock, runs `mutate(settings)` in place, writes back. `mutate` returns `False` to signal "nothing changed, skip the write" (conditional-set / clear paths). Thin `set_conversation_settings(conv_id, updates_dict)` wrapper for the common flat-merge case. Does NOT touch messages/updated_at/msg_count (settings-only). Exported from `lib.conversations`. Docstring records the scale-out seam: when horizontal scale lands, per-conv serialization moves onto the shared lease store and ONLY this module changes (callers already route through it).
- **All 13 racy sites migrated:** `routes/chat_tool_state.py` (tool-toggle PATCH), `routes/conversations.py::patch_conv_settings`, `routes/chat_queue.py` (autopilot arm/disarm), `lib/message_queue.py::dispatch_next_queued` (activeTaskId, reuses the dispatch `db`), `lib/scheduler/_shared.py` + `lib/swarm/integration.py` (activeTaskId, reuse `db`), and `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` ×6 (`_get_or_persist_objective` mint-once, `_get_or_persist_run_id` mint-once, `_clear_run_id` conditional-clear, `_store_run_record` **autopilotSummaries ACCRETION** — the highest-value one, `_start_followup_task` + kick activeTaskId). INTENTIONALLY left: `manager.py:1971/1978` write settings+messages+updated_at TOGETHER in one atomic startup-recovery UPDATE that owns the row exclusively (multi-column, no concurrent writer at boot) — not a settings-only merge, correctly not split.
- **Also fixed (audit finding #5, isolated silent-failure).** `routes/conversations_compaction.py::list_compactions` returned `{compactions:[], error:'query_failed'}` with HTTP **200** on a DOUBLE query failure → the viewer silently rendered "no compactions" and HID existing archives on a transient DB hiccup (CLAUDE.md §2 violation). Now returns 500 via `api_internal_error('query_failed')` so the frontend `openCompactionViewer` catch shows its "historyFailed" retry banner. Verified the frontend caller (`Api.compactions.list` → `get()` throws `ApiError` → existing catch renders the banner) — safe contract change.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_settings_store.py` (4, warmed-DB, run DIRECTLY per the env quirk): sequential-merge keeps both keys; absent row → None; `mutate`→False skips the write (updated_at untouched); ★ `test_concurrent_writer_not_clobbered` = a classic lost-update stress test — two threads each `read n → write n+1` a shared counter 60× via the helper; correct serialization → final == 120. NEUTER = move the SELECT+parse BEFORE `with _lock_for(...)` (reproducing the bare-RMW bug) → got **60** (half the increments lost) → the concurrent test FAILED exactly as designed; restored byte-identically → 4/4 green. ### 2026-07-05 — Project Brain self-containment: feed summaries no longer HARD-TRUNCATED at write time (data loss) + long board titles/summaries render expandable-to-FULL, never a clipped fragment
- **Owner's ruling (accepted, executed).** #2 "Chinese UI shows English content" → do NOT build translate-on-write (wrong layer, hot-path latency; live agent data isn't UI chrome). Chrome already translates — leave rendering as-is for language. #3 "self-containment" is the REAL bug and is MECHANICAL truncation, not writing discipline. Fix the root cause.
- **Storage-vs-display finding (reported before touching code).** Two DIFFERENT mechanisms; only ONE was lossy: (a) **Board epic titles are stored FULL** — `post_task` caps at `_TITLE_MAX_CHARS=2000` (`project_board.py:145`, a cap already RAISED once precisely because a tight cap "clipped titles mid-word"), and `_boardCard` rendered the full `_esc(t.title)`; so the panel never lost title data — but it also never CLAMPED, so a long multi-sentence epic was a wall of text. The mid-word "…for a cl" fragment the owner saw is in the injected `[PROJECT BOARD]` **system-reminder** prompt block (context-assembly display cap) + tool-result truncation, NOT the panel and NOT storage. (b) **Feed summaries were HARD-TRUNCATED at WRITE time** — `emit_project_event` did `summary[:_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS]` (280) BEFORE the INSERT (`project_feed.py:160`), so the second half of a sentence was discarded and never reached the DB → the panel physically could not expand it. THIS is the data-loss bug.
- **Fix — backend (`lib/conversations/project_feed.py`).** Keep the cheap 280-char DISPLAY `summary`, but PRESERVE the untruncated text in `payload['summary_full']` — added `_SUMMARY_FULL_MAX_CHARS=4000` (generous: > a 2000-char title + prefix + reason; guards a pathological multi-KB summary). Only written when the summary actually exceeds the display cap (no redundant copy for the common short row) and NEVER clobbers a caller-supplied `payload['summary_full']`. `payload` is now always coerced to a dict (`dict(payload or {})`) so the event body + push frame carry it.
- **Fix — frontend (`static/js/project-brain.js`).** (1) `buildActivityRow` renders `fullText = (ev.payload && ev.payload.summary_full) || ev.summary || kindLabel` through the EXISTING `_clampBlock(_esc(fullText), fullText)` (was flat `textContent = ev.summary`); `ingestEvent` now calls `_wireClampToggles(row)` after insert so the per-row Show more/less binds. (2) `_boardCard` renders the title through `_clampBlock(_esc(t.title), t.title||'')` (was flat `_esc(t.title)`); `renderBoard` calls `_wireClampToggles(el)` once after the single-shot innerHTML (covers all cards). Short content (< 240-char threshold) gets NO clamp chrome — `_clampBlock` returns a plain inner div. The full text is ALWAYS the expandable source, never a clipped fragment.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** Backend: 3 new cases in `tests/test_project_feed.py` — long summary preserves `summary_full` verbatim (caught a real `.strip()` nuance in my first draft: emit strips the summary, so the expected value must too); short summary carries NO `summary_full`; caller-supplied `summary_full` + other payload keys survive. Frontend: NEW `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_full_expand.py` (jsdom, 3) drives the REAL shipped `renderBoard` + `ingestEvent`/`buildActivityRow` (both on `window.ProjectBrain`): a long board title is `.pb-clamp`-wrapped with the FULL title as text + toggle expands; a long activity summary renders the FULL `payload.summary_full` tail (NOT the 280 cap); short content is plain. TWO source-patched-COPY neuters (shipped file byte-identical after each): NC-A reverts `_boardCard` to flat `_esc(t.title)` → long title not clamped → fails; NC-B makes `buildActivityRow` read `ev.summary` only → full tail dropped → fails. Both fired correctly.
- **Verification.** Targeted sweep 67/67 green (feed 24 + board 35 + full_expand 3 + tabs_clamp 2 + css_cascade 3); ruff clean on all edits; `node --check` clean on `project-brain.js` AND the rebuilt bundle. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-5e517075.js`** (grep confirms `summary_full` present; minified). `styles.css` untouched this pass. **KNOWN pre-existing flake (NOT my change):** `test_frontend_project_brain.py::test_cross_project_isolation_at_push_routing` + `::test_NC_isolation_wildcard_subscription_leaks` TIME OUT at the 60s node-subprocess cap — they load the REAL `push.js`, whose `setInterval(_sendPing, …)` heartbeat (push.js:79) keeps the node event loop alive so the process never exits naturally. PROVED pre-existing: the test ALSO hangs against the pristine git-HEAD `project-brain.js` (temporarily restored, then reverted byte-identical — md5 068f6dbb…). My render-path change is a pure synchronous string wrap (no timers), and the isolation frames use short summaries → cannot introduce a 60s hang.
- **Scope/Git discipline (4-step guard).** Edits: `lib/conversations/project_feed.py` (summary_full preservation), `static/js/project-brain.js` (2 render sites + 2 clamp-wire calls), `tests/test_project_feed.py` (+3), NEW `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_full_expand.py`, rebuilt bundle. The working tree carries heavy PRE-EXISTING sibling scale-out/brain diffs (the whole tabs/clamp overhaul in project-brain.js shows as uncommitted vs HEAD) — my hunks verified isolated via `git diff --unified=0` grep. NOT committed (owner attribution). Server NOT restarted (new bundle serves on next natural start; a hard-refresh picks up both the bundle and the earlier styles.css tab fix).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A write-time hard cap on a human-readable payload is DATA LOSS, not a display choice — if a value might be shown expandable, PRESERVE the full text (a cheap capped display value + a bounded full value in the payload) so the UI can expand it; a clip with no "show more" affordance drops the tail forever. (2) Distinguish stored-truncation from display-truncation before "fixing" — the board titles were already stored full (the fragment the owner saw was a prompt-injection display cap, a separate surface), so the board fix was a DISPLAY clamp, while the feed fix was a real STORAGE change. (3) When a jsdom harness loads `push.js`, its ping `setInterval` prevents node from exiting → the subprocess runs to the timeout cap; that's harness fragility, provable by running against the pristine HEAD file, not a regression from an unrelated render edit.


### 2026-07-05 — Project Brain tab clicks did nothing: a CSS cascade tie (equal specificity → source order) that the jsdom test structurally could not catch
- **Symptom (owner-flagged).** Clicking tabs in `#projectBrainTabs` (Charter/Board/Activity/Team) never switched the visible surface. The JS was innocent: `_selectTab()` in `static/js/project-brain.js` correctly toggles `pb-tab-panel-active` on the panels and `pb-tab-active` on the tabs (verified live).
- **Root cause = CSS cascade, not JS.** The panels carry BOTH classes: `<div class="project-brain-col … pb-tab-panel pb-tab-panel-active">`. In `static/styles.css` the three rules `.pb-tab-panel{display:none}`, `.pb-tab-panel-active{display:flex}`, `.project-brain-col{…display:flex}` are ALL single-class → equal specificity (0,1,0) → the cascade fell back to SOURCE ORDER, and `.project-brain-col{display:flex}` came LAST → every panel resolved `display:flex` regardless of the active class. All four stacked; `.project-brain-columns{overflow:hidden}` clipped the lower three → "clicking does nothing".
- **Fix.** Qualify the show/hide rules to out-specify the layout rule (now (0,2,0) > (0,1,0)): `.project-brain-col.pb-tab-panel{display:none;height:100%}` / `.project-brain-col.pb-tab-panel-active{display:flex}`. Added an explanatory NOTE comment above the block. `static/styles.css` is served DIRECTLY (not through the JS bundler) → no bundle rebuild; a hard-refresh picks it up.
- **Why the existing test missed it + new guard.** `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_tabs_clamp.py` (jsdom) PASSED the whole time because jsdom resolves `classList` but does NOT apply external stylesheets — it is structurally blind to a cascade bug. NEW `tests/test_project_brain_tab_css_cascade.py` (3 tests, pure-Python) parses `styles.css`, resolves the class-specificity-then-source-order cascade for an element with the panel's real class set, and asserts inactive→`display:none` / active→`display:flex` + a structural guard that the rules are compound. DOUBLE-NEUTER: reverted the CSS to the bare `.pb-tab-panel{display:none}` ordering → `test_inactive_panel_is_hidden` FAILED (resolved `flex`) + the structural guard FAILED, reproducing the reported bug exactly; restored → 5/5 green (3 new + 2 jsdom), ruff clean.
- **Also noted (NOT changed — flagged for scope).** The `@media (max-width:720px)` block still sets `.project-brain-columns{grid-template-columns:1fr}` — a dead no-op left over from the old 4-column grid layout (the surface is now tabs, `display:block`). Harmless; left in place to keep this fix surgical.
- **i18n / cross-conversation self-containment (owner's 2nd + 3rd points — analysis, no code yet).** The panel CHROME is fully bilingual (tab labels, empty states, buttons all have valid `data-i18n` keys under `projectBrain.*` in `i18n.js`). What reads as "everything inside is English" is the CONTENT the agents wrote: charter decisions, board epic titles, activity summaries are stored as free-text English prose and are NOT translated (nor should the i18n layer translate live user/agent data). Several board titles are also TRUNCATED mid-word (e.g. "…a frame published on replica B for a cl"), which is the self-containment problem: cross-conversation payloads must be written self-contained and complete, not clipped. This is a WRITING-DISCIPLINE issue for the agents composing charter/board/feed entries, not a rendering bug — surfaced to the owner for a direction decision (translate-on-write? enforce a min-length/no-truncation contract? bilingual summaries?).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edits: the tab-panel CSS block + comment in `static/styles.css`; NEW `tests/test_project_brain_tab_css_cascade.py`. NOT committed (tree carries heavy sibling scale-out/brain diffs for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When an element carries a layout class AND a show/hide class of EQUAL specificity, the hide rule MUST be compound (qualify it with the layout class) or it loses on source order — a bare single-class `display:none` sitting near a sibling single-class `display:flex` is a latent cascade trap. And a jsdom `classList` test is NOT a substitute for resolving the actual CSS cascade: a computed-`display` test is what catches this class of bug.

### 2026-07-05 — i18n locale-split: ANALYZED and REJECTED (caching regression) — the current i18n-in-immutable-core-bundle design is optimal for a no-build project
- **Context.** Third and final item of the "better alternatives to the bundle mechanism" plan (after #3 allowlist-hardening + #1 image-gen deferral shipped). Proposal: stop shipping ALL UI-locale strings at boot; ship only the active locale.
- **Measured weight (real numbers).** `static/js/i18n.js` = **222,180 raw / 68,346 gzip** — the single heaviest core file. Structure is KEY-MAJOR: one `_i18n` object of **1821 keys**, each `{ zh: '…', en: '…' }` inline (NOT locale-major — there is no "en block" to lift out). Per-locale string values alone: zh ≈ 55.4 KB raw / 23.1 KB gz; en ≈ 56.1 KB raw / 21.8 KB gz. So the theoretical boot saving from dropping the non-active locale ≈ **~21 KB gzip**.
- **Decision (owner-ratified): DO NOT SHIP.** Three blockers, the third decisive:
  1. **No server-visible locale signal.** `tofu_ui_lang` lives ONLY in `localStorage` (i18n.js:11, `setLanguage` i18n.js:2182) — there is NO cookie. `routes/common.py::index_page` cannot know the active locale from the request, so server-side active-locale selection is infeasible without introducing a new cookie state channel.
  2. **Inlining fragments the shared-HTML cache.** `_bundled_index_cache` (routes/common.py) is a SINGLE-entry cache keyed on `(bundle_tag, styles_tag, feature_tag, html_mtime)` — the served HTML is byte-identical for every user. Inlining a per-locale blob makes the HTML vary by locale and breaks that invariant.
  3. **DECISIVE — inlining converts a first-visit-only cost into a per-reload cost.** Today i18n strings ride inside `bundle-<hash>.js`, served `Cache-Control: immutable, max-age=1yr` → downloaded ONCE EVER, then cache-hit forever. The index HTML is served `no-cache`. Inlining the active locale into the per-request HTML means the user re-downloads those ~21 KB gz on EVERY page load, forever — strictly WORSE than today for repeat visitors, and worst on the exact flaky/reload-heavy VS-Code-forwarded connections that motivated the perf work. The "~21 KB off boot" is really "~21 KB off the FIRST visit only"; every subsequent load costs ZERO today vs a recurring inline cost after the split.
- **Why this differs from #1/#3 (which WERE pure wins).** The deferred feature bundle (#1) is ALSO served immutable → cached forever → pure win. Minify (earlier) is a pure win. Locale-split is the ONE item where the mechanism is already the right shape and "improving" it trades a robust first-visit-only immutable-cached cost for a recurring `no-cache` cost (server-inline path) OR a boot-time blocking request waterfall (both-deferred + client-bootstrap path — the very latency the bundle mechanism exists to kill, rejected). There is no clean win: a separate immutable `i18n-<hash>.js` would still ship BOTH locales (saves nothing on boot) unless paired with server-selection (blocker #1/#3 again).
- **Conclusion — objective MET by #3 + #1.** "Are there better alternatives to the bundle mechanism?" → For a no-build vanilla-JS project, NO mechanism worth swapping in (esbuild/Rollup/Vite violate no-build; native-ESM/import-maps reintroduce the request waterfall). The concat + line-preserving-minify + deferred-feature-bundle design is the right shape; it was HARDENED (#3: closed-system parity test + shared `_APP_SCRIPT_SRC_SUBPATTERN`, which also surfaced+fixed a real push.js dev-fallback orphan) and DEEPENED (#1: image-gen deferral, −6.5 KB gz off boot). Locale-split (#2) analyzed and correctly rejected. Do not re-attempt without a cookie-based server-locale channel AND a per-locale immutable-cached file design that avoids the `no-cache` HTML re-download — and even then the win is first-visit-only, so the bar is high.

NOT committed (tree carries sibling work for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted (owner approval; new bundles serve on next natural start).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A "kept in core because blocked by X" claim in a manifest comment ROTS — re-verify the actual load-time surface against source before trusting it (here the blocker was attributed to the wrong file: the global + its readers were core, the deferred file only CALLED them at runtime). (2) When deferring a module, the COMPLETE onclick entry-point set must be DERIVED (grep every onclick → resolve each to its defining file), never hand-picked — a missed handler is a silent dead button, and lookalikes (`toggleImageGenTool`/`_toggleAllIgModels`) that live in CORE must NOT be stubbed. (3) The `node --check` gate earns its keep: a `*/` sequence inside a JS block comment silently closes the comment — the gate turned a would-be white-screen into a caught build error. (4) Replace brittle `len()==N` manifest assertions with structural checks so they survive the next deferral instead of failing spuriously.


### 2026-07-05 — P2 contract-change last gate: exhaustive consumer audit of the `GET /api/v1/conversations` default-shape change (CLEAN) + truthful OpenAPI annotation
- **Why.** Owner review correctly held that flipping the list endpoint's DEFAULT from full-messages → metadata-only is a LIVE contract change and demanded (1) proof no in-tree consumer silently breaks on the missing `messages`, and (2) the OpenAPI/`@api_meta` must now describe the new contract truthfully.
- **(1) Exhaustive consumer audit — VERDICT: CLEAN, no call site needs a fix.** Swept the whole repo (JS + Python + tests + SDKs + compat + facade) for bare-list callers and for code reading `.messages` off list elements. 16 surfaces checked:
  - **Frontend:** the ONLY bare-list fetch is `core/conversations.js:536-537` — BOTH branches pass `?meta=1` (reads `messageCount`/`title`/`settings`, never `.messages` off list elements; `.messages` is read only off the single `prefetched` obj). `api.js` has NO `Api.conversations.list()` method at all (the list is the raw `apiUrl(...?meta=1)` meta carve-out) → no unified-client path can hit the bare endpoint.
  - **Headless `list_conversations` agent tool (`lib/conv_ref.py:64`, the one the reviewer flagged):** runs its OWN SQL `SELECT id, title, created_at, updated_at, json_array_length(messages) as msg_count …` and uses ONLY the count (`r['msg_count']`) — it NEVER calls the HTTP list endpoint and never reads bodies. Independently re-verified by reading the function. Unaffected.
  - **compat surfaces** (`lib/compat/openai.py`, `lib/compat/anthropic.py`), the **`tofu.chat` in-process facade** (`tofu/__init__.py`), and both **SDKs** (`clients/python`, `clients/typescript`) expose NO conversations-list → N/A.
  - **No duplicate list handler** in `routes/api_v1/conversations.py` (the proxy stubs were deleted 2026-05-29; registration lives solely in `routes/conversations.py`).
  - **No `?full=1` caller exists anywhere** except the new opt-in test — confirming nothing in-tree relied on bodies via a path that now needs the flag. The 3 pre-existing test callers assert only `c['id']`.
- **(2) OpenAPI truthfulness fix (`routes/conversations.py::list_convs`).** The endpoint had NO `@api_meta` → the spec documented it with an empty description + a generic `{ok:true}` 200 (so it never LIED about bodies, but it also didn't describe the real contract). Added an accurate `@api_meta`: summary "List conversations (metadata-only by default)", documents the `full`/`meta`/`prefetch` query params, and a 200 response schema = array of items with `msgCount` in the default shape and `messages` explicitly annotated "Present only with ?full=1". Ordering follows the proven sibling pattern (`@route`→`@_db_safe`→`@api_meta`→`async def`); verified the `_api_meta` propagates through `@_db_safe`'s `functools.wraps` to the registered view — `build_spec(server.app)` now emits summary/params/array-schema correctly (not the generic default). ruff clean.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Only `routes/conversations.py` touched (added `api_meta` import + the decorator). NOT committed; server NOT restarted (the OpenAPI spec is generated on request, so the new annotation serves live once the process restarts naturally).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A default response-shape change is a contract change: before shipping, GREP EVERY consumer surface (frontend unified client AND raw carve-outs, headless agent tools that might use their OWN SQL vs the HTTP path, compat adapters, SDKs, in-process facade, and any duplicate/proxy handler) for both (a) bare-endpoint callers and (b) `.messages`-off-list-element reads — a spot-check of "the frontend + a couple tests" is not a sign-off. And when you narrow a default, document it in `@api_meta` so a headless SDK consumer isn't handed a stale/empty contract (an un-annotated route defaults to a generic `{ok:true}` schema that silently misdescribes the response).


### 2026-07-05 — Backend P2 + P3 (the two remaining audited fundamentals): default conversation LIST is now metadata-only (?full=1 opt-in) + queued-message append is CAS-guarded
- **P2 — `GET /api/v1/conversations` over-fetched full message BODIES (`routes/conversations.py::list_convs`).** The default (non-`?meta=1`) list path ran `SELECT id, title, messages, created_at, updated_at, settings … ORDER BY updated_at DESC` — pulling EVERY message of EVERY conversation (potentially megabytes) for a headless caller that just wants the list. The UI never hits this (it always uses `?meta=1`, the ETag-cached sidebar path — confirmed `core/conversations.js:536-537` passes `?meta=1` on BOTH branches). FIX: default is now metadata-only — `SELECT id, title, msg_count, …` (skips the messages column entirely; `msg_count` is a stored column so callers still get counts) via a new `_conv_row_to_meta_dict` (returns `msgCount`/`msg_count`, NO `messages`). Full bodies are opt-in via `?full=1` (legacy shape, `_conv_row_to_dict`). Confirmed NO in-tree caller depends on bodies in the list response: frontend uses `?meta=1`; the 3 test callers (`test_api_integration`, `test_conversations_async`) assert only `c['id']` presence, not `messages`. Verified against a warmed DB: default → no `messages`, `msgCount=2`; `?full=1` → `messages` present, len 2.
- **P3 — `dispatch_next_queued` did a CAS-less read-modify-write of the messages blob (`lib/message_queue.py`).** Both persist paths (pre-built + legacy) did `SELECT messages` → append → UNCONDITIONAL `UPDATE conversations SET messages=…`. `_dispatch_lock` serializes dispatches WITHIN one process but does NOT guard against a concurrent frontend/other-writer UPDATE between the SELECT and the UPDATE → last-writer-wins clobber (a racing settings PATCH or partial-stream checkpoint silently dropped). FIX: new `_append_user_msg_with_cas(db, conv_id, user_msg)` — re-reads `messages, updated_at`, idempotent-appends, and `UPDATE … WHERE … AND updated_at=?` with a bounded (4×) re-read retry (mirrors `manager._sync_partial_to_conversation`); on CAS exhaustion, ONE unconditional fallback write so the queued turn is NEVER dropped (correctness > the rare lost concurrent write; idempotent append prevents dupes). Both dispatch paths now route through it; the now-dead legacy `SELECT messages, updated_at` + parse block was removed.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (real on-disk revert).** NEW `tests/test_queue_append_cas.py` (2, standalone warmed-DB): plain append lands + bumps msg_count; a concurrent writer bumps `updated_at` + appends its OWN message BETWEEN the helper's SELECT and UPDATE (one-shot patched `db.execute`) → the helper CAS-misses, retries against the fresh tail, and lands its message WITHOUT dropping the concurrent writer's (`['first','CONCURRENT','queued']`). REAL neuter: dropped `AND updated_at=?` on disk → the concurrent writer's message was CLOBBERED (`['first','queued']`), test FAILED (exit 1); restored → 2/2 green. Regression: `test_queue_redispatch_after_restart` (3) still green — the CAS refactor preserved the end-to-end append→persist→spawn→drain behavior. NEW P2 pytest cases in `tests/test_conversations_async.py` (`test_list_convs_default_is_metadata_only` asserts no `messages` + `msgCount==2`; `test_list_convs_full_includes_bodies` asserts `?full=1` restores bodies). ruff clean on all edits.
- **KNOWN harness note (not a regression).** The `-m api` suite (Quart test client) can't reach the schema in THIS sandbox — `no such table: conversations` hits the WHOLE api suite equally (incl. the UNCHANGED `test_get_conv_404_for_missing`), the documented "DB tests pass run DIRECTLY, fail under bare pytest" quirk. So the new P2 pytest cases + the P3/checkpoint DB tests were VERIFIED by running the handler SQL/helpers directly against a warmed DB (the pattern the passing standalone tests use); they'll pass under a properly-bootstrapped `make test-api`.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edits: `routes/conversations.py` (list default + `_conv_row_to_meta_dict`), `lib/message_queue.py` (`_append_user_msg_with_cas` + route both paths through it), + 2 test files. Live peer `mr7hh5n6` (finish-tag) — no collision. NOT committed (tree carries sibling work). Server NOT restarted.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A list endpoint's DEFAULT should ship metadata, not full child collections — full bodies are an explicit opt-in (`?full=1`); the cheap cached path (`?meta=1`) shouldn't be the only way to avoid the over-fetch. (2) A per-process lock is NOT a substitute for a DB optimistic lock: `_dispatch_lock` serializes same-process dispatches but a cross-connection writer still races it — any read-modify-write of a shared blob needs `WHERE updated_at=?` CAS + bounded retry, with a final unconditional fallback so the write is never dropped.


### 2026-07-05 — Bundle allowlist trap CLOSED STRUCTURALLY: single-source-of-truth strip sub-pattern + closed-system parity test across all 5 manifests (surfaced + fixed a real pre-existing push.js dev-fallback orphan)
- **Why.** The bundler's "which file is an app script" decision was declared in FIVE places that must agree — `_BUNDLE_FILES`, `_DEFERRED_FILES` (both `lib/js_bundler.py`), the `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE` strip regex (`routes/common.py`), the `_CRITICAL_FILES ⊆ _BUNDLE_FILES` invariant, and `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS` ↔ deferred-defined-fns parity. The code-split (deferred bundle) had **widened** the classic silent-orphan trap (skill `js-bundler-allowlist-orphans-scripts`, hit 3×), not left it flat: a file added to `_DEFERRED_FILES` but forgotten in the strip set (or vice versa) is a new variant. Only 2 of the 5 edges were guarded, and NONE tied the hand-written strip regex to the manifests — the regex was a wholly independent third definition of "app script", so a regex tweak could stop stripping a bundled file's raw tag → both the tag AND the bundle load it → duplicate-IIFE crash (the exact hazard the regex's own comment warns about).
- **Design (owner-approved; NOT a regex rewrite).** Deliberately did NOT rebuild `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE` from an enumerated 90-file alternation — that would sacrifice its load-order-agnostic PATTERN match (`static/js/…`) and risk the multi-line-comment carve-out for zero safety gain. Instead: extracted the shared sub-pattern `static/js/(?!bundle-)[\w./-]+\.js` into ONE module constant `_APP_SCRIPT_SRC_SUBPATTERN` that BOTH the compiled `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE` (3× interpolation) AND a new pure predicate `is_stripped_app_script(src)` consume — so the predicate can never become a re-typed 6th copy. Verified the rebuilt regex is **byte-identical** to the original compiled pattern.
- **Test (`tests/test_bundle_manifest_parity.py`, 9 tests — closed system).** Edge 1: every top-level `static/js/*.js` on disk ∈ (`_BUNDLE_FILES ∪ _DEFERRED_FILES`) except a JUSTIFIED whitelist (`relay-admin.js`). Edge 2: every manifest entry exists on disk (stale-rename / api-keys.js class). Edge 3 (**bidirectional, via the REAL predicate**): every bundled file has a dev-fallback `<script>` tag in index.html, AND every index.html tag the strip regex REMOVES is rebuilt by a manifest — driving the shipped `is_stripped_app_script` so the regex↔manifest edge is closed structurally, not by imitation; + an assertion that the shared sub-pattern is literally embedded in `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE.pattern`. Edge 4: `_CRITICAL_FILES ⊆ _BUNDLE_FILES` (mirrored here so the whole system is in one file). Edge 5: real parity — each `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS` name (`openOrchestration`/`openTaskMode`/`togglePaperMode`) must actually be DEFINED (`function X`/`window.X =`) in a `_DEFERRED_FILES` source, upgrading the sibling test's `len()==3` sanity check; + no file in BOTH manifests (double-load). Whitelist is SELF-DOCUMENTING: `test_unbundled_whitelist_is_justified` asserts `relay-admin.js` IS a `<script>` in `static/admin.html` and is NOT one in index.html — so a genuinely-orphaned new file can't hide behind the exemption.
- **REAL BUG SURFACED + FIXED.** Edge 3's forward direction FAILED on first run: **`push.js` was in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (and is CRITICAL) but had NO `<script>` tag in index.html** — so if bundling ever failed, the dev-fallback path would silently drop the live-push channel (pushSubscribe / "N running" badge / translate status), with nothing actionable in logs. Fixed by inserting the one missing dev-fallback tag between `api.js` and `feature-loader.js` (matching `_BUNDLE_FILES` order). This is a pre-existing latent orphan the new test caught — the whole point of the epic.
- **DOUBLE-NEUTER (both on-disk, per owner request; proves the two load-bearing edges).** (1) Dropped `(?!bundle-)` from the shared sub-pattern → edge-3's boundary assertion FAILED (`is_stripped_app_script('bundle-a3f8b2c1.js')` now True — the predicate really consumes the shared pattern, and would strip the built bundle's own tag); restored → byte-identical, green. (2) Emptied `_UNBUNDLED_WHITELIST` → edge-1 FAILED with `['relay-admin.js']` (the disk-⊆-manifests orphan guard bites); restored → green.
- **Results.** 31/31 green (9 new + 10 `test_artifacts_bundle_registration` + 12 `test_bundle_corruption_guard`). ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-e38e3533.js`** (the push.js tag is dev-fallback-only; push.js was already IN the core bundle, so bundle CONTENT is unchanged — the new hash reflects only the sibling-dirty source mtimes triggering a rebuild, not my edit). No `_BUNDLE_FILES` edit.
- **Scope/Git discipline (4-step guard).** Both `routes/common.py` (+100) and `index.html` (+59) were already sibling-DIRTY in the working tree; my edits are confined to (a) the `_APP_SCRIPT_SRC_SUBPATTERN`/`is_stripped_app_script`/regex-rebuild block in common.py and (b) the single `+<script defer src="static/js/push.js">` tag in index.html — verified via targeted `git diff` grep (the `+<!-- Real-time network latency -->` line near push.js is a pre-existing sibling comment, NOT mine). New test file is wholly new. Live peer `mr7hn42q` on integrated perf/sync (round 62) — no evidence it touches js_bundler.py/common.py; kept clear of the perf files. NOT committed (tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted (owner approval; new bundle serves on next natural start).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When N declarations must agree on "what is an app script", the fix is (1) collapse the DUPLICATED pattern to ONE constant both the regex and any predicate derive from — a re-typed copy is just an (N+1)th drift source — and (2) a single closed-system test asserting every edge (disk↔manifests↔regex↔index.html + the two invariant lists), with a self-justifying whitelist for curated exceptions rather than a bare exemption. Runtime auto-discovery is the WRONG shape here (hand-ordered load dependencies + intentional exclusions like relay-admin/feature-loader can't be inferred from `os.listdir`) — enforce closure in a TEST, keep the ordered manifests as the runtime source of truth. A parity test's first run is where latent orphans surface (here: push.js's missing dev-fallback tag).


### 2026-07-05 — Frontend bundle CODE-SPLIT: core boot bundle + on-demand feature bundle (−13.1% gzip off time-to-first-paint), the biggest measured frontend fundamental
- **Why (owner directive: "push forward without regard to cost", close the biggest measured fundamental).** The served JS was ONE monolithic `bundle-<hash>.js` = **2,011,737 raw / 496,191 gzip**, and a measure-first audit found ~61% of gzip was feature-gated code most sessions never open. Split the three heaviest, cleanest-to-defer features into a SECOND bundle fetched on first use.
- **Method (measure-first, 2 parallel audits).** (1) byte-weight analyst: paper-reader 54KB gz + orchestration 36KB gz + task-mode 12KB gz are the big clean wins; settings/ (92KB gz) and i18n (66KB gz, 2 locales × 1821 keys inline) are bigger but riskier (settings entangled; i18n is load-first infra). (2) dependency-safety coder: verified DEFER-SAFE = paper-reader/orchestration/task-mode/image-gen/myday (no core LOAD-time refs to their symbols; all `typeof`-guarded inside fn bodies; clean zero-arg onclick entry points); MUST-STAY = scheduler/optimizer/timer (load-time badge-polling IIFEs). I scoped this landing CONSERVATIVELY to the 3 lowest-entanglement wins (excluded image-gen — core reads its undeclared `imageGenMode` global at conv-restore, `main.js:513`; and myday — boot reminder toast) to prove the mechanism before widening.
- **Architecture (both bundles share window scope — plain concatenated `<script>`s, NOT ES modules).**
  - `lib/js_bundler.py`: new `_DEFERRED_FILES = [orchestration, task-mode, paper-reader]` (order matters: task-mode reads orchestration's `_ORCH_*` at runtime). Refactored the build loop into a shared `_assemble_bundle(files, prefix, critical)` (scan→minify→concat→hash→write→node-gate); `build_bundle()` builds BOTH (core `bundle-<hash>.js` required + fatal-fallback on a critical file; deferred `feature-<hash>.js` optional — its failure degrades to "that feature won't open", surfaced by the loader). New `get_feature_bundle_filename()`.
  - NEW `static/js/feature-loader.js` (CORE bundle, before main.js): `_loadFeatureBundle()` (idempotent Promise, injects the feature `<script>` once from `window.__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__`, resets on error so a flaky-network click retries) + `_onReady(fn)` helper + installs a lazy STUB for each of `openOrchestration`/`openTaskMode`/`togglePaperMode` that loads the bundle then dispatches to the REAL fn (which by then overwrote the stub). Guard: if `__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__` is absent (dev fallback → individual `<script>` tags, real fns already present) NO stub is installed — never clobbers a real fn.
  - `paper-reader.js`: its unconditional `DOMContentLoaded` init (`_loadPaperLibrary`+drag-drop, `:4437`) → `_onReady(...)` so it runs when the module loads AFTER boot (a bare DOMContentLoaded listener would silently never fire post-boot). Its other init (`:1192`) already had the `readyState!=='loading'` else-branch → safe.
  - `routes/common.py::index_page`: injects `<script>window.__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__="static/js/feature-<hash>.js";</script>` immediately BEFORE the core bundle tag (so the global is defined before feature-loader.js runs); `feature_tag` added to the `_bundled_index_cache` key so a feature-hash change re-renders. `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE` already strips ALL app `<script>` tags (incl. the deferred three + feature-loader) → replaced by the bundle, no double-load. index.html: added `feature-loader.js` `<script>` (dev fallback) + `openOrchestration`/`openTaskMode` to the pre-boot LoadGuard stubs.
- **★ BUG I introduced AND fixed (critical, own-source deletion).** First rebuild SILENTLY DELETED `static/js/feature-loader.js`: `_clean_old_bundles` removed any `.js` file `startswith('feature-')` that wasn't the current feature bundle — and the SOURCE `feature-loader.js` starts with `feature-`. A runtime-assembled artifact deleted its own source. FIX: anchor the cleaner to the hashed OUTPUT pattern `^(?:bundle|feature)-[0-9a-f]{8}\.js$` (`_BUILT_BUNDLE_RE`), never a prefix `startswith`. Memory `bundle-cleaner-must-not-delete-source` recorded. (This is exactly the corruption-guard skill's "must never delete its own source" rule.)
- **MEASURED WIN (real gzip bytes, before/after).** Boot path: **496,191 → 431,184 gzip = −65,007 (−13.1%)**. Deferred feature bundle: 276,430 raw / 66,184 gzip, loaded ONLY on first Paper/Studio/Tasks open. Core+feature raw (2,014,047) ≈ old total + feature-loader → no code lost, just moved off the boot path. Verified split correctness by grep: 0 feature-fn definitions in core / 3 in feature; loader machinery in core / 0 in feature. Verified the served-HTML rewrite end-to-end (inlined `_APP_SCRIPTS_RE`): core tag ×1, `__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__` ×1, all 3 deferred + feature-loader tags stripped.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** NEW `tests/test_frontend_feature_lazyload.py` (4): jsdom drives the REAL feature-loader — stub installed → first call injects the feature `<script>` exactly once → after simulated load the real fn dispatches with forwarded args → second call no new injection; dev-fallback (no `__FEATURE_BUNDLE_SRC__`) preserves a pre-existing real fn; NEUTER = a mutated COPY whose `_installFeatureStub` is a no-op → no injection (proves the stub is load-bearing; shipped file untouched); + a no-node static invariant that JS `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS` == bundler `_DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS`. ### 2026-07-05 — Integrated frontend+backend performance & sync fundamentals: killed the per-5s full-conversation search_text/FTS rebuild on partial checkpoints + consolidated the divergent-guard reconcile timers into ONE
- **Method (measure-first).** Spawned 3 parallel `coder` audits — backend request-path perf, frontend↔backend sync correctness, frontend load/render — BEFORE touching anything, then verified every finding against source. Scope deliberately EXCLUDED the finish-tag / incomplete-render render guard (`finish_info.js`/`chat_render.js` finish-bar logic) since live peer `mr7hh5n6` owns that (messaged them; posted+claimed board epic `pt_3be8300459344cd3`). Also out of scope: the parked §10 scale-out Epics B/C/D (Redis/PgBouncer) — these are single-box fundamentals that help EVERY deployment.
- **Audit verdict.** Most hot paths are already in good shape (meta cache + covering `idx_conv_meta`; in-memory SSE loop with no per-frame DB; parallel boot `Promise.all` + prefetch-folded first conv; in-place status-patch conversation list with 50-row windowing; correct IDB hydrate-before-fetch). TWO real fundamentals + several lower-ROI items remained. Two stale JOURNAL/memory claims were DISPROVEN by the sync agent: queued-message durability is CLOSED (`redispatch_orphaned_queue_on_startup` wired at `manager.py:2039`), and `_sync_partial_to_conversation` DOES now have a `WHERE …updated_at=?` CAS.
- **Fix 1 — backend perf (highest ROI), `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py` `_sync_partial_to_conversation` (~L1691).** The 5s streaming checkpoint used to rebuild the FULL `search_text` (`build_search_text` walks EVERY message) AND DELETE+INSERT the SQLite FTS row on EVERY checkpoint — cost scales with the whole conversation, not the streamed delta, repeated ~every 5s for the whole turn. It is PURE WASTE: the terminal `_sync_result_to_conversation` (L1367/1374) ALWAYS rebuilds `search_text` from the final messages, so a mid-stream `search_text` is superseded on completion; and indexing a not-yet-final tail makes mid-stream search hits point at unsettled content. FIX: partials now write ONLY the reload-critical columns (`messages`/`updated_at`/`msg_count`); the `build_search_text` call + `update_conversation_fts` call are removed from the partial path. Search indexing is owned SOLELY by the terminal sync. Verified: terminal sync still indexes settled content (behaviour preserved, not removed).
- **Fix 2 — sync correctness, `static/js/main.js` (~L1049) + `static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js`.** There were THREE visible-idle list-reconcile paths; the 60s `main.js` timer had a WEAKER guard — it checked `visible` + `_editingMsgIdx` but OMITTED `activeStreams.size===0`, so it could fire a full id-keyed list merge + `renderConversationList` DURING an active stream (needless mid-stream churn + a divergent contract across timers; not data-loss because `loadConversationsFromServer`'s 304/count-drop/allowTruncate guards still block truncation). This is exactly the "eventual clean move: ONE consolidated reconciler" that the 2026-07-05 cross-device-reconcile entry logged as a follow-up. FIX: DELETED the 60s timer; the fully-guarded 25s `_crossDeviceReconcile` (visible AND `activeStreams.size===0` AND not editing, shared `_bootLoadInFlight` latch) is now the SOLE visible-idle reconciler, and I folded the deleted timer's `requestIdleCallback` INP-yield into it so that benefit isn't lost.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (real on-disk reverts).** NEW `tests/test_partial_checkpoint_no_search_text.py` (2, standalone DB harness like `test_startup_reconcile.py` — run DIRECTLY, DB-warm quirk): (1) a partial checkpoint GROWS the tail content but leaves `search_text` at its pre-existing sentinel, AND an exploding `build_search_text` stub proves the fn is NOT called on the partial path; (2) the terminal sync DOES rebuild `search_text` from settled content (indexing preserved). REAL on-disk neuter: re-added the `search_text=` rebuild to the partial UPDATE → test #1 FAILED (`got 'question\npartial answer so far'` — the reindexed content the assertion catches, exit 1); restored → 2/2 green, region byte-restored. Existing `test_frontend_cross_device_reconcile.py` still green (its idle-guard neuter still bites; my rIC-yield takes the `else _run()` branch under bare node so the latch-set-then-cleared assertions hold). Regression sweep: `test_startup_reconcile` 3/3, `test_committed_message_parity` 3/3, `test_chat_manager_migration` 21/21 — all green. ruff clean. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-ca977dd1.js`** (grep-confirmed `_crossDeviceReconcile`/`requestIdleCallback` present; the `60000`/`6e4` interval gone from `main.js`).
- **NOT shipped (logged as follow-ups, deliberately not gold-plated).** (a) Backend P2: the default (non-`meta`) conversation LIST over-fetches full `messages` bodies for headless/API-v1 clients (UI already uses `?meta=1`) — gate full bodies behind `?full=1`. (b) Backend P3: `dispatch_next_queued` (`message_queue.py`) does a CAS-less read-modify-write of the messages blob (last-writer-wins), mitigated by `_dispatch_lock` — low severity; add `AND updated_at=?` + bounded re-read. (c) Frontend's biggest remaining win: bundle is 2.01 MB raw / 496 KB gzip single monolith with ~595 KB of feature-gated code (paper-reader/orchestration/task-mode/myday/project-brain/image-gen/branch) shipped at boot + i18n shipping all locales — lazy-`import()` a second bundle + locale-split would cut TTI payload ~30%. This is a larger, riskier change (touches `_BUNDLE_FILES` + code-splitting seam) — left for a dedicated pass rather than bundled into this surgical one.

Live peer `mr7hh5n6` on the finish-tag epic — no file/logic collision (I touched neither `finish_info.js` nor the `chat_render.js` finish-bar guards). - **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A periodic checkpoint that re-derives a WHOLE-conversation artifact (search_text/FTS) on every tick is O(conv-size)×frequency waste when a terminal writer already rebuilds it — checkpoints should persist only what a mid-stream RELOAD needs, and leave derived-index rebuilds to the single terminal writer. (2) When N timers do the same reconcile with DIVERGENT guards, that's a latent bug even if truncation guards mask the data-loss — consolidate to ONE fully-guarded path and fold in any unique benefit (here the rIC INP-yield) rather than leaving the weaker duplicate. (3) Always verify stale JOURNAL/memory claims against CURRENT source before "fixing" them — two of the audited "bugs" were already closed.


### 2026-07-05 — Premature/incomplete "finish tag" on an UNFINISHED message (poor-signal / cross-device static render): gated `renderFinishInfo` on a terminal signal + live-tail
- **Symptom (owner).** On a flaky connection / cross-device reload, a conversation renders with a "message finish" bar carrying ONLY the model tag (no ✓/tokens/cost) even though the turn is still running — the finish tag has not actually concluded. This is a display bug, not data loss; it self-heals once SSE reconnects and stamps `finishReason`/`usage`.
- **Root cause (single mismatched guard).** `renderFinishInfo(msg)` (`static/js/ui/finish_info.js:562`) emitted a bar whenever ANY of `finishReason`/`usage`/`model`/`preset`/`effort` was truthy. But the backend mid-stream checkpoint `_sync_partial_to_conversation` (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py:1557`, docstring L1566-67) DELIBERATELY persists `model`/`preset` while WITHHOLDING the terminal-only fields (`finishReason`/`usage`/`toolSummary`) until completion. So a still-running assistant message — persisted mid-stream, then fetched by another device or re-rendered before SSE reconnects — carries `model` but no terminal signal, and the STATIC `renderMessage()` path (`chat_render.js:1178`) drew a bogus finished bar. (Same bug class as the `renderChat`-full-rerender memory, but here the trigger is the no-reconnect / cross-device window, NOT a mid-stream re-render.)
- **Why NOT a blunt `finishReason||usage` guard (owner's edge, verified).** `build_result_meta` (`manager.py:597`) stamps `meta['finishReason']`/`meta['usage']` only `if task.get(...)` is truthy — they are NOT unconditional. Two classes of GENUINELY-finished messages carry only `model`: (1) **legacy** messages persisted before the usage/cost-persistence change (confirmed via the `persisted-cost-snapshot-on-message` skill); (2) **degenerate empty completions** — the orchestrator can set `finishReason=None` + empty `usage` on a stream that finished with no tokens (`persist_task_result` warns about exactly this at `manager.py:719`). A pure guard would BLANK their bar → a real regression.
- **Fix (distinguishes "not finished" from "finished, model-only").** `renderFinishInfo(msg, isLiveTail)`: emit whenever a TERMINAL signal (`finishReason || usage`) is present. A model-only message (no terminal signal) renders NO bar ONLY when `isLiveTail` — computed at the SINGLE call site (`chat_render.js:1178`) as *"assistant message that is the last message of the active conv AND (`activeStreams.has(conv.id)` OR `conv.activeTaskId`)"*, reusing the existing last-assistant predicate pattern at `chat_render.js:1206-1208`. A finished-but-model-only message is NOT the live tail → keeps its bar (no legacy/degenerate regression). `renderFinishInfo` stays pure-of-`msg`+one bool; the LIVE `#streaming-msg` bubble never routes through this path (verified: `streaming_ui.js` doesn't call `renderFinishInfo`; renders its own bar via `finishStream`) so the live bar is untouched.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (on-disk, per owner request).** NEW `tests/test_frontend_premature_finish_bar.py` — extracts the REAL shipped `renderFinishInfo` via brace-match, evals with cost/format helpers stubbed, drives every shape: model-only+livetail → "" (bug case suppressed); model-only+NOT-livetail (+ undefined) → bar kept (legacy/degenerate — no regression); `finishReason` → bar even on live tail; `usage`-only → token bar; empty → "". In-harness neuter strips `if (!_terminal && isLiveTail) return ""` on a MUTATED copy → model-only+livetail re-emits the premature bar. REAL on-disk neuter: reverted the guard in the shipped file → test FAILED (the Python stale-guard assertion caught it), restored → **md5 `0061d628357dc2677cc7efbc7e580e36` byte-identical**, 14+ PASS green. Regression sweep with `finishstream_no_put` + `cross_device_reconcile` + `buried_ghost_sweep` = 4 green; ruff clean; `node --check` clean both files.
- **Bundle.** finish_info.js + chat_render.js both already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. Rebuilt → **`bundle-4bfa59ce.js`** (grep-confirmed post-minify: `isLiveTail`×4, `_terminal&&isLiveTail`, `_isLiveTail`×2). Server NOT restarted (owner approval; serves on next natural start).
- **Scope/Git discipline (4-step guard).** Both files were already sibling-DIRTY (finish_info.js +918/-201, chat_render.js +546 — pre-existing session work: file-changes helpers, `premature_close` label, etc.). My edits confined to exactly two spots (the `renderFinishInfo` signature+guard; the call-site `_isLiveTail` block) — verified via `git diff` grep. Live peer `mr7hn42q` is on integrated perf/sync work whose epic note EXPLICITLY excludes the finish-tag render guard ("owned by mr7hh5n6" = this conv) → no collision. NOT committed (tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work for the owner to attribute).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A finish/terminal-state UI predicate must key on a signal the backend stamps ONLY at completion (`finishReason`/`usage`) — NOT on early-stamped identity fields (`model`/`preset`/`effort`), which are set mid-stream by design. When suppressing a "done" affordance, distinguish "not finished yet" (the live running tail) from "finished but sparse" (legacy / degenerate-empty) — a blunt terminal-only guard silently regresses the latter. The mid-stream persistence contract (`_sync_partial_to_conversation` withholds terminal fields) is the authoritative source of truth for what "not finished" looks like on disk.

### 2026-07-05 — Cross-device conversation-list drift: added a 25s visible-idle reconciliation poll (option 2) so a phone + desktop converge without a refocus
- **Symptom (owner, verified against code).** Opening the app on a mobile browser and on the desktop simultaneously shows the two conversation lists "surprisingly out of sync." Root cause is architectural, NOT data loss: the conversation list is reconciled with the server by **PULL only** — there is no cross-DEVICE push channel. `BroadcastChannel` (`_handleCrossTabMsg` in `static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js`) is same-machine/same-origin only, so a phone and a computer never share it; and the only cross-device refresh triggers are `visibilitychange` (pulls only when the tab REGAINS focus while idle: `visible && activeStreams.size===0 && _editingMsgIdx===null`) and `_startOfflineRecoveryPolling` (a 15s interval GATED on the presence of `server_offline` convs → no-ops in the normal case). A phone left visible-but-untouched never re-pulls. Over the owner's flaky VS Code port-forward this is pronounced: `visibilitychange` refreshes get suppressed (a stuck/attempted stream keeps `activeStreams` non-empty, or the fetch fails and `loadConversationsFromServer` swallows it). It is *display* drift that self-heals on refocus — the server is authoritative and the stale-truncate guards (0-msg-sync skip, `save_conv` 409, count-drop/`allowTruncate`) prevent a stale device clobbering fresher state.
- **Decision.** Option 3 (push fan-out over `/api/push` keyed by user) is the "right" fix but is **§10-gated / parked as Epic B** (`pt_823ff5a3bf004c40`) — deliberately NOT coupled into ad hoc. Shipped **option 2**: a periodic visible-idle reconciliation poll.
- **Fix (`static/js/core/cross_tab_sync.js`, appended `_crossDeviceReconcile` + `setInterval(…, 25000)`).**
  - Idle guard **byte-identical** to the `conv_saved` cross-tab refresh (`document.visibilityState==='visible' && activeStreams.size===0 && _editingMsgIdx===null`) → can never fire over a live stream or an in-progress edit; a hidden/background tab short-circuits before any fetch (no network churn on mobile).
  - **Reuses `loadConversationsFromServer()` verbatim** — no re-implemented merge. Its 304 / count-drop / `allowTruncate` guards are untouched, so a periodic re-pull can only ADD/UPDATE, never truncate fresher server state.
  - **Shares the window-scoped `_bootLoadInFlight` latch** with the boot-reconnect backoff (`_bootReconnectWithBackoff`) and the 60s `main.js:1049` poll — set synchronously before the async load, cleared in `.finally` — so overlapping loads across the three timers are impossible.
  - Cadence **25s** (sane middle of the requested 20–30s band).
- **KNOWN LATENT GAP (logged, intentionally left out of scope).** There is a PRE-EXISTING visible-idle reconciliation timer at **`static/js/main.js:1049`** (`setInterval(…, 60000)`) that also calls `loadConversationsFromServer()` and shares `_bootLoadInFlight` — but its guard is **weaker**: it checks `visibilityState==='visible'` + `_editingMsgIdx` but **omits the `activeStreams.size===0` check**. So the 60s timer can fire a list re-pull DURING an active stream (harmless today because `loadConversationsFromServer` won't overwrite a streaming conv, but it's a divergent-guard smell). My new 25s timer is the stricter, fully-guarded one and layers cleanly (shared latch). The eventual clean move is **ONE consolidated visible-idle reconciler with the full idle guard**, not two timers with divergent guards + a redundant third. Left as a follow-up rather than editing the sibling-adjacent `main.js` region.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (all green; clean-cache).** NEW `tests/test_frontend_cross_device_reconcile.py` — loads the REAL shipped `cross_tab_sync.js` under bare node, stubs window globals + `loadConversationsFromServer`, drives `_crossDeviceReconcile()` directly: idle → fires exactly ONE load with the latch set-then-cleared; suppressed under active-stream / hidden-tab / editing / latch-held. NEUTER: strips the idle-guard block on a MUTATED copy (shipped file never touched) — `neuter_patch_applied` proves the guard string genuinely matched (not a silent skip), and `neuter_fires_when_it_should_not` proves it then fires with EVERY idle condition violated → the guard is load-bearing. 17 assertions green. Regression sweep with `test_frontend_poll_reconnect_hint` + `test_frontend_cache_hydrate_boot` + `test_frontend_buried_ghost_sweep` = 10 green. `node --check` clean; ruff clean. `core/cross_tab_sync.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → ships on next build.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edit confined to the appended `_crossDeviceReconcile` block; the `conv_restored` case + the `_streamFrameArg` visibilitychange refactor visible in `git diff` are PRE-EXISTING sibling work in the dirty tree (untouched, verified via hunk headers). NOT committed (tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted (owner approval; new bundle serves on next natural start).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Cross-TAB sync (BroadcastChannel) is NOT cross-DEVICE sync — same-machine only. Absent a push channel, cross-device convergence needs a periodic PULL, but it must carry the SAME idle guard as the focus-refresh (never clobber a live stream/edit) and SHARE the in-flight latch so N timers can't stack. When you add such a timer, GREP for existing reconciliation intervals first (`main.js:1049` here) and record any divergent-guard duplicate as a consolidation follow-up rather than silently adding a third.


### 2026-07-05 — Follow-up (owner review catch): applied the fetch_url fix's OWN guardrail to the streaming `web_search` branch — it re-implemented the search path instead of delegating (thread-pool LEAK + dropped exception safety net)
- **Why.** The owner correctly flagged that the joint-optimization sign-off was incomplete: the streaming pre-exec `web_search` branch (`streaming_tool_executor.py:_execute_one`, single + batch) RE-IMPLEMENTED the search pipeline inline (`resolve_vertical` + `perform_web_search` + its own `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` for the vertical plan + hand-rolled `_search_diag`/`_engine_breakdown`/display assembly), and — exactly like the `fetch_url` case just fixed — its result is injected into `_tool_result_cache` as AUTHORITATIVE (serial pipeline skips re-exec). Same invisible-loss bug class, one function over.
- **Real diff vs the serial single-source-of-truth `handlers/search.py:_web_search_one` (3 concrete divergences, not "looks similar"):**
  1. **Thread-pool LEAK.** `_web_search_one` does `_vertical_pool.shutdown(wait=False)`; the inline streaming copy created `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` per vertical query and NEVER shut it down → a leaked pool per streamed search/batch-query with an active vertical.
  2. **Dropped exception safety net.** `_web_search_one` wraps `perform_web_search` in try/except → on failure returns `([], {'reason':'exception','reason_detail':…}, None, vertical_result)` and still resolves the vertical (timeout=10). Streaming didn't wrap it: a single-search exception escaped to the outer handler (no graceful `search_diag`); batch produced a raw `Search failed for "q": <exc>` string instead of serial's formatted "internal error (see logs)" block.
  3. **Vertical timeout divergence** (streaming hard-coded 5s; serial uses 10s on the search-failure path).
