Metadata-carrier parity preserved exactly: `display_results` (with `_q` per-query tagging + `fetched`/`fetchedChars`), `engine_breakdown`, `search_diag` (only when 0 results), singular `vertical` dict for single-query, and the intentional `{'batch': [...]}` carrier for batch (consumed at `tool_dispatch.py:1063` → frontend `verticals` array). Lazy import avoids the search.py↔executor cycle. Batch spec tuple order corrected to `(query, freshness, vertical)` to match the serial worker.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (real on-disk reverts).** NEW `tests/test_streaming_websearch_delegation.py` (5, pure-pytest, patches `handlers.search._web_search_one` + `tofu_search.search.format_search_for_tool_response`): single routes through `_web_search_one` with the serial arg contract + carries `engine_breakdown`/stripped-`full_content` display; 0-results carries `search_diag`; single vertical → singular dict carrier (NOT `{'batch'}`); batch → `{'batch':[…]}` carrier with per-query `query` key + `_q` tagging + `=== Search: q ===` headers; + neuter test asserting a `RuntimeError` from `_web_search_one` propagates (proving it's actually invoked). REAL neuter: reverted single branch to inline `perform_web_search` → 4 single-dependent tests FAILED (incl. the mock never called); reverted batch worker likewise → batch test FAILED; restored both → 5/5 green, region byte-restored. Full sweep: websearch + fetch_url + bridge_config + streaming_and_prefetch = 45 green; ruff clean.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** Edits confined to the `web_search`/`fetch_url` branches of `_execute_one`; the L74/186 hunks are pre-existing sibling work (untouched), verified via `git diff` hunk headers. Live peer `mr77zwjj` on unrelated epic — no collision. NOT committed (tree carries sibling work); server NOT restarted (backend-only, no bundle change).
- **Guardrail / lesson (reinforced).** When you fix an instance of a bug class, GREP THE WHOLE FILE for sibling instances of the same pattern before sign-off — the `fetch_url` and `web_search` fast paths sat 40 lines apart with the identical authoritative-cache-over-a-stale-reimplementation hazard. A reviewer catching the second instance means the first fix's own documented guardrail wasn't applied exhaustively. "I only audited X" is not a sign-off when Y has the same shape.

- **Symptom (owner).** The standalone autopilot toggle works great, but picking "自动驾驶" from the 编排流程 (orchestration) dropdown "performs oddly" even though it's "clearly designed to be the same."

This BYPASSED the `TOFU_AUTOPILOT_VIA_FLOW` flag whose own docstring says it must default OFF with the live `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` path AUTHORITATIVE. The engine path diverges on 4 axes vs standalone (full parity table built in-conv): VU-turn events (`endpoint_critic_msg`+`_isEndpointReview` vs `autopilot_vu_*`+`_isVirtualUser`), **worker substrate** (single-task SubAgent loop vs a chain of real chat tasks via `maybe_run_autopilot`→`autopilotNextTaskId` — the real "feels odd"), run-level grouping (no `runId`/`autopilot_run_concluded`/summary fold), loop control (the ONLY matching axis — both share `agent_verdict.classify_verdict(verifier_role='virtual_user')`).
- **Backend fix — Option C, single writer (`lib/orchestration_endpoint_runner.py::resolve_chat_flow_entry`, head of fn before the selection branch).** When `flowBuiltin=='autopilot'` and NOT `autopilot_via_flow_enabled()`: set `config['autopilot']=True`, CLEAR `config['flowBuiltin']=None` (so the selection branch can't re-grab it), `audit_log('autopilot_builtin_to_live', …)` + `logger.info` (routing override leaves a trace), and `return None`. Confirmed fall-through: `routes/chat.py:393` → None + not endpoint → `routes/chat.py:437` `else` → `spawn_task` (normal task) → `orchestrator.py:943` `maybe_run_autopilot` fires because `is_autopilot_enabled` returns True on `cfg['autopilot']` (`autopilot.py:672`) → full `autopilot_vu_*` + `autopilot_run_concluded` family, `_isVirtualUser`/`_autopilotRunId` persistence, runId fold, baton on `done_evt` (`orchestrator.py:945-947`). Mapping lives in ONE place (the resolver "where all flagging/precedence lives"); nothing added to `conv_config.py` or `routes/chat.py`.

Made `builtin:autopilot` a UI alias for the autopilot toggle: (1) `setActiveFlow('builtin:autopilot')` delegates to `toggleAutopilot()` (covers NEW selections); (2) `_applyFlowUI('builtin:autopilot')` normalizes to `activeFlow=''`+`_applyAutopilotUI(true)`+`_applyEndpointUI(false)` (covers RESTORE/RELOAD/sync of a conv persisted with the stale value). **Choke point #2 deliberately lives in `_applyFlowUI` so it covers the sibling-diff-locked `_restoreConvToolState` line at `main.js:595` WITHOUT editing that sibling-held region** — a single choke point every caller funnels through. Result: dropdown = byte-identical to the toggle — autopilot badge, info-rail "Autopilot" chip (`info-rail.js:_collectModes` — flow empty → falls to the `autopilotEnabled` branch), and the `_buildToolbarOverrides` → `/config/resolve` payload (`autopilot:true, activeFlow:''`).
- **VERIFIED non-issue (owner question #3).** `activeFlow` drives NO send-time bubble — the endpoint/planner bubble is gated ONLY on `endpointEnabled`/`endpointMode`/`_isEndpointPlanner` (`sse_pipeline.js:279-280`, `stream_lifecycle.js:63`), never on `activeFlow`. Dropdown left `endpointEnabled=false` and the backend now returns a plain autopilot task (no `endpointMode` in SSE `state`), so no stray endpoint bubble is seeded; the `autopilot_vu_*` handlers are event-type-keyed, so the VU bubble already rendered identically. Only the toolbar/info-rail IDENTITY diverged — which the frontend fix closes.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (all green: 21).** `tests/test_chat_flow_dispatch.py` (16): `test_builtin_autopilot_maps_to_live_path` (dropdown → None + cfg mutated), `test_builtin_autopilot_equals_standalone_toggle` (dropdown outcome == `{autopilot:True}` toggle outcome), `test_builtin_autopilot_escape_hatch_still_engine` (`TOFU_AUTOPILOT_VIA_FLOW=1` → still `run_flow_via_chat`, cfg untouched), `test_neutering_option_c_regresses_to_engine` (NC: patch `autopilot_via_flow_enabled→True` → dropdown regresses to the endpoint-critic engine path); UPDATED `test_selected_flow_always_wins_no_flag_needed` (it USED TO ENCODE THE BUG — asserted `flowBuiltin:'autopilot'` IS `run_flow_via_chat`; now covers flowId/flowDefinition/`flowBuiltin:'endpoint'` only); `AutopilotE2ETest` UNTOUCHED (still exercises the flagged engine path). `tests/test_frontend_builtin_autopilot_toggle_parity.py` (jsdom, 2): Path A (toggle) vs Path B (dropdown) parity on every axis + endpoint-flow-unaffected control; NC byte-reverts BOTH choke points → dropdown regresses to `activeFlow='builtin:autopilot'`+autopilot OFF → parity fails (proves both are load-bearing; either alone still converges so the NC must revert both). Regression sweep with `test_frontend_autopilot_vu_verbatim` + `test_frontend_autopilot_fold` = 21 green. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-d8fd158e.js`** (grep-confirmed post-minify: `builtin:autopilot`×5, `setActiveFlow`, `_applyAutopilotUI`). Both edited JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (`main/` path). `node --check` clean; ruff clean.
- **FORWARD-LOOKING FLAG (not a blocker; for whoever validates the engine path).** When someone eventually sets `TOFU_AUTOPILOT_VIA_FLOW=1`, the BACKEND takes the engine path but the two FRONTEND choke points STILL alias the dropdown to the autopilot toggle — so the UI would show the autopilot identity while the backend runs the engine. Acceptable today (the flag is dev/validation-only and the frontend can't read server env), but the eventual clean fix is to surface the resolved run-mode in the SSE `state` snapshot and let the frontend reflect THAT rather than guessing from `activeFlow`. Noted here + in the skill.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** 4-step Git guard: `resolve_chat_flow_entry` sits inside uncommitted prior-session flow-selector work (whole fn shows as `+`); `setActiveFlow`/`_applyFlowUI` likewise inside an uncommitted `+` hunk — prior-session work, not a live sibling (only live peer `mr6pcerd` is on Project Brain, unrelated). Edited ONLY `lib/orchestration_endpoint_runner.py` + `static/js/main/main_toolbar_ui.js` (+ 2 new test files + skill note); `main.js`/`conv_config.py`/`routes/chat.py`/`info-rail.js` carry ONLY pre-existing sibling diffs — I touched none. NOT committed (working tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted (owner approval required; the new bundle serves on next natural start).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A "selection = opt-in" resolver branch can silently OVERRIDE a feature's own default-off flag — when a builtin duplicates a toggle, special-case it to the toggle's authoritative path at the SINGLE resolver choke point rather than letting the generic selection branch grab it. (2) "Backend behaves the same" ≠ "frontend behaves the same": a dropdown vs a toggle are different frontend STATES even when they now hit identical backend code — converge the UI identity too (badge, info-rail chip, config payload), and put the restore/reload normalization at a choke point (`_applyFlowUI`) that every caller funnels through so you needn't edit a sibling-locked region. (3) When a fix has TWO choke points that each independently converge, the double-neuter MUST revert BOTH — reverting one leaves the other masking the regression.

### 2026-07-05 — chatui ⋈ tofu-search joint optimization: closed host↔library config drift (0.3.2/0.4.1 knobs unpassed) + fixed an INVISIBLE fetch_url content-loss bug on the streaming pre-exec path
- **Method.** Measure-first: spawned 3 parallel `coder` audits (version/config drift; lxml thread-safety regression check; runtime call-site integration map) before touching anything, then verified every finding against source. tofu-search had drifted to **v0.4.1** while chatui consumed it with stale wiring.
- **Fix A — config drift (highest tunability win), `lib/search_bridge.py` + `requirements.txt`.** `sync_search_config()` never forwarded the tofu-search **0.3.2 pre-fetch relevance gate** knobs (`prefetch_gate_enabled` / `prefetch_gate_min_query_terms` / `prefetch_gate_min_fetch`) nor the **0.4.1 adaptive-proxy** knob (`proxy_dual_attempt`). CRITICAL detail: the three `prefetch_gate_*` fields have **NO env-var mapping inside** `tofu_search.configure()` (unlike the `FETCH_*` / `TOFU_SEARCH_PROXY_*` fields), so unless the bridge passes them EXPLICITLY they silently run library defaults and are **un-tunable from the chatui host**. Added all four to the `configure(...)` call + the log line, with a new `_env_bool(key, default)` helper (env `PREFETCH_GATE_ENABLED` → `_lib.PREFETCH_GATE_ENABLED` fallback; `PREFETCH_GATE_MIN_QUERY_TERMS`/`_MIN_FETCH` ints; `TOFU_SEARCH_PROXY_DUAL_ATTEMPT` bool). Bumped `requirements.txt` floor `>=0.4.0`→`>=0.4.1` (the version that defines `proxy_dual_attempt`; an older `configure()` rejects the kwarg).
- **Fix C — INVISIBLE content-loss bug (highest ROI), `lib/tasks_pkg/streaming_tool_executor.py`.** The streaming pre-exec `fetch_url` path (both batch ~448 and single ~501) used the OLD text-only `fetch_page_content`, while the serial handler `handlers/search.py:_fetch_url_one` had since gained binary-asset staging (`_stage_binary_asset` → `fetch_url_bytes` → `data/fetched/` for `read_files`) and text-asset passthrough (SVG/JSON/source raw, skipping the article filter). Because the streaming result is injected into `task['_tool_result_cache']` as **AUTHORITATIVE** (the serial pipeline finds the cache hit at `tool_dispatch.py:1013` and SKIPS re-execution), a binary/text-asset URL pre-executed during streaming **silently returned nothing** — and the empty result was cached, so the loss was invisible (no error, no fallback). Fix: route both streaming modes through `_fetch_url_one` / `_format_fetch_display` (single source of truth), via a lazy import (search.py imports from executor → cycle avoided). Parity pinned exactly: single-URL reads `fn_args.get('reason','')` (matches serial :529); batch passes `fetch_reason=''` (matches serial batch worker :614).
- **Fix B — dep hygiene (tofu-search `pyproject.toml`).** `lxml>=5.3` was listed as a HARD DIRECT dep, misleading since tofu_search never imports lxml itself — audit confirmed all bs4 uses `html.parser` (`search/_common.py:soup_of`, all 4 SERP engines, `html_extract.py:321`), and the only lxml consumer (`trafilatura.extract`) is already serialized under `_TRAFILATURA_LOCK` precisely because lxml 6.x/libxml2 segfaults under concurrent threads. Kept the pin (trafilatura transitive) but added a comment documenting it's transitive + the DO-NOT-switch-to-lxml-parser rule. No code change — the `html.parser` convention is upheld everywhere (no regression).
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (real on-disk reverts).** NEW `tests/test_streaming_fetch_url_delegation.py` (4, pure-pytest, patches `handlers.search._fetch_url_one`): single-URL routes through `_fetch_url_one` with the right arg contract + surfaces staged-asset content; failure includes `error_msg` detail; batch calls per-URL with `fetch_reason=''` + carries `File Asset` display rows; + a same-file neuter test. REAL neuter: reverted the single-URL branch to `fetch_page_content` on disk → the 2 single-URL tests FAILED (asset content + error detail vanished — the invisible-loss bug reproduced); reverted the batch branch to drop asset content → the batch test FAILED; restored both → 4/4 green, region byte-restored. NEW `tests/test_search_bridge_config.py` (3, pure-pytest, patches `tofu_search.configure` + stubs `_lib`): the 4 new knobs are passed with defaults; env overrides honoured; `prefetch_gate_enabled` false via env. Full sweep: `test_streaming_fetch_url_delegation` + `test_search_bridge_config` + `test_streaming_and_prefetch` + `test_smoke` = 76 green; tofu-search own suite 216 green; ruff clean both repos; no circular import (runtime-verified `configure()` accepts the 4 knobs + delegation targets import under PYTHONPATH).
- **Scope/Git discipline.** 4-step Git guard: `streaming_tool_executor.py` was already sibling-DIRTY (pre-existing hunks at L74/186/517 = `_has_executable_target` guard etc., NOT mine); my edits confined to the `fetch_url` block (L428 region), verified via `git diff` hunk headers. Live peer `mr77zwjj` is on the unrelated autopilot/orchestration epic — no collision. NOT committed (working tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work for the owner to attribute). Server NOT restarted (owner approval required; these are backend-only, no bundle change).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) When a library grows a new config field with NO env-var fallback inside its own `configure()`, the host bridge MUST pass it explicitly or it's silently untunable — audit `configure()`'s internal env_mapping against the full field set on every library bump. (2) A pre-exec/cache path that becomes AUTHORITATIVE (its result suppresses the real handler) must delegate to the SAME single-source-of-truth function as the serial path — any capability the serial path gains after the fast path was written (here: binary/text-asset staging) is silently lost, and cached-empty means NO error surfaces. Route fast paths through the canonical fn, don't reimplement a stale subset.


### 2026-07-05 — Project Brain panel UX overhaul: 4-column grid → responsive TABS + long-text clamp-with-expand (fixes the "one char per line" + "unreadable wall of text" report)
- **Why (owner screenshot).** On a narrow / port-forwarded viewport the panel was unusable: (1) `static/styles.css` `.project-brain-columns{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1.15fr 1fr}` had NO min-width floor and NO breakpoint, so inside the `width:min(960px,94vw)` panel each of the 4 kanban columns collapsed to ~60px → long epic titles wrapped one character per line; (2) the per-conversation influence banner + the Charter column rendered a full committed decision (can be `_DECISION_MAX_CHARS`=2400 chars) unclamped → one wall of text.
- **Fix 1 — TABS (root fix for the narrow-column collapse).** `index.html`: added a `.project-brain-tabs` role=tablist bar (Charter / Board / Activity / Team) with count badges; each old column now carries `pb-tab-panel` + `data-pb-panel`. CSS: `.project-brain-columns` is now `display:block`; `.pb-tab-panel{display:none}` / `.pb-tab-panel-active{display:flex}` show ONE surface at a time at full width (col-body `max-width:820px;margin:0 auto` for readable measure). JS (`project-brain.js`): `_selectTab(name)` (marks one tab+panel active), `_initTabs()` (one-shot click delegation, idempotent), `_setTabCount(id,n)` (badge, hidden on 0). Wired into `openProjectBrain` (`_initTabs()` + `_selectTab(_state.tab||'charter')`). Badges: Charter=pending proposals, Board=open+claimed (active epics), Team=live peer count (set in `project-brain-peers.js:renderPeers`). The old per-column `.project-brain-col-head` sticky headers were dropped (the tab IS the header now).
- **Fix 2 — CLAMP long text.** `_clampBlock(innerHtml, rawText)` wraps text > `_CLAMP_THRESHOLD` (240 chars) in a collapsed `.pb-clamp` (max-height:7.8em + gradient fade) with a Show more/less toggle; `_wireClampToggles(el)` delegates the toggle → `.pb-clamp-open`. Short text is returned bare (no chrome). Applied at every long-text site: charter north-star + each committed decision + each proposal (`renderCharter`), and the influence-banner north-star + decisions (`renderInfluence`). i18n `projectBrain.showMore/showLess` (zh: 展开全文/收起). Icon `chevronDown` (rotates 180° when open).
- **Charter question answered (owner asked "is it permanent, never revoked?").** No — the charter is NOT write-once. It's read→propose→human-gated-commit (`commit_charter` bumps `version` under an optimistic lock; `content` is overwritable; `repair_truncated_decisions` rewrites decision text in place). A PENDING proposal is revocable via `dismiss_proposal` (the Reject button). What does NOT yet exist is a first-class "retract ONE committed decision" control (decisions are an append list) — flagged as a possible follow-up, not built.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_tabs_clamp.py` (2 jsdom over the REAL shipped `project-brain.js` + real index.html tab/panel fragment; drives via *ForTest hooks injected INSIDE the IIFE in a COPY so they can reach closure-locals `_selectTab`/`_initTabs`/`renderCharter`): tab switch → exactly one `.pb-tab-panel-active`; long (900-char) decision → exactly 1 `.pb-clamp` (short one bare); toggle → `.pb-clamp-open`. NC neuters `_selectTab`'s panel-HIDE half (`classList.add` never remove) → two panels visible at once → assertion flips; shipped file byte-identical after. Full frontend sweep: tabs_clamp + board_defer_ux + peer_stop + peer_nudge + i18n_key_coverage + api_isolation = 24 green. Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-d0500bc4.js`** (grep-confirmed post-minify: `_initTabs`/`_selectTab`/`_clampBlock`/`pb-tab-panel`/`_wireClampToggles`/`pbTabCountPeers`). All edited JS already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** 4-step Git guard: heavily-dirty tree (normal), NO live siblings. Co-owned files (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `project-brain.js`, `project-brain-peers.js`, `i18n.js`) APPENDED/edited only in the panel-layout regions. NOT committed (working tree carries sibling scale-out/brain work). Server NOT restarted (owner approval required to serve the new bundle).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A multi-column dashboard inside a fixed-width side panel MUST either set a per-column min-width + breakpoint or go single-view (tabs) — an unfloored `1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr` grid degrades to one-char-per-line on a narrow viewport. And any prompt-injected field with a large char cap (charter decision = 2400) needs a UI clamp — the injected block is bounded for the MODEL, but the panel must bound it for the HUMAN too. Test closure-local UI fns by injecting *ForTest hooks INSIDE the IIFE in a copy (they can't be reached from the window export otherwise).


### 2026-07-05 — Project Brain completeness pass: closed the two audited gaps — agent-readable activity feed (`project_feed_read` tool) + operator-initiated hard-abort (Team-panel Stop) + stale `_boardActionBtn` docstring
- **Why (audit).** A two-front code audit (backend pillars + frontend/route surface) confirmed the Project Brain's PERCEPTION+COLLABORATION is otherwise complete and wired end-to-end, but found the objective "fully perceive what other conversations are DOING" was NOT met, plus one asymmetric intervention surface:
  1. **Feed perception hole (P1).** The cross-conversation ACTIVITY FEED (`project_feed.read_project_feed`) was written everywhere (task lifecycle / board / peer notes) but had NO agent tool and NO system-context injection — `system_context.py` injects only the charter block (`render_charter_block`, ~L966) and board block (`render_board_block`, ~L998). An agent could see who is live NOW (`project_peer_status`) and the epic lanes (`project_board_read`) but never the chronological narrative of what siblings had been doing. Route/UI-only.
  2. **Hard-abort asymmetry (P2).** The agent-requested `project_intervene(hard_abort=True)` path was human-gated via `request_human_guidance` (Approve/Deny card IN the requesting chat), but a human sitting in the Team panel had NO way to authorize OR initiate a stop of a runaway sibling.
- **Gap #1 fix — `project_feed_read` agent tool (on-demand, NOT always-on injection — deliberate).** DESIGN CALL: the feed can hold up to `_PROJECT_EVENTS_KEEP` (500) events and CHANGES every turn a sibling acts; injecting even a capped slice each turn would bloat context AND bust the append-only prompt-cache prefix (the project's cache-prefix-stability invariant). Board+charter are small STABLE summaries suited to always-on injection; the chronological pulse is PULLED. Wiring mirrors the peer tools exactly: `_fmt_feed` + `project_feed_read` branch in `lib/conversations/project_peer.py:execute_peer_tool` (clamps limit to [1,60], default 25; marks the caller's own conv; reuses `read_project_feed`, no second aggregation) → `PEER_FEED_TOOL` schema + `PEER_TOOLS`/`PEER_TOOL_NAMES` in `lib/tools/conversation.py` → registry `conv_ref` spec `provides`+`idempotent_tools` (read-only) → handler auto-routes via `PEER_TOOL_NAMES` (`_handle_peer_tool`, badge verb `feed`). Reachability PROVEN: schema+name-set+`tool_registry.lookup`+end-to-end `_execute_tool_one` dispatch, not just the pure branch.
- **Gap #2 fix — operator-initiated hard-abort (Option b: operator STOP with danger-confirm, NOT a pending-approval lane).** Chose operator-INITIATED over surfacing the agent's pending approval in the panel: the agent path already renders Approve/Deny in the requesting chat (duplicating it = a second channel racing the same blocking `guidance_id`); the genuinely-missing capability is the human wanting to stop a runaway sibling DIRECTLY. Self-contained: the authenticated confirm IS the human approval → passed server-side as `approved_by` (from `g.auth_ctx.name/key_id`, never blank) → honored by the SAME pure `_authorize_hard_abort` gate → `intervene_peer(hard_abort=True)` aborts the TASK only, audit-logged + feed-mirrored. New `POST /api/v1/project/brain/peer-abort` (`routes/api_v1/project.py`, after `brain/peer-message`) + `Api.project.brainPeerAbort` (`static/js/api.js`) + `_buildStopAffordance` in `static/js/project-brain-peers.js` (danger button shown ONLY on a RUNNING conversation peer — idle/sub-agent get none; themed `showConfirm` danger-gate with a `window.confirm` fallback so the gate is never bypassed; card-click guard extended to ignore `.pb-peer-stop` clicks). i18n keys `projectBrain.peerStop*` (zh+en) + CSS `.pb-peer-controls`/`.pb-peer-stop*` (SVG `ban` glyph per §3.4, `--pb-red` danger accent). Bundle rebuilt → **`bundle-01cdf2cc.js`** (grep-confirmed post-minify: `_buildStopAffordance`, `brainPeerAbort`, `peerStopConfirm`). Both peers JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Gap #3 — stale docstring.** `_boardActionBtn` (`static/js/project-brain.js:515`) said `act ∈ complete|block|reopen`; corrected to `complete|block|defer|reopen|resume`.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER.** `tests/test_project_feed_read_tool.py` (14, pure-pytest for tool logic/formatter; `flask_client` for the route) — formatter (empty/rows/self-mark), read+clamp (limit=0 is falsy→default 25; floor only bites on negatives), full agent-dispatch reachability, `NC-SCHEMA` (byte-remove `PEER_FEED_TOOL` → schema stops advertising it; made SCHEMA-level + NON-POLLUTING: reloads only `lib.tools.conversation`+`lib.tools`, NOT `lib.tasks_pkg.executor` — reloading executor recreates the `tool_registry` singleton and strips every other handler for the rest of the session, which caused 2 spurious `test_project_board_defer` failures until fixed), `NC-DISPATCH` (no-op the feed branch → returns unknown-tool), + peer-abort route (stops target / audit-stamped / refuses without convId/toConvId). `tests/test_frontend_peer_stop_affordance.py` (3 jsdom, drives the REAL shipped fns) — Stop present only on running conv peer; confirmed→abort with right args; denied confirm→no abort; NC neuters the confirm gate → a denied stop now aborts (proves the gate is load-bearing). Updated the existing nudge-composer NC anchor (`test_frontend_peer_nudge_composer.py`) for the widened card-click guard. Full sweep: `test_project_feed_read_tool` + `test_frontend_peer_stop_affordance` + `test_project_peer` + `test_frontend_peer_nudge_composer` + `test_frontend_i18n_key_coverage` + `test_project_board_defer` + `test_tool_registry` = 85 green; i18n-key ratchet + frontend API-isolation ratchet green; ruff clean; no circular import.
- **Scope/Git discipline.** 4-step Git guard first: heavily-dirty tree (normal — large uncommitted sibling scale-out/brain work), NO live siblings (`project_peer_status` empty), my new modules (`project_peer.py`/`project_feed.py`) are UNTRACKED (no HEAD collision); co-owned tracked files (`conversation.py`, `registry.py`, `handlers/misc.py`, `project.py`, `api.js`, `i18n.js`, `styles.css`, `project-brain*.js`) were only APPENDED to, outside existing sibling regions. NOT committed (working tree carries sibling work for the owner to attribute).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A capability that is WRITTEN everywhere but has no agent-facing READ path is a perception hole even when the data exists — expose it as a tool, and prefer an on-demand tool over always-on injection for any surface that is large or mutates every turn (context bloat + prompt-cache prefix bust). (2) A human-gate that only fires on the AGENT's request is half a feature — give the operator a direct, confirm-gated initiator too; the authenticated confirm can BE the approval token. (3) An NC that reloads `lib.tasks_pkg.executor` recreates the `tool_registry` singleton and silently strips other handlers for the rest of the pytest session → keep tool-registration NCs SCHEMA-level (reload only the schema source), and prove routing separately via `tool_registry.lookup`.


### 2026-07-04 — Two more i18n leaks found by widening the missing-key ratchet beyond `projectBrain.*` (`swarm.autoContinue` never localized; stray `data-i18n-html="browser.lnaPathHint"` clobbered JS output with the raw key)
- **How found.** The 2026-07-04 `projectBrain.*` ratchet (`tests/test_frontend_i18n_key_coverage.py`) only policed ONE namespace. Ran a namespace-agnostic scan (all `t()`/`_t()` literals + all `data-i18n*` attrs across `static/js/**` + `index.html`/`admin.html`, excluding dynamic-concat prefixes) → **2** real missing keys.
- **Bug 1 — `swarm.autoContinue`** (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js:753`). The swarm auto-continue banner has a WORKING manual fallback (`t(k) !== k ? t(k) : "Continued automatically…"`), so no raw key leaked — but the key was never in i18n.js, so zh users ALWAYS saw the English string (no localization). Fixed: added the key (zh: 子智能体完成后自动继续 / en) after `swarm.phase.noResult`.
- **Bug 2 — `browser.lnaPathHint`** (`index.html`, the `<p id="browserLnaPath" data-i18n-html="browser.lnaPathHint">`). Worse AND redundant: this `<p>` is ENTIRELY JS-rendered by `_applyBrowserLnaWarning` (`main_toolbar_ui.js:562`), which sets `innerHTML = t('browser.lnaPathLabel') + " <code>"+dir+"</code>"`. The stray `data-i18n-html` (a) pointed at a NON-EXISTENT key and (b) made `_applyI18n()` overwrite the correct JS-rendered OS path with the literal raw key `browser.lnaPathHint` on every language switch. The attribute was leftover cruft — the JS owns the element. Fixed by REMOVING the attribute (not by adding a key that would still clobber the JS output).
- **Durable fix — widened the ratchet.** Added 3 tests to `test_frontend_i18n_key_coverage.py` (now 8): `test_every_referenced_key_is_defined_all_namespaces` (ALL namespaces, JS + HTML), `test_html_data_i18n_keys_are_defined` (the index/admin `data-i18n*` surface where bug 2 lived), + a negative control proving the widened scanner extracts a synthetic non-`projectBrain` key. The `_ANY_T_CALL_RE` uses `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_$.])_?t\(` so it matches only bare `t(`/`_t(`, never a `.format(`/`.at(` tail.
- **Double-neuter (real, on-disk revert).** Dropped `swarm.autoContinue` → `test_every_referenced_key_is_defined_all_namespaces` FAILED; re-added the stray `data-i18n-html` → `test_html_data_i18n_keys_are_defined` FAILED; restored both → 8/8 green, files byte-clean (md5 verified). Proves both fixes are load-bearing and the widened ratchet has teeth.
- **Bundle.** Rebuilt → `bundle-e30fb411.js`: grep confirms `swarm.autoContinue` present post-minify, `lnaPathHint` absent. Both edited JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; `index.html`'s bundle tag is serve-time-rewritten by `routes/common.py` (no allowlist change). Restart needed to serve the new bundle (bundler is pure-Python, no hot reload) — NOT done (owner approval required per prefs).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A single-namespace i18n ratchet is a false sense of safety — leaks live in every namespace and on the HTML `data-i18n*` surface too; police ALL of them. And a `data-i18n*` attribute on a JS-rendered element is a CLOBBER trap: `_applyI18n()` re-runs on language switch and overwrites the JS output with `t(key)` — if the element's content is JS-owned, it must NOT carry a `data-i18n*` attribute at all.


### 2026-07-04 — CORRECTION to the "Parked lane" entry + i18n missing-key ratchet (`projectBrain.actDefer/actResume/deferReasonPrompt` rendered as raw keys on prod)
- **Correction.** The 2026-07-04 "Project Brain Board: human decision surface for PARKED epics" entry CLAIMED it added `laneDeferred`, `actDefer`, `actResume`, `deferReasonPrompt` to `static/js/i18n.js`. That claim was FALSE for three of the four: only `laneDeferred` (and the pre-existing `actReopen`) actually landed. `actDefer`, `actResume`, `deferReasonPrompt` were NEVER written to i18n.js — so the Park button, the Resume button, and the defer-reason prompt rendered the RAW keys (owner saw literal `projectBrain.actResume` in the UI). Root cause of the visible bug: `t(key)` returns the KEY STRING when the key is missing (silent fallback), and `project-brain.js`'s `_t(key, fallback)` calls `t(key)` — so `t()`'s own missing-key fallback fires FIRST and `_t`'s `fallback` arg is dead code on the missing-key path. The three keys are added FOR REAL this turn (i18n.js ~2097–2100 + deferReasonPrompt), bundle rebuilt → `bundle-eec90741.js` (grep-confirmed present post-minify).
- **Ratchet (new, prevents recurrence).** `tests/test_frontend_i18n_key_coverage.py`: scans source JS (excludes `i18n.js` itself + `bundle-*.js` build artifacts) for literal `projectBrain.*` keys, EXCLUDES dynamic concatenation prefixes (token ends in `.` OR is immediately followed by `+`, e.g. `'projectBrain.' + labelKey`, `"projectBrain.boardVerb." + verb`, `"projectBrain.lane" + status...`), and asserts every remaining COMPLETE literal key exists in i18n.js. CI now fails the moment someone references a `projectBrain.*` key without adding its i18n entry — no more hand-spotting raw keys.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A JOURNAL entry is not proof the code landed — verify the claimed file actually contains the change (grep i18n.js), don't trust the prose. And `_t(key, fallback)` wrappers over a `t()` that already returns the key on miss have a DEAD fallback arg — the only real protection is a ratchet that asserts key presence at CI time.


### 2026-07-04 — Standalone test-runner prod-DB pollution: shared `guard_standalone_db` helper + SELF-DISCOVERING ratchet (killed the whack-a-mole list)
- **Symptom (owner).** A stray `queue test` / `requeue-test` conversation appeared in the live sidebar and never auto-cleared. Root cause: `tests/test_queue_redispatch_after_restart.py` has a `if __name__ == '__main__': main()` block; run as `python tests/x.py` it SKIPS `conftest.py` entirely, so none of the 2026-06-28 data-loss guards fire. With `.env`'s ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres`, `_core._BACKEND` froze on PROD PG and its `_seed_conv` wrote `requeue-test` rows straight into the live DB. Same mechanism class as the 2026-06-28 mass-deletion incident, different entry point (standalone runner, not the E2E fixture).
- **Fix — ONE shared helper, not per-file patches (`tests/_standalone_guard.py`, NEW).** `guard_standalone_db(context, *, init_schema=True)` = (1) FORCE sqlite + throwaway `TOFU_DB_PATH` (force, not setdefault; honours `TOFU_ALLOW_PG_TESTS=1`) BEFORE any DB import; (2) re-use conftest's keystone `_assert_test_database` (belt-and-suspenders); (3) `init_db()` to bootstrap the fresh sqlite schema. Single source of truth — no divergent inlined copies. Key insight: importing `tests.conftest` runs `_install_shim_for_collection` (force-sqlite) as a side-effect, so a standalone runner that imports the helper gets force-sqlite for free; the helper makes that explicit + adds the assert + schema.
- **Wiring — 15 files.** Custom-`main()` runners (queue_redispatch, cache_prefix_stability, chat_manager_migration, committed_message_parity, paper_review_mode, partial_sync_no_husk, task_supersede_and_stuck, terminal_cas_retry, startup_reconcile, translate_migration): guard as first line of `main()`. unittest / module-top-import runners (abort_dangling_tool_round, endpoint_flow_parity, endpoint_flow_parity_live, stale_recovery_authoritative): guard in the `if __name__` block (`init_schema=False` where `setUp`/live path bootstraps). messages_rows + swarm_snapshot_persist: guard at MODULE TOP (they import the DB layer at module top, so it must precede the freeze; swarm_snapshot_persist's `setdefault('TOFU_DB_BACKEND','sqlite')` trap — DEFEATED by ambient pg — was REPLACED). Already-safe (skipped): billing_janitor + branch_routes (`reset_sqlite_for_tests`/direct-force in setUpClass), paper_title_recovery (`reset_sqlite_for_tests` in main).
- **The durable win — SELF-DISCOVERING ratchet (owner-directed; killed the hand-maintained list).** First attempt hardcoded a 13-file list — exactly the fragility being removed (a new runner months from now wouldn't be policed). Replaced with a scanner: enumerate `tests/test_*.py` with a `__main__` block + a DB-write signature (`get_thread_db`/`upsert`/`create_task`/`persist_task_result`/`INSERT INTO`/`dispatch_next_queued`/`_seed_conv`), assert each is guarded (shared helper / self-force / conftest import / `pytest.main(` re-entry) or in an auditable `_KNOWN_EXEMPT`. It found **24** DB-touching runners — 7 MORE than the original audit (paper_export_double_encode, paper_ingest_persist, chat_stream_snapshot_offload, …), all already covered. Two refinements after false positives: (a) AST-based signature detection via `_real_code_identifiers` — a signature that appears ONLY inside a string literal / comment / code-fixture (test_keep_tool_history_cost, test_hook_taxonomy) does NOT count; (b) `pytest.main(` in `__main__` is safe-by-construction (re-enters pytest → conftest). Residual false positives (test_chat_flow_dispatch, test_orchestration_endpoint_runner — pure in-memory unittests that only STUB `persist_task_result` to a no-op, never connect) → `_KNOWN_EXEMPT` with explicit per-file reasons.
- **Proof (`tests/test_db_guard.py`, +8 → 14 tests, all green).** Unit: `_force_sqlite_env` overrides ambient postgres + honours the opt-in. RATCHET: `test_all_standalone_runners_are_guarded` (self-discovering, ≥13 sanity floor — found 24). NEGATIVE CONTROL: `test_ratchet_would_catch_an_unguarded_newcomer` synthesises a fresh unguarded runner and proves the scanner flags it, then clears it once the guard is added (not a vacuous pass). BEHAVIORAL + DOUBLE-NEUTER (subprocess): a real child with ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres` + guard resolves `sqlite`; the SAME child WITHOUT the guard resolves `pg` — proving the guard is load-bearing (it flips the resolution). ruff clean; edits confined to `tests/*` (no `lib/`/`routes/` source touched).
- **Cleanup.** Located the 2 polluting rows in prod PG (`cv-requeue-basic`, `cv-requeue-autopilot-only`, title `requeue-test`, user_id 1 — content `"first question"/"first answer"` + `"q"/"a"`, unmistakably `_seed_conv` fixtures), owner-approved delete → `DELETE 2`, re-query confirms 0 remain.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A standalone `python tests/x.py` runner is a conftest-bypass vector: it must self-guard the DB. The durable fix is ONE shared helper every such runner calls, POLICED by a SELF-DISCOVERING ratchet (scan for `__main__` + DB-write signature), never a hand-maintained list that rots. Make the scanner AST-aware so string-literal fixtures don't false-positive, treat `pytest.main` re-entry as safe, and keep an auditable `_KNOWN_EXEMPT` (with per-file reasons) for the residue. Verify with a real subprocess double-neuter (guard → sqlite, no-guard → pg), not just a static grep. Also: used read-only SELECTs for all prod diagnosis and did NOT `git stash` this time (per the logged `git worktree` lesson).

(Needed the `_ensure_schema` autouse `init_db()` fixture for the bare-pytest DB-warm quirk.)
- **Part 2 — the 3 infra decisions (owner delegated with rule: "most long-term / robust; ignore migration cost").** Read the design docs' open-question sections and RESOLVED, recorded in `docs/EPIC_B §7a` + `docs/EPIC_D §5a`:
  1. **Redis = MANAGED HA** (not self-run single) — it's the single B+C substrate on every replica's critical path; self-run single = fleet-wide SPOF. §4 fail-open seam retained as a failover-blip backstop, not steady state. No AOF/RDB durability imposed (bus best-effort; lease keys self-heal from heartbeats within one `lease_ttl`).
  2. **D2 pooler = MANAGED PgBouncer HA, transaction-pooling** — self-run single = new SPOF; managed/HA removes it. Transaction pooling confirmed → session-state audit IN SCOPE (`_post_connect_setup` + `SET`/prepared-stmt/advisory-lock → `SET LOCAL`/txn scope).

The correct lever is now the **Resume button I built**: the human clicks it per-epic when infra is provisioned + they authorize §10 work.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "parked pending human decision" status is only half a feature without a human-facing surface to MAKE the decision — a backend status that no UI can transition is as stuck as no status at all. Build the transition control (Resume) alongside the status. And the un-park direction was free: `reopen_task`/`/board/reopen`/`boardReopen` already supported `deferred → open` — always check whether the existing lifecycle lever already covers the new state before adding a route.
