### 2026-07-03 (follow-up #4) — poor-network content loss: two CRITICAL total-loss vectors FIXED (frontend `state`-snapshot blank + backend terminal-CAS silent drop). 4-lane audit → 2 root-cause fixes, double-neutered.
- **Owner report.** On a poor network, messages that were SENT and already GENERATING are later found completely GONE. Frontend/backend message sync unreliable.
- **Method.** 4-lane audit (backend write-back durability + frontend SSE/poll/reconnect + send-path/queue/reload + independent architectural reviewer). Key non-obvious finding: the backend ALREADY checkpoints mid-generation to the DB every ~5s (`_maybe_checkpoint_during_stream` → `checkpoint_task_partial`, manager.py:~2064, `_STREAM_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL=5`, first-delta immediate). So this is NOT a "write-only-at-end" design — losses come from specific holes that DISCARD or OVERWRITE a nearly-durable copy, clustered on the network-flaky paths. Two were CRITICAL total-loss vectors; both fixed this PR.
- **Fix #1 — frontend `state`-snapshot blank (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`), the direct "found completely GONE" vector.** On reconnect the SSE `state` snapshot replays the server's LAST checkpoint. On a flaky reconnect it can land BEFORE a fresh 5s checkpoint is written (cold-replay race / wrong replica), so its `content`/`thinking` can be empty or SHORTER than the client's accumulated buffer. FIVE handler sites assigned it RAW (`assistantMsg.content = ev.content || ""` at :738, plus critic :731, worker :691, and two planner sites :563/:617) — no length guard, unlike `_pollFallback`'s merge. An empty snapshot BLANKED the in-progress message → `updateStreamingUI`'s wait branch painted "等待中…". **Root-cause fix:** new shared helper `_snapshotLonger(msg, ev, field)` (keep-the-longer; a snapshot may only GROW a field, never shrink it — same invariant as `_pollFallback` + the 2026-05-31 content-regression detector), applied at ALL FIVE sites. Fresh-message object literals (`{content: ev.content || ""}`) are UNCHANGED — a newly-created msg has no prior content to preserve, so the snapshot IS authoritative there.
- **Fix #2 — backend terminal-CAS silent drop (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`, `_sync_result_to_conversation`).** The terminal write did a SINGLE-SHOT optimistic-lock UPDATE (`WHERE updated_at=?`); on a miss it logged *"frontend likely synced first (safe)"* and RETURNED — discarding the final turn. But on a poor network the frontend's `finishStream` sync may itself have failed, so a concurrent partial-checkpoint / meta write bumps `updated_at` while NOBODY persisted the answer → lost from `conversations.messages` (survives only in `task_results`). `_sync_partial_to_conversation` already retried 3×; the terminal path did not. **Root-cause fix:** bounded CAS-retry loop (`_MAX_TERMINAL_CAS=3`) mirroring `_sync_partial`. On a miss it re-reads the fresh row and re-applies the SAME content-length guard via a local `_apply_result_to_tail(msgs)` closure: if the fresh row already holds content ≥ ours → genuine frontend-won → skip (the historical "safe" case, preserved); otherwise re-merge onto the fresh tail (only ever GROWS content/thinking + fills terminal metadata — idempotent) and re-CAS. **NOTE:** the 2026-05-31 skill (`sync-fixes-2026-05-31`, item "M1") explicitly REJECTED this as out-of-scope ("benign-skip is correct semantics; task_results carries canonical data"). That ruling is now OVERTURNED by direct evidence that on a flaky network the frontend does NOT necessarily win, so the skip drops the only durable copy in `conversations.messages`.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (both bit, both restored byte-identical).** `tests/test_terminal_cas_retry.py` (drives REAL `_sync_result_to_conversation`, forces a CAS miss by having a wrapped `db.execute` bump `updated_at` before the first UPDATE): `test_terminal_cas_retry_persists_after_miss` (★ the fix — full answer persisted after miss) + `test_terminal_cas_skips_when_frontend_won` (★ behaviour preservation — a concurrent LONGER frontend write is NOT shrunk). Neuter `_MAX_TERMINAL_CAS=3→1` → retry test FAILS ("terminal write LOST after CAS miss — got ''"), frontend-won stays green; restored, md5 `7f8ac5eb…`. `tests/test_frontend_state_snapshot_keep_longer.py` (drives REAL `_snapshotLonger` under node + source guards on all 5 sites): empty/shorter incoming keeps current (★ fix), longer/equal/empty-current adopt incoming (★ behaviour preservation). Neuter helper → `return (ev&&ev[field])||""` → `empty_incoming_keeps_current`+`shorter_incoming_keeps_current` FAIL, adopt-longer stays green; restored, md5 `0e8ef5f2…`.
- **No regression.** `test_chat_manager_migration.py` 21/21 green; frontend `stream_deferred_no_wipe` + `twflush_msg_fallback` + `ghost_tail` + `buried_ghost_sweep` all clean. `node --check` clean, ruff clean, `py_compile` clean. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-9b6e3354.js` (contains `_snapshotLonger`, 5 sites). NOTE: an uncommitted sibling-conversation working-tree already carried ~422 lines of scale-out edits in sse_pipeline.js; `_snapshotLonger` was NOT in git HEAD and the on-disk raw overwrites were still live at session start, so this is the authoritative landing of the fix (coherent: helper defined once, 10 usages, zero remaining raw overwrites).
- **PARKED (owned, not dropped):**
  - **#4 — queued human message not crash-durable.** When a task is running, a new send is stored ONLY in `message_queue`, never in `conversations.messages` (routes/chat.py:~592). `dispatch_next_queued` fires only on task-completion / human-send / brain idle-drain — there is NO startup re-dispatch of orphaned `KIND_REAL` rows (only autopilot rows resume). Server restart → message shown in the queue bar, then stranded with no transcript trace. Fix candidates: persist the queued user msg as a `pending` conv message at enqueue time, and/or add a startup `KIND_REAL` re-dispatch scan. Real total-loss path; needs its own PR (touches queue semantics + startup recovery).
  - **#3 — architectural (charter-level, Epic C).** Recovery still resolves through in-memory routing: the checkpoint freshness guard reads the LOCAL in-proc `_conv_latest_task` dict (manager.py:~1467) and poll recovery depends on the task being live in `_tasks`. Robust model = treat the durable DB checkpoint as unconditional source of truth on any poll miss (crash OR misroute), returning persisted content immediately with a `reconnect` hint rather than withholding durable bytes pending affinity re-route. Filed under the scale-out Epic C board task; NOT a one-PR fix.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A reconnect `state` snapshot is a REPLAY, not ground truth — it may only GROW a message field, never shrink it; route every overwrite site through one keep-the-longer helper (fresh-message literals excepted). And an optimistic-lock terminal write must RETRY on miss with a re-read + content-length re-check, never silently drop — "frontend likely synced (safe to skip)" is false exactly when the network is bad, which is when the backend is the only writer left.


### 2026-07-03 (follow-up #3) — parked item #2 closed: poll `reconnect:true` hint was UNCONSUMED → the frontend half of Epic C's affinity re-route. Latent (redis-only), fixed pre-emptively before the sharded backend ships.
- **Scope.** Triaged the three 2026-07-03 parked findings via 2 grounded parallel audits (SSE state-overwrite, poll reconnect) + own analysis of the swarm `'*'` finding. Verdicts: (#1 SSE `state` empty-overwrite) — ALREADY FIXED in-tree by a peer (`_snapshotLonger` at all 5 state-handler sites; my earlier stale read predated the peer edit — file grew 1809→1830L); (#3 swarm `'*'` wildcard) — NOT a bug (swarm frames are keyed by `convId`; `swarm_push.js` self-filters via `conversations.find(c=>c.id===convId)` — the convId lookup IS the isolation, unlike presence/project which need a `root` match, so no project-root guard is warranted); (#2 poll reconnect) — the one real, fixable defect. Only #2 needed code.
- **Root cause (#2, LATENT not live).** `routes/chat.py` `chat_poll` (via `_running_checkpoint_verdict(sharded)`, chat.py:79) emits `status:'running'` + `r['reconnect']=True` (chat.py:~1973) when a DB `running` checkpoint exists but the task is absent from THIS replica's memory — but ONLY when `_sharded` (`TOFU_RUNTIME_STATE_BACKEND=='redis'`). Charter Epic C §4.1: report running+reconnect (task alive on another replica; re-route via taskId affinity), NOT flip to interrupted, no cross-replica probe. The FRONTEND `_pollFallback` (sse_poll_fallback.js) consumed `data.status`/`content`/… but NEVER `data.reconnect`; its terminal check is `if (data.status !== "running")`. With the hint, status IS `running` → the loop polls THIS (task-less) replica forever → bubble hangs on "running". inproc default returns `('interrupted', False)` (no `reconnect`) → loop terminates correctly → single-box byte-identical. So it's **dormant today, guaranteed to activate the moment redis ships** — the frontend half of the same uncommitted Epic C landing, closed now to prevent a certain regression.
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/sse_poll_fallback.js`, additive).** After the SyncFix stale-discard block, a new guard: `if (data.reconnect === true && data.status === 'running' && typeof _trySSE === 'function' && !aborted)` → re-open SSE via `_trySSE(convId, taskId, stream, assistantMsg)` (reuses the SAME `stream`/controller — abort still works, no duplicate stream; affinity routes to the owning replica). If SSE re-attaches (`_trySSE` truthy) it owns finishStream/twStop → poll `return`s (yields). If it still fails → fall through, keep polling. BOUNDED by `_MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS=3` (new `_reconnectAttempts` counter) so a pathological "every poll hints, SSE never attaches" setup can't spin the re-open path forever — after the cap it just keeps polling (bubble stays live; terminal/offline paths still apply). AbortError inside `_trySSE` → clean finish.
- **Test + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_poll_reconnect_hint.py`, NEW).** Loads the REAL shipped `sse_poll_fallback.js` under bare node, stubs window globals + `_trySSE`. Scenario A: `_trySSE`→true → exactly 1 poll, 1 re-open, loop yields (no spin). Scenario B: `_trySSE`→false, first 5 polls hinted then `done` → re-open attempted but BOUNDED to ≤3, polling continues, loop terminates on the eventual non-running status (`content==='final answer'`). Double-neuter: guarded the block with `if (false && …)` → test FAILED (A_sse_reopened/A_poll_yielded bite; B spins to the poll ramp), restored byte-identical (md5 `067e3203…`). Sibling `test_frontend_poll_null_resp.py` still green. `node --check` clean. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-f932bd58.js` (contains "reconnect hint (sharded)").
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a backend field is emitted only under an opt-in env flag (here `TOFU_RUNTIME_STATE_BACKEND=redis`), a frontend that ignores it isn't "safe" — it's a latent defect that ships broken the day the flag flips. A poll loop whose terminal predicate is `status !== 'running'` MUST also consume any affinity/reconnect hint that rides alongside a `running` status, or it polls a task-less replica forever. Bound any "re-open the stream" retry so it can't become an infinite re-open loop. And re-verify a peer-editable file's CURRENT bytes before proposing a fix — my stale read of `sse_pipeline.js` nearly duplicated a peer's already-landed `_snapshotLonger` fix.


### 2026-07-03 (follow-up #2) — parked item #1 (SSE `state` empty-overwrite) closed: fix was ALREADY in the tree (peer-authored `_snapshotLonger`), I added the missing regression test + double-neuter + bundle
- **Owner directive.** The "comprehensive chatInner sync fix" wasn't done while `sse_pipeline.js` still had an unconditional `assistantMsg.content = ev.content || ""` in the plain-assistant `state` branch — same bug class as the `_twFlush` wipe, live today (NOT scale-out gated). Fix it to the same standard (reset-safety analysis + guarded idiom + test + double-neuter + bundle + journal/skill).
- **Reset-safety verdict (stated explicitly, as required).** Traced every reset path. A `state` snapshot is NEVER the vehicle for a legitimate content reset: `state` / `retry_reset` / `delta_reset` are mutually-exclusive `else if` arms on `ev.type`; both reset events clear BOTH the message AND the buffer to `""` together (retry_reset also drops error + this-attempt toolRounds). A `state` event is a full RESYNC — an empty/short `ev.content` only ever means a lagging (server observed between content-lock cycles) or reconnect-before-accumulation snapshot. Stale snapshots from an aborted/superseded task are already discarded by the SyncFix guard (sse_pipeline.js:505–519) before reaching the branch. ⇒ keep-longer CANNOT resurrect intentionally-cleared text (after a reset both sides are `""`; client-longer only happens via un-flushed deltas, where keeping the longer side is correct). So line 717's unconditional wipe was a pure bug.
- **What I found.** When I went to apply the guarded idiom, the fix was ALREADY in the working tree (uncommitted): a shared helper `_snapshotLonger(msg, ev, field)` (sse_pipeline.js:59, `return incoming.length >= current.length ? incoming : current`) routed into ALL state-snapshot write sites — plain assistant (738), critic (730), planner (563/617). A live peer conversation (`mr4vsmu0`, topic: network-loss info-loss) authored it; it matches my reset-safety analysis exactly. I did NOT re-edit sse_pipeline.js (peer live on it — messaged them to coordinate; my work is test-only + bundle, which just READ the file at runtime).
- **My contribution (the missing piece).** `tests/test_frontend_state_snapshot_no_wipe.py` (NEW) — drives the REAL `state` handler via the existing `window.__sse_test__.dispatchSSEEvent` seam under jsdom: (1) empty state over populated msg → content/thinking PRESERVED; (2) shorter state over longer accumulated → PRESERVED; (3) genuinely-longer state → APPLIED; (4) `retry_reset` STILL clears to `""` (proves keep-longer doesn't block real resets). DOUBLE-NEUTER reverts `_snapshotLonger` body to `return incoming` in a tmp COPY → `empty_state_preserves_content` FAILS (wipe returns) while `retry_reset_clears_content` stays green; real file untouched. Plus a source guard asserting `_snapshotLonger(assistantMsg, ev,` is present.
- **No regression.** SSE-dispatch 27-scenario characterization suite + twflush + deferred-no-wipe all green (5 suites). `node --check` clean. Bundle was STALE (bundle-252778d6.js lacked `_snapshotLonger`) → rebuilt `bundle-74ab8a3b.js` (now contains it).
- **Parked items #2 (poll `reconnect:true` unconsumed — deployment/scale-out-gated, inert on single-box) and #3 (swarm `'*'` subscription — filtered by `convId==='*'` guard + per-conv lookup, alleged missing project-root guard UNPROVEN) remain correctly parked.**
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Before fixing a bug, GREP the working tree for it — a sibling conversation may already own the fix; re-editing a file another conv is live on risks clobbering in-flight work. Coordinate via project_message, contribute the missing complement (here: the test), and rebuild the bundle so an uncommitted fix actually ships. And any `ev.field || ""` overwrite on a resync/reconnect/poll snapshot is a wipe hazard — keep-longer, and verify real resets ride a separate event.


### 2026-07-03 (follow-up, owner pushback) — the buried-ghost sweep's PERSISTENCE was silently dead: `_serverMsgCount` count-drop guard ignored `allowTruncate` → swept ghosts RESURRECTED on reload; + Case-D→Case-E fall-through could auto-fire an unrequested turn
- **Owner ruling.** The `_twFlush` fix above was verified, but "comprehensive check AND fix" wasn't done: one parked finding was NOT a separate feature — it was a proven regression of the SAME-DAY buried-ghost fix, living in the exact subsystem the objective names. Fix it before closing.
- **Bug 1 (HIGH, the resurrect).** `syncConversationToServer` (conversations.js:~188) guarded `if (conv._serverMsgCount && conv.messages.length < conv._serverMsgCount) return;` — and this ran BEFORE and WITHOUT consulting `allowTruncate` (which only took effect ~130 lines later at the Layer-1 staleness check + the PUT body). The same-day `_sweepBuriedGhostAssistants` (main_init_tasks.js Case D) shrinks `conv.messages` below the server count then calls `syncConversationToServer(conv, {allowTruncate:true})` to persist the removal — but that call hit the line-188 guard and BAILED. Net: buried ghosts swept from the DOM each load, never removed server-side → **resurrect on every reload**. Same hazard for the Case-D `delete` pop and any edit/regen truncation. The frontend guard was the ODD ONE OUT: the Layer-1 staleness check (`if (!allowTruncate && conv.messages.length > lightMsgs.length)`) and the backend guard (routes/conversations.py `allow_truncate` bypass) both already honoured the flag.
- **Fix 1 (root, not special-case).** Gate the count-drop guard on `!allowTruncate` — `if (!allowTruncate && conv._serverMsgCount && conv.messages.length < conv._serverMsgCount) return;`. A caller passing `allowTruncate:true` has DELIBERATELY reduced the list (sweep / Case-D delete / edit-regen) and must persist it. The stale-async-overwrite race path (see `stale-async-sync-overwrite-msg-regression` skill) NEVER sets allowTruncate, so it stays protected. One-line, mirrors the two siblings.
- **Bug 2 (MED, unrequested turn).** Cases A/B/C in `initActiveTasks` each end with `continue`; Case D did NOT. Its `_ghost==='delete'` branch does `conv.messages.pop()` (removing an empty ghost) then fell straight into the Case-E block IN THE SAME iteration — which sees the now-exposed recent trailing `user` msg and queues `startAssistantResponse` (fires 3s later) → re-running (and re-billing) a turn the user never asked for, potentially duplicating a completed answer. Only the `delete` pop can expose a user tail: the SWEEP touches mid-list only, and the `interrupted` stamp leaves an assistant tail — so both correctly still flow to Case E's own guarded check.
- **Fix 2 (surgical).** Added `continue;` right after the Case-D delete-branch sync. A ghost reconcile must never auto-fire an LLM turn.
- **Tests + DOUBLE-NEUTER (both new, both drive REAL shipped code).** `tests/test_frontend_sync_allowtruncate_guard.py`: drives REAL `syncConversationToServer` (evals conversations.js), stubs only `Api.conversations.put`; asserts allowTruncate:true + (msgs<serverCount) → PUT FIRES with the shorter body + `allowTruncate` flag; default + drop → BLOCKED; equal/growth → fire. Double-neuter reverts the guard to un-gated in a tmp COPY → `allowTruncate_put_fires` FAILS (block returns) while `default_drop_blocked` stays green. `tests/test_frontend_casee_no_autostart_after_ghost_delete.py`: drives REAL `initActiveTasks` end-to-end (stubs the network+timer seam, `setTimeout` synchronous), seeds a ghost-on-recent-user conv + a genuine-orphan control; asserts the ghost is popped AND does NOT auto-start, while the control DOES (guard is surgical). Double-neuter removes the `continue` in a tmp COPY → `ghost_no_autostart` FAILS (fall-through returns), control still starts. Both neuters proven to bite. GOTCHA: `initActiveTasks` reads `sessionStorage` at the top + `_ensureNewest` reads `_editingMsgIdx`/`showStreamingUIForConv` — miss a stub and the outer try/catch SWALLOWS the throw so the loop never runs (both convs silently unprocessed; `ghost_no_autostart` falsely "passes" because nothing ran). Stub them.
- **No regression.** 10 suites green incl. `test_frontend_delete_conv_undo` + `test_frontend_buried_ghost_sweep` (the legitimate allowTruncate truncation callers). `node --check` clean both files. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-252778d6.js`.
- **Still parked (confirmed NOT live regressions of an in-scope fix — leave for separate triage): SSE `state` empty-overwrite (sse_pipeline.js:717), poll `reconnect:true` hint unconsumed under sharded backend, swarm `'*'` project-root isolation.**
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An early-return guard that runs BEFORE consulting a bypass flag silently defeats every caller that passes the flag — order the guard so `allowTruncate` (or any deliberate-override) is checked in the SAME predicate, and make the frontend guard match its backend twin. And in a `for` loop of reconcile CASES, every branch that MUTATES the tail must `continue` or the next case acts on the mutated state — a `pop()` that exposes a user tail + a Case-E auto-start = an unrequested, billed LLM turn.


### 2026-07-03 — chatInner backend→frontend sync audit (5 parallel agents) → the load-bearing root cause: `_twFlush` read `buf.content` RAW with no message-checkpoint fallback (fixed correct-by-construction via shared `_streamFrameArg`)
- **Owner report.** "Project is very unstable, including the logic for the frontend to synchronize status from the backend to display internal elements of `chatInner`. Comprehensive check + fix."
- **Method.** Fanned out 5 independent audits (4 coder lanes + 1 reviewer, no shared findings): LIVE SSE render, stream-lifecycle/conv-switch, reconnect/init/ghost-sweep, poll-fallback/push transport, and an architectural second-opinion. All 5 — PLUS the code's own comments (sse_pipeline.js:359-364 reconnect-seed block explicitly names it) — converged on ONE root cause.
- **Root cause (HIGH, load-bearing).** `_twFlush` (static/js/core/health_stream_timer.js), the HOTTEST per-frame render path, built its `updateStreamingUI` arg by reading `buf.content` / `buf.thinking` / `buf.toolRounds` **RAW** — with NO message-checkpoint fallback, unlike EVERY other render site (`showStreamingUIForConv` does `buf?.content || lastMsg.content`; its 300ms deferred re-render too). `twStart` mints an EMPTY buffer, so whenever anything fed `_twFlush` an un-seeded buffer — a re-entry that skipped the seed, a field-only `twUpdate` (e.g. an HG-translation flag flip via `_autoTranslateHumanGuidance`), or the cross-tab visibility flush before the seed landed — `updateStreamingUI({content:''})` hit its `!content && !thinking` → "等待中…" branch and WIPED the already-checkpointed content. This is exactly why `connectToTask` carried TWO "band-aid" buffer seeds (fresh-connect L329-346 + re-entry L367-372): they papered over a missing fallback in the render path itself. The SAME bug class lived in the cross-tab visibilitychange flush (cross_tab_sync.js:87, raw `buf.content`).
- **Fix (correct-by-construction, not another band-aid — reviewer's recommendation).** New shared helper `_streamFrameArg(convId)` (health_stream_timer.js, before `_twFlush`): builds the `updateStreamingUI` payload applying the fallback (`buf.content || ckpt.content`, thinking likewise, tool-rounds via `getToolRoundsFromMsg(ckpt)` guarded on `buf.toolRounds.length` so an empty `[]` doesn't blank the panel), where `ckpt` = the trailing `assistant`/`_isEndpointReview` message. Returns `null` when no buffer. Routed BOTH `_twFlush` and the cross-tab flush through it. The invariant — buffer authoritative ONLY once it holds data, else the trailing streaming message is the truth — now holds regardless of caller. The two `connectToTask` seeds become harmless defense-in-depth (left in place; their locked test still green).
- **Safety proof (why the fallback can't resurrect erased text).** `retry_reset` AND `delta_reset` (sse_pipeline.js:841-888) clear the MESSAGE (`_rrTarget.content=""` / `_drTarget.content=""`) TOGETHER with the buffer — so after a reset the fallback reads `""` and stays empty (no resurrection of inter-round narration). Worker/planner turn rotations (L1108-1305) assign a FRESH empty `newAssistant` — checkpoint empty there too. Verified by reading each reset branch before shipping.
- **Test + DOUBLE-NEUTER (`tests/test_frontend_twflush_msg_fallback.py`, NEW).** jsdom drives the REAL shipped `_twFlush` + `updateStreamingUI` (evals streaming_ui.js then health_stream_timer.js in bundle order): (1) `_streamFrameArg` empty-buf+ckpt → falls back; (2) `_twFlush` empty-buf+ckpt → renders real content, NO 等待中… chip; (3) genuinely-empty stream (empty buf AND empty ckpt) STILL shows 等待中… (fallback must not fabricate); (4) live buffer wins over stale ckpt. Neutered `_twFlush` back to raw `buf.content` → checks (2) `twflush_no_wait_over_checkpoint` + `twflush_renders_checkpoint` FAILED, (3) `empty_stream_still_waits` stayed PASS (test discriminates); restored, 10/10 PASS. GOTCHA: a synchronous rAF stub makes `_twFlush` infinite-recurse via its `<33ms` rate-cap reschedule — stub rAF as a non-invoking no-op and drive `_twFlush()` directly with an ever-advancing `performance.now()`. Plus source-guards on `_streamFrameArg` fallback + both call sites.
- **No regression.** 3 streaming suites (twflush + deferred-no-wipe + stuck-placeholder-heal) + 6 broader (autopilot warmup/vu, sse-dispatch, ghost-tail, buried-ghost-sweep, streaming-ui) all green. `node --check` clean both files. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-6131c6a3.js` (contains `_streamFrameArg`).
- **Other audit findings PARKED (real but lower-severity, not in scope of the "unstable sync" root cause; logged for a follow-up).** SSE `state` handler `assistantMsg.content = ev.content || ""` unconditionally overwrites the durable message with a possibly-empty snapshot (sse_pipeline.js:717); poll `reconnect:true` hint never consumed under sharded backend → bubble stays "running" (sse_poll_fallback.js:236); swarm `'*'` wildcard subscription lacks the project-root guard its siblings have (swarm_push.js:77); Case-D buried-ghost sweep sync blocked by the `_serverMsgCount` guard so ghosts can resurrect on reload (main_init_tasks.js:252 vs conversations.js:189); Case-D → Case-E fall-through (missing `continue`) can auto-restart an old turn. These did NOT reproduce the reported "等待中… snap-back" symptom (that was `_twFlush`); triage separately.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When N render sites must honour "buffer-or-checkpoint," don't rely on every CALLER to pre-seed the buffer — put the fallback in ONE shared payload-builder the render path calls, so the invariant holds by construction. Band-aid seeds at the call sites are a smell that the render path itself reads raw state. And a synchronous rAF stub + a rate-capped flush = infinite recursion; drive the flush directly in tests.


### 2026-07-03 — "Deleted a message, now can't continue + chat cluttered" → two ROOT causes: (P2) transient empty-stop mislabeled `content_filter` (terminal, no retry), (P1) buried empty-ghost placeholders never swept. Both fixed + live conv repaired.
- **Owner report (conv `mr3jfcw10pianj`).** After deleting a message the chat became cluttered with blank bubbles and the conversation could not continue. The delete itself was fine — it was the moment failures started piling up.
- **PROBE FIRST (owner directive: prove gateway behaviour before touching the classifier).** New `debug/repro_conv_empty_stop.py` rebuilds the conv's EXACT wire body (`build_api_messages_from_db` → `build_body`, 692 msgs / ~737k prompt tokens) and streams it raw. **6/6 clean**: `finish=stop`, 400–635 chunks, 4–5k chars content, `prompt_tokens=736855`, 39–52s. So the production empties were **NOT** a content-policy block (that's HTTP 450 / deterministic) — they were **transient** gateway artifacts on a huge prompt. NOT context overflow either (Opus-4.8 = 1M window, compaction threshold 777k, gateway accepted 830k `cache_r`).
- **P2 root cause (the "can't continue" blocker).** `lib/tasks_pkg/llm_fallback.py` labelled ANY round-0 `finish=stop` + empty content `content_filter` (terminal, NO retry) whenever the stream layer had NOT set `_stream_anomaly`. But `lib/llm/_sse_core.py:813` only sets `_empty_stop`/`_stream_anomaly` when `finish=stop AND not content AND chunk_count>0` — so a whitespace-only body (`content` truthy) or a zero-chunk clean-`[DONE]` close (the production `content=0chars` case) slips through UNFLAGGED, and the terminal `content_filter` heuristic fired instead of the `empty_stop` retry bucket (cap 2, in `analyse_stream_result`). The transient empty dead-ended as a fabricated safety block.
- **P2 fix (root, not patch).** New pure helper `_flag_empty_stop_for_retry(assistant_msg, finish_reason, task, round_num, usage)` replaces the heuristic at BOTH the primary and fallback-model sites: a round-0 empty/whitespace-only stop that the stream layer didn't already flag gets `_empty_stop`+`_stream_anomaly` set on `usage` (mutated in place) → `analyse_stream_result` routes it through the empty_stop/zero_byte retry bucket, and only surfaces as honest `abnormal_stop` after retries exhaust — never a fake `content_filter`. A GENUINE policy block is still HTTP 450 `ContentFilterError` (llm_fallback.py:~422) and stays terminal, untouched.
- **P1 root cause (the clutter).** `_classifyGhostTail` (static/js/main/main_init_tasks.js) only ever inspected `conv.messages[length-1]`. Once a NEWER turn was appended on top of an empty placeholder (from an aborted/failed/empty-stop turn the user retried), that placeholder was no longer the tail → nothing removed it → repeated failed attempts STACKED blank "Agent" bubbles mid-transcript (conv had 4 buried empties at idx 79/80/81/84).
- **P1 fix (root).** New pure `_isBuriedEmptyGhost(msg)` + `_sweepBuriedGhostAssistants(conv)`; wired into Case D (runs for locally-loaded non-streaming convs, BEFORE the tail reconcile, persists with `allowTruncate`). Sweeps every BURIED empty placeholder (removes even settled aborted/interrupted empties mid-list — they render body-less badge-only = clutter) while LEAVING the tail for `_classifyGhostTail` (its locked test stays green). Special turns (endpoint/VU/image-gen), thinking-only interrupted turns, error envelopes, real tool rounds are all preserved.
- **Tests + double-neuter (both bit, restored byte-identical).** `tests/test_empty_stop_not_content_filter.py` (9 cases: helper branches + end-to-end that flagged usage → `analyse_stream_result` returns `continue` not terminal, and surfaces `abnormal_stop` not `content_filter` when exhausted) — neutered helper `return True`→`return False` → 4 asserting tests FAILED, 5 negative stayed green; restored md5 `6591221f…`. `tests/test_frontend_buried_ghost_sweep.py` (19 node checks incl. the exact mr3jfcw10pianj shape) — neutered sweep `splice`→`return 0` → FAILED; restored md5 `31182f1e…`. All 40 touched tests pass (incl. existing test_retry_budget_envelope / test_stream_anomaly_retry_widening / test_sse_core_parity / test_frontend_ghost_tail — no regression). ruff clean, `node --check` clean. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-edd35bce.js` (contains `_sweepBuriedGhostAssistants`/`_isBuriedEmptyGhost`).
- **Live conv repaired.** Confirmed quiescent (`activeTaskId=None`, 0 running task_results), backed up messages to `/tmp/mr3jfcw10pianj_messages_backup_*.json` (25 MB), then removed buried ghosts 79/80/81/84 via the same predicate (mirrors backend `_delete_message_blocking` persistence: msg_count, search_text, FTS, lastMsg settings, preserved created_at). **86 → 82 msgs**, no remaining buried ghosts, tail clean (user→assistant 1070c→user→assistant 59c aborted).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "200-OK empty stop = content policy block" heuristic is wrong: a real block is HTTP 450, a plain empty stop is transient — never make an empty stop TERMINAL without first exhausting the empty_stop retries. And a ghost-cleanup that only inspects the tail leaks: once a newer turn stacks on an empty placeholder it's buried forever — the sweep must scan all non-tail positions. Prove the gateway's actual behaviour with a raw-request replay probe BEFORE editing the classifier.


### 2026-07-03 — Project Brain: cold-start epics were CLAIMED but never WORKED (idle-conv queue never drained) + new "Team/Peers" cohesion column
- **Owner report.** Two complaints: (1) "tasks awaiting claim are not being claimed at all"; (2) the panel doesn't convey conversations working as one team.
- **Root cause #1 (the real bug, not a symptom).** The autonomous flywheel is `sweep_all_active_projects` (scheduler 30s tick) → `select_dispatchable` → `dispatch_epic` (CLAIMS the epic + ENQUEUES a `workflow_step` kickoff into the target conv) → … then the kickoff must be drained + started. But **nothing drains an IDLE conversation's queue.** Every caller of `dispatch_next_queued` is the post-task-completion hook (`manager.py:876`, fires only when another task in that conv finishes), the human send path (`chat.py`), or the manual call in the flywheel test. So for the cold-start case the pillar was BUILT for (open epic, no human tab on that conv): sweep claims it (badge flashes "auto"), the kickoff rots in `message_queue`, the 30-min soft lease expires → `read_board` reports it `open` again, and `_epic_already_queued` sees the stale kickoff still queued → blocks re-dispatch. The epic oscillates open↔claimed and is **never worked** = exactly "awaiting claim, not claimed." `dispatch_epic`'s own docstring even referenced an "idle-conv kickstart" that **did not exist**.
- **Why the suite missed it.** `test_full_autonomous_flywheel` **manually** called `dispatch_next_queued(conv)` at step 4; the NC only asserted the epic got **claimed**, never that a task **ran**. The gap was the manual drain.
- **Fix #1 (`lib/conversations/project_dispatch.py`).** New `_drain_idle_target(target)`: after `dispatch_epic` succeeds for a conv with NO live task, drain it via the SAME `dispatch_next_queued` seam the completion hook uses (spawns from the scheduler thread). Wired into BOTH `sweep_dispatch` and `on_epic_completed`. Invariants held: (a) only drains a conv with no live non-aborted task (`_conv_has_live_task`); (b) GUARD — only drains a conv whose **conversation row EXISTS** (`dequeue_next` DELETEs the queue row before `dispatch_next_queued` checks the conv, so draining a missing conv silently LOSES the kickoff — the guard leaves it queued so a later sweep retries; this also keeps the fake-conv-id unit tests green); (c) does NOT re-acquire the non-reentrant `_dispatch_lock` (dispatch_next_queued takes it). Also: kickoffs were enqueued with EMPTY config → a drained task would have no model/projectPath and couldn't work — new `_resolve_dispatch_config(conv)` resolves the target conv's stored settings via the scheduler's `build_task_config`. And `dispatch_next_queued` (`lib/message_queue.py`) now propagates `_brainDispatch`/`_boardTaskId` markers onto the persisted user turn (mirrors the `_peerMessage` block) so the spawned turn is attributable as brain-dispatched, not mistaken for human input.
- **Tests #1 + double-neuter NC.** `tests/test_project_brain_integration.py`: new `test_cold_start_tick_spawns_task_in_idle_conv` rides the REAL `_check_and_run_due_tasks` tick and asserts a task is actually **SPAWNED** (handed to `spawn_task`), carries `projectPath`, and the persisted turn is `_brainDispatch`+`_boardTaskId` (markers live on the conv ROW — stripped from api_messages, so assert via `_persisted_last_user`, not `task['messages']`). `test_NC_idle_drain_is_load_bearing` byte-reverts the `_drain_idle_target(target)` call → baseline spawns 1, neutered spawns 0 (kickoff rots — the shipped bug), source restored byte-identical (md5 `4dc241f4…`). Updated the existing flywheel test (the sweep now self-drains at step 2, so its old manual-drain step is gone). NC reloads `project_dispatch` FIRST then `scheduler`. 93 brain tests green, ruff clean.
- **Fix #2 (cohesion — the "Team/Peers" column).** The panel had Charter/Board/Activity + the per-conv Influence lens but no conversations-as-a-ROOM surface. `project_peer_status` (presence ⋈ task ⋈ claimed-epic) and `project_message` exchanges existed in the backend but were invisible at project level. Added: new REST `GET /api/v1/project/brain/peers` (backed by `build_peer_status`, convId OPTIONAL + excluded from roster) + `Api.project.brainPeers`; a 4th HTML column `#projectBrainPeersBody`; new `static/js/project-brain-peers.js` (`window.ProjectBrainPeers`) rendering the LIVE roster (each sibling: title · presence dot green=running/amber=idle · advancing «epic» · round/file, sub-agents indented+dashed) + the peer-message THREAD extracted from the feed by the `payload.fromConv/toConv` markers (intervention rows red-bordered). Wired into project-brain.js open/refresh/live/conv-switch via `_refreshPeers`. Registered in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (after project-brain.js, idx 95), dev `<script>` tag, i18n (`projectBrain.team`/`peersEmpty`/`peersHere`/`peerSubAgent`/`peerAdvancing`/`peerEditing`/`peerThread`, ZH+EN), CSS (grid 3→4 cols, `.pb-peer-*`/`.pb-peers-*` roster+thread). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-e58004b0.js`.
- **Tests #2 + NC.** `tests/test_frontend_project_brain_peers.py` (jsdom, loads REAL project-brain-peers.js): asserts 3 roster cards, dot states `[active,idle,idle]`, sub-agent card, "advancing" doing-line, and thread = exactly the 2 fromConv/toConv notes (a plain note WITHOUT those markers excluded). NC byte-reverts the `if (!pl.fromConv || !pl.toConv) continue` filter → the non-peer note leaks (thread 2→3); shipped file restored (md5 `6cb4a0bc…`). GOTCHA: `node -e SCRIPT a b` → `process.argv === [node, a, b]` (no script slot) — SRC is `argv[1]`, not `argv[2]`.
- **Playwright pixels.** Rendered the real 4-column panel + real styles.css with a populated Team column: 4 columns at distinct x-offsets (1/232/464/730), active dot `rgb(34,197,94)` green. Reads as a cohesive room (roster + cross-conversation message thread). Dark theme confirmed from pixels; light-theme body-class guess didn't apply the theme (component is fully var-driven, not overclaiming light pixels).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An enqueue-into-idle-conv path is INERT unless something drains it — `dispatch_next_queued` fires only on task-completion or human-send, NEVER for a cold-start idle conv. A "self-starting" flywheel test that manually calls the drain proves the gears, not the flywheel; the acceptance assertion must ride the real scheduler tick and assert a task SPAWNED, not merely CLAIMED. And `dequeue_next` deletes-before-conv-check, so only drain a conv whose row exists or you silently lose the kickoff.


### 2026-07-03 — Streaming bubble snapping back to "等待中…" (Waiting…) mid-generation on reconnect — 300ms deferred re-render read a still-empty buffer + connectToTask never seeded it (conv `mr4cgdakrl6s5i`)
- **Owner report.** On a streaming + auto-translate conversation: (1) fast conv-switch briefly showed the real English, (2) force-refresh showed the Chinese translation but NO English, (3) the bubble said "等待中…" even though generation was in progress.
- **Root cause (one mechanism, two defects on the reconnect path).** The "等待中…" card IS the streaming bubble; `updateStreamingUI`'s `wait` branch (`streaming_ui.js:325`) fires ONLY when `!content && !thinking`. So the bubble was being painted with EMPTY content while the task was live and the checkpoint English was already persisted on `assistantMsg.content`. Two connected bugs:
  1. `connectToTask` (`sse_pipeline.js`) seeded `buf.toolRounds` after `twStart` but NOT `buf.content`/`buf.thinking`. `twStart` mints an EMPTY buffer, so it stayed empty until the first NEW SSE delta.
  2. `showStreamingUIForConv`'s 300ms deferred re-render (`stream_lifecycle.js`) read `dBuf.content` RAW — no `|| lastMsg.content` fallback like the INITIAL render one block above. So: initial render showed real English (from `lastMsg.content`) → 300ms later the deferred timer fired `updateStreamingUI({content:''})` from the empty buffer → wiped it back to "等待中…".
- **Why it explains all three symptoms.** #1 fast-switch = you caught the initial render before the 300ms wipe. #3 "等待中" while generating = the deferred render clobbered content with the empty buffer. #2 refresh→Chinese-only = the auto-translate watchdog/push filled the SEPARATE `translatePreview` zone with Chinese while the `content` zone stayed blank (empty buffer).
- **Fix.** (1) `sse_pipeline.js`: after `twStart(convId)`, seed `buf.content = assistantMsg.content` / `buf.thinking = assistantMsg.thinking` (mirrors the SSE `state`/`delta` handlers). (2) `stream_lifecycle.js`: the deferred re-render now falls back `dBuf.content || _deferLastMsg.content || ""` (+ thinking + `getToolRoundsFromMsg`), exactly like the initial render — the buffer is authoritative only once it has data; until then the message checkpoint is the truth.
- **Test + double-neuter NC (`tests/test_frontend_stream_deferred_no_wipe.py`, new).** jsdom drives the REAL shipped `updateStreamingUI`: empty msg → 等待中 (baseline), FIXED deferred arg (empty buf + checkpointed msg) → NO wait chip + English rendered, and a byte-shaped NC arg (raw `dBuf.content`) → wait chip reappears. Plus two SOURCE guards (fix #1 seed lines in sse_pipeline.js, fix #2 `_deferLastMsg` fallback in stream_lifecycle.js). NC PROVEN LIVE: reverted both JS fixes → source guards FAIL; restored (`cp` from /tmp backup) → 4 relevant suites green (deferred-no-wipe + translate-preview-survives-rebuild + streaming-ui + sse-dispatch). `node --check` clean. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-c3b9daa6.js`.
- **Follow-up (same day, reviewer catch): closed the twUpdate-path coupling.** The twStart+seed above only runs on the FRESH-connection branch (`!activeStreams.has(convId)`). A re-entry that finds an existing stream (overlapping reconnect race; a caller re-invoking `connectToTask` on a live conv) SKIPS twStart+seed, and `_twFlush` (`health_stream_timer.js`) reads `buf.content` RAW with NO message fallback — so an empty buffer there could still paint "等待中…" over checkpointed content. That safety was implicit (relied on the fresh-path seed + the `loadConversationMessages` MERGE_ACTIVE_TASK `if(!buf.content)` seed) and undocumented. Added a STRICTLY-ADDITIVE defensive seed right after `const stream = activeStreams.get(convId)` that runs on EVERY entry: `if(!_reentryBuf.content && assistantMsg.content) …` for content/thinking/toolRounds — fills an empty buffer field from the persisted turn but NEVER clobbers a field the live `_trySSE` closure is accumulating (guarded on empty). Chose additive-seed over adding a msg-fallback to `_twFlush` because `_twFlush` is the live-streaming single-source-of-truth render; a msg fallback there could resurrect stale/wrong-message content. Test extended: +2 runtime checks (fills-empty / never-clobbers-live) + a source guard on the re-entry block; NC on the seed line bites. Bundle `bundle-ad8bce5d.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A deferred/second render that reads a stream buffer MUST use the same `buf.field || msg.field` fallback the initial render uses — a freshly-`twStart`ed buffer is empty, so a raw-buffer paint wipes real checkpoint content back to the "Waiting…" branch. And any reconnect that creates OR re-enters a stream must SEED an empty buffer from the persisted message (additively — never clobber live deltas), not just `toolRounds`. `_twFlush`'s raw-`buf.content` read makes the seed load-bearing, so it must run on every `connectToTask` entry, not only the fresh branch.


### 2026-07-03 — Cross-conversation file-edit records: the RESIDUAL leak was frontend, not backend — a coarse `_fcFingerprint` collided in the MODULE-GLOBAL file-changes cache (`finish_info.js`)
- **Owner report.** Still seeing file-edit records from one conversation displayed on an UNRELATED conversation — despite backend Fixes 1–5 (see skill `file-history-cross-conversation-attribution`).
- **Where it was NOT.** Two parallel audits (backend serve paths + frontend write paths) confirmed the whole authoritative chain is conv+task isolated: `derive_round_modified_files` (commit_round.py:79) filters `get_modifications(conv_id=…)` then `taskId==task.id`; chat_poll/cold-replay key by task_id row; the fh `diff_name_status` side-channel is enrichment-only behind the `last_writer_task_id` + `_project_lock` gate; every frontend write (`sse_pipeline`, `main_init_tasks` Case B/F, `cross_tab_sync`, `_handleRoundCommitted`) resolves its target via `convId`/per-iteration `const conv` closure. None can write conv A's list onto conv B's message object.
- **Root cause (the real one).** `_extractedFileChangesCache` (finish_info.js:787) is a MODULE-GLOBAL `Map` shared across ALL conversations, feeding the file-changes bar FALLBACK path (messages lacking a server-authoritative `modifiedFileList` — mid-stream / project-tracking-off). Its key, `_fcFingerprint`, was COARSE: `roundCount:lastStatus:lastToolName:lastResultCount`. Two unrelated messages in different conversations sharing that shape (e.g. each: one `write_file`, `done`, 1 result) minted the IDENTICAL key `"1:done:write_file:1"` → conversation B's message read conversation A's cached file list. That is the residual leak; it never touched the backend, which is why Fixes 1–5 (all backend/journal) never closed it.
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/finish_info.js`).** Rewrote `_fcFingerprint` to be CONTENT-FAITHFUL: invariant `same fingerprint ⟺ same extractor inputs ⟹ same output`. It now walks ALL write-capable rounds (`write_file/apply_diff(s)/insert_content(s)/run_command`), projecting exactly the fields `lib/tool_changes.py` consumes — `toolArgs.path` + `edits[].path` (NOT the whole `toolArgs`; write_file args carry the entire file `content`, which must never bloat a cache key), plus `results[0]`'s `fileChanges`/`writeOk`/`badge`/`title`. Empty-write messages still share a key (identical `[]` output — correct).
- **Test + double-neuter (`tests/test_frontend_fc_fingerprint_isolation.py`, NEW).** jsdom loads the REAL `finish_info.js`; asserts distinct files→distinct fp, identical input→identical fp, edits[]/run_command/writeOk all distinguished, and `content` body NOT in key (two writes to same path differing only by body share a key; key length <200). Double-neuter: reverted `_fcFingerprint` to the coarse key inline → `distinct_files_distinct_fp` FAILED (proving the test discriminates); restored byte-identical (md5 `b4283877…`). Also re-ran the 3 suites that stub `_fcFingerprint` (streaming_ui, autopilot warmup/vu) + tool_changes → 36 passed. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-5267db8a.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A coarse cache key is safe only when the cache is scoped to a single owner. `_extractedFileChangesCache` is process-global across conversations, so its key MUST be a faithful function of the extractor inputs — a "coarse enough to detect changes worth refetching" key silently aliases two owners' data. When hunting a cross-conversation display leak, don't stop at the backend serve paths: a global frontend cache keyed by a lossy fingerprint is an equally valid vector, and here it was THE one.
- **Follow-up (same day, owner pushback: "is this still not backend single-source-of-truth?").** Correct critique — the faithful-hash fix CLOSED the leak but left the smell: isolation still rested on a collision-free hash of content in a PROCESS-GLOBAL Map. Two layers were conflated: (1) the derivation LOGIC is already backend-SSOT (`lib/tool_changes.py` via `POST /api/v1/messages/extract-file-changes`; the frontend never re-parses) — that stays; (2) the RESULT CACHE was the shared-global-state smell. Fixed structurally: the cached list now lives on the OWNING MESSAGE object via a `WeakMap` (`_fcResultByMsg` = msg → {fp, files}) — a message can only ever read ITS OWN entry, so cross-conversation leakage is impossible BY CONSTRUCTION, not avoided by a good hash. The fingerprint demotes to a per-message STALENESS token (does my cached list still match my current toolRounds?) plus a request-DEDUP key; the global `_extractedFileChangesPending` (fp → Promise) stays but holds only in-flight Promises (never a rendered result — identical input ⟹ identical output, safe to coalesce). `_extractFileChangesFromRoundsAsync(rounds, msg)` + the batch prefetch now write per-owning-message (re-checking each msg's fp on landing so a mutation between request and response never mis-stamps); `_extractFileChangesFromRoundsCached(msg)` reads the WeakMap owner-scoped. Call sites: `renderFileChangesBar` + streaming `updateStreamingUI` pass `msg`.
- **Test upgrade + structural double-neuter.** `tests/test_frontend_fc_fingerprint_isolation.py` now also asserts the STRUCTURAL guarantee: two DISTINCT message objects with BYTE-IDENTICAL toolRounds (a genuine real fp collision) do NOT share a cache entry — a never-fetched clone of msgA reads `null`, not msgA's list. Double-neuter: reintroduced a global content-keyed lookup → `clone_not_leaked_from_original` FAILS (clone reads the original's list — the exact leak), `cached_B_owns_b` stays green; restored byte-identical (md5 `48e6a47d…`). 16 PASS floor. Full affected sweep 36 passed. Bundle `bundle-c3b9daa6.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson (upgraded).** "Make the hash faithful" is a patch; "scope the cache to its owner" is the fix. When a cache holds per-entity data, key it by the ENTITY (object identity / WeakMap), not by a content fingerprint — then a hash collision degrades to a harmless cache miss instead of a cross-entity leak. Reserve content-fingerprint keys for caches whose value is a pure function of that content AND are safe to share (here: the in-flight request-dedup map).

### 2026-07-02 — Real-time network-latency signal indicator in the topbar (ping/pong RTT on the push WebSocket) + single-writer concurrency fix
- **Request.** Owner wanted a live network-latency indicator on the page (signal-bar style) to tell at a glance whether slowness is the network — a real diagnostic, not a metric toy.
- **Mechanism (no new connection, no polling endpoint).** Piggyback a ping/pong on the ALREADY-open `/api/push` WebSocket. Client sends `{action:'ping', t:<clientTs>}` every 4s; server echoes `{channel:'system', type:'pong', t}`; client RTT = `now - t`. Pure echo, ZERO shared state → works identically on whatever replica the socket landed on (no cross-replica coupling).
- **Backend (`routes/push.py`).** New `ping` branch. Extracted the inline `_receiver` dispatch into a module-level `_handle_client_frame(client, raw)` so the routing is unit-testable without a live socket. **CONCURRENCY FIX (the real bug, caught in review):** the first cut wrote the pong via `await websocket.send_json(...)` directly from `_receiver`, while `_sender` also writes the same socket — two coroutines writing one ASGI WebSocket concurrently can interleave/corrupt frames (Hypercorn `websocket.send` is not concurrent-safe). Fixed by routing the pong through `client.enqueue(...)` — the SAME queue `_sender` drains — so `_sender` stays the SOLE writer. `QueueFull` drops-oldest, fine for a disposable probe. **Log-silent:** the ping branch has NO logger call (4s/client cadence would flood `app.log`); `_sender` only debug-logs on the 30s keepalive-ping heartbeat-failure path, not per frame.
- **Frontend transport (`static/js/push.js`).** Added the RTT probe inside the `_push` IIFE: `_startPinging()` (4s interval, started in `onopen`), `_stopPinging()` + `offline` emit in `onclose`, `_onPong(t)` (ignores stale/mismatched `t`), `PING_TIMEOUT_MS=8000` → `timeout` state if no pong. Public API `pushGetLatency()` / `pushOnLatency(fn)` (fires current reading immediately for late subscribers). Pong routed in `onmessage` BEFORE the handler fan-out (`if type==='pong'`). **Already-open race fix:** `_startPinging` was only wired into `onopen`; if the socket was ALREADY open when a late caller invoked `pushConnect()` (e.g. presence.js opened it first), `connect()` early-returns and onopen never re-fires → pinging never starts → indicator stuck at "—". `connect()` now kicks `_startPinging()` on the already-open early-return path (idempotent via `_pingTimer` guard).
- **Socket-opens-on-load (verified, not assumed).** Server `push_ws()` registers the client + runs `_sender`/`_receiver` regardless of subscriptions; NOTHING closes an unsubscribed socket (`_receiver` blocks on `receive_json`, `_sender` returns a 30s keepalive ping on drain timeout). Client `connect()` opens the WS unconditionally. `net-latency.js initNetLatency()` calls `pushConnect()` on DOMContentLoaded → so a healthy-network user with zero channel subscriptions still sees the indicator light up.
- **UI (`static/js/net-latency.js`, new).** 4 signal bars + ms label in the topbar (`#netLatencyBadge`). State→visual: good `<150ms` 4 bars green / ok `<400ms` 3 amber / poor `≥400ms` 2 orange / timeout 1 red / offline 0 gray. Tooltip shows exact `Nms (quality)`. Pure runtime subscriber on `pushOnLatency`. Registered in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (after main.js — reads `t()`/`pushOnLatency` at runtime) + dev-fallback `<script>` tag + `net.*` i18n (ZH/EN) + `.net-latency-badge`/`.net-bar` CSS (theme-variable-driven, state colours via `data-state`).
- **Tests + double-neuter (`tests/test_push_latency.py`, 4 cases).** Asserts `{action:'ping',t}` → `{type:'pong',t}` lands on the client's OUTBOUND QUEUE (via `drain()`) — proving the single-writer path, not a second direct write — incl. a FIFO-ordering case (pong appended after an already-queued `content_delta`) and a non-ping-produces-no-pong absence case. NC PROVEN: neutering the `client.enqueue` → the 3 pong-asserting tests FAIL, the absence test correctly stays green; restored → 21 passed (latency + push-hub suites). `ruff` clean, `node --check` clean on push.js + net-latency.js. Bundle rebuilt `bundle-2f8dd253.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any second coroutine that needs to emit on a shared ASGI WebSocket MUST enqueue onto the single-writer queue, never call `websocket.send_json` directly — concurrent writers corrupt the frame stream intermittently. And a "starts on onopen" hook is a trap for late callers: if the resource may already be open, the entry point must also kick the hook on the already-open path (idempotently).

### 2026-07-02 — Project Brain: charter decisions were stored truncated at 280 chars (feed cap leaking into commits) + two stacked "项目" bars both opened the panel — root-caused, fixed whole chain, live data repaired (commit 1e7fc5f)
- **Report.** Panel showed every charter decision clipped mid-word ("...ethos: pro", "...1. SINGLE SHAR"); the injected `[PROJECT CHARTER]` block was identically clipped; and two bars under the top bar (both labelled "项目") both just opened the Project Brain panel — reading as a duplicate.
- **Root cause (truncation) — proven from the live DB, not the rendered pixels.** Both stored decisions were EXACTLY 280 chars = `project_feed._SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`, NOT the charter's own `_DECISION_MAX_CHARS`. A decision inherited the feed-row summary: `propose_amendment` emits a `proposed_decision` whose `summary` arg is capped to 280 by `emit_project_event` (full text survives in `payload.proposal`), then BOTH `pending_proposals()` (`summary or payload.proposal`) and `renderCharter` (`p.summary || p.payload.proposal`) were summary-FIRST, so the commit's `add_decision` was the 280-char version → stored permanently. Not a CSS clip (CSS is `white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere`, no line-clamp).
- **Fix (whole chain, root not patch).** (1) `pending_proposals()` → payload-first (`payload.get('proposal') or summary`). (2) `renderCharter` ptext → payload-first (`(p.payload && p.payload.proposal) || p.summary`). (3) Cap reconciliation: `_DECISION_MAX_CHARS` 600→2400, now a SINGLE shared ceiling for both the proposal full text and the committed decision; `propose` retargeted from `_DECISION_MAX_CHARS*4` to the constant (same 2400 value); the feed 280 cap stays scoped to feed rows ONLY (comment locks the invariant). (4) New `repair_truncated_decisions(project_path)` — idempotent, re-sources any decision that is a strict PREFIX of a longer feed `payload.proposal`, re-caps to 2400, bumps version, audit-logged.
- **Live data repaired.** Ran the repair on this project: charter v2→v3, decision[0] 280→1410, decision[1] 280→2400; injected block ~560→3985 chars, now ending on a whole word.
- **CAVEAT (honest, ground-truth).** decision[1] ends at 2400 ("...availab") because its SOURCE feed `payload.proposal` is itself only 2400 chars — that proposal was clipped at PROPOSE-time under the old `600*4=2400` cap. That lost text is UNRECOVERABLE (the full original was never persisted anywhere); the repair restored the maximum available, and the fix prevents recurrence. Verified: feed payload_len == 2400 for that proposal.
- **Two-bar disambiguation (chose relabel+deep-link over merge — they carry genuinely different data).** Row 1 = collab bar (`#presenceStrip`, project-WIDE counts). Row 2 = per-conversation influence bar (`#convInfluenceBar`). Both said "项目", both `openProjectBrain()`. Fix: relabel the influence bar lead `项目大脑`→`本对话` (This chat) so scope reads distinctly; new `openProjectBrainInfluence()` opens the panel AND scroll+flashes the Influence lens (`.pb-influence-flash` keyframe) instead of landing at the top; index.html onclick + i18n `barLead`/`barOpenHint` updated. Merging was rejected: it would lose the project-wide-vs-this-conv distinction.
- **Tests + double-neuter NC (proven bite, byte-identical restore).** Backend `tests/test_project_charter.py` +5 (full pending text, full commit chain, cap==2400, repair idempotency, NC summary-first). Frontend jsdom (real shipped JS + real index.html fragment) `tests/test_frontend_project_brain.py` +4 (full-text render+commit, deep-link flash, +2 NC). NC bite PROVEN LIVE: manually reverted `pending_proposals` to summary-first → `test_pending_returns_full_proposal_not_feed_summary` FAILED; restored → md5 `6a4bd232…` unchanged (project_charter.py) / `2b609ecd…` (project-brain.js). Sweep: 82 passed (charter+brain+influence+collab+feed). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-314b1f47.js` (contains `openProjectBrainInfluence`×2, `pb-influence-flash`×3, payload-first ptext, `本对话`). Ruff clean.
- **Commit `1e7fc5f` (author rangehow), 7 files scope-exact.** `git add` of only: lib/conversations/project_charter.py, static/js/project-brain.js, static/js/i18n.js, index.html, static/styles.css, tests/test_project_charter.py, tests/test_frontend_project_brain.py. Committed the INDEX (no pathspec, per the `git commit -- <path>` override trap). Post-commit `i18n.js`/`styles.css` show residual ` M` — that is a SIBLING conversation's concurrent peer/board-verb work (`.ptool-peer-*`, `boardVerb.*`) written after my `git add`, NOT mine; my edits are confirmed present in the commit and I left the sibling's residual untouched.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A per-consumer cap (feed's 280-char one-line summary) must never become the source a DURABLE record is derived from — the summary is for the feed row; the payload is the truth. When two derivations of "the proposal text" exist (pending API + JS renderer), BOTH must prefer the full payload or a commit silently inherits the truncated one. And verify truncation against the STORED bytes (DB read + source-payload length), not the rendered pixels — 280==`_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` was the smoking gun that pointed at the feed, not the CSS.


### 2026-07-02 — Transport-optimization sweep (frontend↔backend SSE/push): audited whole stack via 4 parallel agents; FIXED #1 (SSE resume-loss cursor bug); handed push-transport findings to sibling mr390e9x
- **Scope / trigger.** Owner asked to thoroughly optimize the frontend↔backend connection/communication (SSE et al.). Ran 4 parallel audit agents (SSE stream / push WS / resilience+fallback / independent arch review) + verified top findings first-hand.
- **Verdict (arch review).** NOT a redundant trio — SSE(primary)+poll(fallback) share ONE source of truth (`task['events']` + monotonic `seq` + durable `task_events`); the push WS carries OTHER channels (paper/translate/swarm/presence), not browser chat. Job = targeted hardening, not a rewrite. Confirmed-good: gzip skipped for `text/event-stream` (server.py:822), `X-Accel-Buffering:no`, 15s SSE keepalive, cursor-based O(indexed) resume, client backoff+jitter+resubscribe.
- **FIX #1 SHIPPED — SSE resume-loss cursor bug (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`).** The SSE wire is `id: N` then paired `data: {...}`. Old code committed the Last-Event-ID cursor (in-mem `_lastEventId` AND persisted `_saveSseCursor`) ON the `id:` line and `return`ed BEFORE the `data:` line parsed/applied. A drop between the two lines advanced the cursor past an unapplied delta → resume (`event_id > cursor`) SILENTLY SKIPPED it. Fix: `id:` line now only STASHES `_pendingEventId`; the cursor commits only after the paired `data:` event parses and is about to apply synchronously (no await between commit and its application in `dispatchSSEEvent`). Added `pendingEventId` to ctx + `makeCtx` seam + `_trySSE` literal + write-back finally.
- **Test + double-neuter NC (`tests/test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py`).** New scenario 27 drives id→data commit, dropped-data-leaves-cursor, retried-event-applied-once; updated #4 (`id_line_noop` now asserts cursor stays null + `id_line_stashes_pending`). PASS floor 57→63. Suite green (1 passed). NC bite: reverted just the id-branch to immediate-commit → flipped EXACTLY 4 discriminating checks (`cursor_not_committed_before_data`, `dropped_data_leaves_cursor`, `id_line_noop`, `id_line_stashes_pending`), nothing else; restored fixed file byte-identical (md5 `902a4053102ccd113316f4b0ad7c41ad`), re-green. `node --check` clean. No bundler change (file already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`).
- **Coordination.** Sent push-transport findings to sibling `mr390e9x` (port-15000 disconnect investigation) — their domain: (1) NO dead-peer watchdog (client push.js drops ping w/o reply, no liveness timer; half-open TCP → `_connected=true` forever) = top root-cause candidate for their bug; (2) Redis bus subscriber thread dies permanently on drop (push_bus.py); (3) P0 auth hole — push_ws() creates PushClient() with zero identity, any client can subscribe/abort ANY task. NOT touching push.py — theirs.
- **Remaining in my lane (not yet done).** #2 busy-poll (`chat.py:1659` `sleep(0.05)` re-slices buffer 20×/s/stream under lock → replace with per-task asyncio.Event wake + 15s heartbeat tick); #6 poll re-ships whole buffer each tick (add cursor to `/api/chat/poll`); #7 two dead-server managers can collide; #8 cold-replay double-serialize. All uncommitted (working-tree changes only).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An SSE resume cursor must be committed AFTER its paired event is applied, never on the id line — the id-then-data wire gap is a real loss window. Verify optimization work against the surface (jsdom harness driving the REAL shipped dispatcher), and prove the test discriminates via a byte-reverting NC that flips only the intended checks.


### 2026-07-02 — Fixed WRONG-AUTHOR leak on both opensource remotes: the install.sh tip commits were authored `tofu-bot` (a stranger's GitHub account, id 106741602) — re-authored to `rangehow` + force-pushed; root-caused to the out-of-band push omitting the identity flags
- **Symptom (owner report).** GitHub showed an unfamiliar `Tofu-bot` avatar as a "contributor" on both `rangehow/ToFu` and `NiuTrans/ToFu`, and the install.sh portability commit was attributed to it. Looked like an identity leak / takeover.
- **Root cause (NOT a compromise).** The token-scoped single-file push from the prior entry committed via ad-hoc `git` OUTSIDE `export.py`'s push path, so it never set the canonical identity (`export.py:2673-2674` → `user.name=rangehow` / `user.email=rangehow@users.noreply.github.com`). The clone picked up `user.name=tofu-bot` / `tofu-bot@users.noreply.github.com`. That LEGACY noreply form (no `ID+` numeric prefix) resolves to whatever account owns the username `tofu-bot` — a real unrelated account (`Tofu-bot`, user id `106741602`) — so GitHub auto-listed it as a contributor. Wrong author metadata, nothing more.
- **Fix (re-author tip, tree byte-identical).** Both tips were a SINGLE `tofu-bot` commit sitting directly on the clean `rangehow` commit `03e0f92` (verified 8 deep on each remote: `03e0f92`→`1f38b9d` all `rangehow`, no lurking `0ce5d57`/`973a3177` sentinel/base64 below — so a single amend, no `filter-repo`). Per remote: shallow clone, `git -c user.name=rangehow -c user.email=rangehow@users.noreply.github.com commit --amend --no-edit --author="rangehow <rangehow@users.noreply.github.com>"`, PROVE `HEAD^{tree}` still `73332349b485ce49580b1b3b6d1b21fdf9777ce5` + `install.sh` md5 still `e212470f5e957112e44e42771d34e07d` + `git diff old..new` empty BEFORE pushing, then `git push --force`.
- **Result (ground-truth `list_commits`, not the local clone).** rangehow/ToFu tip `3004435`→**`32f49d9`**, NiuTrans/ToFu tip `1e12adf`→**`a8ca4fd`**. Both new tips: author+committer `rangehow` (login `rangehow`, id `88258534`); tree unchanged `73332349…`; ZERO commits on `main` reference `tofu-bot@users.noreply.github.com` or id `106741602`. The `Tofu-bot` contributor tile is derived from authorship and drops off after GitHub reindexes now that no commit references it.
- **Root-cause fix (recur-proofing).** Any out-of-band token-scoped commit (the recipe in the entry below) MUST pin `git -c user.name=rangehow -c user.email=rangehow@users.noreply.github.com` (matching `export.py:2673-2674`) — otherwise the clone's ambient/global git identity leaks into a public commit and re-links a stranger's account. `export.py`'s own push path already does this; only hand-run git needs the reminder.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A commit's AUTHOR is separate from WHO pushed it (auth ≠ authorship) — a correct token + correct push can still stamp the wrong person if `user.name`/`user.email` aren't pinned. And the legacy `name@users.noreply.github.com` form is account-linkable by username, so a wrong name silently attributes your work to whoever holds that handle. When rewriting public history to fix it: confirm the bad author is ONLY the tip (log deep first), amend author AND committer, prove tree-SHA + file md5 unchanged before force-push, and verify absence from the REMOTE via `list_commits`, not the local clone.

### 2026-07-02 — macOS install.sh portability fix SHIPPED to both opensource remotes (rangehow/ToFu + NiuTrans/ToFu main) via token-scoped single-file git push
- **Context.** The seven macOS/BSD portability edits (stdbuf/`sed -u` probe-and-degrade, `date -Iseconds` fallback, four portable `mktemp`, guarded `sort -V`) were verified locally at `/tmp/live_install.sh` (md5 `e212470f5e957112e44e42771d34e07d`, 82,387 B, `bash -n` clean). Getting them to the branch Mac users actually `curl` was the remaining crux.
- **Transport failure + recovery (own it).** First attempts to land the file via GitHub MCP inline-content commits FAILED and BROKE `rangehow/ToFu` main: commit `0ce5d57` wrote the literal sentinel `__READ_FROM_FILE__` (18 B), `973a3177` wrote a truncated-base64 223-B fragment, plus a stray `install.sh.part` (deleted in `435ed26`). Root cause: an 82 KB file can't be reliably emitted inline in a single tool arg (every large paste truncated). Correct fix was NOT more inline commits.
- **Correct mechanism (the one already in-repo).** The GitHub credential is `export.py:2584 _GH_TOKEN`; the opensource push targets TWO remotes (`origin`=rangehow/ToFu, `niutrans`=NiuTrans/ToFu, both branch `main`). Did a SCOPED single-file push (NOT `export.py --mode opensource --push`, which would sweep the 464 dirty in-progress files): read token programmatically (never echoed; redacted from all git stderr via `sed`), `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://<token>@github.com/<repo>` into /tmp, `cp` the verified file over `install.sh`, **verify md5==e212470f… AND `bash -n` BEFORE `git add install.sh` + commit + push**, only `install.sh` staged.
- **Result (ground-truth verified via raw CDN, cache-busted).** `rangehow/ToFu` main commit `dc4d66e`, `NiuTrans/ToFu` main commit `1e12adf`. Both `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/install.sh` now 82,387 B, md5 `e212470f5e957112e44e42771d34e07d`, `_TOFU_STDBUF` guard present (4×), ZERO unguarded `stdbuf -oL tee` / `sed -u $` / `mktemp -t ` / `| sort -V |` / `date -Iseconds)`. NiuTrans's pre-push file was the ORIGINAL unfixed 81,689-B installer (my broken commits only ever hit rangehow), so its diff was the clean +22/-8 of the 7 edits. Tokened temp clones deleted after push (`.git/config` held the credential).
- **Guardrails / lessons.** (1) A fixed file that never ships fixes nothing — the acceptance bar is the LIVE `raw` blob on EVERY consumer remote (rangehow AND NiuTrans), md5-verified, not a local edit. (2) Don't hand-craft GitHub API commits for large files — inline content truncates silently and you can BREAK the live branch; use a token-scoped `git clone`+`cp`+`push` where git handles the bytes. (3) Verify md5 + `bash -n` in the clone BEFORE commit, stage ONLY the one file, never `git add -A` on an export tree. (4) The token lives in `export.py`; a scoped push reuses it without running the full 464-file export.

- **Guardrail / lesson.** A dispatch no-op is still a chance to observe drift: the claim leases silently ticking toward 0 with the durability risk unresolved is the actual signal worth surfacing. Don't fabricate work to satisfy the dispatch; DO report the state change that matters.

### 2026-07-02 — Pillar #6 follow-up: made the hard-abort intervention path REACHABLE (was dead code) + made an arriving peer message OBSERVABLE (was indistinguishable from user input)
- **Owner verification caught two real gaps** after the initial Pillar #6 landing. Both were "looks done, isn't reachable/visible end-to-end" — exactly the class the owner insists on testing from the surface.
- **Gap 1 (the unmet acceptance criterion): `project_intervene(hard_abort=True)` was UNREACHABLE dead code.** `cfg['interventionApprovedBy']` was READ in `project_peer.py` and SET in zero places (no UI/route/flow), so the coercive path ALWAYS degraded to a refusal — advisory-only, not "intervene". **Fix (root cause, not a token-injection hack):** `intervene_peer` gained an injectable `approval_fn(prompt) -> approver|None`. When `hard_abort=True` and no token is pre-supplied, it now REQUESTS human approval via that callback instead of silently refusing; grant → stamp `approved_by`, run `abort_running_tasks_for_conv` (task only), `audit_log('intervention', approved_by=<who>)`; deny → `denied_by_human` (stays advisory). The pure `_authorize_hard_abort` remains the FINAL arbiter (NC-GATE still bites). The handler `_make_intervention_approval_fn` (`handlers/misc.py`) wires `approval_fn` to the SAME `request_human_guidance` seam `ask_human` uses — emits a `human_guidance_request` (choice: Approve/Deny, `intervention:true`) the UI already renders + resolves, blocks until the human decides. **Autopilot auto-DENIES** a coercive kill (a VU may answer questions but must never green-light stopping a sibling). A pre-supplied token (already-authorized headless caller) short-circuits the request.
  - **Bug caught by the end-to-end surface test (why reachability-from-surface matters):** the first extraction of `_make_intervention_approval_fn` to module scope referenced `round_entry` which wasn't a param → `NameError` → caught → treated as deny → APPROVE silently did nothing. Would have shipped as "approve is a no-op". Fixed by threading `round_entry` in. Now locked by `test_handler_hard_abort_approved_runs_from_surface`.
- **Gap 2 (observability): an arriving `KIND_PEER_MSG` was structurally indistinguishable from user input.** `dispatch_next_queued` (legacy branch) built the turn as `role:'user'` but only copied `images/pdfTexts/replyQuotes/convRefs` — the `_peerMessage`/`_fromConv` markers were DROPPED, so the persisted turn looked byte-identical to something the human typed (the agent saw the `[Peer message … (conv X)]` text prefix, but the UI could not attribute/badge it). **Fix:** propagate `_peerMessage`+`_fromConv` onto the dispatched `user_msg` (`lib/message_queue.py`); render a distinct SVG-icon provenance banner (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`, `.peer-msg-banner` in `styles.css`, i18n `peer.messageBanner` EN+ZH) on any user turn carrying `_peerMessage`. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-c0781678.js`).
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_peer.py` 17→26, all pass) + NC bites PROVEN.** New: approval-granted FULL path (approval_fn grants → abort called + audit `approved_by` stamped), deny path (approval_fn None → `denied_by_human`, no abort), pre-supplied-token short-circuit, 3 handler-surface tests (approve/deny/autopilot through `request_human_guidance`), peer-marker-survives-dispatch (DB-free, `_HybridRow` fake). New NCs: **NC-DENY** (neuter the deny branch → denied abort runs → deny test FAILS) and **NC-OBSERVE** (neuter marker propagation → markers absent → observability test FAILS); both byte-reverting. Functionally confirmed both NCs FAIL the corresponding functional test, then restore. Regression: peer+board+brain_summary+message_queue+dispatch = **78 passed**; py_compile + `node --check` clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "human-approval-gated" action is only real if something can REQUEST the approval — a gate keyed on a config token nobody sets is dead code, not a safety feature. Wire it to the existing `request_human_guidance` seam (grant→run, deny→advisory, autopilot→deny), and TEST it from the agent surface (execute_peer_tool), not just the pure gate — that surface test is what caught the `round_entry` closure NameError that made "approve" a silent no-op. Separately: a turn injected into another conversation's queue as `role:'user'` MUST carry propagated provenance markers or it is indistinguishable from human input — copy the markers at the dispatch seam AND render them.
