### 2026-07-02 — Reading/Review Mode default model now tracks the frontend toolbar preset (config.model → serverModel) instead of always seeding chatModels[0] — + DB-free jsdom regression guard with a byte-revert NC bite
- **Owner ask (user preference).** In Reading Mode (Report) and Review Mode, the default generation model should be consistent with the model configured in the frontend toolbar preset, not an arbitrary first-in-list model.
- **Root cause (`static/js/paper-reader.js::_populatePaperReportModelDropdown`).** When no model had been explicitly chosen for a view (`!view.model`), the picker auto-seeded `_selectPaperReportModel(chatModels[0].model_id, view)` — the FIRST visible chat model — independent of the app-wide toolbar selection (`config.model`, falling back to the configured `serverModel` / "默认模型"). So Report/Review frequently started on a different model than the rest of the app.
- **Fix (seed block only; scope unchanged).** When `!view.model`, seed from the frontend preset — `config.model` first, then `serverModel` — but ONLY if that id is among the available (capability-clean, non-hidden) chat models; otherwise fall back to `chatModels[0]` exactly as before (covers fresh/open-source deploys whose hardcoded default isn't in the user's providers). Report + Review share this one function, so both views are covered by the single edit. Semantics are "default AT OPEN": the seed fires once while `!view.model`, so an explicit paper-picker choice is never overwritten, and a LATER toolbar switch does not retro-actively change an already-seeded paper view (a default, not a live mirror — an explicit paper pick still wins).
- **Guard (`tests/test_frontend_paper_model_default.py`, 2 tests — sibling to `test_frontend_paper_no_autostart.py`).** DB-free jsdom harness loads the REAL shipped `paper-reader.js`, drives `_populatePaperReportModelDropdown` for both views against a fixed `_registeredModels=[m-first, m-preset, m-other]` (preset deliberately NOT first, so seeding to it discriminates from `chatModels[0]`). Asserts (1) `config.model='m-preset'` → both `_paperReportModel`/`_paperReviewModel` seed to `m-preset` (not `m-first`); (1b) `config` absent but `serverModel='m-preset'` → seeds from serverModel; (2) preset not in the list → falls back to `m-first`; (3) an explicit prior pick (`view.model` preset) is preserved. The "default at open" contract is written into the test comments so it's explicit not accidental.
- **Verification (actual output + byte-revert NC).** `pytest tests/test_frontend_paper_model_default.py` = **2 passed** (7/7 harness PASS). **NC bite:** byte-reverting the seed block to `_selectPaperReportModel(chatModels[0].model_id, view)` → harness flips `FAIL report_seed_from_preset` / `report_seed_not_first` / `review_seed_from_preset` / `report_seed_from_servermodel` while `report_fallback_first` + both `*_explicit_pick_preserved` stay PASS (discriminating); shipped file restored byte-identical (md5 `3ad61c4c3d17dd0bc58d1100becb0df8`). `node --check` clean; `paper-reader.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (server restart + hard-refresh, no bundler edit). Neighbors `test_frontend_paper_no_autostart.py` (2) + `test_frontend_paper_regen_refresh.py` (1) still green.
- **Pre-existing failures noted (NOT caused by this change).** In this working tree `tests/test_frontend_typecheck.py::test_frontend_typecheck_does_not_regress` fails on `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js(733,55): TS2304 Cannot find name '_t'` (a file untouched here; tsc reports zero errors for `paper-reader.js`/`main_toolbar_ui.js`), and `test_frontend_review_venue_race.py::...resolves_venue_before_generating` fails on `one_start`/`langkey_*`. Proven pre-existing by reverting my seed block and re-running: both still FAIL without my edit. Left for their owners.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A per-feature model picker that auto-seeds `chatModels[0]` silently diverges from the app-wide toolbar model; seed feature defaults from the frontend preset (`config.model` → `serverModel`), gated on availability, with a first-model fallback for deploys where the preset isn't a real provider model. Keep it a "default at open" (fires only while `!view.model`) so an explicit per-feature pick always wins.

### 2026-07-02 — MCP batch-commit tool line showed only `main @ owner/repo`, never the committed paths — batch-file arg shapes (`files[]`/`delete_paths[]`/`paths[]`) now render every path
- **Owner report.** `github-batch/batch_commit` in the tool-call line displayed `github-batch/batch_commit — main @ rangehow/ToFu` with no indication of WHICH files were committed.
- **Root cause (`lib/tasks_pkg/tool_display.py::_mcp_arg_suffix`).** The MCP display helper only scans FLAT top-level `fn_args` keys (`_MCP_RESOURCE_KEYS`: `file_path`/`path`/`name`/`branch`/…). But `batch_commit` carries paths INSIDE `files=[{path,content},…]` + `delete_paths=[…]`; `batch_delete` uses `paths=[…]`; the official `github/push_files` uses `files=[{path,content}]`. None match the flat scan, so resource fell through to `branch` (`main`) and container to `owner/repo` → uniform `main @ owner/repo`, paths never shown.
- **Fix.** New pure helper `_mcp_batch_paths(fn_args)` extracts `(path, is_delete)` tuples from the `files`/`delete_paths`/`paths` list shapes (returns `[]` for non-batch calls). `_tool_display_mcp` checks it first: when non-empty, renders `head — N files @ owner/repo:` followed by one `• path` per line (deletes prefixed `− `), and exposes the multiline form as `_display_query` so it survives into the SSE `tool_start` event. The frontend already turns `\n → <br>` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js:785`), same convention as the `web_search`/`fetch_url` batch renderers — no frontend change needed. Non-batch MCP calls still route through `_mcp_arg_suffix` unchanged (links/suffix preserved).
- **Verification (actual + byte-revert NC).** `tests/test_mcp_tool_links.py` +`BatchCommitPathDisplayTest` (4 tests: batch_commit lists all paths incl. `−` delete marker + `_display_query` parity; batch_delete; official push_files; non-batch call unaffected — no `\n`). Suite = **13 passed**. NC: neutering the guard (`if batch_paths:`→`if False:`) fails the 3 batch tests while `test_non_batch_mcp_call_unaffected` stays green (discriminating); `cp`-restore → md5 `90b60cf4…`, 4/4 pass. `py_compile` clean.
- **Dual-source drift fix (follow-up, same session).** `lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/mcp.py::_post_build` rebuilt the PERSISTED results-row `meta['title']` via `_mcp_arg_suffix(fn_args)` DIRECTLY — a second code path independent of `_tool_display_mcp`. So after a `batch_commit` completed, the title regressed from the per-path list to `batch_commit — main @ owner/repo` (the live `tool_start` line was fine — it reads `round.query`). Fixed by extracting the head + batch-path/suffix composition into ONE helper `tool_display.compose_mcp_display(fn_name, fn_args) → (display, is_multiline)`; BOTH `_tool_display_mcp` and `_post_build` now call it, so the live line and persisted title cannot diverge (incl. the batch one-path-per-line form).
- **Verification (actual + byte-revert NC).** `tests/test_mcp_tool_links.py` +`PostBuildTitleTest` (2 tests) drives the REAL `_post_build` closure (monkeypatch `get_bridge`, stub `simple_call` to capture the `post_build` callback, invoke against a fresh `meta`): asserts `meta['title']` for `batch_commit` contains every path + `− delete` marker + `3 files` and is NOT the branch-only label; flat `create_issue` title unchanged (`github/create_issue — Bug @ a/b`). Suite = **15 passed**. NC: reverting `_post_build` to the direct `_mcp_arg_suffix` logic fails `test_batch_commit_title_has_paths` while `test_flat_arg_title_unchanged` stays green (discriminating); `cp`-restore → md5 `1a7a75ac…`, 15/15. `py_compile` clean on both touched modules.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** MCP display arg-extraction is flat-key only — any tool that nests its primary resource inside a LIST (batch commits, multi-file ops) needs an explicit list-shape branch, and it must live in ONE composition helper (`compose_mcp_display`) that BOTH the live tool-line (`_tool_display_mcp`) and the persisted-title rebuild (`handlers/mcp.py::_post_build`) call. Two independent label computations for the "same" MCP display WILL drift — here the post-execution title silently reverted the batch-path rendering.


### 2026-07-02 — Project-brain tools render blank + a phantom `fetch_url({urls:[]})` — root-caused BOTH from the PG copy of conv `mr35arziyiquic`, fixed the streaming-prefetch phantom gate + the missing conv-meta renderer
- **Owner report.** Read conv `mr35arziyiquic` from PostgreSQL: (1) the Project-Brain tools show NOTHING to the user in the transcript, and (2) it fired a bogus `fetch_url({"reason":"placeholder","urls":[]})`. Enhance the tool style-rendering.
- **Evidence (pulled the real row via `lib.database._core._new_pg_connection`, not guessed).** `conversations` row (user_id=1, 2 msgs); the assistant turn's `toolRounds[]` (10 rounds) is the render source. Round[0]=`project_board_read` (`toolContent` 1863 chars, `results[0]={source:"Board",badge:"read",snippet:120c}`), round[1]=`project_charter_read` (135 chars, `source:"Charter"`). Round[3] is the phantom: `toolName=fetch_url`, `toolArgs={"reason":"placeholder","urls":[]}`, `results=[{url:"",title:"Page: ",source:"Prefetch",fetched:false,snippet:"Failed"}]`, `toolContent="Failed to fetch ."`.
- **Root cause #1 (phantom executed by the STREAMING PREFETCH, not the handler).** `urls:[]` is falsy → batch mode skipped → falls to single-URL mode with `url=''`. `StreamingToolAccumulator.on_tool_call_ready` pre-executes any `_STREAMABLE_TOOLS` call with truthy `fn_args` — it never checked for an actual target — so `_execute_one('fetch_url', …)` ran `fetch_page_content('')` and CACHED `"Failed to fetch ."` under `source:"Prefetch"`. The real handler then hit that cache and never got to reject it. Hence the `Prefetch` source + empty-URL "Failed" row.
- **Root cause #2 (blank display).** `project_board_read`/`project_charter_read`/`list_conversations`/`get_conversation`/peer tools return their real prose in `round.toolContent` (+ a short `snippet`) with `source` in {Board,Charter,Conversations,Peer}, but hit NO special branch in `_renderUnifiedToolLine` (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`) → fell through to the bare generic `<div class="ptool-line">` that renders only icon+name+badge. All 1863 chars of board content were dropped on the floor.
- **Fix #1 — prefetch phantom gate (`lib/tasks_pkg/streaming_tool_executor.py`).** New pure predicate `_has_executable_target(fn_name, fn_args)` (fetch_url needs a non-empty `url` or a `urls` entry with a url; web_search needs a non-blank `query`/`queries`; project tools always pass — their handler validates). `on_tool_call_ready` now gates pre-execution on it, so a phantom defers to the normal handler instead of caching a bogus Prefetch row.
- **Fix #1b — handler rejects empty target (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/search.py`).** `_handle_fetch_url` single-URL path now strips + checks `url`; empty → clear "fetch_url requires a non-empty url" tool-content + a `{title:"No URL provided", source:"N/A"}` row via `_finalize_tool_round`, instead of fetching the empty string.
- **Fix #2 — conv-meta renderer (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js` + `styles.css` + `i18n.js`).** New `_isRoundConvMeta` (set of board/charter/conv-ref/peer tool names) + `_renderConvMetaBlock` — a collapsible `<details open>` card that renders the full `round.toolContent` as Markdown (falls back to `meta.snippet` mid-stream), with a family SVG icon (board/charter/peer added to `_webToolSvg`; conv-ref icons already existed) + a source chip (Board/Charter/Conversations/Peer) + the action badge. Wired in `_renderUnifiedToolLine` just before the generic fallback (after `badgeHtml` is computed; skipped for `status==='rejected'`). CSS `.ptool-convmeta-*` mirrors the memory-block accent/collapse language (theme-var driven, so light/tofu inherit). i18n `tool.noContent` (zh/en).
- **Verification (actual output + biting NC + byte-revert).** `tests/test_streaming_and_prefetch.py` +6 tests (phantom-empty-urls / no-target / blank-query skip, real-url still submits, `_has_executable_target` truth-table) → **33 passed**; +`test_frontend_api_isolation` = 37 passed. **NC BITES:** neutering the gate (`and _has_executable_target(…)` → `and True`) → exactly the 3 skip tests FAIL (the neutered version fired REAL web/fetch calls — visible in the log); `cp`-restore → md5 identical, guard live. `node --check` clean on tool_rounds.js/i18n.js; bundle rebuilt `bundle-f1e32ca2.js` (contains `_renderConvMetaBlock`/`_isRoundConvMeta`/`ptool-convmeta`, 12 hits). Re-ran the routing decision against the REAL PG row: rounds 0/1 now `routed_convmeta=True`, round 3 (fetch_url) correctly not routed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) The streaming prefetch path is a SECOND execution site that bypasses the handler's validation — any "the model sent junk args" guard must exist HERE too, or a phantom gets cached under `source:"Prefetch"` and the handler never runs. (2) A tool that returns prose in `toolContent` needs an explicit renderer branch; the generic `ptool-line` fallback shows name+badge only and silently drops the content. When adding a new prose-returning tool (conversations/brain/peer family), add its name to `_CONV_META_TOOLS` (or give it a dedicated block) — do not rely on the generic line.

(3) Board corrected: posted 3 STATUS epics (`pt_67b6d20b…` B, `pt_c0935c4d…` C, `pt_096e5b7b…` D) recording design-complete + implemented-in-working-tree + test counts + "do NOT re-implement" + what remains (uncommitted + infra-parked). Did NOT mark B/C/D DONE — implementation is uncommitted and the scale rollout still gates on infra.
