### 2026-07-02 — Swarm follow-up tools (await_agents / get_agent_result) no longer rejected as "非真实工具" on a continuation turn with swarmEnabled=false — root fix: a live-or-pending swarm force-enables its tools for that turn; + panel no longer shows 0/N·Unconfirmed·无结果 despite received+injected updates
- **Owner report (conv `mr2ysg473scxv8`).** An Agent bubble spawned a 2-agent swarm (`d5f50acc`+`b4989cda`), both agents COMPLETED and their `<swarm-update>`s were RECEIVED + `injected → context` (chips prove it) — yet (a) later rounds the model called `get_agent_result`/`await_agents` and both were rejected **`非真实工具`** with irrelevant did-you-mean suggestions (merge_memories/insert_contents), and (b) the swarm panel rendered `0/2 · Unconfirmed · 无结果`. "Did something change the system/tool of our messages? How could the model see this tool but be unable to use it?"
- **Root-cause (evidence-first, task_events as SoT, two turns not one).** DB proved 2 `task_results`: T1 `d5c869ab` (21 rounds, **interrupted**) shipped swarm tools + `spawn_agents` executed OK; T2 `f4517e62` (61 rounds) did NOT ship swarm tools yet the model called `get_agent_result`(r37)/`await_agents`(r42) → rejected. Stored `conversations.settings.swarmEnabled = **false**`. Chain: per-turn `_tool_schema` (orchestrator.py:1318) is the SoT for `_known_tool_names` → the hallucination gate (`ingest_tool_call`, tool_dispatch.py:1315). `_build_swarm` only emits the 3 tools when `swarm_enabled` (registry.py:909; `swarm_enabled=cfg.get('swarmEnabled',False)`, model_config.py:145). **BUT** the swarm-inbox drain/inject (orchestrator.py:1607-1690) is **completely UNGATED** — it injects a `<swarm-update>` whose text instructs the model to call `get_agent_result`/`await_agents` even on a `swarmEnabled=false` turn. T1 interrupted → T2 was an ordinary manual/continue turn (NOT the `_start_autocontinue_turn` path, which already hard-sets swarmEnabled=True) → schema legitimately omitted the tools → the injected instruction became a guaranteed hallucination-rejection that stranded the completed agent work.
- **Bug 1 FIX (backend, root — force the tools, do NOT gate the drain off).** New pure helpers in `lib/swarm/tools.py`: `augment_with_swarm_tools(tool_list)` (idempotent append of the 3 MASTER tools; returns same object + `[]` when all present → no prompt-cache churn) and `resolve_turn_swarm_tools(tool_list, *, swarm_enabled, has_pending_or_live)`. New `lib/swarm/integration.py::has_live_or_pending_swarm(task)` = live `_get_session(swarm_key)` OR `agent_inbox.has_pending(swarm_key)` (conv-scoped key so a continue turn sees its own swarm; fail-open on error). Orchestrator seam (after `_assemble_tool_list`, before `task['_tool_schema']=tool_list`): when `not swarm_enabled` and a swarm is live-or-pending, force the 3 tools in (lift `max_tool_rounds` off 0 if the turn had no other tools), `has_real_tools=True`, and a **greppable WARNING** `🐝 swarm_enabled=False but a live-or-pending swarm exists — force-enabling swarm tools … (bypassing tool-schema latch)`. Runs AFTER `latch_tool_list` so it BYPASSES the per-conversation tool-schema latch on purpose — correctness of the pending-swarm turn wins over prompt-cache stability. Mirrors what `_start_autocontinue_turn` already guaranteed; now the manual/continue turn is covered too.
- **Bug 2 FIX (frontend, `static/js/ui/streaming_swarm_panel.js`).** The completion proof SURVIVED reload the whole time — `_handleSwarmInboxInject` persists synthetic `_inboxInject` tool rows carrying `inboxAgentIds` into `toolRounds` — but `_recoverSwarmAgents` never read them, so a fire-and-forget swarm (no `_swarmSnapshot`, no sibling await/get rounds) recovered every agent as `unknown` → `finished=0/total=2` → `0/2` + "Unconfirmed" limbo pill + `无结果`. New `_swarmInjectedAgentIds(allRounds)` harvests those ids; recovery precedence is now **sibling-result status > inbox-injected `done` > `unknown`**. Flips the pill off Unconfirmed, the count to 2/2, the cards off 无结果. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-0eadb5e6.js`, contains `_swarmInjectedAgentIds`); all 3 touched files (`ui/streaming_swarm_panel.js`, `ui/streaming_ui.js`, `ui/sse_handlers_lifecycle.js`) already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Verification (actual + BOTH NC bites byte-reverting).** `tests/test_swarm_pending_tool_force.py` (10, pure helper incl. an end-to-end contract with the real `classify_tool_call`) + `tests/test_orchestrator_pending_swarm_seam.py` (5, executes the guard block extracted VERBATIM from orchestrator.py source against `_known_tool_names`) + `tests/test_frontend_swarm_inbox_recovery.py` (jsdom, real shipped JS). **NC #1 (backend):** neuter the orchestrator guard (`if not swarm_enabled:`→`if False:`) → `test_pending_swarm_turn_gets_swarm_tools_in_schema` FAILS ("Extra items in the left set: await_agents/spawn_agents/get_agent_result") + `test_guard_block_present_in_source` FAILS; `cp`-restore → md5 `8752689234e7cebae96ecbc95892cb9c`, 15/15 pass. **NC #2 (frontend):** revert `_recoverSwarmAgents` status line to `res.status || "unknown"` → agents recover `unknown`, panel reverts to `0/2`+Unconfirmed+无结果 (`agentA_done`/`agentB_done`/`panel_*` all FAIL); `cp`-restore → md5 `ac97a5758abb8b97d18b4e40bfe74667`, green. Broader regression: `test_swarm_tool_scoping`+`test_agent_inbox`+`test_core_tool_isolation`+`test_frontend_swarm_{stale,recovery,inbox_recovery}` = 60 passed. `py_compile`+`ruff` clean on all touched backend files.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The swarm inbox drain is deliberately UNGATED (stranding completed agent work is worse than a stray tool) — so the per-turn tool schema MUST keep pace: whenever a `<swarm-update>` can be injected (live session OR pending inbox for the conv), the follow-up tools `await_agents`/`get_agent_result`/`spawn_agents` MUST be in `_tool_schema` regardless of `swarmEnabled`, and this force MUST bypass the tool-schema latch. And any per-agent completion that is proven only in live-only `_swarmAgents` needs a reload-durable mirror the recovery path actually reads — here the persisted `_inboxInject` rows already existed; `_recoverSwarmAgents` just never consulted them.


### 2026-07-02 — Codified "chat-inner bubble = pure backend projection" + proved it: autopilot VU SETTLED render now verbatim from `ev.vuMessage` (dropped the `|| buf.content` dual-source fallback)
- **Owner directive (durable).** Bubble rendering in `chatInner` must rely SOLELY on backend runtime state. No dual mechanism (frontend + backend) that requires SYNC — that's what makes a stuck bubble un-diagnosable. Sharpened line: **transient vs settled**. Accumulating streaming deltas into a live buffer = OK (painting an in-flight stream). The moment a turn/VU reply SETTLES, the bubble must be a VERBATIM projection of ONE backend-authoritative record — no `|| buf.content` fallback that makes the frontend-accumulated copy a second source of truth; no frontend heuristic deciding bubble lifecycle the backend doesn't itself assert.
- **Convention (`.tofu/skills/separation-of-concerns-directive.md`, +51 lines).** New "Chat-Inner Bubble = Pure Backend Projection" clause: the transient/settled line + two concrete bans (1: no local-buffer fallback for settled state — an empty settled value the backend INTENDS must render empty; if it's wrongly empty that's a backend bug to fix at source; 2: no frontend-only lifecycle heuristics — `*_start`/`*_done`/`*_cancel` are asserted by backend, the client obeys, it does not reconstruct). Guardrail names the NC test.
- **Backend confirmed authoritative (no change needed).** `_append_vu_message_to_conv` (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py:1018`) builds `vu_msg={'role':'user','content':text,'toolRounds':rounds,...}`, writes it to the DB (the one truth), AND that SAME dict ships as `vuMessage=vu_msg` on `AUTOPILOT_VU_DONE` (autopilot.py:1620). Empty `content` is a LEGITIMATE "keep going" VU reply; the `vu_result is None` bail (autopilot.py:1533/1583/1590) emits `VU_CANCEL` (removes bubble), NOT a `DONE` with empty content. So there is no path where DONE ships a wrongly-empty record — dropping the fallback exposes no hole.
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/streaming_render.js`, `autopilot_vu_done` branch).** Replaced `entry.msg.content = finalMsg.content || (buf && buf.content) || entry.msg.content || ""` + the two-branch toolRounds fallback with verbatim projection: `entry.msg.content = finalMsg.content || ""` and `entry.msg.toolRounds = Array.isArray(finalMsg.toolRounds) ? finalMsg.toolRounds : []`. (Root cause of the recent "stuck at Autopilot…" / `_isContentBearing` phase-hack saga — the frontend was inferring/reconstructing state the backend owns.)
- **Verification (actual output + biting byte-revert NC).** New `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_vu_verbatim.py` (2 tests) drives the REAL `_handleAutopilotVuEvent` under jsdom: vu_start → delta (fills buffer with STALE text) + tool_start (stale round) → vu_done carrying an authoritative record with `content=''`, `toolRounds=[]`. Asserts settled msg == backend record VERBATIM (empty content, zero rounds), NOT the stale buffer. Decoupled from `streaming_ui.js` (twUpdate stubbed no-op) since the verbatim logic is pure in-memory in `_handleAutopilotVuEvent`. **NC = genuine byte-revert:** rewrites the fix lines back to `|| (buf && buf.content) ||` into a temp copy and proves the same verbatim assertions FAIL against it (the empty backend content gets overwritten by stale buffer). **2 passed**; existing `test_frontend_autopilot_warmup.py` (3) + `test_frontend_typecheck.py` (3) still green = no regression. `node --check` clean; `streaming_render.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → server restart + hard-refresh, no bundler edit. Temp harness files cleaned up.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The `||` fallback only DIVERGES when the backend record's field is FALSY — precisely the legitimately-empty case — so it silently substitutes stale local state exactly when correctness matters most, and a stuck bubble becomes impossible to diagnose from one place. Settled render reads ONE record verbatim; empty-when-shouldn't-be is a backend bug fixed at source, never papered over frontend-side.


### 2026-07-02 — Project Brain gains a SIXTH pillar: cross-conversation COMMUNICATION + INTERVENTION (agent-initiated peer messaging + live peer status + advisory/gated intervention) — closes "it's not a unified brain, conversations can't talk to or intervene in each other"
- **Owner diagnosis (verified, then "stop asking, build it").** The five existing pillars (feed/charter/board/presence/dispatch) give shared PERCEPTION but it's ambient/past-tense, and the ONLY conversation→conversation write path was `dispatch_epic`→`enqueue_message(KIND_WORKFLOW)` — one-way, engine-initiated. `abort_running_tasks_for_conv` (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py:274`) existed but was NOT exposed as a cross-conv tool. So: no agent-initiated communication, no intervention verb.
- **Built — new `lib/conversations/project_peer.py` (three project-scoped agent tools), advisory-first throughout:**
  1. **`project_peer_status(conv_id?)`** — READ-ONLY LIVE introspection. Pure `_join_peers` merges `presence.snapshot` (active peers + phase/file/statusLabel) ⋈ live task registry (`_live_task_by_conv` → current tool-round + status) ⋈ board `claims_by_conv` (which epic each advances). This is LIVE state, the complement to `get_conversation` (history). Caller's own conv excluded.
  2. **`project_message(to_conv_id, text)`** — agent-initiated peer messaging. NEW `message_queue.KIND_PEER_MSG` (priority **40**: after human `real`=10, before `workflow_step`=50) — dispatchable, seen on the target's **NEXT** turn, NEVER interrupts a live turn mid-stream. Mirrors ONE feed `note` stamped with the sender. Body is PLAIN advisory content (frames itself as a peer note, not a human instruction).
  3. **`project_intervene(to_conv_id, message?, hard_abort?)`** — advisory by DEFAULT (a high-priority peer note routed through the same rate-limited messaging seam). A genuine hard abort (`abort_running_tasks_for_conv`) is SEPARATE + AUDIT-GATED: `_authorize_hard_abort` refuses without a non-empty `approved_by`; on the agent surface the token must come from `cfg['interventionApprovedBy']` (human-set), else the request degrades to a guided refusal. Emits `audit_log('intervention', approved_by=...)`; aborts the TASK only, never the host/process.
- **Loop/storm guard (owner hard constraint — A→B→A auto-amplification must be IMPOSSIBLE, proven).** (a) Per-ordered-(sender,target) sliding-window rate limit — `_prune_and_check`, cap `_PEER_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW=3` / `_PEER_MSG_WINDOW_S=120s`; total per-window traffic bounded by `N·(N-1)·cap` by construction. (b) No self-send. (c) **No auto-relay** — a received peer message is plain turn content that invokes NO send path; the only way to send is an explicit model tool call. In-memory `_peer_msg_history` under `_rate_lock`, pruned every check (bounded).
- **DRY (per owner "reuse the join, don't hand-roll a 2nd aggregation").** Extracted pure `project_board.claims_by_conv(board_tasks)` — the single source of the claim→conv join — and refactored `build_brain_summary` to consume it too, so the collab-bar and peer-status views can never drift.
- **Wiring (no phantom-tool trap).** `PEER_TOOLS`/`PEER_TOOL_NAMES` in `lib/tools/conversation.py`; registered in `registry._build_conv_ref`'s project block (same `project_enabled and project_path` gate as board/charter) + added to the `conv_ref` ToolSpec `provides` (also backfilled the pre-existing charter/board names that were missing from `provides`) + handler `_handle_peer_tool` in `handlers/misc.py`; `project_peer_status` added to the idempotent set. Smoke-verified all three resolve via `tool_registry.lookup`.
- **Tests (`tests/test_project_peer.py`, 17 pass) + 3 byte-reverting NC bites PROVEN FUNCTIONALLY (not just the NC-asserting-broken test passing).** Pure cores over DB harnesses; messaging/intervention paths monkeypatch `enqueue_message`/`emit_project_event`/`abort_running_tasks_for_conv` so the suite is DB-free (bare-CI `no such table: conversations` is the known bootstrap artifact, does NOT gate). **NC-STORM:** remove the rate cap in `_prune_and_check` → `test_rate_limit_storm_guard` FAILS (4th message goes through). **NC-GATE:** remove the approval check in `_authorize_hard_abort` → `test_intervene_hard_abort_refused_without_approval` FAILS (unapproved abort runs). **NC-JOIN:** remove the `exclude_conv` filter in `_join_peers` → `test_join_peers_excludes_self` FAILS (self leaks). Each restored byte-identical (md5 confirmed). Regression: board+brain_summary+message_queue+dispatch+brain_integration+live_paths = **38 pass**; `py_compile` clean on all 8 touched modules.
- **Design-first discipline (§10).** Posted the epic to the Board (marked DONE) + a Charter proposal recording the four committed invariants (KIND_PEER_MSG distinct from workflow; next-turn-never-mid-stream; structural storm guard + no-auto-relay; advisory-first with audit-gated hard-abort; reuse claims_by_conv) for human commit. Owner pre-authorized implementation this turn.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "unified brain" needs bidirectional AGENT-initiated communication, not just shared read surfaces + one-way engine dispatch. When adding a conversation→conversation write path: (1) use a DEDICATED queue kind so it's distinguishable from engine dispatch; (2) make it next-turn (never mid-stream) so it can't corrupt a live turn; (3) make the anti-storm property STRUCTURAL (rate limit + no-auto-relay), not a convention; (4) keep it advisory — only an audited, human-approved action may be coercive, and it must touch the task only.


### 2026-07-02 — Reading Mode: Report/Review no longer AUTO-GENERATE on tab open — a manual "Generate" prompt now gates fresh runs so the user can tune model/language/venue first
- **Owner ask (user preference).** In Reading Mode, opening the Report/Review page must NOT immediately start generating — otherwise the settings (model, generation language, target venue) can't be adjusted before the run begins. Let the user click to generate manually.
- **Root cause (`static/js/paper-reader.js::_loadOrGenerateReport`).** The function has a 4-step ladder run on every Report/Review tab open (via `_switchPaperTab`): (1) resume a locally-polling stream, (1.5) honour a pending regenerate intent, (2) reconnect to a running server-side task, (3) paint a DB cache hit, (4) **else start a brand-new generation**. Step 4 called `_generatePaperReport(false, view)` unconditionally, so navigating to the tab fired a fresh run before any setting could be touched. The venue-switch (`_loadOrGenerateReview`, l4136) and report-language-switch (l255) paths route through the same function, so they auto-fired too.
- **Fix (gate ONLY step 4; steps 1–3 preserved).** Step 4 now calls a new `_renderReportStartPrompt(view)` instead of auto-starting. It renders the empty-state copy + an accent "Generate" button wired to `_generatePaperReport()` / `_generatePaperReview()` (a user click). Everything that resumes/reconnects/cache-hits is UNCHANGED — an already-generated or in-flight report still displays instantly on tab open (that is not a fresh generation). Both `_generatePaperReport` and `_regeneratePaperReport` already only fire from explicit clicks. Confirmed NO residual background pre-generation on the upload/arxiv-fetch path (the historically-existing `_preGenerateReport`-style silent stream is gone; all generation now funnels through the gated `_loadOrGenerateReport` or an explicit button).
- **Supporting edits.** `static/js/i18n.js`: reworded `paper.reportEmptyTitle`/`reportEmptyHint`/`reviewEmptyTitle` (they said "switch to this tab to generate", implying auto-gen) + added `paper.reportGenerate`/`paper.reviewGenerate` button labels (EN+ZH parity). `index.html`: both Report + Review static empty states now carry the Generate button + manual-start copy (so the first pre-JS paint is consistent). `static/styles.css`: new `.paper-report-generate-btn` (accent-filled, soft glow, hover lift) beside `.paper-report-empty`.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on `paper-reader.js` + `i18n.js`; both confirmed in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (change ships in the content-hashed bundle → server restart + hard-refresh). `styles.css` served directly (hard-refresh only). CSS braces balanced (6284/6284).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Report/Review generation is expensive + setting-dependent (model / gen-language / venue scorecard), so it must be USER-INITIATED. When gating auto-start, cut ONLY the "start a new task" branch of `_loadOrGenerateReport` — the resume-running-task / reconnect / DB-cache-hit branches must stay automatic, else a returning user loses instant display of work already done.


### 2026-07-02 — Autopilot VU bubble: a PHASE-ONLY first frame (rate-limit stall) now lazily stands up the bubble — closes the "stuck at `Autopilot…`" gap on reconnect/late-connect
- **Context.** Owner flagged a finished bubble stuck at `● Autopilot…` (screenshot, conv `mr286f1h3mx1mi`). First established (evidence-first, via `task_events`) that this is NOT a missing-renderer/duplicate-code bug: task `de2b62f4` (status=`running`) emitted 6 `phase` frames — `llm_thinking` → `waiting_model` → `retrying/限流中` → `tool_exec` (events 2754–2756, first delta 2757) — all wrapped as `autopilot_vu_event` and routed through the SAME `updateStreamingUI` phase path the agent uses; app.log showed the task alive at 14:33 (Round 2 waited `elapsed=78.5s` on a rate-limited `claude-opus-4.8`). So the `Autopilot…` was the warm-up placeholder during a first-token stall. Same family as `flow-autopilot-perceived-hang-is-subagent-logging-blindspot` + the `autopilot-mode` warm-up parity note.
- **The real latent gap (owner-directed, worth fixing because it reproduces the EXACT symptom).** The rate-limit stall emits phase-only frames for tens of seconds before any delta. `_handleAutopilotVuEvent`'s lazy-creation fallback (fires when an `autopilot_vu_event` arrives WITHOUT a preceding `autopilot_vu_start` — reconnect / late-connect / dropped start frame) treated only `tool_start` + `delta(content|thinking)` as content-bearing. A replay cursor landing AFTER `vu_start` but inside the phase-only window saw only `phase` frames → every one dropped (`if (!_isContentBearing) return`) → the VU bubble never materialized → the user stared at a dead warm-up state during precisely the window where the phase chip is the ONLY liveness signal. Not narrow, since rate-limiting is the common case.
- **Fix (`static/js/ui/streaming_render.js`, 1 line + comment).** Added `(itype === "phase")` to `_isContentBearing`, so a phase-only first frame lazily stands up the bubble; the existing `phase` branch then sets `buf.phase` + flushes. Non-rendered interactive inner types (`stdin_request`/`write_approval_request`/`human_guidance_*`) still do NOT create the bubble — the VU IS the user, it hosts no widgets.
- **Verification (actual output + byte-revert NC).** Extended `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_warmup.py` (+2 tests, +2nd harness). `test_autopilot_phase_only_frame_lazily_creates_bubble` drives the REAL `_handleAutopilotVuEvent` under a FAITHFUL SYNCHRONOUS substrate (`twStart`/`twUpdate`/`twStop` mirror `health_stream_timer.js` minus rAF batching, so deterministic) with a phase-only `retrying` frame (`⏳ …限流中…`) + NO `vu_start`; asserts bubble created + `#streaming-msg` in DOM + `stream-phase-retrying` chip + `限流中` detail. `test_nc_old_guard_drops_phase_only_frame` shims the OLD guard to prove the assertions discriminate. **Suite = 3 passed** (incl. the pre-existing warm-up test). **NC BITES on the source (byte-revert):** removing `(itype === "phase")` → the real-function test FAILs all 4 assertions (`bubble_created` / `streaming_msg_in_dom` / `retry_chip_rendered` / `rate_limit_detail_shown`) while `precondition_no_bubble` stays PASS (harness sound); `cp`-restore → md5 `50fd64e4…` identical. `node --check` clean. `streaming_render.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` — server restart + hard-refresh only, no bundler edit.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For the autopilot VU bubble, "content-bearing" for the lazy-create decision MUST include `phase` — during a rate-limit first-token stall the phase chip is the only frame that arrives for tens of seconds, so dropping it on a reconnect is exactly what produces a permanent-looking `Autopilot…`. Keep the non-rendered widget-request types excluded (the VU hosts no interactive widgets). The stall itself is model capacity/quota — the fix makes the liveness signal VISIBLE on reconnect, it does not (and should not) shorten the wait.

### 2026-07-02 — Autopilot didn't resume after a server crash mid-VU-call → startup recovery now re-kicks any conv still carrying an armed marker
- **Owner report.** Conv `mr2umxurvdbbeg` finished its reply but Autopilot showed "待接管（当前回复结束后）" and never took over — "明明生成完了，autopilot 为什么不接？"
- **Root cause (evidence-first, from logs).** The finished bubble was follow-up task `3e0cd4b0` (16 rounds, M-TraceId `b26d3706…`). At **11:50:58** it finished `finish_reason=stop`; at **11:50:59** the end-of-turn hook `maybe_run_autopilot` fired and DID spawn the VU sub-task `fa26d181` (which began building its first LLM request at 11:51:02). Then the whole server went **silent at 11:52:44** and **`server.boot` at 14:06:47** — the process was killed/restarted ~2h15m later WHILE the VU call was in flight. Because `maybe_run_autopilot` runs synchronously BEFORE the parent's `done` event, the crash meant: no VU reply persisted, no follow-up spawned, and **no `done` baton** (confirmed: `3e0cd4b0` has NO `■ DONE` line; the last one is the prior task `6dd1fd5a`). On restart `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` restored the interrupted reply (`Marking stale task 3e0cd4b0 … Recovered conv=mr2umxur`) — which is why the bubble looks complete + green — but recovery had **NO autopilot-resume path**, so the run was left settled-but-armed (the `autopilot_armed` marker from 02:00:05Z was still persisted → the "待接管" chip). It would only continue on the next manual send / empty-Enter kick.
- **Fix (additive, 3 files).** (1) `lib/message_queue.py::get_autopilot_marker_config(conv_id)` — reads the send `config` (model/tools/searchMode) stored on the armed-marker row. (2) `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py::resume_armed_autopilot_after_crash(conv_ids)` — for each crash-recovered conv that STILL has `has_autopilot_marker`, re-kick via `kick_autopilot(conv_id, marker_cfg)` (the same idle empty-Enter machinery); un-armed convs (clean `[VU: TASK_DONE]` / disarmed → marker cleared) are left alone; `kick_autopilot` self-refuses if a live non-VU task is already running (no double-drive); best-effort per conv (one failure never aborts the batch). (3) `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` now collects `recovered_conv_ids` and, AFTER the commit (so the carrier sees merged messages), calls the resume helper. Lazy import at the call site (no module-load cycle).
- **Verification.** New `tests/test_autopilot_resume_after_crash.py` (6, pure-unit, all DB/kick mocked): only-armed-convs-resume, reuses-marker-config, empty-input-noop, kick-refusal-not-counted, one-conv-failure-doesn't-abort-batch, + an NC-bite that neuters the `has_autopilot_marker` gate and proves an un-armed conv is then wrongly resumed (the gate is the load-bearing check). 6 passed; `test_autopilot_kick.py` 8/8 (non-api). `py_compile` clean on all 3 edited modules. NOTE: `test_autopilot_arm.py` + `test_message_queue.py` fail in THIS shell with `sqlite3 no such table: message_queue/conversations` — a pre-existing bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact (`warmup_db` itself errors with no-such-table here), NOT caused by this change (my edits don't touch the arm path; the resume test mocks the DB entirely).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** `maybe_run_autopilot` runs synchronously before the `done` baton, so a crash mid-VU-call strands the loop: the parent reply is recoverable but the loop is not, unless startup explicitly resumes it. Any end-of-turn hook that owns loop continuation must have a restart-resume counterpart keyed on a DURABLE marker (here the armed-marker queue row), because in-flight task state does not survive a restart.
- **Follow-up (owner review — close the "armed-but-idle" reachable gap; make the marker the AUTHORITATIVE resume source).** The first cut gated resume on `recovered_conv_ids` (a proxy for "had an in-flight/interrupted task at crash"). That covered the exact incident but MISSED a reachable state the same guardrail warns about: a conv carrying an armed marker but with NO running/interrupted task at crash (armed-from-idle whose carrier never spawned, or the marker persisted while the conv sat settled) is absent from `recovered_conv_ids` → never re-kicked → silently stranded — the very failure class. Reworked to scope resume off the DURABLE markers themselves, not off recovery: (1) new `lib/message_queue.py::list_armed_autopilot_convs()` — one `SELECT DISTINCT conv_id … WHERE kind='autopilot'` returning every armed conv (survives restart). (2) `resume_armed_autopilot_after_crash(extra_conv_ids=None)` now enumerates `list_armed_autopilot_convs()` as the authoritative candidate set, unions `extra_conv_ids` (the recovery set) only for logging symmetry, and re-gates each via `has_autopilot_marker`; `kick_autopilot` self-refuses on a live non-VU task, so calling unconditionally is safe. (3) `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` now calls it **UNCONDITIONALLY** (was gated on `if recovered_conv_ids:` — which would skip an armed-but-idle-only boot). Confirmed the startup ordering is safe: this runs in `server.py::_init_database` right alongside `rehydrate_swarms_on_startup`, which ALSO spawns background agent tasks at boot — so spawning a resume carrier here is the established pattern, and VU events buffer on the task for late-connect/poll replay (no event-loop-readiness wedge beyond what swarm rehydration already accepts).
- **Verification (updated).** `tests/test_autopilot_resume_after_crash.py` reworked to 8 pure-unit tests (marker scan + kick mocked): only-armed-resume, **armed-but-idle-conv-resumes-even-when-not-recovered** (the gap), resumes-with-no-recovered-ids-at-all, reuses-marker-config, no-markers-noop, kick-refusal-not-counted, one-failure-doesn't-abort, + an NC-bite `test_NC_recovered_only_gating_misses_armed_idle` proving the old recovered-only gate strands the armed-idle conv while the real marker-scan helper resumes it. 8 passed; `test_autopilot_kick.py` 8/8. **NC BITES on the source (byte-revert):** patching the helper's `candidates = armed | {…}` back to recovered-only (`candidates = {c for c in extra_conv_ids …}`) → exactly the two armed-but-idle tests FAIL; `cp`-restore → md5 `72e276e2…`, 8/8 green. `py_compile` clean on all 3 modules.
- **Guardrail / lesson (extended).** "Resume must be keyed on the DURABLE marker" means the marker SCAN is the source of truth, not any proxy set (recovered tasks / active-task-id). A resume that iterates the recovery set will always miss the armed-but-idle conv. Enumerate the markers, re-gate each, call the idempotent kick unconditionally — and call the resume UNCONDITIONALLY at boot (an armed-but-idle-only restart has an empty recovery set but still needs resuming).


### 2026-07-02 — Install white-screen, ACTUAL root cause (DISTINCT class from the 2026-07-01 corrupt-source fix): the OPENSOURCE EXPORT SANITIZER rewrote a JS identifier into a hyphenated bareword key (`meituan:` → `your-provider:`) → `Unexpected token '-'`. Fixed the replacement token to a valid identifier + added an export-time `node --check` safety net that fails the build loudly.
- **Owner evidence (reviewer screenshot of the OLD broken `bundle-7c314a3b.js:42772`).** `:42772` was a LINE number, not a byte offset. The failing line was `your-provider: '<svg …>'` — a JS object key with a hyphen but no quotes, which the parser reads as subtraction (`your - provider`) → `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '-'`, white-screening the whole app. NOT the corrupt-source/merge-conflict/NUL class guarded by `tests/test_bundle_corruption_guard.py` (2026-07-01) — the source is perfectly valid; the EXPORT sanitizer CORRUPTS it on the way out.
- **Root cause (`export.py::_sanitize_source_opensource`).** For opensource builds it did a blind `content.replace('meituan', 'your-provider')` on every non-brand-asset file. Brand registries carry `meituan` as an UNQUOTED object key: `static/js/settings/branding.js` (`meituan: '<svg…>'` at l26, `meituan: '#FFC300'` at l44) and `static/js/settings/visibility_defaults.js` (`meituan:'Meituan'` at l74+l173). The rewrite turned each into `your-provider:` = invalid JS. The `_is_brand_asset` allowlist only exempted paths ending in `settings.js`/`main.js`/`.css` — the 2026-05-28 settings.js monolith split ORPHANED the brand registries into `settings/*.js`, drifting the list. The targeted `meituan:'Meituan'`→`default:'Default'` fixes (steps 11) only ever covered `settings.js`+`main.js`, so the split's children fell through to the blind hyphen rewrite.
- **Fix — two layers (owner-directed; NOT the fragile "add two more filenames to the allowlist" trap, which just resets the drift for the next refactor).**
  1. **Class fix (file-agnostic):** the replacement token is now a VALID JS identifier — `content.replace('meituan', 'yourprovider')` (display token `YourProvider` was already valid, unchanged). `yourprovider` is a safe bareword key wherever `meituan` was, so exported JS parses regardless of which file carries the key. Confirmed the only identifier-position hazard was `meituan`: every other hyphenated replacement token (`sankuai`→`example-corp`, `三快`→`your-corp`, `M-TransferContext-INF-CELL`/`gray-release-ai-gpt-test` header tokens, `.sankuai.com` domains) lands ONLY inside quoted strings / regex literals / JSON values / CSS — never a bareword JS identifier (swept the whole tree).
  2. **Safety net (makes "others stop hitting this" durable):** new `export.py::_verify_exported_js_syntax(dest)` runs `node --check` over every exported `static/js/**/*.js` (best-effort; no-op when node absent, mirroring `lib/js_bundler._node_syntax_ok`). Any file that fails to parse → raise `ExportSyntaxError` and FAIL the export loudly (before push). Wired into the non-dry-run path for BOTH `internal` and `opensource` modes (both sanitize JS). Catches ANY future find-replace regression at BUILD time, not on a user's fresh install.
- **Verification (actual output + two biting NCs, byte-reverting).** New `tests/test_export_js_sanitize_syntax.py` (6 tests): runs the REAL `_sanitize_source_opensource` over the REAL repo `branding.js` + `visibility_defaults.js` and asserts each output `node --check`s clean; a tree-wide sweep of EVERY `static/js` file with an unquoted `meituan:` key (file-agnostic — catches a newly-orphaned file, asserts swept≥2); a minimal-object-literal class assertion (`your-provider` never emitted); + the safety-net raise/pass pair. **All 6 pass** (node present). **NC #1** (revert class fix → `your-provider`): the 4 content tests FAIL with the EXACT production error — `branding.js:26 your-provider: '<svg…` → `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '-'`; the 2 safety-net tests (own synthetic JS) stay green; restore → byte-identical. **NC #2** (neuter the safety net to early-return, never raise): `test_verify_exported_js_syntax_raises_on_broken` FAILS; restore → byte-identical. Both suites together = **18 passed** (6 sanitize + 12 corruption-guard). `py_compile` clean; the 6 `ruff` "errors" are PRE-EXISTING nested-backslash-in-f-string warnings on untouched print lines (2076/2106/2109…) under ruff's 3.10 target — not in my inserted code. Confirmed real sanitized output: both files emit `yourprovider:` with zero raw `meituan` left.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** (1) A sanitizer that rewrites tokens in CODE must never turn an identifier into a non-identifier — the replacement token has to be a valid JS identifier wherever the original could sit as a bareword key. A hyphen is illegal in an unquoted key. (2) Do NOT gate correctness on a per-file allowlist — it drifts on every refactor (the settings.js split silently orphaned the brand registries here, exactly as it earlier orphaned them from the `_BUNDLE_FILES` critical set). Prefer a file-agnostic transform + an output validator. (3) This is a DISTINCT failure class from the 2026-07-01 corrupt-source bug: that one is conflict-markers/NUL in an otherwise-healthy install (caught by `_scan_source_corruption`); THIS one is a valid source corrupted by the export find-replace (caught by the class fix + `_verify_exported_js_syntax`). The bundler's `_node_syntax_ok` would refuse to SERVE the broken bundle on a node-equipped machine, but the common no-node fresh install ships it silently — so the fix must be at EXPORT time.

### 2026-07-02 — Project Brain panel: root-caused the "truncated text" (a STORAGE cap, not a CSS clamp) + full visual redesign of the panel/columns/influence-lens
- **Owner report (screenshot).** The 项目大脑 (Project Brain) overlay showed board epics cut mid-word with NO ellipsis ("…for a cl", "…falsely reported `i", "…hard ceiling, no"), and asked (1) don't omit the inner text, (2) the whole panel looks ugly — redesign it.
- **Issue 1 root cause (evidence-first, NOT a rendering bug).** A mid-word cut with no ellipsis is the signature of a raw `str[:N]` slice, not a CSS line-clamp. Traced it to the DATA layer: `post_task` (`lib/conversations/project_board.py`) hard-sliced every epic title to `_TITLE_MAX_CHARS = 280` AT STORAGE TIME — the clipped string was then shown in the panel AND injected into the prompt board block (`render_board_block`). The display CSS already wrapped fully (`word-break:break-word`, no `-webkit-line-clamp`), so the text was lost before it ever reached the browser; no frontend change could recover it. **Fix:** raised `_TITLE_MAX_CHARS` → 2000 (epics carry multi-sentence design descriptions). Already-stored epics stay clipped (historical data); new/edited epics keep full text + wrap. No test pinned the 280 value.
- **Issue 2 — full CSS redesign** (`static/styles.css`, the entire Project Brain block, ~110 lines). Kept EVERY class name load-bearing for `project-brain.js`. Highlights: scoped local design tokens via `color-mix`; brand accent hairline down the panel's leading edge; tinted gradient head; per-column status dots (Charter=accent / Board=green / Activity=amber) on sticky tinted heads; layered elevation cards with color-coded left stripes (open=amber/claimed=accent/done=green), lift-on-hover + one-shot fade-in (NO pulsing, per preference); board lane counts as color-coded pill badges; amber inset-stripe proposals; richer influence-lens chips + group-head dots; dashed quiet empty states; `overflow-wrap:anywhere` everywhere so long epics wrap instead of clip; a `max-width:720px` responsive fallback stacking the 3 columns.
- **Verification.** `py_compile` clean; `tests/test_project_board.py` = 21 passed; CSS braces balanced (6280/6280). `styles.css` is served directly (not bundled) — hard-refresh only, no rebuild.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** "Truncated text with no ellipsis" in a panel is almost always an upstream DATA cap, not a CSS clamp — grep the producer (`[:N]` slices, `TITLE_MAX`) before touching styles. A cap that feeds BOTH a UI surface and a prompt block silently degrades both.


### 2026-07-02 — Turn-level AUTO-RETRY: a settled turn that failed with a TRANSIENT error now re-runs itself transparently (no manual Retry click) — new self-heal layer above the inner per-round budgets
- **Owner ask.** "Recently many conversations stop due to various errors. Users fire many conversations at once; we should avoid requiring user intervention (auto-retry / auto-fix)." Evidence-first: histogrammed `logs/error.log` — the real user-facing terminal failures are `500`/`429`/`503`, `SSE error:` (incl. the now-fixed image-MIME 400), premature/abnormal stream close, and `no_slot`/`timeout`/`network`. (The `no such table: conversations` spam is the known bare-CI bootstrap artifact, not a live failure.)
- **Gap (confirmed, not guessed).** Tofu already has DEEP intra-turn resilience: SSE anomaly retries ×16 (`stream_handler.analyse_stream_result`), `_llm_call_with_fallback` model-swap, `PromptTooLongError`→reactive compaction, MCP auto-reconnect. And every terminal error is a TYPED envelope carrying `retryable` (`lib/error_envelope.py::_RETRYABLE_KINDS`). BUT once a turn *settled* to `status='error'` — even with a `retryable=True` kind — the conversation just stopped and waited for a manual Retry click. With many parallel convs, any single transient blip stranded one, forcing babysitting. There was NO turn-level auto-retry.
- **Design (pure verdict + orchestrator seam).** New `lib/tasks_pkg/turn_retry.py`: pure, unit-testable `should_auto_retry_turn(envelope, attempt, cfg) -> (retry, backoff_s)`. Eligible kinds = a STRICT subset of retryable (`ratelimit`/`no_slot`/`timeout`/`network`/`endpoint_unreachable`/`premature_close`/`abnormal_stop`/`server_offline`/`tool_timeout`) — all fire at the stream/dispatch boundary, so a fresh run has a real chance AND cannot double-execute a committed tool. Persistent kinds (`quota`/`permission`/`content_filter`/`invalid_image`/`prompt_too_long`/`model_limit`/`internal`/`dispatch_exhausted`) are NEVER auto-retried (a re-run just re-fails + wastes tokens). Bounded: `_AUTO_TURN_RETRY_MAX=3`, exponential backoff 3→6→12s cap 30 + jitter (fleet de-sync), abort-interruptible. Opt-out: `cfg['disableAutoTurnRetry']` (hard off) / `cfg['autoTurnRetryMax']` (numeric, 0=off) — mirrors `disableModelFallback` for headless benchmarks.
- **Seam (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`).** New `_maybe_auto_retry_turn(task, cfg)` called at BOTH terminal exits for non-endpoint, non-aborted tasks: (a) top of `_finalize_and_emit_done` (the error-break path) and (b) the FATAL `except` (the raise path — a first-round 429 with no fallback raises past finalize, so it needed its own guard). When it fires: emits `retry_reset` (new event) + `phase:retrying`, backs off, RESTORES the pristine turn input, resets per-turn accumulators (content/thinking/error/status/toolRounds + inner-retry counters) to a clean `running`, and re-invokes `run_task`. Only the FINAL (successful or budget-exhausted) attempt emits the terminal `done` — the retry chain produces exactly ONE done.
- **Pristine-input restore is the crux (root-caused via sub-agent).** `run_task` does `messages = list(task['messages'])` (LOCAL copy), injects system context into it, appends completed tool rounds, and writes the whole thing back to `task['messages']` at the END (even on error-break). So a naive re-run would DOUBLE-inject system blocks + replay a half-finished round. Fix: snapshot `task['_turn_input_messages']` ONCE at `run_task` entry (non-endpoint only; preserved across attempts) and restore it before each re-run — i.e. re-run from the ORIGINAL input, exactly the semantics of a manual Retry. In-memory only (`persist_task_result` writes explicit columns, never the raw task dict).
- **Frontend (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js` + event registry).** Sub-agent proved the live bubble APPENDS content deltas and the JS model value resets ONLY on a state snapshot (never mid-stream) — so re-streaming without a reset would STACK old+new text. New non-terminal `retry_reset` event (registered in `lib/agent_core/events.py` with an `EventSpec`, so `test_event_registry.py` drift passes) clears `assistantMsg.content/thinking/toolRounds` (+ endpoint-critic variant, keeping Continue checkpoint rounds) so the re-run renders clean. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-d628b83f.js`, contains handler).
- **Verification (actual + biting NC + byte-revert).** New `tests/test_turn_auto_retry.py` (12): pure verdict (retryable-within-budget / persistent-never / budget-exhaustion / opt-out / cfg-cap / non-dict / backoff-monotonic) + seam tests driving the REAL `_maybe_auto_retry_turn` with `run_task` monkeypatched to a spy (retries+reinvokes, restores-pristine, non-retryable-finalizes, abort-during-backoff, budget-exhausted). **NC PROVEN (byte-reverting):** (1) neuter the pristine restore → `test_seam_restores_pristine_input_on_retry` FAILS; (2) add `'quota'` to `_AUTO_RETRY_KINDS` → `test_persistent_kinds_never_retry` FAILS; both `cp`-restored → md5 identical. `test_event_registry` 5/5 + `test_zero_byte_round0_retry` 6/6 unchanged = 23 passed; orchestrator imports clean; ruff clean; bundle node-checks.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A turn-level retry must (a) re-run from the PRISTINE input, never the write-back (which carries injected system context + partial rounds), (b) only fire for kinds that fail at the stream/dispatch boundary (so no committed tool double-executes — verified prior tool results live in `task['messages']` as history), (c) guard BOTH the error-break AND the raise/FATAL exit (a first-round 429 raises past finalize), and (d) emit an explicit client reset (`retry_reset`) because the live bubble appends deltas and only resets on a state snapshot. It sits ABOVE the inner per-round budgets and composes with them; endpoint mode is excluded (its Planner→Worker→Critic loop owns its own replan semantics).


### 2026-07-02 — Review Mode prompt re-tuned to READ like a human reviewer: Weaknesses now "precise, not numerous" (hunt real problems / hidden flaws), Summary & Strengths de-forensicized
- **Owner ask (ML researcher, ICLR/NeurIPS/CVPR/ACL reviewer).** Review Mode's weaknesses should be PRECISE not numerous — strive to surface the real pain points (真问题) and hidden flaws. And the Summary + Strengths were written "far too specifically — a human reviewer would not phrase them this way"; put ourselves in a human reviewer's shoes.
- **Root cause (`lib/paper/review.py`, both EN + ZH prompt templates).** The old anti-slop rule `"Every strength and every weakness MUST be anchored to concrete evidence — a specific table/figure/§/number"` applied the SAME forensic microscope to all three sections. Result: Summary read like a spec sheet (mandatory number+benchmark+comparison-point), Strengths bolted a table/§ citation onto every clause, and Weaknesses was quota-driven ("4–8 bullet points") which rewards padding with cosmetic nitpicks over finding the one decisive flaw.
- **Fix (per-section discipline, not one-size-fits-all).**
  - New top anti-slop rule: **"Write like a human reviewer, not a report generator"** — Summary/Strengths in the reviewer's own words at a natural abstraction; save the microscope for Weaknesses.
  - **Weaknesses rule rewritten**: "precise, not numerous — find the REAL problems and the hidden flaws." Typically 2–4 decisive, decision-bearing weaknesses (unsound claim / unfair-or-under-tuned baseline / unruled-out confound / claim-vs-shown gap / the one missing ablation the central claim rests on). Explicit ban on padding to a quota with typos / "more datasets would be nice" / "writing could be clearer"; rank by decision-impact and cut the long tail; encouraged to name a flaw the authors themselves missed. The **anchoring** HARD constraint was RESCOPED to Weaknesses only ("A weakness with no anchor is deleted") — that's where per-clause specificity earns its keep.
  - **Summary** section body: "neutral 3–5 sentence paraphrase in YOUR OWN words … you do NOT need to pack in exact numbers/benchmark names/deltas here — a high-level characterization is what a real Summary looks like."
  - **Strengths**: 3–6 → **2–4** bullets "in a reviewer's natural voice … be honest rather than exhaustive: if the paper has one real strength, list one … Do NOT bolt a table/figure/§ citation onto every strength … Do NOT manufacture strengths to look balanced."
  - **Weaknesses** section body: "quality and precision over quantity (typically 2–4) … Prefer one deeply-argued deal-breaker over five shallow observations."
  - ZH template edited in lockstep (EN+ZH parity): 像人类审稿人一样写 / 缺点宁精勿多 / 概述用你自己的话 / 优点 2–4 条不求全不硬造 / 缺点质量与精度高于数量.
- **Preserved (so existing assertions + intent hold).** The exact anti-slop trigger phrases the tests key on ("anchored to concrete evidence", "summarize the paper once", "significantly improves"/"banned phrases", "actionable", "rating and confidence must be justified", "fetch_url"+"not proof"; ZH 禁止注水/锚定/fetch_url) were kept verbatim — the reproducibility + novelty-verification discipline and the venue scorecards are untouched.
- **Verification.** `tests/test_paper_review_mode.py` 12→13: added `test_review_prompt_human_reviewer_voice_and_precise_weaknesses` asserting the new framing (EN "write like a human reviewer" / "your own words" / "do not need to pack in exact numbers" / "precise, not numerous" / "quality and precision over quantity" / hidden-flaw clause / "a weakness with no anchor is deleted"; ZH 像人类审稿人一样写 / 用你自己的话 / 宁精勿多 / 真问题). All 13 pass; `py_compile` clean on review.py + the test. NC: the two decisive phrases ("write like a human reviewer", "precise, not numerous") are strings authored this turn — absent from the prior version by construction — so the new test cannot pass against the old prompt. No engine/route/cache-key/scorecard change; this is a pure prompt-wording tuning.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A peer-review prompt must not apply one uniform "cite a number for every clause" rule across Summary/Strengths/Weaknesses — that produces a forensic-audit voice no human reviewer uses. Scope the microscope to Weaknesses (where anchored evidence is the whole point), let Summary/Strengths breathe in the reviewer's own words, and make the Weaknesses instruction reward a small set of decisive/hidden flaws over a padded quota.


### 2026-07-02 — Sidebar gains a second settled-state flag: INCOMPLETE / interrupted (amber), complementing the just-added ERROR (red) — "if a turn didn't finish, alert the user"
- **Owner ask (follow-up to the error dot).** "There should also be a prompt for interruptions — in short, if it's not completed, the user needs to be prompted to pay attention to it."
- **Design — three settled buckets, reusing the authoritative finishReason vocabulary from `finish_info.js`.** `_convStatusFlags` (`static/js/ui/conversation_list.js`) now computes `errored` AND `incomplete` in one tail scan of the latest assistant turn (guarded by `!streaming`, so a live turn never flags):
  - **errored (red)** — `msg.error` OR an ERR-tier `finishReason` (`error` / `server_offline`). (Folds the hard-failure finishReasons into the error bucket added last turn.)
  - **incomplete (amber)** — a `finishReason` that is neither NORMAL (`stop`/`end_turn`/`stop_sequence`/`tool_use`/`tool_calls`) nor ERR: `aborted`, `interrupted`, `length`/`max_tokens`, `tool_rounds_exhausted`, `content_filter`, `premature_close`, `abnormal_stop`, … — i.e. "stopped without finishing, not a hard error". ALSO trips when an idle turn has NO finishReason and NO output at all (bare placeholder = a dangling generation from a crash/restart before any tokens landed).
  - **normal** — clean finishReason, or (legacy turns) no finishReason but real content → no flag.
  - `errored` wins over `incomplete` when both could apply.
- **Tier lists** live in two module-level `Set`s (`_FINISH_NORMAL`, `_FINISH_ERR`) mirroring `finish_info.js`; everything not in either set that carries a finishReason is treated as incomplete (open-ended, so a new abnormal reason is caught by default rather than silently NORMAL).
- **Wiring (same 3 paths as the error flag).** `_convStatusHtml` new `.conv-incomplete-dot` + `.conv-status-tag.conv-status-incomplete` branches (below `errored`); `_statusHash` extended with the flag; `_applyConvItemStatus` in-place selector gains `.conv-incomplete-dot`; JSDoc updated.
- **Visual.** Amber (`#f59e0b`) STATIC dot with soft glow + one-shot fade-in — same "settled, not in-progress" language as the red error dot, deliberately NOT the blinking amber of the awaiting-human LIVE dot. Tag `未完成 / Incomplete` on tinted amber. Tofu-theme square-badge dot variant added; tag inherits base color.
- **i18n.** `sidebar.incompleteTag` (未完成 / Incomplete) + `sidebar.incompleteState` (上次生成被中断，未正常完成 / "Last generation was interrupted and did not finish"). EN+ZH parity.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on `conversation_list.js` + `i18n.js`; both already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. `styles.css` served directly. Server restart + hard-refresh to pick up the new bundle.


### 2026-07-02 — macOS install.sh fix: log-tee redirect no longer hard-depends on GNU `stdbuf` / `sed -u` (was aborting the install, leaving an empty tofu dir)
- **Owner report (terminal screenshot).** Mac install failed; assistant self-diagnosed `stdbuf not found`, tofu dir left empty. "帮我解决下".
- **Root cause.** `install.sh:173` set up the transcript log via `exec > >(stdbuf -oL tee >(stdbuf -oL sed -u '…' >> LOG)) 2>&1`. Both `stdbuf` (GNU coreutils) and `sed -u` (GNU extension) are ABSENT on stock macOS/BSD. With `stdbuf` missing, the process-substitution readers die immediately (`stdbuf: command not found`); the terminal's stdout is now wired to a dead pipe, so subsequent build output is lost to SIGPIPE and the log file is created empty — the install collapses before fetching a single package. Reproduced with a coreutils-free PATH + a BSD-style sed shim: OLD form → `old.log` empty + `stdbuf: command not found` ×2.
- **Fix (`install.sh`, same redirect block).** Probe both tools and degrade gracefully: `_TOFU_STDBUF="stdbuf -oL"` only if `command -v stdbuf`; `_TOFU_SED_U="-u"` only if `echo x | sed -u '' ` actually succeeds (BSD sed rejects `-u`). The `exec` line interpolates the two (empty on macOS) so it becomes plain `tee >(sed '…' >> LOG)` — colours still stripped from the log, terminal still sees raw output, just without the (nice-to-have but non-portable) line-buffering. Linux with GNU coreutils is byte-equivalent to before (both vars populated).
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** `bash -n install.sh` clean. NC in a coreutils-free sandbox (symlinked minimal PATH, no `stdbuf`, sed shim that errors on `-u`): OLD form → empty log + `command not found`; NEW form → `PROGRESS_LINE` captured in log, colour escape stripped, empty stderr. Confirmed the GNU path (stdbuf present, `sed -u` accepted) still strips colour identically.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any `install.sh` shell that must run on a user's Mac cannot assume GNU coreutils: `stdbuf`, `sed -u`/`-r`, `readlink -f`, `date -d` are all GNU-only. Probe-and-degrade at the point of use; never let an optional convenience (line-buffering, ANSI stripping) sit on the critical `exec` redirect that every later line of output depends on.
- **Follow-up (owner asked for a full GNU-only audit + propagation path).** (1) **Propagation:** Mac users install via `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rangehow/ToFu/main/install.sh | bash` (README/README_CN/docs/INSTALL) — GitHub's raw CDN mirroring `main` of `github.com/rangehow/ToFu`, NOT this repo copy and NO build step (unlike the Windows `.exe`). The fix reaches Mac users ONLY after this `install.sh` is committed+pushed to `main` there (raw CDN cache ~5 min). (2) **Full sweep** (sub-agent + independent grep, whole 1622-line file). Real hits fixed: **`date -Iseconds`** (l194, BSD `date` has no `-I`; non-fatal inside `$()`-in-`echo` but cosmetic-broken log header) → `date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`; **`sort -V`** (l1113, absent on old BSD `sort`, on the bundled-`vendor/*.whl` path under `pipefail` → could abort) → `{ sort -V 2>/dev/null || sort; }`; **`mktemp -t <prefix.XXXXXX[.sh]>`** ×4 (l416/997/1303/1316) — BSD `-t` treats the arg as a PREFIX (no `XXXXXX` expansion) → switched to explicit path template `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/name.XXXXXX"`. **Self-caught bug:** my first mktemp fix appended `.sh` OUTSIDE the `$()` (`$(mktemp …).sh`) → the var pointed at a file mktemp never created (real file lacked `.sh`); since `TMP_INSTALLER` is only `curl -o`'d then `bash <file>`'d, the `.sh` is cosmetic — dropped it entirely (l416). Confirmed **clean (zero hits):** `grep -P`/`-oP`, `date -d`/`+%s%N`, `readlink -f`, `base64 -w`, `xargs -r`, `find -printf`, `nproc`/`sha256sum`/`md5sum`/`realpath`/`getopt`/`timeout` (curl `--max-time` / `pg_ctl -t` are unrelated), GNU `head`/`tail` long-opts, gawk-isms, `-z` NUL flags. Already-guarded (left as-is): `sed -i` has a `Darwin` `-i ''` branch (l1557); `sed -E`/`-r`-in-comment/`awk '{print $N}'`/`tr` ranges/`grep -oE`/`-qx` are all BSD-safe.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC, BSD-shimmed sandbox).** `bash -n` clean after all 7 edits. Shim PATH (fake `date` rejecting `-I`, fake `sort` rejecting `-V`): date fallback → `2026-07-02T06:16:16Z`; **sort NC BITES** — bare `sort -V | tail` under `set -eo pipefail` → `rc=1` (would abort), guarded form → `rc=0` picks a wheel; mktemp form creates a REAL existing file (`/tmp/miniforge.hkfABP`, `-f` true) whereas the broken `.sh`-appended form left `$F exists=` blank (proving the self-caught bug).


### 2026-07-02 — Sidebar now flags conversations whose final generation ended in ERROR (new settled-failure dot + tag, distinct from the in-flight states)
- **Owner ask.** "If the final generation status of a conversation is an error, there must be a prompt in the sidebar to alert the user. Make it look visually appealing."
- **Gap.** `_convStatusFlags` (`static/js/ui/conversation_list.js`) tracked four live states (streaming / translating / memory-prefetch / awaiting-human) → dot + tag, but had NO representation for a conv that finished with an error. A failed turn left the row visually identical to a successful one; the error was only visible after opening the conv (`msg.error` envelope rendered by `renderErrorEnvelope`).
- **Fix (one flag, threaded through all 3 render paths).** Added an `errored` flag: true iff the conv is NOT streaming AND its most-recent assistant message carries an `error` (envelope dict or legacy string, matching how `chat_render.js` gates on `msg.error`). It's the LOWEST priority state — a still-streaming conv shows the streaming dot, not the error one; only a settled turn counts. Wired into `_convStatusFlags` (return shape + JSDoc), `_convStatusHtml` (new `.conv-error-dot` + `.conv-status-tag.conv-status-error` branches), the `_statusHash` (so a turn flipping to/from error re-renders — the hash early-return would otherwise skip it), and the `_applyConvItemStatus` in-place dot-reconcile selector (added `.conv-error-dot` so the fast path can add/remove it without a full rebuild).
- **Visual design.** Settled failure ≠ in-progress, so the error dot is a STATIC red (`#ef4444`) with a soft glow and a one-shot fade-in — deliberately NOT pulsing/blinking like the live-state dots (streaming pulse / awaiting-human blink), which reads as "this is done, and it failed" rather than "something is happening". Tag `出错 / Error` in red-on-tinted-red (`rgba(239,68,68,0.12)`), matching the existing tag family's shape. Tofu theme gets a matching square-badge dot variant; the tag inherits the base color through the theme's shared `.conv-status-tag` shape rule.
- **i18n.** `sidebar.errorTag` (出错 / Error) + `sidebar.errorState` (上次生成以错误结束 / "Last generation ended with an error") — used for both the dot `title` tooltip and the tag. EN+ZH parity.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on `conversation_list.js` + `i18n.js`; both confirmed present in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (so the change ships in the bundle — server restart + hard-refresh needed). `styles.css` served directly, no rebuild.


### 2026-07-02 — Two owner-reported issues: (1) streaming/phase status bar truncated the error to one ellipsized line → now wraps; (2) `SSE error: messages.55.content…` root-caused to a mislabeled image data-URI media type and fixed at the outbound builder
- **Owner report (screenshot).** A finished Agent bubble (claude-opus-4.8) showed the amber `stream-phase-retrying` bar clamped to `⟳ … SSE error: messages.55.co…` on one line, and asked: (1) the streaming bar should WRAP, not omit text; (2) diagnose the SSE error.
- **Issue 1 — bar wrapping (`static/styles.css:327`).** The base `.stream-phase-text` was `flex:1;white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis` inside a `.stream-phase{display:flex;align-items:center}` capsule — so any long phase detail (a retry carrying the API error text) was single-line + ellipsized. Changed to `.stream-phase{align-items:flex-start}` and `.stream-phase-text{flex:1;min-width:0;white-space:normal;overflow-wrap:anywhere;word-break:break-word}` (dropped `nowrap`/`overflow`/`text-overflow`). Now the retry/phase text wraps to as many lines as needed; the ⟳ icon top-aligns to the first line and the animated `…` dots trail the last line. Short phases (thinking/waiting) never wrap so they look unchanged. `styles.css` is served directly (not bundled) — no rebuild.
- **Issue 2 — SSE error root cause (evidence-first, not guessed).** The truncated phase detail hid the real API message. Pulled the full text from the live conv's `task_events` (PG): `messages.55.content.0.image.source.base64: The image was specified using the image/jpeg media type, but the image [does not appear to be in that format]` — Anthropic Messages API HTTP 400 (surfaced through `_handle_sse_error` → `Exception('SSE error: …')`). Root cause: a chat image block carried a `data:image/jpeg;base64,<bytes>` URI whose bytes are actually a PNG. `_validate_image_blocks` Case 3 (`lib/llm/body.py`) sniffed the magic bytes only to confirm it was *a* known image and passed the block through UNCHANGED — it never reconciled the DECLARED header media type with the sniffed one. Mislabeled URIs are tolerated by every OpenAI-compat gateway but HARD-REJECTED by the strict Anthropic path (`openai_body_to_anthropic` forwards the header verbatim), killing the turn.
- **Fix (`lib/llm/body.py`, `_validate_image_blocks` Case 3).** After sniffing the true MIME from magic bytes, compare it to the declared `data:<mime>;…` header; on mismatch rewrite the header to the sniffed type (payload bytes untouched) + `logger.warning`. Makes the outbound data URI self-consistent for every provider. Self-consistent URIs are left BYTE-IDENTICAL (no needless prompt-cache churn). This is the outbound-builder analogue of the existing Case-1 local-file path, which already derives MIME from magic bytes.
- **Verification.** New `tests/test_image_media_type_reconcile.py` (5): png-as-jpeg→corrected, jpeg-as-png→corrected, self-consistent URI left byte-identical, payload preserved on rewrite, + an NC asserting a mislabeled jpeg header is never left in place (the exact 400 trigger). `py_compile` clean; `pytest -k "image or body"` = 110 passed (the lone `test_conv_ref_scope` error is the known bare-CI `no such table: conversations` bootstrap artifact, unrelated); `test_anthropic_outbound.py`+`test_cc_alignment.py` = 43 passed; new suite = 5 passed.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** An image `data:` URI has TWO independent truth sources — the header media type and the actual bytes — and only strict validators (Anthropic) enforce agreement. Any inbound image normalization must reconcile them at the OUTBOUND builder (once, in `_validate_image_blocks`), not trust the declared header. And when a status bar carries API error text, it must wrap — an ellipsized one-line clamp hides exactly the diagnostic the user needs.

- **Follow-up (owner review closed two gaps before sign-off).** (a) **RIFF/WebP false-positive.** The magic map used a bare `b'RIFF'` prefix for `image/webp`, which also matches WAV/AVI/ANI — so a correctly-labeled non-WebP RIFF payload would be sniffed as `image/webp` (a NEW media-type mismatch). Extracted a `_sniff_mime(head)` helper: PNG/JPEG/GIF stay fixed-head prefixes; WebP now requires the full RIFF-container signature (`head[:4]=='RIFF' AND head[8:12]=='WEBP'`). A WAV (`RIFF…WAVE`) is now correctly rejected as "not an image" (→ text placeholder) instead of mislabeled webp. Both Case 1 (local file) and Case 3 (data URI) route through the one helper so they can't drift. (b) **Replay/swap-path coverage.** `build_body` runs `_validate_image_blocks` on the fresh-build path, but the dispatch pre-built-body swap path (`lib/llm_dispatch/api.py::_adapt_stream_body_for_slot`, `is_body=True`, when the model is swapped onto Claude mid-flight) ran only `_strip_trailing_assistant_for_claude` + `_downscale_oversized_images` — NOT `_validate_image_blocks`. So my "next send auto-corrects" claim held for a fresh build but a model-swap onto Claude carrying a stored mislabeled URI would have 400'd again. Added `_validate_image_blocks(body['messages'])` to that Claude branch (before the downscale pass), giving the swap path the same self-consistency guarantee.
- **Verification (updated).** `tests/test_image_media_type_reconcile.py` now 9: + real-WebP-kept-byte-identical, + real-WebP-mislabeled-as-jpeg→corrected-to-webp, + RIFF-but-not-WebP(WAV)→dropped-not-mislabeled, + swap-path-runs-reconciliation-on-prebuilt-body (drives the real `_adapt_stream_body_for_slot(is_body=True)` seam with a Claude slot). **NC PROVEN (byte-reverting):** deleting the swap-path `_validate_image_blocks` call → only `test_swap_path_runs_reconciliation_on_prebuilt_body` FAILS, other 8 stay green; `cp` restore → md5 `4ef8445e…`, 9/9 pass. `py_compile` clean on body.py + api.py; `test_backend_unit`+`test_anthropic_outbound`+`test_cc_alignment`+reconcile = 104 passed.
- **Guardrail / lesson (extended).** (1) A 4-byte magic prefix can't express a container format whose discriminant lives at a byte OFFSET — WebP's `RIFF` head is shared with WAV/AVI, so sniff `RIFF….WEBP`, never `startswith(b'RIFF')`. (2) There are TWO seams that put a body on the wire: `build_body` (fresh) and `_adapt_stream_body_for_slot(is_body=True)` (dispatch model-swap). Any message-normalization invariant that Anthropic enforces (image media-type, trailing-assistant, empty-content, thought-signature) must be applied on BOTH, guarded on the target model — fixing only `build_body` leaves the mid-flight-swap path exposed.

- **Follow-up 2 (owner review — root-cause the fix at the actual boundary, not every feeder).** The real Anthropic-protocol seam is `openai_body_to_anthropic` (reached by the STREAMING path via `_sse_core.prepare_request` for BOTH sync `dispatch_stream` and async `async_dispatch_stream` — they share `_adapt_stream_body_for_slot` AND `prepare_request` — and by the non-stream `chat.py`). Its `_media_type_and_data` extracted `media_type` from the `data:` header and **trusted it verbatim** — so any feeder that skipped `_validate_image_blocks` (or a future new seam) would still emit a mismatched `source.media_type` and 400. **Fix (`lib/llm/anthropic_outbound.py::_media_type_and_data`):** sniff the real MIME from the base64 prefix and prefer it over the declared header, right at the last transform before the wire. Now the strict path is self-consistent REGARDLESS of which upstream seam fed it — reconciliation at every feeder is now defense-in-depth, not the sole guarantee. **De-duplication:** promoted the sniffer to a module-level `lib/llm/body.py::sniff_image_mime` (single source of truth; the local `_validate_image_blocks` closure now aliases it) and `anthropic_outbound` imports it LAZILY inside the function (no module-load cycle; `body.py` never imports `anthropic_outbound`). Best-effort: undecodable/unrecognized bytes keep the declared header unchanged (never blocks a request).
- **Verification (final).** `tests/test_image_media_type_reconcile.py` now 13: + `test_anthropic_boundary_reconciles_unvalidated_body` (feeds `openai_body_to_anthropic` a body that NEVER passed `_validate_image_blocks` → asserts `source.media_type` sniffed to png + base64 payload untouched), + boundary-reconciles-webp, + boundary-leaves-self-consistent, + an NC asserting the boundary never emits the declared jpeg for png bytes. **NC PROVEN (byte-reverting):** neutered `_media_type_and_data` back to trusting the declared header → exactly the 3 boundary tests FAIL (the self-consistent one still passes, correctly), the other 10 stay green; `cp` restore → md5 `83af0b87…`, 13/13 pass. `py_compile` clean on body.py + anthropic_outbound.py + api.py; `reconcile`+`test_anthropic_outbound`+`test_cc_alignment`+`test_backend_unit`+`test_continue_lossless` = 139 passed.
- **Guardrail / lesson (final).** The DEFINITIVE fix for a strict-validator wire invariant belongs at the boundary transform that actually talks to that API (`openai_body_to_anthropic`), sniffing/validating what it EMITS — not scattered across every feeder that happens to build a body. Feeders reconciling too is fine as defense-in-depth, but the boundary must not trust an arriving header it can cheaply verify. Confirmed the STREAMING anthropic path (the screenshot's live agent) reaches this boundary on both the raw-messages and pre-built-body branches, and both sync + async dispatch share `prepare_request`, so all three seams (fresh build, mid-flight swap, non-stream) now converge on one self-consistent transform.

- **Follow-up 3 (source guard at the birthplace + the "why still failing" was a deploy gap, not a code gap).** Owner reported the 400 STILL firing (`messages.54.content.0.image.source.base64: … image/jpeg media type, but the image appears to be a image/png image`, model `aws.claude-opus-4.7`). Investigation (evidence, not guessing): the running server PID predated my 11:15–11:20 edits — Python doesn't hot-reload, so the live process was executing pre-fix bytecode. On-disk fix verified correct end-to-end for the exact path (`aws.claude-opus-*` on sankuai is the OpenAI-compat `/chat/completions` wire, NOT `api_protocol='anthropic'`, so the `build_body`→`_validate_image_blocks` layer is the one that matters there). **ROOT CAUSE birthplace found:** `lib/tasks_pkg/conv_message_builder.py::_build_user_message` built the data URI as `f'data:{img.get("mediaType","image/png")};base64,…'` — trusting the DB-stored `mediaType` verbatim. That is where the mislabeled URI is BORN (a PNG uploaded/saved with `mediaType='image/jpeg'`). **Fix:** sniff the base64 prefix with the shared `sniff_image_mime` and correct `media_type` before constructing the URI (best-effort, payload untouched, `logger.warning` on correction). Now four layers reconcile: source (conv_message_builder) → build_body → dispatch swap → anthropic boundary; the source guard means the DB never even emits a mismatched URL.
- **Restart (authorized, narrow).** Owner authorized restarting OUR tofu server (not a host restart). SIGTERM'd stale PID; a supervisor respawned it cleanly — new PID `1900692` started 14:06:47, `[boot +8.1s] Ready — handing off to Hypercorn`, single listener 127.0.0.1:15000, no crash-respawn. Confirmed the live process loads the new code (cwd = project dir; on-disk modules carry `sniff_image_mime` + the `Corrected mislabeled stored image` guard). **End-to-end proof on the REAL failing conv `mr286f1h3mx1mi`:** `build_api_messages_from_db` → `build_body('aws.claude-opus-4.7')` logged `[MsgBuilder] Corrected mislabeled stored image mediaType 'image/jpeg' → 'image/png'` and produced 0 still-mislabeled image blocks on the wire (was the exact 400 trigger). Zero recurrence of the media-type 400 in app.log since the 14:06 restart.
- **Verification (source guard).** `tests/test_image_media_type_reconcile.py` now 17: + `test_source_guard_corrects_png_stored_as_jpeg` / `_corrects_webp_stored_as_png` / `_leaves_correctly_labeled_untouched` + NC. **NC PROVEN (byte-reverting):** deleting the sniff-and-correct block in `_build_user_message` → exactly the 3 source-guard tests FAIL (correctly-labeled still passes), `cp` restore → md5 `a3f24011…`, 17/17 pass. `test_image_media_type_reconcile` + `test_conv_message_builder` = 68 passed; `py_compile` clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson (deploy).** When a fix "still doesn't work," FIRST rule out stale bytecode: compare the server process start time (`ps -o lstart`) against the edit mtime — Python caches imported modules for the process lifetime, so an on-disk fix is inert until restart. Don't add more code layers to chase a bug your fix already covers on disk. AND: fix the invariant at its BIRTHPLACE (the DB→URI constructor), not only at the wire boundaries — a value written wrong upstream should be corrected where it's first materialized so every downstream consumer inherits the correct form.

### 2026-07-02 — 缓存"服务端随机未命中"溯源:建立 post-translation 线上指纹机制,判决从"排除法猜测"升级为"字节确证",并抓出 _downscale 阈值=5 回改真凶(旧 stochastic 结论被推翻)
