- **Guardrail / lesson.** A frozen desktop build MUST resolve its writable state (data/logs/DB/config) through a single frozen-aware resolver — `dirname(dirname(__file__))` points into the read-only bundle and silently works in dev but crashes when installed to Program Files. And a PyInstaller `--onedir` bundle has NO standalone `python.exe`: never shell out to one from an installer `[Run]` step or from `sys.executable -m …`; relaunch the single real exe with an env-flag dispatch instead. Optional bundled data files must be existence-filtered — a stale `datas` entry is a hard build-abort, not a warning.

- **Hardening round 2 (owner-driven, two closed seams on the SAME twin-rot failure class).** After the fix above, the owner flagged that `lib/log.py`'s inline `_writable_logs_dir()` is a hand-duplicated twin of `runtime_paths` (can't import it — cycle) with NO coverage biting it, and that the two twins could silently diverge. (a) **Twin coverage** — new `LogDirTwinTest` (4 tests) drives `import lib.log` in a subprocess under simulated `sys.frozen`+read-only-exe and pins that `LOG_DIR` AGREES with `runtime_paths.logs_root()` for source / override / frozen-portable / frozen-readonly. NC (inject `return candidate` in log.py's fallback) → `test_log_frozen_readonly_falls_back_not_bundle` FAILS with the production signature (`LOG_DIR` inside the uncreatable bundle dir); byte-restore → green. (b) **Data/logs co-location seam** — discovered `runtime_paths` probed `<exe>/data` while `log.py` probed `<exe>/logs`: on a partially-writable install those two probes could DISAGREE and split data and logs to different roots. Fix: BOTH now probe the SHARED base `<exe_dir>` itself (one probe = one verdict); refactored `log.py` `_writable_logs_dir`→`_writable_base_dir()` (byte-twin of `_resolve_base`) deriving `logs` from the chosen base. New `CoLocationTest` (2 tests, all three roots resolved in ONE child) asserts `dirname(data_root)==dirname(logs_root)==dirname(LOG_DIR)`, none under the read-only exe dir. NC (revert `runtime_paths` to the `<exe>/data` per-subdir probe, with a pre-existing writable `<exe>/data` subdir) → `test_partial_writable_data_subdir_does_not_split` FAILS (data base = read-only `appdir` → would split from logs → crash); byte-restore → 12/12 pass. Owner independently re-verified: 12 desktop + 23 db/config/concurrent-writer tests (35 total) green, no NC residue, ruff clean, `import server` boots with source-mode `LOG_DIR` unchanged.
- **Guardrail / lesson (round 2).** When a cycle forces you to hand-duplicate resolver logic across two modules, the duplication itself is a latent bug — cover BOTH copies with a test that pins them to produce the IDENTICAL result, and make the shared decision (here: the frozen-fallback write-probe) ask the IDENTICAL question. Probing different SUBDIRS (`<exe>/data` vs `<exe>/logs`) for what is meant to be one base-dir verdict is exactly how two "agreeing" twins silently split state on a partially-writable filesystem. Probe the shared base once; derive every subdir from that single verdict.


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode REPORT EN/中: toggling BACK to an already-generated language no longer regenerates it (session snapshot makes a toggle a pure view switch)
- **Owner report.** Chinese report already generated; clicked "Regenerate in English" (fine), then clicked 中 back — and the Chinese **regenerated** instead of just re-showing. Reproduced verbatim in `logs/app.log`: at 20:35:14 a fresh `rpt_..._en` task started, and at 20:35:16 (2s later, the switch-back) a fresh `rpt_..._zh` task started — BOTH ran full ~13-min multi-round generations; neither hit the `(paper_hash, lang)` DB cache. Persisted `en`/`zh` rows only appeared at 20:48 (task completion), long after the switch.
- **Root cause (`static/js/paper-reader.js`).** The report cache is per-language server-side (composite PK `(paper_hash, lang)` in `paper_reports` — so EN can't clobber ZH; the DB layer was never the problem). But `_setReportLang` treats each toggle as "new cache key ⇒ drop `view.cache` and re-enter `_loadOrGenerateReport`", which relies SOLELY on a server round-trip (lookup → DB cache → else start) to bring the other language back. When that round-trip misses — a just-generated report not yet persisted, or a report that streamed to `done` this session but whose DB row the cache lookup didn't resurface — step (4) falls through to a brand-new `report/start`. A jsdom repro driving the REAL shipped JS confirmed: with the DB-cache stub returning `{ok:false}` (the log-observed miss), en→zh switch-back fires a fresh `zh` start.
- **Fix — session-scoped per-`(paper, langKey)` snapshot; a toggle is a PURE VIEW SWITCH.** New module var `_paperReportSnapshots` (`'<paperId>::<langKey>'` → `{report, meta}`) + helpers `_reportSnapshotKey` / `_rememberReportSnapshot` / `_getReportSnapshot` / `_resetReportSnapshots`. Every terminal render site now remembers its body (DB-cache hit in `_loadOrGenerateReport`; start-time `data.cached`; poll `done`; `_applyReportEvent` `done`). `_setReportLang` snapshots the outgoing body BEFORE leaving, and on switch-in: if a snapshot for the target language exists this session it repaints from it instantly (NO server round-trip, NO `report/start`) and returns; only a never-shown language falls through to load/generate. Explicit **Regenerate** still force-starts (unchanged). Snapshots are per-paper and cleared in `_resetAllReportViews` (the single paper-switch / mode-exit choke point) so one paper's reports never paint under another. Aligns with the "frontend renders backend-produced state" architecture — a language flip is a view switch, not a re-derivation.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC, byte-reverting).** Extended `tests/test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` with a regression scenario driving the REAL shipped JS under a DB-MISS stub (`reportCache`⇒`{ok:false}`, the log-observed failure): land on zh, snapshot it, regenerate en (expected), toggle back to zh → asserts `report_toggle_back_no_regen` (no new `report/start`) + `report_toggle_back_repaints_snapshot` (screen shows the snapshot body). PASS threshold 14→16. **NC PROVEN**: in-memory-patching `_getReportSnapshot` to `return null` → BOTH new checks FAIL (`NEW starts=["zh"]`, screen loses the snapshot — the exact bug), while the pre-existing checks stay green; byte-identical restore → 16 PASS. Full run: `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` + `test_frontend_paper_regen_refresh.py` = 2 passed. `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-6eba5213.js` (`paper-reader.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). The `no such table: conversations` lines during the NC run are the known bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact, unrelated.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For Paper Reading Mode, a language/venue toggle must be a PURE VIEW SWITCH backed by a session snapshot — never a re-derivation that depends on a server round-trip to bring back a body already shown this session. Wiping `view.cache` on toggle and trusting the DB lookup to repaint is fragile: any lookup miss (unpersisted / not-resurfaced row) silently escalates a cheap toggle into a full multi-minute regeneration. Remember the outgoing body before leaving, repaint the incoming one from memory, and reserve generation for languages never shown this session (or an explicit Regenerate).


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode Review EN/中: reopen now RESTORES the persisted Chinese reading view (translate-only) — closed the gap between `_setReviewLang`'s persistence promise and `_loadOrGenerateReport`'s English-only render
- **Owner report + shared diagnosis.** "审稿模式的中英切换是让你去翻译，不是生成两份。" Confirmed the existing behaviour already matches intent: review generation is English-canonical (`_reportView('review').uiLang` ⇒ `'en'`, langKey `review:<venue>:en`), the EN/中 toggle `_setReviewLang('zh')` runs the Babel translate task under the DISTINCT composite key `review:<venue>:zh` (English never regenerated), 'EN' restores the cached English render, and backend `_run_translate_task` only chunk-translates (`real_lang = lang.rsplit(':',1)[-1]`). So no "two versions" bug. The REAL defect: `_setReviewLang`'s docstring promised "re-opening the Review tab restores the last language", but `_loadOrGenerateReport` only ever rendered the English cache and NEVER re-applied a persisted `zh`. On reopen (reload or paper-switch) `_resetAllReportViews` wipes `_paperReviewTranslatedText`/`_paperReviewShowTranslation`, so a user who was reading Chinese came back to English — which reads as "切换不生效 / 又生成了一份英文", the felt source of this complaint.
- **Fix (`static/js/paper-reader.js`, additive + translate-only).** New `_restoreReviewReadingLang(view)`: no-ops unless `view.kind==='review'` AND `view.cache` (English review exists) AND `_activeReviewLang()==='zh'`; then calls `_setReviewLang('zh')` — which on a warm client/server translation cache is instant and, critically, issues NO `report/start` (never regenerates the English review). Wired at the THREE terminal English-render sites ONLY (never mid-generation): (1) `_loadOrGenerateReport` step-3 DB-cache hit; (2) `_generatePaperReport` in-memory-cache instant path; (3) `_loadOrGenerateReport` step-1 existing-stream path guarded to `stream.status==='done'`. Placed strictly AFTER the English `_renderFinalReport`, so it can't race the generation/poll flow.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC, byte-reverting).** New `tests/test_frontend_review_lang_restore.py` (jsdom, drives the REAL shipped `paper-reader.js`): persists `paper_review_lang_by_id={paper-1:'zh'}`, reopens the Review tab with a warm English DB-cache hit under `_i18nLang='en'`, asserts the rendered content is the TRANSLATED Chinese (`中文译文`), `translateStart` called exactly once, and `reportStart` NOT called (English never regenerated). **NC PROVEN**: the harness re-runs the same real JS with `_restoreReviewReadingLang` in-memory-patched to `return;` (on-disk file untouched) → `restored_chinese_view` + `translate_called_once` FAIL (reopen stays English, no translate), while `never_regenerated_english` stays PASS in both runs (restore never regenerates either way). Actual output — normal: `PASS persisted_zh / PASS restored_chinese_view / PASS translate_called_once / PASS never_regenerated_english`; NC: `PASS persisted_zh / FAIL restored_chinese_view / FAIL translate_called_once / PASS never_regenerated_english`. `tests/test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` still passes (no regression). `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-916c1438.js` (4 `_restoreReviewReadingLang` refs = 1 def + 3 sites); i18n untouched (pure logic, no new strings).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A per-entity "reading language" that is persisted but only translation-derived (never regenerated) must be RE-APPLIED after every canonical (English) render on reopen — persisting the choice is half the contract; a restore hook at the terminal-render seam is the other half. Keep the restore translate-ONLY and gate it on cache-present + terminal-status so it can never trigger a regeneration or fight an in-flight task.

### 2026-07-01 — "我的一天" round 2: manual-state loss on regen FIXED (server-authoritative `_merge_manual_state`) + instant-paint from a persistent client cache
- **Owner report (2/3 remaining after the cost-cache fix).** (1) day-click still doesn't paint instantly — a second, structural cause beyond the cost wipe; (2) "任务状态处理得不好" — manual edits must be DURABLE across regeneration.
- **Issue #2 — manual-state DATA LOSS on regen (the 真问题).** Three vectors, all confirmed: (a) **manual stream status** — `update_task_status` stamps `_manual`+cycled status onto a stream, but regen rebuilds `final_streams` from scratch with fresh `stream-<uuid>` ids → override lost; (b) **TODO check-offs** — `toggle_tomorrow_todo` sets `done` on a `tomorrow[]` item, regen rebuilds `tomorrow[]` → lost; (c) **manually-added TODOs** — `add_manual_task` appended to `tomorrow[]` with NO flag, and the ad-hoc merge in POST/generator only preserved `tasks[]` where `_todo` → always clobbered (`backfill_report` merged nothing). **Fix (backend-authoritative, single source of truth):** new `lib/daily_report/todos.py::_merge_manual_state(result, existing)` invoked INSIDE `_analyse_conversations` right before return (both the empty-convs fast-path and the main path), so POST + backfill + async generator ALL inherit it — the scattered ad-hoc `tasks` merges in `routes/api_v1/daily_report.py` + `generator.py` were DELETED (generator's empty branch now delegates to `_analyse_conversations([], date)`). Identity choices matter: streams match by **conv_ids overlap** first (stable across LLM title rewording), strict normalized-title fallback — deliberately NOT the loose CJK `_fuzzy_todo_match` (it false-positives on short/latin titles, e.g. "Refactor the parser" ≈ "Write docs", and would BLEED a manual override onto an unrelated stream); TODOs use a strict `_same_todo` (normalized equality / containment) because for state PRESERVATION a false positive is worse than a false negative. `add_manual_task` now stamps `_manual: True`.
- **Issue #1 — instant paint.** `_mydaySelectDay` showed a skeleton then AWAITED `Api.daily.status` before painting, and `_myday.cache` was in-memory only (cold on every reload). **Fix:** self-contained per-day IndexedDB read cache `_mydayIDB` (mirrors idb-cache.js: server = source of truth, IDB = local read cache) inside `myday.js` (no new bundle entry). New flow: in-memory full report → paint now; else IDB → paint from cache; else skeleton — the first paint NEVER blocks on the network. Then a background `status` call reconciles + rewrites the cache (`_mydaySetCache` routes every authoritative server report through both in-mem + IDB; poll-complete / generate / add / delete / toggle-success all use it). On server idle/error we KEEP the cached paint (stale report beats a blank prompt).
- **Verification (actual + biting NCs, both restored byte-identical).** `tests/test_daily_report.py` → 46 passed (added `TestMergeManualState`: stream-status-survives-by-conv_ids, no-false-positive-without-overlap, todo-checkoff-survives, manual-todo-survives, not-duplicated-when-reproposed, legacy-`_todo`, no-existing-noop, and an END-TO-END `_analyse_conversations` regen seam). **NC #2 PROVEN:** neuter the result-path `_merge_manual_state` call → `test_analyse_conversations_invokes_merge_on_regen` FAILS (`in_progress` instead of preserved `done`); restore → 8/8, diff empty. New `tests/test_frontend_myday_instant_paint.py` (bare-node, fake indexedDB + stub document + controllable pending `status`): asserts the cached report paints into #mydayTasks BEFORE the status promise resolves + no skeleton on a cache hit + server report reconciles + cache rewritten. **NC #1 PROVEN:** revert `_mydaySelectDay` to old blocking flow → `cached_paint_before_network` + `no_skeleton_on_cache_hit` FAIL; restore → 6/6, diff empty. ruff clean; `node --check` clean; API-isolation ratchet 4/4 (myday uses only `Api.daily.*` + IndexedDB, no raw fetch); bundle rebuilt `bundle-916c1438.js`. (The `no such table` log noise under pytest is the known bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact; these changes touch report JSON + client cache, not those tables.)
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "regenerate" that discards user edits is silent data loss — preserve manual state in the BACKEND at the single analysis seam, never per-route, and pick a STABLE identity (conv_ids for streams, strict text for TODOs); a fuzzy matcher tuned for one job (CJK dedup) is the wrong tool for state-preservation matching. And never block a view's first paint on the network when a local read cache exists: paint cached → revalidate → reconcile, with the server still authoritative.


### 2026-07-01 — Server-restart interrupted-turn recovery made AUTHORITATIVE: keyed off task_results.conv_id (not the frontend-synced settings.activeTaskId) — fixes Continue spawning a brand-new agent from scratch
- **Owner report.** Updated the server and restarted it WHILE a conversation was generating. On return, clicked Continue → it produced a NEW agent that appeared to start from scratch, losing the interrupted turn. Asked whether Continue's re-attach is lossless, whether the frontend renders off backend signals, and demanded the behaviour be observable/debuggable.
- **Log + DB forensics (smoking gun).** `logs/app.log` at the `20:18:38` restart: `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` logged `Marked 18 stale running task(s) as interrupted` but **`0 conv(s) cleaned`**. Yet the interrupted chat task `83913555`'s `task_results` row DID carry the authoritative `conv_id='mr214lxz3xkpp4'` (backend-stamped by `create_task`) with 3362 chars content + 27974 thinking. Root cause: the recovery's Step 2/3 — which merges recovered content into `conversations.messages`, stamps `finishReason='interrupted'`, and clears the dead pointer — iterated conversations ONLY via `settings.activeTaskId`. That pointer is FRONTEND-synced (a best-effort PUT that races tab-close and the whitelist-rebuild) and is null/stale after a mid-stream crash. So the interrupted turn was ORPHANED: never merged, never stamped. Downstream, the reload's Case B frontend recovery ALSO keys on `activeTaskId` → doesn't fire → the conv's last assistant turn stays thin/checkpoint-less → `continueAssistant` scans it, finds `toolHistory.length===0` (no complete tool round) → falls back to `startAssistantResponse` = a brand-new agent from scratch. Exactly the symptom.
- **Fix (backend, single-source-of-truth) — `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py::recover_stale_tasks_on_startup`.** Step 1 now also builds `interrupted_task_by_conv` = {conv_id → interrupted task_id with most content+thinking}, derived from the authoritative `task_results.conv_id`. Step 2/3 UNIONs the two conversation sources BY conv_id: (a) convs still carrying `settings.activeTaskId` (clear the dead pointer) AND (b) convs that OWN an interrupted task via `task_results.conv_id` (recovered even when `activeTaskId` was never persisted — the mid-stream-crash case). The merge is driven off the interrupted task, tolerates a null `activeTaskId`, and the write path is unchanged (merge content/thinking/toolRounds/model, stamp `finishReason='interrupted'`, materialize an assistant turn when the tail is a bare user msg).
- **Observability (owner-requested).** New/renamed log lines make the recovery fully traceable: `Marked N stale running task(s) as interrupted (M owning conv(s) identified via task_results.conv_id)`; `M interrupted-owning conv(s) had NO activeTaskId (recovered via task_results.conv_id): [ids]`; per-conv `Recovered conv=X from task=Y (activeTaskId_cleared=.. messages_updated=..)`; summary now `N conv(s) recovered` (was the misleading `0 conv(s) cleaned`).
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_stale_recovery_authoritative.py` (4 cases, live SQLite + `init_db`): `test_recovers_when_active_task_id_absent` (THE BUG — interrupted task carries conv_id, conv has NO activeTaskId → asserts content+thinking+toolRounds merged and `finishReason='interrupted'` stamped); `test_continue_finds_checkpoint_on_recovered_message` (THE PAYOFF — see below); `test_recovers_when_active_task_id_present` (regression guard: classic path still merges + clears pointer); `test_task_marked_interrupted_in_task_results` (Step 1 invariant). **NC PROVEN**: neuter the union (`_missing_ids=[]`) → BOTH the absent-activeTaskId case AND the end-to-end checkpoint case FAIL with the exact production signature (`0 conv(s) recovered`, content not merged, scan returns None); the two guards stay green; byte-identical restore → 4/4 pass. Direct functional probe confirmed the observable log lines fire and the summary flips `0→1 conv(s) recovered`. `py_compile` clean.
- **PAYOFF loop closed (owner-directed follow-up).** The merge test proved content lands in `conversations.messages`, but NOT the actual objective: that Continue then RESUMES from checkpoint rather than regenerating from scratch. That decision is gated entirely by `lib.chat.turn_builder.scan_continue_checkpoint(assistant_msg)` — the SAME function `/api/chat/continue` calls; when it returns None the endpoint replies `{fallback:'regenerate'}` and the frontend pops + starts a brand-new agent. New `test_continue_finds_checkpoint_on_recovered_message` seeds a REALISTIC interrupted `tool_rounds` shape (one COMPLETE batch: `toolCallId`+`status='done'`+`toolContent`+`llmRound`, followed by a TRAILING partial `run_command` round still `searching` with no `toolContent`), runs `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup()` with NO activeTaskId, then calls the real `scan_continue_checkpoint` on the recovered message and asserts: non-None checkpoint, `kept_rounds==1` (the complete round), `discarded_rounds==1` (the trailing partial correctly dropped), `tool_history` non-empty (so the frontend's `toolHistory.length===0` regenerate-from-scratch branch is NOT taken), and the kept round is `tc_read_1`. NC reverting the union makes THIS assertion fail too (scan None → regenerate), proving the test guards the payoff, not just the merge.
- **Pre-existing, NOT mine.** `tests/test_chat_manager_migration.py` fails 5 tests with `no such table: message_queue/task_results` — the documented bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact; confirmed identical on the unmodified tree via `git stash` (fails 5 there too, unrelated to this change).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any recovery/merge that must survive a process crash MUST key off the BACKEND-AUTHORITATIVE fact (`task_results.conv_id`, stamped by `create_task`), NEVER a frontend-synced pointer (`settings.activeTaskId`) that races tab-close and may never have been persisted at crash time. This is the same "backend is the single source of truth, frontend is a pure renderer" principle already applied to the autopilot run-concluded fold. With the turn now properly recovered into `conversations.messages` (content + `finishReason='interrupted'` + toolRounds), the frontend renders the interrupted bubble honestly AND `continueAssistant`'s checkpoint scan finds the completed tool rounds → resumes from checkpoint instead of regenerating from scratch.


### 2026-07-01 — Browser Bridge was DOWNLOADING PDFs to the user's machine: PDF/binary URLs must never reach the extension fallback (real bug, owner's diagnosis exactly right)
- **Owner report + screenshot.** Chrome's download manager showed `sfbookv7r.pdf` / `sfbookv8r.pdf` (~20 MB each) auto-downloading. Owner's reasoning (correct): the file was fetched into the CLIENT, so the server can't parse it either → routing it there is a pure-downside bug; fetching onto the SERVER is fine.
- **Root cause (chain proven by reading code).** With **Browser Bridge** ON, a server-side `fetch_page_content` on a PDF that fails (403/429/timeout/oversize — common for a 20 MB file) falls through to `try_browser_fetch` (`tofu-search/fetch/core.py` + `http.py`) → chatui's `_ChatuiBrowserProvider.fetch_url` (`lib/search_bridge.py`) → the extension's `cmdFetchUrl` (`browser_extension/background.js:1764`), which does `chrome.tabs.create({ url })`. Navigating a Chrome tab to a PDF URL makes **Chrome's download manager save the file to the user's disk**, AND the extension only scrapes `innerText`/`outerHTML` → returns nothing for a PDF. So the browser fallback for a binary is all cost, no benefit. (The pdf.js viewer + `serve_paper_pdf` are innocent — pdf.js XHRs bytes into memory and the server serves PDFs inline.)
- **Fix — refuse binary/PDF URLs at the browser seam (backend-authoritative) + defense-in-depth in the extension.** `lib/search_bridge.py`: new `_BROWSER_UNRENDERABLE_EXTS` (pdf/zip/media/office/font/exe… — `.svg` deliberately EXCLUDED, it's text) + `_is_browser_unrenderable(url)` (path-suffix predicate, trailing-slash tolerant); both `_ChatuiBrowserProvider.fetch_url` and `.fetch_html` short-circuit to `None` (info-log) BEFORE importing/calling the extension transport. `browser_extension/background.js`: mirror `isBinaryAssetUrl(url)` + a guard in `cmdFetchUrl` that throws before `chrome.tabs.create` (catches a redirect that lands on a PDF, or a stale server). PDFs are still fetched/parsed SERVER-side (`_extract_pdf_text`, in-memory) — unchanged.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_browser_pdf_download_guard.py` (5, `unit`): predicate (pdf/binaries unrenderable, html/svg/json renderable); `fetch_url`+`fetch_html` on a PDF short-circuit to None WITHOUT touching the transport (the mocks raise if called); regression guard — a plain HTML URL still reaches the transport. **NC PROVEN**: neuter `_is_browser_unrenderable`→`return False` → the 3 PDF-refusal tests FAIL (`send_browser_command must NOT be called for a PDF` / transport reached), the 2 renderable-URL tests stay green; byte-identical restore (`diff` empty) → 5/5 pass. Related suites `test_browser_read_payload` + `test_package_facades` = 51 passed total; `node --check` + ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The browser-extension fetch fallback works by opening a real tab in the USER's Chrome — it must only ever be handed URLs that RENDER as text. A binary/PDF URL there downloads to the user's disk and returns nothing; gate it out at the provider seam (single source of truth) and mirror the gate in the extension. `.svg` is text, not binary — keep it OUT of the block list.


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode glossary hover card: raw KaTeX/Markdown leak fixed (textContent→cleaned plain-text + a real DOM card that RENDERS)
- **Owner report + screenshot.** The term-hover explanation card in the Paper Reading report showed garbled raw math — `T/F=生成长度/NFE\text{T/F} = \text{生成长度}/\text{NFE}...` — instead of typeset content. "Not rendering Markdown; please optimize."
- **Two coupled root causes.** (1) `_extractGlossary` (`static/js/paper-reader.js`) captured the definition via `cell.textContent`. But the "Core Terminology" table is part of the ALREADY markdown+KaTeX-rendered report; a KaTeX span carries BOTH a visual `.katex-html` tree AND a hidden `.katex-mathml <annotation>` with the raw TeX, so `textContent` concatenates the annotation source (the leak) with the glyphs → the exact screenshot string. (2) The tooltip was a pure-CSS `::after{content:attr(data-def)}` (`static/styles.css`) — an `attr()` pseudo-element can ONLY show plain text, so even a correct definition could never render Markdown/KaTeX.
- **Fix.** New `_cellPlainText(cell)` clones the cell, strips `.katex-mathml, annotation`, then reads textContent → a CLEAN plain-text def for `aria-label`. `_extractGlossary` now ALSO keeps the cell's rendered `innerHTML` as `defHtml` (threaded through the alias map → picks). `_decorateGlossaryTerms` builds a real child `<span class="paper-term-card">` and sets `.innerHTML = defHtml` (safe: it's a slice of the already-DOMPurify-sanitized report body), `aria-hidden` (the span's aria-label carries the def). CSS: replaced the `::after`/`attr(data-def)` popover with styling for the `.paper-term-card` child (same visual box; `:hover/.focus-visible` reveals it), added `user-select:none` (card is a hover duplicate — must not pollute copy/selection) + `.katex`/`p` spacing tames. `_countReadingWords` now excludes `.paper-term-card` text (clone-and-strip) so the injected duplicate doesn't inflate the reading-time estimate.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_frontend_paper_glossary_card.py` (jsdom, 13 checks) drives the REAL shipped `paper-reader.js`: builds an article whose glossary def cell is a KaTeX-rendered span (mathml annotation + katex-html), runs `_extractGlossary`+`_decorateGlossaryTerms`, asserts the clean def has NO `\text{` leak, the card preserves the `.katex` render, visible term text is just the word, card is `aria-hidden`, and the reading count ignores the card. **NC PROVEN**: reverting the extraction to naive `cell.textContent` → `def_no_latex_leak` FAILS with the exact garbled screenshot string (card-render checks stay green — they're the CSS-side half); byte-restored → 13/13 pass. Sibling `test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` still passes; `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-442c37df.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Never derive text from an already-KaTeX-rendered node with bare `textContent` — the hidden `.katex-mathml` annotation duplicates the raw TeX and leaks. And a hover definition that must show math/markdown cannot be a CSS `attr()` `::after` (plain-text only) — use a real DOM child element carrying the sanitized rendered HTML, marked `aria-hidden` + `user-select:none` and excluded from any `textContent`-based metric.


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode "Export to Markdown" 404s on REVIEW exports: proxy double-encodes the composite `lang` query param; fixed backend-authoritatively
- **Owner report.** "Many exports in Reader Mode aren't working — why does 'Export to Markdown' on the review interface give `{"error":"report not found","ok":false,"request_id":"35c2157f44fd"}`?"
- **Log forensics (smoking gun, that exact request_id).** `access.log`/`app.log` show `GET /api/v1/paper/report/export?paper_hash=…&lang=review%253Aneurips%253Aen&format=md 404`, Referer `…vscode-zw05.mlp.sankuai.com/proxy/15000/`. `%253A` = a DOUBLE-encoded colon (`:`→`%3A`→`%253A`). The VS Code web proxy re-encodes already-percent-encoded escapes in the query string; Quart decodes once, so `export_report` saw the literal `review%3Aneurips%3Aen` → no `paper_reports` row → 404. Confirmed the frontend bundle (`exportUrl` in api.js) is CORRECT (single-encodes `%3A`); the mangling is purely the proxy hop. DB rows are present and correct (`SELECT DISTINCT lang` → `en`, `zh`, `review:neurips:en`, `review:neurips:zh`); the endpoint returns 200 for the exact stored key.
- **Why "many but not all".** Plain REPORT exports use `lang=en`/`zh` — no reserved chars, nothing for the proxy to re-encode → always worked. Every REVIEW export uses the composite key `review:<venue>:en` (colons) → double-encoded → 404. Review *display* survives because it's a POST (`/report/cache`) with `lang` in the JSON BODY (proxies don't rewrite bodies) — only the GET export's query string breaks.
- **Fix (backend = single source of truth, `routes/paper.py::export_report`).** Before the `(paper_hash, lang)` lookup: `if '%' in lang: lang = unquote(lang)` (guarded, logged at debug) — peels the extra encode layer a double-encoding proxy leaves behind. Added `from urllib.parse import unquote`. Idempotent for correctly-encoded requests (`review:neurips:en` has no `%`, untouched) and for plain `en`/`zh`. Chose the backend over patching api.js because it's proxy-agnostic and the export is a plain browser navigation (anchor/`window.open`) we don't fully control.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** Manual endpoint probe: double-encoded review `%253A` → 200 (was 404), single-encoded `%3A` → 200, raw colon → 200, plain `en` → 200, genuinely-absent venue `review%253Aiclr%253Aen` → 404 (correct). New `tests/test_paper_export_double_encode.py` (2, live `server.app` + temp SQLite, seeds a `review:neurips:en` row): (1) double/single/raw review lang all export 200, plain report ok, absent venue 404; (2) **NC** monkeypatches `routes.paper.unquote` to a no-op → the double-encoded key 404s again (the exact production failure) while the raw-colon key still 200s (proving the row IS present and only the decode is at fault); restore → pass. `test_paper_review_mode.py` (12) still green; ruff + py_compile clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any GET whose query param can legitimately contain reserved chars (`:`, `/`, …) — here the composite Review-Mode cache key `review:<venue>:<uilang>` — must tolerate a double-encoding reverse proxy: `unquote` once when the value still carries `%XX`. State that must round-trip through a URL prefers a body (POST) or an opaque token over a colon-bearing query param. The frontend was correct; don't assume the wire matches the shipped code when a proxy sits in front — read `access.log` for the ACTUAL bytes.


### 2026-07-01 — Review Mode: ALWAYS educate straight → smart (curly) quotes on the final review body (backend-authoritative, math/code/URL-safe)
- **Owner directive.** "审稿模式一定要注意把所有的 dumb quote 变成 smart quote." A peer review must render with typographic quotes regardless of what the model emits — and per the project's architecture preference (backend = source of truth), this is NOT left to the prompt/model; the backend educates the quotes deterministically.
- **What / where.** New `lib/paper/review.py::smarten_quotes(text)` (+ helpers `_educate_segment`, `_PROTECT_RE`): straight `"`→`“`/`”`, `'`→`‘`/`’` (apostrophes/possessives/decade-elisions → `’`), applied ONLY to prose. The hard rule is that a straight quote which is SYNTAX rather than punctuation is preserved verbatim: it masks out KaTeX math (`$...$` / `$$...$$` — where `'` is a derivative prime, `"` a double-prime), inline/fenced code (`` `...` `` / ```` ```...``` ````), and URLs (`](...)` link targets, `<autolinks>`, bare `http(s)://`), educates the gaps, then restores the masked spans unchanged. Exported via the `lib.paper` facade. Wired in `lib/paper/report_engine.py::_run_report_task` — gated on `is_review_lang(lang)`, applied to `full_content` BEFORE image injection / DB persist / `done` event, so the enriched body, the `paper_reports` row, and the live stream all carry smart quotes. Plain explainer reports (same engine) are untouched.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_paper_review_smartquotes.py` (6 tests): prose curling; math/code/URL preservation with surrounding prose still educated (`It's $f'(x)$ said "so".` → curls the prose, keeps the prime); idempotence + quote-free no-op; engine-wiring proves a REVIEW body is curled (`"novel"` gone, `$f'(x)$` intact) while a PLAIN report keeps straight quotes. **NC PROVEN**: monkeypatching `rv.smarten_quotes` to a pass-through → the engine review body keeps `"novel"` and has no `“`, the positive assert FAILS; restore → curls again. All 6 pass; the existing `test_paper_review_mode.py` (12) still green; ruff + py_compile clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Typography normalization on model output is a backend post-process, not a prompt hope. When curling quotes in Markdown that also carries KaTeX, the ONLY safe implementation masks math/code/URL spans first — otherwise `$f'(x)$` primes and quoted URL params get corrupted. Keep it review-only (gated on the composite `review:` lang key); explainer reports are left as-is.


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode Review EN/中 translate button "translation failed": composite review `lang` colons leaked into the OPAQUE translate task_id → double-encoded `%253A` over the proxy tunnel → poll 404s forever
- **Owner report.** The translate button on the Review interface keeps toasting "translation failed".
- **Forensics (proven in `logs/error.log`).** Repeating `GET /api/v1/paper/translate/poll?task_id=tr_1782908385856_216bef0c_review%253Aneurips%253Azh&cursor=0 404`. `%253A` = a colon encoded TWICE. Review translation uses the COMPOSITE cache key `review:<venue>:zh` (colons) as the `lang`, and `routes/paper.py::start_translate_task` minted the task_id as `f'tr_{ts}_{phash[:8]}_{lang}'` — so the colons landed inside the OPAQUE task_id. The frontend echoes that id back into the poll query param (`Api.paper.translatePoll` → `_qs` single-encodes → `%3A`); the owner is on a VS Code proxy tunnel that re-encodes `%` (same signature as the codebase-wide `brain/summary?path=%252Fmnt...` 200s), so it arrives `%253A`. Server decodes once → `...review%3A...`, which never matches the runtime's raw-colon dict key → `_translate_runtime.get(task_id)` is None → 404 → the poll loop throws → the "translation failed" toast (`_setReviewLang` catch). The review REPORT path dodged this because it builds its id from `venue`+`ui_lang` joined with UNDERSCORES (`rvw_..._neurips_en`); the whole-paper Babel path only ever passes bare langs ('zh').
- **Fix (`routes/paper.py`, task_id mint only).** `lang_slug = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9]+', '_', lang).strip('_') or 'x'` → `task_id = f'tr_{ts}_{phash[:8]}_{lang_slug}'`. The task_id is opaque (grep-confirmed: never reverse-parsed anywhere), so slugifying only the id segment is safe; the REAL composite `lang` (with colons) still keys the cache lookup, dedup index, and `paper_translations` DB row unchanged. No frontend change needed — the client just echoes whatever id the server returns.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_paper_migration.py::test_translate_composite_lang_task_id_is_url_safe` drives the REAL `/api/v1/paper/translate/start` with `lang='review:neurips:zh'` (force=True, aborts the worker immediately), asserts `':' not in tid` + `quote(tid)==tid` + the composite lang still resolves in the dedup index + the same id round-trips through `/translate/poll` as **200 (not 404)**. **NC PROVEN**: reverting the mint to `..._{lang}` → test fails with `task_id leaked colons: 'tr_..._review:neurips:zh'`; byte-restored → 16/16 pass. ruff + `ast.parse` clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any OPAQUE handle echoed back into a URL (path OR query) must be URL-SAFE at MINT time — never splice a value that may contain `:` `/` `%`. Encoding at call time is insufficient: a proxy tunnel can double-encode `%`, and an exact dict-key `get()` then never matches. When a composite cache key doubles as (part of) a task id, sanitize the id while keeping the real key for the cache/dedup/DB.


### 2026-07-01 — "我的一天" cost cache: every conv/message delete was NUKING the whole daily_cost_cache (root cause of "历史开销不持久" + "每次点开加载很久")
- **Owner report.** My Day: historical per-day cost isn't persisted; opening a past month reloads for ~10s every time; task state handling feels off.
- **Forensics (proven).** The cost IS persisted — `daily_cost_cache` had 30 June rows in the DB. But `_delete_message_blocking` (`routes/conversations.py:777`) and `_delete_conv_blocking` (`:1151`) both called `invalidate_day_cost_cache()` with **NO argument** → `DELETE FROM daily_cost_cache WHERE user_id=?`, wiping ALL persisted days. Reproduced live: 30 rows → 0 after one no-arg call. Consequence chain: any delete wipes the whole table → next calendar open must live-rescan the entire month (`app.log`: `Monthly costs 2026-06: … (0 cache hits, 30 live-computed past days) in 10.07s`), vs `0.0s` on a warm cache. From the user's side the cost "never sticks" and every open is slow.
- **Fix — scoped invalidation.** New `lib/daily_report/cost.py::_cost_days_for_messages(messages, conv_start, conv_end)` (set of `'YYYY-MM-DD'` a message list contributes cost to — only `usage`-bearing messages count; timestamp fallback mirrors `_scan_costs_in_range`) + `invalidate_cost_cache_for_messages(...)` which calls the per-day `invalidate_day_cost_cache(date_str)` ONLY for the touched days. Exported from the package facade. Both delete handlers now capture the removed messages (delete_message: `_deleted_originals` snapshot before `pop`; delete_conv: SELECT messages+timestamps BEFORE the DELETE) and call the scoped helper — never the whole-table wipe. `invalidate_day_cost_cache(None)` (real bulk clear) is retained for genuine bulk operations.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** `tests/test_daily_report.py::TestScopedCostInvalidation` (5 tests): usage-only day extraction, timestampless→conv-span fallback, non-list tolerance, and the guard `assert None not in calls` (the delete path must NEVER pass None to the day-invalidator). NC proven: the old whole-table path passes `None` → the new assertion fails. Live DB probe: seed day10+day11, delete a day10 message → day10 gone, day11 survives. Full suite 38 passed; ruff clean; backend-only (no JS/bundle touched).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Cache invalidation must be SCOPED to what actually changed. A convenience "clear everything" call on a hot write path (delete) silently defeats a persistent cache and turns every subsequent read into a full rescan — the classic "cache that's always cold" anti-pattern. When a delete can only affect a bounded key set, invalidate exactly that set.
- **Still open (not yet addressed this session).** Owner also flagged task-STATUS handling feeling off — not yet diagnosed; the cost-persistence bug was the dominant, provable issue and was fixed first.


### 2026-07-01 — Autopilot fold: CENTRALIZED "run concluded" as a backend-authoritative fact + symmetric close-out (killed the frontend inference)
- **Why (owner).** The frontend's `_apRunConcluded` INFERRED run-end from client state — the last run folded only when `!activeStreams && !activeTaskId && !pendingCarrier`. That heuristic WAS the inter-turn-gap mis-fold's root class: between autopilot turns the stream is briefly gone AND `activeTaskId` briefly null, so "nothing in flight" is ALSO true mid-run. Worse, the two close-out paths were ASYMMETRIC: a clean `[VU: TASK_DONE]` emitted a run-level fact (`autopilot_summary` + sidecar summary), but a manual Stop / toggle-off / supersede emitted NOTHING — so the frontend had no choice but to guess. Directive: make the backend the single source of truth for "this run is over" and have the frontend READ it, not infer it.
- **Design (locked by owner — two hard constraints).** (1) **No `status:'running'` record** — persisting a mid-run marker into `settings` would be clobbered by `syncConversationToServer`'s whitelist rebuild (a PUT that doesn't yet hold the record wipes it). Only the TERMINAL fact is persisted. (2) **One map, not two** — extend the EXISTING `settings.autopilotSummaries[runId]` record (already whitelisted+tested) to carry BOTH the terminal fold-fact AND the optional report: `{runId, status:'concluded', reason:'task_done'|'stopped', content?, translatedContent?, ts, _summaryId}`. No parallel `autopilotRuns` map.
- **Backend (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`).** `_store_run_summary` → generalized into `_store_run_record(conv_id, run_id, *, reason, text='', translated='')` (monotonic RMW: `task_done` reason + report are STICKY, a later bare `stopped` never downgrades them); `_store_run_summary` kept as the `reason='task_done'` wrapper. New `conclude_run(conv_id, reason='stopped', run_id='')` — the manual-stop close-out seam: resolves the run id (pinned `autopilotRunId`, else the newest `_autopilotRunId` message stamp via `_resolve_recent_run_id`), writes the concluded record, clears the run pin. Wired symmetrically: (a) the clean-`TASK_DONE` branch now ALWAYS concludes (falls back to `_store_run_record(reason='task_done')` even when the reporter output is empty); (b) `disarm_autopilot` calls `conclude_run(reason='stopped')` and RETURNS the record as `result['runConcluded']` (so an idle disarm with no live SSE stream still folds instantly on the calling client). SSE event `autopilot_summary`→`autopilot_run_concluded` (payload `summary`→`record`); registry (`lib/agent_core/events.py`) renamed `AUTOPILOT_SUMMARY`→`AUTOPILOT_RUN_CONCLUDED`.
- **Frontend.** `_apRunConcluded` (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`) now reads ONLY `conv.autopilotSummaries[runId].status==='concluded'` (or structural supersede) — the entire `activeStreams`/`activeTaskId`/pending-carrier inference DELETED. `_handleAutopilotSummary`→`_handleAutopilotRunConcluded` (`streaming_render.js`) consumes `record`, tolerates legacy `summary`/`summaryMessage` field shapes, and merges monotonically (`_applyAutopilotRunConcluded`: a bare `stopped` never clobbers a `task_done` record with a report). New `_applyDisarmResponse` applies the disarm response's `runConcluded` and re-renders — wired into both disarm call sites (toggle-off `main_toolbar_ui.js`, queue-cancel `main_send_pipeline.js`). SSE dispatch (`sse_pipeline.js`) routes `autopilot_run_concluded` (legacy `autopilot_summary` type string dropped so the event-registry drift test stays green). Comment in `conversations.js` updated. Summary/record STILL never enters `conv.messages` (prior constraint preserved).
- **Verification (actual + BOTH required source-level NCs, both restored byte-identical).** **NC① (frontend)** — reverted `_apRunConcluded` to the old stream/task/carrier inference → `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_collapse_gating.py` failed EXACTLY: `gap_no_fold`, `gap_turns_unfolded` (inter-turn mis-fold returns), `record_folds_regardless_of_client_state` (old logic refuses to fold a concluded run while "busy"), `manual_idle_no_record_no_fold` (old logic folds an idle run with NO backend record — the premature-fold bug); clean-done/superseded/panel checks stayed green. **NC② (backend)** — made `conclude_run` a no-op returning None → `tests/test_autopilot_summary.py::test_conclude_run_writes_authoritative_stopped_record` failed at `assert rec is not None` (manual-stop fold depends on the backend write, not frontend inference). New tests: `test_conclude_run_writes_authoritative_stopped_record` (resolves run id + writes concluded(stopped) + clears pin), `test_store_run_record_manual_stop_is_concluded_without_report` (concluded, reason, NO content, not a message), `test_store_run_record_task_done_reason_is_sticky` (racing stop never downgrades task_done/report). Rewrote the collapse-gating harness to gate on the backend record (gaps no-fold because no record exists; manual-stop folds via a `stopped` record; independence-from-client-state case); rewrote the legacy `test_frontend_autopilot_fold.py` boundary-walk harness to supply a conv whose run ids are all concluded (the DOM range-walk only runs post-conclude). Full sweep: autopilot_summary(12) + kick + poll_handoff + event_registry + conv_message_builder + both fold suites + sse_dispatch = **88 passed**; ruff + `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-caf4e45c.js`. Direct functional probe on a bootstrapped SQLite DB confirmed `conclude_run` writes the record + clears the pin and `task_done` stickiness holds end-to-end.
- **Pre-existing, NOT mine.** `test_frontend_typecheck` regressed with 11 TS errors — ALL in `main.js`/`presence.js`/`project-brain.js`/`project.js` (a sibling "Project Brain" epic's undeclared `window.*` globals), NONE in any of the 5 JS files I touched; proven by scoping the failures. `test_autopilot_arm.py` `no such table` failures are the known bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact (fail at the test's first setup line `clear_autopilot_marker`, in untouched code; the schema is only created when `server.app` boots).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A multi-turn autonomous run's fold timing is a BACKEND fact, not a client inference — never gate a fold on absence-of-stream/task/carrier (that's true in the inter-turn gap too). Persist ONLY the terminal fact (a `running` marker races the frontend's whitelist-rebuild PUT), keep ONE per-run record carrying both status and the optional report, and make BOTH close-out paths (clean TASK_DONE + manual stop/disarm) write it symmetrically — the manual path must also return the record so an idle disarm folds without a reload. Bite it two ways: an NC that reverts the frontend to inference, and an NC that neuters the backend write.


### 2026-07-01 — Autopilot armed-marker "stuck in queue" fixed at the frontend gate: the sentinel is never dispatchable, so it must not count toward the queue badge / dispatch-poll (backend was already correct)
- **Owner report + diagnosis.** "autopilot接管在队列里的排出很不顺畅 — is this a frontend-only component with no backend?" NO: the backend is complete and correct. `lib/message_queue.py` models the autopilot armed-marker as a distinct non-dispatchable turn source (`KIND_AUTOPILOT`, priority 90); `dequeue_next` + `_get_queue_depth` BOTH exclude it (`kind!=KIND_AUTOPILOT`) because it's a persistent flag the end-of-turn hook consults, not a turn that ever gets dequeued & started as a task. So it's not a fake/unfinished feature — the owner's instinct ("once autopilot has taken over, treat it as dispatched, not queued") matched the backend's existing semantics; the FRONTEND just wasn't mirroring them.
- **Root cause (3 frontend gates using raw Map length).** Several gates used `pendingMessageQueue.get(convId).length > 0` as "there's pending work the backend will start next", which the sentinel falsely inflates: (1) the Stop-button badge (`static/js/ui/send_button.js:45`) rendered `queue-badge` = 1 for an armed-but-idle autopilot → looks like a message permanently stuck in the queue; (2) `finishStream` (`static/js/ui/stream_lifecycle.js`) inserted a "Dispatching queued message…" ghost bubble + fired `_checkForQueuedTask` hunting a dispatch that never comes (the doomed retry-with-backoff loop = the "排出不顺畅"); (3) `finishStream` skipped `syncConversationToServer` expecting a backend dispatch. (`renderPendingQueueUI`'s own header ALREADY excluded the sentinel via `_realCount`, so only these gates were wrong.)
- **Fix — one shared helper mirroring the backend.** New `_dispatchableQueueCount(convId)` in `main/main_send_pipeline.js` = `pendingMessageQueue.get(convId).filter(it => it.kind !== 'autopilot').length`, the frontend twin of `_get_queue_depth`. Routed the badge (`send_button.js`), the `_checkForQueueTask` retry gate + both `finishStream` gates (`stream_lifecycle.js`) through it, all `typeof`-guarded (helper is defined in a bundle file loaded AFTER its callers, but every call is inside a runtime function body). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-b1848108.js` (11 `_dispatchableQueueCount` refs present).
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_queue_badge.py` (bare-node, `unit`): loads the REAL shipped `send_button.js` + the REAL `_dispatchableQueueCount` (sliced verbatim out of `main_send_pipeline.js` via regex, so the test bites the actual logic) and drives 3 queue states — sentinel-only → badge hidden, real+sentinel → badge 1, two reals → badge 2. **NC PROVEN**: neutering the helper to `return q.length` → the sentinel-only + real+sentinel cases FAIL (`badge_hidden_for_sentinel_only`, `badge_one_with_sentinel` — the screenshot bug reproduced), the two-reals regression guard stays PASS; byte-identical restore (bundle hash returns to `b1848108`) → 8/8 PASS. `node --check` clean on all 3 files; the sibling node-based autopilot suites (`test_frontend_autopilot_fold` / `_collapse_gating`) still pass. (The `sqlite3 no such table` failures in `test_message_queue`/`test_autopilot_arm` are the documented bare-CI DB-bootstrap artifact — this change is pure frontend JS, zero Python touched.)
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The autopilot sentinel is a NON-DISPATCHABLE turn source: every frontend gate meaning "is there pending work the backend will start next?" must use `_dispatchableQueueCount`, never the raw `pendingMessageQueue` Map length — otherwise an armed-but-idle autopilot looks like a stuck queued message and spins a doomed dispatch-poll loop. The single frontend helper is the deliberate mirror of the backend's `_get_queue_depth`; keep them in lockstep.


### 2026-07-01 — Paper Reading Mode: vanishing-upload FIXED at the root (server-authoritative ingest + PAPER_DIR-missing guard) + per-paper EN/中 language toggle for report & review
- **Owner report + forensics (real bug, proven in `logs/app.log`).** Owner uploaded a PDF; it vanished on exit. Two coupled root causes: (1) **ENOENT on write** — `routes/paper.py::upload_paper` did `open(filepath,'wb')` but `PAPER_DIR` (`uploads/papers/`) is only `os.makedirs`'d ONCE at import in `lib/paper/hashing.py:17`; on this FUSE/cross-DC mount it was gone at write time → `2026-07-01 15:46:05 [ERROR] [Paper:Upload] Failed to save …: [Errno 2] No such file or directory` → the whole upload 500'd and the PDF bytes were LOST. (2) **fire-and-forget persistence** — the ingest endpoints never wrote the `paper_library` row themselves; they relied on the client's best-effort `libraryUpsert` PUT (`.catch`-swallowed, un-awaited). A tab-close/refresh that raced (or, on the 500, replaced) the PUT left a **ghost `qa=0 imgs=0` row with no PDF/hash** (also in the log) — the exact screenshot: entry in the bookshelf, PDF pane on the empty landing.
- **THE REAL FIX is #2, not #1 (server-authoritative ingest).** New `routes/paper.py::_persist_ingested_library_row(paper_id, …)` writes the bookshelf row at INGEST time via `_core_schema.upsert(PAPER_LIBRARY, …, retry=True)`, preserving an existing row's `created_at`/`qa_history`/`babel_cache`. Wired into BOTH ingest paths: `upload_paper` (after a successful disk write) and `fetch_arxiv_stream` (at the `done` SSE stage, on the generator thread). The client mints the bookshelf id UP FRONT (`_newPaperEntryId()`) and sends it — upload as a `paper_id` form field, arxiv-fetch as a body key — so the server-persisted row and the client entry share ONE id (endpoint echoes `id`). A paper now survives even if the client PUT never lands.
- **#1 makedirs guard (necessary but insufficient).** `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(filepath), exist_ok=True)` added before every PDF write (`upload_paper`, `fetch_arxiv_stream`, sync `fetch_arxiv`) — kills the ENOENT.
- **Client hardening (`static/js/paper-reader.js`, `api.js`).** `_saveActivePaperState` now RETURNS the persist promise; both ingest flows `await` the first persist (exit/refresh can't race it; `beforeunload` is a backstop only). On upload/fetch FAILURE the optimistically-created entry is REMOVED (`_paperLibrary.filter` + `_setActivePaperId('')` + re-render) so a failed ingest never leaves a ghost row. `_createPaperEntry` accepts an explicit id; `upload` API gained a `paper_id` form field; `fetchArxivStream(url, paperId)`.
- **Feature — per-paper EN/中 language toggle (report + review).** Owner: switch report/review between EN & 中, and the review toggle must be **bidirectional + always visible** (was gated on UI=zh). **Report**: generation language is now a PER-PAPER persisted choice (`_PAPER_REPORT_LANG_KEY` map, like the review-venue map), derived fresh from `_activePaperId` each call (no module global to drift), default = current UI lang; `_setReportLang` persists + resets local state + drops the in-mem cache + reloads → really regenerates against the `(paper_hash, lang)` cache key. **Review**: English stays canonical (generated/cached/exported); `_setReviewLang` is bidirectional — '中' shows the on-demand Babel translation under the distinct composite key `review:<venue>:zh` (never regenerates the English), 'EN' restores the original; per-paper persisted (`_PAPER_REVIEW_LANG_KEY`), always available regardless of `_i18nLang`. `_toggleReviewTranslation` kept as a thin compat wrapper. HTML: EN/中 segmented control (`.paper-report-lang-toggle`) in both toolbars (review's replaces the old translate button); CSS + i18n `paper.reportLangTitle` (EN+ZH) added; bundle `bundle-f4fe2078.js`.
- **Verification (actual + BITING NCs).** New `tests/test_paper_ingest_persist.py` (3, live `server.app` + temp SQLite + `init_db()`): upload persists the row with ZERO client PUTs; **NC** no-`paper_id` → no row (id-driven); upload into a MISSING `PAPER_DIR` succeeds via the guard. **Both NCs proven**: (a) comment the upload `makedirs` → missing-dir test 500s (vanish reproduced); (b) `if False and client_paper_id` → zero-PUT persist test fails ("ingest did not persist"); byte-restored → pass. New `tests/test_frontend_paper_lang_toggle.py` (jsdom, 14 checks) drives the real shipped `paper-reader.js`: report default→zh persist+regenerate-in-zh+reload+back-to-en; review default-en→zh-translates-not-regenerates (works with `_i18nLang='en'`)→persist→back-to-en-restores-English. **Both NCs proven**: no-op `_persistReportLang` → report persistence checks fail; `_setReviewLang('zh')` early-return → review translate/show/persist checks fail; restored → pass. Full: ingest 3 + lang-toggle 1 + regen-refresh 1 + report-abort 6 = **11 passed**; migration+review under pytest = 26 passed (the 1 `test_review_and_report_rows_coexist` failure is the PRE-EXISTING `no such table: paper_reports` bootstrap artifact — fails identically on the untouched tree). ruff + py_compile + `node --check` clean; i18n EN+ZH parity verified; `paper-reader.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Server-owned artifacts (PDF bytes, bookshelf rows) must be persisted by the SERVER at ingest — a fire-and-forget client PUT is not durable and races tab-close; and a failed ingest must clean up its optimistic client entry, never leave a ghost. A dir created once at import is NOT safe on a FUSE/cross-DC mount — re-`makedirs(exist_ok=True)` at every write. A "language switch" that shares one cache key space is really TWO different behaviours: report REGENERATES per `(hash,lang)`; review TRANSLATES (English canonical) — model them separately, persist per-paper, and never gate a reading toggle on the app UI language.

- **FOLLOW-UP (owner-directed, same session) — reap PRE-EXISTING ghost rows + prove the arxiv SSE-thread persist end-to-end.** The ingest fix stops NEW ghosts, but the owner's screenshot IS an OLD ghost already in the DB — leaving it renders the exact broken row we diagnosed. (1) `GET /api/v1/paper/library` now HARD-SKIPS ghost rows via new `routes/paper.py::_is_ghost_library_row(paper)` — a row is a ghost when `pdfFilename` is empty OR its file is missing from `PAPER_DIR`; logs `Reaped N ghost row(s)` at info. **NON-DESTRUCTIVE by design**: skipped, NOT deleted — a FUSE/cross-DC flap can transiently report a real file missing (a stat `OSError` is treated as NOT-ghost so a real paper is never hidden), and a recovered mount makes the paper reappear on the next listing; deletion would be irreversible loss on a transient error. (2) Confirmed the `fetch-arxiv-stream` persist runs on the SSE GENERATOR THREAD with a live DB conn — `_pool_get`/`_pool_put` is a module-level threading-lock pool, **context-free** (no Quart app/request context), the identical path the sync upload handler uses.
- **Verification (+3 tests, all NCs bite).** `tests/test_paper_ingest_persist.py` now 6 (was 3): ghost-reap (seed empty-`pdf_filename` row → excluded from listing, healthy kept; **NC** patch `_is_ghost_library_row`→`False` → ghost REAPPEARS; restore → gone); reap-is-non-destructive (row still `COUNT=1` in DB after listing); **arxiv-stream E2E** drives the REAL `/api/paper/fetch-arxiv-stream` (mocked `http_get`+`parse_pdf`+`fetch_arxiv_title`), drains the SSE to the `done` stage, asserts the row persisted with ZERO client PUTs — **NC** `if False and client_paper_id` at the generator-thread persist → the E2E test FAILS (row absent), proving the persist is what creates the row AND that it genuinely executes on that thread; byte-restored → pass. Full: ingest 6 + lang-toggle 1 + regen-refresh 1 + report-abort 6 + migration 15 = **29 passed** under pytest; ruff clean.


### 2026-07-01 — Reading-Mode Review "Stop is not smooth": 3 real bugs — (1) Stop button hidden during the 10–40s /start, (2) phantom "Failed" from a 30s client timeout, (3) backend keeps searching ~94s after Stop
- **Owner report (审稿 Stop 很不丝滑).** Picked the wrong model → only 重新生成, no 停止; switched model + 重新生成 → generation "报错了" (the `Failed`/`重试` screenshot); meanwhile 后台还在大量产生搜索. All THREE reproduced verbatim in `logs/app.log` + `error.log`.
- **Log forensics (smoking guns).** (a) `POST /report/start 200 SLOW (36.754s)` — the start round-trip does heavy SYNCHRONOUS prep (image-manifest extraction, injection sanitize, prompt build) for 10–40s BEFORE it returns a task_id. (b) `reportStart` used the api.js DEFAULT 30s client timeout → the 36.7s start blew the AbortController → the `catch` painted `Failed` while the server task ran on orphaned (client never learned the task_id). (c) `Force regen — aborting old task rvw_671541` at 19:01:21, but that task's `web_search → 2505085 chars in 94.6s` finished at 19:02:55 → `stopped by user — 0 chars in 103.8s`: **94 s of searches AFTER Stop**, because `run_batch_concurrent` was not abort-aware — an in-flight batch ran to completion. Stacking two rapid force-regens (19:01:21 + 19:01:46) multiplied concurrent searching tasks = "大量搜索".
- **Fix 1 — Stop visible immediately (`static/js/paper-reader.js`).** `_generatePaperReport` now creates a PROVISIONAL running stream (`_makeReportStreamState(..., taskId='')`) + `_syncReportToolbar(true)` BEFORE the `await reportStart`, so Stop shows the instant generation is requested (was only shown AFTER the slow start returned). New `stream.pendingStop` flag: `_stopPaperReport` with no task_id yet sets `pendingStop` instead of silently no-oping; the post-start attach reads it and fires `_stopPaperReport(view)` the moment the real task_id lands → a Stop pressed during the 10–40s window is honoured, not dropped. Provisional stream is cleared on the cache-hit path, the error `catch`, so no task_id-less zombie stream can be resume-polled later.
- **Fix 2 — no phantom "Failed" (`static/js/api.js`).** `reportStart` now `timeout: 0` (was default 30s). A task-start endpoint that spawns a background job must not carry a client deadline that manufactures a failure while the server succeeds; the task is polled afterwards. (Review reuses the same endpoint, so this covers both tabs.)
- **Fix 3 — Stop actually halts searches (backend, root cause).** `run_batch_concurrent(..., abort=predicate)` (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/_adapter.py`): a `() -> bool` checked at the START of every worker slot; when it trips, not-yet-started items short-circuit to `None` instead of firing. Threads already running can't be killed, but the pool serialises beyond `max_workers`, so the queued tail is skipped — a Stopped report stops spraying dozens more queries. Threaded through `_execute_report_tool(..., abort=)` → both `web_search`/`fetch_url` batch calls, and both engines pass `abort_signal.is_set` (report_engine + qa_engine). A raising predicate is treated as "not aborted" so it can never wedge a batch.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** `tests/test_paper_report_abort.py` +2 (now 6): `test_batch_runner_skips_queued_items_after_abort` (max_workers=1, first worker sets the event → ≤3 of 20 run, rest skipped `None`) + `test_batch_runner_no_abort_runs_all` (regression guard: no predicate → every item runs). **NC PROVEN**: neutering the guard to `if False and abort():` → all 20 items run (`ran 20/20`, the bug), test FAILS; byte-identical restore (`diff` empty) → 6/6 pass. QA mock `_fake_tool` signature updated for the new `abort` kwarg → qa_agentic 10/10. injection_guard 10/10, report_dedup 4/4 unchanged. ruff + py_compile + `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-f4fe2078.js` (contains `pendingStop` + `reportStart timeout:0`).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "start task then poll" endpoint must (1) show its Stop affordance BEFORE the start round-trip (which can be slow), (2) carry NO client timeout on start (a background-spawning POST that times out client-side leaves an orphan + a phantom error), and (3) record a Stop pressed pre-task-id so it fires when the id arrives. And cooperative abort must reach the LEAF concurrency primitive: an abort seam that stops the round loop but not the in-flight tool BATCH still lets ~1.5 min of searches run — the batch runner itself must honour the same abort signal.

### 2026-07-01 — Fixed the `[poll] Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')` client-error spam (real production bug in the poll fallback)
- **Symptom (from `logs/error.log`).** Recurring ERROR lines tied to REAL conversation IDs + the real VS Code proxy URL: `[CLIENT-ERROR] [poll] Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')`. Logged at ERROR (not WARN) because `routes/common.py::client_error` only downgrades `[debuglog]`-prefixed messages. A benign VS Code tunnel blip was surfacing as a scary null-deref, masking the real cause (network) and polluting the log.
- **Root cause.** `static/js/ui/sse_poll_fallback.js::_pollFallback` polls via `Api.chat.poll(taskId)`, which is declared with `onError:'null'` (`static/js/api.js`) — so a network failure (fetch throws / tunnel drop) resolves to `null`, NOT a Response. The guard `if (!resp || !resp.ok)` correctly caught it, but then fell through to `throw new Error(\`Poll HTTP ${resp.status}\`)` — dereferencing `.status` on the `null` `resp`. That deref ITSELF threw the TypeError, which the catch block forwarded to `_reportClientError`. The circuit-breaker/recovery machinery downstream was already correct; the ONLY bug was the exception message.
- **Fix (one line + comment).** `throw new Error(resp ? \`Poll HTTP ${resp.status}\` : 'Poll network error (no response)')`. A null resp now feeds the existing consecutive-error counter → health check → 2-min recovery-wait path a clean message.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_frontend_poll_null_resp.py` (bare-node harness, `unit`) loads the REAL shipped `sse_poll_fallback.js`, stubs the window globals, makes `Api.chat.poll` return `null` once then aborts the stream, and asserts the message handed to `_reportClientError` is the clean network message and does NOT match `cannot read propert`. **NC PROVEN**: reverting the throw to `\`Poll HTTP ${resp.status}\`` → the captured message becomes the EXACT production log line `[poll] Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')` and the test FAILS; byte-identical restore → pass. `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-cac943c7.js` (`sse_poll_fallback.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`).
- **Triage note for next session.** `logs/error.log`/`app.log` are ~90% test-suite negative-control artifacts (fake conv IDs `nonexistent`/`convhallu`/`task_hal`/`/proj/race`, fake models `limmodel_*`/`ctxmodel_*`, `deadbeef` session IDs, intentional `RuntimeError`, `roundtrip_test.pdf`, `no such table: conversations/task_results/timer_watchers` from bare-CI bootstrap). The `test_endpoint_poll_recovery.py` `no such table: conversations` failures are pre-existing bare-env bootstrap artifacts, unrelated. Filter noise; key on REAL conv IDs + real URLs when hunting genuine production bugs.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Any consumer of an `Api.*` helper declared with `onError:'null'` MUST treat a `null` return as "network failure", never assume a Response — a `?.` or a `resp ?` ternary at every `resp.status`/`resp.json()` site. Same class as any optional-chaining gap on an error path that only fires under a network drop (rarely exercised in dev).


### 2026-07-01 — paper.py's 3 ABORT endpoints migrated to the `register_task_routes` factory; POLL stays custom (documented) — slice #3 of the same-interface effort
- **Why.** `routes/paper.py` hand-rolled 6 poll/abort endpoints (report/qa/translate × 2) that wrap `TaskRuntime` instances but re-implement cursor replay + manual `task['abort_event'].set()`, while `routes/api_v1/orchestrations.py` already uses the shared `register_task_routes` factory correctly. The abort halves are uniform → prime dedup target.
- **Decision: (b) — migrate ABORT now, keep POLL custom.** Three hard blockers make factory-poll too invasive this slice: (1) **response shape** — paper poll emits engine-specific keys (`report`/`answer`/`text`/`partial`/`progress`/`meta`/`resolvedTitle`/`paper_hash`), but the workers set `task['status']`/`task['full_text']` DIRECTLY and never call `runtime.finish()`, so `task['result']` is None → the generic `runtime.poll()` would return NO report body; (2) **URL shape** — paper poll is `?task_id=` (query) vs the factory's `/<task_id>` (path); (3) **named coupling** — the `/api/v1/agents/paper/*` façade name-calls `poll_report_task`/`poll_translate_task` (`agents.py:196,222`). Abort has none of these: uniform, not name-called, and aligning to `/abort/<task_id>` matches orchestrations' `/run/abort/<id>`. Documented the poll deferral (needs a factory response-enricher hook) in a block comment at the registration site.
- **Factory contract confirmed.** `register_task_routes(bp, runtime, *, url_prefix, enable_poll, enable_abort, ...)`: abort → `POST <prefix>/abort/<task_id>`, calls `runtime.abort(task_id)` which sets `task['abort_event'].set()` **under `runtime._lock`** — the SAME event `AbortSignal.from_event` reads (slice #2), and STRONGER than the old bare `.set()` (atomic status-check can't mark a racing finish 'done'). Endpoint names `task_abort_<safe_kind>` — the 3 runtimes have distinct kinds (`paper-report`/`paper-qa`/`paper-translate`), no collision on the shared blueprint. Called with `enable_poll=False` ×3 at the end of paper.py.
- **What changed.** Deleted the 3 async `abort_*_task` handlers; added the import + 3 `register_task_routes(..., enable_poll=False)` calls. Frontend `api.js` `reportAbort`/`qaAbort`/`translateAbort` moved from `POST …/abort {task_id}` (body) to `POST …/abort/${encodeURIComponent(taskId)}` (path). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-bd3e87c7.js`.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC).** New `tests/test_paper_migration.py::test_all_factory_abort_routes_set_event` drives ALL THREE factory abort routes end-to-end against the live `server.app`: asserts each reaches the RUNNING task (`abort_event.is_set()`) + 404 on unknown. Updated 2 existing tests to the path-segment URL + shape. **NC PROVEN**: replacing `ok = runtime.abort(task_id)` with a falsey no-op in `_task_routes.py::_abort` → both the report-abort test AND the new all-three test FAIL (`assert False` on `is_set()` — abort never reaches the task, falls through to the "already finished" branch); byte-identical restore (`git diff` empty) → pass. `test_frontend_backend_contract.py` 3/3 (the 3 factory abort routes resolve against the live `url_map`; the query→path client change still matches), `test_frontend_api_isolation.py` ratchet green, `test_agent_poll_routes.py` (façade poll still name-calls the retained custom handlers) green. Full sweep = 56 passed; migration 15/15 standalone. ruff + py_compile + `node --check api.js` clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A factory migration is only safe where the endpoint is UNIFORM — abort (set-event + ok/404) fits; poll does NOT when the worker sets task fields directly instead of `runtime.finish()` (so `runtime.poll()` can't see the result) AND a façade name-calls the handler. Migrate the uniform half, document why the other stays, and prove the shared seam actually carries the behaviour with an NC that toggles the factory's one wiring line and drives an END-TO-END adopter test. The abort URL moved from body-key to path-segment — a frontend-visible change — so the api.js clients + the contract test are part of the same atomic change.
- **FOLLOW-UP (explicit, next seam) — migrate paper POLL to the factory by fixing the ROOT CAUSE, not by bolting enrichers on.** The reason poll can't use the factory today is structural: the paper report/qa/translate workers mutate `task['status']`/`task['full_text']`/`task['tool_rounds']`/`task['progress']` DIRECTLY and never call `runtime.finish(result=…)`, so `runtime.poll()` has no `task['result']` to return — the report/answer body would be missing. The correct fix is to route the workers' terminal write through `runtime.finish(result={...})` (packing report/answer/text/partial/progress/meta/resolvedTitle/paper_hash into the canonical result envelope) so the SHARED `runtime.poll()` carries the body, THEN switch `enable_poll=True` and drop the 3 custom poll handlers. Do NOT add per-key response-enricher hooks to `register_task_routes` — that would re-scatter engine-specific shape into the factory, the opposite of this effort's intent. Two coupled edges to update in the same change: (1) the frontend `reportPoll`/`qaPoll`/`translatePoll` clients move from `?task_id=` (query) to the factory's `/poll/<task_id>` (path); (2) the `/api/v1/agents/paper/*` façade currently NAME-CALLS `poll_report_task`/`poll_translate_task` (`agents.py:196,222`) — repoint it at the factory routes (or the runtime) before deleting the handlers. Gate the whole change on the contract test + an end-to-end poll NC that proves the report body survives round-trip through `runtime.poll()`.


### 2026-07-01 — Shared agent-loop seam `lib/agent_loop.py` (AbortSignal + run_agent_loop); first adopters report_engine + qa_engine (slice #2 of the same-interface effort)
- **Why.** The tool-*execution* layer (`_execute_tool_one` + `ingest_tool_call`) and the SSE layer (`_sse_core`) are already single-seam, but every engine still hand-rolls the `for rnd in range(max+1)` shell + its abort plumbing, and the abort SIGNAL itself is spelled three incompatible ways: `threading.Event` (paper report/QA `task['abort_event']`), a `task['aborted']` flag (chat orchestrator/endpoint), and an `abort_check` callback (swarm). `report_engine` + `qa_engine` were near-verbatim twins of the same loop. Isolated slice; scoped to ONLY these two adopters.
- **The seam (`lib/agent_loop.py`, new).** (a) `AbortSignal` wraps ANY of the three mechanisms behind one `.aborted` predicate; it's also callable and exposes `.is_set()` so it drops straight into `dispatch_stream(abort_check=…)`. Classmethods `from_event` / `from_task_flag(key='aborted')` / `from_callback` / `never`; a broken predicate is caught+logged (never wedges the loop). (b) `run_agent_loop(*, abort, max_tool_rounds, round_tools, dispatch, execute_tool, on_round_result=None, on_tool_round=None) -> LoopOutcome` owns the round loop + the THREE abort checks — **(1) before-round**, **(2) post-stream**, **(3) between-tools** — promoting report_engine's proven triple placement to the default. Round `max_tool_rounds` is offered `tools=None`. Everything engine-specific stays in the caller via `dispatch(rnd,tools)->(msg,finish,usage)` / `execute_tool(rnd,tc)` / the two hooks. The loop deliberately does NOT catch exceptions, so a dispatcher `AbortedError` reaches the caller's own handler unchanged.
- **Adopters.** `report_engine._run_report_task` + `qa_engine._run_qa_task` rewired: the inline `for rnd` bodies became `_dispatch` / `_execute_tool` closures + `_begin_tool_round` (interim-draft discard, the `## TL;DR`-rendered-twice fix) + `_accumulate_usage` (report only) hooks; per-round content buffer moved to a shared `_round={'content':''}` holder so `_dispatch` (reset) and `_begin_tool_round` (discard) share it. All emitted events, usage accumulation, title/enrich/persist tail, and the `AbortedError`/`Exception` handlers are byte-for-byte preserved. NOT touched (adopt later, higher risk): orchestrator (premature-retry ceiling + dangling-round sweep), endpoint, swarm, timer.
- **Verification (actual + biting NC on check 3).** New `tests/test_agent_loop.py` (11, `unit`): the 3 AbortSignal wrappers + broken-predicate safety + the 3 check placements + final-round-gets-`None` + exception-propagation. **NC PROVEN end-to-end through the seam**: patching the between-tools check to `if False and abort.aborted:` in `run_agent_loop` → the EXISTING `test_paper_report_abort.py::test_abort_between_tool_calls_stops_before_running_tools` FAILS with `second tool ran despite abort: 2` (the "Stop has limited effect" bug reproduced via the shared seam, driving the REAL `_run_report_task`); byte-identical restore → 4/4. Full sweep: agent_loop 11 + report_abort 4 + qa_agentic 10 + injection_guard 10 + report_dedup 4 + review_fixes 21 = **60 passed**; review_mode 12/12 standalone. The 1 `test_review_and_report_rows_coexist` failure under a combined pytest run is the PRE-EXISTING bootstrap artifact (`no such table: paper_reports`) — fails identically in complete isolation with its own bootstrap, unrelated to this change (already documented). ruff + py_compile clean on seam + both engines + the new test.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When N engines share a loop shape but differ in I/O, extract the CONTROL FLOW + the abort-check placements into a seam and inject the I/O as closures/hooks — the loop must NOT catch exceptions (let `AbortedError` propagate) and must keep the between-tools check as a hard default (it's the "Stop during a slow tool" fix). A biting NC that toggles the seam's check and drives an EXISTING end-to-end adopter test proves the abstraction preserves the original behaviour. `AbortSignal` unifying the three mechanisms means the next adopters (swarm callback, chat/endpoint `task['aborted']` flag, timer via `never()`) need no re-plumbing — only their loop shell swaps.


### 2026-07-01 — Project Brain panel: fixed the "all blank / ugly" report — (1) empty-backfill left the Activity column a permanent VOID, (2) shell-loaded convs lost the path, (3) empty-state CSS polish
- **Owner report + forensics (backend was NOT the bug).** Owner: 项目大脑「都是空白的、渲染很丑」. Ruled the backend OUT by direct probe on the exact active path `/mnt/.../chatui`: `read_board` → 1 (now 2–3) done epic, `read_project_feed` → 72 events, `build_brain_summary` → `epicsDone:1, activePeers:2` — all correct. Served `bundle-3432735d.js` was byte-identical to disk and contained every project-brain symbol; `styles-c8ee9392.css` had all `.pb-*` rules; served-hash == `get_styles_hash()`. So the "blank" was a pure FRONTEND render defect, not stale bundle / missing data / wrong table (the feed table is `project_events`, not the mis-named `project_feed` — verified). NOTE the tofu theme resolves its vars (`--bg-secondary:#EDEBE2` etc.), so it's not an unstyled-var issue either.
- **Root-cause bug — blank Activity VOID (`static/js/project-brain.js`).** `openFeed()` calls `closeFeed()` first, which does `list.innerHTML=''` — wiping the shipped `.pb-activity-empty` ("暂无动态") placeholder. The async backfill then renders rows; but when the backfill returns ZERO events (a brand-new project, or a project whose pulse hasn't landed yet) NOTHING is rendered and the placeholder is NEVER restored → the column is a permanent empty void (exactly the screenshot). `renderBoard`/`renderCharter` both emit their own empty-state, so only the FEED path had this gap. Fix: new `_ensureActivityEmptyState()` (re-inserts the placeholder iff the list has no `.pb-activity-row`), called in BOTH the backfill `.then` and `.catch`.
- **Secondary fix — path resolution for shell-loaded convs.** `_displayedProjectPath()` resolved ONLY `getActiveConv()→_getConvProjectPath(conv)`; a conversation loaded as a sidebar shell may not carry `projectPath` in-memory yet even though the active-project singleton `projectState.path` is set → panel opened with an empty path → every column empty. Added a fallback to `projectState.active && projectState.path` (mirrors how the rest of the app resolves the active project), keeping the trailing-slash strip.
- **Visual polish (CSS-only, `static/styles.css`).** Column bodies are now `flex-direction:column` so empty states can center; `.pb-activity-empty` / `.pb-charter-empty` / `.pb-board-empty` are `flex:1; align/justify:center; min-height:180px` (were top-clinging `padding:24px` blocks → the "很丑" flat look); column heads gained `background:var(--bg-tertiary)` for stronger separation on the low-contrast tofu palette; `.pb-board-lane-empty` kept as a small inline dash (per-lane, not per-column).

- **THE REAL ROOT CAUSE (owner-pushed; I'd wrongly waved it off first pass) — trailing-slash write/read key divergence.** The board showed 任务板为空 while epics existed. The write side (agent tools → `emit_project_event` / `post_task` / presence / `ensure_project_state`) keys on `mcfg['project_path']` = the raw `conv.projectPath` (frontend `_getConvProjectPath` returns it verbatim, NOT slash-stripped). The read side (`project-brain.js` `_displayedProjectPath` + `presence.js` `_norm`) strips trailing slashes with `.replace(/[/\\]+$/, '')`. So a `conv.projectPath` carrying a trailing slash writes rows under `/proj/x/` but the panel queries `/proj/x` → MISS → empty board/feed/charter despite data. PROVEN: `read_board('/…/chatui')` → done=3, but `read_board('/…/chatui/')` → done=0 (both hit the live route: no-slash `200` with data, slash `200` empty). Today's stored rows are all clean, so it's latent-but-real — an asymmetric normalization across the read/write boundary is a bug regardless of current data.
- **Root-cause fix — one canonical seam `normalize_project_path` (`lib/conversations/project_feed.py`).** Strips trailing `/`+`\\` to match the frontend regex byte-for-byte.
