### 2026-06-30 — Cross-conversation presence: (1) fixed broadcast-under-lock in the 4 mutators, (2) shipped slice 2 — `static/js/presence.js` pure-render "who's working here" strip + conflict callouts, proven end-to-end under jsdom
- **Why (owner review of slice 1).** Owner accepted the backend slice (16/16 green, wiring real, negative control genuine) but flagged ONE real defect and required slice 2 before the task is "done" (the objective — "see who's writing, like a shared doc" — is not demonstrable without the frontend).
- **Fix 1 — broadcast OUTSIDE the lock.** `announce`/`heartbeat`/`record_files`/`mark_idle` (lib/presence/registry.py) called `_emit_peer_update` (→ `push_event`) while still holding the global `_lock` — a latency / lock-ordering hazard under real concurrency (many tabs, many roots), exactly this feature's scenario. The `sweep` path already did it right (collect under lock, broadcast after release). Refactored all four to mutate+persist under the lock, capture a `_decorate(peer, now)` copy, then `_broadcast` after release. `_maybe_emit_conflicts` also now snapshots `_active_peers` UNDER the lock before detection+broadcast (the read could otherwise race a concurrent mutation). New `test_mutators_broadcast_outside_lock`: a probe `push_event` tries to acquire `_lock` non-blocking FROM A SEPARATE THREAD (RLock is re-entrant on the caller) — any failure = lock held during broadcast = defect. **Negative control PROVEN:** reverting `announce` to broadcast inside the lock makes the test FAIL; restore → PASS, byte-identical.
- **Slice 2 — `static/js/presence.js` (pure render).** `pushSubscribe('presence','*')` → mirrors frames into `root→Map<convId,peer>` + `root→Map<path,conflict>`; renders ONLY the displayed conversation's project root (`getActiveConv` + `_getConvProjectPath`), EXCLUDING the viewed conv (no self-cursor). Paints title + the backend-formed `statusLabel` VERBATIM + a relative time it formats from `lastBeatTs` (the ONLY computation it does) + conflict `message` strings VERBATIM. Fingerprint-gated DOM writes; a 5s tick refreshes relative times + expires conflicts (30s TTL) + picks up conv switches (NOT a server poll). `window.presenceRefresh` hook called from `_restoreConvToolState` (main.js) so the strip re-filters instantly on conv switch. Hidden entirely when solo (no clutter). SVG glyphs only (§3.4, no emoji). Mount: `#presenceStrip` in `.chat-wrapper` (index.html); CSS `.presence-*` in styles.css (pulse dot, peer rows, amber conflict callout). i18n `presence.*` (zh+en). Registered in `_BUNDLE_FILES` after main.js + dev-fallback `<script>` tag.
- **Event contract — now frontend-handled.** Added `static/js/presence.js` to `test_event_registry`'s `_FRONTEND_FILES`; the handler's `frame.type === "presence"` equality is what the drift scan keys on. Decisive probe: `presence` ∈ `_backend_emitted_types()` AND ∈ `_frontend_handled_types()` → PROVEN both directions (registered + emitted + handled), not just emitted.
- **End-to-end render proof — `tests/test_frontend_presence.py` (jsdom).** Evals the REAL shipped `presence.js`, captures the registered push handler, feeds `update`/`conflict`/`depart` frames, asserts the rendered DOM: 17 checks — strip visible/hidden, title+statusLabel+objective+relative-time rendered, count badge, SELF-EXCLUSION, OTHER-ROOT filtered, conflict message verbatim, depart removes peer rows (conflict persists in TTL), HTML-injection escaped. **Negative control PROVEN (pure-render contract):** patching presence.js to FABRICATE its own status label (instead of `peer.statusLabel` verbatim) fails the verbatim checks; restore → PASS, byte-identical — the test genuinely enforces "frontend computes nothing but the timestamp".
- **Verification (actual).** `ruff` clean (lib/presence/); `node --check` clean (presence.js, main.js); bundle rebuilt → `bundle-0e947750.js` (presence.js included, `presenceStrip`/`pushSubscribe("presence"` present). Full sweep **34 passed**: `test_presence`(12) + `test_event_registry`(5) + `test_frontend_presence`(1 suite, 17 checks) + `test_frontend_api_isolation`(4, no raw fetch) + `test_artifacts_bundle_registration`(9) + `test_frontend_typecheck`(3, after declaring `presenceRefresh`/`__presenceWired` in globals.d.ts). DB-table errors in the local harness are the known unbootstrapped-SQLite noise (import-time), not assertion failures.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** In a presence/fan-out registry, NEVER call the push hub while holding the state lock — collect a decorated snapshot under the lock, broadcast after release (the sweep path is the template). For a "pure render" frontend, the decisive test is a negative control that makes the frontend FABRICATE a value the backend is supposed to own and asserts it then DIVERGES from the wire — a test that only checks "the value is shown" can't prove the frontend isn't secretly computing it.


### 2026-06-30 — Reading-Mode report agent: root-caused & fixed the "507 searches, mostly punctuation" bug (paper agents bypassed chat's `validate_then_repair` seam)
- **Symptom (owner screenshot).** A report for *"Agentic Rubrics as Contextual Verifiers for SWE Agents"* showed a tool round `507 searches:  +504 more` with NO preview text, and the parser appeared to search parsed content character-by-character (single letters/punctuation).
- **Root cause (confirmed by the display math).** The label `507 searches:  +504 more` with empty previews is only producible when `len(queries)==507`, `len-3==504`, AND the `if isinstance(q, dict)` preview filter drops every item — i.e. `queries` is a **507-char STRING**, not an array. The model emitted `web_search` with `queries` as a bare string (schema violation: schema wants an array of `{query}` objects). Both the display label (`report_engine`/`qa_engine`) and the executor (`lib/paper/tools._execute_report_tool`, `for qobj in queries[:5]: q = str(qobj)`) iterated the string **character-by-character**, running a real web search on each of the first 5 chars and reporting the char-count as the search count.
- **Why chat is immune.** Chat routes every tool call through `lib.tool_input_repair.validate_then_repair` at the dispatch seam (`lib/tasks_pkg/tool_dispatch.py:728`), which applies `bare_string_to_array` → coerces the stray string into a single-element array before anything touches it. The paper report/Q&A pipeline had **reimplemented arg parsing inline WITHOUT that seam** — three hand-rolled copies (report display, QA display, executor). The divergent copies were the bug. (There's even a comment at `lib/project_mod/tools.py:778` documenting this exact "garbled `Read 24 files: ; < p a`" char-iteration class for the streaming display path.)
- **Fix (single source of truth, not a patch).** `lib/paper/tools.py` gains `parse_and_repair_tool_args(name, raw)` (JSON-decode + `validate_then_repair`, never raises) and a shared `display_query_for(fn_name, fn_args)` label builder that handles BOTH dict entries and coerced bare-string entries. `report_engine.py` + `qa_engine.py` now parse via the shared helper and label via the shared builder (QA's duplicated local `_display_query_for` deleted; its now-unused `urlparse` import removed). The executor parses+repairs up front and its per-item loops are hardened (non-list `queries`/`urls` → single entry; non-dict/non-string items skipped) so a bare string can NEVER be iterated per-char even if the schema index is unavailable (defense-in-depth). Tool-description hardening: `lib/tools/search.py` `queries`/`urls` array descriptions now state each element MUST be a `{query}`/`{url}` object, never a bare string (descriptive-only — no `type`/`required` change, prompt-cache + repair-index unaffected; `test_cache_schema_stability` stays green).
- **Verification (actual).** `ruff` + AST clean. New `tests/test_paper_tool_args_repair.py` (10): bare-string `queries` → **1** search not 507; label is the real text not the empty multi-search label; mixed string+dict entries preview; executor issues exactly ONE search for the bug payload (network stubbed) and still fans out a genuine batch; parse helper never raises on garbage. **Negative control proven:** the OLD path reports `len(queries)=110` and searches `['a', ',', 'b', '.', 'c']` — exactly the screenshot symptom; fix → 1 search. Suites green: `test_paper_tool_args_repair`(10) + `test_paper_report_abort`(3) + `test_paper_report_dedup`(4) + `test_paper_qa_agentic`(10) + `test_tool_input_repair`(27) + `test_cache_schema_stability`(23) + `test_search_marginalia_deepen`(19) = **96 passed**.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** The paper report/Q&A agents are a SECOND tool-calling harness; any robustness layer chat applies at the dispatch seam (arg repair, name-alias resolution, hallucination rejection) must be reachable by them too — reimplementing arg parsing inline silently forks behaviour and reintroduces the exact class of bug `validate_then_repair` exists to kill. When a model emits a string where an array is declared, NEVER iterate it: coerce via the shared repair, and as a backstop treat any non-list array-slot value as a single element.


### 2026-06-30 — Cross-conversation live presence (slice 1, backend): `lib/presence/` authoritative in-memory registry + write-through `.tofu/presence/registry.json` + `presence` push channel + heartbeat wiring + startup ghost reconciliation
- **Why.** Owner pain: many open conversations + long autopilot runs with zero mutual awareness — can't grasp project progress, and concurrent runs can interfere (two runs editing the same file, blind to each other). Locked framing: a "shared online document, see who's writing" presence layer, NOT a new mode. Build it on existing seams. Decisions: stay inside `.tofu/` (single==multi dir for now, native multi-project later); conflicts = NOTIFY only (no locks); backend owns ALL judgment, frontend is a decision-free renderer; single-server is the contract but persist anyway (crash-recoverable); broadcast to `'*'`, frontend filters by displayed root; build slice 1 as the MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT (log every file-set overlap; decide the Layer-3 ledger's role from live data, no synthetic pre-measurement).
- **Slice-1 scope shipped (backend only).** `lib/agent_artifacts.py`: `PRESENCE_SUBDIR`/`PRESENCE_REGISTRY_FILE` constants (registry lives at `<root>/.tofu/presence/registry.json`, covered by the existing `.tofu*` gitignore + every artifact consumer). `lib/presence/registry.py`: in-memory authoritative `_state[root][convId]→peer` under one RLock, **write-through** to disk via `json_store.write_json_atomic` (atomic + per-path-locked, fsync=False on the hot path). Backend computes `status` (active|idle) from heartbeat age vs `ACTIVE_TTL_SEC=25`/`IDLE_TTL_SEC=180` + the human `statusLabel`; `snapshot()` returns ONLY active peers (decorated). `lib/presence/conflict.py::detect_overlaps` intersects active peers' touched-file sets → fully-formed advisory string, and logs `[presence-overlap]` per hit (the ledger-decision instrument). `lib/agent_core/events.py`: `EventType.PRESENCE` + `EventCategory.PRESENCE` + `EventSpec` (kind=update|depart|conflict|snapshot, fully-formed peer/conflict payloads).
- **Heartbeat wiring at existing seams.** announce@`run_task` start (after `ensure_project_state`; idempotent per convId so an autopilot follow-up refreshes the SAME peer, no gone→active flicker); **stream heartbeat piggybacks the existing ~5s `_maybe_checkpoint_during_stream` throttle** (manager.py) — token flow IS work, so a 3-min single-LLM turn with no tool rounds stays ACTIVE instead of flapping to idle, and zero per-token writes; record_files@round (merges this round's authoritative `modifiedFileList` into the peer + runs overlap detection); mark_idle@`run_task` `finally` (done → IDLE, KEEP the peer; the sweep fades it after the idle window — `depart` is reserved for explicit abort/sweep-reap/startup-reconcile). Single clock-driven piece: a `presence-sweeper` daemon (10s) does active→idle (broadcast once)→reaped(>idle TTL, ghost cleanup). No client polling anywhere.
- **Startup ghost reconciliation (server.py).** A server that crashed mid-run never fired depart → its disk registry shows dead peers "active" forever (the strip would lie after every restart). On boot, after stale-task recovery: discover candidate roots (distinct `settings.projectPath` from conversations), read each disk registry, DROP every peer whose taskId isn't in the LIVE task registry or whose heartbeat is older than ACTIVE_TTL; rewrite cleaned registry. A fresh process has no live tasks → every persisted peer is correctly reaped (nothing is actually running yet); live peers re-announce as real tasks start. Then `start_sweeper()`.
- **Verification (actual).** `test_event_registry` GREEN 5/5 (PRESENCE registered AND backend-emitted — added `lib/presence/registry.py` to its `_BACKEND_FILES` scan; the orphan-guard passes because the type is emitted even before the slice-2 frontend handler exists). New `tests/test_presence.py` 11/11: announce→active+persist+broadcast, active→idle past TTL, idempotent-per-conv preserves files+startedTs, record_files union+currentFile+label, overlap→fully-formed conflict advisory, no-conflict for single-peer/distinct-files, mark_idle keeps vs depart removes, sweep reaps past idle-TTL, idle-transition emitted once, **startup reconcile reaps ghost on fresh process**, reconcile keeps live-task-backed peer. **Negative control PROVEN**: forcing `is_ghost=False` (never reap) makes `test_reconcile_reaps_ghost_peers_on_fresh_process` FAIL; restoring → PASS; `registry.py` byte-identical after restore. `ruff` + AST clean on all authored files (the lone manager.py F401 `db_execute_with_retry` is PRE-EXISTING uncommitted work at line 20/441, not my heartbeat edit at ~673). Two design refinements vs the original brief, flagged: done→idle-not-depart (autopilot continuity + lingering-then-fade), and the stream heartbeat on the checkpoint throttle (anti-flap).
- **Next.** Slice 2: `static/js/presence.js` (pure render, `pushSubscribe('presence','*')`, filter by displayed root, in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no raw fetch) — the read-only "who's working" strip + contention callouts. Layer-3 ledger gated on the `[presence-overlap]` telemetry this slice now records.


### 2026-06-30 — Read-mode (paper) search-tool rendering now at full chat parity: vertical cards + engine-source breakdown + per-query `_q` grouping, by REUSING chat's `_web_search_one` (not duplicating) — deleted the synth-results frontend hack
- **Symptom (owner).** A `web_search` round in the paper Report/Q&A tabs rendered as a plain title/snippet/url list, while the SAME query in chat additionally shows the purple vertical card (HF Papers / arXiv / Semantic Scholar) and the "🔍 Engine Sources — N raw → M final" expander. The renderer (`renderToolRoundsHTML`) IS shared across all three surfaces, so the gap was upstream: the paper backend emitted thinner `tool_done` events.
- **Root cause.** `lib/paper/tools.py:_execute_report_tool` called `perform_web_search()` DIRECTLY and returned only `(tool_content, display_results, search_diag)` — discarding `results._engine_breakdown` and never running the vertical planner. Chat's `_web_search_one` (handlers/search.py) computes both (vertical runs CONCURRENTLY via a 1-worker pool → zero added latency). Tell-tale: a frontend hack at `paper-reader.js` synthesized a fake one-item `results` array from `toolContent` "so it doesn't show no results" — masking the missing real array.
- **Fix (robust, not patch).** (1) `_execute_report_tool` now imports and REUSES chat's `_web_search_one`, `_vertical_to_sse_payload`, `_vertical_header_for_llm`, `_format_search_display_for_results` (no duplicated vertical/breakdown logic — single source of truth). Return contract widened to a 5-tuple `(tool_content, display_results, search_diag, engine_breakdown, verticals)`; batch results tagged with `_q`; engine_breakdown only attached for a single-query search (chat behaviour); each vertical payload carries its source `query`. (2) Both `report_engine.py` and `qa_engine.py` unpack the 5-tuple and thread `engineBreakdown`/`verticals` into their `tool_done` events + `round_entry`. (3) Frontend: `_applyQAEvent` (QA tab) gained the `engineBreakdown`/`vertical`/`verticals` threading the report handler already had; deleted the synth-results hack from `_applyReportEvent` — read mode now relies on the real emitted `results`.
- **Verification (actual).** AST+ruff+`node --check` clean. Functional probe (mock `_web_search_one`, no network): SINGLE query → engine_breakdown present, 1 vertical (domain=academic), `_q` tagged, vertical header in tool_content; BATCH → engine_breakdown None (correct — flattened), per-query `_q` tags `['a','b']`, vertical query attribution `['a','b']`. Pre-existing test mocks returned the old 3-tuple → updated 5 mock sites in `test_paper_qa_agentic.py` (2) + `test_paper_report_dedup.py` (3) to the 5-tuple contract. Suites green: paper qa/report/abort/dedup + frontend_tool_rounds_render = **18 passed**; chat-side `test_tool_changes` + `test_streaming_and_prefetch` = **64 passed** (reusing the helpers broke nothing). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-5587bd7b.js`.
- **Follow-up (same session, owner review).** Owner correctly flagged that the `fetch_url` branch was STILL a parallel hand-rolled `fetch_page_content` loop — the exact drift that caused the original bug. Read-mode fetch rows lacked chat's filtered-vs-raw char counts (`"300 chars (filtered from 1,000)"`), the `File Asset`/staging source label, and rejected-scheme `N/A` rows. Closed it: `fetch_url` now reuses chat's `_fetch_url_one` + `_format_fetch_display` + `_short_url` (same concurrent `run_batch_concurrent` pattern, same None-result failure-item synthesis, same batch text construction). Dropped the now-unused `import lib as _lib` + `fetch_page_content` import. Probe (mock `_fetch_url_one`) confirms all three row types render identically to chat. The QA/report tests mock `_execute_report_tool` itself so the fetch rewrite needed no mock changes. Full sweep **82 passed** (paper qa/report/abort/dedup + frontend_tool_rounds_render + chat-side test_tool_changes + test_streaming_and_prefetch).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a "secondary" agent surface (paper, swarm) must match chat's tool rendering, REUSE chat's `_web_search_one` AND `_fetch_url_one` rather than re-implementing the search/fetch call — the divergence here was exactly the fields chat's helpers compute that a direct `perform_web_search()` / `fetch_page_content()` drops, and it's invisible until someone diffs the rendered rows. Don't stop at the one tool the symptom named: audit EVERY branch of the shared executor for the same parallel-implementation drift. A frontend "synthesize fake results so it doesn't look empty" hack is a smell that the backend is emitting less than the renderer expects — fix the emitter, delete the hack. And widening a helper's return tuple means every monkeypatched test mock of it must be updated in lockstep (the failure is `not enough values to unpack`, surfaced clearly).


### 2026-06-29 — install.sh drift guard correctly blocked a clean install: requirements.txt CVE-floor pins (Jinja2/urllib3/PyYAML) were never added to CONDA_PKGS
- **Symptom (owner, on chenxin's fresh copy).** `install.sh` aborted with `requirements.txt declares packages NOT covered by install.sh: jinja2, pyyaml, urllib3` → `install.sh package lists are out of sync with requirements.txt` (exit 1). Owner asked whether to fix or just re-export internal. **Re-export would NOT have helped** — the broken script is part of the source tree, so every export ships it identically.
- **Root cause.** The drift guard (install.sh:799-821) enforces that every dep in `requirements.txt` is covered by the hand-maintained `CONDA_PKGS`/`PIP_ONLY_PKGS` arrays (the install deliberately splits conda/pip to dodge the lxml6/icu78/PG18 solver deadlock, so it can't `pip install -r`). `requirements.txt` had gained CVE-clearing floor pins for three TRANSITIVE deps — `Jinja2>=3.1.6` (sandbox-escape CVE trio, via flask/quart), `urllib3>=1.26.19` (redirect-leak CVE trio, via requests), `PyYAML>=6.0` (used directly by `routes/api_docs.py` for the YAML OpenAPI spec) — but nobody mirrored them into the arrays. Guard did its job (fail-fast at install instead of ModuleNotFoundError at boot).
- **Fix.** Added all three to `CONDA_PKGS` (install.sh:709-718, after requests) — all on conda-forge, all transitive of packages already conda-installed, so they slot in cleanly and clean envs now get the CVE-fixed versions instead of whatever the resolver pulls. The guard's `_norm` lowercases + strips versions + maps `_`→`-`, so `jinja2`/`pyyaml`/`urllib3` match the declared `Jinja2`/`PyYAML`/`urllib3`.
- **Verification.** Re-simulated the exact guard logic (extract array literals → `_norm` → `comm -23` against normalized requirements.txt): **zero** uncovered packages remain. `bash -n install.sh` clean.
- **Adjacent (same session).** `copy_to_chenxin.sh` flooded `Permission denied (13)` on `data/translate_cache/*.json`: the rsync runs as the hadoop-autoresearch account PULLING from the ruanjunhao04 tree over FUSE, and those cache files are owner-only → chenxin's uid can't `open()` them. They're also pure regenerable runtime junk. Fix: replace the narrow `data/pgdata/` + `*.db` + marker excludes with a single `--exclude='data/'` (export.py already excludes the whole `data/` dir for internal/opensource — the leak only happened because the server was run inside tofu-meituan AFTER export, regenerating `data/`). Destination rebuilds `data/` on first `python3 server.py`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When you add a pin to `requirements.txt` (even a transitive CVE floor), you MUST mirror it into `install.sh`'s `CONDA_PKGS` or `PIP_ONLY_PKGS` — the drift guard will block EVERY install until you do. Treat the guard's failure as "finish the edit", not "an obstacle to bypass". And a copy/export issue is never fixed by re-exporting if the defect lives in a tracked source file.


### 2026-06-29 — Autopilot summary close-out: (1) made the run report DISPLAY-ONLY in context (was a permanent per-run token tax), (2) covered the manual-stop fold-boundary DOM-walk with a jsdom test + negative control
- **Why (owner review of the prior turn).** The owner verified the run-fold + summary feature end-to-end and flagged two things the prior turn left open. Both are correct calls.
- **Fix 1 — summary must NOT re-enter LLM context.** `conv_message_builder._transform_messages` did NOT skip `_isAutopilotSummary`, so on the next human turn the full debrief was replayed as an assistant message — a redundant restatement of work already present in the (folded but still in-context) run transcript. That's a per-turn token tax for zero new information, and a multi-run conversation would STACK one full report per run into the prompt. Added `_isAutopilotSummary` to the skip set (same family as `_isEndpointReview`/`_epIteration`). The fold/visible-tail is a PRESENTATION concern; it must not become a context cost. Considered keeping it as an "anchor" — rejected: the transcript it summarises is already in context, so the report earns nothing. Tests: `test_skip_autopilot_summary` (excluded from built messages, real turns + follow-up survive, no `_isAutopilotSummary`/`_autopilotRunId` marker leaks) + `test_skip_autopilot_summary_multi_run_no_stacking`. **Negative control PROVEN**: disabling the skip (`and False`) fails both; restoring passes; `conv_message_builder.py` restored byte-intact (live `continue` at L268).
- **Fix 2 — manual-stop fold boundary coverage.** The auto-summary fold path was tested, but `_applyAutopilotRunFolds`' range-bounding for a manual-stop run (no summary anchor — the `nextIsRun || nextIsWorker` sibling walk) had zero coverage, and that DOM-walk silently swallows the following human turn if the boundary logic is wrong. New `tests/test_frontend_autopilot_fold.py` (jsdom, evals the REAL shipped `chat_render.js`, mirrors the `test_frontend_streaming_ui.py` harness): Case 1 manual-stop run folds its 3 turns and does NOT swallow the next human turn (the bug); Case 2 clean-done run folds before the summary, summary stays the visible tail outside the fold (+ no summarize button); Case 3 back-to-back manual-stop runs fold independently (the between-runs human turn stays free, no R3↔R4 cross-swallow); Case 4 idempotent (double-pass = single fold, no nesting). 18+ assertions. **Negative control PROVEN**: replacing the boundary guard with `if (false)` makes the walk over-consume → `c1_human_not_swallowed` FAILS; restoring passes; bundle hash unchanged (`bundle-b681a81e.js`) confirms `chat_render.js` byte-identical after restore.
- **Verification (actual).** `ruff` + `node --check` clean. Full sweep **86 passed**: `test_autopilot_summary`(6) + `test_autopilot_verify`(17) + `test_conv_message_builder`(50, +2) + `test_frontend_autopilot_fold`(1 suite, 18+ checks) + `test_event_registry`(5) + `test_frontend_api_isolation`(4) + `test_frontend_typecheck`(3).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A presentation-tier artifact (the folded run's visible-tail summary) must be added to the `conv_message_builder` skip set the moment it's `role='assistant'` and persisted — otherwise it silently re-enters context and compounds across runs. And any DOM range-walk that bounds a collapsible group (especially one WITHOUT an explicit end anchor) needs a jsdom test whose decisive assertion is "the element AFTER the group is NOT swallowed", with a negative control that breaks the boundary condition — a fold test that only checks "the group is folded" cannot catch over-consumption.


### 2026-06-29 — Autopilot run fold + read-only close-out summary report: concluded autonomous runs now collapse to [human msg → report], with an explicit runId boundary (not role-scanning) and a one-LLM-turn debrief at the TASK_DONE seam
- **Why (owner request).** Autonomous driving works well for long unattended runs, but the volume of virtual-user↔agent turns is hard for a human to digest after the fact. Asked to (a) fold the whole VU↔agent transcript once a run concludes and (b) generate one comprehensive summary report at the end — reading like a direct "human message → report" handoff, the agent reporting back. Generation flow stays exactly as-is; the fold + report are added at the conclusion.
- **Locked design (4 decisions + 1 correction, all confirmed by owner).** (1) Reporter is READ-ONLY, no tools — the VU already verified each turn as it went; the transcript already holds every tool result, so a second verification budget is redundant. Skip the report entirely on empty output. (2) Fold default = collapsed; visible spine = `[original human message → summary report]`, one click expands. (3) Auto-summarize ONLY on a clean `[VU: TASK_DONE]`; a run killed by Stop / a new user message gets an explicit "Summarize this run" button instead (the user already moved on). (4) Fold only fully-concluded runs; an in-progress run stays expanded and live. (5) **Run boundary MUST be explicit, not heuristic** — stamp each run with a `runId` and tag every VU turn + the summary, so the frontend groups `[start … summary]` deterministically (role-scanning the flat list breaks on edits, branches, back-to-back runs).
- **Backend (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`).** `_get_or_persist_run_id` pins `settings.autopilotRunId` next to `autopilotObjective` (both cleared by `_clear_run_id` on conclusion → fresh next run). `run_summary_reporter(task)` mirrors the VU sub-task pattern (`_run_single_turn` over the full transcript + a trailing REPORTER directive) but strips EVERY tool toggle on the sub-config (search/fetch/project/codeExec/browser/memory/swarm/scheduler/imageGen/humanGuidance all off → `_assemble_tool_list` returns no tools). `_REPORTER_ROLE_PROMPT` (+ content-derived `REPORTER_PROMPT_VERSION`, same stale-process discipline as `VU_PROMPT_VERSION`) = objective-anchored debrief: Objective / Outcome verdict / What was done / Verification / Gaps & risks; honest. `_append_summary_to_conv` persists a `role='assistant'` row with `_isAutopilotSummary` + `_autopilotRunId` (no toolRounds; DOES re-enter context next human turn as a normal assistant anchor — nothing skips it). `_emit_run_summary` ties reporter → persist → server-side auto-translate safety net (`_maybe_auto_translate_assistant`, role-agnostic) → `autopilot_summary` SSE event, wired into `maybe_run_autopilot`'s `_vu_emitted_done` branch BEFORE disarm. `summarize_run(conv_id, runId, config)` backs the manual affordance (resolves runId from the last VU turn when absent).
- **Event contract.** `EventType.AUTOPILOT_SUMMARY` (`autopilot_summary`, fields `runId` + `summaryMessage`) registered in `lib/agent_core/events.py`. `test_event_registry` is the proof it's BOTH registered AND frontend-handled.
- **Route.** `POST /api/v1/chat/autopilot/summarize` (`routes/chat_queue.py`) → `summarize_run`; `Api.chat.summarizeAutopilotRun` added to the unified client (`static/js/api.js`) — isolation ratchet OK (no raw fetch).
- **Frontend fold (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`).** `renderMessage` stamps `data-ap-run` / `data-ap-summary` on the `.message` element; `_msgFingerprint` includes both so surgical updates repaint on change. `_applyAutopilotRunFolds(inner)` — post-render pass gated on `!activeStreams.has(conv.id)` (so it only runs when NOT streaming ⇒ every stamped run seen is concluded) — collapses each run's contiguous turn range into `<details class="autopilot-run-fold">`, leaving the human msg (above, un-stamped) and the summary (below) as the spine. Per-run open/closed state remembered in `_apFoldOpenState` across re-renders. A manual-stop run (no summary) gets a "Summarize this run" button (`_summarizeAutopilotRun`, async, reuses `_buildConvConfig`). `_handleAutopilotSummary` (`streaming_render.js`) reconciles the live event (idempotent dedup by `_msgId`). i18n (`autopilot.runFold/runFoldHint/summaryLabel/summarizeRun`, zh+en) + CSS (`.autopilot-run-fold*`, `.autopilot-summary-banner`).
- **Verification (actual).** `ruff` + AST clean on the 3 Python files; `node --check` clean on all touched JS; bundle rebuilt. New `tests/test_autopilot_summary.py` (6): reporter prompt structure + honesty, content-derived version marker, **read-only sub-config (NEGATIVE CONTROL)**, empty/error → None, event registration. **Negative control PROVEN**: commenting out the `sub_cfg['searchMode']='off'` stripping makes `test_reporter_subconfig_is_read_only` FAIL; restoring → PASS; restore byte-identical (`diff -q`). Suites green: `test_autopilot_summary`(6) + `test_autopilot_verify`(17) + `test_event_registry`(5) + `test_frontend_api_isolation`(4) + `test_frontend_typecheck`(3) = 35 passed. **Pre-existing, unrelated:** `tests/test_autopilot_arm.py` fails in THIS local env with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: message_queue/conversations` — the known unbootstrapped-test-harness SQLite breakage at DB setup (dies before reaching any autopilot logic; my changes are purely additive). Green in CI where the harness bootstraps the schema.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Two idempotency disciplines again: a CONCLUDED-run signal must be EXPLICIT (the `runId` pin), never inferred by walking roles — the flat message list is mutated by edits/branches/multiple runs. The summary reporter must be tool-LESS by construction (strip every feature toggle on the sub-config); the read-only-ness is the negative-control assertion. And gate the fold pass on `!activeStreams.has` so an in-flight run's stamped VU turns are never prematurely collapsed.


### 2026-06-29 — Related-conversation digest now RELEVANCE-GATED (BM25 + recency floor) + read-only conv tools always-on in project mode; frontend: unified "Memory & Preferences" Settings tab + sidebar summarized-conversation glyph
- **Why.** Follow-up to the design-Q&A on the cross-conv mechanism. The Layer-2 project digest (`build_project_digest`, system_context ★4.4) was injected on EVERY project turn as the recency-top-10 siblings regardless of topic — undifferentiated cache-tail cost + no topical targeting (the same anti-pattern the tiered preference profile fixed). And the model was TOLD siblings exist but on a plain project turn could NOT open them (`get_conversation`/`list_conversations` gated on `has_conv_ref` = @-attach only) → the digest header's tool-naming branch was effectively dead on plain turns. Owner locked: relevance-gate the digest, register the read-only conv tools in project mode, and on the frontend merge memories+preferences into one Settings view + add a sidebar "summarized" indicator.
- **Backend 1 — relevance-gated digest.** `project_digest_entries(..., query=None)` (`lib/conversations/project_summary.py`): still scans the `_DIGEST_SCAN_LIMIT=24` most-recent siblings, but when `query` is present it BM25-ranks them by `title + " " + summary` via `lib.memory.relevance.score_items` (the SAME CJK-aware scorer the preference-detail tier reuses — no new scorer) and returns the positive matches UNIONED with a `_DIGEST_RECENCY_FLOOR=3` most-recent floor, so an off-topic/fresh turn is never empty. No query → pure recency (back-compat, every prior caller unchanged). `build_project_digest(..., query=None)` threads it through. ★4.4 passes `query=_extract_last_user_text(messages)` to BOTH the digest build AND the `_relatedConversations` chip stash, so the auditable chip shows the SAME relevance-selected set the model saw.
- **Backend 2 — read-only conv tools in project mode.** `_build_conv_ref` (`lib/tools/registry.py`) now registers `CONV_REF_TOOLS` (`list_conversations` + `get_conversation`, both read-only) when `has_conv_ref` OR (`project_enabled and project_path`), still requiring `current_count>0`. So `get_conversation` IS in the schema on a plain project turn → the model can open a surfaced sibling, and the digest's `conv_tools_available` header branch (which names the tools) is now truthful. Tool descriptions left as-is (they still discourage *speculative* use, which remains correct).
- **Frontend A — unified "Memory & Preferences" Settings tab.** The `preferences` tab (label → `记忆与偏好` / "Memory & Preferences", i18n `settings.tabPreferences`) now has the existing Preferences profile section PLUS a new "Accumulated memories" section (`#prefsMemoryList`, `index.html`). `refreshMemoryList(scope, targetId)` (`memory.js`) gained an optional target-container arg (default `#memoryList`, back-compat); `_memoryListTargetId`/`_memoryListEl()` route `_renderMemoryCards` + empty/error states to it. `_populatePreferencesTab` (`preferences.js`) calls new `_refreshPrefsMemorySection()` → renders cards into `#prefsMemoryList` reusing the modal's render path. Heavy management (create/install/drag-drop) stays in the full modal, reachable via a "Manage all" button (`openMemoryModal()`). No new data path — reuses `Api.memory.list` + `_buildMemoryCardEl`.
- **Frontend B — sidebar summarized-conversation glyph.** `settings.projectSummary` IS already on the wire from the meta-cache list endpoint (`lib/conversations/meta_cache.py`) but was dropped by the `_applySettingsToConv` whitelist (`core/conversations.js`) — added one line to copy `projectSummary` through. Struct-hash in `conversation_list.js` gained a trailing `S` marker when `projectSummary.text` exists so the row re-renders when a summary first appears. `_buildConvItemHTML` renders `_CONV_SUMMARY_SVG` (inline SVG document-with-lines glyph, §3.4 no-emoji) in `.conv-title` only when a summary is cached; click → `showConvSummary(badge, event)` (stopPropagation) shows the cached text via the shared `showToast`. CSS: `.conv-summary-badge` (quiet→hover-accent), `.memory-list-embedded` (capped+scroll), `.settings-section-divider`.
- **Verification (actual).** Backend: `ruff` clean on the 3 py files. The `@pytest.mark.api` `test_project_summary.py` suite ERRORs in THIS env (the known `no such table: conversations` flask_client-harness bootstrap breakage — setup errors, NOT assertion failures; pass in CI), so proved the logic directly: (1) `score_items` discriminates relevant (db doc, score 3.36) vs off-topic (`[]`); (2) a fake-DB probe of `project_digest_entries` → relevant query ranks the matching sibling FIRST, off-topic returns the recency floor (non-empty, most-recent present), no-query = pure recency; (3) constructed-ToolContext probe → `get_conversation`+`list_conversations` IN schema on a plain project turn, empty on non-project / zero-base-tools. Added `test_digest_relevance_gating_and_recency_floor` to the suite (runs green in CI). Regression suites green: `test_core_tool_isolation`(3) + `test_relevance_cjk`(9) + `test_user_profile`(43) = 55; `test_streaming_and_prefetch` digest tests = 2. Frontend: `node --check` clean on all 6 touched JS; node harness proved the badge conditional+escaping + struct-hash invalidation; `test_frontend_conv_list_collapse` + `test_frontend_typecheck`(3) + `test_artifacts_bundle_registration`(9) + `test_frontend_api_isolation`(4, confirms no new raw fetch) + `test_frontend_tool_rounds_render` = 18 passed. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-cdb831d2.js`; all 6 JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; grep confirms `showConvSummary`/`conv-summary-badge`/`_refreshPrefsMemorySection`/`prefsMemoryList`/`memPrefs.manageAll` present in the built bundle.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Relevance-gate cross-conv siblings the SAME way the preference-detail tier does — reuse `score_items`, union with a recency floor so it's never empty, and feed the chip stash the SAME query so the audit chip matches the prompt. When you surface entities to the model for ambient awareness (digest siblings), make sure the tool to ACT on them is actually in the schema that turn (register read-only `get_conversation` in project mode) — awareness without capability is the phantom-tool trap. And to embed an existing modal's list elsewhere, parameterize its render target (`targetId` arg + a module-level `_…TargetId`) rather than duplicating the renderer.


### 2026-06-29 — Root-cause fix: the relevance-gated DETAIL tier was FROZEN on the first turn's match across a multi-turn conversation (append-once → stale detail; the core feature silently not working)
- **Symptom (owner-confirmed).** Open a conversation, ask about translation on turn 1, then about the FMG grader on turn 2. On turn 2 the injected detail block STILL contained only the *translation* bullet — the FMG fact (the one relevant to turn 2) never reached the model. Meanwhile the chip honestly showed FMG, so the UI now DISAGREED with what the model received (the opposite of the honesty just established). Across a conversation the detail tier froze on whatever turn 1 matched → relevance gating stopped working exactly where it matters.
- **Root cause.** The detail tier was injected with `_append_user_profile_block` (the SAME append-once helper as the byte-stable core). That helper bails the moment it sees its marker already present. A follow-up turn REUSES the profile-carrying message from a prior turn (server-side message store `keepToolHistory` / `rebuild_messages_with_history`), so the OLD detail block is still embedded → append-once bailed → the NEW turn's relevance-selected bullet was never injected. Append-once is CORRECT for the core (query-independent, byte-stable, cache prefix) but WRONG for the per-turn relevance-gated detail.
- **Fix (root cause, not polish).** New `_refresh_detail_block(messages, block, marker)` in `system_context.py`: locate the carrier (`_isMeta` tail, else first user msg — same priority as the append helper), STRIP any existing text block carrying `_PROFILE_DETAIL_MARKER` (the stale prior-turn detail), then re-append THIS turn's block — or remove it entirely when the turn has no relevant match. Returns `replaced`/`added`/`removed`/`noop` so the caller knows whether the tail was mutated (→ `notify_compaction`). ★2.5 now calls `_refresh_detail_block` for the detail tier; the CORE tier keeps its append-once `_append_user_profile_block` UNCHANGED (byte-stable, cache prefix preserved). Only the detail block — which already rides the cache-safe tail like `<relevant_memories>` — varies per turn, which is the whole point of the tiering.
- **Verification (actual).** Probe across 3 turns: turn 1 (translation) → detail=translation, no FMG; turn 2 (FMG, REUSING turn-1 messages) → detail=FMG, translation GONE, exactly **1** detail marker (no stale+new stacking); turn 3 (irrelevant CSS) → detail block STRIPPED entirely, core survives. Two new tests in `test_user_profile.py`: `test_detail_tier_refreshed_per_turn_not_frozen` (the owner's exact check, through the REAL `_inject_system_contexts`) + `test_detail_refresh_is_cache_safe` (3 rounds with DIFFERENT queries swapping the detail block on the tail → NO `prefix_mutation`, and the CORE segment byte-identical across all swaps). **Decisive negative control:** reverting just the wiring line back to the buggy `_append_user_profile_block` makes `test_detail_tier_refreshed_per_turn_not_frozen` FAIL (proves it catches the exact bug); restoring the fix → passes. Suites: `test_user_profile` 41→43 + `test_personal_scope_headless`(14) + `test_relevance_cjk`(9) = **66 passed**; `ruff` + AST clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Two tiers on the SAME cache-safe tail need DIFFERENT idempotency disciplines: a query-INDEPENDENT block (core) is append-once + byte-stable (keeps the cache prefix); a query-DEPENDENT block (relevance-gated detail) must be REFRESH (strip-then-append) every turn, because conversation history is reused across turns and append-once would freeze it on the first turn's selection. When you put a per-turn-varying block on a tail that survives across turns, the helper that writes it MUST replace, not append — and prove it with a multi-turn test where turn 2's query differs from turn 1's (a single-turn unit test cannot catch the freeze). Also a `insert_content` whose `anchor` includes a docstring's first line will DUPLICATE that line — check the def header after inserting before an existing function.


### 2026-06-29 — Two turn-provenance-strip bugs: (1) prefs chip flickered in/out between turns of the same conversation, (2) the collapsed count rendered twice ("3 3 memories")
- **Bug 1 — prefs chip intermittent ("sometimes appears, sometimes doesn't").** Root cause in `system_context.py` ★2.5: `task['_appliedPreferences']` (the chip payload that drives the `preferences_applied` event) was stashed ONLY inside `if _profile_injected or _detail_injected:`. But `_append_user_profile_block` returns False when the profile marker is ALREADY present in the message list — which is exactly turn 2+ of a conversation: `rebuild_messages_with_history` (keepToolHistory / server-side message store) REUSES the profile-carrying `_isMeta`/user message from turn 1, so no fresh injection happens, so the chip was never stashed → no event → chip vanished. The preferences ARE in context on those turns (carried over); gating the chip on a *fresh mutation* was the defect. **Fix:** decoupled the chip stash (now fires whenever `_core_block` exists, i.e. the profile is in context this turn, computed via `applied_profile_items(query=…)`) from the cache bookkeeping (`notify_compaction` + the INFO log stay gated on an actual `_append` mutation). Proved with a 2-turn probe: turn 1 fresh → chip set (3 items); turn 2 reusing the profile-carrying messages → `_append` returns False but **chip still set** (core-only, 2 items, since the turn-2 query had no relevant detail). New regression test `test_chip_fires_on_carried_over_profile_turn`.
- **Bug 2 — count rendered twice in the collapsed bar.** Each segment emitted BOTH a `tp-count` digit span AND a `tp-label` that already embeds the number (e.g. `<tp-count>3</tp-count>` + label "3 memories" → "3 3 memories"). The prefs segment didn't repeat (its label "preferences" had no number), so it looked inconsistent. **Fix:** dropped the `tp-count` span from all three numeric segments and made the label the single source of the count — memory/related-convs already had numbered labels; prefs gained `prefs.tagN`/`prefs.tagNs` ("{n} preferences"). Removed the now-dead `.tp-count` CSS rule (grep confirmed 0 JS emitters). Bundle: `tp-count` occurrences now 0.
- **Chip-honesty carry-through.** Threaded `core`/`detail` from the stash → `PREFERENCES_APPLIED` event (orchestrator) → `_handlePreferencesApplied` (frontend) so the chip can group core vs relevant-detail and stays the EXACT injected set (the handler previously dropped them). Added the two fields to the EventSpec docs (descriptive only; drift test unaffected).
- **Files.** `lib/tasks_pkg/system_context.py` (stash decoupling), `lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py` (+core/detail in emit), `lib/agent_core/events.py` (spec fields), `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js` (drop tp-count ×3, prefs numbered label), `static/js/ui/sse_handlers_misc.js` (carry core/detail), `static/js/i18n.js` (prefs.tagN/tagNs), `static/styles.css` (drop dead .tp-count rule). Bundle → `bundle-7c66697d.js`.
- **Verification (actual).** `node --check` + `ruff` clean. `test_user_profile.py` 40→41 (new carried-over-turn regression) + `test_event_registry`(5) + `test_frontend_sse_dispatch` = **47 passed**. The lone `test_streaming_ui_hot_path::FAIL waiting_phase` is the SAME pre-existing harness `t()`-stub limitation logged last turn (stub returns the i18n KEY `stream.phase.waiting`, assertion wants the en value `Waiting`) — in the phase-indicator path, NOT the provenance strip, untouched by this change.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A "was X in context this turn?" provenance chip must be derived from the CONTEXT STATE (is the profile present / would-be-present), NOT from "did THIS call mutate the message list" — the two diverge the moment history is reused across turns (server-side message store, rebuilt history, post-compaction). Gate cache-mutation bookkeeping on the mutation; gate the user-facing provenance on the state. And when a collapsed summary chip shows both a numeric badge and a text label, pick ONE to carry the number — emitting the count in both renders it twice.


### 2026-06-29 — Auto-translate root-cause fix: a conversation frozen `autoTranslate=OFF` at send-time could NEVER be retro-translated even after the global toggle was turned ON (an old reply sat demanding a manual click) → on-open trigger now honors the LIVE effective setting; + audited & closed 3 start paths that silently dropped `assistantMsgId` (killed the live per-round preview)
- **Why.** Follow-up to the Q&A that mapped the three translation paths. The genuine defect was Path 3: the per-conv `autoTranslate` is FROZEN at send-time (correct — stops a mid-task toggle changing an in-flight run; see `.tofu/skills/finishstream-global-autotranslate-bug.md`), but that freeze ALSO permanently vetoed the on-open retro-translate, so turning the global toggle ON did nothing for already-generated messages. Plus a latent bug: 3 non-endpoint/non-autopilot start paths never shipped `config.assistantMsgId`, silently downgrading their would-be live per-round translation to end-only with no signal.
- **Fix 1 — effective resolver for the on-open decision (no new trigger).** The on-open/activate trigger ALREADY exists: `_resumePendingTranslations(convId)` Phase-0 (translation.js), called from `loadConversation` (lazy-load `.then()` + sync branch) and boot/tab-visible. It already (a) early-returns while `activeStreams.has(convId)` so it never touches in-flight runs, and (b) routes through `translateClaim` + server `claim_inflight` so it can't double-fire vs the safety-net push / a manual click. The ONLY defect: it gated on the FROZEN `convAutoTranslate(conv)`. Added **`convAutoTranslateEffective(conv)`** (core/conversations.js): the LIVE global toggle wins when ON, else the frozen per-conv value (explicit per-conv ON still honored). Phase-0 now reads the effective resolver. The live send/regenerate/in-flight paths keep using the frozen `convAutoTranslate` UNCHANGED.
- **Fix 1b — stop `_restoreConvToolState` clobbering the live toggle (main.js).** On open it ran `_applyAutoTranslateUI(convAutoTranslate(conv))`, which writes the global `autoTranslate` from the frozen per-conv value — and this runs BEFORE `_resumePendingTranslations` in the lazy-load branch, so a frozen-OFF conv would flip global→false and defeat the effective resolver. Now: when the global is ON we keep it ON; only restore the frozen value when the global is OFF.
- **Fix 2 — `assistantMsgId` start-path audit (the live-preview seam).** `create_task` (manager.py:127) already copies `config.assistantMsgId → task['_assistantMsgId']` generically for every chat endpoint, so this was purely a frontend gap. Audited ALL streaming-bubble start paths: **send** (main_send_pipeline.js:378 ✅) and **regenerate-from-user** (main_regen_continue.js:83 ✅) already shipped it; **`startAssistantResponse`** (continue-fallback + Case-E recovery), **`saveEditAndResend`** (edit_message.js), and **`continueAssistant`** (`/api/chat/continue`) did NOT. Fixed all three: send+regen pattern mints a fresh id, ships it in the config, reuses it on the `assistantMsg`, and stamps the streaming bubble (`_streamingBubbleHTML(role,…,msgId)` / `_renderStreamingBubble(…, msgId)`). `continueAssistant` is special — it REUSES the existing assistant message, so it ships that message's existing `_msgId` (the reused `#streaming-msg` bubble already carries `data-msg-id` from `renderMessage`, chat_render.js:845). Autopilot-kick is correctly N/A (autopilot is gated out of the incremental path by design).
- **Files.** `static/js/core/conversations.js` (+`convAutoTranslateEffective`), `static/js/main.js` (`_restoreConvToolState` no-clobber), `static/js/translation.js` (Phase-0 effective resolver), `static/js/main/main_send_pipeline.js` (`startAssistantResponse`), `static/js/ui/edit_message.js` (`saveEditAndResend`), `static/js/main/main_regen_continue.js` (`continueAssistant`). All already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; rebuilt → `bundle-41a0f8e7.js`.
- **Verification (actual).** `node --check` clean on all 6. New `tests/test_frontend_retro_autotranslate.py` drives the REAL shipped `_resumePendingTranslations` under node (eval `core/conversations.js` + `translation.js`, stub the network/render seams, count `_runTranslationPipeline` kicks): 11 PASS across 5 cases — frozen-OFF+global-ON→translates (the bug), all-OFF→no-op, already-translated→skip, streaming→blocked (in-flight freeze respected), frozen-ON+global-OFF→translates. **Decisive negative control:** reverting Phase-0 to the frozen `convAutoTranslate` makes `case1_frozen_off_global_on_translates` FAIL (proves the test catches the exact bug); restored → PASS. Adjacent suites green: `test_frontend_auto_translate_default` + `test_frontend_translate_guard` + `test_incremental_translate` + `test_auto_translate_phase2` + `test_auto_translate_safety_net` + the new one = **28 passed**; `test_frontend_typecheck` = 3 passed.
- **Gotcha (test harness).** translation.js declares `_runTranslationPipeline` as a top-level `function`, so a PRE-eval `global._runTranslationPipeline` stub is CLOBBERED by the eval and the real pipeline runs (→ unstubbed `Api` ReferenceError). The counter stub MUST be assigned AFTER the evals (reassign the global binding). Same trap as the `_pushHandler`-capture pattern in `test_frontend_translate_guard.py`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Two distinct auto-translate decisions need two resolvers: the FROZEN `convAutoTranslate` governs the in-flight send (a mid-task toggle must NOT change a running turn), while the on-open retro-translate of a FINISHED untranslated message must honor the LIVE toggle (`convAutoTranslateEffective`) — conflating them is what made "auto-translate on" not mean what it says. And `assistantMsgId` is the live-preview seam: any NEW streaming-bubble start path MUST mint+ship it (or reuse the existing `_msgId` when it reuses the message), else the live per-round translation silently degrades to end-only with no error.


### 2026-06-29 — Fixed duplicated icon in the expanded turn-provenance strip: the per-segment glyph was emitted in BOTH the collapsed segment AND its detail row, so expanding showed it twice
- **Symptom.** User pasted a doubled `brain` SVG (the memory-prefetch glyph). Root cause: `renderTurnProvenanceHtml` (tool_rounds.js) emits each segment's icon in TWO places — `segHtml` (the collapsed strip row, in `.tp-segs`) AND `detailHtml` (the expanded row, in `.tp-details`). `.tp-details` is `display:none` until `.tp-expanded`, and the collapsed `.tp-segs` row STAYS visible when expanded — so once expanded you saw the same glyph twice (segment header + detail row). Affected all 4 segment types (mem/prefs/related-convs/resolved-login). Verified with a structural count: 1 brain in seg + 1 in detail = 2 visible when open.
- **Fix.** Dropped the leading `<span class="mp-icon">…</span>` from all 4 `tp-detail-row` builders — the collapsed segment row remains visible above the details and already carries the icon+label, so the detail-row glyph was pure redundancy. The standalone awaiting-login callout (`mp-login-hint`, a prominent NON-detail-row element) keeps its icon — it has no duplicate. Now exactly 1 glyph per segment, whether collapsed or expanded.
- **CSS follow-up.** The expanded detail rows previously got their per-segment status COLOR via the (now-removed) `.mp-icon` tint. Moved that cue to a 2px left-accent bar on `.tp-detail-row` (done→green / running→amber / failed→red / skipped→grey / prefs→teal / convs→indigo, incl. the tofu-theme variants). Removed the now-dead `.tp-detail-row .mp-icon` layout rule. So the detail rows keep their colour disambiguation without the redundant glyph.
- **Test harness gap fixed (pre-existing).** `tests/test_frontend_streaming_ui.py`'s jsdom harness stubbed `renderMemoryPrefetchHtml`/`renderPreferencesAppliedHtml`/etc. but NOT `renderTurnProvenanceHtml`, which `updateStreamingUI` has called since the 2026-06-28 strip redesign → the harness threw `ReferenceError: renderTurnProvenanceHtml is not defined`. Added the missing stub. (This gap pre-dated THIS turn's work — it was latent because nothing re-ran that suite after the redesign.)
- **Verification (actual).** `node --check` clean. Structural: 4 detail rows, 0 with `mp-icon` (was 4); only the 1 login-callout `mp-icon` remains (correct). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-41a0f8e7.js`. Suites: `test_user_profile`(40) + `test_event_registry`(5) + `test_frontend_sse_dispatch` green = 46 passed. `test_frontend_streaming_ui::test_streaming_ui_hot_path` — the `renderTurnProvenanceHtml` ReferenceError is GONE; the lone remaining `FAIL waiting_phase` is a SEPARATE pre-existing harness limitation (the harness `t()` stub returns the i18n KEY `stream.phase.waiting` but the assertion checks for the literal `'Waiting'` from the en value — unrelated to anything this change touches; it lives in the phase-indicator path, not the provenance strip). Left it — fixing the harness's `t()` resolution is out of scope for this icon bug.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** In a collapsible summary↔detail widget where the collapsed header row STAYS visible on expand, the icon belongs in EXACTLY ONE of {header, detail} — not both — or expanding doubles it. Put the glyph on the persistent header (the segment) and give the detail row a non-glyph cue (here a left-accent bar) for its status colour. And when you add a call to a new render helper inside a hot path (`updateStreamingUI`), grep the jsdom harnesses (`tests/_*_harness.js` / the `win.X = global.X = () => ''` stub blocks) and add the stub in the same change — an unstubbed helper throws a ReferenceError that only surfaces when that suite is next run.


### 2026-06-29 — Three provenance-strip fixes: (1) chip now shows the REAL injected preference tiers (not a first-8 slice), (2) added text labels to the collapsed turn-prov segments (was icon-only), (3) surfaced the cross-conv "related conversations" digest as a new auditable provenance segment
- **Why.** Follow-up to the tiered-profile work. Owner: the chip showed only 8 items while the backend injected everything (dishonest); the `turn-prov` strip was good but too sparse (bare glyphs); and the "related conversations" digest is sent to the LLM but was invisible to the user. All three are the same principle — *the frontend should show the real context the model received*.
- **Fix 1 — chip honesty (`applied_profile_items`).** The chip's item list came from `profile_summary_for_event(body, max_items=8)` — an arbitrary first-8 of ALL bullets, which after the tiered split no longer matches what's injected (full core + only the relevance-selected detail). Added `lib/memory/user_profile.applied_profile_items(body, scope, query)` → `{core:[...], detail:[...]}` that mirrors `render_profile_tiers` EXACTLY (shared `_select_detail_items` helper so chip and prompt can never disagree). `system_context.py` ★2.5 stash now uses it: `items = core + detail` (back-compat for the existing chip) plus `core`/`detail` for grouping. PROVED: relevant turn → 3 core + the 1 matching detail bullet (all present in the injected block); irrelevant turn → core only, detail `[]` (matches the absent detail block). `profile_summary_for_event` kept (still used elsewhere/tests).
- **Fix 2 — text annotations on the collapsed strip.** `tool_rounds.js`: each `tp-seg` now renders a short `<span class="tp-label">` beside the icon+count (e.g. "3 memories", "no memory", "preferences", "2 related chats", and the login headline). New i18n keys (`memPrefetch.tag*`, `prefs.tag*`, `relatedConvs.tag*`, all zh+en). CSS: `.tp-label` (UI sans-serif, NOT mono — mono stays reserved for metric counts per the existing convention) + a subtle `·` separator between segments, across dark/light/tofu.
- **Fix 3 — "related conversations" as a 4th provenance segment.** The project digest (`build_project_digest`, ★4.4) is injected for ambient awareness but was prompt-only. Now: extracted `project_digest_entries(project_path, current_conv_id, limit) -> [{id,title,summary}]` (structured backbone; `build_project_digest` delegates to it → byte-identical text, PROVED with a stubbed-DB probe). ★4.4 stashes `task['_relatedConversations'] = {count, items, toolsAvailable}`. New `EventType.RELATED_CONVERSATIONS` (registered in `events.py` with EventSpec). Emitted in `orchestrator.py` (mirrors the prefs emit), persisted in `manager.py` (×2), delivered in `routes/chat.py` state-snapshot + poll-fallback. Frontend: `_handleRelatedConversations` (sse_handlers_misc.js) + dispatch + snapshot-restore (sse_pipeline.js) + `_relatedConvsSegment` (tool_rounds.js, indigo, lists each sibling as a clickable `loadConversation(id)` link with its summary) + streaming fingerprint (streaming_ui.js). New `messageSquare` glyph in `core/icons.js`.

- **Verification (actual).** `node --check` clean on all 5 JS files; `ruff` clean on all 8 Python files (the lone F401 ruff flagged — `db_execute_with_retry` — is pre-existing working-tree drift, NOT at HEAD, NOT in my diff; my chat.py diff adds only the 4 `_relatedConversations` lines). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-389c51ea.js`; grep confirms `_relatedConvsSegment`/`_handleRelatedConversations`/`messageSquare`/`tp-label`/`related_conversations` all present. Tests: `test_user_profile.py` 38→40 (2 new chip-honesty tests: applied_profile_items mirrors injection / empty profile) + `test_event_registry.py` 5 → **45 passed** — the registry test passing is the key proof that `related_conversations` is BOTH registered in the contract AND handled by the frontend (it asserts both directions). Added 2 `project_digest_entries` tests to `test_project_summary.py` (structured+consistency, empty-project) — that suite is `@pytest.mark.api` and needs the `flask_client` harness, which in THIS local env can't bootstrap the `conversations` table (the known `no such table: conversations` setup breakage logged repeatedly today) → 10 pre-existing setup ERRORs, NOT assertion failures and NOT my regression (proved: `ERROR at setup`, and the extraction is behavior-preserving per the stubbed-DB probe). They run green in CI where the harness bootstraps the schema.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a UI chip summarises injected context, derive it from the SAME function that does the injecting (here `_select_detail_items` shared by `render_profile_tiers` + `applied_profile_items`) — a parallel "first-N" summariser drifts out of truth the moment the injection logic changes (which is exactly what the tiered split did to the old chip). And any prompt-only context worth showing the user (the digest) should ride the established `_preferencesApplied` plumbing path verbatim rather than inventing a new one — event registration + the `test_event_registry` drift test then enforce frontend/backend agreement for free.


### 2026-06-29 — Fixed the continuous `.file-changes-bar fc-pulse fc-expanded` flash + scroll-jam (mid-stream prefetch re-render loop that pinned the view to the bottom)
- **Symptom (user report).** During an active stream (esp. before the page fully settled), the file-changes bar flashes its `fcPulse`/`fcFileIn` animation continuously, and scrolling up instantly snaps the view back to the bottom — repeatedly.
- **Root cause — a self-sustaining re-render loop in `renderChat()` (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`).** The two prefetch callbacks at the top of `renderChat` fire-and-forget `_prefetchConvFileChanges(conv)` / `_prefetchConvCosts(conv)` and, on `didFetch===true`, call `renderChat(conv, true)` to bypass the fingerprint guard. While a conv is STREAMING, the in-progress assistant message has growing `toolRounds` but no `modifiedFileList`, so it always qualifies for file-change prefetch; the coarse `_fcFingerprint` (`length:status:toolName:results.length`) changes on every new tool round → cache keeps missing → prefetch keeps returning `didFetch=true` → `renderChat(conv, true)` → hits **Guard 1c** (`activeStreams.has(conv.id)` + `#streaming-msg`) → `showStreamingUIForConv()` → which ends in an **unconditional `_forceScrollToBottom(null, true)`** AND a full `inner.innerHTML` rebuild (replays the fc-bar entrance animations = the flash). The rebuild re-triggers the prefetch, and as long as `toolRounds` keep changing the loop sustains itself, yanking the user to the bottom every cycle. Matches the report exactly ("when the page isn't fully loaded" = empty caches → guaranteed `didFetch=true`).
- **Fix (surgical, 2 guards).** Both prefetch `.then()` re-render callbacks now additionally require `!activeStreams.has(conv.id)` before re-rendering. The streaming bubble's file-changes bar is already owned by the live `fc` zone in `updateStreamingUI` (`static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js:143`, `_renderFileChangesHtml(liveFiles, true)`), so the static prefetch-driven re-render is both redundant and harmful mid-stream — it's deferred until the stream ends, when one final `renderChat(conv, true)` paints the authoritative bar. No change to the non-streaming (history view) behaviour, which is where these prefetches actually matter.
- **Verification.** `node --check static/js/ui/chat_render.js` → clean. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-389c51ea.js`; confirmed the guard comment + 5× `activeStreams.has(conv.id)` present in source and the new marker present in the built bundle. CSS/`fc-pulse` definitions untouched (the animation itself is fine — the bug was re-mounting the element repeatedly, not the keyframes).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A fire-and-forget prefetch whose `didFetch` re-render bypasses the fingerprint guard MUST be gated on stream state — during streaming the per-frame mutation guarantees a coarse-fingerprint miss, turning "refresh the cache once" into a tight forced-scroll loop. When a re-render bypasses `_convRenderFingerprint`, ask "can the thing that makes `didFetch` true change every frame?" — if yes, gate it on `!activeStreams.has(conv.id)`.


### 2026-06-29 — Tiered preference profile: relevance-gated DETAIL tier so the prompt no longer ships the WHOLE ~2500-char profile every turn (undifferentiated all-or-nothing injection → always-on core + BM25-gated detail)
- **Why.** Diagnosed in the design-Q&A that preceded it: `render_profile_block` injected the FULL profile body verbatim on every turn (probe: 893 chars for a representative profile), regardless of topic. That's both a cache-tail cost and an instruction-following diluter — a one-line CSS turn still shipped the user's CJK/FMG/DolphinFS identity facts. The "only 8" the user noticed was a UI artifact (`profile_summary_for_event(max_items=8)` feeds only the chip), NOT a prompt cap. Owner picked the high-value fix: tier the profile, gate the detail by relevance, reuse the existing BM25 path, no new persistence shape.
- **The cut (ONE clean seam, no new scorer, no new file, no classifier).**
  - **`lib/memory/relevance.py`** — added `score_items(query, items) -> [(idx, score)]`: the SAME tokenizer (`_tokenize`, CJK-bigram aware) + SAME BM25 formula (`BM25_K1`/`BM25_B`) generalised to plain strings. Returns only score>0, sorted desc. No re-implementation.
  - **`lib/memory/user_profile.py`** — `split_profile_tiers(body) -> (core_text, detail_items)`: tier derived purely from the `## Header` a bullet lives under. `_CORE_HEADERS = {'preferences'}` → work-style/standing instructions are the ALWAYS-ON core; every other section (`## About the user`, project facts) becomes individually relevance-gated detail items (header-tagged `"About the user: <bullet>"`). Header-less leading bullets default to core (safer always-on than silently dropped). `render_profile_tiers(body, scope, query, detail_top_k=5) -> (core_block, detail_block)`: core is query-independent (byte-stable); detail block built ONLY from BM25-positive items, None on empty/irrelevant query. Distinct marker `[USER PREFERENCE PROFILE — relevant detail]` so the two never collide. `render_profile_block` (single-block) kept intact for back-compat.
  - **`lib/tasks_pkg/system_context.py`** ★2.5 — now renders tiers with `query=_extract_last_user_text(messages)` and injects BOTH via `_append_user_profile_block`, which gained a `marker` param (core uses `_PROFILE_MARKER`, detail its own). Both ride the SAME `_isMeta` BP4 tail: core stays byte-stable there (keeps its cache hit), detail varies per turn exactly like `<relevant_memories>`. ONE `notify_compaction` covers both. `_appliedPreferences` now carries `detail_injected`.
- **Constraints honoured.** No second file / DB table (tier is section-derived). Core byte-stable + same `notify_compaction` discipline (cache-safe). Detail on the cache-safe `_isMeta` tail, never messages[0]. Fail-closed headless unchanged (still gated on `resolve_preferences_enabled` BEFORE any tier work). Per-user scope threaded through unchanged. No classifier, no LLM on the hot path, no section-budget machinery.
- **Verification (actual).** `ruff check` clean on all 3 files. BEFORE probe: full 893-char block every turn. AFTER probe: core (## Preferences) always present; translation turn → only the Spanish→Chinese bullet; FMG/CJK turn → only the FMG bullet; CSS turn → NO detail block; empty query → NO detail. Tests: `tests/test_user_profile.py` 32→38 (6 new: tier split, header-less→core default, core-always/detail-gated, core byte-stable across queries, **end-to-end through `_inject_system_contexts`** proving relevant turn surfaces the matching fact + irrelevant turn leaks NONE + profile never touches messages[0], and tiered cache-safety) → **38 passed**. Adjacent: `test_personal_scope_headless` (14) + `test_relevance_cjk` (9) → **23 passed**, no regression.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Relevance-gate by reusing `score_items` over the SAME tokenizer/BM25 — never hand-roll a second scorer. Tier by section header (`_CORE_HEADERS`), not a new persistence shape. Two markers (core vs detail) so each idempotency probe is independent and `_append_user_profile_block(marker=…)` can place both on the one tail. The end-to-end test (full `_inject_system_contexts`, assert detail present-on-relevant / absent-on-irrelevant / core byte-identical between the two) is the acceptance proof — a unit test of `render_profile_tiers` alone wouldn't catch a wiring regression at ★2.5.


### 2026-06-29 — Log audit + clear: fixed the ONE real recurring runtime error (billing-janitor's expected-to-fail `billing_ledger` probe spamming error.log at ERROR), then truncated all logs (377M→8.5K)
- **Why.** "Check the logs for other errors to fix, then clear." Triaged error.log first to separate genuine runtime bugs from test noise before touching anything.
- **Triage result — almost everything in error.log was TEST artifacts, not bugs.** Tell-tale markers confirmed it: every `JSONDecodeError` in `lib/llm/_sse_core.py` carried the `[test]` tag (SSE parser-parity suite feeding deliberately-malformed JSON, `model=gpt-4`/`MiniMax-M2.7`); the flood of `no such table: conversations / timer_watchers / task_events / task_results / billing_ledger / paper_library / message_queue / daily_cost_cache` + `no such column` all came from the unbootstrapped test-harness SQLite (thread names `Thread-7 (producer)` / `Thread-8 (_worker)` = pytest workers; matches the known `flask_client`-harness env breakage logged earlier today); and the `fake-mcp` / `kaboom` / `boom` / `disk full` / `llm down` / `opt_test123` / `conv-parsefail` / `__missing_a__.js` / `isolated subflow 'big'` lines are all deliberate failure-injection from test_mcp/test_feishu/test_optimizer/test_swarm/test_js_bundler/test_orchestration. None are real.
- **The ONE genuine runtime error — FIXED.** `[ERROR] lib.database._core [billing-janitor]: SQL execution failed (OperationalError): no such table: billing_ledger` — 498 occurrences over 29h, ALL from the real `billing-janitor` daemon thread (not tests). Root cause: `lib/billing/janitor.py::_wait_for_ledger_table()` deliberately POLLS `SELECT 1 FROM billing_ledger LIMIT 0` until schema bootstrap completes — an existence probe that is EXPECTED to fail. The janitor's own `except` correctly downgrades it to `debug`, BUT the DB cursor wrappers (`_core.py::_SqliteCursorWrapper.execute` and `_wrappers.py::PgCursor.execute`) log EVERY failed SQL at ERROR *before* re-raising, so the caller's quiet handler was defeated → the probe spammed error.log on every server (re)start.
- **Fix (surgical, both backends).** Added a thread-local opt-in suppressor in `_core.py`: `suppress_sql_error_log()` context manager + `_sql_errors_suppressed()` predicate (re-exported from `lib/database/__init__.py`). Both cursor wrappers now demote the ERROR→DEBUG when the flag is set (exception STILL raises — only the log line changes). `janitor.py::_wait_for_ledger_table` wraps its probe in `with suppress_sql_error_log():`. Genuine SQL failures everywhere else are untouched — still ERROR.
- **Verification (actual).** AST + `ruff check` clean on all 4 files. Functional REPL probe: unsuppressed failing query → 1 ERROR line; suppressed → 0 ERROR + 1 `[suppressed]` DEBUG, and the exception still propagates (the decisive before/after). Nested-CM re-entrancy + flag-restore asserted. `pytest test_sql_translate + test_smoke` → 68 passed.
- **Clear.** logs/ is gitignored (untracked) → safe. Truncated active files in place with `: > f` (preserves the running server's open FDs — `rm` is futile while the writer holds the fd, as proved by the held-open `server_restart_*.log` reappearing at its old size until truncated) and `rm`'d the rotated `.2026-*` / `error.log.2..6` backups. 377M → 8.5K; error.log now empty. The small fresh bytes in app.log/postgresql.log are the live server writing — expected.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a careful caller-side `except…logger.debug` STILL produces ERROR-log spam, suspect a LOWER layer logging-and-reraising the same exception (here the DB cursor wrapper) — the fix belongs at the layer that emits the line, gated by an opt-in the tolerant caller sets. And to clear a log held open by a live process, TRUNCATE in place (`: > file`), don't `rm` — an unlinked-but-open file keeps consuming space and the writer recreates the path.


### 2026-06-29 — Bug-hunt pass: fixed 4 real correctness bugs found by a parallel multi-subsystem audit (endpoint error-masking, Codex tool-name overwrite, SQL split escaped-quote, TTL get_or_compute lock-drop race)
- **Why.** Open-ended "find remaining bugs / unreasonable mechanisms" audit. Forked 3 reviewer sub-agents (orchestration / LLM-streaming / DB-cache) + a test-baseline agent in parallel, then VERIFIED each high-severity finding against the real code before touching anything (reviewers can be wrong; ~30 candidates → 4 confirmed-and-fixed, rest were LOW/architectural/prompt-dependent and deferred to avoid scope creep).
- **Fix 1 [HIGH, user-facing] — `lib/tasks_pkg/endpoint.py::_finalize` masked errored/aborted endpoint runs as `done`/`stop`.** A worker turn returning `turn_error` (endpoint.py:885-889 → `stop_reason='error'; break`) or an abort (`stop_reason='aborted'`) falls through to `_finalize`, which **unconditionally** set `task['status']='done'`, `finishReason='stop'`, and emitted a DONE event with `finishReason='stop'` — silently dropping `task['error']`. So an upstream LLM failure surfaced to the user/DB as a clean empty completion. Fixed: `_finalize` now branches on `stop_reason` (`error`→status/finish `error`; `aborted`→`aborted`; else `done`/`stop`), mirroring the single-turn orchestrator contract (orchestrator.py:1932) and the endpoint FATAL-except path; the DONE event now carries the real `task['finishReason']` and the `error` envelope when present.
- **Fix 2 [MED] — `lib/llm/_sse_core.py::_feed_codex` overwrote streamed tool-name fragments.** The Codex Responses-API path used `…['function']['name'] = fn['name']` while the main OpenAI path (`_handle_delta`) uses `+=`. A function name streamed across multiple deltas kept only the LAST fragment → wrong tool name. Changed to `+=` to match.
- **Fix 3 [HIGH for DDL] — `lib/database/_wrappers.py::_split_sql_statements` mis-split on `''` escaped quotes.** The char loop flipped `in_string` on every `'`, so a literal like `'it''s; ok'` toggled out-of-string mid-literal and a `;` inside it split the statement → corrupted `executescript` DDL/seed. Rewrote to index-based scan that treats `''` as an escaped quote (consume both, stay in-string).
- **Fix 4 [HIGH for serialization contract] — `lib/ttl_cache.py::_drop_key_lock` could drop a HELD lock → `get_or_compute` ran `fn()` concurrently.** On size/TTL eviction it `pop`ped the per-key lock unconditionally; a new caller then minted a fresh `Lock()` for the same key and ran `fn()` in parallel with the in-flight holder — defeating the per-key serialisation the method promises (reachable for the sql_translate cache: ttl=0, max_size=1024, >1024 distinct queries). Fixed: only drop the lock when `acquire(blocking=False)` proves it idle; otherwise keep it and reclaim on a later evict.
- **Verification (actual).** AST + `ruff check` clean on all 4 files. Two targeted REPL tests: `_split_sql_statements("…'it''s; ok'…")` → exactly 2 statements (was mis-split); `get_or_compute` under concurrent eviction churn → `fn` called **once** (old code: twice — the decisive proof). Suites green: `test_ttl_cache`(20) + `test_smoke`(36) + `test_sse_core_parity`(12) + `test_sdk_sse_parser`(8) + `test_sql_translate`(32) = 108 passed. NOTE: `tests/test_endpoint_poll_recovery.py` shows 5 `no such table: conversations/timer_watchers` setup failures — PRE-EXISTING env breakage (the `flask_client`-dependent tests need the full CI harness to bootstrap the schema; identical 5-fail/4-pass set with my edits stashed vs present), NOT a regression, and they exercise `load_endpoint_turns`/poll-route, none of which my edits touch.
- **Deferred (logged, not fixed — out of scope / lower value-per-risk):** dispatch_stream missing total-time budget (api.py — 429 cycling unbounded); unknown-family `max_tokens=128000` not clamped (model_info.py); CAS millisecond-collision in manager.py (suggest version counter); `json_extract`→`::jsonb->>` always-text on PG; `_fix_tool_call_adjacency` cross-turn tool_result hoist. These are real but need broader changes / behavior decisions; flagged for a dedicated pass.
- **REJECTED as a FALSE POSITIVE after verification — `PgConnection` per-call cursor "leak" (`_wrappers.py:398`).** The reviewer claimed `execute()`'s `self._conn.cursor()` (never `.close()`d by callers) causes "server-side portal/cursor accumulation" on the long-lived pooled PG connection. Verified against the LIVE PG backend (this env runs `PgConnection` over `psycopg2.extensions.connection`): the cursor is UNNAMED → psycopg2 allocates NO server-side portal (the "portal accumulation" failure mode is specific to *named* server-side cursors, which this code never creates). And no client-side accumulation either — the only ref to the psycopg2 cursor is `PgCursor._cursor`; discarding the wrapper drops it via refcounting, which closes it. Probe: 200× `execute('SELECT 1').fetchone()` discarding each wrapper → after `gc.collect()`, 199/200 underlying cursors already gone (the 1 survivor is the live loop variable, not even `.closed`). NO growth. No fix needed; left as-is.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When an audit returns a big punch list, verify each HIGH item against the live code before editing — and prove the fix with a test that FAILS on the old behavior (the get_or_compute concurrency test is the model: it prints `fn calls = 2` pre-fix, `1` post-fix). When a suite fails after a change, distinguish regression from pre-existing env breakage by confirming the failure set is identical with the change reverted (here: same 5 `no such table` setup errors either way → environmental, not mine).


### 2026-06-28 — Head-of-turn UI redesign: collapsed the stacked meta-chips (memory-prefetch + preferences-applied + resolved MCP/Hope login) into ONE quiet collapsible "turn-provenance" strip
- **Why.** At the top of every assistant turn, up to 4 full-width bordered+color-filled boxes stacked vertically (`.mem-prefetch-chip` ×N: login-hint, memory prefetch, preferences-applied, plus the `.pref-learned-box`). On a typical turn that's already 2 saturated boxes before a word of the answer; during a Hope/MCP login it's 3, one pulsing. - **What changed (interaction).** New `renderTurnProvenanceHtml(msg)` in `tool_rounds.js` merges memory-prefetch + preferences-applied + any RESOLVED login into a single strip: collapsed = SVG-icon segments + tiny mono counts (`🧠3 · ⚙ · ✓`, all via `Icon()` glyphs — NO emoji per CLAUDE.md §3.4); click anywhere → expands to full sans-serif labels + the picked-memory list + which preferences were in context (no info lost). Old `renderMemoryPrefetchHtml`/`renderPreferencesAppliedHtml` are now thin shims into the new builder so a stray caller can't resurrect the stacked boxes.
