- **Polish.** Added `chevronDown` glyph to `core/icons.js` (replaced the raw `▾`); headlines use the UI sans-serif, monospace reserved for metric numbers/counts. Learned-preference card softened (hairline border, near-transparent bg) to match — kept SEPARATE per owner's call because it has Confirm/Dismiss buttons.
- **Container-state accent (follow-up).** First pass emitted `tp-running`/`tp-done`/`tp-has-failed` on the container but only styled the per-segment classes — the container state was computed-but-inert (dead attribute, exactly the rot this task targeted). Fixed: a 2px left accent bar — amber pulsing (running) / green (done) / red (has-failed), across all three themes (dark base + `[data-theme=light]` + `[data-theme=tofu]` with its own kinako pulse keyframe). Base border is transparent and reserves the box, so toggling left color is layout-shift-free. A preferences-only strip has no `state` on its segment → `tp-done`, which is correct (nothing in-flight, nothing failed).
- **Files.** `static/js/core/icons.js`, `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`, `static/js/ui/chat_render.js`, `static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`, `static/js/i18n.js`, `static/styles.css`. No `_BUNDLE_FILES`/blueprint changes — all files already bundled.
- **Verification (actual output).** `node --check` clean on all 5 JS files. Bundle rebuilt: `[Bundle] Built bundle-ff3c998e.js (95 files, 2609KB raw)`. In-bundle: `renderTurnProvenanceHtml` 7 refs, `turn-prov` 6, `chevronDown` 3, `login.awaiting` i18n 5. Regression (want 0): dead `_renderPreferencesAppliedHtml_unused` 0, raw `mp-chevron>▾` 0, emoji in provenance/login builders 0. CSS state rules present at `styles.css:16936–16950` (3 rules × 3 themes + 2 keyframes). NOTE: CSS ships via `styles.css` (served separately), NOT the JS bundle — so the bundle hash is stable across a CSS-only change; don't mistake the unchanged hash for "the edit didn't land."
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When you compute a state value and stamp it onto the DOM as a class/attribute, make sure SOMETHING actually styles it — an emitted-but-unstyled class is silent dead UI (the reviewer caught this; it's the same class of rot — inert computed output — that the broader optimization arc was about). And a stable bundle hash after a CSS-only edit is EXPECTED (CSS isn't in the JS bundle), not a sign the change was lost.

### 2026-06-28 — Decoupling pass: extracted _compute_write_breakdown (the pure cache-write decomposition, ~210 LOC) out of orchestrator.py (2259→2049 LOC) into lib/tasks_pkg/write_breakdown.py, behind a re-export. ONE disciplined cut at the genuinely clean seam; left run_task + _finalize_and_emit_done in place (deliberately).
- **Why.** The "decouple aggressively" half of the objective was untouched. Did it measurement-first, NOT a blind split of all three monoliths.
- **Structural assessment (AST, evidence).** `orchestrator.py` 2259 LOC, 7 top-level functions: `run_task` (1132L), `_finalize_and_emit_done` (585L), `_compute_write_breakdown` (196L), `_finalize_dangling_tool_rounds` (79L), `_check_suspicious_completion` (46L), `_emit_tool_round_phase` (15L), `_run_single_turn` (75L). `run_task` + `_finalize_and_emit_done` = 76% of the file.
- **Recommendation (and why only ONE cut).**
  - `run_task` (1132L) — a cohesive run-loop with shared loop state; splitting would SCATTER it (high churn). LEFT ALONE. The repo's prior orchestrator extractions (`commit_round.py`, `auto_translate.py`) carved out *helpers*, never the loop.
  - `_finalize_and_emit_done` (585L) — large but a **21-positional-param** signature = tightly coupled to run_task's locals by data flow, interleaved with fallback-LLM + autopilot hooks. Medium seam, medium risk — payoff didn't justify it this pass. LEFT ALONE.
  - `_compute_write_breakdown` (196L) — the CLEAN seam: a **pure function** `(task, api_rounds, round_num) → dict|None`, no `append_event`/DB/`build_body`/shared closure, only `int`/dict ops + `logger` + its two private constants (`_ENVELOPE_MAX_TOKENS`, `_READ_DROP_WASTE_TOKENS`), and exactly ONE call site (`run_task`, orchestrator.py:1794). Textbook `commit_round`-style extraction. EXTRACTED.
- **What changed.** New `lib/tasks_pkg/write_breakdown.py` (244L w/ docstrings) holds the function + its two constants + a HOT_PATH header. `orchestrator.py` replaced the ~210-LOC block with a 3-symbol re-export (`from lib.tasks_pkg.write_breakdown import _compute_write_breakdown, _ENVELOPE_MAX_TOKENS, _READ_DROP_WASTE_TOKENS  # noqa: F401`), mirroring the existing `_repair_json` re-export convention. Zero caller changes — the sole call site uses the same name.
- **Verification (actual output).** AST OK on both files. Import+identity: `orchestrator._compute_write_breakdown IS write_breakdown._compute_write_breakdown`, both constants equal (800/2000). Functional invariant: sub-items sum to EXACTLY `write`; empty input → `None`. **The decisive proof: a PRE-EXISTING `tests/test_write_breakdown.py` (17 tests) imports the function FROM `lib.tasks_pkg.orchestrator` (the re-export path) and PASSES unchanged** — the strongest behavior-preservation evidence possible. Combined `pytest test_write_breakdown + test_package_facades + test_abort_dangling_tool_round + the 3 new suites + smoke` → **190 passed**. Baseline (known 2 failures) unperturbed: this touches no swarm/frontend.
- **Pre-existing lint NOT mine (flagged, left).** ruff flags 2 F401 in orchestrator.py: `os` (L13) and `_patch_assistant_message_with_git` (L51, in the untouched `commit_round` import block). `git show HEAD:...orchestrator.py | ruff` shows ZERO F401 at HEAD → these are WORKING-TREE drift from earlier uncommitted edits, NOT my extraction (my diff replaced only the write-breakdown block, which referenced neither). `_patch_assistant_message_with_git` is imported directly from `commit_round` everywhere else (nobody imports it via orchestrator), so its orchestrator re-export is dead — but removing a documented re-export in a tree with 200+ uncommitted files is out-of-scope risk I won't take blind. Left both; flagged for a dedicated lint pass. My re-exported symbols are `# noqa: F401`-marked and ruff-clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** Decouple by EVIDENCE: AST the file, find the function that is already a pure top-level helper with a single call site and no shared closure — that's the seam — and leave the cohesive loop and the 21-arg finalizer alone (splitting them scatters, not decouples). A pre-existing test written against the OLD import path is the ideal extraction safety net: if it passes through the re-export unchanged, behavior is provably preserved. And when ruff flags adjacent dead imports, check `git show HEAD` before claiming/disclaiming them — here they pre-dated the edit, so they're neither my regression to hide nor my cleanup to smuggle in.
- **STATUS — objective substantively complete.** Tier-1 cleanup ✅ · testing (91 new behavioral tests, 3 gaps closed) ✅ · logging (audited clean) ✅ · decoupling (one evidence-driven cut; remaining monoliths assessed and deliberately left) ✅. The `_finalize_and_emit_done` / `manager.py` / `tool_dispatch.py` splits remain available as future passes but were judged lower value-per-risk than the work done.


### 2026-06-28 — Test-coverage pass #3 (FINAL of the three gaps): added tests/test_daily_report.py (33 behavioral tests) — cost rollup math, transcript building, fuzzy TODO matching, robust JSON extraction/repair, stream post-processing. All three audit-identified zero-coverage subsystems now closed.
- **Why.** Last and largest of the audit's zero-coverage gaps: `lib/daily_report` (2089 LOC). Closes the "advance testing" half of the original objective for the identified gaps (feishu + optimizer + daily_report all now have behavioral suites).
- **Coverage ceiling (the explicit ask — and it's HIGH here).** Unlike optimizer's log-miner analyzer, daily_report's SUBSTANTIVE logic is genuinely pure and well-reachable, so this suite is mostly real behavioral coverage, not graceful-degrade stubs:
  - **cost.py** — `_qwen_cny` (tiered CNY pricing) + `_calc_msg_cost_cny` (the core rollup: token-key aliasing prompt/input + completion/output, cache write/read multipliers, legacy-preset→model mapping, qwen-vs-USD branch, empty→0.0). `lib` pricing globals + `lib.pricing.get_pricing_data/lookup_pricing` STUBBED so the math is deterministic regardless of the live pricing table.
  - **conversations.py** — `_safe_int_ts` (str/float/None coercion), `_build_transcript_from_messages` (multimodal content-list flattening, out-of-window filtering, tool-name extraction, missing-field/empty tolerance, budget), and `_analyse_conversations` empty fast-path + LLM-output stream post-processing (conv_id validation, status normalization) with `_run_llm_analysis` + the yesterday-writeback helpers STUBBED.
  - **todos.py** — `_normalize_todo_text`, `_fuzzy_todo_match` (exact/substring + char-Jaccard + LCS), and `_close_yesterday_remaining_todos` / `_mark_yesterday_todos_done` driven on an IN-MEMORY `_prev` dict with `_defer_save=True` → zero disk I/O.
  - **llm.py** — `_extract_json_result` + `_repair_truncated_json` (direct parse, ```json fences, legacy bare-list, embedded-in-prose, truncated-at-clean-boundary salvage, mid-string-unsalvageable) + `_pick_persona` (pure stats→persona, always well-formed).
  - DB-coupled (`_scan_costs_in_range` / `_get_monthly_costs` / `_extract_convs_for_date` family) covered ONLY for graceful-degrade-on-DB-error (`get_thread_db`→raise → `{}`/`[]`). Full DB seeding out of scope.
- **TWO of my initial expectations were WRONG — corrected to match real behavior (the value is documenting the real contract, not asserting a guess).**
  1. `test_stream_post_processing_validates_conv_ids` — I expected the named stream to keep ONLY `["c1"]`. Reality: with a SINGLE unclaimed conv (`c2`), the `len(unclaimed) >= 2` branch doesn't fire; the `elif unclaimed:` branch folds `c2` into the LAST stream. So the real, correct assertions are: the bogus `"nonexistent"` id (not in `all_conv_ids`) IS dropped, and every REAL conv is accounted for across streams (`{c1, c2}`). Verified the fold logic empirically before rewriting.
  2. `test_truncated_json_is_repaired` — my fragment was cut MID-STRING (`"secon`), which `_repair_truncated_json` cannot salvage (returns None → `([],[],[])`). Verified empirically that a fragment cut at a CLEAN value boundary (`{"title": "second"`) IS salvaged (closes the open `[`/`{`). Split into two tests: clean-boundary→repaired, mid-string→unsalvageable. Both now document the actual repair contract.
- **Isolation / determinism.** No network, no live LLM (`_run_llm_analysis`/pricing stubbed), no real DB (`get_thread_db`→raise exercises the except path). `unit`-marked (file `pytestmark` + per-class), 0.58s.
- **Verification (actual output).** `pytest tests/test_daily_report.py -q` → **33 passed in 0.58s**, PYTEST_EXIT=0 (after correcting the 2 wrong expectations; the suite caught my own mistakes before I could claim done). Combined `pytest tests/test_daily_report.py tests/test_optimizer.py tests/test_feishu.py tests/test_smoke.py -q` → **127 passed** (33+37+21+36). **Mutation probe** on the core rollup: zeroed the `output_cost_usd = out * out_p / 1e6` term → `test_calc_cost_usd_model_with_stubbed_pricing` **FAILED** as designed (total no longer matches expected); `test_alternate_token_keys` correctly stayed green (it asserts two equivalent inputs are EQUAL — both shift identically under the mutation, so the absolute-value test is the right detector, by design). Restored from backup. Baseline: daily_report touches no swarm/frontend → known 2 failures unperturbed by construction; full ~190s tier NOT re-run.
- **NOT added to the smoke list** (per instruction) — behavioral, not an import guard; `lib.daily_report` is already import-guarded from Tier-1.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a test of LLM-output post-processing or a JSON-repair routine fails, FIRST check whether your EXPECTATION matches the real code path (folds, branch thresholds, what the repairer actually salvages) before suspecting a bug — assert the real contract, don't bend the code to a guessed one. Verify the exact behavior with a 5-line REPL probe (`_repair_truncated_json(fragment)`) rather than guessing. And pick the mutation-probe TARGET test deliberately: an equality-between-equivalent-inputs test won't catch a uniform scaling bug — an absolute-expected-value test will.
- **STATUS — all three audit zero-coverage gaps CLOSED.** feishu (21) + optimizer (37) + daily_report (33) = 91 new behavioral tests, all `unit`, all mutation-probed, none added to the smoke list. Remaining from the broader objective: the Tier-3 monolith decoupling backlog (orchestrator.py 2259 LOC, manager.py/tool_dispatch.py ~1900 each) — deferred, higher-effort, separate pass.


### 2026-06-28 — Test-coverage pass #2: added tests/test_optimizer.py (37 behavioral tests) for the Daily Optimizer's DECISION logic — registry invariants, LLM-output validation, the whitelist auto-apply GATE, and analyzer's pure scoring/clustering slice
- **Why.** Audit gap #2: `lib/optimizer` (1796 LOC) had zero behavioral tests. Picked second after feishu. The security-relevant surface is the auto-apply gate (only `block_search_domain` may auto-apply; everything else must land in `pending_review` for human approval per CLAUDE.md §10) and the trust boundary on LLM-proposed actions.
- **Coverage ceiling (the explicit ask — honest, not padded).** `analyzer.py` (734 LOC) is MOSTLY log-file + DB readers: the `_collect_*` collectors walk `APP_LOG`/`AUDIT_LOG_FILE`/`ERROR_LOG` and the SYSTEM/CHAT DBs (`get_thread_db`). Those DB-coupled collectors are NOT unit-tested beyond their graceful-degrade contract — testing them fully would need a seeded multi-domain DB, not worth it for a nightly read-only miner. What IS genuinely unit-testable and valuable: (a) the pure parsers (`_parse_app_log_ts`/`_parse_audit_line`/`_audit_ts_aware`/`_classify_error_signature`/`_domain_of`), (b) the real SCORING/CLUSTERING core — `_collect_app_log_signals` (regex tallying) and `_collect_recurring_issues` (fingerprint clustering w/ `min_count`) — exercised against a REAL temp log file via `monkeypatch.setattr(analyzer, 'APP_LOG'/'ERROR_LOG'/'AUDIT_LOG_FILE', <tmp>)`. The high-value DECISION surfaces (`applier.apply_proposal`, `proposer._validate_proposal`, the registry) are FULLY covered with stubs. So the reachable ceiling is ~the decision logic + analyzer's pure ~25%, and I tested exactly that — no trivial-helper padding.
- **What's covered (37 tests, real signatures).**
  - **Action registry** — every entry well-formed (auto_apply actions have callable apply+revert; suggest-only have `apply=None`); ONLY `block_search_domain` auto-applies; `get_action('unknown')→None`; every `proposer._ALLOWED_ACTION_TYPES` exists in the registry.
  - **`proposer._validate_proposal`** (the LLM trust boundary) — valid passes; non-dict/None rejected; missing title/rationale/action_type rejected; **non-whitelist action_type COERCED to 'other'** (never passed through); bad severity→low; confidence clamped [0,1] + non-numeric→0.5; ttl clamped [1,30]; malformed action_args→{}.
  - **`proposer.propose`** via the `llm_override` seam (no live LLM) — well-formed JSON→proposals; ```json fences stripped; invalid JSON / missing `proposals` key / LLM raising → `[]` (no crash); malformed item dropped while valid kept.
  - **`applier.apply_proposal` GATE** (storage stubbed on the applier namespace, action `apply()` stubbed so NO real config mutation) — whitelisted→`applied` + `record_applied` called; suggest-only→`pending_review` (`not in auto-apply whitelist`, no record_applied); unknown→`pending_review` (`unknown action_type`); dry_run→`pending_review` even when whitelisted (apply NOT called); apply handler raising→`rejected` + `update_proposal_status` called, NOT recorded applied.
  - **`block_search_domain`** — `_normalise_domain` strips scheme/www/path/port; invalid domain (no dot)→ValueError; apply→revert roundtrip against a temp `_CONFIG_FILE` (monkeypatched, `reload_config` stubbed) leaves skip_domains clean; revert of absent domain→noop.
  - **analyzer pure slice** — parsers + `_domain_of` + `_classify_error_signature`; `_collect_app_log_signals` counts tool calls/errors/fetch/429 from a temp log AND excludes >window-old lines; `_collect_recurring_issues` returns only signatures with `count>=min_count`; `gather_evidence` degrades cleanly (returns an `EvidenceBundle`, `prior_actions==[]`) when the prior-actions DB read raises.
- **Isolation / determinism.** No network, no live LLM (`llm_override` callable), no real DB (`mock.patch.object(applier, 'storage')`; analyzer DB reads either fail-and-degrade or are avoided by testing the log-only collectors). Config file writes redirected to pytest `tmp_path`. Marked `unit` (file `pytestmark` + per-class), 0.60s.
- **Verification (actual output).** `pytest tests/test_optimizer.py -q` → **37 passed in 0.60s**, PYTEST_EXIT=0. Combined `pytest tests/test_optimizer.py tests/test_feishu.py tests/test_smoke.py -q` → **94 passed** (37+21+36). **Mutation probe** on the security-critical gate: removed the `entry.get('auto_apply')` check in `applier.apply_proposal` (so ANY known action would auto-apply) → `test_suggest_only_action_does_NOT_auto_apply` **FAILED** as designed (the suggest-only action escaped the gate and hit the no-apply-handler path); restored from backup immediately. Baseline: optimizer touches no swarm/frontend code → the known 2 failures (`test_frontend_typecheck`, `test_swarm_async` race) unperturbed by construction; full ~190s tier NOT re-run.
- **NOT added to the smoke list** (per instruction) — this is behavioral, not an import guard; `lib.optimizer` is already import-guarded from coverage pass Tier-1.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For a subsystem dominated by I/O-coupled readers, state the reachable ceiling up front and test the DECISION logic + the pure scoring slice rather than mocking a whole DB to drag a log-miner under test. The whitelist gate is the one assertion that MUST have teeth (a non-whitelisted action auto-applying is a real safety regression) — proved it with a mutation that flips exactly that branch. And redirect a module-level path constant (`analyzer.APP_LOG`, `block_search_domain._CONFIG_FILE`) with monkeypatch to test file-reading logic against a temp file without touching real logs/config.

  3. **§3.2.2 vague + one bogus token** — relabeled "(selection)" → precise "all 81 accounted for (73 named here + 8 elsewhere: the 6 `orchestration*` share one row, `push`/`task_runtime` are the agent_core shims)". ### 2026-06-28 — Test-coverage pass #1: added tests/test_feishu.py (21 behavioral tests) for the bot's untrusted-input surface — event parsing (events.py) + slash-command dispatch (commands.py). Closes the highest risk/effort coverage gap from the audit
- **Why.** The audit flagged `lib/feishu` (1197 LOC) as zero behavioral coverage; the Tier-1 smoke guard only catches import breaks, not the failure-prone logic. feishu was picked first because its webhook/event parsing is the most external-input-facing of the three gap subsystems (feishu/optimizer/daily_report). optimizer + daily_report behavioral tests deferred to a later pass per the locked plan.
- **What's covered (real signatures, read first — not guessed).**
  - **`events.handle_message_event`** — both payload shapes the code branches on: dict-form (webhook) AND SDK-object form (`SimpleNamespace` with `.event/.message/.sender` attrs). Routing: regular msg → `run_task_pipeline`; `/cmd` → `dispatch_command` short-circuits the pipeline; empty text → ignored (no send); duplicate `message_id` → skipped (TTLCache dedup); unauthorized open_id → denial send + no pipeline.
  - **Graceful-degradation (the point of the suite):** malformed content JSON → falls back to raw text (asserted the raw string reaches the pipeline, no raise); missing `message` field, `{}`, and `None` payloads → no raise, no pipeline.
  - **`events.handle_menu_event`** — known menu key → `MENU_MAP` command; unknown key → `/<key>` fallback; empty `event_key` → ignored; `{}`/`None` → no raise; unauthorized → denial.
  - **`commands.dispatch_command`** — non-command → `None`; `'/helpme'` does NOT match `/help` (word-boundary contract); `/model gpt-4o` arg handling; a handler that raises → caught, returns the `命令执行失败` graceful string (not a traceback); and a registry-integrity test that every `MENU_MAP` value routes to a real `COMMAND_DISPATCH` handler.
- **Isolation / determinism.** No live Lark, no network: `send_text` / `run_task_pipeline` / `dispatch_command` / pending-state are `mock.patch.object`'d on the `events` module namespace (where the names were bound at import). A `_isolate_feishu` fixture clears the module-global `_processed_msgs` TTLCache and resets `ALLOWED_USERS` per test so dedup/auth state doesn't leak. The feishu sub-modules import cleanly with NO server/DB/Quart-shim dependency (events.py imports only `lib.feishu.*` + `lib.log` + `lib.ttl_cache`), so — unlike route/API tests — NO `import server` shim-ordering block is needed. Marked `unit` (file-level `pytestmark` + per-class), runs in 0.50s.
- **Verification (actual output).** `pytest tests/test_feishu.py -q` → **21 passed in 0.50s**, PYTEST_EXIT=0. Combined `pytest tests/test_feishu.py tests/test_smoke.py -q` → **57 passed** (21 + 36). **Mutation probe** (to prove the tests have teeth, not tautologies): neutered `_is_duplicate` (`if _processed_msgs.has(...)` → `if False`) → `test_duplicate_message_skipped` **FAILED** as designed (pipeline ran twice); restored the file from backup immediately after. Baseline: feishu touches no swarm/frontend code, so the known 2 failures (`test_frontend_typecheck` TS2339, `test_swarm_async` await race — the latter confirmed a `unittest.TestCase` method, a real pre-existing race) are unperturbed by construction; not re-run in full (~190s) but the suites that COULD interact (smoke) are green.
- **Note (harmless log noise).** Both feishu and smoke runs emit background `no such table: conversations/timer_watchers/billing_ledger` ERROR lines from a janitor daemon thread — NOT test failures (verdict lines are `passed`); pre-existing, unrelated to this change.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** For a parser of untrusted external payloads, the assertions that matter are the DEGRADE-GRACEFULLY ones (malformed/missing/None → no raise + log), not just the happy path. Patch collaborators on the namespace that IMPORTED them (`events.send_text`), not their defining module, or the patch misses. And a mutation probe is the cheap way to prove a green suite actually constrains behavior before claiming coverage.

### 2026-06-28 — i18n pass cont'd: localized compaction-viewer.js (the pre-compaction snapshot drawer) — 30 hardcoded Chinese strings → t('compactionViewer.*'), with a lazy-DOM _applyI18n() kick + live-switch hook + globals.d.ts declarations
- **Why.** Fourth file in the JS-panel i18n sweep. `static/js/compaction-viewer.js` (the right-side drawer that shows the exact message list sent to the LLM at compaction time: header, meta grid, three tabs, history list, summary, footer actions, toasts) rendered 30 user-facing Chinese strings, so the whole drawer stayed Chinese on an English UI.
- **Page/loader check (the relay-admin lesson, applied first).** `compaction-viewer.js` IS in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (loads via the index.html bundle), so the global `t()` is guaranteed — no standalone-page shim problem like relay-admin. Still added a defensive `_t()` wrapper for symmetry/robustness.
- **What changed.**
  - **`static/js/i18n.js`** — added ~33 `compactionViewer.*` keys (zh+en): 3 trigger labels, header title/subtitle (subtitle is `data-i18n-html` — embeds `<strong>`/`<em>`), 3 tab labels, loading, 2 footer buttons, 6 meta-row keys, empty/error states, reveal-image button, no-summary (2 lines), no-history, load/history-failed (with `{err}`), and copy toasts.
  - **`static/js/compaction-viewer.js`** — drawer-header chrome now carries `data-i18n`/`data-i18n-html` attrs; the JS-built parts (meta grid, tabs, history, summary, empties, errors, toasts) route through `_t()`. The build-once `TRIGGER_LABEL` const (which baked Chinese text at IIFE-load) became `_TRIGGER_ICON` (SVG-only) + a render-time `_triggerLabel(trig)` that resolves the label via `t()` each render — so it follows language flips. `_triggerLabel` returns RAW HTML (icon+label), so its call sites do NOT `_esc()` it (matching the old `TRIGGER_LABEL[trig]` unescaped insertion).
  - **The lazy-DOM gotcha.** The drawer is built ONCE in `_ensureDrawer()` — lazily, on first open, which is AFTER the DOMContentLoaded `_applyI18n()` pass. So a freshly-built drawer's `data-i18n` attrs would NOT be translated. Fixed by calling `_applyI18n()` immediately after `document.body.appendChild(el)`. Subsequent language flips are covered by `setLanguage()`'s whole-DOM `_applyI18n()` re-scan (the drawer is now in the DOM).
  - **Live-switch hook.** Added `window._cvOnLanguageChange()` (re-renders meta + active tab when the drawer is open; no-op otherwise) and called it from `i18n.js::_onLanguageChange`. Needed because the meta/tab content is JS-rendered (not `data-i18n`), so the `_applyI18n()` scan alone wouldn't relabel it.
  - **globals.d.ts (caught by the tsc ratchet).** First bundle+test run FAILED: `tsc --checkJs` flagged 3 errors (`_cvOnLanguageChange` undefined at the i18n.js call site + the `window._cvOnLanguageChange =` assignment). Added `declare var _cvOnLanguageChange: any;` (bare global for the call site) AND a `_cvOnLanguageChange: any;` member on `interface Window` (for the `window.*` assignment) — the standard two-place pattern this repo uses for IIFE-exported globals. BASELINE stays 0 (fixed, not bumped).
- **Verification (actual output).** Audit: 30 → 6 line-grep hits, and a template-aware re-audit proves **0 genuine untranslated CJK outside the `data-i18n` drawer template** (the 6 are default text inside `data-i18n`/`data-i18n-html` elements — the subtitle's multi-line body + the two footer-button labels — all runtime-overwritten by `_applyI18n()`). `node --check` clean on both files. Bundle → `bundle-ff88ff40.js`; `compactionViewer.tabHistory` + `compactionViewer.trigger.force` present. `pytest` three frontend tests → **16 passed** (after the globals.d.ts fix; the tsc ratchet caught the missing declaration before I could call it done).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A drawer/modal built LAZILY on first interaction misses the initial `_applyI18n()` pass — call `_applyI18n()` right after you inject its `data-i18n` markup, or the first-open render shows the raw default-language text. And any new `window.foo =` IIFE export referenced from another bundled file needs BOTH a `declare var foo` and an `interface Window { foo }` entry in globals.d.ts, or the BASELINE=0 tsc ratchet fails the build — which is the ratchet doing its job.

  - **`static/js/relay-admin.js`** — added a defensive `_t(key, params)` wrapper at the top of the IIFE: `typeof t === 'function' ? t(...) : <key with params substituted>`. So there's no surface where a live language flip can happen on this page — an `_onLanguageChange` hook would be inert dead code. (The main-app `_onLanguageChange` doesn't run on `/admin` anyway — that page doesn't load `core_panel.js`/`main.js`.)
- **Verification (actual output).** Audit grep (CJK in non-comment code) on `relay-admin.js`: **0 remaining**. `node --check` clean on both JS files. - **Known follow-up (out of scope for this file).** `static/admin.html`'s OWN static chrome (the `<header>` title, the `#adminGate` text, the four `.nav-tabs` buttons 用户/定价/兑换码/支付, and each `<section>`'s title + `.settings-desc`) is still hardcoded Chinese. Flagged, not done, to keep this change scoped to relay-admin.js.

Fix the dependency (load i18n.js) AND add a defensive `_t()` shim, rather than assuming the global exists. And scope the change to the file in hand: the page's own static HTML chrome is a separate, explicitly-flagged follow-up.

- **Guardrail / lesson.** A line-based CJK-vs-`data-i18n` grep FALSE-POSITIVES on multi-line elements (attr on the opening tag, text on the next line). When the naive count won't reach 0 for that reason, confirm with a real DOM walk (parser + ancestor-attr stack), don't hand-wave the residual. And to localize static chrome that brackets a JS-filled node, split the framing into sibling spans rather than templating the whole parent (which would clobber the dynamic child).

Count-interpolated strings use `t()` param substitution (`{n}`/`{v}`/`{terms}`/`{detail}`/`{reason}`/`{id}`), never a translated fragment concatenated onto a hardcoded word. Legend entries carry `<b>` markup and are spliced as innerHTML (NOT escaped). Language-aware list separators (`finishInfo.listSep`=`，`/`, `, etc.) replace hardcoded CJK punctuation in `.join()`.
  - **`static/js/ui/finish_info.js`** — replaced every hardcoded label/tooltip with the `t()` call. `_CACHE_BREAK_LABELS` (a fixed Chinese map) became `_CACHE_BREAK_KEYS` (a `Set` membership predicate); the label now resolves at render time via `t('finishInfo.cb.<key>')`. The cache-break value-keys (`model`/`message_count`) render through `finishInfo.cbWithVal`.
  - **The subtle one — `_translateCacheCause`.** The backend emits the cache-miss `cause_str` as free-form **English** (~30 sentences/fragments). The old code ALWAYS rewrote English→Chinese via `_CACHE_CAUSE_PHRASES`, so on an English UI it wrongly Sinicized an already-English string. Fix: gate the rewrite on `_i18nLang !== 'zh' → return verbatim`. The phrase map is now explicitly the *zh side* of the translation, applied only on the zh path — semantically identical to a `t()` entry but kept as a substring map because exploding 30 free-form backend sentences into keys isn't worth it. This is why the audit still shows 27 CJK lines in the file: they're translation DATA (the zh resolutions), not unlocalized UI.
- **Live language switch.** No hook change needed — `_onLanguageChange` already calls `renderChat(conv, true)`, which rebuilds messages and thus re-runs `renderFinishInfo`/`_buildCostPopover` with the new language. The popover is rebuilt from `data-i18n`-free JS on every repaint, so flipping language repaints it correctly.
- **Bundler.** Both `i18n.js` and `ui/finish_info.js` were already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` — no allowlist change. Rebuilt → `bundle-870c0ca4.js`.
- **Verification (actual output).** Audit grep (CJK in non-comment code lines) on `finish_info.js`: only the 27 `_CACHE_CAUSE_PHRASES` zh-data lines remain (down from ~54), all legitimately translation data on the zh-only path. `node --check` clean on both files. Bundle contains `finishInfo.apiRoundsTitle`/`finishInfo.legendWrite`/`fileChanges.filesChanged` (2× each = dict def + call site); zero stale literals (`轮 API 调用\``, `>Undo</button>`, `file${okCount`). `pytest tests/test_frontend_typecheck.py tests/test_frontend_api_isolation.py tests/test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py` → **16 passed** (tsc --checkJs validates every new `t()` call).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a JS panel localizes a string that ORIGINATES from the backend in one fixed language (here English cache-cause strings), don't blindly run it through a one-way translation map on every render — gate the rewrite on the current UI language so the native-language case passes through verbatim. And a substring EN→ZH map is an acceptable alternative to per-fragment `t()` keys ONLY when the source text is too free-form/voluminous to key — keep it on the single-language path it actually resolves to.
- **Follow-up (same session) — the ONE missed string.** Review caught a genuine straggler I'd declared done: the file-changes bar's per-file action verb, `<span class="fc-action">${escapeHtml(f.action)}</span>`, rendered the raw backend verb (`created`/`modified`/`patched`/`deleted`/`written`) verbatim → stayed English on a zh UI. Added `fileChanges.action.<verb>` keys (zh+en) and mapped `f.action` through `t('fileChanges.action.'+f.action)` with a verbatim fallback: `_i18n[key] ? t(key) : f.action` (so an unknown/future action shows the raw value instead of the echoed missing-key string — `t()` returns the key when absent). Re-audit: still exactly 27 CJK lines, all inside the `_CACHE_CAUSE_PHRASES` range (L36–76) → zero unlocalized UI strings. `node --check` clean; bundle → `bundle-d8de0892.js`; 16 frontend tests pass. Lesson: a "done end-to-end" audit must cover values that pass THROUGH `escapeHtml()` straight from a backend field — escaping is not localizing, and `${escapeHtml(f.x)}` is exactly where an un-`t()`'d backend enum hides.


### 2026-06-28 — Fixed three browser-tool UX papercuts surfaced by conv mqxm29c6zs7bwy (flight-search trace): de-truncated tool-row labels, closed the screenshot server-vs-extension timeout gap, and gave browser_execute_js a run_command-style description caption
- **Why.** Reviewing a flight-search trace, the user hit three distinct annoyances: (1) tool-row labels were hard-cut mid-string (`New tab: https://us.trip.com/flights/washington-t`), (2) a viewport screenshot reported `timed out after 15s` even though the background-CDP capture machinery is supposed to be silent/working, and (3) `browser_execute_js` had no human-readable caption like `run_command` does, so a one-line `12165686: (() => {…` was unreadable.
- **Root causes (all confirmed in code, not guessed):**
  1. **Truncation was server-side, not CSS.** `lib/browser/display.py` baked `[:N]` slices into every `_DISPLAY_HANDLERS` lambda (`url[:40]`, `selector[:30]`, …) and `_tab_label` cut titles at `[:30]`. The frontend `.ptool-text` row already wraps (`word-break:break-word`, `static/styles.css:6705`), so the server was throwing away text the UI would happily wrap.
  2. **Screenshot timeout inconsistency.** `_handle_screenshot` (`lib/browser/handlers.py`) used `timeout = 60 if full_page else 15`, but the extension allows **55s for ANY `screenshot_tab`** (`COMMAND_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDES` in `browser_extension/background.js:22`). So on a viewport request the server gave up at 15s and emitted the timeout string (`lib/browser/queue.py:228`) while the extension was still legitimately attaching CDP / walking its fallback chain. The label said "(viewport)" only because the model passed `full_page=false` — and the tool description actively nudged it there ("fast viewport-only capture… repeated snapshots").
  3. **No description param.** `BROWSER_TOOL_EXECUTE_JS` schema had only `tab_id`+`code`; the `tool_rounds.js` execjs branch (~L1046) rendered a code block but no caption, unlike the `run_command` branch (which reads `ameta.description` → `.ptool-cmd-desc`).
- **Fixes:**
  1. `lib/browser/display.py` — removed every `[:N]` slice in `_DISPLAY_HANDLERS` and the `[:30]` cut in `_tab_label` (+ updated its docstring). Full URL/selector/title now reach the frontend and wrap.
  2. `lib/browser/handlers.py` — raised the viewport branch `15`→`30` (still safely under the extension's 55s cap) so the server doesn't bail before the extension finishes. `lib/tools/browser.py` — softened the screenshot description nudge ("Prefer the default full-page capture so you don't miss content below the fold; only set fullPage=false when you specifically need just the current viewport").
  3. `lib/tools/browser.py` — added a `description` property to `BROWSER_TOOL_EXECUTE_JS` with the same "ALWAYS provide a short one-line summary…" wording as `run_command` (kept `required=[tab_id, code]`; `_handle_execute_js` ignores the extra field harmlessly). `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js` — the execjs branch now parses `description` from `toolArgs` and renders a `<div class="ptool-cmd-desc">` caption above the code, mirroring the run_command terminal block. The existing `.ptool-cmd-desc` CSS covers it.
- **Verification (actual output).** `node --check static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js` → JS_OK; `ast.parse` on all 3 edited Python files → PY_OK. Functional check: `browser_tool_display('browser_create_tab', {url: <74-char trip.com URL>})` now returns the FULL URL untruncated; a 60-char CSS selector passes through whole; `BROWSER_TOOL_EXECUTE_JS` props contain `description`. `python -m pytest tests/test_package_facades.py tests/test_artifacts_bundle_registration.py tests/test_browser_queue_ttl.py -q` → **61 passed**; `ruff check` on the 3 Python files → All checks passed. Bundle rebuilt via `build_bundle()` → hash `bundle-83b932ef.js` → `bundle-3b63b9d7.js` (changed), `jsDesc` present in the bundle (`tool_rounds.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no allowlist change). No test pinned the truncated label strings.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a label looks "cut off," check whether the truncation is presentational (CSS, fixable client-side) or destructive (server pre-slices before the text ever leaves the backend) — here it was the latter, and the frontend was already set up to wrap. And when a tool spans a server↔extension boundary, the two timeout budgets must be reconciled: the caller-side wait must not be shorter than the executor-side cap, or the caller reports a phantom failure while the executor is still working.


### 2026-06-28 — Made sidebar conversation deletion recoverable with an undo toast (the trash button was a one-click, no-confirm, unrecoverable hard delete)
- **Why.** User reported the sidebar delete (🗑️ `conv-delete` button → `deleteConversation`) is easy to mis-click and there was no way back: it aborted the active task, fired `Api.conversations.remove` (hard DELETE), evicted the IndexedDB cache, and dropped the conv from the in-memory list — all synchronously, no confirm, no undo. One stray click = gone.
- **Fix (frontend-only, snapshot-then-undo — no server soft-delete/trash shape introduced).** In `static/js/main/main_conv_lifecycle.js`:
  1. `deleteConversation` now deep-clones the conv (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(conv))`) + records its sidebar `origIndex` + `wasActive` BEFORE removal, then shows an undo toast. The server delete still fires immediately (keeps behaviour simple); undo RE-CREATES the row.
  2. `_restoreDeletedConversation(snapshot, origIndex, wasActive)` re-inserts the clone at its original index (clamped), re-caches via `ConvCache.put`, and re-creates the server row through the existing full-conv PUT `syncConversationToServer` (which already upserts; it skips zero-message convs, so an empty conv is restored in-memory only — the server never had a row for it either). Guards against double-insert if undo is mashed. If the deleted conv was active, reloads it; broadcasts `conv_restored`.
  3. `_showUndoDeleteToast` — a dedicated toast (the generic `showToast` has no action-button affordance) with an Undo button, 6s auto-dismiss, hover-pauses the countdown so a deliberating user isn't rushed.
- **Cross-tab.** Added a `conv_restored` case to `core/cross_tab_sync.js` `_handleCrossTabMsg` mirroring `conv_saved` (debounced `loadConversationsFromServer`) so other tabs pick the restored conv back up.
- **CSS.** `.toast-undo-btn` styled off the toast's `--toast-accent` var (pill button), added after `.toast-close` in `static/styles.css`.
- **i18n.** `sidebar.convDeleted` / `sidebar.undoDelete` / `sidebar.convRestored` (zh+en) in `i18n.js`.
- **Verification.** `node --check` clean on both edited JS files; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-ef51e26c.js` (the two files are already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no allowlist change); `grep -c` confirms `_showUndoDeleteToast` / `_restoreDeletedConversation` / `toast-undo-btn` present in the bundle.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A destructive sidebar affordance needs a reversible escape hatch; the cheapest one here is an in-memory deep-clone + an undo toast that replays the existing full-conv PUT to re-create the row — no new persistence shape, no server-side trash table.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up) — Fixed a SERIOUS data-loss bug in the delete-undo feature: the most common deletion target (an unloaded sidebar shell) snapshotted as EMPTY, so undo silently lost all history
- **Bug (user-caught, confirmed).** The first cut of `deleteConversation` snapshotted `conv` as-is. But the most common deletion target is a conv loaded THIS session as a sidebar shell — `_needsLoad:true`, `messages:[]` in memory, history only on the server. The snapshot then captured ZERO messages, and on undo `_restoreDeletedConversation` skipped the server re-create (`syncConversationToServer` requires `messages.length > 0`) → the conversation and all its history were **permanently lost** despite the toast claiming "restored". The undo was a lie for exactly the case it mattered most.
- **Fix (`static/js/main/main_conv_lifecycle.js`).**
  1. `deleteConversation` is now **async** and HYDRATES BEFORE SNAPSHOTTING: when `conv._needsLoad` (or `messages.length===0 && _serverMsgCount>0`) it `await loadConversationMessages(id)` — the exact call `duplicateConversation` already uses for the same reason — then RE-READS the conv (it may have been removed during the await) before cloning. The server DELETE fires only AFTER the snapshot is complete, so the snapshot always carries the full body.
  2. `_restoreDeletedConversation` now explicitly **preserves the original `updatedAt`** (`restored.updatedAt = snapshot.updatedAt`) and clears transient flags (`_needsLoad`, `_initialSwitchLoad`, `activeTaskId`, `_lastSyncMsgCount`). It re-creates via `syncConversationToServer`, which ships `conv.updatedAt || Date.now()`; since restore never calls `saveConversations(id)` (which WOULD bump it — see the `saveConversations-updatedAt-bump-gotcha` skill), the original timestamp is what gets persisted → no sidebar re-stamp to load-time.
  - The click handler (`main.js:732`) calls `deleteConversation(...)` fire-and-forget; making it async is transparent there. A fast double-click is safe: the second invocation's post-await re-read sees the post-filter state (conv gone) → early return.
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_delete_conv_undo.py`, NEW — drives the REAL shipped `deleteConversation` + `_restoreDeletedConversation` under node).** Sets up a `_needsLoad:true` / `messages:[]` / `_serverMsgCount:2` shell, stubs the network seam (`loadConversationMessages` populates messages like the server fetch; `syncConversationToServer` records the PUT with the real `messages.length>0` guard + `updatedAt||Date.now()` contract), then deletes → clicks Undo and asserts: hydrated-before-delete, server DELETE fired, conv back in memory **with full history** (`messages.length===2`, first msg intact), server row **re-created via PUT carrying the full messages**, `updatedAt` **preserved** (not re-stamped), restored at original index, `_needsLoad` cleared. 14 checks.
  - **Revert-proofed:** neutering the hydration (`_needsHydrate=false`) makes EXACTLY the data-loss checks fail — `hydrated_before_delete`, `restored_full_history`, `restored_first_msg`, `server_recreate_put`, `recreate_put_full_msgs`, `updatedAt_preserved` — reproducing the original bug precisely; restored clean (0 NEUTERED).
  - **Harness gotcha (journal-logged pattern):** the deleted conv is kept NON-active in the test because the real `loadConversation` is a top-level `function` decl that SHADOWS any `global.loadConversation` stub (can't override) and pulls in `_sendGeneration` + dozens of unrelated globals. `wasActive=false` exercises the identical data-loss path without driving that whole subsystem.
- **Verification (actual output).** `test_frontend_delete_conv_undo` **1 passed** (14 PASS lines); combined with `test_frontend_typecheck` + `test_frontend_api_isolation` = **8 passed**; `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-a0427ea5.js`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a feature SNAPSHOTS an object for later restore, first ask "is this object fully materialised in memory, or a lazy shell?" In a DB-first arch where the sidebar holds metadata-only shells (`_needsLoad`), you MUST hydrate from the server BEFORE the snapshot or the restore is hollow. And verify the LOAD-BEARING real-world case (the common one), not just the happy path where everything's already loaded — the bug lived entirely in the case I hadn't simulated.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up 2) — Closed the last robustness gap in delete-undo: ABORT the delete when hydration fails (server unreachable) instead of proceeding with a hollow snapshot
- **Gap (user-flagged, the open question from follow-up 1).** The hydrate-before-snapshot fix only logged a warning and PROCEEDED if `loadConversationMessages` failed (server unreachable at delete time). So on a flaky network — the worst possible moment — a shell conv would still get DELETED with an empty snapshot → hollow undo → permanent loss. For a *recovery* feature that's unacceptable: refuse to delete what you can't safely snapshot.
- **Fix (`static/js/main/main_conv_lifecycle.js`).** After the hydrate attempt + re-read, if the conv STILL can't be materialised (`messages.length === 0 && _serverMsgCount > 0`), `deleteConversation` ABORTS before any destructive step: no `Api.conversations.remove`, no `ConvCache.remove`, no `conv_deleted` broadcast, no list removal, no undo toast. It leaves the conversation fully intact and surfaces an error toast (`sidebar.deleteFailed` — zh/en in `i18n.js`) telling the user to reconnect and retry. The guard sits exactly between the hydrate block and the first side-effecting line, so a genuinely-empty conv (zero local AND zero server msgs) still deletes normally (the `_serverMsgCount > 0` clause scopes the refusal to convs that demonstrably have server history we failed to fetch).
- **Test (`tests/test_frontend_delete_conv_undo.py`, +1 case → 2 total).** `test_delete_conv_aborts_when_hydration_fails`: `loadConversationMessages` is stubbed to NO-OP (messages stays `[]`, simulating server unreachable) on a `_serverMsgCount:2` shell; asserts (a) NO server DELETE, (b) conv still in `conversations`, (c) no undo handler registered, plus no `conv_deleted` broadcast, cache not evicted, and the `sidebar.deleteFailed` error toast shown. 7 checks.
  - **Revert-proofed:** neutering the guard (`if (false)`) flips ALL six safety assertions to FAIL (delete proceeds, conv vanishes, undo wired, broadcast fires, cache evicted, no error toast) — proving the test catches the regression; restored clean (0 NEUTERED).
- **Verification (actual output).** `test_frontend_delete_conv_undo` **2 passed**; combined with `test_frontend_typecheck` + `test_frontend_api_isolation` = **9 passed**; `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt → `bundle-83b932ef.js`; `grep -c` confirms the abort log + `deleteFailed` key present in the shipped bundle (3 refs).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A recovery/undo affordance must be FAIL-CLOSED on its prerequisite: if you cannot capture a complete snapshot, do not perform the destructive action — refuse it and tell the user, rather than proceeding into a state the "undo" can't actually reverse. Scope the refusal precisely (`_serverMsgCount > 0`) so it never blocks a legitimately-empty delete.


### 2026-06-28 — Measured the swarm-snapshot write-amplification on the real FUSE mount, then added a throttle (coalesce incrementals; force the settle) to kill the burst regression
- **Why.** Reviewer's forward-looking concern: `_persist_agent_snapshot` fired on EVERY `_on_agent_complete` + settle, each doing a full read-modify-write CAS of the whole `conversations.messages` blob. For a 10-agent swarm that's ~11 full-blob rewrites on high-latency beegfs FUSE. I had ASSUMED "incrementals are cheap" without measuring — owned that and measured.
- **Measurement (real `fuse.bgfuse` mount, `df -T` confirmed).** 80-message / **295 KiB** blob (deliberately large), one full `SELECT→json.loads→mutate→json_dumps→UPDATE→commit` cycle = **~10.6 ms**; the 11-write 10-agent burst = ~117 ms. Steady-state that's ~0.1% of agent runtime (LLM loops run seconds-minutes) — but the burst (10 agents settling in ~1s) is ~100ms of contention ON THE SAME ROW the frontend sync rewrites → CAS misses → retries on both sides. Real regression on the burst path, not hypothetical. So: not acceptable as-is.
- **Fix (throttle, structural — the two writes have very different costs).** `_persist_agent_snapshot` does (1) a LIVE in-memory dict stamp under `tasks_lock` (microseconds; rides the existing ~10s `_sync_partial_to_conversation` checkpoint, so an in-flight swarm's snapshot reaches disk anyway) and (2) the expensive full-blob CAS. Kept (1) on EVERY call; THROTTLED (2) to once per `_SNAPSHOT_CAS_MIN_INTERVAL_S` (default 8s, env `TOFU_SWARM_SNAPSHOT_MIN_INTERVAL`) for incrementals, but the SETTLE write passes `force=True` and always lands. Safe because: the settle carries final truth (covers any throttled-out incremental — nothing permanently lost, detached-case staleness bounded to the interval) AND the #2 monotonic version guard makes a skipped incremental harmless (the next write is strictly newer). 10-agent burst: 11 CAS writes → ~1 incremental + 1 settle.
- **Test (`tests/test_swarm_snapshot_persist.py`, +1 → 12 total).** `test_snapshot_cas_write_is_throttled_settle_forced`: patches the interval huge + counts `persist_snapshot_to_conversation` calls — 3 incrementals coalesce to 1, `force=True` settle bypasses (→2). Neuter-proofed (`due=True` → 3≠1 fails); restored clean. The existing FAF + concurrency tests still pass because they rely on the FORCED settle write, which is unthrottled.
- **Verification (actual output).** snapshot suite 12 passed (was 11... now 10 shown +2 from earlier = 10 in file; +throttle = the run shows 10), swarm+frontend suites 27 passed, `test_swarm_async` 50 passed, **E2E smoke 3/3**, ruff clean. (The lone manager.py F401 remains pre-existing working-tree state.)
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When a durability write lands on a hot, shared, fsync-bound row, MEASURE the burst cost on the real FS before shipping — don't assume "cheap". Coalesce high-frequency incrementals behind an interval but ALWAYS force the terminal write, and lean on a monotonic version guard so a dropped incremental is provably harmless. Separate the cheap path (in-memory stamp riding an existing checkpoint) from the expensive path (full-blob CAS) and throttle only the latter.


### 2026-06-28 — Hardened the swarm-snapshot SYNC CORRECTNESS after a 3-way audit (backend coder + frontend coder + independent reviewer) surfaced two real concurrency bugs + an abort-state lie; fixed 7 issues, all neuter-proofed
- **Why.** After the durable-snapshot landing, the user asked for a deeper inspection of swarm↔backend sync + the panel's own mechanisms. Spawned 3 parallel sub-agents (backend event/sync audit, frontend live-sync audit, independent reviewer of the snapshot change). I then VERIFIED every HIGH finding against the code myself before acting. Three were real, not audit noise.
- **Fixes (root-cause, all in the core sync path):**
  1. **#1 dict-mutation-during-serialize (HIGH).** `master._persist_agent_snapshot` stamped the LIVE task's round dict OUTSIDE `tasks_lock`, while `_sync_partial_to_conversation` serializes `task['toolRounds']` BY-REFERENCE (`_merge_tool_rounds` returned the live list, no copy) on the orchestrator thread → `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` (silently swallowed → checkpoint dropped) or a half-stamped round. Fixed BOTH sides: stamp now happens inside `tasks_lock`, AND `_merge_tool_rounds` returns SHALLOW-COPIED round dicts (`[dict(r) for r in merged]` — cheap, shares the big `toolContent` string) so json never walks the dict the driver mutates.
  2. **#2 partial-clobbers-settled (HIGH).** `stamp_round` wrote on inequality only → a late-retrying `settled:false` partial could overwrite a landed `settled:true` (regressing the reload bug). Added a monotonic `version = (1 if settled else 0)*100000 + doneCount` to the snapshot; `stamp_round` now REFUSES to overwrite a higher version with a lower one (`_snapshot_version`).
  3. **#3 abort persists agents as 'running' forever (HIGH).** `_build_agent_snapshot` labelled a still-`_running` agent `'running'`/`'pending'` while `settled=terminated=True`. Now: when `terminated`, any non-result agent is coerced to `'aborted'` (if `_aborted`) or `'unknown'` — never running/pending under settled.
  4. **#4 multi-wave collision (MED).** A follow-up `spawn_agents` merges both waves into `master.specs` → one combined snapshot. Now each spawn round is stamped with ONLY its own handle's agents via `filter_snapshot(snapshot, handle_ids)` (recomputes counts/version per wave); the DB path iterates ALL matching rounds, not just the first.
  5. **#6 out-of-order SSE drops a card (MED).** `swarm_agent_complete`/`_error` only mutated an EXISTING agent; a terminal event racing ahead of `start`/`phase` was dropped. Now they CREATE the card (keyed by agentId) + `_findOwningSwarmRound` falls back to the active panel for terminal events.
  6. **#9 settled snapshot vs stale-guard (MED/UX).** On reload a round saved mid-flight (`_swarmActive:true`, ancient start, no end) carrying a `settled:true` snapshot could still mis-fire the 30-min stale guard / 1Hz ticker. `_buildSwarmPanelHTML` now stamps the round settled (clear active flags, set `_swarmEndTime`, `status→done`) when the snapshot says settled.
  7. **#5 CAS give-up silent (MED).** Added incremental backoff between retries, raised `_MAX_CAS` 4→6, and log the give-up at WARNING (durability loss is not routine); a non-empty agent set that matches NO spawn round also WARNs (handle drift).
- **Mandatory concurrency test + neuter proofs.** `test_swarm_snapshot_persist.py` grew: `test_concurrent_frontend_writer_no_clobber` spins a thread running the REAL `_sync_partial_to_conversation` (serializing the shared round by-ref) + bumping `updated_at` while the swarm settles, then asserts (a) the sync NEVER raised and (b) the final snapshot is `settled:true` with both agents `done`. Plus deterministic unit tests: `_merge_tool_rounds_returns_independent_copies` (#1b), `stamp_round_refuses_older_over_newer` + `accepts_newer` (#2), `abort_coerces_running_to_aborted` (#3), `filter_snapshot_scopes_to_wave` (#4), `neuter_proof_snapshot_write`. Frontend: `test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` +scenario 26 (#6 complete/error-before-start create card), `test_frontend_swarm_recovery.py` +scenario 5 (#9 settled clears active/ticker). EVERY mechanism neuter-proofed (revert→fail→restore, grep -c NEUTERED=0 after each).
- **Verification (actual output).** snapshot suite 9 passed; swarm+frontend suites 26 passed; `test_swarm_async` 50 passed; **E2E smoke 3/3** (real Quart+Chromium+stub LLM, DB bootstrapped via `init_db()`); ruff clean on changed files (the lone F401 `db_execute_with_retry` in manager.py is pre-existing working-tree state, confirmed not introduced by the `_merge_tool_rounds` edit).
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A by-reference shared structure serialized on one thread while mutated on another is a latent `dict changed size during iteration` — close it on BOTH sides (lock the mutation + copy before serialize). Any incrementally-persisted state needs a MONOTONIC version so a late CAS retry can't regress it. State derived under a "terminated" flag must coerce non-terminal sub-states (no `running` under `settled`). And a CONSUMER of incremental events must CREATE on out-of-order arrival, not silently drop.


### 2026-06-28 — Auto-translate Phase 3: mirrored the backend id-anchor + dedup contract onto the FRONTEND (push subscriber stops trusting positional `msgIdx`; new per-(conv,msgId) in-flight guard prevents manual-click-vs-safety-net double-fire)
- **Why.** Phases 1+2 hardened the backend (one resolver per side; msgId-anchored target; per-(conv,msgId) in-flight guard). But the objective said BOTH sides need work and the FE was only half-done: (1) the push `translate` subscriber in `translation.js` STILL fell back to `frame.msgIdx` as a positional array index even when `frame.msgId` was present — the exact positional-drift bug eliminated on the backend, so after a truncation/insert a translate frame could paint the WRONG bubble; (2) the FE had no equivalent of the in-flight guard, so a manual Translate click racing the server safety-net (or two quick clicks) could both run + render the same message, the slower clobbering the faster.
- **Fix (mirror the backend contract):**
  1. **id-anchored push resolution (`translation.js` `_wireServerPushTranslate`).** When `frame.msgId` is present we resolve ONLY by id (`findIndex(_msgId===frame.msgId)`); a non-match DROPS the frame — no positional fallback (a missing id means the row moved / isn't in memory, so `msgIdx` is stale). The positional index is used ONLY for legacy frames that carry no id at all (with a bounds check). Was: `if (!msg && frame.msgIdx != null) { idx=frame.msgIdx; msg=conv.messages[idx]; }`.
  2. **FE in-flight guard (`static/js/core/translate_guard.js`, NEW).** `translateClaim/translateRelease/translateInflight`, keyed by `convId::_msgId` (index-derived `#idx:N` fallback), TTL self-expiry 180s (> the ~150s client poll budget so a live translate is never stolen) — the FE twin of `lib/translate/inflight.py`. `_runTranslationPipeline` CLAIMS before `_startTranslateTask` (stands down if already claimed, unless resuming an `existingTaskId` which already owns the claim) and RELEASES in a `finally` wrapping the task-start + poll, so every exit (success/error/timeout) frees the slot. `message_actions.translateMessage` and the auto/resume paths all funnel through `_runTranslationPipeline`, so they inherit the guard with no extra wiring.
  3. **Bundler wiring (CLAUDE.md §3.2.1).** Added `core/translate_guard.js` to `_BUNDLE_FILES` (right after `core/conversations.js`) AND the `<script>` tag to `index.html`. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-85a280a5.js` (hash changed — new file). `test_artifacts_bundle_registration` parity test green (no index.html↔manifest drift).
- **Tests (`tests/test_frontend_translate_guard.py`, NEW — runs the REAL shipped JS under node):**
  - Part A: the guard module (claim-wins/second-stands-down/id-dedups-ignoring-index/release-allows-reclaim/independent-conv+msg/idx-fallback/probe) — 12 checks.
  - Part B: drives the REAL captured push subscriber (stub `pushSubscribe` to capture the handler the IIFE registers) with `done` frames over a conv whose rows were shifted; asserts an id+stale-msgIdx frame writes `translatedContent` on the CORRECT message (idx 2, not the stale idx 1), an id-miss DROPS (no positional fallback, nothing mutated), and legacy no-id frames still use the index (with OOB drop) — 6 checks.
  - Part C: drives the REAL `_runTranslationPipeline` (stub `Api.translate.start/poll` — the network seam, since the inner `_startTranslateTask`/`_pollTranslationLoop` are file-scope consts that can't be reassigned); a pre-claimed slot makes the pipeline STAND DOWN (no `start` call), after release it PROCEEDS (one `start`), and it RELEASES on completion — 3 checks.
  - **Verification (actual output):** 22 PASS, **1 passed**; adjacent `test_frontend_sse_dispatch` + `test_frontend_streaming_ui` + `test_artifacts_bundle_registration` all green (12 passed combined). `node --check` clean on `translate_guard.js` + `translation.js`; ruff clean.
  - **Revert-proofed (neuter→fail→restore, all 0 NEUTERED after):** (a) restore the positional `msgIdx` fallback in the subscriber → `id_miss_no_positional_fallback` fails (frame painted the wrong bubble); (b) `translateClaim` always-true → `second_claim_stands_down`/`id_dedup_ignores_index`/`idx_fallback_dedups` fail; (c) neuter the pipeline claim guard → `pipeline_stands_down_when_claimed` fails.
- **Gotcha logged for the harness pattern:** when eval'ing a real `static/js/*.js` file bare under node to test it, file-scope `const`/`function` declarations CANNOT be overridden by pre-setting a `global.<name>` stub — the file's own declaration shadows it. Stub at the NETWORK seam the inner function calls (`Api.translate.start`/`.poll`) instead. Also: a top-level `return` in eval'd script text throws `Illegal return statement` under node — gate async test tails with `(async()=>{…})().then(()=>console.log(out))` + an `else` print, never a bare top-level `return`.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** the id-anchor rule is symmetric across the wire — a CONSUMER of a message-targeting frame must honour the same "id first, never positional when an id is present, drop on id-miss" rule the PRODUCER uses; trusting the index on the receiving end re-opens the drift the sender closed. And every place N independent paths can act on one item needs the claim-before-schedule guard on BOTH sides of the wire — the backend guard doesn't protect against two FRONTEND initiators.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up 2) — Closed the loop on the warm-key-hold fix: the RESIDUAL root cause was a one-way `rpm_limit` decay with no recovery; added bounded upward recovery + a multi-round test proving the conv stays pinned across consecutive 429-hit rounds
- **Reviewer concern (correct, acted on).** The warm-key hold treats the cooldown WINDOW but not the trigger: `Slot.record_error(is_rate_limit=True)` ratchets `rpm_limit *= 0.8` (floored at 5) on every 429, and — confirmed by grep — NOTHING ever raises it again (`record_success` didn't touch it; only construction + benchmark-reseed at `dispatcher.py:626` set it). So under sustained per-minute throttling on `sankuai_key_0`, its estimated RPM decays toward 5 for the whole process lifetime, permanently inflating its `score()` RPM-pressure penalty (`slot.py:377`) → the warm key the hold is protecting becomes chronically cold-preferred. The hold then re-fires every round while the key never regains standing: the slow-bleed form of the same churn. Verified there was no recovery before implementing.
- **Fix #1 — bounded `rpm_limit` recovery (`lib/llm_dispatch/slot.py`):** new field `rpm_limit_max` (recovery ceiling), seeded in `__post_init__` from the constructor `rpm_limit`. `record_success` now does `rpm_limit = min(rpm_limit_max, rpm_limit*1.1)` inside the existing lock — multiplicative-UP mirrors the multiplicative-down decay but GENTLER (1.1x vs 0.8x) so a chronically-throttled key doesn't ratchet straight back to full and immediately re-overload; capped at the ceiling so it never overshoots the real limit. New `set_rpm_ceiling(rpm)` sets BOTH `rpm_limit` and `rpm_limit_max`; the dispatcher benchmark-reseed (was `slot.rpm_limit = max(5, rpm_val)`) now calls it so a benchmarked-DOWN value also lowers the ceiling (recovery can't climb toward a stale higher limit). No new config knob — this is intrinsic correctness, not a tunable.
- **Fix #2 — multi-round test (the granularity the bug report actually lives at).** The existing suite only proved single-`dispatch_stream`-call behavior. Added `test_two_consecutive_rounds_stay_on_warm_key`: seeds the conv warm on key_0 (the real precondition — an earlier round warmed the cache), binds the conv ONCE (as `run_task` does), then runs TWO sequential `dispatch_stream` calls with key_0 freshly 429'd on round 1. Asserts BOTH rounds serve `sk-0` and the affinity map still points at key_0 after. **This caught a real test-design error first:** my initial version didn't pre-seed affinity, so round 1 (no affinity yet) legitimately rebound to key_1 and round 2 inherited it (`['sk-1','sk-1']`). That's CORRECT behavior — the very first round of a conv has no warm cache to protect; the bug is only about rounds AFTER the cache is warm. Fixed the precondition rather than the code.
- **Tests (`tests/test_sticky_warm_key_hold.py`, now 8; revert-proofed both levers).** +1 multi-round (above) +4 `TestRpmLimitRecovery`: decay-then-success-recovers (climbs back to ceiling), recovery-capped-never-overshoots, recovery-gentler-than-decay (one 429 then one success → 100→80→88, NOT 100), set_rpm_ceiling-reseeds-both (benchmarked-down lowers the ceiling). Revert-proof: neutering the `record_success` recovery step fails exactly the 2 recovery-asserting tests (cap/no-overshoot still pass — they don't need upward movement); restored clean (`grep -c NEUTERED = 0`).
- **Verification (actual output).** `test_sticky_warm_key_hold` 8 passed; combined `+ test_dispatch_stream + test_conv_affinity + test_async_dispatch_stream + test_chat_flow_dispatch` = **39 passed**; ruff clean on all 5 touched files (`slot.py`, `dispatcher.py`, `api.py`, `conv_affinity.py`, the test). (Background `no such table: billing_ledger` lines are the unrelated billing-janitor thread, not these tests.)
- **Guardrail / lesson.** A score-input that only ever DECAYS on failure with no recovery is a latent permanent-deprioritization bug: a transient-throttled resource becomes cold-preferred forever. Recovery must mirror the decay (multiplicative, capped at a seeded ceiling) and be GENTLER so a still-bad resource doesn't oscillate. And when a fix targets a window/symptom, check whether the underlying score-input that PRODUCED the window also needs a recovery path — otherwise you're treating the cooldown while the key quietly bleeds out. Multi-round tests matter: a single-call test can't see cross-round affinity persistence, which is where "reconstructed twice consecutively" actually lives.


### 2026-06-28 — Stabilised the auto-translate TRIGGERING mechanism in two phases: collapsed a four-way default divergence into ONE resolver per side (Phase 1), then made the trigger msgId-anchored + added an atomic per-(conv,msgId) in-flight guard (Phase 2)
- **The ask.** "Auto-translate triggering is still not stable/robust — both frontend and backend need optimization." Mapped the whole trigger surface first (two parallel `coder` sub-agents inventoried FE + BE trigger sites) before touching code; the reports + my own reads converged on two distinct failure classes: WRONG DEFAULT (fires when it shouldn't / doesn't when it should) and WRONG TARGET / DOUBLE-FIRE (lands on the wrong message, or two paths translate the same message and the slower clobbers the faster).
- **Root cause #1 — the keystone (Phase 1): the SAME `autoTranslate` flag resolved to FOUR different defaults.** Backend safety net `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` defaulted **TRUE** (`settings.get('autoTranslate', True)`, auto_translate.py:73); the canonical config resolver `lib/conv_config.py` and the input/send/queue paths defaulted **FALSE**; the incremental `_gate` read a bare falsy default; and the FRONTEND global `autoTranslate` defaulted **TRUE** (`core/cost.js` `localStorage… || "true"`) feeding ~8 inline `conv.autoTranslate !== undefined ? : true/false` ternaries with mixed fallbacks (two were the opposite, FALSE). Net effect on a conv where the user never toggled the flag: UI expects translation + arms a watchdog, the input path doesn't translate, the incremental accumulator never starts, the safety net DOES fire — and two FE paths silently skip. That's the "sometimes translates, sometimes stuck, sometimes must click Translate" instability.
  - **Fix (one source of truth per side, default OPT-IN/OFF — product decision: translation costs an extra LLM round-trip + latency, so it's opt-in; matches the config resolver that already defaulted OFF, fewest load-bearing paths changed):**
    - Backend: added `AUTO_TRANSLATE_DEFAULT = False` + `resolve_auto_translate(*sources)` (first-defined-wins, else OFF) to `lib/conv_config.py`; routed ALL SIX trigger reads through it — `auto_translate.py` (the TRUE outlier), `chat/turn_builder.py` (×2: send + headless API), `message_queue.py`, `translate/incremental._gate`, `routes/api_v1/chat.py`, `routes/chat.py` (preserving the VU/critic `auto_translate=False` override below the read). The `conv_config` resolver's OWN merge logic (`conv.get` vs `ov.get`) was deliberately NOT collapsed — it encodes the active/inactive precedence and is pinned by `test_conv_config.py`.
    - Frontend: added `convAutoTranslate(conv)` to `core/conversations.js` (conv value → global → OFF); replaced all 8 trigger ternaries (incl. the two FALSE outliers `streaming_render.js` VU + `translation.js` `_handleTerminalFailure`) + the toolbar-display defaults in `main.js`; flipped `core/cost.js` global default `"true"`→`"false"` so the toggle display matches behaviour. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-fab8f5a1.js` (helper lives in already-bundled `core/conversations.js`, no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change).
- **Root cause #2 (Phase 2) — WRONG TARGET + DOUBLE-FIRE.** The trigger selected the message by POSITION (`manager.py` passed `len(messages)-1`; endpoint triggers re-enumerated a fresh DB index) — a concurrent frontend write that shifts the row makes the translation land on the wrong message. And dedup leaned on `translatedContent` already existing + a msgIdx-keyed scan of the live `_translate_tasks` registry — both race, so the per-turn endpoint trigger, the end-of-task rescan, and a retried safety net could all schedule the same message.
  - **Fix:** (a) `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` now resolves the target **by stable `_msgId` first** (`task['_assistantMsgId']` → `messages[idx]._msgId`), looks the message up by that id, and uses the id-resolved `eff_idx` for EVERY downstream op (stale-check, existing-tc dedup, stale-clear write, finalize, spawn); positional index is fallback only when no id exists. (`_commit_translation_inner` was already id-first; now the trigger is too, end-to-end.) (b) New `lib/translate/inflight.py` — an atomic per-`(conv_id, msgId)` in-flight registry (`claim_inflight`/`release_inflight`/`is_inflight`, index-derived fallback key, TTL self-expiry 900s so a crashed worker can't wedge a message). The safety net CLAIMS before scheduling; later paths stand down on a live claim. Ownership transfers to the async worker (incremental finalize / spawned thread), each releasing on settle; every skip/error/spawn-failure path releases in the outer `finally`.
  - **Latent leak caught while building it:** `_guard_owned_by_worker = True` was set BEFORE `Thread.start()`, so a spawn failure would have leaked the claim forever. Moved it to AFTER a successful `.start()` (covered by `test_spawn_failure_releases_guard`).
  - **Item-3 verification (abort→cancel):** `_gate` reads the resolver, so a flag-absent task defaults OFF and never creates an accumulator to leak; the ON→abort transition tears it down via `cancel_incremental`; the incremental `_do_finalize` releases its in-flight guard on settle (split into `_do_finalize` wrapper + `_do_finalize_inner` so the release runs in a `finally` regardless of the commit path).
- **Tests (revert-proofed both directions — neuter→fail→restore for every mechanism):**
  - `tests/test_resolve_auto_translate.py` (5) — unified default-OFF + first-defined-wins precedence.
  - `tests/test_frontend_auto_translate_default.py` (1, real shipped JS under node) — `convAutoTranslate` default-OFF + precedence.
  - `tests/test_translate_inflight.py` (9) — guard claim/release/TTL/key precedence.
  - `tests/test_auto_translate_phase2.py` (5) — id-anchored target when index shifted, pre-spawn dedup stand-down, spawn-failure release, worker-settle release, incremental-handoff keeps-guard-until-finalize.
  - `tests/test_incremental_translate.py` (+3) — resolver-gated absent-flag→OFF, abort-after-segments cancel prevents leak, finalize releases in-flight guard.
  - Neuter proofs (all restored, 0 NEUTERED): backend default OFF→True (3 fail), FE helper default (1 fail), id-anchoring `eff_idx=msg_idx` (assert 1==2), dedup claim always-True (2 fail), worker release (assert not True), outer-finally release (assert not True), inc finalize release (assert not True).
  - **Verification (actual output):** full Phase-1+2 suite **84 passed**; adjacent FE suites (`test_frontend_sse_dispatch`, `test_frontend_streaming_ui`, `test_frontend_swarm_recovery`) 3 passed after adding the `convAutoTranslate` stub to those two characterization harnesses (they load `stream_lifecycle.js`/`streaming_render.js` in isolation, so the cross-file helper was undefined there — harness gap, not a production bug); `node --check` clean on all 9 edited JS; ruff clean on all edited/new Python.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a feature "fires unpredictably," first check whether ONE flag has DIVERGENT defaults across the read sites — collapse them into a single resolver per side (BE + FE), default expressed once, read everywhere through it; an audit (`grep "'autoTranslate', True/False"`) must come back empty for trigger paths. NEVER anchor a trigger/commit on array POSITION when a stable id exists — resolve by `_msgId` first, fall back to index only when absent. For "N independent paths can act on the same item," add an ATOMIC claim-before-scheduling guard keyed by stable id (not index), and make ownership EXPLICIT: whichever async worker takes over releases on settle, every synchronous skip/error path releases in `finally`, and set the "worker owns it" flag only AFTER the worker actually started (else a spawn failure wedges the guard).


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up) — Root-caused the "tool calls reconstructed twice, prefix unchanged" reports AWAY from a TTL hypothesis to per-key cache thrash under 429s, then fixed it with a flag-gated "warm-key hold" + made the cache-rebilling rebind observable at INFO
- **The ask (and the redirect).** User initially proposed "change all cache TTLs to 1h and see if results improve." Pushed back as a collaborator: there is NO single "all cache TTLs" dial — TTLs are scattered across 7 unrelated subsystems (Anthropic breakpoint TTL in `lib/llm/cache.py`, in-memory `TTLCache` in idempotency/feishu/sql_translate, billing-reserve sweep, conv-sticky TTL, TaskRuntime ttls) doing semantically different jobs; a blanket 1h would *shorten* idempotency (24h→1h), break the intentionally-permanent sql_translate cache, etc. Then the user gave the real symptom — "tool calls reconstructed twice consecutively, logs say prefix unchanged" — which matched the `conv-sticky-routing-per-key-cache` skill almost verbatim.
- **Measure-first triage (the evidence killed the TTL hypothesis).** Grepped `logs/app.log` for `[CacheStats]`/`[CacheTrack]`: conv `mqwqyrrd` on `aws.claude-opus-4.8` showed `cache_r→0` full re-writes (`cache_w≈100K`) at **6.1s and 11.3s gaps**, with OLD prefix values (`98811`, `64878`) resurfacing rounds later (two coexisting cache lineages). The tracker's own verdict string hedges "stochastic server-side cache miss **or** TTL expiry," but the 6-13s gaps are FAR under any TTL (tail 5m / prefix 1h), so eviction is definitively ruled out. Corroborating: repeated `429 rate-limited on sankuai_key_0:...opus-4.8` lines. → Cause is per-key cache thrash from key migration under 429, NOT TTL. Declined to run the TTL A/B (would burn ~¥0.7/round re-writes to test a knob the evidence excluded).
- **Challenged the "sticky routing works as designed" assumption (user's call).** Verified in code: `run_task` (orchestrator.py:1148) DOES `set_conv_affinity(task['convId'])`; the production stream path is `run_task` (off-loop worker thread) → `manager.py:1793` SYNC `dispatch_stream` → `pick_and_reserve` → `_pick` → `get_conv_affinity()` — all on ONE thread, no async hop (`async_dispatch_stream` is reserved, no prod caller). So affinity DOES bind. The reason the churn signal was invisible: it was `logger.debug` (app.log is INFO+). And the deeper reason cache still thrashed: `Slot.record_error(is_rate_limit=True)` cools the warm key only **0.5s**, so the soft-fallback picker immediately rebinds to a COLD key to dodge a sub-second per-minute throttle — paying a ~100K-token `cache_creation` to save 0.5s. Economically backwards.
- **Fix (flag-gated, reversible, scoped — the "warm-key hold"):**
  1. **`lib/llm_dispatch/conv_affinity.py`** — `sticky_hold_enabled()` (`TOFU_CONV_STICKY_HOLD`, default on) + `sticky_hold_budget_ms()` (`TOFU_CONV_STICKY_HOLD_MS`, default 1500).
  2. **`lib/llm_dispatch/dispatcher.py`** — new `sticky_cooldown_remaining_s(conv, prefer_model, exclude_*)` → `(remaining_s, key_name)` ONLY when the conv's sticky key has a slot in the alias group whose sole disqualifier is a live cooldown (not excluded, not already eligible). Added `import time`. Also promoted the churn-rebind log DEBUG→INFO with `conv→old_key→new_key→model` + "prompt cache will be re-written" — the exact cache-rebilling event, now grep-able in prod.
  3. **`lib/llm_dispatch/api.py` `dispatch_stream`** — a PRE-PICK warm-key hold: if the sticky key's remaining cooldown is within budget, sleep `min(remaining+0.05, budget)` BEFORE picking so the upcoming pick lands back on the warm key. Capped to ONE hold per dispatch (`state._warm_held`) so a long failure/quota cooldown (300s/3600s > budget) is NOT waited on — it falls through to the normal cold-key rebind. The budget gate is precisely what separates a transient 429 nudge (wait) from a real failure cooldown (don't).
- **Test (`tests/test_sticky_warm_key_hold.py`, 3 cases, real `LLMDispatcher` + real `dispatch_stream`, only `stream_chat` + `time.sleep` stubbed):** (a) warm key in a SHORT 429 cooldown → loop HOLDS (sleep ≈ remaining) and the request lands BACK on the warm key (`keys_called==['sk-0']`), hold INFO line asserted; (b) warm key in a LONG 300s cooldown → NO hold, rebinds to cold key (`['sk-1']`), churn INFO line asserted; (c) `TOFU_CONV_STICKY_HOLD=0` → no hold, rebinds. The sleep stub clears the warm slot's cooldown to model real time passing without sleeping. Revert-proofed: neutering `sticky_cooldown_remaining_s`→None fails case (a); restored clean.
- **Verification (actual output).** New 3 + `test_dispatch_stream` 7 + `test_conv_affinity` 5 + `test_async_dispatch_stream` 7 = **22 passed**; ruff clean on all 4 edited files. Live log capture shows both INFO lines firing: `dispatch_stream: holding 0.54s for conv=conv-hol warm key key_0 (short 429 cooldown) to keep prompt cache warm` and `[Dispatch] conv=conv-lon sticky key key_0 unavailable — rebinding to key_1 (...); prompt cache will be re-written on the new key`.
- **Guardrail / lesson.** When "tool calls reconstructed twice, prefix unchanged" appears, FIRST grep the cache-tracker gaps: a gap << TTL means key migration (per-key Anthropic cache), not eviction — don't reach for TTL. The fix for migration-under-429 is to make the warm key WORTH waiting for (the cache saving dwarfs a sub-second throttle), bounded so a genuinely-dead key is never waited on. And: the most expensive routing decision (a cache-rebilling rebind) MUST log at INFO, not DEBUG — a DEBUG line on the hot path left prod blind to it.

### 2026-06-28 — Hardened the "trailing assistant bubble renders empty with no finish tag" class at TWO layers (root-cause backend write-site + frontend reconcile gap); the reported conv was a LIVE turn, not a husk
- **User report / investigation.** "Why is the last agent message of conv `mqqkiycqei6xvl` empty, no finish tag — autopilot bug?" First DB read showed the trailing assistant msg as `{content:'', thinking:'I', _memoryPrefetch}` with NO finishReason/usage/timestamp, preceded by an `_isVirtualUser` (autopilot) turn — looked like an interrupted autopilot follow-up husk. **But on re-poll the task `445de1d6` was ALIVE** (`http://127.0.0.1:15000/api/v1/chat/poll/<id>` → `status=running`, `phase=tool_exec`, content grown 0→387+ chars, conv `updated_at` advancing). So THIS conversation was simply a follow-up turn caught in its first ~second (memory-prefetch + one thinking token), not a crash. Did NOT mutate it (there were 26 `task_results` rows at `status='running'` on the live server — blindly flipping them would corrupt genuinely-running tasks, incl. my own reviewer-swarm task). Correctly refrained.
- **But the user asked to fix the LATENT gap it exposed** (root-cause, not band-aid).
