The husk class is real: a turn that streams a stray reasoning fragment then dies (server crash) while `task_results.status='running'` leaves `{content:'', thinking:'I'}` persisted with no finishReason → renders as a blank, finish-tag-less bubble (`renderFinishInfo` returns '' with no finishReason/usage/model) AND slips past the frontend Case-D ghost-cleanup (its `!lastMsg.thinking` guard is defeated by the 1-char fragment). The backend `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` + the Case-B poll path (`routes/chat.py:1792` flips a not-in-memory `running` row to `interrupted`) DO heal it — but only at server boot / a completed page-load poll cycle respectively, so a husk can linger.
- **Fix — two aligned layers:**
  1. **Backend write-site (durable, removes the class).** `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py::_sync_partial_to_conversation`: when the last message is NOT already an assistant row (i.e. the checkpoint would CREATE a new trailing row), require real `content` before appending — `if not content: return`. A thinking-only first checkpoint is deferred; once content arrives the row is created with the accumulated thinking written alongside (nothing dropped). Updating an EXISTING assistant row (the frontend placeholder — the normal in-flight path) is unaffected.
  2. **Frontend reconcile (defensive).** `static/js/main/main_init_tasks.js`: extracted the Case-D decision into a pure `_classifyGhostTail(lastMsg)` → `'delete' | 'interrupted' | null`. A trailing assistant turn with empty content, no finishReason/usage/error, and no REAL tool round (a `done`/results/`toolContent` round counts; an empty/`searching` one doesn't) is a ghost: truly-empty (no thinking) → delete (unchanged); thinking-only → STAMP `finishReason='interrupted'` (preserve recovered thinking + `_memoryPrefetch` provenance) so it renders honestly with the "Interrupted" badge instead of a blank bubble. Gated by `!conv._needsLoad && !activeStreams.has(conv.id)` (Cases A/B/C already consumed active-task convs; the `activeStreams` check is belt-and-suspenders so a LIVE streaming turn — legitimately `content:''`+thinking — is never touched). Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-3e0b3eb8.js`.
- **Tests (revert-proofed both directions):**
  - `tests/test_partial_sync_no_husk.py` (3 cases, real DB via `init_db()` bootstrap fixture): a thinking-only checkpoint onto a trailing VU-user turn does NOT append a husk; a content checkpoint DOES materialize the row + keeps accumulated thinking; an EXISTING placeholder still receives a thinking-only update (guard doesn't over-fire). Neuter `if not content:`→`if False:` → only the husk-defer case fails (proven; other 2 still pass).
  - `tests/test_frontend_ghost_tail.py` (19 checks, real shipped JS under node): `_classifyGhostTail` matrix (the exact `mqqkiycqei6xvl` husk → 'interrupted'; empty → 'delete'; settled/has-content/has-finishReason/has-usage/has-error/real-round → null; empty-searching-round still ghost; non-assistant/null → null) PLUS loads the REAL `ui/finish_info.js` and asserts `renderFinishInfo` renders a NON-empty HTML containing "Interrupted" for a finishReason-only message (closes the "stamp still renders blank" risk). Neuter the 'interrupted' branch → exactly the 2 interrupted-classification checks fail.
- **Verification (actual output).** New tests 4 passed; adjacency `test_autopilot_poll_handoff`+`test_frontend_tool_rounds_render`+`test_frontend_swarm_recovery` 13 passed combined; `node --check` clean; ruff clean on new tests. The 4 `test_chat_manager_migration.py` failures are the pre-existing `no such table: task_results` DB-bootstrap gap (PROVEN unrelated: identical 4-fail/17-pass with my `manager.py` edit reverted) already documented in this journal. The lone ruff F401 (`db_execute_with_retry` unused, manager.py:20) is pre-existing dev-tree drift on an import line I did not touch.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a trailing assistant bubble "renders empty with no finish tag," FIRST check whether the task is actually still live (poll the running server) before concluding it's a dead husk — a turn caught in its first second looks identical to a crashed one, and mutating `running` task_results rows on a live server corrupts in-flight work. The durable fix for the genuine husk class is at the WRITE site (don't persist a content-less trailing row from a thinking-only checkpoint), with the frontend reconcile PREFERRING to stamp `interrupted` (honest render, preserves recovered thinking) over deleting, gated so a live stream is never reconciled.


### 2026-06-28 — RESEARCH (proposal, no code shipped): "should we build advanced engines in-house?" → verdict NO, consolidate the ONE proven dual-write persistence pattern; wrote `docs/proposals/STREAMED_STATE_PERSISTENCE.md`
- **Question.** User asked whether the project — now large — would benefit from building custom in-house "engines" (frontend streaming rendering, various backend functions, …) for performance / robustness / readability / modularity. This is a strategy question, not a code task; answered as a careful collaborator (the right answer might be "don't build").
- **Method.** Two parallel `coder` sub-agents inventoried the actual code (frontend streaming/render layer; backend SSE-persistence + LLM-SSE + DB layers) — factual "what exists, how big, where the fragility lives," no solutions. Synthesised against the JOURNAL incident history.
- **Verdict — don't greenfield; the project ALREADY has its engines.** The team has hand-rolled `event_log.py` (composite-PK dedup + collision canary + 2-pass TTL prune), `_sql_translate.py` (SQLite→PG bridge), `_sse_core.py` `SSEAccumulator` (3-protocol translation), and a frontend coalescer + ~15 fingerprint sites. Project size is a reason to CONSOLIDATE, not to build new engines (a rewrite of working hot-path code is the bigger risk on a large codebase, and a custom FE VDOM would violate CLAUDE.md §3.2 no-framework/no-build). The clean, library-backed pieces (`push.py`, `events.py`, transport shells, DB pool) were explicitly left alone.
- **Two recommendations, one dropped after verification.** (Dropped) "finish the `_core_schema.py` migration to retire `_sql_translate.py`'s regex bridge" — FALSE: that migration is COMPLETE; `_PK_MAP` now holds only external `tofu-trading` tables, guarded by `TestPkMapNoDeadEntries`, and the bridge is load-bearing for the external package. This was the `tofu-stale-migration-status-docs` trap again (acted on CLAUDE.md prose that already said "migration COMPLETE"). (Kept) the single high-leverage initiative below.
- **The one initiative — durable streamed-state persistence.** Root cause behind FOUR separate 2026-06-28 incidents (swarm panel fails to expand on reload; endpoint critic/worker thinking vanishes at finalize; `event_id` collision storm; orphaned `task_events`): **streaming state is RECONSTRUCTED at render from live SSE rather than PERSISTED as authoritative state.** The swarm-snapshot fix (write the truth down via dual-write CAS onto the spawn round) proved the cure; the proposal formalises it.
- **Key structural correction (made during review, important for whoever implements).** First draft claimed "three persistence paths collapse into one primitive." WRONG — there are TWO different shapes: (1) swarm = CAS-stamp ONE field (`_swarmSnapshot`) onto ONE located tool round (agent-id intersection) — this IS what a `persist_streamed_field(locate_round, field, value)` primitive models; (2) endpoint = `_sync_endpoint_turns_to_conversation` rewrites the WHOLE turn array by index, and `thinking` ALREADY rides durably inside the turn dicts (the critic fix made that true). Forcing endpoint through the single-round-field CAS would be a worse fit, not a consolidation. So: the primitive generalises ONLY the swarm/single-round-field shape (one caller on day one; future tool-round-attached fields reuse it); the endpoint path stays separate. **What binds the two shapes is the CONTRACT + RATCHET, not a shared function** — a ratchet test asserts "every FE-reconstructed streamed field has a durable persisted counterpart," whichever mechanism provides it. That's the real anti-band-aid mechanism.
- **Deliverable / phasing.** `docs/proposals/STREAMED_STATE_PERSISTENCE.md`. Phase A (low-risk, scoped): extract `persist_streamed_field` from `lib/swarm/snapshot.py` as a delegating wrapper (gate: existing `test_swarm_snapshot_persist.py` stays green), leave the endpoint path as-is, document the mechanism-agnostic contract in CLAUDE.md, add the ratchet test. Phase B (named, GATED, not started): make the persisted `task_events` log the single render source — deferred because its blast radius crosses the fragile `append_event ↔ event_log` sequencing seam that produced this week's collision/orphan incidents.
- **Status.** Proposal only — NO code changed, awaiting greenlight on Phase A step 1. Logged here for cross-session continuity.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up) — Made the orphan-table cleanup DEPLOYMENT-WIDE: a startup self-heal drops `agent_sessions` (empty-guarded) + `_aio_test` so instances we never touch converge to "live ∖ Core ∖ external = ∅" by themselves
- **Why (user-raised).** The earlier manual drops fixed THIS box, but the two orphans were minted by the same trashed bootstrap (`agent_sessions` ← removed `lib/agent_backends/session_store.py`) and leaked-test path (`_aio_test` ← `tests/test_db_aio.py`), so they almost certainly exist in OTHER deployments' DBs too. A manual op won't run on instances we don't touch → the durable fix is an idempotent, guarded self-heal at the schema-init path.
- **Fix (single source of truth + 3-layer wiring):**
  1. **`lib/database/_orphan_heal.py` (new).** `heal_orphan_tables(conn, table_exists, count_rows)` iterates a `_ORPHANS` registry `(name, require_empty, reason)`: `agent_sessions` is `require_empty=True` (drop ONLY when `count(*)==0` — a fail-safe so a hypothetical out-of-tree fork still writing it can never have its data destroyed; a non-empty one is LEFT + `audit_log('db_orphan_table_nonempty_kept')`); `_aio_test` is `require_empty=False` (never a real table → dropped regardless). Best-effort, never raises (a heal failure must not abort schema init); every drop emits `logger.warning` + `audit_log('db_orphan_table_dropped')`. Adding a future orphan = one tuple.
  2. **Wiring.** Both `_schema_pg.py` and `_schema_sqlite.py` gained a `_count_rows(conn, table)` helper and call `heal_orphan_tables(...)` at the TOP of `init_db()` — crucially BEFORE the schema-version fast-path `return`. That placement is the whole point: existing deployments are already at the current `_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so the slow DDL path is skipped; putting the heal before the fast-path makes it run on EVERY startup (it's two `_table_exists` probes when clean — negligible) so an already-current instance still converges on its next boot.
  3. **Test (`tests/test_orphan_heal.py`, 4 cases).** empty orphans dropped; non-empty `agent_sessions` SPARED (+still present); non-empty `_aio_test` STILL dropped (require_empty=False); clean DB = no-op. Plus an E2E check driving the REAL `init_db()` twice on a temp sqlite DB (inject orphans → re-init hits the version-cache fast-path → both orphans still dropped, proving the heal runs before the fast-path return). 4/4 + 91/91 regression (parity+sql_translate+db_aio) green; ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** a one-off manual DROP only heals the box you're on. When an orphan was minted by code that runs on every deployment (a since-removed subsystem's bootstrap, or a test that leaked into prod), the convergent fix is a guarded self-heal in `init_db` placed BEFORE the schema-version fast-path (else already-current instances skip it). Guard a "drop" on emptiness whenever the table COULD still be written by something out-of-tree; only drop unconditionally what is unambiguously never-real (test scratch).


### 2026-06-28 — Fixed run_command (and any tool) stuck on "Running…" forever after Stop: the abort short-circuits left the tool round in `searching` with no terminal event; backend now SWEEPS dangling rounds at task end + a real secondary bug (interactive run_command path was not abort-aware) fixed
- **User report / RCA (confirmed against code):** terminating a conversation while a `run_command` shows "Running…" leaves it "Running…" forever — live AND after reload. Root cause is a backend state-persistence gap, surfaced as a frontend render symptom. A tool round renders "Running…" purely off `round.status === "searching"` (`tool_rounds.js:1986` → `_renderUnifiedToolLine(r, r.status==="searching")`). The normal completion path always reaches `_finalize_tool_round` (status→`done`), but EVERY abort short-circuit returns BEFORE it: `_execute_tool_one` top guard (`lib/tasks_pkg/executor.py` — `if task.get('aborted'): return …` ), the streaming executor's twin guard + cancelled pending futures (`streaming_tool_executor.py:250-253,607-680`). The orchestrator terminal block (`orchestrator.py:_finalize_and_emit_done`) set `finishReason='aborted'`/`status='done'` but NEVER walked `task['toolRounds']`, so the `searching` round was persisted verbatim into `conversations.messages` and re-rendered as "Running…" on reload. The frontend abort handler (`sse_pipeline.js`) set `finishReason='aborted'` on the message but never swept lingering `searching` rounds either.
- **Fix (write the terminal state down — single source of truth, 3 aligned layers):**
  1. **Backend sweep (authoritative).** New `orchestrator._finalize_dangling_tool_rounds(task)` — walks `task['toolRounds']`, and for every round NOT in a settled/interactive-resolved state (`done/error/aborted/rejected/skipped/awaiting_*/submitted/pending_approval`) with no `results`, calls the REAL `_finalize_tool_round` (emits a terminal `tool_result`-class event so the live stream agrees) then stamps `status='aborted'` + a `{interrupted:true, source:'Interrupted'}` meta. A round that has real `results` but a stale non-terminal status is normalized to `done` without fabricating an error. Logged per round per the logging discipline. Wired into `_finalize_and_emit_done` right after `finishReason` is set, inside a try/except (best-effort, never blocks termination) — runs on EVERY exit, not just abort (a cancelled streaming future can dangle on a normal-error exit too).
  2. **Frontend mirror (defensive).** `tool_rounds.js`: a new branch BEFORE `isSearching` renders any `status==='aborted'` (result-less) round as a static `.ptool-interrupted` line with a `.ptool-badge-interrupted` "interrupted" badge — NO spinner, NO "Running…" block; rounds with real results fall through to the normal renderers. `sse_pipeline.js`: on `AbortError`, in addition to `finishReason='aborted'`, flip any still-`searching` (result-less) tool round to `aborted` so the live DOM doesn't lag the backend's persisted snapshot. CSS added in `styles.css`. Bundle rebuilt → `bundle-68eead92.js` (both files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`).
  3. **Secondary bug found while building the test — interactive run_command path was NOT abort-aware.** The cooperative-abort kill (the 2026 `_run_command_simple` fix: poll `task['aborted']` every ~0.2s, store `_subprocess_pid/_pgid`, `start_new_session=True`, `_kill_process_tree`) was NEVER applied to `_run_command_interactive`, and `run_command()` called it WITHOUT `task=` — and `_handle_project_tool` ALWAYS passes a `stdin_callback`, so EVERY chat run_command takes the interactive path. Net effect: a Stop during a long interactive command could neither be cooperatively killed (no abort poll) NOR SIGTERM'd by `chat_abort` (no `_subprocess_pid` stored). Fixed: thread `task` through, store pid/pgid, `start_new_session=True`, add the abort check + `_kill_process_tree` in the loop, clear the task ref on exit, and surface `aborted=True` via `_format_run_output`. Proven by the test runtime dropping from a 15s join-timeout to ~1s kill.
- **Tests (production-path, revert-proofed both directions):**
  - `tests/test_abort_dangling_tool_round.py` (NEW, 3 tests) drives the REAL pipeline against a REAL `conversations` row + `create_task` + `persist_task_result`→`_sync_result_to_conversation`: (a) start a real `sleep 30` via the REAL `_execute_tool_one`/run_command on a worker thread, abort mid-flight, run the terminal sweep, assert NO `searching` round in the PERSISTED conversation; (b) reproduce the executor abort short-circuit directly (with `aborted` pre-set the REAL `_execute_tool_one` returns "Task aborted by user." leaving the round `searching` — the bug), then sweep→`aborted`, persisted conv clean; (c) the sweep preserves `done`/`awaiting_human` rounds and only touches the dangling one. NEUTERING the sweep (`return 0`) fails (b)+(c), reproducing the stuck-"Running…" verbatim (`Executor: Skipping tool run_command — task aborted` + round stays `searching`); restored clean.
  - `tests/test_frontend_tool_rounds_render.py` extended (+2 scenarios, `min_pass` 30→36): a reloaded `status:'aborted'` run_command round with an `interrupted` meta renders `.ptool-interrupted`+`.ptool-badge-interrupted` and NO `.ptool-cmd-running`/`.ptool-spinner` (the cardinal symptom); an aborted round WITH real results still uses the normal command renderer.
- **Verification (actual output).** `test_abort_dangling_tool_round` 3 passed; `test_frontend_tool_rounds_render` passed (38 internal checks ≥ min_pass 36); combined abort+render+run_command_meta = 17 passed; orchestrations sweep (`test_orchestrations` + `phase_and_output`) = 54 passed; frontend render+completion+swarm_recovery+sse_dispatch = 7 passed. `node --check` clean on both edited JS; ruff clean on `run_command.py` + the new test. (Pre-existing: the 2 ruff F401s in `orchestrator.py` are on untouched import lines = dev-tree drift; and `test_chat_manager_migration.py`'s 4 `no such table: task_results` failures reproduce on the clean tree in a fresh process — an unrelated DB-bootstrap gap, NOT this change.)
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a tool round "sometimes shows Running… forever," the question is whether its terminal state is WRITTEN DOWN or only inferred at render — an abort short-circuit that returns before `_finalize_tool_round` leaves the round `searching` and that status is persisted verbatim. Fix at the source store: sweep `task['toolRounds']` once at task termination (covering executor + streaming-executor + cancelled-future paths) and emit the terminal event, with the frontend PREFERRING the persisted terminal status and only mirroring defensively. Also: any code path that runs a subprocess on behalf of a task MUST be abort-aware end-to-end — check `task['aborted']` in its loop AND store `_subprocess_pid/_pgid` for the SIGTERM path; an abort-aware "simple" path means nothing if the actually-used "interactive" path was missed.


### 2026-06-28 — Closed the DB-migration acceptance gap: the in-tree Core migration was self-consistent but TWO orphan tables existed in live PG with no Core definition; dropped both + fixed the test-leak source + set the real acceptance criterion (live ∖ Core ∖ external = ∅)
- **User question:** "Have all our database tables been migrated?" Initial answer verified the CODE's self-consistency only — 33 Core `define_table` defs, both `_schema_pg.py`/`_schema_sqlite.py` wire every table via `create_if_absent` (no hand-authored CREATE TABLE), `_PK_MAP` holds only external `trading_*` tables, 81 parity/translate tests green. **That was necessary but NOT sufficient:** the true acceptance criterion is whether every table actually PRESENT in production is accounted for, which requires diffing the live DB against the Core metadata — not just confirming the code agrees with itself.
- **The gap (found by live introspection, not code reading).** `SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'` on the live `tofu` PG DB returned **64 tables**. Cross-referenced against the 33 Core tables + the out-of-tree `trading_*` set, exactly two were UNACCOUNTED:
  1. **`agent_sessions`** — DDL `(conv_id text, backend text, session_id text, created_at/last_used_at timestamptz default now())`, PK `(conv_id, backend)` + `idx_agent_sessions_backend`. **0 rows, `n_tup_ins=0` — never written.** RCA: it backed `lib/agent_backends/session_store.py`, a session store mapping `conv_id → backend-native session_id` for EXTERNAL CLI agents (Claude Code / Codex `--resume`). The whole `lib/agent_backends/` subsystem was **trashed 2026-06-21** (only copy left is under `.tofu_trash/.../lib/agent_backends/session_store.py`). The bootstrap that created the table went with it, but the empty table was orphaned in prod. Classification: **(b) confirmed-dead** → guarded DROP, not a Core def. Runtime-safety reverified: `grep` for `agent_sessions`/`session_store` = ZERO live matches; the two `agent_backends` hits are stale prose in `lib/tasks_pkg/__init__.py:72` + `manager.py:61` comments (no import/query).
  2. **`_aio_test`** — scratch table created by `tests/test_db_aio.py::_setup_table` (9 rows). Test residue leaked into prod PG — the same test-harness-touching-prod class hardened earlier today (ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres` historically defeated conftest's force-sqlite, so the test's `CREATE TABLE _aio_test` via the shared `_pool_get()` landed on production). Classification: **test leak** → DROP + fix at source.
- **Fixes (all three, verified):**
  1. **Dropped both orphans on live PG** (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS agent_sessions; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _aio_test;`). Confirmed `to_regclass` → NULL for both and `idx_agent_sessions_backend` gone (DROP TABLE cascades its indexes). Re-ran the acceptance diff (live public tables ∖ Core metadata ∖ `trading_*` ∖ sqlite-only `conversations_fts`) → **`[]` (empty)**. Live count 64 → 62; Core 33; zero unaccounted.
  2. **Fixed the leak at source** (`tests/test_db_aio.py`): `_setup_table` now `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _aio_test` in a `try/finally` teardown so the scratch table can NEVER persist in whatever DB the session resolved to. Belt-and-suspenders on top of conftest's forced-sqlite + the session-first `_db_guard_session`/`pytest_configure` gate (which already makes prod-PG reach impossible going forward). 10/10 tests pass.
  3. This journal entry.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** "have all tables been migrated?" is NOT answered by code self-consistency (Core defs ↔ bootstrap wiring ↔ parity tests) — that only proves the code agrees with itself. The acceptance criterion is **live-DB public tables ∖ Core-metadata ∖ external-plugin tables = ∅**, RE-CHECKED after any subsystem removal (a removed feature's bootstrap stops creating its table, but the already-created table is orphaned in every existing deployment). When a subsystem is trashed, audit the live schema for tables it created and schedule a guarded drop. Any test that creates a scratch table MUST drop it in teardown — a leaked scratch table in prod is a test-isolation failure, not just clutter.


### 2026-06-28 — ROOT-CAUSED the swarm "Parallel Execution" panel that "sometimes fails to expand" on reload: backend now PERSISTS a durable per-agent snapshot onto the spawn round; killed the 3rd frontend band-aid by writing the authoritative state down
- **User report / diagnosis (confirmed against code):** the swarm panel is NOT stored as a panel — only the underlying tool rounds are; the agent dashboard is RECONSTRUCTED at render. `round._swarmAgents` (+ `_swarmActive`/`_asyncRunning`/`_swarmStartTime`) are synthesized LIVE on the frontend from `swarm_*` SSE events (`sse_handlers_swarm.js`) and NEVER persisted. On reload `_isRoundSwarm` (`tool_rounds.js:58`) only renders when `_swarm` AND (`_swarmAgents.length` OR `results.length`); `_recoverSwarmAgents` (`streaming_swarm_panel.js`) rebuilds from the spawn handle JSON in `toolContent` + sibling `await_agents`/`get_agent_result` rounds → 3 failure modes: (a) missing `_swarm`, (b) unparseable/ghost handle, (c) FIRE-AND-FORGET (spawned, never awaited) → every agent renders as `unknown` stub. This was the THIRD frontend patch of the same class (empty-body recovery, stale-pill guard, reconcile sweep) — the signal that the authoritative state was never written down.
- **Fix (write the truth down, 3 aligned layers):**
  1. **`lib/swarm/snapshot.py` (new).** `persist_snapshot_to_conversation(conv_id, agent_ids, snapshot)` — best-effort, CAS-guarded (mirrors `_sync_partial_to_conversation`), never raises. `find_spawn_round(messages, agent_ids)` matches the spawn round by INTERSECTING the handle's agent ids (disambiguates multiple waves/panels in one conv). `stamp_round` writes `_swarmSnapshot` + asserts `_swarm:true`.
  2. **`lib/swarm/master.py`.** `_build_agent_snapshot()` materialises per-agent `{id,role,model,objective,status,elapsed,tokens,preview,modifiedFiles,error}` from the authoritative `_results_by_id` (+ scheduler running/pending for in-flight; `unknown` only when terminated & no result) — normalises `completed→done`. `_persist_agent_snapshot()` DUAL-WRITES: (1) stamps the LIVE chat task's spawn `round_entry` (reached via `manager.tasks`/`tasks_lock` by conv_id+id-intersection) so the in-turn `_sync_*_to_conversation` persists it and doesn't clobber it; (2) direct CAS into `conversations.messages` for the detached/fire-and-forget case (spawning turn already ended). Wired into `_on_agent_complete_callback` (incremental) AND the driver `finally` settle (final, `settled:true`).
  3. **Frontend.** `_recoverSwarmAgents` (`streaming_swarm_panel.js`) PREFERS `round._swarmSnapshot.agents` (real status, fire-and-forget safe) before the handle+sibling fallback; `_isRoundSwarm` (`tool_rounds.js`) now treats a snapshot-only round as renderable. The stale-guard + reconcile sweep are UNCHANGED (kept as the offline fallback). Frontend re-sync preserves the field: `syncConversationToServer` spreads each message (`...m`), so the backend-written `_swarmSnapshot` rides through untouched; CAS guards races.
- **Tests (revert-proofed, both directions):**
  - `tests/test_swarm_snapshot_persist.py` (NEW, 2 tests) drives the REAL production path: `execute_swarm_tool('spawn_agents')` + a real `MasterOrchestrator`/`StreamingScheduler` on its daemon thread (only the LLM-bound `_build_sub_agent` factory patched to a canned `_FakeAgent` — no network), a real `conversations` row holding the spawn round, the real CAS write. Asserts the SETTLED snapshot lands on the spawn round with each agent's real status/preview/tokens/modifiedFiles — WITHOUT any `await_agents` call (the fire-and-forget case). Neuter `_persist_agent_snapshot` body → both fail (proven; it even fired the real auto-continue path, confirming it's the genuine swarm pipeline).
  - `tests/test_frontend_swarm_recovery.py` extended: a reloaded fire-and-forget spawn round (no `_swarmAgents`, no `await_agents` sibling) carrying ONLY `_swarmSnapshot` renders real agent cards + the pencil "edited 2" pill; harness now also loads `tool_rounds.js` to exercise the `_isRoundSwarm` gate. 22/22 PASS. Neuter the frontend snapshot branch (`if(false&&…)`) → exactly the 5 `faf_*` checks fail (status→unknown, preview/modifiedFiles/body/pencil lost). Restored clean (grep -c NEUTERED = 0).
- **Verification (actual output).** `test_swarm_snapshot_persist` 2 passed; `test_frontend_swarm_recovery`+`stale`+`tool_scoping`+`frontend_sse_dispatch` 19 passed; `test_swarm_async` 50 passed (unittest); ruff clean on all changed/new Py. **E2E smoke lane: 3/3 passed** (real Quart/Hypercorn boot + real headless Chromium + stub LLM) once the sqlite DB is bootstrapped — incl. `test_bundle_loaded_in_browser` (loads the edited `tool_rounds.js`/`streaming_swarm_panel.js`) and `test_tool_round_renders` (the SSE→`tool_rounds.js` render path my `_isRoundSwarm` change touches). The 2 earlier e2e failures were PROVEN environmental (`no such table: conversations` at server-warmup — an unbootstrapped temp `TOFU_DB_PATH` I had over-specified; bypasses conftest's app-import bootstrap), NOT a regression: re-running against an `init_db()`-bootstrapped sqlite path → all 3 green.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a panel "sometimes fails to expand," check whether its state is PERSISTED or merely RECONSTRUCTED at render — repeated frontend recovery band-aids (empty-body, stale-pill, reconcile) are the tell that the authoritative state was never written down. Fix = write it down at the source-of-truth store (`conversations.messages` tool round), dual-writing the live task + a CAS direct write so it survives the detached/fire-and-forget path; the frontend then PREFERS the persisted snapshot and the existing offline guards remain as fallback. Source streamed-only fields from the authoritative `_results_by_id`, never the live SSE-synthesized array.


### 2026-06-28 — RECOVERED ~2300 production conversations the E2E suite silently deleted + closed the hole at 3 layers (the test harness must NEVER touch the production DB)
- **User report:** "server 15000 lost a lot of conversations." MEASURED, didn't guess: live `tofu` DB (PG 15439) held **153 convs**; the 06-27 18:28 startup warmup logged **3142**; `pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_del=5496` with autovacuum at 03:47 → ~2990 real rows genuinely DELETED, not corruption (no subtrans/PANIC/TOAST-heal in logs).
- **Root cause (PROVEN from app.log, not theorised).** At **06-27 22:21** app.log shows a burst of **2268 `[delete_conv] Deleted conv …` lines** (1530 in one minute) across `db-aio_0/1/2` — but access.log shows **ZERO `DELETE /api/v1/conversations` HTTP requests** in that window. So the deletes were IN-PROCESS, not via HTTP. The smoking gun: at 22:21:14 an agent task (`966ac345`, writing `tests/test_e2e_smoke.py`) ran `pytest`; at **22:21:16 a SECOND server booted** ("🫧 Tofu starting up") and connected to **PRODUCTION PG 15439/tofu**. Chain: (1) the agent's shell had ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres` (it's in `.env`), which DEFEATED conftest's `setdefault('sqlite')` → `lib.database._core._BACKEND` froze to `'pg'` at import; (2) the `live_server` fixture booted the REAL app against production PG (and sets `cfg.accesslog=None`, hiding the browser DELETEs from access.log); (3) the visual-E2E `page`/`_cleanup_test_convs` fixtures do a snapshot-diff cleanup (`ids_after - ids_before` → `deleteConversation(cid)`), and with an empty/not-ready `ids_before` baseline the "diff" became the ENTIRE production sidebar.
- **Recovery (data was safe in the nightly dump).** The 06-27 02:00 `pg_dumpall` (11.1 GB, PRE-loss) held the tofu-DB conversations block (2807 real convs). Method: took a pre-recovery safety dump of live; extracted ONLY the tofu-DB `COPY public.conversations` block (the dumpall spans 5 DBs — `keyan`/`scratch_restore`/`tofu`/`tofu_misroute_bak`/postgres — so `\connect tofu` line-scoped the awk); loaded it into a `_recover_stage` staging table; `INSERT … SELECT … ON CONFLICT (id,user_id) DO NOTHING` → restored **2974 convs**, preserving the 9 created after the dump. Live `tofu` 153 → **3127** (2816 real); all `search_tsv` repopulated by the BEFORE trigger; API `?meta=1` now serves 3127. (Tip: FUSE makes a single big `COMMIT` time out — run the COPY in autocommit, no explicit BEGIN/COMMIT.)
- **Prevention — defense-in-depth in `tests/conftest.py` (3 independent layers, each alone stops the incident):**
  1. **FORCE sqlite, not setdefault.** `_install_shim_for_collection` + `_configure_test_env` now OVERRIDE `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=sqlite` + a temp `TOFU_DB_PATH` unless `TOFU_ALLOW_PG_TESTS=1`. An ambient `postgres` env can no longer reach the DB layer. Proven: with `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres TOFU_PG_PORT=15439`, importing conftest resolves `_core._BACKEND=='sqlite'`.
  2. **Keystone guard `_assert_test_database()`** — called by `flask_app` AND `live_server` BEFORE the app handles a request. HARD-ABORTS the session (`pytest.UsageError`) if the resolved DB is PG and not a test-marked DB (name must contain `test`/`scratch`/`_ci`/`pytest`) with explicit `TOFU_ALLOW_PG_TESTS=1`. Single call-site-agnostic chokepoint — no future live-server fixture can escape it.
  3. **Snapshot-diff delete is fail-safe.** The `page` fixture now refuses to bulk-`deleteConversation` when the baseline is UNTRUSTED (`conversations` global not an array at snapshot time → can't tell "test made N" from "sidebar IS N"); `test_visual_e2e._cleanup_test_convs` bails when `ids_before` is empty. Falls back to the pattern-gated server purge only.
- **Also hardened (audit agent's separate finding, latent landmine #1):** `lib/database/_bootstrap.py::_restore_from_sql_dump_if_present` does a `pg_dumpall --clean --if-exists` restore (DROPs every DB). Added a guard: probe `count(*) FROM conversations` first; if the target already has convs, QUARANTINE the dump (`.skipped-nonempty-target`) + `logger.critical` instead of clobbering, unless `TOFU_FORCE_DUMP_RESTORE=1`.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_db_guard.py` (5 cases) pins the guard logic — sqlite safe; pg+production refused; pg+testname WITHOUT opt-in refused; pg+opt-in+production-name refused; pg+opt-in+testname allowed. All green; ruff clean; conftest/test_visual_e2e AST+ruff clean; collection unaffected.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** the test suite shares the production DB on this host (ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres` defeats a `setdefault`), and the E2E cleanup fixtures DELETE conversations — a catastrophic combination. A test harness must FAIL CLOSED against a non-test DB at the app-boot chokepoint, and any snapshot-diff "delete what I created" cleanup must treat an empty/unready baseline as "delete NOTHING," never "delete everything." Recovery source of record: the 02:00 `pg_dumpall_*.sql` nightly (multi-DB; scope the awk to the `\connect tofu` block).
- **Follow-up (same day) — closed two guard BYPASSES a review caught:** the keystone `_assert_test_database` was only wired into `flask_app`/`live_server`, but two paths reach the real DB OUTSIDE those fixtures: (a) `tests/test_sdk_e2e._boot_real_server` (and its caller `test_ecosystem_sdk_compat`) imports `server.py` + boots its OWN hypercorn; (b) `tests/test_sdk_parity_e2e._setup_once` imports `server.py` independently; (c) the autouse `_purge_leaked_test_conversations` session fixture issues `DELETE FROM conversations` at session START before any guard. Fixes: (1) added a session-FIRST autouse `_db_guard_session` fixture and made `_purge_leaked_test_conversations(_db_guard_session)` DEPEND on it (pytest then orders the gate first); (2) added a function-level `_db_is_test_safe()` refusal INSIDE `_purge_test_conversations` (it's callable directly from page teardown); (3) `_boot_real_server` + `_setup_once` each call `_assert_test_database` before importing the app. New `test_db_guard.py` cases pin the sdk_e2e/parity own-boot refusal (raises before creating a tmpdir).
- **Follow-up 2 (same day) — a THIRD own-boot bypass + made the gate truly universal:** review found `tests/test_e2e_headless_api._setup_once` ALSO boots `server.py` via `spec_from_file_location` with no guard. Rather than keep playing whack-a-mole per helper, added the keystone gate to the ONE place that runs before ANY test module is imported: **`pytest_configure` now calls `_assert_test_database('pytest_configure (session start)')`**. Because `pytest_configure` fires after conftest import (force-sqlite already ran) but before collection, it gates EVEN module-level `spec_from_file_location('server.py')` boots (test_hook_taxonomy, test_request_parser, …) that no fixture covers. Belt-and-suspenders kept: explicit `_assert_test_database` in `test_e2e_headless_api._setup_once` + the two sdk helpers, and in the two STANDALONE `__main__` runners (`test_restart_smoke._standalone`, `test_server_async.__main__`) that skip conftest entirely when run as `python tests/x.py` (verified the guard refuses when `_core` is pg-frozen before the conftest import; in the benign case conftest's force-sqlite neutralizes the env first). Audit of every `server.py` import/boot site in `tests/`: all 13 run under pytest (covered by the universal `pytest_configure` gate + force-sqlite) and the 5 with standalone `__main__` blocks each call the guard. `test_db_guard.py` now 8 cases incl. `test_headless_api_setup_refuses_production_db`; 135 e2e/server-boot tests collect clean; ruff clean. The guard is now genuinely call-site-agnostic.


### 2026-06-28 — Fixed orchestration-flow agents' "thinking refreshes then vanishes instantly": the FlowExecutor→chat-bubble bridge streamed thinking live but DROPPED it at the turn boundary; now carried through step_complete/step_trace + adapter messages + the two finalize SSE events + the critic frontend gap
- **User report:** agents on the 编排流程 / "自动驾驶" front-end (the dropdown that routes `flowBuiltin`/`flowDefinition` through `_run_flow_as_endpoint_task` → `EndpointEventAdapter` — a LIVE production path) showed thinking that refreshed during the turn then disappeared the instant it completed. "Clearly, rendering it the same way as a normal agent would be fine." Correct diagnosis.
- **Root cause (traced, not guessed).** The flow path is *designed* to render identically to a first-class agent turn: `SubAgent.on_thinking` → `stream_sink('thinking')` → engine `step_delta{kind:'thinking'}` → adapter `_on_step_delta` → wire `delta{thinking}` → frontend accumulates `assistantMsg.thinking` + `updateStreamingUI` shows the live block. **That half worked.** The gap was at FINALIZE: `FlowExecutor._default_runner` returned only `output`/`status`/`tool_log` (never `result.reasoning_trace`), and `EndpointEventAdapter._on_step_complete` built the persisted planner/worker/critic message dicts with `content` ONLY — no `thinking` field — and emitted `endpoint_planner_done`/`endpoint_critic_msg` with no `thinking`. So streamed thinking was ephemeral: shown during the turn, absent from the finalized message → blinked out the instant the turn completed / the conv re-rendered / a reload hit `_sync_endpoint_turns_to_conversation`. The contrast was decisive: the LIVE endpoint path (`lib/tasks_pkg/endpoint.py:706/720/866/1172`) puts `thinking` in every turn dict + `endpoint_planner_done`; the FlowExecutor adapter never did.
- **Fix (robust, 3 aligned layers — full thinking, not the truncated trace):**
  1. **Engine (`orchestration_engine.py`).** `_default_runner`'s `_stream_sink` now accumulates every `kind=='thinking'` chunk into a per-node `_thinking_parts` buffer (the FULL streamed reasoning — deliberately NOT `SubAgentResult.reasoning_trace`, which is capped at 2000 chars/round). The runner returns `'thinking': ''.join(_thinking_parts)`; `_run_node_step` extracts it and includes it on BOTH the `step_complete` event AND the durable `step_trace` entry (new `thinking`/`thinking_truncated` fields, bounded by `_TRACE_OUTPUT_CHARS=16000`), so Task Mode / `/flow-trace` get it too.
  2. **Adapter (`orchestration_endpoint_adapter.py`).** `_on_step_complete` reads `ev['thinking']` and attaches it to the planner, worker, AND critic message dicts, plus adds `thinking` to the `endpoint_planner_done` and `endpoint_critic_msg` SSE events — byte-mirroring what the live endpoint path already does.
  3. **Frontend (`static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`).** The `endpoint_critic_msg` handler set `_epCriticMsg.content = ev.content` but never assigned thinking → critic bubble lost it on finalize + reload even if the backend sent it. Now applies `ev.thinking` (with fallback to the value accumulated from live deltas, so the live endpoint path that omits it is unaffected). Planner already applied `ev.thinking`; worker thinking now survives because the adapter persists it in the DB-sync turn dict.
- **Tests (revert-proofed, both directions):**
  - `tests/test_orchestration_endpoint_adapter.py::ThinkingPropagationTest` (3 new): (a) finalized planner/worker/critic message dicts carry `thinking`; (b) `endpoint_planner_done`/`endpoint_critic_msg` SSE events carry `thinking`; (c) END-TO-END via the engine's REAL `_default_runner` (patching `lib.swarm.agent._default_dispatch_stream`/`_default_build_body`, no LLM) streaming a 6000-char thinking blob → asserts `step_complete` + `step_trace` carry the FULL text (>2000, proving it's the live accumulator not the capped `reasoning_trace`).
  - `tests/test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` scenario 7 extended: `endpoint_critic_msg{thinking}` → the persisted critic message in `conv.messages` keeps `thinking` (PASS threshold bumped 52→53).
  - **Neuter-proof demonstrated:** adapter `thinking=ev.get('thinking') or ''` → `''` fails the 2 adapter message/SSE tests; engine `''.join(_thinking_parts)` → `''` fails the engine end-to-end test; frontend `_epCriticMsg.thinking` assignment removed → fails `critic_msg_keeps_thinking`. All restored cleanly (grep -c NEUTERED = 0).
- **Verification (actual output).** Orchestration sweep `test_orchestrations.py + phase_and_output + endpoint_adapter + endpoint_runner + engine + emits_subflow + io + role_params + nested_canvas + chat_flow_dispatch` = **210 passed**. Combined final `orchestrations + phase_and_output + endpoint_adapter + endpoint_runner + engine + chat_flow_dispatch + frontend_sse_dispatch` = **127 passed**. `node --check sse_pipeline.js` clean; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-2b9c3dfd.js` — `sse_pipeline.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no allowlist change). Pre-existing `resolve_scope` F401 in `orchestration_engine.py` is on an import line I never touched (accumulated dev-tree drift, not this change).
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a path is meant to render "like a normal agent," a field that streams LIVE can still be silently dropped at the FINALIZE boundary — verify the persisted message dict + the finalizing SSE events carry it, not just that it appears mid-stream. And source streamed reasoning from the live chunk accumulator, never from `reasoning_trace` (2000-char cap).


### 2026-06-28 — Fixed the 4000-hit `event_id collision … cold replay will be missing this event` log storm: timer-poll tool proxy now sets `_suppressEvents=True` (measured-first; the ReferenceErrors were a red herring)
- **Measure-first triage.** Surveyed `logs/error.log` (1.9 MB) before touching code. Two candidate signatures stood out: (a) live client `ReferenceError: renderMemoryPrefetchHtml is not defined` / `_retriggerHgTranslations is not defined` at 03:35 today, and (b) `[EventLog] event_id collision …` repeated **4000×**. Ruled (a) OUT as a non-bug by verification, not assumption: both symbols ARE top-level `function` declarations and both source files ARE in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; the live on-disk bundle (`bundle-5929451b.js`) contains both (`grep -c` = 1 each). The errors came from a STALE cached bundle (`bundle-a0e8171f.js`) a client held across the 2026-06-27 streaming_ui decomposition deploy — self-healing on hard-refresh, no code change warranted. Lesson reaffirmed: a `ReferenceError` for a hoisted symbol in a plain-concatenation bundle is almost always a stale-cache artifact, not a real scope bug — confirm against the CURRENT bundle before chasing it.
- **Root cause of (b) — the real bug.** Every collision was on a `tmr_*` task, always the same shape: `event_id=0 type=tool_progress` + `event_id=1 type=tool_result`, re-minted from 0 on EVERY poll. `lib/scheduler/timer.py::_execute_poll_tool` builds a throwaway `task_proxy` keyed on the *timer id* with a fresh `events: []` but WITHOUT `_suppressEvents`. The proxy is never registered in the chat `TaskRuntime`, so when a poll's tool (`run_command`, etc.) runs through `_execute_tool_one → _finalize_tool_round → manager.append_event`, that function takes its LEGACY fallback (`seq = len(task['events'])` = 0,1,… because the list is fresh each poll) and then persists rows keyed `(timer_id, 0)`/`(timer_id, 1)` into `task_events`. The next poll re-mints the same seqs → composite-PK collision → `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` drops the row and trips the data-loss canary. The writes were pointless: there is no SSE consumer for a poll (the UI renders the per-poll timeline from `tool_trace`), and the proxy's `events` are discarded.
- **Fix (1 line + comment).** Added `'_suppressEvents': True` to the poll proxy — the exact precedent already used by the swarm sub-agent proxy (`lib/swarm/agent.py:962`) for the same "shared/unregistered id, no SSE consumer, events would leak/collide" reason. `manager.append_event` short-circuits on `_suppressEvents` before minting a seq or persisting, so a poll now writes ZERO `task_events` rows. Audited all 3 real callers of `_execute_tool_one`: main agent (real registered task — fine), swarm (already suppressed), timer (now fixed). No other unsuppressed-proxy sites.
- **Test (revert-proofed).** New `tests/test_timer_poll_event_suppression.py` (2 tests): drives the REAL `_execute_poll_tool` with a stubbed `_execute_tool_one` that emits a genuine event via the production `append_event` path. Asserts (1) the proxy carries `_suppressEvents=True`; (2) two consecutive polls persist ZERO rows under the timer id (`read_events(timer_id) == []`). Reverting the one-line fix makes BOTH fail and reproduces the production warning **verbatim** (`event_id collision on task=tmr_7205 event_id=0 type=tool_progress …`) — proving the test guards the exact bug. All 14 timer tests green; ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** any code path that runs `_execute_tool_one` on a task dict whose `id` is NOT registered in the chat `TaskRuntime` MUST set `_suppressEvents=True` — otherwise tool events flow through `append_event`'s legacy len()-based seq fallback and collide in `task_events` on repeat (timers) or leak onto a shared parent stream (swarm). The collision canary in `event_log.py` is doing its job; a non-zero rate is a real "someone built an unsuppressed throwaway proxy" smell.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up) — Closed the prune blind spot the collision exposed: `_opportunistic_prune` now has a second pass that reaps ORPHANED `task_events` rows (no `task_results`) by their own `ts_ms`, not just terminal-task rows
- **The blind spot (user-flagged).** The collision's *first* (successful) write of each colliding pair left orphaned `(tmr_*, 0/1)` rows keyed on timer ids that NEVER get a `task_results` entry. The existing `_opportunistic_prune` deleted only rows whose `task_id` JOINs a terminal `task_results` row — so orphans were structurally invisible to it and would litter forever. Confirmed live: 159 distinct `tmr_*` task_ids in `task_events`, ALL 159 orphaned (0 with a `task_results` row).
- **Wider finding (measured, not assumed).** Orphans are NOT just timers. A live audit found **16 orphan tasks total**: 5 large ones (`675d9f09`/`26b46dfb`/… 1454/1072/600/535/511 events, all `done=1`, ~5.8h old) = the **autopilot follow-up chat chains** from the prior entry — terminal chat tasks that emit a full event stream but never write a `task_results` row. So "unregistered-id event writer" is a recurring shape, not a one-off; the prune needed a general fix, not a `tmr_`-specific one. (For contrast: 17 of 33 task_ids in `task_events` DO have a `task_results` row — normal chat tasks are fine.)
- **Fix.** Added Pass 2 to `_opportunistic_prune` (`lib/tasks_pkg/event_log.py`): `DELETE FROM task_events WHERE ts_ms < cutoff AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM task_results tr WHERE tr.task_id = task_events.task_id)`. Keyed on the row's OWN `ts_ms` (the `idx_task_events_ts` index already exists) since there's no `task_results.completed_at` to lean on. The `ts_ms < cutoff` age guard (same 6h `EVENT_TTL_MS`) is the safety mechanism — it can NEVER reap an in-flight unregistered task, because any poll's lifetime and the SSE-reconnect window are far under 6h. Future-proofs the reaper against any new orphaned-id writer. Pass 1 (terminal JOIN) is unchanged.
- **Test (revert-proofed).** `tests/test_event_log_orphan_prune.py` (3 tests): aged orphan reaped; fresh orphan SPARED (in-flight guard); terminal-task Pass 1 still reaps. Neutering Pass 2 (`AND 1=0`) fails ONLY `test_aged_orphan_is_reaped` while the other two stay green — proving Pass 2, the safety guard, and Pass 1 are independent.
- **Live verification (real data, safe).** Ran the fixed `_opportunistic_prune` against the live DB: it reaped 0 of the current 4194 orphan rows because ALL are <6h (the 5 big chains sit at ~5.8h, just under cutoff) — the guard correctly spared still-SSE-resumable events. To prove the production query reaps real orphan data without harming live state, inserted a synthetic 7h-old chat-id orphan and re-ran: it was deleted (`2→0`) while the legitimate <6h autopilot chains were untouched (`2526→2526`). So the GC works; it simply hadn't fired on a row old enough yet — the big chains will be reaped automatically within ~12 min of crossing 6h. Deliberately did NOT force-delete the <6h orphans (they're still replayable on reconnect). 17/17 timer+event-log tests green; ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** a JOIN-based GC (`task_events` ⋈ `task_results`) silently can't see rows whose join key never materialises — any "fire-and-forget" writer that emits events under an id that never reaches the terminal table creates permanent litter. When a table has its own timestamp column, add an age-bounded NOT-EXISTS sweep as a backstop; the age bound doubles as the in-flight safety guard.


### 2026-06-28 (follow-up²) — Proved the autopilot orphans are LEGITIMATE cache litter, not amputated history (user pushed back: "is Pass 2 masking a real persistence bug?")
- **The challenge.** Fair concern: normal chat tasks write `task_results` (17 of 33 task_ids do); if autopilot follow-up worker tasks are SUPPOSED to and don't, Pass 2 would silently delete the only durable record of those turns 6h later — turning a persistence gap into permanent data loss, the opposite of the canary's purpose. Had to prove case (3) "orphans are litter by design" vs case (2) "real bug, fix at source" with code + live-data evidence before declaring done.
- **Two task types (code trace).** `maybe_run_autopilot` (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`) spawns: (a) the **VU sub-task** — `create_task('', vu_messages, ...)` with `_inline_messages=True`/`_vu_subtask=True`/`convId=''`; `_sync_result_to_conversation` returns early on `_inline_messages`, so it NEVER persists by design; and (b) the **follow-up worker** — `_start_followup_task` → `create_task(conv_id, ...)` → `spawn_task` → full `run_task` → `persist_task_result` → unconditional `_upsert_task_row`.
- **Where durable history actually lives.** The 2026-06-10 pre-sync fix (`.tofu/skills/autopilot-presync-parent-before-vu-spawn.md`) commits each parent turn's FINAL content to `conversations.messages` BEFORE spawning the follow-up. The architecture treats `conversations.messages` as the source of truth for DB-backed chat turns — `task_results.tool_rounds` is even stored NULL for them (`_tool_rounds_have_dedicated_home`). So `task_results` AND `task_events` are both per-task CACHES; neither is canonical.
- **Live-data proof — chain `675d9f09→26b46dfb→966ac345` in conv `mqvzj2ktr2gsrr`.** Inspected orphan event payloads: full turns (699–1043 `delta`, `tool_*`, `messages_snapshot`, `round_committed`, `done:stop`), `675d9f09.done.autopilotNextTaskId == 26b46dfb` (the chain). `966ac345` (last link) HAS a `task_results` row (conv `mqvzj2ktr2gsrr`, 26990 chars); the earlier two do NOT. BUT the conv itself has **20 messages (10 assistant + 7 VU), every assistant `finishReason=stop`, ZERO frozen checkpoints** — so all those turns are fully preserved in the canonical store regardless of the missing cache rows.
- **Whole-DB safety scan (the decisive test).** The REAL data-loss symptom is a "frozen VU-parent checkpoint" (assistant msg with no `finishReason` + content that's a strict prefix of a `task_results` row, immediately followed by an `_isVirtualUser` msg — what `debug/backfill_truncated_vu_parents.py` repairs). Scanned ALL 13 VU-bearing conversations: **0 frozen checkpoints, 0 amputated turns.** The 2026-06-10 fix is holding; nothing is being lost.
- **Verdict: case (3).** Orphaned `task_events` (and absent `task_results` cache rows) for finished autopilot turns are redundant SSE-replay cache whose content is already durable in `conversations.messages`. Pass 2's 6h age guard guarantees we never touch a row inside the cold-replay reconnect window, so it's a true backstop, not a cover-up. Deliberately did NOT "fix" the absent follow-up `task_results` rows: it's a harmless cache inconsistency from the freshness-guard `_autopilot_child` skip the 2026-06-10 fix intentionally tuned; reworking it to satisfy a cache row nothing reads post-sync would risk destabilising a working persistence path (the exact `finishReason=None` truncation bug it fixed). `cleanup_old_tasks` only evicts the in-memory runtime dict, never DB `task_results` (only `_delete_conv_blocking` does), confirming no TTL deleter is racing the cache.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** before adding a GC sweep, PROVE the rows it reaps are non-canonical. The test is not "does this id have a `task_results` row" but "is the turn's content durable in the source-of-truth store (`conversations.messages`) independent of the cache". For autopilot, verify via the frozen-checkpoint scan, not the presence of a per-task cache row. A missing secondary-cache row is not data loss when the primary store is intact.


### 2026-06-27 — Stood up the Playwright app-level E2E lane (the integration-bug net jsdom can't be): real Quart/Hypercorn boot + real headless Chromium + hermetic stub LLM, 3 tests green, CI lane + revert-proof
- **Context / correction.** Originally declared Phase 2 "environment-blocked" because headless Chromium failed with `libatk-1.0.so.0: cannot open` and there's no root/apt here. That was WRONG — the project already runs rootless Chromium via a conda-forge env (`$MF/envs/hb`) + runtime `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (the mechanism `lib/fetch/playwright_pool.py` relies on). With `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:…/sysroot/usr/lib64`, all 10 missing libs resolve and `chromium.launch(headless=True, args=['--no-sandbox','--disable-gpu'])` renders + runs JS. **Lesson (again): check for the project's existing escape hatch before concluding "impossible".**
- **Fixed the `browser` fixture (`tests/conftest.py`).** Added `_ensure_chromium_library_path()` (mirrors the tofu-search helper): prepend `$CONDA_PREFIX/lib` + cos7 sysroot + `CHROMIUM_EXTRA_LIB_DIRS` to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, then `launch(headless=True, args=['--no-sandbox','--disable-gpu'])`. No-op on a CI runner that already has the libs; rootless fallback on shared nodes. Skips with the concrete missing-lib reason only when launch genuinely can't happen.
- **New `tests/test_e2e_smoke.py` (3 tests, tier `visual`+`slow`), hermetic.** Boots the REAL app via the existing session `live_server` (in-thread Hypercorn) + drives the `page` fixture. Asserts: (1) `test_bundle_loaded_in_browser` — `renderToolRoundsHTML`/`updateStreamingUI`/`_buildSwarmPanelHTML` are DEFINED in-browser → proves the js_bundler allowlist (§3.2.1) wired the served bundle end-to-end (NO unit test checks the actually-served bundle); (2) `test_send_message_streams_and_renders` — a sent message streams + finalizes a real assistant message; (3) `test_tool_round_renders` — a web_search tool round renders `.ptool-panel` in the live DOM (SSE tool_start/result → tool_rounds.js).
- **The stub-seam saga (THE hard part — two distinct failure modes, both real).**
  - **Seam discovery.** The orchestrator's PRIMARY loop calls `_llm_call_with_fallback` (`lib/tasks_pkg/llm_fallback.py`), which did `from lib.tasks_pkg.manager import stream_llm_response` — its OWN module binding. Patching only `manager`/`orchestrator` MISSED it → a REAL model (`aws.claude-opus-4.8`) streamed. Fix: patch the binding on ALL THREE sites (`manager`, `orchestrator`, `llm_fallback`).
  - **Return shape.** Real `stream_llm_response` returns `msg` as a DICT (`msg['content']`/`['tool_calls']`), not a string — `_llm_call_with_fallback` unpacks it as a dict. Stub now returns `{'role','content','tool_calls'}`.
  - **web_search has TWO call sites.** The handler (`handlers/search.py:84`, bare global `perform_web_search`) AND the streaming pre-executor (`streaming_tool_executor.py` does a LOCAL `from tofu_search import perform_web_search` inside the function). Patching `search_h.perform_web_search` alone missed the pre-exec → a real search hit `api.marginalia.nu` and timed out. The only seam covering BOTH is `tofu_search.perform_web_search` (the source attribute) — patch THAT + the handler global.
  - **`newChat()` is mandatory.** I'd dropped it while diagnosing; that caused `ABORT RECEIVED elapsed=0.1s` — without a fresh conv the send collides with the open conv and the task manager auto-aborts it as superseded (memories `test_e2e-newchat-isolation` + `swebench-abtest-convid-autoabort`). Restored `newChat()` + a settle delay in both chat tests.
- **Loud-guard sentinel (anti-false-green).** A module-level `_SENTINEL = {'stream_calls','search_calls'}` the stubs increment; each chat test asserts the counter advanced. If the patch ever misses and a REAL model/search runs, the test FAILS LOUDLY instead of passing on real output. Patch installed at SESSION scope (autouse) before `live_server` handles a request; restored in teardown.
- **Constraint #3 (CI + Make).** Added an `e2e` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`pip install playwright` + `playwright install --with-deps chromium` on the rooted runner + `pytest tests/test_e2e_smoke.py -m visual -ra`) and a `make test-e2e` target (documented in the header).
- **Constraint #4 (revert-proof, demonstrated).** Removed `ui/tool_rounds.js` from `_BUNDLE_FILES`, rebuilt → `test_bundle_loaded_in_browser` FAILED with `renderToolRoundsHTML missing in browser — bundler allowlist regression`; restored → green. So the net genuinely catches an integration regression unit tests can't.
- **Verification:** `make test-e2e` = **3 passed in ~18s** (real app, real Chromium, stub provably in effect via sentinels, no network); ruff clean on the new test + conftest; `ci.yml` valid YAML. DB forced to SQLite (`TOFU_DB_BACKEND=sqlite`) to avoid the slow ambient-PG `transcript_archive` deletes.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** to make a live-server E2E hermetic you must patch EVERY binding site of the seam (a `from x import y` creates a private binding per module) AND match the real return SHAPE, AND cover tools that have a separate streaming pre-exec path — then prove the stub ran with a sentinel so a patch-miss can't masquerade as a pass. And rootless Chromium on an HPC node is a solved problem here via conda libs + `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; don't declare it impossible.


### 2026-06-28 — Fixed autopilot "VU message sent but agent never replies until manual regen": closed a post-`_autopilot_deciding` race that let the SSE generator synthesize a baton-LESS done; ALSO recovered a `git checkout` self-inflicted data loss via `.tofu/file-history`
- **User report:** in autopilot mode the virtual-user (VU) bubble appears, but the follow-up agent turn never streams — the user must click regen to see it.
- **Method — measured, not guessed.** Confirmed the BACKEND was healthy: `logs/app.log.2026-06-27` shows reliable `[Autopilot] Spawning follow-up task …` chains (e.g. `675d9f09→26b46dfb→966ac345`). So the follow-up task IS spawned; the gap is the frontend never ATTACHING to its SSE stream. The attach baton (`autopilotNextTaskId`/`autopilotVuMessage`) rides on the `done` event → frontend `_attachAutopilotFollowup`→`connectToTask`. VU bubble visible ⇒ `autopilot_vu_done` + `_append_vu_message_to_conv` succeeded ⇒ the hook ran; so the only way the agent stays idle is a **baton-less done reaching the client.**
- **Root cause (a NEW window, sibling of the documented `_autopilot_deciding` gate).** `routes/chat.py`'s SSE generator synthesizes a late/snapshot `done` from `extract_task_meta(task)` at THREE sites whenever `_task_terminal()` (= `status!='running' and not _autopilot_deciding`). `extract_task_meta` does NOT include the autopilot baton. The orchestrator's `_finalize_and_emit_done` set `_autopilot_deciding=True` around `maybe_run_autopilot`, but cleared it in a `finally:` ~70 lines BEFORE `append_event(done_evt)` (a `compute_cost`-per-round block + a logging block sit in between). In that gap `status=='done'` + `_autopilot_deciding==False` + the real baton-carrying done NOT yet buffered → a fresh/looping SSE reader synthesizes a baton-less done and `return`s, closing the stream. Frontend gets done-without-baton → no `_attachAutopilotFollowup` → conv idle until manual regen. The `compute_cost` block widened the window enough to hit in practice. The kick path (`autopilot._run_autopilot_kick`) had the identical clear-before-append ordering.
- **Fix (root-cause + belt-and-braces):**
  1. `orchestrator.py` + `autopilot.py`: keep `_autopilot_deciding=True` until AFTER `append_event(done_evt)`; clear it only on the success path post-append (and immediately in the `except` so a hook failure still finalizes). So `_task_terminal()` never reports terminal before the baton-carrying done is in `task['events']`.
  2. `routes/chat.py`: new local `_apply_autopilot_baton(evt)` stamps the baton from the transport-agnostic `task['_autopilot_followup']` stash onto EVERY synthesized done (all 3 sites). Mirrors what `chat_poll` already does. Defends cold-replay / resume / any residual race regardless of timing.
- **Test:** `tests/test_autopilot_poll_handoff.py::test_sse_synthetic_done_carries_baton` — drives the live SSE generator into the fresh-snapshot synth-done path for a terminal autopilot task with `_autopilot_followup` set but NO buffered done; asserts the synthesized done carries `autopilotNextTaskId`. **Revert-proofed:** neutering `_apply_autopilot_baton` to `return evt` makes it FAIL (synthetic done = `{"type":"done","finishReason":"stop"}`, no baton). Full sweep green: `test_autopilot_poll_handoff` (7) + arm/kick/verify (39) + `test_sse_resume_guard` (6) + `test_chat_flow_dispatch` (12) + `test_api_v1_chat_route` (5) + event/checkpoint suites = all pass.
- **⚠️ SELF-INFLICTED DATA-LOSS + RECOVERY (the scary part).** Mid-task I ran `git checkout -- routes/chat.py` to undo a temporary neuter — but `routes/chat.py` had UNCOMMITTED working-tree changes (the live 1890-line version with `_warm_resume_serviceable` + prefs snapshot fields); HEAD is a stale 1625-line version. The checkout reverted ALL of it, surfacing as `ImportError: cannot import name '_warm_resume_serviceable'` in `test_sse_resume_guard`. No git stash, no dangling blob held it. **Recovered from `.tofu/file-history/backups/`** (the agent file-history snapshot mechanism): it had hash-named, versioned snapshots of `routes/chat.py` (`7c79d77…@vNNN`). `grep -l _warm_resume_serviceable` + a per-version map of {lines, has-`_warm_resume_serviceable`, has-`_apply_autopilot_baton`, mtime} pinpointed **v250** = the correct pre-checkout base WITH 2 of my 3 baton edits already applied (v251 was the checkout disaster: warm=0). `cp`'d v250 back, re-added the 1 missing live-loop baton site, AST-verified, re-ran tests green.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** NEVER `git checkout -- <file>` to undo a temporary edit when the working tree has uncommitted changes you didn't author — it nukes them silently (here HEAD was wildly stale vs the running tree). Undo temporary edits with a matching reverse `apply_diff`, not `git checkout`. When it does happen, `.tofu/file-history/backups/` is the recovery source: snapshots are content-hash dirs with `@vNNN` versions; grep them for a unique symbol, then diff versions by line-count/symbol-presence/mtime to find the exact pre-incident snapshot.


### 2026-06-27 — "Push it forward, no cost ceiling": MEASURED the frontend coverage gap before building, found the SSE suite already deep, and closed the real hole — a render-layer characterization harness for `tool_rounds.js` (the 2283L unguarded monolith)
- **Framing correction (cost is no object ≠ build engines for their own sake).** Re-affirmed the standing verdict: the build/buy boundary is correct; reinventing markdown/HTTP/PDF would LOWER robustness regardless of budget. Unlimited cost changes WHICH work is worth doing (test depth), not the quality bar.
- **Measured the gap against the TREE first (cheap, reversible — the memory's rule).** Enumerated existing jsdom coverage vs the big files' function inventories instead of estimating. Key finding that **changed my own recommendation**: the SSE dispatcher I'd flagged as "the biggest unguarded gap" is in fact DEEPLY covered — `tests/test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` drives 25 scenarios / ~54 assertions through the REAL `dispatchSSEEvent` with every event type + the documented bug-guards (critic-routing, stale-state, ghost-panel, dedup). My "build a broad SSE suite" idea was largely ALREADY BUILT. Lesson reinforced: measure, don't assume — same trap as the SSE-decomposition false start.
- **The genuine gaps (evidence, not estimate):** (1) the SSE test verifies STATE mutation (`round.status`, `_swarmAgents`, `_rejected`), but the RENDER layer that turns that state into DOM — `renderToolRoundsHTML` → `_renderUnifiedGroup` → `_renderToolGroupsHTML` → `_renderToolSlot` → `_renderUnifiedToolLine`(900L!)/`_buildSwarmPanelHTML` in `tool_rounds.js` (2283L, the largest frontend file) — had ZERO direct coverage; (2) no real-browser E2E layer exists (`playwright` is only a fetch-runtime dep + a pool-dispatch unit test, NOT app-level).
- **Phase 1 done — `tests/test_frontend_tool_rounds_render.py` (the missing TWIN of the SSE-state test).** Built on the shared `tests/_jsdom.py::run_harness` + `_jsdom_harness.js::setup` infra (loads `ui/streaming_swarm_panel.js` as an extra_target first — it defines `_buildSwarmPanelHTML` — then `ui/tool_rounds.js`, same window scope, mirroring the bundle order). Drives real `rounds` arrays (the exact shape the SSE dispatcher produces) through the PUBLIC entry `renderToolRoundsHTML(rounds, isStreaming)` and asserts DOM structure: empty→blank; single done web_search→`.ptool-line` in `.ptool-panel`; searching→`.ptool-panel-active`; rejected/hallucinated→`.ptool-rejected`+`.ptool-badge-reject`+suggestion chip; `ask_human` skipped→`.hg-skipped-line`; submitted→`.hg-submitted-line`+spinner; a same-`llmRound` batch→ONE `.ptool-turn` with `.ptool-turn-head` + `data-batch-size=3`; solo turns→no parallel head; **truncation: 130 inactive rounds→`.ptool-truncated` `data-hidden-count=80` + exactly 50 `.ptool-line` shown** (the `slice(-50)` + STATIC_LIMIT=100 contract); swarm round→inline `.sw-panel` with `data-prn-kind="swarm"`; mixed tool+swarm+tool→3 `[data-prn]` slots in chronological order. **31 assertions, all fired (verified by dumping PASS lines — not stub no-ops).**
- **Revert-proofed (the safety-net proof).** Injected 2 contract breaks into `tool_rounds.js` (rename `.ptool-rejected`, change `slice(-50)`→`slice(-40)`) → harness FAILED on `truncated_shows_50` + `rejected_class`; reverted → green. So it genuinely guards the render contract, which is the prerequisite no-regression net for the eventual `tool_rounds.js` decomposition (next monolith).
- **Verification:** full `tests/test_frontend_*.py` sweep = **22 passed** (was 21; +1 new), `-ra` shows no hidden skips. No bundler/index.html change needed (test-only addition; no new shipped JS file).
- **Next (flagged, not yet started — needs user steer):** Phase 2 = a Playwright app-level E2E smoke layer (boot the app, send a message, assert streaming render + tool rounds + swarm panel). Genuinely greenfield and the only thing that catches the INTEGRATION-class bugs in this journal ("click does nothing", "panel done but tool spinning", welcome-page sidebar) that unit harnesses structurally cannot. Phase 3 = decompose `tool_rounds.js` 2283L now that it has a render safety net, via the `js-monolith-harness-first-extraction` recipe.


### 2026-06-27 — Frontend testing MECHANISM hardening: closed the CI skip-gap, built a shared jsdom harness, fixed 2 latent bugs (artifacts filter empty-state + tsc ratchet drift)
- **Context:** follow-up to the conv-list collapse fix — user asked to (a) look for other issues and (b) establish a frontend testing mechanism.
- **Found & fixed — CI gap (the big one):** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test` job runs `pytest -ra` with NO Node, so EVERY `tests/test_frontend_*.py` silently `pytest.skip`'d in CI (they gate on `_node_deps_available()` / `_tsc_available()`). The jsdom harnesses + the `tsc --checkJs` BASELINE=0 ratchet were running ONLY on local machines that happened to have `npm install`'d. Added a dedicated **`frontend` CI job** (actions/setup-node@v4 node 20 + `npm ci || npm install` + `pip install -e .[test]` + `pytest tests/test_frontend_*.py -ra`). Added `make test-frontend` + documented it in the Makefile header. The `-ra` makes residual skips visible so a missing dep can't hide a whole suite again.
- **Found & fixed — latent bug #1 (artifacts filter, HIGH, real):** `_filterLibrary` (`static/js/artifacts.js`) computed a `visible` counter but never used it — a zero-match filter query set every `.artifact-lib-row` to `display:none` with NO empty-state, so the library looked blank/broken. Exact sibling of the conv-list bug (a control left with zero visible items + no fallback). Fix: append/toggle a `.artifact-lib-noresult` line when `visible===0 && rows>0`; added `.artifact-lib-noresult` CSS. Exposed `_filterLibrary` on the existing `window.Artifacts` `// Exposed for tests / debug` block (a testability seam, not a behavior change).
- **Found & fixed — latent bug #2 (tsc ratchet drift, surfaced ONLY because I ran the suite):** with Node present the `tsc` ratchet flagged **6 errors > BASELINE=0** — pre-existing expando-prop reads (`_wired` in `main_toolbar_ui.js`; `_qaCls`/`_qaSig` in `paper-reader.js`) that had drifted in undetected precisely BECAUSE the frontend tests never ran in CI. Fixed at source per the documented path: declared the three expandos on the `Element` interface in `static/js/globals.d.ts`. tsc back to **0**.
- **Mechanism — shared jsdom harness (kills ~60 lines of boilerplate per test):** a 3-agent audit quantified ~450 LOC of copy-pasted JSDOM-bootstrap + global-stub + node-subprocess plumbing across 7 harness files. Built `tests/_jsdom_harness.js` (`setup({root, html, targets, globals})` → `{window, document, check, report}`; neuters tickers, stubs the common globals, **indirect-eval**s targets into GLOBAL scope so top-level `function`s are callable by name) + `tests/_jsdom.py` (`run_harness(target_js, body_js, *, extra_targets, min_pass, label)` — dep-guard skip + node run + PASS/FAIL parse). **Gotcha solved:** direct `eval` inside `setup()` makes target functions LOCALS of `setup` (invisible to the body → `ReferenceError: renderConversationList is not defined`); indirect eval `(0, eval)` runs at global scope so `function foo(){}` becomes a `globalThis` property. Ported `test_frontend_conv_list_collapse.py` to the shared helpers (proved it still catches the regression: revert fix → FAIL) and wrote `test_frontend_artifacts_filter.py` with it (also revert-proofed). New harness now ~50 lines, was ~150.
- **Audit also CLEARED (not bugs):** `myday.js _collapsedCats` (stores only user-toggled state, renders expanded by default); the `renderChat`/`renderConversationList` `typeof` guards (functions exist, tsc-verified); `relay-admin` tab-visibility (fails closed correctly). Flagged-but-deferred: folder-tab CSS `max-height:94px` vs JS `collapsedMax=94` magic-number coupling (`main_folders_mobile.js`) — could strand tabs if they drift; not fixed (no current repro).
- **Verification:** full frontend suite **21 passed** (13 files; +2 new), tsc **0**, bundle rebuilt, both new tests revert-proofed, ruff + `node --check` clean on all new files. Skill doc: `.tofu/skills/frontend-jsdom-test-mechanism.md`.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** a test suite that `pytest.skip`s in CI is worse than no suite — it looks green while testing nothing. Always check the CI job actually INSTALLS the deps the tests gate on. And when you finally run a long-skipped ratchet, expect accumulated drift (here: 6 tsc errors) — fix it at source, don't bump the baseline.


### 2026-06-27 — Fixed "clicking a sidebar conversation on the welcome page does nothing": the new date-group feature collapsed the SOLE populated group, rendering ZERO clickable rows
- **User report:** on the welcome/new-chat page, clicking a conversation row in the left sidebar was unresponsive.
- **Method — measured, not guessed:** spawned 3 parallel `coder` agents instead of theorising. Agent A ruled out a JS throw / bundle load-order break (fresh bundle passes `node --check`, every moved symbol defined exactly once, `loadConversation`'s welcome-path calls all resolve). Agent B ruled out DOM interception (welcome screen adds no overlay/`pointer-events`; `#convList` is never replaced so the boot-time delegated listener survives; the mobile `.conv-item` listener `return`s early on desktop). Both pushed the cause "elsewhere". A 3rd agent built a **jsdom end-to-end harness** that actually dispatched a click and was the decisive test.
- **Root cause (proven by the harness):** the sidebar's new collapsible date-group feature (`_buildConvPlan` / `_collapsedConvGroups` in `static/js/ui/conversation_list.js`) starts the ">30 days" (`older`) bucket COLLAPSED (`new Set(['older'])`). `_buildConvPlan` does `if (curCollapsed) continue;` — it emits NO `.conv-item` rows for a collapsed group. For a user whose conversations are ALL older than 30 days AND with no active conv (welcome page → `activeConvId===null`, so the `activeKey` force-expand escape hatch never fires), the entire sidebar collapses behind a single `older` header: **0 clickable rows**. The click handler's `e.target.closest('.conv-item')` matches nothing, so the click "does nothing" — there is literally nothing to click. Harness Run B (convs aged to 40d) emitted `CLICKABLE_ROWS=0`, only a collapsed `older` header; the wiring itself was healthy (Run A with recent convs reached `loadConversation` + `renderChat` cleanly, no throw).
- **Fix (minimal, targeted):** in `_buildConvPlan`, compute `_soleGroupKey` (the only populated group when `Object.keys(counts).length === 1`) and add `&& key !== _soleGroupKey` to the per-group `curCollapsed` decision. A group that holds ALL the rows is force-expanded regardless of its remembered collapsed state, so there is always something to click. Updated the `_buildConvPlan` docstring + the `_collapsedConvGroups` comment to state the new exception.
- **Verification (jsdom, both directions):** new `tests/test_frontend_conv_list_collapse.py` loads the REAL shipped `conversation_list.js` under jsdom: (1) all-old + no active conv → 3 rows rendered, `older` force-expanded; (2) mixed recent+old → `older` STAYS collapsed (default preserved), only the recent row clickable. **Confirmed it catches the regression:** reverting the `&& key !== _soleGroupKey` clause makes scenario 1 FAIL (`allold_rows_rendered`, `allold_older_force_expanded`); with the fix all 4 checks pass. Bundle rebuilt (`conversation_list.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). `test_frontend_conv_list_collapse` + `test_frontend_swarm_recovery` + `test_frontend_streaming_ui` = 3 passed; `node --check` clean. Users hard-refresh for the new bundle.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** a collapsible-group UI must never let the DEFAULT-collapsed state hide EVERY row — when a group is the only populated one, force it open. And "click does nothing" with healthy wiring usually means the clickable element was never rendered; reproduce with a jsdom harness that dispatches a real click rather than reading the handler in isolation (reading mislead two agents here — both said "wiring is fine, look elsewhere", and the harness found the missing rows).


### 2026-06-27 (follow-up) — Issue #2 WAS a real bug after all: made tool-row completion DATA-DRIVEN instead of sniffing leftover spinner CSS classes (a reviewer correctly rejected my earlier "not a bug" dismissal)
- **Correction to the previous entry.** I'd concluded the frontend tool-row completion was "already correct, purely status-driven" after spot-checking only the generic line + run_command renderers. A reviewer pushed back: the spinner-clearing decision in `_syncToolRoundsDOM` (`static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`) was actually a fragile DOM-class SNIFF, and I never proved the marker-class chain was exhaustive. They were right.
- **The real mechanism (verified by enumeration).** The "settle this slot to done" branch fired ONLY when the existing slot DOM still contained one of four spinner classes: `.ptool-active` / `.ptool-cmd-running` / `.ptool-pending` / `.code-exec-running`. I mapped EVERY active-state branch in `_renderUnifiedToolLine` against that set: generic line (`.ptool-active`), web_search orbit (`.ptool-active`), run_command/code_exec (`.ptool-cmd-running`), `_renderCodeExecBlock` (`.code-exec-running`), timer initial-wait (`.ptool-active`), stdin (`.ptool-cmd-stdin` → own branch), hg-card (`.hg-card` → own branch), hg-submitted (`.hg-submitted-line` → own branch). Today's renderers happen to be covered — BUT the coverage is incidental, not contractual: any active renderer (existing or future) whose markup doesn't emit one of those four exact classes would keep its spinner until an UNRELATED later event forced a full slot rebuild. That is precisely the user's complaint — "a tool only marks complete when the next tool arrives". The `await_agents` row LOOKED like this bug because await *blocks* up to 120s before its tool_result is even emitted (the separate backend fix in the prior entry), but the render fragility is a genuine independent latent bug.
- **Root-cause fix (data-driven, not class-sniffing).** Each slot now stamps `data-rendered-status` with the status it was last rendered at. The settle-branch keys off a status MISMATCH (`slot.getAttribute('data-rendered-status') !== round.status`) instead of sniffing CSS classes — so a `searching → done` flip (or `→ rejected`, or `→ awaiting_*`) re-renders the slot the instant the round's OWN status changes, for EVERY renderer regardless of its markup. The mismatch branch fires exactly once per transition (stamp updated after), so while a round STAYS interactive (`awaiting_human`/`awaiting_stdin`) the dedicated live-DOM-preserving branches below still own it (stamp == status → mismatch false → fall through), keeping the input-field/button-protection behaviour intact. The fingerprint gate already moves on any status change, so the sync runs.
- **Test (proves the fix is real, not theatre).** New `tests/test_frontend_tool_completion.py` — jsdom harness loading the REAL `_syncToolRoundsDOM` with a stub `_renderUnifiedToolLine` whose ACTIVE markup carries NONE of the four legacy marker classes (the worst case). Drives `tool_start(searching) → tool_result(done)` for ONE round with NO other event, asserts the slot shows done markup with no spinner + correct `data-rendered-status` stamp; plus fingerprint-moves-on-flip and idempotent-no-thrash scenarios. **Verified it catches the regression:** temporarily reverting the branch to the old class-sniff makes `done_no_spinner` / `done_markup_shown` / `done_stamp` / `s2_done_no_spinner` FAIL; with the fix all pass. Full frontend jsdom sweep green: `test_frontend_tool_completion` + `test_frontend_streaming_ui` + `test_frontend_sse_dispatch` + `test_frontend_swarm_recovery` + `test_frontend_approval_card_render` = 5 passed. `node --check` clean; `streaming_ui.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` (no allowlist change). Users hard-refresh for the new bundle.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** never conclude "render is already correct" from spot-checking two code paths — enumerate the whole branch set against the trigger condition. And a re-render decision must key off DATA STATE (the round's own status), never off sniffing leftover DOM/CSS from a prior render; the latter silently breaks whenever a new renderer doesn't emit the magic class.
