### 2026-06-27 — Decomposed the 1862-line `ui/streaming_ui.js` monolith into 3 cohesive files (swarm-panel + stream-lifecycle extracted), harness-first, byte-for-byte — the chosen "consolidate, don't build new engines" win
- **Why this, and why NOT a new engine.** Started from a broad ask: "the
  project is huge — should we build advanced engines in-house (frontend
  streaming render, backend, …) for performance/robustness/readability/
  modularity?" After surveying the codebase (3 parallel coder agents +
  first-hand reads) the honest verdict was: **the build/buy boundary is
  already correctly drawn.** The painful-to-get-right pieces are already
  in-house (LLM multi-protocol SSE core `lib/llm/_sse_core.py` ~781L; 3-layer
  context compaction ~5700L; agent loop + push hub; search/fetch already
  EXTRACTED to the standalone `tofu-search` package). The commodity pieces are
  correctly libraries (markdown = `marked`+`DOMPurify`+`katex`+`hljs` wrapped;
  PDF = pymupdf/docling; browser = playwright). Building an in-house
  incremental markdown parser would *reduce* robustness (CommonMark isn't
  regular; a late token can reparse the whole doc) — the existing tail-freeze
  approach above `marked` is the right call. **So the high-leverage work is
  CONSOLIDATION of what's already built, not new engines.**
- **A false start, corrected by the user (logged as a lesson):** my first
  proposed refactor was "decompose the SSE God-router + de-dupe 21 handler
  headers" — but that 4-phase decomposition was **already complete** (memory
  `sse-dispatch-ctx-extraction-harness`: `sse_pipeline.js` 2918→1466, 21
  property-only handlers in 5 files, the `_hctx()` snapshot IS the intended
  end-state, not duplication). I'd let a sub-agent's survey (which also

  truth. **Lesson: re-verify sub-agent summaries against the tree before

- **Target chosen:** `ui/streaming_ui.js` (1862L) over `tool_rounds.js` (2283L)
  and over dep-trimming (`markdown`/`orjson`/`sqlalchemy` — real but

- **The split (pure move, byte-for-byte, NO logic change):**

### 2026-06-27 — Fixed the "swarm panel shows ALL agents done while the await tool keeps spinning to the 120s hard cap" desync at its backend root: `await_agents` now breaks the moment the swarm driver terminates instead of blocking on stranded agents
- **User report:** the frontend swarm panel renders every agent complete, but the model's `await_agents` tool call keeps spinning until it times out — a visible frontend/backend contradiction. Plus a general principle: a frontend tool call should be marked complete the instant its `tool_result` is attached/sent, NOT only when the next tool arrives.
- **Method — measured, not guessed (spawned 2 parallel `coder` agents):** one audited the JS render layer (`tool_rounds.js`/`streaming_ui.js`), one audited the backend await/scheduler (`master.py`/`integration.py`/`scheduler.py`).
- **Issue #2 (premature/late completion) — NOT a bug.** The render layer is *purely* `status`-driven: the spinner is gated only by `round.status === "searching"` (the `isSearching` arg to `_renderUnifiedToolLine`, derived per-round at `streaming_ui.js:457` and `tool_rounds.js:1981`), with **no** "is-last-round"/"active-tail" heuristic. `_handleToolResult` (`sse_handlers_tool.js`) sets `r.status='done'` the instant the `tool_result` SSE lands; the `_syncToolRoundsDOM` fingerprint includes status so a `searching→done` flip re-renders immediately. Backend confirms the emission is synchronous: `simple_call` (`handlers/_adapter.py`) runs the tool executor then *immediately* calls `_finalize_tool_round → append_event(tool_result)`. So for normal tools the UI is already correct and does not wait for the next tool. Parallel tools each emit their own `tool_result` from their pool worker as they finish (not batched). Left untouched.
- **Issue #1 (panel done but await spins) — REAL backend root cause.** In `MasterOrchestrator.await_agents` (`lib/swarm/master.py`) the `mode='all'` wait loop broke only on `to_wait.issubset(_results_by_id)` or the wall-clock deadline. But once the driver thread exits it sets `self._terminated = True` (`master.py:461`) and fires the terminal `swarm_phase:complete` event, whose frontend handler (`sse_handlers_swarm.js`, contract locked by `test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` scenario 25) **sweeps every agent card to `done`** — *including stranded agents that never produced a result* (e.g. specs removed by `scheduler.cancel_pending()` on abort, or otherwise dropped). Such an agent stays in await's frozen `to_wait` but can NEVER newly enter `_results_by_id`, so the loop kept re-parking on `_completion_event.wait()` until the `AWAIT_AGENTS_HARD_CAP_SEC=120` clamp — exactly the "panel done, tool spinning to timeout" the user saw.
- **Fix (root-cause, minimal):** the wait loop now also breaks when `self._terminated` is True (a new `swarm_terminated` flag distinguishes this from a real wall-clock `timed_out`). On that break the still-unsatisfied ids are reported as `still_running` with `timed_out=False` and a clear, actionable note ("the swarm has finished — N agents completed, M never produced a result … will NOT complete … re-spawn if needed"), plus an INFO `[Master:…] await_agents BREAK-ON-TERMINATED` log line (§2). Result: the await tool returns *promptly* the instant the swarm is done, so its row stops spinning in lockstep with the panel's complete-sweep. The happy path (all requested agents actually completed before the driver exited) is unchanged — `to_wait` empties first and the existing early-return/issubset break fires before the `_terminated` check ever matters.
- **Tests:** +2 white-box tests in `tests/test_swarm_async.py::TestAwaitAgents`: `test_await_breaks_when_swarm_terminated_with_stranded_agent` (driver terminated + one recorded + one stranded `_running` id → await returns <2s, `timed_out=False`, stranded id in `still_running`, note names it) and `test_await_terminated_but_all_done_is_clean` (terminated with everything done → no spurious timeout/strand). Full `test_swarm_async.py` (50) + `test_swarm_tool_scoping.py` (14) = 64 passed; `test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` + `test_frontend_swarm_recovery.py` green (frontend contract untouched). AST clean.
- **Flagged, deliberately NOT changed:** `await_agents` is NOT in `tool_dispatch._SERIAL_BLOCKING_TOOLS` (unlike `ask_human`/`timer_create`/`await_task`), so it runs in the parallel pool. It's not broken today only because `TOOL_PARALLEL_TIMEOUT` defaults to 300s > the 120s await cap; if either constant changes the pool could time out a still-running await (a fresh desync). Hardening = add `await_agents` to the serial set, but that's beyond the reported bug and carries its own risk, so left as a noted latent fragility.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when "panel done but tool still spinning", check whether the panel's terminal sweep (which marks stranded/never-ran cards done by design) can outrun a backend blocking-wait that has no termination escape. A blocking `await`/wait loop must break on the owning subsystem's `_terminated`/done flag, not only on its success condition + wall clock — otherwise a never-arriving result pins it to the hard cap.


### 2026-06-27 — Reserve-janitor follow-up: the sweep query threw on the PostgreSQL primary (aliased HAVING), caught by running it on live PG; rewritten as a subquery + added a partial index
- **Context:** the prior entry's reserve-janitor (`lib/billing/wallet_janitor.py`) passed its SQLite tests, but the user (correctly) insisted on verifying against the PostgreSQL primary before closing — the tests never exercised PG dialect.
- **The bug (real, would have silently no-op'd in production):** `find_stale_reserves` filtered the grouped aggregates with `HAVING held_micro > 0 AND ...` referencing the SELECT alias `held_micro`. SQLite tolerates a SELECT alias in HAVING; **PostgreSQL does NOT** — running the exact query on the live PG instance threw `UndefinedColumn: column "held_micro" does not exist`. Because `sweep_stale_reserves` wraps the query in a try/except that logs `ok=False` and returns, the janitor would have reclaimed NOTHING in production (PG is the primary) while looking healthy — the SQLite green was a false positive.
- **Fix:** rewrote the query to compute the aggregates in an inner subquery and filter the alias in an OUTER `WHERE ... > 0` over that subquery. Portable across PG + SQLite, and avoids repeating the long `-COALESCE(SUM(CASE ...))` expression. Re-ran the literal query on live PG → `ok=True`, and `EXPLAIN` is clean.
- **Index (user concern #2 — full scan every 5 min on an append-only table):** `EXPLAIN` showed a `Seq Scan` at the test's 63 rows (correct at that size). For production scale added a **partial index** `idx_ledger_reserve_sweep ON billing_ledger(user_id, ref_id) WHERE ref_type = 'reserve'` to BOTH `_schema_pg.py` and `_schema_sqlite.py`, and bumped SQLite `_SCHEMA_VERSION` 29→30 so existing installs create it. Honest finding while verifying: with `enable_seqscan=off` the planner actually picks the PRE-EXISTING `idx_ledger_ref (ref_type, ref_id)` — that index already index-serves the `ref_type='reserve'` filter, so the catastrophic "scan 10M rows" case was already mitigated; the new partial index is a narrower/ordered refinement (lets PG group reserve-only rows), not the thing that prevents the full scan. Kept it (harmless, strictly narrower) without overstating it.
- **Verification (both backends, pasted to user):** live PG raw-query `ok=True`; `test_billing_janitor` 5 passed on **live PG** and on SQLite; `test_billing` (19) + `test_billing_phase2` (17) + janitor (5) = 41 on SQLite; `test_core_schema_parity` + `test_sql_translate` = 81 passed (index + version bump don't break PG/SQLite DDL parity).
- **Guardrail / lesson:** a billing/ledger SQL change that passes ONLY on SQLite is NOT verified — the production primary is PG, and PG rejects aliased-HAVING (and other SQLite-isms). Run the literal query against live PG (`find_stale_reserves`/`EXPLAIN`) before declaring done. When a query filters a computed aggregate, use a subquery + outer WHERE, never `HAVING <alias>`. And before adding an index, `EXPLAIN` first — an existing index (`idx_ledger_ref`) may already cover the predicate.


### 2026-06-27 — Implemented the wallet reserve-janitor that the docstring only promised (a real money-correctness gap): orphaned `reserve` holds are now reclaimed on a 5-min scheduler timer
- **Context:** a stopgap audit (TODO/FIXME/HACK sweep across lib+routes+JS+JOURNAL) flagged `lib/billing/wallet.py`'s docstring claim of "a janitor sweep (TODO: separate file) cancels orphaned reserves older than stale_reserve_ttl (default 30 min)" — but NO such sweep, function, or scheduler task existed. Confirmed by grep: the only artifact was the docstring TODO.
- **The actual bug:** a billable LLM request does `reserve(-estimate)` up front and releases the hold inside `settle()` (`reserve_release(+estimate)` + `debit(-actual)`). If the process crashes / the request aborts between those two steps, the hold is never released — the credits stay subtracted from the user's *usable* balance forever, with nothing to ever reclaim them. Money silently leaks out of usable balance.
- **Orphan definition (verified against the ledger model in `lib/billing/ledger.py`):** both `settle()` and a standalone `reserve_release()` write a `kind='reserve_release', ref_type='reserve', ref_id=X` row. So a hold is "closed" iff such a row exists for its ref_id. An **orphan** = a `reserve` row whose `(user_id, ref_id)` has summed `reserve` + `reserve_release` amounts still net-negative (held > 0) AND whose most-recent `reserve` row is older than the TTL.
- **Fix (root-cause, reuses existing idempotent semantics):**
  - New `lib/billing/wallet_janitor.py::sweep_stale_reserves(ttl_seconds=None)`. One grouped SQL query (`GROUP BY user_id, ref_id ... HAVING held_micro>0 AND last_reserve_ts<=cutoff`) over `billing_ledger` — uses the existing `idx_ledger_ref`/`idx_ledger_kind` indexes, and groups so multiple reserve rows on one ref sum correctly. For each orphan it calls the existing `wallet.reserve_release(...)`, which is **idempotent on ref_id** → running the sweep twice is a free no-op (the 2nd sweep sees the release row the 1st wrote and excludes it). TTL via `TOFU_BILLING_RESERVE_TTL` env (default 1800s, §3.5). `audit_log('billing_reserve_reclaim', ...)` per reclaim + `log_context`/summary log per §2. Fail-open: a missing `billing_ledger` table (billing never activated) or transient DB error → `ok=False`, nothing reclaimed, no crash.
  - Wired into the scheduler exactly like the `pg_backup` precedent: new `task_type=='reserve_reclaim'` handler in `_execute_task` (ignores `command`, so the LLM can't inject code), new idempotent `_ensure_default_reserve_reclaim_task()` (name-matched 'Billing Reserve Reclaim', `*/5 * * * *`), called from the readiness-gated `_deferred_resume` thread next to pg_backup/optimizer registration.
  - `lib/billing/wallet.py` docstring TODO replaced with a pointer to the implemented janitor; `sweep_stale_reserves` exported from `lib/billing/__init__.py`.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_billing_janitor.py` (5): stale orphan reclaimed; fresh reserve untouched (don't let a live request over-spend); already-settled reserve left alone; double-sweep no double-release (idempotency); explicit `ttl_seconds` arg overrides default. Backdating helper mutates the `reserve` row's `ts` directly (the only ledger mutation in the suite) to simulate elapsed time. Run: `test_billing_janitor` (5) + `test_billing` (19) + `test_billing_phase2` (17) = **41 passed** on SQLite; ast + import checks clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** when a docstring promises a "janitor/sweep/cleanup (TODO)", grep for the function before trusting it — here the promise existed for the whole life of the reservation system with zero implementation. The reclaim reuses `reserve_release`'s ref_id idempotency rather than inventing a new release path, which is what makes both transaction-safety and double-run-safety fall out for free.


### 2026-06-27 — Root-caused "Reading Mode keeps searching HPV in the background" → it doesn't; it's SERP pollution fetched BEFORE relevance filtering. Fixed at the source: a pre-fetch relevance gate in tofu-search (0.3.2)
- **User report:** "which conversation is searching HPV in the background?"
  then, correctly, pushed back twice when I mis-attributed it to a chat
  conversation (substring matches in `search_text` / a research-topic title are
  NOT tool calls — same trap as the swarm-tool-persistence memory).
- **Actual root cause (traced via vendor.log, not guessed):** NO conversation
  searched HPV. The mayoclinic HPV/cervical/throat/endometrial-cancer pages were
  fetched by `ThreadPoolExecutor-1032` as the **page-fetch step of a Paper
  Reading-Mode deep-report** (`rpt_1782538037820_eaf4c892_zh`, paper "Agentic
  Rubrics as Contextual Verifiers for SWE Agents"). The same pool batch also
  fetched `researchgate.net/.../R2E-Gym_...` — the report's own
  `web_search query='R2E-Gym hybrid verifiers SWE agents Jain 2025'`
  (vendor.log:28602 `step4_page_fetch=29.6s`). The Mayo Clinic links were
  **junk SERP results** an engine returned for that academic query.
- **The mechanism (the real bug):** `tofu_search/search/orchestrator.py` runs
  "1+4 merged" — it submits EVERY engine-returned URL to the fetch pool the
  instant an engine responds, and only judges relevance at **step 5** (the
  optional LLM content filter), which runs *after* the expensive fetch. So junk
  pages get fetched (wasting budget, flooding the user's browser extension via
  the bridge, all timing out at 25s) and only then dropped. Worse: this
  deployment has `filter_enabled=False`, so there was NO relevance defense
  before fetch at all.
- **Fix (in tofu-search itself, benefits chat + Reading Mode + every consumer):**
  new `tofu_search/search/prefetch_gate.py` — a cheap, pure-Python, no-LLM,
  **fail-open** lexical gate run inside `_submit_fetches_for_batch()` BEFORE
  submitting to the fetch pool. Reuses the BM25 tokenizer from `rerank.py`
  (no second notion of "query terms"). `partition_fetchable()` declines to
  FETCH a result whose `title+snippet` shares ZERO query terms, BUT:
  (a) no-ops for queries with `< prefetch_gate_min_query_terms` (default 2)
  meaningful terms; (b) always admits the leading `prefetch_gate_min_fetch`
  (default 3) candidates (recall floor — engines already rank by relevance);
  (c) a skipped result is **kept as a snippet-only candidate** (still added to
  `unique_results`), so rerank/format still see it — only the page FETCH is
  skipped. Config knobs on `SearchConfig` (default-on, conservative). `deepen.py`
  already had the analogous `_score_candidate` gate, so this just brings the
  primary fetch path in line.
- **Versioning/integration:** tofu-search `0.3.1 → 0.3.2` (`__init__`,
  pyproject, CHANGELOG). chatui `requirements.txt` floor bumped to `>=0.3.2`.
  The bridge (`lib/search_bridge.sync_search_config`) needs NO change — it only
  overrides the fields it passes, so the on-by-default gate survives the sync
  (verified). chatui imports the sibling `TOFU_SEARCH_PATH` checkout, confirmed
  picking up 0.3.2 with gate live.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_prefetch_gate.py` (12: unit gate decisions +
  orchestrator integration showing off-topic NOT fetched but still returned as
  snippet). Updated `tests/test_orchestrator_race.py` fixture to disable the
  gate (its synthetic data has zero query overlap by design; Race-to-N is
  orthogonal) with proper yield-teardown so the global toggle doesn't leak.
  Full tofu-search suite **178 passed**, ruff clean.
- **Guardrail / lesson:** "X keeps searching for Y in the background" is often
  SERP pollution in a page-fetch step, NOT a deliberate query. Trace the
  browser-pool batch to the OWNING `web_search` query (co-fetched URLs in the
  same `ThreadPoolExecutor-NNNN` reveal it), don't grep titles. And the search
  pipeline's relevance defense must be BEFORE fetch, not only the post-fetch LLM
  filter (which is also disable-able).


### 2026-06-27 — Paper report: made TL;DR + glossary genuinely self-contained (prompt) AND added glossary hover-definitions across the whole report (frontend) for immersion/retention
- **User report (with an Agentic-Rubrics report screenshot):** the report is
  still not reader-friendly. Three concrete gripes: (1) the 一句话总结 doesn't
  say whether the method is TRAINING vs INFERENCE, what a score (54.2%) actually
  means, or what the ceiling is; (2) glossary cells aren't self-contained —
  e.g. "selection rule" is used but never defined, and "a continuous score in
  [0,1]" never says HOW the score is derived; (3) long reads lose focus — wants
  better immersion + genuine knowledge gain.
- **Diagnosis (two layers):** gripes #1/#2 are CONTENT quality → the report
  prompt (`lib/paper/prompts.py`, EN + ZH). Gripe #3 (and reinforcing #2) is the
  RENDER layer (`static/js/paper-reader.js`) — the report already emits a Core
  Terminology table up front, but a reader deep in §Method has forgotten it, so
  the report stops being self-contained exactly where it matters.
- **Prompt changes (both languages, symmetric):**
  - TL;DR now MUST: (a) state the contribution KIND (training / inference /
    data / eval-protocol), (b) make every number interpretable in place
    (metric + benchmark + comparison + direction, never a bare "54.2%"),
    (c) give the ceiling/floor (oracle / random / SOTA) so headroom is visible,
    (d) not use any term it only defines later.
  - Core Terminology now MUST: (a) be SELF-CONTAINED — a definition may not lean
    on an undefined sub-term ("selection rule", "reward model", "proxy metric")
    without either giving it its own row or glossing it inline; (b) for any
    DERIVED/SCORED/PREDICTED quantity, say HOW it's produced (e.g. "[0,1] score
    from the judge's averaged token-probability / a learned regression head /
    normalized vote count"), not merely what it represents.
  - ZH edits landed via `insert_content` (pure-CJK anchors) after apply_diff
    kept 99%-failing on an invisible byte mismatch in the emoji-bearing
    section-header lines.
- **Frontend — glossary hover-definitions (new, additive):**
  - `_extractGlossary(article)` finds the Core Terminology table (first column
    header == "Term"/"术语"), tags it `.paper-glossary`, returns `[{term,def}]`
    (skips the prompt's "(term)"/"…" placeholder rows; defs capped 260c).
  - `_glossaryAliases(term)` expands a cell into matchable aliases: strips
    parentheticals but keeps real abbreviations ("Test-Time Scaling (TTS)" →
    ["Test-Time Scaling","TTS"]), splits slash/、/， variants ("Best@K / Oracle
    Pass@K / Random@K" → 3), drops CJK meta-notes ("（本文首创）","（高/低效用）").
    Length-gated: CJK ≥2, Latin ≥3 (abbreviations ≥2).
  - `_decorateGlossaryTerms` walks the rendered `<article>`, wraps later
    mentions in `<span class="paper-term" tabindex="0" data-def aria-label>`;
    longest-alias-first matching, Latin word-boundary guards, skips headings /
    code / links / katex / the glossary table itself, and decorates each term
    AT MOST ONCE PER h2 SECTION (reset on H1/H2) to avoid noise. Wired into
    `_renderFinalReport` after callouts/figures, before heading indexing (so the
    spans don't perturb the TOC). All render routes (stream-done, in-memory
    cache, server cache, DB fetch) funnel through `_renderFinalReport`, so it
    covers every path.
  - CSS `.paper-term` = dotted underline + accent on hover/focus; `::after`
    popover (`content:attr(data-def)`) reusing the app's tooltip pattern, capped
    320px (240px on ≤640px). No emoji (§3.4). `paper-reader.js` already in
    `_BUNDLE_FILES` → no allowlist change.
- **Verification:** `node --check` clean; `python3 ast.parse` clean; CSS braces
  balanced 5946/5946; alias parser unit-checked against all 9 screenshot terms;
  `tests/test_paper_title_recovery.py` 18/18 pass (the only test that parses
  report section structure — confirms the TL;DR/glossary prose additions didn't
  break Paper-Card title extraction or H1 repair). Bundle rebuilt
  `bundle-e0f0209d.js`. Users hard-refresh to pick it up.
- **Deliberately NOT done:** no in-report quiz / spaced-repetition (heavier,
  needs persistence + its own UX); the hover-glossary is the high-leverage
  immersion win that also directly fixes the self-containment gripe. Flagged for
  a later pass if the user wants active recall.


### 2026-06-27 — Fixed the PERMANENT empty-diff "apply in a new conversation" banner on multi-root conversations: the single→multi-root transition now re-establishes the tool-schema latch instead of reporting a phantom divergence forever
- **User report (screenshot):** a conversation with two workspace roots
  (`chatui` + `tofu-search`) showed the deferred-toolset banner ("工具改动将在
  新会话生效（保持缓存命中）") with NO per-tool diff chips. Asked why the
  cache entry shows no tool changes at all — and (correctly) pushed to find why
  the tool-schema *bytes* drifted, not just describe the banner mechanism.
- **Mechanism (settled first):** `latch_tool_list` flags divergence on a
  full-bytes md5 (`_hash_tool_list` → `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)`), while
  `_tool_latch_diff` only computes a set-difference over tool NAMES, and
  `orchestrator.py:672` drops `toolsetDiff` when both added/removed are empty.
  So a byte change with NO name add/remove → `toolsetDiverged:true` with an
  empty diff → `_renderToolsetDiff` falls back to the generic banner text. The
  frontend was working as designed; the question was why the bytes drifted.
- **Diagnostic added (kept as a permanent safety net):** new
  `_diagnose_byte_drift(snapshot, fresh)` in `lib/tools/registry.py`, called
  from `latch_tool_list` ONLY in the diverged-but-empty-name-diff branch. It
  walks the two same-name lists positionally and logs the FIRST offending
  tool + which field (`position` / `description` / `parameters`) changed, §2.6
  truncated: `[ToolLatch] conv=X diverged with EMPTY name-diff (byte-level
  schema drift) — tool='list_dir' field=parameters frozen=… fresh=…`. This is
  what let us attribute the drift; it stays for any FUTURE genuinely
  non-deterministic schema (e.g. a real MCP server emitting a timestamp).
- **Evidence gathered (not guessed):** app.log showed the empty-diff
  divergence RECURRING — conv `mqvx5bzq` hit `added=[] removed=[]` across 3
  tasks. BUT grep found ZERO `tools=changed` cache breaks for those convs: the
  latch return path is `return copy.deepcopy(snapshot), diverged`, so it always
  served the FROZEN bytes — detected-but-held, cache intact. Also corrected a
  shared misread: **`tofu-search` is NOT an MCP server** (configured MCP
  servers are github/github-batch/hope/overleaf/xuecheng/llm); the pills are
  workspace ROOTS, so this is a MULTI-ROOT conversation.
- **Root cause (a structural latch-timing disagreement, not a flapping
  schema):** proved `with_multiroot_hint` is idempotent (`'rootname:' not in
  desc` guard) AND deterministic (run1==run2 byte-identical). The two freeze
  mechanisms latch at DIFFERENT moments with DIFFERENT content: round 1 started
  SINGLE-root → the tool-schema latch froze the hint-LESS `list_dir` schema;
  later a 2nd root was added → `multiroot_active` goes sticky-ON → fresh
  assembly now carries the `rootname:` hint on every `path` description. Fresh
  (hinted) ≠ frozen (hint-less) by CONTENT, same NAMES → permanent empty-diff
  banner for the life of the conversation. Dismiss couldn't help either —
  `_revertToolsToCacheSafe` has no family for the multiroot hint.
- **Fix (the CORRECT semantics — re-establish, don't suppress):** going
  multi-root is a LEGITIMATE one-time schema change; the model in THIS
  conversation needs the `rootname:` guidance immediately, so suppressing the
  multiroot delta from the divergence signal would be a correctness regression.
  Instead, on the OFF→ON multiroot-sticky transition we re-establish the latch,
  mirroring the `clear_all_tool_list_latches` MCP-mutation precedent:
  - `mark_multiroot_sticky(conv_id)` now RETURNS `True` only on the OFF→ON
    transition (was `None`); idempotent on repeat marks.
  - `ToolContext.multiroot_active`: when `mark_multiroot_sticky` reports the
    transition, call `clear_tool_list_latch(conv_id)` + log. Timing is the key:
    `multiroot_active` is read DURING `assemble_tool_list`, which runs BEFORE
    `latch_tool_list` in the same `_assemble_tool_list` call — so the clear and
    the re-freeze happen in the SAME round, capturing the HINTED list with zero
    phantom-divergence window. Result: round 2 (root added) → `diverged=False`,
    served list carries the hint; rounds 3+ byte-stable. One deliberate cache
    rebuild when the root is actually added (cost already justified by the real
    schema change), then stable. The banner never appears.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_cache_schema_stability.py` +1 class
  (`TestMultirootTransitionReestablishesLatch`, 3 tests): single-root round 1
  → multi-root round 2 asserts `diverged=False` after the flip + hint present +
  empty name-diff; rounds 3+ stay stable; `mark_multiroot_sticky` fires the
  clear exactly once. Suite now 23 (was 20). Full run:
  `test_cache_schema_stability.py` (23) + `test_readonly_roots.py` (12) +
  `test_conv_config.py` (44) = **79 passed**.


### 2026-06-27 — Browser-bridge modal now DETECTS Chrome 142+ and surfaces "Local Network Access" (LNA) prompt guidance, since the extension provably cannot grant the permission itself
- **User report:** during browser-extension-assisted web search (client-side
  browser performs the search to bypass risk control), Chrome 142+ pops the new
  "www.X.com 想要 访问本地网络中的其他设备" permission per-site; with many tabs
  opened the user must click through each one. Asked if the extension can
  configure this away, then — accepting it can't — asked to DETECT it in the
  browser-tool UI and guide the user to the setting.
- **Why the extension can't auto-grant (verified, not assumed):** Chrome's LNA
  (shipped default-on in Chrome 142, Oct 2025) gates any public→private/loopback/
  `.local` request behind a per-origin prompt. The CDP `Browser.PermissionType`
  enum DOES include `localNetworkAccess`/`localNetwork`/`loopbackNetwork` and we
  already drive CDP via `chrome.debugger` for screenshots — BUT `chrome.debugger`
  exposes only a restricted tab-level domain allow-list (Accessibility, DOM,
  Emulation, Fetch, Network, Page, Runtime, …); the **`Browser` domain is NOT in
  it**, so `Browser.setPermission` over a tab session is rejected. And
  `chrome.contentSettings` has no `localNetworkAccess` type. So an in-extension
  silent grant is impossible today — the honest fix is browser-level config
  (`chrome://flags/#local-network-access-check` → Disabled, or the managed
  policy `{"LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls":["*"]}`).
- **What shipped (detect + guide, no false promise):**
  - **Extension (`background.js` v4.4→v4.5, manifest 4.5.0):** parses Chromium
    major from `navigator.userAgent` once at load into `CHROME_MAJOR`, sends it
    as `chromeMajor` on every `/api/browser/poll` body. The version MUST come
    from the extension (the browser actually running the bridge), not the UI
    viewer's UA — they can differ (remote/tunnel/cloud-IDE viewing).
  - **Backend (`lib/browser/queue.py`):** `mark_poll(client_id, chrome_major=0)`
    stores `chrome_major` per client; `get_connected_clients()` surfaces it.
    `routes/browser.py` poll handler parses `int(data.get('chromeMajor') or 0)`
    (debug-logs non-numeric, defaults 0). `routes/api_v1/browser.py` status adds
    top-level `chromeMajor = max(...connected clients)` + api_meta doc.
  - **Frontend:** `_checkBrowserStatus` calls new `_applyBrowserLnaWarning(d.chromeMajor)`
    (`main_toolbar_ui.js`) — shows `#browserLnaWarning` ONLY when a connected
    extension reports Chromium ≥142. Click-to-copy policy JSON + OS-specific
    managed-policy path (Linux `/etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/tofu-lna.json`,
    Win registry hive, mac `defaults write`) derived from the viewer UA. Amber
    `.browser-lna-warning` block in `index.html` + `styles.css`, mirroring the
    green local-shortcut box. 5 new i18n keys (`browser.lna*`). No emoji (§3.4) —
    amber color conveys warning.
- **Conventions:** both edited JS files (`main/main_toolbar_ui.js`, `i18n.js`)
  already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → no allowlist change; bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-3dd9297a.js`). CSS content-hash bundler regenerates on restart.
- **Verification:** `node --check` (3 JS) + manifest JSON + `ast.parse` (3 py)
  all clean; `test_browser_queue_ttl`/`test_browser_async_poll`/
  `test_package_facades`/`test_bridge_auth` = 82 passed (mark_poll signature +
  client-dict shape changes covered). Users must reload the unpacked extension
  to pick up v4.5 (older extensions just omit `chromeMajor` → warning stays
  hidden, graceful).

## How to use this file

- **Read it first.** At the start of a session, read this journal to understand
  how the project reached its current state before making changes.
- **Keep it current — on your own initiative.** After any meaningful change,
  append a dated entry yourself. This is a standing, pre-authorized action: you
  do NOT need to ask the user before adding an entry, and you should not pause
  to request permission to update the journal. Do not rewrite or delete past
  entries — the history is the point; only ever append.
- **Record the *why*, not just the *what*.** A diff shows what changed; this
  journal explains the reasoning a future reader (human or model) could not
  reconstruct from the code alone.


### 2026-06-27 — Per-user preference-profile scoping: closed the multi-user identity-leak gap WITHOUT changing the personal-install (open/private) experience at all
- **Context:** the previous entry stored IDENTITY facts ("About the user") in
  the profile, but `profile_path()` was a SINGLE global file — so a multi-user
  *interactive* deployment would mix one tenant's identity into everyone's
  prompt. The headless API was already fail-closed (`preferencesEnabled` via
  personal_scope); this entry fixes the interactive multi-user path.
- **The key insight (design):** the scope key is just `AuthContext.user_id`,
  which is populated ONLY by multi-user login (`_mint_session_key` in
  routes/api_v1/users.py). Open mode (synthetic local-admin) and private mode
  (a Bearer key with no tenant binding) both leave `user_id` empty. So
  `scope = ctx.user_id or ''` gives: open/private → the EXISTING global file
  (byte-identical, zero migration, zero UX change); multi-user → a per-tenant
  file. Fail-safe by construction — a request with no tenant binding can only
  ever reach the single-owner profile.
- **Storage (`lib/memory/user_profile.py`):** every function took an additive
  `scope: str = ''` param (default → legacy path, so all existing callers and
  tests are byte-identical). `profile_path(scope)`: `''` → unchanged
  `<data>/memories/.tofu_user_profile.md`; non-empty → `<data>/memories/profiles/
  <sanitized>/.tofu_user_profile.md`. New `_sanitize_scope` = charset-restricted
  prefix (≤32, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) + sha256[:16] suffix → readable AND
  traversal-proof (a hostile `../../etc` user_id can't escape `profiles/`). New
  `resolve_profile_scope(ctx)` reads `ctx.user_id` defensively (None/junk → '').
- **The wiring problem & fix:** the post-turn consolidation runs in a DETACHED
  daemon (no request context), so identity must be captured in the request
  thread. `create_task` (lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py) now stamps
  `task['_profileScope'] = resolve_profile_scope(current_auth())` (best-effort;
  no request ctx → ''). Both consumers read it from the task:
  `system_context.py` ★2.5 (`load_profile(scope)`/`render_profile_block(...,scope)`)
  and `profile_consolidate.run_profile_consolidation` (threads scope into all
  three write paths: reinforce/distil/new). REST GET/PUT `/api/v1/profile`
  resolve scope directly from `current_auth()`. The legacy `/profile/pending`
  route stays unscoped (dead now that nothing stages).
- **Why this is the right seam:** ONE scope key (`user_id`) reused from the
  existing auth model — no new identity concept, no new config, no per-surface
  special-casing. Orthogonal to `preferencesEnabled` (which still decides
  WHETHER to inject at all on headless); scoping decides WHICH file. The two
  compose: a headless multi-user caller that opts into preferences gets ITS
  tenant's profile, never the operator's.
- **Tests (+5 in test_user_profile, now 32):** empty-scope == legacy global
  path (no `profiles/` segment); scoped paths isolated + traversal-proof
  (realpath stays under `profiles/`); profiles don't leak across scopes + global
  untouched; `resolve_profile_scope` truth table (open admin/private key → '';
  login key → user_id; None → ''); consolidation writes to `task['_profileScope']`
  not global. Sweep green: test_user_profile (32), personal_scope_headless (14),
  + `-k "profile or personal_scope or cc_alignment or conv_config or
  compat_openai"` = 138 passed/2 skipped. No other callers of the profile fns
  exist (grep-verified) — all access funnels through the 4 updated sites.
- **Remaining nuance (flagged, not a bug):** the per-tenant files live under
  `<data>/memories/profiles/` in the Tofu INSTALL (not a user project), so the
  `.tofu` artifact-registry consumers (gitignore/export) don't apply there; the
  filename keeps the `.tofu` prefix regardless. No frontend change needed — the
  UI already calls `Api.profile.get/saveItems` which carry the session cookie,
  so the browser automatically sees its own tenant's profile.


### 2026-06-27 — Live per-round translation: translated segments now stream into the bubble DURING the task (no more "wait until the end"), via a task-start-minted assistant msgId
- **User pushback (correct):** the prior session fixed the orphaned-accumulator
  reliability bug but PUNTED on the headline ask — "why wait until everything is
  finished before translating it all at once? tool-round content can be
  translated DURING streaming." The deferral excuse ("no committed _msgId on the
  streaming bubble") was a shortcut: the infra to do it right already existed,
  and the user explicitly authorized the root-cause fix (mint the assistant
  _msgId at task start instead of at end-sync).
- **What was already there:** the incremental `_Acc` worker already translates
  each round's segment in the background AS the round closes (overlapping tool
  execution) + caches it; it already has a `_push` on the `translate` channel;
  the frontend already renders `_translatePartial` as live markdown. The ONLY
  missing pieces were (a) push the translated-so-far after each segment instead
  of holding until finalize, and (b) a stable id to route that partial to the
  still-streaming bubble (which has no DB index mid-task).
- **Fix — server (`lib/translate/incremental.py`):** `_Acc` now stores
  `self.msg_id = task['_assistantMsgId']`. New `_assemble_progressive()`
  (coverage-GATELESS — best-effort join of segments closed so far) +
  `_push_progressive()` emit a `running`/`partial` frame (`statusKind:in_progress`,
  routed by `msgId`, `msgIdx:None`) right after EACH segment translates (both the
  normal and already-Chinese branches). No-op when `msg_id` is unknown → graceful
  degradation to the existing end-of-task display.
- **Fix — id plumbing (root cause):** `create_task` (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`)
  now copies `config.assistantMsgId` → `task['_assistantMsgId']` (was only ever
  READ, never set — always empty). The safety net
  (`auto_translate.py`) prefers `task['_assistantMsgId']` for the final commit's
  `msg_id`, so the in-stream preview and the committed translation address the
  SAME message. Frontend send + regenerate paths
  (`main_send_pipeline.js` / `main_regen_continue.js`) now mint the assistant
  `_msgId` via `_newClientMsgId()` BEFORE the POST, ship it in
  `config.assistantMsgId`, reuse it verbatim on the `assistantMsg` object, and
  stamp it on the streaming bubble (`_renderStreamingBubble(conv, cfg, msgId)`
  → `_streamingBubbleHTML(role, …, msgId)` → `data-msg-id`).
- **Fix — frontend live paint (`static/js/translation.js`):** the
  `_wireServerPushTranslate` running-frame handler now calls new
  `_renderStreamingTranslatePreview(convId, msgId, partial)` FIRST: if
  `#streaming-msg`'s `data-msg-id` matches the frame, it paints the
  translated-so-far markdown into a dedicated `[data-zone="translatePreview"]`
  block inside the live bubble (spinner head + md body + caret) — so the Chinese
  fills in round-by-round AS THE TASK RUNS. Falls through to the existing
  settled-message indicator path when the target isn't the live bubble. Partial
  is also stashed on `msg._translatePartial` so a conv-switch full re-render
  keeps it.
- **Tests:** +`test_progressive_partial_pushed_before_finalize` (asserts ≥2
  partial frames, routed by msgId with msgIdx=None, accumulating both segments,
  and NO done frame before finalize) and
  +`test_no_progressive_partial_without_msg_id` (graceful degradation: no
  partials but finalize still commits). NOTE: `_Acc._push` does
  `from lib.push import push_event` at call time, so the capture fixture must
  patch `lib.push.push_event`, not the `inc` alias. Full sweep: incremental(13)
  + safety_net(4) + conv_config(44) + chat_manager_migration(21) +
  translate_migration(10) + package_facades(42) + noop/flip = 134+ green. Bundle
  rebuilt (`bundle-8bf95fd1.js`).
- **Scope/guardrail:** still gated on `autoTranslate` + non-endpoint/autopilot;
  the progressive partial is display-only (committed translation is unchanged,
  still coverage-gated at finalize). Endpoint/autopilot paths untouched. Requires
  server restart (Python) + hard refresh (new bundle hash).

### 2026-06-27 — Auto-translate reliability: fixed orphaned incremental accumulators (the "must click Translate every time" bug) + closed the safety-net/cancel test gaps
- **User report (3 gripes):** (1) after a conversation completes, translation
  *sometimes* fails to auto-start — they must hit Translate manually every
  time; (2) translation is slow; (3) "didn't I say tool-round content can be
  translated DURING streaming? why wait until the very end?"
- **Method — measured before theorising (spawned a log-analyst + a
  test-coverage auditor in parallel).** The runtime logs DISPROVED the naive
  "incremental translation isn't firing" theory: it IS the dominant path
  (`[AutoTranslate] … Incremental translator owns this translation` 29×, real
  `[IncTranslate] ✓ finalized` lines, whole-message fallback only 3×). The
  smoking gun was instead **24+ `[IncTranslate] worker idle-timeout —
  abandoning (finalize never called)` in error.log** plus 25 incomplete
  cache-verdict commits. ~43% of accumulators were created then never
  finalized.
- **Root cause (orphaned accumulators).** The orchestrator creates a per-task
  `_Acc` (background worker translating each round's prose segment) on the
  first `submit_round_segment` during the tool loop. But the ONLY thing that
  commits those segments is `finalize_incremental`, reached at the very END of
  `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` — AFTER four early-returns
  (settings.autoTranslate off, already-translated, already-Chinese,
  frontend-task dedup) AND only when the task ends with `content and not
  error`. On every one of those skip/abort/error paths the worker was
  orphaned: its segments were translated but never committed → no
  `translatedContent` → the user sees untranslated text and must click
  Translate (gripe #1). The zombie worker then idled 300s and logged the scary
  warning. A second source: `manager._sync_result_to_conversation` skips the
  safety net entirely when the task errored / produced no content.
- **Also confirmed: a gate divergence.** `incremental._gate` reads
  `task['config']['autoTranslate']` (defaults **False** in
  `lib/conv_config.py::resolve_conv_config`) while the safety net reads conv
  `settings.autoTranslate` (defaults **True** in `auto_translate.py`). When
  config says ON but settings say OFF, the accumulator is created then the
  safety net early-returns → exactly the orphan above.
- **Fix (make accumulator lifecycle airtight — every path either finalizes or
  cancels):**
  - New `lib/translate/incremental.py::cancel_incremental(task)` + a `'cancel'`
    item the `_Acc` worker drains (drops segments, self-removes from registry,
    logs once). Exported from the package facade.
  - `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` now tracks `_inc_handed_off` (True only
    when `finalize_incremental` adopts the task) and a `finally:` block calls
    `cancel_incremental` on EVERY non-handoff exit. Cheap no-op when no
    accumulator exists (the common autoTranslate-off case).
  - `manager._sync_result_to_conversation` adds an `else` arm: when the task
    has no content / errored, cancel any dangling accumulator instead of
    leaving it to idle-timeout.
  - Richer idle-timeout log (now names conv + segment count + "neither finalize
    nor cancel arrived") so a future leak is diagnosable, not misleading.
- **Tests (confirmed gaps closed):** +3 in `test_incremental_translate.py`
  (cancel tears down without committing; cancel-without-accumulator is False;
  finalize-then-late-cancel is harmless / no double commit); **new**
  `tests/test_auto_translate_safety_net.py` (4) drives the real
  `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` with an injected fake DB and asserts cancel
  fires on the autoTranslate-off and already-Chinese skip paths, does NOT fire
  on the happy handoff, and isn't attempted when `task=None`; +3 in
  `test_conv_config.py` pinning the `autoTranslate` config default (False) so
  the gate divergence can't widen silently. Full sweep:
  incremental(11)+safety_net(4)+conv_config(44)+noop/flip/migration +
  chat_manager_migration(21)+package_facades(42) all green.
- **Honest scope note on gripe #3 (live mid-stream display).** The incremental
  translator ALREADY does the per-round translation work in the background
  *during* the task (overlapping with tool execution) — it is not a single
  end-of-task call. What's deferred is the *display*: a streaming assistant
  bubble has no committed `_msgId`/`translatedContent` slot (msg ids are minted
  only at task-end sync, manager.py:206; streaming_render skips the live
  message and renders it via a dedicated element), so there is a real
  architectural blocker to painting a translation onto the still-streaming
  bubble. This change makes the end-of-task display RELIABLE and instant
  (segments pre-translated, now never dropped) rather than faking live paint.
  True in-stream per-round display would need server-minted msg ids during the
  loop + a frontend streaming-bubble translation slot — flagged, not attempted.
- **Gripe #2 (slow):** the dominant cost is the engine's `capability='cheap'`
  dispatch with model-rotation retries (logs show a 64s qwen outlier); the
  incremental path already hides most of it behind tool execution. No engine
  change made — over-tuning the retry budget risks the truncation/flip
  detectors that exist for good reason. Left as-is with the reliability fix as
  the high-leverage win.

### 2026-06-27 — Preference profile: broadened capture to user IDENTITY, switched new prefs from propose-then-confirm to AUTO-APPLY+inform, and replaced the Settings textarea with per-item editable rows
- **User asks (3):** (1) drop the "ask the user questions" idea; (2) stop

  textarea is unpleasant — show individual preferences instead. Also: be more
  thoughtful by perceiving who the user is (identity), not just work-style.

  headers: `## Preferences` (working style) and `## About the user` (role,
  domain, stack, expertise, recurring goals, locale) — with a hard "only what

  (`bundle-6ee4b991.js`).
- **KNOWN GAP reaffirmed (now more urgent):** `profile_path()` is still a SINGLE
  global file with no per-user scoping. For work-style prefs on a single-owner
  app that's fine; now that we store IDENTITY facts too, a multi-user *interactive*
  deployment would mix one person's identity into everyone's prompt. Headless
  surfaces remain fail-closed (`preferencesEnabled` via personal_scope), so the
  API leak is already covered — but identity-keyed paths should land before
  multi-user UI. Not done here (out of scope).

### 2026-06-27 — Fixed "Project tool does nothing; appears overlapping Settings": a DUPLICATE `<div id="settingsTab_skills">` open tag left every later modal nested inside `#settingsModal`
- **User report (screenshot):** clicking the Project Co-Pilot toolbar button
  did nothing; the project modal only became visible (mispositioned, overlapping
  the right half) when Settings was open. Suspected my browser-bridge CSS.
- **Ruled out my changes first.** My browser-CSS additions (`.browser-local-shortcut`
  / `.browser-zip-warning`) are scoped to those classes only; `styles.css` braces
  balanced (5918/5918), `_minify_css` output balanced (5917/5917) and ALL of
  `.modal-overlay` / `.pm-workbench` / `.stg-modal-overlay` survive minification.
  My `index.html` edits were all INSIDE `#browserModal` (line 1752+), downstream
  of the break. The working tree also had heavy unrelated uncommitted edits from
  other sessions (timer panels, paper viewer, emoji→SVG, MCP/skills tab rewrite).
- **Root cause (found with an HTMLParser nesting probe, not eyeballing):** every
  modal AFTER settings — `previewModal`, `projectModal`, `browserModal`,
  `memoryModal` — reported `depth=2 parent=settingsModal` instead of being
  body-level siblings (depth=1). Tracing div-depth at each `settings-tab-panel`
  boundary showed all panels open at depth-before=4 EXCEPT `settingsTab_skills`,
  after which depth jumped to 5. index.html lines 1437-1439 had the skills panel
  opening tag DUPLICATED:
  ```
  <div class="settings-tab-panel" id="settingsTab_skills">
  <!-- ═══ Skills Tab ═══ -->
  <div class="settings-tab-panel" id="settingsTab_skills">
  ```
  with only one matching `</div>`. That orphan `<div>` meant `settings-content`
  → `settings-body` → `#settingsModal` never closed, so all following modals
  became DESCENDANTS of settingsModal. While Settings is closed
  (`.modal-overlay` `display:none`), a descendant project modal is unconditionally
  hidden (click → nothing); when Settings opens, the project modal renders as a
  visible child overlapping it. Exactly the reported symptom.
- **Fix:** deleted the duplicate opening `<div id="settingsTab_skills">` line.
  Re-ran the HTMLParser probe: all 9 modals (settings/sysPrompt/update/dailyReport/
  preview/project/browser/memory/apply) now at depth=1 parent=(body), final
  unclosed structural depth 0.
- **Guardrail / method (recorded):** when a modal "does nothing on click but
  appears nested in another modal," it's a DOM-nesting bug from an unbalanced
  tag UPSTREAM, not a z-index or CSS bug in the modal itself. Diagnose with an
  `html.parser.HTMLParser` depth probe over `index.html` (report each modal's
  parent + depth) — naive `<div>`/`</div>` counting masks the location; the
  parent-tracking probe pinpoints it. Duplicate-open from a bad merge is the
  classic cause.

  reconstruct from the code alone.

### 2026-06-27 — Browser-tool timeline UX overhaul: human tab labels (no raw ids), inline screenshot rendering, code-block for execute_js, and de-emoji'd badges
- **User report (screenshot of a Ctrip booking run):** four gripes — (1) rows
  read `Screenshot (viewport) 12165686` / `12165686: (() => {…` — the opaque
  numeric tab id is meaningless to a human; (2) screenshots are slow and the
  captured image isn't shown inline (frontend should render it like image-gen);
  (3) `browser_execute_js` rows render as a cramped truncated one-liner — should
  borrow the run_command terminal-block style; (4) tool badges are full of
  emoji (📸✅❌🔍🖱️🍪➕✖🔗🖼️), against CLAUDE.md §3.4.
- **Fix 1 — never show a raw tab id (`lib/browser/display.py`).** `_tab_label`
  fell back to `str(tab_id)` whenever no page title was cached — which is the
  common case right after `browser_create_tab` (it cached nothing). Added a
  parallel `_tab_urls` cache; `update_tab_title(tab_id, title=None, url=None)`
  now also stores the URL (both args optional, back-compat with all 2-arg
  callers). New `get_tab_hostname()` parses the netloc. Label precedence:
  cached title (quoted, ≤30c) → page hostname → the generic word `tab`. The id
  is never surfaced. Wired URL caching into every handler that learns one:
  `list_tabs`/`read_tab`/`navigate`/`get_interactive_elements`/`summarize_page`
  and crucially `create_tab` (so the very next wait/screenshot/execute_js row on
  the new tab shows `trains.ctrip.com`, not `12165686`).
- **Fix 2 — inline screenshot (`handlers/browser.py` + `tool_rounds.js`).** The
  screenshot meta now carries `imageDataUris=[{uri:dataUrl,format,filename}]`
  (the same field read_files/inspect_image already use); the frontend image-grid
  block condition was widened to include `browser_screenshot`, so the captured
  PNG/JPEG renders as a clickable `<img>` instead of a useless "N chars" row.
  Speed: dropped `optimize=True` from the JPEG re-encode (a 2nd Huffman pass that
  ~doubles encode time on tall full-page captures for a few % size gain).
- **Fix 3 — execute_js code block (`tool_rounds.js`).** Added a dedicated
  `browser_execute_js` branch in `_renderUnifiedToolLine` that reuses the

  `<pre class="ptool-cmd-code">`, and a collapsible "Show result" pane fed from
  `round.toolContent`). The display label is now just `Execute JS in <tab>`
  (the code lives in the block, not the one-liner). No new CSS — inherits the
  existing terminal-block + light-theme rules; no new top-level JS file → no

  emit plain text (`ok`/`error`/`captured`/`clicked`/`opened`/`closed`/`done`/

  screenshot display text and the 🖼️ from the read-image meta title/badge in

- **Verification:** `node --check` + `ast.parse` clean on all 5 files; bundle
  rebuilt (`bundle-321a4603.js`); emoji sweep of browser handler/display files
  empty; functional check confirmed labels (`trains.ctrip.com` pre-title →

### 2026-06-27 — browser_screenshot now captures background tabs WITHOUT the tab-switch flicker: added a viewport-CDP path so captureVisibleTab (the only API that foregrounds the tab) is a true last resort
- **User report:** the screenshot tool "still requires navigation" — taking a
  shot visibly switches/foregrounds the target tab, disrupting the user. Asked
  whether we can grab the page in the background instead.
- **Diagnosis (traced in `browser_extension/background.js`):** there were three
  capture paths. `_screenshotFullPageCDP` (default) uses `chrome.debugger` + CDP
  `Page.captureScreenshot` and already runs fully in the BACKGROUND — no tab
  activation. The flicker came from `_screenshotViewport`, the FALLBACK (and the
  `fullPage:false` path), which uses `chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab` — an API
  that can only grab the *foreground* tab, so it did
  `tabs.update(tabId,{active:true})` → 500ms wait → capture →
  `tabs.update(originalTabId,{active:true})`. That forced activation IS the
  visible "navigation". So any time full-page CDP failed (DevTools already
  attached, etc.) or a caller asked for a fast viewport shot, the tab got yanked
  to the front.
- **Fix:** added `_screenshotViewportCDP(tabId, format, quality)` — same CDP
  attach/`Page.enable`/`detach` shape as the full-page path, but
  `Page.captureScreenshot` with `captureBeyondViewport:false` → captures the
  tab's current viewport in the background, no activation. Rewired the chain in
  `cmdScreenshotTab`: full-page request → `_screenshotFullPageCDP` → (on fail)
  `_screenshotViewportCDP` → (on fail) `_screenshotViewport`; a `fullPage:false`
  request → `_screenshotViewportCDP` → (on fail) `_screenshotViewport`. Only the
  last-resort `captureVisibleTab` activates the tab now, and only when CDP can't
  attach at all. Each fallthrough still records `fallbackReason` so the
  server-side handler/log surfaces why CDP was unavailable.
- **No server change needed:** `_handle_screenshot` already reads
  `fullPage`/`fallbackReason` from the result; the viewport-CDP result carries
  `fullPage:false` (correct — it's a viewport shot) plus the reason.
- **Versioning:** manifest `4.3.0 → 4.4.0` + header comment `v4.3 → v4.4` so
  users reload the unpacked extension to pick it up. `node --check` clean.
  Updated the `browser-extension-fullpage-screenshot-cdp` skill with the new
  fallback chain.
- **Caveat (called out):** CDP attach still flashes Chrome's brief yellow
  "extension is debugging this browser" banner while attached (detached
  immediately after) — unavoidable for any debugger-based capture, but far less
  disruptive than foregrounding the tab. True zero-banner background capture
  isn't possible via captureVisibleTab.

### 2026-06-27 — Browser-bridge install UX: fixed the missing extension icon + "nulls ago" status string, and added a zero-friction "Load unpacked directly" path for same-machine users
- **User report (screenshot):** the installed extension showed Chrome's grey
  "T" placeholder instead of an icon; the modal status read "Extension
  connected (… nulls ago)"; and the guidance never told the user they must
  UNZIP the download before dragging it in. Plus a general ask: where we can do
  the work for the user, we should.
- **Bug 1 — no icon (manifest).** `browser_extension/manifest.json` shipped
  `icon16/48/128.png` on disk but declared **neither** a top-level `icons` map
  **nor** `action.default_icon`, so Chrome fell back to the placeholder in both
  `chrome://extensions` and the toolbar. Fix: added both blocks pointing at the
  existing (valid 16/48/128 RGBA) PNGs. Pure manifest change — files already
  present, already in the download ZIP.
- **Bug 2 — "nulls ago".** `_checkBrowserStatus` (`main_toolbar_ui.js`) did
  `\`…, ${d.secondsAgo}s ago\`` but `/api/v1/browser/status` returns
  `secondsAgo: null` until the first extension poll lands → the literal string
  "nulls ago". Fix: `const ago = (d.secondsAgo != null) ? \`${d.secondsAgo}s ago\` : "just now"` used in both the single- and multi-client branches.
- **Guidance gap — "do it for them".** Chrome forbids programmatic install of
  unpacked dev extensions, so true one-click is impossible. BUT the unpacked
  extension already sits on the server's disk, so a same-machine (self-hosted)
  user can skip download+unzip entirely and just **Load unpacked** that folder.
  - `routes/api_v1/browser.py::browser_status` now returns `extensionPath` (the
    absolute `…/browser_extension` dir) **only to a loopback peer** — gated on
    `_remote_is_loopback()` from `routes/api_v1/auth.py` (real socket peer, not
    a spoofable `X-Forwarded-For`). A remote viewer (LAN IP, Docker port-map,
    tunnel, cloud IDE) loads the extension into THEIR Chrome, where the
    server-side path doesn't exist — so for them the box stays hidden and they
    fall through to the download+unzip steps (which now carry the unzip
    warning). Suppression is logged at debug. Verified: in-process test client
    (peer `<local>` → loopback) gets the path; the 4 existing browser v1 tests
    still pass.
  - New green callout box `#browserLocalShortcut` at the top of the modal
    (`index.html`), populated by `_applyBrowserLocalShortcut(extPath)` —
    click-to-copy path via the existing global `_safeClipboardWrite`. Hidden
    when `extensionPath` is null.
  - For the download path: step 1 retitled "下载并解压扩展 / Download & unzip",
    desc now bolds **务必先解压 / be sure to unzip**, plus an amber
    `.browser-zip-warning` line stating **Chrome can't load a .zip directly**.
- **Conventions honored:** new top-level JS symbol lives in an already-bundled
  file (`main_toolbar_ui.js`), no `_BUNDLE_FILES` change needed. No emoji icons
  (§3.4) — dropped the ⚠ from the warning, used amber color instead. HTML-
  bearing i18n strings use `data-i18n-html` (textContent would strip tags). New
  i18n keys: `browser.zipWarning`, `browser.localTitle`, `browser.localDesc`,
  `browser.clickToCopy`; updated `browser.stepDownload`/`stepDownloadDesc`.
  CSS-only additions are in `styles.css` (content-hash bundler regenerates on
  restart). Verified: JS/JSON/Python syntax all clean.

### 2026-06-27 — Made prompt-cache invalidation attribution PRECISE (names the exact msg[i].field), stopped benign L1 compaction from masking real breaks, prefix-gated sort_tool_results, and made the cost popover display-only
- **User mandate (point 2 of the cache-effectiveness audit):** "precisely
  pinpoint all causes and record exactly which change led to the invalidation"
  — a report that still says "stochastic server-side miss OR TTL OR silent
  edit" is the guesswork the user wants eliminated. So this was implement, not
  describe.
- **Grounded the gating question first (not assumed):** in steady state default
  L1 `micro_compact` RARELY produces `saved>0`. Every built-in L1 step gates on
  `ctx.is_in_cache_prefix(idx)` (= `idx < get_cache_prefix_count = prev_msg_count-2`);
  cold tool results have small indices → almost always inside the prefix →
  skipped, and the only out-of-prefix msgs are the last ~2 (inside the 40-deep
  `MICRO_HOT_TAIL`, never "cold"). So `saved>0` fires only on TRANSIENT rounds
  (cold start prefix_count==0, post-eviction, big parallel fan-out, or the
  `ignore_cache_prefix` arm). Durable write-back is idempotent and happens while
  the msg is OUTSIDE the prefix, so no latent real miss hides there. ⇒ fix #2 is
  a correct but LOW-FREQUENCY fix; the dominant levers are precise attribution
  (#1) and the frontend (#4).
- **#1 Precise attribution (`cache_tracking.py`):** added `_hash_prefix_fields`
  (per-message, per-FIELD hashes: role/content/tool_calls/tool_call_id/
  reasoning_content/thinking_signature/reasoning_details) + `_diff_prefix_fields`
  (names the exact `msg[i].field` that changed, capped at 6 + `…`), mirroring
  the existing `_diff_tool_hashes`. New `CacheState.prefix_field_hashes` slot.
  `detect_cache_break` now computes culprits on the prev-range and threads them
  into `_resolve_break_cause(prefix_culprits=…)`: the `prefix_mutation` cause
  string and the sub-threshold terminal branch now append `[changed:
  msg[1].content, msg[2].tool_calls]` instead of the three-way guess. The
  TTL/stochastic-server guess remains ONLY when bytes are provably identical.
  PREFIX-MUTATION log line now prints `changed=[…]`.
- **#2 Stop L1 masking detection (`compaction/_pipeline.py`):**
  `notify_compaction` now fires ONLY for mutations that touch the cached prefix
  — `compacted` (L2 force) OR `adv_saved>0` (advanced) OR (`saved>0` AND
  `ignore_cache_prefix`). Default out-of-prefix L1 (`saved>0` alone) no longer
  raises `compaction_pending`, which had blanket-suppressed all 4 detectors on
  exactly the transient rounds where a real break is likeliest. Zero new false
  positives: default L1 can't mutate the compared range by construction.
- **#3 Prefix-gate `sort_tool_results` (`cache_tracking.py` + orchestrator call
  site):** added optional `conv_id`; a tool-result run is sorted only when it
  lies fully OUTSIDE `get_cache_prefix_count` (`run_start >= prefix_count`). A
  run inside/straddling the prefix is skipped — re-ordering already-cached bytes
  can only force a miss. Default `conv_id=''` keeps legacy sort-everywhere for
  the existing tests/debug callers. This was the only every-round in-place edit
  lacking BOTH a prefix guard and a notify.
- **#4 Frontend display-only (`static/js/ui/finish_info.js`):**
  `_cacheBreakReason` now renders the backend cause string VERBATIM (translated)
  for server_side/no_cache_reuse/prefix_mutation instead of prepending a fixed
  Chinese label that could CONTRADICT it (`服务端缓存失效` over a cause saying
  eviction is unlikely). Unknown/future keys show their backend value verbatim
  rather than fabricating a label from the raw dict key; unknown key with no
  value is omitted (no invented cause). Collapsed-tag tooltip no longer
  fabricates `未复用缓存` when every reason is empty — it states the round count
  plainly. Capped writeBreakdown rows now render `的来源（约）` with the
  components, not an exact-looking equation.
- **Tests (all green):** added 3 classes to `tests/test_cache_improvements.py`
  (12 new): `TestPrefixCulpritAttribution` (content vs tool_calls field named;
  stable prefix → no culprit), `TestL1DoesNotMaskRealBreak` (L1-only doesn't set
  pending; L2 still does; end-to-end real break surfaces despite co-occurring
  L1), `TestSortToolResultsPrefixGate` (prefix run not reordered; tail still
  sorted). `test_cache_improvements` 51 passed; broader sweep
  (`-k "compaction or cache"`) 427 passed / 2 skipped incl. `test_write_breakdown`;
  `test_new_features`/`test_user_profile`/`test_log_noise_reduction`/
  `test_server_message_store` 94 passed/1 skip. `node --check finish_info.js` OK.
- **Not done (out of scope, flagged):** the `compaction_pending` single-boolean
  can still mis-target if two LLM rounds elapse before `detect_cache_break` runs;
  and `get_cache_prefix_count` accuracy after a stale-state eviction remains the
  latent failure mode for L1's prefix safety. Both pre-existing, deferred.


### 2026-06-27 — Fixed the project-digest "phantom tools" mismatch: the cross-conv reminder advertised list_conversations/get_conversation on every project turn, but those tools register only on an @-attach
- **Symptom (user-noticed):** the startup `<system-reminder>` digest said *"Use
  `list_conversations(scope="project")` … and `get_conversation(...)` to read
  one in full"* — but on a plain project turn neither tool is in the model's
  schema, so it's told to call tools it can't. Same class as the documented
  `using-tools-section-filters-by-registered-tools-2026-06` lesson.
- **Root cause (two independent gates):** digest injection
  (`system_context.py` step 4.4) is gated on `project_enabled and project_path`
  → fires on EVERY project turn. The conv-ref tools (`registry.py::_build_conv_ref`)
  are gated on `ctx.has_conv_ref` → register ONLY when the user @-attached a
  conversation. Common case (project mode, no @-attach) = digest present, tools
  absent. The ONLY place hardcoding the tool names in prompt text was
  `build_project_digest`'s header (`lib/conversations/project_summary.py`).
- **Fix (keep the digest, make the header tool-aware — ambient awareness is the
  POINT of Layer 2, so suppressing the whole digest would be wrong):**
  - `build_project_digest(..., conv_tools_available: bool = True)`: two header
    variants. `True` → the tool-instructing header. `False` → a tool-free
    "For ambient awareness: this project has N related conversation(s). You
    cannot open them this turn, but knowing they exist may inform your answer:"
    Entry rendering (`• "title" — summary [id]`) is UNCHANGED in both.
  - `system_context.py` step 4.4 computes
    `_conv_tools_available = bool(tool_names and {'list_conversations','get_conversation'} & tool_names)`
    (it already received `tool_names`) and passes it through.
  - **Idempotency marker shrunk** `'related conversation(s) you can'` →
    `'related conversation(s)'` — the substring BOTH headers share, so the
    re-injection probe matches either variant (the tool-free header lacks "you
    can consult"). Verified no other code referenced the old marker string.
- **Tests:** +`test_digest_header_advertises_tools_only_when_available`
  (project_summary) and +2 injection-level tests in test_streaming_and_prefetch
  (`_digest_header_tool_free_when_conv_tools_absent` asserts
  build_project_digest called with `conv_tools_available=False` AND no tool name
  leaks into the assembled prompt; `_advertises_tools_when_conv_tools_present`
  the converse). Full sweep green: project_summary(10) + streaming_and_prefetch(35)
  + cc_alignment(31) + user_profile(22) = no regressions. Updated
  `docs/CROSS_CONV_AWARENESS.md` (signature note + new decision 7).
- **Guardrail reaffirmed:** never name a tool in ANY injected prompt text unless
  it's in this turn's `tool_names`. The digest header now joins
  `section_using_tools` as a tool_names-gated injection.


### 2026-06-27 — Fixed the #1 search-observability hole (tofu-search pipeline diagnostics were silently dropped) + deepened the chatui↔tofu-search decoupling (browser SERP parsing moved INTO the library)
- **Trigger:** review of recent search-tool usage. `app.log` showed slow
  searches as a bare `[Search] web_search BATCH: 4 queries in 128.6s` with **no
  breakdown of where the time went**. Root cause found by grepping the logs:
  `server.py`'s log router classifies by name prefix —
  `_BIZ_PREFIXES=('lib.','routes.','server')` → `app.log`; everything else is
  "vendor" → `vendor.log` at **WARNING-only**. The extracted search library logs
  under **`tofu_search.*`**, so ALL its INFO-level pipeline diagnostics (per-engine
  result counts/timings, streaming fetch race-to-N, content-filter reductions, the
  `step1_engines=.. step4_page_fetch=90.6s ..` timing breakdown) were dropped on
  the floor, and its WARNINGs were buried among **3407 lines** of routine
  playwright tracebacks in vendor.log. An operator literally could not diagnose a
  slow search from the business log.
- **Fix 1 (chatui, the important one):** added `'tofu_search'` to `_BIZ_PREFIXES`
  in `server.py`. Now the library's diagnostics flow into `app.log` (INFO) and
  `error.log` (WARNING+) like first-class business logs. This is correct because
  tofu-search IS this project's search subsystem (extracted 2026-06), not a random
  third-party dep.
- **Fix 2 (tofu-search → 0.3.1, log hygiene):** `tofu_search/log.py` only attaches
  its own stderr handler when the ROOT logger is handler-less (true standalone
  use). When embedded in a host that already configured root logging, records now
  PROPAGATE to the host's handlers instead of double-printing to stderr — the host
  controls routing. Verified both paths: embedded → 0 pkg handlers, propagate=True;
  standalone → 1 console handler.
- **Fix 3 (tofu-search, noise):** routine Playwright worker `queue.Empty` timeouts
  no longer log `exc_info=True` — an over-budget network render is expected, not a
  crash; the warning now states the timeout value. (Was the bulk of vendor.log.)
- **Decoupling (the user's other ask — keep chatui thin):** `lib/search_bridge.py`
  used to hand-roll a ~50-line regex DDG-SERP parser for the browser-search
  fallback — duplicating logic the library already owns. Replaced with a new
  **`BrowserProvider.fetch_html(url)`** seam: chatui supplies ONLY the transport
  (extension WebSocket → raw HTML), and tofu-search parses it with the same
  engine-grade bs4 parser via the new
  `search.engines.ddg.parse_ddg_html_text()`. `search_via_browser` now prefers
  `fetch_html` and only falls back to the legacy host-`search()` when it's
  unavailable. Net: bridge lost ~22 lines + the duplicated parser; SERP parsing
  lives in exactly one place. Also added a `[Bridge] tofu-search config synced: …`
  log line so the (previously silent) config push is observable.
- **Compat:** bumped `requirements.txt` floor to `tofu-search>=0.3.1` — the bridge
  no longer overrides `search()`, so an older library would leave browser-search
  dead. tofu-search `__version__`/pyproject → 0.3.1 + CHANGELOG entry.
- **Verification:** tofu-search suite **156 passed**; chatui
  `test_auth_sources_xhs.py` **21 passed**; functional check of the DDG parser
  (ad-skip + uddg-unwrap), the `fetch_html` fallback path, and both logging modes;
  `ruff check` clean on all 6 changed files in both repos. NOT yet published to
  PyPI / pushed — local dev uses `TOFU_SEARCH_PATH` sibling checkout.



### 2026-06-27 — Decoupled app-personal state (memory store + preference profile) from the headless API, and built a permanent registry so future personal features can't get silently re-bundled
- **User concern (architectural):** Tofu's personal config — memory, the user
  preference profile, system-prompt organisation — belongs to the *interactive
  Tofu app*, not the headless API. If a capability isn't actually provided, the
  prompt must not describe it (hallucination guard). And they asked for a
  PERMANENT mechanism so adding new features later doesn't recreate this messy
  bundling.
- **Diagnosis (traced, not guessed):** the prompt side was already mostly
  correct — `system_context.py` gates `<memory_accumulation>` on
  `memory_enabled` and the swarm/tool-name sections on their flags, and
  `build_static_prompt` only names registered tools (the
  `using-tools-section-filters-by-registered-tools` fix). The leak was in the
  **defaults**: `memoryEnabled` defaults to `True` (`model_config.py:142`, for
  the UI via `conv_config.py`), and the headless builders inherited it. So a
  bare `/api/v1/agent/run` (the "you bring the model" headline endpoint) landed
  on memory ON, and worse, the **operator's personal preference profile** (the
  server-global `<data>/memories/.tofu_user_profile.md`) rode `memoryEnabled`
  and got spliced into an unrelated BYO caller's prompt — a privacy/isolation
  leak on a shared deployment. The compat shims only half-fixed it
  (`setdefault('memoryEnabled', False)` ONLY when `tools` was present).
- **Fix — single-source-of-truth registry (mirrors `lib/agent_artifacts.py`):**
  - **New `lib/agent_core/personal_scope.py`**: `PERSONAL_CAPABILITIES` registry
    (one `PersonalCapability` per app-personal cfg flag, each fail-closed on
