### 2026-06-26 — Mobile composer polish: hid the desktop-only input-footer hint and unified the toolbar control sizes to a consistent 40px band
- **User report:** on mobile the input footer mentioned send-method
  (Enter/Ctrl+Enter) and drag-and-drop file upload — neither of which is
  usable on a touch device; the toolbar buttons had inconsistent sizes; the
  whole composer felt cramped.
- **Fixes (all in `static/styles.css`, scoped to `@media(max-width:768px)`):**
  - **Footer hidden.** `.input-footer{display:none!important}` (was just
    `font-size:10px`). The `#inputHint` text only describes desktop affordances
    (`Enter send · Ctrl+Enter/Shift+Enter newline · 📎 or drop files`); on a
    phone sending is the ⏎ button and files come via the attach (+) button.
    The JS that sets the hint (`refreshInputSendHint` / `_applyImageGenUI` in
    `main_folders_mobile.js` + `main.js`) still runs harmlessly against the
    hidden element — no JS change needed. Also frees vertical space.
  - **Unified 40px touch-target band.** Before: send 44×44, more 36×36, search
    `min-height:44px` (padding-width), attach 36×36, model picker ~32px → a
    visibly mismatched row. Now ALL controls are 40px tall: `.send-btn`,
    `.mobile-more-btn`, `.attach-btn` are 40×40 squares; `.search-mode-toggle`
    is a 40×40 icon-only square (`padding:0`, centered, was a wide pill);
    `.preset-toggle` is `height:40px`. Row gaps `4px→8px`, `.input-actions`
    padding `4px 8px 6px → 8px 10px 10px`, textarea `min-height 40→44`,
    `padding 10/8 → 12/10`, `.input-box margin-top 6→8` — more breathing room.
  - **Tofu specificity war (per the two mobile-CSS memories).** The tofu theme
    sets its own `padding`/sizing on `.search-mode-toggle` / `.preset-toggle` /
    `.send-btn` / textarea / `.input-actions` at specificity 0,2,0, which beats
    the plain `.class` mobile rules (0,1,0). Re-asserted the 40px sizing + new
    spacing with matching `[data-theme="tofu"]`-prefixed `!important` rules
    inside the existing tofu-mobile block so the row stays consistent in both
    the default and tofu themes.
- **Cache-busting:** none needed — `lib/css_bundler.py` content-hashes
  `styles.css` (recomputes on mtime+size change) → `styles-<hash>.css`
  regenerates on server restart and the `<link>` tag in the served HTML
  changes automatically. Restart + hard-refresh to see it.
- **Scope:** CSS-only, entirely within the mobile media query; desktop layout
  untouched.



### 2026-06-26 — Root-caused & permanently fixed the "VS Code terminal spewed searches I never ran" incident: leaked TEST timer_watchers rows resurrected as 40 zombie poll-agents flooding web_search
- **Symptom (user report):** after the :15000 box became unreachable and was
  restarted, the web-VS-Code terminal dumped a massive backlog of logs
  including nonsense searches the user never issued, e.g.
  `[Search] Bing: 10 results … query='2026年6月26日 杭州是否已完成电动自行车备案'`,
  `'2026 FIFA World Cup host country'`, `'2026 NBA Draft first overall pick'`.
- **Root-cause chain (verified in logs + DB, not guessed):** the search came
  from a thread named `timer-poll-tmr_2e76a607` — the **Timer Watcher**
  subsystem (`lib/scheduler/timer.py`), not any user chat. The DB had **40
  `status='active'` timers, ALL with `conv_id='conv-parsefail'`,
  `source_task_id='task-x'`, instruction `'Is the run finished?'`** — verbatim
  the timer minted by `tests/test_timer_parse_failure.py::_make_timer()`. So the
  origin was a TEST leaking active rows into the **production** DB (ambient
  `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres` defeats conftest's SQLite `setdefault`, per the
  earlier sidebar-leak entry; the conftest self-heal purge covered only
  `conversations`, not `timer_watchers`). Four design weaknesses then amplified
  it: (1) `_build_poll_tools` defaulted `searchMode` to `'multi'` even for
  `tools_config={}`, so every poll agent got `web_search`; with an ungrounded
  "is the run finished?" instruction the cheap poll models hallucinated a query
  to "check". (2) `resume_active_timers()` re-spawned EVERY active row on every
  boot with no age cap / no concurrency cap → 40 × 10s polls fired at once
  (search handler logged 60–78s `SLOW` under the load — likely what made the
  box unreachable pre-restart). (3) skipped polls (unchanged check_command) did
  NOT increment poll_count, so a timer could never reach max_polls to retire
  (the long-standing 2026-04-20 memory). (4) `no such table: timer_watchers`
  races + `event_id=0` collisions while polling.
- **Immediate remediation:** cancelled the live zombies via
  `cancel_timer` loop over `list_active_timers()` → DB went from 40 active to
  **0 active / 0 in-memory threads** (split across cancelled/exhausted/triggered).
- **Permanent fix (defense-in-depth, all four layers):**
  - **Fix 1 (origin):** `tests/test_timer_parse_failure.py` gained an autouse
    teardown deleting `WHERE conv_id='conv-parsefail'`; conftest gained
    `_purge_test_timers()` (pattern-gated to `conv-parsefail` / `test-conv%` /
    `source_task_id='task-x'`) wired into the session-start+end autouse purge
    alongside `_purge_test_conversations`. Verified: 0 `conv-parsefail` rows
    after a test run.
  - **Fix 2 (amplifier):** `resume_active_timers()` rewritten — pass 1
    age-sweeps any active timer older than `max(24h, poll_interval*max_polls*1.5)`
    to a new `status='expired'` (new `_mark_expired` helper); pass 2 re-spawns
    survivors capped at `TOFU_TIMER_RESUME_CAP` (default 20), logging the
    overflow (retried next boot). Age floor tunable via `TOFU_TIMER_MAX_AGE_HOURS`.
  - **Fix 3 (the actual search flood):** `_build_poll_tools` no longer defaults
    search/fetch ON — `searchMode` default `''`, `fetchEnabled` default `False`.
    A bare watcher gets read_files (+ project/code tools when configured) but
    NOT web_search. **Behavior change, called out:** timers that want web access
    must set `searchMode`/`fetchEnabled` in their `tools_config`.
  - **Fix 4 (immortality):** the skipped-poll branch in `start_timer_loop` now
    calls `_increment_poll_count(tid, 'skipped', …)` so every timer
    deterministically advances toward max_polls.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_timer_resume_guardrails.py` (7 tests: no-search
  default, search/fetch only when enabled, over-age expiry, fresh-timer kept,
  resume cap bounds respawns, skipped-poll increment) + existing
  `test_timer_parse_failure.py` (5) all pass; broader `-k "scheduler or
  proactive or timer or poll"` sweep = **80 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions**.
  Both timer test files marked `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`.



### 2026-06-26 — MCP install robustness, round 2: closed the worker/proxy-timeout gap (async install + poll) and a concurrent double-pip TOCTOU
- **Why:** Round 1 moved the blocking pip into the Flask worker thread (off the
  MCP event loop). But that left a synchronous multi-minute POST. Verified the
  server runtime first: it's **Quart + Hypercorn (ASGI)**, `python server.py`
  (no gunicorn/uwsgi; Dockerfile `CMD ["python","server.py"]`), and Hypercorn
  sets only `keep_alive_timeout`/`graceful_timeout` — **no per-request worker-kill
  timer**, so the bundled server won't kill a 300s install. HOWEVER the app
  explicitly supports reverse proxies (cloud-IDE/notebook; `_detect_reverse_proxy`
  in server.py) whose response timeouts WOULD cut a multi-minute POST and leave a
  half-installed package — the same "install times out" symptom one layer down.
- **Fix — async install + status poll:**
  - `lib/mcp/client.py`: new in-process job registry `start_install_job(command)`
    / `get_install_job(command)` — runs `prewarm_vendored_launcher` on a daemon
    thread, returns `{state: installing|ready|error}` immediately. Ready fast-path
    (launcher already resolves) skips the thread entirely.
  - `routes/api_v1/mcp.py`: `install_from_catalog_v1` now returns HTTP **202
    `{status:'installing'}`** for a vendored launcher needing cold install instead
    of blocking; new GET `/catalog/install/status?id=` polls and, on `ready`,
    performs the fast handshake via the extracted `_connect_after_install` helper
    (shared with the sync path). Error state still surfaces
    `_launcher_install_hint` + `stderr_tail`.
  - `static/js`: `Api.mcp.catalogInstall` drops `timeout:0` (request is fast now);
    new `catalogInstallStatus`. `_mcpDoInstall` + `_mcpQuickInstall` poll via the
    new `_mcpPollInstall` (2.5s interval, 6-min cap, live "已等待 N 秒" copy).
- **Fix — concurrency (#2 TOCTOU):** `_try_autoinstall_launcher` released
  `_install_lock` between the `_install_attempted` check and the pip run, so a
  startup pre-warm racing a user click could launch TWO simultaneous `pip install`
  of the same source. Added per-command locks `_install_cmd_locks`; the
  check-then-pip section now holds the command lock (pip body extracted to
  `_run_pip_install`). The second caller waits, then re-resolves.
- **#1 confirmed safe:** the boot pre-warm runs on the fire-and-forget
  `mcp-auto-connect` daemon thread (server.py:1536), never `.join()`ed;
  `asyncio.run(_startup())` returns before `hypercorn_serve` — slow boot pip can't
  delay HTTP accept.
- **Tests:** added to `tests/test_mcp_install_nonblocking.py`:
  `test_concurrent_autoinstall_runs_pip_once` (provably fails "pip ran 2x" when the
  per-command lock is reverted), `test_start_install_job_async_and_pollable`,
  `test_start_install_job_ready_fast_path`. All MCP suites green: 61 passed
  (install 6 + launcher-resolve 32 + call_health 7 + catalog_internal_only 7 +
  tool_links 9). Python/JS syntax checked.



### 2026-06-26 — Fixed "installing llm-mcp times out": cold pip ran ON the MCP event loop; made the install frontend robust (A–E)
- **Symptom:** Clicking Install for `llm-mcp` in the MCP App-Store tab timed out
  with a generic "无法连接到服务器". Other vendored servers (hope-mcp/xuecheng-mcp)
  usually didn't, because they were already resident from an earlier install.
- **Root cause (verified in code):** `llm-mcp` isn't on PyPI, so it hits the
  first-connect auto-install path. `_try_autoinstall_launcher` runs a BLOCKING
  `subprocess.run(['pip','install',…], timeout=300)` — and it was called *inline*
  inside the `_server_owner` coroutine (`lib/mcp/client.py`), i.e. directly on the
  single shared MCP event-loop thread. A cold pip resolve/build froze the entire
  loop (every server's keepalive/tool-calls/connects) while three timeouts raced:
  the browser's 30s `fetch` abort (`catalogInstall` used the default), the 65s
  readiness ceiling (`MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT*2+5`), and pip's own 300s. The 30s
  browser abort won → "timeout". (Contrast `_reconnect_server`, already correctly
  offloaded via `run_in_executor`.)
- **Fix (full set A–E):**
  - **A** Offload the pip install off the loop: the `_server_owner` fallback now
    `await loop.run_in_executor(None, _try_autoinstall_launcher, command)`.
  - **B** Pre-install before connect: `install_from_catalog_v1`
    (`routes/api_v1/mcp.py`) calls the new `prewarm_vendored_launcher()` in the
    Flask worker thread (blocking pip is fine there) BEFORE `connect_server`, so
    connect is just the fast handshake. Autoinstall-during-connect stays a fallback.
  - **C** Realistic budget: `Api.mcp.catalogInstall` now passes `{timeout:0}` (no
    client abort) and the modal shows a "首次安装需下载依赖，可能耗时约一分钟" notice.
  - **D** Surface the real reason: on pre-warm failure the route returns the
    captured `_install_last_error` / `_launcher_install_hint` (real pip stderr +
    the manual `pip install` command); the modal renders `stderr_tail` on ok:false.
  - **E** Pre-warm at startup: `server.py`'s MCP boot thread calls the new
    `prewarm_all_vendored()` (runs even with zero configured servers — the
    fresh-install case). `install.sh`'s bundled-MCP step now also installs from a
    SIBLING checkout (`../<name>`), not only `vendor/`, so dev clones get the
    launchers on PATH too.
- **Also:** rewrote the stale `llm-mcp/README.md` — it falsely claimed a vendored
  Node CLI tgz + `LLM_BIN`/`NODE_BIN`/`LLM_MCP_FORCE_DEFAULT`. The package is
  pure-Python (only `mcp>=1.0.0`; HTTP+SSO in `src/llm_mcp/native/`), no Node, no
  subprocess. Corrected prerequisites, config table, auto-login flow, safety rails.
- **Regression test:** `tests/test_mcp_install_nonblocking.py` drives
  `_async_start_owner` with a vendored command not on PATH and a fake SLOW pip; a
  concurrent heartbeat coroutine must keep ticking. Verified it FAILS (1 tick) when
  reverted to the inline call and PASSES (many ticks) with the offload. Full MCP
  suites green: `test_mcp_install_nonblocking` + `test_mcp_launcher_resolve` (35) and
  `test_mcp_call_health`/`catalog_internal_only`/`tool_links` (23).


### 2026-06-26 — Made the enlarged unit tier DETERMINISTIC: two consecutive full `-m unit` runs now agree exactly (3162 tests, 2 known out-of-scope failures), after killing the real root of the flakiness — a live background scheduler running inside the test process
- **Trigger:** a reviewer's independent full run showed 5 failures (not the 3 I'd
  claimed) with a SHIFTING set — the signature of cross-test pollution / flakiness
  that varies with run composition. A tier that returns 3 on one machine and 5 on
  another is not green. Held to making it deterministic.
- **The dominant root cause (finally found):** importing `server` (which many
  tests do via the `flask_client`/`flask_app` fixtures) calls
  `routes.register_all` → `start_scheduler_worker`, which spun up a REAL 30s-tick
  scheduler thread + a deferred timer-resume thread. Those threads ran **live LLM
  polls and live web searches** (Marginalia/Bing/Brave — visible in the captured
  logs: `[Timer:tmr_…] Poll #110 parse FAILURE (model=gpt-4.1-mini)`, real
  `marginalia.nu` HTTPS calls) against the shared DB for the whole pytest session.
  They stole CPU/IO and intermittently pushed timing-sensitive tests past their
  timeouts — so the SAME test passed alone but failed in the full run, and the
  failure set drifted with which tests warmed the scheduler. **Fix:**
  `lib/scheduler/manager.py::start_scheduler_worker` now early-returns when
  `TOFU_DISABLE_SCHEDULER` is set; conftest sets it (collection-time, before the
  `server` import, AND in `_configure_test_env`). This is the single change that
  removed most of the nondeterminism.
- **`test_endpoint_messages::test_multi_iteration_message_shapes` — fixed the
  real defect AND the misclassification.** It flaked on a 60s internal timeout.
  Probing the loop revealed WHY: the endpoint anti-analysis-spiral guard injects
  SYNTHETIC critic turns (no LLM call) whenever a worker produces zero
  state-changing tool calls — which a plain-text mock worker ALWAYS does — so the
  loop ran extra iterations to its stuck-guard, ~47s, flaky past 60s. I first
  tried a MockLLMRecorder STOP-on-exhaustion fallback, but that MASKED
  `test_stuck_stops_loop` (which deliberately exhausts the queue to reach the
  stuck guard) — reverted it. The honest fix: these endpoint-loop classes are
  INTEGRATION-grade (each runs real compaction + cache-session + memory-prefetch
  + per-round persistence around the mock LLM; `test_multi_iteration` ~94s,
  `test_stuck_stops_loop` ~58s, file ~300s with high per-test variance under
  load). Marked the **7 loop-running classes** `@pytest.mark.slow` (left the pure
  helper / verdict-parsing classes `unit`) and raised the wait 60→180s. They now
  run in the dedicated `slow` tier, not the fast default `unit`/`ci`.
- **`routes/chat.py::chat_active` hardened** (`t['convId']`→`t.get('convId','')`)
  — a legacy/minimal task dict left in the process-global `tasks` registry by
  another test made `GET /api/v1/chat/active` 500 with `KeyError: 'convId'`,
  polluting `test_server_async` (health, json_compressed) +
  `test_restart_smoke::test_sync_route_runs_under_quart`. Correct hardening for a
  shared mutable registry; cannot regress.
- **Determinism PROVEN:** two back-to-back full `python -m pytest -m unit`
  (junit-xml parsed, `--timeout-method=signal`):
  - Run 1: 3162 tests, **2 failures**, 7 skipped, 184s.
  - Run 2: 3162 tests, **2 failures**, 7 skipped, 194s.
  Identical fail set both times: `test_frontend_typecheck` (the real TS2339 in
  `paper-reader.js:2248`) and `test_swarm_async::test_await_no_ids_includes_
  early_finishers` (the real `await_agents` race). Both are pre-existing,
  out-of-scope product/source bugs; NO in-scope / orchestration / pollution test
  fails. Tier time also dropped 393s→~190s (slow endpoint tests deselected).
- **Method that worked (recorded as guardrail):** classify every full-run
  failure by re-running the file ALONE — pass-alone is pollution (hunt the
  leaker, harden the global, or DISABLE the noisy background daemon) or an
  intrinsic-slowness timing flake (re-tier `slow`); fail-alone is real. And never
  declare a tier green off ONE run — require two consecutive full runs with
  identical fail sets.


### 2026-06-26 — Leaked test conversations in the sidebar: root-caused to MISSING visual-E2E fixtures + no self-heal, fixed with (a) real `page`/`live_server`/`browser`/`screenshot_dir` fixtures and (b) a pattern-gated session-autouse purge (cleaned 421 accumulated junk rows)
- **User report:** many test scripts create sidebar conversations that never
  disappear — e.g. a "Hello, this is a test message!" row that persists.
- **Two root causes, confirmed against code + an empirical DB probe:**
  1. **The visual-E2E fixtures never existed.** `tests/test_visual_e2e.py`
     (tier `-m visual`) references `page` / `live_server` / `browser` /
     `screenshot_dir`, and its docstring claimed *"The `page` fixture
     (conftest.py) automatically cleans up any conversations created."* But
     `git log -S "def page"` / `-S "def live_server"` returns NOTHING across
     all history — those fixtures were aspirational. So every visual test
     errored at setup and the promised snapshot-diff cleanup never ran. The
     `★ newChat()` calls added per the `e2e-test-newchat-isolation` skill were
     necessary but insufficient — they isolate WHICH conv a message lands in,
     but nothing deleted the conv afterward.
  2. **The suite runs against PRODUCTION PG, not the temp SQLite.** conftest's
     `_configure_test_env` does `os.environ.setdefault("TOFU_DB_BACKEND",
     "sqlite")`, but the dev/CI host has ambient `TOFU_DB_BACKEND=postgres`, so
     `setdefault` is a no-op and `lib.database._core._FORCE_SQLITE` is False →
     backend resolves to `pg` at import time (verified: a fresh import with the
     ambient env yields `_BACKEND='pg'`). The parity tests already document
     this ("get_thread_db has no test-DB isolation … every seeded row MUST be
     deleted afterwards or it leaks into the user's sidebar") and self-clean via
     an autouse `_CREATED_CONVS` + `finally` fixture. The visual + several
     `test_api_integration` paths did not, so their rows leaked into the real DB.
- **Fix (a) — real fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`** (appended after
  `flask_client`, all SESSION-scoped, instantiated only when a `-m visual` test
  requests them → ZERO cost to unit/api runs):
  - `live_server` boots `server.app` on an ephemeral port via in-thread
    Hypercorn with a `shutdown_trigger` event — the proven pattern lifted from
    `tests/test_sdk_e2e.py::_boot_real_server`. Serves the SAME process app +
    DB, so the `page` cleanup can see the rows it created.
  - `browser` launches headless Chromium via raw `playwright.sync_api`
    (`pytest-playwright` is NOT installed). Skips cleanly (not errors) if
    Playwright or a Chromium build is missing.
  - `page` navigates to the live app, snapshots `conversations.map(c=>c.id)`
    before the test, and on teardown deletes the diff via browser-side
    `deleteConversation(...)` (a server-only DELETE gets re-synced back by the
    cached conv list — see `_cleanup_test_convs`), then closes the page and
    runs a server-side pattern-purge as a safety net.
  - `screenshot_dir` → `tests/screenshots/` (created if missing).
- **Fix (b) — self-healing pattern purge** (`_purge_test_conversations` +
  `_purge_leaked_test_conversations` session-autouse fixture, runs at session
  START — healing junk a prior crashed run left — AND END). Deletes rows ONLY
  by test-only id prefixes (`parity-%`, `test-conv%`, `test-minimal%`,
  `test-endpoint%`) or distinctive synthetic E2E `search_text` strings
  (`Hello, this is a test message!`, `Test sidebar entry`, the two
  `Conversation … Message`, `Sent via keyboard shortcut`). Generic E2E phrases
  ("What is 2+2?", "First question", …) are deliberately EXCLUDED — a real user
  could type those; those are cleaned only by the precise snapshot-diff in
  `page`. Best-effort: every statement/commit/close is try-wrapped + logged,
  never raises, never fails a test.
- **Verification:**
  - `ast.parse` clean on `tests/conftest.py` + `tests/test_visual_e2e.py`.
  - Functional probe: seeded 2 test-pattern rows + 1 innocent real row, ran
    `_purge_test_conversations` → both test rows GONE, the real row PRESENT.
    **It purged 421 rows** — direct proof of how many leaked conversations had
    accumulated in the sidebar over time.
  - `pytest tests/test_api_integration.py -m api` → **22 passed** (new
    session-autouse purge + lazy E2E fixtures don't disturb the existing suite).
  - `pytest tests/test_visual_e2e.py -m visual --collect-only` → 21 tests
    collect (previously errored at setup); `--setup-only` shows the
    `_purge… → screenshot_dir → browser` chain resolving and the test SKIPPING
    cleanly (Chromium absent here) instead of erroring.
- **Follow-up (not done, out of scope):** the deeper fix is to make the
  live-server/`get_thread_db` path honor an isolated DB even under ambient PG
  (e.g. route the `live_server` fixture through `reset_sqlite_for_tests`), so
  the E2E tests CAN'T touch the real sidebar at all. (b) makes leaks self-heal
  regardless; (a) makes them clean up per-test; full DB isolation would make
  the prod DB untouchable. Deferred to keep this change scoped to the reported
  symptom.


### 2026-06-26 — Opensource export+push: drove the public build from 40 unit failures + a red CI-lint job to GREEN, fixing 3 export-specific defect classes at SOURCE (not in the export tree)
- **Task:** export an internal + an opensource build, push opensource to GitHub
  (rangehow/ToFu + NiuTrans/ToFu, per the export-push-workflow skill). Followed
  the "run CI locally before push" rule — which surfaced that the public build
  was NOT shippable as-is.
- **First local `pytest -m unit` on the export: 40 failures** (source has only
  the 2 known-flaky). Triaged by re-running each in isolation + a baseline
  sub-agent that ran the same set in the SOURCE tree. Three defect classes, all
  EXPORT-SPECIFIC and all fixed at source so future exports stay correct:
  1. **ruff --fix stripped re-export imports** → the single highest-impact bug.
     `export.py` runs `ruff --fix` on `lib/ routes/ tests/`; in
     `lib/tasks_pkg/endpoint_review.py` the 6-name `from lib.agent_verdict import (...)`
     includes 4 PURE RE-EXPORTS (`STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS`, `accumulate_usage as
     _accumulate_usage`, `detect_stuck as _detect_stuck`, `replan_enabled as
     _replan_enabled`) consumed by `endpoint.py`. ruff saw them unused-in-file
     and deleted them → `ImportError: cannot import name '_accumulate_usage'`
     killing endpoint mode, cascading into ~30 failures (test_endpoint_*,
     test_orchestration_endpoint_runner, test_endpoint_flow_parity, + shared-
     state pollution into test_chat_manager_migration, test_e2e_headless_api,
     test_sdk_e2e, test_ecosystem_sdk_compat, test_event_emit,
     test_chat_flow_dispatch). **Fix:** `# noqa: F401` on each re-export line
     (verified the noqa SURVIVES the export's ruff --fix). This is the F401
     re-export trap from the export-must-run-ci skill — now bitten in anger.
  2. **Internal-only tests can't pass in an opensource build by design.**
     `test_export_no_pkg_collision.py` does `from export import …` but export.py
     is the maintainer tool, intentionally not shipped → `ModuleNotFoundError:
     No module named 'export'`. `test_mcp_catalog_internal_only.py`
     (`test_internal_entries_present_in_internal_build`, `_flagged`) +
     `test_mcp_call_health.py::test_hope_card_ships_360s_default` assert
     hope/llm/xuecheng MCP cards are present, but those launchers are stripped
     and `TOFU_OPENSOURCE_BUILD` is baked on. **Fix (source):** guard them to
     self-skip in opensource — `pytest.importorskip('export', …)` (module-level)
     and `@pytest.mark.skipif(is_opensource_build(), …)`. They still RUN+PASS in
     the source tree (verified 18 passed there). The hidden-in-opensource /
     no-leak assertions in the same files keep running in both builds.
  3. **CI lint job was already RED before today.** Exported `.github/workflows/
     ci.yml` runs `ruff check .` (WHOLE tree), but `ruff.toml`'s header only
     documents `ruff check lib/ routes/ tests/` and has NO `exclude`. The shipped
     `debug/` dir (148 scratch/benchmark scripts, never imported by the app)
     tripped **446** F-errors → lint red since at least the v0.13.0 push. **Fix:**
     added `'debug'` to `OPENSOURCE_EXTRA_EXCLUDE_DIRS` in export.py (same class
     as scripts/benchmarks/outputs/posters). Also removed a stale orphan
     `install.py` (1 F541; gone from source since v0.10.0, survived only because
     the tar-pipe export OVERLAYS and never deletes removed-from-source files).
     `ruff check .` on the final tree → All checks passed.
- **EXPORT TAR-PIPE GOTCHA (recorded for next time):** the export is an additive
  tar overlay — files removed from source (or newly dir-excluded) are NOT deleted
  from the dest. After adding a dir to OPENSOURCE_EXTRA_EXCLUDE_DIRS you must
  `git rm -r --quiet <dir> && rm -rf <dir>` in the dest to actually drop it;
  same for orphan files. The exclude only stops the NEXT copy from re-adding it.
- **Result:** unit tier 40 → **2** failures; `ruff check .` clean. The 2 left
  (`test_pg_copy_self_heal::test_step3_still_defers_for_same_path_remote`,
  `test_swarm_async::TestAwaitAgents::test_await_no_ids_includes_early_finishers`)
  are PRE-EXISTING real bugs — fail in source too, both test files byte-identical
  to v0.13.0 push, production code untouched → CI was already red on exactly
  these 2 before my work; not a regression I introduced. One is already flagged
  in this journal as deliberately-not-touched (load-bearing conn-accounting race).
- **Push:** internal exported to ../tofu-meituan (local only, push disabled by
  policy). Opensource pushed via the standard pipeline to BOTH origin
  (rangehow/ToFu) and niutrans (NiuTrans/ToFu) on main — commit d05010a. No
  `--bump` (regular sync, not a release). Verified final pushed tree: debug=0,
  install.py=0, working tree clean, ruff clean.


### 2026-06-26 — Two write-tool fixes from a forensic question: temp-dir scratch writes are now UNTRACKED, and silent absolute-path workspace-root auto-registration is now OBSERVABLE (new `workspace_root_added` event)
- **Origin:** user noticed a session where the agent "started writing to
  `llm-mcp`" with no tool call shown, file edits counted under the
  `llm_platform:` prefix, and asked whether `/tmp` files should get a prefix.
  Diagnosis (confirmed against code): (1) `_resolve_write_path`
  (`lib/project_mod/write_tools.py`) silently `add_project_root()`s the nearest
  existing ancestor on an absolute-path write outside all roots — no SSE/tool
  round, only an `app.log` line; (2) `_mod_attribution` maps to the deepest
  *registered* root, so `llm-mcp` being a SUBDIR of the `llm_platform` root
  means no extra root was ever created and the `llm_platform:` prefix is honest;
  (3) `_FORBIDDEN_CREATE_ROOTS` omits `/tmp`, so `write_file('/tmp/x.py', …)`
  would auto-register a bogus `tmp:` root + journal the edit, while
  `run_command` writes to `/tmp` stay untracked (snapshot only walks
  `base_path`). The temp inconsistency was a genuine latent bug.
- **Fix 1 — temp scratch is untracked (root-cause, no hardcoded paths):** new
  `_temp_roots()` (cached; sourced from `tempfile.gettempdir()` honouring
  `$TMPDIR`/`$TEMP`/`$TMP`, plus `/tmp` + `/var/tmp` realpath-normalized
  fallbacks) + `_is_temp_path()`. `_resolve_write_path` now has a step **1.5**
  (AFTER the registered-root check, BEFORE system-path refusal): a temp-dir
  target returns the abspath WITHOUT registering a root. The three write fns
  gate `_record_modification` behind new `_should_record_modification(target)`
  — which skips ONLY temp paths that fall OUTSIDE all registered roots (a user
  who legitimately opens a project under `/tmp/proj` is still tracked). Net:
  `write_file` to `/tmp` now behaves exactly like `run_command` to `/tmp` —
  completes, never appears in the file-changes bar or undo history.
- **Fix 2 — observable auto-registration (new event):** registered
  `EventType.WORKSPACE_ROOT_ADDED` (`workspace_root_added`, CONTEXT category)
  in `lib/agent_core/events.py`. The write layer (which has only
  `conv_id`/`task_id`, not `task`) signals a genuinely-NEW root via a
  per-thread collector (`_signal_root_added` / `drain_root_added_signals` on a
  `threading.local`) — race-free because the
  handler→`execute_tool`→`_resolve_write_path` chain is synchronous in one
  thread and `execute_tool` stringifies the write result (dropping extra
  fields, so the dict can't carry the signal). `_resolve_write_path` only
  signals when the anchor wasn't already a root (re-resolved roots are silent).
  `lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/project.py` drains the signal right after the write
  tool runs (next to the artifact-promotion post-hook, the established
  precedent) and emits via `emit(task, WORKSPACE_ROOT_ADDED, roots=[…])`.
  Frontend: `_handleWorkspaceRootAdded` (`static/js/ui/sse_handlers_misc.js`) +
  dispatch branch (`ui/sse_pipeline.js`) → a brief `showToast` naming the added
  root(s); i18n key `workspaceRoot.added` (zh+en).
- **Tests (`tests/test_temp_write_and_root_signal.py`, 9, all pass):** temp
  detection; temp write → succeeds, no root registered, no signal, no
  modification recorded; `_resolve_write_path` temp returns abspath + no root;
  non-temp abs write outside roots → NEW root registered + exactly one
  `{rootName,path}` signal + consume-once drain; subdir-of-existing-root write
  (the `llm_platform/llm-mcp` case) → no new root, no signal, BUT still
  journaled. Hermetic temp-root detection: the suite overrides
  `_temp_roots._cache` to a designated subdir (so `mkdtemp`'s own temp-dir
  ancestry doesn't pollute the "non-temp" fixtures) and restores it in
  tearDown.
- **Verification:** `test_temp_write_and_root_signal` (9) +
  `test_readonly_roots` (12, regression — write/RO funnel through the same
  `_resolve_write_path`) + `test_event_registry` (5, orphan check green — new
  type is both backend-emitted and frontend-handled) + `test_event_emit` (12) =
  **38 passed**. `ast.parse` clean on all 4 Python files; `node --check` clean
  on all 3 JS files. Bundle rebuilt **`bundle-c7277075.js`** — confirmed
  `_handleWorkspaceRootAdded` / `workspace_root_added` / `workspaceRoot.added`
  all present. Restart + hard-refresh to serve.



### 2026-06-26 — Chrome Web Store submission kit for the Browser Bridge extension (`docs/chrome-web-store/` + `scripts/package_extension.sh`)
- **Why:** User wants the browser extension listed so install is one-click
  instead of download-ZIP + drag-to-`chrome://extensions`. Chose "option B"
  (prep the Chrome Web Store submission) over Firefox AMO. The submission itself
  needs the user's Google account + $5 registration + identity — cannot be
  automated; I prepared 100% of the materials.
- **Key finding — 6 of 16 manifest permissions are DEAD:** grep of
  `browser_extension/` proved `webNavigation`, `clipboardRead`, `clipboardWrite`,
  `declarativeNetRequest`, `management`, `offscreen` appear ONLY in
  `manifest.json`, never called in `background.js`/`popup.js` (tab-load waiting
  uses `chrome.tabs.onUpdated` → needs only `tabs`; no clipboard/DNR/management/
  offscreen calls anywhere). Unused perms = automatic review rejection + scarier
  install warning. `management` especially is a classic reject trigger. The
  store build drops all 6.
- **Verified-USED heavy perms (kept, each justified):** `<all_urls>`,
  `scripting`, `tabs`, `activeTab`, `storage`, `cookies` (getAll/set/remove),
  `history` (search), `bookmarks` (getTree), `debugger` (ONLY for full-page
  `Page.captureScreenshot` via CDP), `notifications`, `alarms` (MV3 keep-alive).
- **Deliverables (all in `docs/chrome-web-store/`):** `README.md` (index +
  expectation-setting), `LISTING.md` (name/summary/description/category),
  `PERMISSIONS_JUSTIFICATION.md` (per-perm blocks + the removed-6 rationale),
  `manifest.store.json` (trimmed to 10 perms + added missing `icons` block),
  `PRIVACY.md` (hostable policy + data-usage form answers + remote-code Yes
  explanation), `ASSETS_CHECKLIST.md` (icon/screenshot sizes + shot list),
  `REVIEW_RISKS.md` (5 concrete policy risks + fallback ladder),
  `SUBMISSION_CHECKLIST.md` (register→package→fill→submit→respond).
- **`scripts/package_extension.sh`:** builds `dist/tofu-browser-bridge-<ver>[-store].zip`
  from the 7 real extension files (never the whole repo); `--store` swaps in the
  trimmed manifest. Tested both builds; store zip validated (10 perms, valid
  JSON). `dist/` already gitignored. Icons confirmed 16/48/128 exact sizes.
- **HONEST risk call (documented, not hidden):** the extension runs
  server-pushed JS (`browser_execute_js`) → trips the Web Store **remote-code**
  policy; `debugger` + broad perms trip **min-permissions**. First-pass
  rejection is the LIKELY outcome. REVIEW_RISKS.md lays out the fallback: ship a
  reduced Chrome build (no `browser_execute_js`, no `debugger`) or go Firefox
  AMO. Told the user this is a decision to make before spending review cycles.
- **Follow-up when accepted:** wire an "Add from Chrome Web Store" button into
  the `#browserModal` (index.html) using the item id, keeping the unpacked-ZIP
  flow as fallback. Deferred until there's a real item id.

### 2026-06-26 — Ran the ENLARGED unit tier end-to-end; drove it from 42 → 3 failures by fixing systemic auth-mode pollution + a task-registry 500, leaving only 3 pre-existing real bugs
- **Why:** after auto-marking the previously-unmarked ~1900 tests into the
  `unit` tier, those tests run in CI for the first time. Ran the full
  `pytest -m unit` (3150 tests) to completion — NOT trusting the partitioned
  sampling — because the only way to know the enlarged tier is green is to run
  it as CI will. First full run: **42 failures** that the parallel partitions
  had NOT shown, because most were CROSS-TEST POLLUTION that only manifests in
  one sequential process.
- **Measurement gotchas (recorded for next time):** (1) `-p no:logging`
  inflates failures — it disables the logging plugin and breaks every
  logging-assertion test (7 phantom errors). (2) Daemon threads (scheduler /
  swarm autocontinue) write to fd1/fd2 after teardown, burying pytest's summary
  line — capture results with `--junit-xml` and parse the XML, don't grep
  stdout. (3) `pytest-reportlog` isn't installed; `--report-log` is silently
  ignored.
- **Triage method:** for every full-run failure, re-run the file ALONE.
  Pass-alone ⇒ pollution (find the leaker or harden the global). Fail-alone ⇒
  real. This cleanly split 42 → {27 auth-contract, ~9 pollution, 6 code-quality
  (slow), 1 chat-poll route, 3 genuinely-real}.
- **Root cause #1 — auth-mode pollution (the big one).** The credential gate
  (`routes/api_v1/auth.py::bearer_auth_before_request`) is a NO-OP in `open`
  mode (conftest's default): unauthenticated / invalid-token requests get a
  synthetic admin principal and return 200, and the per-key usage counter
  (step 7) never records. ~27 `*_requires_auth` / `invalid_token` /
  `usage_for_self` assertions therefore needed `private` mode. The self-
  contained `unittest.TestCase` auth files were setting
  `os.environ['TOFU_AUTH_MODE']='private'` in `setUpClass` and restoring in
  `tearDownClass` — which is BOTH insufficient (setUpClass runs ONCE, outside
  the per-test fixture window) AND a leak source (a class that forgot to
  restore poisoned every downstream test). **Fix, two layers:**
  - **conftest `_auth_mode_override`** now captures a session `_AUTH_MODE_
    BASELINE` and restores it on test EXIT ONLY (cleans any leak), while a
    `@pytest.mark.auth_mode(...)` marker sets the mode on ENTRY. Critically it
    does NOT force the baseline on entry — an earlier attempt that did clobbered
    classes whose setUpClass legitimately set private, surfacing as a route
    `TypeError` (handler ran without an auth context).
  - **Converted every auth-contract file to a class-level `pytestmark =
    pytest.mark.auth_mode('private')`** (re-applies per test) and DELETED the
    setUpClass/tearDownClass env mutation: test_api_v1_integration,
    test_e2e_headless_api, test_sdk_e2e, test_ecosystem_sdk_compat,
    test_usage_and_metrics_routes, test_agent_poll_routes, test_orchestrations
    (CrudTest + TaskRunHttpTest). `pytestmark` reaches `unittest.TestCase`
    methods (verified). In-process-server files (sdk_e2e) work because the
    server reads the mode per-request and the fixture sets it before each test.
- **Root cause #2 — task-registry 500 polluting 3 server-route tests.**
  `routes/chat.py::chat_active` did `t['convId']` (hard key) over the process-
  global `tasks` registry. Tests / external harnesses insert legacy/minimal
  task dicts without `convId`; a later `GET /api/v1/chat/active` then 500s with
  `KeyError: 'convId'`, failing `test_server_async` (health, json_compressed)
  and `test_restart_smoke::test_sync_route_runs_under_quart`. **Fix:** read
  every field defensively (`t.get('convId','')`, …) — correct hardening for a
  shared mutable registry, cannot regress (real tasks always have the keys).
- **Slow/expensive tests re-tiered (per the "tag slow ones slow" directive):**
  `test_code_quality.py` (~6-min full-tree AST scan, also pollution-flaky) →
  module `pytestmark = pytest.mark.slow`; `test_cost_comparison` (real paid LLM
  call) → `@pytest.mark.live_llm`. Both leave the default unit/ci tier (run in
  dedicated steps). This alone cut the tier from ~960s → ~390s.
- **Plus the route-migration stragglers the full run exposed:**
  `/api/v1/chat/poll` (test_chat_manager_migration), and the auth files' own
  invalid-token paths.
- **Progression (each a full `pytest -m unit` run, junit-parsed):**
  42 → 21 → 13 → 6 → **3** failures; 3150 tests; ~390s; 7 skipped.
- **The 3 remaining are pre-existing REAL bugs, NOT test-script defects (left
  for follow-up, explicitly out of "organize the test scripts" scope):**
  1. `test_frontend_typecheck` — real TS2339 in `paper-reader.js:2248`
     (`bar._readWords`/`_readTotalMin` DOM expandos need a `globals.d.ts` decl).
  2. `test_swarm_async::test_await_no_ids_includes_early_finishers` — real race
     in `await_agents` (snapshots too early, drops an early finisher; fails in
     isolation).
  3. `test_db_thread_conn_lifecycle::test_close_thread_db_releases_for_reuse` —
     PG-only; its `active-pooled==baseline` exact-equality races concurrent
     daemons (billing-janitor/scheduler) in the full sequential run; passes in
     isolation + partitions. A test-isolation fragility in load-bearing conn-
     accounting assertions — not touched to avoid a wrong fix.
- **Verification discipline:** every fix re-validated by (a) the touched files
  together AND (b) a fresh full-tier junit run, so pollution fixes are proven
  against the real sequential ordering, not just in isolation. Backend changes:
  `routes/chat.py` (1-line defensive read) + `tests/conftest.py` + test files.
  No JS/CSS → no bundle rebuild.


### 2026-06-26 — Autopilot couldn't run ANY command + the cryptic `X exit ?` badge: a conv_id mismatch routed run_command's read-only check to the wrong (race-clobbered) root registry, and marker-less refusals rendered as `exit ?`
- **User report (screenshot):** an Autopilot worker bubble's `run_command`
  rounds (`python -m pytest …`, `cd /tmp && python -m pytest …`) showed a red
  **`X exit ?`** badge; the model then said *"I can't run commands here, so let
  me verify by reading the actual files."* Asked: why can't autopilot run code,
  and why is the error so opaque?
- **Forensics (DB-confirmed, conv `mqudxzusnh3eme`, autopilot VU sub-task
  `4832ea83`):** the two failing rounds are stored as `exitCode='?'`,
  `output=''`, `badge='exit ?'`, `kind=user`. Crucially the raw `toolContent`
  was: **`"run_command refused: the working directory '…/chatui' is inside a
  READ-ONLY workspace root…"`**. There is NO `run_command: $ …` execution log
  line between the round's tool_start events — the command was refused before it
  ran. (`read_files`/`grep_search` in the SAME VU worked.)
- **Root cause A — functional (why autopilot can't run code): conv_id mismatch.**
  Workspace roots are REGISTERED under `task.get('convId') or task.get('id')`
  (`orchestrator.py` ~L1095) and read back the same way by the streaming tool
  executor (`streaming_tool_executor.py:262`, which is why read_files/grep
  worked). But the project-tool handler executed `run_command` with the BARE
  `conv_id=task['convId']` (`handlers/project.py:281,296`). The autopilot VU
  sub-task is deliberately created with `convId=''`, so its roots register under
  its TASK id (RW, parent had `readonly=0`) but the run_command read-only check
  used `''` → fell back to the globally-shared `_roots` registry, which under
  concurrency had been clobbered to `access='ro'` by an unrelated task. `pytest`
  is classified *destructive* by `_is_destructive_command` (everything
  non-whitelisted is), so the RO-root guard (`project_mod/tools.py:640`) refused
  it. **Fix:** `handlers/project.py` now computes
  `_root_conv_id = task.get('convId') or task.get('id') or ''` and uses it for
  BOTH the no-project read_files branch and the main `execute_tool` call —
  exactly mirroring how roots are registered and how the streaming executor
  reads them. One key everywhere; sub-tasks with empty convId resolve their own
  RW roots instead of leaking into the shared registry.
- **Root cause B — UX (the meaningless badge): marker-less refusals rendered as
  `exit ?`.** Every `run_command` guard/refusal/skip/start-error returns a
  plain-text string with NO `[exit code: N]` marker (read-only refusal,
  `Error: No project path.`, dangerous-pattern block, catastrophic-delete,
  `Empty command`, pre-hook block, `Task aborted by user.`, start errors).
  `_build_run_command` (`lib/tools/meta.py`) parsed any marker-less string to
  `exitCode='?'` + (often) empty output → the frontend's `meta.exitCode ?? "?"`
  rendered the cryptic red **`✗ exit ?`** and discarded the actual reason.
  **Fix:** when the `[exit code]` marker is absent AND it isn't a timeout, the
  command NEVER RAN — classify it as `exitCode='not-run'`, `notRun=True`, set
  `reason`/`output` to the full message, and pick a specific human badge via new
  `_classify_not_run_badge()` (`read-only` / `no project` / `blocked` /
  `aborted` / `empty` / `start failed` / `not run`). Same logic mirrored in the
  code_exec handler (`handlers/code_exec.py`). Commands that DID run (carry the
  marker) are completely unaffected — incl. the end-anchored exit-code parse
  that ignores `[exit code: N]` inside the command's own stdout.
- **Frontend (`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`):** the run_command/code_exec block
  now detects `notRun` (`meta.notRun===true || exitCode==='not-run'`), renders a
  distinct amber `⊘ <badge>` status (class `.ptool-cmd-notrun`) and shows the
  reason INLINE (new `.ptool-cmd-reason`, not hidden behind the collapse toggle)
  so the user sees *why* immediately — never `✗ exit ?` again. CSS added for
  base + `[data-theme="light"]` + `[data-theme="tofu"]` (reuses the timeout
  amber palette).
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_run_command_not_run_meta.py` (13, all pass):
  every marker-less refusal → `not-run` + correct badge + reason surfaced + never
  `'?'`; success/failure/negative-exit/timeout/abort-with-marker/own-stdout-marker
  all unaffected. `test_read_before_edit_gate` (20) + `test_write_approval_gate`
  (12) + autopilot suites `arm`/`kick`/`verify` (39) all green. `ast.parse` clean
  on the 3 Python files; `node --check` clean on tool_rounds.js. `tool_rounds.js`
  already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → restart rebuilds the bundle, hard-refresh to serve.
- **Note (deeper truth):** in a GENUINELY read-only root, `run_command` running
  `pytest` will still be refused (by design — `_is_destructive_command` treats
  any non-whitelisted command as a mutator). That's correct; the autopilot bug
  was purely the conv_id mis-routing making an RW root *look* read-only. The UX
  fix ensures that even a legitimate refusal now states its cause clearly.

- **Symptom (user screenshot, MCP rows):** `llm/experiment_fork` rows showed a

### 2026-06-26 — Personal-preference profile, OPTIMIZATION: moved the layer-3 consolidation OFF the synchronous done path into a daemon thread (was adding a cheap-LLM round-trip to EVERY substantive turn's completion)
- **Problem (reviewer-caught, contradicted the "optimize this" objective):** the
  layer-3 consolidation pass was called INLINE in `_finalize_and_emit_done`,
  right before `append_event(task, done_evt)`, gated only on
  `memory_enabled and has_real_tools and not error`. So every substantive
  tool-using turn BLOCKED its own completion on a full cheap-LLM round-trip —
  pure added latency on the common path (most turns yield zero preference
  change), and under the rate-limiting this journal documents, that cheap call
  can itself stall for seconds. Shipping a per-turn synchronous LLM call that
  delays every completion is the opposite of optimized.
- **Fix — mirror `_spawn_async_commit_round`** (the established pattern for
  "run after the done event in a daemon thread, deliver via a follow-up SSE"):
  - **`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`:** removed the inline consolidation block
    entirely. The tail of `_finalize_and_emit_done` is now
    `append_event(done_evt) → persist_task_result → _spawn_async_commit_round →
    _spawn_async_profile_consolidation`. The consolidation call no longer sits
    on the path between loop-exit and the done event. The gate
    (`memory_enabled and has_real_tools`) is stashed as
    `task['_profileConsolidateEligible']` at the prefetch gate (where both
    locals are in scope; `_finalize`'s signature has neither).
  - **`lib/tasks_pkg/commit_round.py` (NEW fns, next to the commit-round
    spawner):** `_spawn_async_profile_consolidation(task, messages, cfg)` →
    daemon thread (gated on `_profileConsolidateEligible` + no error) →
    `_run_profile_consolidation_async` runs `run_profile_consolidation`, then for
    each learned/staged pref emits a post-done `preference_learned` event via
    `append_event` (best-effort live SSE/push fan-out) AND persists onto the
    conversation's assistant message via `_patch_assistant_message_with_prefs`
    (mirrors `_patch_assistant_message_with_git`, so the chip survives reload
    even when the SSE reader already closed). `messages` captured by reference —
    consolidation only READS it, so a post-done snapshot is fine.
- **Frontend: ZERO changes.** The `preference_learned` event, the chip renderer,
  the Confirm/Dismiss wiring, and the snapshot/poll restore are all unchanged —
  only the trigger moved sync→async, emitting the SAME event a beat later.
  Bundle unchanged (`bundle-a54bf517.js`); backend-only → just restart.
- **Tests (3 new, all pass) — proving the done path no longer waits:**
  - `test_consolidation_spawn_does_not_block_done` — makes the consolidation
    pass `sleep(2.0)`; asserts `_spawn_async_profile_consolidation` RETURNS in
    `< 1.0s` (essentially instant), then confirms the daemon really started the
    slow work in the background. This is the direct proof the cheap-LLM
    round-trip is off the synchronous path.
  - `test_consolidation_gated_off_spawns_nothing` — ineligible flag / error →
    no thread spawned, consolidation never called.
  - `test_consolidation_daemon_emits_preference_learned` — the daemon body
    produces the `preference_learned` event(s) + stashes `_preferencesLearned`
    on the task (event still reaches the frontend).
- **No regression:** `test_user_profile.py` 22/22 (incl. the earlier over-cap
  distil + cross-task cache-safety required tests, still green) +
  `test_event_registry` 5/5 + `test_cache_improvements` + `test_streaming_and_prefetch`
  = **103 passed**. `ast.parse` clean on both touched Python files. Endpoint-mode
  tasks early-return before the spawner (they don't run consolidation) — an
  acceptable scope limit, not a regression.


### 2026-06-26 — Fixed browser-extension ZIP download 500 (`send_file() got an unexpected keyword argument 'download_name'`) at the Flask→Quart shim
- **Symptom:** `GET /api/browser/download` returned a 500 internal-error envelope
  with `raw: "send_file() got an unexpected keyword argument 'download_name'"`.
- **Root cause:** installed **Quart 0.19.5**'s `send_file` / `send_from_directory`
  still use the pre-Flask-2.0 kwarg name `attachment_filename`; they do NOT accept
  Flask 2.0+'s renamed `download_name`. Route code (`routes/browser.py:179`,
  `routes/translate.py:155`) does `from flask import send_file` — which resolves
  to Quart's version via the `_install_flask_shim()` in `server.py` — and passes
  the modern `download_name`, so Quart raised `TypeError`. Two latent call sites,
  same bug.
- **Fix:** added `_compat_download_name()` adapter in `server.py::_install_flask_shim`
  that wraps the genuine async `send_file`/`send_from_directory` BEFORE `_sync_safe`,
  and — only when the target signature lacks `download_name` but has
  `attachment_filename` — renames the kwarg. Keeps route code on the standard
  modern Flask spelling regardless of installed Quart version, and is forward-safe
  (no-op once Quart adds `download_name`). Marked the adapter with
  `__wrapped__`/`_quart_async_wrapper` so `_genuine()` unwraps cleanly on re-import.
- **Verified:** `download_name='x.zip'` now flows into Quart's real `send_file`
  body (only fails afterward on the unrelated "Not within an app context", as
  expected outside a request). `ast.parse` clean on server.py. Restart required.

### 2026-06-26 — Personal-preference profile, LAYER 3: the propose-then-confirm consolidation loop + the "Noted: you prefer X" moment (now the feature delivers real value — something finally WRITES the profile)
- **Why:** Layers 1+2+chip (earlier today) put a bounded, always-on, cache-safe
  profile in place, but NOTHING ever wrote `.tofu_user_profile.md`, so the
  "preferences applied" chip could never fire in real use — zero visible value.
  Layer 3 is the writer: a post-turn consolidation pass that learns preferences
  and stages new ones behind a confirm gate.
- **Consolidation entry point — `lib/memory/profile_consolidate.py` (NEW):**
  `run_profile_consolidation(messages, task)` reuses the SAME cheap model wired
  in `prefetch.py` (`dispatch_chat(capability='cheap')`). It feeds the model the
  current profile + recent surface (`_build_recent_turns_text`, reused) and asks
  for a conservative JSON `actions` list. Three action kinds:
  - **reinforce** → AUTO-applied via `apply_reinforcement` (Hermes-style
    replace-by-unique-substring; ambiguous/missing match = no-op).
  - **new** → STAGED via `stage_pending` (NEVER written silently — the gate).
  - **distil** → AUTO-applied full-body rewrite, ONLY offered when the profile
    is over cap (the cap's forcing function). Best-effort: any failure logs +
    returns []. Gated on `PROFILE_CONSOLIDATE` flag.
- **Trigger:** `lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py` runs it right BEFORE the done
  event (gated `memory_enabled and has_real_tools and not error`), so each
  learned/staged item rides the SAME done SSE stream as a `preference_learned`
  event. `preference_learned` re-added to `lib/agent_core/events.py` (removed in
  the layer-1 pass because the orphan test correctly rejects a
  registered-but-unwired type — now it's wired, registry green again).
- **Propose-then-confirm gate (storage, `lib/memory/user_profile.py`):** new
  primitives `apply_reinforcement` (replace-in-place), `apply_new_preference`
  (append-under-header, cap-flagged), and a pending store
  (`stage_pending`/`load_pending`/`resolve_pending`) persisted to
  `.tofu_user_profile_pending.json` (registered in `agent_artifacts.py` as
  `USER_PROFILE_PENDING_FILE`). `resolve_pending(id, accept, edited_text)` is
  the confirm/dismiss path — accept writes the (optionally user-edited) text;
  either way the proposal is removed.
- **REST surface (`routes/api_v1/memory.py`):** `GET /api/v1/profile`
  (`{body, chars, cap, over_cap, pending}`), `PUT /api/v1/profile` (hand-edit /
  clear), `POST /api/v1/profile/pending/<id>` (`{accept, text?}`). The frontend
  Confirm/Dismiss buttons POST the last.
- **The "Noted: you prefer X" moment (frontend):** new
  `renderPreferenceLearnedHtml` (`tool_rounds.js`) renders a card per
  learned/staged pref; PENDING rows show Confirm/Dismiss buttons wired to

### 2026-06-26 — Personal-preference profile (layers 1+2+chip): a bounded, always-on, cache-safe `USER.md`-style profile injected on the `_isMeta` tail, with a quiet "preferences applied" chip
- **Why:** Our memory store is 100%-task-flavored (60+ `.tofu/skills` notes, 40
  global — all bug patterns / subsystem maps / API quirks; ZERO personal
  preferences). Both placements we had are wrong for a standing preference: the
  BP1–3 system prefix is cache-poison for anything that mutates (the
  memory-count hint was ripped out for this; the timestamp A/B showed 4.3×), and
  the per-turn BM25 prefetch reranker is *designed to drop* anything without a
  task-step (so "always answer in Chinese" never survives). Prior art (OpenClaw
  `USER.md`, Hermes Agent bounded `USER.md` + post-turn consolidation) converges
  on a small, bounded, **always-injected** file refined in place — with a hard
  cap as the forcing function.
- **Design pivot:** a preference must be BOTH always-on AND cache-stable. The
  trick (same as CLAUDE.md placement): put it on the prepended `_isMeta` user
  message (BP4 5-min-TTL tail), NEVER messages[0]. A profile edit then re-writes
  only the cheap tail once; the expensive system+tools prefix stays cached.
- **Layer 1 — storage (`lib/memory/user_profile.py`, NEW):** ONE bounded file,
  global/per-user, at `<data>/memories/.tofu_user_profile.md`. NOT part of the
  BM25 corpus — never searched, always present. Hard cap `USER_PROFILE_CHAR_CAP
  = 2500` (~800 tok); over-cap is FLAGGED not truncated (truncation corrupts
  meaning; the flag is the forcing function for the layer-3 consolidation pass).
  `load_profile`/`save_profile` (atomic via `write_text_atomic`; empty body
  deletes the file)/`render_profile_block` (wraps in `<system-reminder>` with
  marker `[USER PREFERENCE PROFILE]`)/`profile_summary_for_event` (bullet lines
  for the chip). Registered in `lib/agent_artifacts.py` as `USER_PROFILE_FILE`
  (`.tofu_user_profile.md`) so the `.tofu` prefix makes every consumer
  (gitignore/export/self-update) recognise it mechanically.
- **Layer 2 — cache-safe injection (`lib/tasks_pkg/system_context.py`):** new
  step ★2.5 in `_inject_system_contexts` (gated on `memory_enabled`), after
  CLAUDE.md. New helper `_append_user_profile_block(messages, block)` appends the
  block to the `_isMeta` carrier (falls back to the first real user msg when
  project mode is off → still the tail, still not messages[0]). It is
  self-idempotent (scans every msg for the marker → endpoint re-entry /
  post-compaction safe). **CRITICAL:** after injecting it calls
  `notify_compaction(conv_id)` because, after round 1, the `_isMeta` carrier
  sits inside `messages[0:N-2]` and would otherwise trip `PREFIX MUTATION
  DETECTED` every round (see `cache-tracking-prefix-mutation-mutators` memory).
  Stashes `task['_appliedPreferences'] = {chars, items}`.
- **The "let users SEE it" requirement (chip):** new registered event
  `preferences_applied` (`lib/agent_core/events.py`), emitted ONCE at task start
  by the orchestrator from `task['_appliedPreferences']`. Persisted to the last
  message (`manager.py` both sites) + to the state-snapshot & poll-response
  (`routes/chat.py`) as `preferencesApplied`, so it survives reload / SSE
  reconnect / poll fallback. Frontend: `renderPreferencesAppliedHtml`
  (`tool_rounds.js`) — a QUIET, collapsed-by-default chip in the SAME visual
  family as the memory-prefetch chip (`.mem-prefetch-chip`) but a calmer teal
  accent (`.pa-chip` in `styles.css`); expands to list which preferences were in
  play. Wired into both render paths (`chat_render.js` finished + `streaming_ui.js`
  streaming, with fp), the SSE handler (`_handlePreferencesApplied` in
  `sse_handlers_misc.js` + dispatch in `sse_pipeline.js`), the state-snapshot
  restore, and the poll fallback. New icon `sliders` in `core/icons.js`; i18n
  keys `prefs.applied`/`prefs.appliedN`/`prefs.fromProfile` (zh+en).
- **Deliberately deferred to pass 2 (per build order):** the propose-confirm
  consolidation loop (the `preference_learned` "Noted: you prefer X" + undo/edit
  moment). I registered then REMOVED the `preference_learned` event spec because
  `test_event_registry`'s orphan check correctly fails a registered-but-unwired
  type — it goes back in when layer 3 emits it.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_user_profile.py` (11, all pass): storage
  round-trip, empty-clears-file, over-cap flagged-not-truncated, render+summary,
  artifact-registry registration, event registered, injection lands on `_isMeta`
  tail (system msg untouched), idempotent, no-meta fallback, and the **HARD
  acceptance criterion** — `test_profile_injection_is_cache_safe` drives 3 real
  rounds of `_append_user_profile_block` + `notify_compaction` + `detect_cache_break`
  and asserts NO `prefix_mutation` break and `total_breaks == 0`, with a negative
  control (`test_without_notify_would_flag`) proving the guard is actually
  exercised. `test_event_registry` 5/5 (no orphan). `ast.parse` clean on all 7
  Python files; `node --check` clean on all 8 JS files. Bundle rebuilt
  **`bundle-b06f70dd.js`** (all JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; no new
  top-level module) — confirmed `renderPreferencesAppliedHtml` / `preferences_applied`
  / `sliders` / `prefs.appliedN` all present in the built bundle. Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve.

### 2026-06-26 — Update modal: surface the CONCRETE check-failure reason (no more vague "try again later") + polish hero/badge/error-card elements
- **User ask (two parts):** (1) the software-update modal's inner elements
  still don't look great — optimize them; (2) the failure copy "无法检查更新，
  请稍后再试 / Could not check for updates. Please try again later." is useless —
  whatever the reason (backend connection lost, GitHub unreachable, rate-limited,
  timeout), STATE IT DIRECTLY.
- **Root cause of the uninformative error (3 layers all collapsed the cause):**
  1. `lib/self_update.py::fetch_latest_release()` returned `None` on ANY failure
     (network / HTTP / parse / no-tags) and `check_for_update()` flattened all of
     it into one string `'Could not determine the latest release.'`.
  2. `static/js/api.js` `Api.update.check` is declared with `onError:'null'`, so a
     thrown `ApiError` (backend down / 500 / timeout) became a silent `null` — the
     frontend literally could not tell "our server is down" from "GitHub is down".
  3. `update.js::_runUpdateCheck` rendered a single hard-coded `t('update.checkFailed')`
     regardless of cause.
- **Fix — backend names the concrete cause** (`lib/self_update.py`): new
  `_fetch_latest_release_detailed() -> (payload, error)` where `error` is
  `{kind, detail, status?}` with `kind ∈ network | rate_limited (403/429) | http |
  parse | no_tags`. `fetch_latest_release()` kept as a thin wrapper (drops the
  detail) so existing callers/`__all__`/tests are unchanged. `check_for_update()`
  now adds `error_kind` + `error_detail` to the payload and sets `error` to a
  cause-specific English fallback. Verified by a throwaway harness: monkeypatched
  `http_get` → `network`/`rate_limited`/`no_tags` all classify correctly.
- **Fix — frontend reads the real cause** (`static/js/update.js`):
  `_runUpdateCheck` now calls `Api.update.check({timeout:12000, onError:'throw'})`
  (overrides the default null) and routes through two new classifiers:
  `_classifyCheckError(ApiError)` distinguishes **backend unreachable** (code
  `network`/`TypeError`) vs **request timed out** (code `timeout`/`AbortError`)
  vs **backend HTTP N** (`e.status>0`); `_githubFailureReason(kind, detail)` maps
  the backend's `error_kind` to localized copy. New `_renderCheckError({title,
  reason})` paints a proper error card (circle-! SVG glyph per §3.4 — no emoji,
  heading + the real reason + a retry button with a refresh icon).
- **i18n** (`static/js/i18n.js`): added `update.checkFailTitle` + per-cause keys
  `errBackend / errBackendHttp / errTimeout / errNetwork / errRateLimited /
  errHttp / errParse / errNoTags / errUnknown` (zh+en). The old vague
  `update.checkFailed` is retained (unused by the new path, left for safety).
- **Visual polish** (`static/styles.css`, base + `[data-theme="tofu"]`):
  - New `.upd-err-card` / `.upd-err-head` / `.upd-err-icon` / `.upd-err-title` /
    `.upd-err-reason` — centered card, ink heading, muted reason, retry chip.
  - `.upd-badge` centered + bolder; the up-to-date `ok` badge gets a rounded
    (tofu: square gold) icon chip behind its check.
  - `.upd-hero`: more breathing room (gap 6→10, padding 18→20, label letter-
    spacing, ver-num 21→22px + tighter tracking). The up-to-date hero now dims
    the arrow (opacity .4) so the redundant "v0.13.0 → v0.13.0" reads as one
    statement instead of a confusing same-number pair.
- **Verification:** `node --check` clean on update.js + i18n.js; `ast.parse`
  clean on self_update.py; the error-kind harness prints the right
  kind+message for network/403/no_tags; `test_self_update_tarball.py` 5/5 green
  (the `check_for_update` update_method assertions still hold — the new keys are
  additive). update.js + i18n.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → no bundler list
  change; restart rebuilds the bundle, hard-refresh to serve.

  - `ask_human`: title/badge de-emoji'd (🙋/✅/⛔/❌ → plain `answered`/`aborted`/

  - scheduler/desktop `simple_call(icon='⏰'/'🖥️')` → dropped the `icon=` kwarg.

- **Fix — `lib/tasks_pkg/executor_image.py`:** image-gen progress/error badges
  `'⏳ editing…'` / `'⏳ generating…'` / `'⏳ rate limited…'` / `'❌ failed'` →
  emoji-free. Kept `✓ {model}` / `⚠ svg failed` (allowed typographic dingbats
  per §3.4 allowlist) and the `✓`/`✗` in LOG strings (console out of scope).

  (+ conv/compact/mcp) were already added in part 1; bundle already
  `bundle-e17ca352.js`. These edits are backend-only → just restart the server.

  comments + allowed `✓`/`⚠`/`✗` dingbats remain. Runtime: `_build_await_post_build`

### 2026-06-26 — Test-suite audit + organization: closed the 58% unmarked-tests CI blind spot, fixed the Quart `app_context()` sync-CM break (54 artifacts tests), and cleared a batch of outdated/misplaced tests
- **Scope:** "organize the test scripts and check for outdated/inaccurate/
  logic-error ones." Suite = 231 files / 3281 tests, all collect cleanly (no
  import errors). Ran the FULL unit tier + all 131 unmarked files + the 16
  api-marked files in parallel partitions (`--timeout-method=signal`), against
  the live local PostgreSQL (`TOFU_PG_PORT=15439`).
- **Headline finding (systemic):** 131 of 231 files (~1900 tests, 58%) carried
  NO tier marker → collected only by `make test-all`, SILENTLY SKIPPED by
  `make test-unit` / `test-api` / `ci`. Core suites
  (`test_orchestration_engine`, `test_core_schema_parity`, `test_api_response`,
  `test_swarm_async`, …) were in that blind spot, so broken tests could rot
  undetected. **Root-cause fix** (`tests/conftest.py`): a
  `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook auto-tags any test missing a tier marker
  (unit/api/visual/slow/live_llm) as `unit` AND emits a one-shot warning naming
  the offending files (so the omission stays VISIBLE and authors are nudged to
  add the right marker). Plus `--strict-markers` in `pyproject.toml`. Result:
  unit-tier collection 1256 → 3129; no test can silently vanish from CI again.
- **Biggest single bug — 54 artifacts-test failures, one root cause:** the
  `tests/test_artifacts_*` suite wraps pure-DB calls in `with
  flask_app.app_context():` (legacy Flask sync style). Under the Flask→Quart
  shim, `quart.ctx.AppContext` implements ONLY `__aenter__/__aexit__` →
  `TypeError: 'AppContext' object does not support the context manager
  protocol`. (This is the "pre-existing AppContext fixture failure" the prior
  journal entry waved off for `test_artifacts_producer_write_file` — it was

### 2026-06-26 — Paper Report: reading-time estimate + scroll-progress bar with a self-learning per-user reading-speed model
- **Feature ask:** Add a reading-time estimate + remaining-time progress bar to
  the Paper Reading Mode Report tab, with a learning algorithm — start from an
  average reading speed, then adapt to the user's personal pace over time.
- **Where:** `static/js/paper-reader.js` (logic), `static/styles.css` (sticky
  bar), `static/js/i18n.js` (labels). All JS already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Learning model (localStorage `paper_reading_wpm_v1`):** a single EWMA of the
  user's reading speed stored as a **Latin-word-equivalent WPM** so one model
  covers mixed-language reports. Cold start = `_READ_WPM_DEFAULT=220` (dense
  technical prose). `_recordReadingObservation()`: first real sample blends 50/50
  with the default (so one quirky session can't swing it); thereafter
  `next = wpm*(1-α) + obs*α`, α=0.25. Clamped to [60,700]. Verified by a
  standalone node harness: 350-wpm reader converges 285→301→313→322→329…; a
  10000-wpm outlier only nudges to ~340 (obs clamped first).
- **Workload counting (`_countReadingWords`):** script-aware — CJK/kana counted
  per-character × `_READ_CJK_CHAR_TO_WORD=0.6` (people read CJK slower per glyph
  than an English word), Latin/numeric by whitespace word runs. (EN "The quick
  brown fox jumps"→5; 10 CJK chars→6; mixed "Transformer 模型 attention"→3.2.)
- **UI:** `_buildReadingTimeBar(article, scroller)` builds a sticky header
  (`.paper-read-time`) injected at the TOP of the `.paper-report-content`
  scroller inside `_renderFinalReport` (final/cached render only — never the
  streaming `#reportBodyContent` skeleton). Shows total ("{min} read"), a live
  remaining readout ("{min} left" → "Finished"), a gradient progress fill, and a
  ✓ badge (SVG, §3.4 — no emoji) when the model has ≥1 learned sample (tooltip:
  "Calibrated to your reading speed (~N wpm)"). Built BEFORE DOM mount (uses
  detached `article.textContent`); tracking wired AFTER mount (needs real
  `scrollHeight`).
- **Progress + session capture (`_wireReadingTimeTracking`):** a passive scroll
  listener (rAF-throttled) tracks max scroll fraction → fills the bar + recomputes
  remaining = total×(1−frac). Active reading time is accumulated only across
  scroll gaps < 12 s (a long idle = stepped away → not counted), so the observed
  WPM = coveredWords ÷ activeMin reflects real reading, not wall-clock.
- **Flush points (`_teardownReadingTracker`):** records a sample only for a
  substantial session (≥120 word-equivalents covered AND ≥20 s active) — filters
  out glances / instant scroll-to-end. Flushed on: leaving the Report tab
  (`_switchPaperTab`), paper switch / regenerate (`_resetReportLocalState`),
  `exitPaperMode`, and `beforeunload`. `_wireReadingTimeTracking` also tears down
  the prior tracker first, so the katex re-render path can't double-count.
- **Status:** `node --check` clean on both JS files; learning math validated via
  a throwaway node harness. CSS uses `color-mix` for the fill gradient (widely
  supported). Restart to rebuild the bundle + hard-refresh to serve.

### 2026-06-26 — Unified rejection + distinct UI for the model's HALLUCINATED (fake) tool calls — `search_web` and friends
- **Origin:** User saw a `search_web` tool round (Swarm sub-agent context) and
  asked what it was — it's NOT this project's tool (the real one is
  `web_search`; MCP tools carry the `mcp__` prefix). Investigation showed a
  plausible-but-fake tool name slipped all the way through `parse_tool_calls`
  (alias resolution failed → passed through untouched) into the executor's
  bare `Error: unknown tool "X"` string returned as a NORMAL tool result. The
  frontend then rendered it as an ordinary completed generic round
  (`🔧 search_web` + spinner → done), with ZERO signal that the call was a
  hallucination that never executed. User asked for a unified backend rejection
  + distinct frontend styling.
- **Root cause / scattered handling (before):** there was no single classifier
  for "this is a fake tool". The drop-guards in `parse_tool_calls` only catch
  spurious proxy artifacts (colon names, `__` prefix, non-alphanumeric — the
  `antml:thinking` class), and the alias layer (`resolve_tool_name`) only fixes
  KNOWN synonyms. Anything else fell to `executor._execute_tool_one`'s
  unknown-tool branch as an ad-hoc error string with `status='done'`.
- **Fix — single rejection chokepoint (backend):**
  - `lib/tool_input_repair.py`: new `classify_tool_call(name, known)` (returns
    `{kind:'hallucinated', attempted, suggestions}` or `None` for a real tool),
    `suggest_tool_names` (stdlib `difflib` + token-overlap + substring boost;
    `search_web`→`web_search`, threshold-gated so nonsense yields `[]`),
    `build_rejection_message` (ONE source of truth for the model-facing text,
    mentions closest tools), and `report_hallucinated` (emits a
    `tool_hallucinated` audit event for the nightly optimizer to cluster which
    fake names a model keeps inventing). All exported.
  - `lib/tasks_pkg/tool_dispatch.py`: new `_known_tool_names(task)` derives the
    live REAL-tool set from `task['_tool_schema']` (the exact list shipped to
    the model this turn = built-ins + MCP + swarm + memory + custom-env), with
    a registry fallback. `parse_tool_calls` now (a) passes `known=_known` to
    `resolve_tool_name` so an MCP/swarm tool wins the exact check and is never
    aliased over NOR mis-flagged, and (b) after alias resolution fails,
    `classify_tool_call` → on a hit: stamp `round_entry['status']='rejected'` +
    `_rejected`, mirror onto the event, and set the standardized rejection as
    `_args_parse_error` so it short-circuits BEFORE dispatch (the fake tool
    NEVER executes). `execute_tool_pipeline`'s parse-error branch was taught to
    keep `status='rejected'` (instead of `_finalize_tool_round`'s forced
    `done`) and carry the `_rejected` descriptor onto the result meta + event.
  - `lib/agent_core/events.py`: documented the additive optional `status` +
    `_rejected` fields on `TOOL_START`/`TOOL_RESULT` (no contract-version bump —
    additive; the wire stays permissive). Event-registry drift test still 5/5.
- **Fix — distinct styling (frontend):**
  - `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`: new `_renderRejectedToolLine` (early-return
    in `_renderUnifiedToolLine` when `status==='rejected'` + `_rejected`):
    struck-through attempted name, a red "not a real tool" badge with a
    circle-slash SVG glyph (§3.4 — no emoji), and a "did you mean `web_search`?"
    suggestion chip. CSS `.ptool-rejected` / `.ptool-badge-reject` /
    `.ptool-reject-name|hint|sugg` in `static/styles.css`.
  - `static/js/ui/sse_handlers_tool.js`: `_handleToolStart` now copies
    `status:'rejected'` + `_rejected` onto the round (renders rejected from the
    FIRST event); `_handleToolResult` respects an incoming rejected status
    instead of unconditionally flipping to `done`.
  - i18n keys `tool.hallucinated` / `tool.hallucinatedTip` / `tool.didYouMean`
    (zh+en).
- **Deliberately unchanged:** the existing drop-guards (colon/`__`/non-alnum)
  stay — those are proxy ARTIFACTS, not model hallucinations, and silent-drop
  is correct (see `antml-thinking-spurious-tool-call-bug` memory). The executor
  unknown-tool branch stays as defense-in-depth (now rarely reached).
- **Why classify against `_tool_schema`, not `tool_registry`:** the registry is
  the process-global built-in set; MCP/swarm/memory/custom tools are NOT in it.
  Using the per-turn schema snapshot guarantees a legitimately-registered
  dynamic tool is never flagged as fake.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_tool_hallucination.py` (12, all pass):
  classifier (real not flagged, `search_web`→suggests `web_search`, nonsense→no
  false suggestion, threshold), `_known_tool_names` (schema snapshot + registry
  fallback), `parse_tool_calls` (fake rejected+not-dispatched, real untouched,
  aliasable `read_file`→`read_files` NOT rejected, MCP-in-schema not rejected),
  and `execute_tool_pipeline` keeps `rejected` + returns the message. JS
  `node --check` clean on all 3 files; `test_frontend_typecheck` shows my files
  contribute ZERO errors (the 2 reported are pre-existing `paper-reader.js`
  drift). Bundle rebuilt **`bundle-e17ca352.js`** (all 3 JS files already in
  `_BUNDLE_FILES`) — restart + hard-refresh to serve. `test_event_registry`
  5/5, `test_tool_input_repair` 27/27, `test_frontend_sse_dispatch` 1/1.
- **Pre-existing failures (NOT mine, proven):**
  `test_tool_registry::test_full_project_ordering_is_cache_stable` fails on the
  current working tree (an uncommitted `inspect_image`/`find_files` tool-order
  drift from another session) — reproduced with my 3 backend files reverted to
  HEAD; and `test_frontend_typecheck` BASELINE=0 predates a large uncommitted
  refactor. Neither touches code I changed.
