### 2026-06-26 — File-changes bar showed the WRONG `chatui:` root prefix for absolute-path writes into an EXTRA workspace root (e.g. overleaf-mcp) — fixed journal attribution at the write tool, not the renderer
- **Symptom (user screenshot, conv `mqtisr2fmisubi`):** A session whose primary
  root is `chatui` edited files by ABSOLUTE path under an extra root
  (`/mnt/.../overleaf-mcp/src/overleaf_mcp/config.py`, …). The "6 files changed"
  bar tagged every card `chatui:` AND showed the full absolute path — even
  though the files live in `overleaf-mcp`.
- **Root cause (`lib/project_mod/write_tools.py`):** `_resolve_write_path`
  accepts an absolute path and, when it's outside every registered root,
  AUTO-REGISTERS the nearest ancestor as a new extra root and returns the
  absolute target. But the three write tools then called
  `_record_modification(base, …, rel_path, …)` with the PRIMARY `base` and the
  original ABSOLUTE `rel_path`. Inside `_record_modification`
  (`modifications.py`), the root-name lookup matches `abs_base` (= primary) →
  records `mod['root']='chatui'` and stores the absolute path. The file-changes
  bar (`finish_info.js::_renderFileChangesHtml` → `f.root`) renders that journal
  attribution verbatim → wrong `chatui:` prefix + absolute path. (The per-tool-
  line pill in `tool_display.py::_resolve_tool_root_name` was already correct —
  it does a longest-prefix match against the registry — so ONLY the
  journal-derived bar was wrong.)
- **Fix:** New helper `_mod_attribution(target, base, rel_path)` in
  `write_tools.py` — for an absolute `rel_path` it re-derives the owning root by
  longest-prefix-matching the resolved `target` against the registered roots,
  returning `(deepest_root_path, path_relative_to_that_root)`; for the common
  relative-path case it returns `(base, rel_path)` unchanged. Called right
  before each of the three `_record_modification` sites (`tool_write_file`,
  `_apply_one_diff`, `_insert_one`). So the journal now records
  `root='overleaf-mcp'` + a clean relative path. This ALSO fixes undo: the
  undo path resolves `base_path` from `mod['basePath']` (now the extra root) and
  joins it with the now-RELATIVE `mod['path']` — previously it relied on the
  absolute path; both are now self-consistent.
- **Pitfall hit while editing:** the first `insert_content` placed
  `_mod_attribution` BETWEEN the `raise ValueError` and the relative-path
  `return` tail of `_resolve_write_path`, severing the function's return for
  relative paths (it silently returned `None` → `os.path.isfile(None)`
  TypeError). Caught immediately by the relative-path test. Re-stitched the
  function tail and moved the helper after it.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_write_tools_root_attribution.py` (4 tests,
  all pass) drives the REAL `tool_write_file` / `tool_apply_diff` /
  `tool_insert_content` with an absolute path under an extra root and asserts
  the recorded mod carries `root='overleaf-mcp'` + a clean relative path AND
  did NOT leak into the primary root's session; plus a relative-path
  no-regression case. Regression: `test_project_tools` 69 +
  `test_readonly_roots` 12 + `test_tool_root_pill` 7 = 88 green;
  `test_write_breakdown` + `test_write_approval_gate` green. The 9
  `test_artifacts_producer_write_file.py` failures are PRE-EXISTING (proven via
  `git stash` — identical failures on the unmodified tree; a Quart `AppContext`
  test-fixture incompatibility, unrelated). Backend-only, no JS/CSS change → no
  bundle rebuild; just restart the server.
- **Why:** Follow-up to the same-day diagnosis (the "stuck at waiting forever"
  autopilot report was a 304s rate-limited first-token stall, not a hang; see
  the prior entry). Logging was fixed for diagnosability, but the USER still
  stared at a bare "Waiting…" pulse for 5 minutes with zero signal. Pulled the
  deferred "waiting for model" phase chip back into scope — a self-driving flow
  that LOOKS dead for 5 min is the actual defect the user reported.
- **Root cause of the silence (two gaps):**
  1. `lib/llm_dispatch/api.py::dispatch_stream` already had an `on_retry`
     callback, but it was NOT fired in the `slot is None` **cooldown-wait**
     branch — which is EXACTLY the stall case: under contention every capable
     slot is cooling from OTHER requests' 429s, so this call returns slot=None
     and waits minutes WITHOUT ever catching a raw 429 of its own → `on_retry`
     never fired → no signal.
  2. The flow/swarm `SubAgent` (`lib/swarm/agent.py`) emitted NO pre-dispatch
     "waiting" signal and didn't pass `on_retry` at all. Its `stream_sink` only
     carried content/thinking deltas — no `phase` channel.
- **Fix (4 layers, data flows SubAgent→engine→adapter→SSE→frontend; phase event
  NOT delta, per the `retry-notification-phase-not-delta` convention):**
  - **`lib/llm_dispatch/api.py`** — the cooldown-wait branch now calls
    `on_retry(attempt, reason='Waiting for model (rate-limited)',
    status_code=429)` on the FIRST cooldown cycle then every ~20 cycles (≈6s),
    so it's bounded (no per-cycle spam). Wrapped in try/except (best-effort UX).
  - **`lib/swarm/agent.py`** — `SubAgent` now (a) emits a `waiting_model` phase
    via the stream sink right BEFORE `_dispatch_stream` (mirrors the normal
    chat path `stream_llm_response`), and (b) passes `on_retry=_on_dispatch_retry`
    which emits a `retrying` phase. New helper `_emit_stream_phase(phase, detail,
    **meta)` forwards `stream_sink('phase', detail, phase=…, **meta)`; tolerant
    of an older 2-arg sink (degrades, never crashes). `stream_sink` contract
    docstring updated to `(kind, chunk, **meta)` with kind ∈ content|thinking|phase.
  - **`lib/orchestration_engine.py`** — `_default_runner._stream_sink` now
    accepts `(kind, chunk, *, phase='', **meta)`: `kind=='phase'` → emits an
    ENGINE-INTERNAL `step_phase` event (kept OUT of the events registry, exactly
    like `step_delta`/`step_trace` — the orphan test only scans `_BACKEND_FILES`,
    which excludes the engine/adapter); else the existing `step_delta`.
  - **`lib/orchestration_endpoint_adapter.py`** — new `_on_step_phase` translates
    `step_phase` → the REGISTERED wire `phase` event (`EventType.PHASE`), carrying
    `attempt`/`statusCode`. ONLY for assistant-side producers (`emits!='user'`);
    a verifier's phase would land on the wrong (user-side) bubble, so it's dropped.
  - **Frontend: ZERO changes needed.** `static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js`'s `phase`
    handler already routes to the worker `buf` (non-critic branch), and
    `streaming_ui.js` already renders `waiting_model` ("Sent to the model,
    waiting for it to start replying…") and `retrying` (⟳ + detail) — the same
    transient indicators the chat composer uses. The contract already existed;
    only the backend wasn't emitting on this path.
- **Verification (event proven end-to-end, no real LLM):** new
  `tests/test_orchestration_endpoint_adapter.py` cases:
  `test_step_phase_for_producer_becomes_wire_phase` (assistant step_phase → wire
  `phase`, and NOT a delta), `test_step_phase_for_verifier_is_skipped`, and
  `test_subagent_waiting_phase_end_to_end` — a REAL `SubAgent` with a mock
  `dispatch_stream_fn` that fires `on_retry` (simulating the cooldown wait),
  driven through FlowExecutor + adapter, asserts a `waiting_model` phase fired
  pre-dispatch AND a `retrying` phase with `statusCode=429` reached the stream,
  alongside the content delta. Adapter suite 7/7.
- **Regression:** targeted suites pass in isolation (engine 45, runner 5, REST,
  swarm_tool_scoping 11, event_registry, chat_stream_direct). The mixed-batch
  shows 3 failures (`test_swarm_async::test_await_no_ids_includes_early_finishers`
  + 2 `test_event_emit::TestConvertedOrchestratorSites`) — PROVEN pre-existing
  cross-test pollution: identical 3 failures reproduce with my new test file
  EXCLUDED, all 3 pass in isolation, and none touch code I changed
  (`_emit_tool_round_phase` / await-agents). Backend-only + 1 test file; the
  frontend `phase` rendering is unchanged so just restart (no bundle rebuild).
- **Not changed (deliberately):** the 304s latency itself (model capacity/quota)
  and `strict_model` (the wait is correct — don't silently swap the model). This
  change makes the wait VISIBLE, not shorter.


### 2026-06-26 — "Orchestration flow / autopilot hangs at waiting forever" was NOT a backend hang — it was a 5-min first-token stall under model rate-limiting + a SubAgent logging blind spot
- **Report:** Picking 自动驾驶 in 编排流程 (activeFlow=`builtin:autopilot`) made the
  frontend "stick at waiting forever" — repro conv `mqtqcp1xh1ka0o`, task
  `794f8f55`.
- **Investigation (logs + persisted `task_events`):** The flow ran through
  `run_flow_via_chat` → FlowExecutor → autopilot graph (worker⇄virtual_user). I
  reconstructed the timeline from the DB event stream (the round-level detail is
  NOT in app.log — see below):
  - 00:42:27 `endpoint_iteration(phase=working, iteration=1)` → frontend stood up
    the worker bubble correctly (the plannerless-flow `initial_phase_for_flow`
    fix from the `orchestration-flow-honest-path-and-trace` memory is working —
    no hanging Planner bubble).
  - 00:42:27 → **00:47:32 = 304 s of TOTAL SILENCE** before the first token.
  - 00:47:32 → 00:53:46 the worker streamed **16 rounds / 678.7 s / 229k tokens**,
    `status=completed`; then VU emitted `[VU: TASK_DONE]`; `endpoint_complete` +
    `done` at 00:54:04; `task_results.status='done'`.
  - **So the backend never hung — it finished.** The 304 s stall was model
    congestion: `aws.claude-opus-4.8` was rate-limited at that moment (the
    PARALLEL task `70e80c63` shows repeated `429 rate-limited on …opus-4.8`).
    The flow worker dispatches with `strict_model`, so it correctly WAITS for
    the chosen model rather than falling back — but the worker bubble just sits
    on a contentless "Preparing…" pulse the whole time, which the user reads as
    a permanent hang.
- **Do the logs sufficiently expose this? NO — this is the real defect.** During
  the entire 678 s / 16-round run the `lib/swarm/agent.py::SubAgent` (which backs
  EVERY FlowExecutor / swarm role) emitted only TWO INFO lines: `RUN START`
  (00:42:27) and `RUN END` (00:53:46). Per-round start, per-round LLM completion,
  dispatch 429/cooling retries and TTFT are ALL `logger.debug` → never reach
  app.log. So from the logs alone you cannot distinguish "alive but slow /
  rate-limited" from "wedged". Contrast the normal chat path (`run_task`), which
  logs one INFO heartbeat per round (`[Task X][R5] stream_llm_response
  complete…`). That asymmetry is exactly why this looked like a backend hang.
- **Fix (`lib/swarm/agent.py::_run_loop`, CLAUDE.md §2 — every path leaves a
  trace):** promoted the two per-round log lines from `debug`→`info`:
  - round START: `[Agent:<id>] ── Round N/<cap|∞> START ── messages=M` — a round
    START with NO matching "LLM done" line below is now the unambiguous signal
    "began round N, still waiting on the model" (i.e. the rate-limit stall is
    visible). `max_rounds=0` now renders as `∞` instead of a confusing `0`.
  - round DONE: `[Agent:<id>] Round N LLM done in T.s — stop=… content_len=…
    thinking_len=… total_tokens=…`. Kept INFO volume bounded (one START + one
    DONE per round; tool-call detail stays debug). No behavioural change — pure
    observability. The streaming itself was always correct (295→659 deltas
    persisted, real content).
- **Not changed (deliberately):** the 304 s first-token latency itself is a model
  capacity/quota issue, not a code bug — the `strict_model` wait is the
  intended, correct behaviour for a user-selected flow (don't silently swap the
  model). A possible FUTURE UX follow-up (out of scope for "investigate the
  backend"): surface a "waiting for model (rate-limited)…" phase chip on the
  flow worker bubble during a long pre-first-token gap, mirroring the chat
  composer's `waiting_model` indicator, so the user sees activity instead of a
  bare pulse. The dispatch cooling-wait already logs only every 20th cycle
  (~6 s), which is fine now that the round heartbeat is INFO.
- **Tests:** `test_swarm_async`(2) + `test_swarm_tool_scoping`(11) +
  `test_core_schema_parity`(1) = 14 green; orchestration engine/adapter/runner/
  REST 94 green. `ast.parse` + import clean (the `\u2500`/`\u221e` escapes decode
  to box-drawing/∞ chars at parse time inside the non-raw format string).



### 2026-06-25 — Paper report TOC jump made the `paper-tabs` bar vanish permanently — scroll the inner container instead of `scrollIntoView()`
- **Symptom (user):** In Paper Reading Mode, clicking a chapter in the report's
  table of contents to jump down made the `.paper-tabs` bar (Q&A / Report /
  Babel PDF) disappear and never reappear, even after scrolling the report back
  to the very top.
- **Root cause:** `_scrollReportToHeading` (`static/js/paper-reader.js`) used
  `el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'})`. `scrollIntoView`
  scrolls EVERY scrollable ancestor to reveal the target — not just the report's
  own `.paper-report-content` (`overflow-y:auto`) scroller, but also its outer
  ancestors `.paper-tab-panel` / `.paper-body` / `.paper-mode-container`, which
  are all `overflow:hidden`. An `overflow:hidden` box is still *programmatically*
  scrollable, so the browser nudged one of them, pushing the fixed-position-feel
  `.paper-tabs` bar (a `flex-shrink:0` sibling above the panel) out of view.
  Because those containers expose no scrollbar, the user couldn't scroll them
  back, and scrolling the INNER report to top doesn't reset the OUTER container's
  scrollTop — so the tabs were gone for good.
- **Fix:** Scroll only the report's designated scroll container manually. The
  handler now `el.closest('.paper-report-content, .paper-report-body')` and does
  `scroller.scrollTo({top: scroller.scrollTop + (el.rect.top - scroller.rect.top)
  - 16, behavior:'smooth'})` (the 16px offset matches the h2/h3
  `scroll-margin-top`). Falls back to the old `scrollIntoView` only if no known
  scroller ancestor is found. The outer `overflow:hidden` chrome never moves.
- **Status:** `node --check` clean on paper-reader.js; bundle rebuilt
  **`bundle-e81c5fa6.js`** (paper-reader.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). Restart
  + hard-refresh to serve. CSS untouched (this is a JS-only scroll-behavior fix).

### 2026-06-25 — Paper report: fixed (1) giant blank gap above the title and (2) heading showing `arXiv:<id>` instead of the paper title
- **Symptom (user screenshot):** Paper Reading Mode report had a large empty
  bordered area above the report, and the top heading read `arXiv:2601.04171v1`
  instead of the paper title — even though the report's own Paper Card carried
  the correct title and the right-hand CONTENTS/TOC was fully populated.
- **Issue 1 — blank gap = CSS grid auto-placement bug (THE main defect).**
  `_renderFinalReport` (`static/js/paper-reader.js`) builds the doc as
  `doc.innerHTML = tocHTML` (the `<nav class="paper-report-toc">` FIRST) then
  `doc.appendChild(article)` (the `<article>` SECOND). The grid
  (`.paper-report-doc`, `styles.css`) declared two columns + `align-items:start`
  but **no explicit rows**, and assigned `.paper-report-article{grid-column:1}` /
  `.paper-report-toc{grid-column:2}`. Because the TOC precedes the article in
  DOM order, CSS grid's *sparse* auto-placement parked the TOC in row1/col2,
  then bumped the article to **row2/col1** — leaving an empty row1/col1 cell as
  tall as the TOC (~630–660px) above the title. Reproduced precisely with a
  Playwright harness (real `marked` + real `styles.css` + the real
  `_renderFinalReport`/`renderMarkdown` extracted from `paper-reader.js`):
  `article top: 684px`, grid rows `630px 16725px`. **Fix:** pin BOTH children to
  `grid-row:1` (`styles.css` `.paper-report-article{...grid-row:1}` +
  `.paper-report-doc > .paper-report-toc{...grid-row:1}`). After: `article
  top: 24px` (just the 24px doc padding), single grid row. CSS-only; no bundler
  involvement (CSS is served directly, not via `lib/js_bundler.py`).
- **Issue 2 — `arXiv:<id>` heading = placeholder H1 baked into the report body.**
  DB inspection (PostgreSQL `paper_reports`, this paper hash
  `eaf4c892…`) showed TWO rows: the newer `en` report correctly starts
  `# Agentic Rubrics as Contextual Verifiers for SWE Agents`, but the older `zh`
  row's body literally begins `# arXiv:2601.04171v1` — a placeholder H1 the
  model emitted (or the engine prepended) when the up-front arXiv title lookup
  failed AND there was no `paper_library` row (this hash had none →
  `_lookup_paper_title` returns the bare `arXiv:<id>`). The correct title was
  sitting in the very same report's Paper Card row the whole time. The old
  repair logic only PREPENDED a heading when one was missing; it never REPLACED
  a placeholder H1. **Fix (server-side, covers every render/cache/export path):**
  - Added shared predicate `_is_placeholder_title(t)` in `lib/paper/images.py`
    (empty OR `^arxiv[:\s]`), exported from the `lib.paper` facade; the engine
    (`report_engine.py`) now imports it instead of redefining a local copy.
  - Rewrote `_ensure_title_heading` (the cache / re-render / export helper) to
    ALSO swap a placeholder `# arXiv:<id>` H1 for the Paper-Card title (via
    `_extract_title_from_report`, falling back to the library title). It still
    prepends when no H1 exists, leaves a correct H1 untouched, and keeps the
    placeholder only when nothing better is available. Never rewrites the DB row
    — repairs the rendered copy.
  - `_run_report_task` (live-generation path): when the model baked its own
    `# arXiv:<id>` H1, it now `re.sub`-replaces that first H1 line with the
    resolved title (was: only prepend-when-missing). So both the live `done`
    event and the persisted report carry the real title.
- **Verification:** new Playwright harness (browser libs loaded via the conda
  env's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` since the system was missing `libatk` etc.) confirmed
  blank gap gone. Title-repair proven on the REAL zh+en DB reports (both now
  render `# Agentic Rubrics…`). Tests: `tests/test_paper_title_recovery.py`
  extended 13→18 (placeholder-H1 repair in `_ensure_title_heading` ×4 + engine
  H1-replacement ×1); full file 18/18 + `test_paper_migration.py` 14/14 green
  (32 together). Restart picks up the Python change; CSS needs only a
  hard-refresh (no bundle hash change — CSS isn't bundled).

### 2026-06-25 — Paper report "Generate" had no Stop button: added clean abort terminal state (backend) + morphing Stop/Regenerate toolbar affordance (frontend)
- **Symptom / gap:** Clicking Generate/Regenerate in Paper Reading Mode's
  Report tab started a long server-owned task with NO way to stop it short of
  switching papers (which only detaches the poller — the task keeps running
  server-side). The plumbing was half-built: `/api/v1/paper/report/abort` +
  `Api.paper.reportAbort` already existed, but nothing in the toolbar called
  it, and the backend had a latent bug — when `_abort_check()` broke the tool
  loop (`report_engine.py`) it fell THROUGH to the `done` path, persisting a
  truncated partial report to `paper_reports` and emitting a `done` event. So
  even if abort had been wired, it would have cached a half-written report.
- **Backend fix (`lib/paper/report_engine.py`, `routes/paper.py`):** Introduced
  a distinct `aborted` terminal status (the runtime cleanup + TTL logic already
  recognised `'aborted'` alongside `done`/`error`, so no churn there). Added an
  `aborted` flag; the in-loop abort check and a NEW post-dispatch check (the
  stream returns a partial msg normally when the abort lands mid-line-iteration,
  no raise) both set it and break. After the loop, an `if aborted:` block sets
  `status='aborted'`, sets `finished_at`, emits a single `{type:'aborted',
  partial: full_content}` event, and `return`s — explicitly BEFORE the
  title/enrich/persist block, so a partial report is never written to the DB.
  Also caught `AbortedError` (raised by the dispatcher between stream retries)
  as the same clean-stop, not an error. The poll endpoint
  (`poll_report_task`) now returns `partial` for `status=='aborted'`.
- **Frontend (`static/js/paper-reader.js`, `index.html`, `i18n.js`,
  `styles.css`):** Added a Stop button to the report toolbar that MORPHS with
  Regenerate (mirrors the chat composer's send↔stop pattern): `_syncReportToolbar(running)`
  shows Stop while `status==='running'`, Regenerate otherwise, and is called on
  every `_paintReportFromState`, at task start, on attach-to-running, and inside
  `_renderFinalReport` (covers cached/empty paths). `_stopPaperReport()` calls
  `reportAbort` best-effort and flips the button to a disabled "Stopping…" — it
  does NOT mutate status locally; the authoritative `aborted` event arrives via
  the normal poll loop. `_applyReportEvent` + the poll-status branch handle
  `aborted` (keep `partial` as read-only `fullText`); `_paintReportFromState`
  renders a red "Generation stopped" banner (SVG stop-square glyph, §3.4 — no
  emoji) above whatever partial markdown was produced, or a banner + hint when
  nothing streamed yet. CSS: `.paper-report-stop-btn` (error-color, pulsing
  square icon) + `.paper-report-stopped-banner`. New i18n keys `paper.reportStop`
  / `reportStopping` / `reportStopped` / `reportStoppedHint` (zh+en).
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_paper_report_abort.py` (3 tests:
  pre-abort → aborted+no done+no dispatch; mid-stream → aborted carries partial,
  NOT persisted/enriched; mid-retry `AbortedError` → aborted not error) — all
  pass; `test_paper_report_dedup.py` 4/4 regression-clean (7 together).
  `node --check` clean on paper-reader.js + i18n.js; bundle rebuilt
  **`bundle-98033e85.js`** (both files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve. Key design choice: status is server-authoritative —
  the Stop click only signals + shows "Stopping…"; the `aborted` event freezes
  the UI, so SSE-drop / tab-switch / restart can't desync the displayed state.

### 2026-06-25 — MCP tool-call line: clickable resource link (Overleaf project / Xuecheng doc) instead of an unreadable id jumble
- **Symptom / UX defect:** The unified tool panel rendered an overleaf edit as
  `🔌 overleaf/edit_file — acl_latex.tex @ 6a1e7…a668` — the `6a1e7…a668`
  short-id is meaningless to a human and not navigable. User asked for a
  hyperlink so they can jump straight to the project. (The name cache from
  the `mcp-tool-display-surfaces-key-args` memory already upgrades the id to
  a human name *when cached*, but it still falls back to the id jumble and is
  never clickable.)
- **Fix (3 layers, data flows id→name→url→label→`<a>`):**
  - **`lib/mcp/project_names.py`** — added two URL caches
    (`_proj_url_cache`, `_doc_url_cache`) + a learned `_overleaf_base`
    (default `https://www.overleaf.com`, overridden the first time a
    `<scheme>://<host>/project/<id>` URL is seen in a tool result → self-hosted
    Overleaf links correctly). New getters `get_project_url` (ALWAYS synthesizes
    `<base>/project/<id>` for a valid 24-hex id, even with an empty cache) and
    `get_doc_url` (returns a URL ONLY when one was harvested — no canonical
    Xuecheng base is assumed). `ingest_tool_result` now also harvests full
    `…/project/<id>` and `…/collabpage/<id>` URLs; `clear_cache` wipes all four
    dicts + the base.
  - **`lib/tasks_pkg/tool_display.py`** — `_tool_display_mcp` now attaches
    `extra['_mcpLinks'] = {label → href}` via new `_mcp_links(fn_args)`. The KEY
    is the EXACT label `_mcp_arg_suffix` rendered for that arg (cached name /
    short-id / doc title-or-id), so the frontend can find+wrap that substring.
    Covers overleaf `project_id` (always) + xuecheng `doc` (when a URL was
    harvested). Flows through `round_entry.update(extra)` + the event copy
    (key doesn't start with `_display_`) so it persists across reload.
  - **`static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`** — new `_linkifyMcpLabels(text, round)`
    runs on the already-escaped `q` in `_renderUnifiedToolLine`: escapes each
    label the same way, `indexOf` first match, wraps in
    `<a class="ptool-mcp-link" target=_blank rel=noopener>`. **XSS guard: only
    `^https?://` hrefs allowed** (rejects `javascript:`/`data:`). CSS
    `.ptool-mcp-link` (accent color, dotted→solid underline on hover) in
    `static/styles.css`.
- **Why this design:** keying `_mcpLinks` by the rendered label (not by
  arg-name) means the link survives the name-vs-id rendering choice — whatever
  string ended up on the line is exactly what gets linkified. `get_project_url`
  synthesizing from the id guarantees the link is present even at the `tool_start`
  event, before any `list_projects`/`status_summary` has populated the name cache.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_mcp_tool_links.py` (8, all pass): synth
  URL from default base, non-hex no-url, label↔link consistency, self-hosted base
  learning, xuecheng harvest-then-link, github no-link. JS verified via node
  harness (human-name + short-id linkified; `javascript:` href rejected).
  `node --check` clean; `tests/test_frontend_typecheck.py` 3/3. Bundle rebuilt
  **`bundle-98033e85.js`** (`ui/tool_rounds.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`) —
  restart + hard-refresh to serve it.
- **Follow-up (same day) — moved the URL source-of-truth to overleaf-mcp + fixed
  a latent self-hosted bug.** Asked "is there a similar issue, and shouldn't this
  live in overleaf-mcp?" — yes on both. The chatui side was *guessing* the host:
  `get_project_url` synthesizes `https://www.overleaf.com/project/<id>` from a
  default base and only learns the real base if it happens to harvest a full URL.
  But of all the overleaf tools, **only `create_project`** embedded a full URL;
  every write (`edit_file`/`create_file`/`rewrite_file`/`delete_file`/`upload_file`)
  and read (`list_files`/`read_file`/`status_summary`) returned just
  `[Name] (6a1e7…a668)` — **no URL**. So on a self-hosted Overleaf the link pointed
  at the WRONG host (www.overleaf.com) until a create_project happened to run, and
  the model never saw a usable link in the result text. overleaf-mcp is the right
  home because it OWNS the authoritative base (`OVERLEAF_BASE_URL` env, already used
  across `compile.py`/`metadata.py`), whereas chatui can only guess.
  - **overleaf-mcp `config.py`:** new `project_url(pid)` = `{BASE.rstrip('/')}/project/{pid}`,
    returns '' for invalid/non-24-hex ids.
  - **`git_client.py::_project_tag`:** now returns `[Name] (short…id) <url>` →
    EVERY write tool's confirmation carries the canonical link.
  - **`server.py`:** `list_projects` appends ` <url>` per line; `status_summary`
    adds a `URL:` line; `create_project` uses `project_url(pid)` instead of the
    hardcoded `https://www.overleaf.com/...`.
  - chatui needed NO change — `ingest_tool_result` already harvests
    `…/project/<id>` from any result text and learns the deployment base from it.
    So the very first `edit_file` now links correctly on self-hosted deploys, and
    sibling projects inherit the learned base.
  - **Tests:** overleaf-mcp `tests/test_project_url.py` (8 — default/self-hosted/
    trailing-slash base, invalid→'', `_project_tag` embeds url; reloads the config
    module per-test to pick up the monkeypatched env). chatui
    `tests/test_mcp_tool_links.py` +1 → 9 (write-tool result carries a harvestable
    URL; self-hosted base learned → sibling link). All green. No JS/CSS change this
    round, so no bundle rebuild needed; the overleaf-mcp server must be restarted to
    emit the new strings.

### 2026-06-25 — Autopilot VU bubble: explicit "Private · not sent" collapsible zone + bounded "sent" reply block (render-layer only)
- **Symptom / UX defect:** User asked whether "Sent to the agent as the next
  message" includes the tool-call content, and where the boundary sits. Traced
  the render: data layer is correct (`conv_message_builder._build_user_message`
  reads ONLY `content` for a `role:'user'` row → VU `toolRounds`/`thinking` cost
  ZERO tokens in the next round; `chat_render.js` emits the `vu-handoff-header`
  inside the `else if (msg.content)` branch right before `.md-content`, which
  wraps only the reply — so the marker is technically accurate). BUT the render
  order was investigation panel → thinking block → "Sent" marker → reply, with
  the two PRIVATE zones sitting ABOVE the marker carrying no "NOT sent" framing
  (the investigation header just said "Autopilot investigation"). So at a glance
  the tool calls looked like they might be part of what's sent — a real
  provenance-legibility defect even though the bytes are correct.
- **Fix (render-layer ONLY — data layer deliberately untouched, it's already
  correct):** In `static/js/ui/chat_render.js::renderMessage`, the VU's
  investigation tool panel + thinking block are now COLLECTED into a
  `_vuPrivateHtml` buffer and emitted inside ONE default-collapsed
  `<details class="vu-private-zone">` whose `<summary>` reads i18n
  `autopilot.privateNotSent` ("Private · not sent to the agent") with an
  eye-off SVG glyph (§3.4, no emoji). The inner `.thinking-block` lazy-load via
  `_toggleThinking` still works because the element exists in the DOM even while
  the `<details>` is closed. The reply (handoff header + `.md-content`) is
  wrapped in a green-accented `<div class="vu-sent-zone">` so the sent region is
  an unmistakable bounded block, gated on `!msg._streamingVu` (live streaming
  still uses the separate `streaming_ui.js` zones — unaffected). New i18n key
  `autopilot.privateNotSent` (zh `私有过程 · 不发送给智能体` / en). CSS:
  `.vu-private-zone` (dashed indigo frame, collapsible summary, rotating ▼) +
  `.vu-sent-zone` (green left rail) added next to the existing
  `.vu-investigation-header` / `.vu-handoff-header` rules.
- **DOM order, finalized VU bubble (after):** `<details.vu-private-zone>`
  (COLLAPSED: investigation-header + tool panel + thinking-block) →
  `<div.vu-sent-zone>` (handoff-header + `.md-content` reply). Before it was
  flat with both private zones bleeding into the sent marker.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on chat_render.js + i18n.js;
  `tests/test_frontend_typecheck.py` 3/3 pass; bundle rebuilt
  **`bundle-cae3526b.js`** (both files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`, no new file)
  — restart + hard-refresh to serve it. Confirmed the token concern needs NO
  action: VU tool process is display-only by construction.

### 2026-06-25 — Messages-as-rows Phase 5 (migrator-first) + Phase 4 status correction; §10.3 schema sign-off recorded
- **Context / sign-off:** User gave §10 sign-off (approved_by=user) to proceed
  with the conversation-store roadmap (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6). Recorded via
  `audit_log('schema_change_approval', …, approved_by='user')`.
- **Phase 4 — verified, NOT built (stale-docs trap avoided):** The roadmap row
  said "add POST .../messages for user-message creation; remove the full-array
  PUT." Tracing the send path FIRST showed the append primitive **already
  exists and is live**: `sendMessage`→`Api.chat.send`→`chat_send`
  (`routes/chat.py:521`) creates the user message server-side via
  `_append_user_msg_idempotent` + `_persist_conv_messages` — no full-array PUT.
  A new `POST /messages` endpoint would be REDUNDANT. The remaining
  `syncConversationToServer` PUTs serve edit/regen/branch/checkpoint (rewrite
  ops, not append) and pass through `save_conv` guards
  (`blocked_msg_regression`, `blocked_stale_checkpoint`, cross-talk count-jump)
  that are **load-bearing safety** from the 2026-05 sync-hardening. So
  full-array-PUT elimination is DEFERRED and explicitly **not benign** (it
  removes those guards). Corrected ARCHITECTURE.md §6 rows 3/4/5 instead of
  writing no-op code. (See memory `tofu-stale-migration-status-docs`.)
- **Phase 5 — migrator-first, landed behind a flag:**
  - New Core table `conversation_messages(conv_id, seq, msg_id, role, content,
    content_json, thinking, translated_content, meta JSONB, created_at,
    updated_at)`, PK `(conv_id, seq)`. Defined ONCE in `_core_schema.py`;
    byte-equivalence proven by 2 new parity tests (PG+SQLite). Wired via
    `create_if_absent` in both `_schema_*.py`; schema version 28→29.
  - **Column-split rationale = the verification invariant:** the four fields
    `build_search_text()` reads (role, content, thinking, translatedContent)
    are hoisted to first-class columns so the search blob reconstructs from
    rows alone; the WHOLE original dict is also kept verbatim in `meta`, so a
    row round-trips field-for-field. content (str) vs content_json (list)
    mirror the str/list branch in build_search_text.
  - New `lib/database/messages_rows.py`: `message_to_row`/`row_to_message`
    (lossless), `backfill_conv` (idempotent delete-then-insert),
    `dual_write_conv` (flag-gated, best-effort, NEVER raises into the JSONB
    write), and the GATE: `verify_search_text_parity` / `verify_conv_parity`
    assert build_search_text is BYTE-IDENTICAL from rows vs the JSONB array.
  - Two flags, decoupled: `TOFU_MESSAGES_ROWS` (write/backfill, default OFF) and
    `TOFU_MESSAGES_ROWS_READ` (read cutover, default OFF, AND requires the write
    flag). Reads must NOT flip until verify_*_parity is proven on real data.
  - Dual-write wired at the two real chokepoints — `persist_conv_messages`
    (the documented single point of truth for send/regen/edit/continue) and
    `_save_conv_blocking` (the full-array PUT) — 4 lines each, no-op when off.
- **Bug caught by the e2e test (kept the test honest):** an unconditional
  `UNIQUE(conv_id, msg_id)` collides because legacy/un-backfilled messages all
  carry `msg_id=''`. Fixed to a **partial** unique index
  `… WHERE msg_id <> ''` on both backends — `_msgId` is unique-per-conv when
  present, empty placeholders may repeat.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_messages_rows.py` (8) + 2 new parity tests — all green
  (56 in the parity+migrator run; 77 across +chat-manager). The lone failure,
  `test_chat_streams_via_http_endpoints` (poll 404), is the known pre-existing
  test-client plumbing issue, on a path these changes don't touch.
- **Not done (by design):** the JSONB→rows production backfill run, and the
  read cutover — both gated on verify_conv_parity passing across real data.

### 2026-06-25 — Future-proofed agent-artifact handling: single registry (lib/agent_artifacts.py) + `.tofu` prefix convention, replacing scattered hardcoded lists
- **Why (user prompt):** "Think more long-term — if we create other things in
  the future, will our mechanisms handle them?" The honest answer for
  yesterday's `_TOFU_ARTIFACT_IGNORES = ('.tofu/','.tofu_trash/','.tofu_sandbox/')`
  tuple was NO: it was yet another hardcoded enumeration, the exact drift trap
  the `export-*` memories document (the `swebench_glm_ab_workdir` /
  `.tofu_env.json` class of bug). I mapped the artifact landscape and found the
  same names independently hardcoded in 5+ places — gitignore (indexer.py),
  export.py (×3 exclude sets), self_update.py (`_RUNTIME_STATE_PREFIXES` /
  `_OVERLAY_SKIP_PREFIXES`), mcp/client.py (`_VENDOR_EXCLUDE_DIRS`) — plus the
  producers each inventing their own literal (file_history `.tofu`, memory
  `.tofu/skills`, run_command `.tofu_trash`, portable_sandbox `.tofu_sandbox`).
  **A live instance of the bug:** export.py excluded `.tofu` + `.tofu_trash`
  but NOT `.tofu_sandbox` → it was leaking into every export.
- **Key insight:** every project-local artifact already shares the `.tofu`
  prefix. That's a usable invariant — consumers can recognise present AND future
  artifacts by PREFIX instead of enumerating exact names.
- **Change:** New stdlib-only module **`lib/agent_artifacts.py`** = single
  source of truth: `ARTIFACT_PREFIX='.tofu'`, `is_agent_artifact(name)` (prefix
  predicate), `GITIGNORE_PATTERN='.tofu*'` (one glob covering all current+future
  artifacts; no embedded slash → matches at any depth), `KNOWN_ARTIFACT_NAMES` +
  per-artifact constants. Adopted it in the seams: (1) `indexer.py` gitignore
  now writes the single `.tofu*` glob (was the 3-tuple). (2) `export.py`
  `_should_exclude` gained a prefix check + `_build_tar_excludes` appends
  `--exclude=.tofu*` — fixes the `.tofu_sandbox` leak AND auto-covers future
  artifacts in all three modes. (3) `self_update.py` `_overlay_skip` is now
  prefix-aware (defensive: never overwrite a `.tofu*` in the install tree).
  Documented the convention as CLAUDE.md §3.6 so contributors name new artifacts
  `.tofu_*`, declare them in the registry, and call `is_agent_artifact()` rather
  than re-listing literals.
- **Result / status:** `lib/agent_artifacts.py` + 5 registry tests +
  rewritten `TofuArtifactGitignoreTest` (single-glob assertions) in
  `tests/test_agent_notes_journal.py` (20 total). Full regression sweep
  98/98 green (journal 20, self_update_tarball 5, export_no_pkg_collision 4,
  project_tools 69). Smoke-verified all seams: registry recognises future
  `.tofu_cache2027`, rejects `lib`; export now strips `.tofu_sandbox` +
  `.tofu_future`, keeps `lib/foo.py`; overlay_skip skips `.tofu_sandbox/bin/rm`.
  NOT migrated (left as deliberate follow-ups, low risk / behavior-sensitive):
  mcp/client.py `_VENDOR_EXCLUDE_DIRS` literal `.tofu`/`.chatui`, and the
  producers' env-overridable knobs (run_command `_TRASH_DIRNAME`). `config.py`
  `IGNORE_DIRS` intentionally untouched — search already skips dot-dirs; that's
  a scan-perf concern, not git pollution.

### 2026-06-25 — Auto-gitignore the assistant's hidden runtime artifacts (.tofu/, .tofu_trash/, .tofu_sandbox/) in selected projects
- **Change:** Generalized the journal-only `.gitignore` helper in
  `lib/project_mod/indexer.py` into `_ensure_gitignored(root, entries, header)`
  and wired a new `_TOFU_ARTIFACT_IGNORES = ('.tofu/', '.tofu_trash/',
  '.tofu_sandbox/')` block into `get_context_for_prompt`. On every context build
  for a WRITABLE primary root, the three hidden runtime-state dirs the assistant
  writes into the selected project — `.tofu/` (file-history backups +
  `.tofu/skills` memories; see `lib/file_history/store.py:95`,
  `lib/memory/storage.py:42`), `.tofu_trash/` (the rm→trash recoverable-delete
  bin; `run_command.py:955`) and `.tofu_sandbox/` (restricted-run PATH shims;
  `portable_sandbox.py:152`) — are appended to `.gitignore` (created if missing,
  appended if present). `_ensure_journal_gitignored` is now a thin wrapper over
  the shared helper. Two robustness upgrades over the old journal-only logic:
  (1) `_within_git_tree(path)` walks ANCESTORS for `.git` (cap 40), so a project
  that is a SUB-DIRECTORY of a repo still gets a `.gitignore` (its artifacts
  would otherwise pollute the parent repo's `git status`); (2) `_gitignore_has_entry`
  matches all slash variants (`.tofu` / `.tofu/` / `/.tofu` / `/.tofu/`) so we
  never append a near-duplicate.
- **Why:** User reported these hidden files frequently dirty selected-project
  trees. The codebase already had a tested precedent (`JOURNAL.md` auto-ignore,
  Option A), so I extended it rather than inventing a new mechanism. Preserved
  the two hard guardrails from the `journal-md-autocreate-injection` /
  `gitignore-timeout-suggest-flow` memories: NEVER conjure a stray `.gitignore`
  in a non-git dir, and NEVER write into a read-only root (gated on
  `primary_is_ro` + `is_readonly_path`). Note: `.tofu_trash/` ALSO drops its own
  self-ignoring `.gitignore` (`*`) via the rm-shim, so this is belt-and-suspenders
  for the cwd-repo case but the canonical fix for the selected-project repo.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_agent_notes_journal.py` extended with a new
  `TofuArtifactGitignoreTest` (6 cases: appended in git repo; appended into an
  existing `.gitignore` preserving content; no stray file in a non-git dir;
  created when a PARENT is a git repo; idempotent + slash-variant-aware across
  repeated builds; read-only root untouched). Full file 15/15 pass;
  `test_project_tools.py` 69/69 regression-clean (84 together). Pure-Python
  context-build change — no bundler, restart picks it up.

  current status / known issues / next steps.


### 2026-06-23 — Auto-translate wrong-language FLIP on mixed EN+ZH input: output-side guard in the engine (verify outcome, don't trust the prompt)
- **Symptom:** An assistant reply that was English lead-in + a large Chinese
  body got auto-translated (target=Chinese) into a译文 that was predominantly
  ENGLISH — the already-Chinese majority was rewritten to English ("原文中文 ·
  译文英文"). The user pushed back that "翻成中文" is not a hard task and asked
  whether the prompt was over-complex.
- **Root cause (two-layer):** (1) The prompt (`lib/translate/prompt.py`) carries
  a heavy anti-verbatim rule ("输出与输入几乎相同=失败，违反即失败") for the EN→ZH
  case; on a mostly-Chinese source a weak cheap model reads that as "don't output
  something close to the input" and performs a language NORMALISATION, flipping
  the Chinese body to English. The later "已经是 {target} 的原样保留" patch is a
  CONTRADICTORY instruction the weak model can't reconcile, so prompt text alone
  can't fix it. (2) The engine's no-op/wrong-language guard in
  `_translate_one_chunk` (`lib/translate/engine.py`) only fired when
  `cjk_ratio(source) < 0.1` (source almost pure English), so it completely MISSED
  mixed input (real case: source cjk_ratio=0.67). This gap was already documented
  in the `translate-no-chunk-and-prompt-keep-target-language` memory as "still
  partial".
- **Fix (chosen for robustness — verify the OUTCOME, don't trust the model):**
  Added a wrong-language-flip detector in `_translate_one_chunk`, placed right
  after the no-op block, reusing the SAME proven machinery
  (`_dispatcher.record_truncation` + `_excluded_models.add` + `continue`) as the
  truncation/empty/no-op guards: when `target=Chinese` AND
  `cjk_ratio(source) >= 0.10` AND output len ≥ 200 AND
  `is_predominantly_english(output)` → reject, exclude that model, retry; a
  different model usually keeps the Chinese intact. After `_MAX_CONTENT_RETRIES`
  it RAISES (forces `c=''`) rather than committing English over a Chinese source
  — refusing to clobber. Considered + rejected the alternatives: (A) more prompt
  rules — weakest, fights model unreliability with more text it already ignores;
  (B) skip mixed-language messages — wrong tradeoff, abandons the legitimate
  English-heavy case; (D) frontend post-check — redundant once (C) exists. New
  status kinds `wrong_language` / `wrong_language_final` added to
  `lib/translate/status.py` + i18n keys `translate.retry.wrong_language*` in
  `static/js/i18n.js` (zh/en).
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_translate_wrong_language_flip.py` (4 tests:
  flip retried→good 2nd model; persistent flip raises; correct ZH not flagged;
  pure-EN→ZH unaffected) — all pass. Regression-clean:
  `test_translate_noop_already_target.py` 4/4 (legitimate ZH→ZH passthrough still
  works), `test_text_lang.py` 20/20. Negative control confirmed the bug case
  preconditions (src cjk=0.67, out English, len 250) and that the old guard
  missed it. Pure-Python engine change + i18n; bundler auto-rebuilds on mtime, so
  just restart. `i18n.js` already first in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.

### 2026-06-22 — Endpoint mode poll-fallback baton: reconstruct multi-turn structure from the conversation when the in-memory task is gone (SSE-drop + eviction/restart desync)
- **Symptom / gap:** Audited the two autonomous-flow terminal paths (endpoint
  Planner→Worker→Critic; autopilot virtual-user) for state-sync gaps that only a
  manual refresh repairs. The **autopilot** baton (`autopilotNextTaskId`/
  `autopilotVuMessage`) is fully landed on all three transports (SSE done, poll
  fallback, init reattach) and is mutually exclusive with endpoint mode
  (`is_autopilot_enabled` returns False when `endpointMode` —
  `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py:112`), so the two never coexist. The **endpoint**
  path had a real gap: endpoint results are persisted into the CONVERSATION
  `messages` (per-turn via `_sync_endpoint_turns_to_conversation`), NOT into the
  single `task_results` content blob (`persist_task_result` skips
  `_sync_result_to_conversation` for endpoint tasks). `/api/chat/poll`
  (`routes/chat.py::chat_poll`) surfaced `endpointMode`+`endpointTurns` ONLY from
  the IN-MEMORY `tasks` dict; its DB branch (task evicted past the 3600s TTL, or
  server restarted — both real for a multi-iteration endpoint run that can span a
  restart) returned the row's single content blob with NO endpoint fields. So
  when SSE timed out mid-endpoint-run and `_pollFallback` outlived the in-memory
  task, the frontend's `if (data.endpointMode && data.endpointTurns)` rebuild was
  false → it fell into the single-`assistantMsg` overwrite branch, stamping the
  last in-progress turn's content onto ONE bubble. A **display-state** desync
  (data was never lost — it lives durably in conversation messages), repaired
  only by force-refresh (which loads conversation messages directly). An
  independent `reviewer` sub-agent confirmed the root cause and added: patch BOTH
  DB sub-branches (done AND interrupted/server-crash), and the cleanest fix is to
  reconstruct `endpointTurns` from the conversation (mirroring
  `load_tool_rounds_from_conversation`) rather than only the in-memory path.
- **Fix (root cause, single source of truth = conversation messages):**
  **(1) `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`:** new `load_endpoint_turns_from_conversation(conv_id)`
  recovery reader — slices the trailing endpoint-turn run (`_isEndpointPlanner` /
  `_epIteration` / `_isEndpointReview`) out of the durable conversation messages,
  the exact inverse of the frontend's `baseEnd` slice. `build_result_meta` now
  persists `endpointMode` + `endpointStopReason` into `task_results.metadata` so
  the DB poll branch can self-identify a finished endpoint task even after
  eviction/restart. Exported the new helper from `lib/tasks_pkg/__init__.py`
  (`__all__` + eager import). **(2) `routes/chat.py::chat_poll`:** the IN-MEMORY
  branch now also surfaces `endpointPhase`/`endpointIteration`/`endpointStopReason`
  (symmetry with the SSE `state` snapshot — both transports hand the frontend the
  identical baton). The DB branch echoes `endpointMode` + reconstructed
  `endpointTurns` (via the new helper) + `endpointStopReason`, keyed on
  `_db_meta.get('endpointMode')` so it covers BOTH `done` and the
  `running`→`interrupted` server-crash sub-branch. **(3)
  `static/js/ui/sse_poll_fallback.js`:** reset `conv._epPollTurnCount=0` at
  `_pollFallback` START so the first endpoint poll of a NEW session always
  repaints from the authoritative turns (the `newEpCount !== prevEpCount`
  re-render guard would otherwise skip when a prior session left the count equal,
  leaving a stale streaming bubble until the terminal finishStream re-render).
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_endpoint_poll_recovery.py` (9 tests, all
  pass): helper slice/empty/missing-conv; `build_result_meta` endpoint signal
  present/absent; in-memory poll carries the full terminal baton; DB-branch
  reconstructs turns after eviction for done AND interrupted; plain task
  unaffected. Regression-clean: `test_autopilot_poll_handoff` 6/6,
  `test_endpoint_messages` 28, `test_endpoint_flow_parity` 3,
  `test_agent_poll_routes` 9 — all green. `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-b6aaa754.js`) — `ui/sse_poll_fallback.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`;
  restart + hard-refresh to serve it. NOTE: `test_chat_manager_migration.py`'s
  `test_chat_streams_via_http_endpoints` fails with a 404 BOTH with and without
  my changes (verified via `git stash`) — pre-existing, builds a 2nd server app
  whose registry doesn't hold the task; not my regression. The working tree also
  carried unrelated pre-existing edits (`routes/api_v1/chat.py`, `lib/scheduler/
  manager.py`, several `__init__.py`) that I did NOT touch and left alone.

### 2026-06-22 — Tool panel now BRACKETS parallel tool calls into collapsible `.ptool-turn` groups (Option B: real nested containers)
- **Change:** The unified tool-activity panel rendered every tool round as a
  flat `<div data-prn>` row, so 3 greps fired together in ONE assistant turn
  looked identical to 3 greps fired across 3 sequential turns — the API-level
  parallelism (multiple tool_calls in one round-trip) was invisible. Now
  contiguous rounds sharing the same `llmRound` (the orchestrator loop index
  the backend already stamps at `lib/tasks_pkg/tool_dispatch.py:711`) are
  wrapped in a `.ptool-turn` container. Multi-call turns get a collapsible
  header ("N parallel calls" + git-fork SVG glyph, §3.4 — no emoji) and a left
  accent rail spanning their rows; a SOLO turn renders with `display:contents`
  so the wrapper vanishes and a single call looks exactly as before.
  **(1) `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`:** new shared helpers
  `_computeToolBatches` (contiguous same-`llmRound` grouping; ONLY groups on
  real llmRound data — legacy rounds without it stay solo, since the old
  roundNum-gap heuristic is too unreliable to *claim* parallelism visually),
  `_countToolTurns`, `_toolPanelHeaderLabel` (header now reads "N tools used ·
  M turns" only when M<N), `_renderTurnHead`, `_renderToolSlot`,
  `_renderToolGroupsHTML`. `_renderUnifiedGroup` rewritten to emit groups; a
  delegated click handler toggles `.collapsed` on a group when its header is
  clicked (scoped to `.ptool-turn-head` so clicking a tool row never toggles).
  **(2) `static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js` `_syncToolRoundsDOM`:** new slots are
  appended into their `.ptool-turn[data-llm-round=...]` container (created on
  demand) instead of directly into `.ptool-panel-body`; a slot that learns its
  llmRound late is relocated; a post-pass keeps each group's header in sync
  (insert when size≥2, update label, remove when it drops to solo). Added
  `r.llmRound` to the rounds fingerprint so a sibling arriving mid-turn
  actually re-renders. **(3) `static/js/upload.js`:** the "expand all"
  (`.ptool-truncated`) handler now calls `_renderToolGroupsHTML` so the
  expanded static view matches the grouped layout. **(4) `static/styles.css`:**
  the `.ptool-panel-body > [data-prn]` perf/interactive/swarm selectors were
  converted from direct-child to DESCENDANT (slots are now one level deeper
  inside `.ptool-turn`) — critical, else `content-visibility` + the
  interactive-card `:has()` overrides silently stopped applying. New
  `.ptool-turn` block: solo = `display:contents`, multi = bordered box with
  left rail + collapsible header, light-theme variants.
- **Why:** User pointed out the serial presentation misrepresents how the model
  actually works (one API round-trip issued N calls concurrently). Chose Option
  B (real nested containers) over Option A (flat DOM + CSS bracketing) for the
  most accurate + long-term-scalable structure: a real container can be
  collapsed as a unit and is the natural home for future per-turn affordances
  (timing, token totals, turn index). The `llmRound` signal is authoritative
  and monotonic/contiguous (one `round_num` per orchestrator iteration, same
  for every tool_call in it), so grouping is exact, not heuristic.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on all three JS files; bundle
  rebuilt (`bundle-04b85dc7.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. Verified the pure
  logic (parallel/sequential/legacy/solo/non-contiguous cases) and the
  end-to-end static HTML (2 containers, 1 parallel header on the 3-call group,
  solo `read` with no chrome, header "4 tools used · 2 turns") via standalone
  node harnesses. No test asserts the old flat structure. Naming note: used
  `.ptool-turn` (NOT `.ptool-batch*`, which is already owned by the apply_diffs
  edit-preview block). Edge case considered: two non-contiguous groups with the
  same `data-llm-round` would collide in the streaming `querySelector` lookup,
  but that can't occur — the backend emits all of a turn's tool_calls
  contiguously and `round_num` is monotonic.

### 2026-06-22 — Runtime payload trim: de-inline sidebar SVG + downscale orchestration role PNGs (1024px→128px)
- **Change:** Two runtime-focused size cuts (user explicitly scoped to bytes
  sent to the browser, NOT disk).
  **(1) Sidebar logo de-inlined — `index.html:91`:** the `<h1>` hand-inlined a
  ~31 KB `<svg class="sidebar-tofu-icon">` that was byte-for-byte the SAME
  VTracer welcome art already on disk as `static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg`.
  Replaced with `<img class="sidebar-tofu-icon" src="static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg"
  width="22" height="22">`. `index.html` 212618 → 181410 (−31,208). Trimmed the
  now-dead `color`/`-webkit-text-fill-color` declarations from the two
  `.sidebar-tofu-icon` CSS rules in `static/styles.css` (they never affected the
  hardcoded-fill paths anyway, and don't apply to an `<img>`); kept
  `flex-shrink`/`opacity`/`image-rendering:pixelated` which still apply.
  **(2) Orchestration role PNGs downscaled — `static/icons/tofu-{researcher,coder,
  analyst,writer,synthesizer,general,router}.png`:** these were 1024×1024 RGBA
  masters (4.5 MB for the 7 served files) but display at max 38px
  (`.orch-chip-ava`/`.orch-insp-avatar`). Resized to 128px (LANCZOS, optimize=True)
  → 4544 KB → 100 KB (−97%). Bumped `_ORCH_ICON_VER` in `orchestration.js`
  `20260618a`→`20260622a` so browsers re-fetch past the `max-age=86400` cache.
- **Why:** User asked for further size optimization, runtime-only. Investigated
  what actually loads: (a) gzip is ALREADY on (`server.py:605` `_compress_response`
  covers text/css + application/javascript ≥256B via an executor) so the 2.57 MB
  JS bundle + 810 KB CSS already ship compressed — nothing to do there; (b) the
  big disk hogs (`static/icons/_gen/` 1.9 MB, `static/posters/` 5.7 MB,
  `images/tofu-cache-article-cover.png` 7.1 MB) are NEVER served — grepped all
  js/html/css/py, zero references — so they're pure local storage, left alone per
  the user's scope. The only real runtime waste was the 1024px role PNGs (lazy,
  loaded only when the Orchestration/Task-mode modal opens) and the inlined
  sidebar SVG (always-loaded in index.html). KEY finding: planner/worker/critic
  roles carry a `.svg` extension in `_ORCH_ROLES.icon` so `_orchIconSrc` serves
  their SVGs — their PNGs are never fetched, so only the 7 bare-name roles
  (`+'.png'`) needed downscaling.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on orchestration.js; bundle rebuilt
  `bundle-45d12457.js`; downscaled researcher icon visually verified (crisp tofu +
  magnifier + book). All 7 PNGs git-tracked → 1024px masters recoverable from
  history if ever needed at higher res. index.html now 188495 (was 254315 at
  session start: −65.8 KB across favicon + sidebar). Restart + hard-refresh
  (favicon + bundle hash + icon cache-bust all changed). NOT touched: the disk-only
  `_gen/`/`posters/`/`cache-article-cover.png` (out of runtime scope).

### 2026-06-22 — Tab favicon: drop the 41.7 KB base64 blob, reference the welcome SVG file
- **Change:** `index.html:16` `<link rel="icon">` used to embed a ~30 KB base64
  string that (when decoded) was the VTracer-traced *welcome* artwork
  (`viewBox="47 33 166 188"`, dozens of soft-shaded sub-paths). Replaced the
  whole data-URI with a plain file reference:
  `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg">`.
  Same artwork the user wanted in the tab — just loaded from the existing file
  instead of inlined. `index.html` shrank 254315 → 212618 bytes (−41,697). The
  sibling `apple-touch-icon` (line 15, a different hand-drawn cube data-URI) and
  `static/manifest.json`'s inline PWA icon were left untouched per scope.
- **Why:** User noticed the asymmetry — the welcome-page icon is a one-line
  `<img src="static/icons/tofu-welcome.svg">` while the tab favicon carried the
  same art as a giant base64 blob. The blob is pure bloat: `routes/common.py`
  rewrites + serves `index.html` on every `GET /`, so the 41 KB rode along every
  page load for zero benefit (a favicon needs no inlining; the file loads fine).
  User explicitly chose to keep the welcome art as the tab icon (not the
  purpose-built `tofu-favicon.svg`), so this is a pure de-inline, no art swap.
- **Result / status:** Verified the single `rel="icon"` base64 line was replaced
  (regex anchored on `;base64,` so the non-base64 `apple-touch-icon` line was not
  touched). No bundler involvement — favicon is a static `<head>` link, not a JS
  module. Browser favicon cache is sticky → hard-refresh to see the new tab icon.
  NOTE / possible follow-up: the sidebar `<h1>` still hand-inlines the SAME
  welcome art as a ~26 KB `<svg>` (`index.html:91`, class `sidebar-tofu-icon`);
  its CSS `color`/`-webkit-text-fill-color` rule is a no-op (paths have hardcoded
  fills), only `opacity`/`image-rendering` matter — both work on an `<img>` too,
  so it could be de-inlined the same way. Left for a separate change.

### 2026-06-22 — Paper report kept Markdown, enriched the render layer (TOC + callouts + figures) + prompt nudge
- **Change:** Decided AGAINST switching Paper Reading Mode's report to
  LLM-generated HTML; instead invested in the client render layer while keeping
  Markdown as the interchange format.
  **(1) Render layer — `static/js/paper-reader.js`:** new `_renderFinalReport(container, text)`
  + helpers (`_decorateCallouts`, `_frameFigures`, `_indexHeadings`,
  `_buildReportTOC`, `_scrollReportToHeading`, `_wireReportScrollSpy`,
  `_slugifyHeading`). It renders the markdown into an off-document
  `<article class="paper-report-article">`, then post-processes the DOM:
  stable de-duplicated `id`s on every h2/h3; a sticky `.paper-report-toc`
  sidebar (suppressed when <3 headings) with an `IntersectionObserver`
  scroll-spy that highlights the in-view section and smooth-scrolls on click
  (old observer disconnected on re-render via `container._reportSpyObs`);
  blockquotes whose first word is a keyword become themed callout boxes
  (`.paper-callout-{takeaway,note,tip,warning,important}` with inline-SVG icons,
  NO emoji per CLAUDE.md §3.4); image-only paragraphs become
  `<figure class="paper-figure">` + `<figcaption>`. Routed ALL FIVE *final*-render
  sites through it (done-stream paint, in-memory cache instant path, two DB-cache
  hits, KaTeX-loaded repaint). Intermediate STREAMING frames still use plain
  `renderMarkdown()`, so live token-by-token rendering is unchanged — enhancement
  only runs once the report is complete.
  **(2) CSS — `static/styles.css`:** new "Paper Report — Enhanced render layer"
  block (centered `1fr / minmax(168px,216px)` grid collapsing to single-column
  <900px, sticky scroll-spy TOC, 5 callout variants with data-URI SVG icons,

  **(3) Prompt nudge — `lib/paper/prompts.py`:** added rule 4 to BOTH

  NOT on ordinary blockquotes or the problem→constraint reasoning chains.

  styling. Model-authored HTML was the wrong trade: it (a) breaks incremental
  streaming (a half-emitted HTML doc renders broken until `</div>` lands, vs.
  markdown which renders fine mid-stream), (b) DESTROYS theming because colors
  would live in the model's markup instead of the stylesheet, killing the
  dark/light/tofu switch, (c) adds an XSS / layout-break surface via `innerHTML`,
  and (d) costs more output tokens. The visual richness the user wanted is a
  render-layer concern, not a source-format concern — so keep MD, style the DOM.

  functions are module-global so the inline `onclick="_scrollReportToHeading(...)"`
  resolves. Gotcha fixed during impl: the callout regex originally used `\b`
  after the keyword, which never fires between two CJK chars (CJK isn't an ASCII
  word char) — so Chinese keywords like `提示：` would never match. Changed to
  `(?:[:：]|\b)` and reordered so the multi-char `takeaway` group (incl. bare
  `关键结论`) is tested before `important`'s broad bare `关键`, otherwise
  `关键结论：` would mis-classify as important. Goes through
  `renderMarkdown`→`DOMPurify.sanitize` first, then DOM transforms on a detached
  article → no new XSS surface. Pre-existing click-to-zoom handler still matches

### 2026-06-25 — Paper Q&A rebuilt as a server-owned AGENTIC TaskRuntime task: tools (web_search/fetch_url) + report-aware + section-aware context (kills the 100k blind truncation) + report-passage quote-to-ask

  papers), and NEVER showed the model the generated report — so "what did you
  mean in the Limitations section?" could not be answered. The objective: let
  users ask about the report and manage context well, leveraging Tofu's agent
  loop.
- **What landed (mirrors the report engine's proven pattern):**
  - **`lib/paper/qa_context.py`** — pure, testable context builder.
    `split_into_sections` (Markdown `#`/`##` headings from pymupdf4llm, preamble
    = section 0; falls back to ~3.5k char chunks when no headings).
    `select_relevant_sections` (lexical token-overlap scoring reusing the
    `arxiv._rerank_by_title` idea, widened by recent dialogue; keep-all when the
    whole paper fits the budget; otherwise greedily fill ~60k chars by
    relevance). `build_qa_messages` injects the FULL report (capped 60k) +
    the selected paper sections into one system prompt, EN/ZH, then recent
    history + the question.
  - **`lib/paper/qa_runtime.py`** — `TaskRuntime('paper-qa', ttl=1800,
    push_channel='paper')`; per-question tasks (not deduped like reports) + a
    light per-paper latest-task index for reattach.
  - **`lib/paper/qa_engine.py`** — `_run_qa_task` runs the SAME tool loop as the
    report engine (reuses `_execute_report_tool` + `_REPORT_TOOLS`), capped at
    `_MAX_QA_TOOL_ROUNDS=4`, emits chat-compatible `tool_start/tool_done/delta/
    delta_reset/done/error` events, and carries the interim-draft discard fix

  - **Routes (`/api/v1/*`):** `qa/start` (looks up the report from

### 2026-06-25 — Paper sidebar titles stuck at `arXiv:<id>`: robust title resolution (API retry → abs-page scrape) + report Paper-Card backfill with live `resolvedTitle` push
- **Symptom (user):** Many Paper-mode sidebar entries show the bare arXiv ID
  (e.g. `arXiv:1706.03762`) instead of the real paper title.
- **Root cause (confirmed against code):** Title resolution had a single
  fragile source. `fetch_arxiv_title` (`lib/paper/arxiv.py`) hit ONLY the arXiv
  Atom API and returned `''` on any failure with NO retry. arXiv's API is
  frequently slow / rate-limited, so it failed often. The frontend then
  hard-froze the fallback `_paperFileName = 'arXiv:' + id`
  (`paper-reader.js:1303`) and persisted it as the `paper_library.title` — never
  re-resolved, even though the real title was available downstream in (a) the
  parsed PDF and (b) the report's `| **Title** | … |` Paper Card row
  (`prompts.py:60`), which we were throwing away.
- **Fix — three layers (all landed):**
  1. **Robust `fetch_arxiv_title`.** Short retry on the Atom API
     (`_ARXIV_TITLE_RETRIES=2`, 1.5s sleep), then a NEW fallback
     `_fetch_title_via_abs_page` that scrapes the abs HTML page's
     `citation_title` meta (preferred) or `<title>` (strips the `[id] ` prefix)
     — a different endpoint rarely throttled in lockstep. Split into
     `_fetch_title_via_api` / `_fetch_title_via_abs_page` helpers. Every failed
     attempt logged per §2.2; final exhaustion is an `error`-level line, never a
     silent empty.
  2. **Report Paper-Card backfill (the self-heal).** New
     `_extract_title_from_report` (parses the EN `**Title**` / ZH `**标题**` row,
     strips md/links, rejects prompt placeholders + bare-arXiv values) and
     `_backfill_library_title` (`lib/paper/images.py`) which upserts the
     recovered title into `paper_library` **ONLY when the stored title is empty
     or a bare `arXiv:<id>` placeholder** — never clobbers a user-renamed or
     correctly-resolved title (mirrors the `_is_placeholder` predicate). Wired
     into `report_engine._run_report_task` after persist, AND into the
     `/report/start` DB-cache-hit branch in `routes/paper.py` (so already-broken
     entries with a cached report self-heal on next open, no engine run). The
     engine's title-prepend now prefers a non-placeholder stored title, else the
     Paper-Card title.
  3. **Live `resolvedTitle` push (no manual reload).** The `done` event +
     poll/cache responses now carry `resolvedTitle`; new frontend
     `_applyResolvedTitle(title, paperId)` updates the in-memory entry +
     `_paperFileName` + sidebar immediately, guarded (only overwrites a
     placeholder local title) and paper-scoped (a background stream for paper A
     can't rename active paper B). Wired into all three consume sites: streaming
     `done`, poll `done`, DB-cache-hit.
- **Headless verification:** New `tests/test_paper_title_recovery.py` (13 tests):
  abs-page fallback recovers when API throttled; API-success path takes no
  needless retry/fallback; all-sources-down returns `''` (no crash); Paper-Card
  extraction EN/ZH/placeholder-reject/link-strip; backfill heals arXiv+empty,
  respects user-renamed, no-row safe; AND two end-to-end engine tests (mocked
  dispatch) proving a finished report backfills an `arXiv:`-row + emits
  `resolvedTitle`, and leaves a renamed row alone. All 13 green. **Live smoke
  test against real arXiv** confirmed both happy paths resolve real titles
  ("Attention Is All You Need", "BERT: …"). Regression-clean:
  `test_paper_report_dedup.py` 4/4, `test_paper_migration.py` 14/14. `node
  --check` clean; `paper-reader.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` — restart +
  hard-refresh. Test-data gotcha caught during verification: `_safe_hash_dir`
  requires 8–64 **hex** chars, so phashes like `hashbackfill…` (contains
  `h`/`s`/`l`) are rejected at the guard — used `abcdef00…` hex phashes.
- **Next (per user's decision #2, NOT started):** rebuild Paper Q&A as a
  server-owned agentic `TaskRuntime` task with `web_search`/`fetch_url`
  (reuse `lib/paper/tools.py`), inject BOTH paper text AND the generated report
  into context, replace blind 100k truncation with section-aware selection, and
  extend `_quotePaperSelection` so a confusing report passage becomes a
  one-click question.

### 2026-06-25 — Browser bridge #2: async-native poll route (releases the worker thread during the long-poll), + desktop bridge parity + test-harness fix
- **Context:** Follow-up to the same-day #1/#3/#5 browser speedups. #2 is the
  root-cause fix for the scalability ceiling: each connected extension's 8s
  long-poll (`/api/browser/poll`) was a SYNC handler blocking a Hypercorn worker
  thread on a `threading.Event` for the whole window — one pinned thread per
  device, forever, even with no browser-enabled task. User explicitly forbade
  the `asyncio.to_thread`/`run_in_executor` band-aid (just moves the block to
  another pool thread) and the adaptive-backoff cadence hack; required a genuine
  asyncio-native wait.
- **Change — `lib/browser/queue.py`:** new `async def wait_for_commands_async()`
  awaits an `asyncio.Event` instead of the `threading.Event`, so the worker
  thread is released for the entire wait. The wrinkle: commands are enqueued from
  SYNC tool threads (`send_browser_command`), not the loop — so an async-waiter
  registry (`_async_waiters`: list of `{loop,event,client_id}`) is woken
  cross-thread via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(event.set)` in a new
  `_wake_async_waiters(client_id)`, called on the enqueue path right beside the
  existing `_notify.set()`. The sync `wait_for_commands` is untouched (kept for
  non-async callers). Per-client routing + the #3 TTL cutoff are preserved
  verbatim — they live in `get_pending_commands`, which the async path calls
  unchanged. CRITICAL teardown: the waiter deregisters itself in a `finally` so
  it leaks on NONE of the three exits — timeout, success, AND `CancelledError`
  (client disconnect mid-wait). Each await slice is capped at `min(remaining,1s)`
  so a missed wake (enqueue in the tiny window between `get_pending_commands` and
  `event.clear()`) is still re-checked promptly, mirroring the sync 1s cap.
- **Desktop parity — `lib/desktop/bridge.py`:** the desktop bridge shares the
  pattern, and although its old poll returned IMMEDIATELY (no long-poll, so it
  wasn't pinning threads), I gave it the same async long-poll
  (`take_pending_commands_async`) — a latency win (agent gets a command the
  instant it's queued instead of on its next 1s poll) with the same cross-thread
  wake + self-deregistering waiter. Exported through `lib/desktop/__init__.py`
  and re-exported from `routes/desktop.py` for back-compat.
- **Routes converted to `async def`:** `browser_poll`, `browser_get_commands`
  (`routes/browser.py`), `desktop_poll` (`routes/desktop.py`) — each now
  `await async_parse_body()` (the project's existing async-body helper; the sync
  `parse_body` shim's `asyncio.run()` fallback would raise inside a running loop)
  and `await …_async(...)`. `browser_post_result` stays sync (quick, non-blocking).
- **Magic-8 → env knob (§3.5):** the hardcoded `timeout=8` became
  `POLL_WAIT_TIMEOUT` in both bridges (`TOFU_BROWSER_POLL_WAIT` /
  `TOFU_DESKTOP_POLL_WAIT`, default 8.0, read at import). MUST stay < the
  extension's 12s `FETCH_TIMEOUT`. conftest sets 0.2 in the test env.
- **Test-harness fix (pre-existing bug surfaced):** `tests/test_bridge_auth.py`
  was already RED on HEAD — 12 failed / 8 passed — because `_SyncClient` in
  `tests/conftest.py` wrapped `get/post/put/...` but NOT `.open(method=...)`, so
  those calls returned an un-awaited `QuartClient.open` coroutine ("coroutine
  never awaited"), and `_SyncResponse.get_json` didn't accept `silent=`. PROVEN
  pre-existing by reverting my 5 files to HEAD (via cp-backup + `git checkout`,
  since the working tree has many unrelated pre-existing edits so a blanket stash
  was unsafe) and re-running: identical 12/8. Fixed the harness (added `'open'`
  to `_METHODS`; `get_json(silent=False)`) — now those 12 tests pass AND become
  real HTTP round-trips through my converted async routes (the strongest e2e
  proof the `async def` + `async_parse_body` + `await wait_for_commands_async`
  chain works under the actual Quart app + bridge-auth gate).
- **Tests / status:** new `tests/test_browser_async_poll.py` (10): coroutine-flag
  asserts; the core cross-thread wake (enqueue from a worker thread wakes the
  awaiter in <2s, NOT the full timeout) for BOTH bridges; fast-path; timeout;
  per-client routing on the async path; TTL cutoff on the async path; and
  registry-no-leak on timeout/success/cancellation. Full sweep 96/96 green
  (`test_browser_async_poll` 10, `test_browser_queue_ttl` 10,
  `test_browser_read_payload` 4, `test_bridge_auth` 20, `test_package_facades` 42,
  `test_server_async` 10). bridge_auth went 40.9s→1.5s after the env knob. JS
  unchanged (`node --check` clean). **Verification gap:** the thread-release under
  real concurrent load (N devices, M free threads) is reasoned + unit-proven but
  not load-tested here. The browser stack review's remaining items (#4 screenshot
  double-encode, #6 MV3 SW-death persistence, #9 content-script server detection)
  are NOT done — separate future work.


### 2026-06-25 — Browser bridge speedups: extension result-nudge (#1), server TTL alignment (#3), html-primary read payload (#5)
- **Context:** Review of the browser stack (extension long-poll ↔ `lib/browser`
  command queue ↔ `routes/browser.py` ↔ tool handlers) surfaced concrete slowness
  / correctness bugs. User confirmed the root causes and asked to build #1/#3/#5
  now, with #2 (async poll route to release the worker thread during the 8s wait)
  scoped NEXT — explicitly NOT the adaptive-backoff band-aid.
- **#1 Result-nudge (`browser_extension/background.js`):** A command result that
  finished mid-window only rode out on the *next* poll — and that poll then blocked
  server-side for the full 8s (`wait_for_commands`), so a result ready at 5s wasn't
  delivered until ~8s. `executeAndReport`'s "nudge the poll loop" comment was a
  no-op. Fix: hold the in-flight poll's `AbortController` in module state
  (`_activePollController`); after pushing a result, abort the idle poll. A
  `_flushPending` flag lets `poll()`'s catch distinguish this deliberate flush
  abort (re-poll INSTANTLY via `setTimeout(poll,0)`, and `unshift` the drained
  `resultsToSend` back so nothing is lost) from the 12s fetch-timeout abort (normal
  100ms reconnect). Splice→controller-assign is synchronous, so `executeAndReport`
  (interleaves only at `await`) always sees the controller once a fetch is live;
  between polls the controller is null and the ≤100ms scheduled poll picks it up.
- **#3 TTL alignment (`lib/browser/queue.py`):** Caller default timeout 30s, but
  `get_pending_commands` delivered commands up to a magic 60s old and
  `_cleanup_stale` evicted at 90s → "zombie" commands fired 30-60s after the model
  gave up, result silently dropped. Fix: store the caller's `timeout` + a
  `cancelled` flag on the command dict; delivery cutoff is now `cmd['timeout']`
  (not 60s) and skips `cancelled`; on caller-giveup `send_browser_command` marks
  the command `cancelled` before popping (so a racing poll won't run it); cleanup
  evicts at `timeout + _STALE_GRACE` (15s) instead of 90s.
- **#5 Read payload (`background.js::_extractContent`):** Both server consumers
  (`handlers._handle_read_tab`, `fetch.fetch_url_via_browser`) prefer
  `html→extract` and discard innerText on success, yet the extension always shipped
  BOTH innerText + up to 2MB outerHTML. Fix: HTML is now the primary payload;
  innerText is computed+shipped ONLY when `html.length < 2048` (the empty/shell/
  redirect case — read_tab waits for load so a real content page incl. rendered SPA
  always has substantial outerHTML; server gates extraction on `len(html) > 200`).
  Saves the innerText reflow + payload on the common path.
- **Version strings unified:** manifest 4.2.0→4.3.0, background.js header v4.1→v4.3,
  popup v4→v4.3 (popup.html badge v4.2→v4.3).
- **Tests / status:** New `tests/test_browser_queue_ttl.py` (10: delivery cutoff
  tracks caller timeout, short-timeout cutoff before old 60s, long-timeout still
  delivered, cancelled skipped, picked_up marking, caller-timeout cancellation +
  late-poll race, cleanup at timeout+grace) and `tests/test_browser_read_payload.py`
  (4: html→extract when text absent + text fallback when html small, for BOTH
  consumers via monkeypatched `send_browser_command`). All 56 pass with
  `test_package_facades.py` (42) regression-clean; `node --check` clean on
  background.js + popup.js. The extension is unpacked-install (not bundled), so no
  `_BUNDLE_FILES` involvement — users reload the extension to pick up background.js.
- **Next (#2, planned NOT band-aid):** convert `/api/browser/poll` (+`/commands`)
  to `async def` blocking on an `asyncio.Event` so the Hypercorn worker thread is
  released during the wait — root-cause fix for one-thread-pinned-per-connected-
  device. Requires an async-friendly notify (per-client `asyncio.Event` or
  `run_in_executor` slice) since the queue currently uses a global `threading.Event`.



### 2026-06-25 — Paper report rendered TWICE: discard interim drafts emitted alongside tool calls (`full_content` cross-round accumulation bug)
- **Symptom (user):** "My reading report seems broken — the output is extremely
  bare-bones / not comprehensive." Asked me to fix headlessly (no front-end).
- **Investigation (headless, real model):** Built a throwaway probe
  (`debug/_paper_report_probe.py`, since removed) driving `_run_report_task`
  end-to-end against the live model on an abridged "Attention Is All You Need".
  The report was NOT bare-bones — it was 55K chars, all 9 sections present and
  rich. The real defect: the **entire report was emitted TWICE** (two complete
  `## ⚡ TL;DR … ## 📝 Technical Reference` sequences). A garbled double-document
  is what reads as "broken". Crucially it was **non-deterministic** — a second
  live run produced one clean copy — because live `web_search` changes the
  model's tool-calling path.
- **Root cause (`lib/paper/report_engine.py::_run_report_task`):** `_on_content`
  did `full_content += text`, accumulating streamed content across **every**
  dispatch round. Tool-calling models (Claude) frequently emit a FULL interim
  DRAFT of the report in a round that *also* issues a `web_search` call, then
  rewrite the whole report from scratch in the terminal (no-tool-call) round.
  So `full_content` = draft + final → persisted/cached report contains the
  report twice. The frontend mirrors the same accumulation
  (`s.fullText += ev.delta`), so the live stream duplicated too.
- **Fix:** Track a per-round `round_content` buffer alongside `full_content`.
  When a round ends WITH tool calls, its prose was a premature draft → strip it
  from `full_content` (`full_content = full_content[:-len(round_content)]`) and
  emit a new `delta_reset` event. Only the terminal round's content survives.
  Frontend `_applyReportEvent` gains a `delta_reset` case that clears
  `s.fullText` / `contentStarted` / `_lastRenderedLen` so the live + poll
  streams drop the draft too. The common single-pass (no-tool) path is
  untouched.
- **Tests:** New `tests/test_paper_report_dedup.py` (4 deterministic tests,
  mock `dispatch_stream` to script the interim-draft+tool-call sequence the live
  model only hit intermittently): draft-discarded / delta_reset-emitted /
  single-pass-unaffected / well-behaved-tool-round-clean — all green.
  Regression-clean: `test_paper_migration.py` 14/14. `node --check`
  paper-reader.js OK; it's already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` — restart + hard-refresh
  to serve the new bundle. Live re-run after the fix: one clean 41K report,
  single `## ⚡ TL;DR`.

### 2026-06-25 — Stale-vs-live VU prompt detectability: content-derived `VU_PROMPT_VERSION` stamped into every directive turn
- **Why:** A pasted "you are simulating the user…" directive carried the OLD
  pre-upgrade `_VU_ROLE_PROMPT` (the reactive "reply briefly / 1-3 sentences /
  tool use is optional" text replaced earlier this session). Grep confirmed the
  source holds only the new PROJECT OWNER / VERIFY / THINK CREATIVELY /
  PROVENANCE prompt — so it was a not-yet-restarted server emitting an
  import-time constant, NOT a code bug. The diagnosis relied on eyeballing prose
  tells (old wrapper line, missing `=== ORIGINAL OBJECTIVE ===` header). User
  asked for a mechanical guard so a future stale paste is identifiable at a
  glance instead of by argument.
- **Change (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`):** added
  `VU_PROMPT_VERSION = sha256(_VU_ROLE_PROMPT)[:8]` (content-derived, so it
  auto-changes whenever the prompt text changes — a forgotten manual bump can't
  drift). Stamped into every VU directive turn TWO ways: visible in the role
  header (`=== Your role for THIS turn: Simulated User [prompt v<hash>] ===`)
  and as a programmatic key `_vuPromptVersion` on the directive message dict.
  A directive carrying an old marker (or none) = a server still running a
  pre-edit constant → restart. Current marker: `4ed6d799`.
