### 2026-06-25 — Benign-backlog completion pt.1: json_store inter-process flock + Phase 3 (msgId-authoritative truncate) + branch.js raw-fetch §3.2.0 fix
- **json_store flock (DONE):** `update_json_atomic` now wraps its RMW in a
  blocking POSIX `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` on a sidecar `<path>.lock` (inside the
  existing `threading.Lock`), closing the cross-process lost-update window. Locks
  the SIDECAR (not the data file) because `write_json_atomic`'s `os.replace`
  swaps the data inode. Degrades to no-op on Windows / no-fcntl / FS-without-flock
  (mirrors `_bootstrap._try_acquire_startup_lock`'s proven policy) — single-process
  behaviour unchanged. New `tests/test_json_store.py::test_update_json_atomic_inter_process_safe`
  (4 subprocs × 30 increments, no lost updates; skips where fcntl absent).
  Docstring + FOLLOWUPS §7 corrected.
- **Phase 3 — msgId-authoritative truncate (DONE, additive):** verification first
  showed the resend/branch index race is ALREADY mitigated (frontend syncs the
  truncated array via `syncConversationToServer({allowTruncate})` BEFORE
  `regenerate` fires, no async gap). So Phase 3 was done the additive way (not a
  risky rip-and-replace): `chat_regenerate` now reads optional `truncateToMsgId`,

  or unresolved (deleted msg). Frontend `saveEditAndResend` + `regenerateFromUser`
  send `truncateToMsgId: msg._msgId` (omitted when absent). `tests/test_regenerate_truncate_by_msgid.py`
  (5: resolve / drift-correction / unresolved→None / falsy / route-wiring).

  `lib.tasks_pkg.manager`, NOT re-exported at the package root → would have been a

- **branch.js raw-fetch §3.2.0 fix (DONE):** `_createBranchOnServer` used a raw

### 2026-06-25 — Autopilot VU: creativity mandate + explicit PROVENANCE contract (private investigation vs. the distilled message the agent receives) + frontend "Sent to the agent" boundary label
- **Why (user prompt):** "The most important thing is to be creative, sometimes
  providing insights the agent hadn't considered. Even if your own reasoning is
  complex, the content passed to the agent doesn't need to carry it — provide a
  clean summary. But the whole thinking process should be visible in the
  frontend, clearly identifying which parts are message context for the next
  agent." Two NEW requirements beyond yesterday's verify-driver upgrade:
  (1) creativity, not just grading; (2) a visible provenance split.
- **Key finding (the split already existed at the data layer):** traced the VU
  data flow end to end. `_append_vu_message_to_conv` stores the VU turn as
  `{role:'user', content, toolRounds, _isVirtualUser}`. When the follow-up task
  is built, `conv_message_builder._build_user_message` reads ONLY `content`
  (plus quotes/refs/pdf/images) — it never reads `toolRounds`, and the VU's
  `thinking` isn't even persisted. So the VU's tool investigation + reasoning
  are ALREADY display-only; only the reply text enters the next agent's API
  context. Nothing needed to change there — the gap was purely (a) the prompt
  never told the VU to exploit this (be creative + distil), and (b) the frontend
  labelled the investigation/thinking but not the CONTENT as "this is what the
  agent receives".
- **Change — prompt (`lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` `_VU_ROLE_PROMPT`):** added
  step 4 "THINK CREATIVELY" (surface edge cases / simpler approaches / hidden
  assumptions / untouched parts of the objective the assistant has NOT
  considered; lead with the insight — it's worth more than a verification
  report) + an explicit `=== PROVENANCE ===` block: "your tool calls and private
  reasoning are NOT sent to the assistant — it only receives your final REPLY
  TEXT; investigate as deeply as you need, but distil — the reply must be a
  clean, self-contained instruction; don't say 'as I found above'."
- **Change — frontend provenance label (`static/js/ui/chat_render.js`):** above
  the VU reply content (only on the finalized bubble, `!_streamingVu`) render a
  `.vu-handoff-header` with an arrow glyph + "Sent to the agent as the next
  message" (i18n `autopilot.sentToAgent`, zh/en). Visual grammar now reads top
  to bottom: indigo "Autopilot investigation · N tool calls" (private) → green
  "Sent to the agent →" (the handoff) → "Thinking Process" (private). New
  `.vu-handoff-header` CSS uses a GREEN "sent" accent to contrast the indigo
  "private process" accent. SVG glyph, not emoji (§3.4).
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_autopilot_verify.py` extended to 16 (new
  `test_vu_role_prompt_has_driver_and_creativity_and_provenance` asserts the
  driver+verify+creativity+provenance mandate survives prompt edits). 16/16 pass;
  regression set autopilot_arm/kick/poll_handoff + endpoint_messages +
  orchestration_engine = 117/117. `node --check` clean on chat_render.js +
  i18n.js; bundle rebuilt `bundle-d02b3da9.js` (all three touched files —
  i18n.js, ui/chat_render.js, ui/streaming_render.js — confirmed in
  `_BUNDLE_FILES`); restart + hard-refresh to serve. NOTE: the backend already
  enforces the provenance boundary (only `content` is replayed); the prompt +
  label make it INTENTIONAL and VISIBLE rather than incidental.


### 2026-06-25 — Autopilot virtual user upgraded from reactive responder → grounded project-owner DRIVER (objective anchor + mandatory verification + grounded TASK_DONE via classify_verdict)
- **Why (user prompt):** "The virtual user of autopilot should not just blindly
  cater to the agent's questions — it needs to deeply invoke tools to figure out
  what we actually need to do next, so it can fully replace humans." The old VU
  was structurally sycophantic: `_VU_ROLE_PROMPT` framed it as "simulate the
  user, reply briefly (1-3 sentences), tool use is optional", and the stop check
  was a bare `_VU_DONE_SENTINEL in text` that trusted the agent's self-report.
  With no objective anchor it drifted toward whatever the agent last proposed.
- **Change (highest-impact slice, root-cause not surface):**
  **(1) `lib/agent_verdict.py` — gating in the SINGLE source of truth:** the
  `verifier_role=='virtual_user'` branch of `classify_verdict` now runs the same
  unresolved-marker scan the endpoint critic's STOP guard uses
  (`_UNRESOLVED_EMOJI_RE` ❌ + `_UNRESOLVED_PHRASE_RE` "NOT met"/"still failing"/
  "still NOT met"/"unresolved"): a `[VU: TASK_DONE]`/STOP whose own reply STILL
  flags unresolved work is downgraded `stop→worker` (audit `vu_done_override`).
  No stop heuristic was forked into autopilot — it imports + delegates.
  **(2) `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` — driver identity:** rewrote
  `_VU_ROLE_PROMPT` to "you are the PROJECT OWNER; the assistant reports to you;
  trust nothing you haven't checked" with a 3-step contract (VERIFY the most
  consequential checkable claim with tools — now MANDATORY, not optional; ASSESS
  the gap vs the objective; DECIDE the genuine next step, not a reply to the
  agent's question). Dropped the "1-3 sentences" cap (it forced shallowness).
  **(3) Immutable objective anchor:** new `_extract_objective` (first real user
  msg, skipping `_isVuDirective`/`_isVirtualUser`, multimodal-aware) +
  `_get_or_persist_objective` (read-through cache pinned to
  `settings.autopilotObjective` so the anchor survives follow-up tasks AND
  compaction). `run_virtual_user` prepends an "ORIGINAL OBJECTIVE (north star —
  does NOT change)" header to the directive turn. **(4) Grounded done:** the stop
  decision now routes through `classify_verdict(text, verifier_role=
  'virtual_user')`; when a premature TASK_DONE is downgraded, the leftover
  sentinel token is stripped from the fed-back reply.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_autopilot_verify.py` (15 tests: verdict
  virtual_user policy clean-done/premature-❌/phrase/unresolved/plain/empty/STOP;
  objective extraction incl. multimodal + skip-synthetic; `run_virtual_user`
  premature-done-keeps-going + clean-done-stops + plain-reply + anchor-injected,
  all via a stubbed `_run_single_turn`, no live LLM). 15/15 pass. Regression
  clean: autopilot_arm/kick/poll_handoff + orchestration_engine + endpoint_
  messages + endpoint_flow_parity = 104/104. Did NOT run
  test_endpoint_flow_parity_live.py (paid LLM). No frontend change — VU still
  streams through the same `autopilot_vu_*` substrate; replies just get more
  substantive + show real tool rounds. Deliberate scope: arm/kick still pin the
  objective lazily on the first VU turn (read-through cache) rather than at
  arm-time — one fewer code path touched, same outcome.



### 2026-06-25 — Cross-conversation awareness, Layer 2: lazy project-summary engine + bounded always-on project digest (+ design note)
- **Goal:** ambient awareness — the model should KNOW sibling conversations of
  the same project exist (and their gist) without the user attaching anything.
  Built as the agreed tiered hybrid: AI title = discovery index; cached
  one-paragraph summary = awareness; bounded digest = injection vehicle.
- **New engine `lib/conversations/project_summary.py`:**
  * `generate_summary(messages)` — 1-3 sentence "outcome + key decisions" via
    the cheap model (reuses the `title_gen` `dispatch_chat(capability='cheap')`
    pattern; outcome-weighted source = first 2 + last 6 text turns, ~4 KB cap).
  * `ensure_summary(conv_id, force=, blocking=)` — generate-if-stale + persist
    to `settings.projectSummary={text,generated_at,msg_count_at_gen}`.
    `blocking=False` returns the cached text immediately and regenerates in a
    daemon thread (hot-path safe). Staleness gate `_is_stale`: regenerate only
    when `msg_count - msg_count_at_gen >= SUMMARY_STALE_GROWTH` (6); floor
    `SUMMARY_MIN_MESSAGES`=3; summary hard-capped `SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`=320.
  * `build_project_digest(project_path, current_conv_id, limit)` — READ-ONLY,
    side-effect-free (never generates): top `DIGEST_MAX_SIBLINGS`=10 most-recent
    OTHER same-project convs as `"title" — summary [id]`, title-only fallback
    when a sibling has no summary yet. `_persist_summary` writes ONLY the
    `settings` column under a lock (never messages/updated_at → no sidebar
    reorder, no race with the message-persist path).
- **Two lazy triggers (both non-blocking, never eager/batch):**
  * **A — post-reply:** `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py::_maybe_refresh_project_summary`,
    called at the end of `persist_task_result`; fires only for completed,
    non-aborted project conversations (`config.projectEnabled` + `projectPath`).
  * **B — on first read:** `lib/conv_ref.py::get_conversation` kicks
    `ensure_summary(blocking=False)` when the model reads a sibling.
- **Digest injection:** `lib/tasks_pkg/system_context.py` step 4.4 — always-on
  in project mode, its own cache-stable `<system-reminder>` block, idempotent
  via a marker probe (mirrors the other context blocks). Tells the model the
  siblings exist + to use `list_conversations(scope='project')` /
  `get_conversation(id)`.
- **Design note:** `docs/CROSS_CONV_AWARENESS.md` records all three layers and
  the six explicit decisions (lazy-not-eager; regenerate only on material
  growth; bounded always-on digest; settings-only persistence; non-blocking hot
  paths; title fallback) + the cost ceiling (one cheap call per conv per ~6 new
  msgs, active/referenced convs only; NO whole-project batch path).
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_project_summary.py` (9, LLM monkeypatched
  → offline/deterministic): fresh-not-regenerated, missing-generated+persisted,
  below-floor-skipped, persist-touches-only-settings, staleness math,
  force-regen, digest bounded/scoped/self-excluded/title-fallback/empty-without-
  project. Combined run with Layers 0/1 + search suite = **62 passed**. Verified
  the engine LIVE against PG: a real 4.8s summary generated for an 8-msg conv,
  2nd call 0.01s cached no-op (staleness proven), persisted correctly; then
  REMOVED that manual-test `projectSummary` from the live row. All-backend
  imports clean. Pure backend Python — no new top-level JS, bundler not
  involved; restart to load. The ONLY red test remains the pre-existing
  `test_tool_registry.py::TestOrdering` `inspect_image` ordering drift
  (confirmed unrelated via stash in the Layer 0/1 session).
- **Lang note:** the summary prompt says "use the conversation's language"; a
  spot-check produced an English summary for a Chinese-TITLED conv — but the
  conv BODY was English (the title was force-translated by title-gen), so it
  was correct, not a bug. No prompt hardening needed.

### 2026-06-25 — Global memories moved to a project-independent SERVER store (`<data>/memories/global/`) — fixes "global never triggers without a project" + makes them genuinely cross-project
- **Symptom / why:** User noticed the memory prefetch never seemed to fire. Root
  cause traced through the full chain: "global" memories were physically stored
  at `<project>/.tofu/skills/global/`, and `_iter_roots(None, None)` returns `[]`
  when no project is attached → `get_eligible_memories(None)` returns `[]` →
  `run_memory_prefetch` bails immediately with `_emit('skipped', reason='no_memories')`.
  So in a project-less chat NOTHING is ever injected. Worse, even WITH a project,
  "global" was a misnomer: A's global memories lived under A and were invisible
  from B — the scope name promised cross-project reach the storage layout never
  delivered. The prefetch GATE itself was never the problem (`has_real_tools` is
  true in nearly every chat because `read_files`/`inspect_image`/`fetch` are
  always-on base tools) — the storage layer was.
- **Fix (`lib/memory/storage.py`):** global memories now live in a single
  server-side store `<data>/memories/global/`, where `<data>` is `$TOFU_DATA_DIR`
  (desktop builds pin this; see `desktop/launcher.py:63`) else `<project_root>/data`.
  New helpers `_server_data_dir()` / `_server_global_memory_dir()`. `list_all_memories`
  now scans the server store FIRST (canonical, wins on id collision), THEN the
  legacy per-root `.tofu/skills/global/` (still READ for back-compat) + each root's
  project dir. `resolve_target_dir('global', None)` no longer raises — global writes
  go to the server store regardless of project; only `scope='project'` still requires
  a `project_path`. A once-per-process, idempotent `_migrate_one_root_globals(root)`
  COPIES (not moves — original preserved, shadowed by id de-dup) each legacy global
  `.md` / `<id>/SKILL.md` into the server store on first read, so pre-existing globals
  become cross-project without loss. Also fixed an adjacent latent bug:
  `delete_memory`'s package-deletion guard only allowed paths under project roots, so a
  global skill PACKAGE in the server store would have been refused deletion — added the
  server-global dir to the allowed-prefix list.
- **Decision — did NOT centralize project memories / did NOT add path-association.**
  User explicitly said linking is fine to skip ("It's fine not to link it for now").
  Project memories intentionally STAY at `<project>/.tofu/skills/` so they travel with
  the repo (clone/copy/other-machine all carry them). Path-as-association-key was
  rejected earlier in the discussion as fragile (paths move/rename, FUSE remounts,
  multi-root ambiguity, clone strands them); if resilience is ever wanted, a stable
  `.tofu/project_id` UUID marker is the robust route, not raw paths.
- **Export:** NO `export.py` change needed. `data/` is already a blanket
  `ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` entry (internal/opensource strip it) and personal mode tars
  `data/` wholesale minus heavy DB globs — byte-for-byte the same tier treatment the
  old `.tofu/` location had (also an ALWAYS_EXCLUDE dir). The new `memories/` subdir
  inherits the parent exclusion (same pattern `lib/config_dir.py` documents). Updated
  the `config_dir.py` docstring note that previously claimed all memories live under
  `.tofu/skills/`.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_memory_global_server_store.py` (6 tests, all
  pass): global create+read with project=None; cross-project visibility (A→B); project
  scope still requires a project + stays local; legacy global migrated on first read
  (idempotent, original preserved); server-store wins on id collision over a stale
  legacy copy. Regression: `test_package_facades.py` green. NOTE: the ONE failing test
  in the suite run — `test_tool_registry.py::test_full_project_ordering_is_cache_stable`
  — is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated (tool-registry `find_files`/`inspect_image` layout in
  other uncommitted working-tree work; verified independent of `storage.py`). Pure-Python
  change; restart to pick up. Tests redirect `TOFU_DATA_DIR` to a tmp dir and clear the
  module's `_migrated_roots` latch for isolation.



### 2026-06-25 — Cross-conversation awareness, Layer 0 + 1: fix the conv_ref false-positive gate + make `list_conversations` project-aware with content search
- **Origin (investigation):** A user saw the "工具改动将在新会话生效" (toolset-diverged)
  banner list `get_conversation` / `list_conversations` as added tools, with no
  frontend toggle for them and no `@`-mention made. Root-caused against the LIVE
  PG store (3278 convs; SQLite `data/tofu.db` is a stale 14-row shadow — do NOT
  trust it): the only conv tripping the gate was THIS one, via `gateASST=2` — i.e.
  the **assistant's own explanatory text** quoted the literal token. `has_conv_ref`
  (`lib/tools/registry.py`) matched the bare substring `[REFERENCED_CONVERSATION`
  in **any** message of **any** role, so a conversation *about* the feature
  self-enabled the tools → schema diverged from the per-conv tool latch → banner.
  No real reference was ever attached (no `convRefs`/`convRefTexts` on any user row).
- **Layer 0 — fix the gate (`lib/tools/registry.py::has_conv_ref`):** now scans
  **user-role messages only** and matches either (1) the structured
  `convRefs`/`convRefTexts` field (authoritative signal on raw rows), or (2) the
  server-injected wrapper signature `[REFERENCED_CONVERSATION` **plus** `title="`
  (what `conv_message_builder` prepends — distinguishes the real block from a
  quoted token). Assistant content is never scanned. Tests: extended
  `tests/test_tool_registry.py` (real-wrapper-on, structured-field-on,
  assistant-prose-must-NOT-trigger regression) — the old test's fake
  `[REFERENCED_CONVERSATION:abc]` (no `title="`) was exactly the false-positive
  shape we now reject, so it was rewritten to the real wrapper.
- **Layer 1 — project-aware + content search (`lib/conv_ref.py`):**
  `list_conversations(keyword, limit, scope='auto', project_path, current_conv_id)`.
  `scope`: `project` filters on `json_extract(settings,'$.projectPath')` (rewritten
  to the PG jsonb accessor by `_sql_translate`, so one SQL works on both backends);
  `all` = everything; `auto` (default) = project when a path is present else all.
  Keyword now matches message CONTENT, not just the title: new `_keyword_clause`
  uses the GIN-indexed `search_tsv` tsvector prefix query on PG (mirrors
  `routes/conversations_search.py`) OR the title, falling back to portable
  `title/search_text LIKE` on SQLite. `current_conv_id` is excluded. Threaded
  `project_path` through `execute_conv_ref_tool` → the `_handle_conv_ref_tool`
  handler (`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/misc.py`, which already receives it). Schema
  doc updated (`lib/tools/conversation.py`) with the `scope` enum + "matches title
  AND content". Tests: new `tests/test_conv_ref_scope.py` (5: project-scope
  excludes other projects; content keyword hits body not title; scope+keyword;
  current-conv excluded; auto→all without a path).
- **Perf note:** the tsvector path dropped the project+keyword query 2764ms→1384ms
  (now under the 2000ms slow-log threshold). Residual cost is the unindexed
  `settings->>'projectPath'` filter; a functional index on it is a sensible
  follow-up but out of scope here (this is a model-invoked tool, not per-keystroke).
- **Result / status:** 39 passed (5 new scope + 34 existing search) + the 4 new
  conv_ref gate tests green; imports clean. ONE pre-existing failure remains —
  `test_tool_registry.py::TestOrdering::test_full_project_ordering_is_cache_stable`
  expects a 6-tool prefix but `inspect_image` is now registered between
  `read_files` and `list_dir`; confirmed via `git stash` that it fails WITHOUT my
  changes too (unrelated working-tree drift), so left untouched rather than mask
  someone's in-progress ordering edit. NOTE: this repo flags `git stash` as
  hazardous (.tofu/file-history); it popped cleanly but avoid it going forward.
- **Next (Layer 2, agreed):** ambient project awareness — tiered hybrid: AI titles
  as the discovery index + a lazily-generated, cached one-paragraph
  `settings.projectSummary` (reuse the `title_gen` cheap-model pattern; regenerate
  only when msg_count grows materially) + a bounded project digest injected into
  system context. Generate summaries lazily (post-first-reply / on first
  `get_conversation`), never eagerly batch-summarize all 174 project convs.

### 2026-06-25 — Native-async path goes LIVE: new on-loop POST /api/v1/chat/stream-direct (+ version sync + doc-accuracy sweep)
- **Context:** Follow-up to the sync-robustness investigation. `async_dispatch_stream`
  was implemented + tested but had NO production caller — every streaming path
  (UI worker AND `/v1` compat endpoints) runs the task off-loop via
  `spawn_task`→`asyncio.to_thread` and just tails the event buffer, so a sync
  worker thread can't `await` it. User chose to make the native-async path live
  the RIGHT way (a real on-loop endpoint) rather than force-wire it into the
  thread worker (which would regress) or do the forbidden Stage-3 async-run_task
  rewrite.
- **#1 version drift (FIXED):** `pyproject.toml` 0.11.0 → 0.13.0 to match the
  runtime `VERSION` file (`lib/version.py` reads VERSION; `tofu.spec`/`package.json`
  needed no change — spec reads VERSION at runtime, package.json is the FE dev-dep
  at 0.1.0). FOLLOWUPS §8 corrected.
- **#2 doc accuracy (FIXED):** corrected `docs/FOLLOWUPS_ASYNC_MIGRATION.md` — §3
  PG full-text "LIKE-only" → DONE (verified the real `to_tsquery('simple','w:*')`
  + GIN `search_tsv` path exists in conversations_search.py:~80; LIKE is just the
  Phase-2 substring fallback); §2/§4 trading items → MOOT (verified the trading
  modules + tests are GONE — externalized to `tofu-trading`).
- **Feature — native-async on-loop streaming (NEW):** `routes/api_v1/chat_direct.py`
  — `POST /api/v1/chat/stream-direct`. `run_direct_stream` (the testable core,
  injectable `dispatch_fn`) runs `async_dispatch_stream` as a background
  `asyncio.Task` ON the loop; its sync `on_content`/`on_thinking` callbacks fire
  on the loop thread (verified: `_sse_core.SSEAccumulator` calls them inline in
  the `aiter_lines` parse loop) so they `queue.put_nowait` straight into an
  `asyncio.Queue`; an async generator drains the queue → OpenAI
  `chat.completion.chunk` SSE frames → terminal frame (finish_reason+usage, or a
  `tofu_error` envelope on dispatch failure) → `[DONE]`. Client-disconnect
  cancels the in-flight dispatch task. Admission-gated (shared `controller`,
  released in the generator's `finally`). **Deliberate scope:** single-turn,
  pure-text(±thinking), SSE-only — NO tool loop / MCP / multi-round / task-replay
  (those need the thread orchestrator; callers use `/chat/completions`).
- **Zero compromise to the thread-worker path:** new isolated module + blueprint
  (`api_v1_chat_direct_bp`, registered in `routes/api_v1/__init__.py`); touches
  NONE of create_task / spawn_task / manager / the orchestrator. `/chat/completions`
  and the UI path are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Test net first + guards extended:** `tests/test_chat_stream_direct.py` (6:
  delta-ordering, role-once, thinking→reasoning_content, terminal+usage,
  dispatch-error→envelope, zero-delta, finish_reason passthrough) against a stub

### 2026-06-25 — Mobile Paper Reading Mode: sidebar showed CHAT instead of the paper library + no exit affordance — both fixed
- **Symptom (user: "the sidebar in reading mode is all wrong"):** On a phone, opening
  the sidebar drawer while in Paper Reading Mode showed the normal CONVERSATION list,
  not the paper library (current paper + library list) that desktop shows.
- **Root cause:** The desktop rules (`static/styles.css:730-739`) make a
  `.sidebar.paper-active` drawer BE the paper library (`.paper-sidebar-overlay`
  display:flex; chat action-row/search/folder-tabs/conv-list display:none). But the
  mobile `@media(max-width:768px)` block (was ~`:1068`) OVERRODE all of that in
  reverse: `.paper-sidebar-overlay{display:none!important}` + re-showed
  action-row/search/folder-tabs/conv-list + the `h1`. So mobile force-reverted the
  paper drawer back to the chat drawer — an obsolete assumption (probably from when
  paper mode was conceived desktop-only). `paper-active` IS applied on mobile
  (`paper-reader.js:414`) and `_renderPaperLibrary()` populates the overlay, so the
  data was there — just CSS-hidden.
- **Fix (`static/styles.css`, in the mobile @media):** replaced the reverting block
  with the CORRECT paper-active behaviour (overlay `display:flex!important`; chat
  bits `display:none!important`; `h1` hidden) — mirroring desktop — plus mobile touch
  sizing for the library: `.paper-lib-item` padding 12px / min-height 48px,
  `.paper-sidebar-new-inline-btn` 24→32px, and `.paper-lib-item-del` forced
  `display:flex` at 32px (it was hover-only `display:none`, so papers were
  UNDELETABLE on touch).
- **Second bug found while verifying (no exit path):** In paper mode the input bar is
  `display:none` (`enterPaperMode`), so its "···" mobile sheet — the only place the
  `#mobilePaperMode` toggle lives — is unreachable. The exit affordance is the topbar
  Paper button, which becomes a back-arrow (`#paperModeBtn.active`), but it sits in
  `.topbar-tools`, a cluster clipped by `.topbar{overflow:hidden}` + `flex:1` title on
  360px → the user could be STRANDED with no way out. Fix: when paper mode is active
  (`.topbar-tools:has(#paperModeBtn.active)`), hide every OTHER topbar tool/update btn
  and pin `#paperModeBtn.active` visible at a 44px touch target. `:has()` is already
  used 16× in this stylesheet (supported on the iOS15.4+/Chrome105+ mobile targets).
- **Result / status:** CSS braces balanced (5808/5808); confirmed the buggy
  `display:none!important` overlay revert is GONE, the paper-active overlay flex rule
  is present, and the back-button guard is in place. Pure CSS — auto-versions via
  `lib/css_bundler.get_styles_hash`, no bundle rebuild. Targets small Android 360px +
  iPhone 390px. Exit path verified: `#paperModeBtn` onclick=`togglePaperMode()` →
  `exitPaperMode()`. Could not do live on-device visual check; verified by structure +
  rule presence. Desktop paper sidebar untouched.


### 2026-06-25 — Sync-robustness pass: #1 SSE warm-resync guard, #2 first-checkpoint window, #4 reload offset-resume, #5 send idempotency; #3 SKIPPED (already robust)
- **Context:** A 4-agent investigation of the frontend↔backend sync mechanism
  found it ALREADY near-best-practice (backend fully decoupled from SSE — a
  disconnect never aborts/stalls; Last-Event-ID offset-resume; durable
  append-only `task_events` cold-replay surviving eviction+restart; poll
  fallback; 5s DB checkpointing; self-healing `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup`).
  Five residual edges were identified; the user asked to harden all five for
  long-term robustness. Verifying each against CODE first (per the
  `tofu-stale-migration-status-docs` discipline) materially changed #3.
- **#1 — Warm-path past-end resync guard (routes/chat.py).** REAL bug: when a
  reconnect's `Last-Event-ID` cursor was AHEAD of the in-memory buffer,
  `task['events'][resume_from:]` sliced to `[]` → the warm stream sent nothing
  (silent stall) and mis-indexed the live loop. New pure helper
  `_warm_resume_serviceable(resume_cursor, n_events)` (`resume_from <= n_events`);
  when not serviceable, fall through to a full state-snapshot resync (mirrors the
  cold path's "MUST emit state before done"). `tests/test_sse_resume_guard.py`
  (6). [Done in the prior turn's start; finalized here.]
- **#2 — Pre-first-checkpoint crash window (lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py).** REAL,
  narrow: `stream_llm_response` init'd `_last_stream_ckpt = time.time()`, so the
  first crash-recovery checkpoint couldn't fire until 5s in — a server crash
  after the first tokens but before the tick lost the whole turn. Fixed: init to
  `0.0` so the FIRST content/thinking delta checkpoints immediately, then the 5s
  cadence resumes (matches the orchestrator tool-loop's existing
  `_last_checkpoint = 0.0`). `checkpoint_task_partial` already no-ops while
  content+thinking are empty, so an early call is harmless.
  `tests/test_stream_first_checkpoint.py` (2: fires-on-first-delta +
  still-throttled-after, proving no per-delta write storm).
- **#3 — "Un-retried final persist." SKIPPED — verification showed it's already
  robust; a fix would be gold-plating.** The investigating agent missed that
  `_upsert_task_row` already passes `retry=True` → `db_execute_with_retry`
  (**4 attempts**, backoff on contention/connection-loss). On top: (a)
  `_sync_result_to_conversation` runs OUTSIDE the try/except and independently
  persists terminal content + finishReason/usage/model to the conversation row;
  (b) `recover_stale_tasks_on_startup` guards `if not last_msg.get('finishReason')`
  and `if len(task_content) > existing` → it will NOT clobber an already-completed
  message on reboot. So "finished result is lost" is wrong: the write is retried
  and there are two durable fallbacks. Adding more retry also cuts against the
  `sync-fixes-2026-05-31` memory's explicit M1 deferral ("task_results carries
  canonical data; benign-skip is correct"). No code change.
- **#4 — Reload offset-resume (static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js).** VERIFIED gap:
  `stream._lastEventId` is in-memory only, so a page RELOAD always did a fresh
  full-snapshot connection (lossless for final state, but lost intermediate
  tool/phase event granularity). Fix: persist the cursor in `sessionStorage`
  (survives reload, per-tab, cleared on tab close) keyed by taskId —
  `_saveSseCursor` on each `id:` parse, seed `stream._lastEventId` from it in
  `_trySSE` when not already set, `_clearSseCursor` on terminal `done`. The
  server's warm/cold replay is UNCHANGED — this only feeds it the cursor it
  already honors. All sessionStorage access guarded (private-mode safe →
  degrades to the existing full-snapshot reload). Custom fetch-based SSE reader
  (not native EventSource), so no free browser reconnect — this is the minimal
  equivalent.
- **#5 — Idempotent send (routes/chat.py + main_send_pipeline.js).** VERIFIED
  gap: `/api/v1/chat/start` + `/api/v1/chat/send` (the UI send path) had only
  `abort_running_tasks_for_conv` (prevents two CONCURRENT tasks, NOT idempotency)
  — a network-retried POST spawned a 2nd task + double-charged. The headless
  `/api/v1/chat/completions` was ALREADY idempotent (existing
  test_idempotency_key_replays) but the UI path was NOT. Fix reuses the existing,
  tested `@idempotent_post()` (lib/idempotency.py) on both handlers (no-op
  without the header → backward-compatible). Frontend now sends
  `Idempotency-Key: <userMsg._msgId>` (the optimistic message's stable id,
  assigned once per logical send) so a retry replays the cached {taskId}.
  `tests/test_chat_send_idempotency.py` (2); mechanism proven e2e by the existing
  completions test against the same decorator+cache.
- **Result / status:** 101 passed across the new + regression suites (resume-guard
  6, first-checkpoint 2, idempotency 2, typecheck baseline still 0,
  chat_manager/orchestrations/task_runtime green). `node --check` clean on both
  JS files; both already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; tsc baseline preserved at 0. The
  ONLY failure is the long-pre-existing `test_chat_streams_via_http_endpoints`
  (404 from a 2nd-server-app registry mismatch — independent of any change).
  Two `insert_content` duplicate-anchor artifacts hit + fixed (the `chat_stream`
  def line). Backend Python + frontend JS; restart + hard-refresh to serve the
  new bundle.

- **DELIBERATELY NOT wired (would have been half-baked):** Timer (`#timerPanel`)

### 2026-06-25 — export.py `--bump` now commits the bumped VERSION back to the ORIGIN tree (kill the self-nagging update prompt) + dry-run no longer mutates VERSION
- **Symptom:** The origin/dev project (the source of truth that produces the
  exported open-source copy) started showing the topbar "update available" badge.
  `lib/self_update.check_for_update` is purely `latest_tag > local_VERSION`
  (`_parse_semver`), and the live `rangehow/ToFu` tags API top tag was `v0.13.0`
  == local `VERSION` 0.13.0 → equal → should NOT fire. So the prompt was either
  stale UI state OR (the latent footgun) a future drift where origin's VERSION
  lags the published tag.
- **Root cause (the real drift mechanism):** `_bump_version` in `export.py`
  writes the new number into the ORIGIN `VERSION` file (`_VERSION_FILE = ROOT /
  'VERSION'`), but only the EXPORTED copy was ever committed + tagged
  (`_git_push` runs in `dest`, tags `vX.Y.Z` there when `is_release`). The origin
  VERSION bump sat UNCOMMITTED, and the published tag drifted ahead of origin's
  last commit — so on the next release the origin machine's own self-update
  checker sees `latest_tag (vX.Y.Z) > origin_VERSION` and nags about a release it
  itself produced. The two only ever stayed in sync by someone manually
  re-committing VERSION on origin.
- **Fix (`export.py`):**
  * **`_commit_version_to_origin(version)`** (new) — after a real `--bump`, runs
    `git commit VERSION -m vX.Y.Z` in `ROOT` (the origin tree). Commits ONLY the
    `VERSION` file (leaves any other in-progress origin edits alone); short-
    circuits via `git diff --quiet -- VERSION` so a no-op re-run makes no empty
    commit; skips cleanly when origin isn't a git checkout (`.git` absent); NEVER
    raises — git-missing / commit-failure is logged + printed as a yellow warning
    so the export itself can't be broken by it. Wired into `main()` right after
    `_bump_version`.
  * **`_next_version(current, part)`** (extracted pure helper) — `_bump_version`
    now delegates the compute to it. The `--dry-run --bump` path calls
    `_next_version` to PREVIEW the next version WITHOUT writing or committing,
    honoring the long-standing dry-run contract ("no files will be written").
    Previously a dry run still mutated `VERSION` on disk via `_bump_version`,
    leaving origin in the exact uncommitted-drift state this change fixes.
- **Why this approach:** The user explicitly scoped it to "write the new VERSION
  back to origin and commit it here." Committing only `VERSION` (not `git add -A`)
  is the minimal, safe write — origin is a shared tree that may carry unrelated
  WIP. Tagging stays on the EXPORTED repo as before (per the
  `tofu-versioning-system` convention: tags + version-prefixed commits only on
  `--bump`); origin gets the commit, not a tag, so its HEAD no longer trails the
  published tag.
- **Result / status:** `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('export.py'))"` OK;
  module imports clean; `_next_version` verified for patch (0.13.0→0.13.1), minor
  (→0.14.0), major (→1.0.0), and malformed input (garbage→0.0.1); confirmed the
  bare import does NOT bump the on-disk `VERSION` (still 0.13.0). NOTE / honest
  scope boundary: this commits to origin's LOCAL git only — it does not `git push`
  origin. If origin tracks its own remote, push it separately; the commit now
  exists so the tag no longer drifts ahead of origin's HEAD. The badge the user
  saw was almost certainly stale UI (re-run the check / hard-refresh to clear it,
  since 0.13.0 == v0.13.0); this change prevents the drift recurring on the next
  real release.


### 2026-06-24 — Fixed frontend typecheck regression: declared Icon/IconDot + 23 other genuine window.* globals in globals.d.ts (BASELINE back to 0)
- **Symptom:** `test_frontend_typecheck::...does_not_regress` failed with

  exists at runtime. The file was added in a prior session WITHOUT the
  corresponding `declare var` in `static/js/globals.d.ts` — exactly the "Keep in

### 2026-06-24 — Extracted two self-contained islands: orchestrator commit-round → commit_round.py, manager auto-translate → auto_translate.py
- **Why (refactor audit P2, the two cleanest remaining cuts):** `orchestrator.py`

  that doesn't belong in a task manager. Both are genuine islands (unlike the
  ControlExecutor): no shared mutable instance state, no recursion back into their
  origin module, used only via module-level functions.

  `derive_round_modified_files` (per-root journal → authoritative round file list,
  conversation-isolated via taskId stamping), `_spawn_async_commit_round` /
  `_run_commit_round_async` (daemon-thread `file_history.make_snapshot` + the
  fh-side-channel attribution filter + `round_committed` SSE event), and
  `_patch_assistant_message_with_git` (persist snapshotId to the conversation
  after the SSE reader closed). Deps: stdlib + `EventType`/`build_event`
  (lib.agent_core.events, leaf) + `append_event` (lib.tasks_pkg.manager). One-way
  dependency (commit_round → manager, never reverse) → no cycle. orchestrator
  re-imports all 4 → its call sites (`_finalize_and_emit_done` @777/861/1004)
  unchanged. orchestrator.py 2561 → 2119 lines.
- **(2) `lib/tasks_pkg/auto_translate.py`** — moved
  `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` + `_maybe_auto_translate_critic` verbatim (the
  server-side safety net: autoTranslate-gate, frontend-task dedup, stale-partial
  re-translation, already-Chinese short-circuit, incremental hand-off). Deps:
  DB helpers from `lib.database` (leaf) + lazy `lib.translate`/`lib.text_lang` —
  NOT manager → no cycle. Both `manager._sync_result_to_conversation` AND

### 2026-06-24 — _ensure_pg_running: lifted the two SAFE self-contained steps (1 + 3b) into helpers + added a test net; left the dangerous ownership/pidfile core INTACT
- **Why (refactor audit P2):** `_ensure_pg_running` (`lib/database/_bootstrap.py`,
  ~486 lines) is a sequential Step-0→1→2→2b→3→3b→4/5 pipeline. The audit proposed
  "split into per-step helpers." But this is the MOST DANGEROUS function in the
  codebase: the `pg-pidfile-deletion-cross-machine-bug` memory documents how the
  Step-3/Step-4 ownership + pidfile-deletion ORDERING caused multi-machine PG
  corruption (swallowed NameError, None-owner logic hole). So decomposition had to
  be surgical — extract only the steps with NO interaction with that ordering.
- **What was lifted (the two genuinely safe, self-contained steps):**
  * **`_pgdata_major_compatible(pgdata) -> bool`** (Step 3b) — the pgdata↔binary
    major-version sanity check. Pure: reads `PG_VERSION` + shells `postgres
    --version`. Returns False (caller bails to SQLite) on mismatch / no-binary,
    True otherwise. Logic moved verbatim; the 4-way outcome (no file / match /
    mismatch / FileNotFound / non-fatal error) preserved exactly.
  * **`_try_explicit_pg_target(pgdata, base_dir, pg_host, pg_port, build_dsn) ->
    (handled, result)`** (Step 1) — the explicit env-target branch. Returns
    `(True, dict|None)` to make the caller `return`, or `(False, None)` to fall
    through to local start (the our-own-local-PG-is-down case). `_build_dsn` passed
    as a param (it closes over pg_dbname/user/password, which stay in the caller).
  The caller now reads: `if not _pgdata_major_compatible(pgdata): return None` and
  `_handled, _r = _try_explicit_pg_target(...); if _handled: return _r`.
- **What was deliberately LEFT INTACT (honest scope boundary):** Step 2 (read our
  port / pg_isready / verify-ours) → Step 2b (scan ports) → Step 3 (remote-owner
  heartbeat) → Step 4/5 (the pidfile-deletion + cross-host startup-lock + pg_ctl
  start + self-heal). This is the ordering-sensitive, corruption-prone core the
  bug-memory protects, and it is UNTESTED. Restructuring it blind would risk
  reintroducing the exact cross-machine pidfile bug — so it stays as one block,
  exactly as the discipline ("don't force it") demands.
- **Test net (added FIRST-class, since the lifted Step 3b was previously UNTESTED):**
  new `tests/test_pg_ensure_running_helpers.py` (9 tests): `_pgdata_major_compatible`
  — no-file→True, match→True, MISMATCH→False, no-binary(FileNotFound)→False,
  probe-timeout(non-fatal)→True; `_try_explicit_pg_target` — no-target→fallthrough,
  reachable→(True,dict), remote-unreachable→(True,None), local-ours-down→
  (False,None) fallthrough. The existing `test_pg_explicit_local_autostart.py` (2,
  end-to-end through `_ensure_pg_running`) is the integration net for Step 1.
- **Result / status:** 11/11 (9 new + 2 existing) GREEN; broader DB sweep
  (core_schema_parity 47, sql_translate 32, db_thread_conn_lifecycle 4 + the 11) =
  94 GREEN. NOTE: a transient "1 failed" appeared once in a combined run then
  vanished on re-run — a known DB test-ordering/shared-state flake, NOT my change
  (each suite passes individually; my helpers are pure and untouched by DB state).
  `_ensure_pg_running` shrank from ~486 → ~370 lines. psycopg2-dependent tests
  `importorskip` cleanly on the SQLite-only CI. Pure-backend, no JS/bundler.


### 2026-06-24 — DECLINED the FlowExecutor ControlExecutor cut (irreducible interpreter core); GraphNavigator was the only clean seam
- **Context:** After extracting `GraphNavigator` (pure topology, last entry) and
  the verdict logic (→ `agent_verdict.py`, earlier), the audit's remaining
  proposal was a `ControlExecutor` for the loop/parallel/branch/subflow
  execution. Investigated whether it's a clean extraction. **It is NOT — and
  forcing it would make the code worse.** No code changed this turn.
- **Why it's not separable (evidence from reading every control method):**
  1. **Bidirectional recursion.** `_walk ⇄ _run_loop / _run_parallel /
     _run_branch` — `_run_loop` calls `self._walk(body_entry, stop_at=lid)`,
     `_run_parallel` calls `self._walk(entry, stop_at=barrier)`, and `_walk`
     dispatches back into all three. A separate class needs a back-reference
     (`control._owner._walk`), relocating the cycle across an object boundary
     for zero decoupling.
  2. **One shared mutable state machine.** Every control method reads AND writes
     the same ~13 runtime fields (`_lock`, `_io_outputs`, `_node_memory`,
     `_pending_feedback`, `_pending_directive`, `_last_producer_snapshot`,
     `_feedback_history`, `_cur_iteration`, `_agents_run`, `_transcript`,
     `_trace`, `_artifacts`, `_initial_context`) — and so do methods that
     legitimately stay (`run`, `_run_role`, `_publish_outputs`, `_compose_*`,
     `_trace_node`). Splitting a single state machine across two objects sharing
     mutable fields = a leaky `self._owner._field` abstraction, strictly worse
     than methods on one object.
  3. **The control layer builds the executor.** `_run_subflow_isolated`
     constructs a nested `FlowExecutor(self._runner, …)` — the control loop IS
     the interpreter core; there's no smaller cohesive unit inside it.
- **Contrast with what WAS extractable:** `GraphNavigator` = pure functions over
  the immutable `nodes/fwd/rev` (a real seam); `agent_verdict` = pure decision
  logic. Those were the two genuine concerns; with them out, the remainder is
  the irreducible interpreter. So `FlowExecutor` is correctly split, NOT
  half-split — the audit's "GraphNavigator + ControlExecutor" hypothesis only
  half-survives contact with the actual coupling.
- **Guardrail for future sessions:** do NOT re-attempt a `ControlExecutor`
  class. If the executor needs further slimming, the only near-zero-risk move
  left is relocating the two already-`@staticmethod` pure helpers
  (`_build_change_manifest`, `_subflow_deliverable`) to module scope — but
  that's cosmetic, near-zero payoff, and was deliberately left undone. The class
  is ~1190 lines of cohesive interpreter post-topology-lift, which is
  appropriate for what it does.


### 2026-06-24 — Split FlowExecutor's graph-topology layer into a GraphNavigator (orchestration_engine.py)
- **Why (refactor audit P1, "FlowExecutor god-object"):** `FlowExecutor`
  (~1370 lines, 40 methods) mixed four concerns: graph topology, control
  execution (loop/parallel/branch/subflow), verdict logic, and tracing/emit.
  The verdict logic was already extracted to `lib/agent_verdict.py` earlier
  this session. The cleanest, lowest-risk next cut is the **pure graph-topology
  layer** — those methods read ONLY the immutable structure (`self.nodes` /
  `self.fwd` / `self.rev`), never runtime state (`_transcript`/`_lock`/`_io_*`),
  so they lift out with zero behavior risk.
- **What:** New `GraphNavigator(nodes, fwd, rev)` class holding the 9 pure
  topology queries, moved verbatim (dropped the `_` prefix → public on the
  navigator): `node_label`, `single_next`, `find_start`, `loop_parts`,
  `find_loop_planner`, `find_common_barrier`, `reachable`, `can_reach`,
  `distance`. `FlowExecutor.__init__` now builds `self._nav = GraphNavigator(
  self.nodes, self.fwd, self.rev)` right after adjacency is constructed; all 20
  internal call sites changed `self._xxx(...)` → `self._nav.xxx(...)`. The
  control-execution / verdict / tracing methods all STAY on the executor — only
  the topology moved, so `_run_loop`/`_run_parallel`/`_run_branch`/`_walk` are
  unchanged except for the delegated structural queries.
- **Behavior preserved exactly:** the moved method bodies are byte-identical
  (only `self.` intra-topology calls became `self.` on the navigator, e.g.
  `loop_parts`→`can_reach`). No test referenced the topology methods directly
  (all exercised through `run()`), so no test changes — and nothing external
  imports them.
- **Result / status:** full orchestration + endpoint sweep 195/195 GREEN,
  IDENTICAL to the pre-refactor baseline (engine 45, emits_subflow, io, nested,
  phase, role_params, orchestrations 40, endpoint_adapter 4, endpoint_runner 5,
  flow_parity 3). Live parity test (`test_endpoint_flow_parity_live.py`) still
  collects + stays skip-gated (NOT run — real paid LLM on this cred'd host, per
  the orchestration-studio memory). `test_swarm_async`/`test_swarm_tool_scoping`
  61/62 — the 1 failure (`TestAwaitAgents::test_await_no_ids_includes_early_finishers`,
  a swarm await-timing test) is PRE-EXISTING: proven independent by reverting
  ONLY `orchestration_engine.py` via `git stash` and re-running (still fails),
  then restoring. Pure-backend, no JS/bundler. Follow-up (left for later): the
  control-execution methods (`_run_loop`/`_run_parallel`/`_run_branch`/
  `_run_subflow_isolated`) could move into a `ControlExecutor`, but they're
  tightly coupled to the executor's runtime state (`_pending_feedback`,

### 2026-06-24 — cache_tracking.py: decomposed the detect_cache_break god-function; REJECTED the _cache_states→TTLCache migration (documented carve-out)
- **Two-part audit item, split verdict.**
- **REJECTED — `_cache_states` dict+Lock → `lib.ttl_cache.TTLCache`.** The audit
  flagged this as a "textbook ttl_cache candidate" (dict + `_cache_lock` +
  `cleanup_stale_cache_states(max_age_s=3600)`). On inspection it is exactly the
  `usage_cache`-style carve-out the `ttl_cache.py` docstring EXPLICITLY excludes,
  for FOUR independent disqualifying reasons: (1) **No iteration API** — `TTLCache`
  stores `(ts, payload)` tuples with no public `.items()`, but `_count_active_on_model`,
  `cleanup_stale_cache_states`, and `get_cache_diagnostics` all scan every live entry.
  (2) **Wrong TTL axis** — eviction here keys on the domain field
  `CacheState.last_update_time` (refreshed every `detect_cache_break` call), not
  cache insertion/access time; the test `_cache_states['ttl-3'].last_update_time =
  now-10` then expects a refresh — domain logic on a MUTABLE state object.
  (3) **Multi-step read-modify-write under one lock** — `detect_cache_break` does
  `with _cache_lock: prev = get(); …mutate prev in place…` which `TTLCache`'s
  per-call locking can't express atomically. (4) **Test contract** —
  `test_cache_improvements.py` treats `_cache_states` as a plain dict (`['nr-2'].total_breaks`,
  `.clear()`, `in`). Migrating would be a net negative (more code, lost iteration,
  changed eviction semantics) — the current bounded-via-`cleanup_stale_cache_states`
  approach is already correct/idiomatic for this rich-state registry. Left as-is.
- **DONE — `detect_cache_break` god-function (~360L) decomposition.** Extracted the
  two densest PURE chunks to module-level helpers, verbatim logic, no behavior
  change: **`_classify_break(...)`** — the Phase-2 break classification returning
  `(api_break, no_reuse, partial_no_reuse)` (the much-commented token thresholds in
  one testable place); **`_resolve_break_cause(...)`** — the cause-string
  disambiguation ladder (client_changes → prefix-mutation → TTL → narrowed
  stochastic-server-miss). The caller still OWNS the `with _cache_lock:` orchestration,
  the in-place `CacheState` mutation, the break-tally, and all logging/return
  shaping — only the pure computation moved out. `detect_cache_break` shrank ~110
  lines (the file netted +~30 with the two documented helpers).
- **Discipline / test net:** existing `test_cache_improvements.py` (43 tests) is a
  strong net — it directly exercises every break predicate (api_break, no_reuse,
  partial_no_reuse, prefix_mutation), the TTL-refresh, and reaches into
  `_cache_states` — so no NEW tests needed; baseline captured GREEN before the edit.
- **Result / status:** 43/43 `test_cache_improvements` green post-refactor; broader
  sweep `test_cache_breakpoints` (42) + `test_cache_schema_stability` (20) +
  `test_write_breakdown` (17) all green (122 cache-related tests total). Pure-backend,
  no JS/bundler.


### 2026-06-24 — Shared _StreamRetryState for dispatch_stream + async_dispatch_stream (added sync behavioral test net FIRST, then extracted)
- **Why (refactor audit P2):** `dispatch_stream` (sync, ~440L) and
  `async_dispatch_stream` (async, ~230L) ran the SAME three-tier
  exclusion/retry state machine (`exclude` models / `exclude_keys` /
  `exclude_pairs`, the 60s periodic reset, the avoid-set relaxation, and the
  per-error set mutations) hand-duplicated around their different transport
  calls. The two had diverged (async was a reduced variant), so the shared
  bookkeeping was a real drift surface — e.g. the async PermissionError handler
  did a flat pair-exclude while sync escalated pair→key when all of a key's
  models were excluded.
- **Two-step discipline (the key decision):** investigation showed the SYNC
  path had ZERO behavioral test coverage (only a signature test) while the
  async path had a full suite (`test_async_dispatch_stream.py`). Extracting
  shared mutation logic out of an untested hot path and calling it
  "behavior-preserving" would be an unverified claim. So:
  **STEP 1 — new `tests/test_dispatch_stream.py`** (7 tests mirroring the async
  suite, against a `_FakeDispatcher` + monkeypatched `lib.llm.stream_chat`,
  `time.sleep` no-op'd): success+`_dispatch` metadata; free non-quota 429 retry
  (proven free via `max_retries=1` + a 429 still succeeding); quota-429 excludes
  the KEY + counts hard; PermissionError excludes the (key,model) PAIR then fails
  over to another key serving the same model (the pair-exclusion invariant from
  the `dispatch-permission-error-pair-exclusion` memory); EndpointUnreachable
  cools the slot + fails over; Abort propagates + releases. All 7 GREEN against
  the pre-refactor code — pins the behavior.
  **STEP 2 — extracted `_StreamRetryState`** (in `lib/llm_dispatch/api.py`,
  before `dispatch_stream`): owns the state + pure transitions
  (`maybe_reset_exclusions`, `eff_exclude_models/keys/pairs`,
  `relax_avoid_if_exhausted`, `note_free_429`/`note_cooldown_cycle`/
  `note_quota_key`/`note_auto_exhausted_key`/`note_permission_pair`/
  `note_unreachable_pair`/`note_generic_error`). Loop control (`continue`/
  `break`/`time.sleep` vs `await async_abortable_sleep`) and the transport call
  STAY in each function — only the bookkeeping is shared, so the two can never
  drift on WHICH set a given error mutates. Both functions rewired to drive the
  state object.
- **Behavior change (intentional, consistency):** the async PermissionError
  handler now uses `note_permission_pair` → it gains the sync side's
  pair→key escalation (exclude the whole key once ALL its models are excluded).
  Strictly an improvement; the escalation only fires when every model for a key
  is excluded, so the common single-pair case is unchanged.
- **Result / status:** 14/14 (sync 7 + async 7) GREEN after extraction; broader
  sweep `test_ephemeral_slot` (11) + `test_streaming_and_prefetch` (33, incl. the
  `dispatch_stream` signature test) + `test_endpoint_flow_parity` (3) all green.
  Two impl gotchas hit + fixed: (a) `insert_content` with position=before
  duplicated the `def dispatch_stream(` anchor line → SyntaxError, removed the
  dup; (b) on first async edit I converted only init+slot-pick and left the async
  exception handlers using the now-deleted bare locals → would NameError, caught
  it by reading the whole function and converting every handler. `dispatch_chat`
  (the non-streaming sibling) was deliberately NOT touched — it has its own
  budget/stream-only logic and was out of scope. Pure-backend, no JS/bundler.


### 2026-06-24 — execute_tool if/elif ladder → per-tool handlers + dispatch registry (project_mod/tools.py)
- **Why (refactor audit P1):** `execute_tool` in `lib/project_mod/tools.py` was a
  ~369-line `if fn_name == … elif …` ladder dispatching 12 project tools, each
  branch a substantial tool-specific handler (read_files arg-recovery, run_command
  snapshot/diff, write-tool result formatting, …). A registry makes the dispatch
  table explicit and each handler independently navigable.

  list_dir, read_files, inspect_image, grep_search, find_files, create_project,
  write_file, apply_diff, apply_diffs, insert_content, insert_contents,
  run_command). A `_EXEC_HANDLERS` dict maps name→handler; `execute_tool` is now a
  thin dispatcher (`handler = _EXEC_HANDLERS.get(fn_name); … return handler(...)`,
  same `Unknown project tool: {fn_name}` fallback). The old per-call `_rb` closure
  (capturing conv_id) is recreated per-handler only where a handler resolves paths;

  ladder) was dropped. `_resolve_base_safe` itself is left in place (a `_`-private

  + stringified-array recovery, run_command destructive/RO-guard/snapshot/diff —
  is byte-identical.
- **`project_tool_display` left as-is:** it's a parallel display-formatting ladder
  with no dispatch logic or coupling; converting it adds churn for marginal benefit.
  The high-value target was the execution dispatcher.
- **Result / status:** 146 tests green (test_project_tools 69, malformed_tool_args 5,
  readonly_roots 12, new_features, tool_changes). End-to-end registry dispatch
  spot-checked: read_files (incl. flat-arg shim), grep_search, list_dir, write_file,
  and the unknown-tool fallback all behave identically to the ladder. tools.py
  866 → 931 lines (handlers add def headers + the registry; the win is an explicit

- **Why (refactor audit P0):** A 4-investigator parallel audit flagged that the
  agent-loop *decision logic* was hand-copied across THREE+ modules with explicit
  "Kept as a local copy … update BOTH sets" comments — the most dangerous kind of
  redundancy because the copies had begun to DIVERGE. Concretely:
  `_classify_verdict`/`_parse_verdict` (verdict gating), `_detect_stuck` (Jaccard
  0.60), `STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS` (deliverable-tool set), and the `[VU: TASK_DONE]`
  sentinel lived independently in `lib/tasks_pkg/endpoint_review.py`,
  `lib/orchestration_engine.py`, and `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py` (sentinel). The
  engine's copy had already drifted from endpoint's: it added a loose
  plain-language STOP/CONTINUE fallback + `virtual_user` inversion + a narrower
  unresolved-marker regex (missing `still NOT met`) + `code_exec` folded into the
  set (vs endpoint special-casing it in the counter).
- **What:** New pure-logic `lib/agent_verdict.py` (imports only `lib.log` +
  `lib.env_compat`) owns: `STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS` (8 tools, no code_exec — endpoint
  counter special-cases it) + `STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS_WITH_CODE_EXEC` (the flat-name
  variant the engine's snapshot counter needs); `VU_DONE_SENTINEL`;
  `replan_enabled()`; `count_state_changing_rounds()`; `detect_stuck(history, *,
  threshold)`; `accumulate_usage()`; and the unified `classify_verdict(text, *,
  verifier_role, loose_fallback, strip_feedback) -> {phase, plan_defect, feedback,
  had_tag}`. The two divergent policies are now PARAMETERS of one core, not two
  copies: endpoint calls it `loose_fallback=False, strip_feedback=True` (strict —
  missing tag → worker, returns cleaned feedback); engine calls it
  `loose_fallback=True` + `verifier_role` (tag-free → plain-language heuristics;
  empty → stop; VU inversion). The unresolved-marker detector uses endpoint's
  RICHER regex (superset incl. `still NOT met`) as the shared one — strictly safer
  (catches one more STOP→worker case), and the engine tests don't assert the gap.
- **Rewire (all behavior-preserving, public surfaces unchanged):**
  * `endpoint_review.py`: imports the helpers under their historical underscore
    names (`_accumulate_usage`/`_count_state_changing_rounds`/`_detect_stuck`/
    `_replan_enabled`/`STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS`); `_parse_verdict` is now a 2-line
    wrapper over `classify_verdict(...)` returning the identical
    `(feedback, phase, defect)` 3-tuple. Dropped now-dead `import re`/`audit_log`/
    local regexes (~225 lines removed; 671 → 427 lines). endpoint.py still
    re-imports the same names from here, so external callers see no change.
  * `orchestration_engine.py`: `_classify_verdict` (kept the `(phase, defect)`
    return + `verifier_role` kwarg) and `_detect_stuck` (kept the instance-method
    reading `self._feedback_history`) are now thin delegations to the core;
    removed local `_VU_DONE_SENTINEL`/`_STATE_CHANGING_TOOLS`/all verdict regexes/
    `_replan_enabled`/dead `import re`+`getenv_compat` (~95 lines removed). Kept
    `_STUCK_JACCARD=0.60` (passed as `threshold`).
  * `autopilot.py`: `_VU_DONE_SENTINEL` now imported from agent_verdict (it's used
    at module-import time to build `_VU_ROLE_PROMPT`, so the import name is kept
    identical). The literal `'[VU: TASK_DONE]'` definition no longer exists
    anywhere — verified by grep.
- **Result / status:** 260 tests green — engine(45)+endpoint_messages(28)+
  flow_parity(3)+adapter(4)+runner(5)+autopilot(28)+orchestrations(40)+
  emits_subflow+io+nested+phase+role_params+poll_recovery. Spot-checked every
  engine verdict branch (VU empty→worker, VU done→stop, loose stop, loose

### 2026-06-24 — Unified the two cost engines: billing now delegates to lib.cost.compute_cost (cache tokens billed; debit == displayed ¥, can't drift)
- **Root cause (from the prior audit):** TWO independent cost systems with TWO
  price tables that drifted. (a) `lib/cost.py::compute_cost` = the rich DISPLAY
  engine over `lib/pricing.py` (100+ models, Anthropic-vs-OpenAI cache-token
  convention detection, per-model cache multipliers, Qwen CNY tiers,
  provider-scoped overrides, live USD→CNY). (b) `lib/billing/cost.py::compute_request_cost`
  = the WALLET-DEBIT engine over a SEPARATE sparse `data/config/pricing.json`
  (7 models → everything else fell to a generic `default_model`), AND its caller
  `settle_task` (`request_flow.py`) forwarded ONLY input/output tokens — so
  `cache_read`/`cache_write` were DROPPED entirely. Net: a cache-heavy turn was
  silently UNDER-debited and the amount charged disagreed with the ¥ shown.
- **Fix (single engine, by delegation — the user asked for root-cause, not a
  patch):** `lib.cost.compute_cost` is now THE one arithmetic core.
  * `lib/cost.py`: exposed per-component USD sub-costs (`inputCostUsd`,
    `outputCostUsd`, `cacheWriteCostUsd`, `cacheReadCostUsd`) at 9-dp precision
    in BOTH the generic and Qwen branches (additive — existing CNY/USD keys
    unchanged, so display output is byte-identical and `test_cost.py` 12/12
    still pass).
  * `lib/billing/cost.py::compute_request_cost`: rewritten as a THIN ADAPTER —
    builds a usage dict, calls `compute_cost(model, provider_id)`, converts each
    USD sub-cost → micro-credits via `MICRO_PER_USD=1_000_000`, sums, then
    applies the relay `default_margin`. New kwargs `cache_read_tokens`,
    `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `provider_id`. Signature is
    keyword-only (`*`) — no positional callers exist (verified). Dropped the
    `get_price`/`ModelPrice` import (rate rows no longer consulted for cost).
  * `lib/billing/request_flow.py::settle_task`: now forwards cache_read /
    cache_write / reasoning tokens + provider_id to `compute_request_cost`.
  * **CRITICAL rounding trap avoided:** billing sums the 9-dp per-component USD
    fields, NEVER the top-level `costUsd` (rounded to 4dp). `$0.00045` 4-dp →
    `0.0004` → 400µ would have broken `test_simple_compute` (expects 450µ); the
    per-component path gives exactly 450µ.
- **What `pricing.json` / `lib/billing/pricing.py` still own:** ONLY
  `default_margin` (the relay markup) for billing. The per-model
  `*_per_mtok_micro` rows + `get_price`/`ModelPrice` are now used only by the
  admin pricing-editor UI (`list_prices`/`save_prices`) and `PricingTest` — NOT
  for any cost/debit. Left in place (deleting would break the editor + tests, a
  separate product call); module docstring corrected to say so. Stale
  "pure-function port of calcCostCny" docstring in `lib/cost.py` rewritten to
  "THE single cost engine" (the JS dual-impl it described was deleted 2026-06).
- **Experimental evidence:**
  * Cache-heavy Claude turn (500 in / 1500 out / 8k cw / 40k cr, margin 0):
    components `{input:2500, output:37500, cache_read:20000, cache_write:50000}`
    = 110000µ. **70000µ (64%) was previously dropped** (only 40000µ charged).
  * Display==debit parity to the micro across 3 cases: claude-opus-4-7
    110000µ==110000µ, gpt-4o 37500µ==37500µ, gpt-4o-mini 450µ==450µ (MATCH=True
    all).
  * Estimate path intact (gpt-4o 5k prompt → 40932µ); unknown model still falls
    back (15/75 USD default → 15M µ for 1M in); default margin still applies
    (450→540µ at 0.20).
- **Tests:** new `SingleEngineUnificationTest` (5 cases: cache billed, debit==
  display across conventions, rich-table model not defaulted, margin over unified
  base, Qwen CNY-native). `test_billing` 19, `test_cost` 12, `test_write_breakdown`
  17, `test_cache_improvements` 43 → 91/91. Imports of all touched modules clean.
- **Status / not done:** pure-backend change (no JS/bundler). The `pricing.json`
  rate rows are now vestigial-for-cost; a future cleanup could drop the admin
  rate-editor entirely and keep only the margin knob, but that's a UI/product
  decision left for the user.


### 2026-06-24 — Full cache/cost-fidelity audit (4 parallel investigators, all evidence-backed): chain is faithful; fixed 2 frontend honesty holes; surfaced 1 real display↔billing divergence
- **Trigger:** User demanded a top-to-bottom audit of the cache/cost system
  (provider → backend → frontend) with experimental proof, on the principle
  "the ONLY source of truth is the backend; the frontend must not fudge".
- **Method:** 4 parallel sub-agents, each required to produce runnable evidence:
  (1) usage ingestion, (2) backend cost + FE authority, (3) per-round accounting
  + persistence + dual-transport, (4) independent FE fidelity review. Key
  claims re-verified by hand in code.
- **Findings (evidenced):**
  * **Usage ingestion FAITHFUL** — `SSEAccumulator.usage` is last-writer-wins
    assignment (`_sse_core.py:413/432/484`), never `+=`; `finalize` only injects
    metadata (trace_id/elapsed), never token counts; empty stays empty (never
    fabricated). Cache-field aliasing (`cache_read_tokens` sankuai /
    `cache_read_input_tokens` anthropic / OpenAI `cached_tokens`) uses a uniform
    `a or b or 0` idiom everywhere — selects ONE alias, never sums two (no
    double-count). Anthropic uncached-only `input_tokens` reconstituted to a
    total in `anthropic_outbound._convert_usage:283-294`. `test_anthropic_outbound`
    12/12.
  * **Cost is server-authoritative** — `lib/cost.py::compute_cost` is the single
    source; stamped onto the SSE done event (`orchestrator.py:946-969`) AND the
    persisted msg + every apiRound (`manager.py:950-977`). The JS `calcCostCny`
    (`core/cost.js:144`) does ZERO pricing math — it's a pure fetch wrapper to
    `/api/v1/messages/cost` (same `compute_cost`); old client pricing tables were
    deleted 2026-06 (grep for `/1e6`/`base_in` in static/js → 0 hits). So the FE
    cannot invent a price.
  * **Accounting consistent** — `accumulated_usage` summed in the SAME `if usage:`
    block that appends each round → totals == Σ per-round by construction.
    toolTokens are real `_safe_count_tokens` of the result, once, on the right
    `llmRound`. Write-breakdown SUM INVARIANT proven exact on the user's real
    3-round trace via harness: R3 (read 134.9k→130.0k, drop 4900) → recacheBody
    4450 / contextWrite 0 (pre-fix mislabeled benign). `test_write_breakdown` +
    `test_cache_improvements` 60/60.
- **Fixes applied (frontend honesty, `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`):**
  * **P2 — no fabricated ¥0 on a cost-fetch miss:** `rdCnyStr` used to print
    `"¥0"` whenever `calcCostCny` returned null — but null means BOTH "no charge"
    AND "fetch pending/failed". Now: if the round consumed billable tokens
    (ri+ro+rt+rcw+rcr > 0) but we have no server cost yet → show `…` (待计算);
    only a genuinely zero-token round shows ¥0. Never a confident ¥0 for a round
    that cost money.
  * **P3 — softened unconditional cache-reuse claims:** the contextWrite tooltip
    ("下一轮即可低价复用，并非浪费") and the legend write line ("下一轮可复用") asserted
    a favorable future outcome the recache-by-read-delta fix proved can fail.
    Reworded to an EXPECTATION ("本轮 cache 读取未下降，预期下一轮可低价复用，若未命中
    会在该轮标注为重新缓存正文" / "未命中则计为重新缓存正文").
- **Surfaced but NOT silently changed (needs a product decision — flagged to
  user):** `lib/billing/` (the wallet-debit path, micro-credits) is ENTIRELY
  SEPARATE from `lib/cost.py` (the displayed ¥) and they disagree:
  (a) `settle_task` (`request_flow.py:138`) calls `compute_request_cost` with
  ONLY input_tokens/output_tokens — `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` are
  DROPPED, so a cache-heavy turn is under-debited vs the ¥ shown; (b)
  `pricing.json` rows missing cache rates → cache billed at 0; (c) missing model
  rows fall to a generic `default_model`. Only active when `billing_enabled()` +
  a per-user wallet (multi-user relay installs); personal/open installs make zero
  ledger calls so display ¥ is the only number and is correct. Left for the user

- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean; `test_write_breakdown + test_cache_improvements

### 2026-06-24 — Cost popover "首次缓存上下文" mislabeled re-billed body as benign: write-breakdown now grounds contextWrite-vs-recacheBody on the cache_read DELTA, not the banner-level break flag
- **Symptom (user-reported, 3-round trace):** Round 3 showed `write 5.8k` =
  上一轮回复 233 + 工具结果 68 + **首次缓存上下文 4.7k** + 消息开销 800, with the
  4.7k tooltip claiming "首次写入缓存…下一轮即可低价复用，并非浪费". But the
  conversation only grew ~300 real tokens that round (prevOutput 233 +
  toolResults 68), so there was no 4.7k of genuinely new context — and
  `cache_read` had FALLEN 134.9k (R2) → 130.0k (R3), a 4.9k drop almost exactly
  matching the 4.7k. It was re-billed body (真实浪费), not warm-up. User: "明显
  有问题吧？还说不是浪费……？"
- **Root cause:** `_compute_write_breakdown` (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`)
  split the residual excess into `contextWrite` (benign) vs `recacheBody`
  (waste) SOLELY by whether `detect_cache_break` had stamped a `cacheBreak`
  flag on the round. That detector's `api_break` gate requires
  `cache_read < prev*0.95` (a >5% RELATIVE drop) — correct for suppressing
  banner noise, but it stays silent on a small-percent yet real-cost drop
  (4.9k on 135k ≈ 3.6%). With no flag, the excess defaulted to `contextWrite`.
  So cost ATTRIBUTION had been outsourced to an ALARM threshold, mislabeling
  every sub-threshold re-bill as "first-time context, not waste".
- **Fix (principled — ground attribution on direct evidence):** the breakdown
  now computes `read_drop = max(0, prev_read - cur_read)` from the rounds' own
  `cache_read_tokens` and splits the excess by it, INDEPENDENTLY of the banner
  gate: confirmed `cacheBreak` → whole excess is `recacheBody`; else
  `read_drop >= _READ_DROP_WASTE_TOKENS` (2000, matches `_MIN_CACHE_MISS_TOKENS`)
  → `recacheBody = min(excess, read_drop)`, remainder → `contextWrite` (a large
  write that BOTH re-bills some body AND adds new context splits correctly);
  else (read held/grew) → all `contextWrite` (genuine warm-up). New `readDrop`
  field exposed; `recacheCause` gets a synthesized `no_cache_reuse` string when
  recacheBody is read-drop-driven (no formal break) so the term is never
  unexplained. Frontend tooltip (`static/js/ui/finish_info.js`) rewritten: the
  重新缓存正文 line now says "未被读回、被重新计费（真实浪费）；本轮 cache 读取较上一轮
  下降 N tok" and only appends "详见下方缓存失效" when an actual banner line exists.
- **Why not lower detect_cache_break's threshold instead:** the 5%-relative
  gate is deliberately noise-tolerant for the WARNING banner (avoids crying
  wolf on normal variation). Cost attribution needs a different, exact signal
  (the read delta) — conflating "should we alarm?" with "how do we label these
  tokens?" was the original mistake. Kept them separate.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_write_breakdown.py` 17/17 (4 new: the exact
  user scenario relabels to recacheBody; read-held keeps contextWrite; partial
  drop splits the excess; sub-threshold drop stays context). Regression-clean:
  `test_cache_improvements.py` 43/43 (detector untouched). `node --check` +
  `python -c import` clean. Pure logic + tooltip change; `finish_info.js` is in
  the bundle → restart + hard-refresh to serve it.



### 2026-06-24 — OAuth B1 confirmed CORS-dead; added B2 curl-assisted manual exchange (the only path that works under geo-block)
- **Evidence:** User authorized Claude, but still got the server's 403 geo-block
  message. A pasted curl proved the smoking gun: it carried
  `Referer: https://…vscode-zw05.mlp.sankuai.com/` (= the BROWSER generated it,
  so B1's `_browserExchange` DID run) yet the result was the SERVER's 403 — meaning
  B1's browser `fetch` failed and fell through to `_serverExchange` (geo-blocked).
- **Root cause:** `console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token` is built for the Claude
  Code CLI (no browser), so it sends NO `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. With
  `Content-Type: application/json` the browser fires a CORS preflight; Anthropic
  doesn't answer it → the POST is blocked before sending → `fetch` throws → fell
  back to the geo-blocked server. CORS cannot be bypassed from JS, so **B1 is dead
  here**. BUT the user's own terminal curl works (no CORS + their VPN reaches
  Anthropic). So the only reliable path is to let the user's terminal do the POST.
- **Fix (B2 curl-assisted):** `static/js/settings/oauth.js` — when BOTH browser
  (CORS) and server (geo-block) exchange fail, `_completeLogin` now calls
  `_showCurlHelper()` instead of dead-ending with an error. It renders the EXACT
  curl (`_buildCurlCommand`, pre-filled with the code + our PKCE code_verifier +
  client_id/redirect_uri, json for claude / form for codex) in a copy-able
  textarea, and repurposes the manual input to accept the **token JSON** the curl
  returns. `_oauthManualSubmit` now detects a `{`-leading paste, parses it, and if
  it has `access_token` routes straight to `_storeBrowserToken` →
  `POST /api/oauth/store-token` (no exchange — the terminal already did it). Verified
  `manager.store_token` accepts Anthropic's real response shape
  (`{access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, account:{email_address}}`). Minor:
  email comes back blank because Anthropic nests it under `account.email_address`
  (our `_extract_email_from_token` looks at top-level `email`/id_token) — cosmetic,
  token works.
- **Status:** `node --check` clean, bundle rebuilt (`bundle-5477d412.js`). Restart +
  hard-refresh. UX now: 登录 → authorize in browser → paste `code#state` → if both
  auto-paths fail, the card shows a curl to run in the local terminal → paste the
  returned JSON → stored + provider provisioned. Updated the
  `oauth-china-geo-block-proxy-flow` skill with the CORS-dead finding + B2.
