### 2026-06-24 — Exported copies OOM-killed at boot: mlockall is now GATED on FUSE-risk + cgroup headroom (not unconditional); yaml._yaml de-classified as required
- **Symptom:** An exported copy (`tofu-personal` on a different box) repeatedly
  died at startup with a bare `Killed` right after
  `[boot] mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) OK — pages pinned` and a
  `Native preload failed (required): yaml._yaml — No module named 'yaml'`
  WARNING, mid-`_NATIVE_PRELOADS` loop (never reached "Native extensions
  preloaded."). No traceback, no faulthandler dump.
- **Root cause (the killer):** `server.py` called
  `mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE)` UNCONDITIONALLY at the top of the file.
  Pinned pages are unreclaimable and charged against the cgroup memory limit.
  On the dev box (cgroup limit 200 GiB, `ulimit -l` unlimited) it's harmless,
  but on a memory-constrained exported container, pinning the entire
  C-extension working set (numpy/lxml/PIL/pymupdf/cryptography/playwright …)
  pushed RSS past `memory.max` → the kernel OOM-killer SIGKILLed the process.
  `Killed` is shell-speak for SIGKILL — uncatchable, so NO Python traceback and
  NO faulthandler dump (the ABSENCE of a /dev/shm dump is itself the OOM
  fingerprint vs a real SIGBUS). mlockall's mitigation (FUSE SIGBUS) is only
  USEFUL on a FUSE mount and only SAFE with memory headroom; applying it
  everywhere made it a net negative on small boxes.
- **Root cause (secondary, non-fatal):** `yaml._yaml` was listed as a REQUIRED
  native preload, but (a) PyYAML was NOT in `requirements.txt` at all — it only
  ever arrived as a transitive dep on the dev box, so a clean export env lacked
  it; (b) its sole use, `routes/api_docs.py::openapi_yaml`, already degrades to
  JSON on ImportError. So it was both mislabeled and undeclared.
- **Fix (long-term, principled — no band-aid):**
  **(1) Gated mlockall (`server.py` top-of-file):** new stdlib-only helpers
  `_tofu_path_is_fuse` (longest-mountpoint match in `/proc/self/mountinfo`,
  fstype startswith `fuse`), `_tofu_cgroup_mem_limit_bytes` (cgroup v2
  `memory.max` then v1 `memory.limit_in_bytes`; `max`/`<=0`/`>=2^62` →
  unlimited), and `_tofu_should_mlock()` returning `(do_it, reason)`.
  `TOFU_MLOCK=0/off/no` forces off, `=1/on/force` forces on; `auto` (default)
  pins ONLY when (project dir OR `sys.prefix` on FUSE) AND (cgroup unlimited OR
  limit >= `TOFU_MLOCK_MIN_LIMIT_GB`, default 8). Boot logs
  `[boot] mlockall skipped — <reason>` when it declines. Reused the project's
  existing FUSE-as-the-real-risk framing (fs_keepalive / cross_dc) rather than
  inventing a parallel detector.
  **(2) `yaml._yaml` required→optional** in `_NATIVE_PRELOADS` and **added
  `PyYAML>=6.0` to `requirements.txt`** (soft feature dep, documented) so the
  YAML OpenAPI route works in clean envs without ever being able to crash boot.
- **Why this over a kill-switch-only patch:** the user explicitly asked for the
  most robust fix that doesn't create a new problem elsewhere. A bare
  `TOFU_NO_MLOCK` env still requires every deployer to know to set it; the
  auto-gate makes the SAFE behavior the DEFAULT (skip when pinning would OOM,
  pin only where SIGBUS is a real risk and there's headroom) while keeping the
  manual override for edge cases. Declaring PyYAML + reclassifying it fixes the
  packaging hole at the source instead of suppressing the warning.
- **Result / status:** `py_compile` clean. Verified the decision logic
  standalone across all branches: dev box (FUSE + 200 GiB) → ON (no
  regression); simulated small-limit container → SKIP with reason;
  `TOFU_MLOCK=0/1/off/force/no` overrides all correct. FUSE detection and
  cgroup-limit read both confirmed against the live box. No tests asserted on
  these boot internals (grep clean), so none broke. Could NOT run a live
  end-to-end boot on the actual small exported container (not available in this
  env) — the gate is verified functionally, not in-situ on the failing host.
  Follow-up for the user on the export box: `rm .tofu_env.json` if a stale
  cross-host marker is present (doubled boot banner = re-exec), and re-run from
  the activated env so `requirements.txt` (now incl. PyYAML) installs.


### 2026-06-24 — file-changes-bar single source of truth: derive across ALL roots + demote fh diff to opaque-writer-gated enrichment
- **Symptom (user-reported, two screenshots):** A conversation whose
  tool rounds clearly wrote `chatui:static/icons/mcp/longcat.svg` and
  patched `chatui:lib/mcp/registry.py` showed only `JOURNAL.md` in the
  final `file-changes-bar` — the real edits were INVISIBLE and a foreign
  file from a CONCURRENT journalling session appeared instead. `chatui`
  was an EXTRA root in that session, not the primary.
- **Root cause (two stacked faults):** (1) **multi-root blindness** —
  `_finalize_and_emit_done` (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`) built the
  authoritative `modifiedFileList` from `get_modifications(project_path,
  …)` = the PRIMARY root ONLY. The modifications journal is keyed
  per-root (`session_dir = md5(base_path)`), so writes to an extra root
  land in THAT root's journal and were never read here → the list came
  back empty. (2) With the list empty, the file-history daemon
  (`_run_commit_round_async`) ran `diff_name_status` against the PRIMARY
  root's project-GLOBAL snapshot index and APPENDED its result — which,
  with the list empty, effectively SEEDED it with the only thing changed
  on the primary root at that instant: another conversation's
  `JOURNAL.md`. The Fix-4 attribution gate failed open (kept empty-writer
  paths on any write-capable round), so the concurrent unstamped write
  slipped through. Exactly the leak the
  `file-history-cross-conversation-attribution` memory warned about.
- **Fix (the source-of-truth hierarchy the user endorsed):**
  * **Authoritative = the round's OWN journalled writes, unioned across
    EVERY root.** Rewrote the `_finalize_and_emit_done` block to scan
    `[project_path] + cfg['projectPaths'][1:]`, call `get_modifications`
    per-root, filter each to `taskId == task['id']` (ts-fallback per
    root), and union. run_command delete/modify classification now
    resolves `os.path.exists` against the mod's OWN `basePath`, not the
    primary, so extra-root deletes classify correctly. This is
    conversation-isolated by construction (every mod is taskId-stamped at
    write time) and alone restores `longcat.svg` + `registry.py`.
  * **fh diff demoted to ENRICHMENT ONLY** — it can never seed or replace
    the journal-derived list. Replaced the Fix-4 read-only WHITELIST
    probe with an **OPAQUE-WRITER** probe in `_run_commit_round_async`: a
    round OWNS an unattributed (`last_writer_task_id == ''`) fh path only
    if it ran a tool that is NEITHER read-only NOR a tracked-edit tool.
    `_TRACKED_EDIT_TOOLS = {write_file, apply_diff, apply_diffs,
    insert_content, insert_contents, run_command}` all journal+stamp
    their edits; only `code_exec` / MCP / unknown are opaque (verified:
    `handlers/code_exec.py` + `handlers/mcp.py` make NO track_edit /
    _record_modification call). Filter: writer set & != own → drop (Fix
    2); writer empty & no opaque writer this round → drop (Fix 5); else
    keep. Probe fails OPEN so a genuine code_exec/MCP side-channel edit
    is never suppressed. This preserves the legitimate side-channel while
    closing the concurrent-conversation leak even on write-capable rounds.
- **Why this hierarchy:** `task['toolRounds']` + the taskId-stamped
  journal are the only inherently conversation-isolated signals; the fh
  `diff_name_status` is project-GLOBAL (walks the shared primary-root
  `tracked.json`) and is the sole leak vector, so it must be subordinate
  and strictly gated, never a seed.
- **Test sync (memory mandates it):** updated
  `debug/test_concurrent_fh_attribution.py`'s
  `_commit_round_simulating_orchestrator` mirror to the opaque-writer
  gate; Task-F now models the legitimate side-channel with `code_exec`
  (not `run_command`, which is no longer opaque); added **Task-G** — a
  tracked-edit-only round (`write_file`+`apply_diff`) must NOT
  misattribute a concurrent unstamped drift file — the exact regression.
- **Result / status:** `debug/test_concurrent_fh_attribution.py` 7/7
  PASS (incl. new Task-G), `debug/test_file_history.py` 34/34 PASS;
  orchestrator syntax + import clean. Pure-backend change (no JS/bundler
  involvement). Memory `file-history-cross-conversation-attribution`
  updated with Fix 5 + corrected invariants (run_command is NOT opaque;
  authoritative list unions all roots; fh is enrichment-only).
- **Follow-up verification (same day):** User asked to "re-run that
  conversation post-restart." That's a live browser+LLM+server flow I
  can't drive, and faking it would be dishonest — so instead I REFACTORED
  the inline derivation out of the giant `_finalize_and_emit_done` into a
  pure, callable `derive_round_modified_files(task, project_path,
  project_paths)` helper (orchestrator behaviour unchanged — the finalizer
  now just calls it) and wrote `debug/test_multiroot_modified_files.py`,
  an INTEGRATION test that drives the REAL helper + REAL
  `_record_modification` journal to reproduce the exact screenshot
  scenario: task X writes `static/icons/mcp/longcat.svg` (created) +
  patches `lib/mcp/registry.py` into an EXTRA `chatui` root while a
  concurrent conv Y patches `JOURNAL.md` (unstamped) into the PRIMARY
  root. Asserts: both extra-root edits present + root-tagged `chatui`,
  correct actions, JOURNAL.md NOT misattributed, and a NEGATIVE CONTROL
  (primary-only scan returns nothing → reproduces the original empty-list
  bug that let the fh side-channel seed the foreign file). 5/5 PASS.
  Regression-clean: `test_concurrent_fh_attribution.py` 7/7,
  `test_file_history.py` 34/34, orchestrator import OK after the refactor.
  This is the closest automated proxy to "re-run the conversation"
  short of a live UI session.


### 2026-06-24 — Settings provider model list: alphabetical cold-sort on load + binary-search insertion sort for in-session adds
- **Request:** Sort the models in the `stg-models-section` (Settings →
  Providers → nested model list) alphabetically, but NOT re-sort on every
  render. Do a one-time "cold sort" up front; for models added later use
  insertion sort, then cold-sort again on a later load.
- **Design (sort the working copy, not the render):** Sorting inside
  `_renderProvidersTab()` would re-order rows on every keystroke/toggle (rows
  jump while editing). Instead, the sort lives on the in-memory editor copy
  `_stgProviders[*].models`:
  * **Cold sort** runs ONCE per editor session, right after the deep-copy in
    `openSettings`'s `_loadServerConfig().then(...)` (`settings/core_panel.js`),
    via new `_coldSortAllProviderModels()` → `_coldSortModels()` (in-place
    `Array.sort` on a case-insensitive `model_id` key, `_modelSortKey`). The
    sorted order persists on Save and the next settings-open cold-sorts again
    from scratch — satisfying "another cold sort later".
  * **Insertion sort** (`_insertModelSorted`, binary-search splice) keeps the
    list ordered for in-session additions without a full re-sort:
    `settings/template_actions.js` `_syncFromTemplate` (template-added models)
    + `_discoverModels` (cloud auto-discover); `settings/model_edit.js`
    `_saveModelEdit` re-positions a model after its id is first set (new
    model) or renamed.
  * Two paths rebuild the whole list, so they cold-sort the result instead:
    `local_endpoints.js` `_discoverLocalModels` (`merged` union) and
    `template_actions.js` `addProviderFromTemplate` (fresh provider's models).
- **Notes:** All helpers defined in `core_panel.js`; callers in
  `local_endpoints.js` (which the bundler loads BEFORE `core_panel.js`) guard
  every call with `typeof ... === 'function'` — safe because the calls are in
  function bodies (runtime), not at IIFE-load time. `_addModel`'s blank push
  is intentionally left unsorted (empty `model_id`); it gets positioned in
  `_saveModelEdit`. `visibility_defaults.js`'s `.models.push` are display-only
  grouping, not the provider list — left alone.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on all four edited files; bundle
  rebuilt (`bundle-320e3427.js`) — restart + hard-refresh to serve it. All
  edited files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. No test asserts model-list order.



### 2026-06-24 — OAuth token-exchange: surface the REAL upstream reason + browser-side exchange (B1) to bypass the server's geo-block
- **Symptom:** After authorizing Claude in the browser and pasting the
  `code#state`, login failed with `提交失败: {"error":"Token exchange failed.
  The code may have expired."}`. The message was a LIE — `logs/app.log` showed
  the server's POST to `console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token` got **HTTP 403
  `{"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}`** with
  `cf-ray: …-HKG`. Probed with 3 different User-Agents (Tofu/claude-cli/browser)
  — all identical 403, so it's NOT a UA problem: Anthropic edge-blocks the
  SERVER's egress IP (corporate proxy `10.229.18.27` → Cloudflare HKG). The
  authorization step worked because it runs in the USER's VPN'd browser; the
  token exchange failed because it runs on the geo-blocked server. Exactly the
  split the `oauth-china-geo-block-proxy-flow` skill documents — and
  `console.anthropic.com` is no longer reachable from this proxy (was in 2026-04).
- **Fix part 1 (accurate errors):** `claude_exchange_code`/`codex_exchange_code`
  collapsed every failure to `None`, and `manager.exchange_code` turned that into
  the generic "code may have expired". Added `OAuthExchangeError(status_code,
  detail)` in `lib/oauth/token_store.py`; both exchange fns now RAISE it with a
  `_explain_exchange_failure()` message that distinguishes 403 edge/geo-block
  ("not an expired code … this server cannot reach the token endpoint from its
  current network") from a real 400/401 invalid_grant ("expired or already used —
  start a fresh login") from a status-0 network error. `manager.exchange_code`
  catches it and returns `{error, status_code, detail}`; the route already passes
  `error` through.
- **Fix part 2 (B1 browser-side exchange):** the browser already has the working
  VPN (it reached `claude.ai`), so it can do the token POST itself. `*_build_auth_url`
  now also returns an `exchange` block (token_url, client_id, redirect_uri,
  code_verifier, state, style=json|form). New `*_store_token()` +
  `manager.store_token()` persist a token the browser obtained (validate →
  `save_token` → `provision_oauth_provider`). New route `POST /api/oauth/store-token`
  + `Api.oauth.storeToken`. Frontend `settings/oauth.js`: new `_browserExchange()`
  does a direct cross-origin `fetch(token_url, mode:'cors')`; `_completeLogin()`
  is now the single path for both postMessage codes and manual paste — it tries
  the browser exchange FIRST, stores via the server on success, and on a NETWORK/
  CORS failure (not a real 400/401 auth rejection) falls back to the old
  server-side `/callback`. A genuine 400/401 is surfaced as-is (retrying
  server-side would just hit the geo-block). `code_verifier` is OUR PKCE secret,
  so handing it to the browser is correct.
- **Caveat / unknown:** whether `console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token` (and
  `auth.openai.com`) send permissive CORS headers for a browser `fetch` from the
  app origin is unverified in this env — the public OAuth clients usually do, but
  if not, the browser fetch rejects and we fall back to the server path (which is
  the geo-blocked one). If CORS blocks B1, the next step is B2: do the exchange
  inside the popup/relay page on the provider's own origin, or a userscript. Not
  built yet.
- **Result/status:** `tests/test_oauth_exchange_errors.py` (10 tests: 403/400/net
  classification through claude/codex + manager; B1 build-params, store_token
  persist+provision, reject-missing-token, unknown-provider) all pass; existing
  `test_oauth_outbound.py` 10/10 green. ruff clean; `node --check` clean; bundle
  rebuilt (`bundle-da56e4b8.js`). Restart + hard-refresh to serve. GOTCHA fixed:
  patch `lib.oauth.claude.save_token` (imported into the module namespace), not
  `lib.oauth.token_store.save_token`.

### 2026-06-24 — fetch_url now handles file-asset URLs: decode text assets inline, stage binary assets to data/fetched/ for read_files
- **Symptom:** `fetch_url` on a direct file URL (the reported case:
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/thesvg/main/public/icons/longcat/color.svg`)
  always returned "Failed to fetch", even though the asset was reachable
  (HTTP 200, `image/svg+xml`, 786 bytes).
- **Root cause:** `tofu_search.fetch.fetch_page_content` only extracts PDF /
  `text/plain` / HTML content types. Two layers conspire: (1) its
  `_should_fetch` guard in `tofu_search/fetch/utils.py` explicitly REJECTS
  asset extensions (`.svg/.png/.gif/.zip/.tar/.mp4/.exe/…`), returning `None`
  before any request; (2) for anything that does get fetched but isn't HTML/
  text/PDF, trafilatura extracts garbage → `None`. The chatui handler
  (`_fetch_url_one`) then reported "Failed to fetch". So every non-page URL
  (SVG, image, archive, font, Office doc) was a dead end.
- **Fix (chatui-side fallback; `tofu_search` left untouched):** Added
  `_try_fetch_file_asset()` in `lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/search.py`, invoked from
  `_fetch_url_one` ONLY when the normal text pipeline yields nothing. It does
  ONE raw `http_get` and branches:
    * **Text-like asset** (ext in `_TEXT_ASSET_EXTS` — svg/json/yaml/source
      code/css/… — or Content-Type matches `text/`, `+xml`, `+json`,
      `image/svg`, …) → decode bytes and return the source INLINE. This is the
      SVG fix: the model gets the actual `<svg>` markup.
    * **Binary asset** (png/zip/docx/font/…) → save to `data/fetched/<name>-<sha1[:8]>.<ext>`
      and return a note telling the model to `read_files(path=...)` (read_files
      handles images/PDF/Office natively). New `FETCHED_DIR` / `fetched_path()`
      in `lib/config_dir.py`, under the gitignored `data/` tree (auto-excluded
      from exports, isolated per project copy).
  **SSRF parity:** the raw download reuses `tofu_search.fetch.utils._host_is_safe`
  so it's held to the SAME private/loopback/cloud-metadata block policy as the
  main pipeline (verified: 169.254.169.254 and 127.0.0.1 are rejected before any
  request). Size-capped at 50 MiB. `_fetch_url_one` return dict gained
  `saved_path` + `is_asset`; `_format_fetch_display` renders a "File:" row
  ("Saved N bytes → staging (read via read_files)") for staged assets. Both
  single + batch fetch paths benefit (shared helper). Tool description in
  `lib/tools/search.py` updated to mention asset handling.
- **Result / status:** Verified end-to-end — the reported SVG now returns its
  786-char source inline; `python-logo.png` stages to
  `data/fetched/python-logo-<hash>.png` (15770 bytes on disk) with a read_files
  hint; display rows render correctly; SSRF guard blocks internal targets.
  `tests/test_image_fetch_ssrf.py` 28/28 still pass. No new test file added
  (validated via standalone harness) — `tests/test_fetch_asset_fallback.py`
  would be the natural home if formalized later.


### 2026-06-24 (follow-up) — Decoupled the file-asset fix to the right layer: text-asset extraction + safe byte-download now live IN tofu-search; chatui keeps only the read_files staging workflow
- **Why revisit:** The first pass (entry above) put BOTH halves of the fix in
  chatui's `_try_fetch_file_asset`, which (a) re-implemented fetching/SSRF/decode
  logic that is tofu-search's job, and (b) DOUBLE-FETCHED — the failed
  `fetch_page_content` call, then a second raw `http_get` in the fallback. User
  asked to decouple properly so "what belongs to tofu-search stays with it".
- **Moved DOWN into tofu-search (fixes every consumer, no double-fetch):**
    * `_should_fetch` (`fetch/utils.py`) no longer rejects `.svg` — only BINARY
      media (`.jpg/.png/.gif/.mp4/.mp3/.zip/.tar/.gz/.exe`). SVG is text.
    * `fetch_page_content` (`fetch/core.py`) gained a text-asset branch (after
      `text/plain`): when `_is_text_asset_ct(ct)` (new helper — `image/svg+xml`,
      `+xml`, `+json`, `text/*` except html/plain, js/yaml/toml) it decodes and
      returns the source VERBATIM, **returning early** so the article-oriented
      bot/SPA/`len>50` gates don't drop a small-but-complete file (a 44-char JSON
      or tiny SVG). Caches like any other hit.
    * New public `fetch_url_bytes(url, timeout, max_bytes)` → `(raw, content_type)`
      | `None`: the SAFE binary-download primitive (scheme check + `_host_is_safe`
      SSRF guard + `fetch_max_bytes` cap), reusing the existing `_do_request`
      session machinery. This is the competency chatui was duplicating.
    * New public `looks_like_text_asset(url)` — extension classifier so a caller
      can decide "treat as verbatim source, skip the prose filter".
    * All four exported from `tofu_search/__init__.py`.
- **Kept in chatui (genuinely host-specific):** `_fetch_url_one` now (1) skips
  the `filter_web_content` article filter when `looks_like_text_asset(url)` (an
  SVG/source file is not prose to be relevance-filtered — this also fixes a
  latent bug where a ≥3000-char source file would have been sent to the LLM
  noise filter); (2) on empty text result calls the slimmed `_stage_binary_asset`,
  which is now ONLY: `fetch_url_bytes()` → write to `data/fetched/` → craft the
  `read_files(path=...)` handoff note. No HTTP/SSRF/decode/text-branch left in
  chatui. Deleted `_try_fetch_file_asset`, `_ext_from_url`, `_TEXT_ASSET_EXTS`,

  `_safe_filename` stays (filename policy is a staging concern). `FETCHED_DIR`/

- **Result / status:** SVG now extracted in the FIRST `fetch_page_content` call
  (zero extra HTTP); PNG still stages to `data/fetched/`; SSRF blocks
  169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 inside `fetch_url_bytes`. New

  svg/json verbatim extraction, bytes happy-path/non-http/SSRF/size-cap/failure,

### 2026-06-24 — Self-update made robust for NON-git deployments: tarball-overlay fallback (exported copies / zip downloads are now updatable)
- **Problem:** The topbar Update button only worked on git checkouts.
  `export.py` strips `.git` (all three modes), so an exported copy had no
  `.git`; `lib/self_update.py::git_available()` returned False and
  `apply_update()` hard-refused with *"Not a git checkout — re-run
  install.sh"*. The version CHECK already worked without git (it hits
  GitHub's *tags* API), only APPLY was git-bound. So exported/zip deployments
  could see "update available" but never apply it.
- **Fix — dual-strategy apply (`lib/self_update.py`):** Split the old
  `apply_update` into `_apply_via_git` (unchanged git pull --ff-only path,
  now tagged `method='git'`, with the not-a-git refuse REMOVED) and a new
  `_apply_via_tarball(tag)`. A thin public `apply_update()` dispatches:
  `git_available()` → git, else tarball (resolving the target tag via the
  same `fetch_latest_release()` the badge uses). Both return the identical
  result-dict shape and emit the SAME `fetch`/`pull`/`deps` progress stages,
  so `routes/api_v1/update.py` and the push-stepper frontend are agnostic to
  which ran (`result['method']` records it). The tarball path:
  (1) **fetch** — stream `…/repos/<repo>/tarball/<tag>` to a temp file
  (`http_stream`, follows GitHub's 302→codeload redirect); reject if <1 KB.
  (2) **pull** — extract (guarding against `..`/absolute path traversal),
  strip GitHub's single `<owner>-<repo>-<sha>/` wrapper dir, then **VALIDATE**
  the tree carries `server.py`/`VERSION`/`lib/` BEFORE touching anything —
  a corrupt/partial download aborts with the live install untouched. Then
  overlay each file onto `_ROOT`, **backing up every replaced original** to
  `.update_backup/<ts>/` first (reversible — git pull doesn't need this, a
  file-copy updater does). Files under `_OVERLAY_SKIP_PREFIXES` (the runtime
  prefixes + `.git/`, venvs, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`,
  `.update_backup/`) are skipped, so `.tofu/` memories+skills, `data/` DB,
  `uploads/`, `logs/`, `.env` are preserved. (3) **deps** — no git to diff
  `requirements.txt`, so if anything changed, pip-install defensively.
  Documented limitation surfaced in `result['detail']`: a tarball overlay
  CANNOT delete files removed upstream (git pull can).
- **Frontend (`static/js/update.js`, `i18n.js`):** `check_for_update` now
  returns `update_method` ('git'|'tarball'). `_renderUpdateDialogBody` dropped
  the dead-end `!git_available` warning branch — non-git now shows the Apply
  button plus a `update.tarballNote` hint (settings/data/memories untouched;
  replaced files backed up to `.update_backup/`). The stepper labels go
  method-aware (Download/Apply vs Fetch/Pull) via `_updateState.update_method`.
  Repurposed the orphaned `update.noGit` string. Bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-c43bca22.js`); both files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`.
- **Housekeeping:** `.update_backup/` added to `.gitignore` (so leftover
  backups don't dirty a later git tree) and to `export.py`'s
  `PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_DIRS` + `ALWAYS_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (never ship per-host
  backups). Route docstrings in `routes/api_v1/update.py` updated to describe
  both strategies.
- **Two real bugs caught by testing (not just theory):** (1) `_overlay_skip`
  originally did `rel.lstrip('./')` — `lstrip` treats `./` as a CHAR SET, so
  `.tofu/skills/x` → `tofu/skills/x`, defeating the `.tofu/` skip and
  CLOBBERING user memories (test showed `preserved 0`). Fixed to a literal
  `./` prefix strip. (2) `_apply_via_tarball` used `http_stream` but the
  module only imported `http_get` → would `NameError` on the first real
  tarball update; the test's monkeypatch of `su.http_stream` surfaced the
  missing import immediately. Both fixed.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_self_update_tarball.py` (5 tests:
  skip-classification incl. the `.tofu` leading-dot regression; overlay
  preserves memories+DB and skips upstream `.tofu`; replaced files backed up;
  invalid archive aborts untouched; `update_method` reflects deployment) —
  all pass. Tests are hermetic (fake tarball via monkeypatched `http_stream`,
  `_ROOT` → temp dir; never hits network or the real tree). PY/JS syntax
  clean. NOT done: a live end-to-end apply against the real GitHub tarball on
  an actual exported copy (no exported deployment in this env) — the download
  → extract → validate → overlay → backup chain is verified structurally and
  functionally with a synthetic GitHub-shaped archive.

### 2026-06-24 — Multi-root memory: READ/search/prefetch unioned across all selected roots; WRITES stay anchored to the primary
- **Request:** In a multi-root project session, memory was scoped only to the
  PRIMARY root (`projectPaths[0]` == `cfg['projectPath']`). The secondary roots
  contributed files to read/edit, but their `.tofu/skills/` were invisible —
  not listed, searched, or prefetched, and new project memories landed only in
  the primary. User asked to share memory across the selected paths, and chose
  to keep WRITES on the main (primary) root.
- **Design (read-across, write-to-primary — mirrors the file-tool reads-unrestricted/writes-anchored split):**
  * **`lib/memory/storage.py`:** new `_iter_roots(project_path, extra_paths)`
    (primary first, dedup, skip blanks). `list_all_memories` now scans the
    primary + every extra root, unioning project- AND global-scoped memories,
    de-duplicated by id with the PRIMARY winning on collision. Threaded
    `extra_paths=` through the read wrappers (`list_memories` / `get_memory` /
    `get_enabled_memories` / `get_eligible_memories`) and the locate-then-mutate
    ops (`update_memory` / `delete_memory` / `merge_memories` / `toggle_memory`)
    — these rewrite/delete a memory in place at its OWN `filepath`, so editing
    an extra-root memory stays in that root. `delete_memory`'s package-containment
    guard now accepts any configured root (not just primary). `create_memory`
    UNCHANGED → always writes to the primary `project_path`; `merge_memories`
    sources from all roots but writes the consolidated output to the primary.
  * **`lib/memory/relevance.py` `search_memories`**, **`lib/memory/injection.py`
    `build_memory_context`**, **`lib/memory/prefetch.py` `run_memory_prefetch`**
    — each gained an optional `extra_paths=` that flows to `get_eligible_memories`.
  * **`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`:** compute `_mem_extra_paths` from
    `cfg['projectPaths'][1:]` right beside `_pp` (always defined, gated on
    `project_enabled and _pp`) — the existing `_extra_paths` for file tools is
    scoped INSIDE the `if project_enabled and project_path:` block, so memory
    needed its own copy at the wider scope. Passed to the `build_memory_context`
    prefetch future and to `run_memory_prefetch`.
  * **`lib/tasks_pkg/handlers/memory.py`:** `_handle_memory_tool` derives
    `_extra_paths` from `cfg['projectPaths']` and passes it as a 3rd positional
    to every op handler (uniform signature; `_memory_create` accepts+ignores it).
    So the model's `search_memories` / `update_memory` / `delete_memory` /
    `merge_memories` tool calls now span all roots; `create_memory` still → primary.
- **Backward-compat / isolation:** every `extra_paths` param defaults to `None`
  → with no extras the union loop runs over `[primary]` only = byte-identical to
  the old single-root path. The Settings REST surface (`routes/api_v1/memory.py`)
  has no multi-root session context and was deliberately left untouched (one
  `_project_path()` at a time — correct, it manages a single root).
- **Result / status:** All edited files syntax-OK. End-to-end functional harness
  PASSED: single-root A doesn't leak B; union sees A+B+global; `get_memory`
  locates B via extras; update/delete of a B-resident memory from an A-anchored
  session stays in/removes from B; `create` always → A; `merge` sources both
  roots, writes output to A, deletes both sources (incl. B's file). Handler-dispatch
  harness PASSED (search finds B, update badges OK). Regression-clean:
  `test_relevance_cjk.py` 9 + `test_package_facades.py` 42 = 51 passed; facade
  re-exports + new signatures verified. No new test file committed (validated via
  standalone harnesses) — a `tests/test_memory_multiroot.py` would be the natural
  home if formalized later.



### 2026-06-24 — Removed the CLI agent-backend selector; repurposed Claude/Codex OAuth subscriptions as live-token dispatch providers
- **Context / request:** User asked to delete the agent-backend selector
  (Codex / Claude Code CLI backends) but KEEP a way to reuse those
  subscriptions' quotas, configured via Settings. Two cleanly separable parts.
- **Part A — removed the CLI backend layer.** Deleted `lib/agent_backends/`
  (the whole pluggable package: builtin/claude_code/codex/detection/protocol/
  session_store/sse_bridge — spawned `claude -p` / `codex exec` subprocesses and
  bridged their JSONL to our SSE), `lib/chat/external_backend.py`,
  `routes/api_v1/agent_backends.py`, `static/js/agent-backend.js`. The `builtin`
  backend was just a passthrough to `run_task()` (which the normal chat path
  already calls), so `_start_external_backend` + the `agentBackend` dispatch
  branches in `routes/chat.py` (chat_start / _start_task_for_conv / send /
  branch_start + abort hook) were pure dead weight once non-builtin was gone.
  Stripped the `agentBackend` field from `lib/agent_options.py` + `lib/conv_config.py`,
  the topbar dropdown + mobile-sheet backend section from `index.html`, all
  `main.js` / `main/main_conv_lifecycle.js` / `main/main_folders_mobile.js`
  references, the `api.js` `agentBackends` client, the bundler allowlist entry,
  the `.agent-backend-*` CSS, and the now-orphaned `agent_sessions` DB table
  (Core schema def + both bootstraps + parity test). Updated 7 test files that
  asserted the `agentBackend` field / route. NOTE: pre-existing working-tree
  drift `test_conv_config.py::test_all_expected_keys_present` fails on
  `systemPromptBlocks` (confirmed via git stash that HEAD has the same failure —
  someone added that key to `resolve_conv_config` without updating the test);
  NOT my regression.
- **Part B — OAuth subscription → real dispatch provider (the new value).**
  The pre-existing `lib/oauth/` login flow stored tokens but `claude_get_valid_token()`
  / `codex_get_valid_token()` had ZERO callers — login worked, but nothing routed
  a request on the subscription. Closed that gap. New `lib/oauth/outbound.py`:
  (1) `resolve_oauth_request(provider, body, headers)` resolves a LIVE token +
  client-identity headers per request (tokens expire hourly, so a statically
  built slot won't do); (2) `provision_oauth_provider` / `deprovision_oauth_provider`
  add/remove a managed `server_config.json` provider on login/logout (with a
  sentinel api_key + `oauth` marker + `reload_config()`+`reset_dispatcher()`).
  Threaded a new `oauth` field through `Slot` → dispatcher slot build → all four
  dispatch call sites in `lib/llm_dispatch/api.py` → `stream_chat` / `async_stream_chat`
  → `prepare_request` (and the non-stream `chat()`). The pre-flight does the
  provider-specific spec:
    * **Codex** (officially tolerated) → `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`
      (existing Responses-API body translation auto-fires on the base_url);
      `Authorization: Bearer` + `chatgpt-account-id` (from the id_token JWT) +
      `OpenAI-Beta: responses=experimental` + `originator: codex_cli_rs` + matching
      `User-Agent` (wrong originator/UA → 403). Marked `stream_only` (no non-stream
      Responses translator).
    * **Claude** (the 2026 block workaround the OSS harnesses use) →
      `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages?beta=true`; token rides **`x-api-key`**, NOT
      `Authorization: Bearer` (Bearer now 401s on subscription tokens — verified
      against earendil-works/pi #2751); `anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,
      oauth-2025-04-20`; and the `system` field MUST begin with the exact literal
      `You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.` as its OWN first
      block (concatenating → 400), injected as a leading system message so
      `openai_body_to_anthropic` hoists it to `system[0]`.
  On login the Settings OAuth tab now auto-registers the provider (no more "go add
  the model manually" hint) and refreshes the providers list; logout removes it.
- **Why this design:** verify the OUTCOME at the seam — the token + spoof headers
  + Claude identity block are all resolved in the single request pre-flight
  (`prepare_request` / `chat`), not baked into a slot, because the token rotates
  hourly. Keeping the subscription as a normal `server_config` provider means it
  flows through the existing dispatcher / fallback / cost machinery unchanged;
  only auth + identity differ. Research correction surfaced to the user: Codex is
  officially supported third-party; Claude was blocked in 2026 but the OSS
  community (opencode, CLIProxyAPI, pi) keep it working via the x-api-key +
  claude-code beta + mandatory identity-block spec above — that's what we
  implemented.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_oauth_outbound.py` (10 tests: claude/codex
  resolve, identity-block prepend + no-double-prepend, beta merge ordering,
  no-token raises, `?beta=true` helper, provision/idempotent/deprovision-only-managed)
  — all pass. End-to-end verified via a standalone harness: dispatcher builds an
  `oauth='claude'` slot from a managed provider, `prepare_request` produces
  `…/messages?beta=true`, token in `x-api-key` (Authorization absent), beta flags
  lead-correct, identity at `system[0]`. Affected suites green (test_agent_options,
  test_event_emit, test_event_registry, test_core_schema_parity, test_compat_anthropic).
  `node --check` clean on all edited JS; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-cf9010ef.js` —
  agent-backend.js no longer referenced). Restart + hard-refresh to serve. NOT
  done: a live end-to-end call against a real subscription (no creds in this env)
  — the header/body spec is verified structurally against the OSS sources but the
  actual upstream acceptance should be smoke-tested after a real login.

### 2026-06-24 — Sub-agents now opt into the per-task extended-TTL cache latch (parity with main orchestrator)
- **Context:** Audited whether sub-requests (swarm sub-agents, scheduler
  prompt/agent/proactive/timer-poll) benefit from prompt caching. Finding: cache
  markers are applied universally at one chokepoint — `add_cache_breakpoints`
  (`lib/llm/cache.py`) called from `_sse_core.prepare_request` (streaming) and
  `chat.py` (non-stream) — so NO subsystem "forgets" markers. Real savings only
  exist where there's a stable repeated prefix: (a) **sub-agents** run a
  multi-round loop → prefix IS cache-read; (b) **scheduler `agent` / timer
  continuation** go through the full `orchestrator.run_task` (which already sets
  `body['_task_id']` at orchestrator.py:1855) → fully cached incl. extended-TTL
  latch; (c) **scheduler `prompt` tasks + proactive/timer polls** are single-shot
  / explicitly stateless (`smart_chat`, capability='cheap'=gemini which isn't even
  in the marker matrix, prompt below min cacheable size) → no prefix to reuse,
  inherently non-cacheable, nothing to fix.
- **The one gap (sub-agents):** `lib/swarm/agent.py` built its body via the
  default `build_body`/`dispatch_stream` but never set `body['_task_id']`. Without
  it, `add_cache_breakpoints` / the `prepare_request` beta-header path fall back to
  the GLOBAL `CACHE_EXTENDED_TTL` (and crucially do not latch a session-stable TTL
  decision), so a sub-agent whose rounds are spaced >5min apart could see its
  prefix expire on the default 5m TTL and get re-billed.
- **Fix:** Set `body['_task_id'] = self.agent_id` right after `_build_body` in the
  agent run loop (`agent.py:472`). `agent_id` (`agent-<role>-<id>`) is constant
  across all of the agent's rounds, so the latch key is session-stable — exactly
  the invariant `latch_extended_ttl` relies on. The dispatcher preserves the key:
  `_adapt_stream_body_for_slot` does `dict(body_or_messages)` (shallow copy keeps
  `_task_id`), and `prepare_request` reads then pops it. Mirrored the orchestrator's
  cleanup: added `release_ttl_latch(self.agent_id)` in `Agent._cleanup`
  (`agent.py:998`) so `_ttl_latch` doesn't leak one entry per sub-agent for the
  process lifetime.
- **Result / status:** `agent.py` syntax OK. Functional check confirms the latch
  lifecycle: decision is recorded, stays STABLE when the global flag flips
  mid-session (round-to-round), and is released on cleanup (no leak). `swarm`
  suites: `test_swarm_tool_scoping.py` all pass; `test_swarm_async.py` 61 passed,
  1 PRE-EXISTING failure (`TestAwaitAgents::test_await_no_ids_includes_early_finishers`
  — an `await_agents` inbox-delivery race) that reproduces with my two edits
  REMOVED, so it is NOT my regression (unrelated to the body/_task_id/cleanup
  change). The working tree carries hundreds of unrelated pre-existing uncommitted
  edits which I left untouched — my change is only the two hunks in `lib/swarm/agent.py`.
  NOTE for next session: `git stash` is hazardous in this repo (snapshots the whole
  workdir incl. .tofu churn — see avoid-git-stash skill); isolate single-file
  reverts by editing the file directly + a /tmp backup, not stash.


### 2026-06-24 — CLS #5: metric-overridden fallback font for Plus Jakarta Sans (font-swap reflow)
- **Context:** Follow-up to the Lighthouse fixes — addressed the deferred CLS
  item. CLS was 0.132 (0.81). The `cls-culprits` + `font-display` insights
  attribute small shifts to web-font loads on `feature-pills` (0.00045),
  `topbarTools` (0.00031), brand `U` (0.0000019). All faces ALREADY use
  `font-display: swap`, so the shift is a **metric mismatch** during swap: the
  generic fallback line box is a different height than Plus Jakarta Sans, so
  boxes resize when the real font lands. NOTE: the dominant 0.131 shift is the
  streaming `message-content` reflowing (structural, not a font issue) — out of
  scope; this fix targets only the font-attributed shifts the insight names.
- **Fix:** Added a `'Jakarta Fallback'` `@font-face` in
  `static/vendor/google-fonts-local.css` that aliases a local sans
  (`local('Arial'/'Helvetica Neue'/'Segoe UI'/'Roboto')`) with **vertical**
  metric overrides matching Plus Jakarta Sans — `ascent-override:103.8%`,
  `descent-override:22.2%`, `line-gap-override:0%`. These were MEASURED from the
  actual TTF (`LDIbaomQNQcsA88c7O9yZ4KMCoOg4IA6-91aHEjcWuA_qU7NSg.ttf`:
  unitsPerEm 1000, hhea ascent 1038 / descent -222 / lineGap 0 → 1038/1000,
  222/1000), not guessed. Inserted `'Jakarta Fallback'` into the body stack
  (`static/styles.css:3`) right after `'Plus Jakarta Sans'`, before
  `-apple-system`.
- **Deliberately NO `size-adjust`:** a wrong horizontal scale makes CLS WORSE,
  and the flagged nodes are single-line flex items whose box HEIGHT shifts, not
  wrap width — so vertical-only override is the safe, correct lever. On a system
  lacking all 4 local fonts the `@font-face` is simply skipped and the stack
  falls through to `-apple-system`/`sans-serif` (harmless no-op).
- **Result / status:** Both CSS files validate (11 @font-face, braces balanced,
  alias survives the minifier — verified). `google-fonts-local.css` is VENDOR
  CSS (NOT hash-busted by css_bundler — only `static/styles.css` is), so it
  needs a HARD-REFRESH to pick up; acceptable for a rarely-edited file. styles.css
  is auto-rehashed at startup. Restart + hard-refresh to serve.


### 2026-06-24 — Lighthouse-driven fixes: 28MB /project/set payload, manifest 401, tofu-theme contrast, CSS minify
- **Context:** User shared a Lighthouse report run against the live (proxied,
  mid-stream) UI. Most red items were ENVIRONMENT NOISE — Speed Index 3.6s +
  "page loaded too slowly" came from 2 in-flight SSE streams + a 3.8MB history
  conv rendering; the 2.3MB "unused JS" was browser extensions (沉浸式翻译
  3MB, Grammarly, Zotero, etc.); 12s main-thread / 9243 DOM nodes were one
  very long endpoint conversation. Real core metrics were fine (FCP 0.8s, LCP
  0.9s, TBT 70ms, Perf 85). Fixed the 4 genuine issues:
- **(1) `/api/v1/project/set` returned 28MB (11MB transfer) — REAL BUG, #1 in
  total-byte-weight.** Root cause: `lib/project_mod/config.py::get_state()` did
  `s = dict(_state)` (shallow copy), which carried the entire
  `_state['modifications']` undo log — each entry stores the full pre-image
  (`originalContent`) of every edited file (`modifications.py:377`). A
  long-running project balloons that to tens of MB, all serialized to JSON.
  The frontend only uses `modificationsCount` (an int). Fix: `s.pop('modifications', None)`
  after computing the count. Verified all `get_state` consumers (project bar,
  `/status`, `/set`, `/paths`) only read `modificationsCount` + `extraRoots`.
- **(2) `static/manifest.json` 401 (errors-in-console, best-practices).**
  `/static/` IS public server-side (`auth.py:141`); the 401 is the VS Code
  proxy stripping the `<link rel="manifest">` request (PWA manifest fetches
  WITHOUT cookies by default — same class as the `vscode-proxy-apiUrl` memo).
  Fix: `index.html:13` → `<link rel="manifest" ... crossorigin="use-credentials">`
  so the request carries `tofu_session`. No-op when not proxied.
- **(3) Accessibility 87 → contrast + viewport.** `color-contrast` was 0,
  all in the **tofu light theme** (Undo/Undo All/分支/原文/model name/第N轮/
  PARALLEL CALLS/TURNS/1.0M, ratios 1.7–3.7:1). Added a consolidated
  `[data-theme="tofu"]` override block in `static/styles.css` darkening each
  flagged fg color to ≥4.5:1 (and raising `opacity` on the ones the base rule
  dims, since opacity blends toward bg and tanks the ratio). Folded the new
  `.tc-preview-btn` rule into the EXISTING tofu `.tc-preview-btn` rule
  (line 18636) to avoid a duplicate selector. Also dropped `user-scalable=no,
  maximum-scale=1.0` from the viewport meta (a11y `meta-viewport` fail) —
  user accepted; kept `viewport-fit=cover`.
- **(4) CSS minify (lowest value, ~126KB raw / smaller gzip).** Rewrote
  `lib/css_bundler.py` to emit a hashed MINIFIED file `static/styles-<hash>.css`
  (mirrors the JS bundler) instead of just appending `?v=`. KEY RISK: styles.css
  embeds 11 `url("data:image/svg+xml,...")` data-URIs whose `//`, `>`, braces
  must survive — so `_minify_css` is a **string/comment-aware char-scanner**
  (protects `"..."`/`'...'` spans, only strips `/* */` + collapses whitespace,
  trims spaces ONLY around `{ } ;` — never `:`/`,`). Verified: 794KB→665KB,
  all 11 data-URIs verbatim, brace balance 0. `routes/common.py` `_APP_STYLES_RE`
  already matches the no-query `static/styles.css` tag (confirmed), so the
  swap works unchanged; updated the stale "content-hashed query string" comment.
  Added `static/styles-*.css` to `.gitignore` (next to `bundle-*.js`). On
  write/minify failure `get_styles_link_tag()` falls back to the un-minified
  source with `?v=` so the page is never style-less.
- **Result / status:** `ruff` clean on all 3 py files; `tests/test_project_tools.py`
  69/69 pass; `get_state` no longer leaks `modifications` (asserted). Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve (CSS bundler regenerates `styles-<hash>.css` at startup;
