### 2026-06-24 — Mid-conversation MCP install was "completely ineffective" (tool-schema latch held it back) + turn-ctx capsule omitted MCP tools — fixed both at the root
- **Symptom (user):** "If I install an MCP tool it becomes completely
  ineffective" + "turn-ctx also needs to display MCP tools".
- **Root cause (issue 2 — not a dead bug, a deferral):** The per-conversation
  tool-schema latch (`lib/tools/registry.py::latch_tool_list`, the (B) cache-
  stability fix) freezes the EXACT tool array a conversation first used and
  serves it byte-identical every round to protect the ~65k-token prompt-cache
  prefix. It was designed to defer composer-toggle flaps to the next NEW
  conversation. But it ALSO caught MCP installs: `_build_mcp`
  (`registry.py:773`) connects + emits the new tools fine, yet `latch_tool_list`
  returns the FROZEN snapshot (only flagging `diverged=True` + an additive diff)
  — so in the CURRENT conversation the MCP tools never reach the model. Verified
  empirically: round-2 after install → frozen 2-tool list, `diverged=True`,
  `added=[mcp__...]`; a brand-new conversation latches fresh WITH the MCP tools.
  An MCP install/uninstall/connect is a deliberate, infrequent, GLOBAL action —
  the one case where "defer to next conv" is wrong.
- **Fix (issue 2 — root, at the seam):** New
  `lib/tools/registry.py::clear_all_tool_list_latches()` drops EVERY
  conversation's latch and returns the count. Key insight that makes it free:
  the prompt cache keys on the tool array's BYTES, not latch identity — a
  conversation whose effective tool set is unchanged re-latches byte-identical
  next round (`diverged=False`, no rebuild); only conversations that genuinely
  changed pay the one-time rebuild. Wired into ALL eight user-initiated MCP
  mutation points in `routes/api_v1/mcp.py` (upsert / delete / connect-one /
  connect_all / disconnect-one / disconnect_all / catalog-install /
  catalog-uninstall both purge+soft) via a local `_invalidate_tool_latches(reason)`
  helper. Chose the ROUTE layer over `bridge.connect_server` so the keepalive
  auto-reconnect loop (which also calls connect_server) does NOT thrash every
  conversation's cache on a transient reconnect. Exported from `lib/tools/__init__.py`.
- **Fix (issue 1 — turn-ctx MCP display):** `static/js/info-rail.js`
  `_collectTools()` only knew hardcoded composer toggles; MCP state lived only
  in the Settings tab's `_mcpCatalog`. Added a module-level `_mcpRail` cache +
  `refreshMcpRailState()` (calls new `Api.mcp.toolsList()` →
  `GET /api/v1/mcp/tools`, groups by server), surfaced as one chip per connected
  server (`MCP: <server> ×N`, new `tone:'mcp'`). Refreshed at boot
  (DOMContentLoaded) and after every catalog mutation (hooked into
  `settings/mcp.js::_populateMcpTab`). The snapshot freezes per-turn via the
  existing `_ctx` persistence (survives reload). Also added an `mcp__` prefix
  rule to `_CTX_FAMILY_RULES` + `_mcpServerOf()` so a latch-diff reconcile maps
  `mcp__<server>__<tool>` fn-names to the same per-server chip (regex verified
  against hyphenated `github-batch` and underscore'd `my_server` names, matching
  `lib/mcp/types.py`'s `mcp__{server}__{tool}` convention). New chip CSS
  `.tctx-tone-mcp` (indigo) in dark/light/tofu themes. New API method
  `Api.mcp.toolsList`.
- **Result / status:** New `TestClearAllToolListLatches` (3 tests) in
  `tests/test_cache_schema_stability.py` → 20/20 pass; `test_mcp_launcher_resolve`
  + `test_plugin_isolation` 30/30; `ruff` clean; `node --check` clean on
  info-rail.js / api.js / settings/mcp.js; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-80374d6f.js`
  — all three JS files already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). Restart + hard-refresh to
  serve. NOTE: `test_tool_registry.py::TestOrdering::test_full_project_ordering_is_cache_stable`
  fails in the working tree but is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated — proved by
  stripping my added function and re-running (fails identically); the working
  tree's `_register_builtins` inserts `inspect_image`/`find_files` differently
  than the committed test expects. The repo working tree carried hundreds of
  unrelated uncommitted edits which I left untouched.


### 2026-06-24 — Cost popover `write` decomposition: round-1's 64k prefix warm-up was MISLABELED as "消息开销 64.1k" (message framing) — added a `contextWrite` term + made the envelope cap unconditional
- **Symptom (user-caught, verified against live DB):** The per-round cost
  popover showed `第1轮 write 64.1k 的来源：消息开销 64.1k`. Framing of 64k tokens is
  physically impossible (~16k messages of JSON wrapping). Pulled the exact task
  from PG (`task_results.metadata.apiRounds`, task `d7884979-8308-42e2-bbf7-d741729d0f5c`,
  conv `mqrfsilhaxe0bo`, model `aws.claude-opus-4.8`) and forward-verified every
  round: round 1 had `prevOutput=0, toolResults=0, recacheBody=0, envelope=64.1k`.
- **Root cause (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py::_compute_write_breakdown`):**
  `envelope` was the catch-all residual `write − prevOutput − toolResults`, and
  the `_ENVELOPE_MAX_TOKENS=800` ceiling was applied ONLY when a `cacheBreak`
  flag was set. Round 1 is the first LLM call → no prior round, no tool results,
  and a cacheBreak flag is impossible on round 1 → the entire first-time
  system+tools+history prefix write fell through to `envelope` and got the
  "消息开销" (framing) label. Same signature on every task's round 1 (also seen on
  `d7061d81`: round-1 envelope 89.5k). The model conflated three distinct things:
  bounded framing, legitimate first-time context caching (warm-up, not waste),
  and re-billed body on a cache miss (real waste).
- **Fix (Option B — general model, chosen over a narrow round-1 special-case):**
  Framing is fundamentally bounded, so cap `envelope` at `_ENVELOPE_MAX_TOKENS`
  UNCONDITIONALLY and attribute the excess by cause: a cache-break round → the
  body we already paid to cache is being re-billed → `recacheBody` (waste);
  otherwise → context cached for the first time → new `contextWrite` term
  (warm-up, not waste). `contextWrite` and `recacheBody` are mutually exclusive
  (the break flag is the discriminator). Five sub-items
  (`prevOutput + toolResults + contextWrite + recacheBody + envelope`) still sum
  to EXACTLY `write`. Frontend (`static/js/ui/finish_info.js`): render the new
  `首次缓存上下文` term in the equation + tooltip (explains it's reusable next round,
  not waste) + legend; envelope tooltip now notes it's capped. The aggregate
  cache-break warn glyph + `recacheBody` "真实浪费" framing unchanged.
- **Result:** Re-ran the NEW function over the real task — round 1 now reads
  `首次缓存上下文 63.3k + 消息开销 800`; the two genuine stochastic-miss rounds (2 & 6,
  `aws.claude-opus-4.8` server-side cache miss — same key 8427, same model, prefix
  unmutated, static 62.2k floor still read back) correctly show `重新缓存正文`
  64.7k / 69.7k; healthy warm-up rounds show `首次缓存上下文`; every round sums to
  write exactly. `tests/test_write_breakdown.py` updated (13 tests pass): added
  `test_first_round_large_write_is_context_not_envelope`,
  `test_context_and_recache_are_mutually_exclusive`, retired the two tests that
  asserted the old "huge residual stays envelope" behavior. `node --check` clean;
  `ui/finish_info.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES` → restart + hard-refresh.
  Reusable inspector kept at `debug/_inspect_write_breakdown.py`.
- **NOTE (separate, NOT a code bug — server-side):** The "2nd round ~100%
  ineffective" the user flagged is a STOCHASTIC server-side cache miss on the
  Opus gateway (~2/7 rounds re-billed 60–75k each), already documented in
  `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py:516`. Our code is correct (it detects + labels
  it). Real mitigation would be enabling 1h ephemeral cache TTL (currently
  `ephemeral_1h=0`, all writes go to the more-evictable 5m cache) or routing to a
  more cache-stable endpoint — billing-affecting, left for explicit follow-up.



### 2026-06-24 — MCP `McpError: Timed out … Waited 120.0s` flood (1135 events, dominated by `hope.watch_job`): root cause was a long-poll-vs-transport timeout MISMATCH + a latent `_run_async` cap bug — fixed with per-server timeout plumbing, hope default=360s, and a call-level degraded gate (§10-approved)
- **Symptom (from the upgraded triage tool):** `Traceback: mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`
  was the #1 error-log bucket (354→1135 lines). Drill-down: **`hope.watch_job`
  dominated** (227 of the matched `[MCP:Call]` lines) and **every single timeout
  waited EXACTLY 120.0s** — the smoking gun that the killer was the global
  transport cap, not a flaky upstream.
- **Root cause:** `watch_job` is a long-poll tool — it blocks server-side
  polling a cluster job until terminal state, with its OWN `timeout_sec`
  default of **300s**. But the MCP client transport killed every call at
  `MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 120` (`lib/mcp/types.py`). A long-poll tool whose budget
  exceeds the transport cap can NEVER return normally → always 120s-times-out,
  the result is wasted, the model retries → the count snowballs. Two latent
  plumbing defects made the existing per-server escape hatch useless: (1)
  `MCPServerConfig.timeout` was honored by `call_tool` (`client.py:1402`) but
  the OUTER `_run_async` wrapper hardcoded `future.result(timeout=MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT
  + 10)` (`client.py:694`), silently capping any per-server timeout >~130s; (2)
  the registry's `HOPE_MCP_TIMEOUT` env spec tunes the hope *subprocess's* own
  timeout, unrelated to the client transport cap. The circuit breaker
  (`MCP_BREAKER_*`) only covers RECONNECT failures, not repeated call timeouts,
  so a server timing out 1000+ times kept getting hammered with full 120s calls.
- **Fix (user-approved all 3 parts; §10 config values signed off):**
  **(A) `_run_async` cap bug** (`lib/mcp/client.py`): added an optional
  `timeout` param; `call_tool`'s two invocations now pass `timeout + 10` (the
  RESOLVED per-server budget + headroom) instead of inheriting the hardcoded
  global. Non-call paths (connect/disconnect) keep the `MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT + 10`
  default. **(B) hope registry default** (`lib/mcp/registry.py`): added a
  catalog-level `'timeout': 360` to the hope card (300s poll + handshake
  headroom) and made `build_server_config` propagate any catalog `timeout` into
  the saved `mcp_servers.json`. **(C) call-level health gate**
  (`client.py` + `types.py`): new `MCP_DEGRADED_TIMEOUT_STREAK=3`
  (`TOFU_MCP_DEGRADED_TIMEOUT_STREAK`, 0=disable) + per-server
  `self._timeout_streak` map. New `_is_call_timeout_error()` classifies a
  timeout (transport read-timeout OR outer future timeout) vs a tool-level
  error. After 3 CONSECUTIVE call timeouts the server is 'degraded' and the
  next call fast-fails with an actionable `MCP Error: server 'hope' is degraded
  …` string (no blocking, no blind retry); any success calls
  `_reset_timeout_streak`. **(Observability)** every call timeout emits
  `audit_log('mcp_call_timeout', server, tool, timeout, elapsed, consecutive)`
  and the degrade emits `audit_log('mcp_server_degraded', …)` — both greppable
  in `audit.log` and countable by the triage tool; the WARNING line names the
  budget so the mismatch is self-documenting.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_mcp_call_health.py` (7 tests: timeout-vs-
  tool-error classification, per-server timeout plumbing = 370 not 130, hope
  card default=360, degraded gate fast-fails after streak, success resets
  streak, tool errors don't bump the streak) — all pass; existing
  `test_mcp_launcher_resolve.py` (17) green; `ruff` clean. Timeout constants
  unchanged for every OTHER server (global stays 120s) — only opt-in/registry
  servers get a longer budget. NOTE: the 360s default applies to NEWLY-installed
  hope cards (via `build_server_config`); an EXISTING `data/config/mcp_servers.json`
  hope entry keeps its current timeout until re-saved — a one-line manual
  `"timeout": 360` edit there (or re-install from the registry) applies it now.



### 2026-06-23 — Error-log triage tool made traceback-aware: group by logical record + bucket tracebacks by terminal exception type (was: one opaque `Traceback` bucket + thousands of stray frame lines in `OTHER`)
- **Why (self-initiated improvement):** `debug/triage_errors.py` (the §3.4.2
  error-log triage tool) already existed but had a demonstrable weakness on the
  LIVE `logs/error.log`: it classified strictly **line-by-line**. A Python
  traceback is ONE logical event spanning ~7 lines (header + frames + caret +
  terminal exception), but the old classifier counted only the
  `Traceback (most recent call last):` header line, dumped the actual exception
  (`RuntimeError: hook failed`) and every frame/code/caret line into the `OTHER`
  bucket, and collapsed every traceback into a single opaque `Traceback` bucket.
  Net effect: `OTHER` was a meaningless ~6000-line catch-all and the operator
  couldn't tell `McpError` from `sqlite3.OperationalError` from `RateLimitError`
  — exactly the actionable signal triage is supposed to surface.
- **Fix (`debug/triage_errors.py`):** (1) New `_iter_records()` groups raw lines
  into **timestamp-anchored records** — a line starting with the
  `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` stamp begins a record; non-timestamped continuation lines
  (traceback body) attach to it. (2) New `_exception_type()` parses a traceback's
  **terminal exception line** (`_EXC_LINE_RE` accepts dotted names like
  `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`; `_EXC_SUFFIXES` filters prose, picking the
  LAST qualifying line so chained "During handling…" tracebacks report the
  outermost type). (3) `SIGNATURES` was split into `SEMANTIC_SIGNATURES` (PREMATURE
  STREAM CLOSE / PREFIX MUTATION / run_command timeout / 429 / DISCONNECTED —
  matched against the WHOLE record first, since they name the actionable category
  even when a traceback co-occurs) and `GENERIC_SIGNATURES` (AttributeError /
  ConnectionError / Timeout — only consulted when there's no semantic match AND
  no parseable traceback). `_classify()` now: semantic → `Traceback: <ExcType>` →
  `Traceback: <unparsed>` → generic → `OTHER`. (4) `triage()` walks records;
  `total_lines` still counts raw lines; the `since` cutoff keys on the record
  head's timestamp; a traceback's stored example is its terminal exception line
  (most informative), not the header.
- **Result on live log:** `OTHER` dropped from ~12k mixed lines to genuine
  uncategorized warnings; tracebacks now bucket as
  `Traceback: mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError` (354 — the dominant issue),
  `Traceback: sqlite3.OperationalError` (no such table: tenant_users, 50),
  `Traceback: lib.llm_errors.RateLimitError`, `ValueError`, `KeyError`, etc. New
  `tests/test_triage_errors.py` (18 tests: record grouping incl. leading-orphan
  lines; exception typing incl. dotted/chained/prose-not-exception; classify
  precedence incl. semantic-wins-over-traceback and `<unparsed>`; end-to-end
  counts + `--since` cutoff + missing-log + render smoke) — all pass; `ruff`
  clean. `debug/` is a namespace package (no `__init__.py`), so the test loads
  the module via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`. Pure-stdlib tool, no
  behavior change to any shipped code path — diagnostics only.


### 2026-06-23 — Swarm panel stuck "Running / 408m9s" after server restart: stale-guard (Option 1) + backend reconciler (Option 2) so an open tab self-corrects
- **Symptom (user screenshot):** A "Parallel Execution" swarm panel read
  **Running / 408m9s** (~6.8h) for a single analyst agent. The agent had been
  dead for a long time and the server had been restarted several times. User's
  hypothesis was "the data must come from the backend." It's the **opposite** —
  the panel's `Running` + ticking timer are 100% FRONTEND state.
- **Root cause:** `_swarmActive` / `_asyncRunning` / `_swarmStartTime` are
  set live from `swarm_*` SSE events (`sse_handlers_swarm.js`) and live only in
  the open tab's JS `round` object — never persisted (see the two swarm-panel
  memories). They're cleared ONLY by a terminal `swarm_phase:complete` event or
  an all-agents-terminal inbox-inject. If the server restarts (or SSE drops)
  AFTER the swarm finishes but BEFORE that event reaches an already-open tab,
  nothing clears the flags and no poll loop is running, so `_tickSwarmTimers`
  (`streaming_ui.js`, 1Hz) keeps recomputing `Date.now() - data-sw-start`
  forever. A hard refresh would already fix it (`_buildSwarmDoneHTML` patches
  `_swarmActive:false`), but the user wanted self-correction without a refresh.
- **Fix — both layers (user explicitly asked for both):**
  **(1) Option 1, symptom guard (`static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`):** new
  `_SW_STALE_MS = 30min`. `_buildSwarmPanelHTML` computes `isStale` when a
  panel is flagged active/async, has NO `_swarmEndTime`, and
  `Date.now() - _swarmStartTime > _SW_STALE_MS`. Stale → `isActive`/
  `stillRunningAsync` forced off, a muted slate **"Stale"** pill (new
  `_SW_STATUS_SVG.stale` clock glyph — no emoji, §3.4) replaces "Running",
  and the runaway elapsed is dropped. `_tickSwarmTimers` also `continue`s past
  any `[data-sw-start]` older than the cap so the live number freezes.
  **(2) Option 2, root reconciliation (`streaming_ui.js` + `api.js`):** new
  `Api.swarm.status(taskId)` → `GET /api/v1/swarm/status/<task_id>` (already
  existed; returns `{active:false, message}` when the session is gone post-
  restart). New `_reconcileStuckSwarmPanels()` runs on a 20s interval (only
  when tab visible): collects every in-memory swarm round still flagged
  active/async with no `_swarmEndTime`, owned by a conv NOT currently streaming
  (a live stream owns its own SSE/poll reconciliation — must not race it),
  resolves the owning task id (`msg._taskId || conv.activeTaskId`), probes each
  distinct task once, and on `active === false` calls `_settleStuckSwarmRound`:
  clears flags, freezes `_swarmEndTime`, applies any backend per-agent statuses,
  and marks still-mid-flight agents `unknown` (NOT a fabricated green "done" —
  same honesty as `_recoverSwarmAgents`), then `renderChat` + `saveConversations`.
  Transient/null probe (onError:'null') leaves the panel UNCHECKED so a later
  sweep retries (server may be mid-restart, the exact moment we care).
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_frontend_swarm_stale.py` (jsdom, evals
  real `streaming_ui.js`; 15 checks): fresh panel still Running+ticker; old
  unsettled → Stale + no runaway timer; old-but-settled (has `_swarmEndTime`)
  stays Complete; `_tickSwarmTimers` freezes runaway / ticks fresh;
  `_settleStuckSwarmRound` clears flags + freezes end + honest `unknown` for the
  evicted agent + applies backend `done`. Passes. Regression-clean:
  `test_frontend_swarm_recovery.py` 1, `test_frontend_api_isolation.py` 4 — green.
  `node --check` clean on both JS files; both already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; bundle
  rebuilt `bundle-a1be5cbe.js`; `.sw-pill-stale` CSS added to `styles.css` via
  the brace-balanced Python-script path (dark/light/tofu variants; 5782→5785
  balanced). Restart + hard-refresh to serve. Gotcha: `_SW_STALE_MS` is a
  `const` in the eval'd module scope and does NOT leak to the jsdom harness
  scope (only `function` decls do) — the test mirrors the 30-min value locally.



### 2026-06-23 — Timer Watcher parse-failure observability: stable poll id + raw LLM output persisted/rendered, WARNING log now correlatable
- **Symptom (user report, screenshot):** A graded-run watcher (`tmr_84bd4fb3`,
  36 polls) showed a wall of red `Could not parse the verification decision
  (LLM did not return valid JSON). Raw: From the JSON file, there are **29
  genom…` rows. The information was "far too incomplete": (1) the LLM's actual
  output was clipped to 200 chars buried inside `reason`, (2) each poll/trigger
  had NO locatable id, and (3) the failure logged only a truncated WARNING that
  couldn't be tied back to a specific poll. User asked for a FE+BE collaboration
  to make a parse failure renderable, ID'd, and properly logged.
- **Root cause:** `poll_timer` (`lib/scheduler/timer.py`) on a parse failure
  threw away the model's full text — it stuffed `content[:200]` into `reason`
  and returned an 8-tuple with no raw output. `_record_poll` had no column for
  raw output, so even what little there was died on refresh/restart. The
  WARNING line carried no poll number / model / id. The SSE `timer_poll_check`
  event likewise had no `pollId`/`rawContent`, so the UI panel
  (`_renderTimerWatcherBlock` in `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`) could only show
  the clipped reason.
- **Fix (full stack):**
  **(1) Backend `lib/scheduler/timer.py`:** `poll_timer` now returns a 9-tuple
  — appended `raw_content` (the LLM's FULL untruncated final text). On parse
  failure it logs at WARNING with `[Timer:%s] Poll #N parse FAILURE (model=…):
  … — raw(Nchars): %r` (full context, repr of first 2000 chars). `_record_poll`
  gained `poll_id` + `raw_output` params and persists them. Both poll loops
  (the in-`timer.py` background `_loop` AND the inline blocking poll in
  `lib/scheduler/executor.py::_execute_timer_create`) mint a stable
  `poll_id = f'{timer_id}.p{N}'`, pass it + the raw output to `_record_poll`
  (raw stored ONLY on parse_error/error — a clean wait/ready needs no dump),
  and add `pollId`/`rawContent` to the `timer_poll_check` SSE event + the
  `_timerPolls[]` round-state entry (so state snapshots / reconnection carry
  them).
  **(2) Schema (v26→v27):** added `poll_id TEXT` + `raw_output TEXT` (both
  `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`) to `timer_poll_log` in `_core_schema.py`, with guarded
  ALTER migrations in BOTH `_schema_pg.py` and `_schema_sqlite.py`, and updated
  the parity DDL in `tests/test_core_schema_parity.py`.
  **(3) Event contract `lib/agent_core/events.py`:** declared the new `pollId`
  + `rawContent` fields on the `TIMER_POLL_CHECK` EventSpec.
  **(4) Frontend:** `ui/sse_handlers_misc.js::_handleTimerPollCheck` captures
  `ev.pollId`/`ev.rawContent` into the poll record; `ui/tool_rounds.js`
  `_recoverTimerPolls` maps `poll_id`/`raw_output` back from the DB poll_log
  (so a refresh/restart rehydrates them); `_renderTimerWatcherBlock` renders a
  monospace `.timer-poll-id` chip on each poll line and, for a parse failure,
  shows the verbatim model output in the expandable detail under a "Raw LLM
  output (unparseable decision)" label (amber-tinted `.timer-poll-raw` `<pre>`).
  CSS for both added in `static/styles.css`. The streaming fingerprint already
  keys on `_timerPolls.length`, so new polls re-render without extra wiring.
- **Result / status:** New `tests/test_timer_parse_failure.py` (5 tests, all
  pass): 9-tuple + raw on parse fail; clean JSON → no parse_error; `_record_poll`
  round-trips poll_id+raw_output; clean poll stores empty raw; columns exist.
  Regression-clean: `test_core_schema_parity.py` (48), `test_event_registry.py`
  (5), `test_frontend_sse_dispatch.py` (1) — 59 total green. `py`/`node --check`
  clean; bundle rebuilt `bundle-3513360d.js` (the 3 edited JS files are already
  in `_BUNDLE_FILES`) — restart + hard-refresh. NOTE: the v27 PG column
  migration runs on the next server `init_db()` (restart); the test fixture
  applies just the two idempotent ALTERs to avoid contending with the live
  server's locks (a full `init_db()` deadlocked against the running server).

### 2026-06-23 — Cache "服务端缓存失效（缓存断点前移）" root-caused by LIVE experiment: it's a STOCHASTIC whole-request server miss, NOT BP4 advancement; body-breakpoint fix A/B-disproven and reverted; shipped relabel + detector-hash widening
- **Method over memory.** The cost popover's `缓存断点前移（尾部 BP4 标记移动…）`
  label was investigated end-to-end. Rather than trust the prior 2026-04 A/B
  (opus-4.6, 8 rounds) or the existing skill memories, built two fresh
  harnesses and ran live on the ACTUAL production model `aws.claude-opus-4.8`
  with REAL signed-thinking replay.
- **Experiments (both kept in debug/):**
  **(1) `debug/cache_prefix_byte_probe.py`** — OFFLINE wire-byte determinism
  probe. Feeds production-shaped history (reasoning_content + thinking_signature
  + tool_calls + tool results) through the REAL `build_body` (full sanitize
  chain + `_inject_claude_reasoning_details`) and `add_cache_breakpoints` for
  round N vs N+1, diffs the shared prefix. Result: **BYTE-IDENTICAL** through
  both stages → the client wire path does NOT mutate body bytes. Falsified the
  "extended-thinking replay mutates the prefix" hypothesis.
  **(2) `debug/cache_live_experiment.py`** — LIVE tool-loop A/B (LEGACY
  tail-only vs CURRENT) + identical-prompt REPLAY. Faithfully feeds each
  round's real assistant message (signature + tool_calls) back like the
  orchestrator does.
- **Findings:** (a) the conversation BODY *does* read back — `cache_read` GROWS
  9k→36k over 20 rounds (a moving tail BP is NOT fatal); (b) the real culprit is
  a **STOCHASTIC ~18% sub-5-min server-side miss** — the identical-prompt replay
  sent BYTE-IDENTICAL input at 3s gaps and calls 3 & 5 returned `cache_read=0` +
  full rewrite while 2/4/6/10 hit. This confirms (now by controlled live replay,
  not just log inference) the `production-cache-miss-root-cause-analysis` skill's
  "stochastic ~6-8% gap-independent server failure." (c) **Crucially, a
  stochastic miss evicts the WHOLE request prefix down to the system+tools floor
  (~9.4k), not just a tail segment** — so the "BP4 marker moved away" story is a
  mislabel.
- **Step 1 (stable intermediate body breakpoint) — IMPLEMENTED, A/B-TESTED LIVE,
  DISPROVEN, REVERTED.** Added a stride-snapped non-moving body anchor in
  `lib/llm/cache.py` (reserve a 4th BP slot for long convs). LIVE A/B vs
  tail-only LEGACY, 20 rounds × 2 runs: total cache_write 71,247 vs 84,893
  (run1, body-BP WORSE) and 77,597 vs 78,766 (run2, tie within ~1.5% noise,
  sign flipped); **0 drops-to-floor in both arms both runs** (the "cut
  drops-to-zero" signal from one 14-round pilot was NOISE). Root reason it can't
  help: the stochastic miss is whole-request and evicts the anchor too. Reverted
  cache.py + its tests byte-for-byte to the pre-session state (careful to
  preserve ~38 lines of UNRELATED pre-existing uncommitted work already in that
  file — did NOT `git checkout` the whole file).
- **Step 2 (relabel) — SHIPPED.** `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py` cause string
  "breakpoint advancement (BP4 tail marker moved…)" → "stochastic server-side
  cache miss (body re-billed; static prefix still cached) — a per-request
  gateway miss reproduced at <5min gaps with identical input". FE translations
  in `static/js/ui/finish_info.js` updated (old strings kept as legacy for
  already-persisted rounds). Bundle rebuilt `bundle-0eeb0fc0.js`.
- **Step 3 (widen the detector hash) — SHIPPED.** `_hash_prefix_content` was
  text-only (`block['text']` + `role`) and BLIND to `tool_calls`/`arguments`/
  `tool_call_id`/`reasoning_content`/`thinking_signature`/`reasoning_details`/
  block order — exactly the wire-affecting fields. Widened it so a future REAL
  prefix mutation surfaces as `PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED` instead of a mislabeled
  `server_side` break. Verified it now catches tool_call-arg + signature
  mutations and is idempotent on identical input. (A guard, not a perf fix — the
  wire is byte-clean today per experiment 1.)
- **Status:** `tests/test_cache_breakpoints.py` + `test_cache_improvements.py` +
  `test_server_message_store.py` = 114 pass (updated 3 cause-string assertions
  to the new wording). `node --check finish_info.js` clean. Honest outcome: 1 of
  3 planned changes was disproven by its own experiment and dropped; 2 shipped.



### 2026-06-23 — Tool-call root pill: attribute ABSOLUTE paths under a non-primary root (longest-prefix match)
- **Symptom (user report):** In a multi-root conversation (primary `chatui` +
  extra `FDP`), a `read_files` call whose `path` was the ABSOLUTE
  `/mnt/.../FDP/hope/op2_train.sh` rendered with NO `FDP:` pill on the
  tool-call line, even though the file lives in the non-primary FDP root.
- **Root cause:** `_resolve_tool_root_name` in `lib/tasks_pkg/tool_display.py`
  only had two attribution paths — (1) explicit `rootname:` prefix (parsed by
  `_split_rootname_prefix`, which DELIBERATELY skips absolute paths), and (2) a
  primary-root fallback that ignores `raw_path` entirely and only returns the
  root whose path == primary. An absolute path under a non-primary root hit
  neither: prefix parse yielded `head=''`, and the fallback could only ever
  name the primary. So `_toolRoot` was never set → no pill.
- **Fix:** Added a middle branch in `_resolve_tool_root_name` (between the
  prefix branch and the primary fallback): when `head` is empty and `raw_path`
  is absolute (`/`, `~`, or `os.path.isabs`), abspath+expanduser it and do a
  LONGEST-PREFIX match against every registered root's abspath (`==` or
  `startswith(root + '/')`). The deepest containing root wins (correct for
  nested roots). Falls through to the existing primary fallback when the path
  is under no registered root. Frontend untouched — `_renderToolRootPill`
  already gates on `projectState.extraRoots.length > 0`.
- **Tests:** New `tests/test_tool_root_pill.py` (7 cases, all pass): abs under
  non-primary → `FDP`; abs under primary → primary; explicit prefix still wins;
  nested roots → deepest; single-root → `''` (no pill); abs outside all roots →
  primary fallback; non-FS tool → `''`. `ast.parse` clean; adjacent
  `test_log_noise_reduction.py` 12 passed / 1 skipped (no regression). Pure
  backend; no bundler involvement.

### 2026-06-23 — `export.py` personal mode no longer carries chat history (config + credentials only)
- **Change (user request):** Personal mode used to be a full self-use clone
  that shipped the chat-history DB via a `pg_dumpall` → `data/pg_backup.sql`
  dump auto-restored on the destination's first boot. The user wanted personal
  mode to keep personal data such as MCP credentials but NOT the chat history.
  Since credentials are file-based (`data/config/mcp_servers.json`,
  `server_config.json`) and chat history is DB-based (PostgreSQL `data/pgdata/`,
  or SQLite `*.db`), the split is clean: stop shipping the DB, keep copying
  `data/config/`.
- **What was edited (all in `export.py`):**
  **(1)** Deleted the now-dead `_dump_source_pg_to_sql()` function (~146 lines
  incl. its big "Why NOT raw-copy pgdata/" comment block) — its sole caller was
  in `_export_personal_via_tar`.
  **(2)** Removed the `_dump_source_pg_to_sql()` call + the source-side
  `pg_backup.sql` cleanup block from `_export_personal_via_tar`; updated that
  function's docstring.
  **(3)** Added `pg_backups` (timestamped dumps dir) to `PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_DIRS`
  and `pg_backup.sql` (staged restore dump) to `PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_FILES`, so a
  stale dump left in the source tree by `lib/database/_bootstrap.py`'s nightly
  backup or a prior export is never tar-copied into the destination (which would
  otherwise re-trigger restore on first boot). `pgdata/` and `*.db` were already
  excluded (`PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_DIRS` / `PERSONAL_EXCLUDE_GLOBS_HEAVY`).
  **(4)** Rewrote the module-docstring personal-mode description + the inline
  `pgdata` comment to state history is dropped and a fresh dest boots with an
  empty DB.
- **Why this is the whole fix:** The destination's `lib/database/_bootstrap.py`
  restores chat history ONLY when it detects `data/pg_backup.sql` at first boot.
  No dump file shipped → fresh empty cluster, no restore path triggered.
  Raw `pgdata/` is never copied (TOAST corruption risk + now history exclusion),
  SQLite `*.db` files are excluded by the heavy globs, and `data/config/` (the
  MCP tokens + provider keys) still copies over untouched.
- **NOT changed:** `internal`/`opensource` modes (already drop the entire `data/`
  dir and strip `mcp_servers.json`), and `_purge_runtime_artifacts` /
  dest-preservation logic (that's about not clobbering the DESTINATION's own
  existing data on re-export — orthogonal to what the source ships).
- **Status:** `ast.parse` clean; no dangling `_dump_source_pg_to_sql` /
  `pg_dump_path` references. Pure backend script change, no bundler/test impact.


### 2026-06-23 — Cost popover "duplicate write every round" ROOT CAUSE: memory-count hint in the cached system prefix + a mislabeled cause string
- **User report:** Cost popover shows a full ~37.9k `write` every round while
  `cache_read` stays PINNED at the ~56.8k static prefix and only ~1.5k of genuinely
  new tool results flowed in. Popover labeled it `服务端缓存失效 … 缓存断点前移（尾部 BP4 标记移动…）`.
  Asked for a deep FE+BE root-cause + fix.
- **Evidence (log-backed, not theory):** `logs/error.log` carries 25× `PREFIX
  MUTATION DETECTED` + 39× `PREFIX RE-WRITTEN` on REAL run_task convs (e.g.
  `conv=mqq1ydgy`: R1 w=26669 r=59325 → R2 w=27145 r=59325 — read FLAT, body
  re-billed). This is the prefix-mutation signature, NOT healthy BP4 advancement
  (empirically BP4-on-tail = ~1 uncached tok/round; a flat-read full-body re-write
  is abnormal).
- **TWO causes found:**
  **(A) Real backend bug — memory count hint mutates the cached system prefix.**
  `lib/memory/injection.py::build_memory_context` returned `You have {N}
  accumulated memories available…`, appended into `messages[0]` (system msg) as a
  cache-stable block by `system_context.py:486-503`. The moment the model calls
  create/delete/merge_memories DURING a turn (this agent does so constantly), N
  changes → `_get_cached_or_compute` emits new bytes → Anthropic's strict-prefix
  cache invalidates EVERYTHING after `messages[0]` → full body re-write, read
  pinned at the tools/static floor. FIX: dropped the live `{N}` from the string
  (kept wording byte-stable); the model still has `search_memories` + the per-turn
  `<relevant_memories>` prefetch block, so the exact count had marginal value.
  **(B) FE/diagnostic mislabel.** The `partial_no_reuse` branch in
  `cache_tracking.detect_cache_break` returns `{'no_cache_reuse': …}` with cause
  "breakpoint advancement (BP4 tail marker moved…)" whenever a big write repeats
  while read is pinned — it does NOT distinguish a genuine prefix-byte mutation
  (the `_prefix_mutated` hash IS available in scope) from benign advancement, so a
  real bug got a benign-sounding label. Recommended (NOT yet applied — file is
  dirty with in-flight refactor): when `_prefix_mutated` is True on a
  partial_no_reuse round, surface `prefix_mutation` instead, and have the FE
  popover name the actionable cause + show which prefix message changed.
- **What was NOT the cause (ruled out):** `<relevant_memories>` prefetch injection
  is cache-safe (tail-only + `notify_compaction`); `build_body`'s sanitize chain
  shares nested `content` blocks via shallow copy but is byte-stable in practice
  for text convs (gateway-terms map is self→self no-op) — a latent risk, not the
  active bug; `_truncate_old_tool_results` idempotency was already fixed 2026-06-22;
  `sort_tool_results` only reorders the tail tool-result run.
- **Status (A):** Fixed in the CLEAN file `lib/memory/injection.py`. Tests green:
  `test_streaming_and_prefetch.py` Memory/skills 5/5 (the patched tests assert the
  `accumulated memories` substring + `memory_accumulation` block, both still hold —
  they never pinned the exact integer). Pure-Python, no bundler; restart to serve.
- **Status (B) — DONE (user asked to fold it into the dirty files too):**
  **(1) `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py:506`** — the `prefix_mutation` early-return
  guard was `prefix_mutation_break and not client_changes and not api_break`. The
  precise gap: when a round BOTH mutated the prefix AND showed a `cache_read` drop
  (`api_break`), the mutation was suppressed and the round fell through to the final
  `return {'server_side': cause}` carrying the "breakpoint advancement (BP4 tail
  marker moved…)" string — the exact `服务端缓存失效（缓存断点前移…）` the popover showed on
  memory-CRUD turns. Dropped `and not api_break`: a changed prefix byte GUARANTEES a
  miss regardless of any read drop, so `prefix_mutation` is the more certain +
  actionable cause and must win over `api_break`. Still defers ONLY to
  `client_changes` (system/tools/model — a concrete, differently-named cause the FE
  labels itself). Genuine BP4-advancement rounds (no byte change → `_prefix_mutated`
  False) keep their correct label. **(2) `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`** — tightened
  the `prefix_mutation` LABEL from `缓存前缀被改写（历史被非幂等编辑）` to just `缓存前缀被改写`,
  since `_cacheBreakReason` renders it as `label（cause）` and the backend cause_str
  already spells out "非幂等编辑 → 整段上下文重新计费" (was duplicated). The `prefix_mutation`
  cause-phrase translations were already present from the in-flight refactor.
- **Verification (B):** New regression tests in `test_cache_improvements.py`
  `TestPrefixMutationDetection`: `test_prefix_mutation_wins_over_api_break` (mutation +
  read-drop → `prefix_mutation`, NOT `server_side`) and
  `test_client_change_still_wins_over_prefix_mutation` (tools change still wins).
  **Negative control PASSED**: temporarily restoring the old `and not api_break`
  guard made the new test FAIL with `{'server_side': 'cached prefix bytes changed…'}`
  (proving the mislabel was real and the test isn't vacuous); reverted byte-for-byte.
  Full `test_cache_improvements.py` 43/43 green; `node --check finish_info.js` clean;
  bundle rebuilt `bundle-09a5efda.js` (label grep-confirmed in the built file).
  Restart + hard-refresh to serve. NOTE: `cache_tracking.py`/`system_context.py`/
  `finish_info.js` remain dirty with the user's pre-existing in-flight cache-popover
  refactor (716 insertions) — I added ONLY the two surgical hunks above and left the
  rest of that work untouched.


### 2026-06-23 — Tool panel: web_search/fetch_url results row now aligns with sibling rows (chrome-on-expand instead of always-on card)
- **Symptom:** In the unified tool-activity panel, a `web_search` (or
  `fetch_url`) row with results looked visibly NARROWER / indented compared to
  the flush `read_files` / `grep` rows above it (user screenshot: a `read` row
  flush to the panel edge, a `web_search` row floating in a little inset well).
  Root cause is structural, not a bug: most tools render as a bare full-width
  `.ptool-line`, but search/fetch-with-results renders as a
  `.ptool-results-block` — a collapsible CONTAINER (it has to hold the
  expandable result list + vertical cards). That block carried an always-on
  `margin: 2px 8px 2px 12px` + `1px` border + tinted background
  (`static/styles.css` ~L6728), so even in its default COLLAPSED state it sat
  inset 12px/8px with a border the neighbors don't have. Compounded inside a
  parallel-batch `.ptool-turn`: the group's `padding-left:12px` override
  (`styles.css:6515`) only matched `[data-prn] > .ptool-line` (direct child),
  not the search header nested one level deeper at
  `[data-prn] > .ptool-results-block > .ptool-line`, so its text also started a
  few px further right.
- **Fix (Option A — "card only when expanded", CSS-only):** Chose this over
  (B) box-everything (too heavy, kills the scannable-list feel) and (C) just
  zero the margin (collapsed row still carries lone border/bg). In
  `static/styles.css`: `.ptool-results-block` is now `margin:0; border:1px
  solid transparent; background:none` by default, and ONLY
  `.ptool-results-block.expanded` gets `margin:4px 0` + tinted border + bg +
  a `.ptool-results-content` top divider. Side margins stay 0 in both states
  so the header never shifts horizontally on toggle — only border/bg/vertical
  margin fade in (added `transition: background/border-color/margin .25s`).
  Extended the batch-group override to ALSO target
  `.ptool-turn:not([data-batch-size="1"]) > [data-prn] > .ptool-results-block
  > .ptool-line` so the nested header aligns with sibling rows inside parallel
  groups. Mirrored the expand-only chrome into the `[data-theme="light"]`
  (~L9146) and `[data-theme="tofu"]` (~L12516) override blocks (both previously
  set border/bg unconditionally on the base block). Net: collapsed search rows
  now read as clean aligned list items (▼ chevron is the sole "expands"
  affordance); expanded promotes into the bordered card that brackets results.
- **Result / status:** Pure CSS, no JS structure change. Per the CSS bundler
  (`lib/css_bundler.py`) edits auto-bust the hash — no version bump or JS
  bundle rebuild needed; hard-refresh to pick up the new stylesheet. Verified
  by reading the edited blocks; the toggle target (`.expanded` on the block)
  and DOM shape (`[data-prn] > .ptool-results-block > .ptool-line.ptool-results-header`)
  in `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js:1065` are unchanged.

### 2026-06-23 — Fixed truncated auto-titles ("更新 GL"): TitleGen's `max_tokens=32` clipped the model output mid-word
- **Symptom:** A conversation that opened with "glm5.2出了，更新一下provider模板相关的吧"
  got the sidebar title **"更新 GL"** — an apparently absurd abstraction. The
  smoking gun was `logs/app.log`: `[TitleGen] generated title='更新 GL' in 1.9s`
  — i.e. the LLM *did* run (this is NOT the first-60-chars fallback) and was
  emitting "更新 GLM-5.2 …" but the completion got cut off right after "更新 GL".
  Same root cause behind other clipped/empty titles in the log ('Project Tool',
  and several `[TitleGen] empty/unusable model output ('')` fallbacks).
- **Root cause:** `lib/conversations/title_gen.py::generate_conversation_title`
  called `dispatch_chat(..., max_tokens=32, capability='cheap')`. 32 completion
  tokens is too small for titles containing Latin/digit tokens ("GLM-5.2",
  "provider" tokenize heavily), so mixed-script titles got truncated mid-word
  while pure-CJK titles happened to fit (why only *some* looked broken).
  Compounding it: the `'cheap'` pool (see `bootstrap.py`) is full of **thinking**
  models (deepseek-v4-pro/flash, glm-4.7, qwen3-max, kimi-k2-thinking); for
  models where reasoning tokens count against `max_tokens` the trace ate the
  whole 32-token budget → empty output → fallback. `max_tokens=32` was a false
  economy: `_clean_title()` already collapses to the first line and hard-caps at
  `TITLE_MAX_CHARS=60`, so a bigger budget never yields a longer title.
- **Fix:** Bumped `max_tokens` 32 → 512 (room for a short title + any reasoning
  trace). Did NOT add `thinking_depth='off'` — `dispatch_chat` has no such
  parameter (and no `**kwargs`), so passing it would `TypeError`; it already
  defaults `thinking_enabled=False`, which forwards to `build_body` and disables
  thinking wherever the model honors the flag. Added a comment explaining the
  budget rationale.
- **Result / status:** `ast.parse` clean. Pure backend change in one function;
  no bundler/test impact. Next new conversation's title will generate with the
  larger budget — existing broken titles are unaffected (titles are generated
  once at conversation creation).

### 2026-06-23 — Toolset-latch "✕" (dismiss) now REVERTS the composer toggles to the cache-safe frozen set instead of leaving them diverged
- **Symptom / request:** When a mid-conversation tool toggle is held back by the
  per-conv tool-schema latch, a banner appears above the composer ("以下工具改动将在
  新会话生效…" + ± diff chips). Its "立即应用" applies the change (one cache rebuild);
  its "✕" dismissed the banner but `dismissToolsetBanner()`
  (`static/js/toolset-apply.js`) only `delete`d `conv._toolsetDiverged/_toolsetDiff`
  and hid the banner — leaving the toolbar toggles in their DIVERGED state (e.g.
  Swarm visibly OFF while the frozen/cached set still has it ON). User asked that
  clicking ✕ instead adjust the input-box tool state back to a safe set that
  won't break the cache.
- **Fix:** New `_revertToolsToCacheSafe(diff)` + a self-contained
  `_SAFE_REVERT_FAMILIES` table in `toolset-apply.js`, called from
  `dismissToolsetBanner()` before clearing the flag. The latch diff is in tool
  FUNCTION-name space (`lib/tools/registry.py::latch_tool_list` → `added = fresh −
  frozen`, `removed = frozen − fresh`); the cache-safe state IS the frozen set, so
  the revert turns **OFF** every `added` family (toggled-on-but-held-back → didn't
  run) and **ON** every `removed` family (toggled-off-but-still-frozen → ran
  anyway). Each family maps fn-names → the matching `_apply*UI(enabled)` setter
  (`_applySwarmUI` / `_applyBrowserUI` / `_applyDesktopUI` / `_applyMemoryUI` /
  `_applySchedulerUI` / `_applyCodeExecUI`[run_command] / `_applyImageGenToolUI` /
  `_applyHumanGuidanceUI` / `_applySearchModeUI`[web_search] ; fetch_url is a
  no-op — always on). The `_apply*UI` setters only flip the global + button class
  (no save/log), so after reverting we call `_saveConvToolState()` +
  `updateSubmenuCounts()` once to persist onto the active conv and refresh the
  count pills. Mapping mirrors `_CTX_FAMILY_RULES` in `info-rail.js` (kept separate
  because that table is private to its IIFE and maps to labels, not setters);
  unknown fn-names have no toggle and are skipped. Because the banner only ever
  renders for the ACTIVE conv, the live toggle globals being reverted are exactly
  this conversation's state. Net effect: next round's fresh assembly matches the
  latch → `diverged` returns to False → NO cache rebuild (the cheap path the user
  wanted). Also updated `toolset.dismissDesc` i18n (zh/en) + the hardcoded
  `title` fallback on the ✕ button in `index.html` to describe the new revert.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on `toolset-apply.js` + `i18n.js`;
  bundle rebuilt (`bundle-16a8b8c8.js`; `_revertToolsToCacheSafe` ×2 grep-confirmed
  in the built file) — `toolset-apply.js` already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve the new bundle + rewritten index.html. Verified by
  inspection + the screenshot case (a `−`/`removed` Swarm chip → ✕ now re-enables
  Swarm to match the cached set). Pure frontend; no backend/test change.


### 2026-06-23 — Paper Reading Mode gets a proper mobile UI: full-screen single-pane + bottom PDF⇄Reader switcher (replaces the cramped 50vh split-stack)
- **Symptom:** Paper Mode's only mobile rule (`@media ≤768px`, `static/styles.css`

  pinned to `max-height:50vh` on top, the Q&A/Report/Babel pane crammed into the
  bottom half. Neither pane ever got the full screen; on a 360px phone both were

  left no way to rebalance.
- **Fix (single full-screen view at a time, the standard split-pane mobile
  pattern):** On ≤768px, `.paper-body` becomes a `position:relative` container
  with `padding-bottom` reserved for a fixed bottom bar; `.paper-left` (PDF) and
  `.paper-right` (Reader = the existing 3 tabs) are both `position:absolute;inset:0`
  and toggled by `.paper-body[data-paper-view="pdf"|"reader"]`. A new fixed
  `.paper-mobile-switch` bar (two big touch targets, **PDF | Reader**, SVG icons
  per §3.4 — no emoji) flips the attribute; it respects `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`
  via a `--paper-switch-h` custom prop set on `.paper-mode-container` (a real
  selector — a bare `--x` inside `@media` does NOT cascade). The absolute panes
  use `width/flex/min-width:…!important` to defeat any **stale inline width** a
  prior desktop divider-drag left on `.paper-left`/`.paper-right` (the drag
  handlers set `style.width`/`style.flex` inline; they can't fire on mobile since
  the divider is hidden, but a desktop→resize→mobile transition could carry them
  over). `#paperQAInput` bumped to `font-size:16px` to stop iOS auto-zoom on focus.
  Switcher styling is pure CSS-variable based so dark/light/tofu themes carry
  through automatically.
- **Wiring:** **(1) `index.html`** — `.paper-body` gains `data-paper-view="pdf"`;
  added the `#paperMobileSwitch` markup as the last child of `.paper-body` (after
  `.paper-right`). **(2) `static/js/paper-reader.js`** — new global
  `_setPaperMobileView(view)` (sets the attribute, syncs the two buttons'
  `.active`, and on `'pdf'` defers one `requestAnimationFrame` then `paperFitWidth()`
  so the PDF refits to the now-visible width — it may have been laid out while
  `display:none` with `offsetParent===null`). Called from `enterPaperMode`
  (`_setPaperMobileView('pdf')` right after `_switchPaperTab('qa')`) so every paper
  opens on the PDF, and from `_quotePaperSelection`/`_askAboutPaperSelection`
  (`_setPaperMobileView('reader')`) so quoting/asking about a PDF selection surfaces
  the Q&A answer instead of leaving the user staring at the PDF. **(3) `i18n.js`**
  — `paper.viewPdf` (原文/PDF) + `paper.viewReader` (阅读/Reader). On desktop the
  switcher is `display:none` and `_setPaperMobileView` is a harmless attribute write
  (the split shows both panes regardless of `data-paper-view`).
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on paper-reader.js + i18n.js;
  paper-reader.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-8f11372a.js`,
  `_setPaperMobileView` ×4 grep-confirmed in the built file; `paper-mobile-switch`
  ×3 in index.html). Restart + hard-refresh to serve the new bundle + rewritten
  index.html. Verified by inspection only — no headless mobile-viewport harness in
  the repo; the logic is a CSS attribute toggle + a fit-width refit, both
  exercised on entry. Desktop layout untouched (switcher hidden, panes keep their
  flex split).



### 2026-06-22 — DISPROVED a perf "blocking-DB-on-the-event-loop" claim for conv_message_builder; landed a CI guard test instead of an unneeded code change
- **Trigger:** Asked to "fully advance the project regardless of cost." Ran 3
  parallel recon agents (git state / test health / perf-cost hotspots). Decisive
  finding: the working tree is **mid-refactor** — ~150 modified `.py` + ~45
  untracked files spanning relay-billing, conv-affinity/provider-pin dispatch,
  PG admin, agent admission, incremental translate; 11 `__init__.py` + `server.py`
  + most of `lib/llm`, `lib/tasks_pkg`, `lib/billing` are DIRTY. Test baseline is
  green (2,976 collect; core-infra 150/150). So broad sweeping edits were OFF the
  table — they'd collide with the user's in-flight surgery. Scoped to clean,
  self-contained files only (user picked Option B).
- **Investigation (the real value):** The perf punch-list's item #6 — "`conv_message_builder._load_messages_from_db`
  does a synchronous `db.execute(SELECT messages)` on the chat hot path; on
  FUSE/cross-DC PG this blocks the event loop; wrap every async call site in
  `asyncio.to_thread`" — turned out to be a **FALSE POSITIVE**. Traced ALL 8
  production call sites of `build_api_messages_from_db` / `build_branch_api_messages`
  and classified each by execution context:
  - `routes/chat.py` `chat_start` / `_start_task_for_conv` / branch route, and
    `routes/api_v1/endpoint.py::endpoint_start`, and `routes/.../autopilot/kick`
    are all **sync `def`** → dispatched to Hypercorn's thread pool by the
    Flask→Quart shim → already OFF the event loop.
  - `lib/message_queue.py::dispatch_next_queued`, `lib/tasks_pkg/autopilot.py`
    `_start_followup_task` / `kick_autopilot` run in **background worker threads**
    → off-loop.
  - The ONLY `async def` caller is `routes/conversations.py::debug_messages`, and
    it is **already** correctly wrapped: `await asyncio.to_thread(build_api_messages_from_db, …)`
    (with a docstring explaining exactly why). The 3 `async def` in `routes/chat.py`
    (lines 1106/1315/1496) are SSE stream generators — none call the builders.
  Conclusion: there is no event-loop block to fix. Wrapping the sync-route sites
  in `to_thread` would be WRONG (no running loop in a thread-pooled sync handler;
  adds overhead/risk for zero benefit). Reported this back rather than manufacture
  a change to look productive.
- **What landed (clean, additive, in `tests/` only):** new
  `tests/test_conv_message_builder_async_safety.py` (4 tests) — a static-AST guard
  (same idiom as `tests/test_compaction_invariants.py`, no app build/DB) that pins
  the verified invariant so it can't silently regress: (1) `debug_messages` keeps
  off-loading the builder via `asyncio.to_thread` (asserts the builder appears as
  a *reference arg* to `to_thread`/`run_in_executor`, never as a direct `ast.Call`
  callee); (2) a sweep of EVERY `async def` under `routes/` (recursive) asserts
  none invokes `build_api_messages_from_db` / `build_branch_api_messages` directly
  on the loop; (3) two self-check tests prove the AST helpers actually detect a
  raw call and accept a wrapped one (so the guards can't pass vacuously).
- **Result / status:** 4/4 pass (0.6s). **Negative control verified**: temporarily
  rewriting `debug_messages` to a raw on-loop call turned both invariant guards RED
  (pinpointing `conversations.py:214`) while the self-checks stayed green; reverted
  byte-for-byte (`git diff HEAD -- routes/conversations.py` empty). The only tree
  change this session is the new untracked test file — nothing in the dirty refactor
  zone was touched. NOTE for future perf work: when a hotspot is flagged as
  "blocking the event loop," ALWAYS classify the enclosing handler as sync `def`
  (thread-pooled by the Flask→Quart shim) vs `async def` first — only `async def`
  on-loop calls are real blocks here.


### 2026-06-22 — Cost popover ⇄ ptool panel: made the per-round seam traceable end-to-end (round-number labels + tool-result inflow line + final-answer tag)
- **Change:** Closed the visual gap between the two panels that report the same
  turn from two different records on one assistant message: the **cost popover**
  (`msg.apiRounds[].usage` — provider-billed truth) and the **ptool panel**
  (`msg.toolRounds[]` — local tiktoken count of each tool RESULT).
  **(1) ptool panel — `static/js/ui/tool_rounds.js`:** new `_groupRoundNo(g)`
  (round № = `llmRound + 1`, matching the popover's `第N轮`; null for legacy
  rounds w/o llmRound), `_roundTagText`, `_renderSoloRoundTag`; `_renderTurnHead`
  gained an `rno` arg (inline `第N轮` chip in the multi-call header). Every group
  now carries `data-round-no` and shows the round tag — solo turns get a thin
  `.ptool-turn-rno-solo` line, multi-call turns get the chip inside the existing
  header. **(2) Streaming parity — `static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`:** group
  creation stamps `data-round-no` from `round.llmRound+1`; the header post-pass
  now adds/removes the solo round-tag and threads `_rno` into `_renderTurnHead`,
  and drops a stale solo tag when a 1-call group grows to ≥2. **(3) popover —
  `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`:** built `_toolMetaByLlmRound` (name+toolTokens)
  alongside the existing name map and a `_roundToolMeta` array; added a concrete
  **inflow line** per round — `↳ 工具结果流入：read_files 18.7k、read_files 3.1k
  （计 21.7k）` — showing the PREVIOUS round's tool results (the actual cause of
  THIS round's `write`), with per-tool sizes identical to the ptool badges. The
  last tool-less round is tagged `↳ 最终回答（无工具）`. The old generic "write 来源"
  note is now suppressed whenever the concrete inflow line renders (no dup).
  CSS: `.ptool-turn-rno(-solo)` (+ light/tofu variants) and
  `.cp-round-inflow`/`.cp-round-final` in `static/styles.css`.
- **Why:** User screenshots showed a 6-round popover and a "7 tools used" ptool
  panel that couldn't be reconciled — counts differ, and a round's `write` (tens
  of K) dwarfed its own output with no visible cause. Pulled the EXACT conv from
  live PG (`mqp5twk7qlclzb`) and proved the data is correct, just unlabeled: 7
  tools collapse into 5 `llmRound` batches (llmRound 0 & 2 each ran 2 tools in
  parallel), the 6th API round is the tool-less final answer (hence 6≠5), and
  index mapping is `apiRound.round = llmRound + 1` (1-based vs 0-based). The
  total-context growth between rounds reconciles to *(prev round's tool results)
  + (prev round's output)* within tokenizer error — so the per-tool badge and
  the per-round write are both real, measuring different layers. The fix is
  presentational: surface the round number on both panels and the concrete
  inflow on the popover so the seam is end-to-end traceable.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on all three JS files; all three
  already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. Simulated the JS render maps against the real conv
  — popover `第4轮` inflow `read_files 18.7k、read_files 3.1k（计 21.7k）` matches
  ptool `第3轮 2 parallel calls: read_files 18.7k, read_files 3.1k` exactly, and
  `第6轮` correctly tagged `最终回答（无工具）`. Bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-10b43386.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. Backend `apiRounds.toolCalls`
  stamp remains the preferred authoritative source when present; the
  toolRounds-derived fallback covers every already-persisted message. NOTE:
  purely frontend + reads already-persisted data, so no server restart strictly

### 2026-06-22 — 自动翻译漏译 ROOT CAUSE: truncation floor mis-calibrated for EN→ZH + silent best-effort commit (added 溯源 trace)
- **User report:** 自动翻译"老是漏译" — long replies get translated only partway,
  the tail silently dropped. Asked to investigate (DB OK) and to build proper
  provenance logging for the auto-translate feature.
- **Diagnosis (DB + logs, evidence-backed):** Queried the live PG `conversations`
  store (60 most-recent convs, 454 messages with `translatedContent`). Built an
  EN-source译文长度比直方图: healthy peak is **0.50** (243 cases — correct, Chinese
  is ~half the byte length of English), but a low tail (ratio 0.09 / 0.18 / 0.19,
  and a cluster ~0.25–0.35) are genuine 漏译. **The user's pasted example is
  literally conv `mqoxkck2` idx 5** (9150→1691 chars, ratio 0.185): the译文 ends at
  "…确认启动路径。" and the ENTIRE `## Diagnosis` / `## Fix` / `Done` second half is
  gone. Failure mode = cheap LLM stops early with `finish_reason=stop` after ~45%.
  Two engine flaws in `lib/translate/engine.py::_translate_one_chunk` let it through
  **silently**: (1) the truncation floor `len(c) < clen*0.20` is calibrated for a
  language pair where output≈input length — for EN→ZH where healthy is ~0.5x, a
  translation that drops HALF the doc (ratio ~0.25–0.35) sails past the 20% gate;
  (2) after exhausting `_MAX_CONTENT_RETRIES`, `break # accept best-effort` commits
  a KNOWN-truncated result with only a buried WARNING — no audit trail, no marker,
  exactly the silent failure the user wanted made traceable.
- **Fix (`lib/translate/engine.py`):** (a) **Target-aware truncation floor** —
  `_short_floor = 0.30 if _target_is_chinese else 0.20` (computed `_target_is_chinese`
  once near `clen`), so half-dropped EN→ZH output is now caught and retried with a
  fresh model instead of accepted. (b) **溯源 provenance** — new `_build_trace(...)`
  helper produces a structured record `{path, model, in_chars, out_chars, ratio,
  attempts, content_fails, dispatch_fails, elapsed, verdict, suspicious, target}`
  attached to the returned usage dict as `_translate_trace` for EVERY path (cache /
  mt / llm) and emitted as ONE grep-able `[Translate:trace] verdict=… [SUSPICIOUS-SHORT]
  path=… model=… in=… out=… ratio=…` line. A `suspicious` flag fires when a committed
  translation cleared the hard floor but is still under a soft floor (0.40 ZH / 0.30
  other) — so silent partial drops stay visible *after the fact* even when not
  retried. (c) When the retry budget is exhausted and a truncated result is accepted,
  emit `audit_log('translate_truncated_accept', …)` to `audit.log` (`verdict='truncated'`).
- **Fix (`lib/translate/runtime.py`):** the async worker's "done" path reads
  `_translate_trace` off the usage dict and, when `verdict!='ok'` or `suspicious`,
  logs a loud `[Translate] Task … committing INCOMPLETE translation: verdict=… …`
  WARNING with conv/msg/ratio — so the auto-translate path leaves a correlated trail
  in `app.log`, not just the engine-level trace.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_translate_noop_already_target.py` +2
  (`test_en_to_zh_half_dropped_is_retried`: a first-attempt ~0.25x output is rejected
  by the new floor and the full-length retry accepted; `test_trace_marks_truncated_
  when_all_attempts_short`: always-short → best-effort accept stamped `verdict=
  'truncated'`). All 4 in-file pass; `test_incremental_translate.py` 8/8 still green.
  Offline smoke test confirms the trace line: a 2000→684 (0.34) commit logs
  `verdict=ok SUSPICIOUS-SHORT … ratio=0.34` + `suspicious:True`. NOTE: this is a
  REPORTING + calibration fix — it does NOT retroactively repair the 291 already-
  committed short translations (a separate re-translate pass via the existing
  `use_cache=False` repair path could, if desired). The deeper structural limit
  (whole-document single LLM call; input-splitting was deliberately removed earlier)
  is unchanged — raising the floor makes the engine *retry* a different model rather
  than accept the drop, which is the right lever given that constraint.



### 2026-06-22 — ROOT CAUSE: project-bar read/write flip-flop is a BACKEND global-state thrash, not a frontend race
- **Symptom:** project bar's read/write badge flipped on its own while typing;
  RO lock vanished; slow load on refresh. Frontend-only fixes (prior two
  entries today) changed NOTHING — correctly pointing at the backend.
- **Smoking gun (`logs/app.log`):** the global project singleton flip-flopped
  continuously, driven by `[run_task-*]` threads:
  `set_project: chatui → cadtrans (new_roots=['cadtrans'])` then
  `cadtrans → chatui (new_roots=['chatui'])` then `chatui → chatui` …
- **Root cause:** `lib/project_mod` keeps ONE global `_state`/`_roots`
  singleton. Two conversations on different primaries (one `chatui (+cadtrans)`,
  one `cadtrans`) each run background `run_task`s that call
  `ensure_project_state()` → `set_project()`; when the primary differs it does
  `_roots.clear()`, wiping the OTHER conv's root AND its `access='ro'` flag. The
  project bar reads this shared global via `/api/v1/project/status`
  (`get_state()`), so it showed whatever the last task set — badge flips, lock
  gone. No frontend fix could help: the UI was faithfully rendering a backend
  state being corrupted by concurrent tasks.
- **Why the global mutation was even unnecessary:** the 2026-05 per-conv root
  registry (`_conv_roots`, fix for the "Unknown workspace root" race) already
  isolates tasks. Both task-side consumers source roots from it given a
  `conv_id`: system-prompt root table (`get_context_for_prompt(path, conv_id)`
  → `get_conv_roots`) and tool path resolution (`_resolve_base` → `get_conv_roots`),
  with the project path passed EXPLICITLY. So a `run_task` never needed to touch
  the global at all — only its `set_conv_roots` call matters.
- **Fix (`lib/project_mod/scanner.py::ensure_project_state`):** when called with
  a `conv_id` (the task path), register the per-conv scope (`set_conv_roots`)
  and `return True` IMMEDIATELY — do NOT fall through to `set_project*()` and
  mutate the global. The global `_state`/`_roots` is now owned SOLELY by explicit
  UI actions (`/api/project/set`, `/api/project/paths`, which call `set_project*`
  with no `conv_id`). Single source of truth restored: the bar reflects the UI's
  active project; background tasks can't thrash it.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_readonly_roots.py` +2 regression tests
  (`TaskDoesNotThrashGlobalTest`: a task `ensure_project_state(other_dir,
  conv_id=…)` leaves the global `path` unchanged and preserves another conv's RO
  flag; conv scope still registered + resolves). Full suite green: readonly 12,
  project_tools 67 (79 together); `debug/test_project_state_race.py` per-conv
  isolation + 8-worker stress still PASS. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-04b85dc7.js`)
  for the earlier frontend changes — restart required for BOTH (backend code +
  bundle). NOTE: the two frontend entries earlier today (toggle sequencing +
  background re-hydrate) are still correct hardening, but THIS backend change is
  the actual cure for the flip-flop.

### 2026-06-22 — Cost popover per-round tool names now DERIVED from toolRounds (works for all existing messages, no restart)
- **Change:** `static/js/ui/finish_info.js::_buildCostPopover` now shows the
  per-round activity line (`↳ 调用 N 个工具：name×k、…`) on EVERY message, by
  deriving tool names from the message's own `toolRounds[]` instead of relying
  solely on the backend `rd.toolCalls` stamp. New `toolRounds` is threaded into
  the popover ctx (from `renderFinishInfo` → `_buildCostPopover({... toolRounds:
  msg.toolRounds || []})`); a `_toolsByLlmRound` map buckets `toolName` by
  `llmRound` (0-based), and `_roundToolNames[i]` resolves each displayed round as
  `rd.toolCalls` (preferred when present) → else `_toolsByLlmRound[rd.round - 1]`
  (the 1-based apiRounds `round` maps to 0-based `llmRound` as `round =
  llmRound + 1`). The activity line and the "write 来源" note's `_prevTcs` both
  read the derived list.
- **Why:** User screenshot: a 15-round popover where round 4 had `write 26.7k`
  but NO round showed which tools it called, so they couldn't trace which round
  generated the tokens. Investigated the live PG store directly: of 784
  messages with `apiRounds`, **186 carry `cacheBreak` but 0 carry `toolCalls`** —
  even the most-recently-updated convs (`CB True / TC False`). Root cause: the
  `api_rounds[-1]['toolCalls']` backend stamp in `orchestrator.py` AND the
  `cp-round-act` render in `finish_info.js` are UNCOMMITTED working-tree code
  (HEAD `d2b38e4` has neither), so the running server never stamps it; and even
  a restart wouldn't backfill the 784 existing messages. But every message
  already persists `toolRounds[]` with `toolName` + `llmRound`, which is exactly
  the data needed — so derive client-side. Verified the mapping against real
  data: a 6-round conv derived `[list_dir,grep_search] / [read_files,run_command]
  / [find_files,grep_search,run_command] / [run_command] / []` correctly (last
  round empty = final text response, no tools — correct).
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean; Python simulation of the JS
  derivation against the latest live message produced the right per-round tool
  lists. Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-c1fa024e.js`, derivation grep-confirmed present)
  — hard-refresh to pick it up (no server restart needed since the fix is
  purely frontend + reads already-persisted data). The backend `toolCalls` stamp
  (still uncommitted) remains a harmless authoritative override — when it
  eventually ships, `rd.toolCalls` is preferred over the derived fallback.



### 2026-06-22 — Project-bar read-only toggle: flip-flop + slow refresh fixed (backend = single source of truth)
- **Symptoms (user-reported):** (1) after the click-to-toggle read/write badge
  landed, the badge would flip back and forth on its own while typing in the
  input box; (2) project info loaded noticeably slower on every hard refresh.
- **Root cause:** read/write state lives in TWO stores that the frontend was
  syncing optimistically and racing: the ephemeral global server state
  (`lib/project_mod` `_roots[name]['access']`, returned by `get_state()` /
  `/api/v1/project/status` — wiped on restart, shared across convs) vs. the
  durable per-conv `conv.readOnlyPaths` (conversations DB). My first toggle impl
  (earlier today) double-wrote on every click — optimistic `_applyProjectData` +
  `_saveConvProjectPath` (a full `syncConversationToServer` PUT), THEN `setPaths`
  (a 2nd PUT to a different backend), THEN a 2nd `_applyProjectData` +
  `_saveConvProjectPath` — with no request sequencing, so a slow/cross-DC
  `setPaths` or rapid clicks resolved out of order and each `_applyProjectData`
  repainted the badge → visible flip-flop. The slow-refresh regression: once a
  conv carries a non-empty `readOnlyPaths`, the drift-detector in
  `loadProjectStatus` hits its `!roMatch` branch on EVERY load (server's
  ephemeral RO flag lost on restart never matches the durable conv list) and it
  `await`ed the heavy `setPaths` (fs `isdir` per root + cross-DC latency probe)
  BEFORE painting the bar.
- **Fix (`static/js/project.js`):** (a) `toggleProjectBarReadOnly` rewritten to a
  SINGLE authoritative round-trip: optimistic LOCAL repaint for instant feedback
  (no conv sync), then render + persist EXACTLY what `setPaths` returns via new
  `_deriveConvPathsFromState(data)` (reads back the backend's RO policy instead
  of guessing). A monotonic `_roToggleSeq` guard drops stale/out-of-order
  responses so only the newest toggle paints/persists — kills the flip-flop.
  Revert path no longer re-PUTs a guessed state. (b) `loadProjectStatus`
  `!roMatch` branch now paints the bar IMMEDIATELY from the durable
  `conv.readOnlyPaths` (the authority, since server RO is ephemeral) and
  re-hydrates the server in the BACKGROUND (fire-and-forget `setPaths`), so the
  load is no longer gated on the slow round-trip.
- **Why this is correct per the single-source-of-truth ask:** ENFORCEMENT truth
  stays on the backend (`_resolve_write_path` → `is_readonly_path`); the durable
  PERSISTENCE truth is `conv.readOnlyPaths`; the ephemeral global server state is
  treated as a cache that gets re-hydrated, never as authority. The UI renders
  what the backend returns, never a local guess that can race.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-71f6cefb.js`)
  — restart + hard-refresh. No backend change needed (`get_state()` already
  echoes `readOnly` per root + top-level primary; `set_project_paths` already
  stamps `access`).
