### 2026-06-22 — Cache-miss popover: collapse the 3-way "or" fallback into ONE confident cause
- **Change:** `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py::detect_cache_break` — the
  `api_break`/`server_side` fallback used to emit the useless string "prefix
  not reused — breakpoint advancement, server-side eviction, or a silent prefix
  byte change" (three candidates at once = effectively no answer). Replaced the
  bare `else` with a disambiguation that uses two facts the function already
  holds at that point: (1) `_prefix_mutated` (the prefix-content hash compare) —
  when False, the cached bytes did NOT change, so "a silent prefix byte change"
  is impossible and is DROPPED; (2) `cache_read` this round — when a substantial
  read REMAINS (`> _MIN_CACHE_MISS_TOKENS`, i.e. the static system+tools prefix
  still reads back), the cache was not wholesale evicted, only the segment past
  the advanced BP4 tail marker stopped reading → judged **breakpoint
  advancement** with "server-side eviction unlikely (static prefix still
  cached)" demoted to a parenthetical. Low-read-but-unmutated still names
  "breakpoint advancement or server-side eviction (prefix bytes unchanged)".
  Only the genuinely ambiguous mutated-prefix path keeps the old 3-way wording.
  Frontend `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`: added the new EN→ZH fragments to
  `_CACHE_CAUSE_PHRASES` (longest-first ordering preserved so the full sentence
  translates before its sub-phrases).
- **Why:** User complaint — the popover's "服务端缓存失效（前缀未被复用——断点前移、服务端驱逐
  或前缀字节被静默改动）" is a three-choice guess that tells them nothing. Investigated
  the live logs first: the conv's `server_side` rounds (mqoqxgr7/mqor5gmw/
  mqoq3qp9…) had NO paired `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED` line (bytes stable → byte
  change excluded) and their reads dropped to a recurring floor (~55535 = the
  static prefix) while only ~8–13k of body fell off — textbook BP4 tail-marker
  advancement (`add_cache_breakpoints` in `lib/llm/cache.py` moves the short-TTL
  BP4 forward every round). So the data already disambiguates; the detector just
  wasn't using it.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_cache_improvements.py` +2 in new
  `TestApiBreakCauseDisambiguation` (substantial-read-remaining → breakpoint
  advancement + excludes silent byte change + "unlikely" parenthetical;
  low-read-unmutated → "prefix bytes unchanged", no silent-byte-change offer).
  Full file green: 41 passed. Pre-existing contracts preserved
  (`test_unexplained_drop_reason_no_contention` still sees 'breakpoint' and no
  'contention'; `test_short_gap_detected_as_server_side` still matches). `node
  --check` clean; bundle rebuilt (`bundle-0c7c8008.js`, new ZH phrase grep-confirmed
  present) — restart + hard-refresh. NOTE: this is a REPORTING-precision fix —
  breakpoint advancement on the 4-marker scheme is structural/expected, not a bug.




### 2026-06-22 — hope-mcp quota-retry: bounded pause cap (give up fast when session never recovers)
- **Change:** `hope-mcp/src/hope_mcp/tools/submit_retry.py`: a paused task now
  gives up after `_MAX_PAUSE_SEC` (env `HOPE_MCP_MAX_PAUSE_SEC`, default 300 =
  5 min) of CONTINUOUS pause instead of sitting paused until the full
  `retry_deadline_sec`. New `paused_since` field (slots + to_dict/from_dict)
  tracks the current pause streak; it's set on pause entry, reset to None on any
  recovery (auto-login `approved` OR an out-of-band `is_session_live` flip at the
  top of the gate — new branch). When `now - paused_since >= _MAX_PAUSE_SEC` the
  loop finalizes `status='failed'` with `session_recovery_failed: True` and a
  clear "session never recovered within Ns" error (no_username → "set
  HOPE_USERNAME or run hope_login"; else → "approve the mobile-push login").
  `snapshot()` now surfaces `paused_for_sec` + `pause_give_up_in_sec`, and
  `pause_reason` advertises the countdown ("giving up in Ns if unrecovered").
- **Why:** Junior flagged the one weak spot in the session-pause design: with no
  `HOPE_USERNAME`, `try_auto_login` returns `no_username` forever, so a paused
  snipe would silently wait out the entire 30-min budget before failing. The cap
  makes an unrecoverable session fail FAST with actionable guidance, while the
  streak-reset ensures an INTERMITTENT session (brief flaps) never accumulates
  toward the cap — only a continuous pause counts.
- **Result / status:** Tests `tests/test_submit.py` +2 (gives-up-at-cap-no-username:
  cap=0.6s + budget=600s proves the CAP not the deadline ends it, asserts
  `session_recovery_failed`, `HOPE_USERNAME` guidance, elapsed<30s, and the
  countdown hint; pause-streak-resets-on-recovery: a flapping dead/alive probe
  with cap=1.0s still reaches success). Full suite green: 157 passed / 2 skipped
  (was 155). Note the precedence inside the loop: the deadline check runs first,
  then the session gate — so a task also can't outlive its overall budget.


### 2026-06-22 — hope-mcp quota-retry: re-validate session on resume + PAUSE (not fail) for auto-login recovery
- **Change:** Closed the login-on-resume gap flagged in the prior entry.
  `hope-mcp/src/hope_mcp/tools/submit_retry.py`: (1) New non-terminal `paused`
  status + `pause_reason` field (added to slots, `to_dict`/`from_dict`,
  `snapshot`). New `_LIVE_STATES = {running, paused}` constant; reaper,
  `get_submit_retry_status` `done` flag, `cancel_submit_retry`, and
  `_on_task_done` all switched from `status != "running"` to
  `not in _LIVE_STATES` so a paused task is never reaped, reports `done:false`,
  and is still cancellable. (2) **Session gate at the TOP of every loop
  iteration** (after the deadline check, before sleep+attempt): probe
  `hope_api.is_session_live()`; if dead → set `status='paused'`, call the
  shared one-shot `preflight.try_auto_login()` (idempotent while a push is
  pending — re-attaches, no duplicate push), persist, sleep one interval, and
  `continue` — WITHOUT incrementing `attempts` or issuing a run_job. On
  `approved` it flips back to `running` and attempts immediately. (3)
  `rehydrate_on_startup()` does ONE shared `is_session_live` probe and seeds any
  resumed `running`/`paused` task as `paused` when the session is dead, so the
  first poll right after restart is honest (`paused`, not a surprise run_job);
  the loop's own gate then recovers it. Summary dict gained a `paused` count.
- **Why:** Junior's exact concern: a resumed snipe whose token lapsed during
  downtime would fire a doomed run_job and finalize `failed`, burning the
  remaining budget. Pausing instead lets the existing auto-login path (the same
  `try_auto_login` preflight uses) recover the session — mid-loop expiry AND
  restart-with-dead-session are now handled by the same gate. A paused iteration
  costs zero run_jobs and zero attempts, so the deadline is the only thing that
  ends a stuck-paused task (or an explicit cancel).
- **Result / status:** E2E across two interpreters (real restart, dead session):
  rehydrate returns `paused:1`, statuses observed `['paused','succeeded']`, and
  exactly ONE run_job fires — only after the session recovers. Tests:
  `tests/test_submit.py` +3 (pause-on-dead-session-then-recover asserting 1
  run_job + ≥1 login; rehydrate-seeds-paused-when-session-dead asserting 0
  run_jobs while paused; paused-task-is-cancellable). Full suite green: 155
  passed / 2 skipped (was 152). Note: `_retry_loop` imports
  `_attempt_run_and_verify` / `try_auto_login` / `is_session_live` lazily at call
  time, so tests `monkeypatch.setattr` the defining modules (submit / preflight /
  hope_api) and the patch is picked up — verified.


### 2026-06-22 — hope-mcp background quota-retry is now RESTART-DURABLE (disk persistence + startup rehydration)
- **Change:** Made the background quota-snipe survive a hope-mcp restart.
  `hope-mcp/src/hope_mcp/tools/submit_retry.py`: (1) `_RetryState` now carries
  its own re-spawn inputs (`run_kwargs`, `base_payload`, `eff_timeout`,
  `eff_interval` — all JSON-safe) + `to_dict()`/`from_dict()`. (2) New
  best-effort disk store: `_state_dir()` resolves
  `HOPE_MCP_RETRY_STATE_DIR` else `<hope home>/.hope/hope_mcp_retry` (co-located
  with the token file, same writable mount), `_persist()` writes one atomic
  JSON file per task (tempfile + `os.replace`), `_delete_persisted()` on
  reap/evict. (3) `_retry_loop(state)` refactored to read all inputs off
  `state` and `_persist()` at every checkpoint (each terminal return, the
  per-iteration still-quota-blocked branch, cancel, crash) — and `spawn_retry`
  persists BEFORE launching the task. (4) New `rehydrate_on_startup()`: loads
  every persisted file; `running` → re-`ensure_future(_retry_loop)`; terminal →
  re-register in memory (no task) so the result stays queryable until TTL;
  corrupt file → log + unlink + skip. Wired into `server.py::run_stdio` right
  after the loop starts (best-effort, never fatal).
- **Why:** Junior flagged that the in-process-only design (previous entry)
  silently drops an in-flight 30-min snipe on restart. Key insight that makes
  this clean: `deadline_ts` is ABSOLUTE wall-clock, so downtime correctly counts
  against the retry budget — a task whose deadline elapsed while we were down is
  finalized as failed on its first resumed iteration WITHOUT issuing a run_job;
  one with budget left just resumes sniping. No clock/relative-time bugs.
- **Result / status:** E2E proof across two fresh interpreters (= real restart):
  proc-1 persists a `running` task → proc-2 `rehydrate_on_startup()` returns
  `resumed:1` and drives it to `succeeded` with the right app_id. Tests:
  `tests/test_submit.py` +4 (persisted-on-spawn incl. transient `info` key
  stripped; rehydrate-resumes-running→succeeds; rehydrate-deadline-elapsed→failed
  with ZERO run_job issued; rehydrate-keeps-terminal-result-queryable). New
  autouse conftest fixture `_isolate_submit_retry` points the state dir at a
  throwaway tmp + resets the module dir-cache (`_STATE_DIR_CACHE/_RESOLVED`) and
  `_TASKS` per test (the dir resolution is cached in module globals). Full suite
  green: 152 passed / 2 skipped (was 148). Knob: `HOPE_MCP_RETRY_STATE_DIR`.
  Persistence is fully best-effort — if no writable dir exists it logs a warning
  and degrades to the old in-process-only behaviour; it can never break the loop.


### 2026-06-22 — hope-mcp quota-snipe retry moved to a BACKGROUND task (non-blocking) + poll/cancel tools
- **Change:** Replaced the blocking quota-retry loop (added earlier today) with a
  background-task design, because the MCP client kills any single tool call at
  ~120s (`MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT=120` in `chatui/lib/mcp/types.py`, applied at
  `lib/mcp/client.py:1402`; the `hope` server has no `timeout` override in
  `data/config/mcp_servers.json`). A 30-min blocking `submit_job` would have been
  killed at ~130s AND frozen the agent turn with zero progress/cancel.
  **New `hope-mcp/src/hope_mcp/tools/submit_retry.py`:** an in-process registry
  (`_RetryState` + `_TASKS` dict, bounded by `_MAX_TASKS=64` + `_DONE_TTL_SEC=1800`
  reaper) running each retry as an `asyncio.Task` on the MCP server's persistent
  stdio loop. `spawn_retry()` launches `_retry_loop` which repeats ONLY
  `run_job`+verify (via the new shared `submit._attempt_run_and_verify`) until
  accepted / deadline / cancellation / a non-quota failure. Two new MCP tools:
  `get_submit_retry_status(task_id)` (read-only poll → running: attempts /
  next_attempt_in_sec / budget_remaining_sec; terminal: full `result`) and
  `cancel_submit_retry(task_id)` (idempotent). **`submit.py` refactor:**
  extracted `_attempt_run_and_verify` (one run_job+verify, normalized verdict)
  and `_quota_failure_message`; `submit_job` now does ONE inline attempt and, on
  a quota rejection with `retry_on_quota=True`, calls `spawn_retry` and returns
  IMMEDIATELY with `pending_retry=True` + `retry_task_id` (never blocks).
  Wired both tools into `server.py` TOOLS schema + TOOL_HANDLERS + `_SAFE_RETRY_TOOLS`
  (status read-only, cancel idempotent → safe to auto-retry after re-login), and
  `tools/__init__.py` eager import.
- **Why:** Answer to the junior's direct question ("does the 30-min retry hang the
  MCP call / can the user see progress or cancel?"). It would have — so option A
  (clamp to <120s) was rejected as a final answer per their instruction; this is
  option C, the proper fix: submit returns a handle, the loop runs in the
  background on the MCP loop (so it survives across tool calls), and the agent gets
  live progress + a cancel path. Only `run_job` is re-POSTed each attempt (code is
  uploaded once before the loop) so retries are cheap.
- **Result / status:** **Found + fixed a real race while testing:** `task.cancel()`
  on a background task that was never stepped (agent cancels right after the
  pending_retry response) transitions it straight to cancelled WITHOUT entering
  the coroutine body, so the `except CancelledError` branch never runs and
  `status` would stick on `running` forever. Fixed with a `task.add_done_callback`
  → `_on_task_done` safety net that reconciles cancelled/exception terminal state.
  Tests: `tests/test_submit.py` now 37 in-file (replaced the 2 old blocking-retry
  tests with: background-spawn-then-succeeds asserting `pending_retry` + run_job
  POSTed 2× while S3/save 1×; gives-up-at-deadline; cancel-flips-to-cancelled;
  unknown-task-id). Full suite green: 148 passed / 2 skipped (deterministic order;
  3 consecutive plain runs also clean — pytest-randomly is NOT installed). The one
  transient `test_get_status_batch` blip in an earlier run is in `jobs.py`
  (untouched) and did not reproduce. Total MCP tools listed now 50.
  **Server restart required** for the new tools + schema to reach the client.


### 2026-06-22 — hope-mcp submit_job: surface GPU-quota rejection + appId 兜底 + quota-snipe retry
- **Change:** Three additions to `hope-mcp/src/hope_mcp/tools/submit.py` (+
  `server.py` schema). **(1) Truncation fix + quota classifier:** the AFO
  admission-webhook quota refusal ("experiment X is restricted to use N GPU …
  now using M") was cut off by the old `("error message:", 40, 200)` window —
  the `now using M` number never reached the caller. Added higher-priority
  needles `("is restricted to use", 100, 300)` and `("admission webhook", 0,
  500)` and widened `error message:` to `400`. New `_classify_submitter_failure`
  (regex `_QUOTA_RE`) returns `{category:'quota_exceeded', experiment, limit_gpu,
  used_gpu}`. **(2) appId 兜底:** new `_extract_rejected_app_id` parses
  `"appId":"…"` from the submit-result JSON line (fallback: `crfile/<id>.yaml`
  path). Surfaced as `rejected_app_id` on the failure envelope — labelled
  distinctly from the normal `app_id` because a quota-rejected CR NEVER becomes a
  YARN app (not in 实验管理, pointless to `watch_job`). Both flow out of
  `_verify_cluster_acceptance`'s `submission_failed` verdict. **(3) Quota-snipe
  retry:** new `submit_job` params `retry_on_quota=False` (default off),
  `retry_deadline_sec=1800`, `retry_interval_sec=30`. Refactored steps 5+6 into a
  `while True` loop: on a `quota_exceeded` verdict it sleeps `retry_interval_sec`
  (clamped to not overshoot the deadline) and **re-POSTs ONLY `run_job`** — init
  / S3 PUT / save_code_version happen once before the loop, so each retry mints a
  fresh run_id with the already-uploaded code (no re-tar/re-upload). Returns the
  real `app_id` the instant the cluster admits, or `ok=False` with
  `quota_retries` count after the budget elapses.
- **Why:** Junior reported repeated P0 submissions failing with `state=UNSUBMITTED`
  and a useless truncated error (`…strategy: Forbidden:`). Root cause: P0 resource
  codes carry an experiment-level GPU quota enforced by the
  `tfjob.validate.mlp.sankuai.com` admission webhook (NOT queue capacity, so
  `get_queue_resource` can't predict it). Two real bugs fell out: the most useful
  sentence was truncated, and the submitter's pre-minted appId (present in the run
  log) was discarded. They wanted (a) the reason shown and (b) auto-poll to snipe
  a freed slot. Blind fixed-interval re-`run_job` is the right design since the
  webhook gate, not the queue, decides admission.
- **Result / status:** `tests/test_submit.py` +7 (extractor keeps quota tail,
  classify+extract appId incl. crfile fallback, surface-no-retry, retry-then-succeed
  asserting run_job POSTed 2× while S3/save POSTed 1×, retry-gives-up-at-deadline).
  Full hope-mcp suite green: 146 passed, 2 skipped. Schema params confirmed wired
  in `server.py`. Verified the three helpers against the verbatim live failing log
  — `now using 1422` survives, `{limit:1312, used:1422}` parsed, appId
  `psx4anqxro4a6ig1` captured.


### 2026-06-22 — turn-ctx capsule now reflects the TOOLS THAT ACTUALLY RAN (latch-aware)
- **Change:** Made the per-turn context capsule (right gutter, `info-rail.js`)
  agree with the backend tool-schema latch instead of blindly mirroring the
  live toolbar. **(1)** New `static/js/info-rail.js::reconcileTurnCtxCapsule(snap,
  diff)` (exported on `window`): given a snapshot `_ctx` and the latch diff
  `{added, removed}` (in tool FUNCTION-name space), it maps function names →
  feature families via `_CTX_FAMILY_RULES` (search/fetch/browser_*/desktop_*/
  generate_image/ask_human/memory*/schedule_*+timer_*+await_task→Scheduler/
  spawn_agents+await_agents+get_agent_result→Swarm-mode) and corrects the note:
  `added` (toggled ON but held back → did NOT run) are DROPPED, `removed`
  (toggled OFF but held back → STILL RAN) are RESTORED. Unknown names surface as
  a raw-name chip (never silently lost); Swarm restores to `modes`, not `tools`.
  **(2)** `static/js/ui/sse_pipeline.js` done-handler: right after the existing
  `onToolsetDiverged(...)` call (where `ev.toolsetDiff` is in scope), find the
  triggering user turn (last `role:'user'` before the assistant), reconcile its
  `_ctx` in place, then `saveConversations(convId)` (persists via the normal
  `lightMsgs` spread → survives reload) + `ConvView.upsertMessage` to repaint.
- **Why:** User toggled Scheduler/Swarm OFF and SENT before clicking "Apply
  Now". The capsule showed the new toolbar state (tools gone), but the
  per-conversation tool-schema latch (`lib/tools/registry.py::latch_tool_list`)
  freezes the tool array a conversation first used and serves it byte-identical
  every round to protect the prompt cache — so a mid-conversation toggle is HELD
  BACK until a NEW conversation or explicit "Apply now". The turn therefore
  actually ran with the OLD frozen set (scheduler/swarm tools still present),
  the exact opposite of what the capsule advertised. `buildTurnCtxSnapshot()`
  reads only the live toolbar globals, so it could never know the latch held the
  change. The backend already computes the precise divergence and ships it as
  `done.toolsetDiff = {added, removed}`; nothing was applying it to the capsule.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on both files. Standalone harness
  of `reconcileTurnCtxCapsule` verified 5 scenarios (scheduler+swarm held-off →
  restored as Scheduler tool + Swarm mode; browser held-on → dropped; empty diff
  → no-op; swarm-off → restored to modes not tools; unknown name → raw chip).
  Bundle rebuilt (`bundle-84b55ad5.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. Both files
  already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. Note: this corrects the capsule POST-HOC when the
  done event reports divergence (the only moment the frontend learns what the
  latch did); a turn whose toggles matched the latch needs no correction.


### 2026-06-22 — ROOT-CAUSED: two consecutive turns full cache_write, no error — non-idempotent old-tool-result re-truncation
- **Change:** Two-part fix (backend PREVENTS, frontend EXPOSES) for the
  screenshot bug (task `40e054ef`, conv `mqovcjp2`): R1 write 88.2k / R2 write
  89.7k, cache_read pinned at 51.4k, NO 缓存失效 line.
  **(A) Backend prevention — `lib/tasks_pkg/server_message_store.py`:**
  `_truncate_old_tool_results` is now IDEMPOTENT. Added module constant
  `_TRUNCATION_MARKER = 'truncated —'` and a guard that skips a tool result
  whose tail already contains it (previously only the micro-compact
  `'[...compacted...]'` marker was recognised, NOT this function's OWN
  `[... truncated — was N chars ...]` note). It also rewrote the note to emit
  `_TRUNCATION_MARKER` so probe and stamp stay in sync.
  **(B) Frontend/backend exposure — `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py` +
  `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`:** `detect_cache_break` already HASHED the
  prefix and logged `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED` but never RETURNED it, so the
  round carried no `cacheBreak` and the popover showed a big write with no
  cause. Now: capture `_prefix_mutated`, and when paired with a real
  `cache_write` (≥`_MIN_CACHE_MISS_TOKENS`) and not post-compaction, return a
  new `{'prefix_mutation': cause}` break (counted in `total_breaks`, logged as
  `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION BREAK`). The frontend adds the `prefix_mutation` label
  ("缓存前缀被改写（历史被非幂等编辑）") + English→中文 cause-phrase translations and
  renders its descriptive value like `server_side`/`no_cache_reuse`.
- **Why:** Confirmed from `logs/error.log`: conv `mqovcjp2` logged
  `call=44 PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED: messages[0:98]` then
  `call=45 ... messages[0:100]` on the two consecutive turns in the screenshot.
  Root cause chain: `_truncate_old_tool_results` runs at the START of every turn
  inside `rebuild_messages_with_history`, against the server-stored messages
  which are LIVE mutable dict refs (`save_messages` stores refs; `get_messages`
  hands them back). Its skip guard didn't recognise its own marker, so an
  already-truncated ~2080-char old tool result was RE-truncated each turn and
  the embedded "was N chars" count drifted (5,000 → 2,080 → …), silently
  rewriting bytes inside the cached prompt prefix `messages[0:N]`. Each new turn
  therefore re-billed the whole conversation body uncached (full cache_write,
  cache_read pinned at the static system+tools prefix). "No error message" =
  `detect_cache_break` only side-logged the mutation; `client_changes` checks
  system/tools/model/count only, so it returned `None` for R1/R2 → no popover
  cause. This is the root cause flagged as the open next-step in the prior
  "prefix re-written while read pinned" entry (that was the *reporting* fix;
  this is the *prevention* + a more precise report).
- **Result / status:** Tests — `tests/test_server_message_store.py`
  +`TestTruncationIdempotency` (3: truncate-once-then-fixpoint,
  five-passes-never-drift, compacted-marker-still-skipped);
  `tests/test_cache_improvements.py` +`TestPrefixMutationDetection` (4:
  surfaced, counts-as-break, stable-prefix-clean, post-compaction-suppressed).
  Full runs green: cache_improvements 43, server_message_store 29,
  keep_tool_history_integration 17 + cost 1 + regen_clears_msg_store 1. JS
  bundle rebuilt (`bundle-f846030e.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. NOTE: the
  prevention removes the per-turn prefix drift entirely; the new
  `prefix_mutation` break is defense-in-depth so any FUTURE non-idempotent
  history edit is named in the popover instead of silently re-billing.


### 2026-06-22 — "Model echoed input after retries" on already-Chinese agent replies
- **Change:** Two-layer fix so a Chinese-speaking agent's reply is no longer
  mis-flagged as an echo by auto-translate (target hard-pinned to Chinese).
  **(1) Primary — `lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py::_maybe_auto_translate_assistant`:**
  before starting the background translate thread, short-circuit when
  `lib.text_lang.is_predominantly_chinese(content)` (CJK ratio ≥ 30%). Mirrors
  the frontend `_isAlreadyChinese` guard the server safety-net was missing — an
  already-Chinese message now never starts a Chinese→Chinese translation. The
  old "translating regardless of content language" debug log is replaced with a
  real skip+log.
  **(2) Defense-in-depth — `lib/translate/engine.py::_translate_one_chunk`:** the
  exact-match no-op branch (`output==input verbatim`) now skips when the source
  is already in the target language (`_src_already_target`: target=Chinese AND
  `is_predominantly_chinese(src)`). Verbatim Chinese output is a legitimate
  pass-through, not an echo. The ratio branch right below already had this
  exemption; the exact-match branch did not. English→Chinese verbatim echoes are
  still caught (no exemption applies).
- **Why:** Junior reported the warning "Model echoed input after retries
  (attempt 5, 8s)" on a Qwen/Kimi reply that was already Chinese. Traced to the
  no-op/echo detector at `engine.py:381` (`status.py` maps `noop_final` →
  that label). Chain: agent replies in Chinese → server safety-net
  `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant` fires with target=Chinese (it lacks the
  already-Chinese skip the frontend pipeline has) → model correctly returns
  ~identical Chinese → exact-match no-op trips every retry → after
  `_MAX_CONTENT_RETRIES=5` it forces `c=''` and raises `ValueError`, surfacing
  the warning AND failing the translation. NOT a deadlock (loop is bounded by
  retries + `_OVERALL_DEADLINE_SEC`), but a real false-positive that wasted 5
  rounds and failed outright. Not a version issue.
- **Result / status:** Backend-only, no JS/bundle change. New test
  `tests/test_translate_noop_already_target.py` (2): Chinese→Chinese verbatim is
  accepted on attempt 1 (no retry, no raise); English→Chinese verbatim echo is
  still flagged (≥2 attempts → ValueError). `test_translate_noop_already_target`
  (2) + `test_incremental_translate` (8) + `test_regen_restores_original_when_translate_off`
  (2) all pass; `lib.tasks_pkg.manager` + `lib.translate.engine` import clean.


### 2026-06-22 — Toolbar scrunched after returning from Paper Reading Mode
- **Change:** Two-part fix in `static/js/main.js::_reflowToolbar` +
  `static/js/paper-reader.js::exitPaperMode`. (1) **Guard:** `_reflowToolbar`
  now bails early (`if (inputInner.offsetParent === null) return;`) when the
  input area is hidden, instead of measuring and writing a bogus width.
  (2) **Re-measure on exit:** `exitPaperMode` calls `_scheduleReflow()` right
  after restoring `.input-area`/`.chat-wrapper`/`paperModeContainer` display, so
  `--toolbar-w` is recomputed once the toolbar is visible again.
- **Why:** User reported the input box "occasionally looks weird" after
  switching back from paper mode, fixed only by switching conversations.
  `enterPaperMode` sets `.input-area { display:none }`. While hidden, any
  `_reflowToolbar` trigger that fires during the paper-mode window
  (`document.fonts.ready`, a model/depth change, `updateContextBar`, etc.)
  measures the toolbar children via `getBoundingClientRect()` — but they're
  inside a `display:none` ancestor, so every rect is width 0. The summed width
  collapses and hits the `w = Math.max(480, …)` floor, so `--toolbar-w` was
  written as the scrunched 480px (matches the overlapping-buttons screenshot).
  Nothing recomputed it on exit, so the bad width persisted until an unrelated
  reflow (conversation switch → `_restoreConvToolState`/`_applyModelUI`) fired.
  "Occasional" = only when a trigger happens to fire while paper mode is open.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean on both files; bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-f846030e.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. Both files already in
  `_BUNDLE_FILES`. The `offsetParent === null` guard is the robust general fix
  (covers any future caller that reflows while the input area is hidden, e.g.
  image-gen mode); the explicit `_scheduleReflow()` on exit guarantees a correct
  remeasure even if no other trigger fires.

### 2026-06-22 — Project-bar folder badges are now click-to-toggle read/write
- **Change:** Made each `.folder-badge` in the project bar
  (`static/js/project.js::_updateProjectUI`) clickable to flip that root
  between writable ↔ read-only without opening the project modal. Stored the
  rendered badge list in a new module-level `_projectBarFolders` ([{path,
  readOnly}]) and added `onclick="toggleProjectBarReadOnly(i)"` per badge. New
  `toggleProjectBarReadOnly(index)` rebuilds the ordered path list + RO set
  from `_projectBarFolders`, flips the clicked root, then mirrors
  `mpApplyFolders`: optimistic `_applyProjectData` repaint + `_saveConvProjectPath`,
  reconcile via `Api.project.setPaths(folders, roList)`, revert on failure.
  Added `cursor:pointer` to `.folder-badge` in `styles.css` and updated the
  hover tooltip to say "click to make read-only" / "click to allow edits".
- **Why:** User wanted a one-click way to toggle a root's access policy from the
  always-visible project bar, instead of the per-row lock button buried in the
  modal (`_mpToggleReadOnly`). The badge already encoded RO state (slate +
  lock glyph), so it was the natural affordance.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-b4cf2888.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. project.js already in
  `_BUNDLE_FILES`; its functions are module-global so the inline `onclick`
  resolves (same pattern as `_mpRemove`/`_mpToggleReadOnly`).
  **Cache note (answer to user's question):** toggling read/write does NOT, by
  itself, corrupt the prompt prefix cache. The RO flag is NOT advertised in the
  cached system prefix in the SINGLE-root case — `get_context_for_prompt`
  (`lib/project_mod/indexer.py`) only emits the "READ-ONLY" text inside the
  MULTI-ROOT block (`if extra_roots:`); a single-root session's prefix is
  byte-identical regardless of RO state, so the cache survives. In a MULTI-ROOT
  session, flipping RO changes the `(PRIMARY, READ-ONLY)` / `(READ-ONLY)` tags
  in that block → the system prefix bytes change → the NEXT request re-warms the
  cache once (one-time write, then reused). It corrupts nothing; it just costs a
  single cache-miss round, exactly like adding/removing a root does today.

### 2026-06-22 — Editing an Autopilot/critic message left the outer 译文 stale
- **Change:** Three-path fix so editing a display-translated message (Autopilot
  virtual-user `_isVirtualUser`, or endpoint-critic `_isEndpointReview`) updates
  the OUTER bubble, not just the 原文 toggle.
  **(1) `static/js/ui/edit_message.js::saveEditOnly`** — branch on
  `_isVirtualUser || _isEndpointReview`: call `_resetTranslationState(msg)` to
  drop the stale `translatedContent`, then re-translate the edited `content`
  INTO `translatedContent` (target=Chinese) via `_runTranslationPipeline`
  (`field:'translatedContent'`). The PATCH now also sends
  `translatedContent:null` + `_translatedCache:null` (whitelisted → key removal)
  so a later sync/reload can't resurrect the old 译文.
  **(2) `saveEditAndResend`** — clear the stale display translation
  (`_resetTranslationState`) in the optimistic local state before the regenerate
  POST.
  **(3) `routes/chat.py` `/api/chat/regenerate`** — detect
  `_isVirtualUser || _isEndpointReview`; on edit, pop
  `translatedContent`/`_translatedCache`/`_translate*` and set
  `restored_original=True` so the client refreshes; and force `auto_translate=False`
  for these messages so the normal user→English path (which sets
  `originalContent`) can't corrupt the VU/critic structure into a double-translation.
- **Why:** Autopilot replies are stored as `role:'user'` + `_isVirtualUser`, but
  they are DISPLAY-translated, the opposite wiring of a normal user message:
  `content` = model-language original (rendered in the 原文 toggle),
  `translatedContent` = UI-language rendering shown in the OUTER bubble
  (`chat_render.js:614-618`). Every edit path updated `content` but never cleared
  `translatedContent`, so the appended text landed only in the toggle while the
  outer bubble kept rendering the pre-edit 译文 — exactly the user's report. The
  normal user-message auto-translate (content→English, sets `originalContent`)
  was also wrong for these messages and would have made it worse.
- **Result / status:** After edit, the outer bubble re-renders the edited
  `content` (when translation cleared) and `saveEditOnly` additionally recomputes
  a fresh 译文 for display. Regression suites pass (regen-translate-off 2,
  chat-flow dispatch 12, frontend API isolation 4). JS bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-e4ecd6a6.js`) — restart + hard-refresh. Render fallback verified:
  with `translatedContent` absent, the `_isCritic` branch renders
  `renderMarkdown(msg.content)` in the outer body.


### 2026-06-22 — Auto-translate reliability watchdog + incremental per-round translation
- **Change:** Two-part fix to server-driven assistant auto-translate.
  **(A) Reliability watchdog** (`static/js/translation.js` + `static/js/ui/streaming_ui.js`):
  the server auto-translate path delivers its result to the live view via a
  SINGLE fire-and-forget push frame on the `translate` channel. `push_event`
  (`lib/agent_core/push.py`) drops frames when no client is subscribed at emit
  time and the per-client queue drops oldest on overflow — there is no
  Last-Event-ID replay on this channel. A dropped `done` frame stranded the
  "翻译中…" spinner forever until a conversation switch re-read the
  DB-committed `translatedContent`. Added `_armAutoTranslateWatchdog(convId,
  idx, msg)`: a keyed, idempotent DB-polling timer (first tick 8s, then 6s, 90s
  budget) that calls `_tryRecoverFromServer` to apply the committed translation,
  or clears the stuck indicator if the budget elapses. Armed from both the
  push `running`-frame handler (spinner shown, `done` lost) and `finishStream`
  (both frames lost). Short-circuits cheaply when `translatedContent` / a client
  task is already present, so it's a no-op when push works.
  **(B) Incremental per-round translation** (new `lib/translate/incremental.py`):
  instead of one big whole-message translation at task end, translate each tool
  round's prose segment AS THE ROUND CLOSES. The orchestrator
  (`lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`) calls `submit_round_segment(task, round_num,
  assistant_msg.content)` right after appending the round's `clean_msg` to
  `messages` (and once more for the final no-tool-call segment). A per-task
  ordered worker thread translates segments sequentially, caching
  `{round_num: translated}`. `_maybe_auto_translate_assistant`
  (`lib/tasks_pkg/manager.py`, now takes `task=`) calls
  `finalize_incremental(...)`: when an accumulator is active it assembles
  `translatedContent` from the cached segments (race-safe commit via the
  existing `_commit_translation_to_db` + a `done` push frame) and the
  whole-message thread is skipped; otherwise it returns False and the legacy
  path runs unchanged.
- **Why:** User reported (1) the auto-translate spinner sometimes hangs and you
  must toggle conversations to reveal the译文, and (2) requested that each
  tool-call's self-contained content be translated incrementally rather than
  waiting for the whole task. The data model made (2) natural: `task['content']`
  is one growing blob, but each round's `assistant_msg['content']` is that
  round's self-contained text segment, and the frontend renders `content` /
  `translatedContent` as single markdown blocks (tool cards are a separate
  panel), so per-round translated segments concatenate back to `translatedContent`.
- **Result / status:** New module is gated (`TOFU_INCREMENTAL_TRANSLATE` kill
  switch + per-conv `autoTranslate` + non-endpoint/non-autopilot) and fully
  exception-isolated — it can never break the agent loop, and declines safely to
  the whole-message path on any doubt (assembly coverage < 85% → whole-content
  fallback; no accumulator → legacy path). Endpoint/autopilot translation paths
  untouched. Tests: `tests/test_incremental_translate.py` (8, gating + assembly +
  coverage fallback + ownership). Regression: chat-flow dispatch (12),
  regen-translate-off (2), frontend API isolation (4), event registry (5) all
  pass. JS bundle rebuilt (`bundle-bc89a449.js`) — restart + hard-refresh to pick
  up. Reuses the existing `translate` push channel + frontend `'*'` subscriber
  (no SSE event-contract change). Known follow-up: the incremental gate reads
  `task.config.autoTranslate` while the legacy net reads conv `settings`; if they
  diverge the incremental path simply declines (safe, no regression).


### 2026-06-22 — Cache-miss detection blind spot: "prefix re-written while read pinned"
- **Change:** (1) Backend `lib/tasks_pkg/cache_tracking.py::detect_cache_break`:
  added a third detector `partial_no_reuse`. Fires when this round AND the
  previous round both have a large `cache_write` (≥ `_MIN_NO_REUSE_TOKENS`,
  20k) yet `cache_read` did NOT grow (`cache_read <= prev_cache_read * 1.05`).
  Returns `{'no_cache_reuse': cause}` and logs a `⚠ PREFIX RE-WRITTEN` WARNING.
  (2) Frontend `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`: translate the backend's English
  `cause_str` to Chinese (`_CACHE_CAUSE_PHRASES` + `_translateCacheCause`),
  reworded the `no_cache_reuse` label to "上下文重新计费（缓存未复用）", and
  suppressed the "healthy warming write" note on rounds that already carry a
  real `cacheBreak` reason (was contradictory).
- **Why:** User reported several consecutive rounds showing a big `write` with
  NO cause in the cost popover. Confirmed from `logs/app.log` conv `mqo09t2g`
  (this very task): R1 w=138k r=55728, **R2 w=141k r=55728** (body re-billed
  uncached), R3 r=194k (finally reused). R2 is a real, expensive miss but
  `detect_cache_break` returned `None`: `api_break` needs cache_read to DROP
  (here it's FLAT), and `no_reuse` needs cache_read==0 (here ~55728, the static
  system+tools prefix still reads). The conversation BODY was re-written every
  other round while the read stayed pinned at the small static prefix — a
  pattern both existing detectors were structurally blind to.
- **Result / status:** Replaying the real R1–R6 sequence, R2 now → `no_cache_reuse`,
  R5 (read actually dropped) → `server_side` via the existing api_break path;
  healthy reuse rounds stay clean. Tests: `tests/test_cache_improvements.py`
  +2 cases (`test_pinned_read_repeated_write_flagged`,
  `test_pinned_read_then_healthy_growth_not_flagged`) — 35 pass; cache suites
  108 pass. NOTE: this is the *reporting* fix (the miss is now explained). The
  underlying cause of the every-other-round rewrite (likely Anthropic gateway
  breakpoint advancement / <5min eviction on input=0 rounds) is logged as a
  WARNING but not yet root-caused — next step if cost remains high.

### 2026-06-22 — Restart progress bar no longer clobbered; journal updates made autonomous

### 2026-06-22 — Restart progress card now pinned open while the server is down (guard the DISMISS paths, not just the re-entrancy paths)
- **Change:** `static/js/update.js::closeUpdateModal()` — early-return when
  `_restartActive` is true, so the update modal cannot be dismissed while a
  restart is in flight.
- **Why:** User reported the restart progress bar "closes as soon as the server
  goes down." The bar's animation is server-independent (driven by
  `requestAnimationFrame` over a time-estimated phase timeline, not live logs),
  but the modal CONTAINING it (`#updateModal`) was still dismissable mid-restart
  via two paths that both route through `closeUpdateModal()`: the × button
  (`index.html:1559`) and a backdrop click (`index.html:1549`,
  `if(event.target===this)closeUpdateModal()`). A stray click while the page was
  unresponsive tore the card away, leaving a dead page with zero feedback. The
  prior 2026-06-22 entry guarded the RE-ENTRANCY holes (`_runUpdateCheck`
  re-paint, double-`restartServer`) but NOT these dismiss holes — this is the
  complementary fix. `_restartActive` is set in `restartServer()` and cleared
  only by `_restartSucceed` (auto-reloads) / `_restartTimeout` (shows timeout),
  so the card stays pinned for the whole down-period and resolves itself.
- **Result / status:** `node --check` clean; bundle rebuilt
  (`bundle-4e34247b.js`) — update.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`. Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve it.
- **Change:** (1) `static/js/update.js`: added a single `_restartActive`
  source-of-truth flag, set synchronously at the top of `restartServer()` and
  cleared in `_restartSucceed`/`_restartTimeout`. Guarded the two re-entrancy
  holes that could overwrite the live restart progress card — `_runUpdateCheck()`
  (covers re-opening the dialog + the retry button) and `restartServer()` itself
  (covers the always-live footer "Restart now" button + double-clicks).
  (2) `lib/project_mod/indexer.py`: reworded `_journal_seed()` and the injected
  "Project Journal" context block to explicitly grant the agent authority to
  append journal entries autonomously — no user confirmation required.
- **Why:** (1) During an in-place restart the topbar update button stays live;
  clicking it re-ran `_runUpdateCheck()` which unconditionally wrote the
  "checking…" spinner over `#updateModalBody`, making the progress bar vanish.
  The passive boot-time update check was NOT the culprit — it only touches the
  topbar badge. (2) The journal is a living dev log the agent maintains; making
  it wait for per-update confirmation defeats the "keep it current across
  sessions" purpose.
- **Result / status:** Restart card survives mid-restart dialog re-opens and
  stray footer clicks. Journal wording now tells the model to update without
  asking. JS is bundled (already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`) — restart + hard-refresh to
  pick up the new bundle hash.

### 2026-06-23 — Root-caused the billing test-harness isolation bug: backend/path globals are frozen at import, so per-class `TOFU_DB_PATH` was a no-op → added `reset_sqlite_for_tests` / `restore_db_state`
- **Symptom:** `tests/test_billing.py` + `tests/test_billing_phase2.py` failed
  non-deterministically (`ValueError: email already registered`, stale-balance
  assertion mismatches) depending on run order, on repeated runs, and whenever the
  ambient env selected PostgreSQL — yet each file passed alone against a pristine DB.
- **Root cause (two layers):** (1) `lib/database/_core.py` computes `_BACKEND` and
  `DB_PATH` as **module-level globals at import time** (`_FORCE_SQLITE` reads
  `TOFU_DB_BACKEND`; `DB_PATH = TOFU_DB_PATH or default` at line ~105). `_core` is
  imported at conftest collection (`_install_shim_for_collection()` → `import server`)
  LONG before any test body. So each billing class's `setUpClass` doing
  `os.environ['TOFU_DB_PATH'] = <tempdir>` + `init_db()` was a **no-op** — the path
  was already frozen, and `init_db()` only (re)creates schema on the *already-open*
  connection. (2) Worse, under the live-PG env `_BACKEND='pg'`, so the SQLite-intending
  unit tests silently shared the production PG and accumulated state (the hardcoded
  emails `alice@`/`bob@`/`frank@`… collide on the 2nd class/run). The earlier session
  (2026-06-23 Stripe entry) misattributed this to "`init_db()` no-op" and declared it
  out of scope; this session fixed it properly.
- **Fix (root cause — a real runtime repoint, not env juggling):** new
  `lib/database/_core.py::reset_sqlite_for_tests(db_path)` (exported via
  `lib/database/__init__.py` facade + `__all__`): forces `_BACKEND='sqlite'`, sets the
  module global `DB_PATH` (read fresh inside `_new_sqlite_connection()` on every
  connect), **drains the shared SQLite pool AND drops every thread-local handle**
  (`_thread_local = threading.local()`) so the next `get_thread_db`/`_pool_get` opens
  against the new file, then re-runs `init_db()`. Returns a `snapshot` dict.
  Counterpart `restore_db_state(snapshot)` swaps the globals back and re-drops
  connections. Both billing base classes (`_BillingTestBase`, `_BillingPhase2Base`)
  now `cls._db_snapshot = reset_sqlite_for_tests(<tempdir>/tofu.db)` in `setUpClass`
  and `restore_db_state(cls._db_snapshot)` in `tearDownClass` (subclasses
  `StripeWebhookTest`/`StripeCheckoutTest` inherit via their `super()` calls). Removed
  the dead `_ensure_db_initialised` helpers and the earlier timestamped-email
  workaround in `StripeCheckoutTest`.
- **CRITICAL gotcha found mid-fix (and fixed):** the FIRST version had only
  `reset_*` with NO restore → it leaked. Running `test_billing*` BEFORE the
  conftest-DB-sharing API suites (`test_api_integration.py`,
  `test_conversation_search.py`) left `DB_PATH` pointing at a now-deleted tempdir
  (the class's `TemporaryDirectory` was cleaned up), so those suites hit
  `OperationalError: no such table: timer_watchers` — 6 failed + 20 errors. This is
  why the helper MUST be symmetric: snapshot on entry, restore on teardown. Verified
  the leak (billing-first → API tests) and the fix (53 passed) directly.
- **Result / status:** billing suite **31 passed** in forward order, reverse order,
  PG-ambient env, forced SQLite, and on a 2nd consecutive run (idempotent). Leak-guard
  sequence `test_billing_phase2 + test_billing + test_api_integration` = **53 passed**
  (was 6-failed/20-error before restore). `test_relay_billing_gate.py` (pure-unit,

- **Working-tree investigation (no external mutator):** `git status` showed 1526
  dirty entries and the JOURNAL described a "mid-refactor". Diagnosed: 1170+ of
  those were DELETIONS under `.tofu/file-history/backups/` — Tofu's own
  content-addressed undo store (2053 tracked files) self-GC'ing round-by-round.
  It had been wrongly committed AND `.gitignore` already had a blanket `.tofu/`
  rule (which would also ignore the legit `.tofu/skills/`, 545 tracked files).
  No merge/rebase/cherry-pick in progress; HEAD clean at `fdd0e21`; 2 near-identical
  WIP stashes (orchestration/conv_config/token_counter snapshot, saved twice) left
  UNTOUCHED per user. **Fix (commit `cc3ab1a`):** `git rm -r --cached
  .tofu/file-history/` (files kept on disk), narrowed `.gitignore` to
  `.tofu/file-history/` + defensive `!.tofu/skills/`, and collapsed a duplicate
  `JOURNAL.md` ignore line (the journal-autocreate appended it twice). Committed
  ONLY those 2053 deletions + `.gitignore` via tight pathspec — zero source files
  swept in. `git status` 1526 → 514 (the 514 are genuine in-flight source work,
  left for the user to commit). Store keeps writing to disk; git ignores it now.
- **Cost-popover `write` breakdown — frontend→backend migration (the real task):**
  The popover's "工具结果流入" line showed tool-result inflow (e.g. 970) next to the
  round's `write` (e.g. 2k) with no accounting for the gap → looked contradictory.
  An earlier same-session frontend fix computed `prevOutput` from
  `rounds[i-1].usage` and `envelope = write − prevOut − inflow` CLIENT-side, but
  that (a) proxied prevOutput from output-side tokens and (b) could print
  sub-items that don't sum to `write` when the output-side counts overshoot the
  provider's input-side `cache_write_tokens`. Moved the math server-side:
  **(1) `lib/tasks_pkg/orchestrator.py`** new module-level
  `_compute_write_breakdown(task, api_rounds, round_num)` → `{write, toolResults,
  prevOutput, envelope, capped}`. `toolResults` = Σ `toolTokens` over tool rounds
  with `llmRound == round_num-1` (the ptool-badge numbers); `prevOutput` =
  `api_rounds[-2].usage` completion/output + reasoning/thinking; `envelope` = the
  residual. CRITICAL INVARIANT: components are capped to `write` in priority order
  (tools, then prev output) so `toolResults+prevOutput+envelope == write` in EVERY
  case, incl. tokenizer-mismatch overshoot (`capped:true` flags the approximation).
  Stamped onto `api_rounds[-1]['writeBreakdown']` in the SAME guarded block as
  `cacheBreak`/`toolCalls` (`round == round_num+1`); rides the `apiRounds` blob to
  the done event + DB (manager.py persists apiRounds whole, no key whitelist).
  **(2) `static/js/ui/finish_info.js`** the inflow line now RENDERS
  `rd.writeBreakdown` (no client arithmetic); legacy rounds w/o the field fall
  back to the plain inflow line. **(3) `tests/test_write_breakdown.py`** (8 tests)
  asserts the sum==write invariant across normal / overshoot / tools-exceed /
  first-round / alias / none / malformed cases.
- **Result / status:** `ast.parse` + `node --check` clean; new suite 8/8;
  regression `test_cost.py`+`test_keep_tool_history_cost.py` 13/13. Bundle rebuilt
  `bundle-4504079a.js` (finish_info.js already in `_BUNDLE_FILES`). Restart +
  hard-refresh to serve it. NOTE: `writeBreakdown` is stamped going forward only —
  messages persisted before this change render on the legacy plain inflow line.


### 2026-06-23 — "36.5k structural overhead" was a real cache regression: first-time tool-result truncation INSIDE the cached prefix re-bills the whole body every round
- **Symptom (user-reported, cost popover):** a round with `write 37.7k`, `cache_read` PINNED at the static ~59k system+tools prefix, only ~1.2k genuinely-new content (893 tool result + 337 prev output) — yet the write-breakdown lumped the unexplained ~36.5k into `结构开销` (envelope). User correctly called BS: genuine per-message JSON/role framing is hundreds of tokens, not 36k.
- **Investigation (2 parallel coders + log evidence):** Agent A said "expected BP4 tail advancement"; Agent B said "matches prefix-mutation". Adjudicated against `logs/error.log`: the smoking gun is `cache_read` PINNED (~56-59k) while `cache_write` CLIMBS MONOTONICALLY with conv size (conv mqq5strz: 27k→115k→120k→124k), with `⚠ PREFIX MUTATION DETECTED` and `⚠ PREFIX RE-WRITTEN` INTERLEAVED on the same conv. Healthy BP4 advancement would make the read GROW to absorb the prior write (the 2026-04 `debug/CACHE_BP4_AB_REPORT.md` shows read climbing 4537→8255 with the SAME `msg[-1]` BP4 placement). So BP4 placement is CORRECT; the body bytes are being mutated between rounds. Root-caused by a 3rd coder: `lib/tasks_pkg/server_message_store.py::_truncate_old_tool_results` truncates by TURN boundary (`old_boundary = user_indices[-2]`) but the Anthropic cache protects by MESSAGE INDEX (`get_cache_prefix_count = message_count-2`). A big tool result enters at FULL size (cached), then the NEXT round a new user msg advances `old_boundary` past it and it is truncated FOR THE FIRST TIME while STILL inside the cached prefix → rewrites cached bytes → whole body re-billed. The 2026-06-22 idempotency marker only stops RE-truncation; it does nothing for the first-time-inside-prefix edit. Happens EVERY round because exactly one more result crosses the boundary inside the prefix each turn — exactly the monotonic write climb.
- **Fix (root cause):** `_truncate_old_tool_results` now takes `conv_id` and skips any index `< get_cache_prefix_count(conv_id)` (the cached prefix floor) in addition to the turn boundary. A result is truncated only once it has scrolled OUT of the prefix — by then it is no longer cached, so the edit costs nothing. Context-control goal preserved; only the TIMING shifts to a cache-safe round. `rebuild_messages_with_history` passes `conv_id` through. When no cache state exists (fresh conv / non-cached provider) `prefix_n=0` → prior turn-boundary-only behaviour. Tests: `TestTruncationCachePrefixGate` (3) in `test_server_message_store.py` — skips inside prefix / truncates once out / falls back without conv_id; negative control confirms old logic mutates idx 3, new logic leaves it byte-identical.
- **Fix (display, part 1 the user asked for):** `_compute_write_breakdown` (orchestrator.py) now splits the residual: on a round carrying `cacheBreak`, the bulk above a realistic framing allowance (`_ENVELOPE_MAX_TOKENS=800`) is reported as `recacheBody` (+ `recacheCause`), NOT `envelope`. All sub-items still sum EXACTLY to `write`. `finish_info.js` renders `重新缓存正文 N` as its own term tied to the 缓存失效 line. Tests: 3 new in `test_write_breakdown.py` (split on break / no-split without break / no-split when residual ≤ ceiling); existing exact-dict asserts relaxed to field checks since two keys were added.
- **Result / status:** `ast.parse`+`node --check` clean; `test_write_breakdown.py` 11/11, `test_server_message_store.py` 29/29, `test_cache_improvements.py` 43/43. Bundle `bundle-6e056323.js`. Restart to serve the backend truncation fix (this is the money fix — stops re-billing the body every round); hard-refresh for the popover term. Memory `cache-bp4-moving-tail-rebills-body` created (note: its title pins the symptom to BP4 but the ACTUAL root cause turned out to be the truncation-inside-prefix mutation, not BP4 placement — BP4 is correct). Secondary suspect `compact_cold_assistant` (no prefix guard) is off-by-default (force_compact/reactive only, which already calls notify_compaction) so not the recurring culprit — left alone.


### 2026-06-23 — `export.py --progress`: live per-file transfer view so the tar copy isn't a black box
- **User pain:** the export "is sometimes very slow" and gives ZERO feedback
  during the copy, so it's impossible to tell whether it's hung or whether it's
  silently carrying files that should have been excluded. Root cause: the actual
  copy is `_stream_tar_copy` (`tar cf - | tar xf -`) — already the fast path on
  FUSE/DolphinFS — but `tar c` ran non-verbose and the code only read stderr at
  the very END via `.communicate()`, so a multi-minute transfer printed nothing.
  And `--exclude=` misses are invisible: tar happily streams a stray
  `*_workdir/`/cache dir and you only notice from the final size.
- **Fix (opt-in, `--progress` flag):** `_stream_tar_copy(..., progress=False)`
  now, when enabled, runs `tar cvf -` (verbose → member names on stderr, archive
  on stdout) and drains that stream in a daemon thread via new
  `_tar_progress_consumer`. It prints a PERMANENT line the first time tar enters
  each TOP-LEVEL entry (`↳ dir lib` / `↳ file top.py`, kind probed against
  `ROOT`) — so an unwanted dir jumps out immediately — plus a throttled (~12fps),
  in-place `transferred N · <current file>` counter on a TTY (tail-ellipsized to
  terminal width). When stdout is piped/captured it skips the carriage-return
  animation and just emits the per-top-level lines + a final count (no CR spam in
  logs). The archive root `./` member is suppressed. Threaded the `progress` kwarg
  through `_export_personal_via_tar` / `_export_via_tar_with_sanitize` /
  `export_project` and added the `--progress` argparse flag. Default OFF →
  historical silent behavior unchanged.
- **Why not a true % bar:** would require a full file pre-count, which on FUSE is
  itself a slow tree walk (the very cost we avoid). A streaming running counter +
  per-top-level breadcrumbs gives the operator what they actually asked for
  (liveness + "what is it carrying") with no upfront walk.
- **Status:** `ast.parse` clean. Functional test on a temp tree confirmed:
  exclude honored (`--exclude=./swebench_workdir` → dir absent at dest),
  per-top-level lines correct, `./` root suppressed, final count right; `--progress`
  shows in `--help`. Pure backend script change, no bundler/test-suite impact.
  Usage: `python3 export.py --mode personal --dest ... --progress`.

### 2026-07-11 — LIVE-PG board OUTAGE root-caused + fixed WITHOUT restart; schema self-heal added; Pillar-7 tail durably deferred. Commits 6f71ea7 + a6029f5.
- **Presenting problem.** User asked why board epics "sit unclaimed many times". Diagnosis chain: (1) the 3 engine epics (block-cooldown/wait-on-path/idle-migration + park-removal) were an UNCOMMITTED-LANDING problem — landed at HEAD in a sibling's 379240e mid-session. (2) That landing left `test_project_tasks_parity` RED (stale goldens + a real `wait_paths` server_default="'[]'" fresh-table bug → stored 4-char "'[]'" not []). - **Live-PG root cause (the "felt broken many times" core).** Two postgres instances run (port 15439=data/pgdata [the server's, per env TOFU_PG_PORT], port 15435=tofu-meituan). The server's DB stored `_schema_version=38` (=HEAD code) but all 5 engine columns were ABSENT. `init_db` version-cache fast-path (`_schema_pg.py:797`) returns before the ADD COLUMN block (line 659) when stored==code — so a RESTART provably would NOT heal it (and would kill 2 live siblings). Version-write (833) and per-column ALTERs (659) are NOT atomic across restarts; on FUSE each `ALTER ... NOT NULL DEFAULT` takes 260-280s, so a prior run committed the version but a later ALTER failed/timed-out → current-by-version-but-column-missing → every boot fast-paths past the fix = silent permanent degradation.
- **Fix WITHOUT restart.** Ran the 5 idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` via `_pg_admin_dsn()` (port 15439, verified `inet_server_port()`=15439 = the column-less DB the server serves). One-at-a-time (blocked_until 0.x s, block_count 260s, block_reason 281s, wait_paths/dispatch_target 0.0s once table hot). `audit_log('manual_ddl_migration', approved_by=...)`. Verified: `read_board` OK (4 open epics, no column error); 101 rows, all 5 columns present+populated.
- **Durable recurrence fix — 6f71ea7's sibling a6029f5.** New `_CRITICAL_COLUMNS` registry + `_missing_critical_columns(conn)` probe run BEFORE the fast-path (mirrors the existing `heal_orphan_tables` slot): version-current-but-critical-column-missing → force full DDL migration to converge. Read-only, best-effort (probe failure never blocks boot), missing-TABLE skipped, version-AGNOSTIC (does not touch _SCHEMA_VERSION so it stays HEAD's 38). Seeded with the 5 engine columns. TDD `tests/test_pg_critical_column_selfheal.py` 5/5 (reports-missing / all-present / absent-table-skipped / probe-failure-best-effort / registry-covers-5). Per-hunk staged mine-only (excluded the co-resident v39 bump + Pillar-7 DDL); fresh-worktree gate at a6029f5: self-heal present, v39+Pillar-7 absent, _SCHEMA_VERSION=38, 5/5 green.
- **Pillar-7 tail = DEFERRED, board pt_facabf6c173e498c (depends_on pt_a86386ef).** Foreign-hunk audit found the "tail" entangled with FOUR other uncommitted sibling epics in the shared files (esbuild-minify in js_bundler.py [28 refs]; charter-CRUD in api_v1/project.py [8 refs]; project_commit-tool in conversation.py [5 refs]; message-delete in routes/conversations.py). project_commit dry-run said "10 clean" = FALSE-CLEAN (byte-identity attributes pre-existing foreign hunks to me because they predate my first touch). Declined the peer's commit request with the factual blocker; recorded the fold-in spec (pg+sqlite→v39; pure-new files; per-file Pillar-7-only hunks) on the epic. v39 reconcile + Pillar-7 work preserved on disk, nothing staged.
- **LESSON.** A schema version integer as a proxy for "all DDL applied" is unsafe when version-write and column-ALTERs aren't atomic across restarts on slow storage — add a column-presence self-heal before the fast-path. And project_commit's byte-identity gate can FALSE-CLEAN a file whose foreign hunks predate your first edit; the hunk-level audit vs HEAD is authoritative, not the tool's optimistic read.
